summary:
Tesla Motors, Inc. filed its Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the period ended March 31, 2016. Total revenues were $1.15 billion, up from $939.9 million in the prior-year quarter, while net loss widened to $282.3 million, or $2.13 per share, from $154.2 million, or $1.22 per share. Gross profit was $252.5 million, with gross margin declining to 22.0% from 27.7%. As of March 31, 2016, cash and cash equivalents stood at $1.44 billion, total assets were $9.19 billion, total liabilities were $8.18 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $970.4 million.

During the quarter, Tesla produced 15,510 vehicles, including approximately 2,650 Model X units. The company unveiled Model 3 and received over 325,000 reservations within one week. It targets 80,000 to 90,000 Model S and Model X deliveries in 2016 and advanced its plan to produce 500,000 total vehicles to 2018. Capital expenditures for 2016 are now expected to be roughly 50% higher than the prior $1.5 billion estimate. Gigafactory cell production is expected to begin in the fourth quarter of 2016.

Customer deposits totaled $391.4 million. Tesla had approximately 20,690 vehicles under its resale value guarantee program and about $565.0 million drawn under its $1.0 billion asset-based credit agreement as of March 31, 2016, of which $350.0 million was repaid in April 2016. The company also has outstanding convertible senior notes due 2018, 2019, and 2021.

This MIT lecture introduces Discrete Stochastic Processes, emphasizing that the central challenge is finding appropriate probability models for real-world problems rather than merely solving well-posed mathematical exercises. The professor distinguishes between probability as a branch of mathematics, where models are precisely specified, and its application to complex systems in business, economics, biology, and engineering, warning that flawed models—such as those used in financial risk analysis—can lead to catastrophic failures even when the underlying mathematics is correct. The course will cover counting processes, Poisson processes, renewal processes, Markov chains, and random walks/martingales, with applications to communication systems, networks, queuing, and risk management. The lecture reviews Kolmogorov’s axioms: a sample space, a collection of events, and a probability measure satisfying non-negativity, the probability of the entire sample space equaling one, and countable additivity for disjoint events. Consequences discussed include the probability of the empty set being zero, the complement rule, and the union bound. Independence is defined as the probability of an intersection equaling the product of individual probabilities, and combined models use Cartesian products. A random variable is defined as a function from sample points to real numbers, with the requirement that the set of sample points mapping to values less than or equal to any real number constitutes an event, ensuring the distribution function always exists. The professor stresses the importance of understanding these foundational definitions and proofs rather than relying solely on intuitive computation.

XYZprinting is presenting the MfgPro220 xPF ultrafast 3D printer at Rapid + TCT 2018. Priced at $19,950 with a 16-liter build volume, it uses LSPc technology and machine learning to produce functional parts at up to 1Z cm per minute, with cognitive software, sensors, and cloud or on-board controls. XYZprinting also announced a partnership with BEGO and Nexa3D for digital dentistry, plus a strategic investment and manufacturing agreement with Nexa3D.

Sensient Technologies (NYSE:SXT) reported quarterly EPS of $0.80, beating the $0.78 consensus estimate, with a 9.13% net margin and 16.73% return on equity. The stock opened at $78.53 with a $3.48 billion market cap. The company declared a $0.30 quarterly dividend payable March 1, yielding 1.53% with a 42.70% payout ratio. KeyCorp raised its price target to $84 with an "overweight" rating, while Zacks upgraded to "hold." Sensient manufactures colors, flavors, and fragrances.

IBM and The Weather Channel developed a 3.2MB Android app for developing countries that uses mesh networking to send messages phone-to-phone via Bluetooth and Wi-Fi across 200-500 feet when centralized networks fail. Each download adds a network node, though critical mass remains a challenge. The technology supports messaging, uses digital signatures for security, and works on older 2G networks. It is launching in Asia, Latin America, and Africa.

The message returns to the House a bill that would donate public lands or land scrip to states and territories to endow colleges teaching agriculture and the mechanic arts, detailing proposed acreage, value, and conditions requiring states to establish colleges within five years and replace any lost funds. The author objects that the bill is inexpedient and unconstitutional. It argues the donation would deprive the Treasury of critical revenue, flood the market with land scrip, depress land prices, and harm veterans’ bounty-land warrants. It warns that using federal resources for state purposes erodes the constitutional separation of powers, that the federal government cannot enforce the fund’s proper use, and that the grant would injure existing colleges and new states by encouraging speculation. Finally, it asserts Congress lacks constitutional authority to give away public lands for education, interpreting "dispose of" as meaning to sell, and distinguishes prior school land grants to new states as measures to enhance settlement and land value.

Collagen production decreases with age, prompting interest in supplements. Collagen, comprising about 30% of natural protein, provides structural support to skin, tendons, and bones. The most common types are I through V. Supplements are primarily animal-derived—marine, bovine, porcine, and chicken—and often contain types I, II, and III. Hydrolysed collagen may be most effective. Potential benefits include improved skin, nail growth, bone density, joint health, muscle support, and possibly hair growth. Studies suggest 2.5 grams daily may benefit joints and skin, 5 grams may improve bone density, and 15 grams with resistance training may increase muscle mass. Experts recommend third-party tested products for at least 12 weeks, though research continues. Natural collagen production can be supported through a balanced diet including protein, vitamin C, and bone broth.

Blue Cross Blue Shield of Mississippi awarded Bell Academy a grant in November 2016 for a new physical education building, which parent volunteers and community members constructed behind the school. Students and teacher Joyce Aycock say the indoor space allows for more activities and less noise than the previous open indoor area and outdoor concrete space. A horizontal rock-climbing wall will be added before the building's ribbon cutting at 9:30 a.m. Friday.

Bethesda Softworks announced Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus for Nintendo Switch on June 29; the physical version requires a download. Bethesda has strongly supported the Switch, also porting Doom and Skyrim. The Switch's hybrid portable/TV design helped it achieve the largest twelve-month install base of any console.

Council officials detailed measures to tackle congestion in the city's north, particularly around Southway and Tamerton Foliot. They are coordinating with utility companies to minimize roadwork disruption through restricted hours and manual traffic controls. For the Derriford Transport Scheme, bus lane restrictions on Tavistock Road have been suspended to maintain two lanes, construction is proceeding concurrently to shorten the programme, and signal timings at George Junction have been adjusted. Lane marking changes at Budshead Roundabout are pending a safety audit, and central reserve work on Tavistock Road should finish within weeks. Roadwork details are available on the council's website and through media alerts.
January 3, 2024 medRxiv preprint "Phase angle clusters in bioimpedance: An alternative to body mass index" is not peer reviewed.

The Department of Higher Education and Training is integrating NSFAS into tertiary systems amid protests over delayed payments. Minister Naledi Pandor called funding delays for continuing students unacceptable, citing system integration challenges that hinder registration data exchange and bursary agreement generation. Government allocated nearly R7.2 billion in 2018 for university and TVET bursaries, with NSFAS baseline funding rising to over R35.3 billion by 2020-21, plus R105 million for administrative capacity. The DA criticised NSFAS and Pandor for failing to specify how many students are affected, why delays occurred, and when funding will be paid.

The Drive concept is a widely used football passing play featuring a 10–12 yard basic route and a 3–4 yard shallow crossing route from the same side, creating a natural triangle read for the quarterback while stressing linebackers. It is effective against man coverage and Cover 4, but struggles against Cover 2 and Cover 3 due to excess underneath defenders. The quarterback peeks the post pre-snap, then progresses through the X go route, slot shallow cross, TE basic route, and running back check-down. Receivers stay on the move against man coverage and sit in zone voids against zone. Variations include pairing it with bunch formations to create rubs against man, or attaching it to the backside of other schemes as a quick outlet against blitzes.

ADT is viewed as undervalued versus newly listed peer Verisure due to strong revenue growth, improving profitability, and high recurring revenue. Partnerships with Google and State Farm, debt reduction, and share buybacks boosting shareholder yield to 11% support the business. Customer churn and static subscriber numbers remain challenges, but investments in AI and smart home solutions aim to improve retention. Peer comparisons suggest a 12-14x P/E ratio implies over 33% upside.

Kim Ok-kiun, a rebel refugee in Japan, was assassinated in Shanghai by Hong Chong-oo, who was turned over to Chinese authorities for transport to Korea. In Tokyo, Japanese police arrested a man plotting to kill rebel Pak Yung-ho; a conspirator took refuge in the Korean legation, and police forcibly removed him after extradition was refused. Kim's body and murderer were delivered to Korean authorities; the body was mutilated in Seoul, and foreign representatives declined to issue an official protest. Uprisings occurred in three southern Korean provinces against oppressive officials; the Korean Government requested U.S. naval support, American missionaries were withdrawn from the interior, and a former official urged more frequent visits by American ships.

This November 2, 2000 email from Joe Bryant of Cheatsheets.net provides Week 10 fantasy football matchup analysis and introduces a new "On Target" feature tracking wide receiver pass targets. The analysis is divided into Passing Game and Rushing Game matchups, categorized as Locks, Prime Matchups, Even Matchups, Downside Matchups, and Defensive Slam Dunks based on whether they favor the offense or defense. Favorable passing offenses include New Orleans, San Diego, Oakland, Green Bay, Indianapolis, and Kansas City, while unfavorable passing matchups include Washington, Atlanta, Dallas, San Francisco, the New York Giants, Philadelphia, Tennessee, Cincinnati, Cleveland, Arizona, and Pittsburgh. Favorable rushing offenses include Washington, the New York Giants, the New York Jets, Indianapolis, New Orleans, Tampa Bay, Denver, and St. Louis, whereas difficult rushing matchups include Carolina, Minnesota, Kansas City, Seattle, Detroit, Cincinnati, Arizona, Cleveland, San Francisco, New England, Tennessee, and Pittsburgh. The article cites defensive statistics such as yards allowed and fantasy points allowed by position, and notes player injuries and lineup changes including Jeff George starting for Washington and Terrell Davis returning for Denver.

This document describes the Versioned Chip Endorsement Key (VCEK) certificate and the AMD Key Distribution System (KDS) interface for software developers supporting virtualized host environments that employ Secure Encrypted Virtualization-Secure Nested Paging (SEV-SNP) technology. The VCEK certificate chain consists of the product-specific AMD Root Key (ARK), the intermediate AMD SEV Key (ASK), and the VCEK, which is a unique per-chip Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (ECDSA) key bound to a specific Trusted Compute Base (TCB) version. VCEK certificates conform to X.509v3, are generated at the time of request, are valid from one day prior to issuance through seven years after issuance, and contain custom extensions describing TCB elements that differ between processor families. The KDS provides an HTTP interface hosted at https://kdsintf.amd.com to retrieve VCEK certificates, certificate chains, and Certificate Revocation Lists. Requests require a case-sensitive product_name determined via CPUID and a hardware ID that is 64 bytes for Family 19h processors and 8 bytes for Family 1Ah processors. The interface allows pre-fetching certificates with future Security Patch Level values to facilitate seamless firmware upgrades and imposes rate limits on identical requests.

UPMSP will declare UP Board Class 10 and 12 results on April 29, 2018, at 12:30 pm on upresults.nic.in and upmspresults.up.nic.in. The Class 10 exams were held February 6-22, 2018, and Class 12 exams February 6-March 12, 2018. Students can also check results via SMS or alternative websites including results.nic.in, indiaresults.com, and examresults.net.

The speaker notes tight checking and difficulty forechecking because Hasek handles the puck outside his net. Frustration with scoring and defense has been addressed. The team must refocus defensively, correct breakdowns against Detroit, and trust coaching decisions.

The invention provides a vehicle radar sensing system utilizing a two-dimensional array of transmitting and receiving antennas disposed at a vehicle. A control applies two-dimensional Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) processing to outputs of the array, achieving an enhanced two-dimensional virtual aperture for improved horizontal and vertical angular resolution simultaneously, rather than via time-multiplexed scans. In an embodiment, the array includes twelve transmitting antennas in three rows of four and sixteen receiving antennas in four columns of four, with receiving antenna columns disposed between spaced apart rows of transmitting antennas to function as 192 virtual receivers. The system detects objects exterior to the vehicle for driver assistance applications, including autonomous or semi-autonomous driving, parking assist, blind spot detection, cross traffic alert, automatic emergency braking, and pedestrian detection. The system may optionally fuse radar data with exterior camera image data and generate alerts or control vehicle systems responsive to detected objects.

Jennifer Thompson mistakenly identified Ronald Cotton as her rapist, leading to his wrongful conviction. Eleven years later, DNA testing exonerated Cotton and matched Bobby Poole. Thompson discusses memory failure under trauma. She and Cotton later became friends, and both are involved with Healing Justice.

Russia's central bank cut its key rate by 50 basis points to 9.25 percent, deeper than expected, as inflation hit a post-Soviet low. It forecasts 4 percent inflation by year-end, plans further gradual cuts, and warned of volatility and $40 oil risks. The next meeting is June 16.

Mauricio Pochettino named a 26-player United States men's national team roster for October friendlies, with players reporting to camp in Austin on Oct. 4. The team will play on Oct. 10 in Austin, Texas, and again four days later in Commerce City, Colorado. The roster features mostly established players after a more experimental September window. Christian Pulisic, who has scored six goals and added two assists for AC Milan this season, is included. Weston McKennie returns for the first time since March, and Antonee Robinson receives his first call-up of 2025 after recovering from knee surgery. Tanner Tessmann and Aidan Morris were selected following strong club performances. Several players were omitted due to injuries or form, including a Gladbach defender and a Norwich City forward, and Pochettino is expected to address one notable absence later on Thursday.

This work presents the fabrication and cryogenic characterization of hybrid NbN/Si-SiGe coplanar waveguide (CPW) microwave resonators for quantum circuits. The devices consist of four CPW resonators capacitively coupled to a feedline, fabricated on a 100 nm NbN film sputtered onto an n-doped Si/Si₀.₇Ge₀.₃ quantum well wafer. A novel fabrication step employs deep reactive-ion etching (SF₆/C₄F₈) through the heterostructure stack in the resonator gaps to a depth of 1 μm, shifting substrate–vacuum interfaces away from high-field regions to reduce intrinsic loss. Transmission electron microscopy confirms the epitaxial quality of the SiGe heterostructure but reveals oxygenation in the 4 nm Si cap layer.

Two samples (S1 and S2) with identical geometries were measured across four cooldown cycles over two years at temperatures up to 1.7 K. Fundamental resonance frequencies were approximately 5.04–5.60 GHz at 50 mK. Internal quality factors (Qi) for S1 ranged from ~860 in the single-photon regime to ~1064 at higher powers, while S2 exhibited Qi values of ~500–600. The Qi remained stable over the two-year period, indicating robust ageing resistance. Power- and temperature-dependent spectroscopy reveal two-level system (TLS) effects, but modeling shows that scattering losses from structural imperfections and the wafer's low surface resistivity dominate over TLS and quasiparticle losses. The coupling quality factor (Qc) remained constant across all measurements.

The study establishes a CMOS-compatible platform integrating NbN superconducting resonators with Si/SiGe semiconductor heterostructures. The use of NbN provides tolerance to magnetic fields and elevated temperatures, while the deep-etch fabrication strategy mitigates material-induced losses. Though the extracted gatemon relaxation time (~14 ns) requires improvement, the work offers a scalable pathway toward hybrid superconducting–semiconductor quantum computing architectures.

The speaker, soon to leave the Presidency and return to private citizenship, thanks his administration and the American people for their support over the past four years. He affirms his confidence in the nation's strength and describes the Presidency as powerful yet constrained by law, custom, and the need for public and congressional support. He warns that single-issue and special-interest groups distort national purpose, stressing that the President must represent all Americans and preserve constitutional authority. He pledges support to the incoming President and highlights three urgent global issues: the escalating danger of nuclear weapons, the need to protect the environment and natural resources, and the primacy of human rights. He argues that American values are fundamental to national unity and global leadership, notes ongoing efforts to ensure a smooth transition and to pray for American hostages in Iran, and concludes by expressing gratitude and bidding farewell.

Minnesota’s Edina School District teaches “white privilege” in kindergarten via the Melanin Project, where K-2 students trace and color hands to reflect skin tones. Professor Shreena Gandhi co-authored an article claiming white people practicing yoga contributes to white supremacy and cultural appropriation.

The ongoing government shutdown may face pressure to end by mid-October as an Oct. 15 military pay date for 1.3 million active-duty service members could force legislators and the White House to compromise. While both sides remain entrenched on the fiscal budget, missing the pay period risks public anger and could prompt a temporary continuing resolution. Prediction markets indicate a 71% probability the shutdown continues past Oct. 14. Other potential catalysts include TSA disruptions, expiring WIC benefits, and Thanksgiving travel, though analysts warn the shutdown could extend into November if military pay is resolved separately.

Subconscious biases regarding gender, race, and ethnicity can lead employers to overlook qualified candidates, as demonstrated by studies showing unequal hiring outcomes. To build a diverse workforce, employers should use behavior-based language in job postings, remove names from resumes before review, require skills-based challenges before collecting other applicant information, and analyze post-interview instincts to ensure they are not based on prejudice.

High-dosage tutoring programs like Teach For America’s Ignite Fellowship improve academic outcomes—middle school math scores grew up to 2.5 times the expected rate and elementary reading up to three times faster—while fostering student confidence and belonging. Effective implementation requires structured training, ongoing coaching, and technology that expands rather than replaces human relationships. Tutoring also functions as a teacher pipeline: research indicates that serving as an Ignite tutor nearly triples the likelihood of applying to Teach For America’s teaching corps, with 550 fellows joining the corps to date. The piece concludes that tutoring should be treated as a core instructional strategy and educator pipeline rather than merely an emergency intervention.

The 2025 World Grand Prix saw Rob Cross defeat Nijman in a last-leg decider, Ratajski beat the first seed 2-0, Menzies knock out the eighth seed, and Cullen beat James Wade 2-0. Noppert faces Wattimena and Anderson faces van Barneveld, with a Round of 16 matchup between van Gerwen/van Duijvenbode and Smith/Gurney.

This case study examines Amazon.com, Inc. on the 20th anniversary of its 1997 IPO, by which time it had grown from an online bookstore founded by Jeff Bezos in 1995 into the fourth-largest U.S. public company. Amazon prioritized long-term market leadership and free cash flow over short-term profitability, reinvesting heavily in expansion, research and development, and customer experience. The company diversified through product category expansion, acquisitions such as Audible, Zappos, and Quidsi, and the launch of the Prime membership program in 2005. It developed consumer electronics including the Kindle, Fire devices, and Echo, and created Amazon Web Services (AWS) in 2006, which represented the genesis of the cloud infrastructure as a service industry. Despite notable failures like the Fire Phone, Amazon maintained a culture tolerant of failed experiments. Financially, shareholders earned nearly a 64,000% return over 20 years, with a market capitalization of $458 billion, though cumulative net income from 1997 to 2016 totaled only $4.9 billion. The case includes financial statements, segment information for retail and AWS, and non-GAAP free cash flow disclosures illustrating Amazon’s focus on sustainable long-term growth.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2020 describes its business, operations, and risks. The company is a technology provider focused on productivity, the intelligent cloud and intelligent edge, and personal computing. It responded to the COVID-19 pandemic by shifting to remote work and virtual events while noting ongoing uncertainty. The filing outlines sustainability commitments, including a goal to be carbon negative by 2030 and to remove all carbon emitted since 1975 by 2050, supported by $1 billion in climate investments. It also details initiatives to address racial injustice and expand digital skills. Microsoft reports financial performance through three segments: Productivity and Business Processes (Office, LinkedIn, Dynamics), Intelligent Cloud (Azure, server products, enterprise services), and More Personal Computing (Windows, Devices, Gaming, Search). It markets products through OEMs, direct sales, and resellers, and announced the closure of its physical retail stores in June 2020. As of June 30, 2020, the company employed approximately 163,000 people. Listed executive officers include Chief Executive Officer Satya Nadella and Chief Financial Officer Amy E. Hood. The filing identifies risks such as intense competition from diverse business models, execution challenges in cloud services, acquisition integration (including the $7.5 billion GitHub purchase), potential impairment of goodwill and intangible assets, cybersecurity threats, and misuse or disclosure of personal data.

Ethereum block production currently relies on out-of-protocol MEV-Boost with trusted relays. The upcoming Glamsterdam upgrade introduces enshrined PBS (ePBS, EIP-7732), which eliminates relays by integrating the builder-proposer auction into the protocol and granting builders additional time to reveal execution payloads and blobs via dual deadlines. This design creates a “free option problem”: after the proposer commits at slot start, a builder can strategically withhold blobs or the payload to prevent an unfavorable block from becoming canonical—particularly when late-arriving external market information moves against on-chain trades—without protocol penalty, thereby degrading network liveness and user experience. The paper presents the first systematic study of this issue, combining theoretical predictions with empirical analysis of historical blocks. Results indicate that while the average option exercise probability is low (0.82%), it rises sharply during volatile periods (to 5.5% of blocks), especially for builders with high CEX-DEX flow dependence. The authors evaluate two mitigations: shortening the option window, which reduces exercise probability but sacrifices scalability; and imposing penalties, including a dynamic mechanism using online gradient descent that achieves low exercise rates with an average penalty of 0.104 ETH.

Ghana's major gold mining firms welcome new government tests by the Precious Minerals Marketing Company to certify export values and tighten control. PMMC officials have access to gold rooms and pre-shipment processes. Ghana, Africa's second biggest gold producer, earned $5.78 billion from exports last year. Akufo-Addo says $5 billion in exports to the United Arab Emirates are unaccounted for; industry watchers attribute this to smuggled artisanal gold, while a small-scale mining ban remains.

China's foreign exchange regulator said capital outflow pressure eased in 2016 and yuan flexibility will increase in 2017. Authorities took steps to curb capital flight and attract foreign investment. Final 2016 data showed a $196.4 billion current account surplus and $26.3 billion capital and financial account surplus. The yuan weakened 6.5 percent against the dollar in 2016 but has gained nearly 1 percent this year.

On October 24–25, 2001, Enron Corp. placed Chief Financial Officer Andrew Fastow on a leave of absence and named Jeff McMahon—previously Enron’s treasurer and head of its industrial-markets group—as his replacement. The move followed an SEC inquiry into partnerships run by Fastow that had engaged in off-balance-sheet transactions with Enron, transactions that contributed to a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity and $35 million in third-quarter losses. Chairman Kenneth Lay stated that replacing Fastow was necessary to restore investor confidence after Enron’s stock price collapsed roughly 50 percent in a week, closing at $16.41 and dragging down shares of other energy-trading companies such as Dynegy. News reports noted that McMahon had earlier raised internal concerns about potential conflicts of interest in the partnerships. Analysts responded with continued uncertainty, several downgrading Enron to “sell” or “market perform” amid fears of undisclosed liabilities, complex financial structures, and possible credit downgrades. Shareholder lawsuits also alleged that Enron misled investors and that executives profited from insider sales ahead of the stock’s decline.

Mary Brunkow, Fred Ramsdell, and Shimon Sakaguchi won the 2025 Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine for discovering regulatory T cells, which prevent the immune system from attacking the body. Sakaguchi identified the cells in 1995; Brunkow and Ramsdell tracked down a fatal autoimmune mutation in mice in the 1990s and revealed mutations in people in 2001. The Nobel Assembly announced the prize on October 6.

The Yankees will start Paul Goldschmidt at first base and bat him sixth in ALDS Game 4 against the Blue Jays, benching Ben Rice. Goldschmidt has started only one postseason game, while Rice started all three games against the Blue Jays and is 2-for-11 in the ALDS. Keeping Rice on the bench provides lineup flexibility, as he can catch if Austin Wells is pinch-hit for or pinch-hit for Goldschmidt later.

Donnell Gibson, a behavior intervention specialist and junior varsity basketball coach at Como Park Senior High in St. Paul, was named an Excellent Educator. After experiencing childhood homelessness and saving a family of 10 from a fire in 2015, he founded the Gibson Foundation. The program mentors young, African-American, inner city men through motivational speakers, college tours, and basketball, using his experiences to help students focus on school and life.

A Business Insider correspondent placed a Temu order after the company resumed direct shipping from China, which it had paused over the summer. Despite concerns about U.S. tariffs and the end of the de minimis exemption for packages under $800, the order arrived within two weeks with no extra duty fees. Previously, Temu and Shein had avoided tariffs by shipping only from U.S. warehouses. Some items were defective, but the author confirmed a month later that no tariff bill arrived. Research noted Shein prices had risen about 30% when tariffs took effect.
Geary County deputies arrested Isaac Torgerson on suspicion of aggravated assault Saturday after a passenger in a Dodge Ram 2500 allegedly waved a gun at another vehicle near Fort Riley.

The email compiles news articles dated October 23, 2001, regarding Enron Corp. Cauley Geller Bowman & Coates filed a class action lawsuit alleging securities fraud and material misrepresentations between January 18, 2000, and October 17, 2001, related to undisclosed losses in broadband, limited partnership investments managed by the CFO, and impaired assets, following a $1.01 billion third-quarter charge and over $1 billion equity reduction. The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission sought information on transactions with limited partnerships managed by CFO Andrew Fastow, causing Enron's stock to plunge over 20 percent to $20.65. Despite meetings where Chairman Kenneth Lay assured analysts the company had no more surprises, investors fled, with shares falling 42 percent in one week and 76 percent year-to-date; some analysts maintained "strong buy" ratings while others downgraded the stock. Enron asked Citigroup to arrange a $750 million loan amid concerns that a possible Moody's downgrade could cut off its $3 billion commercial paper program; the company disclosed at least $3.5 billion in available credit lines. Articles detailed complex off-balance sheet financing through partnerships such as LJM2, Whitewing, and Marlin II, which removed debt from Enron's books but led to a $1.2 billion equity reduction and concerns about asset values and debt covenants. A Texas Monthly article traced Enron's aggressive corporate culture, "rank and yank" performance reviews, and rapid expansion under Jeff Skilling and Ken Lay, noting Skilling's abrupt August resignation after six months as CEO. During a conference call, Lay disputed investor Richard Grubman's valuation of Marlin II water assets and declined to raise earnings guidance despite a planned 60 million share reduction. Separately, AES Corp. complained to Indian Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee about government interference in Orissa state, following a similar September appeal by Enron over its Dabhol project; AES threatened to withdraw, joining Cogentrix and Enron in reducing foreign power investments in India.

A February 28, 2001 Enron email forwards news articles from February 23, 2001 regarding California’s energy crisis. Governor Gray Davis announced a tentative “agreement in principle” for the state to buy Southern California Edison’s transmission grid for approximately $2.7 billion and continued negotiations with PG&E and San Diego Gas & Electric to purchase 26,000 miles of utility transmission lines, aiming to help the utilities manage nearly $13 billion in debt and avoid bankruptcy. For the first time since January 13, California had no power alerts as supplies improved, though the state had spent close to $2 billion on electricity and requested another $500 million, with total costs projected to reach $2.6 billion to $3 billion by mid-March. The California Public Utilities Commission ruled that PG&E and Edison are not responsible for power costs above their ratepayer revenue, potentially shifting hundreds of millions to taxpayers. Legislators introduced a bill (SB 47X) under which small generators producing about 30 percent of the state’s power agreed to cut their prices roughly in half. Davis faced criticism for setting and missing multiple deadlines, while Republicans struggled to attack him on the issue due to their prior support for deregulation. Other articles noted local opposition to an Enron hydroelectric plant and power lines in the Cleveland National Forest, a proposal to give rate discounts to residents living near power plants, and one legislator returning utility campaign contributions.

A positive meeting addressed game plan adjustments. While physical play is part of the game this time of year, the team must focus on speed and skating. The goaltender has been great despite the team not playing its best, giving them chances to win both. They must bring their best effort, as the game becomes more mental, and bring the intensity and emotion of the home crowd.

Hungary's education system is shaped by its demographics, multiparty parliamentary government, and economy. Public education has been compulsory since 1868, currently for ages six to sixteen, with a structure spanning pre-primary through post-secondary schooling. Teacher preparation varies by level, with recent reforms introducing five- to six-year undivided programs emphasizing pedagogy and practical training.

Hungary established its first separate school for deaf students in 1802 and maintains a long history of special education. A professional committee diagnoses disabilities and recommends services, though parents make final placement decisions. The Hungarian Act on Public Education of 2011 defines disability categories and guarantees free compulsory primary and accessible secondary education. As of 2019, 60% of special needs students learn in inclusive settings. Special education teachers complete a four-year university program in one of eight specialties, followed by a two-year compulsory traineeship and ongoing in-service training every six years.

Current challenges include difficult diagnosis procedures—particularly for autism—limited physical accessibility in older school buildings, and incomplete inclusion, as many students with disabilities still attend specialized schools. Teacher preparation issues include reliance on frontal teaching methods, insufficient training for general educators regarding disabilities, low wages that are the lowest in the OECD, and higher attrition in public compared to private and church-run schools. The article recommends improving early diagnosis referral systems, increasing building accessibility, expanding teacher training in special education, raising teacher salaries, and adopting retention practices from church-run institutions to better support students with disabilities.

Donchian Channels, invented by Richard Donchian, are calculated using an upper band (the high of the last N bars) and a lower band (the low of the last N bars). Originally designed as a trend-following indicator for breakouts, they have historically worked well for commodities and currencies but are less effective for stocks in modern, faster-moving markets. Backtesting on the S&P 500 from 1960 to 2021 showed a 4.57% unleveraged CAGR, below buy-and-hold returns of 7.15%, though with lower drawdown. Conversely, using the channels as a mean-reversion indicator for stocks—tested on SPY from 1993 to 2021—yielded better results, with a 5-day lookback producing a 9.16% CAGR, small drawdowns, and a high win rate. The authors note that Donchian Channels are visually similar to but distinct from Bollinger Bands, and conclude that the tool remains effective for trend-following in commodities and currencies and as a mean-reversion strategy for stocks.

Stock futures were little changed after the S&P 500 ended a seven-day winning streak. President Donald Trump suggested some furloughed federal workers may not receive back pay during the ongoing government shutdown. The remark followed a draft White House memo arguing that employees on unpaid leave are not guaranteed retroactive pay, which conflicts with recent Office of Personnel Management guidance and a 2019 law stating furloughed workers shall receive back pay. The administration claims Congress must specifically appropriate those funds. The stance is viewed as pressure on Senate Democrats to support Republicans' stopgap funding bill. Trump warned of substantial permanent layoffs if the shutdown continues. Democrats are demanding Affordable Care Act tax credit extensions in any short-term deal. The American Federation of Government Employees criticized the administration's argument as a misinterpretation of law.

Canadian lumber shares fell after BMO downgraded the sector ahead of NAFTA talks, citing U.S. duties, a stronger Canadian dollar, and litigation. BMO said a lumber dispute resolution was unlikely soon, with little substantive negotiation, but long-term prospects appear positive.

Treatment options for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) are limited by universal resistance to androgen signaling inhibitors and frequent taxane resistance. The androgen receptor splice variant AR-V7 is constitutively active and correlates with docetaxel resistance, whereas the ARv567 variant remains sensitive to docetaxel. In M12 isogenic prostate cancer cells, AR-V7 expression increased microtubule (MT) polymerization rates by over 40% compared to AR-wild-type cells, while AR-wild-type did not drastically alter MT dynamicity. MT dynamics are analyzed computationally by automated tracking of EB1/EB3 comets in confocal microscopy using Kalman filtering and spatiotemporal clustering. Patient-derived organoids from primary, lymph node, and distant metastatic tissues were established, with tumor cell selection optimized by reducing Y-27632 ROCK inhibitor concentration, as high-grade tumor cells are more resilient to apoptosis than benign tissue. In androgen-independent mCRPC, circulating tumor cells can be as small as approximately 6.6 µm in diameter, only slightly larger than leukocytes, and are detectable via PSMA rather than AR expression. MT dysregulation is linked to drug resistance through multiple mechanisms: pVHL loss or GSK3β-mediated phosphorylation increases MT turnover; Op18 (STMN1) upregulation attenuates MT polymerization and is associated with taxane resistance; ERG fusion proteins inhibit effective docetaxel-tubulin engagement; and both faster and slower than normal MT turnover rates are hallmarks of resistance. Low doses of MT inhibitors can paradoxically increase polymerization rates. The work proposes correlating live-cell MT dynamics signatures with gene expression in organoids to predict drug susceptibility, validating sensitization strategies—such as targeting the tubulin transcriptome, using NAD+ to restore MT homeostasis, or GSK3 inhibitors—in patient-derived xenografts. Ultimately, quantitative profiling of MT dynamics in patient cells ex vivo is suggested to inform personalized tubulin inhibitor selection and dosing.

While further testing is needed and clinical use remains years away, the technique could help address the worldwide shortage affecting millions who require transplants due to corneal blindness or scarring.

This study describes a reproducible method to prioritize AI-detected chest X-ray abnormalities for urgent lung cancer reporting. Across seven Greater Manchester trusts, researchers analyzed 1,282 retrospective CXRs from confirmed lung cancer patients and 13,802 prospective primary care CXRs using the Annalise Container CXR AI system in shadow mode. The system detects 124 findings, which were grouped into priority categories and evaluated via three strategies based on prevalence ratios: maximizing specificity, maximizing sensitivity, or balancing both through clinical judgement. The final strategy, incorporating clinical review of empirical data, selected 32 high-priority findings and achieved 95.87% sensitivity, 79.11% specificity, and 99.95% negative predictive value. By systematically combining observed prevalence in cancer and non-cancer cohorts with expert input, the approach offers a data-driven framework to address radiology workload demands, reduce diagnostic delays, and support safe AI integration prior to live clinical deployment.

Select Security acquired Intelligent Technology Inc. and Carolina Security Group, adding nearly 1,000 customers, key team members, and a Charlotte branch to consolidate western North Carolina operations. The Non-Farm Payrolls (NFP) report, released monthly by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics on the first Friday at 8:30 a.m. ET, tracks job changes in non-agricultural businesses and is a key indicator of U.S. economic health. It heavily influences Federal Reserve interest rate decisions and causes significant volatility across financial markets. Higher-than-expected readings are generally viewed positively for the economy and the U.S. dollar, while lower readings are negative. The bond market is the most affected, as strong job growth raises expectations of interest rate hikes, which depresses bond prices, while weak data has the opposite effect. Equities tend to react positively to strong data, and the report is closely followed by forex traders for USD direction. Backtests on SPY since its 1993 inception show an average open-to-close gain of 0.09% on NFP release days, but negative average returns in the one to five trading days following. TLT backtests show an average negative return of -0.02% on release days and poor performance thereafter. The article concludes that NFP data is difficult to predict and that backtests reveal no reliable trading edge from macroeconomic number releases.

The ICRC launched the nationwide public awareness campaign "Pehlay Zindagi" in Islamabad to urge citizens to give way to ambulances. Running until December 2017 with over 30 partners, the initiative includes a pledge application, website, and media outreach as part of the Health Care in Danger project. The lecture explores pseudorandomness in d-regular graphs parameterized as (n, d, λ) graphs, where all non-trivial adjacency eigenvalues are at most λ in absolute value. Via the expander mixing lemma, a small λ ensures the graph has low discrepancy between actual and expected edges across vertex subsets.

Deterministic constructions such as Cayley graphs are presented. Paley graphs, formed from quadratic residues modulo a prime p ≡ 1 (mod 4), serve as an explicit example; computing their eigenvalues through roots of unity and Gauss sums shows their non-trivial eigenvalues are small relative to their degree, confirming they are pseudorandom.

For Cayley graphs, a theorem by Conlon and Zhao establishes that the discrepancy property (DISC) and the eigenvalue property (EIG) are equivalent up to a constant factor, a relationship that fails for general graphs. The proof employs Grothendieck’s inequality, which states that the semidefinite relaxation of a bilinear form over ±1 vectors exceeds the original maximum by at most a constant factor.

The lecture then presents the Alon–Boppana bound: for fixed degree d and growing n, the second largest eigenvalue satisfies λ₂ ≥ 2√(d−1) − o(1). This bound is optimal and arises from the spectral radius of the infinite d-regular tree. Two proofs are outlined: one constructs a distance-weighted test vector and applies the Courant–Fischer characterization; the other uses the trace method, lower-bounding closed walks of length 2k by counting walks on the infinite d-regular tree via Catalan numbers.

Forecasters mistook a 70-mile wide radar signature over Colorado for birds before identifying it as swarms of Painted Lady butterflies. They say flying insects are uncommonly detected by radar. The Supreme Court, Appellate Division, reversed Solomon Montlake’s conviction for first-degree grand larceny and granted a new trial. The court rejected Montlake’s plea of former jeopardy based on a prior dismissal of the jury during the prosecution’s case, ruling that a trial judge may discharge a jury before submission when a substantial reason arises during trial, and that the prosecutor’s repeated accusations that defense counsel was a criminal justified the dismissal. The court distinguished this from post-submission discharges, which are limited by statute. It also held that cross-examining an alibi witness about unpaid rent was improper, as it did not show moral turpitude, but found this insufficient to reverse. The court reversed, however, because the trial judge erroneously instructed the jury that they could not acquit on the alibi defense unless convinced the defendants “could not have been” at the crime scene—a standard requiring exclusion of any possibility. The court held that the burden of proof as to alibi is not on the defendant, and if alibi evidence raises a reasonable doubt about presence, acquittal is required; the general reasonable doubt charge did not cure this specific error.

The passage documents AMD AGESA software interfaces and initialization procedures for processor and platform bring-up. It describes entry points including AmdInitReset for minimal post-reset processor initialization and execution cache allocation; AmdInitEarly for full processor initialization and power management configuration; AmdInitPost for main memory initialization and transition to post-memory operation; AmdInitEnv for transferring temporary artifact data to permanent buffers; AmdInitMid for graphics display configuration; AmdInitLate for generating operating system information tables such as ACPI, DMI, WHEA, CRAT, and CDIT; and AmdInitRtb, AmdInitResume, AmdS3LateRestore, and AmdS3FinalRestore for suspend and resume operations. Each procedure specifies required parameter structures, dependencies such as stack availability, and status codes. The text also defines required and optional host environment call-outs, including buffer allocation and deallocation, system reset, SPD data reading, AP task execution, and various hooks for memory and voltage adjustments. Additionally, it details build-time options and platform configuration elements specified in a platform-specific Options.c file, which control inclusion or removal of features such as memory types, interleaving, ACPI table generation, processor family and socket support, and VRM properties.

The bank sued Hepner on a promissory note. The trial court excluded the testimony, holding the cashier’s knowledge was not attributable to the bank, and directed a verdict for the bank. The appellate court affirmed, ruling an agent’s knowledge is imputed to the principal only if the principal would have received notice acting for itself, and declined to presume the payee would have disclosed the fraud to the bank’s board. The rule for a new trial was discharged.

The passage details SD Memory Card command protocols and operational specifications. It defines APP_CMD (CMD55) for application-specific commands (ACMDs), including rules for command interpretation, APP_CMD status bits, and exceptions for ACMD41. It describes the Switch Function command (CMD6), which configures function groups such as Access Mode, Command System, Driver Strength, and Power Limit through Mode 0 (query support and power consumption) and Mode 1 (set function) operations, returning 512 bits of status data with busy indicators and maximum current consumption. The text specifies command formats, response types (R1, R1b, R2, R3, R6, R7), CRC7 and CRC16 protection, Card Command Classes (CCC), and card state transitions. It distinguishes between SDSC, SDHC, and SDXC card behaviors, including byte versus block addressing, block lengths, and write protection. Clock control guidelines, read/write/erase timeout conditions, and UHS-II command differences are provided. The passage extensively defines Speed Class specifications for SDSC/SDHC and SDXC, covering Allocation Units (AU), Recording Units (RU), performance metrics (Performance Write, Performance Move, Read Performance), FAT and Continuous Information update cycles, and the Speed Class Control Command (CMD20) for optimizing stream recording. It also covers the SD Status structure, task status, power limit definitions for UHS modes, and requirements for host power supply capability.

A study of U.S. mortality data from 1999 to 2020 proposes excess deaths and years of potential life lost (YPLL) as national metrics to track Black-White health inequities. Analyzing CDC WONDER data for non-Hispanic Black and White individuals under 85, researchers estimated 658,356 excess deaths among Black females and 1,154,108 among Black males, with approximately 35 million and 47 million excess YPLL, respectively. After declining from 1999 through the early 2010s, age-adjusted excess mortality and YPLL plateaued until 2019, then reversed sharply in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic, reaching levels comparable to 1999. Heart disease drove the most excess mortality, while perinatal conditions had the highest YPLL rates. The greatest YPLL disparities occurred among infants, whereas excess mortality generally increased with age after childhood. The authors attribute these persistent disparities largely to social factors and structural barriers, and recommend annual public reporting of race-based excess deaths and YPLL to spur accountability and new interventions.

A Simple Moving Average (SMA) is a technical indicator that calculates the average closing price of a security over a specified period to identify trend direction and potential support or resistance levels. Backtests indicate that short-term SMAs (e.g., 5-day) are effective for mean-reversion strategies—buying when the price crosses below and selling when it crosses above—while long-term SMAs (e.g., 200-day) work better for trend-following, buying when the price crosses above and selling when it crosses below. The 200-day trend-following strategy produced a 7.89% CAGR with roughly half the maximum drawdown of buy-and-hold (28% versus 56%), and the best crossover result was buying above the 200-day SMA and holding 200 days for a 10.93% average return per trade. Shorter periods increase sensitivity and trading frequency but may cause more false signals, whereas longer periods smooth volatility. Compared to the Exponential Moving Average (EMA), the SMA assigns equal weight to all prices, creating more lag; the EMA reacts faster by weighting recent prices more heavily. The SMA can be applied to non-price data such as volume or economic indicators, but it can mislead with seasonal or cyclical stocks and generate false signals in range-bound markets. It is a lagging indicator, and its starting point can skew results in volatile markets. While an SMA could theoretically be zero if all closing prices were zero, this is practically impossible. The optimal SMA period varies by asset and requires backtesting. Moving average strategies have become less potent since the 1990s due to widespread computerization, though they remain usable, often best as part of a multi-parameter strategy such as a trend filter.

The document describes embodiments for multicarrier communication systems, including carrier aggregation and scheduling in 5G/NR and LTE networks. It details physical layer transmission mechanisms such as OFDM, radio resource structures, frame and slot configurations, and uplink/downlink signal processing. The text outlines network architectures involving base stations (gNB, eLTE eNB), 5G core networks (NGC), and interfaces (NG, Xn, Xx), supporting multi-connectivity, dual connectivity, and tight interworking between 5G and LTE RANs with master/secondary base station roles, cell groups (MCG/SCG), and bearer configurations (MCG, SCG, split). It describes Timing Advance Groups (TAG), random access procedures, PUCCH offloading to secondary cells, and time alignment timers. The document further covers centralized gNB deployment scenarios with central unit (CU) and distributed unit (DU) functional splits, network slicing, and Licensed Assisted Access (LAA) with Listen-Before-Talk (LBT) procedures for unlicensed spectrum. Additionally, it addresses logical channel mapping to bearers and transmission time intervals/numerologies, logical channel prioritization, and bandwidth part (BWP) management—including configuration, activation/deactivation, default and initial active BWPs, BWP switching timers, control resource sets, search spaces, and associations between downlink and uplink BWPs for paired and unpaired spectrum.

The DAWN-plasma trial was a randomized, multicenter, open-label phase II study comparing four units of high-titer convalescent plasma plus standard of care (SOC) to SOC alone in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. Between May 2020 and January 2021, 489 patients were randomized 2:1. The primary endpoint—proportion alive and free of mechanical ventilation at Day 15—showed no significant difference between the plasma (83.7%) and control (84.1%) groups. No significant differences were found in secondary endpoints, including mortality or clinical status at Days 15 and 30. Serious and severe adverse events were similar between arms, and transfusion-related side effects occurred in 5.9% of the plasma group. The intervention did not alter the natural course of antibody titers, though higher baseline and Day 6 neutralizing-antibody titers correlated with better outcomes. The study concluded that early high-titer convalescent plasma did not significantly improve clinical outcomes.

A prospective hospital-based follow-up study of 228 adults with acute intestinal obstruction was conducted at Amana, Mwananyamala, and Temeke regional referral hospitals in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, from December 2021 to July 2022. Participants had a median age of 34 years and a male-to-female ratio of 3:1. Surgical diagnoses included adhesions (98 cases), hernia (48), volvulus (37), and abdominal tumors (20). Post-operative outcomes were 76% discharged home, 5.3% mortality, 9% surgical site infection, 0.9% wound dehiscence, 0.4% anastomotic leak, 3.5% referred to another facility, and 5.3% unknown. The median hospital stay was 4 days. The authors note that adhesions were the leading diagnosis, differing from prior developing-country reports where hernias typically predominate, and suggest this may reflect referral bias. They also note that the 5.3% mortality rate is within the wide range reported in literature, and that tests for confounders and interactions were non-significant.

Averaging down is a trading strategy where an investor buys more shares after a price decline to lower the average purchase price and reduce the breakeven point. While this can increase profitability if prices recover, it risks amplifying losses if prices continue to fall. The strategy may suit long-term investors or planned scale-in approaches, but is generally discouraged for short-term traders lacking knowledge of the underlying company. A backtest on the S&P 500 ETF (SPY) using RSI signals and two 50% equity entries showed similar returns to a non-averaging strategy but with smoother performance, improved risk-adjusted returns, and lower drawdowns. The article concludes that stocks are the best asset class for averaging down due to mean reversion tendencies, and success depends on backtesting and having a margin of safety.

This work examines incorporating structural information into Bayesian optimization (BO) for therapeutic antibody development. BO suits low-data optimization of developability and binding properties given costly wet lab experiments. The authors investigate how to integrate structural information into surrogate models, which antibody properties benefit, whether antibody-specific models outperform general protein models, and if structure is necessary. They propose a protein language model "soft constraint" as a novel sequence-only prior. BO employs uncertainty-aware surrogate models, typically Gaussian processes, and acquisition functions to optimize expensive black-box functions.

This study compared a chest radiograph-based biological aging clock (CXR-Age) with first-generation (Horvath Age) and second-generation (DNAm PhenoAge) epigenetic clocks in 2,097 Project Baseline Health Study participants. CXR-Age correlated moderately with chronological age (r=0.50), while epigenetic clocks correlated highly (r≈0.93–0.95), and CXR-Age acceleration was not significantly associated with epigenetic age accelerations. CXR-Age and DNAm PhenoAge acceleration were both associated with higher coronary artery calcium, greater 10-year ASCVD risk, lower pulmonary function (particularly DLCO), worse frailty and disability metrics, while Horvath Age showed no significant associations. CXR-Age associations with functional measures were significant in adults as young as 45, unlike DNAm PhenoAge. Plasma proteomic analysis identified CDH13 and ApoD as significantly associated with CXR-Age acceleration, and thirteen proteins with DNAm PhenoAge acceleration, including CDH13. Radiographs with high CXR-Age acceleration frequently showed lung abnormalities. The authors conclude that CXR-Age and DNAm PhenoAge capture different aspects of biological aging, and routine chest radiographs could enable opportunistic biological age screening to inform clinical decisions.

This medRxiv preprint describes PhenoID, a natural language processing pipeline that extracts and normalizes dysmorphic phenotypic findings from electronic health record notes to Human Phenotype Ontology terms. The system uses a two-step transformer-based architecture—an extractor to identify finding spans and a normalizer to map them to HPO IDs—and was trained on a manually annotated corpus of 3,826 organ system observations. Evaluated against six existing normalizers, PhenoID achieved state-of-the-art performance with an F1 score of 0.717 on normalization and 0.715 on combined extraction and normalization. Error analysis with gold-standard spans yielded an F1 of 0.820, revealing that extraction limits overall performance and that common normalization errors stem from ontology gaps, descriptive phrasing, and attention misplacement. The authors note limitations in author diversity and semantic understanding, suggesting future improvements may incorporate large language models.

SpaceX is launching an HPE-built supercomputer, the “Spaceborne Computer,” to the International Space Station aboard a Falcon 9 rocket. Unlike typical space hardware, which is physically hardened against radiation, this off-the-shelf system relies on special software to detect dangers and make safety adjustments. Capable of one trillion calculations per second, it could process massive amounts of data—such as high-resolution satellite imagery—on board, reducing the need to transmit it all to Earth. HPE engineer Mark Fernandez expects the device to boot up on September 4, after which his team will run tests and monitor it for one year. NASA and HPE say success could pave the way for more powerful computers and future deep-space missions, including Mars, where communication delays make autonomous data processing essential.

Since 2008, the Personalized Medicine Conference in South San Francisco has addressed genomic health with biotech, pharmaceutical, and medical leaders. On June 2, 2017, SF State University’s Department of Biology will host Personalized Medicine 10.0, reviewing a decade of advances under the theme "Has It Changed Your Life?" Topics include bioinformatics, oncology, gene therapy, and genome editing. Keynote speaker Amylynne Santiago Volker will describe the first case of a life saved by genetic sequencing and stress the need for provider training, accurate interpretation, and insurance coverage. Founded by SF State professor Michael Goldman and Genentech alumni, the conference features prominent speakers and is open to the public.

Japan raised April sentiment assessment, first upgrade in four months, after upbeat BOJ tankan, but maintained economy is recovering gradually. Cabinet Office said business conditions are improving, leaving unchanged assessments of consumer spending, capital expenditure and exports. It expects gradual recovery as employment and wages improve, but overseas uncertainty warrants attention.

Methods, apparatus, and computer-readable media are provided for automatic classification of objects in 3D point clouds in near real-time. A processor obtains a 3D point cloud representing an external surface, extracts surface normals to define a translational and rotational invariant coordinate system, and computes a first classification statistic (e.g., a spin image) and a second classification statistic (e.g., a covariance matrix) to estimate membership in N classes. If the first and second estimates disagree, a third classification statistic (e.g., iterative closest point) is computed by fitting the point cloud to model point clouds of only the two candidate classes, and the object is assigned to the best-fit class. An associated apparatus includes a laser source, splitter, optical coupler, optical detector, and processor configured to perform these steps. The passage also describes LIDAR range detection techniques, including chirped heterodyne and homodyne systems, k-d tree nearest-neighbor searching, and experimental classification results.

Apple Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended April 1, 2017. For the quarter, net sales were $52.9 billion, up 5% year-over-year, with net income of $11.0 billion and diluted earnings per share of $2.10. The filing also notes the European Commission’s State Aid Decision ordering Ireland to recover additional taxes from the Company, which Apple is appealing.

Research published in PNAS demonstrates that limiting nutrients can harness competition among pathogens to prevent drug resistance and extend existing drug effectiveness. In a malaria mouse study, researchers manipulated a nutrient used by parasites alongside traditional drugs. When mice were given the nutrient, drug-resistant strains emerged in 40 percent of treated mice, causing treatment failure. When the nutrient was limited, infection did not rebound in a single mouse; resistant parasites did not grow even when initially present in far greater numbers than typical, confirming competition rather than nutrient scarcity alone prevented resistance. Researchers suggest identifying resources for which drug-resistant strains have greater needs than sensitive strains and limiting those resources as a combination therapy. This ecological approach could be integrated into drug development to extend the lifetime of drugs and treat infections even when drug-resistant pathogens are present.

The London-St. Thomas unemployment rate rose to 5.5 per cent in September as the labour force dropped by 3,000. Only about 75 per cent of the 25-54 population is working, ranking last among 15 Ontario cities. A King's University College study found half of working adults have full-time permanent jobs, while the rest are in precarious employment linked to stress, depression, and family strain. Across Canada, unemployment held at 6.2 per cent; Ontario added 35,000 jobs and unemployment fell to 5.6 per cent, the lowest since 2000.

NVIDIA’s Blackwell RTX 50 Series architecture introduces fifth-generation Tensor Cores supporting FP4 quantization, which reduces AI model memory requirements by more than half compared to FP16 while maintaining quality. The fourth-generation RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection throughput and add hardware-accelerated Linear Swept Spheres for rendering hair and fine geometry. Mega Geometry technology uses Cluster-level Acceleration Structures and Partitioned Top-Level Acceleration Structures to enable high-fidelity ray tracing of complex scenes with dynamic level-of-detail and high object counts. Shader Execution Reordering 2.0 improves thread coherence and neural shading performance. The new AI Management Processor, a dedicated RISC-V scheduler, offloads GPU context scheduling from the CPU to reduce latency and improve multitasking. DLSS 4 features Multi Frame Generation, producing up to three additional frames per rendered frame with lower VRAM usage, and transitions to transformer-based AI models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA to improve image stability and detail. Blackwell also introduces neural shaders via the Cooperative Vectors API, enabling real-time techniques such as Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. For video, the ninth-generation NVENC and sixth-generation NVDEC add 4:2:2 chroma sampling support and improve encoding and decoding speeds and quality, while DisplayPort 2.1b UHBR 20 delivers up to 80 Gbps bandwidth. Power efficiency innovations include advanced power gating, separate voltage rails for cores and memory, accelerated frequency switching, and ten-times-faster sleep state entry. The product lineup comprises the GB202-based GeForce RTX 5090, the GB203-based RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti, and the GB205-based RTX 5070.

Sara Zaske's daughter, who had not wanted a phone in Germany where few classmates owned them, felt she needed one upon moving to California and finding herself the only student in her class without a smartphone. Cell phone ownership among children varies widely by country: about 51% of German children ages 6 to 13 have mobile phones; across Europe, about 46% of children 9 to 16 own smartphones; in the United States, about 45% of children 10 to 12 have smartphones with service plans and 42% of children 8 and younger have tablets; in South Korea, about 72% of children 11 to 12 own smartphones; in Taiwan, usage rises from 45% at age 11 to 71% at age 15; and in Australia, the median age for first phone use is 8. The American Academy of Pediatrics states there is no "right" age for a child to receive a phone, but recommends avoiding digital media for children under 18 to 24 months and limiting screen time to one hour for children 2 to 5.

A new embedded atom method (EAM) potential for the tungsten-hydrogen-helium (W-H-He) system was developed to simulate radiation damage in fusion reactor materials. Building upon the Mason W-H potential, the model targets accurate binding energies and relaxation volumes for light-gas defects, addressing limitations of existing potentials that overestimate relaxation volumes and poorly describe voids. Using a generalized Finnis-Sinclair formulation that permits negative electron densities, the authors fitted the potential to density functional theory (DFT) data—including defect formation energies, binding energies, relaxation volumes, and gaseous configurations—via a global minimization algorithm followed by local refinement. The potential incorporates a weakly attractive tungsten-helium interaction on the order of a few meV, a repulsive helium embedding function that avoids attraction to negative electron densities, revised helium-helium interactions fitted to high-pressure hexagonal close-packed DFT data and experimental virial coefficients, and hydrogen-helium interactions validated against vacuum dimer binding energies. Qualitative DFT charge density analysis confirms non-negligible electronic interactions for helium within the tungsten lattice.

The Renewable Energy Alaska Project is training residents from diesel-powered Southeast Alaska villages as home energy assessors through the Home Energy Leader Program, which runs through July 31. Participants from communities including Kake, Angoon, Hoonah, Yakutat, and Metlakatla learn to conduct $25 household assessments, identifying simple upgrades—such as switching to LED bulbs or using insulated coffee pots—that can reduce electric bills by nearly 10 percent. Republic Services has been charging Southern Nevada commercial property owners trash fees—including container delivery, removal, exchange, and industrial dry run fees—that were not approved by local lawmakers. The Las Vegas City Council plans to introduce an ordinance codifying several of these fees. Municipal ordinances require city councils and county commissioners to approve such charges, yet elected officials across Las Vegas, North Las Vegas, Henderson, and Clark County were unaware of or could not recall approving them. A commercial waste consultant said she stopped paying certain container fees five years ago after Republic failed to provide proof of approval. This Mendelian randomization study investigated causal relationships among gut microbiota, plasma metabolites, and fibromyalgia (FM) using European-ancestry GWAS summary statistics from the MiBioGen, Chen et al., and FinnGen consortia. Bidirectional and multivariable MR analyses identified six gut microbial taxa causally associated with FM: family Enterobacteriaceae, genus Butyricicoccus, genus Coprococcus1, and order Enterobacteriales were protective, while genus Eggerthella and genus Ruminococcaceae UCG005 were risk factors. No reverse causality was detected. Eighty-two plasma metabolites were associated with FM, with pathway enrichment highlighting caffeine metabolism, α-linolenic acid (ALA) metabolism, and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and incretin synthesis, secretion, and inactivation. Specific metabolites included AFMU (protective) and 7-Methylxanthine and 1-Methylxanthine (risk) in caffeine metabolism; EPA and SDA (protective) in ALA metabolism; and EPA (protective) and Oleoyl-EA (risk-related) in the GLP-1/incretin pathway. Mediation analysis showed that 2,3-dihydroxypyridine and palmitoylcholine mediated the effects of family Enterobacteriaceae and order Enterobacteriales on FM, accounting for 14.91% and 12.34% of the total effect, respectively. The authors suggest that dysregulation in these metabolic pathways contributes to inflammation, oxidative stress, and energy metabolism abnormalities in FM, and propose dietary interventions—limiting caffeine, increasing omega-3 intake, adopting a low-glycemic-index diet, and reducing oxalate consumption—to alleviate symptoms. Limitations include the lack of demographic data for subgroup analyses, exclusive European ancestry, and the need for experimental validation.

The passage describes implantable medical devices, including cochlear implants and other hearing prostheses, comprising a magnet encompassed by a body. In exemplary embodiments, structural components such as plates within the body are configured to move away from one another upon initial rotation of the magnet when subjected to an externally generated magnetic field (e.g., from an MRI). This movement tensions elastomeric body material or resilient elements, generating a counteracting force that limits further magnet rotation and reduces torque imparted to the device's support apparatus. Some embodiments include a magnet apparatus within a container where the magnet can revolve relative to the container while rotation is constrained by the plates. The elastomeric body may have a slit to enable passage of the magnet for insertion or removal. Various embodiments detail different plate geometries, materials, interlocking features with the body, and alternative housing and spring arrangements to tune resistance forces.

The article identifies three bullish candlestick patterns validated through backtesting on the S&P 500 via the SPY ETF from 1993 to October 2021: the Bearish Engulfing Pattern, Three Outside Down Pattern, and Bullish Harami. Trades used a straightforward exit rule: closing the position when the current day's close exceeded the previous day's high. The Bearish Engulfing Pattern produced 296 trades with a 0.53% average gain, 5% CAGR, 71% win ratio, and 16% maximum drawdown. The Three Outside Down Pattern generated 112 trades with a 0.7% average gain, 2.3% CAGR, 78% win ratio, and 14% maximum drawdown. The Bullish Harami resulted in 306 trades with a 0.33% average gain, 3.1% CAGR, 76% win ratio, and 25% maximum drawdown. The authors note that while candlestick patterns are popular for visualization, most lack predictive value, and quantitative traders often criticize them due to reliance on anecdotal evidence rather than quantified tests.

The RSI, ADX, and IBS indicators are used for short-term mean-reversion and trend-following strategies. RSI (0-100) measures momentum, with values above 70 indicating overbought and below 30 oversold conditions; backtesting suggests 2-3 day periods work best. ADX measures trend strength without indicating direction, with 5-10 day periods and 30-40 thresholds performing best. IBS (0-1) is a mean-reversion indicator where low values signal bullish and high values bearish conditions. Individual backtests on QQQ and SPY showed risk-adjusted returns of approximately 32% (IBS), 18% (RSI), and 10.3% (ADX). Combining two indicators on SPY yielded 270 trades, a 0.86% average gain per trade, 56% risk-adjusted return, and only one losing year (2018 at -5.5%). On QQQ, the combined strategy averaged 1.3% per trade with no losing years since 2000. The strategy was published in October 2020 and has shown positive out-of-sample performance.

The Chaikin Oscillator, developed by Marc Chaikin in the 1980s, measures stock momentum and accumulation/distribution by oscillating around zero. It is calculated in four steps: determining the money flow multiplier, calculating money flow volume, updating the Accumulation/Distribution Line (ADL), and subtracting a longer EMA of the ADL from a shorter one, commonly using 3- and 10-day periods. The indicator signals buying pressure when above zero and selling pressure when below, and generates signals through crosses and divergences. Quantified tests of ten S&P 500 trading strategies—including zero-line crosses, flipped mean-reversion criteria, and combinations with RSI—found no significant profitability. Results included a 2.4% CAGR for zero-cross strategies and modest metrics for RSI combinations, such as 216 trades averaging 0.3% per trade, a profit factor of 1.6, and drawdowns of 17–18%. The authors concluded the oscillator showed limited predictive value in their tested strategies, though positive values indicate accumulation and negative values indicate distribution.

The present application is a continuation of prior U.S. applications and incorporates by reference related concurrently filed applications. The disclosure describes an autonomous vehicle management system (AVMS) that controls autonomous vehicle operations safely using artificial intelligence and machine learning. The AVMS receives sensor data to generate and update a three-dimensional internal map representing the vehicle's state and environment. Based on the map, goals, and safety considerations, it generates a plan of action and controls vehicle systems to execute it. The system uses techniques including convolutional neural networks for object detection and reinforcement learning for planning. To improve safety, the AVMS dynamically controls sensor behavior regarding what, when, and how data is captured and communicated; simulates “what-if” scenarios by modifying internal map parameters to evaluate and eliminate unsafe actions; generates model confidence scores by comparing inferring data points to training datasets to override untrusted predictions; and provides users with planned future actions and reasons via a user interface. For reinforcement learning, it employs a Safety Sanity Index and interruptible commands to override unsafe actions. The AVMS comprises subsystems including sensors interface, localization, perception, planning, controls, and information. The perception subsystem builds the internal map using a multi-layered graph data structure storing object attributes and environmental information at varying resolutions. The planning subsystem generates plans, performs what-if simulations, and can prune decision trees. The controls subsystem executes plans and monitors vehicle dynamics. The information subsystem outputs vehicle state and planned actions to users.

The disclosure provides methods and apparatus for acknowledgement/negative acknowledgement (ACK/NACK) feedback in wireless networks with multiple transmission reception points (TRPs). A base station may send a user equipment (UE) information indicating physical downlink control channel (PDCCH) monitoring occasions for each TRP, whether cross-TRP ACK/NACK feedback is allowed, and if allowed, rules for performing ACK/NACK feedback bundling. The base station may also indicate a downlink assignment index (DAI) definition specifying whether DAIs from the TRPs are independent (counting grants per TRP) or joint (counting grants across all TRPs and scheduled carriers). The UE receives the configuration, determines an ACK/NACK codebook size based on the monitoring occasions and DCI/DAI information, and transmits either joint ACK/NACK feedback in a physical uplink control channel (PUCCH) according to the bundling rules or separate ACK/NACK feedbacks to individual TRPs. In multi-TRP downlink, transmissions may use a single DCI granting one transport block across layers from different TRPs, or multiple DCIs each granting one transport block per TRP. Bundling rules may specify joint ACK when data from at least one TRP is successfully received or joint NACK when data from at least one TRP fails, depending on whether payloads are the same or different. The DAI definition supports networks with tight or loose TRP coordination. The UE may send individual PUCCHs per TRP via time-division multiplexing, different resources, or concurrent transmission from multiple uplink TRPs.
