Alan Oppenheim discusses designing a digital low-pass IIR filter using impulse invariance and bilinear transformation, based on analog Butterworth prototypes. The squared magnitude of an analog Butterworth filter is 1/(1 + (jω/jω_c)^(2N)), with cutoff frequency ω_c and order N; its poles are equally spaced on a circle of radius ω_c in the s-plane, and the stable filter uses the left half-plane poles. The digital filter specifications are a passband edge at 0.2π, a stopband edge at 0.3π, passband ripple within 1 dB, and stopband attenuation below −15 dB. For impulse invariance, analog frequencies are related by Ω = ω/T. Solving the Butterworth equations gives N ≈ 5.8858, so N = 6 is chosen; to compensate for aliasing, the passband is met exactly at 0.2π and the stopband specification is exceeded at 0.3π. For the bilinear transformation, critical digital frequencies are pre-warped to analog frequencies. With T = 1, the equations give N ≈ 5.3, which is rounded up to N = 6. Because aliasing is not a problem, the stopband is met exactly at 0.3π and the passband is exceeded. The bilinear design yields slightly better high-frequency attenuation than the impulse-invariant design. These methods generalize to bandpass, bandstop, and highpass filters via frequency transformations, and the next lecture will cover FIR filter design.

MDC breakaway leader Thokozani Khupe criticized male rivals as cowardly and defended splitting from Nelson Chamisa, whom she accused of hijacking the party. Khupe was elected leader at an extraordinary congress where Obert Gutu, Nixon Nyikadzino, and others won senior posts. She defended the election of Linda Masarira as spokesperson, citing 50-50 gender representation in the standing committee. Chamisa sought a court interdict to block Khupe from using the MDC name. The Bulawayo High Court reserved judgment, and the Zimbabwe Electoral Commission stated that parties sharing names or symbols must resolve such disputes in court before nomination day.

The defensive end (DE) is a prioritized position in modern football, responsible for disrupting opposing offenses by stopping the run and pressuring the quarterback. Lining up on the edge of the offensive line, DEs use a rare combination of size, strength, and athleticism to execute gap-sound assignments, force ball carriers inside, and win one-on-one matchups against tackles to generate sacks, hurries, and batted passes. Typically standing 6'3" to 6'7" and weighing 270–290 pounds, the position requires strength, quickness, recognition, and consistent technique. Elite players like Reggie White, Bruce Smith, and Dwight Freeney change defensive trajectories by generating pass rush without blitzing, allowing more defenders in coverage, and setting the tone against the run.

Sierra Linarducci's father purchased $10,000 in bitcoin when it was valued at $4,000 to help pay for her Indiana wedding. Since then, its value has quadrupled to over $16,000, covering the entire wedding and extras; he pays vendors using a BitPay card. While bitcoin has gone mainstream, experts warn of its volatility and risk, with some comparing it to gambling. Others see potential in blockchain technology. The family feels fortunate about the investment timing.

The Inquiry is assembling research for peace conference planning, covering geography, demographics, economics, law, and military affairs, with preliminary reports due from January to mid-February 1918. The Executive Committee will edit material into brief, graphic digests and conference issue briefs, limiting costs to essential staff and supplies. A December 22, 1917 memorandum assesses the Allied military situation regarding the Berlin-Bagdad project, stating that while offensives into Austria-Hungary are no longer possible, Allied control of Saloniki, Bagdad, Palestine, and Arabia nullified German threats to the Suez Canal, Red Sea, and Persian Gulf if these areas remain in non-German hands.

Utah County hired former federal public defender Kathryn N. Nester to represent Tyler James Robinson, the 22-year-old accused of fatally shooting conservative activist Charlie Kirk on Sept. 10 at Utah Valley University. Robinson could face the death penalty. The defense contract is expected to cost $750,000 over the next year, while the prosecutor’s office will receive about $600,000. A county commissioner said funding both the defense and prosecution is mandatory but unfortunate for taxpayers.

After poor first two games, the team won twice at home with third and fourth line contributions. They now have better legs and puck movement, stressing smart defense, creating scoring chances without risks, and citing patience, speed and road success for confidence.

AncestryDNA tests show Britons average 16,000 relatives, though most think they have six cousins. North West residents have 20,000, while the South East, South West and East Anglia are below average. It marks DNA Day.

The TLV321x devices include an internal Power-On Reset (POR) circuit that holds the output low for up to 32µs after the supply voltage crosses 1.65V during ramp-up; once the supply meets the minimum voltage and the delay elapses, the output reflects the differential input state. The comparator produces a logic low output when the input voltage is below a reference voltage and logic high when above it, with propagation delay varying between low-to-high and high-to-low transitions. Overdrive voltage beyond the reference influences propagation delay, with smaller overdrive increasing delay. The devices provide 1.8mV of internal hysteresis, but external hysteresis can be added via positive feedback to prevent noisy chatter. Inverting hysteresis configurations require a three-resistor network referenced to the supply, while non-inverting configurations require a two-resistor network and a voltage reference, with equations defining trip voltages and total hysteresis. A typical low-side current sensing application uses an amplifier and comparator to detect over-current conditions. Design requirements include placing a 0.1µF low-ESR ceramic bypass capacitor directly between the supply and ground pins, minimizing coupling between inputs and outputs, and avoiding parallel input and output traces without an intervening supply or ground line.

The President addresses Congress on the state of the Union, invoking Abraham Lincoln's principle that "right makes might" as the democratic faith that won the war and must guide the nation amid a global rejection of democracy for autocracy. He argues the United States must lead by example through just domestic laws and by protecting weaker nations internationally. He urges passage of a revised budget bill to establish a national budget system, noting that fiscal year 1920 receipts rose while expenditures and the public debt fell significantly. He warns that maturing war debt and railroad payments under the Transportation Act strain finances, necessitating rigid economy, salvage operations, and adequate tax revenues, including simplified income and profits taxes. He calls for medical care and vocational training for disabled veterans, and renews recommendations regarding agricultural support, cold storage regulation, price marking on interstate goods, and federal licensing of interstate corporations. He requests a supervised loan to Armenia and independence for the Philippine Islands, which have fulfilled the conditions for stable self-government.

This document standardizes the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) for Secure Encrypted Virtualization - Encrypted State (SEV-ES) and Secure Nested Paging (SEV-SNP), which protect guest register state from the hypervisor. The GHCB is a 4KB decrypted page used during Non-Automatic Exits (NAE) to selectively share guest state, while Automatic Exits (AE) require no state exposure. Version 2 introduces hypervisor feature advertisement via a bitmap, initial SEV-SNP support, and enhancements such as Page State Change, APIC ID list retrieval, VMPL execution, SNP Guest Requests, VLEK certificates, trusted I/O (SEV-TIO), and Secure AVIC. The GHCB MSR protocol enables early communication—including protocol negotiation, CPUID requests, GHCB GPA registration, AP reset hold, and termination—before the GHCB page is established. SEV-SNP guests must register the GHCB GPA. The document defines required NAE events, GHCB field usage, the VALID_BITMAP, error codes in SW_EXITINFO1/2, and protocols for MMIO, MSR, I/O, and page state changes. It also specifies the Secrets Page Guest Reserved Area format, including 64-bit message sequence numbers, and the EFI Confidential Computing Blob configuration table for passing firmware pages to the OS.

Lasik treatment is a common, pain-free eye surgery to correct vision, available in Dubai, that eliminates the need for glasses or contact lenses. Vision is fixed immediately, patients can resume most activities within 24 hours without bandages or stitches, and long-term expenses are reduced by eliminating costs for check-ups, glasses, and lenses.

The "Great American Eclipse" on August 21 will be the first total solar eclipse to cross the U.S. coast-to-coast in 99 years. The moon will pass between the sun and Earth, blocking the sun for almost an hour and a half. A total eclipse will be visible from Oregon to South Carolina, while other parts of North America will see a partial eclipse. Salem, Kansas City, Nashville, and Charleston are in the path, and many are booking hotels.

The Zipper Offense is a basketball strategy originating with the 1960s Celtics and still used in the NBA. It features a dribble-clear wing entry that allows baseline shooters to break high off ball-side down screens, creating opportunities for outside shots, point-guard dribble penetration, and strong post-ups. The offense includes structured phases with specific reads and counters against defensive actions such as overplays, switches, double teams, and sagging defenders. If the initial options are not available, it provides for ball reversal and weakside attack. The set can flow into various continuities, including motion, single/double, flex, triangle post, and side screen actions. Variations include Zipper Curl, Blocks, Back, and sideline out-of-bounds entries. Successful execution requires coordinated footwork, timing, and non-verbal communication, taught through breakdown drills. Game strategies emphasize scouting opponents and exploiting defensive weaknesses, while teams must also be prepared to defend against the offense due to its widespread use.

This paper studies the transportation of theorems about typeability in the Edinburgh Logical Framework (LF) across schematically defined contexts. When LF encodes relational specifications using higher-order abstract syntax, typing judgements involve non-empty contexts with regular structures. The authors develop the notion of context schema subsumption—based on the type subordination relation—to formalize when a formula valid under one context schema implies validity under another. This is cast within the logic L_LF and realized as a sound proof rule in the Adelfa proof assistant, enabling the reuse of metatheorems across different typing contexts.

The passage catalogs diplomatic developments involving the United States and various countries regarding German submarine warfare and neutral trade, including Latin American, Chinese, Siamese, and Liberian severance of relations with and declarations of war against Germany and Austria-Hungary; disposition of German ships seized by Brazil, Cuba, Uruguay, and others; U.S. fleet visits and South Atlantic naval cooperation; British trade restrictions, shipping controls, and mail interference; and protocols regarding diplomatic officers, enemy aliens, armed merchant ships, and neutral duties.
The Florida Second District Court of Appeal denied W.K. Neuman's certiorari petition challenging a circuit court order upholding the Board of Adjustment's fence/wall variance denial.

Coaches should address the context of soccer tackling, including general concepts, Law 12 of the Laws of the Game, and referee interpretations, before teaching specific techniques. Legal tackling is a defender’s attempt to dispossess an opponent without contact that violates Law 12; poor tackles can result in direct free kicks, bookings, or penalty kicks. Tackle type depends on player and ball positioning. Defenders should mark opponents, remain goal-side, delay and contain, maintain a cushion, and tackle only when the opportunity is right. A successful tackle may simply kick the ball away. Law 12 defines illegal contact as careless, reckless, or using excessive force, warranting direct free kicks, yellow cards, or red cards, respectively. Legal contact includes shoulder-to-shoulder fair charges with at least one foot on the ground and no excessive force. Referees assess whether the tackle is a legitimate attempt to play the ball, the force used, and the angle; clean ball contact does not override illegal contact with the opponent. Defenders must avoid two-footed lunges, late tackles, leading with cleats, and tackling from behind, while keeping one foot on the ground. Coaches should drill tackling across the field, avoid mismatched skill levels, teach attackers avoidance moves, and ensure players do not rely on a single tackling style.

Amazon launched Chime, a voice, video, chat, and online meetings service entering a crowded market. It supports group conferences up to 100 people with screen sharing and recording, offers cross-platform native apps and Google Calendar and Outlook integration, and allows attendees to switch clients without dropping the connection, backed by AWS infrastructure.

US Walmart and Sam's Club employees can earn an associate's or bachelor's degree in business or supply chain management for $1 per day after 90 days, with the company covering remaining costs at three universities. Through Guild Education, workers receive coaching and training credits. 1.4 million are eligible and 68,000 are expected to participate over five years. There is no penalty for leaving or failing to complete the degree. The program phases out a previous 15% tuition discount.

Amendment 3 (4 May 2021) notes post-hoc changes. Of 499 patients assessed, 489 were randomized. Day 15 visit was done in 434 patients and 423 had Day 30 visit; disposition in Figure 1, deviations in Appendix 8.9.

Bruce Bochy and the Texas Rangers mutually agreed to end his managerial tenure after a three-year stint that included the franchise's first World Series title in 2023 and an 81-81 finish this season. Bochy, 70, is the winningest active manager with 2,252 career wins and four World Series titles. The Rangers offered him a front office advisory role, and former Marlins manager Skip Schumaker is a potential replacement. The Giants fired manager Bob Melvin after missing the playoffs for a fourth straight season, and the Twins fired Rocco Baldelli after a 70-92 record. The Mets will retain manager Mendoza. Blue Jays shortstop Bichette hopes to return for the ALDS, while Ohtani is likely to pitch Game 3 if his series goes that far. The Red Sox will be without Giolito against the Yankees due to an elbow injury, and Willie Mays' memorabilia collection sold for over $6.5 million.

Charlotte Olson, 12, of Vorhees, New Jersey, delivered 1,303 books to Cooper University Health System for the Read and Reach Out program after collecting over 2,000 via donation boxes, businesses, and social media. She raised $250. The program, established in 1998, allows doctors to gift books to patients across 92 state sites serving 75,000 children annually. Charlotte is working toward a community service award for National American Miss Pre-teen New Jersey 2017.

U.S. Treasury yields fell sharply and the dollar initially slumped after President Trump said he favors low interest rates and that the dollar is "getting too strong," though the currency later recovered. Trump also said China is not a currency manipulator and left open re-nominating Fed Chair Janet Yellen. The drop in 10-year yields flattened the yield curve, hurting European bank stocks and pushing major European indexes lower. Asian stocks were mixed, supported by strong Chinese trade data. The euro and euro zone bond yields faced pressure from French election uncertainty. Oil prices recovered earlier losses while gold remained near a five-month high.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 26, 2020 states that the company designs, manufactures and markets smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables and accessories, and sells related services including advertising, AppleCare, cloud, digital content and payment services. The company is headquartered in Cupertino, California. For fiscal 2020, total net sales increased 6% to $274.515 billion, net income was $57.411 billion, total cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities were $191.830 billion, and total assets were $323.888 billion. The company effected a four-for-one stock split on August 28, 2020, increased its share repurchase authorization to $225 billion, raised its quarterly dividend to $0.205 per share beginning in May 2020, and repurchased $72.5 billion of common stock during the year. Key risk factors include the COVID-19 pandemic, global economic conditions, intense competition, dependence on component suppliers and outsourcing partners, intellectual property and litigation, regulatory and trade restrictions, data protection requirements, and reliance on key personnel. The company is subject to ongoing legal proceedings but, except as described in Note 10, does not expect a material loss beyond recorded accruals. As of October 16, 2020, approximately 17.0 billion shares were outstanding and there were 22,797 shareholders of record.

MeTro is elastic surgical glue made from natural protein that seals wounds in 60 seconds under UV light. Developed by University of Sydney and US researchers, it can replace stitches in organs that expand and contract, like lungs and hearts. The gel includes a degradable enzyme timed to healing, has been tested on rodents and pigs, and could treat internal wounds. Clinical testing is next. Results published in Science Translational Medicine.

Cover 3 employs four underneath droppers and three deep defenders (MOFC) to limit big plays and stop the run, while disguising alignment pre-snap and adding defenders to the run fit. The coverage forces long throws to the flats and timely throws over the middle. Offenses exploit weaknesses in the seams and flats using quick-game passes, RPOs that read the flat defender, four-vertical concepts, and flood concepts like sail that overload one side. Examples from Ole Miss, Michigan, Oklahoma, and BYU demonstrate these methods.

A proposal to locate the Organization in an internationalized district composed of part or all of the Free Zone of the Pays de Gex and a section of the Canton of Geneva is cited. A memorandum by Leo Pasvolsky outlines proposed exploratory discussions with British Colonial Secretary Colonel Stanley during his January 15–18 Washington visit. While the official topic is the Anglo-American Caribbean Commission, informal talks may address six questions on dependent territories where U.S. and British views diverge, though neither side is ready for definitive positions. The six areas are: trust territories versus colonies; independence versus self-government within empire; international accountability; a declaration of standards; regional advisory commissions; and their relation to the general international organization.

The President addresses Congress to report on the state of the Union, noting domestic prosperity in agriculture, mines, manufactures, and commerce. He states that the people have affirmed the constitutional equality of states and citizens, the inviolability of constitutional rights, and devotion to the Union, while condemning geographical parties. He criticizes certain Northern associations for attacking the Constitution and seeking to change the domestic institutions of Southern states, warning that such efforts lead toward civil war. He identifies three stages of sectional indirect aggression: agitation for emancipation in the South, obstruction of fugitive slave extradition by Northern states, and disputes over territorial slavery restrictions, defending the repeal of the Missouri Compromise line in the Kansas-Nebraska Act as a constitutional necessity because Congress lacks power to impose such domestic restrictions. He reports that disorders in Kansas, caused largely by outside intervention, have been suppressed by federal military force without bloodshed, and asserts that the President possesses no authority to supervise territorial elections. He summarizes Treasury reports showing customs receipts over $64 million, expenditures of about $60 million, and a reduction of the public debt to roughly $31 million, while urging a reduction in customs revenue. He notes the Army's operations against hostile Indians, the Navy's increased strength, Interior Department land sales and recommendations, and the Post Office's growing deficit. On foreign affairs, he reports that disputes with Great Britain over enlistment and Central America are settled or near settlement; discusses benefits of the 1854 fisheries and reciprocity treaty; notes pending negotiations with Denmark over Sound dues; declines to accede to the Paris Declaration abolishing privateering without an amendment to exempt private property from seizure by public armed vessels; states complaints against Mexico continue; withholds recognition from contending Nicaraguan factions; and details disputes with New Granada over tonnage duties, a tax on mail crossing the Isthmus, and a violent riot in Panama against U.S. citizens and the railroad company, which prompted him to station U.S. naval forces there to protect persons and property while demanding indemnity and security. He concludes by expressing satisfaction with the nation's peace and prosperity and preparing to leave office.

The NR7 trading strategy, developed by Tony Crabel in 1990, is a narrow-range volatility strategy that enters on low-volatility days. The authors backtested it on the S&P 500 (SPY) from 1993, finding a 7.8% CAGR, 0.27% average gain per trade, and 25% max drawdown, which they deemed insufficient. They optimized the lookback period without improvement, then added one undisclosed parameter, improving the average gain to 0.46%, reducing drawdown to 13%, and cutting trade frequency while maintaining a high win rate. Unlike mean reversion strategies, the NR7 does not necessarily buy on weakness, with 67% of trades entering on up days, offering portfolio diversification. The authors caution about data quality and offer the original strategy's code to Silver members.

This case study examines the 2008 global financial crisis, triggered by the collapse of the U.S. housing market following years of price inflation fueled by subprime mortgages, relaxed lending standards, and soaring household debt. By October 2008, global stock markets had plunged, credit markets froze, and the International Monetary Fund warned of systemic meltdown. MIT Sloan professors Andrew Lo and Simon Johnson offered competing frameworks: Lo argued the crisis reflected hardwired human behaviors—greed during prolonged prosperity and fear of the unknown during collapse—while Johnson blamed a banking "oligarchy" that took excessive risks, backed by implicit government support. Macroeconomic causes included the repeal of the Glass-Steagall Act, the unregulated multi-trillion-dollar derivatives market (notably mortgage-backed securities and credit default swaps), increasingly close Wall Street-Washington relationships, and a global pool of money that doubled between 2000 and 2008 and sought higher-yield investments. The U.S. government responded with the Troubled Asset Relief Program (TARP), the Public Private Investment Program to purchase toxic loans, and stress tests for the 19 largest banks. Johnson criticized these measures as insufficient and advocated government-managed receivership to break up and re-privatize failed banks, arguing anything "too big to fail" is too big to exist. For the long term, Lo recommended more effective regulation emphasizing transparency, creation of a Capital Markets Safety Board to investigate financial failures, new risk-based accounting standards, corporate governance reforms including placing quantitative experts in management and having risk officers report directly to boards, banning corporate campaign contributions, and expanding financial technology education. By early 2009, markets had stabilized modestly, but the ultimate effectiveness of government interventions and the full extent of collateral damage remained unknown.

The nation, though unprepared, has entered the war primarily to defend its national rights and honor, recognizing that the nation's fate and the safety of the world depend on the western battlefront of Europe. It commits to sacrifice to make America and the world safe and to crush barbarity, while outlawing any nation violating international compacts. Regardless of potential allied disasters, it will fight on, making the world's cause its own, testing popular government's capacity for self-defense and establishing a renewed, loyal American citizenship.

SIG Plc named Ernst & Young as auditor after UK regulators began investigating Deloitte's audit of its 2015 and 2016 statements, focusing on cash and supplier rebates. SIG is reviewing historic accounts after whistleblowing allegations of profit overstatement, but maintained full-year profit expectations.

Canada's S&P/TSX composite index rose for a seventh consecutive day to a record high, led by financial services gains following strong Canadian and U.S. economic data. U.S. stocks opened little changed. Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen said delaying rate hikes would be unwise without specifying timing, while expressing uncertainty about Trump administration policies. Strong U.S. retail sales and consumer price data bolstered rate hike prospects. Oil prices fell below $56 per barrel after a report showed a larger-than-expected rise in U.S. crude inventories, signaling ample supply despite OPEC's record compliance with output cuts.

North Wales Police's summer anti drink and drug driving campaign, launched June 14, saw 55 drink-drive and 40 drug-drive arrests in over two weeks. Inspector Dave Cust warned offenders face disqualification, fines, and job loss. Police use patrols and technology to catch offenders, and urge reporting via 101, Crimestoppers, or 999.

The first fixture after the AGM was the annual ladies versus men game, with the ladies winning 20–16 (163 shots to 157) after six rounds of triples over 10 ends. CMB BC also defeated March Town 3–2 in the Ivan Henson Memorial Trophy final, winning overall shots 66–62.

This paper presents a non-LTE (NLTE) abundance analysis for neodymium (Nd II) in metal-poor FGK stars, constructing a novel Nd I/Nd II model atom from experimental atomic data in VALD, NIST, and linemake using the code FORMATO3 for the NLTE radiative transfer code MULTI2.3 with 1D MARCS model atmospheres. Calibrating the hydrogen collision scaling factor against solar and benchmark star HD 222925 observations determines SH = 0.1, yielding solar NLTE abundances consistent with meteoritic values and higher than LTE; tests demonstrate that supplementing the atom with theoretical high-energy levels or hyperfine structure data has a negligible impact on the resulting NLTE corrections. The authors derive NLTE abundances for a sample of metal-poor stars and generate a six-dimensional grid of NLTE corrections (ΔA_NLTE) for 122 observed Nd II lines across stellar parameters typical of FGK stars (4000 K ≤ Teff ≤ 6500 K, 0.5 ≤ log g ≤ 4.5, −3.0 ≤ [Fe/H] ≤ −1.0), confirming that linear interpolation reproduces direct calculations to within ~0.004 dex.

The grid reveals significant NLTE effects ranging from −0.3 dex to +0.5 dex depending on stellar properties and line characteristics. For optical lines, corrections are generally positive—typically ~0.1 dex for main-sequence dwarfs and ~0.2 dex for giants with lower Nd abundances—and increase toward larger positive values for lower Teff, log g, and [Fe/H], with the largest corrections (up to ~+0.5 dex) occurring for blue, low-excitation-potential lines in cool, metal-poor giants. Near-infrared H-band lines show negative corrections, particularly for warmer giants. NLTE corrections tend to diminish toward zero as Nd abundance increases, and saturation effects reduce reliability for lines with reduced equivalent widths above −5.0. The authors conclude that LTE analyses of optical Nd II lines in cool, metal-poor giants risk underestimating r-process abundances, recommend adopting 1D NLTE corrections for r-process research, and advise using moderate- to high-excitation-potential lines when possible. Future work aims to expand the parameter grid to cooler spectral types and apply the corrections to large samples of Milky Way metal-poor stars and other lanthanide elements.

Doug Ford held his first major rally as Ontario Progressive Conservative leader in Toronto, telling nearly 2,000 supporters he would "take back this province" and build a majority government by appealing to voters dissatisfied with Liberal Premier Kathleen Wynne. He criticized the government's financial mismanagement and throne speech promises, vowing to cut taxes, hydro rates, and regulations; bring back manufacturing jobs; and advance northern Ontario mining projects. Former leadership rivals Christine Elliott, Caroline Mulroney, and Tanya Granic Allen joined him onstage. Supporters cited his personality and policies, including eliminating the carbon tax, as reasons for backing him.

The speaker praises his longtime NHL coach for their strong communication and role in his success. He values John, an experienced late-season backup goalie addition. He describes a game where, after opponents scored early on a power play, his team killed penalties effectively, scored shortly after a kill, and converted on their own power play. He stresses staying positive, reviewing tapes to make adjustments, and the importance of special teams in playoff success.

The New York Mets defeated the Chicago Cubs 9-4 after rallying from a 4-1 deficit. Matt Harvey allowed three home runs in four innings and said he plans to see a doctor, citing physical struggles and reduced velocity following surgery to remove a rib. Curtis Granderson hit his 300th career home run to open a five-run eighth inning, Lucas Duda hit a three-run homer, and T.J. Rivera added an RBI single. Second baseman Neil Walker left with a left leg injury. The Mets won for the fifth time in six games, while the Cubs lost for the sixth time in eight games.

Alexei Ponikarovsky called tomorrow's game a must-win. Despite being down in the series, the team stays positive. He said they must get more pucks in the net and rebounds, get shots through, be in the goaltender's face more, citing a Rangers series where they were shut out twice but won.

The speaker thanks President Clinton and Vice President Gore for their service and for a contest ended with grace, affirming the peaceful transfer of authority. The address describes the American story as one of flawed people united by enduring ideals, particularly the promise that everyone belongs and deserves a chance. The speaker pledges to build a single nation of justice and opportunity, stating that Americans are bound by ideals rather than blood or birth. The speech calls for civility, courage, compassion, and character. Specific commitments include reclaiming schools, reforming Social Security and Medicare, reducing taxes, building defenses, confronting weapons of mass destruction, and remaining engaged in the world to defend allies and promote freedom. The speaker emphasizes compassion for those in poverty through both government and religious and charitable institutions, and calls on citizens to serve rather than spectate. Citing John Page's letter to Thomas Jefferson regarding an angel in the whirlwind, the address concludes that the work to make the country more just and generous continues.

The Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) is a 4 KB decrypted page enabling communication between SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests and their hypervisor, formatted to mirror the SEV-ES VMCB save state area while exposing only required fields. Version 2 introduces SEV-SNP support, hypervisor feature advertisement through a 52-bit FEATURES bitmap, and additions including XSS MSR reporting, restricted APIC emulation, and multi-VMPL support. Revisions 2.01 through 2.04 incrementally added 64-bit guest request sequence numbers, a Versioned Loaded Endorsement Key (VLEK) GUID, expanded hypervisor error codes in SW_EXITINFO2, guest APIC ID lists, page state change notifications, SEV-TIO for trusted PCIe devices, Secure AVIC backing page support, and updated debug and EFI protocol documentation.

The GHCB resides at a guest-specified, 4K-aligned guest physical address stored in VMCB offset 0xa0 and MSR 0xc001_0130. The GHCB MSR protocol uses the lower 12 bits to negotiate protocol versions, request CPUID and SEV information, manage AP reset hold, register or unregister the GHCB GPA, change page states, run different VMPL levels, query hypervisor features, and request termination. SEV-SNP guests must register the GHCB GPA before first use.

Non-Automatic Exit (NAE) events are handled via VMGEXIT. The guest copies required register state into the GHCB, sets the VALID_BITMAP, and populates SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1, and SW_EXITINFO2; the hypervisor processes the request and returns results or error codes. Supported NAE events include IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, MMIO access, Page State Change, SNP Guest Request, SNP Extended Guest Request, SNP AP Creation, #HV doorbell page configuration, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, SNP TIO Guest Request, Secure AVIC backing page registration, and Termination Request.

The SEV-SNP Secrets Page includes a 96-byte guest reserved area for communicating sequence numbers and an AP jump table address between operating environments. The SEV-SNP Confidential Computing Blob EFI Protocol passes the secrets page and CPUID page from firmware to the OS.

SEV-ES guests detect support via CPUID function 0x8000_001f. SMP booting relies on an AP Reset Hold protocol or, for SEV-SNP, the AP Creation NAE event. NMI delivery requires hypervisors to intercept #DB and guests to signal "NMI Complete." Debug register support is either hardware virtualized or emulated through the #VC handler. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported. With Restricted Injection, the hypervisor delivers events through a shared #HV doorbell page containing PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields; guests atomically acknowledge interrupts and perform end-of-interrupt operations either implicitly or via explicit VMGEXIT.

In *Johnson v. The State*, James Johnson was convicted of murdering his father and sentenced to life imprisonment. The court affirmed the denial of his motion for a new trial. It held that the presence on the second trial's jury list of jurors previously stricken or disqualified at the first trial was not grounds for objection, as no specific jurors were shown to be legally disqualified. The court found no error in admitting evidence that Johnson had spoken of his father's life insurance before the homicide and sought help obtaining the money afterward, ruling it admissible to show his belief and possible motive. The court also upheld the jury charge stating Johnson admitted a murder occurred but denied his guilt, noting his own statement to the jury referred to the killing as a murder while claiming innocence. The court found no error in the remaining grounds and affirmed the verdict as supported by the evidence.

The latest "Fifty Shades" film has spurred retailers to compete for bondage consumers, though online sales dominate. Coco de Mer launched an official collection with E.L. James, and Ann Summers released its first S&M cinema ad. After the 2015 film, online bondage sales rose over 42 percent, and overall online sales of sex toys, bondage, and lingerie grew 62 percent since 2014. The global market is predicted to reach £24 billion by 2020.

An NPR/Marist poll finds one in five U.S. jobs is held by contractors, a share that could reach half within a decade, while 30 percent of Americans work extra jobs beyond full-time work. Emily Doherty works full-time at a museum and performs at living-history sites to pay student loans and make ends meet, leaving little personal time. Total student loan debt nears $1.4 trillion. Jon Jacobs, a therapist and father, switched from bartending to driving for Lyft for flexibility to spend time with his children, despite lower pay. Susan Lambert of the University of Chicago says multiple jobs affect well-being and family life. Doherty hopes for financial stability and is saving to visit family.

The Ninth Circuit granted in part Harnek Singh's petition and granted Baljinder Kaur's petition for review of Board of Immigration Appeals removal orders. Singh's case was remanded for consideration of his adverse-credibility challenge and asylum eligibility. Kaur's case was remanded for plenary consideration of her claims, including due process, with her testimony accepted as credible.

Green Monday, the last Monday at least 10 days before Christmas, features several laptop deals from various retailers. Options include an HP Envy x360 convertible for $700 (save $170), a 14-inch Razer Blade for $1,600 (save $200), an HP Laptop 14t for $190 (save $110), a Dell laptop at Staples for $380 (save $140), and a Lenovo 14-inch touchscreen 2-in-1 at Best Buy for $330 (save $70). The article states deals will be updated periodically but warns that waiting too long may mean missing holiday delivery deadlines.

In July 2020, the NHL and NHL Players’ Association negotiated a return-to-play plan for the pandemic-interrupted 2019-20 season and a CBA extension through 2025-26. The 2013 CBA established a 50/50 revenue sharing split between players and owners, making the measurement of league revenue and player compensation critical. For the 2020 negotiations, player agent Emilie Castonguay represented the players, while NHL Commissioner Gary Bettman represented the owners. Discussion items included regular-season ticket sales, broadcasting rights, concessions, player salaries, signing bonuses, deferred salary, and contract buyouts. Castonguay knew higher league revenue or lower player compensation would favor players, while Bettman knew the opposite, and both recognized that extreme positions could threaten the 50/50 split and lead to lost games.

Scientists have created hybrid embryos using frozen northern white rhino sperm and southern white rhino eggs, advancing efforts to save the sub-species, of which only two females remain. Researchers plan to harvest eggs from the surviving females, Najin and Fatu, to produce pure northern white rhino embryos for implantation in southern white rhino surrogates, hoping for the first calf in about three years. They are also working to convert frozen skin cells from deceased animals into egg cells. Some conservationists criticize the project as too late and costly, arguing resources should instead protect other endangered rhino species. The team awaits Kenyan permission to perform the egg extraction by year-end, though concerns remain about risks to the animals' health.

Teb Lokey forwarded a Texas Monthly article to Enron colleagues tracing the company’s transformation from a pipeline firm into a trading colossus under Jeff Skilling and Ken Lay. Enron built an aggressive, “knowledge-based” culture that recruited top graduates, offered uncapped merit bonuses, and used a harsh forced-ranking performance system known as “rank and yank.” It employed mark-to-market accounting to book projected profits immediately and abandoned projects when margins fell. After Skilling became CEO in February 2001, Enron faced a stock price drop from $80 to around $35, blame for California’s energy crisis, costly troubles with a power plant in India, the implosion of its telecommunications division, and growing Wall Street skepticism about its finances. Skilling resigned abruptly after six months, citing the personal sacrifices the job had required. Ken Lay returned as CEO, promising to refocus on core energy businesses, soften the performance review process, and end indiscriminate trading.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on July 19, 2018, furnishing a press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2018 as Exhibit 99.1. The report was signed by Frank H. Brod, Chief Accounting Officer.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated February 26, 2020, reporting results from its Annual Meeting of Shareholders held that day. Shareholders elected seven directors: James Bell, Tim Cook, Al Gore, Andrea Jung, Art Levinson, Ron Sugar, and Sue Wagner. They approved the ratification of Ernst & Young LLP as the independent registered public accounting firm for 2020 and an advisory resolution on executive compensation. Three shareholder proposals—regarding proxy access amendments, sustainability and executive compensation, and freedom of expression policies—were not approved. The report was signed on February 27, 2020, by Katherine Adams, Senior Vice President, General Counsel and Secretary.

This Foreign Relations volume documents the intellectual foundations of Reagan administration foreign policy (1981–1988) through speeches, memoranda, and other records. It illustrates primary themes—including a policy reset following Vietnam, Watergate, and the Iran hostage crisis, a world structure hospitable to U.S. values, an activist foreign policy with bipartisanship, and U.S.-Soviet restraint and reciprocity—of senior officials including President Reagan, Secretaries Haig and Shultz, Defense Secretary Weinberger, and National Security Affairs Assistants. A 2018–2022 declassification review withheld no documents fully and made minor excisions in three documents.

This study investigated the relationship between serum cardiac troponin T (cTnT) and respiratory dysfunction in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) using a discovery cohort (University Hospital Bonn, n=297) and a validation cohort (Krupp Hospital Essen, n=49). Serum cTnT levels correlated negatively with the ALSFRS-R respiratory domain and with pulmonary function test parameters including FVC, SVC, FEV1, and PEF; these associations remained significant after adjustment for confounders. In contrast, serum neurofilament light chain (NfL) correlated with overall ALSFRS-R but not with respiratory function. ROC analyses indicated cTnT could detect clinically relevant declines in SVC, FVC, and PEF, with optimal cut-offs between 14.00 and 17.80 ng/L. The authors conclude that cTnT reflects respiratory muscle involvement, is independent of NfL, and can serve as a biomarker for respiratory capacity in ALS.

Ryshonda Harper Beechem became Pelahatchie, Mississippi’s first black mayor in June 2017, winning by 12 votes. She has since clashed with the Board of Aldermen, which has overridden her vetoes, acted without consulting her, and cut her salary by 75 percent to $250 per month, equal to the aldermen. Beechem vetoed the cut, citing “no confidence” in the board amid a state auditor’s investigation into alleged misappropriation of funds. Three clerks resigned in early 2018, and the board tried to appoint an interim clerk without her input. The relationship has grown hostile, with the board voting unanimously against her, while residents debate online, some alleging racism and others calling the mayor unprofessional.

This study prospectively examined the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on health-related quality of life (HRQOL) in head and neck cancer (HNC) survivors using data from the NET-QUBIC cohort. Among 318 survivors who completed patient-reported outcome measures at 36 months—199 before and 119 during the pandemic—no statistically significant overall differences were found in changes in HRQOL, physical activity, distress, anxiety, depression, fear of recurrence, or loneliness between 24 and 36 months follow-up. However, subgroup analyses revealed differential effects: the pandemic negatively affected physical activity in females, appetite loss in survivors receiving multimodality treatment, swallowing in those with moderate to severe comorbidity, and fear of cancer recurrence in those with a lifetime major depressive disorder. Conversely, it was associated with decreased painkiller use in survivors living alone and reduced financial problems in those with cancer progression at 24 months. The authors conclude that while the pandemic did not alter HRQOL overall, specific subgroups experienced meaningful changes, supporting the development of personalized supportive care.

The speaker said their team rattled opponents by putting the puck behind them, expressed confidence their goalie would bounce back, and noted they got frustrated after the second goal, abandoned their system, took penalties, were outplayed, and got off their game after a good start.

The Cleveland Indians defeated the Minnesota Twins 3-1. Danny Salazar earned the win, allowing one run over six innings with seven strikeouts. Michael Brantley tied the game with an RBI ground ball and hit a solo home run for the final run. Edwin Encarnacion drove in the go-ahead run, while Yan Gomes reached base three times. Bryan Shaw recorded his 86th hold. The teams play again tomorrow night at 8:10 PM with Josh Tomlin facing Phil Hughes.

Twitter shares fell 9 percent after fourth-quarter revenue of $717 million missed estimates of $740.1 million and first-quarter guidance of $75 million to $95 million fell short of the expected $191.3 million. Monthly active users rose 4 percent to 319 million, daily active users increased 7 percent, and advertising revenue dipped to $638 million. BTIG upgraded the stock Wednesday due to Trump-driven engagement.

Text2MBL is a framework that translates textual descriptions into Building Information Modeling (BIM)-based modular building layouts (MBLs) through sequential, action-level code generation. Addressing the complexity of modular construction and the lack of direct text-to-BIM methodologies, the system formalizes MBLs into four hierarchical classes—Modules, Unit, Room, and Utils—incorporating spatial relationships including adjacency, connectivity, and conjointness, along with hierarchical containment constraints. A proof-of-concept was implemented in Autodesk Revit using its C# API. By representing design as executable action sequences, the framework bridges the gap between natural language and BIM formats, abstracts complex geometric reasoning, and reframes generation as a sequence-to-sequence task. The authors curated a dataset of 198 real-world MBL designs, each paired with executable BIM code and two textual descriptions, and fine-tuned Qwen2.5 large language models to learn the mapping from text to code. Evaluation assessed executable validity, semantic fidelity, and geometric consistency.

The article describes the football route tree as a coaching tool to organize and teach pass routes, noting that specific route assignments vary by team. It outlines short routes including the hitch (5–6 yards, pivot to quarterback), slant (roughly 45 degrees inside), quick out (5 yards, 90 degrees to sideline), stick (5 yards, sit or break away from the middle), flat (2–3 yards past the line of scrimmage, horizontal), whip (initial in-breaking steps before turning out), and option routes (receiver chooses a path based on the defense). It also covers intermediate and deep routes: the go or fly (deep outside), seam (vertical middle), corner (from the slot, roughly 45 degrees to the sideline at 10–12 yards), post (break toward the goal posts at 10–12 yards), post-corner (post break then outside corner), square out (10–12 yards, hard 90 degrees to the sideline), dig (10–15 yards, sharp break to the middle), curl (10–12 yards, break back toward the quarterback to sit), comeback (vertical then break back to the ball), drag (horizontal, drifting 6–8 yards across the field), and shallow cross (within 2–3 yards of the line of scrimmage, across the field). The passage details each route’s depth, break angle, and tactical purpose.

Paralyzed Veterans of America thanked Deputy Secretary Tom Bowman for his service and wished him well in retirement. The organization looks forward to working with Acting Secretary Peter O'Rourke and prioritizes implementing the VA MISSION Act, hoping leadership changes will not hamper efforts. It advocates for veterans with spinal cord injury or disease.

A 2018 study found women are 11% of the cybersecurity workforce; discrimination, negative feedback in male-dominated settings, and lack of educator support are key barriers. Glance Pay executives Angela Griffin and Paola Ashton linked diversity to business growth, innovation, and the company's U.S. expansion. No ability gap exists despite the gender gap, and women are encouraged to engage with peer networks and organizations such as Girls in Tech and Women Who Code. Addressing bias and fostering inclusion benefits organizations. Glance Technologies owns the Glance Pay mobile payment system and is developing blockchain and cryptocurrency initiatives.

A speaker describes his team’s loss in a tight game where they were one shot away from winning the Stanley Cup, calling it the most painful loss he has experienced. He notes both sides played tight, his team never quit, and Khabibulin made huge saves. He mentions the team fought through injuries all year, wanted to win for Dave Andreychuk and the city, and acknowledges the young defense group gained experience. He says the loss will sit with the team for a while but believes they will get another chance and it will motivate them.

This study evaluated the health impact and cost-effectiveness of Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection screening and tuberculosis preventive treatment (TPT) for formerly incarcerated individuals in Brazil using a Markov state transition model. Comparing combinations of tuberculin skin tests (TST) or interferon gamma release assays (IGRA) with four TPT regimens against no screening, all intervention strategies were cost-effective. A strategy using TST with a 3-month isoniazid and rifapentine regimen cost $242 per disability-adjusted life year averted and was estimated to avert 31 lifetime tuberculosis cases and 4.1 lifetime tuberculosis deaths per 1,000 individuals. Greater health benefits and more favorable cost-effectiveness ratios were found for younger individuals, those with longer incarceration durations, and those screened soon after prison release, though the intervention remained cost-effective across all subgroups. While IGRA testing and shorter TPT regimens produced greater health benefits, the analysis was inconclusive regarding the optimal strategy between TST/1HP and IGRA/1HP at the cost-effectiveness threshold. The authors conclude that Mtb infection screening and TPT are highly cost-effective for this population.

This study uses 3D representative volume element finite element models to compare the biomechanical effects of two collagen fiber architectures in arterial tissue with varying wall thickness: abrupt fiber terminations versus continuous fibers spanning thickness gradients. Under uniaxial loading, the abrupt termination network produced substantial stretch and stress disparities between thin and thick regions, with stretch differences reaching 20% at λ=1.5 and 32.5% at λ=2. In contrast, the continuous fiber network reduced these disparities to 0.68% at λ=1.5 and approximately 2% at λ=2, yielding more uniform stress distributions and a lower maximum tissue stress. The continuous architecture homogenized deformation by transferring load across regions and increasing local fiber volume density in thinner regions (51.9% versus 26.0% in thick regions). Fiber tortuosity, modeled via recruitment stretch, further modulated behavior: prior to fiber engagement, geometric thickness differences dominated, but after recruitment, fiber architecture governed the mechanical response. These findings challenge the classical view that wall thickness alone dictates local stress fields, demonstrating that collagen fiber continuity is pivotal. The authors note that constant-thickness computational models may provide accurate mechanical and failure predictions when fiber continuity is confirmed, even without local thickness measurements. Limitations include idealized geometry and boundary conditions; future work should investigate mixed fiber architectures, complex geometries, multiaxial loading, and experimental validation.

Asteroid 2025 TF, roughly 1 to 3 meters wide, flew within 428 km of Earth over Antarctica on October 1. It was detected hours after the flyby by the Catalina Sky Survey and posed no danger. This application is a continuation of U.S. patent application Ser. No. 17/258,524, filed Jan. 7, 2021, which is a national phase of PCT/IL2019/050819, filed Jul. 22, 2019, claiming priority to U.S. Provisional Application Ser. No. 62/718,773, filed Aug. 14, 2018, entitled “Comprehensive eye solution for functional impairment of the eye due to facial paralysis.” The disclosure relates to an apparatus and method for transcutaneous nerve stimulation, particularly non-invasive facial nerve stimulation for artificially eliciting eye blink in humans with acute facial paralysis. The Facebook-Cambridge Analytica scandal highlighted data surveillance risks, but the passage argues the deeper problem is not lack of consent. It introduces “personalized choice architecture,” the practice of using individually tailored data to subconsciously nudge decisions, which threatens personal autonomy and democratic processes by exploiting unique user traits rather than general human biases. This Statistical Analysis Plan details data handling and presentation for a clinical trial of dasiglucagon and GlucaGen®. A total solar eclipse will cross the United States on August 21, 2017. Most of the country will see a partial eclipse, but a 70-mile-wide path from Oregon to South Carolina will experience totality. The moon's shadow will reach the Oregon coast at 10:16 a.m. PT (1:16 p.m. ET) and leave the Atlantic coast at 2:49 p.m. ET, taking one hour and 33 minutes to cross the country at varying speeds. During totality, the sky will darken, stars will appear, temperatures will drop, and observers will see Baily's Beads and a diamond ring effect. The next total solar eclipse will occur on July 2, 2019, over the southern Pacific and South America; the next U.S. eclipse will be on April 8, 2024. NASA offers an interactive map with exact times and coverage levels. Except during the brief period of totality, viewers must wear ISO 12312-2 compliant eclipse glasses. NASA and other outlets will provide livestreams, and smartphones and cameras can photograph the eclipse with proper precautions.

This study introduces AnveshanaAI, an adaptive, practice-based AI/ML learning platform framed around three research questions on automated question generation, platform fairness and scalability, and simulation-driven pedagogy. The system is built on a dataset of over 10,000 problem–answer pairs across core AI/ML domains, annotated with Bloom’s taxonomy levels, difficulty ratings, and tags, and augmented through difficulty scaling and cross-mode adaptation into coding, simulation, debugging, and viva-style formats. Its modular architecture employs fine-tuned Mistral-7B models, Docker-based execution sandboxes, vector databases, and Whisper-based speech recognition, while offering gamified learner interfaces and administrator tools for challenge design, performance analytics, and data export. Experimental evaluation demonstrates high annotation quality with balanced cognitive coverage, stable fine-tuning convergence yielding a final perplexity of 2.04, a BERTScore F1 of 0.427 with recall of 0.818, and interpretable attention to educationally relevant tokens. The dataset and training configuration are publicly available to support reproducibility.

The passage discloses methods and systems for Polkadot, a scalable heterogeneous multi-chain framework providing shared security, interoperability, and scalability among blockchains. It comprises a relay chain managed by a decentralized network of nodes, including validators, collators, nominators, and fishermen. Validators receive and validate candidate blocks and state-transition proofs from collators in assigned parachains, participate in a Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus process to seal relay chain blocks, and can be punished for misbehavior through bond reduction or burning. Nominators stake tokens to back validators; collators maintain parachain full nodes and produce unsealed block candidates with proofs; fishermen report illegal validator actions for rewards. Parachain headers are sealed within relay chain blocks, and interchain transactions are routed asynchronously between parachain ingress and egress queues, with hyper-cube routing used to limit connectivity growth at scale. The relay chain logic is WebAssembly-based, and the system supports governance and upgrades without hard forks, utilizing a Nominated Proof-of-Stake validator selection process.

This randomized, controlled, superiority trial compared radial extracorporeal shock wave therapy (rESWT) plus a specific rehabilitation program (RP) versus sham rESWT plus RP in 36 semi-professional athletes with acute hamstring muscle complex injury type 3b. The eight-week RP consisted of acute, subacute/regeneration, and functional phases with criteria-based progression. The rESWT group received up to nine sessions using a Swiss DolorClast device. The primary outcome, time to return to sport, was significantly shorter in the rESWT + RP group (mean 25.4 days) than in the sham + RP group (mean 28.3 days; p = 0.037). Patient satisfaction at six months and re-injury rates within six months did not significantly differ between groups. The study concluded that adding rESWT to this specific RP reduces time to return to sport without increasing re-injury risk, and that this RP alone is superior to other reported rehabilitation programs.

In *Jane Richmond v. Walter M. Richmond*, the court held that alimony depends on the specific circumstances of each case and cannot be set solely by the defendant’s actual rents and profits or the complainant’s actual wants. The court held that children must be maintained according to the father’s condition in life without imposing a financial burden on the mother, and that the court retains authority to modify the allowance upon a change of circumstances. The decree constitutes a lien on the defendant’s estate and authorizes sequestration or other equitable process for nonpayment.

A concrete dome on Enewetak Atoll containing radioactive waste from 1950s US nuclear tests is leaking into the Pacific Ocean, according to veterans involved in the cleanup. The lecture explains the theorem of irrelevance, which states that in white Gaussian noise only the signal’s own degrees of freedom matter, making all modulation schemes equivalent for noise analysis while secondary issues like synchronization remain relevant. For independent signals, symbol-by-symbol and joint-sequence maximum-likelihood detection yield identical results, but for dependent signals—such as coded systems—joint detection achieves a lower error probability, motivating the shift from algebraic coding to probabilistic decoding. The professor then discusses orthogonal, simplex, and biorthogonal codes, noting that orthogonal and simplex codes have identical error probabilities but different energy requirements, whereas biorthogonal codes maintain the same energy while roughly doubling the error probability. By conditioning on the noise in the signal’s direction and using bounds, the error probability for large orthogonal sets can be upper-bounded; when the energy per bit exceeds the Shannon limit (E_b/N_0 > ln 2), the error probability falls exponentially with the number of bits, illustrating the core of the channel capacity proof. The lecture then transitions to wireless communication, contrasting it with wired channels by emphasizing time-varying fading, interference, and multi-user access. It focuses on cellular networks, where mobiles connect to fixed base stations that interface with wired infrastructure, and identifies the mobile-to-base-station link as the reverse (multi-access) channel and the base-to-mobile link as the forward (broadcast) channel. Base-station placement depends heavily on electromagnetic modeling, while mobile design relies on coarser channel characteristics. The differing delay tolerances of voice and data are noted, and the discussion previews physical modeling topics such as narrowband versus wideband systems, carrier frequencies, Doppler shift, and idealized propagation models for the next session.

The passage describes a display apparatus including a flexible vibration module on a rear surface of a display panel, and a method of manufacturing the module. The flexible vibration module vibrates the panel to generate sound or haptic feedback, and includes a piezoelectric composite layer with alternating first portions of inorganic piezoelectric material and second portions of organic flexible material, disposed between electrode layers and protection films. This structure provides piezoelectric characteristics, stiffness, flexibility, and impact resistance, enabling use in curved, rollable, bendable, and flexible displays. Embodiments include varying geometric patterns and sizes for the portions, a bimorph structure with two composite layers for enhanced sound pressure, and multiple vibration modules with partition members and air gaps to separate sound channels for stereo output. The manufacturing method involves forming the piezoelectric composite, forming first and second electrode layers, applying voltage for polarization, and forming protection films.

The bullish engulfing pattern is a two-candlestick formation appearing after a downward price swing, where a larger bullish candlestick completely engulfs a smaller bearish candlestick, signaling a potential bullish reversal. The passage outlines how to identify the pattern, build a trading plan, analyze market conditions, and determine entry and exit points based on profit targets, stop losses, or opposing signals. It also covers advanced trading techniques, risk management strategies, backtesting methods using historical data with strict rules, common mistakes to avoid, and the benefits of trading this reversal signal.

This prospective cohort study of 264 adults hospitalized with COVID-19 at Johns Hopkins Hospital evaluated whether baseline point-of-care lung ultrasound (LUS) findings, using a mean LUS score (mLUSS) across available lung zones, predicted progression to ICU-level oxygen support or death. The mLUSS, calculated on a 0–3 scale per zone without requiring all 12 zones, was significantly associated with increased risk of progression to ICU-level care (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 3.61) and 28-day mortality (aHR 3.10). A lines were associated with decreased risk of clinical deterioration and death, while pleural line abnormalities were strongly associated with increased risk of death and mechanical ventilation, and B lines were associated with increased 28-day mortality. These findings remained consistent in sensitivity analyses adjusting for symptom duration, excluding asymptomatic individuals, and accounting for unavailable lung zones. The authors conclude that baseline LUS findings and mLUSS are independently associated with ultimate oxygen requirements or death, supporting LUS as a prognostic triage tool that can be reliably implemented by trained operators even when not all lung zones are obtainable.

This study reports the first instance of precision therapies (targeted and immunotherapy) surpassing traditional cytotoxic treatments in routine community-based care for advanced cancer patients, resulting in improved overall survival. Investigators implemented pathologist-directed comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) with a 523-gene assay immediately at diagnosis for 3,216 patients with advanced solid tumors between September 2019 and November 2021. Overall, 49% of cases had at least one guideline-based actionable biomarker, and 67% had actionable mutations for guideline-based therapies or clinical trial matching, compared to 33% using a legacy 50-gene panel. Among treated patients, biomarker-matched targeted therapy or immunotherapy was utilized more frequently than chemotherapy alone. Median overall survival was 25 months for targeted therapy versus 17 months for chemotherapy only (HR 0.66, p<0.001), and among NSCLC patients, 26 months versus 16 months (HR 0.55, p=0.032). The findings demonstrate a paradigm shift toward precision oncology in a community health system.

FoLix is a new FDA-cleared, noninvasive fractional laser treatment for hair loss that offers a nonsurgical alternative to hair transplants. It stimulates natural hair growth in men and women by creating microscopic channels in the scalp to trigger a controlled healing response, boost circulation, and signal existing follicles. Each in-office session takes 20 to 30 minutes, requires no anesthesia, and has little to no downtime. Patients typically undergo three to six sessions in the first year, followed by maintenance treatments up to twice yearly, with costs ranging from $750 to $1,250 per session. Dermatologists say it is best suited for those in early to moderate stages of hair loss with intact but underperforming follicles, and it is not intended for individuals with complete baldness or extensive scarring. Mild, temporary side effects may include redness, tightness, scalp sensitivity, and temporary shedding. Doctors recommend consulting a physician before treatment, as hair loss can result from various causes beyond genetics or aging.

This qualitative case study examined COVID-19 distance education experiences of seven visually impaired students in Turkish professional music education, reaching 80% of such students nationwide through semi-structured interviews analyzed via content analysis. Institutions primarily used synchronous methods, and participants independently used computers, phones, or tablets; however, course materials were largely insufficient or inaccessible because special needs were not considered in their preparation. Assessment practices varied between individual and general arrangements. Students identified spatial and temporal flexibility and greater social acceptance as strengths, while citing technical deficiencies in audio synchronization and transmission, low productivity, and instructors’ technological incompetence as key weaknesses. Participants recommended text-to-audio conversion tools, screen-reader-compatible systems, Braille notation archives, longer lesson durations, and rapid technical support. The study concluded that the distance education process largely ignored visually impaired learners, making educational access dependent on parents, peers, or large print. It emphasized that equal opportunity requires customized materials, disability-specific technologies—including screen readers, speech recognition, Braille printers, and interactive audio materials—and structured professional support.

The United States sued Hale County, Alabama, alleging that 1965, 1971, and 1973 enactments changing County Commissioner elections from district-based to at-large violated Section 5 of the Voting Rights Act of 1965 because they were not federally precleared. Defendants claimed the Act did not apply because Hale County itself was not individually designated as a covered jurisdiction in the Federal Register. In an October 18, 1976 opinion and order, the court held that a state’s designation under the Act automatically covers its political subdivisions, making the at-large acts unlawful. The court permitted the November 2, 1976 election to proceed provisionally, ordered defendants to submit the changes to the Attorney General, and mandated a return to district-based elections if preclearance was denied and no declaratory judgment suit was filed in the D.C. District Court. A January 24, 1977 supplemental opinion rejected the defendants’ statutory argument under 42 U.S.C. § 1973b(b), relying on legislative history and Supreme Court precedent—including *Allen v. State Board of Elections*, *Perkins v. Mathews*, and *Beer v. United States*—to affirm that coverage of a state encompasses all its political subdivisions.

This application describes flexible cable interconnects for quantum computing systems, particularly cryogenic environments with isothermal plates. The flex cables include shielded metal striplines and grounding planes, connect to rigid boards that may host filters, attenuators, or amplifiers, and can incorporate absorptive composite materials for high-frequency electromagnetic attenuation. They provide high-density, low-thermal-load signal routing with fanout structures for mechanical integrity, and can bypass intermediate isothermal plates. Conductors may be non-superconducting (e.g., stainless steel) at higher temperature stages and superconducting (e.g., niobium, titanium-niobium, or aluminum) at lower stages, with connections via solder bumps, wire bonds, flip-chip assemblies, or compliant joints. The systems are designed to support quantum processing units with fifty or more superconducting qubits.

A comprehensive analysis of baseline C-reactive protein (CRP) data from the phase 3 LIVE-AIR trial found that baseline CRP was the strongest predictor of progression to invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) or death in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. While lenzilumab, a GM-CSF neutralizing antibody, significantly improved survival without IMV (SWOV) compared to placebo in the overall population (HR: 1.54; p=0.0403), participants with baseline CRP <150 mg/L—representing 78% of the study population—demonstrated the greatest clinical benefit, including improved SWOV (HR: 2.54; nominal p=0.0009), more ventilator-free days, fewer ICU days, and faster time to recovery. Patients with baseline CRP ≥150 mg/L, described as experiencing hyperinflammation and imminent risk of respiratory escalation or death, did not show significant benefit. Lenzilumab reduced CRP levels more rapidly than placebo, and no treatment-emergent serious adverse events attributable to lenzilumab were reported. The findings suggest baseline CRP may be a useful biomarker to guide lenzilumab therapy.

Teagasc survey of 314 farmers in southeast Ireland found higher CVD and cancer mortality than other occupations. 20% never consulted a doctor; 57% visited one in 12 months, below average. 39% reported ill health mainly back pain, arthritis, and anxiety. 20% smoked, 88% drank alcohol regularly, 22% binge drank weekly. The NVIDIA Ampere GA10x GPU architecture introduces significant advancements over Turing. Its Streaming Multiprocessor (SM) doubles peak FP32 throughput by enabling FP32 processing on both datapaths, allowing the GeForce RTX 3090 to deliver over 35 TFLOPS. The GA102 GPU is composed of seven Graphics Processing Clusters (GPCs), 42 Texture Processing Clusters (TPCs), and 84 SMs, with 112 Raster Operations units (ROPs) now integrated into GPCs to boost rasterization performance.

The architecture features second-generation RT Cores that double the ray/triangle intersection testing rate over Turing and add an Interpolate Triangle Position unit to accelerate ray-traced motion blur by up to 8x. These cores also support concurrent execution of ray tracing with graphics or compute workloads. Third-generation Tensor Cores support new data types including TF32 and BF16, and implement Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity to double throughput for sparse matrices, accelerating AI training, denoising, and DLSS up to 8K resolutions.

Memory technologies include GDDR6X, which uses PAM4 signaling to achieve up to 936 GB/s of bandwidth on the RTX 3090, and GDDR6 for professional cards such as the NVIDIA RTX A6000 and A40, which feature 48 GB scalable to 96 GB via third-generation NVLink providing 112.5 GB/s total bandwidth between two GPUs. The platform also adopts PCIe Gen 4, offering up to 64 GB/s peak bandwidth.

Additional capabilities include RTX IO for GPU-based loading and decompression via Microsoft DirectStorage, reducing CPU overhead and accelerating game asset streaming; up to 1.9x greater power efficiency than Turing; and Error Detection and Replay (EDR) technology for the GDDR6X interface to improve overclocking stability. The NVIDIA A40 data center GPU delivers up to 2x FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to 5x (10x with Sparsity) AI throughput compared to the previous generation. Display and video features support 8K60 and 4K120 output through DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a and HDMI 2.1, alongside hardware-accelerated AV1 decode via fifth-generation NVDEC and seventh-generation NVENC encoding.

Christopher K. Merker conducted a five-year PhD study on public pension fund governance after finding institutional investment boards were imperfect and lacked reliable governance data. Analyzing 35 public pension plans from 2008–2012, he discovered significant performance variability, with annualized returns ranging from 15% to –4.2%, and more than half underperforming a balanced index. He found that asset owner governance—codified group investor behavior—was the principal driver of these gaps, as behavioral biases affecting individual investors also influenced trustees. Key performance factors included low turnover, frequent meetings, retired board members, staff involvement, professionalism, engagement, and diligence, while investment expenses were statistically insignificant. Using a Fiduciary Effectiveness Quotient (FEQ), Merker determined that top-quintile governance scores outperformed the bottom quintile by nearly two to one, with each FEQ improvement unit correlating to a 0.36% performance increase. The study concludes that measurable, effective governance directly improves investment results.

Ray tracing realistically simulates lighting but is computationally intensive. Previous GPUs could not perform real-time ray tracing for games, requiring rasterization. A cross-sectional study assessed contraceptive knowledge, attitude, and practice among 217 female students at NTA TV College in Jos, Plateau State, Nigeria. Levels of good knowledge, attitude, and practice were 55.3%, 47.5%, and 50.7%, respectively. About 74% had ever had sex. Main sources of contraceptive information were friends and the internet, while condoms and oral contraceptive pills were most commonly used. The primary reason for non-use was fear of side effects. Multivariable logistic regression identified being a young adult as a significant predictor of good knowledge; being a diploma student, living off-campus, and having good knowledge as significant predictors of good attitude; and being from the state's indigenous population and ever having engaged in sex as significant predictors of good contraceptive practice. The authors concluded that knowledge, attitude, and practice levels were relatively low and recommended urgent improvements in advocacy, policies, and youth-friendly sexual and reproductive health services.

The TPS7H500x-SP is a family of radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting topologies including buck, flyback, forward, and push-pull at frequencies up to 2 MHz. The document details slope compensation to prevent subharmonic oscillation above 50% duty cycle using an RSC resistor, and frequency compensation via Type 2A or 2B networks around the transconductance error amplifier. Thermal shutdown occurs above 175°C with resumption below 160°C. A design example for a 500 kHz synchronous push-pull GaN converter with 5 V output specifies a transformer turns ratio of 2.5, 40 μH primary inductance, 170 V primary and 80 V secondary GaN FETs, 0.47 μH output inductor, 2.3 mF output capacitance to address ripple and single-event transients, and a 7.5 Ω current sense resistor. Layout guidelines recommend routing sensitive traces away from power magnetics and switch nodes, separating analog and power grounds at a single point, placing bypass capacitors close to the controller, and connecting the CFP package backside metal to the AVSS plane.

This MIT 2.830J lecture introduces the Control of Manufacturing Processes course, taught by Duane Boning and David Hardt with teaching assistant Hayden Taylor. Lectures are live video-linked between Cambridge and Singapore, with recorded versions available when holidays prevent live attendance. All course materials are distributed through the Stellar website. Prerequisites include manufacturing process experience and basic probability and statistics. Two textbooks are required: May and Spanos’s semiconductor process control text and Montgomery’s *Introduction to Statistical Quality Control*. Grading is based on approximately eight weekly individual problem sets comprising about 40% of the grade, two quizzes comprising about 40%, and a collaborative team project during the final third of the semester involving presentations and a team report. The course emphasizes understanding and reducing manufacturing variation and improving quality in unit processes. Key topics include statistical process control, design of experiments, empirical and physical process modeling, and feedback control. Examples discussed include semiconductor fabrication, microfluidics, metal forming, and assembly processes. The instructors present a generic process model linking equipment settings and disturbances to output variations, framing the course’s structure around detecting disturbances, optimizing process robustness, and applying active control strategies.
