The passage provides technical specifications for the Texas Instruments TMS320DM814x and TMS320DM8127 DaVinci Digital Media Processors, covering analog video output terminal functions, supply voltage requirements, boot configuration pin settings, pin multiplexing and pullup/pulldown resistor guidelines, system interconnect architecture, recommended operating conditions, power and reset management procedures, clock generation and PLL configurations, interrupt controller mappings, and peripheral interface details including DCAN, EDMA, JTAG, and EMAC switch registers.

This study translated and cross-culturally adapted the Waterloo Footedness Questionnaire-Revised (WFQ-R) into Arabic (WFQ-Ar) for Saudi adults. Following Beaton’s guidelines, two forward translations were synthesized, back-translated, reviewed by an expert committee, and pilot-tested with 30 participants before evaluating measurement properties with 290 Arabic-speaking adults. The adaptation required minor linguistic changes, including rewording one item and changing the answering grid from abbreviations to full words. Face validity was supported by participant interviews and expert consensus; content validity was supported by the absence of floor and ceiling effects. Exploratory factor analysis confirmed a single-factor structure explaining 55.79% of variance. Internal consistency was excellent (Cronbach’s α = 0.93), test-retest reliability was excellent (ICC = 0.94), and the standard error of measurement was 4.5 points. Construct validity was supported by a significant moderate correlation (r = 0.48) with a single-item foot dominance question. The authors concluded that the WFQ-Ar is a valid, reliable, and clinically useful tool for assessing footedness in Arabic-speaking populations, though further testing in other Arabic-speaking countries and clinical populations is needed.

CJ Affiliate (Commission Junction), founded in 1998, is one of the oldest affiliate marketing networks, connecting advertisers and publishers. It is free to join, though applicants need a website or social media profile with relevant content and a US or Canada-based audience. The platform provides tracking, management, and payment processing, along with promotional tools, granular reporting, and thousands of niche programs that can be filtered. Publishers apply to programs, share links, and earn commissions while CJ handles technical issues and payments. Payments are sent via direct deposit, check, or Payoneer within 20 days of month-end, requiring a $50 minimum ($100 outside America); CJ charges a 5–10% commission on sales. The platform has a learning curve and strict approval but is considered user-friendly for beginners and advanced users. Alternatives exist for those who prefer other networks.

Seasonal trading involves regular price patterns at specific times. Silver exhibits seasonality, with January and July as the best-performing months and June and September as the worst. This pattern may be driven by industrial users placing orders at the beginning of the new year. A backtested strategy since 2001 holds silver from December through February and July through August. It returned an extra 3.9% per year, a risk-adjusted return of 26.93% compared to 7.33% for buy-and-hold, and reduced maximum drawdown from -71.65% to -23.34%.

In March 2001, California faced a severe energy crisis marked by rolling blackouts, soaring electricity costs, and state intervention to purchase power for struggling utilities Southern California Edison and Pacific Gas and Electric. Governor Gray Davis requested an additional $500 million for power buys, bringing the state’s total to $4.7 billion, while the utilities began repaying the state approximately $105 million. The Public Utilities Commission approved consumer rate increases of up to 46 percent, though projections showed more households would be affected than initially estimated. President Bush declared a national energy crisis, rejected the Kyoto Protocol, and advocated for increased domestic production and Canadian energy imports. California lawmakers expedited power plant construction by easing environmental regulations and advanced over 190 conservation bills, including roughly $1 billion in demand-reduction programs. State Controller Kathleen Connell projected a $7.4 billion state shortfall over 18 months. Utilities were ordered to provide detailed blackout notifications to San Francisco and Huntington Beach, while law enforcement struggled to enforce a vague outdoor lighting curfew. Republicans sued Governor Davis to disclose long-term power contract details, and political pressure mounted over the administration’s handling of the crisis.

The ADS868xW supports internal (4.096 V, default) and external voltage references selected by the INTREF_DIS bit in the RANGE_SEL_REG register. The internal reference requires a 4.7 µF decoupling capacitor at REFIO and is factory-trimmed and temperature-compensated, though solder heat can cause output shifts. In external mode, a 4.096 V source is applied to REFIO and the internal buffer drives REFCAP with a 10 µF capacitor. The ADC accepts single-ended and differential bipolar/unipolar inputs and outputs straight-binary data with an LSB size of FSR / 2^16. Alarm functions include a programmable input alarm with high/low thresholds and hysteresis, and an AVDD alarm with fixed 4.7 V and 5.3 V thresholds; active and tripped flags are stored in the ALARM_REG and can be appended to output data. The device uses a multiSPI interface supporting legacy SPI and source-synchronous protocols, single or dual SDO outputs, and daisy-chain topologies. It operates in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states controlled by the RST and CONVST/CS pins. Data transfers use 32-bit frames (optimal, short, or long) to write or read nine configuration registers that manage device ID, reset and power modes (including NAP and power-down), interface protocols, data output flags, input ranges, and alarm settings. AVDD and DVDD require decoupling capacitors.

The present disclosure provides methods for encoding a single digital video bitstream usable by both SDR and HDR systems. One method involves receiving an HDR master, a reference SDR master, and target SDR display properties at an encoder. The encoder finds a color volume transform that converts HDR values into SDR values substantially matching the reference SDR master when processed by the target SDR display's operations. The encoder converts HDR values to SDR values using this transform, generates metadata identifying the transform, and encodes the SDR values into a bitstream. SDR decoders decode and display the SDR values, while HDR decoders use the metadata to perform an inverse color volume transform to reconstruct HDR values. An alternate method encodes HDR values directly into the bitstream and provides metadata for SDR decoders to convert decoded HDR values to SDR values. The transform can be determined by minimizing differences between candidate presentation values and reference values, and metadata may include parametric functions, scaling factors, or lookup tables.

Ella Ravenscroft, a 20-year-old model and former Miss Teen Galaxy England, is warning about skin cancer risks after using sunbeds up to twice weekly for two years. Lasting peace requires equality of rights among nations regardless of size or power, based on common rather than individual strength. A study of 81 cerebrospinal fluid, blood, and tissue samples from 24 patients with advanced lung cancer investigated cerebrospinal fluid tumor-derived DNA (CSF-tDNA) analysis using CAPP-Seq for leptomeningeal disease (LMD) diagnosis and monitoring. CSF-tDNA variant allele fractions were significantly higher than plasma circulating tumor DNA (median 32.7% versus 1.8%; P < 0.0001), and concentrations in the two compartments were positively correlated (Spearman’s ρ, 0.45; P = 0.03). For definitive LMD diagnosis, cytology was 81.8% sensitive and CSF-tDNA was 91.7% sensitive. Detectable CSF-tDNA was strongly prognostic for overall survival (HR = 7.1; P = 0.02). Among patients with progression on targeted therapy, resistance mutations such as EGFR T790M and MET amplification were common in peripheral blood but rare in time-matched CSF, indicating spatial heterogeneity in resistance mechanisms. In a prospective cohort of 12 patients treated with osimertinib, those with CNS progression had increased CSF-tDNA variant allele fractions at follow-up lumbar puncture, and post-osimertinib CSF-tDNA was strongly prognostic for CNS progression (HR = 6.2; P = 0.009). The authors conclude that CSF-tDNA detection is feasible and may improve LMD diagnostic sensitivity, enable prognostication, and inform therapeutic strategies that account for anatomic compartment differences in resistance.

Hexane is a crude oil-derived hydrocarbon solvent. Pure hexane is used in laboratories, while solvent-based hexane extracts vegetable oils, removes unwanted tastes and odors, and serves as an industrial cleaning agent. Health hazards include weakness, numbness, and blurred vision; OSHA limits exposure to 500 ppm. An alternative oil extraction method uses sodium hydroxide and methanol but faces moisture challenges. Asia Pacific, led by China, dominates global production, while North America and Europe see growth from automotive rubber demand. Rising population and refined cooking oil demand are expected to boost hexane demand.

In 2016-17, 719 people were admitted to hospitals in Devon, Cornwall and Isles of Scilly for eating disorders, the highest on record and more than double 2010-11's 298. Cases included two children under 10, 13 aged 10-12, 91 aged 13-15, and 117 aged 16-18, plus older adults. Anorexia made up 45% of cases, bulimia 24%, and women and girls comprised 94%. Charities called the figures worrying, stressing early intervention and noting that rising admissions may reflect increased awareness or insufficient outpatient care rather than more sufferers.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated June 14, 2021, reporting its entry into an underwriting agreement with Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC to issue and sell $5.0 billion in unsecured notes in four $1.25 billion tranches: 0.309% notes due 2023, 0.584% notes due 2024, 1.550% notes due 2028, and 2.000% notes due 2031. Net proceeds of approximately $4.98 billion are intended for general corporate purposes. The notes are governed by a September 16, 2016 indenture and a June 16, 2021 Officers’ Certificate, with specified maturities, interest payment dates, optional redemption terms, and covenants limiting liens and sale-leaseback transactions. If both a change of control and an investment-grade ratings downgrade occur, NVIDIA must offer to repurchase affected notes at 101% of principal. The notes are unsecured senior obligations structurally subordinated to subsidiary liabilities. Chief Financial Officer Colette M. Kress signed the report on June 16, 2021.

Victor Tony Jones, convicted of killing two people in 1990, is scheduled for execution on Tuesday. He has asked the Supreme Court to block his execution, but the court has denied all of the more than 30 emergency stay requests it has received this year, typically without explanation. If Jones is executed, he would become the 34th person put to death in 2025, reflecting the highest execution total in roughly a decade. The surge follows President Trump’s January order ending the Biden administration’s moratorium on federal executions. Florida has played a significant role, with Jones potentially becoming the state’s 13th execution this year. The court’s streak of emergency denials contrasts with its 2024-25 term rulings favoring death row inmates in three cases. The justices are also set to hear a case this term on how courts should evaluate multiple IQ scores to determine intellectual disability in capital defendants.

The $75,000 LIHI contract for Camp Second Chance covers the first four months. Signed November 21, 2017, it requires LIHI to operate the encampment and provide case management. It specifies stay duration, notes campers provide security and lack veto power, and bans minors. 2018 contract unfinalized; renewal discussed.

Tesla's entry into the U.S. auto industry centered on the 2016 launch of the Model 3, a $35,000 electric vehicle designed for mass-market scale that attracted over 500,000 pre-orders. By 2018, the company faced severe production challenges and financial strain, recording a $743 million quarterly net loss and falling short of the 5,000-unit weekly output needed for profitability before finally hitting the target after months of "production hell" and CEO Elon Musk's admission that excessive automation was a mistake.

The case situates Tesla within a $270 billion U.S. passenger car market dominated by established automakers such as GM, Ford, and Toyota, characterized by high barriers to entry, low brand loyalty, and accelerating shifts toward electrification, autonomous driving, connectivity, and mobility services.

Founded in 2003, Tesla executed a "Master Plan" to enter at the luxury high end with the Roadster, Model S, and Model X before moving down-market with the Model 3. The company pursued extreme vertical integration, manufacturing up to 80 percent of Model 3 components in-house—including battery packs at its Nevada Gigafactory—but encountered significant quality and assembly-line issues after bypassing traditional beta production testing.

Tesla bypassed independent dealerships, selling through company-owned stores while building a proprietary Supercharger network and service centers. Its 2016 "Master Plan, Part Deux" envisioned fully autonomous vehicles operating in a shared ride-hailing fleet. Although Tesla was credited with forcing industry-wide innovation toward sustainable transportation, questions remained about its long-term profitability and survival.

DLSS 4 transitions from convolutional neural networks to transformer-based AI models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing, improving temporal stability, reducing ghosting, and enhancing motion detail and image quality. The North Carolina Court of Appeals affirmed the trial court’s dismissal with prejudice of Lewis Williamson’s appeal challenging the Town of Surf City’s closure of a 20-foot portion of North Shore Drive under N.C.G.S. § 160A-299. Williamson contended the Town acted improperly by intending to construct public facilities on the portion of the street vested in the Town through the closing. The court held the closure valid because the Town complied with all procedural requirements of § 160A-299 and, as an adjacent landowner, obtained a vested interest in part of the closed street under § 160A-299(c). The court found the statute contains no limitation on a town’s authority to close a street based on its intent, distinguished *Wooten v. Town of Topsail Beach*, and rejected Williamson’s argument that the statute requires closing the entire length and breadth of a street, citing *Wofford v. Highway Commission*.

This study examined relationships among person-centered care (PCC), trust in physicians, and medication adherence, and trust's mediating role, in Japanese hemodialysis patients. Poor adherence, reported in over 50% of such patients, worsens chronic kidney disease management and increases mortality. PCC may improve adherence, but evidence is limited. In this multicenter cross-sectional study at six outpatient facilities (April 2022–February 2023), approved by Fukushima Medical University, adult hemodialysis or combined hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis patients who could complete questionnaires were included; those without regular prescriptions, with severe dementia, or complete blindness were excluded. Adherence was measured with the Japanese ASK-12 scale.

This application, a continuation of International Application No. PCT/CN2019/130905 claiming priority to Chinese Patent Application No. 201910196567.3, discloses a rotating shaft mechanism and a foldable mobile terminal. The mechanism comprises a main shaft assembly, a swing arm assembly with at least one connecting rod group and at least one swing arm group, and a support assembly with support plates. Swing arms are fixed to the two housings and rotatably connected to the main shaft assembly on axes parallel to but different from those of the connecting rods; each swing arm is slidably and rotatably connected to at least one corresponding connecting rod. When folded, the swing arms rotate inward, driving the support plates to rotate inward and enclose folding space for the flexible display, while the connecting rods and swing arms rotate so that the folded mechanism thickness approximates that of the two stacked housings. Engaging gears on the connecting rods ensure synchronous rotation. A limiting mechanism with cooperating cams and an elastic part restricts rotation positions to maintain folded and unfolded states. A flexible blocking layer attached to the main shaft assembly covers notches to improve appearance. The mobile terminal includes the mechanism, two housings, and a flexible display, wherein folded non-adhesive display areas form a droplet or semi-arc shape within the enclosed space, achieving uniform thickness and improved folding and bending effects.

This study develops hybrid forecasting models for COVID-19 confirmed and death cases in five intensely affected countries: USA, India, Brazil, Russia, and UK. Because COVID-19 datasets contain both linear and nonlinear patterns, single models such as ARIMA, ARNN, or SVM are inadequate. The authors propose hybrid ARNNS and SVMAR models to generate short-term and long-term memory out-of-sample forecasts, reducing bias and variance in predictions. Daily case data from the Global Change Data Lab, spanning more than 300 observations through January 15, 2021, are used. The data are non-normally distributed and do not exhibit spiky dwindling trends. The analysis aims to provide policymakers, health professionals, and economists with realistic pandemic estimates to inform decision-making.

The railway between Lincoln and Grimsby opened in 1848, decades before the local football clubs were founded, to transport goods and fish. Its River Witham bridge at Stamp End was designed by MS&LR engineer John Fowler using William Fairbairn’s tubular iron girder design. It is possibly the oldest surviving wrought iron box girder railway bridge in Britain, maybe even the world, and predates the Menai and Royal Albert bridges in using the technology. The bridge originally had a central iron span with timber side spans, which were replaced by metal decks in 1903; the structure was reinforced in 1948 and received a new steel central deck in 1968. Network Rail recently replaced it in a £7m project.

A multicenter cross-sectional study of 1,411 patients treated at emergency departments in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, between August and September 2022 measured SARS-CoV-2 S-IgG, NC-IgG, and serum neutralization against Wu01, BA.4/5, and BQ.1.1. S-IgG seroprevalence was high (95.6%), but only 67.7% of participants were vaccinated according to national recommendations and 45.7% reported prior infection. Neutralizing activity was markedly reduced against BQ.1.1 compared to Wu01 and BA.4/5, with geometric mean ID50s decreasing 23.6-fold and 4.2-fold, respectively; only 73.8% of a stratified sub-sample showed detectable BQ.1.1 neutralization. S-IgG levels were the strongest predictor of neutralization for all variants, yet 59.6% of participants with S-IgG below 1,000 BAU/ml lacked detectable BQ.1.1 neutralization. The authors conclude that despite high seroprevalence, substantial immune evasion by BQ.1.1 and incomplete vaccination compliance leave a considerable proportion without protective neutralizing activity, underscoring the need for improved vaccine uptake.

Scientists developed kirigami-inspired parachutes made from perforated Mylar disks that unfurl automatically and fall straight down regardless of initial orientation. In tests, the parachutes landed closer to targets than traditional designs. A 0.5-meter prototype lowered a 1-kilogram bottle from 60 meters, reducing its fall speed to about 14 meters per second. Though generating less drag than conventional parachutes, the simple-to-make disks show promise for humanitarian aid, drone deliveries, and potential space missions.

Intraday trading involves buying and selling financial instruments within the same trading day, using methods such as scalping or day trading. In the U.S., pattern day traders must maintain at least $25,000 in equity and are limited to 4x leverage. Success requires a backtested, quantified trading plan, realistic goals, trading liquid stocks, choosing a reputable broker, and periodically assessing results. While intraday trading can be profitable, most traders lose money because it is a zero-sum game and strategies are difficult to backtest due to intraday noise. Popular strategies include scalping, momentum, news-based, and trend following. The best markets are those with high liquidity and volatility, such as stocks, futures, and options, though stocks are preferred over forex. The best time to trade is the first two hours after the market opens. Common technical indicators are generally viewed as less effective on intraday timeframes than on daily data.

The North Carolina Court of Appeals reversed the trial court's dismissal of controlled substance charges against Ryan Jeffery Adams, which was based on double jeopardy after a tax liability on seized drugs was docketed and partially paid. The court held the dismissal conflicted with prior North Carolina appellate decisions in *State v. Ballenger* and *State v. Creason*. It rejected the defendant's reliance on the Fourth Circuit's *Lynn v. West*, noting federal appellate decisions are not binding on North Carolina courts, and stated reexamining prior holdings or modifying the statute was beyond its authority.
The court of appeals judgment in State v. Montecalvo was reversed based on same-day State v. Szefcyk.

Netflix fell 0.68% in premarket trading Monday despite signing producer Shonda Rhimes to create future shows for the platform while her existing series remain on ABC. The decline may reflect a Barron's article calling for shares to drop 50% as content producers like Disney leave for rival services and company debt rises. Netflix is up 32.95% this year.

The passage describes design patterns for containerized and distributed systems. For single-node patterns, it covers documenting containers using Dockerfile directives such as EXPOSE, ENV, and LABEL; the sidecar pattern for augmenting application containers; the ambassador pattern for brokering external interactions, including client-side sharding, service discovery, and request splitting for experimentation; and the adapter pattern for standardizing interfaces such as monitoring, logging, and health checks. For multi-node distributed patterns, it introduces microservices and details replicated load-balanced services, including stateless and session-tracked replication, caching layers, and SSL termination. It also examines sharded services, covering sharding functions, consistent hashing, and hot sharding; the scatter/gather pattern for parallel request processing, its overhead and straggler problems, and replicated sharded implementations; and event-driven Function-as-a-Service architectures, highlighting benefits like simplified deployment and automatic scaling, as well as challenges from forced decoupling and operational complexity.

The Buck Sweep is a misdirection off-tackle run with two pullers, popularized by Tubby Raymond and the University of Delaware as a signature Wing-T play. Designed to exploit defensive indecision and hit vertical creases off-tackle or outside, it conceals the ball through layered hand-offs and backfield motion. Its angle-blocking scheme allows smaller linemen to displace defenders horizontally, though the play requires precise timing, spacing, pullers who can block in space, and extensive practice. Blocking assignments are specified for each position against 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts. Variations include a Shotgun Wing-T version featuring a QB shuffle and potential read option, and an I-Wing version where the tailback takes a counter step with otherwise similar blocking and backfield paths.

Concerns that Google will discontinue Inbox by Gmail have grown amid a looming Gmail redesign that incorporates some Inbox features and a perceived slowdown in Inbox updates. However, a Google spokesperson stated there are no changes planned for Inbox, which remains a product for specific workflows and testing innovative features. Recent unannounced updates, including A.I.-powered Highlights, unsubscribe suggestions, and follow-up reminders, indicate ongoing development. Inbox also retains exclusive features such as automatic bundles, trip organization, integrated cross-service reminders, and a distinct interface. Since its 2014 launch, Google has positioned Inbox as a potential long-term replacement for Gmail while maintaining both services. With a non-trivial and growing user base, including 10 million Android installs, Inbox does not appear abandoned or scheduled for discontinuation.

Freelance writer Oobah Butler created a fake TripAdvisor listing for “The Shed at Dulwich,” a nonexistent restaurant at his London garden shed. Using fabricated reviews, a website with photos of household products posing as dishes, a burner phone, and an appointment-only format without a specific address, the listing was approved by TripAdvisor in May 2017. Through fake reviews from friends and family, the restaurant climbed from last place to become London’s top-ranked restaurant by November, drawing global reservation requests and 89,000 views in a single day. Butler exposed the hoax in Vice, though TripAdvisor stated it had already penalized the listing and removed some reviews. The incident highlighted vulnerabilities in online review verification and the ease of manipulating platform algorithms. Butler later opened the shed for one night, serving instant food to actors and real customers who had seen the listing.

Stroke causes heterogeneous upper extremity motor impairments that complicate recovery and assessment. This study characterizes forearm muscle coordination in seven chronic stroke and seven able-bodied individuals using an easy-to-use, wearable high-density EMG (HD-EMG) sleeve across functional hand, wrist, and forearm movements. The authors evaluate isolated control and muscle coupling via co-contraction indices and correlation metrics, and assess sub-muscle coordination through muscle synergy analysis, comparing synergy composition between groups. Following artifact correction and sleeve standardization, HD-EMG data were mapped to six forearm muscle groups. The work demonstrates the feasibility of combining HD-EMG features that correlate with functional movement ability, providing preliminary identification of motor-related biomarkers that could be leveraged to improve stroke rehabilitation, movement disorders research, and clinical care.

Port Gregory experienced repeated power outages from Thursday through Monday, spoiling food and preventing use of medical equipment. Using cryogenic four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM), which detects polarization via asymmetries in Kikuchi band intensities, researchers mapped polar textures in SrTiO3 down to ~20 K. Below the antiferrodistortive transition (T_AFD ≈ 105 K), the material hosts locally polar nanodomains with a correlation length of ~20 nm and periodic spatial ordering at a length scale of ~25 nm. Upon cooling below T_q ≈ 40 K, the quantum paraelectric regime exhibits fragmented, smaller polar clusters (~14 nm correlation length) and a loss of periodic ordering. This evolution indicates that quantum paraelectricity arises from a re-entrant disordering of preformed polar nanodomains driven by quantum fluctuations, rather than from a complete absence of polarization. The authors suggest these textures likely underlie anomalous low-temperature properties and motivate study of their relation to externally tuned ferroelectric and superconducting orders.

Apple historically held most of its cash in foreign subsidiaries to avoid repatriation taxes, but recent U.S. tax reform has given the company greater access to those reserves. Wrexham led 12-10 at halftime, but Aidyn Jones and Owain Davies scored second-half tries to put Dinbych ahead, and they held on after Jack Ratcliff replied. The dollar jumped to two-month highs against yen and seven-week highs against euro on Friday after U.S. September jobs data showed a 0.5 percent rise in average hourly earnings despite hurricane-related payroll declines. Traders price in a 93 percent chance of a December Fed rate hike.

The S&P 500 fell 0.11 percent Friday, ending a six-day run of record highs, while the Nasdaq rose 0.07 percent to a sixth record close. September nonfarm payrolls fell by 33,000, the first drop in seven years, due to hurricanes. Walgreens and CVS each fell 4.9 percent on Amazon drug-sale fears, and Costco dropped 6 percent. For the week, the S&P 500 rose 1.2 percent, the Dow added 1.6 percent, and the Nasdaq gained 1.5 percent.

Kuwaiti parents were sentenced to death for torturing their 3-year-old daughter to death. They were accused of keeping her body in a freezer. The verdict requires appeals and supreme court review. Executions are rare in Kuwait.

The speaker said the team is unaccustomed to the media attention but accustomed to playing on the road, having started every series away from home. After a disappointing loss to the Devils where they were too passive and failed to make the game difficult or get enough shots on Brodeur, they stressed the need to play harder, be more greasy, and stick with their plan. They noted the team has persevered through tight, adverse situations and one-goal games, and expressed confidence that the lacking effort and skating is an easy fix for the next game.

Singapore Airlines will restart non-stop Singapore-Newark flights on October 12, 2017, becoming the world's longest route at approximately 9,537 miles. The airline discontinued the route in 2013 because its Airbus A340s were unprofitable, but will now use the new Airbus A350-900ULR, of which it is the launch customer. Scheduled flight times are about 18 hours and 45 minutes to Singapore and 18 hours and 25 minutes to Newark, saving over four hours versus connecting flights. The aircraft will have 161 seats in a two-class layout with 67 business and 94 premium economy seats and no standard coach. Service will begin three times weekly before moving to daily after one week. Newark will be the carrier's fifth U.S. destination, and Singapore plans future non-stop A350-900ULR service from Los Angeles.

The American Occupational Therapy Association's Academic Fieldwork Coordinators Academic Leadership Council Research Promotion ad hoc committee conducted a mapping review of United States fieldwork education literature from 1989 to 2020. Using the AOTA Occupational Therapy Education Research Agenda – Revised (2018) as a framework, the committee screened 1,619 abstracts and reviewed 165 full-text articles, yielding 67 included studies. The review found that literature disproportionately addresses Level II occupational therapy fieldwork while Level I fieldwork and occupational therapy assistant programs remain underrepresented. Of the seven Education Research Agenda categories, only four were represented, with Instructional Methods and Learner Characteristics and Competencies predominating; no articles mapped to Theory Building, Signature Pedagogies, or Promotion of Diversity, Inclusion, and Equity. The authors conclude that these persistent gaps require collaborative research among academic fieldwork coordinators, faculty, fieldwork educators, practitioners, students, and consumers, and recommend that future Education Research Agenda revisions formally incorporate fieldwork-specific categories.

Peruvian police may expel two foreigners for allegedly inciting protests against Hudbay Minerals' Constancia copper mine. The interior ministry said they entered as tourists but violated that status by inciting opposition to mining, disturbing public order. Hudbay suspended operations in November amid protests demanding development projects.

Egypt's Antiquities Ministry announced a 4,400-year-old tomb near Cairo's pyramids, likely belonging to Hetpet, a high-ranking 5th Dynasty female official. The tomb contains wall paintings of hunting, fishing, and monkeys. Archaeologists are excavating another tomb believed to be hers in Giza's western necropolis.

This lecture summarizes the collective Thomson scattering spectrum. The scattered power depends on a spectral density function derived from electron density fluctuations using a test particle formalism. For Maxwellian plasmas, susceptibilities are defined using the w function and the collective parameter alpha = 1/(k λ_De). In the incoherent limit (alpha → 0), the spectrum reflects individual electron scattering with no plasma response. For high-frequency modes, electron plasma waves (Langmuir waves) emerge with a dispersion relation ω² = ω_pe² + 3T_e k²/m_e, yielding electron density and temperature from resonant peaks. For low-frequency modes, ion acoustic waves appear when zT_e/T_i > 3, providing information on ion temperature and charge. The Salpeter approximation shows that as alpha increases, the ion feature dominates the total scattered cross-section over the electron feature. Electron-ion drift breaks symmetry in ion acoustic wave damping, causing peak asymmetry that enables measurement of the local current component along the scattering vector. Practical complications include magnetic field effects, collisions damping coherent features, and finite volume, time, or collection angle averaging that can broaden spectra and obscure parameters. Current research addresses non-Maxwellian distributions and multi-angle scattering diagnostics.

The shiitake mushroom market is projected to reach USD 26.7 billion by 2022 and USD 35.4 billion by 2023 at a 15.31% CAGR. Asia Pacific held 82.54% share in 2017, with China at 97%. Growth is driven by nutritional and medicinal benefits. Dried and fresh segments grow at 14% and 15.59%; pharmaceutical and cosmetic applications witness highest growth. Major players include Bonduelle SA, Mitoku Company, and The Mushroom Company.

Turkey’s education administration is highly centralized and bureaucratic, with top-down appointments and limited accountability, transparency, or participation, and the country falls behind OECD averages in PISA scores and GDP. This study proposes an alternative local education boards model grounded in good governance principles. Using a mixed-methods exploratory sequential design, the authors analyzed qualitative data from 16 OECD countries that exceed OECD averages in PISA and GDP, and quantitative data from a survey of 421 teachers and administrators in Seyhan, Adana. The research found that high-performing OECD countries manage education through diverse local boards including teachers, parents, students, mayors, and NGOs. Survey results showed that 61.5% of participants prefer local administration, 61% favor elected boards over directorates, and respondents support diverse representation in provincial, district, vocational, and school boards, with most operational duties decentralized to local units while general policy and law-making remain central. The proposed Local Education Boards model features a central National Education Supreme Council and Ministry implementation unit, alongside provincial/district education boards, vocational boards, and school boards responsible for local planning, budgeting, personnel, and supervision. The study concludes that replacing Turkey’s single-authority directorate system with participatory, decentralized board structures is necessary to improve education quality, democratic participation, and sustainable development, and recommends pilot testing the model.

A federal judge denied the government's request to delay transgender individuals enlisting in the military starting January 1. The Pentagon will comply; the White House said DOJ is reviewing legal options.

Texas teachers, parents, and administrators worry that a new law replacing the STAAR standardized test with three shorter exams throughout the school year may increase rather than reduce student stress and testing time. The law, HB 8, takes effect in 2027-28 and bans practice tests while requiring scores to be released within about two days. However, critics note that the system largely codifies testing practices many districts already use, and the end-of-year exam will still heavily influence high-stakes A-F school accountability ratings. A required study on reducing testing weight in ratings is not due until 2029-30 and is not mandatory to implement. Skeptics fear strict STAAR-like testing protocols—such as seating charts and managed breaks—could apply to all three exams. Some educators advocate for using less stressful, norm-based assessments like MAP and want greater teacher input in designing the new tests. Florida's similar switch to three tests reportedly increased total testing minutes.

NVIDIA RTX IO integrates with Microsoft DirectStorage to enable GPU-based lossless decompression, reducing CPU overhead and improving I/O performance by delivering compressed data directly from NVMe SSDs to the GPU. The NVIDIA A40 data center GPU, based on the GA10x Ampere architecture, delivers up to 2x FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to 5x AI throughput compared to the Quadro RTX 6000, with 48GB of memory scalable to 96GB via NVLink, PCIe Gen4, and virtual GPU support. Ampere GPUs support 4K at 120Hz and 8K at 60Hz via DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC and HDMI 2.1. They feature fifth-generation NVDEC hardware decoding, including the first GPU hardware AV1 decode support up to 8K60 HDR, and seventh-generation NVENC encoding up to 8K HEVC. The GA10x architecture provides up to 2x performance gains in shading, ray tracing, and AI through second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores with structural sparsity, and GDDR6X memory. The GeForce RTX 3090 incorporates 24GB GDDR6X and 10,496 CUDA cores, while the RTX 3070 uses GA104 with GDDR6 and outperforms the RTX 2080 Ti. The RTX A6000 workstation GPU features 10,752 CUDA cores and 48GB GDDR6. Error Detection and Replay (EDR) technology for GDDR6X detects memory transmission errors to prevent crashes during overclocking.

A bug in Atlassian's Jira and Confluence exposes private AWS server keys via a vulnerable proxy allowing server-side request forgery attacks, risking network compromise and data theft. Atlassian fixed the flaw, rated 6.1 by NIST, but many organizations still run outdated versions. A researcher found over a dozen exposed major companies and government agencies; some fixed or shut down servers after notification, while others remain vulnerable. Updating the software is recommended.

Spotify, Comcast, and Oracle recently announced co-CEO structures, joining a small but notable wave of companies adopting the once-unusual model. Data shows co-CEOs lead about 1.2% of Russell 3000 companies, a figure that has remained stable over five years, though experts predict more boards may consider the structure amid rapid change. Research indicates companies with dual leaders posted higher average annual shareholder returns than single-leader firms from 1996 to 2020. However, the model presents risks, including unclear authority, power struggles, and operational ambiguity. Companies like Netflix have maintained co-CEOs long-term, while others such as Chipotle and Sony have used it temporarily or reverted to a single CEO. Leadership experts emphasize that success requires clearly defined roles, aligned strategic vision, and strong collaboration between the two leaders. Some observers caution that the structure should be used sparingly due to governance concerns and dual compensation costs, and note that power imbalances can persist when a new co-CEO joins an established leader.

The author argues that England manager Gareth Southgate must abandon his cautious tactical approach and outdated 4-2-3-1 formation to avoid a group-stage exit at the 2018 World Cup after a 1-0 qualifying win over Slovenia. Dele Alli should be the only No. 10, with Raheem Sterling deployed on the wing. Ahead of friendlies against Brazil and Germany, Southgate should adopt a more adventurous system, such as three centre backs with advanced wing-backs, to utilise the attacking strengths of Alli, Marcus Rashford, and Harry Kane.

NVIDIA Corporation filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended October 25, 2015. Revenue for the third quarter was $1.305 billion, up 7% year-over-year, with net income of $246 million compared to $173 million in the prior year period. For the nine months ended October 25, 2015, revenue was $3.609 billion with net income of $406 million. GPU business revenue increased 12% in the quarter and 9% year-to-date, driven by high-end GeForce gaming products. Tegra Processor revenue declined 23% in the quarter and 14% year-to-date due to lower OEM smartphone and tablet sales, partially offset by growth in automotive infotainment. The company recorded $8 million and $97 million in restructuring and other charges related to the wind-down of its Icera modem operations, with an additional $25 million to $35 million expected in the fourth quarter. A $21 million charge was recorded for the voluntary recall of SHIELD 8-inch tablets. The company is engaged in patent litigation with Samsung and Qualcomm. NVIDIA completed a $400 million accelerated share repurchase and paid $152 million in dividends during the nine-month period, subsequently announcing an 18% quarterly dividend increase and an intention to return approximately $1.0 billion to shareholders in fiscal year 2017. As of October 25, 2015, the company held $471 million in cash and cash equivalents and $4.257 billion in marketable securities, with $1.406 billion in long-term debt.

In *Berenice M. Brubaker v. State of New York* (Court of Claims, May 5, 1961, Claim No. 34735), the claimant, later substituted by Ralph Hartwell Brubaker as administrator of the estate, sought damages for the State’s appropriation of approximately 365 acres near Massena for the St. Lawrence River Project. The State made four appropriations between May 1955 and May 1957: roughly 183 acres north of Middle Road; a 0.15-acre permanent flooding easement; a 25-acre parcel; and a 55.38-acre transmission line easement. Applying *United States v. Miller* and *Shoemaker v. United States*, the court held that for the first taking, no increase in value caused by the government’s commitment to the project could be included, as there was no proof the land was probably within the original project scope; it found the highest and best use industrial and awarded $32,000. For the later takings, the land was treated as adjacent property, and the court awarded $100 for the flooding easement, $39,750 for the 25-acre parcel (including direct and consequential damages), and $27,700 for the transmission easement, finding that taking destroyed the remaining market value. Interest was awarded on each sum from specified dates until judgment.

The passage describes a display device including a substrate, a pixel electrode, an opposing electrode, an encapsulation portion with alternately deposited organic and inorganic layers, and a planarization layer covering an edge portion of the encapsulation portion. An edge side surface of the planarization layer forms a larger angle with the substrate surface than an edge side surface of the encapsulation portion. The planarization layer provides a flat upper surface for forming patterns such as touch electrodes and touch wiring, which reduces dead space and parasitic capacitance, while the encapsulation portion blocks moisture penetration.

In *Bost v. Illinois State Board of Elections*, a majority of Supreme Court justices appeared inclined to allow Rep. Michael Bost to challenge an Illinois law counting mail-in ballots received up to 14 days after Election Day, reversing lower court findings that he lacked standing. While broad “candidate standing” proposed by Bost’s attorney Paul Clement drew resistance, several justices, including Elena Kagan and Neil Gorsuch, seemed receptive to a standard requiring candidates to show the challenged law places them at an electoral disadvantage relative to prior rules without proving likely defeat. Justices Sotomayor and Ketanji Brown Jackson questioned whether Bost, who holds a safe seat, could meet even that standard. Illinois’s solicitor general initially accepted Kagan’s test but later retreated, arguing standing requires showing the law would affect the outcome or cause reputational injury by tainting victory. Justices also expressed concern about forcing such challenges into post-election litigation and the difficulty of fashioning remedies.

This study employs scanning electron microscopy in-situ microscale four-point probe measurements coupled with microstructural characterization to quantify electrical resistivity contributions in Al-Mg-Si alloys. Three alloys with varying Al, Si, and Mg contents were synthesized and overaged through heat treatments to stabilize non-coherent Si and Mg₂Si precipitates. Macroscopic Van der Pauw and microscopic four-point probe methods measured electrical resistivity. X-ray diffraction and electron microscopy confirmed Al, Si, and Mg₂Si phases and revealed large grains, permitting the neglect of grain boundary, dislocation, and vacancy contributions. Bulk resistivity increased with higher total solute content, and heat treatment at 350°C for 72 h yielded the lowest resistivity across all compositions. Direct microscale measurements demonstrated that grain interior resistivity depends on heat treatment rather than alloy composition, remaining similar across different compositions under identical treatments. Individual Si and Mg₂Si precipitates contributed equally to resistivity regardless of shape, as their intrinsic resistivities are orders of magnitude higher than the aluminum matrix, making the effective resistivity depend primarily on precipitate volume fraction rather than phase identity. Consequently, bulk resistivity increased linearly with total solute concentration, with the slope determined by heat treatment and the intercept corresponding to grain interior resistivity.

Y-Cross is a versatile drop-back passing concept used across football offenses, typically featuring a post route, a deep crosser, and a running back in the flat as its core, with various backside tags. Designed to create big plays and intermediate completions, it can be adapted to personnel by using either a tight end or slot receiver as the crosser. The concept is effective against man coverage and Cover 4, but less ideal against Cover 3 due to the post safety. The quarterback's progression generally reads post, then deep crosser, then running back check-down or dig, with reads adjusted based on safety movement. Variations include a post-wheel combination and a curl-flat tag for use against single-high defenses.

H. White, and Kate and Anna. It includes letters from Secretary of State John Hay and U.S. Counsel Herbert H. D. Bitcoin hit a six-week high on Tuesday, rising 4.4 percent to $9,340.88 after a 50 percent first-quarter loss, driven by news that Goldman Sachs hired a digital asset head and Barclays is exploring a cryptocurrency desk. A Thomson Reuters survey found one in five financial institutions may trade cryptocurrencies within 12 months. The rally lifted other digital currencies, pushing total market capitalization to $427 billion and 24-hour volume to $28 billion, the highest since early March and February 10. Analysts said regulatory challenges persist.

DWI arrests in Wichita Falls have declined, with 25 between January 1 and March 19 this year, down from 39 in 2016 and 38 in 2017, and only five over St. Patrick’s Day weekend. Sgt. Harold McClure credits increased public awareness, rideshare services like Uber and Lyft, and police presence. An Uber study found 90% of riders feel it reduces drunk driving.

It presents a specific backtested trading strategy with defined rules, Python code, and performance statistics from 713 trades. The text addresses multiple trading styles—scalping, day trading, swing trading, and position trading—while warning that most short-term traders fail to make money. It covers fundamental, technical, and sentiment analysis, citing tools such as moving averages, Fibonacci retracements, candlestick patterns, and support and resistance levels. This study presents a bibliometric analysis of artificial intelligence (AI) in STEM education from 2020 to 2024, using citation analysis of 35 journal articles sourced from the Dimensions database. The analysis found a significant increase in publications and citations in 2024, with 15 publications receiving 234 total citations, averaging 15.62 citations per publication, while no citations were recorded for 2021 through 2023. The United States led contributing countries with nine documents and 103 citations, followed by China with five documents and zero citations. The most cited authors were Nesra Yannier, Kenneth R. Koedinger, and Scott E. Hudson, each with one document cited 55 times. The most cited journal was the *International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education* (55 citations), and the most cited article was “Active Learning is About More Than Hands-On: A Mixed-Reality AI System to Support STEM Education” (55 citations). Carnegie Mellon University was the most cited institution (55 citations). The reviewed literature indicates that AI benefits STEM education by enabling personalized learning, advanced analytics, and instructional automation, thereby improving student engagement, knowledge levels, and learning outcomes. However, challenges include ethical concerns, data privacy, learner autonomy, the need for increased AI literacy among stakeholders, and potential negative effects on student engagement when AI assumes a predominant role in monitoring and controlling the learning process. The research spans interdisciplinary journals, and the study concludes that balanced implementation is necessary to maximize AI’s benefits while addressing its limitations.

The Trump administration’s proposal to impose a $100,000 fee on new H-1B visas could imperil thousands of jobs at U.S. colleges and universities, which employed more than 16,000 workers through the program as of June 30. Institutions rely on these visas to hire academic staff, researchers, and physicians, many of whom are connected to medical centers. Nearly half of the 16,797 approved college visas were concentrated at just 50 institutions, and the top 100 hold about 70 percent of the total. While the fee does not apply to current visa holders and it remains unclear if universities must pay it for new applications, experts warn that many institutions could not afford it. The directive allows exemptions if the secretary of homeland security deems the hiring in the national interest, and higher education advocates argue that research and medical roles qualify.

Leonard Achan argues that although natural disasters cannot be prevented, their health impacts can be reduced through better preparation and hardened infrastructure. Citing hurricanes Maria, Harvey, and Irma, he notes post-storm hazards including contaminated floodwaters, toxic chemical releases, mold, disease-carrying mosquitoes, and nursing home deaths from lack of air conditioning. He recommends elevating disaster preparedness, educating the public, securing hazardous sites, strengthening seawalls, making electrical grids storm-resistant, and treating disasters like preventable diseases to protect lives before, during, and after events.

At the California Democrats State Convention on Feb. 25, Dave Min and Hans Keirstead won state party endorsements in their respective races against Republican Reps. Mimi Walters and Dana Rohrabacher in Orange County, though both faced opposition from fellow Democrats during the contentious process. No candidates for governor or U.S. Senate reached the 60 percent endorsement threshold. In three other targeted GOP House districts, leading Democratic candidates Mike Levin, Bryan Caforio, and Jay Chen also failed to reach the threshold. Among convention delegates, Kevin de Leon led Dianne Feinstein for Senate, while Gavin Newsom received the most support for governor with 37 percent.

European scientists from five institutions are establishing October 10 as International Coccolithophore Day to highlight microscopic ocean algae that regulate climate by capturing carbon dioxide, producing oxygen, and forming calcite plates that create geological climate records. These organisms generate over 1.5 billion tonnes of calcium carbonate annually, storing carbon in deep-sea sediments while nourishing marine food webs, but climate change threatens their survival. Research teams across Europe study their carbon storage, viral and bacterial interactions, ocean distribution, and fossil records to understand past and future climate impacts. The campaign aims to increase ocean literacy, policy focus, and public recognition of their planetary role.

A Tennessee woman's video of her son Keaton recounting bullying prompted support from athletes and entertainers. The video received over 18 million views, and a crowdsourcing page raised over $29,000. Delanie Walker invited the family to a game, Tyler Byrd and teammates plan to visit Keaton at school, and entertainers including Kelsea Ballerini, Dale Earnhardt Jr., and Snoop Dogg offered support.

This study used the UK Health Improvement Network (THIN) database, with replication in the UK Biobank, to compare prodromal symptoms and drug prescriptions before diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB). All three conditions showed increased frequencies of investigated health conditions in the five years before diagnosis, with distinct prediagnostic profiles: memory problems were more frequent before AD, tremor before PD, and hallucinations, confusion, falls, and depression before DLB. Autonomic dysfunctions such as constipation, urinary disorders, and hypotension were more strongly associated with PD and DLB than with AD. Lower prescriptions of antihypertensive and antidiabetic medications were observed before all three diagnoses, while beta-blockers were more frequently prescribed before PD and DLB than AD. Statin prescriptions were lower before PD compared to AD and DLB, a finding replicated in the UK Biobank. Among PD patients, those who developed dementia within five years after diagnosis had higher pre-diagnosis prescriptions of drugs for hypercholesterolemia, constipation, depression, and psychosis than those who did not. The findings highlight long-term prodromal phases and differential associations with medications across these neurodegenerative diseases.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2015. Total revenues for the three and six months ended June 30, 2015 were $955.0 million and $1.89 billion, increases driven by higher Model S deliveries. Net losses were $184.2 million and $338.4 million, with basic and diluted net loss per share of $1.45 and $2.68. Gross margin was 22.3% for the quarter, down from 27.7% in the prior year. As of June 30, 2015, cash and cash equivalents were $1.15 billion, total assets were $6.47 billion, total liabilities were $5.70 billion, and stockholders' equity was $715.9 million. The company continued developing Model X, with customer deliveries planned for late Q3 2015, and constructing the Gigafactory in Nevada, with first production targeted for Q1 2016. Tesla also announced new Tesla Energy storage products. It entered into a $150 million Warehouse Facility and a $500 million senior secured asset-based revolving credit agreement, under which $50 million was borrowed. The 2018 convertible senior notes became convertible in Q3 2015 after the stock price exceeded 130% of the conversion price for the required period. Tesla expects 2015 capital expenditures of about $1.5 billion and plans to deliver 50,000 to 55,000 Model S and Model X vehicles in 2015.

Gunmen kidnapped 52 farmers, mostly Uzbeks, from three villages in Afghanistan's northern Jowzjan province. Police blamed Taliban fighters; elders are negotiating for their release and a rescue operation may follow. A Taliban spokesman could not confirm the report. Last week, gunmen attacked Red Cross workers there.

Gold trading is speculating on gold prices via futures, options, spot markets, stocks, CFDs, and ETFs, typically cash settled without physical delivery. Gold serves as a store of value, currency, and safe haven asset to hedge market losses. The article backtests a weekend swing trading strategy on the GLD ETF from 2004 to 2021. Holding from Thursday close to Friday close averaged 0.14% with a 1.4 profit factor, while buying Thursday close and selling Monday open averaged 0.19% with a 1.3 profit factor. Adding one simple parameter improved results to acceptable levels for small positions. Gold exhibits an overnight positive bias, though trading it is difficult due to its dependence on macro news.

Investing.com headlines note AMD shares surge after an AI chip deal with OpenAI, gold rallies above $3,900/oz amid yen weakness and U.S. rate cut bets, and Evercore’s Emanuel says a bubble scenario could take the S&P 500 to 9,000 in 2026. This study reviewed 18 Voluntary National Reviews (VNRs) from Eastern Mediterranean Region countries (2016–2021) to assess comprehensiveness of reporting on health-related Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) targets and indicators. While all VNRs established SDG monitoring mechanisms and 17 prioritized targets to national contexts, comprehensiveness varied by country income level: high-income countries reported on more SDGs and had higher reporting rates for mortality and morbidity indicators (60%), while low-income countries reported the fewest means-of-implementation indicators (14.7%). Only eight VNRs explicitly mentioned 2030 targets. Nine reported data availability, with SDG3 data availability ranging from 48% to 93% among those countries; 14 VNRs cited limited data availability as a core challenge, noting insufficient human resources, low data quality, and lack of disaggregation. The most frequently reported indicators were maternal mortality (100%), neonatal mortality (83%), and under-5 mortality (78%). Trend data were uncommon, with Qatar alone reporting trends for all SDG3 indicators, and WHO/EMRO data were often omitted from VNRs despite routine country reporting. Indicators derived from civil registration and vital statistics and disease surveillance systems were reported more often than those from routine health information systems or national surveys. The authors conclude that weak national health information systems and data gaps hinder evidence-based action, and strengthening regulatory frameworks, civil registration systems, and population-based surveys is essential to achieving health-related SDGs in the region.

Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones was fined $250,000 by the NFL for an obscene gesture toward fans at MetLife Stadium during the Cowboys' 37-22 win over the Jets. The passage describes the ADS868xW ADC technical specifications, including an integrated high-bandwidth, low-noise ADC driver and selectable internal or external 4.096V voltage reference. The internal reference is factory-trimmed and temperature-compensated but can shift due to solder heat; external references use an internal buffer. The ADC supports single-ended and differential bipolar/unipolar inputs with straight-binary output. Alarm features monitor analog input levels against programmable thresholds and AVDD against fixed 4.7V and 5.3V limits, providing active and tripped flags. The device uses a multiSPI interface supporting legacy SPI, dual-SDO, and source-synchronous protocols, along with daisy-chain topologies. Operational states—RESET, ACQ, and CONV—are controlled by the RST and CONVST/CS pins. Programming occurs via 32-bit data transfer frames using read, write, set, and clear commands across nine configuration registers. Application information covers industrial analog input modules, programmable input alarms with hysteresis, and power-saving NAP and power-down modes. Power supply decoupling and PCB layout recommendations are also provided to optimize performance.

Peppertype supplies templates, copywriting frameworks, and autocorrect for small businesses. The author recommends Jasper.ai and discloses that the article contains affiliate links.

An international team including Princeton University and the Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory developed an AI tool called Diag2Diag that uses existing sensor inputs to generate synthetic, highly detailed plasma data for diagnostics that cannot directly capture it, particularly at the plasma edge where stability is critical. Trained on data from the DIII-D National Fusion Facility and detailed in *Nature Communications*, the system could make future commercial fusion reactors more compact, affordable, and reliable by reducing hardware needs. It also provided evidence supporting the magnetic island theory for suppressing edge-localized modes via resonant magnetic perturbations. Developers note potential applications in spacecraft and robotic surgery.

Origin PC announced a new Eon15-S gaming laptop starting at $999 with an Nvidia GeForce 1050Ti, Intel Core i3, and 120GB SSD. A $100 upgrade adds a Core i5 and double storage. Unlike Dell's $899 Inspiron 15 7000, it offers an IPS display and 24/7 US-based lifetime support. CNET will test and review the laptop soon.

The Supreme Court declined to hear Ghislaine Maxwell's appeal. Maxwell, serving a 20-year sentence for sex trafficking of a minor, argued a 2007 non-prosecution agreement between Jeffrey Epstein and the Southern District of Florida barred her prosecution. The 2nd Circuit ruled such agreements bind only the issuing district. Solicitor General D. John Sauer said the clause was too unusual to warrant review. The Court denied the petition during its Sept. 29 conference.

The 5-Day Low of The Range Strategy enters long positions when IBS is below 0.25 and the close is lower than the previous five days' lowest low, exiting after five days. From January 1993 onward, it generated 517 trades with 309 winners, a 60% win ratio, and a 0.46% average return per trade, surpassing the 0.11% average for any five-day period. Profitability peaks between three and seven days, producing a 10.76% annualized return over 510 days in the market compared to 2,826 days for buy and hold. The strategy has underperformed recently. It can be adapted for short selling using a 0.75 or 0.9 range criterion, though short strategies are less profitable and harder to trade than long strategies.

The MicroGEM Sal6830™ SARS-CoV-2 Saliva Test, the first saliva-based RT-PCR point-of-care (POC) device with emergency use authorization, uses patient self-collected saliva deposited directly into a sealed cartridge, eliminating operator handling of biohazards and reducing sample mix-ups. Unlike other POC platforms requiring nasopharyngeal swabs and operator-mediated sample transfer, it is designed for non-laboratory trained healthcare workers and captures intact virions via a bead-based system.

In a study at two U.S. clinics, six non-laboratory trained operators tested blinded samples, correctly identifying all 24 negative samples and 23 of 24 positive samples (one was invalid). In a prospective clinical comparison with the Cepheid Xpert Xpress CoV-2/Flu/RSV test, Sal6830™ showed 87.2% positive percent agreement, 97.2% negative percent agreement, and 93.3% overall agreement; differences were attributed to Sal6830™ detecting intact virions while the comparator detects viral debris. Nine healthcare workers completing a usability questionnaire found the device easy to use, well integrated, and easy to interpret, and all felt confident using it without technical support.

The study concludes that Sal6830™ enables accurate RT-PCR COVID-19 detection in POC settings by non-laboratory trained staff using simple self-collected saliva.
State of Washington v. Douglas John Nelson reversed and remanded.

This patent application describes a voice-directed inspection system, method, and device for supporting multiple inspectors simultaneously inspecting a business asset. A host computer provides an inspection plan to a site computer, which manages distribution of the plan’s sections. Multiple inspection assistance devices, each comprising a portable computer and headset, request assignments from the site computer. The site computer determines if multiple unfinished, non-interfering sections exist and assigns distinct sections to different devices. Each device provides audible commands to its inspector, receives audible completion updates, and transmits updates back to the site computer, which forwards them to the host computer. The system enables parallel inspections of large or complex assets, improving efficiency while allowing real-time or batched progress reporting.

Neural Radiance Cache (NRC) is a neural shader that caches radiance; it trains tiny neural networks on live game data to infer multi-bounce lighting from single-bounce path-traced rays, improving GPU performance and indirect light quality.

The Supreme Court in *New York State Rifle & Pistol Ass’n v. Bruen* announced a two-step test for Second Amendment challenges: courts must determine whether the Amendment’s plain text covers the challenged conduct, and if so, whether the government’s regulation is consistent with the Nation’s historical tradition of firearm regulation. Critics, including Justice Breyer and Judge Reeves, argue the test is deeply impractical because judges are lawyers, not historians, and lack historical expertise. The author contends this criticism misapprehends the judicial role, as judges decide cases and adjudication inherently requires answering historical questions about past events and laws. Originalists respond that legal evidence is durable, the plain-text step is largely settled by precedent, and judges possess legal tools—such as burden-shifting—to resolve uncertainty without acting as legislators through means-ends scrutiny. While identifying historical traditions requires work, early firearms regulation was limited and legal sources are reliable. The author concludes that because constitutional law is rooted in history, judges must engage with the past despite the difficulty.

The speaker celebrates winning the cup and praises Buffalo's series. They reflect on missing last year's playoffs, the grueling ten-year journey since winning the Stanley Cup, and the team's adversity and injuries, noting Hull played hurt and expressing pride in the veteran team's experience and hard work.

The lecture advocates for a "decision mentality" in poker, focusing on expected value rather than actual outcomes. It outlines three levels of hand reasoning: Level 1 (hand versus a specific hand), Level 2 (exploitative play evaluating one's hand against an opponent's range using pot odds and equity), and Level 3 (optimal play considering range versus range to make opponents indifferent). The professor explains the importance of effective stack size, table position—from under the gun to the button—and equity, which can be calculated based on outs, opponent ranges, or remaining cards. Pre-flop recommendations include raising to roughly 2.25 big blinds when antes are present, going all-in with 12 or fewer big blinds, and playing tighter ranges in early position while expanding to approximately 55% of hands on the button. The lecture also uses a "Who's Taller" analogy to explain the necessity of blinds and antes, briefly defines bluffing and value betting, and demonstrates equity calculations with examples.

In the UK, nearly half of ovarian cancer cases are diagnosed in emergency care, with only around one-third identified at the earliest stages. Low public awareness and dismissal by healthcare providers contribute to late diagnosis, and 90% of women do not know the four main symptoms: persistent bloating, difficulty eating or feeling full quickly, urinary frequency or urgency, and persistent pelvic or tummy pain. Other potential signs include lower back pain, digestive discomfort, unexpected post-menopausal bleeding, and unusual fatigue. There is currently no screening test; while a CA-125 blood test can indicate higher protein levels, it cannot diagnose ovarian cancer on its own. Ovarian Cancer Action provides a free online symptom checker and a downloadable symptoms diary to help women identify patterns and seek medical advice sooner. Early detection offers a 95% survival rate, compared to 16% at stage four, yet less than a third of cases are diagnosed at stages one or two. Experts emphasize that symptom awareness is vital and encourage everyone to recognize the signs to support timely medical intervention.

Hurricane Maria struck Puerto Rico on September 20, 2017, causing over US $82 billion in damages and destroying around 80% of crop value. Prior studies of excess mortality had limitations in duration, cause scope, and population displacement. This research proposes a semiparametric Poisson model to estimate cause-specific excess deaths, controlling for temporal variation, intra-annual seasonality, and population displacement. The model incorporates period and cause indicators with interactions, a smooth function for day of year, and year effects. Excess deaths are estimated by comparing post-emergency and baseline predictions using a population size unaltered by displacement to avoid double counting.

DryShips Inc. (NASDAQ: DRYS) filed a 6-K on April 17th reporting issuance of 7,912,449 shares at an average price of $1.79, raising $14.5 million of a $30 million Fixed Amount Requested through Kalani Investors, the third consecutive failure to fulfill a request. Shares outstanding totaled 54.92 million, with 16.8% dilution from April 10th through April 17th. With $173.4 million remaining under the current Prospectus Supplement and an equity market capitalization of $106 million, market demand remains weak, with equity issuance at only 8.86% of volume traded. The author suggests DryShips may pursue debt financing and issue remaining equity after a debt-related price bounce, while the company is now further from the $75 million equity market value threshold for F-3 issuance.

Hendrik Bessembinder's 2017 study of 26,000 US stocks from 1926 to 2015 found that only 43% outperformed one-month Treasury Bills, while just 86 stocks generated half of all returns. Although stocks historically produced average annual returns of about 10%, the median stock performed poorly, making individual stock picking risky. A similar Norwegian study of the Oslo Stock Exchange from 1985 to 2017 confirmed this concentration, finding that only 2.7% of IPOs accounted for all value creation. The passage concludes that because most stocks fail to beat Treasury Bills, investors should either buy passive funds or maintain significant diversification when selecting individual stocks.

Dylan Drysdale, Tim Loughran, and Garry Cullum won class titles at the 2017 Molecule ProKart Series final at KartSport Hamilton. Cullum secured a record fourth title. In Wifiplus KZ2, Mat Kinsman won heats and the Pre-Final but crashed in the Final, where Aaron Wilson won; Drysdale took the series title by four points over Wilson, with Kinsman third. In KZ2 Masters, Enrico van der Griend crashed in heat three, and Tim Loughran won the round and series, with Brett Hollander second and van der Griend third. Cullum won all KZ2 Restricted races and the series by 20 points over Regan Hall, with Aaron Wooley third. Time penalties were issued for kerb hopping.

If a referee does not stop play for an injury, either team may kick the ball out. The opposing team then takes the throw-in and should return the ball backward to the team that kicked it out. Neither team should exploit this courtesy. Similarly, if the referee stops play for an injury, the team receiving the dropped ball should return possession to the opponent if the injured player's team had clear possession.

Predictive maintenance (e-Maintenance) is a critical component of e-Manufacturing, integrating real-time monitoring with e-Business tools such as ERP and CRM via web-enabled technologies to achieve near-zero downtime and optimal asset performance. Key research needs include predictive intelligence, data-to-knowledge conversion, secure informatics platforms, distributed computing, and workforce training. Reconfigurable maintenance systems enable intercompany cooperation, diagnostic knowledge sharing, and adaptation to demand changes through variable maintenance policies. Modular systems utilize distributed architectures, sensor-based remote monitoring, and expert systems that leverage historical data to detect adverse conditions, assess reliability, and support dynamic reconfiguration. In conclusion, modern production environments require integrated reconfigurable maintenance systems to respond rapidly to market fluctuations, reduce costs, ensure quality, and maintain overall production reliability.
NASA plans to use a nuclear device via HAMMER to destroy Bennu before it reaches Earth. Bennu has a 1 in 2,700 chance of hitting Earth on September 21, 2135, and has been monitored since 1999.

As the constitutional executive for a set term, he will execute laws, manage foreign relations and revenue, command forces, and communicate with Congress. He pledges to respect executive limits, preserve peace abroad, honor state sovereignty, practice strict economy to extinguish national debt, and equally favor agriculture, commerce, and manufactures. This study examines how the discourses of Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC) Presidents have shaped education policies and national identity construction. Following the 1974 Cyprus Peace Operation and 1983 TRNC declaration, the education system was restructured with close ties to Turkey, emphasizing Turkish Cypriot national identity. The Turkish Cypriot Education Council implemented structural reforms in teacher training, curriculum, infrastructure, and quality improvement. History textbooks have historically presented Turkish identity-centered narratives emphasizing Turkish-Greek conflict and Turkish Cypriot victimization, though since the early 2000s, EU harmonization and post-2004 Annan Plan reforms introduced more pluralistic, reconciliatory approaches; these initiatives have faced setbacks and societal resistance over concerns of identity erosion. Presidential priorities varied: Rauf Denktaş emphasized national identity and Turkey integration; Mehmet Ali Talat focused on European harmonization and modernization; Derviş Eroğlu stressed Turkey cooperation and technical education; Mustafa Akıncı promoted multiculturalism and peace; and Ersin Tatar emphasized national identity and Turkey integration. Key policy elements include Turkish-medium instruction, educational cooperation with Turkey, internationalization of higher education, and debates over secularism versus religious education. The study concludes that education policies should adopt scientific neutrality, multi-perspective history curricula, and long-term strategic frameworks independent of political ideology, while balancing cooperation with Turkey and local educational autonomy.

New England Patriots wide receiver Malcolm Mitchell, who caught six passes for 70 yards during the team’s Super Bowl comeback win over the Atlanta Falcons, overcame literacy struggles while at the University of Georgia by teaching himself to read starting with children’s books. He launched Read with Malcolm, a youth literacy initiative that promotes book ownership and reading benefits for students in underserved communities, responding to findings that children with the lowest reading scores account for a majority of non-graduates and that many low-income families lack age-appropriate books. Mitchell, who graduated with a communications degree, was drafted by the Patriots, and wrote the children’s book *The Magician’s Hat*, will receive the Promise Hero Award from America’s Promise Alliance. He credits his mother, Pratina Woods, as a key inspiration and aims to empower children to read and overcome adversity.

Digital accessibility remains critically low globally, with only 5.2% of top websites meeting WCAG Level AA standards, partly due to inadequate accessibility training in Computer Science (CS) curricula. India, home to the world’s largest computing student population, lacks formal and informal accessibility education initiatives. To address this gap, the authors designed and delivered a one-day, hands-on workshop for 73 Indian software professionals and CS educators around Global Accessibility Awareness Day. The workshop comprised five modules—Accessibility Basics, Design, Development, Reporting, and Teaching Accessibility—supplemented by thematic booths featuring assistive technology demos, case studies, and lightning talks. Pre- and post-workshop surveys evaluated changes in knowledge, confidence, and attitudes. Participants, who included individuals with disabilities and represented varied experience levels, rated all core activities positively; 100% would recommend the workshop, 90% agreed it was effective and engaging, and 52% reported a significant shift in their perception of accessibility. Qualitative feedback identified demand for advanced technical training, AI applications, inclusive design for neurodiverse users, organizational policy strategies, and real-world case studies. The authors recommend future workshops distribute preparatory materials, customize content by professional role, replace disability simulations with lived experiences, and provide continued engagement opportunities. The study concludes that experiential, informal training effectively builds accessibility capacity across India’s academic and industry sectors, though sustained follow-up is needed to ensure workplace application.
