Threat model failures include assuming users pick strong passwords, relying on outdated cryptographic key sizes such as Kerberos’ 56-bit DES keys, trusting all certificate authorities in the SSL/TLS ecosystem, and failing to account for physical hardware compromises. Mechanism failures include iCloud’s missing rate limiting on the Find My iPhone API, Citibank’s insecure account ID handling in URLs, an Android SecureRandom bug that exposed Bitcoin private keys, SSL certificate null-byte injection attacks, and buffer overflows that corrupt stack return addresses to execute injected shellcode or existing code via return-to-libc attacks. The professor notes that defenses like non-executable stacks are imperfect, and a better design principle is minimizing the trusted computing base. Administrative details include two quizzes and no final exam during finals week.

Tesla, Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2018, reports unaudited consolidated financial statements. Total assets were $27.91 billion, total liabilities were $22.64 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $3.91 billion. For the three months ended June 30, 2018, total revenues were $4.00 billion with a net loss of $742.7 million; for the six months, revenues were $7.41 billion with a net loss of $1.53 billion. Net cash used in operating activities was $528.0 million for the six months, while financing activities provided $770.3 million. On January 1, 2018, Tesla adopted ASC 606 using the modified retrospective method, changing revenue recognition for certain vehicle sales with resale value guarantees to sales with a right of return and reducing the opening accumulated deficit by $623.2 million. The company has two reportable segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. As of June 30, 2018, total debt was $10.91 billion, customer deposits were $942.1 million, inventory was $3.32 billion, and accrued warranty was $524.0 million. During the period, Tesla recognized a $13.3 million abandonment loss on in-process research and development acquired from SolarCity. In March 2018, stockholders approved a 20.3 million stock option performance award to the CEO tied to market capitalization and operational milestones.

Wyong Race Club and owner Gary Leafe are disputing $8300 compensation after his horse Eyes To Heaven was attacked by dogs at the track on December 29, with the club seeking a settlement. Jockey Hugh Bowman is appealing two careless riding charges to be eligible to ride Winx in the Apollo Stakes on February 17. Trainer Michael Tubman celebrated his 70th birthday with a Rosehill win by his mare Bye See. Broadcaster Gary Harley and trainer Evan Holland were unhurt after being bumped by a horse at Gosford. Trainer Brad Widdup, who recently left Godolphin, is aiming for more Sydney Saturday runners after recent success. Stewards questioned Corey Brown’s ride on Exceltic in the Canonbury Stakes. Gerald Ryan’s colt Menari is being prepared for The Galaxy, while Terravista trialled ahead of the Lightning Stakes and TJ Smith Stakes. Kinky Boom firmed for the Golden Slipper after winning at Caulfield; trainer Tony McEvoy also trains favourite Sunlight.

The author rejects Yale professor Keith E. Whittington’s argument that professors must self-censor to protect academic freedom following the Kirk assassination. The author contends that Whittington’s “germane and competent” standard for classroom speech is excessively restrictive and enforced with viewpoint discrimination. While Whittington warns that offensive speech risks legal protections for academia, the author asserts academic freedom is a fundamental right protecting all faculty expression, even controversial or offensive views, because free inquiry is essential to academia. The author challenges Whittington’s citation of AAUP advice on discretion, noting the 1940 Statement did not use that term and 1970 Interpretive Comments affirmed controversy as central to academic freedom. The author concludes that demanding discretion out of fear destroys rather than defends the right.

Microsoft Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2016, reported revenue of $20.5 billion, down from $21.7 billion in the prior year quarter, and net income of $3.8 billion compared to $5.0 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $0.47 versus $0.61. For the nine months ended March 31, 2016, revenue was $64.7 billion and net income was $13.7 billion.

Total assets as of March 31, 2016, were $181.9 billion, up from $176.2 billion as of June 30, 2015. Cash and cash equivalents were $7.2 billion, long-term debt increased to $40.9 billion from $27.8 billion, and total stockholders' equity decreased to $74.8 billion from $80.1 billion.

Beginning in fiscal year 2016, the company reports under three new segments. For the quarter, Productivity and Business Processes generated $6.5 billion in revenue, Intelligent Cloud generated $6.1 billion, and More Personal Computing generated $9.5 billion. Revenue from Windows 10 licenses is recognized ratably over the device life, resulting in net deferrals of $1.6 billion for the quarter and $4.6 billion for the nine months recorded in Corporate and Other.

Operational highlights included commercial cloud annualized revenue exceeding $10 billion, Office 365 Consumer subscribers reaching 22.2 million, Microsoft Azure revenue growing 110%, Windows 10 active on over 270 million devices, and Xbox Live monthly active users increasing 26% year-over-year to 46 million.

During the quarter, the company repurchased $3.6 billion of common stock and declared dividends of $0.36 per share. Restructuring charges related to the phone business restructuring plan totaled $780 million to date, with actions expected to eliminate up to 7,800 positions.

The filing notes early adoption of new accounting guidance for share-based payments, pending adoption of standards for revenue recognition, financial instruments, and leases, and disclosures regarding various legal proceedings and contingencies.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated November 28, 2018, reporting results from its 2018 Annual Shareholders Meeting held that day. Of 7,677,511,729 shares entitled to vote, 6,722,310,265 were voted. Shareholders elected all fourteen director nominees, approved the compensation of named executive officers on an advisory basis, and ratified the appointment of Deloitte & Touche LLP as the independent registered public accounting firm for fiscal year 2019.

British consumer credit complaints rose to 7,281 in the second quarter from 5,846 a year earlier, the Financial Ombudsman Service said, criticising lenders for inadequate repayment checks. Payday loans accounted for nearly half. Payment protection insurance remained the most complained-about product, with 42,401 new cases and a compensation deadline of August 29, 2019.

The study investigates ferroelectric topological textures in barium zirconate titanate (BZT, Ba(ZrxTi1−x)O3) using finite-temperature molecular dynamics simulations with a first-principles parameterized effective Hamiltonian. Motivated by prior predictions of −2 antiskyrmions in bulk rhombohedral BaTiO3 (BT), the work explores whether substituting Ti with Zr can stabilize the requisite rhombohedral phase above room temperature while preserving or enriching topological quasiparticle behavior.

In an ordered 12.5% Zr superlattice with a doubled unit cell along [111], stable nanodomains hosting nontrivial topology are induced at 1 K. The chemical doubling causes the texture to split into two distinct regions along the nanodomain axis: one half contains a −2 antiskyrmion composed of six −1/3 topological quarks, while the other half hosts a +4 skyrmion composed of six +2/3 quarks. The two halves share the same vortex skeleton but differ by an integer charge offset of +1 per vortex, attributed to the reversed chemical motif (Ti–Zr–Ti versus Zr–Ti–Zr) and modified local anisotropy. An alternative field-theoretic interpretation models the chemical doubling as a static binary background that imposes a gauge-covariant sign flip, accounting for the integer offset without requiring core displacement.

For randomly distributed Zr ions (0–12.5%), nontrivial topological textures remain robust at 1 K but become increasingly distorted with concentration. Random substitution introduces quenched anisotropy and disorder that pin and shear vortex lines, producing a patchwork “skyrmion-glass” state with spatially heterogeneous fractional charges and fluctuations in the plane-resolved topological charge along the nanodomain axis.

Thermal stability assessments show that the critical temperature for nanodomain collapse is non-monotonic with Zr concentration: it decreases initially (minimum near 6–8% Zr) and partially recovers toward 12.5%, reflecting competition between ferroelectric softening and disorder pinning. Pure BT exhibits the highest stability (~65–110 K depending on diameter), while random BZT textures persist up to nearly 100 K, with larger diameters generally more robust.

Near room temperature, the 12.5% ordered superlattice remains rhombohedral (transition ~320 K on cooling, ~345 K on heating). Although zero-field retention of nanodomains at 293 K fails, a local electric field of ~350 kV/cm along [111] writes and stabilizes cylindrical domains whose walls carry a uniform +4 topological charge (volatile operation). In contrast, the 12.5% random composition under the same field destabilizes into a multidomain state due to disorder-assisted nucleation.

The work establishes BZT as a platform for engineered ferroelectric topology, demonstrating that chemical substitution can enrich the zoo of emergent textures through fractionalized charges, that textures survive random substitution and finite temperature, and that field-stabilized states are achievable near room temperature in ordered structures. The authors suggest epitaxial strain, electrostatic engineering, and compositional patterning as routes toward nonvolatile room-temperature retention and multi-state functionality.

Using QSGŴ many-body perturbation theory, the authors investigate WSe₂/CrI₃ van der Waals heterostructures and find that QSGW and QSGŴ predict type I band alignment with both band edges localized on WSe₂, unlike LDA's type II prediction. The A and B excitons of WSe₂ are preserved, and novel interlayer excitons emerge energetically between them, exhibiting significantly enhanced brightness compared to intralayer CrI₃ Frenkel excitons. Proximity-generated magnetic fields from CrI₃ induce spin splittings in the WSe₂ excitons, with the largest splitting (~1000 GHz) occurring for the B exciton in ferromagnetic trilayers, while bilayer and antiferromagnetic trilayer configurations show smaller splittings (tens to hundreds of GHz). These splittings are highly sensitive to the van Hove alignments between Cr-d and W-d states. The robust interlayer excitons combine the brightness of Wannier-Mott excitons with magnetic character, establishing these heterostructures as a promising platform for photonic and spintronic applications.

On May 23, 2001, Dr. Madhav Godbole, chairman of the Maharashtra committee renegotiating the Dabhol Power Company (DPC) agreement with Enron, resigned after criticism by NCP leader Sharad Pawar, but withdrew it hours later after Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh and the state Cabinet affirmed full confidence in him. Pawar had called the committee's approach "negative" but later clarified these were personal views. The Centre, seeking to avoid a Centre-state dispute, said it would act as facilitator and accept the Godbole panel's recommendations, with Power Minister Suresh Prabhu reassuring DPC lenders that steps were being taken to resolve the crisis. The Centre also proposed involving the Power Trading Corporation to sell Dabhol power in deficit states, and an inter-ministerial committee was formed to examine proposals. Meanwhile, Maharashtra referred the DPC dispute to the Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission to buy time and defer arbitration. DPC had issued a preliminary termination notice to the Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB) over unpaid bills. Domestic lenders, who had suspended Phase II disbursements, hoped for resolution at a Friday meeting but noted they lacked Centre counter-guarantees unlike foreign lenders. The controversy prompted other states like Karnataka to review private power projects. Extracts from the Godbole committee report highlighted serious flaws in Dabhol's base-load design, noting Maharashtra needed load-following capacity, and that the project's tariff was higher than initially proposed despite "protracted negotiations." The report also suggested a judicial enquiry into the deal and stated Maharashtra needed only a marginal portion of Phase I power.

Michael Liersch of JPMorgan offers five tips for inexperienced investors. First, create a budget to track spending and determine how much to invest. Second, reframe decisions by focusing on long-term financial goals rather than immediate sacrifices, and view market declines as opportunities. Third, maintain a long-term perspective and avoid emotional reactions to market fluctuations. Fourth, seek input from a partner, family member, or financial adviser who can challenge your views. Fifth, begin with small steps like paying down debt or contributing to an IRA, and automate savings to build momentum.

Asia-Pacific stocks rose as U.S. officials downplayed North Korea military risks. Japan's economy grew 4.0% annualized in April-June. U.S. consumer prices rose in July. U.S. stocks posted their biggest weekly decline in months. Fed and ECB will publish July minutes; Dallas Fed's Kaplan said rates are appropriate.

The reproduction number (R) is a widely used measure of pathogen propagation but fails to control for the quantity of diagnostic tests performed, resulting in biased estimates of time-varying viral spread. This paper proposes the acceleration index (ε), an elasticity that measures the proportional responsiveness of cases to tests by comparing current and average viral speeds. The authors demonstrate that R is a special case of ε and is less accurate when tests vary over time: R overestimates spread when testing is high and underestimates it when testing is low. Applying the framework to French COVID-19 data from May 2020 to October 2022, they find that R significantly underestimated viral acceleration relative to ε, especially during the autumn 2022 Omicron wave; similar patterns in five other countries are noted in an appendix. The study concludes that public health authorities should use the acceleration index—or a test-adjusted R incorporating infectivity and test intensities—to accurately track pandemic dynamics and inform interventions such as lockdowns, as ε provides a more parsimonious, unit-free, and sufficient statistic for viral spread.

Pershing Square's US long portfolio increased marginally from $5.96B to $6.01B in Q2 2017, with seven positions remaining steady. The top three holdings—Restaurant Brands International (~41%), Chipotle Mexican Grill (~20%), and Mondelēz International (~10%)—accounted for ~71% of the portfolio. New stakes included Automatic Data Processing (~3%), where Ackman initiated a proxy fight. Air Products and Chemicals was fully disposed of at ~$145 per share. Howard Hughes Corp increased by one-third through warrant conversion, while Mondelēz saw continued selling. Steady positions included Platform Specialty Products and Nomad Foods. Other holdings included Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. Pershing Square Holdings has underperformed the S&P 500 since 2012, though the original flagship fund has returned ~20% annually. Ackman's short book includes Herbalife at 9% capital allocation.

The Poland Local Board of Education dissolved teacher Cassandra Kibler’s contract after her Ohio teaching license was revoked over allegations of an inappropriate relationship with a student. In other business, Strollo Architects presented two facility options to reduce operational costs, involving campus consolidations, closures, new construction, and repurposing Dobbins Elementary for athletics. The board took no action and will review the proposals.

Compilation of May 7–8, 2001 news articles regarding Enron and energy markets. In California, power traders and generators including Enron profited from the state’s electricity crisis, while Enron won a federal appeals ruling allowing it to supply state universities through investor-owned utilities rather than the spot market, saving the company $12 million monthly. Enron may bid for U.K. power stations to reduce trading risk and capitalize on price volatility under a new electricity trading system. Scottish Power is restructuring and its chief executive declined to comment on reports it may buy Enron’s Portland General unit. In India, lenders to Enron’s Dabhol Power Company threatened legal action against the company, the Maharashtra State Electricity Board, and the government over payment defaults and disputed tariffs; Indian customs blocked Rs 300 crore of DPC equipment over duty disputes, and DPC confirmed a May 11 meeting with a Maharashtra state negotiating committee. Northern Border Partners, whose general partners include Enron and Williams Cos., completed its $100 million acquisition of Midwestern Gas Transmission from El Paso Corp. BP Amoco is considering a $200 million liquefied natural gas terminal in Tampa, Florida, while Enron plans a pipeline from the Bahamas to serve the Florida market.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2017, describes its business, operations, and risk factors. The company’s strategy centers on building best-in-class platforms and productivity services for an intelligent cloud and intelligent edge infused with artificial intelligence. It operates three reportable segments: Productivity and Business Processes, comprising Office, LinkedIn, and Dynamics; Intelligent Cloud, comprising server products, Azure, and enterprise services; and More Personal Computing, comprising Windows, Devices, Gaming, and Search Advertising. In December 2016, Microsoft completed its acquisition of LinkedIn Corporation for $27.0 billion. Research and development expense was $13.0 billion in fiscal year 2017. As of June 30, 2017, the company employed approximately 124,000 people. As of December 31, 2016, the aggregate market value of common stock held by non-affiliates was $466.5 billion, and as of July 31, 2017, there were 7,702,243,979 shares outstanding. The filing outlines risks including intense competition; execution challenges in cloud and subscription transitions; impairment of goodwill and intangible assets; intellectual property, piracy, and infringement claims; cyber-attacks and security vulnerabilities; government litigation and regulatory actions, including data protection laws such as the EU General Data Protection Regulation; potential tax liabilities; and hardware quality and supply chain issues.

Syrian rebels faced a Wednesday deadline to accept Russian-brokered surrender terms for southern Daraa and Quneitra provinces or face renewed military assault. Moscow rejected rebel proposals for a ceasefire, army withdrawal, and safe passage, insisting instead that the regime army and local police return to pre-2011 positions alongside Russian military police. The regime has expanded its control of Daraa to around 60 percent, displacing between 270,000 and 330,000 people, many of whom are blocked from entering Jordan and Israel. More than 140 civilians have been killed since the offensive began on June 19. The UN Security Council scheduled an emergency meeting for Thursday, while Jordan's foreign minister visited Moscow to call for a ceasefire.

NVIDIA Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 28, 2019, reports revenue of $2.58 billion, down 17% year-over-year, and net income of $552 million, or $0.90 per diluted share. GPU business revenue declined 21% to $2.10 billion, while Tegra Processor revenue increased 2% to $475 million. Gaming revenue fell 27%, Data Center revenue decreased 14%, Automotive revenue rose 30%, and Professional Visualization grew 4%. Gross margin was 59.8%, and operating expenses rose 19%. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $8.48 billion. The company entered into an agreement to acquire Mellanox Technologies Ltd. for approximately $6.9 billion, subject to regulatory approvals, and intends to return $3.0 billion to shareholders by the end of fiscal year 2020 through dividends and share repurchases, though repurchases may be delayed until after the Mellanox closing. The filing also discloses pending securities litigation related to channel inventory and cryptocurrency mining disclosures.

This study examined Ethiopian national education policy intentions and secondary school principals' and teachers' conceptualizations of curriculum differentiation (CD). Analysis of the 2023 Education and Training Policy, the 2020 General Education Curriculum Framework, and the 2012 Guidelines for CD and Individualized Educational Programs revealed incoherent policy intentions: the former two emphasize tracking through school types, streams, and fields of study, while the latter emphasizes differentiating curriculum components within inclusive classrooms. Interviews with two principals and 17 teachers from one regular and one special day secondary school found diverse conceptualizations, ranging from viewing CD as gifted programs, student placement into tracks or subjects, special curricula for ability groups, identification of talent, to general curriculum planning—often reflecting a lack of awareness. The study concludes that absent coherent policy guidance and limited practitioner engagement in reforms have produced misaligned conceptualizations and practices, particularly the conflation of high academic achievers with gifted students through separate school types. It recommends aligning policy intentions, operationalizing CD clearly, and increasing curricular flexibility in secondary education.

Former FBI Deputy Director Andrew McCabe was fired on March 16, two days before his scheduled early retirement at age 50, amid an Office of the Inspector General investigation into his approval of unauthorized media disclosures related to the Hillary Clinton email probe. Under the Federal Employees Retirement System, he is at risk of losing access to his estimated $60,000 annual pension and health insurance coverage until age 57 and eight months. While some lawmakers have offered him temporary Capitol Hill employment to help him qualify for benefits, experts say such work must be in a primary law enforcement position or require another 10 years of service. McCabe can file an appeal.

The St. Louis Blues have nine core players signed through at least the next three seasons at a combined $47.425 million cap hit, including Vladimir Tarasenko, Alex Pietrangelo, Colton Parayko, and Jake Allen. While some deals carry risk, such as Alexander Steen’s potential regression, several contracts appear to be bargains. The team faces upcoming decisions on defensemen with shorter-term deals, including Jay Bouwmeester and RFA Joel Edmundson. Forwards Paul Stastny and Robby Fabbri are entering key contract years, creating pressure to re-sign or trade them. Despite a cautious approach that has meant letting some veterans walk and lacking a surplus scorer, the Blues hold several favorable contracts and avoid burdensome deals, leaving them in a strong salary cap position.
Simone Askew became the first black woman to serve as first captain of West Point's Corps of Cadets. She assumed duties Monday following a 12-mile march with 1,200 cadets.

On February 24, 2021, NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K announcing financial results for the quarter and fiscal year ended January 31, 2021. The filing includes a press release (Exhibit 99.1) and CFO commentary by Colette M. Kress (Exhibit 99.2), furnished but not deemed "filed" under the Securities Exchange Act. Colette M. Kress signed the report as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

The league viewed Las Vegas as a successful NHL market prospect despite building, ownership, and economic issues. There was no timetable, and the process was unrelated to Seattle. Early market enthusiasm was evident at the team name announcement. The expansion team's Stanley Cup Finals appearance is viewed as a positive story reflecting the nature of sports. The speaker reiterated a scientific view that there is insufficient information to draw a link, and noted the franchise prioritized community outreach to expand its fan base.

The ISDA Press Report for June 4, 2001, covers proposed Basel II capital rules, derivatives developments, and regional financial news. Basel II, targeted for agreement by year-end 2001 and implementation in 2004, faces criticism from Australian regulators that residential mortgage risk weightings are unfairly high; Asian central bankers who cite infrastructure gaps delaying readiness; and global banking groups that warn of excessive conservatism, high compliance costs, complexity, and negative effects on smaller and emerging-market banks. Derivatives officials hope some Basel II calibrations will be revised, though the 15% "W" factor charge on credit derivatives remains contested, with ISDA set to argue for its abandonment in July. The industry is also finalizing standardized documentation for convertible default swaps and addressing successor-entity issues for credit derivatives, spurred by AT&T's pending restructuring. Deutsche Bank and ABN-Amro withdrew from Argentina's debt exchange over potential U.S. securities violations, risking millions in fees. California's electric-grid operator faces federal scrutiny over diminished board independence due to state government influence. Finally, structured option-based investment products are gaining traction in developed markets and are viewed as viable for retail investors in India.

The Dow hit a record high despite a likely government shutdown. The S&P 500 fell 2.36% last week, dropping over 3% from Thursday's record high to a local low of 6,212.69, its lowest close since early July. An index closed 1.96% lower Friday on Apple weakness, with potential support near 22,300. The VIX surged to 21.90, its highest since June 23. Markets are set to open roughly 0.5% higher Monday, with S&P 500 futures near 6,300. Crude oil fell 2.79% Friday and another 2.1% after OPEC+ agreed to raise September output by 547,000 bpd. The U.S. threatened 100% secondary tariffs on buyers of Russian crude, and Goldman Sachs forecasts oil at $64 in Q4 2025. Analysts warn the correction may not be short-lived, with focus on earnings from Palantir and AMD.

Central Illinois is using traps and a Decatur lab to test mosquitoes for West Nile virus in under 24 hours, enabling rapid spraying. The state saw its first human case in mid-May, two months earlier than last year, prompting a CDC investigation. No human cases have been reported in Macon County, though a mosquito batch tested positive in June. Illinois recorded 90 human cases and eight deaths last year.

The bark Cape Horn Pigeon sailed in December 1891. On September 10, 1892, while whaling in the Okhotsk Sea, it was arrested by an Imperial Russian naval officer, taken to Vladivostok, and detained until October 1. The crew was forced to serve the Russian vessel. The captain protested and telegraphed the U.S. legation. The U.S. Chargé d’Affaires contacted the Russian ministry, which replied that the bark had been released. Russia’s 1893 note did not support the officer’s claim that the Okhotsk Sea was closed.

No. 15 Florida defeated Auburn 114-95 on Tuesday night. Canyon Barry scored a season-high 30 points for the Gators, who won their seventh straight game. The score was tied 50-50 at halftime before Florida dominated the second half. Thirteen players scored in double figures. Barry's school-record streak of made free throws ended at 42. Florida shot 56 percent from the field and made 11 of 19 3-pointers. Auburn fell to 16-10, 5-8 in the SEC.

An Islamic State car bomb killed 24 people and wounded 67 in Baghdad's Sadr City on January 2, 2017, while the group cut a key road to Mosul, its last major stronghold. U.S.-backed Iraqi forces are battling fierce resistance to retake Mosul, having recaptured a quarter of the city since October. Prime Minister Haider al-Abadi and French President Francois Hollande affirmed their commitment to defeating terrorism. Militants also attacked military positions away from Mosul, killing pro-government fighters near Baiji and executing nine Sunni tribal fighters near Udhaim, while a separate Baghdad blast killed one civilian.

This study uses China Education Panel Survey data from 13,981 students to examine the relationship between parental education level and child cognitive ability via multiple linear regression. It finds a significant positive correlation, with each additional year of parents’ maximum education increasing children’s cognitive ability by 0.019 points. The effect is mediated by educational expectations and parent-child interaction, is stronger for girls than boys, stronger in urban than rural areas, and stronger among children with lower cognitive ability. The study provides policy implications for addressing cognitive disparities and the “Matthew effect.”

This lecture addresses portfolio-level public market financing for sustainable real estate. It defines Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) as publicly traded companies investing primarily in income-generating real estate, which offer liquidity and geographic diversification. In the United States, REITs receive pass-through tax benefits if at least 75% of their income and assets are in real estate and they distribute 90% of income. While the U.S. originated modern REITs, other countries have adopted them with varying structures; China’s recent infrastructure-focused REITs, launched via quasi-government corporations during the pandemic, differ from the U.S. model and lack comparable tax advantages. The lecture notes that institutional investors, particularly European and Canadian pension funds, increasingly pressure REITs to adopt ESG and net-zero targets. Empirical research suggests REITs with larger shares of green-certified properties have higher returns on equity and assets and lower beta, though endogeneity and reverse causality remain concerns. Ongoing research examines the gap between REITs’ "green talking" and "green doing" and its impact on stock performance.

The lecture also covers green bonds, fixed-income instruments issued by governments or companies to fund green projects. REITs and government-sponsored enterprises like Fannie Mae issue green bonds, which can reduce the issuer’s cost of capital. The Green Bond Principles provide a framework to validate use of proceeds and mitigate greenwashing.

Finally, the lecture emphasizes data, measurement, and benchmarking to ensure credibility. Tools mentioned include the EPA’s Portfolio Manager, Measurabl, DNV, CRREM, and GRESB, which benchmarks portfolio-level ESG performance. Studies indicate higher GRESB scores correlate with better private equity and REIT returns and lower loan costs. However, the lecture cites MIT Sloan’s "ESG Confusion" project, which finds that ESG ratings across providers are inconsistent, noisy, and poorly correlated.

The NVIDIA Ampere GA10x GPU architecture, fabricated on Samsung’s 8nm process, includes the GA102 and GA104 and succeeds the Turing architecture. It delivers up to 1.7x faster traditional raster performance and up to 2x faster ray tracing. The GA102 incorporates 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, and 336 third-generation Tensor Cores. Its Streaming Multiprocessors double FP32 throughput by processing FP32 on both datapaths. Second-generation RT Cores double the ray/triangle intersection rate and add an Interpolate Triangle Position unit for hardware-accelerated ray-traced motion blur. Third-generation Tensor Cores support fine-grained structured sparsity, TF32, and BF16, doubling inferencing throughput and enabling 8K DLSS. The architecture introduces GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling for speeds up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/sec of bandwidth on consumer cards, while the professional RTX A6000 and data center A40 use 48 GB of GDDR6, scalable to 96 GB via third-generation NVLink. Additional features include PCIe Gen 4, ROPs integrated into Graphics Processing Clusters, RTX IO for GPU-based asset loading and decompression, HDMI 2.1, AV1 hardware decode, seventh-generation NVENC, and Error Detection and Replay (EDR) technology for memory overclocking. The product lineup includes the GeForce RTX 3090, 3080, and 3070, and the professional NVIDIA RTX A6000 and A40, with the latter offering up to 2x the power efficiency of the previous generation.

Scott Hughes introduces a general relativity course for which Sean Carroll’s textbook is primary, supplemented by Schutz’s *A First Course in General Relativity* (second edition), Misner/Thorne/Wheeler’s *Gravitation* as a reference, and Wald’s *General Relativity* for mathematically minded students. The grade is based entirely on eleven problem sets, with no final exam. The first half of the course covers mathematical foundations leading to the Einstein field equations, while the second half applies them to topics such as cosmology, black holes, neutron stars, and gravitational waves.

The lecture then adopts a geometric viewpoint, defining spacetime as a manifold of events endowed with a metric. A manifold is a collection of points with connectedness properties, an event is a point in space and time independent of coordinate labels, and the metric provides a notion of distance between events. Hughes introduces an inertial reference frame as a lattice of uniformly ticking, orthogonal measuring rods and clocks synchronized via the Einstein procedure, which relies on the invariance of the speed of light; in this course, the speed of light is set to one.

He defines the displacement vector between two events as a geometric object whose existence is independent of the observer, though its components differ between observers and are related by a Lorentz transformation. He establishes notation: Greek indices (μ, ν) for spacetime components (0,1,2,3) and Latin indices for spatial components, using the Einstein summation convention and distinguishing dummy indices from free indices. A spacetime vector is defined as any quartet of components that transforms between inertial reference frames in the same manner as the displacement vector and obeys the linearity laws of a vector space.

The passage details AGESA procedures for managing pre-memory stacks and creating data structures. The first stackless assembler procedure initializes the processor and cache to establish a pre-memory stack before main memory is available, dividing it among cores, mapping it to global address space, and setting MTRRs. It handles protected and real modes, creates a UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF instance, and must run on all cores. The second stackless assembler procedure removes the pre-memory stack when main memory becomes available, disabling Cache-as-RAM mode without modifying MCRR settings and flushing cache lines; it must run on all cores. Both return AGESA status codes. The passage also describes AmdCreateStruct, which allocates and pre-initializes storage for AGESA parameter blocks using PreMemHeap, PostMemDram, or ByHost methods.

This paper investigates the capability of deep learning to predict mammographic density on low dose mammograms (approximately 10% of standard dose) for younger women, using the ALDRAM dataset of 147 women aged 30-45 and training on the PROCAS dataset. ResNet-18 models were trained separately on standard and simulated low dose images. The study finds that averaging predictions across cranial-caudal (CC) and mediolateral oblique (MLO) views, as well as across multiple model runs, improves the similarity between standard and low dose predictions. Variation in predictions was not significantly related to patient age or exposure dose ratio. However, higher breast density and smaller breast area (which correlates with image size) were associated with greater prediction differences and systematic under-prediction by the low dose model. Large discrepancies between CC and MLO predictions, or between repeated low dose models, suggest increased uncertainty in low dose estimates. The results support the feasibility of low dose mammography for density assessment but indicate that corrections may be needed for dense and small breasts.

The passage discusses the health impacts of ultra-processed foods (UPF) and the limitations of existing categorical food processing classification systems, which suffer from inconsistency and poor reproducibility. It introduces FPro, a continuous machine learning-derived score ranging from 0 (unprocessed) to 1 (ultra-processed) that uses nutrient concentrations to quantify processing, and GroceryDB, a database of over 50,000 food products collected from Walmart, Target, and WholeFoods. Results indicate that ultra-processed products constitute the majority of inventory across these stores, with WholeFoods offering relatively more minimally-processed items and Target offering more ultra-processed items. FPro variability differs by category: some, like cereals and milk substitutes, show wide processing ranges, while others, like chips and mac & cheese, are uniformly highly processed. The study finds that higher processing generally correlates with cheaper calories, though this varies by food category. It also presents IgFPro, an ingredient-level score that identifies which specific ingredients and additives most contribute to ultra-processing. The authors contend that continuous scoring improves upon categorical systems for consumer decision-making and public health interventions, but acknowledge that FPro is limited by its reliance on nutrition facts and cannot fully capture food matrix alterations undetectable by nutrient panels alone.

VirtualLink simplifies VR setup via a single USB-C connector, enabling VR on small form factor devices. Turing GPUs replace previous SLI Bridge technology with NVLink for GPU-to-GPU data transfers; the TU102 includes two second-generation NVLink links providing 100 GB/sec bidirectional bandwidth, while the TU104 includes one link. Two-way SLI is supported, but 3-way and 4-way configurations are not. Turing introduces RT Cores to accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing, enabling real-time ray tracing and a hybrid rendering model that combines rasterization with ray-traced reflections, shadows, and ambient occlusion. RT Cores allow Turing to run ray tracing approximately 10 times faster than Pascal GPUs. NGX leverages Turing Tensor Cores for AI-based graphics features, including Deep Learning Super-Sampling, which renders at a lower input sample count and infers results comparable to Temporal Anti-Aliasing with roughly half the shading work, as well as InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. Mesh Shading introduces Task and Mesh Shaders to reduce CPU draw call bottlenecks and increase the number of objects renderable in real time. Variable Rate Shading allows dynamic adjustment of shading rates per 16x16 pixel region for algorithms such as Content Adaptive Shading, Motion Adaptive Shading, and Foveated Rendering. Texture Space Shading decouples visibility and appearance sampling, improving efficiency and temporal stability by reusing shaded texels, particularly for VR stereo rendering. Multi-View Rendering supports up to four views per pass, expanding Pascal’s Simultaneous Multi-Projection for advanced VR displays and single-pass rendering of multiple instances or shadow maps. Turing also supports DirectX 12 Tier 3 bindless resource views and Tier 2 resource heaps. The TU104 GPU includes RT and Tensor Cores and is used in products such as the GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000, while the TU106 GPU used in the GeForce RTX 2070 lacks NVLink and SLI support. RTX-OPS is a workload-based performance metric that weights Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 operations to quantify hybrid rendering throughput.

This lecture explores the economics of spam and security, distinguishing financially motivated attacks from ideological or state-sponsored ones that lack economic leverage points. The professor argues that spammers persist because infrastructure costs are low and profits exceed risks; for example, Chinese "text message cars" can recoup hardware costs in one day while facing minimal fines. The spam ecosystem comprises three stages: advertising (e.g., email and text messages sent cheaply via botnets), click support (using domain registrations, DNS redirection, and fast-flux techniques to avoid takedowns), and realization (processing payments through merchants, payment processors, and banks). Conversion rates are extremely low, so spammers rely on volume and cheap labor, including outsourced CAPTCHA solving. To avoid fines and maintain access to limited banking partners, spammers often properly classify credit card transactions and actually deliver goods. The lecture also discusses cyber arms dealers, corporate "hackbacks" using creative legal justifications like trademark infringement, and policy changes by Visa to classify pharmaceutical sales as high-risk and prohibit illegal transactions.

A self-driving Uber SUV struck and killed 49-year-old Elaine Herzberg in Tempe, Arizona, in the first death involving a fully autonomous test vehicle. Uber suspended all road-testing in Phoenix, Pittsburgh, San Francisco, and Toronto. The National Transportation Safety Board and National Highway Traffic Safety Administration sent investigators. Experts say the fatality could hurt the technology's public image and lead to more state and federal regulations. Autonomous vehicles have been promoted as a way to reduce traffic deaths, but the crash highlights safety concerns amid varying state regulations and voluntary federal guidelines.

Tecomaria capensis (Bignoniaceae), or Cape Honeysuckle, is a scrambling shrub or small tree up to 6 m with opposite compound leaves and year-round orange-red trumpet-shaped flowers. It occurs in thicket and forest margins in southern, eastern, and tropical Africa and is listed as Least Concern by SANBI. Browsed by game and stock and visited by sunbirds, butterflies, and bees, it is traditionally used to treat fever, pain, and dysentery. Its wood is carved into isixhoxho necklets for nursing mothers. It requires well-drained soil, compost, watering until established, and late winter pruning.

Various executive committees oversaw U.S. covert actions from 1961 onward. The Special Group (Augmented) ran Operation Mongoose (1961–1962) against Castro, while the Special Group (Counter-Insurgency) coordinated counter-insurgency from 1962. In 1964, the Special Group 5412 became the 303 Committee; in 1970, NSDM 40 renamed it the 40 Committee and added the Attorney General. These committees approved hundreds of covert actions but reviewed only a small fraction of CIA projects—14 percent by the 303 Committee and 25 percent by the 40 Committee—focusing on major operations, sometimes rejecting proposals. The 1974 Hughes-Ryan amendment required explicit presidential findings and expanded congressional oversight for covert actions.

In United States v. Willie Tyler (M.D. Pa. Nov. 15, 2016), Judge William W. Caldwell denied the defendant’s motions to dismiss the indictment and bar retrial on witness-tampering charges. Following a 2000 conviction for tampering with a witness by murder and intimidation under 18 U.S.C. § 1512, Tyler successfully sought collateral relief, arguing that intervening changes in law established his actual innocence. On remand, the government conceded it could not prove guilt under the “official proceeding” provision, but the court vacated the convictions and ordered a new trial under the “investigation-related communications” provision after finding Tyler failed to show actual innocence on that theory.

The court rejected Tyler’s Confrontation Clause claim that a hearsay statement by the victim to a narcotics detective was inadmissible, ruling it was offered not for its truth but to show the victim would have communicated with a federal officer, consistent with prior Third Circuit precedent. The court also rejected his Double Jeopardy claim based on a prior state-court trial, applying the dual sovereignty doctrine, and distinguished Burks v. United States because the vacatur was based on legal error rather than insufficient evidence. Finally, the court rejected his Due Process claim of outrageous government conduct and an alleged Brady violation regarding a state investigator’s DEA status and a late-disclosed witness statement, finding no prejudice or conduct warranting dismissal.

One year after Hurricane Helene caused severe flooding in western North Carolina in September 2024, four school districts continue recovery efforts. Henderson County’s Atkinson Elementary reopened in December 2024 after replacing floors and now partners with the Boys & Girls Club, which housed students during repairs and now provides mentors and after-school transportation. McDowell County’s Old Fort Elementary reopened for the 2025–26 school year after students temporarily merged with Pleasant Gardens Elementary; the building received new flooring, doors, paint, and elevated HVAC units. Watauga County’s Valle Crucis School remains in transition after 70 percent of the building flooded; students were housed at community sites during 2024–25, and a new building’s opening was delayed by workforce shortages, while the district works to preserve the dry historic rock facade. Yancey County permanently closed Micaville Elementary; students moved to expanded campuses at Burnsville and Blue Ridge elementary schools, though countywide drainage and infrastructure issues persist.

Cell phone ownership among children varies significantly worldwide. In the United States, many children receive smartphones at young ages, with about 45% of 10- to 12-year-olds having service plans and 42% of children 8 and younger owning tablets. In Europe, about 46% of children ages 9 to 16 own smartphones, with usage rules and access varying by country. In South Korea, roughly 72% of 11- to 12-year-olds own smartphones, while in countries like Ghana and Malawi, ownership rates are much lower. Other regions show mixed patterns: in Taiwan, phone use rises from 45% at age 11 to 71% at age 15; in Turkey, parents disagree on the appropriate age; and in Australia, the median age for first phone use is 8. The American Academy of Pediatrics states there is no "right" age for a child's first phone, but recommends avoiding digital media for children under 18 to 24 months and limiting screen time to one hour per day for children ages 2 to 5.

Professor Hong introduces an MIT quantum field theory (QFT) course aimed at developing the formalism for quantum dynamics of fields, culminating in quantum electrodynamics. QFT is essential for describing fundamental interactions and serves as a universal language in theoretical physics. This first semester of a three-part sequence focuses on core concepts, while subsequent semesters cover technical details. He advises that QFT extends quantum mechanics to infinite degrees of freedom, so difficulties often stem from gaps in quantum mechanics intuition—particularly the Heisenberg picture—and recommends focusing on the concrete physical problems behind formalisms, learning from examples, and completing problem sets, where much of the learning occurs. He also notes that his notation differs from standard textbooks.

The lecture then addresses the principle of locality: physical effects propagate between neighboring points rather than acting at a distance, with fields serving as the mathematical device. Local theories assign dynamical variables to each spatial point, and equations like Maxwell’s involve only values and derivatives at a single point. The lecture defines scalar, vector, tensor, and spinor fields, and introduces the action principle for classical fields. The Lagrangian is a spatial integral of a local Lagrangian density depending on fields and their first derivatives, ensuring local equations of motion and proper initial conditions. From this, canonical momentum density, Hamiltonian density, and the Euler-Lagrange field equations are derived. Restricting to translationally and Lorentz-invariant theories, examples include Maxwell theory, Einstein gravity, and real scalar field theory. For a scalar field with potential \(V(\phi)\), the momentum density is \(\pi = \dot{\phi}\), and the equation of motion is \(\Box\phi + \partial V/\partial\phi = 0\). The simplest nontrivial case, \(V = \frac{1}{2}m^2\phi^2\), yields the linear Klein-Gordon equation, whereas higher-order terms lead to nonlinear dynamics.

This work presents a quantum algorithmic framework for sparsifying generalized linear models (GLMs) to accelerate a broad class of regression tasks. By constructing ε-approximate sparsifiers—small weighted subsets that preserve the total loss objective—the framework yields quadratic speedups in the number of data points m over classical methods for linear, multiple, ridge, Lasso, Huber, ℓp, and γp regression. The approach combines multiscale leverage score overestimates (MLSO), computed via quantum leverage score approximation, with quantum importance sampling based on state preparation and sum estimation. Given query access to an m×n data matrix with row sparsity r and a family of (L, θ, c)-proper loss functions, the algorithm produces an rO(log(smax/smin)·n/ε²)-sparse ε-approximate sparsifier in time rO((nω + nr² + r√(mn)/ε)·log(smax/smin)). The results subsume prior quantum speedups for linear regression and establish new quantum algorithms for ℓp, Huber, and related regressions.

Digital Foundry's analysis of Monster Hunter World finds adequate visuals but disappointing performance across all consoles. The base PS4 runs at 1080p with unstable uncapped frame rates, while the base Xbox One performs worse at 864p with lower frame rates and ragged frame times. On enhanced consoles, Resolution mode renders the PS4 Pro at 1800p via checkerboard rendering versus the Xbox One X's native 1728p, yet the One X lacks some distant assets and runs slightly slower. Frame-rate mode limits both to 1080p, where the One X generally leads in frame rate but still misses assets. Graphics mode also uses 1080p with extended draw distances, restoring the missing One X assets while giving the One X a marked performance edge over the Pro. Strengths include detailed monsters, characters, and environments, while weaknesses include reduced contrast, clipping, and poor motion blur. The report concludes the game is a technical disappointment with poor optimization, especially on the Xbox One X, though the gameplay remains enjoyable.

The Flex offense relies on continuous "Pick the Picker" baseline and down screens to burden defenses and create open shots for patient teams, while constantly maintaining two weakside rebounders. A "Pop" variation adds a weakside double screen, allowing the receiver to pop out to the elbow. Suzanne Nimocks of McKinsey forwarded a December 6, 2000 memorandum to Enron’s Steven Kean providing a periodic update on international electric power sector privatization and restructuring from June through November 2000. The update reports that governments worldwide are opening generation markets to foreign investors, unbundling state-owned utilities, and introducing wholesale and retail competition, although some international players have scaled back investments in favor of less risky markets such as the U.S. and Europe. This study analyzed SEER 2000–2018 data to determine mortality rates and predict overall survival for U.S. patients with soft-tissue sarcomas (STS), including heart cancer. Of 55,261 identified cases, 24,849 met inclusion criteria (mean age 59; 56% male; 82% white). The analysis focused on six sarcoma types: Liposarcoma, Leiomyosarcoma, Synovial Sarcoma, Spindle Cell Sarcoma, Giant Cell Sarcoma, and Myxofibrosarcoma. Using Kaplan-Meier, log-rank, and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models, the study found that increasing age, male sex, non-white race, advanced cancer stage, and higher tumor grade negatively affected survival. Giant Cell Sarcoma had the shortest median survival (42 months), while Myxofibrosarcoma had the highest overall survival rate (75%) and Spindle Cell Sarcoma the lowest (37%). Metastatic disease carried a 3.66-fold higher hazard of death than localized disease. Surgery significantly reduced mortality across all sarcoma types; chemotherapy and radiation also improved survival for most types, though primary systemic therapy showed contradictory outcomes. The authors developed all-cause mortality nomograms to estimate 5- and 10-year survival probabilities based on patient demographics, tumor characteristics, and treatment. Nomogram predictions indicated that surgery alone yielded greater than 90% 5- and 10-year survival, chemotherapy alone yielded greater than 80%, and no chemotherapy yielded 55% and 46%, respectively; radiation alone did not significantly improve survival. Calibration between predicted and actual probabilities was excellent. Limitations included missing SEER data on histological subtypes, surgical margins, cancer recurrence, radiotherapy details, and some confounders, as well as the need for external validation. The authors conclude that surgery, radiation, and chemotherapy are associated with better STS survival and that the nomogram provides a tool for predicting overall survival probability.

This is the first lecture of MIT course 14.271 on Industrial Organization (IO), primarily taught by Glenn Ellison with guest lectures by Tobias and Jean Tirole. The course covers IO theory on Wednesdays and empirical work on Mondays, focusing on structural empirical methods and the interplay between theory and empirics. IO is described as inherently theoretical because many policy questions cannot be answered with natural experiments, though empirical work is central to testing model assumptions and refining theory.

The lecture begins with monopoly pricing. A monopolist maximizes profit where marginal revenue equals marginal cost, yielding the Lerner index: (price minus marginal cost) divided by price equals negative one over the elasticity of demand. Markups therefore depend on demand elasticity, not demand levels. Monopoly creates deadweight loss, but other potential costs include productive inefficiency, quality distortions, rent-seeking behavior, and equity concerns regarding transfers from consumers to firms; the course will generally assume quasi-linear preferences and set aside income effects.

The model extends to multiproduct pricing, where a firm must account for diversion ratios—the effect of one product’s price on another’s sales. For substitutes, markups exceed the single-product formula. For complements, firms may price one good below marginal cost to drive sales of the other, as seen in examples like printers and ink, newspapers and advertising, or search engines paying for default placement.

On product quality, a monopolist optimizes quality based on the marginal consumer’s valuation rather than the average consumer’s, which can lead to under- or over-provision relative to a social planner. In a homogeneous population model, however, the monopolist’s quality choice is socially optimal.

Regarding durable goods, a monopolist with commitment power in a two-period model maximizes profit by setting the monopoly price in the first period and committing to no second-period sales, because selling early to high-value buyers has no opportunity cost. Without commitment, the firm has an incentive to cut prices after early adopters buy, leading to declining price sequences and lower profits. The Coase conjecture suggests that with infinitely frequent repricing and no commitment, prices drop immediately to cost and profits vanish. The lecture notes several reasons this extreme outcome may not occur, including price adjustment costs, firm reputation, inflows of new customers, consumer irrationality, rental models, best-price guarantees, and capacity constraints.

Finally, the lecture introduces information design, noting that firms and intermediaries strategically choose how much product information to provide. Providing partial information can change consumer demand structures. An example illustrates that an intermediary revealing coarse value categories can induce a monopolist to set a lower price than under full information, potentially increasing both consumer surplus and profit. The next lecture will cover empirical papers on monopoly pricing.

The lecture discusses natural sandwich structures and mechanically efficient designs in nature. Examples of sandwich panels include monocotyledon leaves such as iris and cattail, which have stiff outer sclerenchyma fiber faces and a low-density parenchyma core; mechanical testing of iris leaves showed their behavior aligns with sandwich beam deflection equations. Seakelp uses a honeycomb core with gas-filled pockets for buoyancy. Bird skulls, including those of pigeons, magpies, owls, and hawks, utilize sandwich constructions with trabecular bone cores to reduce weight. Cuttlefish bones are calcium carbonate sandwich structures with air pockets that control buoyancy. Horseshoe crab and Galapagos tortoise shells also exhibit sandwich-like constructions.

The lecture also examines palm stems, which maintain a constant diameter as they grow taller by depositing additional cell wall layers, creating a radial density gradient: low-density tissue in the center and high-density tissue at the periphery. Data from Paul Rich shows density varies with the radius squared, the modulus varies with density to the 2.5 power, and strength varies with density squared. This gradient increases flexural rigidity by a factor of 2.5 relative to uniform density and closely matches the bending strength distribution to the stress distribution, efficiently placing material where stresses are highest. Bamboo exhibits a similar radial density gradient. The next class will address bio-mimicking and test review.

Senior House Republican Rep. This study evaluates Temperature Scaling (TS) for calibrating Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) that classify brain tumors from T1-weighted MRI images. A lightweight CNN was trained on a composite dataset and tested under clean conditions and five synthetic noise types: Gaussian, Poisson, Salt & Pepper, Speckle, and Uniform. While TS offered limited improvement on the small clean dataset, it consistently reduced Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL) and Expected Calibration Error (ECE) across all noise scenarios without degrading accuracy, precision, recall, or F1-score. Experiments with ResNet50 confirmed that TS improves calibration and reduces false positives and false negatives in deeper architectures. The authors conclude that TS effectively enhances model reliability under noisy medical imaging conditions and plan future work comparing it against other calibration methods on larger datasets.

The lecturer finishes proving Cantor's theorem: for any set A, the cardinality of A is strictly smaller than that of its power set P(A), implying infinitely many infinite sizes. The proof uses an injection from A into P(A) and a contradiction argument assuming a bijection g: A → P(A), defining B = {x ∈ A : x ∉ g(x)} to derive the contradiction b ∈ g(b) if and only if b ∉ g(b). The lecturer likens this to the liar paradox.

The lecture then introduces the characterization of the real numbers R via the theorem that there exists a unique ordered field containing Q with the least upper bound property. An ordered set is defined by trichotomy and transitivity, with examples including N, Z, and Q, and a non-example being the power set of N under inclusion. The lecturer defines upper bounds, lower bounds, supremum, and infimum, and states the least upper bound property: every non-empty subset bounded above has a supremum in the set. While Z has this property, Q does not. For the set E = {q ∈ Q : q > 0, q² < 2}, the lecturer proves that if a supremum existed in Q, it would satisfy x² = 2, completing the argument that x² < 2 leads to a contradiction and deferring the x² > 2 case.

This case study investigated how two middle grades teacher candidates (TCs) viewed, experienced, and used translanguaging with multilingual young adolescents during a year-long Professional Development School (PDS) experience, and how their ESL-focused coursework prepared them. Data from interviews, field notes, and observations revealed that both TCs held positive, asset-based views of translanguaging and felt their undergraduate coursework provided theoretical tools and scaffolding strategies. However, both struggled with practical implementation due to a theory-practice gap, expressing uncomfortability and lack of experience working with multilingual learners despite ESL endorsements and over 100 clinical hours. Their cooperating teachers (CTs) rarely used or modeled translanguaging in classrooms, relying instead on English-dominant instruction. Patricia, a bilingual TC, employed technological supports and peer grouping for students' native languages but in limited managerial capacities rather than integrated curricular ways. Ruby, a monolingual TC, felt unable to implement translanguaging because she did not share her students' languages and voiced persistent unpreparedness. The authors conclude that teacher education programs must provide professional development for CTs on creating linguistically inclusive spaces and modeling translanguaging, and they call for more middle-grades-specific research and training on the practice.

RDRAND and RDSEED use slow MMIO reads, suitable for non-latency-sensitive cryptography; hybrid approaches improve latency-sensitive performance. AMD Zen includes a hardware RNG; AMD Secure RNG library abstracts low-level access via an easy API for key generation.

Divergence in trading refers to a mismatch between price swings and oscillator movement, indicating potential reversals or momentum shifts. A Divergence Trading Strategy uses indicators such as RSI, MACD, Stochastic, or CCI to identify classical and hidden divergence patterns, each with bullish and bearish forms. Classical divergence typically suggests potential trend reversals, while hidden divergence often signals trend continuation after pullbacks. The strategy offers early momentum detection and clear entry/exit signals across various markets and time frames, but traders should confirm signals with volume analysis and avoid mistakes like overtrading or poor risk management. The passage presents a backtest of a simple S&P 500 (SPY) strategy showing strong profit factors and Sharpe ratios for short-term settings, alongside an equity curve with low drawdowns but few trades. It also cites historical examples: classical bullish divergence on Nasdaq 100 (March 2020), hidden bullish on TSLA (March 2020), classical bearish on S&P 500 (February 2020), and hidden bearish on Nasdaq 100 (December 2018), stressing the importance of systematic backtesting.

President Andrew Johnson’s May 29, 1865 proclamation appoints William W. Holden provisional governor of North Carolina to enable loyal citizens to reorganize state government and restore the state’s constitutional relations with the federal government. Holden must convene a convention of loyal delegates, elected by voters who have taken the amnesty oath and were qualified under North Carolina law prior to May 20, 1861, to amend the state constitution. The proclamation directs federal military, judicial, and executive departments to resume operations in North Carolina, assist the provisional governor, and give preference to qualified loyal residents in appointments.

The Missouri Court of Appeals affirmed the circuit court's grant of summary judgment for defendants Bank of St. Louis and two employees in Harvey F. Euge's pro se malicious prosecution action. Euge sought damages for his indictment and conviction on a bogus check charge, which the Missouri Supreme Court later reversed. The appellate court held that a conviction creates a presumption of probable cause that survives reversal on appeal unless the conviction was obtained by false testimony or improper means. Because the undisputed facts showed Euge used a fictitious name to transact business and deposited a check later returned for insufficient funds, probable cause existed as a matter of law. The Supreme Court's reversal was based on a narrow, novel statutory interpretation that the check was not "bogus," which did not negate the established probable cause. The court also held that where facts are undisputed, probable cause is a question of law for the court, not the jury.

Video object segmentation-aware audio generation is introduced as a new task for synthesizing audio conditioned on text, video, and visual segmentation masks, enabling precise object-level control in artificial Foley. The proposed SAGANet extends the pretrained MMAudio model with a lightweight control module that fuses global and localized focal-crop visual features—extracted via segmentation masks—using gated cross-attention, requiring training of only a fraction of parameters. The Segmented Music Solos dataset, comprising solo musical instrument videos with sounding-object segmentation masks, is curated for training and evaluation. Trained solely on single-source videos, SAGANet generalizes to multi-source scenes, significantly improving temporal synchronization, semantic alignment, and audio quality over the base model.

Power traces should be short, direct, and at least 15 mils per Ampere. Place the inductor, output capacitors, and output diode close together to reduce EMI, lead inductance, and resistance. Connect grounds directly to a ground plane, using planes on both sides or between power and signal layers on multilayer boards, with one via per 200 mA. Arrange switching current loops to curl in the same direction during both power states to reduce radiated EMI. Use a ground plane with a dedicated high di/dt power ground section for the PGND pin, which may be separated and connected at a single point. Bypass VCC to power ground and VREF to signal ground with low ESR/ESL ceramic 1-mF capacitors. Connect power MOSFET sources, input returns, and bulk capacitors to power ground, clamp the output with a Schottky diode to VCC and PGND, and route analog circuitry bypasses to signal ground.

UAE delayed Barakah's first reactor until late 2019 or early 2020. Korea Electric Power Corporation leads construction of the plant, which will produce 5,600 megawatts, about 25 percent of UAE needs. Remaining reactors are 93, 83, and 72 percent complete. No reason was given.

This work presents an ontological model and the ACXON algorithm to enable robots to compare competing plans and generate contrastive explanatory narratives. Extending the OCRA ontology using the DUL foundational ontology, the model formalizes plan qualities—cost, expected makespan, and number of tasks—and defines relations to infer which plan is better or worse, validated through competency questions and a drink-delivery scenario implemented with Knowrob and Prolog. ACXON retrieves divergent knowledge from a time-indexed knowledge graph and constructs textual contrastive narratives at three specificity levels using casting, clustering, ordering, and grouping. Evaluated against the AXON baseline with IPC planning domains, ACXON significantly reduces the number of knowledge tuples and communication times for specificity levels two and three, while both methods yield similar Dale–Chall readability scores. The authors also describe a refinement to restrict knowledge retrieval to specific object classes, shortening narratives for potential personalization, and identify future work including user studies and contextual explanation timing.

The Tenth Circuit affirmed the dismissal of Charles A. Meeker’s § 1983 complaint against defendants involved in a New Mexico child abuse investigation that transferred custody of his daughters to the state. The district court dismissed claims for failure to serve four defendants, res judicata from prior suits, and because guardian ad litem Deborah Grout was not a state actor. The appellate court held Meeker could not represent his minor daughters because a parent acting as next friend must be represented by an attorney under Fed.R.Civ.P. 17(c) and 28 U.S.C. § 1654. It adopted the district court’s reasoning and held that, per Polk County v. Dodson, a guardian ad litem exercises independent judgment for the minor and does not act under color of state law, and is therefore not liable under § 1983.

The RSPCA investigated 2,902 animal cruelty complaints in Nottinghamshire in 2017, down about eight percent from 2016. Cases included two kittens beaten to death by their owner, who was jailed for 20 weeks, and 40 animals kept in stacked cages without food, water, or blankets, with five dogs put down. Most complaints concerned dogs (1,702), cats (737), and horses (281). Nationally, 141,760 complaints were investigated. The RSPCA urged the public to report concerns via its 24-hour helpline.

The Louisiana Court of Appeal reversed a judgment dismissing a suit by the Gretna Trust & Savings Bank, as dative testamentary executor of Priscilla Lewis’s succession, against David Lewis. The bank sought to recover $505.58 Lewis withdrew from his mother’s account after her August 4, 1929 death, and claimed rent. Lewis admitted the withdrawal but argued the funds repaid loans he made to her. The court found the account belonged to the deceased, held that a creditor cannot satisfy his own claim by taking succession assets, and ruled the withdrawal illegal. The rent claim was unproven. The court entered judgment for the bank for $505.58, with interest and costs.

The article argues that Treasury liquidity patterns, not seasons, explain the adage "Sell in May and come back in November." Analysis of U.S. Treasury cash balances from 2006 to 2017 shows consistent annual peaks in January, May, and November. January peaks correspond to Federal Reserve Reverse Repurchase Agreement Operations. May peaks result from tax refund distributions, which primarily flow to wealthy individuals who invest in stocks, creating a market pop; the adage reflects selling after this rise, as fiscal flows flatten through summer. November peaks follow Fed Treasury buybacks, which provide liquidity that can fuel a year-end rally. The author suggests 2018 may see a significant May boost due to recent tax law changes and the current market retrace, while noting that February and November patterns warrant further study.

Weak gravitational lensing from surveys including KiDS, DES, and HSC achieves percent-level cosmological precision but is limited by intrinsic alignment (IA) uncertainty and baryonic feedback. This paper focuses on IA, which can bias inferred parameters by 4–5σ if ignored. Several IA models are reviewed, including NLA, extended-NLA, TT, and TATT, alongside observational evidence for a strong color-dependence in alignments. The authors present a novel pipeline that infuses NLA, extended-NLA, and TT models into the SkySim5000 N-body simulation, introduce an extended-TT model, and couple tidal fields with HOD galaxies to probe non-linear bias. These catalogues validate theoretical models, quantify IA impacts on non-Gaussian statistics beyond two-point functions, and study source clustering. The paper details cosmic shear two-point correlation functions, non-Gaussian statistics, and the Kaiser-Squires inversion for convergence maps.

The company adopted ASC 842 on January 1, 2019, recognizing right-of-use assets of $1.29 billion and lease liabilities of $1.24 billion and de-recognizing build-to-suit leases with a net $97 million adjustment to accumulated deficit. On May 16, 2019, Tesla acquired Maxwell Technologies, Inc. for $207 million in common stock. A declaration of principles on interim Palestinian self-government is being signed by the leadership of Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization at an event cosponsored by the United States and Russia. The address acknowledges the region’s long history of conflict, references prior peace efforts including the Camp David accords and the Madrid conference, and salutes the leaders of Israel and the PLO, as well as Norway, for their roles in reaching the agreement. It pledges active United States support to implement the principles and ensure greater security, calls for the accord to catalyze broader peace progress, and urges dedication to the region’s next generation to end cycles of hatred and achieve lasting reconciliation.

Researchers at Karolinska Institutet found poor sleep associated with accelerated brain aging in 27,500 UK Biobank participants. Using MRI and machine learning, they estimated brain age from over 1,000 phenotypes based on five self-reported sleep factors. Brain age exceeded chronological age by roughly six months per one-point decrease in healthy sleep score, with poor sleepers showing brains about one year older. Low-grade inflammation explained over ten percent of the link. Other possible mechanisms include impaired brain waste clearance and cardiovascular effects. Limitations include self-reported data and a healthier-than-average participant pool.

The Directorate General of Goods and Services Tax Intelligence has demanded over Rs 6,000 crore from banks for GST on free services to minimum-balance customers, calculated retrospectively over five years using charges for non-compliant customers as the value. Banks will likely challenge this; if upheld, costs would pass to customers. This is criticized as ham-fisted tax terror despite government promises.

Petty's cause of death was deferred pending further tests. He died at 66 after cardiac arrest and life support removal due to no brain activity, surrounded by friends, family and bandmates in Santa Monica. Tributes included Nathan Followill. Brent fell to US$55.62 and U.S. crude to US$52.84. Despite OPEC record compliance, rising U.S. stocks, revived U.S. output, and a stronger dollar limited gains. Saudi Arabia exceeded cuts, but Iraq's 40% compliance may threaten cohesion, while non-OPEC producers delivered smaller cutbacks.

Restoration Affiliates (RA) is a collaborative partnership founded in 2011 by leaders of four regional restoration firms—Rich Piltch of ARS, Damon Gersh of Maxons Restoration, Andy Goldberg of RestoreCore, and Ras Fenger of Disaster One—to allow independent regional companies to compete with national players like Belfor by providing national coverage and local expertise to large insurance and property management companies. By fall 2013, RA had grown to 21 members with combined revenues of $300 million. The organization operates as a democratic LLC with equal shareholders, a nine-person board, standing committees, and membership criteria requiring commercial focus, minimum $5 million revenue, and adherence to industry service standards. Members pay dues and referral fees on cross-member projects. Guided by a "Go-Giver" philosophy of cooperation, RA faces strategic questions regarding the authority of its hired administrator, communication and tracking systems, service consistency, pricing rules for referred work, territory overlap, marketing approach, and whether to adopt one or both member-developed disaster planning software platforms. RA recently secured a three-year nationwide contract with Forest City Enterprises, validating its model as a national solution for regional firms.

The paper presents a uniform method for synthesizing codensity presentations of monads based on the principle that codensity equals density plus duality. It defines a codensity setting as a decomposition of a functor into a dual equivalence, the opposite of a dense functor, and a contravariant right adjoint. The main theorem establishes that in any such setting, the monad induced by the dual adjunction is the codensity monad of the composite functor, reducing codensity proofs to better-understood density arguments. The authors apply this framework to recover and simplify known codensity presentations—including those for ultrafilter, filter, double dualization, Isbell, Vietoris, sobrification, Giry, Radon, Kantorovich, and semiring-valued measure monads—and to establish new presentations for the filter monad on topological spaces, the lower Vietoris monad, and the expectation monad. The paper concludes by proposing future extensions to formal monad theory and additional probabilistic powerdomains.

This eulogy honors Henry Clay, who died in Washington in 1852. Born in Hanover County, Virginia, on April 12, 1777, to undistinguished parents, he received limited early education but became a lawyer in Lexington, Kentucky. His public service spanned nearly fifty years, from 1803 to 1852, including terms in the Kentucky Legislature, the U.S. House of Representatives (where he served as Speaker), the U.S. Senate, and as Secretary of State from 1825 to 1829. The speech praises his instrumental role in declaring the War of 1812, resolving the Missouri question through compromise, addressing Nullification, and managing the slavery question to preserve the Union. It highlights his extraordinary eloquence, indomitable will, and devotion to human liberty, citing his support for Greek and South American independence. Though a slave owner, he opposed slavery in principle, advocated for gradual emancipation in Kentucky, and served as President of the American Colonization Society. Despite three failed presidential campaigns, he remained a dominant, nationally revered figure whose influence transcended party divisions.
The passage compiles quotes from various figures criticizing taxation, banking debt, corporate tax breaks, and education control.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on January 30, 2017, reporting its entry into an Underwriting Agreement with several underwriters for the issuance and sale of seven series of senior unsecured notes with maturities between February 6, 2020, and February 6, 2057, and interest rates between 1.850% and 4.500%. Harvard visiting professor Carlos Portugal Gouvêa was arrested October 1 for firing a pellet gun near a Jewish temple during Yom Kippur, saying he hunted rats. Kelly Keefe will become ERC president on Jan. 1, the first woman to lead the Northeast Ohio HR services provider in its 97-year history. She succeeds Pat Perry, who will continue as chairman.
