UNC Chapel Hill placed professor Dwayne Dixon on leave while investigating allegations of advocating politically motivated violence. Dixon, a former member of Silver Valley Redneck Revolt, was arrested in 2018 at a Ku Klux Klan counterprotest; the case was dismissed. The investigation follows social media posts by Turning Point USA spokesperson Andrew Kolvet linking Dixon to Georgetown University fliers for the John Brown Gun Club, a Redneck Revolt affiliate referencing Charlie Kirk’s killing. Kolvet called for Dixon’s firing after a Fox News article cited his past group membership. Dixon said he left the group in 2018. UNC did not confirm what prompted the investigation but said the conduct could lead to termination. Faculty groups condemned the action as capitulation to right-wing pressure based on unsubstantiated rumors, and a reinstatement petition has over 900 signatures. Dixon is among dozens of faculty investigated following right-wing social media identification since Kirk’s death.

U.S. manufacturing has nearly 390,000 open jobs requiring advanced skills due to automation, but many blue-collar workers lack qualifications. The AP's "Future of Work" series explores how technology and global pressures are transforming workplaces, making advanced training essential.

The Department opposes dividing the General Assembly into regional sections as unwise and premature, fearing it would impair the effectiveness of the international organization and recommending postponement until after it is firmly established. Background is provided for the February 21 Conference of American Republics in Mexico City, where the United States objective is to discuss the Dumbarton Oaks proposals without assuming inconsistent commitments, as it did with Latin American Ambassadors in Washington. The Dumbarton Oaks Proposals provide for an International Court of Justice as the principal judicial organ with an annexed statute based on the Permanent Court of International Justice. A preliminary jurists meeting was suggested but not agreed upon; it is recommended that about fifteen jurists selected by the four powers convene immediately upon issuance of United Nations Conference invitations to draft a statute based on the present one and alternative implementation procedures, leaving the question of revision versus a new statute for the Conference.

This pre-post study analyzed the effect of enforcing Kenya Health Sector Referral Guidelines 2014 on orthopaedic and trauma facility referrals to Kenyatta National Hospital (KNH), comparing five months before and after July 1, 2021. Of 468 facility referrals, most originated from Nairobi and neighboring counties, with approximately three-fifths from government facilities. While referral volume increases were not statistically significant by facility type, enforcement significantly reduced direct referrals from Tier II and III health facilities and increased referrals from Tiers IV, V, and VI. Forty-three facilities, predominantly private and lower-tier, stopped referring patients to KNH. Major referral factors included human resource capacity, infrastructure, orthopaedic equipment and implant availability, patient preference, and financial considerations. The study concluded that enforcing national referral guidelines reduced inappropriate lower-tier referrals to KNH and recommended sustained sensitization, human resource strengthening, and adherence to referral standard operating procedures.

The 1-2-2 zone defense is effective against outside shooting teams, facilitates fast breaks, and protects leads late in games. The point positions at the top of the circle, wings stand at the elbows, and baseline players position above the blocks, shifting while the ball is in the air. Player assignments vary based on whether the ball is in the corner, on the wing, or in the middle. Baseline players work in unison, wings operate opposite each other and cover weakside rebounding, and the point guards the ball out front or defends the high post. Adjustments include wing corner shifts, a corner trap, switching to a 2-1-2 zone on the first pass, and extending into a half- or full-court press.

New research from Emory University suggests probiotics may protect the liver from damage. In a study, mice fed a diet rich in Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG) showed improved antioxidant responses and protection against oxidative liver damage from high doses of acetaminophen. The protein Nrf2, which regulates genes that fight free radicals, was identified as pivotal in this protective mechanism. While acetaminophen overuse can cause severe liver damage or death through oxidative stress, researchers note that further human studies are needed to confirm these findings. Probiotics should not replace medical treatment.

Despite decades of education expansion, major shortfalls in access, quality, and equality persisted globally by 2020, measured against the UN Sustainable Development Goals and Incheon Declaration’s 2030 vision, under which education is both a goal and a means to realize other goals. COVID-19 aggravated these deficiencies through school closures affecting approximately 91% of students and a hasty shift to distance learning, which severed contact for many learners, worsened inequalities for the disadvantaged, and strained school finances, while also forcing a conservative sector to adopt technology. The paper posits that Comparative and International Education (CIE) must analyze these varied pandemic impacts across societal contexts to guide effective technology use toward 2030 targets. It further identifies critical field weaknesses requiring remediation: the “black box syndrome,” absence of autochthonous theory, Northern hegemony, weak university presence, and lack of demonstrable academic, practical, and policy impact. The author concludes that a reinvigorated CIE can harness pandemic lessons to not merely restore but surpass pre-pandemic education levels and build improved systems.

The U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit granted a request allowing the Education Department to fire half the 550 employees at its Office for Civil Rights. The decision stays an injunction that a federal judge had maintained despite a July Supreme Court ruling in New York v. McMahon, finding the case did not differ enough to reach a contrary result.

In Closson v. Billman, the court affirmed a judgment for defendants in a material man’s lien action. The contractor agreed to furnish materials and build a house, and the plaintiff joined the contractor in a bond conditioned on completing the work “according to the contract.” The court held the plaintiff was a guarantor, not a surety, and was liable on the bond for material liens because the contract required the contractor to pay for materials, and the bond incorporated that duty. The court further held that an answer asserting this guaranty liability was a sufficient defense to avoid circuity of action; that contemporaneous guaranty contracts require no notice of acceptance; and that the guarantor bears the burden to plead and prove an omission to give notice of default and damage from such omission.

Mesh shading moves object list processing from the CPU to the GPU, enabling more objects per scene. The disclosure describes route planning systems, methods, devices, and computer-readable media for vehicles such as automatic guided vehicles using a topological map. To improve accuracy and efficiency by accounting for other vehicles that affect node information, a scheduling system obtains a topological map and preprocesses it by modifying node information—such as weight values, passability, and turn capabilities—based on motion status information and nodes occupied by other vehicles. Start and destination nodes are determined in the modified map, total costs associated with nodes between them are calculated based on the modified node information, and route planning is performed accordingly. Preprocessing may include a first preprocessing that modifies nodes within a preset region around static vehicles and a second preprocessing that modifies nodes on planned but unpassed routes of moving vehicles. A processing device with location, map, motion status, and route determination modules may determine the target route using algorithms such as A-star or Dijkstra, with node costs including weight, distance, turn, and heuristic components.

In Deposit National Bank v. Hay, W. T. Hay appealed an order refusing to stay execution on real estate conveyed to his wife before his 1915 bankruptcy and 1916 discharge. The court dismissed the appeal, holding Hay lacked standing because he had no interest in the property; it was not scheduled in bankruptcy, and if fraudulent, title passed to the trustee, while if valid, it remained with his wife. The court ruled that questions about the bank’s right to proceed after discharge and the effect of a sheriff’s sale must be raised by the wife, not Hay.

This case study examines the National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL) as Commissioner Lisa Baird, appointed in March 2020, navigated the COVID-19 pandemic. The NWSL, founded in 2013 after the failures of the WUSA and WPS, operated as a single-entity league historically supported by U.S. Soccer, which subsidized salaries for allocated national team players and managed front office functions. Despite the USWNT’s international success and a passionate, digitally active fan base, the league received minimal mainstream media coverage and faced persistent financial challenges.

Days into her tenure, Baird suspended the 2020 preseason and organized workstreams covering medical protocols, finance, competition format, host cities, player concerns, childcare, and social justice. A federal PPP loan enabled the league to pay players. In June 2020, the NWSL became the first U.S. professional league to resume play, staging the Challenge Cup in a Utah bubble with strict health protocols, no fans, and broadcasts on CBS and Twitch; the tournament recorded zero COVID-19 cases and historic viewership. A Fall Series followed in regional pods. The league’s 2020 viewership rose 493% over 2019.

For 2021, the NWSL faced expansion with new teams including celebrity-backed Angel City FC, increased player allocation money, the first direct NWSL contracts for USWNT stars, a planned rebrand for its 10th anniversary, separation from U.S. Soccer operational control, and the start of NWSLPA collective bargaining negotiations, all while seeking to broaden media exposure, deepen fan engagement, and maintain its social justice platform.

Cu-doped NiO thin films were synthesized on ITO-coated glass substrates using spray pyrolysis at 450 °C with a 1.5-minute deposition time, using nickel chloride hexahydrate with 7 wt% copper chloride dihydrate added for doping. XRD confirmed successful substitutional Cu doping into the cubic NiO lattice, with the (111) peak shifting from 37.2° to 37.0°, lattice parameters increasing from 4.18 Å to 4.20 Å, and crystallite size decreasing from 21 nm to 20 nm. FESEM showed well-dispersed crystalline grains with homogeneous substrate coverage. UV-Vis spectroscopy revealed enhanced visible-light absorption and a bandgap reduction from 3.70 eV to 3.65 eV. Raman analysis showed disappearance of the TO mode and red shifts in LO and second-order modes, while photoluminescence exhibited intensity quenching and peak red shifts, indicating increased defect density and non-radiative recombination centers. Electrical characterization under exposure to approximately 1 vol% LPG showed the NiO:Cu film current increasing from 265 mA to 480 mA at 5 V, compared with 249 mA to 327 mA for undoped NiO, with resistance changes of 8 Ω and 4 Ω, respectively. Gas sensitivity at 5 V was 1.8 for NiO:Cu and 1.3 for NiO, with the doped film demonstrating higher sensitivity above 1 V bias. These improvements were attributed to enhanced charge transport, increased adsorption sites, and optimized surface reactivity resulting from Cu-induced lattice distortion and defect states.

A study in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences suggests dopamine is key to mother-infant bonding. Researchers observed 19 mothers and found their brains secreted more dopamine when watching videos of their own babies than other infants. Mothers with higher dopamine levels provided more sensitive, optimal care, while less responsive mothers secreted less dopamine, hinting at brain mechanisms behind caregiving struggles. Researchers believe this process may continue as children age and extend to other close relationships. Better maternal care may promote normal infant brain development, whereas poor care is associated with lower school achievement and increased mental and physical disease risk in adulthood. Whether fathers or other caregivers experience similar dopamine responses requires further study, and the small sample size may limit general applicability.

Post-secondary and occupational therapy (OT) students commonly experience trauma and adverse childhood experiences (ACEs), which can negatively affect academic performance, attendance, self-efficacy, and daily functioning. Trauma responses may appear as physical, behavioral, cognitive, social, and environmental challenges. The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) trauma-informed care (TIC) framework comprises six principles—safety, trustworthiness, peer support, collaboration, empowerment, and cultural responsiveness—and ten implementation domains spanning governance, training, physical environment, policy, and evaluation. Despite high trauma prevalence, few OT programs integrate TIC or ACEs content into curricula, and educators often lack awareness of trauma’s educational impact. Effective models include the PATH simulation-based training, which improves knowledge and self-efficacy, and peer-led health and wellness coaching. Recommended educational strategies include trauma-informed professional development, advance notice of triggering material, classroom check-ins, self-care modules, predictable routines, culturally responsive instruction, universal design, and peer support. Embedding TIC across institutional levels aims to prevent re-traumatization, create supportive learning environments, and enhance student engagement, retention, and graduation rates.

The study employs an individual-based mathematical model to assess the global risk of selection and spread of Plasmodium falciparum pfhrp2/3 gene deletions, which cause false-negative results on HRP2-based malaria rapid diagnostic tests. Incorporating updated parameters—including HRP3 cross-reactivity, fitness costs, treatment-seeking behavior, microscopy use, and linkage between pfhrp2 and pfhrp3 deletions—the model generates two risk metrics. The Innate Risk Score estimates how quickly clinically relevant misdiagnosis would reach 5% if HRP2-based RDTs were used universally, while the Prospective Risk Score incorporates current deletion prevalence and actual RDT usage to forecast continued spread. Results indicate that lower malaria prevalence is the strongest driver of selection. The model predicts that numerous countries, particularly in the Horn of Africa, East Africa, and parts of West Africa, are at high risk of reaching the 5% threshold within 20 years. The authors note substantial uncertainty in surveillance data and model parameters, and suggest the findings can inform prioritization of molecular surveillance and deployment of non-HRP2-based diagnostic strategies.

Scientists created human egg cells from skin cells through somatic cell nuclear transfer, using a chemical called roscovitine and fertilization to induce meiosis. The proof-of-concept effort produced early embryos, but none developed beyond the blastocyst stage or contained correct chromosome numbers due to random chromosome pairing, making them nonviable. Though currently too inefficient and risky for clinical use, the technique could eventually help treat infertility or allow same-sex male couples to have genetically related children. Researchers estimate at least a decade before clinical trials, which likely could not take place in the United States due to prohibitions on genetically modifying human embryos.

The lecture examines protein folding through fixed-angle linkages, modeling protein backbones as chains with rigid bond lengths and angles. It addresses four algorithmic problems. First, span: computing the maximum or minimum flat span is NP-hard, while the general 3D problem remains open, though orthogonal chains permit linear-time solutions. Second, flattening: determining whether a fixed-angle chain has a non-self-intersecting flat state is NP-hard. Third, flat state connectivity: it is unknown whether all flat states of an open fixed-angle chain are connected; positive results hold for orthogonal, obtuse, and certain equal-angle chains, while a partially rigid fixed-angle tree demonstrates disconnection. Fourth, locked chains: locked configurations exist for equilateral and equiangular fixed-angle chains, but whether obtuse equilateral equiangular chains can be locked is open. Finally, the lecture presents "producible protein chains," modeling ribosome synthesis as production from a cone. For chains with turn angles bounded by the cone half-angle (alpha-producible), a helical canonical configuration (alpha CCC) exists. The main theorem proves that all producible configurations lie in one connected component, all flat states are producible, and therefore such chains are flat-state connected, offering a mechanical model for protein folding.

Gas colic is the most common but least serious form of colic, occurring when gas produced during normal hindgut fermentation fails to pass through the large colon and builds up. It is largely preventable and primarily caused by two widespread practices: limiting forage and stall confinement. Additional causes include stress, ulcers, intestinal inflammation, inadequate exercise, dehydration, and rapid feed changes. Restricting forage disrupts digestion, causes acid accumulation and gorging, and increases gas production, while confinement reduces hindgut motility, trapping gas. Horses require continuous forage availability—ideally through pasture turnout and slow feeders—to support natural grazing, reduce stress, and maintain digestive health. Feed changes should be gradual, taking approximately one week for hay and two to three weeks for new feeds. Supplements such as B vitamins, yeast, and colostrum may support digestive health, while minimizing inflammatory ingredients like sugar and soy is recommended.

Richard L. Helzer was convicted of two counts of gross indecency and being a sexually delinquent person. The trial court allowed five peremptory challenges for the jury and reserved ruling on his request for 20 challenges based on the possible life sentence for sexual delinquency. The Court of Appeals reversed and remanded for a new trial. On appeal, the court held that sexual delinquency is an alternate sentencing provision, not a penalty enhancement, and that a defendant charged as a sexually delinquent person must, unless waived, be tried before a separate jury empaneled after conviction on the principal charge. That jury must be afforded 20 peremptory challenges because of the possible life sentence, while the jury for the principal charge receives only the number appropriate to that charge. The sexual delinquency charge must be brought in the original indictment before trial on the principal charge begins, though amendments prior to trial are permissible, and no reference to it may be made to the jury trying the principal charge. The court affirmed the gross indecency conviction, reversed the sexual delinquency procedure, and remanded for a separate jury hearing on that charge only, declining to reach constitutional claims raised by the defendant. Chief Justice Kavanagh dissented, arguing the sexual delinquency statute is void for vagueness.

The American Cancer Society updated its guideline to recommend that average-risk adults begin colorectal cancer screening at age 45 rather than 50, citing rising cancer incidence in younger and middle-aged populations and microsimulation modeling showing a favorable benefit-to-burden balance. The recommendation for ages 45–49 is designated "qualified" due to less direct evidence, while screening for ages 50 and older remains a "strong recommendation." Adults in good health with a life expectancy greater than 10 years should continue screening through age 75; decisions should be individualized for ages 76–85, and screening is discouraged after age 85. Recommended options include annual high-sensitivity stool-based tests, multi-target stool DNA testing every three years, colonoscopy every 10 years, CT colonography every five years, and flexible sigmoidoscopy every five years, with no test prioritized. All positive non-colonoscopy results should be followed by timely colonoscopy. The guideline was published in *CA: A Cancer Journal for Clinicians*.

Asus Zenfone 5Z launched in India, exclusive to Flipkart from July 15. It features a 6.2-inch FHD+ notch display, Snapdragon 845, Android 8.0 Oreo, and a 3300mAh battery with AI charging. It comes in three variants priced Rs. 29,999 to Rs. 36,999 with 6GB/8GB RAM and up to 256GB storage. The phone has a 12MP+8MP dual rear camera, 8MP front camera, and launch offers include ICICI card discounts, no-cost EMI, and Jio cashback and data.

AMC management proposes doubling authorized shares to 1.1 billion, risking dilution. Net debt remains above $3 billion and Q3 box office revenues were weak. AMC trades at a discount to peer CNK due to losses, negative equity, and cash burn. The company was hard-hit by the pandemic as attendance plunged. Taylor Swift and AMC tie up again for promo film distribution ahead of her album release, which topped the weekend box office with $33M, while "One Battle After Another" conquered the weekend box office with a $22.4M debut.

Newark police seek public help locating nine suspects in seven unsolved shootings and robberies from June 2016. Director Anthony Ambrose released suspect photos, including Guillermo Borges and three men in a May grocery robbery. Authorities ask tipsters to call 1-877-NWK-TIPS, visit www.newarkpd.org, or use the department's app; tips are confidential and may yield rewards.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting underwriters exercised their option to purchase an additional $127.5 million of its 2.375% Convertible Senior Notes due March 15, 2022. The Option Notes were issued on March 30, 2017. In connection with the offering, the Company entered into additional note hedge transactions, paying approximately $26.6 million to reduce potential dilution, and additional warrant transactions, receiving approximately $6.9 million for warrants to acquire up to approximately 0.8 million shares at $655.00 per share. The Additional Warrants are separate from the Option Notes. The report was signed by Chief Financial Officer Deepak Ahuja on March 30, 2017.

American Girl will release its first male doll, Logan Everett, on Thursday as part of a contemporary series; he plays drums for Tenney Grant. The company is also bringing back Felicity Merriman and releasing dolls Z Yang and Nanea later in 2017. Dolls cost $115 each, or about $140 with accessories and a book.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture introduces GDDR6 memory with 14 Gbps signaling and redesigned interface circuits, delivering approximately 50% higher effective bandwidth over Pascal alongside larger L2 caches, such as 6 MB in the TU102. The display engine supports 8K at 60 Hz via DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2, HDR tone mapping, and enhanced NVENC and NVDEC capabilities. Turing TU102 and TU104 GPUs use NVLink for two-way SLI, providing up to 100 GB/s bidirectional bandwidth in TU102, and support VirtualLink over USB-C to consolidate VR headset power, display, and data in a single connector.

The architecture enables real-time ray tracing through dedicated RT Cores that accelerate BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection, achieving over 10 Giga Rays per second—roughly 10 times Pascal’s performance—within a hybrid rendering pipeline combining rasterization and ray tracing for effects like reflections, shadows, and ambient occlusion. Tensor Cores power NVIDIA NGX AI features, including Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS) for improved image quality with reduced shading cost, plus InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez.

New shading capabilities include Mesh Shading with Task and Mesh Shaders to reduce CPU bottlenecks, Variable Rate Shading (VRS) for per-region shading rate control, Texture Space Shading (TSS) to decouple visibility and appearance sampling, and Multi-View Rendering (MVR) for up to four hardware views per pass. Turing supports DX12 Tier 3 bindless resource views and Tier 2 resource heaps. The family comprises the TU102 (RTX 2080 Ti), TU104 (RTX 2080, Quadro RTX 5000, Tesla T4) with NVLink, and TU106 (RTX 2070) without NVLink/SLI. Performance is measured by RTX-OPS, a workload-based metric weighting Tensor, CUDA, RT, and integer operations.

The University of Manchester Students' Union launched Earth Week with a panel featuring Asad Rehman of Friends of the Earth and Martin Empson of Campaign Against Climate Change. Rehman discussed climate change's disproportionate impact on developing countries, noting the richest 10% of countries produce 50% of emissions while millions are displaced annually. He called for legal protection for climate refugees rather than vilification, linking the issue to the #NoBanNoWall campaign. Empson encouraged involvement through protests, petitions, contacting MPs, and donations, urging environmental and migration movements to collaborate.

Quantum spin relaxation in radical pairs is critical for quantum computing, spintronics, and quantum biophysics, including avian magnetoreception. Modeling these systems involves three key computational challenges: ensemble averaging over initially random nuclear spin states, exponential scaling of Hilbert and Liouville spaces with the number of nuclei, and stable long-time propagation. Existing approaches, from classical vector treatments to full quantum methods, struggle with accuracy or exponential scaling. This work introduces tensor network techniques—specifically matrix product states (MPS), matrix product density operators (MPDO), and vectorised MPDO—to simulate radical pair dynamics, using time-evolution schemes such as TDVP for long-range interactions. The aims are to bring recent tensor-network methods to spin chemistry, present the radical-pair problem to physicists, and demonstrate quantum-biological simulations.

A cave rescue expert with over 30 years of experience describes the rescue of 12 boys and their soccer coach from a flooded cave in Thailand as one of the most difficult he has encountered. The basic tenet of cave flood rescues is to wait for water levels to subside rather than risk rescuer lives, but monsoon conditions may keep the cave flooded for months. The boys were found alive 1.2 miles inside after nine days—an unusually long time for such situations. Warm cave temperatures prevented hypothermia, but prolonged starvation left them too weak to attempt a strenuous escape, requiring rescuers to gradually reintroduce food. Extraction options include teaching the boys cave diving, which is extremely dangerous for novices; drilling or finding a new entrance, both highly difficult; or waiting for floodwaters to recede. If the boys' location remains safe from further flooding and divers can supply them, they can survive with delivered food and care; otherwise, risky diving may be the only option.

Canada's Privacy Commissioner is investigating a 2016 Uber breach affecting over 57 million users. Authorities in the U.S., U.K., and Australia are also investigating, and an Alberta class-action lawsuit has been filed. Uber paid hackers $100,000 disguised as a bug bounty. The Commissioner cannot issue fines but can take companies to Federal Court. Uber says it is cooperating.

President-elect Trump tweeted on January 2, 2017, that CNN’s book “Unprecedented” used the “worst cover photo” of him, though he hoped the book would do well. The tweet added to recent Twitter attention surrounding Trump, which included his briefly following an account called “Emergency Kittens” on January 1 and a tweet claiming he knew Hillary Clinton would lose when her campaign canceled its fireworks. Trump also retweeted a New Year’s message from Ivanka Trump. Many Twitter users responded to his complaint about the CNN cover photo by calling him vain and suggesting he focus on more important matters.

Terry Rozier had a career-high 31 points and seven rebounds in his second career start, and Jayson Tatum added a career-high 27 points as the short-handed Boston Celtics beat the Atlanta Hawks 119-110. Rozier, who had a triple-double in his first start Wednesday, started in place of injured Kyrie Irving, one of four Celtics sidelined. Boston outscored Atlanta 41-20 in the third quarter to take a 19-point lead. Prince led the Hawks with a career-high 31 points and eight rebounds, while Dennis Schroder added 25.

Sources familiar with the Bank of Japan’s thinking say the central bank will not rush to exit ultra-loose monetary policy, as the risk of sharp yen appreciation and stubbornly low inflation make policymakers hesitant to taper stimulus or raise rates quickly. While Japan’s economy is growing strongly and the BOJ has hinted at modestly adjusting yield targets next year, any move would likely be a one-off rather than the start of a sustained hike cycle. Governor Haruhiko Kuroda’s impending departure in April and political pressure to prevent yen spikes and support stock prices further complicate normalization. Analysts warn that delaying an exit leaves the BOJ with scant tools to fight future shocks, though acting too soon could choke off the recovery.

The Supreme Court of Arizona held that A.R.S. § 13-4033(B) bars a defendant from directly appealing a contested post-judgment restitution order entered pursuant to a plea agreement that caps the restitution amount. Frank Hoffman pleaded no contest to DUI and agreed to pay restitution not to exceed $53,653.45. Following a contested hearing, the court ordered him to pay $40,933.45. The superior court dismissed Hoffman’s direct appeal, ruling that he could challenge the order only through Rule 32 post-conviction relief. The Supreme Court affirmed, concluding that such a restitution order is part of the “sentence” under § 13-4033(B), a interpretation that serves the legislative goal of reducing direct appeals from plea agreements and avoids a hybrid system of appellate review. The court rejected Hoffman’s arguments that § 13-4033(A)(3) authorized the appeal, that the state’s right to appeal rendered the statute absurd, and that Rule 32 relief was inadequate. The court also disapproved of prior appellate decisions that had assumed jurisdiction over similar appeals without addressing § 13-4033(B).

This preprint presents a blood-based, non-invasive test for detecting glial malignancy (GLI-M) in individuals with intracranial space occupying lesions (ICSOL). The test enriches circulating glial cells (CGCs) from 5 mL of peripheral blood using a proprietary circulating tumor cell enrichment medium that selectively permits survival of malignant cells, and identifies CGCs via immunocytochemistry profiling for GFAP and OLIG2 co-expression. Analytical validation demonstrated high recovery, linearity, sensitivity (92.5–95.0%), specificity (100%), and accuracy. Clinical validation studies, including case-control and prospective cohorts, evaluated the test’s ability to detect GLI-M and differentiate it from benign brain tumors (BBT), non-glial CNS malignancies, and epithelial malignancies with brain metastases. Results showed high sensitivity and 100% specificity across most cohorts, including 100% sensitivity and specificity in a prospective multi-center study of 68 patients, and 92.9% sensitivity with 100% specificity in a prospective cohort of 31 patients. Orthogonal fluorescence in situ hybridization verification of EGFR amplification in matched blood and tumor samples showed 100% concordance. The test covers common GLI-M subtypes representing approximately 97% of cases but does not detect rare subtypes such as CNS lymphoma or gliosarcoma, nor does it determine tumor grade or subtype. The study was funded by Datar Cancer Genetics Private Limited, and several authors are employees or the founder of that company.

Higher wind supply and easing demand curbed European prompt power prices, while forwards tracked lower coal. Germany's Wednesday baseload contract fell 16 percent to 28.75 euros/MWh and France's dropped 20 percent to 27.75 euros. Traders cited a bearish outlook as French nuclear supply improved and demand falls next week. Gas and oil gained.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended December 25, 2021 reports total net sales of $123.9 billion, an 11% increase from the prior year, net income of $34.6 billion, and diluted earnings per share of $2.10. Net sales by category were iPhone $71.6 billion, Services $19.5 billion, Mac $10.9 billion, Wearables, Home and Accessories $14.7 billion, and iPad $7.2 billion. Total assets were $381.2 billion, including $37.1 billion in cash and cash equivalents, and outstanding term debt was $117.8 billion. The company repurchased $20.4 billion of common stock and declared a quarterly dividend of $0.22 per share. The filing notes continued COVID-19-related supply shortages and describes legal proceedings including the Epic Games lawsuit.

U.S. stock futures rose modestly ahead of the Federal Reserve's expected interest rate hike and Chair Janet Yellen's statement. Tuesday options volume was average, with the CBOE put/call ratio at 0.64. Apple CEO Tim Cook confirmed autonomous vehicle plans, boosting AAPL stock nearly 1% and driving over 1.1 million options contracts. Tesla options volume increased on positive news, while Micron Technology rebounded following a bullish analyst note.

Carleton University is hiring a chair in the "conjuring arts" to research perception and deception, supported by a $2 million matching grant from The Slaight Family Foundation. Named after Allan Slaight, the five-year renewable position has drawn about 80 applicants and will study deception, including fake news and political persuasion, while creating a digital magic archive. The article cites a University of London study where 87% of participants solved a card trick without a false move, but only 60% after seeing an empty hand, suggesting people cling to initial assumptions. Magician Michael Close notes that people rationalize what they cannot logically explain.

On July 31, 2018, Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC reporting under Item 2.02 that it issued a press release and data sheet regarding its financial results for the third fiscal quarter ended June 30, 2018, attached as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2. Luca Maestri, Chief Financial Officer, signed the report.

Adam Henrique and Travis Zajac discussed their team's performance after facing the Kings in the Stanley Cup Finals. They acknowledged the opponent's strengths, including solid goaltending, puck-moving defensemen, and contributions from all four lines. Both admitted their team started nervously, failed to execute on dumps and forechecks, and turned over pucks too often, but improved as the game progressed. They felt they remained competitive despite not playing their best, expressed confidence they could perform better by getting pucks behind the defense, creating traffic, and cycling, and noted that returning a key player added depth. They anticipated the series would remain physically intense.

Former U.S. Senator Mark Begich's entry into the Alaska governor's race as a Democrat has caused concern among some Democrats and independents that he and independent Gov. Bill Walker will split votes, potentially allowing a Republican victory. The race is shaping up as a three-way contest between Begich, Walker, and the eventual Republican nominee, with state Sen. Mike Dunleavy seen as an early GOP favorite. Begich says he would not run if he did not think he could win. Walker, who won in 2014 on a unity ticket with Democrat Byron Mallott, planned to run in the Democratic primary but opted to gather signatures for the general election after Begich entered. The Democratic party backs Begich. Key issues include Alaska's budget deficit, oil-wealth fund dividends, and school choice. Dunleavy advocates deeper cuts and full dividend payouts, while Begich says Walker lost sight of an overall vision for Alaska amid budget battles.

This is the November 23, 2001, daily edition of Energy Central Direct, an email news digest sent to paul.d.thomas@enron.com. The newsletter compiles energy industry news across multiple categories. Top electric power stories include the Los Angeles City Council voting to retain its partnership in a Nevada power plant, German utility E.ON AG planning U.S. acquisitions, a federal ruling preventing Southern Co. from charging unregulated rates for some wholesale sales, and FERC scheduling a workshop to expedite hydroelectric relicensing. The edition extensively covers Enron Corp.'s financial deterioration, including Dynegy Inc.'s attempt to speed up its planned acquisition, a $690 million debt payment triggered by a credit downgrade, an employee lawsuit alleging $400,000 in stock losses, U.S. energy traders scaling back deals with Enron, and statements of concern from FERC and Oregon regulators regarding Enron's utility subsidiary Portland General Electric. California coverage addresses orders restricting the grid operator's advance data sharing to traders, PG&E bankruptcy proceedings, state budgetary problems, and consumer advocate worries over potential cuts to low-income utility discount programs. Additional sections report on mergers and acquisitions, power plant projects and proposals in the U.S. and abroad, international developments in Europe and Latin America, rate decisions, transmission and reliability issues, renewable energy initiatives, and personnel changes. The digest also includes a Restructuring Today section, an RER eMetrix load forecast for CAL ISO, and subscriber service information.

Mobile games on sale this week for iOS and Android include A Good Snowman is Hard to Build, Ace Attorney, Assassin's Creed Identity, Kensho, Royal Trouble, Runic Rampage, Spite & Malice HD, and Warhammer 40,000, available at discounted prices or free. Ebberston, Mulgrave and Ganton were victorious at the first triple-header T20 Cayley Cup Finals Day at North Marine Road on Sunday. Ganton beat Kirkbymoorside by nine wickets in the Division Two final. Mulgrave defeated Sherburn by 28 runs in the Division One final. Ebberston won against Filey by six wickets in the Premier Division final. The winning captains received their cups, and thanks were given to the umpires, scorers, Scarborough Cricket Club, groundsman John Dodds, and Beckett League secretary Simon Dobson.

The author, who has panic disorder (PD), notes that PD affects 2–3% of Americans while anxiety disorders affect 18.1%. Clinically, “anxiety attack” is not a formal term; anxiety is persistent worry, whereas a panic attack is a sudden burst of intense fear lasting under 30 minutes, often without trigger in PD. Symptoms include palpitations, sweating, trembling, shortness of breath, chest pain, dizziness, and fear of dying. Experts recommend learning these signs, writing reassuring facts and mantras on an index card, visualizing panic as a passing wave that peaks around ten minutes, using smartphone games or music for distraction, and practicing slow, deep breathing daily to use during episodes.

Using data from 1,190 households in the 2019 National Survey of Early Care and Education, this study identified five distinct Child Care and Early Education search types through Latent Class Analysis of up to two information sources families used when searching for care for a focal child under age 6 within the past 24 months. The five types were: (1) CCR&R or Friends/Family; (2) Internet Search or Social Media; (3) Known Providers or Friends/Family; (4) Social Media or Friends/Family; and (5) Friends/Family or Internet Search. About half of families reported using one source and half used two. The analytic sample was somewhat higher-income, more likely to be two-parent working households, and more English-speaking than the overall population. Multinomial logistic regression found search types varied significantly by whether families sought information on type of care, whether the focal child had a condition affecting care provision—with Search Types 1 and 3 more likely to include such children—and U.S. geographic region, with Search Type 3 more common in the West and Search Type 5 more common in the Northeast. Most other family and child characteristics showed no significant relationship with search type. The study is limited by recording only the first two mentioned sources and by excluding households that did not conduct a recent search or considered only one provider.

The NVIDIA A100 GPU includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth and SECDED ECC protection across memory, L2 cache, L1 caches, and register files. Its 40 MB L2 cache is 6.7x larger than the Tesla V100’s, divided into two partitions providing 2.3x L2 read bandwidth, and supports Compute Data Compression for up to 4x bandwidth improvement and 2x effective capacity. The GPU contains 108 SMs with third-generation Tensor Cores delivering 16x higher peak mixed-precision compute than standard FP32 FMA, and supports fine-grained structured sparsity. It does not include display connectors, RT Cores, or an NVENC encoder.

Architecture optimizations include a new asynchronous global-to-shared memory copy instruction, 164 KB of shared memory per SM, and data sharing across 32 threads per warp. The design targets strong scaling for deep learning by feeding Tensor Cores with higher L2 and DRAM bandwidth.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) can partition each A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances, each with dedicated compute and memory system paths for quality of service and fault isolation. GPU Instances are built from GPU slices containing Sys Pipes, GPCs, L2 cache slices, and frame buffer memory. Within GPU Instances, Compute Instances enable simultaneous context execution and Volta-style MPS functionality.

Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/sec total bandwidth across 12 links, while PCIe Gen 4 delivers 31.5 GB/sec per direction and supports SR-IOV. The architecture improves error and fault detection, isolation, and containment.

Additional hardware features include five NVDEC units, a five-core NVJPG JPEG decode engine, an Optical Flow Accelerator, and improved atomic throughput—11x for FP16 and 2.7x for FP32 over V100.

CUDA 11 supports Task Graphs, asynchronous copy and barriers, L2 cache residency controls, and Cooperative Groups. The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs connected via NVSwitch, delivering 5 PFLOPS, and leverages MIG and the NGC software stack for flexible AI infrastructure deployment.

The Sixth Circuit affirmed Dr. Howard W. Ellzey’s conviction for conspiring to and illegally distributing controlled substances. The court found substantial evidence supported the verdict, including that Ellzey wrote nearly 29,000 amphetamine prescriptions at two Memphis offices with minimal patient examination, and that individuals recruited people to obtain prescriptions for resale. The court rejected challenges to the indictment’s use of “distributing,” the admission of 29,000 prescriptions as evidence of intent, jury instructions, and voir dire, finding no merit in other alleged errors.

U.S. stocks rallied after Trump's election on hopes for tax cuts, infrastructure spending, and deregulation, but gains faded amid bumpy legislative progress. Hospital stocks fell 7.1 percent before inauguration then rose 4.1 percent as Affordable Care Act repeal stalled. Infrastructure stocks gained 13 percent initially but only 2.4 percent afterward as a package failed to materialize. S&P 500 banks surged 20.8 percent post-election but added 3.1 percent since inauguration amid loan growth and deregulation concerns. Russell 2000 rose 12.6 percent then 5.3 percent on tax cut hopes, though doubts persist over legislative struggles and international distractions.

The lecture covers web security vulnerabilities and defenses. It demonstrates the Shellshock bug, where custom HTTP headers set malformed Bash environment variables to execute arbitrary commands, and cross-site scripting (XSS), where untrusted input reflected in HTML executes JavaScript, sometimes bypassing browser filters. Discussed XSS defenses include browser filters, HTTP-only cookies, privilege separation on separate domains, content sanitization (e.g., Django templates), constrained markup languages like Markdown, Content Security Policy (CSP) to restrict content sources and inline scripts, and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. The lecture also addresses SQL injection and path traversal, stressing rigorous input encoding. It explores session management alternatives to traditional cookies, such as stateless Message Authentication Codes (MACs), DOM storage, and client-side certificates. Protocol vulnerabilities like URL parsing mismatches and the GIFAR attack—embedding a JAR file inside a GIF to bypass same-origin checks—are explained. Finally, it describes covert channel timing attacks using CSS link colors, cache timing, DNS caching, and rendering times to infer browsing history, along with browser mitigations.

UK scientists found bumblebee queens exposed to neonicotinoid pesticides were 26% less likely to lay eggs, potentially causing wild population declines. Published in Nature Ecology and Evolution, the study exposed queens to thiamethoxam at field-comparable levels. Researcher Nigel Raine called the impact significant but noted nutrition and parasites also affect bees. The findings may support tighter EU restrictions on neonicotinoids; pesticide companies and farmers oppose this, citing reduced yields and increased alternative pesticide use.

Swarthmore students take themselves seriously and stress over grades and internships, but the author argues it is acceptable to make mistakes and laugh at oneself. Although expectations for academics and accountability are high, errors are not life-altering and often provide valuable lessons. The campus environment is unique and intense. Students should give themselves and others a break, assume good intent, ask for clarification during conflicts, and use laughter as a coping mechanism.

Eagles wide receiver A.J. Brown broke his silence on frustration over limited targets, having exceeded 30 yards only once (109 yards, one touchdown). He said wanting the ball is about sparking the struggling offense, not personal stats. Teammate DeVonta Smith has also posted modest numbers. While Philadelphia is 4-0 despite limited receiver production, offensive coordinator Kevin Patullo needs to find ways to increase their involvement.

The lecturer notes that problem set 8 is new territory; exercise 8.2 lacks necessary background and should be skipped, while 8.3 (BCJR decoding) is contingent on covering the algorithm in lecture, with noise variance set to 1. The lecture then presents Hadamard transform realizations of Reed-Muller codes, defining the transform over F2 via recursive tensor products of a self-inverse 2×2 matrix. Reed-Muller codes are generated by selecting rows of this matrix by weight. Graphical realizations using simple equality and zero-sum nodes produce low-complexity cyclic representations; fixing certain variables yields realizations of specific codes like the (8,4,4) code. Agglomerating constraints can remove cycles to create cycle-free realizations resembling trellises, but at higher state and branch complexity. The lecturer mentions that Reed-Muller codes meet the cut-set bound in such cycle-free forms and briefly notes related graphical models in the appendix (factor graphs, Markov fields, Bayesian networks). The lecture then introduces Chapter 12: the sum-product algorithm for APP decoding. On cycle-free graphs, it computes exact a posteriori probabilities in finite time (equivalent to the BCJR algorithm on trellises); on graphs with cycles, it becomes iterative and approximate. APP decoding minimizes bit error probability and produces soft outputs (intrinsic and extrinsic information) essential for iterative decoding of concatenated codes. The algorithm uses past/future decomposition along graph cut-sets for efficient computation.

This preprint proposes a brain-predicted disease duration (DD) gap derived from conventional MRI to quantify multiple sclerosis (MS)-specific structural damage independently of healthy brain ageing. Using deep learning on a multicentric cohort of 4,392 patients, the authors modeled disease duration and compared the DD gap against the conventional brain-age gap (BAG) and an alternative MS-specific brain-age (MS-age) gap. The DD model achieved a mean absolute error of 5.63 years and explained more variance in disease duration than established MRI biomarkers. The DD gap was nearly orthogonal to BAG, whereas the MS-age gap remained moderately correlated with it. Cross-sectionally and longitudinally, the DD gap significantly improved explanation of physical disability (EDSS) beyond BAG alone, while the MS-age gap did not. Artificial lesion removal affected DD and MS-age predictions but not BAG. The authors conclude that the DD gap captures MS-specific neurodegeneration distinct from accelerated ageing, providing a complementary biomarker for disease severity and progression. Limitations include the inherent noise of clinical onset dates and potential confounding by disease-modifying treatments.

The Situation Calculus is a logical language for specifying artificial intelligence dynamical systems. Reiter’s successor state axioms addressed the frame problem for Markovian actions, where preconditions and effects depend only on the current situation. Gabaldon extended this to non-Markovian theories, allowing dependence on past situations. This paper uses non-Markovian Situation Calculus to model a taxonomy of obligations, adopting the obligation modality embedding from [37] via a deontic accessibility fluent O(s′, s) and the abbreviation Oblg(ϕ, s). The authors present the sequential temporal Situation Calculus with non-Markovian control, a door-opening running example, and sections formalizing obligation types, their properties, interactions between violation and compensation, related work, and future directions.

Five years after archaeologists confirmed Richard III's skeleton was found beneath a Leicester car park, the discovery profoundly affected several individuals. Dominic Smee, who shares the king's adolescent onset idiopathic thoracic scoliosis, served as Richard's body double in a Channel 4 documentary after intensive combat and riding training, an experience that transformed his self-esteem and led him to lecture about his experiences. Michael Ibsen, a descendant of Richard's sister Anne, provided the DNA sample that confirmed the remains' identity and built the king's coffin, though the accompanying media attention was overwhelming. Mike Mistry, the car park attendant who had worked above the grave for over 15 years and painted the "R" marking the burial spot, found himself in the spotlight talking to international visitors before being made redundant in 2016. Ian Churchward, a Devon-based musician, was inspired to transform his folk-rock band, The Legendary Ten Seconds, into a Ricardian act, producing multiple albums and a concept album about the king's life.

The TPS7H500x-SP are radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies at up to 2 MHz. The TPS7H5001-SP, TPS7H5002-SP, and TPS7H5003-SP allow configurable maximum duty cycles of 50%, 75%, or 100% via the DCL pin; the TPS7H5004-SP supports only 50%. In the 50% mode, OUTB and synchronous rectification outputs are active only for the TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP.

Peak current mode control uses the CS_ILIM pin, where the sensed current (with a 150 mV offset) is compared to COMP/2 to generate PWM. A CS_ILIM voltage of 1.05 V triggers cycle-by-cycle limiting and hiccup mode; a capacitor on HICC sets the delay before switching stops and the restart time, with a minimum recommended value of 3.3 nF. The FAULT pin triggers shutdown if it exceeds 0.6 V for longer than 0.4–1.4 µs, followed by a delay and soft-start restart. Slope compensation is set via a resistor on RSC to prevent subharmonic oscillation, and Type 2A or 2B frequency compensation is applied at the COMP pin. Thermal shutdown activates above 175°C and releases below 160°C.

A design example for a 500 kHz synchronous push-pull GaN converter with 5 V output specifies a 205 kΩ timing resistor, 25 ns dead time, 50 ns leading-edge blank time, 33 nF soft-start capacitor, transformer turns ratio of 2.5, 40 µH primary inductance, 170 V primary GaN FETs, 80 V synchronous rectifier GaN FETs, 0.47 µH output inductor, and 2.3 mF output capacitance to mitigate single-event transients. Current sensing uses a 1:100 transformer and a 7.5 Ω resistor, with a 3.3 nF hiccup capacitor and a 102 kΩ slope compensation resistor. Type 2A compensation uses 40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, and 47 pF. The controllers operate from a 4 V to 14 V input and require layout practices including separating analog and power grounds, minimizing high di/dt loops, and routing noisy traces away from sensitive signals.

A Fox News Halftime Report newsletter argues that weakening political parties increases partisanship and factionalism, citing California’s top-two primary system and the growth of independent voters. In Texas, a Quinnipiac poll shows Republican Sen. Ted Cruz leading Democratic challenger Beto O’Rourke 50 to 39 percent. President Trump continues to claim the FBI improperly used a confidential source in his 2016 campaign despite Rep. Trey Gowdy’s assessment that the bureau acted appropriately; the New York Times also reports Trump previously pushed Attorney General Jeff Sessions to reverse his recusal from the Russia investigation. Republicans are airing more immigration-focused campaign ads while Democrats focus on health care. Trump is scheduled to appear at a high-dollar fundraiser for the America First Action super PAC. Phoenix Mayor Greg Stanton resigned to run for Congress in Arizona’s 9th District. Rep. Steve Scalise attended his first GOP congressional baseball practice since being wounded in a 2017 shooting. A group of Long Island Rail Road passengers were filmed singing Billy Joel’s “Piano Man” together on a commuter train.

Asian equities mostly fell after the U.S. Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 basis points and detailed balance sheet unwinding, though markets viewed the hike as dovish. Japan's Nikkei fell 0.6 percent, South Korea's Kospi dropped 0.75 percent, Australia's S&P/ASX 200 declined 1.13 percent, and Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell 0.91 percent, while mainland Chinese indexes rose slightly. Traders doubted the Fed would achieve three hikes this year amid weak inflation. Toshiba shares fell 2.68 percent on legal action from Western Digital. Oil hit seven-month lows. Australian jobs data beat expectations with 42,000 new jobs, lifting the Australian dollar, while New Zealand's first-quarter GDP rose 0.5 percent, missing forecasts. The Bank of Japan began a two-day meeting and the Bank of England was due to announce its rate decision.

His father Patrick Kane is supportive. He notes Buffalo's hockey growth. He plays wing or center. Mentors include Don Harkins, John Hines, Dale Hunter, and Dave Gagner. He chose OHL. He grew up in Buffalo and wants to bring a cup there, though any team holding his rights is special. He likes Briere.

Junior County, a 6-foot-4 combo guard from Wasatch Academy and the No. 4 shooting guard in the 2026 class, committed to UConn. County, ranked No. 43 overall in the SC Next 100, chose the Huskies after his final visit last weekend, citing his relationship with coach Dan Hurley and the program's intensity. He averaged 13.6 points, 4.8 rebounds and 3.4 assists on the Nike EYBL circuit. County is Hurley's first commitment in the 2026 class, following three straight top-10 recruiting classes for UConn.

Researchers from the Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology and collaborators traced the common ancestor of living fungi to roughly 1.4–0.9 billion years ago, indicating that fungi diversified hundreds of millions of years before land plants. To overcome the scarcity of fungal fossils, the team calibrated the molecular clock by identifying 17 rare horizontal gene transfers between fungal lineages and combining these with fossil evidence. The findings suggest that ancient fungi partnered with algae to recycle nutrients, break down rock, and create primitive soils, acting as ecosystem engineers that prepared terrestrial environments for the later emergence of plants.

United Airlines took subtle jabs at Delta and American to position itself as a premium carrier. It promised uncrowded airport lounges, contrasting with Delta’s overcrowded Sky Clubs, and touted seatback entertainment on more than 146,000 seats across 765 planes, unlike American’s tablet-holder approach. United’s third-quarter premium cabin revenue rose 6% year-over-year. Delta has raised lounge prices and fees and is opening select, higher-end Delta One Lounges to manage crowding. United’s stock fell over 7% after earnings but is up 34% over the past year, while Delta is up 6.5% and American is down 8.6%.

San Diego County confirmed its first human West Nile Virus case this year in a Spring Valley woman. Symptoms appear two to 14 days after bites. The county reported 32 dead birds, eight mosquito batches, and one horse tested positive. California: 231 ill, 12 dead. Officials urge repellent, protective clothing, and removing standing water.

Beijing's top official, Zhang Xiaoming, set three "bottom lines" against harming national sovereignty, challenging central authority, or subverting the mainland. Tensions flared after pro-independence lawmakers were ousted, fueling fears of eroded autonomy. Unpopular leader Leung Chun-ying will not seek re-election, while hardliner Regina Ip announced her candidacy, raising concerns of tighter Beijing control.

Beijing ordered 15 real estate portals to remove misleading ads, feng shui content, and offers to help with residence permits or school enrollment by Wednesday to cool its housing market. Recent measures include higher down payments on second homes, suspended mortgages over 25 years, and bans on third-property purchases.

Education regulators are reviewing a whistleblower's claim that Ohio's now-shuttered online charter school, the Electronic Classroom of Tomorrow (ECOT), intentionally inflated attendance figures tied to state funding using ActivTrak software. A former technology employee said school officials ordered staff to manipulate student data after the state demanded the school return $60 million in overpayments for the 2015-2016 school year. The state found the software duplicated learning hours and challenged ECOT's attendance claims. The whistleblower reported his concerns to the Ohio Department of Education and Republican Auditor Dave Yost. ECOT's former lobbyist denied the allegations. Democratic officials called for a criminal investigation, while a Republican prosecutor said no criminal referral has been received.

In his final Oval Office address, the President expresses gratitude to the American people, Vice President Gore, and his administration for two terms of service. He cites domestic achievements including record job growth, declining crime and welfare rolls, improved education and health coverage, poverty reduction, and environmental protections. He notes America's role as a global force for peace and prosperity with strong alliances. He offers three priorities for the future: maintaining fiscal responsibility and debt reduction; continuing international leadership to advance security, freedom, and equitable global trade while addressing terrorism, crime, and poverty; and uniting America's diverse population around shared values with fairness for all regardless of race, religion, gender, sexual orientation, or origin. He wishes success to the incoming President, George W. Bush, and affirms his continued commitment to service as a citizen.

The passage states that American strategic superiority ended the 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis, but policymakers later ignored Soviet declarations of military buildup and assumed permanent Soviet inferiority. It notes that fifteen years after Secretary McNamara's 1965 assessment, the Soviet Union leads the U.S. in most strategic military categories. The text criticizes the Carter Administration for weak, inconsistent responses to Soviet actions in Cuba and Afghanistan, and for slashing defenses after President Ford's budget would have maintained the margin, which has damaged American credibility and allied confidence. It argues that weakness provokes aggression, citing World War II, and advocates restoring a "margin of safety" through stronger conventional and strategic forces, combating terrorism, consulting allies, and upholding American principles to achieve peace.

This study examines 361 blockchain courses across 533 AACSB-accredited U.S. business schools, finding that 151 universities (approximately 28%) offer at least one course, primarily at the undergraduate level (72%). Computer Science (70) and Information Systems (67) departments host the majority, though courses also appear in diverse departments including Biology and Political Science. While 89 public and 62 private universities offer courses, a higher percentage of private institutions (36% versus 24%) provide them, and larger undergraduate populations correlate with higher offering rates. Thematically, the largest category is Fundamentals and Overview (140 courses), followed by Digital Assets and Cryptocurrencies (71) and Technical Development (66). The paper highlights blockchain's cross-functional enterprise impact across management, finance, supply chain, IT, law, and procurement, requiring interdisciplinary cooperation and a blend of technical, social, methodological, and personal competences. Course content increasingly intersects with artificial intelligence (30 courses), the Internet of Things (18), and non-fungible tokens (15). The authors conclude that academic blockchain education is growing and interdisciplinary but varies in scope, urging future research to evaluate alignment with industry needs and to replicate the study to assess curricular evolution.

Seven-year-old Joseph Nyberg created "Heart Cents" to raise money for St. Joseph's heart patients after his grandfather died of heart disease. He collected pennies and dollars in Savannah and Richmond Hill for a month, raising over $200. A family matched the funds, bringing the total to $422, and an anonymous donation later added $250, for a total of $672 and 14 Heart Cents. The money covers costs like transportation and co-pays, and Joseph plans to keep collecting year-round to honor his grandfather.

The disclosure relates to noninvasive devices and methods for monitoring physiological parameters by processing data from optical sensors located at multiple patient measurement sites. Unlike conventional single-site monitors or prior multi-site oximeters that process each site's data independently, the described system combines raw or minimally processed data from multiple sensors into combined sensor data to generate a single measurement of parameters such as oxygen saturation, pulse rate, perfusion index, or glucose. The system includes sensors positioned at different measurement sites—such as a cephalic site (e.g., nose) and a peripheral site (e.g., finger)—with each sensor potentially having multiple light emitters and photodetectors arranged in a three-dimensional spatial configuration conforming to the site's anatomy. This spatial distribution provides topology information to validate sensor positioning and creates diverse light path lengths to improve measurement robustness. A signal processor can combine all sensor outputs using a single algorithm to produce the single measurement, or alternatively process individual site data independently. Combining data from multiple sites reduces errors and noise while providing a more comprehensive assessment of patient physiology than single-site measurements.

This application is a continuation of prior U.S. patent applications concerning torque sensing in a surgical robotic wrist. It discloses a surgical robotic component with an articulated terminal portion comprising distal, intermediate, and basal segments. The distal and intermediate segments connect via a first articulation permitting rotation about a first axis; the intermediate and basal segments connect via a second articulation permitting rotation about a second axis. The intermediate segment includes a third articulation—such as a universal joint, spherical joint, or pair of revolute joints—permitting rotation about third and fourth axes, and contains a first torque sensor for sensing torque about the third axis and a second torque sensor for sensing torque about the fourth axis. In at least one configuration, the first and second axes are parallel and the third and fourth axes are transverse to the first axis. Optional third and fourth torque sensors may sense torque about the first and second axes. The terminal portion may be located at the end of a surgical robot arm to attach a surgical instrument, or at the end of a surgical instrument to attach an end effector. The wrist-mounted torque sensors measure forces applied to the instrument or end effector from multiple directions for use in a force feedback mechanism. The arrangement eliminates kinematic singularities, allows the instrument shaft to extend along the terminal joint axis, provides motion similar to a human surgeon's wrist, and enables a relatively slim, lightweight arm suitable for multiple arms to operate in close proximity.

Southern California home prices rose significantly in the year ending May, with Los Angeles County up 8.3 percent, the Inland Empire up 8.2 percent, and Orange County up 6.2 percent, according to CoreLogic. The gains reflect a lean housing supply, as many homeowners with low mortgage rates avoid selling to avoid higher rates on a new home, while demand from buyers and renters outnumbers those looking to sell.

This book aims to regularize distributed system design through common patterns. While focused on distributed systems, its first section addresses single-node patterns because groups of co-located containers are the atomic elements of distributed systems. The text outlines motivations for splitting single-machine applications into multiple containers: resource isolation to protect critical services from background tasks; team scaling and modular reuse by enabling small teams to own focused, reusable components; and separation of concerns to simplify testing, enable independent deployment, and improve rollout reliability. Subsequent chapters describe single-node patterns assuming tightly dependent, coscheduled containers that may share volumes, filesystems, network namespaces, and memory—a grouping called a pod in Kubernetes.

Valid writes require a minimum of 32 SCLKs per data transfer frame. Read protocols include legacy SPI-compatible with single or dual SDO-x, and source-synchronous (SRC). The device defaults to SPI-00-S on power-up; other SPI protocols are selected via SDI_CTL_REG and SDO_CTL_REG. During SPI-compatible reads, RVS remains low, short frames read required MSBs, and long frames enable daisy-chain operation. Dual SDO-x mode is enabled via SDO_CTL_REG and launches two bits per SCLK edge on SDO-0 and SDO-1.

The passage documents AMD AGESA firmware interface procedures and host call-outs for processor and platform initialization. It describes stackless, pre-memory assembler routines that establish and later remove temporary cache-as-RAM stacks using a register-passing model, and standard procedures for creating and releasing parameter structures via pre-memory heap, post-memory DRAM, or host-allocated methods. The text details the boot sequence entry points—AmdInitReset, AmdInitEarly, AmdInitPost, AmdInitEnv, AmdInitMid, AmdInitLate, and AmdInitRtb—each performing progressively advanced initialization of execution caches, HyperTransport links, main memory, power management, graphics, and ACPI/DMI/WHEA table generation. It also covers S3 suspend and resume procedures that save and restore processor context to non-volatile and volatile storage. Required host-environment call-outs include buffer allocation, deallocation, and locating; system reset; SPD reading over SMBus; AP task dispatch and idle control; PCIe slot reset; and hooks before DRAM initialization and training. Optional call-outs support IDS NV storage, heap rebasing, external voltage adjustment, and FCH or graphics customization. Platform configuration structures govern processor core leveling, memory interleaving, VRM properties, PCIe topology, display, SATA, USB, and FCH settings. Procedures return status codes such as AGESA_SUCCESS, AGESA_WARNING, AGESA_ERROR, and AGESA_FATAL. Several low-level stack and MTRR procedures apply only to x86-64 architecture, whereas AArch64 APUs rely on the Platform Security Processor for early DRAM and stack initialization.

The Supreme Court of Louisiana affirmed the dismissal of a suit against Alfred R. Willis. United Distributors, Inc. sued Willis, Henry R. Burke, and Airco Appliance & Hardware, Inc. in solido to recover a note, claiming Willis was bound by a personal guarantee he signed in March 1953 in connection with his prospective acquisition of a 50% interest in the corporation. Two days later, Willis abandoned the venture, the plaintiff was informed, and the plaintiff’s salesman returned all other executed papers but retained the guarantee without Willis’s knowledge. The disputed note was executed by Airco a year later under Burke’s sole operation. The court held that because Willis’s sole motive for signing the guarantee was to become a stockholder, and the plaintiff knew this consideration failed, the guarantee became ineffective under Revised Civil Code Articles 1825, 1826, and 1827.

VIX futures, introduced in 2004 and traded on the Cboe Futures Exchange (CFE), are financial derivatives based on the VIX Index, a real-time measure of 30-day implied volatility in the U.S. equity market created in 1993. They allow market participants to speculate on volatility, hedge equity risk, diversify portfolios, and engage in arbitrage, though they do not precisely track the spot VIX and can incur long-term performance drag from rolling contracts. Trading strategies typically incorporate technical or fundamental analysis, risk management, and position sizing.

Key factors affecting VIX prices include the stock market cycle phase and contango or backwardation effects arising from the mean-reverting nature of spot VIX. Seasonally, the index tends to perform better in summer and fall, remain stagnant in winter, and decline in spring.

Contracts include full-size (index value multiplied by $1,000) and mini (one-tenth) versions, trading under the symbol VX with a tick size of $50 and minimum fluctuation of 0.05. Regular trading hours are Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 3:15 p.m. CT, with extended sessions available. Monthly contracts are financially settled on a Wednesday 30 days before the subsequent month's S&P 500 option expiration. As of December 19, 2022, futures traded at 22.450, with an all-time high of 80.850 in March 2020; the spot index reached an all-time high of 89.53 in October 2008 and a low of 8.56 in November 2017. The greatest risk stems from adverse leveraged price movements magnifying losses.

Researchers developed simultaneous ADF-EDS-EELS tomography to achieve nanoscale three-dimensional mapping of structure, chemical composition, and valence states in a single low-dose acquisition, overcoming the limitations of conventional two-dimensional and single-modality techniques for beam-sensitive materials. Applied to LiNi1/3Co1/3Mn1/3O2 (NCM111) lithium-ion battery cathodes after 50, 100, and 200 electrochemical cycles, the method revealed that chemical composition evolved uniformly throughout primary particles, whereas valence state changes and transition metal inhomogeneity were strongly surface-localized and depth-dependent. The cathode suffered progressive capacity fading, with structural phase transitions from layered to spinel-like after 100 cycles and to rock-salt after 200 cycles. Oxygen content remained stable through 100 cycles then declined sharply at 200 cycles, while transition-metal-rich segregation increased, especially near the surface, with cobalt showing the most pronounced segregation. Valence states exhibited strong depth dependence: pristine particles and those cycled up to 100 cycles showed higher Mn4+ and Co3+ in the core and lower valences toward the surface, attributed to local transition metal segregation rather than oxygen vacancies or secondary phases; by 200 cycles, Mn2+ and Co2+ increased sharply as the rock-salt structure formed. The coupled evolution of inhomogeneity and valence states followed non-monotonic trends, indicating that degradation arises from the interplay of structural phase transitions, transition metal migration, and dissolution-driven segregation. The findings highlight that 3D valence and inhomogeneity are active contributors to cathode stability, and the method is generalizable to other complex functional materials.

Brayan Rocchio's eighth-inning solo home run off a 99.9 mph pitch from Tigers reliever Troy Melton sparked a five-run rally, leading the Guardians to a Game 2 victory and forcing a decisive Game 3 in the AL Wild Card Series. Mumma Brothers Drilling Co. appealed a tax case regarding sales and use taxes on drilling equipment. The Indiana Court of Appeals affirmed the trial court’s judgment that the taxpayer, a contractor that installs water well equipment, was subject to tax under Ind. Code 6-2-1-38(k). The court rejected the taxpayer’s claimed exemption under Ind. Code 6-2-1-39(b)(6) for machinery used in direct extraction, holding that the exemption applies to extraction for resale, not for personal or business consumption where the water is not resold. The court strictly construed the exemption against the taxpayer.

The Combo defense counters spread offenses using three outside pass denials and two interior baseline zone defenders. Defenders force sideline drives, protect middle, deny return passes, trap penetrations, jam picked-up dribbles, forcing non-ball handlers to handle ball. If corner players shoot and handle well, switch to a quarter-court 1-3-1 trap.

The Elliott Wave theory, discovered by Ralph Nelson Elliott in the 1920s and 1930s after studying 75 years of stock data, is a technical analysis principle stating that asset prices move in recognizable wave patterns. It classifies waves into two main types: impulse waves, which consist of five sub-waves and move in the direction of the trend, and corrective waves, which consist of three sub-waves and move opposite to the trend. Technical traders in stock, forex, and commodity markets use the theory across various timeframes, often alongside indicators such as moving averages, stochastic oscillators, and RSI to confirm trading decisions. However, the theory is highly subjective, making it difficult to backtest, and it lacks clearly defined entry and exit rules. There is no single best timeframe for applying the theory, as its suitability depends on the trader’s individual style.

The Supreme Court debated whether restitution under the Mandatory Victims Restitution Act is criminal or civil in Holsey Ellingburg’s case, which concerns whether retroactive application violates the ex post facto clause. Both Ellingburg’s counsel and the government agreed the MVRA should not increase his punishment, leaving an appointed attorney to defend the sentence. Justice Alito emphasized civil aspects, including victims’ ability to enforce restitution as judgment liens and congressional intent to assist victims. Justices Kagan and Jackson countered that incorporating restitution into criminal sentencing indicates a penal purpose. The author predicts the Court will likely reject applying the statute to Ellingburg.
