Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) frequently develops resistance to androgen signaling inhibitors and taxanes, leaving limited treatment options. The passage describes how androgen receptor (AR) wild-type and splice variants—specifically ARv7 and ARv567—differentially associate with microtubules (MTs) and influence taxane sensitivity, with ARv7 linked to resistance and increased MT polymerization rates. A computational approach using automated tracking of EB1/EB3 comets is presented for quantifying MT dynamics in living cells. Studies in isogenic M12 cell lines and patient-derived organoids reveal differential MT regulation between taxane-sensitive and resistant cells, and the authors optimize organoid culture by modulating Y-27632 ROCK inhibitor levels to favor tumor cell growth. The text notes that androgen-independent mCRPC can feature small, PSMA-positive circulating tumor cells and bypass AR via FGF/MAPK signaling. It further examines how pVHL and GSK3β regulate MT homeostasis, with pVHL loss or GSK3β activity increasing MT turnover, and discusses how proteins such as Op18 and ERG, as well as MT post-translational modifications, contribute to drug resistance. The authors propose correlating live-cell MT dynamics with gene expression signatures to predict tubulin inhibitor susceptibility, using circular Hough transform to detect paclitaxel-induced MT bundling as a response marker. They suggest that targeting MT regulatory pathways—including GSK3, NAD+ metabolism, or protein degradation—could help anticipate and overcome drug resistance.

NVIDIA RTX IO enables rapid GPU-based loading and decompression of game assets through Microsoft DirectStorage, offloading CPU work to improve I/O performance by up to 100x and enable near-instantaneous loading. The NVIDIA A40 data center GPU, based on the GA10x Ampere architecture, delivers up to 2X FP32 throughput, 2X ray-tracing throughput, and 5X (10X with Sparsity) AI throughput, with 48GB of GPU memory scalable to 96GB via NVLink, PCIe Gen4, and virtual GPU software support. Ampere GPUs support 4K at 120Hz and 8K at 60Hz via DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1 with DSC. Fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware-accelerated decoding including the first GPU AV1 hardware decode support (up to 8K60 HDR with low CPU usage), while seventh-generation NVENC supports encoding up to 4K on H.264 and 8K on HEVC. The GA10x architecture delivers up to 2X performance in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI via second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores with structural sparsity, and GDDR6X memory. The RTX A6000 workstation GPU includes 48GB GDDR6 and professional certifications; the GeForce RTX 3090 includes 24GB GDDR6X; and the RTX 3070 uses GDDR6 and outperforms the previous generation RTX 2080 Ti. Error Detection and Replay (EDR) technology for GDDR6X detects transmission errors during overclocking to indicate memory limits before crashes occur.

The Eleventh Circuit affirmed Alexis Perez’s 51-month sentence for conspiracy to commit mail fraud. Perez appealed, arguing the district court erred by denying a three-level reduction under U.S.S.G. § 2X1.1(b)(2) for an incomplete conspiracy and a minor-role reduction under § 3B1.2. The court held that Perez and his co-conspirators had taken “crucial steps,” had a detailed plan, and were on the verge of executing the scheme, so the district court correctly declined the § 2X1.1(b)(2) reduction. The court also held that the district court did not clearly err in finding Perez played an “important” role in planning and preparation and was not less culpable than other participants, warranting denial of the minor-role reduction. The court noted a sentence appeal waiver was unenforceable because the district court did not question Perez about it, and Perez could not adopt his codefendants’ arguments because his appeal was not consolidated with theirs.

Price action trading is a technical analysis method that uses historical price movements, chart patterns, and candlestick formations to generate trade entry and exit signals with minimal reliance on indicators. A day trading price action strategy applies this analysis to intraday charts, identifying patterns such as reversals, continuations, and harmonic structures to time trades. While some traders use pure price action with tools like trend lines and support/resistance levels, others combine it with indicators such as moving averages, VIX, or RSI. The passage stresses that backtesting is essential to determine a strategy's viability, though price action strategies are often difficult to code and test. It presents an example backtest using WTI crude oil futures to illustrate how performance varies by market and time period. Common approaches include trend following, breakouts, reversal trades, and scalping, and the text advises using quantified, backtested rules and diversifying across strategies and markets.

To pay off debt effectively, reduce credit card use, establish a spending plan and emergency fund, and direct extra money toward balances. Cut unnecessary spending, prioritize high-interest debts first, reallocate paid-off funds to remaining debts, and make gradual lifestyle changes to avoid overwhelming deprivation.

Google honored German physicist Max Born with a 2017 Doodle for his 135th birthday. Born, born December 11, 1882, in Breslau, Germany, was a professor at the University of Göttingen for 12 years, where scientists including Werner Heisenberg and J. Robert Oppenheimer joined him. He maintained a 40-year friendship with Albert Einstein despite scientific differences. Forced to emigrate to England in 1933 under Nazi rule, he was later expelled from Göttingen by Hitler. Born won the 1954 Nobel Prize for the Born Rule, which uses mathematical probability to predict the location of wave particles in a quantum system. He died January 5, 1970, at age 87.

The passage describes the interface between AGESA™ software and host BIOS. For UEFI, the integration spans SEC, PEI, DXE, and RTB phases using specific PEIMs, DXE drivers, and build tools such as MASM and Microsoft C/C++ compilers. Key initialization procedures include AmdInitReset, AmdInitEarly, AmdInitPost, AmdInitEnv, AmdInitLate, and AmdInitRtb, along with S3 resume routines (AmdInitResume, AmdS3LateRestore, AmdS3FinalRestore). The host environment must implement required call-outs, allocate buffers, preserve pre-memory data, and avoid modifying cache controls during the Cache-As-Ram period.

Schoenfeld told Finnish Foreign Minister Witting that U.S. attitudes toward Finland were less favorable than reported, leaving a note. Witting defended aims including the Karelian and Onega Isthmuses, equated German and British policies, and cited Finnish "realism" from Russian experience, which Schoenfeld challenged. Al-Qaida-linked militants shot down a Russian Su-25 jet in Syria’s Idlib province on Saturday, killing the pilot after he ejected and resisted capture. NVIDIA Corporation's 2015 Form 10-K covers the fiscal year ended January 25, 2015. The Delaware-incorporated, Santa Clara-based company operates a fabless semiconductor business through two reporting segments: GPU and Tegra Processor. Its visual computing platforms address four markets—Gaming, Enterprise, High Performance Computing & Cloud, and Automotive—via brands including GeForce, Quadro, Tesla, GRID, and Tegra-powered SHIELD and DRIVE. Sales to the largest customer accounted for 11% of fiscal 2015 revenue, and 75% of revenue came from outside the United States and Other Americas. The company faces risks from intense competition, manufacturing dependencies, customer concentration, and intellectual property disputes, including patent infringement lawsuits filed against Qualcomm and Samsung in September 2014 and a countersuit by Samsung in November 2014. During fiscal 2015, NVIDIA returned $1.00 billion to shareholders through $813.6 million in share repurchases and $186.5 million in dividends, and announced plans to return approximately $600.0 million in fiscal 2016. The company also carries $1.5 billion in 1.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2018.

Slowing pay growth and rising inflation are worsening the UK outlook, squeezing households and raising post-election business uncertainty. Employment rose 109,000 in the three months to April to a joint-record 74.8%, with robust hiring into May. However, regular earnings grew just 1.7%, the weakest since January 2015, while consumer prices rose 2.9%, causing real pay to fall. Consumer spending is strained and likely to drag on growth, leaving the economy reliant on exports and business investment. Moderating input costs suggest inflation may cool later this year, but wage growth shows no sign of improving. The Bank of England is expected to keep interest rates on hold until the outlook clears.

The bill lets district and charter schools create innovation plans and seek state board rule waivers, allows LEAs to use state restricted and private funding, and requires annual State Board reports to the Education Interim Committee. Strong relationships with adult and peer mentors are crucial for student academic success, provided through school, afterschool, and community programs, as well as naturally through teachers, extended family, and community leaders. Following COVID-19 disruptions that disproportionately impacted low-income students, students of color, and those with disabilities—leaving students months behind in math and reading and disconnected from school—mentoring is especially critical. Meta-analyses and research syntheses indicate that mentoring programs significantly improve academic outcomes, including attendance, grades, test scores, classroom behavior, school connectedness, and graduation rates. Exemplary school-based programs such as Big Brothers Big Sisters, Gear Up, AMPED, Project Arrive, Success Mentors, and Check and Connect have improved academic performance, attendance, credits earned, and graduation rates. After-school models including Quantum Opportunities, Village Model of Care, and Canada’s Pathways to Education have raised GPAs and college acceptance. Naturally occurring mentoring relationships with teachers and school personnel also strongly predict educational attainment, school attachment, and improved attitudes toward school, with particular benefits for students of color. However, mentoring relationships are inequitably distributed, with youth of color and low-income youth reporting fewer mentors. Expanding access through private and public investment and supportive policies is essential to ensure all students benefit.

Spanish police dismantled a network recruiting transsexuals through fake Venezuelan "Miss Trans" competitions, freed over 20 victims, and arrested 14 suspects. It earned up to 1 million euros and imposed 15,000-euro debts.

A longitudinal evaluation of 11 SARS-CoV-2–positive nursing home residents in Georgia (October 2020–April 2021) characterized antibody kinetics post-infection and post-vaccination with the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine. Post-infection, 90% of participants developed detectable Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA antibodies and 80% developed IgM, with median detection times of 13–16 days. Pan-Ig and IgG titers rose and remained elevated, while IgM and IgA began declining by 30–50 days. At first antibody detection, two-thirds of participants remained RT-PCR positive, but no specimens were viral culture positive. One unvaccinated participant maintained detectable antibodies for at least 150 days. Following Pfizer vaccination, all 10 vaccinated participants developed Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA, and 60% developed IgM. Post-vaccination geometric mean titers were substantially higher than post-infection titers, with IgG increasing up to 200-fold. All vaccinated participants achieved IgG levels correlating with 80% vaccine efficacy. Limitations included a small sample size, use of only the Pfizer vaccine, monthly specimen collection, and evaluation prior to the emergence of the Delta and Omicron variants. The findings indicate that nursing home residents mount robust and durable humoral immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 infection that are significantly augmented by vaccination.

The Indianapolis Colts lost 13-7 in overtime after a late penalty negated a go-ahead conversion pass in blizzard conditions. Oclaro (OCLR), an optical networking company, reported a 47% revenue increase and 460% EPS growth to $0.79 for fiscal 2017, with margins expanding to 39%. An outside day is a two-bar price pattern where the second bar fully engulfs the first bar’s range, signaling increased volatility and potential trend continuation or reversal depending on context. Configurations vary based on the direction of each bar, with opposite-direction combinations forming outside reversals. Although the pattern is popular among price action traders, it is subjective and requires backtesting. Backtests of SPY day trading strategies showed an average gain of 0% from open to close after an outside day, a negative 0.07% return when the close was higher than the prior day, and a positive 0.06% return when the close was lower. The authors conclude that outside day patterns produce largely random, non-tradable results for day trading and are most effective only when combined with additional technical analysis such as trend, support and resistance, and Fibonacci levels.

The United States Court of Customs and Patent Appeals affirmed the Commissioner of Patents' decision upholding the dismissal of Lever Brothers Company's opposition to Thrift-D-Lux Cleaners, Inc.'s application to register the service mark "Thrift-D-Lux Cleaners" for dry cleaning and pressing services. Lever Brothers opposed based on its prior "Lux" trademark for soaps and its "Lux Laundry" program. The court held that "Thrift-D-Lux" conveyed "thrift" and "de luxe" rather than "Thrifty Lux," found the term "de luxe" to be in common public use, distinguished cited precedents, noted the tenuous relationship between a goods mark and a service mark, and concluded that Lever Brothers failed to show likely confusion or damage.

The Appellate Division affirmed the dismissal of plastic surgeon James Horne’s complaint against the New York State Department of Health, in which he alleged disability discrimination under Executive Law § 296 over his medical license revocation. In Noble et al. v. The Thompson Oil Co. to the use of Brown et al., the court affirmed judgment for assignees of a Pennsylvania judgment against defendants who pleaded a New York foreign attachment judgment and payment as a bar. The court held that the assignment, valid in Pennsylvania, was valid everywhere and fully divested the assignor of attachable interest before the New York attachment issued. Because the assignees and the debt were in Pennsylvania, the New York court lacked jurisdiction over the persons or property, rendering its judgment void as to the assignees. The court ruled that the Full Faith and Credit Clause does not preclude jurisdictional inquiry; that a plaintiff in foreign attachment stands in no better position than the debtor; and that assignees, not being parties or privies, were not bound by the New York proceedings. Any error in ordering oyer of the New York record was waived.

A study identifies 50 objects in low-Earth orbit—primarily pre-2000 rocket bodies, mostly Russian—that account for half of the debris-generating collision risk. Provided herein is technology for detecting gastric neoplasia, particularly stomach cancer, by assessing DNA methylation states of specific biomarkers. Case-control studies identified 123 novel DNA methylation markers and validated optimal panels, including 10 tissue markers (e.g., ARHGEF4, ELMO1, ABCB1), 30 tissue markers (e.g., ELMO1, ARHGEF4, EMX1), and 12 plasma markers (e.g., ELMO1, ZNF569, C13orf18). Methods comprise assaying methylation states of these markers in biological samples—such as gastric tissue, plasma, or stool—and comparing them to normal controls to detect neoplasia. Also provided are compositions, kits, reagents, and computer systems for performing these analyses.

The lecture wraps up stochastic methods, emphasizing that knowing expected results beforehand is essential to verify calculations and detect errors. Multidimensional integrals often involve a probability density or weighting factor times a function, as seen in the Boltzmann distribution and Bayesian analysis, where likelihood multiplied by prior knowledge provides the weighting for parameters. Metropolis Monte Carlo can evaluate such integrals, though step sizes must be carefully chosen to avoid repeated rejections or insufficient spatial sampling; accuracy scales as one over the square root of the sample size, making high precision expensive. Reducing problem dimensionality by removing irrelevant degrees of freedom is highly beneficial.

For non-stationary problems with intractably large state spaces, Kinetic Monte Carlo using the Gillespie algorithm is employed. An example with a 10x10 catalytic surface having four states per site yields 4^100 possible states, making direct matrix methods impossible. The Gillespie algorithm generates random numbers to determine event times and types. To manage data, desired averages should be computed on the fly. Initial conditions may be drawn from a Poisson distribution. Computational tricks include treating fast processes like diffusion as infinitely fast, artificially slowing them, or excluding very low-probability events to reduce the state space. Low-probability events inherently have larger relative statistical error.

Molecular Dynamics solves classical equations of motion, typically with the velocity Verlet algorithm and thermostats, to simulate time-dependent properties on femtosecond to nanosecond scales. It is poorly suited for static equilibrium or slow processes compared to Metropolis Monte Carlo. The lecture stresses matching the method—Metropolis Monte Carlo, Kinetic Monte Carlo, or Molecular Dynamics—to the specific problem. For Monte Carlo integrals, rewriting the integrand as a probability density times a function allows more efficient sampling, and marginal integrals can eliminate unimportant parameters. Announcements include office hours on Kinetic Monte Carlo and a poll for scheduling the final review session.

In *In re Buchanan*, the petitioner, convicted of murder in New York and sentenced to death, sought a writ of error from the U.S. Supreme Court, claiming he was denied due process and an impartial jury because juror Paradise became mentally and physically incapacitated during deliberations. The New York Court of Appeals had affirmed the judgment, concluding that the jury reached its verdict before the juror fell ill and that conflicting evidence regarding his mental competency presented a question of fact for the trial court. The Supreme Court held that a juror’s physical and mental condition and competency to return a verdict is a question of fact that it cannot review on a writ of error to a state court in an action at law, and denied the application.

The passage provides technical rules and implementation details for integrating AMD AGESA software with a host BIOS. It prohibits calling unpublished interface functions and warns against enabling code execution caching before main memory initialization except through provided AGESA functions. It defines returned status codes—SUCCESS, UNSUPPORTED, BOUNDS_CHK, ALERT, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL, and FATAL—that indicate severity and direct required host actions, noting that errors are logged in a circular buffer. The document explains the binary module architecture, where a host Bridge calls the AGESA Dispatcher and AGESA uses a Call-Out port and Router to access host services, operating in 32-bit protected mode with deprecated 16-bit real mode support. It covers UEFI environment integration across SEC, PEI, and DXE phases, including stack establishment via AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK and Cache-As-Ram requirements. The core initialization sequence comprises entry points such as AmdInitReset, AmdInitEarly, AmdInitPost, AmdInitEnv, AmdInitLate, AmdInitRtb, and AmdInitResume, each with specific parameters, duties, and dependencies. Additional procedures manage structure creation and release, event log retrieval, APIC and PCI address lookup, core and DIMM identification, and MMIO rule updates. The text also describes build methods (Binary Modules versus Source Integration), required environment variables, and platform-specific configuration through options files.

A defensive switch occurs when a beaten first defender exchanges roles with the second (support) defender, who must remain positioned inside, goalside, and behind the first defender to block the direct path to goal. The second defender initiates the exchange, takes on the ball carrier, and uses oral commands like “support,” “jockey,” or “tackle” to direct the first defender, who then covers the second’s mark or retreats to a support position if there was no mark. Scenarios include basic switches down the sideline or inside, alternative midfield switches trading marks with or without the ball, and switches when an opponent sprints past a defender. Once the threat passes, the same player who called the switch announces “switch back” to return to original positions. Instruction progresses from stationary positioning and relative movement at half-speed, emphasizing proper stance and communication, to full-speed game conditions.

The passage describes methods, apparatuses, and systems for downlink assignments for downlink control channels. In one embodiment, a user equipment monitors first and second downlink control channel candidates in respective first and second control resource sets having different sets of orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing symbols, receives at least one downlink assignment, and determines a downlink data channel allocation and a demodulation reference signal symbol location for the corresponding channel based on the assignment and both symbol sets before decoding. In another embodiment, the user equipment receives an indication of associated search spaces for different control resource sets whose demodulation reference signal ports are quasi-collocated with different reference signals, determines a third set of monitoring occasions as a subset of the first and second sets, and monitors candidates in common slots if they carry the same downlink control information. The passage further discloses that if multiple control resource sets of different duration collide with a downlink shared channel allocation, the demodulation reference signal location may be based on the control resource set ending in the later symbol; that multiple downlink control channels may schedule associated downlink shared channels carrying the same transport block, enabling soft combining and a single hybrid automatic repeat request-acknowledgement feedback; and that transmission configuration index interpretation updates are applied after a downlink shared channel reception window.

In *Lewis v. Bayer AG*, the court granted in part and denied in part plaintiffs’ motion for class certification for claims arising from the prescription drug Baycol (Cerivastatin). The court certified only Class I, defined as Pennsylvania residents who were prescribed and ingested Baycol and have not been diagnosed with rhabdomyolysis or congestive heart failure, solely for medical monitoring benefits. Arthur Conner, Milton Angert, and Lisa Frost were appointed class representatives. The court found numerosity satisfied for all classes due to approximately 700,000 consumers. Certification was denied for Class II (nationwide medical monitoring), Class III (nationwide personal injury), and Class IV (Pennsylvania personal injury). The court held that individual issues of fact predominated for the personal injury classes regarding causation, medical history, dosage, and warnings. For the nationwide classes, conflicts of law among states defeated commonality for medical monitoring, unjust enrichment, negligence, and consumer protection claims. While commonality was found for Class I’s medical monitoring claim, the court held that Class I’s claims under the Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law and unjust enrichment lacked commonality and typicality due to individualized reliance and factual issues. The court concluded that a class action was a fair and efficient method for Class I’s medical monitoring claim. The parties were directed to submit notification proposals within 30 days.

Adm. Michael Rogers emphasizes that embracing rapid change and unconventional ideas is critical for Air Force cyber advancement. While the Air Force cross-trains active-duty cyber defense and offensive specialists, Tech. Sgt. Kyle Hanslovan of the Maryland Air National Guard’s 175th Cyberspace Operations Group suggests that ANG units’ structure, operational flexibility, and diverse civilian experience offer models for evolving all cyber forces. The 175th COG leverages Guardsmen’s backgrounds in government and private cybersecurity, which Col. Jori Robinson says enhances military training and creates a lethal, innovative force. The Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) mandates that students with disabilities receive a free appropriate public education (FAPE); alleged violations may be adjudicated through special education due process hearings, where hearing officers issue binding written decisions and remedies. Pennsylvania has historically been among the most litigious states for IDEA compliance and remained so during the COVID-19 pandemic, with city Local Education Agencies (LEAs) such as the School District of Philadelphia and Pittsburgh Public Schools experiencing notable compliance failures during mandated school closures. The present study employs an ex-post facto design to analyze 323 published hearing officer decisions—reduced from 347 after removing duplicates—from the Pennsylvania Office for Dispute Resolution involving city LEAs, uploaded between March 16, 2018, and March 15, 2022. Dividing the data into two-year periods before and after March 16, 2020, the study examines whether city LEAs were involved in more hearings after the pandemic, whether significant relationships exist between the pandemic and hearing officer ruling outcomes, and what remedies were owed. Ruling outcomes are categorized on a five-point scale from fully favoring the student to fully favoring the LEA, and remedies include Independent Educational Evaluations, compensatory education, and financial reimbursements. The research aims to identify training needs for LEAs in accordance with Office of Special Education Programs guidelines.

This lecture compares policy gradient and value function methods in model-free optimal control and introduces actor-critic algorithms that combine them. Policy gradient methods scale to high dimensions and offer guaranteed convergence, but they are local searches with high variance and require many samples. Value function methods are data-efficient and compact but often lack convergence guarantees, can diverge with function approximation, and are unstable because small value changes can cause large policy shifts. Actor-critic methods represent both a policy and a value function simultaneously, using the critic to reduce variance and guide updates while the actor retains strong convergence guarantees; key works cited include Konda and Tsitsiklis (2003), Sutton (1999), and Peters’ Natural Actor Critic. The lecturer presents his thesis on “Toddler,” an underactuated walking robot with actuated ankles that used an actor-critic approach with a linear function approximator and a low discount factor (gamma=0.2). Updating parameters once per footstep and aiming for a deadbeat return map, the robot learned to walk in about one minute and converged in roughly 10–20 minutes, showing robustness to disturbances and terrain changes without a dynamics model. This is contrasted with ASIMO’s fully actuated ZMP control, which is less efficient and robust. The lecture concludes with project deadlines: write-ups are due May 21, with oral presentations on May 12 and 14.

According to aqicn.org's analysis of 2014 WHO data from 1,622 urban locations in 92 countries, Pakistan has the world's most polluted urban areas (PM 2.5: 115.7), followed by Qatar and Afghanistan. Australia has the least polluted urban areas, followed by Brunei and New Zealand. The UK ranked 21st, while Estonia is Europe's top performing nation. Rankings reflect only urban air quality weighted by city population.

Under a bilateral trade deal, the United States is allowing China to export cooked poultry in exchange for China accepting U.S. beef and liquefied natural gas. Only cooked poultry is permitted, likely to reduce avian influenza transmission risks. While proper cooking eliminates viral threats, concerns remain regarding cross-contamination, salmonella, campylobacter, antibiotic residues, and heavy metals such as lead and cadmium from coal pollution, compounded by weaker enforcement of safety rules in China compared to strict U.S. standards. NVIDIA’s RTX Blackwell architecture introduces fifth-generation Tensor Cores supporting FP4, reducing AI model VRAM requirements—FLUX.dev drops from over 23GB at FP16 to under 10GB—and doubling throughput. Fourth-generation RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection throughput and add Mega Geometry, which uses Cluster-level Acceleration Structures (CLAS) and Partitioned Top-Level Acceleration Structures (PTLAS) to enable real-time ray tracing of high-detail LOD systems and high object counts across all RTX GPUs from Turing onward. Blackwell also adds hardware-accelerated Linear Swept Spheres (LSS) for strand-like geometry, offering roughly 2x the speed and 5x less VRAM than triangle-strip alternatives.

DLSS 4 leverages Blackwell’s neural rendering focus to introduce Multi Frame Generation, creating up to three additional frames per rendered frame with a 40% faster AI model using 30% less VRAM, and enhanced Flip Metering for smooth pacing. It also transitions to transformer-based AI models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, replacing CNNs to improve temporal stability, motion detail, and lighting quality. Shader Execution Reordering (SER) 2.0 doubles reorder logic efficiency, and the AI Management Processor (AMP)—a dedicated RISC-V scheduler—offloads GPU context scheduling from the CPU to reduce latency and improve multitasking.

Blackwell supports neural shaders via the Cooperative Vectors API, enabling techniques like RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression (up to 7:1 VRAM reduction), Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin (subsurface scattering), and RTX Neural Faces. Video capabilities include hardware encode/decode for 4:2:2 chroma, a ninth-generation NVENC with ~5% quality improvements for AV1/HEVC and AV1 UHQ mode, and DisplayPort 2.1b with up to 80 Gbps UHBR 20 bandwidth. Power efficiency innovations under Max-Q include advanced power gating, accelerated frequency switching (1000x faster), and low-latency sleep states (10x faster than Ada). The architecture comprises the flagship GB202 (RTX 5090, 92.2 billion transistors), high-end GB203 (RTX 5080/5070 Ti, 45.6 billion transistors), and performance-segment GB205 (RTX 5070, 31 billion transistors).

In *Clark v. Rau*, Kathrine Clark appealed pro se from a Chatham County Superior Court order granting Ricky Rau sole legal and physical custody of their three minor children and modifying child support. The majority affirmed, holding that Clark’s appellate brief failed to comply with Court of Appeals Rules 22 and 25 by omitting a statement of facts, citations to the record, and distinct enumerations of error with supporting argument. Because no transcript of the hearing was filed, the court presumed the regularity of the proceedings and assumed sufficient evidence supported the trial court’s findings. The majority further held the custody order was not facially deficient despite not explicitly reciting the “best interest of the child” standard, because neither party requested specific findings and the trial court’s finding of a material change in circumstances substantially affecting the children’s welfare essentially satisfied that standard. In dissent, Presiding Judge Barnes, joined by Presiding Judges Miller and Ellington and Judge McFadden, argued the order was facially deficient for omitting a best-interest finding. The dissent contended that Clark’s notice of appeal and brief, construed liberally under OCGA §§ 5-6-30 and 5-6-48(f), sufficiently identified the judgment and errors to authorize review, and the judgment should be vacated and remanded for application of the proper legal standard.

A bear market is mechanically defined as when the market trades below its 200-day moving average. Since 1960, the S&P 500 has spent roughly 30% of its time in such conditions, with bear markets starting on average about twice a year and lasting approximately 25 trading days. Investors often commit cognitive mistakes, such as buying high and selling low, which can cause losses even in top-performing funds. To make money in a bear market, the article recommends two steps: backtest trading strategies with strict rules across both bull and bear cycles, and trade both long and short sides. Short strategies typically become more effective during bear markets, while long strategies can also improve due to short-covering rallies. Long-term investors should continue buying to take advantage of lower prices. The key is to stick to a backtested plan, avoid emotional reactions to pessimistic news, and remain adaptable rather than holding strong bullish or bearish opinions.

The passage provides design and layout guidelines for the UC1825B-SP controller. Output diode voltage stress is calculated as Vout plus Vin(max), and the selected diode has a 60-V rating. For push-pull topologies, main switching MOSFETs require a voltage rating 2.5 to 3 times the input voltage because they see twice the input voltage plus ringing when off. The output filter uses approximately 1145 µF of capacitance and a 500 nH inductor to attenuate ripple, with a 0.5 Ω resistor to damp peaking. Type IIB compensation was chosen with a crossover frequency near 5 kHz. The sense resistor is sized using a CS pin threshold of approximately 1 V. Figures 8-6, 8-7, and 8-8 show tests conducted at 48-V input and 10-A output. The controller operates from a 10-V to 30-V input and supports push-pull, forward, half-bridge, and full-bridge topologies. Layout recommendations include using low-EMI inductors, routing feedback traces away from the inductor, placing bypass and compensation components close to the IC, keeping power traces short and thick, employing ground planes, and isolating high di/dt power ground from signal ground. The document also contains packaging information and legal disclaimers.

Strength training benefits fitness but requires correct techniques and proper warm-up and cool-down to prevent injuries. Common injuries discussed include rotator cuff injuries from repetitive overhead motions, hamstring injuries from sudden powerful movements, herniated discs from poor weightlifting movement, tendonitis from repetitive motions, and tennis or golfer's elbow from repetitive wrist and arm movements. Symptoms include pain, inflammation, numbness, tingling, and weakness. Treatments include rest, painkillers, gentle exercise, physiotherapy, and surgery depending on severity. Prevention involves good posture, regular stretching, dynamic warm-up movements, static cool-down exercises, using appropriate weights, increasing intensity gradually, not pushing through pain, and allowing recovery time. Consulting a doctor for persistent pain and a qualified fitness instructor before starting is advised.

Solid-state electrolytes (SSEs) offer a solution to lithium-ion battery limitations, but discovering novel oxide SSEs is challenging due to complex quaternary structures. To address this, the authors developed TOPIC (TOpology-constrained Prediction of Inorganic Crystals), a crystal structure prediction algorithm that generates candidate structures under oxygen-corner-sharing (CS) bond topology constraints, significantly reducing the configurational search space. TOPIC employs machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) for efficient energy evaluation during the search and validates final candidates with density functional theory (DFT). The algorithm successfully reproduced known oxide SSEs, including garnet-type LLZO, and identified a new metastable polymorph of LiTa2PO8 with enhanced conductivity. Leveraging the finding that low lithium ratios (≤1.0) favor stable CS frameworks with high ionic conductivity, the authors screened quaternary oxide compositions. They identified 92 candidate materials with potentially high ionic conductivity, 15 of which were DFT-validated to have room-temperature conductivities exceeding 0.1 mS cm⁻¹. Notable discoveries include the NASICON-type Li4Hf2Si3O12 with a predicted conductivity of 14.09 mS cm⁻¹ and several novel structural prototypes. The study establishes the Li ratio as a key descriptor and derives design principles linking Li content, framework topology, and ionic transport, offering a scalable route to explore new oxide electrolyte chemistries.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU architecture features 108 SMs and 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, delivering up to 312 TFLOPS of dense mixed-precision FP16/FP32 performance—2.5x the Tensor Core performance and 20x the standard FP32 throughput of the Tesla V100. A100 adds support for TF32, BF16, and FP64, with TF32 providing up to 8x the throughput of FP32 on A100 without code changes, and FP64 delivering 19.5 TFLOPS (2.5x V100). The architecture introduces Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity, which enforces a 2:4 pattern to double inference throughput by skipping zero computations. Memory enhancements include 192 KB/SM of combined L1/shared memory, 40 MB of L2 cache (6.7x V100), 40 GB of HBM2 DRAM with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth (1.7x V100), and Compute Data Compression. A100’s Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) capability can partition the GPU into up to seven isolated instances for quality of service and fault isolation. Third-generation NVLink offers 600 GB/sec of total bandwidth (2x V100). CUDA advances include asynchronous copy, Task Graphs, asynchronous barriers, and L2 cache residency controls. The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs via NVSwitch to deliver 5 PFLOPS of AI performance.

The David Swensen Portfolio, or Yale Model, is a diversified investment strategy developed by David Swensen, who served as Yale University’s chief investment officer from the mid-1980s until his death in 2021. From 1985 to 2020, the Yale Model generated an annualized return of 12.5%, outperforming the S&P 500’s 9.7% over the same period. Investors can implement the strategy using ETFs, though allocations can be adjusted based on individual goals and risk tolerance. A backtest using selected ETFs showed 6.23% annual returns, underperforming the S&P 500 in the tested period but with lower drawdowns. A prospective observational study of 157 patients hospitalized for acute decompensated heart failure evaluated whether bioimpedance spectroscopy (BIS) predicts clinical outcomes. BIS measured overhydration (OH) and the OH-to-extracellular water ratio (OH/ECW) at admission and discharge in subgroups with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). Over a mean follow-up of 10.7 months, 32.5% of patients experienced major adverse cardiovascular events and 28.7% were rehospitalized for heart failure. Although CKD patients had higher baseline fluid overload and HFrEF patients showed significantly greater reductions in OH/ECW with diuresis, BIS parameters did not significantly predict outcomes in any subgroup. The authors conclude that while BIS effectively monitors fluid status in acute decompensated heart failure, particularly in HFrEF, its prognostic utility in CKD and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction is limited and warrants further investigation.

The lecture introduces wireless communication, contrasting it with wired systems by focusing on fading caused by multipath propagation and Doppler effects. While a single Doppler shift can be tracked by frequency recovery, multiple paths with different relative Doppler shifts create fast multipath fading that periodically cancels the signal. Using a ray tracing model, the channel is described as a slowly time-varying linear filter characterized by attenuated and delayed impulses, where standard linear time-invariant Fourier analysis does not apply. At baseband, frequency recovery tracks the average Doppler shift, but the varying Doppler shifts between paths create a Doppler spread. This spread determines how long the channel appears time-invariant and dictates the necessary rate for channel measurements in wireless systems.

This lecture examines combinatorial bounds and algorithms for folding polygons into convex polyhedra by gluing polygon boundaries to themselves, represented by gluing trees. A valid Alexandroff gluing yields a topological sphere, has no crossings, and glues at most 360 degrees of material at any point. To avoid infinite families from rolling belts, gluings are classified by combinatorial type: an abstract gluing tree together with a specification of which polygon vertices and edges occur at tree junctions.

For general polygons with n vertices, the number of combinatorially distinct gluings has tight exponential bounds of 2^Θ(n). The upper bound arises because there are at most n+4 leaves (n vertices plus at most four fold points with 180° curvature), giving O(n) nodes, 2^O(n) possible abstract trees, 2^O(n) vertex/edge colorings at junctions, and n choices for the starting vertex. A matching exponential lower bound is shown by a spiky star polygon with convex angles near 0° and reflex angles near 360°, which yields 2^Θ(n) gluings even in the edge-to-edge case. Deciding whether any gluing exists for a general polygon currently requires exponential time, and whether a polynomial-time decision algorithm is possible remains open.

For edge-to-edge gluings—where whole edges are glued to whole edges—there is a polynomial-time algorithm to decide existence, though enumerating all gluings still requires exponential time in the worst case. For polygons of bounded sharpness, where every reflex angle is bounded away from 360° by a constant γ, each leaf of the gluing tree has curvature at least γ; because total curvature is 720°, the number of leaves is bounded by a constant (720/γ). This yields a polynomial bound on the number of gluings and a polynomial enumeration algorithm.

Algorithmically, edge-to-edge enumeration uses dynamic programming on vertex intervals, trying all matching edge pairs and combining solutions to sub-problems; this runs in exponential time, which is optimal for listing all solutions. The decision variant stores only the solution that minimizes the angle glued at each interval’s endpoints, achieving O(n³) time. For general gluings, the dynamic program handles vertex-to-edge sub-problems by tracking intervals along edges where vertices may glue; this enumeration algorithm runs in exponential time but becomes polynomial for bounded sharpness because the number of intermediate solutions is polynomial.

Examples include the Latin cross, which has exactly five edge-to-edge gluings and 85 total gluings that form 23 distinct convex polyhedra. Convex polygons such as the equilateral triangle or square admit rolling belts, producing infinitely many gluings. Finally, if all edge lengths are equal and no rolling belts exist, subdividing every edge in half converts every non-edge-to-edge gluing into an edge-to-edge gluing.

Guests must execute HLT with interrupts disabled; hosts must re-enter guests if interrupts or non-maskable events are pending at an HLT intercept, and guests must then examine interrupt state. Doorbell page configuration uses VMGEXIT SW_EXITCODE 0x8000_0014 via GHCB for GET, SET, or QUERY; the host may clear the RMP assignment, and the guest must access the mapped page with C=0 in its PTE. Hosts emulate APIC behavior by presenting the highest-priority ready interrupt in the doorbell page’s PendingEvent field, delivering #HV based on prior PendingEvent and NoFurtherSignal values, tracking NoEoiRequired, and performing EOI cycles when the guest acknowledges interrupts or clears NoEoiRequired. Guests acknowledge interrupts by atomically exchanging PendingEvent with zero, perform EOI by atomically exchanging NoEoiRequired with zero or via an APIC register write, and must validate vectors and dispatch non-maskable events even when EFLAGS.IF is clear.

Martin Braithwaite left Middlesbrough FC in January to secure regular playing time and guarantee his place in Denmark’s World Cup squad, despite signing a four-year deal six months earlier. The author argues he took the easy way out rather than fighting for his place under Tony Pulis, comparing him to teammates who persevered. With rival Viktor Fischer competing for a squad place, Braithwaite chose a more familiar environment. Meanwhile, Middlesbrough could still achieve promotion and reach the Wembley play-off final on May 26, potentially showing Braithwaite what he missed.

The passage presents various MLB headlines and reports that the Texas Rangers are focusing their managerial search on internal candidate Skip Schumaker to replace Bruce Bochy. Rangers president Chris Young stated they have a lead internal candidate and have not yet considered external options. Schumaker, a special adviser and the 2023 NL Manager of the Year with the Marlins, was hired in November. Bochy, the 70-year-old winningest active manager with 2,252 wins and a four-time World Series champion, agreed to end his three-year Texas tenure after an 81-81 season. Rangers GM Ross Fenstermaker said Schumaker has been very involved in his advisory role despite living on the West Coast, and Bochy has been offered an advisory role with the club.

ASTROCO is a conformer-style encoder for self-supervised learning on astronomical time series. It addresses limitations of pure transformer models like Astromer—their inability to capture short-lived local phenomena and regulate noisy measurements—by combining multi-head self-attention with depthwise convolutions, Gated Linear Units, and gated feed-forward networks. The model fuses photometric values, uncertainties, and sinusoidal time embeddings through learned projections, pretrains via masked reconstruction, and mixes features across all layers using trainable weights for sequence embeddings. On the MACHO R-band dataset, ASTROCO-S and ASTROCO-L achieve lower reconstruction error and higher macro-F1 scores than Astromer v1/v2, with the smaller model requiring less training time and hardware.

The passage examines the potential of large language models (LLMs) to generate novel social science theories, acknowledging concerns about originality and validity that require human-AI collaboration. It then addresses the need for evolved regulatory frameworks for generative AI, highlighting legal and ethical challenges such as misinformation, deepfakes, and bias across sectors. Rapid technological iteration complicates existing legal frameworks, while gaps between industry and government and a lack of international consensus increase compliance difficulties. Micro-level risks, including jailbreaking prompts identified by users, further impede timely regulation. The authors recommend partnerships among industry, academia, and policymakers; forward-looking governance combining top-down and bottom-up approaches; transparent mechanisms for reporting and updating regulations; and using social computing to monitor regulatory needs in specific communities.

The paper overviews twelve shared tasks organized by NFDI4DS, a German consortium that supports the research data lifecycle in Data Science and AI with a focus on FAIR principles, transparency, and reproducibility. Hosted at venues including NSLP, SDP, CLEF, SemEval, and ISWC, these tasks serve as mechanisms for community engagement and driving methodological progress. Seven completed tasks are described: software mention detection (SOMD 2025), scientific visual question answering (SciVQA), scientific fact-checking of climate change social media posts (ClimateCheck), field of research classification (FoRC2025), LLM-based automated subject tagging (LLMs4Subjects), large language models for ontology learning (LLMs4OL-2024), and scholarly question answering over linked data (Scholarly QALD). One ongoing task, CheckThat!Lab Task 4 at CLEF 2025, addresses scientific web discourse. Four future tasks are under development: detecting dataset and machine learning model mentions, converting GitHub README files to knowledge graphs (ReadMe2KG), clinical uncertainty quantification for decision support (CURED), and benchmarking algorithm generalisability (Algorithm2Domain). Collectively, these community-driven competitions contribute to building a sustainable, interoperable, and accessible national research data infrastructure.

Defensive strategies against the Triangle Offense include traditional NBA "Show and Recover" tactics and aggressive SOS disruptive approaches. Basic NBA defenses emphasize "packing it in" to deny inside shots, forcing perimeter attempts, and using four phases to deny corner cuts, defend post feeds with weakside help, show and recover on screen/rolls, and congest the weakside. SOS disruptions apply full-court pressure to block the initial flow, employing switches on post splits and contact switches on weakside screens. All Out SOS Disruption initiates first-pass wing traps to force the offense into a "free lance" mode, utilizing specific rotations—including "Triangle I," "Mid-I," "Low-I," and "Base Go" traps—for passes out of traps to corner or skip pass receivers.

This study examines the Times Higher Education World University Rankings (THE WUR) from 2015 to 2025 for the top five higher education institutions (HEIs) in ten populous Asian countries—Bangladesh, China, India, Indonesia, Japan, Pakistan, the Philippines, the Russian Federation, Thailand, and Vietnam—using a multiple case study design and document analysis. The research finds that Chinese and Japanese HEIs demonstrated the strongest positive trends, with several institutions reaching top global positions. Russian HEIs maintained stable rankings, while Indian HEIs showed overall advancement despite limited consistent top-tier presence. Conversely, HEIs in Indonesia, Pakistan, the Philippines, and Thailand exhibited neutral or declining patterns. Bangladeshi HEIs, as recent entrants, maintained neutral, low rankings, and Vietnamese HEIs displayed the most pronounced downward trend. The study concludes that most Asian HEIs lag behind global competitors and lack stable ranking profiles. It recommends diversifying international research networks, expanding funding, strengthening global marketing, and establishing overseas offices to enhance visibility and competitiveness.

The lecture discusses renormalization and summing logarithms in the effective theory, using b to s gamma as an example. One-loop calculations yield 1/epsilon^2 ultraviolet divergences, canceled by counterterms. The resulting anomalous dimension comprises a regular piece and a cusp piece proportional to log(mu/w), where w represents the hard scale (e.g., mb). The cusp term drives the leading Sudakov double logarithms when running the Wilson coefficient from the hard scale down to mu. In a theory with fixed coupling, this produces a Sudakov exponential; with a running QCD coupling, the solution becomes a more complex exponential involving ratios of alpha_s. Physically, the cusp corresponds to a kink in ultrasoft Wilson lines. When operators contain one building block per collinear direction, external kinematics fix the momentum labels, yielding simple product-form renormalization. When multiple fields share a collinear direction, some labels depend on loop momenta, leading to integral anomalous dimension equations such as the DGLAP equation. The lecture then examines Deep Inelastic Scattering in the Breit frame, identifying the incoming proton as collinear and the virtual photon interaction as hard. The relevant lowest-dimension operators involve collinear quarks or gluons with Wilson lines, and the forward proton matrix element of the quark operator corresponds to the parton distribution function. The next lecture will combine this operator with the hard Wilson coefficient to derive a factorization theorem and discuss the renormalization group evolution.

Giuriato and Lovecchio (2025) investigated whether increasing physical education hours with cognitively demanding activities improves attention in middle school students. The study included 75 participants from Classes 6 and 7, with 41 students in the experimental group and 34 in the control group. Class 6 received four hours of physical education per week, while Class 7 received two hours. The intervention incorporated cognitive-based activities such as agility drills, coordination circuits, and strategic team games. Attention was assessed using the Bells Test in October and December, measuring processing speed (bells identified in 30 seconds) and sustained attention (bells identified over 120 seconds). Results showed significant improvements in attention speed for both experimental groups, but sustained attention improved significantly only in the Class 6 experimental group. Control groups exhibited no significant changes. The authors conclude that increased physical education hours, especially with cognitively engaging activities, enhance short-term attention, though further research is needed on long-term effects and specific activity contributions.

The Rockwood School District in Missouri uses grade-level, whole-class reading instruction rather than cross-grade ability grouping. All students participate in daily phonics and comprehension lessons, followed by flexible, needs-based small groups, independent reading, and targeted interventions. The district incorporates movement-based learning and scaffolds for emerging readers while challenging advanced students with complex tasks. Citing research that low reading groups rarely catch up and ability grouping can widen gaps, the district reports that its 2024–25 kindergarteners outperformed national proficiency averages by over 17 percentage points in some areas, with first and second graders also exceeding national averages. The author argues that strong Tier I instruction and keeping students in shared classroom cohorts builds literacy and confidence without separating learners by ability.

The passage describes methods, data processing systems, and hardware for configuring an activation module in a Deep Neural Network (DNN) implementation using a programmable lookup table (LUT). The method involves providing calibration data to a representation of the hardware, monitoring inputs to an activation module in that representation to determine a range of input values, generating lookup data approximating the activation function over that determined range, and loading the lookup data into the hardware LUT. During operation, the activation module performs the activation function over the determined range using the LUT. For multiple activation functions, the process may be repeated, and the LUT may switch between two data sets to allow concurrent loading of a next function while performing a current one. Input values outside the determined range may be clamped to the closest extreme value. An offset may be subtracted from inputs to center the range about a predefined value. The activation module may estimate outputs by interpolating between adjacent LUT entries, using the most significant bits as a lookup address and the remaining bits for interpolation. The LUT may comprise two data stores holding alternating adjacent points for simultaneous lookup. The range may be determined from maximum and minimum observed values or from a histogram of input value probabilities. The determined range may be less than the full possible input range, with the number of generated entries equal to the LUT size. A data processing system includes a configuration module, which may be software, to perform the monitoring and lookup data generation. The hardware may also include a Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU) that can bypass the LUT, and may clamp out-of-range values before LUT lookup. The passage further describes integrated circuit manufacturing methods, computer-readable storage media, and integrated circuit definition datasets for producing such hardware.

China announced it will shut down its domestic ivory market by the end of 2017. This review article synthesizes literature on higher education quality, covering studies on online teaching service quality during the COVID-19 pandemic, leadership spirituality, resistance to change, e-learning factors and gender differences, quality assurance frameworks, and the roles of rankings, accreditation, virtual universities, artificial intelligence, and institutional support. High-dosage tutoring, such as Teach For America’s Ignite Fellowship, accelerates student learning and builds confidence when it includes structured training, coaching, and relational support rather than relying on technology alone. Research indicates that tutoring nearly triples the likelihood of fellows applying to teaching programs, particularly among men, people of color, and non-education majors, with hundreds of tutors transitioning into classrooms. The author argues that tutoring should be treated as a core, funded instructional strategy and teacher pipeline rather than merely a temporary academic intervention.

Platinum futures are standardized, physically delivered CME Globex contracts representing 50 troy ounces of platinum, offering exposure to a rare and volatile metal used in jewelry, automotive catalytic converters, and other industries. A platinum futures strategy employs technical and fundamental analysis, backtesting, and risk management to speculate, hedge, or diversify a portfolio. The passage presents backtests of a monthly long/short strategy (473 trades, 64% win rate, 0.57% average gain, profit factor 1.7) and a seasonal strategy (60 trades, 75% win rate, 0.66% average gain, profit factor 2.3), noting both are largely uncorrelated to the stock market. Platinum prices are driven by supply and demand, industrial and jewelry demand, seasonality, and geopolitical conditions in major producing nations such as South Africa and Russia. Trading occurs nearly around the clock, and market access is available through futures brokers, CFDs, or ETFs. Key strategy considerations include positive statistical expectancy, diversification benefits, trading costs, and the inherent difficulty of commodity trading, which lacks a natural edge and is susceptible to erratic news.

Biosecurity screening software monitors DNA orders for hazardous proteins, but AI can tweak known toxins to evade detection. A study found that software patches improved screening programs' ability to flag AI-designed harmful proteins, though about 3 percent of variants still slipped through. This study introduces GeoSQL-Eval, the first end-to-end automated evaluation framework for Large Language Model (LLM) generation of PostGIS GeoSQL queries, and GeoSQL-Bench, a corresponding benchmark dataset. Addressing the inadequacy of existing NL2SQL and geospatial benchmarks for spatial database contexts, the framework systematically evaluates LLM performance across five capability levels—conceptual understanding, structured SQL generation, semantic alignment and invocation, execution and result accuracy, and robust generalization and reasoning—using metrics including execution pass rate, syntax accuracy, schema hit rates, argument matching accuracy, and entropy-weighted rankings.

GeoSQL-Bench contains 14,178 tasks in three categories: 2,380 multiple-choice and true/false questions on PostGIS function knowledge; 3,744 syntax-level SQL generation questions; and 2,155 table schema retrieval questions spanning 82 databases across eight themes derived from UN-GGIM and ISO 19115 standards. Data construction employed GPT-4o-assisted generation with expert review.

The evaluation of 24 models across six categories found that general reasoning-enhanced models (particularly GPT-5, o4-mini, and DeepSeek-R1-0528) and general non-reasoning models achieved the highest overall performance. However, semantic alignment and table schema retrieval remained significant bottlenecks, with syntax accuracy substantially exceeding execution pass rates. PostGIS function errors and SQL syntax errors constituted approximately 70% of total errors. The study also publicly released the GeoSQL-Eval leaderboard platform for ongoing model assessment.

Nearly two decades after Hurricane Katrina devastated New Orleans' Lower Ninth Ward, many residents remain displaced due to lack of funds and gentrification, leaving abandoned homes and empty lots. The city and state have since implemented extensive climate adaptation measures. New Orleans has built evacuation centers, raised homes, and promoted rain gardens and solar power. The Greater New Orleans Urban Water Plan emphasizes "living with water" through green and blue infrastructure like the Mirabeau Water Garden rather than relying solely on pumping. Louisiana's 2017 Coastal Master Plan outlines $50 billion in projects to restore wetlands, build levees and flood gates, and relocate some residents. Scientists note that oil and gas extraction has accelerated coastal subsidence, while rising sea levels now pose an increasing threat to the region's extensive oil infrastructure. Researchers say Louisiana's experiences offer valuable lessons for coastal cities worldwide.

The cup and handle pattern is a bullish continuation formation on a price chart that resembles a U-shaped cup followed by a smaller handle, which is a trading range or slight downward drift on the right side. It forms after a price rally, signaling a consolidation period before an upward breakout to continue the trend; an inverted version signals continuation in a downtrend. Popularized by William O’Neil in 1988 as part of the CANSLIM method, the pattern typically sees decreasing volume during the cup and handle formation, with a significant increase in volume confirming a breakout above the handle’s resistance. Key criteria include formation within an existing trend, a rounded cup bottom, and a handle that does not dip below the halfway point of the cup’s depth. The pattern can develop over several months to more than a year. Traders often place stop-loss orders below the handle’s lowest point or the cup’s bottom and project profit targets by measuring the cup’s depth from the breakout point. Backtesting is difficult due to discretionary variables; referenced studies show mixed results, with one S&P 500 test from 2016–2018 underperforming the index, while another manual study found a 26% failure rate and a 38% average gain. High market volatility can distort the pattern and reduce reliability, whereas low to moderate volatility produces clearer formations. Common mistakes include entering before the pattern completes, ignoring volume, setting inaccurate profit targets or stop-losses, and neglecting broader market conditions. The pattern reflects a psychological shift from pessimism and fear to optimism, shaking out weak holders before a potential advance, and is most effective when used alongside other technical indicators and fundamental analysis.

Higher-order Feynman diagram corrections, such as self-energy loops, produce integrals that diverge to infinity, which historically prevented reliable calculations. Introducing a cutoff scale makes the theory sensible, though an infinite contribution remains. Through renormalization, these infinities are absorbed into bare masses and couplings. Because experiments are conducted at specific energy scales, theoretical predictions remain meaningful. The electromagnetic, weak, and strong coupling constants run with energy and do not converge naturally at high scales. Introducing new particles could change this running behavior, potentially allowing unification at a single scale. Physical masses and couplings are therefore evaluated at specific scales.

Federal funding cuts and threats to higher education are now challenging the city’s competitive edge.

The lecture discusses the induced graph removal lemma: if an n-vertex graph has few induced copies of a fixed graph H, it can be made induced H-free by adding or deleting fewer than epsilon n^2 edges. Because the standard Szemerédi regularity lemma leaves irregular pairs that obstruct the proof when both edges and non-edges must be controlled, the lecturer introduces the strong regularity lemma. This produces a pair of partitions P and Q, with Q refining P, such that P is epsilon_0-regular, Q is extremely regular (epsilon_{|P|}-regular), and their energies differ by less than epsilon_0. A corollary gives an equitable partition into parts V_i containing large subsets W_i such that every pair (W_i, W_j) is regular and the edge densities between most V_i and V_j closely match those between the corresponding W_i and W_j. Using this corollary, the induced removal lemma is proved by partitioning, cleaning (adding or removing edges between V_i based on W_i densities), and counting: any surviving induced copy of H would yield many original copies, contradicting the sparsity hypothesis. The lecture further states the infinite removal lemma, which extends this to infinite families of forbidden patterns and requires the regularity parameter to depend on the number of parts. Finally, the results imply in property testing that every hereditary graph property is testable with a one-sided error oblivious tester.

Dollar-cost averaging involves investing fixed amounts at regular intervals to smooth volatility, while lump sum investing deploys a large amount immediately. The article backtests a lump sum buy and hold strategy using a diversified portfolio of five asset classes, such as U.S. stocks, foreign stocks, bonds, REITs, and commodities. It concludes that historically, lump sum investing offers a higher probability of success over long-term horizons, preferably at least ten years, with earlier start times yielding greater average returns, and that the impact of financial crises becomes insignificant over time.

NeoWorld is a deep learning framework that generates an infinite, interactive virtual world from a single image by progressively unfolding 2D object-centric representations into 3D as users explore or issue natural language commands. It employs a hybrid scene structure combining lightweight 2.5D Gaussian layer backgrounds with full 3D foreground objects to balance computational efficiency and immersive realism. The system uses panoptic segmentation and a compact codebook-based embedding for object-centric attribute binding, followed by an image-to-3D module with coarse-to-fine alignment to convert relevant objects to 3D. A large language model interprets user prompts for object selection and manipulation, enabling physics-based animation. Experiments demonstrate that NeoWorld outperforms prior 2D, 2.5D, and video diffusion baselines in 3D consistency, scene quality, object-centric segmentation accuracy, and text-guided dynamic interaction, while maintaining efficient rendering. As a cascade of pre-trained modules, its robustness is limited by potential error propagation from alignment failures, LLM misinterpretation, reconstruction errors, and segmentation inaccuracies.

News articles from June 2001 detail California's energy crisis, including soaring wholesale electricity and natural gas prices, accusations of market manipulation by companies such as Enron, and the failure of the state's 1996 deregulation plan. Federal regulators introduced a price-mitigation plan, while a California Senate committee approved subpoenas for eight out-of-state power generators—including Enron—demanding documents on bidding and pricing. A PBS "Frontline" documentary, "Blackout," examined the crisis and Enron's role as a major trader. Internationally, lenders met in Singapore to salvage Enron's $2.9 billion Dabhol power project in India amid tariff disputes with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board, while USX-Marathon replaced Enron in a $25 billion Saudi natural-gas venture. In October 1944, American, British, and Chinese representatives discussed dissolving the League of Nations. The League’s Supervisory Committee moved to form a Conciliation Committee on dissolution and transfer, requesting United States consultation; officials made no commitment, recommending no United States initiative and leaving the matter for the United Nations Conference. At a January 31, 1945 meeting on Dumbarton Oaks Proposals, Chilean Ambassador requested correction of December 29, 1944 minutes on “assuring respect for international treaties” in Chapter I, recalling it was essential with only placement in question; Mora asked his remarks be recorded.

Tuberculosis (TB) caused an estimated 1.4 million deaths in 2019 and 1.6 million in 2021, with COVID-19 reducing diagnoses and access to treatment. Extrapulmonary TB (EPTB), including lymph node and pleural TB, comprises about 16% of cases but is less studied than pulmonary TB. Standard therapy uses rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol.

The authors present a whole-body physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model that, for the first time, includes pleural and lymph node compartments and simulates all four first-line drugs at extrapulmonary sites. Using ordinary differential equations, tissue:plasma partition coefficients, and pharmacokinetic parameters calibrated against clinical plasma and lung data, the model predicts tissue concentrations relative to WHO critical concentrations.

Results show rifampicin and isoniazid generally exceed critical concentrations in most tissues, though the model over-predicts rifampicin in pleural fluid. Ethambutol falls below critical concentrations in brain, kidney, bone, and skin. Pyrazinamide fails to reach critical concentrations in any organ. The model does not account for drug-drug interactions or rifampicin autoinduction, but provides a foundation for evaluating and optimizing EPTB treatment.

Microsoft Corporation filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2017. For the three months ended September 30, 2017, total revenue was $24.5 billion, operating income was $7.7 billion, net income was $6.6 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $0.84. The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition system with a built-in analog front-end. Each analog input features internal clamp protection allowing swings up to ±18V, a programmable gain amplifier supporting single-ended and differential bipolar inputs with independently configurable ranges and antialiasing low-pass filter bandwidths, and a wide-common-mode rejection circuit supporting up to ±12V. The device outputs 20-bit conversion data in straight-binary or two’s-complement format via a source-synchronous interface configurable for 2-lane or 4-lane SDR and DDR operation; the 20-bit result is output MSB-first in a 24-bit packet. A free-running sampling clock is required, and the SMPL_SYNC signal synchronizes multiple devices. The ADS9803 includes an internal precision voltage reference, which can be disabled for an external reference, and provides a data output randomizer, simple and moving data averaging modes to improve SNR, and fixed-pattern, digital-ramp, and alternating test patterns for interface debugging. A speed-boost mode enables up to 8MSPS on a selected channel pair. Configuration and readback use a three-bank SPI interface that supports daisy-chain topology. The device requires a specific register initialization sequence after power-up or reset, and supports reset and power-down via hardware pins or register writes. For ATE applications, the device achieves a post-calibration total unadjusted error of 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C and offers a wide-bandwidth mode for fast settling with external multiplexers. It operates from AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD supplies with no required power-up sequence; layout guidelines recommend isolating analog and digital signals and placing bypass capacitors close to supply and reference pins.

Researchers established the K-T collaborative EVT registry by harmonizing data from South Korea’s CRCS-K (7,835 patients) and Taiwan’s TREAT-AIS (2,106 patients), creating a unified dataset of 9,941 patients to study endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) outcomes in East Asian populations. Baseline comparisons showed Taiwanese patients were older, had more vascular risk factors and more severe strokes, exhibited less pre-stroke functional independence, and experienced longer treatment timelines than Korean patients. Successful recanalization and symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage rates were similar between cohorts, but Taiwanese patients had lower 90-day functional independence while Korean patients had higher 90-day mortality. Analysis of age effects revealed that patients aged 80 and older (24.9% of the registry) experienced significantly lower rates of favorable functional outcomes and higher mortality compared with younger patients, although symptomatic hemorrhage risk did not differ by age. Age showed a nonlinear relationship with functional recovery and mortality, most pronounced between ages 75 and 85. Multivariable analysis identified pre-stroke functional independence, baseline stroke severity, and bridging thrombolysis as key predictors of outcomes across age groups. The study concludes that while advanced age is associated with poorer EVT outcomes, carefully selected elderly patients—including those with pre-stroke independence who receive bridging therapy—can still achieve meaningful benefits, supporting individualized treatment approaches rather than age-based exclusion.

Federal Reserve raised the federal funds rate by 0.25 points to 1 to 1.25 percent, the second increase within half a year and third since Janet Yellen ended the post-2007 flatline. Rates remained at 0.25 percent for seven years until December 2015.
