The lecture defines Probabilistically Checkable Proofs (PCPs) and constructs them from the GKR protocol for any NP language (specifically 3SAT), achieving completeness 1, soundness 1/2, and polylog n query and randomness complexity. A PCP is an oracle string where a verifier uses r bits of randomness to make q non-adaptive queries; it accepts valid instances with probability at least c and rejects invalid ones with probability at most s regardless of the proof.

In the construction, the prover computes low-degree extensions of the witness and each circuit layer. The PCP contains all possible sumcheck transcripts for every layer i, every evaluation point z, and every partial randomness sequence. Parameters are engineered so H^m equals the circuit size s and the field F is polylog s, ensuring the PCP remains polynomial in size despite the large randomness. The verifier simulates the GKR protocol by querying these transcripts and checking consistency across layers. Soundness follows from the sumcheck protocol and a union bound over 2d sumchecks, requiring F to be sufficiently large. Because the verifier lacks the witness, a low-degree test is required for the input layer extension. This yields an efficient PCP verifiable with only polylog n queries.

This study investigates the impact of mydriasis on image gradability and artificial intelligence performance for diabetic retinopathy screening using portable fundus cameras. Paired non-mydriatic and mydriatic images from 327 patients were captured with the Phelcom Eyer device and graded by masked ophthalmologists; a ResNet-200d model trained on the mBRSET dataset classified images as normal or diabetic retinopathy. Mydriatic images showed significantly higher gradability (82.1%) than non-mydriatic images (55.6%; p<0.001). In the non-mydriatic group, systemic hypertension, older age, longer diabetes duration, male gender, and Indigenous race were significantly associated with lower image quality. The model achieved higher accuracy (82.91% versus 79.23%), F1 score (0.83 versus 0.79), and area under the curve (0.94 versus 0.93) in the mydriatic group, with fewer false positives, though the difference between groups was not statistically significant (p=0.3279). The authors conclude that while mydriasis improves image quality and may reduce unnecessary referrals, non-mydriatic imaging remains pragmatic where dilation is unavailable. They note limitations including a single camera model, paired-image selection bias, and non-specialized operators, and recommend future research to optimize artificial intelligence for non-mydriatic images and validate results across broader datasets.

Former president Robert Mugabe returned from Singapore to face allegations over the June 24 Bulawayo bomb blast that killed two and injured over 40, including Vice President Kembo Mohadi. Emmerson Mnangagwa’s government accuses Mugabe’s Generation 40 (G40) allies of involvement, with Mnangagwa telling the BBC he has a "hunch" Grace Mugabe’s faction was responsible. A family source said the Mugabes were unperturbed, returning from Dubai. Tensions escalate ahead of July 30 polls, as Mugabe opposes Mnangagwa’s government and has warmed to the MDC Alliance. Mugabe’s nephew Patrick Zhuwao warned Prime Minister Theresa May that Mnangagwa could use the blast to target enemies without evidence, while G40’s Jonathan Moyo criticized the claims.

Sherwin Gatchalian urged the Department of Education to address delays in teachers' performance-based bonuses persisting since 2012-2013. Teachers await 2016-2017 bonuses; Mateo blamed failed biddings and clearance delays, while Teachers' Dignity Coalition said funds were allocated in fiscal year 2016.

Image registration, which optimizes a coordinate transform to align a moving image to a fixed image, is limited by memory and compute at ultra-high resolutions. This paper proposes IO-aware fused kernels and Flash Fused Distributed Primitives (FFDP) to scale registration to arbitrarily large problems. A composite implicit grid sampler, implicit Parzen windowing for mutual information, and a fused localized normalized cross-correlation kernel reduce single-GPU memory overhead from O(N) to O(1) for key operations. The distributed framework introduces Grid Parallel sharding with boundary synchronization, a ring sampler that avoids materializing the full moving image, and distributed loss functions. The authors register a 250 µm in-vivo MRI to a 100 µm ex-vivo human brain volume—over 570× larger than standard clinical data with 11.8 billion parameters—in about one minute on eight GPUs. Experiments demonstrate that FFDP accelerates traditional registration pipelines by up to 7.48× and deep learning pipelines by up to 6.14× while reducing memory usage, and achieves higher accuracy and efficiency than state-of-the-art methods at 250 µm resolution.

Sergey A. Yablonsky's paper develops a multidimensional data-driven Artificial Intelligence (AI) innovation framework examining the relationship between AI, Big Data (BD), and Advanced Analytics (AA). The study addresses the need for enterprises to digitally transform through AI-driven strategies and proposes a taxonomy to classify AI/BD/AA dimensions. Using a methodology combining literature review and semi-structured expert interviews guided by Nickerson et al.'s approach, the research identifies seven overlapping business platform areas infused by data and analytics: Information Systems, Customer Experience, Data and Analytics, IoT, Ecosystems, Trust, and Integration platforms. The paper introduces an AI/BD/AA micro-level value chain comprising four key activities: AI Awareness/Big Data Acquisition, Measurement of AI/Big Data Curation, AI Reporting and Interpretation/Big Data Storage, and AI Decision making/Big Data Usage. It presents a five-level maturity framework for AI enterprise innovation: Human Led/Initial Analytics; Human Led, Machine Supported/Advanced Analytics I; Machine Led, Human Supported/Advanced Analytics II; Machine Led, Human Governed/Advanced Analytics III; and Machine Controlled/Advanced Analytics IV. Each maturity level corresponds to specific stages of the AI/BD/AA value chain. The framework aims to help organizations evaluate human-machine relationships, assess automation scope, and make strategic investment decisions regarding AI-based transformation across industries.

In *Bryson v. The State* (A06A1344, 638 SE2d 181), the court affirmed Robert Pearl Bryson’s convictions for two counts of aggravated sodomy, four counts of aggravated child molestation, one count of child molestation, and two counts of failure to register as a sex offender. On appeal, Bryson claimed insufficient evidence for the sodomy, molestation, and failure-to-register counts; erroneous denial of motions to quash and to sever; improper denial of his trial counsel’s motion to withdraw; erroneous admission of a no contest plea; and ineffective assistance of counsel. The court held that victim testimony was sufficient for the sex-crime convictions and that Bryson’s flight from Georgia without reporting his change of residence supported the failure-to-register conviction. It found the motions to quash untimely or meritless, held that severance was unnecessary because the charges were connected, and ruled that the trial court did not abuse its discretion in denying counsel’s withdrawal. The no contest plea was properly admitted to show a prior conviction for registration purposes. Finally, the court concluded Bryson knowingly waived his ineffective assistance claim by declining to raise it at his motion for new trial hearing. Count 9 was merged into Count 8 for sentencing.

The Supreme Court of Mississippi affirmed Ulysses S. Gandy’s second manslaughter conviction and ten-year sentence for a 1976 two-car collision that killed three people. After his first conviction was reversed and remanded, a new jury again found him guilty. Gandy argued the verdict was against the overwhelming weight of evidence, the court improperly refused a jury instruction on intoxication factors, wrongly admitted sketches of the accident scene, and erred by not giving the jury a recess during deliberations. The court held that conflicting testimony about Gandy’s intoxication and the vehicles’ positions was for the jury to resolve, and sufficient evidence supported that he was intoxicated and drove into the wrong lane, constituting culpable negligence. It found no reversible error in refusing the instruction because other instructions adequately covered the issue. It ruled the sketches were properly admitted as demonstrative evidence illustrating witnesses’ personal observations. It also rejected the recess claim. The judgment was affirmed.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K with a report date of February 2, 2015, stating it entered into an underwriting agreement with Goldman, Sachs & Co. and Deutsche Bank Securities Inc. for five series of notes: $500 million floating rate notes due 2020, $1.25 billion 1.55% notes due 2020, $1.25 billion 2.15% notes due 2022, $1.5 billion 2.50% notes due 2025, and $2 billion 3.45% notes due 2045. The notes are senior unsecured obligations to be issued under an April 29, 2013 indenture and a February 9, 2015 officer’s certificate, with quarterly interest on the floating rate notes and semi-annual interest on the fixed rate notes.
GBMC neonatologist Dr. Maria Pane cares for the "sickest and tiniest patients," involves parents in rounds, looks forward to the Father's Day 5K NICU fundraiser, and values team input.

Researchers developed a meta-population SIR model to assess how Google Community Mobility Reports (GCMR) explain SARS-CoV-2 transmission dynamics, applying it to regions in Norway, Sweden (February 2020–July 2021), and Germany (Bavaria and Berlin, February–December 2020). The model linked four GCMR settings—retail and recreation, grocery and pharmacy, transit stations, and workplaces—to contact frequencies with additive effects, while temperature (as a seasonality proxy) and virus variants (Alpha, Delta) had multiplicative effects on transmissibility. Fitted to weekly hospitalization data, the model attributed 60.0% of infections to the four GCMR settings in Sweden, 38.7% in Norway, and approximately 65% in the German regions, with the remainder captured by weekly region-specific random effects. In Norway and Sweden, transit stations and workplaces contributed most to baseline transmission, whereas retail and recreation was dominant in Germany. A 20°C temperature increase was associated with roughly a 40% reduction in transmissibility, while the Delta variant approximately doubled transmissibility compared to the wildtype; Alpha showed around a 20% increase in Norway. The authors conclude that GCMR data are clearly associated with infection dynamics but note limitations in linearity assumptions and measurement accuracy, suggesting more direct contact frequency data would improve future real-time assessment.

News articles from July 9–10, 2001, report that California energy crisis records show diverse suppliers—including Canadian and public utilities—charged higher average prices than the Texas firms Governor Davis criticized, though Davis' office cited long-term profits by out-of-state generators. The state spent nearly $8 billion on power in early 2001, with average prices falling from $316/MWh in January to $243 in May. Settlement talks over California's $8.9 billion refund demand ended without agreement; a judge will propose a plan for hundreds of millions. Duke Energy refused to publicly release bidding data sought by a Senate committee, while California's attorney general was cleared to share subpoenaed documents from Reliant, Mirant, and Dynegy with Oregon and Washington. Enron expects to meet Q2 earnings targets of 42 cents per share. Enron's Dabhol Power CEO Neil McGregor resigned after his contract expired amid a seven-month payment dispute with India's Maharashtra State Electricity Board, which owes $48 million and stopped purchasing power. Chairman Kenneth Lay confirmed the resignation and said resolving the $2.9 billion project requires more work; Phase II construction is halted. Lay stated Enron has no immediate plan to quit India, discussed options including a possible sale, and sought help from the Confederation of Indian Industry, though India's government rejected a central utility buy-out. Despite a 43 percent year-to-date stock drop, analysts rate Enron a "buy," citing strong core trading growth. Separately, Enron Broadband Services was revealed as a key investor in Tropic Networks' $60 million financing.

Grief is a unique, highly personal emotional reaction to the loss of someone or something cared about, whether through death or significant life changes such as becoming a carer, declining health, retirement, or moving home. It can cross generations and may occur anticipatorily before an impending loss, such as a terminal illness. The grieving process is not linear; people may experience emotions including numbness, denial, relief, yearning, guilt, anger, restlessness, disturbed sleep, loss of confidence, and profound sadness. There is no right or wrong way to grieve, and the intensity and duration depend on individual factors. While the person who died will always be missed, the intense period of grief does not last forever, and eventually good days typically outnumber bad days. Those struggling should speak to friends, family, or a GP, and various organisations offer bereavement support.

The speaker accepts the nomination for the Presidency, thanking Texas and Dallas and citing a first grader’s description of presidential duties. He contrasts his party’s vision of hope, confidence, and growth with the opposition’s record of pessimism, fear, and limits, noting that under their policies inflation, interest rates, taxes, and poverty rose, while his administration reduced federal spending growth, cut taxes, created six and a half million jobs, lowered inflation, and strengthened the military. He cites repaired alliances, the mission in Grenada, and asks the Soviets to return to nuclear arms reduction negotiations. He criticizes the opposition for blocking a balanced budget amendment, Presidential line-item veto authority, an anticrime bill, tuition tax credits, and enterprise zones. He recounts the Olympic torch relay across the United States and the replacement of the Statue of Liberty’s torch, linking them to American unity and the nation’s future. He affirms a commitment to individual freedom, limited government, and continued prosperity.

Researchers led by Vanderbilt University have advanced hyperlensing by improving hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) crystal quality through isotopic purification of boron, as reported in Nature Materials. The purified crystals reduce optical losses and triple polariton lifetime, enhancing imaging resolution by approximately tenfold. In principle, lenses made from this material could resolve objects as small as 30 nanometers—the scale of small viruses—while using low-energy infrared light that does not harm living cells. Unlike electron and atomic-force microscopes, hyperlenses can image living organisms in their natural environments and provide spectroscopic data. The technology could impact biological, medical, communications, and nanoscale optical fields, and researchers believe further improvements are possible with larger crystals.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition system with a built-in analog front-end. It features simple and moving data averaging to improve SNR; simple averaging reduces the output data rate by a factor of 2, while moving average does not affect it. The device supports fixed, digital ramp, and alternating test patterns for debugging, enabled via registers 0x13 through 0x1B in bank 1 for channel groups CH[4:1] and CH[8:5]. Reset or power-down can be triggered via the RESET or PWDN pins, or through corresponding register writes in bank 0 and bank 1; following reset or power-up, registers initialize to default values and require an initialization sequence with a free-running sampling clock. Speed-boost mode allows up to 8MSPS for a user-selected channel pair while the remaining six channels idle. The 16-bit configuration registers are organized in three banks and accessed via SPI; register bank 0 is always accessible, while banks 1 and 2 are selected using REG_BANK_SEL. Multiple devices support daisy-chain topology, configured by the DAISY_CHAIN_LEN register and requiring N × 24 SCLKs for register writes. Register functions include data format, test pattern selection, averaging, speed-boost, analog input bandwidth, power-down, output lane configuration, common-mode range, and gain error correction. For ATE applications, the device achieves a post-calibration TUE of 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C and provides low-noise (22.7kHz) and wide-bandwidth (700kHz) modes, with wide-bandwidth settling to 99.95% full scale in 7.5µs. The ADS9803 operates from AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD supplies with no required power-up sequence, and layout recommendations include isolating analog signals from digital noise and placing bypass capacitors close to supply and reference pins.

Beating the offside trap requires attackers to recognize when defenders advance to create offside positions, adjust to remain onside, and use the space behind the defense. Recognition comes from scouting or noticing frequent offside calls. Players must be patient, avoid running offside, and not interfere if forced into an offside position. Tactics include dribbling through without passing, timed through passes, horizontal or lateral runs, checking runs, short passes, deep-lying vertical runs, bending runs back toward the halfway line, back-passes, delaying via possession, delayed runs, and using a designated “non-runner” on free kicks. Fakes before free kicks may expose the trap. If a defender fails to move up, attackers should immediately capitalize, often resulting in a one-on-one with the goalkeeper. Success may discourage the opponent from using the trap again.

The Patriots had one of their worst offensive performances against the Miami Dolphins but trailed by seven in the final minute until Stephen Gostkowski's half-hearted onside kick, which the Dolphins recovered to win.

Roma are reportedly keen on signing out-of-favour Manchester United winger Januzaj as a cut-price replacement for Mohamed Salah in talks to join Liverpool after a disappointing Sunderland year.

Ocean acidification from absorbed CO2 damages calcifying organisms, but researchers found periwinkles can adapt by producing less-dense, less-soluble shells, suggesting some calcifying organisms could adapt to future acidic conditions.

EUR/USD climbs to 1.1840, advancing a fourth session after U.S. inflation data triggered a dollar pullback. Investors await ECB and FOMC minutes on QE tapering and balance sheet reduction. Resistance at 1.1846, support at 1.1722.

Jack Hough of Barron's suggests Netflix stock could lose more than half its value, citing Disney and Facebook's upcoming streaming services, Amazon Prime competition, cash burn, and accounting tactics. The author counters that competition fears are overblown, noting Netflix quadrupled subscribers despite Amazon Prime Video and YouTube. Netflix has raised prices multiple times without losing customers, demonstrating pricing flexibility. With 104 million streaming accounts and growing, its scale creates a moat through cost distribution and appeal to content creators. The author concludes that Netflix has historically surpassed bearish predictions and betting against it is risky.

A study in Pediatrics found that from 1990 to 2015, nearly 17,000 children under 6 were treated in emergency rooms for window blind injuries, averaging nearly one death monthly and two injuries daily. While most injuries were minor, entanglement in blind cords—accounting for under 12% of cases—caused nearly 80% of hospitalizations and over 94% of deaths. Researchers and safety advocates say voluntary standards are insufficient and call for mandatory rules requiring cordless or inaccessible-cord blinds. The Window Covering Manufacturers Association proposed requiring stock products to be cordless by late 2018, while custom blinds could still have cords. The CPSC recommends cordless window coverings in homes with children.

Ryan Kerr, 26, of Evercreech, was remanded in custody at Taunton Crown Court after admitting assaults including punching a woman and leaving a man unconscious in a pub. He showed no remorse, telling a probation worker one victim deserved it, and will be sentenced on October 13.

Pan Finance covers global financial and economic news, including: China blacklisting Canadian firm TechInsights for analyzing Huawei’s AI chips and banning Chinese collaboration after it reported Huawei used international components; the EU challenging Italy over bank mergers and pushing climate reform for development banks; the Bank of England warning of AI bubble risks; Fifth Third acquiring Comerica for $10.9 billion; gold surging above $4,000; Turkey securing a €974 million highway loan; the U.S. freezing $18 billion in New York City infrastructure funds; Germany probing Temu; and the IRS raising 2026 tax brackets.

Shannon Bard announced that Zapoteca, the Portland restaurant she and her husband owned, has closed permanently. The Bards, who opened it six years ago, cited changing priorities as their children reach college. They still operate Toroso, Salud, a cooking school and catering company.

Peterborough City Council leader John Holdich reported pledging £4 million for homeless families and bringing 179 long-term empty homes back into use in the past year, and 663 over five years. He noted government grants have been cut by 80% from £55 million to £10 million over eight years, urged residents to respond to Phase Two budget consultation, and promoted the Stand Up For Peterborough campaign against future funding cuts. He stated that two Public Space Protection Orders introduced six months ago have reduced anti-social behaviour, including littering and unauthorised cycling. He also announced the launch of CHUMS, a new mental health service for children and young people with mild-moderate issues.
People v. Roldán (No. 2032), decided June 26, 1923, reversed the judgment and acquitted the defendant per case No. 2037. Three justices concurred; Wolf took no part.

Jeff Horn will defend his WBO welterweight title against Gary Corcoran in Brisbane. A win could lead to a 2018 bout with Terence Crawford, while a loss risks obscurity. Horn aims to dispel notions of a hometown decision in his win over Manny Pacquiao. Promoter Bob Arum said victory secures major fights next year, with Crawford as mandatory. Corcoran, a 17-1 underdog ranked 10th by the WBO, is fighting outside Britain and Ireland for the first time. The buildup featured Corcoran's camp accusing Horn of head-butting Pacquiao, and Corcoran claiming he would bite if confronted similarly, prompting taunts between trainers.

The NAAIM Exposure Index, compiled by the National Association of Active Investment Managers, measures average US Equity market exposure based on weekly member surveys of firms' equity exposure as of each Wednesday. The indicator line is a two-week moving average of responses. It estimates investor sentiment, with high readings suggesting bullishness and low readings suggesting bearishness, potentially serving as a contrarian indicator. However, the index is not predictive and offers limited value for forecasting future movements, providing insight only into managers' past two weeks of adjustments. Backtests showed poor performance as a trading strategy, with better contrarian indicators such as the VIX available. Investing when weekly readings fell below the 10-week moving average yielded a 4.4% CAGR versus 2.5% when above, though varying periods and extreme readings did not significantly improve results.

Lubrizol Corp. will invest US$80 million to expand TPU production in North America, Europe, and Asia. North America will add capacity this year. Songjiang, China inaugurated new lines, with further Asian investment in 2019. Europe will extend capabilities for elastomers, aliphatics, and adhesives, with a major expansion in 2019.

Facebook released a detailed 8,000-word public rule book outlining its community standards for permitted posts, covering topics including drug use, bullying, hate speech, and violence, to increase transparency. Users may now appeal individual content removals, and Facebook will provide more specific reasons for takedowns. The company employs 7,500 moderators and automated software to enforce rules, which are reviewed biweekly at internal forums and updated based on feedback from outside experts. The document prohibits content such as videos of cannibalism wounds, admissions of non-medical drug use, cursing at minors, and hacked material except in limited newsworthy cases. Government requests to remove content violating local laws are reviewed separately by legal teams and blocked only in the requesting country. The standards do not address false information or personal data use.

This study used EEG during median nerve electrical stimulation to compare neural noise in 19 adults with Tourette syndrome (TS) and 19 matched controls, operationalizing neural noise as trial-by-trial response variability. While early and mid-latency somatosensory evoked potential (SEP) components showed no group differences in amplitude, timing, or topography, the P100 (P2) component was significantly increased in TS and positively associated with tic impairment. Trial-by-trial variability was substantially higher in the TS group at rest but normalized following stimulation. The TS group also exhibited flatter 1/f power spectral density slopes at high-beta and gamma frequencies, consistent with increased neural noise. Inter-trial phase coherence increased after stimulation in both groups, though the TS group showed a shallower initial rise. These findings indicate that sensorimotor neural recruitment is less stable at rest in TS, likely due to abnormal subcortical activity, but stabilizes with stimulation, alongside altered central somatosensory processing.

A federal jury cleared retired Little Rock police lieutenant David Hudson of accusations that he used excessive force in punching Jon "Chris" Erwin seven times outside a Little Rock restaurant in October 2011. The incident, captured on video, fueled national debate about police force. After two days of testimony, jurors unanimously decided Hudson's actions were reasonable from his perspective. Erwin sustained facial injuries and sought medical treatment, though no medical evidence supported his attorney's suggestion of post-traumatic stress disorder. Misdemeanor charges against Erwin were previously dropped for procedural reasons. The city and restaurant had settled Erwin's claims before trial, meaning Hudson would have personally paid any damages. Hudson testified that Erwin became agitated, refused orders, and put his hands on him while he was trying to remove unruly party guests, forcing him to punch and then tackle Erwin to effect the arrest. Witnesses offered conflicting accounts, with some testifying that Erwin's group appeared intoxicated and disruptive. This work investigates Ontology Design Patterns (ODPs) for process modeling in Materials Science and Engineering (MSE). It establishes three requirements for ontology-based process modeling: Process Structure, Data and Resources, and Project Goals and Participant Roles. The authors survey six ontologies—P-PLAN, Metadata4Ing (M4I), OPMW, WILD, General Process Ontology (GPO), and PMDcore—and manually extract ODPs mapped to these requirements. A baseline automated method is introduced that applies semantic similarity via sentence transformer embeddings to align ontology concepts with textual requirements, followed by modular ontology extraction using the ROBOT framework with the STAR method. Evaluated against expert-curated ground truth using precision, recall, and F1-score, P-PLAN achieves the highest scores for Process and Resource ODPs, while PMDcore alone supports all three categories including Project ODP. The approach shows promise for automated ODP identification but is constrained by bias toward annotation quality, sensitivity to requirement formulation, and independent per-ontology processing that misses cross-ontology patterns. Future directions include expanding to additional MSE subdomains, integrating ontology mappings, mitigating annotation bias, and developing a platform to publish patterns and facilitate community feedback.

The Coppock Curve strategy, created by economist E.S.C. Coppock in 1965, is a long-term smoothed momentum indicator primarily for stocks. Calculated as a 10-month weighted moving average of the sum of the 14-month and 11-month rate of change, its parameters were derived from Coppock's study of mourning recovery periods. Trading signals occur when the curve crosses above zero for entry and below zero for exit. Backtested on monthly charts since 1960, the strategy generated about 12 trades over 63 years, all profitable, with reduced drawdowns, roughly 25% less market exposure than buy-and-hold, and superior risk-adjusted returns. It remains valid for exploiting bullish market bias while filtering corrective phases.

This MIT lecture covers sustainable real estate finance at the asset level, focusing on green, healthy, and climate-resilient buildings. It explains how tenant demand and willingness to pay rent premiums for sustainable features generate higher cash flows and asset values, connecting the physical space market to capital markets. The lecture places real estate within the broader emerging field of sustainable finance, noting that BlackRock CEO Larry Fink’s 2020 letter identifying climate risk as a financial risk helped catalyze industry and academic discussion.

Using portfolio theory, the lecturer describes how green buildings function as a superior asset class with lower risk and higher returns compared to conventional brown buildings, shifting the efficient frontier and attracting capital inflows. Brown buildings with negative climate externalities face higher default risk, declining values, and capital flight. On the debt side, climate hazards such as wildfires and flooding increase mortgage default risk when property values fall below loan balances, creating challenges for government-backed mortgage and insurance programs regarding social justice and political pushback against pricing climate risk into loans. Conversely, green mortgages illustrate that banks offer better terms—such as higher loan-to-value ratios and lower interest rates—for energy-efficient properties because they carry lower default risk, as reduced utility costs free up income for payments and the assets hold higher values. This same logic supports financing vehicles that lend more upfront for renovations based on expected post-improvement appreciation. Finally, the lecture notes that private equity firms increasingly incorporate ESG criteria into investment memos and due diligence, aligning social value with business value to pursue higher returns.

A blitz is a defensive football play in which five or more defenders rush the quarterback to disrupt the offense, compared to the typical four rushers. While it increases pressure on the quarterback, it reduces coverage defenders and risks exploitation by mobile quarterbacks or quick passes. The defensive coordinator usually designs these plays to outsmart the offense and get the defense off the field. Types include the conventional blitz; the zone blitz, where a linebacker rushes and a defensive lineman drops into coverage; the safety blitz; the cornerback blitz; the zero blitz, which leaves no deep safety and is often used against anticipated runs; and the run blitz, aimed at stopping the run. Offenses can beat a blitz with quick passes to open receivers—often running backs—using mobile quarterbacks to evade rushers, and employing max protection schemes that keep extra blockers in to slow the rush while looking for one-on-one matchups downfield.

In Romania, rapid technological and social development means initial Library and Information Science (LIS) education does not fully prepare graduates for specialized labor market demands, making lifelong learning indispensable. This paper integrates behavioral framing effects into information design by extending the Bayesian persuasion model with a framing-to-belief oracle that maps natural language framings to receiver beliefs. The authors study three sender optimization variants: recommendation-only, framing-only, and joint framing and recommendation. Theoretical results demonstrate that framing-only optimization is computationally intractable (NP-hard), yields discontinuous sender utility, and is highly sensitive to belief oracle errors. Conversely, joint optimization produces continuous utility and admits a quasi-polynomial-time approximation scheme. Empirically, the authors propose a practical hill-climbing method using LLMs to optimize framing and approximate the belief oracle, combined with analytical recommendation optimization. Case studies of a realtor and a clothing brand show high efficacy when evaluated by LLM-simulated receivers, while human subject studies confirm directional correctness with greater variance. The work concludes that joint optimization of framing and recommendations is the more tractable and promising paradigm for LLM-driven persuasive communication.

The passage describes the adapter pattern, which modifies application container interfaces to conform to standardized monitoring, logging, or health check interfaces without altering the application container itself, enabling modular reuse; examples include using a Prometheus exporter for Redis, Fluentd to normalize log formats, and an adapter container to perform rich health checks for MySQL. It then introduces microservices as multi-node distributed architectures that offer reliability, agility, and independent scaling compared to monolithic systems, though they increase debugging and design complexity. The text explains replicated load-balanced services, where identical stateless replicas behind a load balancer provide redundancy and horizontal scaling; readiness probes signal when an application is ready to serve, while session tracking ensures requests from specific users route to the same replica. Application-layer enhancements include adding a caching layer (e.g., Varnish) to improve performance, implementing rate limiting for denial-of-service defense, and using nginx for SSL termination. Sharded services are presented as a means to handle stateful systems where each shard serves only a subset of requests, increasing total cache capacity; replicated sharded caches improve reliability. Sharding functions must be deterministic and uniform, with consistent hashing minimizing disruption during scaling, and hot sharding allowing dynamic adjustment of heavily loaded shards. The scatter/gather pattern parallelizes request processing across nodes to reduce latency, though it faces overhead and straggler problems; replicating shards addresses reliability and availability concerns. Finally, the passage covers Functions as a Service (FaaS) and event-driven processing, which simplify deployment and automatic scaling but complicate operations, are ill-suited for long-running background tasks or services requiring large in-memory datasets, and may become economically inefficient under sustained load. FaaS patterns include the decorator pattern for transforming requests and responses, event handlers for asynchronous tasks such as two-factor authentication, and event-based pipelines.

The lecture covers numerical methods for the second-order wave equation, which can be written as a first-order system with eigenvalues c and −c, representing waves traveling in both directions. The professor analyzes the leapfrog method, first for a semidiscrete formulation (method of lines) where spatial discretization introduces dispersion through the sinc function, producing second-order accuracy. For the fully discrete case, substituting an exponential ansatz yields a quadratic equation for the growth factor g; stability requires both roots to have magnitude at most one, which holds when the Courant number r = cΔt/Δx is less than or equal to 1, corresponding to the CFL condition. The next lecture will introduce staggered grids.

Gold prices are influenced by supply and demand, US Dollar value, and demand from investors, central banks, and jewelry. From 1955 to 2022, gold hit 80 monthly all-time highs, averaging 1.25 yearly, but had none between 1981 and 2005. The authors developed and backtested a strategy for trading gold near all-time highs using World Bank monthly closing prices. Though the rules require membership, the strategy shows a decent equity curve with about one-third market exposure, lower returns, and roughly half the maximum drawdown, helping identify gold bull regimes.

The Wing-T is a football offense developed by Harold “Tubby” Raymond at the University of Delaware from 1966 to 2001, often called the Delaware Wing-T. It uses misdirection, unusual formations, and a diverse run game to deceive aggressive defenders by making different plays look as similar as possible. The offense requires at least two capable running backs, including a fullback who can run inside and catch passes, an athletic quarterback with good footwork, and smaller, quicker offensive linemen who excel at pulling and trapping. Its strengths include slowing down aggressive defenses, providing experienced coaches with extensive adjustments, and being uncommon in modern football. Its primary weakness is the lack of a traditional dropback passing game from standard formations, though teams can incorporate spread sets. Common formations include the Wing, Wing-Slot, and Unbalanced. Key running plays are the Buck Sweep, Down Play, and Trap, while common pass plays include the Waggle, Single Receiver Option Route, and Play Action Vertical Pass. Though largely extinct in major college football, the Wing-T remains popular in high school and has influenced modern spread coaches such as Gus Malzahn.

This work demonstrates controlled defect engineering in monolayer MoS₂ using high-energy (1 MeV) electron beam irradiation, where defect density is tuned by varying exposure time (30–120 s). Systematic characterization via Raman, photoluminescence (PL), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM), and first-principles calculations reveals that irradiation induces chalcogen vacancies and lattice disorder. Raman modes shift and the defect-related LO(M) intensity increases, while PL shows excitonic blueshift, intensity quenching, and emergence of defect-bound peaks (D1 ~1.64 eV, D2 ~1.73 eV). XPS detects increased Mo⁵⁺ and Mo⁶⁺ states and Mo–O bonding at sulfur vacancies, and KPFM indicates p-type doping through a work function increase from 4.8 eV to 5.24 eV. Temperature- and power-dependent PL confirm the bound nature of defect states and enhanced electron–phonon coupling. Circular polarization-resolved PL shows valley polarization of the A exciton drops from 62% to 38%, attributed to defect-mediated intervalley scattering. First-principles calculations confirm that oxygen at sulfur vacancies creates acceptor states near the valence band, producing the observed defect PL peaks via conduction band-to-acceptor transitions and reducing valley polarization. The results establish high-energy electron irradiation as a reliable, controllable approach for modulating defects and optoelectronic properties in monolayer TMDs.

The ADS868xW devices operate in ACQ and CONV states, entering ACQ on power-up, after asynchronous reset, or after conversion, and entering CONV on a CONVST/CS rising edge. A low-power NAP mode is available in the ACQ state. Programming uses nine configuration registers accessed via data transfer frames that begin at the CONVST/CS falling edge; valid write operations require a minimum of 32 SCLK cycles. The multiSPI interface supports legacy SPI protocols for configuration and single SDO-x, dual SDO-x, or source-synchronous protocols for reading data. Output data words can contain conversion results, register data, or fixed patterns with optional flags. Register maps include controls for device ID, reset and power modes, SPI and SDO protocols, output data flags, input ranges, and alarm thresholds with hysteresis. The device is a 16-bit SAR ADC with an integrated analog front-end and reference, suitable for industrial analog input modules. Power supply recommendations require decoupling AVDD and DVDD with 1µF and 10µF capacitors placed close to the pins. The device supports NAP and deep power-down modes to reduce power consumption. Layout guidelines recommend partitioning analog and digital sections and placing bypass capacitors near supply pins without intervening vias.

The article presents a long-only trading strategy for the Global X Robotics and Artificial Intelligence ETF (BOTZ), an ETF founded in 2016 that invests in companies benefiting from robotics and AI adoption. The strategy combines a short-term Donchian Channel indicator (length 3) with a 200-period Exponential Moving Average filter to identify bullish trades and reduce false signals. Backtested on a daily timeframe from September 2016 onward, the strategy outperformed buy-and-hold returns with lower volatility. Optimization across various inputs indicated robustness, as most settings remained profitable; the authors selected non-optimal values to avoid curve fitting. However, the strategy generated only 87 trades, limiting statistical reliability and increasing the risk of curve fitting due to the ETF’s limited price history. The authors strongly recommend out-of-sample backtesting and an incubation period before live trading. Preliminary results on a 2-hour timeframe also appeared promising, though the article cautions that short-term trading requires further validation.

The present disclosure relates to digital twin simulations. A digital twin is a virtual representation of a physical asset that tracks changes across its lifespan using real-time data from sensors and IoT devices. Embodiments describe a computer-implemented method, system, and computer program product for executing simulations that bypass one or more input parameters. The method includes capturing a real-time data feed from a data collection device to create a digital twin model representing the physical asset; creating multiple separate versions reflecting changes to components and performance over time; configuring simulation input by selecting at least one version and at least one component to bypass; and outputting simulation results. The system includes a creation engine, data collection engine, version management module, simulation engine, and reporting engine. Users can select current or previous versions, construct hybrid models from components of multiple versions, bypass selected components, substitute alternative components, and provide overriding values for non-simulated portions to use as input for simulated sections. The workflow involves data collection, deviation detection, version creation, simulation configuration, execution, and result reporting. Implementations may use networked, cloud, or containerized computing environments.

Fabry–Perot cavities are essential in quantum and classical optics, but conventional polished mirrors are too large for compact, scalable systems. This work demonstrates a simple, scalable method to fabricate visible-range microcavities using buckled dielectric membrane mirrors. The fabrication employs standard silicon processing: wet thermal smoothing of a silicon wafer, deposition of SiO2/Ta2O5 dielectric layers, photolithography, and a Bosch etch to create freestanding, rotationally symmetric micromirrors with diameters of 600 µm and radii of curvature from 0.9 mm to 21 mm. Using a swept-ring-down method at 780.24 nm, the microcavities achieved a maximum finesse of 0.89 × 10^6 and a maximum quality factor of 2.3 × 10^9; finesse decreases with increasing cavity length due to diffractive losses, while the quality factor rises and then plateaus. The surface roughness upper bound is ≤90 pm. The mirrors can be assembled into compact 45 µm and 1 mm cavities, achieving finesses of 0.616 × 10^6 and 0.263 × 10^6 and quality factors of 7.45 × 10^7 and 6.74 × 10^8, respectively. These devices are suitable for quantum networking interfaces, neutral atom and ion trap systems, and compact classical optics applications such as filtering and laser stabilization.

The application claims priority as a continuation of U.S. Nonprovisional Patent Application Nos. 16/746,658; 15/972,958; 15/601,345; and 15/333,889, each entitled "Security Appliance." Network security appliances are typically managed remotely via a network, but denial of service attacks can prevent remote administration and require manual reboot or disconnection. The described security appliance includes a local touch screen or input/output interface that provides direct command and control over network functionality and configuration without requiring remote login. During denial of service attacks, the local interface is given priority access to processing resources and memory, enabling mitigating actions such as shutting down ports, blacklisting sources, or modifying filter rules without rebooting or disconnecting from the network. The appliance may apply packet processing rules via geoprocessing-based analysis using minimum bounding rectangles and R-tree indexing for faster matching. A management server may distribute mandatory rules for known threats to all appliances and randomly distribute potential rules for inactive threats to subsets based on likelihood, reducing memory and bandwidth usage. The local interface may buffer packets from unrecognized devices until user authorization is provided, and the appliance may reserve resources and elevate UI priority during attacks.

High-stakes standardized testing influences curriculum and teaching methods, constraining education freedom even within school choice programs. Some states require private schools in choice programs to take state exams aligned with public school standards, and many states mandate ACT or SAT exams for graduation or scholarships. The author argues these tests have degraded standards, citing changes to the SAT and AP exams. While banning standardized tests is not recommended—since universities have reinstated them after test-optional experiments—the author advocates for assessment choice, allowing schools and students to select tests aligned with their educational approaches. The Classic Learning Test is presented as one alternative grounded in classic literature and history. States should provide diverse testing menus for school choice programs and ensure alternatives are accepted for public college admissions and scholarships. Arkansas and Florida have enacted reforms allowing multiple tests. Testing choice is necessary to prevent testing monopolies from limiting educational diversity.

The Supreme Court will hear a challenge to Colorado’s 2019 law banning conversion therapy for minors. Therapist Kaley Chiles argues the ban violates her First Amendment free speech rights because her counseling relies solely on talk therapy, making the law a content- and viewpoint-based restriction subject to strict scrutiny. She contends Colorado lacks evidence of harm and that the law is over- and underinclusive. Colorado and the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 10th Circuit maintain the ban regulates medical conduct, not speech, warranting rational basis review; the state cites evidence linking conversion therapy to depression and suicide among youth and warns that a ruling for Chiles could destabilize healthcare regulation. The federal government supports Chiles, arguing that as applied to her the law targets disfavored speech and should be reviewed under strict scrutiny, which the state likely cannot survive.

The Canadian Society of Palliative Care Physicians released a report concluding that expanding palliative care across Canada would improve care while reducing costs. Shifting patients to residential hospices saves approximately $600 daily. With Canada's aging population increasing healthcare spending, the CSPCP urges government action to improve access to these services.

Embodiments relate to enhanced trick-play modes for streaming video. A streaming client maintains a normal buffer window of continuous video content for normal playback and, using metadata with frame address information, maintains a trick-play window that buffers only a selected subset of frames—such as key frames at approximately equal intervals—for portions outside the normal buffer window, without buffering intervening ranges. During trick-play operations, the client plays video using only the buffered subset. The client may request specific individual frames via byte-range requests, adaptively select frames from multiple bitrate streams based on performance metrics and playback rate, and expand the normal buffer by requesting intervening frames while reusing the already-buffered subset. Trick-play windows may be created based on user input, predicted playback position exceeding the normal buffer, or proximity to metadata jump points, and multiple trick-play windows may be maintained for different rates or qualities.

Breast cancer is the most common cancer in the UK, with around 56,000 new cases annually. Regular self-examination is crucial for early detection. Lumps can vary in size and texture—sometimes pea-like, other times hard and irregular—and may appear in the breast or armpit. Individuals should check for changes in shape, size, skin dimpling, redness, rashes, or nipple discharge and inversion. Self-exams should be done every two weeks to monthly, ideally a week after menstruation, using circular motions while lying down and sitting up, and can be easier in the shower. Doctors will review medical and family history and may refer patients if concerned. Risk factors include genetic mutations, early menstruation, late menopause, not having children, and combined HRT use over five years; breastfeeding and an active lifestyle may reduce risk. Men can also develop breast cancer, typically presenting as a lump. Early diagnosis significantly improves treatment effectiveness and survival rates, with over three-quarters of women surviving at least 10 years.

A 167-million-year-old fossil lizard named *Breugnathair elgolensis* discovered on Scotland’s Isle of Skye in 2016 exhibits snake-like jaws and hook-like teeth alongside a lizard’s short body and limbs. After nearly a decade of study by an international team including the American Museum of Natural History, the specimen was placed in a new predatory squamate group called Parviraptoridae, displaying both snake-like and gecko-like features. Researchers say this unusual combination indicates either that snake ancestors were very different than expected or that snake-like predatory features evolved independently. The fossil does not conclusively establish whether the creature is a snake ancestor or a stem-squamate.

The District Court of Appeal of Florida, Second District, reversed the Unemployment Appeals Commission's order denying Genel Altimeaux unemployment benefits. Following a workplace dispute over pay at Ocean Construction, an appeals referee found Altimeaux voluntarily quit based solely on supervisor Milliken's testimony from an initial hearing that Altimeaux did not attend due to lack of notice. After remand, a second hearing produced no testimony that Altimeaux personally quit; another supervisor testified he never heard Altimeaux quit, and Altimeaux denied quitting. The court held that Milliken's prior uncross-examined testimony was incompetent under section 120.569(2)(j), Florida Statutes, and the remaining evidence failed to support a finding of voluntary quit. The court reversed and directed reinstatement of Altimeaux's unemployment award.

The Pin and Pull is an outside run play using down blocks and pullers to create favorable angles and lead blockers in space. Strengths include getting extra blockers to the point of attack, versatility with pre-snap alignments, and allowing the tailback to run from the C-gap to the sideline. Weaknesses include needing at least two pulling guards and a speed back who can stress the defense horizontally. Unlike the Buck Sweep, which requires a simultaneous inside run threat, it is a true perimeter run. The passage details blocking assignments against 3-4 Odd and 4-3 Even fronts and describes the Pin and Pull Toss and TE-Wing Pin and Pull Toss variations.

This paper introduces COTUTOR, a generative AI model for personalized education that integrates Bayesian Knowledge Tracing, convex optimization, and signal processing. It operates as an interactive chatbot that collects real-time multimodal student signals—including submission and grading data, participation logs, and queries—to estimate knowledge states and iteratively optimize learning strategies and resource allocation. Formulating knowledge tracing as a convex optimization problem provides interpretability, globally optimal tracking, and efficient inference relative to autoregressive LLMs. COTUTOR was implemented in programming education using Online Judge submission data and integrated with platforms such as My Code Weapon and Nemobot. A case study formulates educational resource allocation and sentiment maximization as a convex optimization problem with priority and budget constraints. The system is evaluated through educational dataset benchmarking and controlled classroom studies, testing hypotheses of superior knowledge state estimation and enhanced learning outcomes compared to baseline methods.

The passage describes multi-camera imaging systems and methods for imaging faint objects in low-light or space environments using arrays of economical or low-performance cameras. The systems address limitations of existing high-signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) cameras—such as narrow fields of view (FOV) and high cost—by co-registering and combining multiple images to achieve higher SNR, increased bit depth, and reduced cosmic ray artifacts.

Three configurations are provided. A Common Field Array arranges cameras to share a common FOV region; a computing system combines the co-registered images to produce a combined image with an SNR at least √N times greater than individual images, where N is the quantity combined. A Hybrid Field Array uses multiple camera arrays with partially overlapping common FOV regions; the computing system combines images within each array and stitches them into a composite image with a wider FOV and improved SNR. An Adaptive Field Array initially configures cameras to form a broad composite FOV; upon detecting a target, the cameras automatically reconfigure to a common FOV containing the target, and the computing system co-registers and combines the images to enhance SNR.

The computing system aligns images using spatial transformations based on common reference objects. The systems support calibration (dark, flat, bias, barrel distortion, and field), data collection via star matching, and data reduction including streak detection, initial orbit determination, and catalog searches to identify uncorrelated targets. Applications include satellite detection and tracking, astrophotography, and tactical night vision.

Researchers from the University of Washington and several small companies conducted the first large-scale trial using poplar trees inoculated with a probiotic to clean up trichloroethylene (TCE)-contaminated groundwater at a California Superfund site. Zircon transforms to the high-pressure scheelite-structured phase reidite under shock compression. This study reports the behavior of trace elements during laboratory shock loading of a natural zircon monocrystal to 13.6 and 51.3 GPa. At 13.6 GPa, the sample remained zircon with strong fracturing and texturing but no phase change. At 51.3 GPa, it transformed to mosaic reidite with weak residual zircon, exhibiting (112)R||(200)Zrn orientation relations. Residual heating was estimated at 21°C for 13.6 GPa and 182°C for 51.3 GPa in pore-free material, with much higher temperatures near pores. Spectroscopic analysis showed that the reidite sample exhibited blue cathodoluminescence with increased rare earth element (REE3+) line intensities and at least two distinct Dy3+ local environments. Bright yellow luminescent speckles, attributed to REE3+ segregation—primarily Dy3+—were observed on planar defects and crystallographic planes. This segregation occurred rapidly on a timescale of tens of seconds without prolonged post-shock annealing. The authors suggest the reconstructive zircon–reidite transition alters oxygen vacancy populations, expelling substitutional trace cations into interstitial positions from which they migrate to extended defects. Consequently, while isotopic characteristics and trace element ratios in the lattices may remain similar to the starting zircon, shock-induced fracturing and phase transition can promote trace element release during subsequent fluid or melt interaction.

This patent application, a continuation of prior “Ladar Transmitter” filings, discloses improved ladar transmitter systems and methods for computer vision. Conventional ladar suffers from high cost, size, power, and data bandwidth requirements, while flash ladar has high pulse energy needs, noisy read-outs, and low signal-to-noise ratios. To improve gaze optimization on scan area regions, the inventors disclose an optical field splitter/inverter placed downstream of scanning mirrors to split and invert the scan pattern, shifting fast resonant scan speeds to the edges and slower speeds to the center. Embodiments include W-shaped reflectors, triangular prisms, and hinged adjustable configurations that can produce overlapped fields. For Lissajous scans, an induced periodic phase drift replaces fixed phase to reduce scan gaps and blindspots in targeted regions via optimized time-varying control. Additionally, a compact beam scanner assembly employs an ellipsoidal conjugate reflector (ECR) reimaging mirror between two scannable mirrors, enabling equally sized, closely spaced mirrors. A coplanar angle constraint ensures the reflected ray fan lies in a plane containing the second mirror center, eliminating distortions and supporting a compact form factor.

The passage describes Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) transmissions and methods, systems, and devices for small data transmission in New Radio (NR). It addresses inefficiencies in LTE small data transmission and limitations of current NOMA approaches, such as sequence collision and degraded channel estimation. To reduce signaling overhead and power consumption, a network apparatus (e.g., a gNB) may configure contention-based radio resources for a configured grant Physical Uplink Shared Channel (PUSCH) and broadcast configuration information (e.g., in a Remaining System Information Block) to UEs, including NOMA parameters such as demodulation reference signal (DMRS) ports, multiple access signatures, and interleavers. A UE in an RRC-IDLE or RRC-INACTIVE state may then transmit small data via the configured grant PUSCH without transitioning to an RRC-CONNECTED state, or with minimal transition. To mitigate sequence collision, UE-specific reference bits constructed from a UE identity and a multiple access identity are jointly encoded with information bits (e.g., using systematic LDPC or Polar coding) and used to generate a preamble or DMRS. The scheme includes bit-level processing (e.g., UE-specific interleaving, rate matching) and symbol-level processing (e.g., modulation, spreading). Extended cyclic prefixes and guard bands may be used to support asynchronous transmission. For UEs in the idle state, data may be secured using a NAS security context, while inactive state UEs may use a stored AS security context. Random Access procedures may also incorporate NOMA for PUSCH transmission to reduce collision probability and latency.

The Tax Court reviewed an IRS Appeals officer’s determination permitting levy of unpaid 1994 and 1996 income taxes reported by petitioner Robert Eugene Poindexter. The Court rejected the IRS argument that section 6330(c)(2)(B) prevented Poindexter from challenging self-assessed liabilities, but granted summary judgment for the IRS because Poindexter failed to provide specific facts identifying errors in the returns, such as incorrect items of income or deduction, as required by Rule 331. The Court also found no factual support for his claims of procedural errors or improper levies. Because Poindexter declined to file amended returns and presented no justiciable issue regarding the underlying liabilities, the Court sustained the collection determination.

The Automated Fare Collection (AFC) System Market was valued at $4.81 billion in 2016 and is projected to reach $12.81 billion by 2024 at a CAGR of 13.3%. AFC automates public transportation ticketing using smart cards and NFC, improving efficiency and security. Growth is driven by technology adoption and government investment, while lack of awareness and limited smart card use are restraints. The market is segmented by component (hardware, software), application (bus, toll, train, car rental), technology (smart card, NFC, OCR, others), and geography (North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, LAMEA). Major players include Cubic Transportation Systems, Thales Group, and NXP Semiconductors.

A new analysis found that during the 2014-2016 West African Ebola epidemic, 3 percent of patients caused over 60 percent of infections. Transmission was driven by people who stayed home and by traditional funeral practices where bodily fluids remained infectious. While each patient infected an average of 2.39 others, many infected no one. Age was a key demographic predictor, as the very young and old attracted many caregivers. Superspreaders also helped drive SARS and MERS outbreaks. The epidemic was stopped through safe burial and quick hospitalization, not vaccines or drugs.

Acting CDC Director Jim O'Neill approved recommendations allowing individuals over 6 months to receive updated Covid-19 shots after consulting providers, and that children under 4 receive MMR and chickenpox vaccines separately. The approvals allow states to order updated Covid vaccines for low-income children through the Vaccines for Children program, which roughly 50% of eligible children could not access during the delay. In *Pelitsie v. National Surety Corporation* (April 3, 1956), the court held that the plaintiff insured failed to comply with a burglary insurance policy clause requiring records that enabled the insurer to accurately determine the amount of loss. The plaintiff maintained a fund of cash and payroll checks, but only recorded an aggregate nightly total on a scratch-pad without listing individual checks or details needed to pursue the drawers. Because the stolen property included checks, the court ruled that such minimal records were insufficient as a matter of law; the plaintiff’s ability to recoup only $182 by remembering two checks demonstrated the inadequacy. The judgment for the plaintiff was reversed, and the case was remanded with directions to dismiss the complaint.

Language enrollment in U.S. K–12 and postsecondary education is declining, threatening programs such as German and French. This article argues that language learning is essential because "language connects" people, cultures, and communities. It proposes fostering "imagined communities"—connections formed through imagination with target-language speakers and cultures—as a classroom approach to increase student interest, retention, and program viability. Implemented via task-based instruction, this method asks students to imagine themselves in authentic scenarios, such as moving to a target-language city, finding housing, using public transit, and shopping, using authentic materials and just-in-time instruction. A yearlong study in eighth-grade German classrooms demonstrated positive outcomes, including deeper cultural learning, increased feelings of connection and community membership, and continued language study beyond requirements. The approach requires no extra funding, only planning time, and can be adapted for all levels (K–16), contexts, and languages by creating plausible scenarios, designing authentic activities and assessments, and allowing student autonomy. Instructors should catalog materials and collaborate to sustain the method. Centering language education on connection through imagined communities provides the essential rationale for language learning and supports program survival.

This work examines the application of global variance reduction techniques (VRTs), originally developed for steady-state Monte Carlo neutron transport, to time-dependent simulations, focusing on their interactions with population control techniques (PCTs). VRTs including splitting, rouletting, Implicit Capture, and weight windows (CADIS, FW-CADIS, and Cooper-Larsen) modify particle weights to guide particles and improve statistical efficiency. PCTs such as Uniform Combing (UC) and Weight-Based Combing (WC) regulate particle counts across time steps; UC scales surviving weights by a constant factor, while WC resets weights to a uniform value. Using the Shift and MC/DC codes, the study finds that UC is generally compatible with VRTs because it preserves weight distributions, whereas WC conflicts with weight-window-based VRTs, causing excessive splitting and memory exhaustion in tested problems. In a Shift pulsed slab problem, FW-CADIS achieved modest efficiency gains but was limited by static weight windows and mandatory WC. In MC/DC simulations of the AZURV1 benchmark and a 1D SCRAM problem, Cooper-Larsen weight windows combined with UC dramatically improved the figure of merit, with time-dependent weight windows outperforming static ones. Implicit Capture paired poorly with UC across MC/DC tests. The results demonstrate that proper selection of VRT and PCT combinations is critical, that steady-state VRTs can be effective in time-dependent contexts, and that time-dependent adaptations of these methods offer further efficiency gains.

The Ninth Circuit affirmed a Tax Court judgment holding Pacific Basin Manufacturing liable for 1975 and 1976 income tax deficiencies. The Delaware corporation, which operated in American Samoa, excluded revenue from sales to its Hawaii parent under 26 U.S.C. § 931(a). Because the parent deposited checks into the taxpayer's Honolulu bank account, the court held the funds were "received within the United States" under § 931(b), making them taxable. It rejected the argument that receipt should depend on the taxpayer's primary physical presence in American Samoa, noting that would render § 931(b) redundant.

Following an FBI raid on his personal attorney Michael Cohen, President Trump pardoned former Bush aide Scooter Libby for his 2007 perjury and obstruction conviction. The White House described the pardon as correcting an injustice by an overzealous prosecutor, while critics claimed it signaled to targets of special counsel Robert Mueller’s investigation that they would be protected. As Mueller’s probe expands into tax, lobbying, and business issues, legal experts debate whether the president’s broad constitutional pardon power extends to self-pardons or pardons issued with corrupt intent, though the Constitution offers no protection from impeachment. Historical precedents include George H.W. Bush’s Iran-Contra pardons and Richard Nixon’s consideration of a self-pardon. The White House has not ruled out pardoning Cohen, and a report alleges Trump’s former lawyer discussed pardons with attorneys for indicted associates, which he denied. Democrats, including Rep. Adam Schiff, have introduced legislation requiring disclosure of evidence related to certain pardons, while New York’s attorney general seeks to close a double jeopardy loophole to preserve state prosecutions. Legal analysts note that pardoned individuals lose Fifth Amendment protections and may be compelled to testify.

This study investigates whether LLMs spontaneously develop egoistic or altruistic behaviors in large-scale social dilemmas using a Schelling-variant migration model with 225 agents and a shared message board. Through mixed-methods analysis—quantitative metrics (Price of Anarchy, Residential Gini Index, behavioral archetype matrices) and qualitative LLM-as-judge coding inspired by Grounded Theory—the authors identify two intrinsic archetypes. "Adaptive Egoists" (e.g., o1-mini, o3-mini, Qwen2.5-7B) default to self-interest, producing sub-optimal collective outcomes, but demonstrate significantly increased altruism when exposed to social norms via the message board. "Altruistic Optimizers" (e.g., Gemini-2.5-pro, Deepseek-R1, Deepseek-V3.1) inherently prioritize system-level welfare, consistently achieving optimal equilibria regardless of communication mechanisms. The findings demonstrate that selecting an LLM for agent-based social simulation constitutes a theoretical choice between models of bounded rationality and idealized pro-social behavior, shifting evaluation focus from task performance to the models’ embodied social tendencies.

This retrospective study of 1,918 adult intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) patients in the ICU from the MIMIC-IV database (2011–2019) examined the association between resting heart rate (RHR) and all-cause mortality (ACM). Patients were stratified into four RHR quartiles. Multivariate Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses demonstrated that RHR >78.5 bpm was significantly associated with higher ACM at 30 days, 90 days, and one year, with the ACM incidence of the upper quartiles approximately 50–100% higher per quartile increase compared with the lowest. Restricted cubic splines identified a nonlinear relationship with an inflection point at 90.3 bpm, suggesting RHR below this threshold is an independent protective factor, while RHR above is an independent risk factor. Subgroup analyses revealed an interaction with age >60 years, and mediation analysis indicated age partially mediated the RHR-ACM association. RHR >90.3 bpm showed predictive value with an area under the curve >0.5. The authors conclude that RHR-based stratification could inform management strategies to improve clinical outcomes, though randomized trials are needed.

Sigi Zheng’s MIT lecture explains how to quantitatively measure the benefits of green buildings and cities using the hedonic pricing model. The lecture recaps prior findings of approximately 6% rent and 7.6% price premiums for green buildings, then focuses on the methodology used to derive these figures. Because environmental benefits are non-market goods, researchers estimate consumers’ willingness to pay through revealed preference—observing actual real estate transactions—rather than stated preference surveys. The hedonic model decomposes a property’s price into observable components (e.g., number of rooms, transit access, parks, LEED certification) plus a residual for unobserved factors, using regression on large datasets to estimate the value of each attribute. For example, a LEED coefficient of 0.06 in a log-price regression indicates a 6% price premium, holding other factors constant.

The lecture highlights the challenge of “apples-to-oranges” comparisons: green buildings often differ systematically from non-green buildings in ways that are hard to observe, such as quality, age, location, or prestige. These differences create endogeneity problems—including omitted variable bias, reverse causality, and selection bias—that can distort estimates. To achieve causal inference, researchers seek a counterfactual scenario in which buildings are identical except for green certification. Techniques to address this include OLS with control variables, fixed effects, Randomized Controlled Trials, geographic matching, propensity score matching, instrumental variables, regression discontinuity, and difference-in-differences. Geographic matching, which compares green buildings to nearby non-green buildings, is particularly common in real estate research to control for locational amenities.

The framework extends from individual buildings to urban amenities. Zheng describes her own research estimating an 8% housing price premium for good school districts in Beijing and discusses New York City’s Bryant Park and High Line Park as cases where private and public investment in amenities increased nearby property values. However, such improvements can also cause environmental gentrification, as higher-income residents with greater willingness to pay displace existing lower-income communities. The lecture concludes that hedonic analysis, even at a conceptual level, is a valuable tool for business and policy decisions, such as evaluating investments in transit-oriented development and public-private partnerships.

The Turtle Trading Strategy is a mechanical, trend-following approach developed by Richard Dennis and William Eckhardt in the 1980s, named after their 1983 experiment in which 14 novice traders were trained and funded to test whether trading could be learned. The experiment succeeded, demonstrating that trading skills could be acquired through disciplined rule-following.

The original rules focused on identifying trend breakouts—such as 20-day or 55-day highs and lows—for entries and exits, while employing volatility-based position sizing using the Average True Range, pyramiding into winning trades, and strict stop-loss orders to limit losses. The Turtles traded a diverse basket of futures, including commodities, bonds, currencies, and stock indices.

The strategy remains viable today, though traders often adapt the original rules with technical indicators. While trend-following indices and hedge funds demonstrate that the approach can still yield returns, backtests from 2007 onward indicate lower performance compared to earlier periods, with long drawdowns and frequent whipsaws. After the experiment, Richard Dennis eventually stopped trading following major losses, while William Eckhardt founded a successful commodity trading advisor, and several Turtles established their own firms with varying degrees of success.

The BC Coroners Service reported 1,422 suspected illicit drug overdose deaths in British Columbia in 2017, a 43% increase from 2016. This study investigates dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) sensitized with mixed natural dyes extracted from mangosteen peel (MP), which contains anthocyanins, and grass jelly leaves (GJL), which contains chlorophyll. Motivated by the need for sustainable alternatives to fossil fuels and costly synthetic dyes, the research systematically combined MP and GJL dyes in volume ratios of 3:1, 2:1, 1:1, 1:2, and 1:3 to optimize photovoltaic performance. Devices were fabricated on ITO-coated glass with TiO₂ photoanodes, iodide/iodine electrolytes, and graphite counter electrodes, then analyzed using UV-Vis spectrophotometry, optical microscopy, FESEM, and I-V measurements. UV-Vis spectra showed that mixed dyes retained the distinct absorption features of both parent dyes, broadening the overall light-harvesting range. Morphological analysis revealed that MP-rich films exhibited cracking, the 1:1 ratio produced a homogeneous and crack-free surface, and GJL-rich films showed mild granularity. Photovoltaic testing indicated that the 1:3 MP:GJL ratio achieved the highest power conversion efficiency of 3.50%, compared to 2.75% for pure MP and 2.12% for pure GJL, attributed to complementary light absorption and improved charge collection. Stability testing over ten cycles showed that GJL-rich ratios maintained performance better than other mixtures, while the 1:1 ratio degraded rapidly. The study concludes that blending MP and GJL dyes at optimized ratios enhances DSSC efficiency, though improving long-term stability remains essential for future development.

Depoe Bay, Oregon, where the Aug. 21 total solar eclipse will first reach land in the continental United States, is preparing for a possible influx of hundreds of thousands of visitors. The ADS868xW integrates a second-order, 500kHz antialiasing low-pass filter and a high-bandwidth ADC driver. It uses either an internal 4.096V reference, enabled by default and requiring a 4.7µF decoupling capacitor, or an external 4.096V reference buffered internally to REFCAP with 10µF and 1µF capacitors. The internal reference is factory-trimmed but sensitive to solder-induced thermal stress, and is temperature-compensated over –40°C to +125°C. The ADC accepts single-ended and differential bipolar and unipolar inputs, providing straight-binary output with an LSB equal to FSR/2^16.

Alarm functions include an input alarm with user-programmable high and low thresholds and hysteresis, and an AVDD alarm with fixed 4.7V and 5.3V thresholds. Both alarms feature active and tripped flags that are readable via the ALARM pin, the ALARM_REG register, or appended to the serial data output.

The device communicates through a multiSPI interface supporting legacy SPI and source-synchronous protocols with single or dual SDO outputs. It operates in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states controlled by the RST and CONVST/CS pins. A 32-bit data transfer frame begins on the falling edge of CONVST/CS and ends on its rising edge, which initiates conversion; short and long frames are also supported. Multiple devices can be daisy-chained, requiring 32 × N SCLK cycles for N devices. Host commands include byte and half-word read, write, set, and clear operations directed at nine configuration registers that manage device ID, reset and power modes, interface protocols, output data formatting, reference and range selection, and alarm thresholds.

In industrial applications, the device serves as a fully integrated 16-bit data acquisition system with programmable gain, accepting up to ±12.288V inputs and settling to 1% in under 5µs. It offers NAP and power-down modes to reduce power consumption. AVDD and DVDD require separate decoupling capacitors located close to the pins, and the PCB layout should isolate analog and digital signals to minimize noise.
