The lecture recaps the LSZ theorem, which obtains scattering amplitudes from momentum-space time-ordered correlation functions by taking an on-shell limit: initial-state momenta correspond to the negative energy root (p⁰ = −ωₚ) and final-state momenta to the positive root (p⁰ = +ωₚ). Amplitudes are computed using truncated, connected Feynman diagrams with external propagators removed; diagrams with loops on single external legs only modify those propagators and are absorbed into a momentum-independent wavefunction renormalization constant Z, which equals 1 at leading order.

The lecture then introduces fermions via the Dirac equation. Motivated by problems with the Klein-Gordon equation (no positive-definite probability, negative energies), Dirac sought a Lorentz-covariant equation first-order in time. This requires Hermitian matrices α and β (minimum size 4×4) and a multi-component spinor ψ. Requiring the squared equation to yield the Klein-Gordon dispersion relation imposes anticommutation relations: {αᵢ, αⱼ} = 2δᵢⱼ, {αᵢ, β} = 0, and β² = 1. Defining γ⁰ = iβ and γⁱ = iβαⁱ gives the Dirac equation (γᵘ∂ᵤ − m)ψ = 0, where the gamma matrices satisfy the Clifford algebra {γᵘ, γᵛ} = 2ηᵘᵛ. Explicit 4×4 representations are provided. In the massless case, a 2-component description using Pauli matrices suffices. Different gamma-matrix representations are physically equivalent up to similarity transformations, with specific forms being convenient for different kinematic regimes. Lorentz covariance of the Dirac equation is deferred to the next lecture.

Phuket Governor Norraphat Plodthong has ordered lifeguards to resume patrols at the island’s beaches by April 1, 2018, following a meeting on March 21. Local administrative offices must provide lifeguards for beaches in Muang Phuket and Kathu districts, while a procured company will cover Thalang district. Local offices without sufficient budgets must request financial support from the Phuket Provincial Administration Organisation (PPAO), contradicting the Governor’s December 12 order that the PPAO would no longer be involved in lifeguard provision. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed at record highs. Figma shares rose 7% and spiked as much as 16% intraday after OpenAI CEO Sam Altman demonstrated Figma's integration into ChatGPT at DevDay. Users can ask Figma to perform tasks within ChatGPT conversations, and the assistant may suggest Figma when relevant. Developers may submit apps later in 2025, with monetization options to come.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2017. For Q1 2017, net sales were $35.7 billion, up from $29.1 billion in Q1 2016, with net income of $724 million compared to $513 million. Diluted earnings per share were $1.48. By segment, North America net sales were $20.99 billion with operating income of $596 million; International net sales were $11.06 billion with an operating loss of $481 million; and AWS net sales were $3.66 billion with operating income of $890 million. For the trailing twelve months ended March 31, 2017, net cash provided by operating activities was $17.63 billion and free cash flow was $10.22 billion. Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt, through Schmidt Sciences, will spend $45 million over five years on projects studying the global carbon cycle, including deploying four uncrewed surface vessels to the rough Southern Ocean around Antarctica. The drone boats will collect continuous data for five years—including during harsh winter months—to help scientists understand the Southern Ocean’s role as a critical carbon sink. The USVs, directed by machine learning, will measure partial pressure of CO2 in areas unreachable by crewed or commercial vessels and make data publicly available. The project operates as a public-private partnership with NOAA, as scientists note that proposed federal budget cuts to climate research agencies are increasing reliance on private funding.

BMW and Brilliance Automotive launched the front-wheel-drive 1 Series sedan in China in July 2016. BMW may bring it to India, where it would rival the Mercedes CLA and Audi A3. The UKL1-based sedan measures 4,456mm long with a 2,670mm wheelbase. Likely Indian variants include the 192hp 120i and 231bhp 125i petrol engines, plus diesel options.

Sherwood was sentenced to 11 years in Houston prison for traveling to engage in illicit contact with a child and ordered to lifetime supervision, sex offender registration, and restricted child and Internet access. Arrested in a 2017 sting after traveling to meet a fictional child, he has a Wisconsin juvenile sexual assault record.

Lab experiments show that jostling microbubbles of air and methane in water can generate tiny electrical sparks, offering a potential explanation for what ignites seeping swamp gas to create will-o'-the-wisps. Researchers led by Yu Xia and Richard Zare used a 3-D printed nozzle to produce tiny bubbles, detecting microlightning when smaller bubbles crowded together and exchanged charges. While some scientists find the idea intriguing, others question whether it fully solves the mystery, noting that swamps differ from lab conditions and will-o'-the-wisps hover in air while the experiments occurred underwater. The work advances triboelectricity and could lead to greener methods for driving chemical reactions and breaking down pollutants.

On February 10, 2016, Amazon.com, Inc.’s Board elected Wendell P. Weeks as a director and Audit Committee member, effective immediately. Weeks received 1,365 restricted stock units vesting over three years and entered into a standard director indemnification agreement. Despite forecast rain, Oroville Dam's spillways may not be heavily tested. The Feather River basin expects 7.5 inches over 10 days—less and more spread out than February's 13.6 inches—with colder weather reducing run-off. Inflows may be a quarter of previous peak. Upstream dams are holding back water, and draining has lowered reservoir to 15 feet below emergency spillway lip. Officials have roughly 72 hours before Friday's rain to create a nearly 40-foot buffer. Jan Null warned sudden warm weather melting record snowpack could cause serious inflows.

This special message to Congress addresses the conservation and proper disposition of the national public domain, which has been reduced from over one billion acres to 731 million, largely through fraudulent or wasteful distribution under obsolete laws. The administration has prosecuted land frauds and withdrawn coal lands and water-power sites, and Congress is urged to validate these withdrawals and authorize the Interior Secretary to make temporary withdrawals pending new legislation. Lands should be classified by the Geological Survey to separate agricultural surface rights from mineral, coal, oil, and phosphate deposits, which should be leased on a royalty basis with anti-monopoly provisions. Water-power sites should be leased for limited terms with graduated rentals to prevent monopoly. Soil conservation is identified as the most critical resource issue, requiring scientific treatment and state and federal cooperation. The reclamation of arid lands has outpaced available funds, leaving settlers in distress; the President recommends issuing up to $30 million in bonds to complete irrigation projects, to be repaid from the reclamation fund. Timber land disposition laws should be repealed in favor of public timber sales, forest reserves maintained, and reforestation undertaken at stream sources. Finally, Congress is asked to fund improvements to the Ohio, upper Mississippi, and Missouri Rivers to develop inland waterways and regulate railroad rates, and to act promptly on these recommendations without awaiting investigations into the Interior and Forest Service.

The passage analyzes backtests linking US consumer confidence to S&P 500 returns. Using OECD US data from 1993, investing only when consumer confidence exceeded its 12-month moving average produced an 8.4% CAGR and 23% max drawdown, compared to buy-and-hold's 10.4% CAGR and 55% drawdown, with the strategy invested only 55% of the time. Investing only when confidence fell below the average yielded a 1.58% annual return. The passage defines the Conference Board's Consumer Confidence Index (CCI), based on monthly surveys of 5,000 households regarding present situations and expectations, and the University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index, a monthly telephone survey. It states that index changes exceeding 5% indicate shifts in economic momentum, and that bullish consumer confidence aligns with better stock market performance.

EUR/USD builds a bearish channel requiring 161.8% Fibonacci reach before resistance breaks; momentum slows with potential wave 4 retracement. This document standardizes the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) for AMD SEV-ES and SEV-SNP, enabling an encrypted guest register state to be selectively shared with the hypervisor. The 4KB GHCB mirrors the SEV-ES VMCB save state area and supports protocol versioning and hypervisor feature advertisement via a FEATURES bitmap. It defines the GHCB MSR protocol for communication before the GHCB page is established, including GHCB GPA registration, CPUID requests, feature support queries, AP reset hold, page state changes, SNP Run VMPL, and termination. The specification details Non-Automatic Exit (NAE) event handling—such as IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, MMIO, SNP Guest Requests, SNP Extended Guest Requests, AP creation, #HV doorbell page configuration, IPI, timer, APIC ID list retrieval, SEV-TIO, Secure AVIC, and termination—and the minimum guest and hypervisor state to exchange via the GHCB VALID_BITMAP. It also covers SMP booting through AP Jump Tables or SNP AP Creation, NMI and debug register handling, the SEV-SNP Secrets Page, the EFI Confidential Computing Blob, and Restricted Injection semantics. System Management Mode and nested virtualization are not supported.

Natalie Grabow, 80, of Mountain Lakes, New Jersey, set the world record as the oldest woman to finish the Kona Ironman World Championship in Hawaii, completing the course in 16 hours, 45 minutes, and 26 seconds. Grabow began competing in triathlons at 60, a year after learning to swim at 59 through books, videos, and practice at the YMCA. She started running in her 40s, progressed through shorter races in her 50s, and qualified for her first Kona at 61. She prepares by working out around two hours daily and eats a healthy diet that includes sweets. At the October 11, 2025 finish line, she tripped on carpeting and was greeted by previous record holder Cherie Gruenfeld. She received her winner's bowl on October 12, 2025. Grabow, a mother of two and grandmother of four, plans to continue competing as long as she can.

Molecular Dynamics simulations use Green-Kubo and Non-Equilibrium MD methods to study thermal properties, both requiring heat flux calculations. LAMMPS calculates heat flux exactly for Non-Equilibrium MD but originally used an atomic stress tensor valid only for pair potentials in equilibrium methods, causing errors for many-body interactions. While exact heat flux formulas have been implemented for specific systems, interfacial heat current and its Spectral Decomposition lacked general many-body implementations. This work extends and implements Torii et al.'s exact formulas in LAMMPS for control volume and control surface heat flux and spectral decomposition for arbitrary many-body potentials, with comparative tests using Tersoff and Stillinger-Weber potentials and results for graphene and MoS2.

Solawave's 4-in-1 Renewal Wand is on sale for over $100 during Prime Day. The red light device targets specific facial areas, vibrating and radiating warmth during three minutes of manual use. WIRED staffers reported skin-tightening results around the eyes. It uses a single 630-nm wavelength. Solawave's Face Mask is also on sale for $227, though other masks have better features and comfort.

NVIDIA RTX IO integrates with Microsoft DirectStorage to enable GPU-based lossless decompression, reducing CPU overhead and improving I/O performance by a factor of two for professional visualization and gaming workloads. The NVIDIA A40 data center GPU, based on the GA10x Ampere architecture, delivers up to 2X FP32, 2X ray-tracing, and 5X (10X with Sparsity) AI throughput compared to the Turing-based Quadro RTX 6000, featuring PCIe Gen4, 48GB of memory scalable to 96GB via NVLink, vGPU support, and EGX Platform compatibility. GA10x Ampere achieves up to 2X performance improvements in programmable shading, ray tracing via second-generation RT Cores, and AI via third-generation Tensor Cores with structural sparsity, and supports GDDR6X memory. The GeForce RTX 3090 incorporates 24GB GDDR6X and 10,496 CUDA cores, while the RTX 3070 uses GDDR6 and lacks NVLink. Error Detection and Replay (EDR) technology for GDDR6X detects and retries memory transmission errors to help identify overclocking limits. The RTX A6000 workstation GPU includes 10,752 CUDA cores and 48GB GDDR6, scalable to 96GB via NVLink.

This study reports first-principles calculations of the tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR) effect in Mn3Sn(01¯10)/MgO(110)/Mn3Sn magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs). Mn3Sn is a kagome noncollinear antiferromagnet with an inverse 120° structure that macroscopically breaks time-reversal symmetry, enabling a finite TMR effect via intrinsic momentum-dependent spin splitting despite the absence of net spin polarization. Using density functional theory and the Landauer–Büttiker formalism with a practically thick MgO barrier, the authors ensure tunneling transport and calculate a TMR ratio exceeding 1000%. The large TMR originates from the x-component spin polarization along the cluster octupole easy axis in Mn3Sn and from momentum-dependent electron screening by the MgO barrier, which exhibits the lowest decay rates near k∥=0. This work provides a realistic assessment of Mn3Sn as a magnetic electrode for antiferromagnetic MTJs suitable for spin-orbit-torque switching.

The NVIDIA A40 is a data center GPU based on the GA10x Ampere architecture for visual computing, AI, HPC, and inferencing. Compared to the Turing-based Quadro RTX 6000, it offers up to 2X FP32 throughput, 2X ray-tracing throughput, and up to 5X (10X with Sparsity) AI and data science throughput. It includes PCIe Gen4, 48GB of GPU memory scalable to 96GB via third-generation NVLink, three DisplayPort 1.4 outputs, and supports NVIDIA vGPU software and Quadro Sync, with virtualization enabled by default. The A40 is compatible with the NVIDIA EGX Platform.

The GA10x Ampere architecture features second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores with structural sparsity, and up to 2X performance gains in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI. It supports 8K60 and 4K120 displays via DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1, GDDR6X memory, and RTX IO for direct SSD-to-GPU loading. It also includes fifth-generation NVDEC with the first hardware AV1 decode support, and seventh-generation NVENC for hardware-accelerated encoding.

The NVIDIA RTX A6000 workstation GPU features 10,752 CUDA cores, 48GB of GDDR6 memory scalable to 96GB via NVLink, and advanced ray-tracing and AI capabilities. The GeForce RTX 3090 incorporates a GA102 GPU with 24GB of GDDR6X memory and 10,496 CUDA cores, while the GeForce RTX 3070 uses a GA104 GPU with GDDR6 memory and outperforms the RTX 2080 Ti. The GA10x memory interface includes Error Detection and Replay (EDR) technology for GDDR6X overclocking.

Daisy-chained devices share CONVST/CS and SCLK signals, with each SDO-0 output connected to next SDI input. The host programs identical configurations. Devices sample inputs on CONVST/CS rising edge and begin MSB-first data transfer on its falling edge via SCLK; host receives last device's data first. An optimal frame for N devices requires 32 × N SCLK capture edges; shorter frames cause erroneous configuration.

The study evaluates distance education in Turkish sports higher education during the COVID-19 pandemic. Using a qualitative case study and descriptive analysis, researchers conducted semi-structured interviews from December 2020 to November 2021 with 14 lecturers across multiple universities.

Data analysis revealed four themes. Positive aspects included independence from time and space, access to resources and lesson repetition, use of information technologies, and socioeconomic benefits such as reduced pandemic spread and lower costs. Negative aspects encompassed social issues like communication barriers and inequality; psychological issues including low motivation; technology and access problems; and educational shortcomings, particularly the ineffectiveness of applied sports lessons. Challenges involved infrastructure and connection deficiencies, difficulties in assessment and lesson management, and ineffective student communication. Management of the process was viewed as ineffective due to decentralized decision-making, insufficient training, and platform inadequacies.

The discussion notes that while distance education provides flexibility, literature confirms similar advantages and disadvantages. The conclusion states that distance education is an alternative when formal education is disrupted, but in sports sciences, the inability to conduct applied courses effectively risks learning losses. The study highlights the need for field-specific instructional design, improved technical and administrative infrastructure, adherence to Law No. 6698 regarding data security, and further research on efficacy.

The passage documents AGESA procedures for system initialization and information retrieval. One stackless assembler routine initializes the processor and cache to establish a pre-memory stack region, maps it to global address space, sets MTRRs, and creates a UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF instance; it must run on all cores and checks whether protected or real mode is active. Another stackless procedure removes the pre-memory stack once main memory is available, disabling CAR mode and flushing caches; it must run on all cores but should only be invoked by the BSP. AmdCreateStruct allocates storage for AGESA parameter blocks via PreMemHeap, PostMemDram, or ByHost allocation methods. Additional procedures retrieve DIMM data eye bitmaps, APIC addresses for x86-64 architecture APUs, available pre-memory execution cache size for x86-64 APUs, PCI base addresses per processor die, current processor core identifiers, and memory address-to-FRU mappings including socket, channel, DIMM, chip select, bank, row, and column details. Most procedures require operational coherent HyperTransport links and an established stack environment; AARCH64 APUs with a Platform Security Processor handle early DRAM initialization separately without using these early stack routines.

A study in the Journal of Neuroscience found that barn owls group elements moving in the same direction to distinguish targets from backgrounds, a visual task previously studied only in primates. Researchers showed owls moving black dots on a grey background and tracked their gazes. The owls spotted target dots moving in a different direction, performing better when the contrasting movement was uniform. Activity in the ocular tectum, a basic visual processing brain area, varied with the dots' movement, suggesting this task does not require complex brain structures.

COPD is a leading cause of death caused almost exclusively by smoking, says Dr. Jordan Taillon. Symptoms include chronic coughing and shortness of breath. Diagnosis involves smoking history and pulmonary function tests. Treatments include inhalers, oxygen, and pulmonary rehabilitation. There is no cure, but quitting smoking prevents disease and stops decline.

At RSA Conference 2017, Intel Security's Chris Young warned that corrupted "small data" in analytical models creates "data landmines" causing faulty decisions and economic loss, citing the 2016 election, and noted that insecure home IoT networks threaten corporate systems. Microsoft President Brad Smith called for the tech industry to act as a "digital Switzerland" with purely defensive principles, and proposed a "Digital Geneva Convention" to prohibit attacks on civilian infrastructure and private sector assets. He urged governments to disclose rather than stockpile software vulnerabilities, advocated for an international agency to attribute nation-state attacks, cited the U.S.-China cyber espionage agreement as a model for norms, and stressed private-sector leadership in building global cyber trust.

This application, a continuation of prior U.S. patent applications, describes systems and methods for location sharing within a social networking environment. Embodiments provide a map graphical user interface displaying avatars representing approximate locations of users and their friends. The system receives location information from a user's client device, determines a current trajectory, and predicts a presumed destination by correlating the trajectory with historical location information and habitual places. It may also extract trajectory patterns from historical data and match them to the current path. The presumed destination and an estimated time of arrival are displayed to selected friends via the map GUI. The system includes client devices, a location sharing server, an API server, an application server, a database, and a social network system. Users may authorize location sharing and define audience groups. If communication with a client device is lost, the system may extrapolate the user's location based on the identified trajectory pattern.
US job growth of 200,000 and wage gains of 2.9 percent fueled Fed rate-hike expectations, boosting the dollar and bond yields while stocks fell. Ten-year Treasury yields hit 2.84 percent.

Lenovo unveiled the ThinkPad 25, a limited-edition retro laptop based on T470 and inspired by the 1992 ThinkPad 700C. Available in limited quantities for $1,899.

The document describes Texas Instruments MSPM0G series microcontrollers, detailing the ARM Cortex-M0+ CPU subsystem, five operating modes (RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, SHUTDOWN), two power domains (PD1 and PD0), and a power management unit. It covers the clock module oscillators and distributed clocks, DMA controller capabilities, event manager routing, and memory organization including flash and SRAM. The text specifies peripheral features such as GPIO, IOMUX, ADC, DAC, comparator, voltage reference, temperature sensor, security accelerators, TRNG, AESADV, keystore, CRC, MATHACL, UART, I2C, SPI, CAN-FD, LFSS, RTC, independent and windowed watchdog timers, and general-purpose and advanced timers. It also includes application schematic recommendations, serial wire debug and boot strap loader interfaces, device factory constants, nomenclature, development tools, documentation support, a revision history from November 2024 to April 2025, and mechanical packaging and orderable information.

The Massachusetts Institute of Technology is the first of nine invited universities to publicly reject the Trump administration’s “Compact for Academic Excellence in Higher Education,” which would mandate campus changes in exchange for preferential federal funding. MIT president Sally Kornbluth said the compact would restrict institutional independence and free expression, calling its premise inconsistent with MIT’s values. While most invited institutions are reviewing the proposal and University of Texas officials have expressed enthusiasm, some state leaders have threatened to cut funding if universities sign. MIT’s decision drew praise from academics and Democratic lawmakers, while some Trump administration allies suggested potential retaliation.

The text urges enlarging the Naval Academy to provide 1,000 additional officers, retiring impaired senior officers, and maintaining an efficient navy to avoid disaster. It cites record Post Office revenues of $121.8 million and the success of rural free delivery, with 10,748 new routes requested, noting its benefits to farmers. Komar Uddin, 68, a spiritual healer, denies sexually assaulting and twice raping a 19-year-old during a ritual at her Leicester home on February 25, 2015. The victim's father invited Uddin to help his daughter, who feared an evil spirit. She told Leicester Crown Court that during the private ritual, while her family was downstairs, Uddin rubbed holy oil on her, sexually touched her, and raped her twice; she initially believed it was part of the treatment. An internal swab contained Uddin's DNA. After being bailed in early 2015, Uddin left the country and was later extradited from Germany. Defence counsel James McLernon suggested the victim lied and instigated sex, which she denied. Prosecutor Richard Thatcher argued Uddin exploited the family's spiritual beliefs. The trial continues.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s 2020 Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2020, reports three operating segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services. The company reported 2020 net sales of $386.1 billion, operating income of $22.9 billion, net income of $21.3 billion, and operating cash flow of $66.1 billion. As of year-end, it held $84.4 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities, and employed approximately 1,298,000 full-time and part-time employees. Vale of Glamorgan Brewery has applied to open the Radyr Tap, a micropub in Station Road, Radyr, which has been without a pub since 2003. The proposal follows a Twitter campaign by a local resident. A consultation runs until June 19, when Cardiff council will decide. Managing director Phil Newbould said the venue will serve local and craft beers, wines, and spirits, with takeaway options, and will offer snacks, artisan meats and cheeses, but no cooked food.

Michael T. Klare contends that President Trump aims to supplant the existing liberal world order with a new system dividing nations by energy preferences: fossil-fuel "carbonites" versus "post-carbon" green-energy states. Trump seeks a trilateral alliance of the United States, Russia, and Saudi Arabia—which together with linked petrostates control roughly 57% of global oil and 59% of natural gas production—while isolating renewable-energy leaders like Germany and China. His steps include revitalizing the U.S.-Saudi alliance through a $110 billion arms deal and energy cooperation; weakening NATO and alienating green-leaning European allies; and withdrawing from the Paris climate accord to promote domestic coal, oil, and natural gas production. Though efforts to improve U.S.-Russia ties and lift sanctions have been hindered by domestic political turmoil over election meddling allegations, energy cooperation remains a stated priority, as evidenced by a recent Russo-Saudi summit.

Prosecutors released three cellphone videos of Nikolas Cruz in which he details his plan to be the next school shooter and kill at least 20 people at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School before the February 14 attack that killed 17 and injured 17. Cruz discusses attack logistics and expresses anger. He faces 17 murder and 17 attempted murder charges; his lawyers seek a guilty plea for life without parole, but prosecutors pursue the death penalty. The videos were released under Florida public records law during pretrial discovery. Cruz has a history of emotional disabilities, expulsion, and violence against animals.

Clark County Schools Superintendent Pat Skorkowsky retired after 30 years, citing a graduation rate increase from 60 to 83 percent and expanded magnet school seats. He noted $60 million budget shortfall and urged successor Dr. Jesus Jara and board to meet with lawmakers in the 2019 legislative session. Skorkowsky advocated for Clark County to retain locally generated marijuana tax revenue, cited school safety improvements, and called for more mental health professionals. He advised Jara to engage community.

Fifty years after Paul Ehrlich’s *The Population Bomb* used a Delhi slum to illustrate overpopulation, critics note similar crowding occurs in wealthy Western cities, raising questions about racial bias in environmental fears. Although megacities in developing nations are growing rapidly, urban areas actually reduce fertility rates and are a solution to population growth rather than its cause. However, cities generate a “consumption bomb,” accounting for three-quarters of global material use and massive waste output, exemplified by London’s enormous resource consumption.

A survey of 304 Belgian medical students across four universities found that knowledge and exposure regarding global surgery were lacking despite strong student interest. Only 24.7% of students had been exposed to global surgery, most commonly via social media, and knowledge of key statistics, Bellwether procedures, and stakeholders was poor. Nevertheless, 95% considered global surgery a relevant topic, 70% supported more compulsory teaching, and 75.3% wanted additional exposure, preferring optional or required teaching programmes, events, and clinical internships; clinical aspects were ranked highest for further learning. While approximately half were interested in surgical careers and over one-third in global surgery or global health, students identified obstacles including personal or family responsibilities, language barriers, lack of established career paths, financial constraints, and a lack of role models and mentorship. Master’s students were less likely than bachelor’s students to desire compulsory global surgery education or additional exposure. The study concludes that global surgery is rarely incorporated into Belgian medical curricula and advocates for integrating pre-clinical seminars and equitable, bidirectional international clinical internships into formal undergraduate education to help meet projected 2030 global surgery workforce needs.

Caterpillar's board maintained its quarterly dividend at $0.77 per share, marking the seventh consecutive quarter without an increase despite a 23-year history of dividend growth and a current yield of 3.25%. While Goldman Sachs added the stock to its "conviction buy" list with a $120 price target, citing improving mining spending, shares have already risen approximately 20% over nine months amid optimism surrounding Trump's pro-energy policies and potential infrastructure spending. However, the author cautions that the stock trades at elevated valuations of 29 times current year earnings, Trump's infrastructure plans remain uncertain, and the company faces declining revenues, earnings, and cash flows with weak 2017 guidance. With the stock near 52-week highs and macro improvements already priced in, the author advises investors to exercise caution rather than buy into recent optimism.

Global equity markets declined as U.S. 10-year Treasury yields neared 3 percent, hitting their highest in over four years amid concerns about government debt and inflation. Commodities fell after the United States hinted it might relieve sanctions on Russian aluminum producer Rusal, pressuring materials stocks. The dollar rose to a seven-week high. Oil prices recovered to close higher after volatile trading. U.S. stocks were mixed ahead of earnings from more than 180 S&P 500 companies, which are expected to report their strongest first-quarter profit gains in seven years.

The authors introduce EchoingECG, a probabilistic student-teacher framework integrating PCME++ and ECHO-CLIP to estimate echocardiogram variables from electrocardiograms. To address complex ECG signals and temporal variability, the framework uses probabilistic vision-language modeling with many-to-many mappings instead of deterministic one-to-one contrastive learning. To reduce dependency on scarce annotated ECG-ECHO datasets, ECHO-CLIP acts as a teacher to distill knowledge into ECG representations through ECHO-ECG pair training. Contributions include a probabilistic multimodal ECG model, a student-teacher distillation method, and uncertainty-aware downstream evaluation.

Steve Stephens broadcast Robert Godwin's fatal shooting on Facebook Live; the video remained up over two hours. US activist Hugo Castro is missing in Mexico after pleading for help on Facebook Live. Democrats hope Jon Ossoff wins Georgia’s 6th District House seat, raising $8.3 million.

Section 11 provides mechanical, packaging, and orderable information for the ADS8681W, ADS8685W, and ADS8689W, which is current but subject to change without notice. It includes footnotes on product status, material types, RoHS values, lead finish options, moisture sensitivity levels, and part marking conventions, along with mechanical dimensions and pin 1 orientation quadrant assignments. Texas Instruments provides all technical resources "AS IS" without warranties, limits liability to the annual purchase price, and states that users are solely responsible for product selection, application design, validation, and compliance. These resources are for development use only, subject to change without notice, and do not grant intellectual property licenses.

A 2018 test of 124 VPN and proxy providers found 20 leaked users' real IPs via WebRTC, while 101 did not. The passage lists specific leaking and non-leaking providers, links to test for leaks, and notes most browsers enable WebRTC by default except Tor Browser, Edge, and Internet Explorer. Users are advised to disable WebRTC or install an add-on if leaks are detected.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on April 20, 2022, reporting its financial results for the quarter ended March 31, 2022, by posting its First Quarter 2022 Update on its website and attaching it as Exhibit 99.1. Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn signed the filing.

Researchers led by Hebrew University PhD student Omri Yosef and Prof. Michael Berger, in collaboration with scientists from Philipps University of Marburg and the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center, found that blocking the Ant2 protein reprograms T cell metabolism in mitochondria. This metabolic shift makes immune cells more active, resilient, and effective at identifying and killing cancer cells. The rewiring can be triggered through genetic modifications or drugs, suggesting potential new clinical applications for cancer immunotherapy.

The U.S. Patent and Trademark Office rejected Crocs' design patent after a five-year legal battle, finding another company filed a similar patent earlier. Crocs plans to appeal the ruling, which comes as the struggling company closes 160 stores and faces declining revenue.

Mark Ryan, headteacher of St. Patrick’s Catholic Primary School in Thornaby, was the subject of an inaccurate newspaper report claiming he took a two-week term-time holiday abroad for a wedding and threatened a parent with fines for a similar absence. In fact, school governors sanctioned a three-day leave (June 7–9) for a close family friend’s wedding as an “exceptional circumstance” under school policy. Ryan, who had requested only one other day off in 22 years, received strong support from governors, staff, parents, parish priest Father Michael Keogh, and the local community. Gary Wilson, chair of governors, defended Ryan’s commitment to the school and stated that leave requests are assessed on individual merits for both staff and parents.

Current cytogenetic testing for hematologic malignancies relies on multiple low-resolution, subjective methods. Optical Genome Mapping (OGM) is emerging as a comprehensive alternative. This study piloted a workflow using Bionano Access/Solve and Variant Intelligence Applications (VIA) software to analyze and report OGM data for ten retrospective myeloid neoplasm cases (nine AML, one MDS), with each case reviewed independently 5–6 times by technologist-director teams to assess reproducibility and efficiency. OGM detected all variants identified by standard of care (SOC) testing and revealed additional reportable findings in five of six positive cases, including complex rearrangements and copy number variants not resolved by karyotype or FISH alone. Tier 1A guideline variants were unanimously identified and classified, while some variability occurred in non-tier 1A variant reporting. Technologist review in VIA averaged approximately 25–47 minutes depending on case complexity, representing roughly a 50% reduction compared to Bionano Access alone. The authors conclude that OGM with VIA offers a streamlined, efficient, single-assay approach to detect and report cytogenomic variants in hematologic malignancies, potentially standardizing interpretation and alleviating laboratory labor shortages.

This study presents a bibliometric analysis of academic publications on Digital Accessibility in Education from 2013 to 2024 using Web of Science (WoS), Scopus, and ERIC databases. The research identifies a significant increase in publications, particularly after 2020, with 502 publications on digital accessibility and 339 on digital accessibility in education recorded in 2024. Scopus hosts the majority of publications across all categories. Journal articles constitute the most common publication type, while primary research areas include Digital Accessibility and Inclusion, Education and Social Sciences, and Computer Science. English is the dominant language, and the United States, United Kingdom, and Spain produce the most publications. Higher education represents the most frequently studied educational level. Citation analysis of WoS data identifies Gorriz (2023) as the most cited document, Chen Weiqin as the most cited author, and the United States and United Kingdom as the most cited countries. The study concludes that digital accessibility research has grown substantially following the COVID-19 pandemic, but greater international collaboration, stronger legal frameworks, and enhanced inclusivity efforts are needed.

Chris King, 57, who received the UK's first double hand transplant last year after a work accident, attended his first rugby match at Headingley Carnegie Stadium. He watched Leeds Rhinos beat Widnes Vikings 42-22, drew the winning golden gamble ticket on the pitch at half-time to applause, and described the day as fantastic.

Jeremiah Merekula says suicide is taboo in Fiji, which has one of the highest rates globally. Since 2011 to March this year, 627 suicides and 694 attempts were recorded, including 56 child suicides and 97 child attempts. He blames lack of help-seeking behavior, community support, and awareness. Lifeline Fiji runs a 24/7 helpline and works with students and parents on emotional wellbeing.

Global stocks fell on Tuesday after U.S. 10-year Treasury yields crossed 3 percent for the first time since January 2014, with the 2-year yield reaching 2.5 percent for the first time since September 2008. European and U.S. indexes declined, though U.S. earnings have been broadly strong. Alphabet dropped 4.93 percent on higher costs and chipmaker AMS slumped on weak sales. Brent crude oil rose above $75 per barrel, its highest since November 2014, supported by OPEC-led production cuts and potential U.S. sanctions on Iran.

Henry L. Stimson advised against raising territorial adjustments or trusteeships, arguing it would provoke distrust, and recommended deferring the subject until the war advanced further and Russia participated in the Pacific war. At a January 26, 1945 meeting in Washington with diplomatic representatives of certain American republics, Under Secretary Grew outlined plans for a Mexico City conference, noted comments from ten republics on the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals, and discussed strengthening the inter-American system. He asserted that preserving peace requires drastic measures and that the world organization must be prepared to use force.

In Hardin v. White, the court held that an injunction bond need not equal double the judgment when the plaintiff seeks only to enjoin the sale of specific property under general execution, not to restrain collection of the judgment itself. The court further held that a judgment creditor who sells real estate under execution for part of a judgment cannot later sell the debtor’s statutory right of redemption under a second execution for the remainder, even if that execution issues under a different decree, where the underlying debt is the same and the creditor is entitled to only one satisfaction. On rehearing, the court rejected the defendant’s factual objections, clarified that two decrees covering the same indebtedness must be treated as identical for this purpose, and affirmed the judgment.

The IMF released a report urging China to prioritize financial stability over development goals, as the pursuit of regional growth targets and job retention has fueled a surge in debt, particularly at the local government level. The fund recommended forming a financial stability sub-committee, increasing staff for the banking watchdog, and improving coordination among regulators to contain risks from high credit growth and rapidly expanding wealth management products. Stress tests of 33 banks revealed potential widespread under-capitalization under a severely adverse scenario, with a capital shortfall equal to 2.5 percent of GDP and nonperforming loans rising to 9.1 percent. China's central bank acknowledged the report's relevance but stated the stress tests do not reflect the full picture and that China has a strong ability to mitigate financial risks.

Chrissy Teigen discussed her anxiety and postpartum depression (PPD) in a Marie Claire interview. Diagnosed shortly after her daughter Luna’s birth in 2016, Teigen experienced PPD for four months and now takes an antidepressant. Despite ongoing struggles, she hopes to expand her family and uses her platform to raise awareness about mental health, encouraging others to seek help.

The Los Angeles Dodgers defeated the Arizona Diamondbacks 9-5 in Game 1 of the NL Division Series on Friday night. Justin Turner homered and drove in five runs, tying a Dodgers postseason record. Clayton Kershaw earned the win despite becoming the first pitcher in franchise history to allow four home runs in a postseason game, yielding solo shots to A.J. Pollock, J.D. Martinez, Ketel Marte, and Jeff Mathis over 6 1/3 innings. Arizona starter Taijuan Walker lasted just one inning in his playoff debut. Yasiel Puig and Corey Seager each drove in two runs for the Dodgers. Game 2 features left-handers Rich Hill and Robbie Ray on Saturday night.

Home Capital Group is negotiating with banks to secure roughly $2 billion to replace an April emergency credit line. Depositors withdrew 95% of savings funds after the former CEO's termination and regulatory accusations, though withdrawals slowed by mid-May. It seeks a rate 2–3% above funding costs.

The narrator enrolled part-time in a journalism program approximately six years ago, transferring credits from an early-1990s associate degree. Uncertain of a specific career goal, they remained open to possibilities while learning new technology alongside predominantly younger peers. Returning to school in their 40s, they rediscovered enjoyment in academic work, healed from junior high bullying that had previously damaged their academic performance, and passed challenging courses. They earned good grades, joined an honors society, contributed to campus media, and attended campus events. After graduating and celebrating on stage, they are now entering a digital storytelling graduate program as a research assistant.

An internal Enron email dated March 19, 2001, circulated news clippings regarding California’s energy crisis. Articles reported that San Diego’s air pollution board voted 4-1 to let the Cabrillo power plant exceed nitrogen oxide emission limits to maintain electricity supply, though burning fuel oil instead of natural gas could increase ozone. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) ordered six suppliers—Dynegy, Williams Energy, Duke Energy, Portland General Electric, Reliant, and Mirant—to justify February prices or refund about $55 million, following a similar January order for $69 million; state leaders and consumer groups criticized the refunds as inadequate given multi-billion-dollar monthly power costs and the $430 per megawatt-hour threshold as too high. OPEC’s decision to cut oil output by 4% prompted Energy Secretary Spencer Abraham to call for increased U.S. domestic production, while Senator Schumer suggested using the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. Various groups used the crisis to advance agendas: automakers unsuccessfully opposed California’s electric vehicle mandate, manufacturers sought overtime rule flexibility, and Westlands Water District sued over Trinity River flows. The Department of Water Resources was spending roughly $350 million weekly on the spot market for near-bankrupt utilities PG&E and Edison, while creditors moved to force Edison into involuntary bankruptcy, causing sharp stock declines. PG&E revised its “Block 50” rolling blackout exemption list, removing about 810,000 customers while adding 690,000. An opinion piece criticized politicians’ attacks on “out-of-state profiteers” as parochial, arguing that wealth transfers cross business rather than state boundaries and that a regional electricity market would be more efficient.

Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a genetic disorder causing abnormal, sickle-shaped hemoglobin cells that do not last as long as normal cells and can block blood vessels. While it affects all backgrounds, it is most common in people of sub-Saharan African descent and specific other regions, impacting about 100,000 people in the U.S. Symptoms include severe pain episodes called sickle cell crises, acute chest syndrome, anemia, jaundice, organ problems, strokes, and infections. Smoking increases the risk of pain episodes and acute chest syndrome. Diagnosis requires a simple blood test, often performed at birth in the U.S., and prenatal tests are available. Management involves regular screenings, vaccinations, daily antibiotics until age five, pain treatment, and potentially blood transfusions or hematopoietic stem cell transplantation for severe cases. Lifestyle recommendations include avoiding tobacco smoke, eating a balanced diet, limiting alcohol, getting plenty of rest, and regular exercise. Medical advancements have improved understanding and quality of life for those with this lifelong condition.

The S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed at record highs, aided by AMD gains. AppLovin shares plummeted after Bloomberg reported that the SEC is investigating the company over data-collection practices and potential targeted-ad violations, following a whistleblower complaint and short-seller reports. The stock had jumped about 80% this year after soaring over 700% in 2024 due to AI ad technology, though short-sellers have criticized its ad tactics.

The speaker credits the players' will to win, preparation, and execution, noting the veteran leadership group has a businesslike approach and understands the importance of response games. He praises Sid for his drive to be the best, exceptional off-ice habits, and example-setting leadership; Jake for his hockey sense, competitive quiet confidence, poise with the puck, and playoff body of work; and Matt Murray for making timely saves, calling it the best game the team has played in the series. He states the team has improved each game and maintains an objective assessment of its play. He says extra rest helps both teams after a long playoff grind, resulting in higher-quality, faster-paced games, and notes the comfort of playing at home before supportive fans. He highlights Horny's north-south physical game, net-front presence, and contagious passion. He emphasizes short-term focus on one game at a time, notes both goalies have performed well in their respective home buildings, and says the team views the upcoming game as a resilient response to a great challenge and opportunity.

Research by the University of Exeter indicates that traditional, inefficient sail-driven fishing methods using hand-hauled dredges sustain oyster stocks in Cornwall's Fal fishery, Europe's only remaining sail-driven commercial fleet. Mechanising the fleet could increase fishing nine-fold and threaten the fishery's survival. While oyster stocks have declined due to disease and motorised fishing, the study concludes these centuries-old methods prevent overfishing and offer insights for sustainable fishery management.

The author expresses fear of violence and an inability to distinguish good from evil due to youth. They describe extreme bullying in schools and on social media, unreported due to fear and unrecognized by adults. Some bullies believe they help victims or act from unhappiness. The author urges ending bullying through kindness at home and school and invites readers to improve the world for future generations.

In a March 26, 1986 opinion, Bankruptcy Judge Clive W. Bare denied a motion to dismiss by East Tennessee Equity, Ltd. and Theodore A. Erck in an action by Thomas E. DuVoisin, as Liquidating Trustee for Southern Industrial Banking Corporation, to recover alleged fraudulent conveyances under 11 U.S.C.A. § 548. Rejecting defendants’ arguments that the trustee lacked standing and that recovery would not equalize creditor distributions, the court held that 11 U.S.C.A. § 1123(b)(3)(B) authorized the trustee to enforce claims retained under the confirmed Modified Plan of Reorganization, and that recovering fraudulent conveyances would benefit impaired unsecured creditors by increasing the value of their stock and ownership rights in the successor-in-interest. The court distinguished cases where plaintiffs sought recovery solely for their own benefit rather than for creditors.

Islamic finance has thrived despite 2016 economic shocks, expanding at 19.7% annually with capital at $3 trillion. Over 300 Islamic banks operate globally, gaining popularity in non-Muslim countries including the UK and US. Consumers increasingly view it as a stable alternative to conventional banking. Over half of Islamic banks are investing $5 million to $20 million in digital initiatives. World Finance Islamic Finance Awards recognize excellence in the sector.

Social media influencers are credible users with large followings whose posts are highly valuable for businesses affected by algorithm limitations. The passage identifies four local influencer types—food bloggers, food enthusiasts, community leaders, and local celebrities—who may enthusiastically promote businesses such as pizzerias, and introduces steps to find them.

Apple Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended December 30, 2017 (Q1 2018) reports net sales of $88.3 billion, up 13% year-over-year, and net income of $20.1 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $3.89. Gross margin was 38.4%. Net sales grew across all geographic segments, led by 26% growth in Japan and 14% in Europe. iPhone net sales rose 13% to $61.6 billion despite a 1% decline in unit sales, while Services and Other Products grew 18% and 36%, respectively. Mac net sales and units both declined 5%. The company repurchased $10.1 billion of common stock, paid $3.3 billion in dividends, and issued $7.0 billion in term debt. The enactment of the U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act in December 2017 resulted in a provisional tax charge of $2.6 billion, contributing to a 25.8% effective tax rate; the company anticipates a 15% effective rate for the remainder of 2018. As of December 30, 2017, Apple held $27.5 billion in cash and cash equivalents, with total assets of $406.8 billion, total long-term debt of $103.9 billion, and total shareholders' equity of $140.2 billion.

Thousands of Budget $aver Cherry Pineapple Monster Pops and Sugar Free Twin Pops distributed in 15 states are recalled for potential Listeria contamination. The FDA warns it can cause serious infections, miscarriages and stillbirths.

Coach Quenneville discussed an intense playoff series, describing it as a relentless battle and commending both teams. He noted Toews has an upper-body injury and is hopeful to be ready for the next game. He praised Corey as rock solid, highlighted line chemistry, and emphasized balanced scoring across all lines. Quenneville stressed forechecking, physical play, speed, strong starts, face-offs, puck possession, and defensive awareness. He addressed home-ice advantage, keeping Viktor ready, ice conditions, special teams, and the importance of sustaining momentum after back-to-back losses. He acknowledged scoring is limited in tight games and called for a consistent approach on both sides of the puck.

Heikin Ashi is a Japanese charting technique, meaning "average bar," imported to the West in the late 1990s and popularized by Dan Valcu in 2004. Unlike traditional candlesticks that display actual open, high, low, and close prices, Heikin Ashi uses calculated values—specifically haClose (the average of the four prices), haOpen (an exponential moving average of the previous haClose with an effective period of 3), and haHigh/haLow derived from the current period's high/low and haOpen—to smooth price movements and highlight trends or consolidation phases. Because its values are artificial and lagging, it cannot be used directly for trade execution and functions as a supplemental indicator rather than a replacement for standard candlesticks.

The article presents backtested strategies demonstrating Heikin Ashi is most effective on long time frames. A simple trend-following approach—buying when haClose crosses above haOpen and selling when it crosses below—tested on the S&P 500 monthly from 1960 produced profitable results with a 49.4% win ratio and favorable asymmetric profit/loss distribution. An alternative mean-reversion strategy incorporating an ADX filter also showed positive metrics, including a 5.27% CAGR with low market exposure. The authors note that Heikin Ashi's parameters can be customized to filter noise.

The article outlines a "Get Rich Portfolio" strategy, arguing that stocks are the best asset class for building wealth over decades. Citing Jeremy Siegel's 1801–2021 research, it states stocks vastly outperformed bonds, bills, and gold. It notes that wealthy individuals are typically business owners, and buying stocks makes investors co-owners of profitable companies. The strategy selects liquid, diversified ETFs ranked by Return/MaxDD ratio, accepting that high drawdowns are the price for superior returns and do not equal permanent losses. The authors propose a moderately aggressive portfolio of weighted stock categories, backtest it, and reference equity curves, drawdown charts, and performance statistics.

A Gallup poll found 44% of Americans believe Trump can prevent major scandals, versus 74% for Obama in 2009 and 77% for Bush in 2001. Trump inspired less confidence than past three president-elects across all categories. Dec. 7-11 poll of 1,028 adults has a ±4% margin of error.

World stocks rose and equity volatility neared record lows on Monday as investors focused on strong economic growth ahead of major central bank meetings, with the Federal Reserve expected to raise interest rates while the Bank of England and European Central Bank are anticipated to hold steady. European and Asian markets gained, supported by positive U.S. employment and Chinese trade data. Bitcoin futures debuted on the CBOE, trading at a premium to the underlying cryptocurrency, though several brokerages have not yet allowed trading and analysts noted the two markets appear disconnected. Sterling edged lower, the dollar index eased near a three-week high, and euro zone bond yields were lackluster. U.S. crude oil prices fell on signs of increased drilling, while spot gold edged slightly higher.

FOX 17 News (WXMI), a Tribune station in West Michigan, seeks a Weather/Multimedia Journalist with at least two years of commercial TV weather forecasting/reporting/MMJ experience. Responsibilities include delivering forecasts for broadcast and digital platforms, producing weather graphics, covering news, and creating content for all platforms. Candidates must demonstrate social media, editing, and shooting skills, and submit a demo reel and proof of digital journalism skills via tribunemedia.com.
Fabinho has reaffirmed his desire to leave Monaco, but vice-president Vadim Vasilyev said last month the club would not sell him or Thomas Lemar in this transfer window, calling them essential.

Trinidad and Tobago won the men’s 4x400 metres relay at the World Athletics Championships in London, denying the United States a seventh successive world title. Lalonde Gordon overtook Fred Kerley on the final straight to secure Trinidad’s first world title in the event in 2:58.12. The United States took silver and Britain won bronze. Jamaica, Bahamas and Botswana failed to qualify for the final.

Julie Armstrong forwarded a compilation of October 22, 2001 news articles to Danny McCarty and Stephen Dowd regarding Enron Corp. The articles reported that the SEC requested information on related-party transactions between Enron and limited partnerships run by CFO Andrew Fastow. Enron shares plunged approximately 20–21 percent to $20.65. Shareholders filed derivative and class action lawsuits alleging the board breached fiduciary duties and that Enron misrepresented financial transactions with the partnerships, which resulted in a $35 million charge, required repurchasing 55 million shares, and reduced shareholder equity by $1.2 billion. Enron posted a $618 million third-quarter loss and stated it would fully cooperate with the SEC, noting the arrangements were reviewed, board-approved, and disclosed. AG Edwards downgraded the stock to "hold," Moody's placed Enron's debt on watch for possible downgrade, and analysts estimated dismantling affiliated companies could cost up to $3 billion. The compilation also noted UniPrime Capital signed a letter of intent for a wind park project with Enron Wind Development Corp.

A 16-year-old girl from Waterloo, Iowa, visited a hair salon with severely matted hair after being unable to brush it due to severe depression. She asked to have her head shaved because she could not bear the pain of untangling it and felt worthless. Hairdresser Kayley Olson refused, spending 13 hours over two days untangling the hair and restyling it into a shoulder-length cut. Olson shared the experience in a Facebook post that was shared over 75,000 times, urging people to take mental health seriously. The teenager said she felt like herself again and would smile for her school pictures.

A 2013 YouTube video shows actress Allison Mack, arrested April 20 on sex trafficking and forced labor charges related to NXIVM, praising the alleged cult and affiliated group JNess. Mack discusses her desired legacy and names Lena Dunham and Miranda July as heroes. NXIVM founder Keith Raniere was arrested weeks earlier.

Tough overtime loss with missed opportunities. Third period success came from getting pucks to the net, but the opponent capitalized. Defeat was painful but a learning experience; going through a lot this season brought the group closer.

FHA loans require lenders to count both spouses' debts and credit when one married partner applies, even if the other is not on the mortgage, which can increase the debt-to-income ratio and reduce borrowing power. This rule applies only to legally married couples, not single or engaged individuals. Applicants whose spouses have credit that hurts the financial profile may consider switching to a conventional loan, which requires only 1.5 percent more down and lacks this requirement. Couples planning to marry may benefit from purchasing beforehand.

MIT Professor Aaron introduces a lecture series on nuclear arms control, highlighting the catastrophic human and climatic effects of nuclear war and introducing MIT Professor Vipin Narang to discuss the India-Pakistan flashpoint. Narang outlines nuclear deterrence theory, distinguishing between deterrence by punishment and denial, and notes the requirements of capability, credibility, and communication. He traces India’s nuclear program to its 1962 war with China and 1974 “Peaceful Nuclear Explosion,” followed by dormancy until Pakistan’s advances spurred weaponization, culminating in 1998 tests and a civilian-controlled assured retaliation posture with a no-first-use policy. Pakistan’s program, motivated by the 1971 war and Indian conventional superiority, began in 1972, utilized stolen uranium centrifuge designs and Chinese assistance, and evolved into a military-controlled asymmetric escalation doctrine featuring battlefield nuclear weapons designed for first use against conventional forces. Narang analyzes post-1998 crises—the Kargil War, the 2001 Indian Parliament attack, and the 2008 Mumbai attack—noting that Pakistan’s nuclear shield has enabled proxy militant attacks while constraining India’s conventional retaliation options. He warns that short missile flight times, immature command and control, the proliferation of tactical nuclear weapons to lower command levels, and the potential for mass-casualty terrorist attacks create severe escalation risks distinct from Cold War dynamics. He also notes the Reagan administration’s tolerance of Pakistan’s program during the Soviet-Afghan war and the subsequent AQ Khan proliferation network. Narang concludes that the combination of an active proxy-militant strategy and nuclear arms racing makes South Asia particularly unstable.

On October 22, 2001, U.S. stocks rose sharply despite widening anthrax concerns, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average gaining 1.9% and the Nasdaq Composite up 2.2%, supported by better-than-expected quarterly earnings from companies including American Express, 3M, and U.S. Steel. Enron Corp. shares plunged approximately 21% to $20.65 after the company disclosed that the Securities and Exchange Commission requested information regarding certain related-party transactions involving limited partnerships organized by Chief Financial Officer Andrew Fastow. Enron stated it would cooperate fully with the SEC and noted that its board had approved and been informed of the arrangements, which were disclosed in filings. The partnerships led to a $35 million charge and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity related to repurchasing 55 million shares. Multiple shareholder lawsuits were filed alleging breach of fiduciary duty and securities fraud, and AG Edwards downgraded Enron to "hold." The company also reported a third-quarter loss and took over $1 billion in charges, while analysts raised concerns that dismantling affiliated companies could cost up to $3 billion. Separately, UniPrime Capital Corporation signed a letter of intent for a partial interest in a wind park ground lease owned by Enron Wind Development Corp.

Corn futures are standardized contracts traded on the CME Globex platform that obligate the buyer to receive and the seller to deliver a specified quantity of corn at a future date; settlement is by physical delivery. The full contract represents 5,000 bushels (symbol ZCH) and the smaller contract represents 1,000 bushels (symbol XCH). A corn futures strategy comprises methodologies and techniques—incorporating technical and fundamental analysis, precise entry and exit signals, position sizing, and risk management—to trade these contracts profitably. Backtests of seasonal strategies referenced in the passage yielded disparate results, including one with a 70% maximum drawdown and another with an average unleveraged gain of 1.13% per trade over 175 trades, a 6-day holding period, and low correlation to equities. Corn prices are affected by weather in major growing regions, key USDA production and supply reports such as the WASDE, demand from China, and broader macroeconomic data. Seasonal tendencies indicate relatively stronger performance during January, February, April, May, October, November, and December compared with the summer months. Trading hours run Sunday to Friday from 5:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. CT with a one-hour daily break. The minimum price fluctuation is 1/4 cent per bushel ($12.50) for full contracts and 1/8 cent ($1.25) for smaller contracts. The all-time high for corn futures was 831.25 cents in 2012, while the all-time low was 100.7 cents in 1960. Significant risks include adverse price movements magnified by leverage and the potential for physical delivery if positions are not closed before expiry, though retail brokers typically close such positions automatically. Alternatives to futures include CFDs and the Teucrium Corn Fund ETF (CORN).

The Side Screen is a continuous on-ball side screen motion offense burdening defenses through quick options, ball reversal, and player movement. Entries include the High Post Rub, Dribble Clear, and Pass & Clear. Basic actions feature wing drives with options to drive, shoot, pass to the post, or kick out. Continuity involves screener rolls, back cuts, reversals, and hand-offs. Counters include post slips against shows and recovers, mismatch isolations against switches, and string-out to 2-1-2 against traps.

The Supreme Court will hear a case on whether state “affidavit of merit” statutes for medical malpractice apply in federal court. The case involves Harold Berk, who sued a Delaware doctor and hospital in federal court because the parties are from different states, though he lacks the state-required affidavit attesting to negligence. Lower courts dismissed the case, treating the statute as substantive under the doctrine from a 1938 Supreme Court case holding that federal courts apply state substantive law but federal procedural rules. Berk argues that federal pleading rules preempt the requirement, while the defendants and supporting states contend there is no conflict and the statute substantively limits malpractice claims. Law professors argue that applying the state requirement in federal court would be chaotic.
