The Draw play is a run disguised as a pass, with a late handoff to exploit defenses expecting a throw. It is most effective in pass-heavy offenses or obvious passing situations but is vulnerable to interior blitzes, which offenses often counter by tagging an RPO. Against 3-4 and 4-3 fronts, offensive linemen take pass sets before blocking or climbing to linebackers, while the quarterback simulates a throw and the tailback takes a shuffle step before receiving the ball. Variations include the QB Draw, which utilizes an athletic quarterback's running ability and often includes a perimeter RPO, and the Lead Draw from 12-personnel Strong-I, where a tight end and fullback adjust blocking assignments.

The application describes methods, apparatuses, and systems for multi-user (MU) wireless transmission. It identifies limitations of IEEE 802.11ac group ID mechanisms, including limited group and user capacity, lack of support for multiple MU transmission schemes such as combinations of orthogonal frequency-division multiple access (OFDMA) and orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) MU-MIMO, and inflexible scheduling with high control overhead. Embodiments provide new MU clustering and scheduling mechanisms supporting numerous clusters, multiple downlink and uplink MU transmission schemes, and flexible per-transmission scheduling. Embodiments employ Null Data Packet (NDP) MU media access control (MAC) physical layer convergence protocol (PLCP) protocol data units (PPDUs) with PLCP headers containing NDP signal (SIG) fields that carry MU control information. A wireless transmit/receive unit (WTRU) may receive a frame, determine whether it meets an NDP condition, process the NDP SIG field to determine an NDP MAC frame type and MU control information, and generate a response. Detailed embodiments describe high efficiency (HE) NDP MAC PPDU formats, including HE-NDP-SIG-A and HE-NDP-SIG-B fields, and NDP MU control frames such as MU-request-to-send (MU-RTS), MU-clear-to-send (MU-CTS), MU-Poll, uplink response/request (ULR), MU schedule, and MU acknowledgement (ACK) frames for reserving transmission opportunities, scheduling resources, synchronizing users, and reducing MAC control overhead in downlink and uplink MU transmissions.

This work uses first-principles calculations to study how stacking geometry controls magnetism in bilayer chromium diiodide (CrI₂). The CrI₂ monolayer adopts a stripe-type antiferromagnetic (AFx) ground state. Among bilayer stackings, the indirect BA′ configuration with intralayer AFx and antiparallel interlayer alignment is the global ground state, whereas direct (AA, AB, BA) and high-symmetry registries are energetically less favorable. Bilayer formation narrows the electronic band gap and strengthens the dominant in-plane exchange couplings by roughly 6–10% compared with the monolayer, preserving the stripe antiferromagnetic order. The stacking symmetry determines which anisotropic interactions are allowed: Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions appear only in inversion-breaking indirect registries, while symmetric exchange anisotropy remains nearly independent of registry. Interlayer exchange is an order of magnitude weaker, yet its sign varies with registry and interlayer magnetic alignment, providing secondary control. Indirect stackings also enable an in-plane electric polarization (up to ~10 µC/cm²) and magnetoelectric coupling via broken inversion symmetry. These findings establish a hierarchy with intralayer exchange as the primary energy scale, stacking symmetry governing anisotropic terms, and interlayer exchange offering fine-tuning, highlighting bilayer CrI₂ as a platform for mechanically reconfigurable spintronic and multiferroic devices.

The Williams Vix Fix is a synthetic VIX indicator invented by Larry Williams in 2007 to create volatility readings for securities beyond the S&P 500, Nasdaq, and Dow Jones 30. While the VIX is derived from implied volatility of stock index options on the CBOE and represents market fear or complacency, the Williams Vix Fix uses the formula (Highest(Close,22) – Low) / (Highest(Close,22)) * 100 to measure price volatility over the last 22 trading days. It closely resembles the original VIX in levels, swings, magnitude, and timing. The article tested multiple trading strategies using the indicator: one on the S&P 500 since 1993 produced 322 trades with 0.5% average returns per trade and a profit factor of 2, while a QQQ strategy since 1999 generated 352 trades with nearly 1% per trade, a 75% win rate, and 12.7% returns compared to 9.2% for buy-and-hold. The indicator is mean revertive and works well on stock indices, including short positions, though it was not tested on other asset classes.

The passage presents pseudospin models for two lead-free organic crystals in the 5-Phenyl-1H-tetrazole (PHTZ) family—APHTZ and MPHTZ—which exhibit long-range ferroelectric (FE) and antiferroelectric (AFE) ordering stable above 410 K. Dipole moments arise from proton tautomerism in hydrogen-bonded tetrazole chains. For the canted FE APHTZ, a two-sublattice Ising model predicts FE order along the a-axis and AFE order along the b-axis; mean-field analysis yields a second-order phase transition, Curie-Weiss permittivity, and a field-induced 90° polarization rotation from the FE-I to FE-II phase under a transverse field, with a tricritical point at 409 K. For the uniaxial AFE MPHTZ, a four-sublattice model reduces to a two-sublattice AFE Ising model, predicting checkerboard AFE ordering, first-order switching to FE at low temperatures, a tricritical point at 413 K, and classical double hysteresis. The authors stress that available experimental data are insufficient for definitive parameter fitting and call for further measurements to test the models.

This study investigated whether genetic variations in vitamin B12 metabolism are associated with Parkinson’s disease (PD) risk, age-at-onset, and progression. Using genome-wide association study summary statistics, pathway-specific polygenic risk scores, rare variant analysis from whole-exome and whole-genome sequencing cohorts, and Mendelian randomization in individuals of European ancestry, the researchers found no robust evidence that common or rare variants in B12 metabolism genes are associated with PD risk. A pathway-specific polygenic risk score including all genes associated with B12 levels showed only nominal significance and did not survive correction for multiple testing. A rare variant association in the CUBN gene identified in one cohort was not replicated in the other and was likely a chance finding. Mendelian randomization revealed no causal relationship between B12 levels and PD risk, age-at-onset, or motor and cognitive progression, and no genetic correlation was detected. The authors suggest that lower B12 levels observed in PD patients may be attributable to non-genetic factors—such as gastrointestinal dysfunction, decreased oral intake, weight loss, and gut microbiota alterations—rather than genetic predisposition. Limitations include the restriction to European ancestry and underpowered datasets for PD progression. The study concludes that B12 metabolism likely does not play a prominent genetic role in PD development or progression, though addressing low B12 remains clinically important to prevent deficiency-related symptoms.

Lorna Gibson concludes a lecture on energy absorption in foams, explaining how to construct energy absorption diagrams from compressive stress-strain curves. By plotting energy absorbed normalized by the solid modulus versus peak stress normalized by the solid modulus on log-log scales, one obtains curves with linear elastic, plateau, and densification regions. The shoulder point—where the plateau ends and densification begins—marks the optimum for efficient energy absorption. These diagrams can be generated from experiments or foam models and can account for different relative densities, strain rates, and temperatures. For elastomeric foams, a single diagram represents all such foams because both modulus and plateau stress depend on the solid modulus; for foams with a yield point, diagrams are valid only for a specific ratio of solid yield strength to modulus. Gibson presents model equations for open-cell elastomeric and plastic foams to derive these curves. She then demonstrates selecting foam material, density, and thickness for impact protection using iterative methods with these diagrams, with examples including packaging and bicycle helmets. She ends with a discussion of woodpeckers, explaining that they lack special cranial cushioning but withstand high decelerations due to small brain size, brain orientation in the skull, and very short impact durations, along with adaptations like stiff tail feathers and zygodactyl feet. The next lecture will address sandwich panels.

Andrew Lo reviews Lehman Brothers' 2007 financial highlights—$19 billion in net revenue, $4 billion in net income, $145 billion in long-term capital, and $282 billion in assets under management—and notes its collapse nine months later. He attributes this vulnerability to Lehman’s high net leverage ratio of 16 to 1, explaining through mortgage examples that leverage amplifies losses; a small decline in asset value can rapidly wipe out capital. He discusses how subprime mortgages with low teaser rates led to defaults when rates reset, and that non-recourse loans allow homeowners to walk away. Lo notes the Federal Reserve was expected to cut interest rates to reduce pressure, though this carries inflation risks. He recounts that Lehman filed for Chapter 11 after the Fed and potential buyers like Barclays declined to provide a backstop, likely wiping out shareholders and hurting creditors. He predicts short-term Wall Street hiring freezes but long-term opportunities, especially for entry-level candidates. Lo then defines inflation and distinguishes nominal from real returns, approximating real return as nominal return minus inflation, and advises matching nominal cash flows with nominal discount rates and real with real. He introduces fixed income securities, describing types (treasuries, agencies, corporates, municipals, mortgage-backed, CDOs), the size of the U.S. bond market as of 2006, and participants (issuers, intermediaries, investors). He explains that bond valuation relies on discounting known cash flows, describes coupon and pure discount bonds (including STRIPS), and lists risks such as inflation, credit, timing, liquidity, and currency. He concludes that market prices of bonds embed forecasts of future interest rates.

The OpenChart-SE project addresses the scarcity of publicly available Swedish electronic health record (EHR) text for clinical natural language processing research by collecting artificial EHRs through citizen science. During a pilot phase from November 2021 to December 2022, 50 artificial EHRs were collected, reviewed by an experienced emergency physician for realism, and released as the open-source OpenChart-SE corpus (version 1) on Zenodo. The dataset covers diverse adult emergency scenarios with varying text lengths, patient demographics, and diagnoses, and is intended for training and validating clinical NLP tools. The project entered its main data collection phase in January 2023, inviting further submissions through its GitHub repository.

Three-dimensional light-field imaging captures complete volumetric scenes in a single snapshot without scanning, avoiding the speed-versus-signal trade-offs and photodamage associated with conventional confocal, multiphoton, and light-sheet microscopy. By recording both the spatial positions and directional components of light rays, it enables computational refocusing, synthetic aperture imaging, and high-speed volumetric reconstruction. Theoretical foundations date back over a century, but modern sensor and computational advances have enabled biomedical applications. The technique is grounded in the four-dimensional plenoptic function, typically parameterized as two-plane coordinates, and implemented using microlens or pinhole arrays in configurations such as unfocused, focused, defocused, wavefront-coded, and Fourier setups. While geometric optics provides an intuitive framework, wave-optics models are required for high-numerical-aperture systems to account for diffraction and achieve high-fidelity reconstructions.

In biomedicine, light-field microscopy acquires four-dimensional spatial-angular data in one camera exposure, enabling high-speed volumetric fluorescence imaging with reduced photobleaching. It has been applied to functional brain imaging in organisms such as C. elegans, zebrafish, and mice, as well as to subcellular and single-cell dynamics. Fourier and extended light-field microscopy improve resolution and reduce artifacts by sampling spatial frequencies. Light-field mesoscopy bridges microscopic and macroscopic scales, with systems like MesoLF, the computational miniature mesoscope, and RUSH3D enabling large-scale neural recording and wide-field 3D imaging, though depth and aberration limits remain. In endoscopy, light-field modules integrated into rigid or flexible probes provide real-time three-dimensional visualization and depth measurement for minimally invasive procedures, using microlens arrays, tunable liquid-crystal or electrowetting lenses, GRIN lenses, and fiber bundles.

Current challenges include an inherent trade-off among imaging speed, spatial resolution, and depth of field, because the space-bandwidth product is fixed; increasing angular sampling reduces spatial sampling. Strategies to mitigate this include scanning, multi-focal lenslets, and deep-learning-based virtual scanning, each sacrificing speed, depth range, or generalizability. High data throughput also limits speed, prompting compressive sensing, event-camera temporal sampling, and spatial compression methods such as squeezed light-field microscopy. Emerging meta-optics approaches use metasurfaces to manipulate phase, amplitude, and polarization in compact formats, though they currently require computational correction for aberrations. Artificial intelligence is increasingly used for fast, high-quality reconstruction via fully end-to-end or hybrid physics-informed networks, yet issues of generalization, interpretability, and hallucination persist. Together, these developments position light-field imaging as a powerful, complementary tool for rapid, volumetric biomedical imaging.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2015. Total revenues were $939.9 million, up from $620.5 million in the prior-year quarter, driven by increased Model S deliveries. The company reported a net loss of $154.2 million, or $1.22 per share, compared to a net loss of $49.8 million, or $0.40 per share, in the first quarter of 2014. Cash and cash equivalents were $1.51 billion as of March 31, 2015, down from $1.91 billion at December 31, 2014. Total assets were $6.12 billion and total liabilities were $5.24 billion.

Tesla has delivered over 66,000 Model S vehicles since June 2012. Gross margin for the first quarter of 2015 was 27.7%, up from 25.0% in the prior-year quarter. The company is developing Model X, with customer deliveries planned for late in the third quarter of 2015, and intends to introduce Model 3 in 2017. Tesla plans to increase combined Model S and Model X production capacity to over 2,000 units per week by the end of 2015 and expects to deliver approximately 55,000 vehicles in 2015. Capital expenditures for 2015 are anticipated to be about $1.5 billion, including investments in the Gigafactory, where first cell production is expected in 2016.

Research and development expenses rose to $167.2 million from $81.5 million, primarily for Model X development. Selling, general and administrative expenses increased to $195.4 million from $117.6 million due to global expansion. Net cash used in operating activities was $131.8 million, compared to $58.7 million provided in the prior-year period. Net cash used in investing activities was $432.3 million, and net cash provided by financing activities was $186.2 million.

As of March 31, 2015, $659.8 million principal amount of 1.50% convertible senior notes due 2018 were classified as current liabilities because the closing stock price exceeded 130% of the conversion price for the required period, making them convertible in the second quarter of 2015. The 2019 and 2021 Notes were not convertible and remained long-term. The company borrowed $77 million under its Warehouse Facility. Other expense, net, was $22.3 million, primarily due to $21.7 million in foreign currency exchange losses. Risk factors discussed include potential delays in Model X and Model 3 and risks regarding market acceptance of vehicles.

This paper examines the need to reform teacher education to prepare educators for 21st-century classrooms. It identifies five critical areas: integrating technology using the TPACK framework; fostering critical thinking and problem-solving through constructivist, inquiry-based methods; preparing teachers for diverse learners through inclusive, culturally responsive, and differentiated practices; promoting collaboration and lifelong learning via professional learning communities and ongoing development; and addressing global challenges such as climate change and social justice to promote global citizenship. Grounded in the TPACK framework and constructivism, the paper argues that teacher education requires a holistic, continuous approach combining technology, inclusivity, critical thinking, and global awareness to improve teaching practices and student outcomes.

The ADS9803 requires a sequence of register writes to initialize after power-up or reset, with a free-running sampling clock connected beforehand. Configuration registers define analog input ranges, bandwidth, common-mode voltage, and data interface output lanes. During normal operation, the device converts analog inputs to digital outputs using a free-running clock. Speed-boost mode supports up to 8 MSPS on a user-selected channel pair while the remaining six channels are idle. The 16-bit configuration registers reside in three banks and are accessed via SPI using 8-bit addresses; register bank 0 is always accessible, while banks 1 and 2 are selected through register 0x03. Register reads require setting SPI_RD_EN and SPI_MODE in bank 0. In a daisy-chain topology, CS and SCLK are shared across devices, SDO connects to the next device’s SDI, and the DAISY_CHAIN_LEN register configures the chain length; register writes require N × 24 SCLKs, and reads use a multi-frame sequence. Register functions include control of SPI mode, daisy-chain length, data format, digital test patterns, gain error correction, analog input bandwidth, power-down, reference selection, output data lanes, and common-mode range. For ATE applications, the device provides high-precision measurement with low total unadjusted error after calibration, supports multiplexed inputs using wide-bandwidth mode for fast settling, and operates from three power supplies with no required power-up sequence. Layout guidelines recommend placing bypass and decoupling capacitors close to respective pins without vias, keeping analog signals away from noise sources, and avoiding crossings between digital lines and analog signal paths.

The Arizona Supreme Court reversed the dismissal of a mandamus petition by the City of Bisbee against Cochise County Treasurer Daniel S. Kitchel concerning penalties and fees collected on delinquent city taxes from 1918 to 1931. The court held mandamus was proper against the treasurer because the funds were held in trust for the city and were never county property, rendering the county and board of supervisors improper defendants. The one-year statute of limitations did not bar claims for amounts collected through June 13, 1931, because the trust was not repudiated until the treasurer’s August 1931 notice refusing to remit; the action was filed within one year. However, a 1931 statute required that penalties and fees collected after June 12, 1931, be credited to the county general fund, barring the city’s claim for later collections. The case was remanded to overrule the demurrer against Kitchel for collections through June 13, 1931.

Oral communication during soccer games is critical and takes the form of short, standardized words or phrases ("calls") that must be immediately understood by all teammates. Players without the ball, particularly those behind it, are often best positioned to direct play because they have the best view of the action. The passage catalogs numerous calls organized by complexity—introductory, basic, intermediate, advanced, and specific to goalkeepers and Defensive Organizers—with meanings tied to specific tactical contexts such as dribbling, defense, passing, and set pieces. Coaches should teach these terms at age-appropriate intervals alongside relevant skills and tactics, ensuring all players learn the vocabulary even if not all calls are used. Some terms are duplicative, allowing coaches to develop a customized team vocabulary. Advanced concepts include decoy calling to influence opponents and non-verbal communication options for loud environments.

This study presents a field-deployable metagenomic next-generation sequencing protocol for detecting SARS-CoV-2 in clinical swab samples using Oxford Nanopore Technology. To overcome the low proportion of viral nucleic acid in metagenomic samples, the authors evaluated sample pretreatments and found that combining DNase I treatment with 0.22 µm filtration most effectively enriched viral reads, yielding 99.9% SARS-CoV-2-specific BLAST hits, 99.3% genome coverage, and a 525-fold increase in mean viral reads compared to no pretreatment. Individual samples with CT-values at or below 30 achieved 85.8–100% genome coverage and successful Delta variant (clade 21J) lineage typing after 20 hours, whereas samples with CT-values at or above 33 showed reduced coverage and typing failures. The workflow is designed to exclude large, non-mobile equipment such as centrifuges, thermal cyclers, and extraction robots, facilitating point-of-incidence detection. However, the method’s sensitivity is lower than RT-qPCR because it primarily detects extracellular viral RNA, and the study was limited to SARS-CoV-2, requiring further validation for other viruses.

Skinimalism is a skincare trend that simplifies routines to a few essential, high-quality products rather than complex multi-step regimens. According to Dr Hazel Parkinson, this approach protects the skin barrier, reduces irritation, and avoids conflicting active ingredients. Benefits include improved skin health—particularly for sensitive or ageing skin—enhanced wellbeing through reduced consumer pressure, and greater sustainability due to less waste and lower costs. While most people can benefit, those with specific conditions like acne, eczema, rosacea, hyperpigmentation, or menopausal skin may still need targeted actives such as retinoids, azelaic acid, or ceramide-rich moisturisers, applied thoughtfully rather than layered excessively. Transitioning to a minimalist routine should be done gradually, tailored to individual age, lifestyle, and skin tolerance.

A Consumer Reports investigation found that more than two-thirds of 23 popular U.S. protein powders and shakes contained lead levels in a single serving exceeding the publication’s daily safety limit, with some products containing over ten times that amount. Plant-based powders were the most contaminated category, averaging roughly nine times the lead found in dairy proteins, because plants absorb environmental heavy metals and processing can intensify contamination. The industry operates with limited federal oversight, no legal lead limits, and minimal FDA inspections. Consumer Reports advises against daily use of most protein powders, noting that average protein needs—0.8 grams per kilogram of body weight—are easily met through whole foods.

The Side Screen Offense, in which a larger player screens for a smaller ballhandler, risks dribble penetration if the on-ball defender is caught. Because switching allows the screener to post up the smaller defender, NBA teams prefer the “Show & Recover” method: the screener’s defender steps out to force the ballhandler wide while the on-ball defender chases over the screen, then recovers once the ballhandler is re-contained. The SOS defense provides three scenarios: above the free throw line, an aggressive contact switch, snuggle pass denial, and smothering the ballhandler; below the free throw line, a baseline trap and Triangle I formation; and an All-Out disruption that traps the point guard before any screen is set, forcing the offense into freelance play, with specific rotations on pass outs and a secondary trap if the screener receives the ball on a base roll.

The article reviews ten AI tools for 2023 designed to automate tasks, improve workflow, and increase productivity across various industries. Described tools include ChatGPT for language processing; DALL-E for image generation; Lumen5 for video and social media content creation; Grammarly for writing enhancement; OpenAI Codex and Tabnine for code generation and completion; Jasper AI for content writing; Surfer SEO for search engine optimization; Zapier for web automation; and Compose AI for natural language generation from structured data. The passage notes that while these tools offer advanced capabilities, their outputs may vary in quality, contain biases or inaccuracies, lack originality, or require significant computational resources, and they should be used as aids rather than replacements for human review and understanding.

The Centre told the Supreme Court it will grant pension benefits to Major Generals and equivalent ranks, including pre-2006 retirees. The court disposed of retired Major General Vains' contempt plea seeking One Rank One Pension, directing compliance within three months.

Speakers praised an individual's timely goals and composure, described setting up Arvi after losing the puck on a backhand, and cited third-period efforts to keep coming and use speed, Pekka's saves, and an empty net goal. They credited Freddy, Sissons, Jarnkrok, and Fiddler for stepping up and stressed the need to continue improving, particularly among centers, in the series.

The Trump administration delayed closing a loophole that exempts some drugs from Medicare price negotiation. The FDA approved another generic version of the mifepristone abortion pill, allowing three American companies to produce it; the decision triggered pushback from anti-abortion groups and Trump-aligned politicians but is unlikely to affect access. The combination of mifepristone and misoprostol accounts for roughly two-thirds of U.S. abortions. Amgen reported that its cholesterol-lowering shot Repatha prevented heart disease death, heart attack, and stroke in a 12,000-patient trial, meeting its two primary goals. The drug, available since 2015, generated $2.2 billion in global sales in 2024, up 36%, and analysts said the results could help it reach a broader market.

A new Hubble image of NGC 2775, located 67 million light-years away in Cancer, reveals a hybrid galaxy with a smooth, gas-devoid elliptical-like center and a dusty ring with star clusters resembling a spiral galaxy. Astronomers debate whether it is a spiral or lenticular galaxy. Evidence of past mergers includes a nearly 100,000 light-year hydrogen gas tail. The updated image adds observations of a red light wavelength emitted by hydrogen clouds around massive young stars.

Intermediate attacking runs in soccer build on individual movement by creating opportunities for the runner and teammates. While basic concepts like timing, spacing, and communication remain, advanced individual runs include back-door runs, drifting, doubling back, holding the run, recycled runs, and setting up defenders. Players also draw opponents away from teammates through decoy runs, dragging opponents, dropping the ball to a trailing teammate, and dummy runs. Teammates can perform offensive switches—horizontal, vertical, or cross-over exchanges—through oral calls or natural recognition, returning to original positions via communicated acknowledgment. Coaching tips emphasize preparing to receive passes, anticipating next moves before ball reception, and moving to meet the ball.

U.S. workers' wages and benefits grew 2.6 percent last year, fastest since 2015, with wages and benefits each up 2.5 percent. Trump touted the gain, but economists say wages should rise faster given 4.1 percent unemployment, noting in the late 1990s wages rose at 4 percent.

Gatwick Airport recorded its busiest July with 4.7 million passengers, up 2.4%, driven by 10.7% long-haul growth. Cargo rose 20.4%, California routes expanded significantly, and new flights to North American and Asian destinations are planned.

A semi-annual ISM survey released Dec 11 found US manufacturing and services firms expect continued growth and rising revenues in 2018. Manufacturing revenues are projected to rise 7.8 percent and services six percent. Over 60 percent of firms report difficulty finding workers, prompting wage increases. Capital expenditures are expected to rise 2.7 percent in manufacturing and 3.8 percent in non-manufacturing.

Jerry Coyne cited a YouTube video claiming CMB data supports a multiverse. The author argues the inflation models with purported evidence do not yield a multiverse with varying physical laws needed for Coyne's argument against fine-tuning. The passage also notes David Gross's Nobel Week Dialogue talk affirming science's resilience, though the author mentions a recent disturbing talk.

The speaker stated a kicking motion call went against the team and acknowledged the Ottawa Senators outworked them, citing penalties, frustration, and a lack of discipline and compete, though the team still had a chance. He praised Ottawa's depth players and noted Chris Kunitz has a lower-body injury unrelated to a prior one; while doctors cleared him to play, the coaching staff must decide if his conditioning suits the Stanley Cup Final intensity. He credited under-the-radar defensive contributions from O'Donnell and the strong play of Samuel Pahlsson's checking line, emphasizing the team must play its best game yet against the Senators.

U.S. hedge funds were active in FAANG stocks in the second quarter. Third Point increased its stakes in Alphabet and Facebook, while Omega Advisors cut its positions in Facebook, Netflix, and Amazon but kept its Alphabet stake unchanged. Jana Partners boosted its Whole Foods stake, later profiting from Amazon's acquisition. The moves largely proved profitable.

Rockefeller scientists led by Shai Shaham discovered an unusual compartmentalized cell-death process in C. elegans, where the tail-spike cell and a neuron sever their core from their extension; the core disintegrates while the extension degrades in two steps. They also found that the protein EFF-1 helps phagocytes seal extensions around dead cell remnants to consume them. The findings may apply to other animals and human disease, and could form a molecular framework for understanding phagocyte function.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2017, reports that the company designs, manufactures, and markets mobile communication and media devices, personal computers, and related software, services, and accessories, including iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, and operating systems iOS, macOS, watchOS, and tvOS. The company manages its business through five reportable geographic segments—the Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan, and Rest of Asia Pacific—and sells through direct channels (28% of 2017 net sales) and indirect channels (72%). Research and development expense was $11.6 billion in 2017. The filing identifies risk factors including global and regional economic conditions, intense competition, frequent new product introductions, reliance on single or limited-source components and outsourcing partners concentrated in Asia, inventory and purchase commitment risks, intellectual property litigation, international trade and currency fluctuations, data security and privacy obligations, and potential changes in tax rates. As of September 30, 2017, the company owned 13.4 million square feet and leased 23.0 million square feet of building space, primarily in the U.S. The company is subject to ordinary course legal proceedings but believes no material loss is probable. Its common stock trades on Nasdaq under the symbol AAPL; as of October 20, 2017, there were 25,333 shareholders of record. The company paid $12.6 billion in dividends in 2017 and expects quarterly dividends of $0.63 per share, subject to Board declaration, with plans for annual increases. In May 2017, the Board increased the share repurchase authorization to $210 billion, of which $166 billion had been utilized by September 30, 2017.

James Walker Morales escaped from Rhode Island’s Wyatt Detention Center on Saturday by climbing a basketball hoop, cutting a fence, and descending from the roof. Officers discovered the 7 p.m. escape at 10:30 p.m.; the prison is on lockdown and two officers were placed on leave. Morales, held on 2015 weapons theft charges, fled to Attleboro, Massachusetts, where police found bloody clothing and recovered a stolen car.

A U.S. government shutdown was expected after midnight as Republicans and Democrats blamed each other for failing to pass a funding deal. The Congressional Budget Office estimated about 750,000 federal workers would be furloughed, costing roughly $400 million per day in compensation. House Speaker Mike Johnson said Democrats were making irrelevant policy demands, including an extension of Affordable Care Act tax credits, and urged them to pass a stopgap bill. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Republicans would be responsible for a shutdown and that Democrats would not support a bill without health-care protections, warning that failure to extend ACA subsidies would cause higher premiums. Jeffries denied Republican accusations that Democrats wanted to provide federal health benefits to undocumented immigrants. Senate Majority Leader John Thune called the ACA tax credit issue a Democratic “made-up problem.”

An Ombudsman Services study found one in five British rail passengers is resigned to poor service, with complaints up 31% to two million last year over punctuality, overcrowding and customer service. Campaigners and an MP called for a rail ombudsman and stronger action. The Department for Transport cited £40 billion in investment and penalties for poor performance, while the Rail Delivery Group acknowledged service issues but noted a long-term complaint decline. Overall consumer complaints rose 6% to 55 million, with many feeling complaining is futile.

The IOMUX manages peripheral function selection and controls for digital IO output drivers, input paths, and SHUTDOWN wake-up logic; not all pins support analog functions, wake-up, drive strength control, or pullup/pulldown resistors, and 5V-tolerant open drain IO lack output-high PMOS, pullup resistors, and clamping diodes. A serial wire debug interface is provided via an ARM-compatible debug port. The boot strap loader enables device configuration and programming through UART or I2C, is protected by a 256-bit user-defined password, is enabled by default, and can be invoked during boot if the BSL_invoke pin matches the expected logic level, automatically if the reset vector and stack pointer are unprogrammed, or at runtime via a SYSRST with BSL entry command. A memory-mapped FACTORY region provides read-only device capability and trim data, with DEVICEID at address 0x41C4.0004 and USERID at 0x41C4.0008. For typical applications, TI recommends 10µF and 0.1µF low-ESR ceramic decoupling capacitors near VDD and VSS, a 47kΩ pullup with a 10nF pulldown capacitor on NRST, a 100kΩ resistor between ROSC and VSS if the SYSOSC frequency correction loop is used, a 0.47µF tank capacitor on VCORE with no other circuits attached, and pullup resistors for 5V-tolerant open drain IO used for I2C and UART. Device prefixes indicate development stage: X for experimental devices and MSP for fully qualified production devices. The April 2025 revision added PSA-L1 certification targeting, updated peripheral instance counts, clarified SRAM bank availability, added package variants, and revised electrical characteristics, thermal information, supply current, POR/BOR thresholds, flash endurance sector flexibility, ADC specifications, temperature sensor conditions, and other module descriptions. Mechanical, packaging, and orderable information is provided, including qualified automotive versions MSPM0G3518-Q1 and MSPM0G3519-Q1.

Anna Mae Blessing, 92, was arrested in Arizona on suspicion of murdering her 72-year-old son after hiding two handguns in her robe and shooting him multiple times in his bedroom. She told police she acted because he planned to place her in an assisted living facility. She is being held on $500,000 bail.

The passage presents low-temperature studies of YbCu1.14Se2, an exchange-disordered triangular magnet synthesized as single crystals with approximately 56.6% Cu occupancy. X-ray diffraction confirms a P-3m1 structure with a well-ordered triangular Yb lattice and disordered Cu vacancies. Magnetic susceptibility indicates a Kramer's doublet ground state with antiferromagnetic exchange. Specific heat measurements show no magnetic ordering transition, exhibit sub-linear temperature dependence fitted by a phenomenological model of disordered quantum singlets, and yield an integrated entropy of roughly 85% R ln(2) between 100 mK and 10 K. AC susceptibility reveals a frequency-dependent spin-glass freezing transition near 0.1 K, while field-dependent measurements lack the 1/3 magnetization plateau characteristic of ideal triangular QSL candidates. These results closely resemble YbMgGaO4 and align with theoretical simulations of disordered triangular magnets, suggesting possible universal behavior in disordered quantum spin liquid materials.

The passage describes a heterogeneous computing system comprising a multi-threaded, coarse-grained reconfigurable computing fabric referred to as a Hybrid Threading Fabric (HTF), designed to address performance, energy, and heat dissipation limitations of existing systems for compute-intensive applications such as Fast Fourier Transforms, finite impulse response filters, artificial intelligence, and 5G networking. The architecture includes configurable circuits, or “tiles,” containing configurable computation circuits, synchronous and asynchronous network interfaces, configuration memory with instruction and spoke/index memories, and control circuitry with memory and thread control circuits and control registers. The system utilizes a synchronous mesh communication network to create synchronous domains for pipelined data flow and an asynchronous packet network for control messaging, memory access, and bridging between domains. Key capabilities include dynamic self-configuration, self-scheduling, conditional branching, backpressure control, and ordered or looped thread execution managed through thread identifiers (TIDs), completion counts, loop tables, continuation and reenter queues, and priority queues. The system also incorporates dispatch and memory interfaces for work distribution and system memory access.

Penn State and USC meet for the 10th time overall and third time in the Rose Bowl, with USC leading the series 5-4. The 1923 game was the first Rose Bowl at the current stadium. Hugo Bezdek coached three different teams to the Rose Bowl in its first 102 games. Penn State has allowed two of the top passing performances in Rose Bowl history. USC will have played during every U.S. presidency since Herbert Hoover. Penn State ties Pittsburgh with its fourth Rose Bowl appearance. The Pac-12 leads the Big Ten 35-31 in head-to-head Rose Bowl matchups.

Point72 Europe London LLP and other hedge funds recently purchased or increased stakes in Hershey Company (NYSE:HSY), with institutional investors owning 51.39% of shares. Analysts assign a consensus "Hold" rating and a $111.55 price target. Insiders sold 4,504,500 shares in the last ninety days, including transactions by Michele Buck and D. Michael Wege. The stock trades near $108.83 with a $23.12 billion market cap, a P/E of 34.77, and a beta of 0.39. Hershey reported Q2 EPS of $1.09 and revenue of $1.66 billion, exceeding estimates. The company declared a quarterly dividend of $0.656 per share, yielding 2.41%. Hershey is a North American producer of chocolate and confectionery products.

Facebook publicly released its Community Guidelines, a detailed manual for human moderators outlining removable content. While one expert praised its transparency, the document blends broad principles—safety, voice, and equity—with bizarrely precise rules apparently forged in reaction to specific news events, such as extensive prohibitions against harassing crisis actors and a narrow definition of infant shaking. Regular internal meetings, described as mini legislative sessions, determine these policies.

A Lewisville mother works as a mystery shopper. Consumer Reports found FDA-approved Contrave produces only five to nine pounds more weight loss than a placebo after 56 weeks for obese or overweight patients with serious conditions. Risks include anxiety, insomnia, headaches, liver damage, seizures, and heart problems. Experts recommend diet, exercise, and behavioral programs.

The speaker, assuming the first executive office, thanks the people and acknowledges the task exceeds his abilities, yet finds encouragement in the wisdom of other constitutional authorities. He urges national unity after the recent contest of opinion, noting that majority rule must be reasonable and minority rights protected by equal law. He warns against political intolerance, argues that differences of opinion are not differences of principle, and expresses confidence in the strength of republican government. He advocates for a wise and frugal government that restrains citizens from injuring one another while leaving them otherwise free to pursue industry. He lists essential principles, including equal justice, peace and commerce with all nations without entangling alliances, support for state governments, preservation of the General Government, election rights, majority decisions, a well-disciplined militia, civil supremacy, economy, debt payment, encouragement of agriculture and commerce, diffusion of information, and freedoms of religion, press, and person. He pledges faithful administration, asks indulgence for unintentional errors, and declares readiness to retire if the people choose a better successor.

Mark Messier announced Robert "Knobby" Knudsen as the winner of the Bridgestone Youth Leadership Award, recognizing his advocacy for children and the Kids Skate for Kids program in Windsor; Knudsen's son and grandson accepted on his behalf. Messier also named Dustin Brown, Shane Doan, and Ryan Callahan as finalists for the Mark Messier Leadership Award, citing their on-ice leadership and off-ice community work. In a subsequent Q&A, Messier praised Brown's charity foundation and maturity, reflected on the difficulty of Stanley Cup playoff runs and a past Rangers-Devils conference final, and stated that NHL rule changes have restored speed, artistry, and skill. He expressed pride in the current Rangers team's development, noting the value of deep playoff experience and the need for organizational depth.

The paper proposes bivariate zero-inflated Poisson (BZIP) models for multivariate count data with excess zeros. The construction extends Liu and Tian (2015) by combining a common Bernoulli inflation factor with latent bivariate Poisson variables generated through comonotonic shocks (BZIP+, positive dependence) or counter-monotonic shocks (BZIP−, negative dependence) from Genest et al. (2018). The authors derive joint probability mass functions, distribution functions, probability generating functions, and correlation structures, analyzing how the inflation parameter and shock parameter separately influence dependence. Estimation is addressed via method of moments, two maximum likelihood implementations, and an EM algorithm. Simulation results across numerous scenarios indicate that likelihood-based methods generally outperform method of moments, though numerical difficulties occur more frequently in the negative dependence model and with high zero-inflation. An application to monthly Australian disaster data illustrates the models, revealing significant zero-inflation and dependence in flood/storm and flood/bushfire occurrences. Multivariate extensions for positive dependence are briefly discussed.

Torsten Sløk argues the U.S. economy is strengthening, not slowing, and criticizes economists for repeatedly forecasting weakness since January that has not materialized. The Atlanta Fed’s GDPNow model forecasts 3.9% third-quarter growth, while consumer spending, business investment, and housing show resilience. Sløk attributes slowing job growth to reduced immigration, not economic weakness. Morgan Stanley’s Mike Wilson contends the economy is transitioning from a three-year “rolling recession” to a “rolling recovery,” though ADP data showed September job losses and a negative August revision. Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell describes a “low-hire, low-fire” environment. Sløk warns that continued Fed rate cuts amid strong growth could increase inflation risks and says the forecasting community has damaged its credibility.

The speaker announces the removal of government offices to the permanent seat of government and congratulates Congress on assembling there. The speaker asks whether Congress will immediately exercise local powers over the District of Columbia, notes the discharge of the temporary army, and recommends improvements to the judiciary system. A treaty with Prussia has been ratified, while negotiations with Great Britain and France continue. The speaker advocates for a defensive navy, fortification of seaports, and domestic arms manufacture. Public revenue has exceeded previous periods. The speaker urges preservation of national institutions, resistance to dangerous innovations, and pledges cooperation.

Nobel Peace Prize winner Beatrice Fihn, executive director of ICAN, warned that a moment of panic or bruised ego could lead to nuclear destruction. She was obviously addressing escalating rhetoric between U.S. President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. Fihn said the risk of nuclear weapons use is greater today than at the end of the Cold War due to more nuclear-armed states, terrorists, and cyber warfare. ICAN is a coalition of NGOs working to ban nuclear weapons.

GoSun introduced the Fusion, a solar-electric oven enabling fuel-free cooking anytime, anywhere. Combining vacuum tube solar technology with a 150-watt electric heating element, it functions day or night, indoors or outdoors, and works through clouds and freezing temperatures. Weighing 10 lbs and feeding up to five people, it cooks at 350°F. GoSun launched a Kickstarter campaign offering exclusive deals to early backers.

Christian Bushman says CPR saved her life after a closet object struck her chest in May 2014. Her sister-in-law, CPR instructor Cathy Carson, performed CPR until emergency responders arrived. Bushman has since learned and taught CPR. A study says women are less likely than men to receive bystander CPR, possibly due to reluctance to touch a woman's chest. Visit We R CPR for certification.

Zimbabwe's Ministry of Health estimates about 44,586 female sex workers aged 15–49. HIV prevalence among them averages 55 percent, compared to the national 13 percent. The HIV and Aids Estimates Report shows AIDS deaths fell from 278 per day in 2005 to 71 in 2016, and 14 percent of Zimbabweans are HIV infected. A parliamentarian warned that ignoring key populations such as sex workers and prisoners may prevent ending HIV and Aids by 2030.

ADS7828 uses internal 2.5V or external reference. A +5V supply requires external reference for full range. Lower reference voltage reduces LSB size, magnifying offset, gain, and noise errors. Internal noise contributes 0.32LSB at 2.5V and 16LSBs at 50mV. Errors are Gaussian.

The lecture transitions from discrete Markov chain policy evaluation to continuous systems using function approximation. After reviewing temporal difference (TD) learning and its limitations in high-dimensional discretized state spaces, it presents least squares function approximation for estimating unknown functions from data. Neural networks are noted as a general but less favorable class for least squares; instead, linear function approximators—linear in parameters but employing nonlinear basis functions such as radial basis functions, barycentric interpolators, Fourier bases, or polynomials—are emphasized because they yield exact analytical solutions. This framework is applied to system identification, where rigid-body manipulator dynamics (e.g., pendulum, acrobot) are observed to be linear in their physical parameters, enabling parameter estimation via least squares from trajectory data, assuming sufficiently rich inputs.

The lecture then extends TD(lambda) to linear function approximators by replacing state eligibility traces with parameter eligibility traces, updating alpha using the gradient of the value estimate (phi(x) for linear cases). Convergence to the true value for 0 <= lambda <= 1 was proven by Tsitsiklis and Van Roy. To address data inefficiency in incremental updates, Least Squares Temporal Difference (LSTD) learning is introduced as a batch method that accumulates data to solve directly for alpha = A^{-1} b, eliminating the need for learning rates and reducing dependence on initial guesses. Incremental LSTD variants are noted for online or periodic systems like walking. The lecture concludes that function approximation enables scaling to higher-dimensional problems and previews subsequent coverage of policy approximation and actor-critic methods.

Most Southeast Asian stock markets edged lower on Monday as caution gripped investors ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy meeting starting Tuesday, with focus on whether policymakers forecast four rate hikes this year instead of three. Thai shares were the biggest losers, while Singapore and Indonesia also slipped. Philippine shares recovered from early falls to close marginally lower, Malaysia closed slightly higher, and Vietnam rose for a sixth straight session to its highest close since March 2007.

The U.S. District Court for the District of Nevada granted AAA Nevada Insurance Company’s motion for summary judgment, holding that Vinh Chau’s policy unambiguously limited liability to $100,000 per person. The court found that, following a fatal accident, Benjamin Buenaventura’s counsel sent a two-week demand to settle for policy limits but failed to identify all heirs or provide a release. Because AAA made repeated unsuccessful attempts to contact counsel to verify all potential claimants, it had a reasonable basis for missing the deadline, and its failure to settle did not constitute bad faith under Nevada law as a matter of law. The court denied the interveners’ Rule 56(f) continuance request, rejected their jurisdictional challenge, and noted the demand appeared to be part of a pattern by counsel to set up bad faith claims.

The passage provides guidance on academic essay writing for students. It states that essays are inescapable coursework and advises selecting interesting topics, using reliable sources, and editing carefully. Students should avoid restating the thesis or introducing new information in conclusions, and should evaluate internet sources for dependability. The text suggests that busy or struggling students can use custom essay writing services, which employ subject-specific experts to produce original papers, and notes that such services can assist with research and help students achieve high grades. It also recommends using tools such as the Hemingway application, FreeMind, and XMind to improve readability and organize ideas.

National Literacy Month highlights literacy inequities. Partnership for Growth LA’s south Los Angeles programs provide culturally responsive books and civic engagement, helping youth like Anastacia Nwosu become “Kid Mayor” and a California Assemblymember field deputy. A 2023–24 pilot increased English Language Arts proficiency by 14.5 points, cut chronic absenteeism from 47% to 5%, and improved social-emotional growth. Despite state approval of AB 152, budget cuts and uncertain federal funding threaten progress. Sustained local support and family reading tools are essential to cultivate leadership.

US$INR January futures are bearish; sell 68.20–68.30 with targets 67.95/67.75 stop loss 68.40. Indian bond yields fell most in eight years on cash-ban liquidity. Rupee posted a sixth straight annual loss. Dollar index fell 0.46% Friday. NSE January contract ended at 68.09; January and February open interest up 6.46% and 1.33%.

The Trap play is a quick-hitting, downhill run scheme in which a pulling guard kicks out an interior defensive lineman, making it especially effective against aggressive pass rushers. Its primary strengths are its speed, the deception it creates in identifying the ball carrier, and its use of angle blocks, which is advantageous for smaller offensive linemen. A key weakness is its difficulty against defenses that squeeze interior gaps, such as Bear fronts or even fronts with linemen in both A- and B-gaps. The passage outlines specific blocking assignments and backfield actions for running Trap against 3-4 Odd and 4-3 Even fronts. It also describes variations, including the Gun Trey Same-Side Trap RPO, which adds a run-pass option from the shotgun but leaves the backside inside linebacker unblocked, and the Wing-T Trap, which uses the same backfield action as the Buck Sweep to force defensive discipline.

A University of Edinburgh study reviewed by Andrew Masterson in Cosmos found that research on biodegradable plastic bags is inconsistent, poorly defined, and too varied to inform policy or regulation, questioning their environmental benefit over conventional plastics.

The passage details the AMD AGESA software interface for host BIOS integration. It describes a binary module execution model in 32-bit protected mode, deprecating 16-bit real mode, utilizing a Bridge to call the AGESA Dispatcher and a Router for CallOuts back to the host BIOS. The document covers UEFI implementation across SEC, PEI, DXE, and RTP phases, including PEIM modules for processor and memory initialization that publish various PPIs, and DXE drivers for late initialization and data table generation. It specifies build environments, tools, and configuration files such as `<plat>Options.c`. The text defines numerous procedures including `AmdInitReset`, `AmdInitEarly`, `AmdInitPost`, `AmdInitEnv`, `AmdInitLate`, and `AmdInitRtb` for system initialization, alongside `AmdCreateStruct`, `AmdReleaseStruct`, and `AmdReadEventLog` for memory management and event logging. It outlines requirements for stack establishment, Cache-As-Ram usage, and memory initialization parameters. Additionally, it describes S3 suspend and resume procedures (`AmdS3Save`, `AmdInitResume`, `AmdS3LateRestore`) for saving and restoring processor and silicon context. Host environment responsibilities include establishing a valid stack, preserving cache controls during Cache-As-Ram, and providing call-out router functions.
Hillview Middle School hosts an outdoor family movie night April 27 at 7:30 pm showing "Sing." One adult per eight children required. Food available. Proceeds benefit LLS and JDRF. RSVP requested.

The speaker addresses Congress to review United States foreign policy, stressing national unity and mutual trust between Americans and their government. He notes that alliances with industrial democracies remain strong, relations with the Soviet Union are more stable, and an opening with China has been achieved. He reviews American involvement in Indochina, stating that North Vietnam violated the 1973 Paris accords, leading to the current crisis in South Vietnam and Cambodia. He requests that Congress appropriate $722 million for emergency military assistance and $250 million for economic and humanitarian aid to South Vietnam, and asks for immediate clarification of restrictions on U.S. military forces to protect American lives and endangered Vietnamese by April 19. He also discusses the need to lift the arms embargo against Turkey, reconsider trade act provisions affecting OPEC nations, continue Middle East peace efforts, pursue a strategic arms agreement with the Soviet Union, maintain relations with China, and protect intelligence capabilities. He argues that the national security budget is the minimum required, urges Congressional action on energy independence, and calls for a unified foreign policy.

The passage describes systems and methods for dynamically providing video overlays. A client device identifies a set-top box presenting information overlaid on a video stream and, based on the identified set-top box and video data, selects a template corresponding to the presented information. The client device presents a replacement video stream along with the overlaid information, mimicking the original presentation by matching position, size, particular portions, alpha blending, and playback speed. The replacement video stream is selected based on the original video stream, which is identified by generating query fingerprints of frames, querying a database of known reference fingerprints, and determining a match. The system includes a query fingerprint generator, a reference fingerprint generator, a video identification system, a set-top box identifier module, a video source identifier module, a video overlay module, and a replacement content server that provides replacement video and templates. Templates correspond to set-top box identifiers and support picture-in-picture, menu overlay, and menu blend configurations. The client device detects changes in video input, modifies replacement video playback speed to match detected input speeds, and handles semi-transparent overlays by incorporating modified screen portions from the intermediate device into the video output stream.

Wayne Richert reported a 6.5-hour ER wait at Norfolk General Hospital, arguing doctors—not bureaucrats—should have authority to call in more doctors when waits exceed two hours. Donna Clarke criticized long-term care bed funding as pre-election timing, arguing seniors in long-term care should not pay medication fees while young people receive OHIP Plus.

Peter DeBoer expressed belief his team can win and turn the series around. He praised returning veterans for providing energy and a rookie for rising to the occasion under pressure. He noted the team needed a win to build momentum after struggling in previous games, but said the players remain resilient and enjoy competing together. DeBoer complimented a veteran player's composure, emphasized the need for scoring, and said the power play generated chances despite the opponent's strong goaltending and penalty kill. He stressed they must end their streak to avoid elimination.

Gas prices hit a 2017 high; national average reached $2.40, highest since 2015. Montgomery's average rose to $2.18. Analysts cited declining oil inventories and geopolitical tensions. GasBuddy predicted prices may peak soon; AAA forecast increases through September. Only 405 stations sold gas for $2 or less, versus over 80,000 last year.

Costa Coffee, the world’s second-largest coffee chain, has opened a new roastery in Basildon, Essex, near Tilbury Docks to support rapid growth. The facility quadrupled roasting capacity to 45,000 tonnes annually, producing up to 2.1 billion cups of coffee a year. The site features sustainable design, including solar panels, rainwater harvesting, LED lighting, and Rainforest Alliance Certified sourcing. Green coffee beans are cleaned, roasted, and monitored for colour and moisture to ensure consistent flavour, while robots pack the finished product, improving productivity by 25 per cent. Costa’s signature blend combines arabica beans for acidity and aroma with robusta beans—including those from Vietnam, the world’s second-largest coffee producer—for body. The company’s Master of Coffee, Gennaro Pellicia, has a £10 million insured tongue; the roastery can train 3,000 baristas annually and includes lab facilities where samples from every bag are tested and roughly 8 per cent of beans are rejected. Built with extra land for expansion, the site is planned to operate for at least 30 years.

Kinder Morgan rose on a pipeline sale. Bank of America fell on lower rates; Petrobras fell on a diesel subsidy. ZTO Express, Booz Allen Hamilton, American Woodmark, KB Home, and American Water Works rose on deals, earnings, housing data, and dividend demand.

The Kiss of Death is an S&P 500 sell signal that occurs when the index drops from an all-time high, falls below its monthly 21 EMA, rebounds above it, and then drops below its recent low. It has triggered infrequently since 1960, including in 1969, 1973, 1978, 2001, 2008, and September 2022, historically preceding major bear markets but generating a false signal in 2022. The trading rules call for selling when the signal triggers and buying back when the S&P 500 closes above its 10-month EMA. A backtest starting in 1967 showed the strategy improved on buy-and-hold returns with a higher CAGR and roughly half the maximum drawdown, though the passage notes it is not foolproof.

Alexis Bateman leads an MIT OpenCourseWare session on multi-stakeholder engagement in supply chains, using palm oil as a case study. The discussion explains that palm oil is a small but deeply embedded component of many products, with opaque supply chains involving growers, mills, middlemen, and major brands such as Nestlé. The class reviews how Greenpeace’s campaign against Nestlé, a consumer-facing brand, prompted the company to examine its sourcing, illustrating that targeting brands can be more effective than addressing deep-tier suppliers.

Students identify stakeholders for Golden Agri-Resources (GAR), including farmers, corporations, consumers, the Indonesian government, certifying bodies, investors, environmental NGOs, and local and international communities affected by slash-and-burn practices. They present differing consultant strategies for GAR: aligning with Greenpeace, excluding outside NGOs in favor of industry self-regulation via the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO), or adopting a market-driven approach with higher standards. Challenges discussed include supply chain transparency, the RSPO’s acceptance of mixed certified and non-certified oil, the cost burden of certification on small farmers, and the fact that only a small percentage of palm oil is certified and sold at a premium.

The lecture distinguishes between confrontational NGOs like Greenpeace and collaborative technical partners like the Forest Trust. It notes that the Indonesian Sustainable Palm Oil (ISPO) standard is mandatory, while the RSPO is voluntary, and students debate whether to treat certification as a carrot or stick and how to support small farmers through productivity improvements, financial incentives, and education.

Additional examples of multi-stakeholder partnerships are provided: Chiquita and the Rainforest Alliance; Dell and Goodwill for e-waste recycling; Walmart and the Environmental Defense Fund; and Starbucks with multiple organizations for packaging, farmer support, and recycling. Industry collaborations such as the Sustainability Consortium, the Electronic Industry Citizenship Coalition, and the Sustainable Apparel Coalition are described as forums for setting standards, sharing information, and addressing issues like conflict minerals and manufacturing conditions.

The session concludes with a discussion of communication strategies and risks, including the shift from corporate sustainability reporting to product-level certifications, the proliferation of hundreds of global eco-labels with varying rigor and limited regulation, and the upcoming visit from the Environmental Defense Fund. A project deliverable is due in one week.

KDKA-TV and WPXI-TV falsely reported on June 22 that a video showed Antwon Rose II firing a gun during the June 19 North Braddock shooting and that gunshot residue was on his hands. Allegheny County Police Superintendent Coleman McDonough corrected the record that day, stating the video did not show Rose firing a gun and the residue claim was false; WTAE-TV did not report the false information. On June 27, DA spokesman Mike Manko criticized local television media for failing to correct the record and feeding wrong information. KDKA-TV retracted its report on air that day, admitting its sources were incorrect. WPXI initially defended its reporting and did not apologize on air on June 27, but issued a written apology on June 28. The New Pittsburgh Courier criticized both stations and questioned whether WPXI’s sources were connected to Officer Michael Rosfeld or had a vested interest in shaping the narrative.

YouTube announced four new YouTube Red series for YouTube Kids: Hyperlinked, DanTDM Creates A Big Scene, The Kings of Atlantis, and Fruit Ninja: Frenzy Force. Debuting in spring 2017 with more to follow, this marks YouTube Red's first family audience investment. YouTube Kids app will soon arrive on LG and Samsung Smart TVs.

Retired Florida State University criminologist Gary Kleck and professor Marc Gertz’s 1993 National Self-Defense Survey, published in 1995, estimated over 2.2 million annual defensive gun uses (DGU) in the United States. The passage states that the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention conducted three studies from 1996–1998 that similarly found about 2.46 million annual DGUs and that guns were used defensively 3.6 times as often as offensively, but the CDC never published the results. Kleck wrote that these results confirm his estimate and noted the CDC never acknowledged the surveys; the passage attributes the suppression to the Clinton administration’s gun control agenda. Dean Weingarten noted the CDC survey timing. The passage argues this undermines anti-gun narratives, demonstrates that government agencies require verification, and supports private gun ownership advocacy.

Tesla Motors filed a Form 8-K on March 11, 2016, disclosing an immaterial error in its 2015 Form 10-K that overstated the Supercharger network's net book value, which should have been $166.6 million as of December 31, 2015. MSPM0C1105/6 are ultra-low-power Arm Cortex-M0+ MCUs up to 32MHz, from 1.62V to 3.6V at -40°C to 125°C. They include up to 64KB flash and 8KB SRAM, an on-chip oscillator, and analog, digital, and communication peripherals. MSPM0 platform combines Cortex-M0+ with ultra-low-power architecture for increased performance and reduced energy.

Fair Isaac unveiled a new pricing model allowing mortgage lenders to bypass credit bureaus by licensing FICO scores directly to mortgage resellers for distribution to borrowers. The company’s shares surged more than 20%, while shares of Experian, TransUnion, and Equifax fell between 4% and 10% as investors viewed the announcement as lessening the role of credit reporting agencies. Lenders will be able to choose between two pricing models. CEO Will Lansing said the change eliminates unnecessary mark-ups. A Raymond James analyst noted the scheme could disintermediate credit bureaus from their mark-up on the FICO score. Federal Housing Finance Agency director Bill Pulte praised the move as a creative solution to help consumers and encouraged credit bureaus to take similar competitive actions.

Finnish official Pekkala reported growing support among the Finnish public, military, and most political parties for a separate peace with the Soviet Union, but noted the Agrarian Party opposed this and expressed lack of confidence in President Ryti and Foreign Minister Witting. Witting resisted breaking from Germany, citing Finland’s dependence on German imports and fear of starvation. The U.S. Minister in Sweden warned that Finland’s deteriorating military situation and a potential Russian offensive could prompt Sweden to assist Finland, risking Swedish-German collaboration, internal political crisis, and a government dangerous to the democratic cause. Soviet Minister Kollontay shared concern over Swedish reaction and advocated for a simple cessation of fighting.

The first trading day of the month effect refers to the S&P 500's tendency to perform significantly better on the first trading day of each month than on other days. Defined as the first trading day rather than the first calendar day, holding SPY from the close of the last trading day of the previous month until the close of the first trading day produces an average gain of 0.24%, six times the average daily gain of 0.04%. While the basic strategy is too unstable and unreliable to trade alone, with most gains concentrated before the 2008/09 financial crisis, improved versions using filters perform better. One filtered strategy reduces trades by one third, yielding an average gain of 0.35% per trade, a 3% CAGR since 1993, a 67% win ratio, and a 5% maximum drawdown. A second strategy buying on the close of the first trading day based on one criterion averages 1.1% per trade over 61 trades with a 2.2% CAGR. The best first days are February and July. The effect likely stems from monthly capital inflows from savers, pension funds, and automatic savings to 401s.

The paper studies profit maximization in repeated bilateral trade via online learning, where a broker aims to maximize profit (payment from the buyer minus payment to the seller) subject to dominant-strategy incentive compatibility and individual rationality. In the stochastic i.i.d. setting with possibly correlated, unknown valuations, the authors present a polynomial-time algorithm achieving $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{T})$ regret against the best mechanism in hindsight, and prove a matching $\Omega(\sqrt{T})$ lower bound, implying offline sample complexity of $\Theta(1/\varepsilon^2)$. In the adversarial setting, they show no-regret is impossible; specifically, no algorithm can achieve sublinear regret relative to a $(2/3+\varepsilon)$ fraction of the optimal profit. They also improve the regret bound for the joint ads problem from $O(T^{3/4})$ to $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{T})$ via a reduction. The authors highlight that the non-parametric mechanism space and non-regular profit function render standard discretization methods insufficient.

The Harrogate Advertiser Business Awards nomination phase is underway, with entries due by noon on March 13. The passage presents former tenured professor Robert Oscar Lopez’s argument that academic freedom is neither a virtue nor a reality, but a false outgrowth of a corrupted tenure system that protects ideologically aligned faculty while leaving adjuncts unprotected. The team credits its success to having fun while working hard. A fearless player blocks shots daily and inspires teammates. An extended break reduced excitement, but arriving and media attention rebuilt hype. A smooth, non-flashy defenseman earned a top defenseman nomination.

A treaty guarantees territorial integrity and political independence under republican government; requires territorial disputes be settled by agreement or arbitration; mandates unresolved disputes be submitted to a permanent international commission for investigation before war; and prohibits hostile military or naval expeditions and arms exports against contracting governments. Mezes will draft general principles without references to individual nations for the Secretary of State. Mediation analysis is central to psychological intervention research. Structural equation modeling (SEM) is standard for identifying latent mediators and accounting for measurement error, but it requires no unmeasured confounding (sequential ignorability), which is rarely achievable. Rank-preserving models (RPMs) permit omitted covariates under a no-effect-modifier assumption but have not been extended to latent variables. This paper introduces the Rank-Preserving Structural Equation Model (RAPSEM), integrating RPM with factor score regression and interaction corrections to incorporate latent constructs while maintaining relaxed assumptions. The authors define controlled direct and controlled mediation effects within the potential outcomes framework and describe the RAPSEM measurement model for latent variables. Subsequent sections address estimation, inference, and simulation studies.

A cross-sectional study in Denan district, south-eastern Ethiopia, determined visceral leishmaniasis (VL) sero-prevalence, associated risk factors, knowledge/attitudes/practices (KAP), and sand fly species from April to August 2021. Among 187 participants, the overall VL sero-prevalence was 9.63%. Significant risk factors included age 19–36, damp house floors, outdoor sleeping, and sleeping near animal shelters. KAP results showed 53.48% had heard of VL, 42% knew sand fly bites cause it, and 36% believed it preventable; prevention practices included bed net use (42%) and insecticide spraying (32%). Entomological surveys identified 12 sand fly species from 823 specimens collected in termite mounds, forest, peri-domestic, and indoor habitats. *Phlebotomus orientalis*, a proven VL vector, was the dominant *Phlebotomus* species (11.42% of total) and most abundant in termite mounds and forests, with none caught indoors. *Sergentomyia clydie* was the most abundant species overall (50.18%). The study concludes that Denan is a relatively high-sero-prevalence new VL focus with poor community awareness, and that *P. orientalis* apparently contributes to transmission, warranting further epidemiological and vector bionomics studies alongside public health education.

Researchers developed a molecular influenza sensor that releases thymol, a thyme flavor detectable by the tongue. Incorporated into gum or lozenges, it could enable rapid, accessible at-home screening before symptoms appear. In lab tests with saliva from flu patients, it released thymol within 30 minutes without affecting cell function. The team plans human clinical trials in about two years and has registered a European patent.

This work investigates whether transformers can learn transitive relations—equivalent to directed graph connectivity—from individual training examples rather than in-context prompts. It compares grid graphs, whose nodes are embeddable in low-dimensional space, against disconnected chain graphs. Experiments show transformers generalize near-perfectly on grid graphs but struggle on disconnected chain graphs. Increasing model size improves learning for grid graphs yet does not improve generalization for disconnected chain graphs. Increasing graph size maintains consistent performance on grid graphs and markedly improves performance on disconnected chain graphs by increasing nodes per chain. Performance degrades for higher-dimensional grid graphs and chain graphs with more components; in these settings, scaling graph size benefits learning more than scaling model size.

Jerome "Jay" Powell succeeds Janet Yellen as Federal Reserve Chair, taking office amid steady economic growth and low unemployment. He faces key decisions on interest rate hikes as wages rise, tax cuts take effect, and global economies expand simultaneously. While Yellen left a normalized policy environment with gradual rate increases, Powell must calibrate further hikes during a late-cycle economy with new fiscal stimulus. The Fed signaled three likely increases this year, starting possibly in March, though policymakers debated the pace due to uncertain inflation and tax cut impacts. Inflation remains below the two percent target but is expected to rise. Officials prefer announcing changes only at quarterly press conferences; exceeding four hikes could unsettle markets.

Four leading candidates for Baltimore County executive—Vicki Almond, Jim Brochin, Johnny Olszewski Jr., and Al Redmer Jr.—addressed real estate and building professionals, promising to encourage smart growth and improve development approvals.
