Jalen Williams is mentioned as an outside candidate following a Kobe-like early career trajectory, while Zion Williamson and LaMelo Ball represent unconventional possibilities following a Curry-like path of college hype and delayed NBA emergence due to injuries. The article emphasizes that market size, rivalries, and off-court factors are nearly as important as talent in determining the league's next face, with Cooper Flagg and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander also mentioned as potential future stars.

An estimated 666 pilot whales stranded in two pods at Farewell Spit, New Zealand. About three-quarters of the first pod died, while the rest and the second pod were re-floated. The beach was closed as workers moved over 300 carcasses and punctured them to prevent gas explosions during decomposition. Wildlife officers remained alert for re-stranding. The area has seen at least nine strandings in the past decade, as its shallow seabed is believed to interfere with whale sonar.

PGA Tour is working with law enforcement to secure Austin tournament amid serial bombings that killed two and injured four. Jhonattan Vegas expressed confidence but called the attacks scary. Latest explosion injured two west of Interstate 35; earlier bombings occurred east of the highway.

The paradox of moral education arises in philosophy of education from unexamined libertarian assumptions about free will—specifically the principle of alternative possibilities and the causa sui (self-origination) condition—which underpin theories of autonomy, authenticity, and moral responsibility. These assumptions create a dilemma: if causal determinism is true, agents cannot act otherwise and lack moral responsibility; if indeterminism is true, actions are random and agents lack adequate control. Harry Frankfurt’s hierarchical theory of the will offers a resolution by grounding moral responsibility in volitional control rather than alternative possibilities. On this account, freedom consists in having the will one wants to have, achieved when first-degree desires align with second-degree desires (desires about desires) through reflexive self-assessment and identification. Because this internalist criterion depends on the agent’s psychological structure rather than on metaphysical conditions, autonomy and moral responsibility remain viable under both determinism and indeterminism. The paradox of moral education is thus dissolved, shifting educational focus toward helping young people understand their will and take responsibility for their actions and attitudes even when they cannot act differently.

In Arthur C. C. Hill v. Jacob Levine (1925), the plaintiff sought specific performance of a land sale contract. The defendant refused to accept title, claiming a fifty-foot frontage restriction in the plaintiff’s 1898 deed created reasonable doubt as to whether it expired in twenty years or thirty. The Superior Court dismissed the bill. The Supreme Judicial Court reversed, holding that the frontage provision was a personal agreement between the original grantors and the grantee, not part of a restriction scheme benefiting other lots, and did not create an equitable easement. The court ruled that the mere possibility of future litigation over a settled rule did not constitute a title defect warranting denial of specific performance, and the deed’s construction was not reasonably doubtful. A decree for specific performance was ordered.

Russia agreed to Syrian peace talks with the US and UN in Geneva for April 24, pending Washington confirmation. UN envoy Staffan de Mistura will reportedly attend. The move follows US cruise missile strikes on a Syrian air base after a chemical attack, and President Trump’s recent expression of hope for renewed dialogue with Russia.

Singer Meghan Linsey was bitten by a brown recluse spider while sleeping in Nashville on February 12. She suffered severe nerve pain, swelling, and facial necrosis, and received hyperbaric oxygen therapy after bringing the spider to urgent care. The venom caused tissue death that left a hole in her face. More than two months later, the wound has healed and she has resumed performing. Linsey shared her story on Instagram to raise awareness about brown recluse spiders, which are found in the southern and central U.S. and have no antidote.

Amid political unrest in the Maldives, President Yameen Abdul Gayoom said Saturday he is willing to hold an early election after the Supreme Court ordered the release of political prisoners, including former President Mohammed Nasheed, and reinstated 12 opposition lawmakers. The reinstatement would cost Yameen’s party its parliamentary majority; Parliament’s opening was indefinitely postponed. Yameen fired two police chiefs since the ruling. Opposition protests demanding prisoner release were broken up by police. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urged the government to respect the order and offered to facilitate talks. Nasheed, whose conviction was overturned, said he would run for president this year.

Microsoft announced Windows 10 accessibility updates for visually impaired users, including an updated Ease of Access panel, improved Narrator with voice-controlled text styling, and enhanced eye control. Some features are available in Insider previews, with more promised later this year.

Marine heatwaves—prolonged periods of unusually warm ocean water—have become longer and more frequent over the past century, with marine heatwave days increasing by 54 percent from 1925 to 2016. These events, which can occur in any season, damage marine ecosystems and industries, as demonstrated by a 2011 Western Australia event that destroyed kelp and seagrass, a 2012 Gulf of Maine lobster fishery disruption, and the 2014–2016 North Pacific “Blob” that caused fishery closures and algal blooms. Anthropogenic climate change significantly increased the likelihood of recent extreme events, including a 2016 heatwave that bleached the Great Barrier Reef and a 2015–16 Tasman Sea event. Scientists are working to develop forecasts to help manage fisheries and aquaculture, but curbing greenhouse gas emissions is essential to limit further damage to marine ecosystems.

British business headlines on April 3 included: Tesco Booker deal doubts; Reckitt Benckiser review; SFO DPA warning; Arcadia pension deficit; Twitter pay-TV deals; Cortexica £4m raise; Babcock £340m deal; Co-op bank stake zero; and Fallon EU trade-security link.

An MIT study found 3,000 shared four-person sedans could serve 98% of Manhattan ride demand, versus 13,600 taxis and 45,000 for-hire drivers currently. Passengers would face average waits of 2.8 minutes and 3.5-minute delays, but the city would see less congestion and pollution. Alternatively, 2,000 ten-passenger vans could work. Many drivers and riders resist ridesharing, and shared or self-driving vehicles threaten thousands of driving jobs.

The passage specifies SD Memory Card Physical Layer Version 6.00 requirements. It defines lock/unlock behavior, force erase interactions with write protection, ACMD6 rejection in locked states, and APP_CMD (CMD55) handling. It details the switch function command (CMD6) for querying and setting function groups—access mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit—including status data structures and busy indications. The text covers High-Speed mode, command system expansion, CMD8 initialization, and functional differences between SDSC and SDHC/SDXC addressing and block lengths. It also defines CRC7/CRC16, command classes (CCC), card state transitions, response types (R1–R7), and status fields. Extensive sections define Speed Class, UHS Speed Grade, and Video Speed Class metrics, including Allocation Units, Recording Units, write/read performance parameters (Pw, Pm, Pr), FAT and CI update procedures, and measurement conditions across card types.

President Trump addressed the World Economic Forum, affirming U.S. friendship and highlighting domestic economic progress. He cited stock market records, the creation of 2.4 million jobs, and historically low unemployment rates. He promoted the United States as open for business, citing significant tax cuts, a reduced corporate tax rate of 21 percent, and the elimination of 22 regulations for every new one. He referenced Apple's plan to invest $350 billion in the U.S. and called for fair, reciprocal trade while criticizing intellectual property theft and industrial subsidies. He also discussed lifting energy production restrictions, increasing military investment, urging allies to contribute to collective security, pressuring North Korea to denuclearize, confronting Iran, and nearly defeating ISIS. In a subsequent discussion with Klaus Schwab, Trump described tax reform as a long-standing priority that spurred unexpected corporate bonuses and investment. This U.S. patent application describes methods and systems for networked data modules, such as loudspeakers, to detect and process speech commands simultaneously. Modules dynamically assume roles—Player, Follower, or Renderer—for audio distribution and command processing. Upon detecting an activation command (Hot Word), each module computes a quality score based on signal power, recognizer confidence, user location, and audio processing. In a centralized approach, a Player module collects scores, mutes group playback, activates microphones on the highest-scoring modules, combines their recorded audio into a server request, and fans out the resulting action and confirmation audio to the group. In a decentralized approach, modules broadcast scores to identify the best module to send audio to the server, then broadcast confidence levels to determine which module performs the requested action and plays an audible confirmation. The system also supports partial processing by selecting the best audio segments from different modules across a synchronized timeline. A control client can manage the group and act as a data source.

Kerberos is a cryptographic authentication protocol for distributed networks originally developed for MIT’s Athena system. It relies on a trusted Key Distribution Center (KDC) that stores shared secret keys for every principal—users and services—and maps string names to those keys. All parties trust the KDC, and users must trust their own workstations; the network itself is untrusted.

Authentication uses two KDC interfaces: an initial login service and a Ticket Granting Service (TGS). A client sends its name to the KDC and receives a TGS ticket and a session key encrypted with the client’s key, which is derived from its password. After decrypting this, the client can discard its long-term key. To access a target service, the client presents the TGS ticket and an authenticator to the TGS, receiving a service ticket and a new session key. The client then presents the service ticket and a fresh authenticator to the target service, which decrypts the ticket with its own key to verify the client and establish a shared session key.

Tickets contain the server name, client name, client IP address, timestamp, lifetime, and a shared key, and are encrypted with the service’s key. Authenticators contain the client name, IP, and timestamp to help prevent replay attacks. Kerberos provides authentication but not authorization; services manage access control separately. Principal names are difficult to reuse because service-side access control lists are not versioned.

The lecture identifies several flaws in Kerberos version 4: it assumed encryption provided integrity, making offline password guessing and reflection attacks possible; it mandated single DES, which is now insecure; and its password-changing protocol allowed an attacker who learned an old password to decrypt subsequent password changes. Kerberos version 5 addresses these by adding explicit message authentication, supporting stronger encryption such as AES, using separate session keys for each direction, binding authenticators to specific messages, and using Diffie-Hellman key exchange during password changes. The KDC is a critical component but can use read-only replicas; if a service is compromised, its key must be changed to prevent traffic decryption and ticket forgery.

Scale-in trading involves gradually building a position size as market entry opportunities arise, implemented as a planned strategy rather than a reaction to salvage losing trades. Retail investors often use it to lower average purchase prices by buying additional shares as prices drop, similar to dollar-cost averaging. Day traders may test the market with a small initial position and add to winning trades to amplify gains while using floating profits to bear the risk of new positions. Institutional traders use scale-in to fill large orders gradually to avoid price impact and front-running. Swing traders apply the approach differently depending on their strategy: mean-reversion traders may add positions at potential reversal levels, while trend-following traders add to winning positions. Scale-out is the counterpart strategy of gradually exiting positions to lock in partial profits while leaving remaining shares to capture further trends. The scale-in strategy differs from double-down and Martingale approaches, which attempt to recover losing positions. Advantages include achieving a more optimal average entry price, reducing slippage in illiquid stocks, and improving risk-adjusted returns; backtesting indicated that while scale-in produced a lower CAGR, it used capital more efficiently. Disadvantages include the high discipline required, the risk of market reversals before a full position is entered or after adding to winners, and the danger of catching falling knives.

This retrospective single-center cohort study of 226 adult aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage patients at Rennes University Hospital (2020–2022) evaluated predictors of rebleeding. Rebleeding occurred in 33 patients (15%). No significant differences were found between patients with and without rebleeding for classical risk factors including systolic blood pressure, WFNS grade, aneurysm size, location, or intracranial hematomas. However, time elapsed since first symptoms was independently associated with rebleeding, with each additional hour increasing odds by 0.7% (OR 1.007). WFNS score was also an independent predictor. Two-thirds of rebleeding events occurred more than 24 hours after onset; patients treated within 24 hours had a 9% rebleeding rate versus 21% in those treated later. The authors conclude that time since headache onset is a significant risk factor, supporting prompt aneurysm securing, preferably within 24 hours. Limitations include the retrospective design, limited event number, and a pragmatic rebleeding definition.

Scientists created hybrid white rhino embryos using stored sperm from the last male northern white rhino and southern white rhino eggs; two lab-grown embryos are frozen and viable for implantation. Researchers aim to extract eggs from the two remaining northern females to produce pure embryos, hoping for a calf within three years, though the process faces biological and technological uncertainties. Critics view the technology as speculative and fear it may encourage complacency about other conservation strategies.

This study assessed the suitability of the German 17-item Speech, Spatial and Qualities of Hearing Scale (SSQ17) for evaluating hearing-related quality of life in unilateral Menière’s Disease (MD). Using data from 97 patients in a multicenter prospective registry (SEMM), researchers found asymmetric hearing loss with worse thresholds in affected ears. The SSQ17 showed excellent internal consistency (Cronbach’s alpha 0.960 total; 0.904–0.956 for subscales) and significant correlations with audiometry: negative correlations with pure-tone thresholds and positive correlations with speech recognition scores in affected ears. No significant differences in SSQ17 scores were observed across diagnostic categories, and no floor or ceiling effects were found except for one item. The authors conclude that the SSQ17 is a viable tool for assessing hearing-loss-related disability in MD patients and a valuable addition to clinical diagnostic tests, though it does not capture the vertigo-related disease burden.

The article analyzes calendar effects in the TLT ETF, which tracks 20-year Treasury bonds, using backtests from 2004 to August 2021. It identifies two persistent patterns: the first seven trading days of the month produce weak negative returns, while the period from the close of the seventh trading day through month-end generates strong positive returns, approximately doubling buy-and-hold returns with only two-thirds market exposure. A combined long/short strategy yielded a 10.2% annual return and 24% max drawdown, compared to 3.8% and 48% for buy-and-hold. The article explains the inverse relationship between TLT price and interest rates and provides complete Python code for the strategies.

A Seattle Public Utilities study found that extreme rainstorms have become more frequent and intense over the last 15 years, though the city’s characteristic short showers and drizzle persist. Based on roughly four decades of data from 17 gauges, what was previously classified as a once-in-a-century storm—4 inches of rain in 24 hours—now occurs approximately every 25 years, while the new 100-year standard exceeds 5 inches. SPU will use the updated data to plan drainage and sewage infrastructure, as the current system was built for lighter rainfall. The department is already constructing a storage tunnel under the Lake Washington Ship Canal to prevent polluted overflow. Officials, including Mayor Jenny Durkan and National Weather Service meteorologists, link the trend to climate change and emphasize the need for improved flood preparation across Western Washington.

Digital laggards struggle to connect goals with strategy, causing misalignment, while digital leaders use data culture as a central coordinating mechanism to align organizations vertically and horizontally. Leaders align beliefs, values, and daily actions, whereas laggards experience gaps between espoused values and behavior due to entrenched habits and insufficient focus. Changing mindsets is the most challenging part of transformation, but laggards can evolve. Technologically mature firms establish beliefs around learning, risk-taking, transparency, and measurement. Organizations typically begin in one of four patterns—data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, or data reliant—and should target focus areas based on their starting point to build a strong data culture.

On November 29, 2001, Enron Corp. stood poised to file the largest bankruptcy in history after Dynegy Inc. abandoned its proposed acquisition following Enron's credit downgrade to junk status and disclosures of severe operational deterioration. The impending collapse prompted Senate Majority Leader Tom Daschle to call for a congressional investigation, led the NYMEX and European power exchanges to restrict or suspend Enron trading, and forced Enron to reopen its electronic platform solely to unwind positions. Major banks and trading counterparties—including J.P. Morgan Chase, Citigroup, and Bank of America, each with roughly $500 million in estimated direct loan exposure, plus energy firms like Reliant Resources and Williams—assessed their financial risk. The crisis rippled across global markets: Houston real estate projects were delayed, UK and German electricity prices turned volatile, the InterContinental Exchange reported surging volumes as traders migrated from EnronOnline, U.S. Treasury bonds rallied on a flight to quality, bank bond spreads widened, and several Japanese money-management funds fell below par value due to Enron bond losses. Enron's complex overseas holdings and approximately $18.7 billion in derivatives liabilities threatened to complicate proceedings, while its metals unit drew rumored interest from buyers such as HSBC and Glencore.

Mapbox, which provides geographic data for apps including Snap and Instacart, announced partnerships with Microsoft, Intel, and ARM to expand into self-driving cars. It will combine its vision software with Microsoft Azure to process camera data for navigation algorithms, optimize software for ARM chips to recognize lanes and road signs faster, and integrate with Intel's Mobileye to deliver cloud-based road data to cars, providing a 200-meter map backup to onboard sensors.

The invention provides a driving assistance system for a vehicle using exterior-viewing cameras and/or non-imaging sensors (radar, lidar) to capture data representative of objects and scenes outside the vehicle. The system detects rearward approaching vehicles and, to avoid or mitigate collision, controls the vehicle to accelerate to the determined speed of the rearward approaching vehicle and/or maneuvers the vehicle into an adjacent lane. The system may autonomously execute these actions in SAE Level 3 and higher operation or provide alerts and guidance in SAE Level 2 driver-assist mode. It handles scenarios including passing slower vehicles ahead and yielding to faster rear traffic by evaluating parameters such as distances, speeds, free space in current and adjacent lanes, speed limits, vehicle-specific restrictions (e.g., trailers, license class), and emergency vehicle presence. The system includes an image processor and ECU, may utilize vehicle-to-vehicle or vehicle-to-infrastructure communication, and can display alerts or instructions to the driver.

NVIDIA’s RTX Blackwell architecture introduces Mega Geometry, using Cluster-level Acceleration Structures (CLAS) and Partitioned Top-Level Acceleration Structures (PTLAS) to reduce BVH build overhead and support high object counts and LOD systems. Fourth-generation RT Cores deliver up to 2x the ray-triangle intersection rate of the previous generation, implement new compression schemes, and add hardware support for Linear Swept Spheres (LSS) for strand-like geometry. Shader Execution Reordering (SER) 2.0 doubles reorder logic efficiency, and the AI Management Processor (AMP), a dedicated RISC-V scheduler, offloads GPU context scheduling from the CPU.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, creating up to three additional frames per traditionally rendered frame, and transitions to Transformer-based AI models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA. Blackwell also enables Neural Shaders via the Cooperative Vectors API, supporting techniques such as Neural Texture Compression, RTX Neural Materials, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces.

The architecture adds hardware encode and decode for 4:2:2 chroma-sampled video, a ninth-generation NVENC with an AV1 Ultra High Quality mode, and DisplayPort 2.1b with up to 80 Gbps bandwidth. Power efficiency improvements include advanced power gating, separate voltage rails for cores and memory, accelerated frequency switching 1000× faster than previous architectures, and low-latency sleep states entered 10× faster than Ada. The Blackwell GPU family includes the flagship GB202 (GeForce RTX 5090), GB203 (RTX 5080/5070 Ti), and GB205 (RTX 5070), each with scaled CUDA Core, RT Core, Tensor Core, and memory configurations.

NVIDIA Corporation filed its Form 10-Q for the second quarter of fiscal year 2016, ended July 26, 2015. Revenue increased 5% year-over-year to $1.15 billion, while net income declined to $26 million from $128 million in the prior-year quarter. GPU segment revenue rose 9%, driven by growth in high-end GeForce gaming products, while Tegra Processor revenue fell 19% due to lower OEM smartphone and tablet sales, partially offset by stronger automotive revenue. Operating expenses included $89 million in restructuring and other charges related to the wind-down of Icera modem operations, which are expected to impact approximately 5% of the global workforce. The company also recorded a $21 million charge for a voluntary recall of SHIELD 8-inch tablets. Sales, general, and administrative expenses increased 25%, reflecting $24 million in legal fees associated with litigation against Samsung and Qualcomm. The effective tax rate was 64.0%, primarily due to a $27 million write-down of a deferred tax asset related to Icera. During the quarter, NVIDIA returned $452 million to shareholders through stock repurchases, including a $400 million accelerated share repurchase agreement, and paid $52 million in dividends. Construction also began on a new headquarters building in Santa Clara, California, financed under a build-to-suit operating lease.

This scoping review examines the current state of anti-inflammatory strategies for depression. A substantial body of evidence indicates that inflammatory processes, particularly neuroinflammation involving NLRP3, NF-κB, and P2X7R signalling pathways, are associated with depression pathogenesis, with elevated cytokines and chemokines affecting neurotransmitter metabolism, neuroplasticity, and mood. Animal studies have identified pharmacological interventions—including SGLT2 inhibitors, vitamin D analogues, natural extracts, and other compounds—and non-pharmacological interventions such as acupuncture, exercise, and photobiomodulation that modulate these pathways and improve depressive symptoms. However, these studies are predominantly short-term, and debate continues regarding single-target versus multi-target modulation and pharmacological versus non-pharmacological approaches.

The review screened 1,057 articles and included 11 randomised controlled trials comprising 907 patients, primarily with major depressive disorder. Trials investigated agents such as fluoxetine, infliximab, ketamine, minocycline, vortioxetine plus celecoxib, SSRIs combined with glycopyrrolate, and lacquer tree extract over two to eighteen weeks. Although the majority of inflammatory markers in these studies were undetectable, reasonably detectable markers included CRP, hs-CRP, sTNFR1, sTNFR2, IL-2, IL-6, and TNF-α. Some anti-inflammatory adjuncts improved symptoms or reduced inflammatory markers, but benefits appeared limited to subsets with higher baseline inflammation, and substantial inter-patient variability, safety concerns, and high costs relative to traditional therapy constrained feasibility. The studies relied on traditional depression rating scales rather than objective inflammation-based endpoints.

The authors note that animal model findings do not readily translate to human depression, which has multifactorial causes, and that clinical inflammatory indicators remain ambiguously defined. They propose systematically validating biomarkers through transcriptomics, blood-level analysis, and healthy population norms, and suggest integrating artificial intelligence for personalised patient assessment and treatment monitoring. They also reference emerging micro-robot technology for targeted drug delivery and real-time feedback. The review concludes that pharmacological anti-inflammatory strategies currently possess limited research value and poor clinical feasibility, advocating a shift toward non-pharmacological anti-inflammatory strategies such as positive thinking and exercise, supported by low-cost, broadly generalisable research.

The Seventh Circuit reversed a district court order dismissing a putative class action by former Illinois arrestees challenging county bail fees. Plaintiffs released from Kane and DuPage County jails sued 19 counties, claiming mandatory bail fees imposed under state law violated constitutional rights. The district court dismissed the entire action for lack of standing and denied class certification as moot. The Seventh Circuit held that the named plaintiffs had Article III standing for their individual claims against Kane and DuPage, reversed the dismissal of those claims, and remanded for reinstatement. It also reversed the dismissal of the class claims against those two counties, noting the district court had certified parallel class actions against them on the same day, and remanded for certification proceedings. Regarding the other 17 counties, the court stated that once a class is certified, standing is assessed for the class as a whole, not just named plaintiffs. Because all counties imposed fees under the same state statute, the named plaintiffs might represent the class against all 19 defendants under a "juridical link" theory if Rule 23 requirements are satisfied. The court remanded for the district court to conduct the class certification analysis.

The United Nations Conference on International Organization met in San Francisco from April 25 to June 26, 1945, to draft the Charter of the United Nations. Delegates from fifty governments approved the Charter, Statute of the International Court of Justice, and Interim Arrangements on June 25; 153 delegates signed it June 26. President Truman ratified the Charter on August 8, and it came into force on October 24, 1945. Using the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals as its agenda, the Conference operated through four commissions, twelve technical committees, four general committees, and an International Secretariat. Records were mimeographed daily and published in a 22-volume series.

The 1942 Foreign Relations series, edited by E. R. Perkins on February 5, 1962, includes six numbered volumes plus an unnumbered volume on China. The Belgium section records a June 16, 1942 mutual aid agreement, a 1942 military service agreement, and March–August 1942 telegrams regarding tripartite negotiations for a U.S.-U.K.-Belgium agreement on Belgian Congo trade. Two March 1942 telegrams detail U.S. interest in representation in stalled Anglo-Belgian economic renewal talks and U.K. reports of delays over pricing, higher American buyer offers, and Belgian demands for mining machinery.

A solid-state photon upconversion system converts near-infrared light to visible emission via triplet-triplet annihilation in a bulk-heterojunction sensitizer integrated with a rubrene annihilator layer doped with 0.5 vol.% DBP. The sensitizer consists of a DIB-SQ donor and PCBM fullerene acceptor blend, optimized at a 1:3 weight ratio to maximize triplet population. Upon near-infrared excitation, charge transfer states form at the donor-acceptor interface; subsequent non-geminate recombination generates triplet charge transfer states and molecular triplets in PCBM, which transfer energy to populate rubrene triplet states. These triplets undergo triplet-triplet annihilation to produce upconverted photoluminescence peaking at 605 nm in the DBP-doped system. Time-resolved and transient absorption spectroscopy, along with magnetic field effect measurements, confirm that rubrene triplets are populated via both direct triplet energy transfer from triplet charge transfer states and indirect transfer through PCBM molecular triplets, followed by triplet-triplet annihilation. The device achieves a saturated upconversion quantum yield of 1.36% and a threshold intensity of 60.5 mW/cm² under 690 nm excitation. This approach repurposes triplet charge transfer state formation—typically a loss channel in photovoltaics—to enhance triplet generation for efficient solid-state upconversion in optoelectronic applications.

In Ángel Bracero v. S. Ramírez & Co., Inc. (No. 4453, argued December 13, 1929, decided July 24, 1930), the plaintiff sued to recover damages for injuries sustained when bags of rice fell on him in a Ponce shop. The majority opinion, delivered by Mr. Justice Wolf, reversed the lower court’s judgment. It found that the plaintiff was an independent contractor and that evidence sufficiently showed the defendant owned or controlled the shop. The majority held that res ipsa loquitur was inapplicable because the plaintiff and other workmen had removed sacks from the pile, so the situation was not under the defendant’s exclusive control, and it concluded that no negligence attributable to the defendant at the time of the accident was proven. In dissent, Chief Justice Del Toro, joined by Mr. Justice Hutchison, argued that the trial court’s findings were supported by evidence, including testimony that the defendant’s agent had been warned the pile was defectively constructed but only propped it up instead of rebuilding it. The dissent maintained this showed gross negligence and that the judgment should be affirmed.

This study assessed ex vivo susceptibilities of Ugandan *Plasmodium falciparum* isolates collected between July 2019 and June 2024 from eastern and northern Uganda to nine antimalarial drugs, alongside sequencing of 80 resistance-associated genes. Of 1,297 isolates, most remained sensitive to commonly used drugs at low nanomolar concentrations. However, susceptibilities to dihydroartemisinin and lumefantrine, components of first-line artemether-lumefantrine therapy, decreased modestly over time. Chloroquine susceptibility increased, while pyrimethamine resistance remained well established. The PfK13 C469Y and A675V mutations were associated with decreased dihydroartemisinin and lumefantrine activity; these mutations were at moderate prevalence in northern Uganda and increased in eastern Uganda since 2021. Mutations conferring chloroquine and amodiaquine resistance were very uncommon, while sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine resistance mutations were highly prevalent. Ring-stage survival assays showed increased parasite survival over time, though not significantly correlated with PfK13 mutations. The findings indicate that while widely used antimalarials generally retain activity, declining susceptibility to artemether-lumefantrine components warrants continued parasitological and genomic surveillance.

This study develops an evolutionary hypergame dynamics framework for the prisoner’s dilemma with voluntary participation, where players possess heterogeneous, limited subsets of strategies rather than full access to the entire strategy space. The model separates adaptation into two timescales: fast introspection reasoning, in which players update strategies via a Fermi function with introspection strength \(w\) serving as a proxy for rationality, and slow evolution of strategy sets driven by relative payoffs. Analyzing a three-strategy system—Cooperation (C), Defection (D), and Loner (L)—in both well-mixed and spatially structured populations, the authors find that weak introspection favors strategy sets containing defection or loner strategies, such as \{D, L\} or \{L\}. In contrast, strong introspection enables the \{C, L\} strategy set to dominate through enhanced self-reciprocity and improved defense against exploitation. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that \{C, L\}’s self-play payoff increases monotonically with \(w\) and the benefit-to-cost ratio, and that \{C, L\} outperforms both \{D\} and \{D, L\} once \(w\) exceeds critical thresholds. Evolutionary simulations confirm that increasing introspection shifts population dynamics toward cooperative, high-payoff equilibria, illustrating that the co-evolution of behaviors and strategy sets under asymmetric information fundamentally reshapes evolutionary outcomes.

InVirtuoGen is a continuous-time discrete flow model for fragment-based drug discovery that operates directly on fragmented SMILES. Unlike autoregressive and masked diffusion models—which rely on arbitrary sequential ordering or fix tokens once unmasked—InVirtuoGen simultaneously refines all sequence positions at every denoising step, decoupling sampling steps from sequence length. The model encodes molecules as randomly shuffled fragment blocks with explicit attachment points, uses a diffusion transformer with bidirectional attention to model long-range dependencies, and is pretrained on roughly one billion molecules from ZINC and UniChem. It achieves state-of-the-art performance in de novo molecular generation and competitive results on fragment-constrained tasks such as linker design and scaffold decoration. Additionally, a hybrid framework combining a genetic algorithm with PPO-based reinforcement learning adapted to discrete flows attains state-of-the-art results on the Practical Molecular Optimization benchmark and improved lead optimization over prior baselines.

The lecture reviews Wald's equality for stopping trials with IID random variables, stating that the expected sum at the stopping trial equals the mean inter-renewal time multiplied by the expected stopping index. It then covers the elementary renewal theorem, which states that the limit of the expected number of renewals N(t) divided by t approaches one over the mean inter-renewal time; the proof requires bounding arguments and truncation. The discussion extends to generalized stopping trials defined by pairs of random variables, such as inter-arrival times and service times. In a G/G/1 queue, the first arrival to an empty system marks a generalized stopping trial and a renewal point. Little's theorem is introduced, showing the time-average number of customers in the system equals the arrival rate times the time-average waiting time, derived by equating the integral of customers in the system over a renewal period to the sum of individual waiting times. Finally, the Pollaczek-Khinchin formula for M/G/1 queues states the expected waiting time in queue is λ times the second moment of service time divided by two times (1 minus ρ), where ρ is the traffic intensity; this indicates that even when ρ is less than one, an infinite second moment of service time yields infinite expected waiting, separating the effects of utilization from service time variability.

Youth suicide is a pressing public health concern in China, with high lifetime prevalence of suicidal thoughts, plans, and attempts among adolescents. Although school-based gatekeeper training is a common international prevention strategy, its efficacy remains unclear, and no rigorous, culturally adapted programs have been developed for Chinese secondary school teachers or parents. Unique sociocultural challenges—such as left-behind children and a severe shortage of qualified school counsellors—limit the direct application of Western programs. This study used the Delphi method to develop the first evidence-based, localized gatekeeper training program for China. Through two iterative rounds (September–November 2022), experts in suicide intervention rated statements on importance, feasibility, and appropriateness for inclusion. The resulting program contains eight modules, combining standard gatekeeper components with localized content on family-school collaboration and barriers to help-seeking.

This work presents a scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy method to generate and detect magnetic monopoles on the surface of three-dimensional topological insulators. Leveraging the topological magnetoelectric effect, the authors investigated image potential states—Rydberg energy levels formed by electron-image charge interactions—in bismuth structures: √3-Bi (topologically trivial), Bi(110) (two-dimensional topological insulator), and Bi(111) (three-dimensional high-order topological insulator). While √3-Bi and Bi(110) exhibited standard image potential states without splitting, Bi(111) displayed intrinsic splitting of peaks for principal quantum numbers n > 1, notably the n = 2 level separating into two distinct sub-peaks. The splitting is attributed to the Zeeman effect arising from coupling between the orbital magnetic moment of the image potential states and the exotic magnetic field generated by electric-field-induced magnetic monopoles, forming electron-dyon quasiparticles. Alternative explanations, including symmetric and antisymmetric image potential state series, quantum well states, and quantum dot confinement, were experimentally ruled out. The splitting energy dependence on the principal quantum number agrees with theoretical modeling, and the magnitude varies with tunneling current—thereby electric field strength—in a manner consistent with the Fowler-Nordheim relationship. These results demonstrate the electric-field-induced generation and manipulation of magnetic monopoles on three-dimensional topological insulator surfaces, providing a solid-state platform for exploring topological field theory and potential applications in quantum computing and novel electronic devices.

This application is a continuation of prior U.S. and Korean patent applications and relates to image encoding/decoding methods and apparatuses, and a recording medium storing a bitstream, using motion vector refinement to improve compression efficiency and reduce computational complexity. The decoding method comprises deriving an initial motion vector for a current block, deriving a refined motion vector by a merge mode-based or prediction block-based motion vector refinement method, and generating a prediction block. The refined L0 and L1 motion vectors are derived by adding differences between initial motion vectors and motion vectors moved within a predetermined search area, and may be mirrored or scaled based on POC differences between L0/L1 reference pictures and the decoding target picture. The prediction block-based method is performed only for bi-directional prediction merge mode when POC differences are equal and the current block has a vertical size of at least 8 and an area of at least 64, using a search area ranging from −2 to 2 integer pixels. The encoding method derives initial and refined motion vectors and entropy-encodes motion compensation information. The disclosure further describes encoding/decoding apparatus configurations and image partitioning using quad-tree, binary-tree, ternary-tree, and multi-type tree structures, along with inter-prediction modes including merge, AMVP, skip, and current picture reference modes.

An inside day is defined as a trading day where the entire price range is contained within the previous day's high and low. It occurs frequently, accounting for roughly 10% of trading days in the S&P 500 since 1993, though frequency varies by market and time frame. The opposite pattern is an outside day, which posts a higher high and lower low than the prior day. According to backtests, inside days are weak standalone trading signals. A strategy buying all inside days in the S&P 500 produced only modest gains, and adding an RSI filter below 50 raised the average gain to just 0.1%. A swing trade variation generated 89 trades since 1993 with a 0.45% average gain and a 2.1 profit factor, but this result did not hold in markets such as gold. Testing two consecutive inside days produced too few trades to be viable. The passage concludes that inside day strategies typically require additional variables to become profitable.
