A retrospective cardiac magnetic resonance study of 15 patients with excessive left ventricular trabeculation (ET) found that intertrabecular recesses have a significantly higher ejection fraction (EF) than the central cavity. Using threshold-based contouring to separate compact wall, trabeculations, central cavity, and recesses, the study showed that accurate assessment halved the number of patients with severely reduced EF and doubled those with EF above 50% compared to guideline-based methods. The trabecular layer operates at high EF, and contouring trabeculations provides more accurate LV volume and EF measurements, which could better guide clinical management and predict prognosis in ET patients.

This paper uses the digital business model perspective and value configuration theory to examine how blockchain companies create and capture value. Through an exploratory multiple-case study of five Chinese firms—ChainArchitect, ChainFinance, ChainNova, ChainSecurity, and ChainDraft—the authors identify a typology of five blockchain-inspired business models. ChainArchitect (platformer/value shop) develops proprietary blockchain architecture as an open platform for third-party applications. ChainFinance (disintermediator/value network) provides blockchain-enabled interbank transfers that displace conventional clearing roles. ChainNova (transformer/value chain) delivers tailored solutions, such as product traceability systems, to revolutionize traditional industry practices. ChainSecurity (mediator/value network) resolves inefficiencies in conventional value chains, for example by improving asset-backed securities processes. ChainDraft (co-innovator/value chain) codevelops firm-specific applications on its proprietary platform and captures value through licensing. Each model features distinct value creation logic, value capturing mechanisms, and challenges—including compatibility with legacy systems, resistance from incumbents, limited transferability of tailored solutions, and difficulties scaling beyond small pilot implementations. The study contributes to theory by showing blockchain can disrupt, mediate, or streamline existing value chains and ecosystems, and informs practice by mapping prevailing models and their associated risks.

This cohort study estimated BNT162b2 and ChAdOx1 vaccine effectiveness across 12 consecutive 4-week periods up to 50 weeks after the second dose in English primary care patients. In the 65+, 18–64 clinically vulnerable, and 40–64 subgroups, cumulative third dose incidence reached ≥90%, and individuals remaining in the two-dose group showed higher hazard ratios for non-COVID-19 death than unvaccinated individuals during the third dose rollout, suggesting selection bias from deferred vaccination due to recent SARS-CoV-2 infection or poor health; consequently, estimated two-dose effectiveness against COVID-19 outcomes beyond 26 weeks was not interpreted for these subgroups. In the 18–39 subgroup, where maximum third dose uptake was 73% and non-COVID-19 death hazard ratios did not change markedly, waning against COVID-19 hospitalisation was approximately log-linear with negligible effectiveness by weeks 35–38, and waning against positive SARS-CoV-2 test was log-linear until weeks 23–26 with negligible effectiveness by weeks 15–18, though this may reflect higher testing uptake in vaccinated individuals rather than true waning. Waning in this subgroup did not appear affected by the omicron variant. The authors conclude that high third dose uptake makes long-term two-dose effectiveness difficult to estimate and that future studies must account for selection bias, testing behaviours, and testing policy changes.

The application describes systems and methods for fast, real-time weather and precipitation forecasting, including fog detection and Runway Visual Range (RVR) estimation. The technology integrates diverse, high-frequency data sources—such as terrestrial and satellite microwave link attenuation, weather radar, numerical weather prediction models, and vehicle-mounted sensors—within a four-server architecture comprising information collection and normalization, offline/background processing, modeling and prediction, and information distribution and alerting components. Data is organized into cadence instances with tile layers and tile stacks, supporting forecast cadences as short as 15 seconds to one minute. The system pre-processes inputs asynchronously, blends multiple precipitation and wind estimates, infers fog and atmospheric liquid water content from microwave signals, and calculates RVR forecasts. A cadence manager optimizes processing by propagating and partially recalculating only changed tile layers across forecast cycles, improving forecast accuracy by 30–70% and speed by up to 50%, to enable near real-time updates for rapidly changing weather conditions.

The application describes digital certificate management methods, apparatuses, and systems for blockchain networks to mitigate risks from a compromised or malicious Certificate Authority (CA). Instead of direct chaining by the CA, a transaction request to write a digital certificate, certificate revocation list, or revocation record into the blockchain is subjected to consensus verification by blockchain nodes. Nodes determine verification results, which are broadcast and tallied against predetermined thresholds to produce a consensus result; the transaction request is responded to or rejected accordingly. A CA-issued digital certificate is invalid before being successfully written into the blockchain. Nodes can subsequently verify transaction requests using certificate revocation lists stored locally in the blockchain ledger. This decentralized verification prevents unauthorized certificate permissions from affecting blockchain security and reduces reliance on remote CA verification services.

This study reports a psychometric validation of the 17-item C19-YRSm, a condition-specific patient-reported outcome measure for Long Covid, using longitudinal data from 1,314 patients across 10 UK services. The instrument comprises Symptom Severity (SS), Functional Disability (FD), Overall Health (OH), and Other Symptoms (OS) subscales. Results indicated good item and scale characteristics, good internal reliability, and strong convergent validity with the FACIT-Fatigue scale. Known-groups validity was demonstrated, with higher SS and FD scores among patients with greater symptom burden and those previously hospitalised or admitted to ICU. Over 30 days, the measure showed responsiveness to change with effect sizes ranging from 0.22 to 0.50, and was more sensitive to change than the EQ-5D-5L. Test-retest reliability was good (SS: 0.86; FD: 0.78). Initial metrics for minimally important differences were identified (SS: 2; FD: 2; OH: 1), with minimal clinically important differences of 4 for SS and FD. Confirmatory factor analysis indicated reasonable fit for a two-factor structure measuring SS and FD. The authors conclude that C19-YRSm is valid, reliable, responsive, and suitable for clinical and research settings to monitor Long Covid symptoms and evaluate interventions.

The document details the design of a push-pull converter using TPS7H500x-SP controllers. The transformer uses a 2.5 turns ratio and 40 μH primary inductance, with magnetizing current set to 6% of output current. Primary-side GaN FETs are rated at 170 V, while secondary-side synchronous rectifier GaN FETs are rated at 80 V with parallel Schottky diodes. The output inductor is 0.47 μH, and output capacitance is 2.3 mF using seven 330-μF polymer tantalum capacitors, with an additional LC filter to reduce ripple and mitigate radiation-induced single event transients. Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins at approximately 35 A using a 1:100 current sense transformer and 7.5-Ω sense resistor. Frequency compensation uses Type 2A with a 10 kHz crossover target, and a 102-kΩ resistor sets slope compensation. A 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor is used. The controller operates from a 4-V to 14-V input with a minimum 0.1-μF bypass capacitor. Layout guidelines emphasize routing feedback traces away from power magnetics, minimizing switch node copper, separating analog and power grounds, placing bypass capacitors close to the controller, and keeping high dv/dt traces away from sensitive signals.

This paper examines statistical independence (SI) in the context of Bell’s theorem, interpreting SI as the claim that random sampling procedures yield representative samples rather than as a probabilistic assumption. It defines superdeterminism as any theory that systematically violates SI by causing such sampling to fail. The authors identify three forms of superdeterminism: (1) deterministic theories with fine-tuned initial conditions, such as Leibnizian Quantum Mechanics; (2) statistical flukes in deterministic or indeterministic theories, where unrepresentative samples arise by chance, as in certain branching interpretations; and (3) nomic exclusion, where laws render certain combinations of hidden variables and measurement settings impossible, illustrated by toy “goblin” models and existing proposals by Donadi, Hossenfelder, and Hance. The paper challenges the view that superdeterminism necessarily requires determinism or fine-tuned initial conditions. It further argues that retrocausal theories, often thought to violate SI, need not do so under a causal-order interpretation, distinguishing them from superdeterminism.

Will Ma introduces Independent Chip Model (ICM) theory for poker tournaments, explaining that chip value is nonlinear because players aim to survive and move up payouts rather than simply maximize chip count. He distinguishes chip expected value (EV) from money EV, noting that maximizing chip EV is a reasonable approximation in most cases, but ICM matters significantly in extreme situations such as the payout bubble, final tables, and satellite tournaments. Using a three-player example, he shows that small stacks have money EV greater than chip EV, while big stacks have money EV less than chip EV. He describes satellites as an extreme case where going all-in first creates leverage and folding pocket aces preflop can be theoretically correct. Ma then analyzes hands from a final table he played, applying ICM principles: shoving medium-strength hands when first to act to exploit opponents' fold incentives, avoiding large pots with the biggest stack, and folding jack-ten offsuit after calculating that ICM required 39.6% equity versus 33% under pure chip EV. He notes ICM disappears heads-up. He concludes by acknowledging selection bias in choosing a tournament he won and previewing remaining lectures, including a guest lecture by Bill Chen.

The running back is a crucial offensive position in football, primarily responsible for efficiently running the ball, protecting it, and gaining positive yardage. Lining up in the backfield, the player must also pass block and catch passes. The name derives from lining up behind the offensive line and running the ball. Also called tailbacks or halfbacks, running backs typically stand 5'9" to 6'2" and weigh 190-235 pounds, possessing speed, agility, vision, toughness, and receiving ability. Teams utilize various types, including short-yardage and all-purpose backs. Notable players include Barry Sanders, Emmitt Smith, Walter Payton, Jim Brown, and LaDainian Tomlinson. Canadians can earn money selling unwanted gifts, averaging $1,037 annually according to Kijiji. Inverse problems for reconstructing PDE-governed physical fields over irregular geometries are ill-posed and computationally prohibitive at scale. Although operator learning and diffusion-based generative models have advanced PDE surrogates, most remain limited to regular domains, leaving inverse problems on complex geometries largely underexplored. This work proposes GeoFunFlow, a geometry-aware diffusion framework that couples a geometric function autoencoder (GeoFAE) with a latent diffusion model. GeoFAE integrates a Perceiver module to handle unstructured meshes of varying sizes and enables continuous reconstruction, while the coupled latent diffusion model enables posterior sampling conditioned on sparse and noisy sensor data. The authors provide theoretical guarantees for accurate posterior approximations and demonstrate state-of-the-art accuracy and efficient inference on benchmarks involving complex geometries. The paper reviews related advances in operator learning and diffusion models for physical simulations, and formalizes the inverse problem as reconstructing fields from limited observations across families of irregular domains, with preliminaries covering operator learning for PDE maps and rectified flow for conditional generative sampling.

The case study examines DeBeers’s strategic dilemma regarding the emergence of synthetic diamonds. Once controlling 80% of global supply, DeBeers saw its monopoly erode in the 1990s due to new producers in Russia, Australia, and Canada, alongside antitrust actions and blood diamond controversies. In response, the company shifted from supply-side control to a demand-driven, brand-focused strategy through its “Supplier of Choice” program, Forevermark certification, retail expansion with LVMH, and privatization, while settling price-fixing and class-action lawsuits. Concurrently, laboratory-grown diamonds—chemically identical to natural stones but 15% to 40% cheaper and marketed as ethically and environmentally superior—gained market traction, with annual sales projected to exceed $2 billion by 2015. Produced primarily through HPHT and CVD methods, synthetics were mostly colored stones under one carat. DeBeers defended natural diamonds by funding detection technology and launching consumer education campaigns emphasizing their unique natural origins, while facing the strategic choice of whether to enter the synthetic market or rely on enduring consumer preference for mined stones.

This study develops machine learning models to detect Medicare overutilization in ophthalmology. Healthcare fraud costs the United States an estimated $100 billion annually, with current detection relying on manual audits and the List of Excluded Individuals and Entities (LEIE) database, which suffers from extreme class imbalance and captures overt fraud rather than subtle overutilization. The authors addressed these limitations by creating a labeled dataset of 663 ophthalmologists—200 overutilizers and 463 non-fraudulent—through expert review by experienced physicians and medical billers of 2015 CMS Medicare Provider Utilization and Payment Data. They engineered 1,028 features from 513 ophthalmology-specific HCPCS codes, including ratios of services to beneficiaries, beneficiaries to total patients, total payments to patients, and drug payments to total payments.

The researchers compared six machine learning approaches—k-nearest neighbor, logistic regression, support vector machines, extreme gradient boosting, multilayer perceptron, and a stacking ensemble—using repeated nested cross-validation. The stacking ensemble achieved the highest performance, with an AUROC score of 0.907 and the best predictive accuracy.

When applied to 2021 data for 17,013 ophthalmologists, the model predicted an 8.6% overutilization rate, identifying 1,457 likely overutilizers. The estimated annual monetary loss in ophthalmology alone was approximately $437.1 million; extrapolated across all Medicare spending, the authors estimate roughly $49.1 billion in annual losses, representing about 5.5% of the Medicare budget. Feature importance analysis identified the ratio of total Medicare payments per patient as the strongest indicator of overutilization, followed by specific HCPCS codes. The study also documents regional variations in overutilization rates and monetary losses across Medicare jurisdictions. Limitations include the relatively small labeled dataset, the inherent uncertainty of model predictions, the difficulty of distinguishing overutilization from intentional fraud, and the need for labor-intensive, specialty-specific expert labeling to apply the methodology to other fields.

This statistical analysis plan details methods for a trial comparing dasiglucagon, GlucaGen, and placebo. Demographic, baseline, and concomitant medication data will be summarized by treatment group. The primary efficacy endpoint, time to plasma glucose recovery (≥20 mg/dL increase within 45 minutes without rescue IV glucose during a hypoglycemic clamp), will be analyzed in the Full Analysis Set using Kaplan-Meier methods, a stratified log-rank test, and a Cox proportional hazards model adjusted for age group and injection site; sensitivity analyses include alternative censoring for rescue IV glucose and linear interpolation. Secondary efficacy endpoints include plasma glucose recovery rates at 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes, and glucose changes from baseline, analyzed via Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel tests and ANOVA. Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic analyses will use non-compartmental methods to summarize plasma dasiglucagon, GlucaGen, and glucose concentrations. Safety analyses will evaluate treatment-emergent adverse events, serious adverse events, local tolerability, vital signs, ECGs (including QTc), laboratory parameters, immunogenicity, and extent of exposure. No imputation for missing data and no interim analyses are planned.

This lecture explains the application of Soft-Collinear Effective Theory (SCET) to dijet production in electron-positron collisions. The relevant degrees of freedom are hard modes at scale q, collinear modes for two back-to-back jets at scale m, ultra-soft modes at scale m²/q, and lambda_QCD modes. Restricting to dijets is achieved by measuring hemisphere invariant masses, requiring m² and m̄² to be much less than q². The analysis distinguishes a peak region, where the ultra-soft scale is of order lambda_QCD and non-perturbative, and a tail region, where it is perturbative and hierarchically larger than lambda_QCD. Using field redefinitions and color identities, the cross section factorizes into a hard function H (the square of the Wilson coefficient), jet functions J for the collinear sectors, and an ultra-soft function S. Kinematics fix the collinear labels to q. The measurement is factorized by introducing delta functions and Fourier transforms. Because the hard, jet, and soft functions naturally reside at different scales—mu_h ~ q, mu_j ~ m, and mu_s ~ m²/q—renormalization group evolution is used to resum logarithms of m²/q². The soft function can be decomposed into a perturbative power-law tail and a non-perturbative lambda_QCD component. The observable thrust, defined as tau = 1 - T, is shown to be the sum of the hemisphere masses, leading to a similar factorization with symmetric single-variable jet and soft functions. Perturbatively, the hard function is computed via matching to the quark form factor, the jet function from the imaginary parts of collinear diagrams, and the soft function from Wilson line matrix elements. The renormalization group equations for the jet and soft functions involve convolutions with delta functions and plus functions.

The MAGIC and LST-1 Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes at La Palma, Spain, operate On-Site Analysis (OSA) pipelines to automatically process raw data for daily checks and rapid analysis. MAGIC's OSA has run since 2012 on a ~50-core system, processing up to 2 TB/day to high-level products including spectra and sky maps. LST-1's OSA, operational since 2021, processes up to 30 TB/day on 1,800 cores to reconstructed events (DL2), with higher-level products being added. Both use Python-based pipelines launched via crontab, process data in parallel through batch systems (Torque for MAGIC, SLURM for LST-1), and follow similar data levels from raw (DL0) to calibrated (DL1), reconstructed (DL2), and instrument response functions (DL3). Next-day results are typically available before 14:00 local time. The systems provide web-based supervision and email alerts, with error-checking and limited recovery procedures currently implemented only for MAGIC. Post-processing data transfer to off-site centres is handled by independent systems. The authors conclude that reliable next-day OSA is essential for very-high-energy observatories, requiring tight coordination with observatory databases and simulations, automation with means for human intervention, and comprehensive error recovery, and they note these systems can serve as prototypes for future CTAO pipelines.

A 1948 directive established the CIA’s Office of Policy Coordination (OPC) to conduct covert actions including propaganda, sabotage, and subversion. Initially guided directly by the State Department and military, by 1950 policy guidance flowed through the Director of Central Intelligence (DCI). During the Korean War, covert action expanded; NSC 10/5 (1951) broadened CIA authority, and by the end of the Truman administration only the DCI and President could authorize operations. The Eisenhower administration narrowed CIA independence through NSC 5412 (1954) and subsequent directives, creating the NSC 5412/2 Special Group—comprising State, Defense, and presidential representatives—to review and approve covert programs. After the 1961 Bay of Pigs failure, the Special Group assumed greater planning responsibility, and by 1963 it adopted informal criteria, including a $25,000 cost threshold, for determining which projects required its review.

The HHLL (Higher High, Lower Low) strategy is a price action reversal approach. It signals buys in a downtrend after a lower low and higher high, followed by a pullback to the initial low, and sells in an uptrend after a higher high and lower low, followed by a pullback to the initial high. It identifies trend reversals via broken swing patterns. Backtesting is difficult due to discretionary top and bottom identification; the ZigZag indicator is unsuitable due to forward-looking elements. A simplified Philip Morris backtest had 118 trades, a 9.8% CAGR, 1.26% average gain per trade, and a 2.2 profit factor. Code and rules are available for purchase.

The author recalls a failed May 2012 general strike in Brooklyn and contrasts it with new strike calls opposing the Trump administration. Novelist Francine Prose and TV creator David Simon called for a Feb. 17 strike, with organizers creating a website demanding that members of Congress stand up for the U.S. Constitution. A March 8 “mass strike” led by women of color, including Angela Davis and Purdue professor Tithi Bhattacharya, aims to build a “feminism for the 99 percent” following the Jan. 21 Women’s March. Avoiding the term “general strike” due to anti-striking laws and the risk of retaliation against vulnerable women, organizers are planning inclusive local actions such as walkouts, boycotts, and demonstrations. Supporters include the Chicago Teachers Union, Black Lives Matter leaders, Palestinian rights groups, and the National Organization for Women. While critics argue a traditional U.S. general strike is unrealistic, organizers draw on these international models. With as many as 5 million people having joined the Women’s March, even partial participation on Feb. 17 and March 8 could help Americans relearn effective large-scale strike tactics.

Fullbacks primarily serve as blockers in pro-style football offenses, lining up in the backfield to assist in run and pass blocking, particularly at the second level. Though less athletic and smaller than tight ends or running backs, they are valued for their toughness, tenacity, and physicality. While rarely carrying the ball, they may be used in short-yardage situations or as occasional pass targets. The position name derives from rugby alignment conventions. Ideal fullbacks are typically 5'11" to 6'1" and 235–250 pounds with a thick build. Notable players include Mike Alstott and Larry Csonka. Despite limited statistical recognition and declining use in spread offenses, the fullback remains essential for traditional rushing attacks.

The passage details SD Memory Card Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00 commands and operations. SET_DSR (CMD4) configures card driver stages. CMD7 selects a single card for Transfer State or returns cards to Stand-by State. Data Transfer Mode uses point-to-point addressed commands; reads (CMD17, CMD18) and writes (CMD24, CMD25, etc.) can be aborted by CMD12. The card signals busy via DAT0 during programming. Block length for memory access is fixed at 512 bytes for SDHC and SDXC cards, which use block addressing, while SDSC cards use byte addressing and variable block lengths up to 512 bytes. Erase, DISCARD, and Full User Area Logical Erase (FULE) operations use CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38 with specific arguments and busy timeouts. Lock and unlock functions use CMD42 with password (PWD), Force Erase Password (FEP), and Card Ownership Protection (COP) states; locked cards restrict data access but accept basic commands. ACMD6 sets bus width, rejected if the card is locked. CMD6 switches card functions including access mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit, returning 512-bit status. CMD8 initializes cards compliant with Version 2.00 or later. CRC7 protects commands and responses, while CRC16 protects data blocks. Hosts must observe timeouts: 100 ms for reads and 250 ms (up to 500 ms for SDXC in some cases) for writes.

The passage describes waveguide devices and methods for achieving uniform output illumination in applications such as head-mounted displays (HMDs), head-up displays (HUDs), and near-eye displays. A central problem addressed is banding—illumination non-uniformity arising from gaps or overlaps in light extracted during total internal reflection (TIR). Embodiments incorporate a debanding optic into a waveguide device having at least one optical substrate, a light source, a light coupler, and a light extractor to mitigate banding and produce a substantially flat illumination profile, preferably with spatial non-uniformity below 10% or 20%. Debanding optics are realized through multiple configurations, including input and output gratings (switchable, stacked, passive, arrayed, multiplexed, or with rolled K-vectors), index layers (such as gradient index, partially reflecting, or polarization-modifying layers), microdisplay components that provide spatially varied numerical apertures or tilted exit pupils, coupling prisms, and light-absorbing films at substrate edges. The passage further describes color waveguide devices utilizing stacked optical substrates with dichroic input stops, and methods for mitigating banding by coupling incident light into TIR within a substrate and extracting it through a debanding optic.

The U.S. Supreme Court’s October 2025 term, beginning October 6, includes major cases on presidential power, civil rights, and social issues. Over the summer, the Court issued 6-3 shadow docket rulings allowing the Trump administration to fire Consumer Product Safety Commission and Federal Trade Commission commissioners, terminate National Institutes of Health grants, and permit Immigration and Customs Enforcement racial profiling in Los Angeles. Oral arguments are scheduled for November on whether President Trump may impose tariffs under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, and for December on whether to overrule a 1935 precedent and allow the president to fire agency heads. The administration also has asked the Court to review the constitutionality of an executive order restricting birthright citizenship, which every federal court has found unconstitutional. The Court will hold over for new arguments a Louisiana redistricting case considering whether Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act’s disparate impact standard violates the 14th and 15th Amendments, with potential implications for employment and housing discrimination laws. Other cases involve the constitutionality of Colorado’s conversion therapy ban, Idaho and West Virginia laws restricting transgender athletes, and a Fourth Amendment case on whether the emergency aid exception requires probable cause for police to enter a home. Decisions are expected by June 2026.

Centers are the leaders and communicators of the offensive line, often compensating for smaller size with high football IQ, grit, and leadership. They require quick decision-making, extensive film study, and vocal leadership. The position demands agility, strength, run and pass blocking, and snapping. Typical centers have thick, compact builds around 6'1" to 6'4" and 310 to 325 pounds. Notable players include Hall of Famer Jim Otto, who never missed a game, and four-time Super Bowl champion Mike Webster. Larry Connors’ %b strategy, from *High Probability Trading* (2009), uses Bollinger Bands for mean reversion. From 2000 to December 2020, a portfolio of 25 ETFs with max five positions yielded 677 trades, a 75% win ratio, 4.84% CAGR, and 16% max drawdown. This preprint describes a transcriptome-wide association study of whole blood from 194 virally non-detectable people living with HIV (PLWH) on antiretroviral therapy (ART) and 361 HIV-negative individuals. It identified 566 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), significantly enriched for immune system processes and cancer-related pathways. Cell-type deconvolution showed altered proportions of several T cell subsets and resting mast cells, and DEGs were expressed across innate and adaptive immune cells. Based on comparison with prior pre- and post-ART data, 234 DEGs were classified as ART-affected and 332 as ART-unaffected; ART-affected DEGs shifted toward but did not fully reach HIV-negative expression levels, and were enriched in immune, viral, nucleic acid metabolism, and cancer pathways, while ART-unaffected DEGs were more narrowly linked to T cell biology but still contributed to broader pathways. Expression quantitative trait locus analysis identified 258 eGenes. Partitioned heritability analysis revealed significant enrichment for blood cell counts and inflammatory diseases, but not for cancer traits or HIV acquisition. Colocalization analysis found limited shared genetic signals with pancreatic cancer, lymphocytic leukemia, and several immune-related traits. Of the DEGs, 111 are known drug targets, including 55 ART-affected and 42 with approved drugs. The study concludes that chronic suppressed HIV and ART are associated with widespread gene dysregulation linked to immune dysfunction and cancer pathways, largely independent of genetic risk for cancer or HIV acquisition, offering potential therapeutic targets for co-occurring conditions in PLWH.

This preprint reports a case-control study of 108 Thai university students (64 with simple dysmood disorder [SDMD], 44 controls) examining serum lipids in SDMD and first-episode SDMD (FE-SDMD), excluding participants with metabolic syndrome. Compared to controls, SDMD and FE-SDMD patients showed significantly decreased lecithin-cholesterol acyltransferase (LCAT) activity and elevated free cholesterol and ApoE, but no substantial changes in HDL-cholesterol, ApoA1, reverse cholesterol transport (RCT), or ApoB. Statistical analyses indicated that LCAT is the most significant predictor of the depression phenome in FE-SDMD, with its effects mediated entirely by free cholesterol and brooding; in contrast, LCAT effects in major dysmood disorder (MDMD) are mediated by atherogenicity. Decreased LCAT and elevated free cholesterol were observed even in patients without subclinical metabolic syndrome, though interactions between SDMD and subclinical metabolic syndrome further lowered HDLc and RCT and raised the ApoB/ApoA ratio. The authors conclude that SDMD and FE-SDMD represent distinct, pre-proatherogenic subgroups of major depressive disorder, and recommend lipid screening for free cholesterol, LCAT, and ApoE in all first-episode patients to identify risk for subsequent neuroimmune, neuro-oxidative, and cardiovascular complications.

The Imperial fault produced major earthquakes in 1979 (magnitude 6.5) and 1940 (magnitude 7.1). Northern zone swarms could trigger a major San Andreas fault event. On October 22–23, 2001, Enron Corp. disclosed that the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) had requested information regarding the company’s related-party transactions with two investment partnerships—LJM Cayman LP and LJM2 Co-Investment LP—previously run by Chief Financial Officer Andrew Fastow. Following the disclosure, Enron’s stock price fell more than 20 percent to $20.65. The inquiry followed Enron’s announcement of a $1.01 billion third-quarter write-off resulting in a $618 million loss, and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity connected to terminating the LJM partnerships. Analysts and investors raised concerns about the company’s opaque financial disclosures, complex off-balance sheet financing vehicles—including the Whitewing and Marlin trusts—and potential dilution of shareholders if Enron’s credit rating fell below investment grade. Moody's Investors Service placed Enron’s debt on review for a possible downgrade. Multiple class action and shareholder derivative lawsuits were filed against Enron, CEO Kenneth Lay, former CEO Jeffrey Skilling, and Fastow, alleging securities fraud and breach of fiduciary duty. Lay stated the company would cooperate fully with the SEC, and Enron scheduled a conference call to address investor concerns.

This work presents a coarse-grained rod-sphere model for the self-assembly of polymer-grafted nanoparticles, such as poly(2-isopropyl-2-oxazoline) (PiPrOx)-grafted silica nanospheres, where flexible bead-chain models are inadequate. The model represents the nanoparticle as a sphere and the crystallized polymer bundle as a rigid tethered rod. Molecular dynamics simulations of 10,648 rod-sphere particles investigated three rod interaction types—lock-and-key, symmetric, and unspecific—across varying temperatures and sphere-to-rod size ratios (R/r). Mesostructures were classified using a dimensionality parameter derived from the gyration tensor and a degree of order parameter. Simulations yielded ordered mesostructures spanning zero to three dimensions—including bulk assemblies, monolayers, bilayers, ribbons, fibers, worms, stars, and spheres—plus disordered gels and liquid phases. Increasing the sphere size relative to the rod creates geometric frustration that reduces mesostructure dimensionality, consistent with surfactant assembly theory. Lock-and-key rods favor bulk, bilayer, ribbon, and star structures; symmetric rods additionally produce fibers and monolayers; unspecific rods enable higher-temperature ordering and yield gels, worms, and liquid phases. Notably, ribbons spontaneously twist into double helices when the sphere radius is comparable to or larger than the rod radius, with pitch decreasing as sphere size increases. The model reproduces experimental PiPrOx-silica structures and offers a framework for designing anisotropic nanoscale building blocks, though it simplifies the experimental system to a single rod and shorter timescales.

In assuming the Presidency after a predecessor twice entrusted with the office, the speaker acknowledges the founders and states he relies on governmental cooperation, the people, and Providence. He describes the nation as prosperous and respected, asserting that preserving its institutions requires upholding the Constitution and the compromises of its framers, who balanced federal and state sovereignty. He argues that fifty years of experience have disproven fears regarding public debt, the loss of the first President’s stabilizing influence, self-government, war, territorial expansion, and federal-state collisions. He identifies slavery as a source of anticipated discord, praises the founders’ forbearance, and declares himself an uncompromising opponent of congressional abolition of slavery in the District of Columbia against slaveholding states’ wishes and of any federal interference with slavery in the states where it exists, pledging to veto conflicting legislation. He commits to strict adherence to the Constitution, confining federal action to delegated domestic and foreign affairs, and outlines a foreign policy of universal friendship, neutrality, equal commerce, and firm defense of national rights. He pledges faithful execution of the office and invokes divine protection.

A professor at MIT lectures on measuring social preferences through interactive games played by the class. The session demonstrates the Dictator game, where a divider chooses how much to share with a passive receiver; the Ultimatum game, where a proposer offers a split that a responder can accept or reject; and the Trust game, where an investor sends money that is multiplied and a responder returns a portion. Variations include public versus private decisions, different stakes using candy, apples, and cash, and allowing communication between participants. The professor also explains and applies the strategy method, eliciting fully contingent plans from players to gather more information efficiently while minimizing payouts. He notes that the in-class demonstrations are less rigorous than standard experimental economics procedures and states that the next class will examine careful research findings and whether these lab games predict real-world behavior.

The flea flicker is a football trick play designed to resemble a run, where the running back receives a handoff and tosses the ball back to the quarterback to throw downfield while the defense is out of position. Credited to Illinois coach Bob Zuppke in a 1925 game, its name comes from his description of a dog flicking off fleas. Because the quarterback relinquishes possession during the play, intentional grounding can be penalized. Examples include a 2022 Michigan Wolverines touchdown against TCU, a reverse flea flicker where Baker Mayfield threw to Dimitri Flowers, and a fake flea flicker where the runner fakes tossing the ball back to the quarterback to clear space.

The ADS868xW features an internal overvoltage protection circuit on each analog input that, together with recommended external protection for surges, ESD, and EFT, uses input and PGA gain-setting resistors and antiparallel diodes to limit current. When powered on with AVDD = 5V and low source impedance, the internal OVP withstands up to ±20V on the input pins; when AVDD is floating, the limit is ±15V. Higher source impedance increases the OVP range but causes gain errors and adds noise. The device includes a programmable gain amplifier that converts single-ended or differential inputs to drive the internal SAR ADC, adjusts common-mode levels, and maximizes dynamic range via RANGE_SEL[3:0] bits using a precisely matched resistor network. A second-order, 500kHz antialiasing low-pass filter follows the PGA, and an integrated high-bandwidth ADC driver supports the sample-and-hold requirements. The device operates with either an internal 4.096V reference—enabled by default and requiring a 4.7µF decoupling capacitor on REFIO—or an external 4.096V reference applied to REFIO with an internal buffer driving REFCAP, which requires 10µF and 1µF capacitors. Internal reference accuracy is factory trimmed but can shift due to solder heat stress; it is temperature compensated over –40°C to +125°C, and the reference buffer exhibits typical drift of 0.5ppm/°C and maximum drift of 2ppm/°C. The ADC supports single-ended and differential bipolar and unipolar input ranges with straight-binary output and an LSB size of FSR/2^16. Alarm features include an active-high ALARM output when configured, a user-programmable input alarm with independent high/low thresholds and common hysteresis, and an AVDD alarm with fixed 4.7V and 5.3V thresholds; active and tripped flags are available in ALARM_REG. The multiSPI interface supports legacy SPI-compatible protocols and source-synchronous modes with single or dual SDO outputs, as well as daisy-chain topologies for multiple devices. The device operates in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states controlled by the RST and CONVST/CS pins, where RST can issue either an application reset or a full power-on reset. Data transfer uses 32-bit frames with commands to read, write, set, or clear register bytes or half-words, and output data can append device address, range flags, alarm flags, and parity bits. Nine configuration registers manage device ID, reset and power control, SDI/SDO protocols, data output formatting, input range and reference selection, and alarm thresholds. The device uses separate AVDD and DVDD supplies, each decoupled with 10µF and 1µF capacitors, and offers NAP and power-down modes to reduce power consumption. Layout recommendations include partitioning analog and digital sections and placing decoupling capacitors close to pins without intervening vias.

This MIT lecture on numerical linear algebra covers solving Ax=b for large sparse matrices via elimination, focusing on "fill-in," where zero entries become non-zero during row operations. It emphasizes that reordering unknowns and equations significantly impacts fill-in. Using a graph model where nodes represent rows and edges represent non-zero entries, elimination removes edges to the pivot node but creates new edges between any two nodes previously connected to it. The lecture discusses reordering strategies including red-black ordering, minimum degree (selecting the node with the fewest connections as the next pivot), Approximate Minimum Degree (AMD), and nested dissection using graph separators (recursively ordering separated subgraphs before their connecting separator nodes). AMD is noted as a commonly favored method, while nested dissection may be preferable for very large or three-dimensional problems. Fill-in is measured by counting non-zeros in the L and U or Cholesky factors. The lecture also cautions that minimizing bandwidth can be counterproductive and describes compact pointer-based lists for representing sparse matrix graphs.

While the September establishment survey showed job losses, the household survey indicated strong labor market growth, with employment rising by 906,000 to a record 154.3 million, unemployment falling to 4.2%, and wages increasing 2.9%. The D.C. Circuit reviewed a Federal Mine Safety and Health Review Commission decision vacating an Administrative Law Judge’s award of Equal Access to Justice Act fees to Contractor’s Sand and Gravel, Inc. (“CSG”). CSG had prevailed against Mine Safety and Health Administration citations alleging improper electrical grounding under 30 C.F.R. § 56.12025; the ALJ found CSG’s frame grounding complied with the regulation and awarded fees, concluding the Secretary of Labor’s position was not substantially justified. The Commission reversed, finding the position substantially justified. The court held the Commission had jurisdiction under 5 U.S.C. § 504(a)(3) to review the ALJ’s award. On the merits, the court ruled the Secretary’s position was not substantially justified because the regulation did not prohibit frame grounding or require a fourth wire, the Secretary offered no evidence that CSG failed to comply with the actual regulatory requirements, and an agency cannot prosecute conduct that violates no existing rule without rulemaking. The court reversed the Commission, restored the ALJ’s fee award, and remanded for determination of costs incurred in the appeal.

Microsoft's September 11, 2015 Form 8-K reports Bradford L. Smith's appointment as President and Chief Legal Officer effective that date. Smith, 56, previously served as General Counsel and Executive Vice President, Legal and Corporate Affairs, and as General Counsel since 2002.

Starting to invest early maximizes wealth accumulation through compounding. Regular, frequent contributions to segregated accounts help build wealth, allow averaging down during market corrections, and enhance compounding by reinvesting interest or dividends. For example, an individual saving €50 monthly from age 20 at 5% return would accumulate €75,000 by age 60, whereas starting at 40 requires €185 monthly. Historical returns for European shares and the German index have been higher. Creating a budget and redirecting variable spending toward investments increases wealth. The article by Antoine Briffa of Calamatta Cuschieri is for educational purposes only, not investment advice.

Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers suffered a season-ending torn ACL and meniscus in his right knee at MetLife Stadium, reviving concerns about the venue's FieldTurf surface. At least 15 players have suffered knee ligament or Achilles tears there since 2020. An opposing team executive said players are "petrified" of playing at MetLife, and NFLPA interim executive director David White raised the turf issue with the Giants. MetLife installed a FieldTurf Core system in 2023 to decrease injuries. The NFL said last year the stadium had one of the lowest injury rates and that there is no plan to change the surface, though over 90% of players prefer grass. Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow also suffered a turf toe injury on FieldTurf Core at Paycor Stadium in Week 2.

Philosophy of education is marginalized within mainstream educational research, which centers empirical quantitative and qualitative methods while relegating theoretical, conceptual, and normative scholarship to peripheral roles. Students often question whether philosophy constitutes research, viewing it as lacking data gathering, and they avoid the field due to economic precarity and the perception that it is professionally inessential compared to empirical approaches favored by funding bodies and job markets. The dominance of “scientistic,” evidence-based discourse—emphasizing randomized controlled trials, generalizability, and impact factors—further devalues philosophical inquiry, despite critiques regarding the limits of inductive reasoning and the neglect of ethical questions about educational ends. Philosophers of education have responded by defending their methods and appealing to values of justice and critical inquiry, though the field remains internally contested regarding its identity, history, and direction. The author argues that the field’s historical sense of precarity and nostalgic “golden years” narrative are largely self-serving fictions that obscure the fact that philosophy of education has always faced marginalization. Rather than seeking a mythical lost unity, the field should embrace its deep pluralism, internal contestation, and critical reflexivity as distinctive strengths, and collectively challenge the orthodoxy that educational research must be empirical.

The S&P 500 rose 2.2% in July, up 7.8% year-to-date, but August started with a 1.6% drop. US large-cap stocks ranked third monthly behind Frontier Markets, with global stocks leading year-to-date. It was a risk-on month with stocks up and bonds down. Medium and long-term trends remain healthy, but short-term technicals are tenuous: 50-day breadth is rolling over from overbought levels with bearish divergence, while volatility and credit spreads see seasonal upturns. Sabine Werner's team at ETH Zurich discovered that cancer cells transfer mitochondria to neighboring fibroblasts via threadlike nanotubes. This influx reprograms the fibroblasts, accelerating their growth and increasing activity of cancer-linked genes. The protein MIRO2 enables the transfer by shuttling mitochondria to the cell edge; without it, transfer cannot occur. In mice, fibroblasts receiving cancer cell mitochondria promoted tumor growth. Cancer cells can also transfer mitochondria to immune cells, weakening their cancer-fighting abilities. The study was published online August 28, 2025.

They agreed that League members should initiate the League’s liquidation. The representative repeated the Soviet desire to include Soviet Republics as initial members while excluding associated and neutral nations, dismissed Switzerland as a host for the organization, and opposed strengthening the Assembly and Court at the Council’s expense. The speaker describes the presidential oath as a mutual covenant to serve the people and uphold the Constitution, Union, and laws equally. He notes the nation’s growth from thirteen to thirty-eight states, westward expansion, increased wealth, education, and social virtues, while acknowledging that not all citizens are prosperous or law-abiding. He advocates for protective tariffs to develop domestic industry, arguing that the elimination of slavery removes sectional obstacles to Southern manufacturing and mining. He affirms the Executive’s duty to enforce all laws uniformly, rejects nullification by individuals or communities, and warns against corporate and civic lawlessness. He supports civil service reform, careful naturalization standards, reducing Treasury surpluses while maintaining the protective tariff, and paying down the public debt. On foreign affairs, he urges non-interference in Europe, opposes European colonialism in the Americas, and seeks peaceful diplomatic relations. He calls for modern naval ships, American steamship lines, improved pensions for Union veterans and their families, the admission of Dakota, Montana, and Washington, election law reform, and education to protect voting integrity. He concludes by urging patriotism over partisanship and expressing confidence in the nation’s future.

The passage proposes a regulatory-grade, semi-public global database for significant AI incidents in financial markets, addressing structural gaps where existing crowdsourced databases omit financial incidents and confidential regulatory reports rarely reach the public. Drawing on aviation’s “black box” and healthcare incident reporting models, the framework mandates that regulators submit standardized reports using percentage-based metrics and omitting temporal data to protect confidential business information and market stability. The database design adapts MiFID II structures with 15 mandatory fields across Market Context, Volume Metrics, Price Impact, and AI-Specific Information, capturing only incidents causing greater than 5 percent price deviation or greater than 20 percent volume anomaly versus 30-day averages. Using 2,999 synthetic records modeled on 20 real regulatory cases, the paper demonstrates systemic risk monitoring—where AI system type impacts trading more than geography and risks propagate uniformly across regions—and market manipulation detection via five distinct trading behavior clusters, including spoofing and layering patterns. The framework aims to reduce information asymmetry, prevent regulatory arbitrage from divergent rules, enable cross-jurisdictional analysis, and bridge traditional oversight with emerging AI governance needs.

Derivatives are financial contracts that derive value from underlying assets such as commodities, stocks, currencies, indices, or interest rates. Common types include futures, options, forwards, swaps, and CFDs. Futures obligate parties to buy or sell assets at predetermined prices on exchanges; options give the right—but not obligation—to buy (call) or sell (put) at a strike price by an expiration date. Forwards are privately negotiated agreements, swaps exchange cash flows between parties, and CFDs represent broker-trader agreements to exchange price differences.

Derivatives are used to hedge risk, speculate on price movements, or access hard-to-trade markets. While producers and institutions often trade to hedge exposure, retail traders frequently speculate, though consistent profitability is difficult due to market volatility, cognitive biases, leverage risks, and the zero-sum nature of the market. The passage advises trading derivatives only when hedging or speculating with a backtested plan, using conservative leverage, and avoiding instruments not fully understood. It recommends Interactive Brokers for retail traders and notes that a backtested put-selling strategy from 1990 to 2015 produced a 10.1% compound return with lower volatility than the S&P 500.

This paper compares pretrained large language models (LLMs) and small proprietary Transformer models for financial transaction understanding at JPMorgan Chase, specifically standardizing messy point-of-sale transactions to identify merchant IDs. Traditional rule-based methods and Enhanced String Distance struggled with noise, scale, and unseen merchants, leaving 20% of transactions unprocessed. The study evaluated Encoder-Only, Decoder-Only, and Encoder-Decoder architectures in both pretrained (SBERT, Llama3-8b, Flan-T5) and proprietary forms. Results showed that fine-tuned LLMs improved over out-of-the-box versions, but small proprietary models achieved comparable or superior accuracy with dramatically fewer parameters and faster, cheaper inference. For example, a proprietary Decoder-Only model with 1.7 million parameters achieved 72.07% accuracy versus Llama3-8b's 72.89%, while reducing inference time from 735 milliseconds to 95 milliseconds per transaction. The proprietary Encoder-Decoder and Encoder-Only models also outperformed their pretrained counterparts. The authors deployed the proprietary Decoder-Only model to handle previously unmanageable "Rawcleansed" transactions, increasing overall transaction coverage from 80% to 94% and generating approximately $13.2 million in annual cost savings. The study concludes that for specialized, high-volume financial tasks, carefully designed small proprietary models can be more efficient and effective than large pretrained LLMs.

Chess, which originated in India about 1,500 years ago, is described as a strategic game that develops tactical skill, decision-making, planning, and logical thinking. The passage details its educational advantages, including improved concentration, memory, creativity, mathematical thinking, critical thinking, and problem-solving abilities. It also fosters positive social-emotional outcomes such as self-confidence, perseverance, emotional regulation, and sportsmanship. Research cited indicates that students who play chess often show greater academic adaptability and success than peers who prefer other sports. The text advocates for classroom integration of chess, ideally starting at ages four to five, as an extracurricular activity or alongside mathematics and geometry. However, it notes significant methodological challenges in proving chess's unique impact, citing potential Pygmalion effects, the difficulty of measuring abstract cognitive benefits, and conflicting evidence regarding its relationship with intelligence and reading skills. While some meta-analyses report modest gains in mathematics and cognitive skills, the passage emphasizes the need for more rigorous, longitudinal, and mixed-method research to confirm these effects.

The Horns Offense is a basketball set utilizing a 1-4 high alignment with two high post screeners. This allows the ball handler to drive off a screen in either direction, clears baseline help, and creates kick-out opportunities when defenders sag. Because screens are available on both sides, the offense is difficult to disrupt by influencing the ball handler away from a single screen.

The basic option involves the point guard driving off a high post screen and choosing to turn the corner, execute a pull-up jumper, return pass to the rolling screener, or kick out to wing shooters. If the initial action fails, the offense transitions to ball reversal and post isolation. Success depends on reading defensive reactions—such as trailing, sagging, going under, switching, trapping, or overplaying—and executing coordinated counters like point drives, kick-outs, post rolls, slips, or pops.

Variations include High Post Rub, Picket Fence, Twin Sides, Loop, and Hand Back Lob, which adapt the twin screen action to personnel. Installing the offense requires proper footwork, timing, non-verbal communication, and experience, taught through breakdown drills and scrimmaging. Game strategies emphasize scouting opponents, varying alignments, and attacking weak defenders. Even teams not running the Horns Offense must be prepared to defend it, as it is one of the most commonly used sets.

The document defines the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol. Version 2 introduces initial SEV-SNP support and hypervisor feature advertisement via a 52-bit FEATURES bitmap, along with additions such as XSS MSR reporting, a GHCB SW_SCRATCH shared area requirement, and restricted APIC emulation. Revisions 2.01 through 2.04 updated the SEV-SNP Secrets Page Guest Reserved Area for 64-bit guest request message sequence numbers; added a Versioned Loaded Endorsement Key (VLEK) GUID and expanded hypervisor error code use in SW_EXITINFO2; introduced support for retrieving the guest APIC ID list, running multiple VMPL levels, and SEV-ES page state change notification; documented an EFI Confidential Computing Blob protocol for communicating the secrets and CPUID pages; and added SEV trusted IO (SEV-TIO) for trusted PCIe devices, Secure AVIC backing page support, a new GHCB MSR protocol function, and clarifications on hardware debug support and hypervisor behavior for unsupported MSR protocol functions.

The GHCB MSR protocol uses the lower 12 bits of MSR 0xc001_0130 for requests and responses, including hypervisor feature support, SEV information, CPUID retrieval, AP reset hold, preferred GHCB GPA retrieval, GHCB GPA registration and unregistration, page state change, Run VMPL, and termination. The GHCB GPA must be 4K-aligned and is saved and restored by hardware through the VMCB. The hypervisor must not intercept MSR 0xc001_0130. SEV-SNP guests must register a GHCB GPA before first use, and registering a new GPA automatically unregisters any previous one.

Non-Automatic Exit (NAE) events require the guest to copy register state into the GHCB, set the VALID_BITMAP, and invoke VMGEXIT. Supported NAE events include IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, MMIO access using a decrypted buffer in the GHCB shared area, Page State Change operations (private, shared, PSMASH hint, UNSMASH hint), SNP Guest Requests using shared request and response pages, SNP Extended Guest Requests returning certificate GUIDs (VCEK, VLEK, certificate chain), AP Creation to manage vCPU VMSA pages at specified VMPL levels, #HV doorbell page configuration for Restricted Injection, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List retrieval, SNP Run VMPL, SEV-TIO Guest Requests for device measurements and attestation reports, Secure AVIC backing page registration and unregistration, and Termination Requests. Hypervisors communicate errors using SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2.

SEV-SNP guests are supplied a secrets page and CPUID page. The secrets page contains a guest reserved area with current guest request message sequence numbers for VMPL0–VMPL3 and an AP jump table physical address, and is communicated to the OS via an EFI configuration table. SMP booting under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP requires hypervisors to avoid updating AP register values on the first reset and to use an AP jump table; SEV-SNP AP Creation supports vCPU hotplug. Under Restricted Injection, the hypervisor delivers interrupts and non-maskable events through a shared doorbell page with PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields. Full hardware debug register virtualization is supported when the DebugVirtualization bit is set; otherwise, the hypervisor intercepts DR7. System Management Mode and nested virtualization are not supported.

A 2016 California law allows law enforcement or family to petition for 21-day Gun Violence Restraining Orders to remove weapons from dangerous individuals, extendable to one year. It produced 190 orders in 2016-17, but only 17 were extended, and law enforcement requested most. Florida Senator Marco Rubio introduced similar national legislation after the Parkland shooting. Author State Senator Nancy Skinner said the law, prompted by the 2014 Isla Vista shooting, lets authorities remove firearms from threatening individuals. Law enforcement failed to serve 31 orders.

AMD Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) enables secure, non-persistent runtime updates to AMD-provided binary firmware components—such as ASP firmware, modules, and register settings—included in AGESA releases, without requiring a BIOS reflash or system reset. SFS does not patch x86 code (e.g., SMM, AGESA, UEFI) or run-once code (e.g., AGESA boot loader), and updates do not persist across reboots. The feature is disabled by default and must be enabled in BIOS via specific APCB tokens. Customers deploy an SFS Deployment Agent that communicates with the AMD Security Processor (ASP) using a TEE_EXT_CMD_BUFFER with strict memory alignment requirements. AMD cryptographically signs all update packages, and customers may optionally co-sign by providing an RSA public key during early boot; the ASP verifies signatures before executing patches. Version tracking uses three monotonic levels: SFS Patch Level (SFSPL), Security Patch Level (SPL), and System Patch Level (SYSPL). Packages apply sequentially at runtime, validate existing firmware versions for compatibility, and apply atomically. SEV firmware updates commit automatically and prevent rollback, while SNP updates require HV-FIXED pages.

Pharmaceutical dosage form testing systems verify drug efficacy, bioavailability, and physical strength through QC tests such as weight variation, content uniformity, hardness, friability, disintegration, and dissolution. The global market is expected to grow significantly due to regulatory requirements and advanced technology, though high costs and a lack of skilled personnel may restrain growth. North America dominates, followed by Europe, while APCEJ and China are emerging regions. Key participants include SOTAX AG, ABC Laboratories, Almac, Dalton Pharma Services, GEA Process Engineering, Micromeritics Instrument Corporation, Quality Chemical Laboratories, and SCYNEXIS, Inc.

IHE podcast covers federal higher ed policy: minority-serving institution cuts, international student restrictions, student borrowing rule making, Compact for Academic Excellence, upcoming news, and other topics.

The passage describes NVIDIA's Blackwell GPU architecture, focusing on power efficiency, DLSS 4, neural shaders, and product specifications. Accelerated frequency switching and faster low-latency sleep states—including entry into the deepest sleep 10x faster than Ada—save power, enabling higher performance bursts and up to 50% power savings in workloads like small language model inference. DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, using fifth-generation Tensor Cores and a new AI model to generate up to three additional frames per rendered frame with 40% faster performance and 30% less VRAM, while enhanced Flip Metering in the display engine improves frame pacing. DLSS 4 also adopts transformer-based neural networks for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, replacing CNNs to improve temporal stability, motion detail, and image quality. Blackwell introduces neural shaders through the Cooperative Vectors API, enabling AI techniques such as RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression—which reduced VRAM usage by over 3x in a demo—Stochastic Texture Filtering, Neural Radiance Cache for indirect lighting, RTX Skin for subsurface scattering, and RTX Neural Faces using generative AI. The architecture includes three main GPUs: GB202 powers the GeForce RTX 5090 with 92.2 billion transistors, 24,576 CUDA cores, and a 512-bit memory interface; GB203 powers the RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti with 45.6 billion transistors, 10,752 CUDA cores, and a 256-bit interface; and GB205 powers the RTX 5070 with 31 billion transistors, 6,400 CUDA cores, and a 192-bit interface.

Researchers document the Voice Reasoning Gap (VRG), a significant and consistent performance degradation in voice-interactive systems compared to text models on complex, multi-step reasoning tasks. They introduce VERA, a benchmark of 2,931 voice-optimized episodes across five tracks (Math, Web, Science, Context, and Factual), to measure reasoning under real-time constraints. Results across 12 systems reveal voice models average 42% lower accuracy than text baselines, with gaps exceeding 68 percentage points on complex domains, and show a stark latency-accuracy trade-off: models achieving sub-1.5-second response times plateau near 10% accuracy. Diagnostic experiments demonstrate the gap persists even with extended thinking time, perfect acoustic conditions, and sophisticated decoupled cascade architectures that separate reasoning from speech synthesis, suggesting a fundamental architectural conflict between irreversible low-latency audio streaming and the iterative, revisable computation required for deep reasoning. Failure analysis identifies distinct architectural signatures: native streaming models tend to produce fluent but incorrect responses, while decoupled cascades exhibit grounding errors and logical contradictions. The authors conclude that bridging the VRG requires fundamental architectural innovations that decouple thinking from real-time speaking, rather than incremental engineering improvements.

Reuters interviewed Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army (ARSA) fighters and refugees in Bangladesh regarding the August 25 attacks on Myanmar police posts. The NVIDIA Ampere GA10x GPU family, including GA102 and GA104, builds on the Turing architecture to deliver up to 1.7x faster raster and 2x faster ray tracing performance. The GA102 GPU, fabricated on Samsung’s 8nm process with 28.3 billion transistors, features 7 Graphics Processing Clusters, 42 Texture Processing Clusters, and 84 Streaming Multiprocessors containing 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, and 336 third-generation Tensor Cores.

Architectural advances include doubled FP32 throughput via dual datapaths in each SM, second-generation RT Cores that double ray/triangle intersection rates and add hardware-accelerated motion blur, and third-generation Tensor Cores supporting TF32, BF16, and fine-grained structured sparsity for up to 2x throughput. The SM also increases L1 data cache and shared memory capacity and bandwidth.

Memory and I/O enhancements include GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling (delivering up to 936 GB/s bandwidth), GDDR6 for professional GPUs, third-generation NVLink providing 112.5 GB/s between two GPUs, and PCIe Gen 4. RTX IO enables GPU-based loading and decompression to reduce CPU overhead.

GA102 powers the GeForce RTX 3090 and 3080, the RTX A6000 workstation GPU, and the A40 data center GPU, while GA104 powers the RTX 3070. The RTX A6000 and A40 include 48 GB of GDDR6 memory, scalable to 96 GB via NVLink. The A40 offers up to 2x greater power efficiency than its predecessor. GA10x GPUs also support HDMI 2.1, 8K display output, AV1 hardware decode, and seventh-generation NVENC.

The TLV32xx comparator family features rail-to-rail inputs extending 200mV beyond the supply rails and 1.8mV of internal hysteresis. Inputs must stay within specified limits, require current limiting to 10mA, and unused inputs must not be tied together but instead tied to voltages within the specified range that provide at least 50mV differential. The family offers push-pull outputs that source and sink current but must not be connected to other outputs or shorted to rails, and open-drain outputs that enable logical OR'ing and level translation with recommended pull-up currents of 100µA to 1mA. Unused push-pull outputs must float, while unused open-drain outputs may float or tie to V-. Internal ESD protection clamps inputs to the rails. A Power-On Reset circuit holds the output low for up to 32µs after the 1.65V threshold is crossed until the supply is at least the minimum supply voltage. Propagation delay depends on overdrive voltage, and external hysteresis can be added via resistor networks. High-speed PCB layout requires 0.1µF bypass capacitors near supply pins and minimized coupling between inputs and outputs.

Gavin will resign as Delta College president in January after serving since 2021 to lead a national coalition defending equity in higher education. The Supreme Court heard arguments in a habeas case involving federal prisoner Michael Bowe, who seeks to challenge his firearm conviction after a court of appeals dismissed his request to file a successive Section 2255 motion. The federal government argued jurisdictional limits were sufficiently clear and a dismissal counts as a denial. A court-appointed amicus defended the lower court ruling. The justices focused largely on jurisdiction, and there did not appear to be five votes to hold that § 2244(b)(1) applies to federal inmates.

Python is an open-source, high-level programming language widely used for algorithmic trading, data analysis, and backtesting because it is easy to learn, offers free commercial-use packages, and supports scientific libraries such as Pandas, NumPy, and Zipline. Algorithmic trading uses computer programs to analyze markets and execute trades based on predefined rules. Backtesting evaluates a strategy’s potential by applying it to historical price data, which helps identify bugs and assess past performance, though it does not guarantee future success and typically excludes trading fees. Common Python backtesting frameworks include PyAlgoTrade, Backtrader, Fastquant, LEAN (QuantConnect), and Zipline, each with distinct advantages and drawbacks; QuantConnect and Backtrader are often highlighted as popular choices. The backtesting process generally involves importing libraries, downloading OHLCV data, splitting it into in-sample and out-of-sample sets, running the test, optimizing variables, and analyzing results. The passage also argues that coding skills are not essential for trading success and suggests that stand-alone software such as Amibroker or Tradestation may be preferable for traders who wish to avoid spending time on platform development.

The lecture introduces data structures for memory hierarchies through two models. In the external memory (or I/O) model, performance is measured by block transfers of size B between a cache of size M and a slow disk. Key results include scanning in Θ(N/B), B-tree search/insert/delete in Θ(log_{B+1} N), sorting in Θ((N/B) log_{M/B}(N/B)), permuting in the minimum of N and the sorting bound, and buffer trees achieving the sorting bound per operation amortized while supporting delayed queries and batch updates.

The cache-oblivious model assumes the algorithm does not know B or M and relies on automatic cache management; a correct algorithm is simultaneously optimal for all values of B and M. Results here match external memory for scanning, search/insert/delete, and sorting, but permuting cannot achieve the min bound, and priority queues require a “tall cache” assumption where M is Ω(B^{1+ε}).

For static cache-oblivious search, a van Emde Boas layout recursively splits a binary tree at its middle level and stores each recursive piece contiguously in memory, yielding O(log_B N) memory transfers. To make it dynamic, an ordered file maintenance structure stores keys in sorted order with gaps, while a static van Emde Boas layout tree sits on top with cross-links storing subtree maxima. Updates modify the ordered file and propagate changes in post-order, initially costing O(log_B N + log² N / B) amortized.

To improve updates, indirection is applied: the top tree stores only N/log N representative items, and the remaining items are held in bottom chunks of size Θ(log N). This slows updates to the top structure by a factor of log N, reducing the amortized structural update cost to O(log N / B). Consequently, search costs O(log_B N), and an update costs O(log_B N + log N / B) including the initial search.

FMI projects the global surface protection films market will reach US$ 2,081.6 Mn by 2027 at 5.7% CAGR from US$ 1,196.2 Mn in 2017. The 50–100 microns segment holds almost 38% share. ChatGPT, an OpenAI conversational AI launched in November 2022, can assist traders by analyzing market data, generating trading ideas, and creating Python code for backtesting strategies. The Supreme Court of Kentucky reversed the Court of Appeals and affirmed the Daviess Circuit Court in a workers’ compensation case under KRS 342.120(4). David Bunch, who had prior back injuries in 1964 and 1976, suffered a work-related back injury in April 1977 resulting in 100% disability. The Workers’ Compensation Board found 15% attributable to the 1977 injury, excluded 55% as prior occupational disability, and assigned 30% to the Special Fund for arousal of a dormant condition. The Court of Appeals had directed that the 55% be apportioned to the Special Fund. The Supreme Court held that the test is the degree of occupational disability immediately before the subsequent injury, not whether the employee was working. It ruled that prior active occupational disability is not compensable by the Special Fund and affirmed the exclusion of the 55%.

Leeds United lost 1-0 to Wolverhampton Wanderers at Elland Road on April 17, 2017, in an EFL Championship match attended by 32,351. Nouha Dicko scored in the 39th minute. Pan Finance, a print journal and news website with offices in London, Lagos, Barcelona, Miami and Sharjah and readership across 150 countries, provides worldwide intelligence on economics and global commerce. Cleveland Browns head coach Kevin Stefanski is noncommittal about naming Shedeur Sanders as the backup quarterback and will let the week play out before deciding. Analyst Stephen A. Smith expressed disbelief that Stefanski has not named Sanders the backup.

Michael Bowe pleaded guilty to federal charges, including a Section 924(c) firearm offense, for a 2008 Florida armored car robbery and was sentenced to 24 years. Starting in 2016, he filed habeas petitions under the federal inmate statute challenging his conviction. Supreme Court rulings in 2019 and 2022 narrowed the definition of a crime of violence, so his underlying robbery convictions no longer qualified. Before the Supreme Court, Bowe seeks to clear procedural hurdles for successive habeas relief. He argues that a gatekeeping provision barring Supreme Court review of successive petition rulings applies only to state inmates, not federal inmates, and raises a constitutional question under the Exceptions Clause. He also contests the application of a provision barring claims presented in prior applications; the government concedes this applies only to state inmates but argues other doctrines could limit repetitive filings. The court appointed a former clerk to defend the lower court’s contrary position.

Air Canada apologized and offered Brett Doyle's family a C$2,500 voucher after bumping his 10-year-old son from an oversold Charlottetown-to-Montreal flight en route to Costa Rica. Coaches placing youth soccer players must consider formations, player abilities, and temperaments. Basic positions—goalkeeper, defender, midfielder, and forward—require specific skills. Coaches should evaluate players through observation, structured drills, scrimmages, and player input. Classic generalizations suggest physical and mental traits for each role, such as height for goalkeepers, endurance for midfielders, and aggression for forwards. After evaluation, coaches select a formation, assign position names, distribute diagrams, and place players. During practice, teams move as units and learn functional expectations for each role. Coaches must avoid type-casting, ensuring all players experience every position to support development. Decisions must also balance competitiveness with equal playing time, varied exposure, and accommodation of differing skill levels.

This study examines digitalization in Ethiopian higher education institutions (HEIs). While digital transformation supports the UN Sustainable Development Goals, Ethiopia faces significant barriers, with only 25% internet penetration—below the least developed country and African averages. Ethiopia has enacted national policies including the national ICT policy, Digital Ethiopia 2025, and higher education-specific frameworks developed by the former Ministry of Science and Higher Education, such as the National ICT Policy and Strategy for Higher Education and TVET and the Digital Skills Country Action Plan. Initiatives including the Ethiopian Education and Research Network (EthERNet), the National Academic Digital Repository (NADRE), and the National Academic Digital Library (NADLE) have been launched but remain limited in scope and resources. Current practices focus primarily on administrative digitization rather than teaching, learning, or research, a limitation exposed during the COVID-19 pandemic. Key deterring factors include poor internet connectivity and bandwidth, inadequate ICT infrastructure and electricity, a state telecommunications monopoly, shortages of skilled ICT personnel, insufficient digital skills among teachers and students, and institutional resistance to change due to past failed reforms. The study concludes that policy alone is insufficient without improved infrastructure, affordable internet, and capacity building, and argues for shifting government focus from HEI expansion to quality and relevance through digital transformation.

US WTI crude futures fell as rising shale output undermined OPEC efforts to support prices. US drillers added rigs for a 13th consecutive week, raising production to 9.24 million barrels per day. While geopolitical tensions in Libya and North Korea eased and Chinese economic data was strong, increased US supply countered these factors. A jury will decide if Tomas Gajowniczek is not guilty by reason of insanity for attempting to murder his partner Alicja Kalinowska in Dublin in June 2016. Short interest is the percentage of shorted shares relative to total outstanding shares, while the short-interest ratio measures the average days needed to cover a short position by dividing shorted shares by average daily volume. FINRA requires broker-dealers to report short positions twice monthly. Empirical studies, including Nasdaq research on Russell 3000 stocks from 2000–2020 and a 2016 CFA Institute report covering 1973–2014, indicate that high short interest predicts weak future returns, with the most shorted stocks performing significantly worse than those with low short interest. Short squeezes, such as GameStop in 2021, occur when short sellers are forced to buy back shares at rising prices, but these events are rare outliers rather than the norm. Short selling is difficult and generally a poor standalone strategy given the market’s long-term upward trend, though it may serve a role in risk mitigation within broader strategies like pairs trading. Overall, the evidence concludes that high short interest is bad for future stock returns.

Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning typically assumes scalar rewards, limiting its applicability to real-world settings where agents face multiple conflicting objectives that are strategically coupled across agents. This paper introduces the Multi-Objective Markov Game (MOMG) and the Pareto-Nash Equilibrium (PNE), which merges strategic stability with multi-objective optimization. The authors prove PNEs exist in finite MOMGs and establish their equivalence to Nash Equilibria of linearly scalarized games. They also propose computationally efficient alternatives—the Weak PNE and Pareto Correlated Equilibrium (PCE)—and develop a decentralized online learning algorithm that provably converges to PCE.
