The passage defines the SEV-ES and SEV-SNP Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol. It describes GHCB negotiation using MSR 0xc001_0130 and VMCB offset 0x00a0 to establish protocol versions and the page table encryption bit. The document details Guest Non-Automatic Exits (NAE), which raise #VC exceptions handled via VMGEXIT, and lists supported NAE events including IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, MMIO access, Page State Change, SNP Guest and Extended Guest Requests, SNP TIO Guest Requests, AP Creation, #HV Doorbell Page operations, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, Secure AVIC backing pages, and Termination Requests. It specifies SMP booting procedures, AP jump tables, and SNP AP Creation. It also covers the SEV-SNP secrets page guest reserved area, CPUID page, EFI Confidential Computing Blob configuration table, and SNP Restricted Injection using a shared #HV doorbell page with PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields for host-to-guest interrupt notification. The document states that System Management Mode and nested virtualization are unsupported and outlines requirements for debug register virtualization and NMI completion signaling.

The Appellate Division unanimously affirmed Vu Ngo's conviction for three counts of first-degree robbery. The court declined to review his unpreserved claim of discriminatory peremptory challenge. It held that his hospital detention was lawful: the initial police approach was not an unlawful detention, subsequent brief detention was not a forcible seizure, and police had reasonable suspicion to justify continued detention for identification and questioning.

This study investigated enlarged perivascular spaces (PVS) in 467 people with various epilepsy subtypes and 473 healthy controls using 3T T1-weighted MRI and the PINGU deep-learning segmentation algorithm. All epilepsy subtypes showed significantly enlarged PVS volume fractions in the basal ganglia compared to controls (101–140% increases, large effect sizes), with no significant differences observed in white matter after adjusting for age and sex. The temporal lobe epilepsy with hippocampal sclerosis group exhibited a contra-lateral asymmetry in PVS distribution not present in controls or other epilepsy subtypes. No association was found between PVS burden and illness duration. The authors conclude that basal ganglia PVS are enlarged across epilepsy subtypes and suggest longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether seizures detrimentally affect glymphatic clearance or impaired glymphatics contribute to epilepsy development.

In a Form 8-K dated June 16, 2016, NVIDIA Corporation reported that Executive Vice President, Chief Administrative Officer and Secretary David M. Shannon will retire at the end of the calendar year. Upon his retirement, Senior Vice President and General Counsel Brian E. Cabrera will lead the legal team, and NVIDIA will recruit a leader for the human resources function.

A returned February 16, 2001 email from Jeff Dasovich to Enron colleagues and external contacts discusses a confidential message for Senator Brulte and Enron’s proposed legislative package for California’s electricity crisis. The proposals include increasing supply (SB28X), decreasing demand (AB31X), re-establishing competitive retail markets through direct access (SB27X), and restoring investor-owned utility solvency (AB18X). The email identifies ambiguities in AB1X that create credit risks for the Department of Water Resources’ power purchases, suggests legislative amendments or a California PUC order to resolve them, and warns of a projected summer supply shortfall of approximately 5,000 MW.

The paper presents a correct-by-construction design and Rocq implementation of a fault-tolerant voter unit for input selection in synchronous N-modular redundant measurement systems used in avionics control. The voter selects a prime unit from redundant inputs measuring the same physical quantity, discarding transient errors and isolating permanently faulty units after a persistence limit, while avoiding frequent prime unit switching to maintain stability. The work defines a fault model with self-identifying health status and deviation faults exceeding a noise threshold δ, under a simultaneous fault hypothesis limiting new faults per cycle among non-permanently-faulty units. It formulates consistent functional requirements (R1–R16) for fault identification, isolation, and output generation, analyzes theoretical limits of soundness and completeness for deviation fault identification, and proves the voter algorithm achieves these limits. The voter unit is designed as a parameterized state transition system with configurable reliability parameters and validity status values of valid, unidentifiable, or not valid. Implemented in the Rocq interactive theorem prover using higher-order logics and dependent types, the state and transition definitions carry embedded proof terms ensuring correctness by construction, yielding verified code extractable to OCaml, Haskell, or Scheme.

This document describes AMD’s Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine, an optional extension to Secure Encrypted Virtualization (SEV) and Secure Nested Paging (SNP) that facilitates migrating pages between system physical addresses while maintaining guest physical addresses. TMPM offloads migration from software, pauses DMA traffic during page copy and IOMMU page table updates, and acts as a trusted agent for SNP guest pages. It requires IOMMU enablement.

The guide defines two primary commands: PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO migrates hypervisor-owned or default pages, including those actively targeted by DMA, by updating IOMMU host page table entries; PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST migrates SNP guest pages from Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid states to destination pages in a Pre-Migration state. Commands support batching up to 128 pages via a Page Migration List, with maximum performance achieved at 128 pages per command.

TMPM uses a dedicated ring buffer and mailbox registers for command submission. Driver initialization requires verifying the ENGINE_READY bit, configuring the ring buffer address and size, and signaling DRIVER_INITIALIZED. Firmware reloads are permitted only when no operations are in flight and require the PSP mailbox protocol; EPYC Family 19h uses a specific reload path identified by FW_VER_Major 71.

Restrictions include mandatory 4KB page alignment for migrated data, and certain structures such as IOMMU page tables, vIOMMU buffers, and the ring buffer itself cannot be migrated. Errors are reported via command status fields, ring buffer status registers, and Machine Check Architecture for hardware failures.

Doctors say most eye cancer cases in India are detected late, stressing awareness of symptoms. Specialized facilities and trained ocular oncologists are scarce, with only about 10 in the country. Retinoblastoma is the most common form in children under five, affecting one in 20,000 kids, and early detection is crucial to save eyesight and lives.

This study investigates how online informal education contributes to personalized learning in formal design education. Distinguishing between formal, non-formal, informal, and random education, the article examines how digitalization has transformed learning through online repositories, multimedia, and global collaborative networks. Employing secondary research and case study analysis, the authors evaluate two synchronous online informal programs in computational design: "Introduction to Computational Design" by Driven by Volumes and "Sustainability through Computational Design" by Rethinking the Future. Findings show that online workshops and courses provide applied, multidisciplinary training, enhance algorithmic thinking, and facilitate rapid digital design production and environmental analysis. However, limitations include financial and resource accessibility barriers, restricted participation capacity, lack of physical interaction, insufficient promotion of socio-cultural values, and exclusion from formal education transcripts. The study concludes that while online informal education fosters personalized learning and professional skill development in design, addressing accessibility and integrating these programs into formal curricula are necessary to maximize their educational impact.

This study develops an integrated environmental education model based on the theory of multiple intelligences for students in expanded educational opportunity schools in Nakhon Pathom Primary Education Area 2, Thailand. The three-phase research involved studying environmental education conditions, developing integration tools, and evaluating effectiveness using questionnaires, structured interviews, and SWOT analysis with 364 students, 44 teachers, and 3 directors. Results identified community pollution issues including agricultural chemical residues in soil, contaminated water, air pollution, and garbage disposal. Students demonstrated moderate environmental education learning levels overall (mean 3.95), with the lowest awareness (mean 3.79), while teachers showed excellent levels (mean 4.48). The model achieved efficiency of 81.51/82.11, exceeding the 80/80 standard, with high content validity (mean 4.60) and construct validity (mean 3.97). Post-study achievement scores (mean 24.63) were significantly higher than pre-study scores (mean 5.90), and student satisfaction with the integrated model was high (mean 3.83).

On January 26, 2015, Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K with the SEC announcing its financial results for the quarter ended December 31, 2014, via a press release furnished as Exhibit 99.1. Frank H. Brod, Chief Accounting Officer, signed the report.

An 1893 anonymous notice by Mr. Kung-i of Pai-ling Shan denounces foreign religious doctrine as false and corrupting, accusing its leaders and adherents of hypocrisy, greed, immorality, and financial exploitation, and threatening attack if they do not depart. In a separate 1894 dispatch, Confucian followers in Seoul petitioned the King to compel Tong Hâk adherents to return to orthodoxy or be exterminated; the King replied that the government would handle the matter and admonished the petitioners to study their own principles, while concerns that Western religion would also be denounced proved unfounded.

The bull market signal strategy buys the S&P 500 when it closes 18 consecutive days above its 200-day moving average during a bear market, and sells when the index drops 20% from its all-time high. Backtested from 1927 to the present, it generated 12 signals, a CAGR of 7.24%, a maximum drawdown of 60% (approximately 25% excluding 1929), and a Sharpe ratio of 0.24. After the signal, the S&P 500 averaged gains of 9.54% after six months and 21.84% after one year, with positive returns 100% of the time at 12 months. Compared to the Golden Cross strategy, which produced 49 signals, this model generated fewer false signals, performed better, and was invested 30% more time. The last signal triggered on February 15, 2023.

A seven-judge Supreme Court Bench ruled that re-promulgating ordinances is a fraud on the Constitution and subverts democratic legislative processes. In cases regarding Bihar teacher appointments, the majority held that the President's and Governor's satisfaction under Articles 123 and 213 is subject to judicial review. The majority deemed laying ordinances before the legislature mandatory, though one judge disagreed and the CJI left the issue open. The Court held that ordinance-making power is conditional and legislative in character, and failure to lay an ordinance before the legislature is a serious constitutional infraction. It ruled that salaries already paid to the teachers should not be recovered.

Ola and Uber drivers in Delhi-NCR threatened a one-day strike Tuesday over low fares and 25% commission. The Delhi High Court permanently restrained two unions from disrupting services. The Sarvodaya Drivers' Association, representing 1.25 lakh drivers, demands fares rise from Rs 6 to Rs 20 per km. Some groups supported the strike, but Delhi Autorickshaw Sangh and Delhi Pradesh Taxi Union refused. The association warned of indefinite action if ignored.

Dr. Thomas Wilson Ikubese, a 2019 presidential aspirant and convener of the YesWeFit Revolution, joined the Alliance for New Nigeria (ANN) after the Nigerian Intervention Movement adopted it on May 29, 2018. He left the National Conscience Party two weeks earlier, accusing its leadership of over-taxation, and will run for president under ANN while urging supporters and young aspirants to join.

St. George welcomed an 11-person delegation from sister city Ibigawa, Japan, in October 2017, continuing nearly 30 years of exchange. The group included four St. George Marathon runners, among them elite entrants Kenji Miyazaki and Mitsue Tomita. Delegates attended a reception, council recognition, and a luncheon where Mayor Jon Pike and Ibigawa Vice Mayor Sunao Isaji exchanged gifts. They will visit Zion National Park during their five-day stay. St. George will send a delegation to the Ibigawa Marathon on November 12.

Non-inverting hysteresis comparator requires a two-resistor network and voltage reference. VIN must exceed VIN1 to switch high and drop below VIN2 to switch low. Hysteresis is the VIN1 and VIN2 difference.

Rain Bird's WPX battery controller suits sites lacking mains power. IP 68 compliant, submersible, it offers 1, 2, 4, or 6 zones, LCD programming, zone-stacking, one to two years on one or two 9V batteries.

A study by Jonathan Rolland and colleagues in Nature Ecology & Evolution found that mammals and birds adapt to temperature changes two to three times faster than reptiles and amphibians. Analyzing nearly 11,500 species over 270 million years, the researchers attributed endotherms' broader habitat colonization to their ability to regulate body temperature and protect developing young. However, Rolland cautioned that current climate change is too rapid for these historical patterns to ensure survival, noting that pollution, hunting, habitat loss, and invasive species are more immediate threats, with extinction rates now 10,000 times higher than normal. Rolland hopes connecting macroevolution to microevolution will help predict how animal groups respond to future environmental pressures.

The passage details SEV-ES/SNP hypervisor-guest communication protocols. The SNP Run VMPL NAE changes a vCPU's VMPL level using an associated VMSA, returning an error if no VMSA exists. The SEV-TIO extension lets guests bind trusted devices, discovered via TEE-IO PCIe capabilities, with setup by VMPL0 firmware or the OS. The SNP TIO Guest Request NAE requires unencrypted data such as Guest PCI ID, MMIO range, and TDISP status, using shared data pages to optionally return measurements, certificates, and a TDISP attestation report. Secure AVIC provides per-vCPU APIC backing pages via REGISTER_BACKING_PAGE and UNREGISTER_BACKING_PAGE actions. A Termination Request NAE allows guest-initiated termination with reason codes. SEV-ES guests identify support through specific CPUID properties. SMP booting uses pre-set AP register values and an AP jump table for UEFI-to-OS transitions; the SNP AP Creation NAE enables vCPU hotplug by initializing AP state from a VMSA page. NMIs require hypervisor #DB interception and a guest "NMI Complete" message. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported. The #HV doorbell page, configured through VMGEXIT, delivers interrupts and non-maskable events via PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields, with specified host presentation and guest acknowledgment and EOI procedures.

The passage describes an augmented reality system for image-guided surgery. A first healthcare professional wears a head-mounted device with a display and a first tracking device, such as a camera, that tracks a patient marker on a patient's body and a tool marker. The patient marker includes an array of elements configured to have a unique appearance at any location and orientation relative to the tracking device, enabling a computer processor to determine the location and orientation of the head-mounted device relative to the patient without triangulation. The processor generates an augmented reality image on the first head-mounted display, overlaying a virtual image of the tool and patient anatomy onto the actual patient body. When both the patient marker and the tool are within the first tracking device's line of sight, the image is generated using only data from the first tracking device. When at least one is not within the first line of sight, the image is generated at least partially using data from a second tracking device, which may be disposed on a second head-mounted device worn by a second healthcare professional or in a stationary position. In some applications, an inertial-measurement unit disposed on the first head-mounted device tracks its movements when the patient marker is not within the first line of sight. The processor may also generate the image by combining data from both tracking devices.

Market corrections, defined as stock declines of 10% to 20%, have occurred on average every year since 1900, typically lasting about 54 days with an average drop of 13.5%. Fewer than one in five corrections escalate into bear markets, which historically see average declines of 33% and last about a year. Despite average intra-year drops of 14.2% from 1980 through 2015, the S&P 500 achieved positive returns in 27 of those 36 years. The passage argues that investors should avoid panic-selling during downturns, as markets generally rise over the long term. It cites Warren Buffett’s optimism about America’s economic resilience and emphasizes that investors determine their own outcomes through decisions to remain patient or sell in fear.

Kuwait will finish cleaning up an oil spill in southern Gulf waters this week, the oil minister said, without citing a cause. It occurred near Ras al-Zour, site of a refinery. Khajfi Joint Operations said facilities were safe and it activated an emergency plan.
A player described scoring on a set play after exchanging passes with Teemu and driving the net. He said it was less emotional than perceived and his team stayed disciplined to finish the game.

The TPS7H500x-SP series controllers feature single or dual primary switching outputs (OUTA/OUTB) and synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA/SRB) with approximately 150-mA peak current capability, requiring external gate drivers. OUTB and SRB are active only when the duty cycle limit is set to 50% via the DCL pin on specific devices. Dead time and leading edge blank time are programmable via external resistors on most variants, with fixed values on the TPS7H5003-SP. The devices use fixed-frequency peak current mode control, with PWM generation based on the CS_ILIM pin compared against a divided COMP voltage, and include cycle-by-cycle current limiting that triggers hiccup mode when a 1.05-V threshold is exceeded. Programmable slope compensation prevents subharmonic oscillation. A FAULT pin enables external protection shutdown, and pulse skipping prevents operational issues during high-frequency or low-duty-cycle conditions. The controllers support configurable maximum duty cycles of 50%, 75%, or 100% depending on the device and DCL pin connection. Thermal shutdown occurs above 175°C. The series is designed for space-grade DC-DC converters up to 2 MHz, supporting topologies such as buck, forward, push-pull, and full-bridge. An example synchronous push-pull design using GaN devices at 500 kHz illustrates component selection for feedback, dead time, blanking, soft-start, transformer, FETs, output filter, current sensing, hiccup, frequency compensation, and slope compensation. The controllers operate from a 4-V to 14-V supply and require careful PCB layout to minimize noise, including separating analog and power grounds and routing sensitive traces away from switching signals.

The speaker advocates moderate, common-sense reform to address systemic evils, rejecting both reactionary and extremist positions. Government should supervise but not conduct business, seeking equality of opportunity and burden. Laws that prohibit all capital combinations are ineffective and harmful; instead, the law should distinguish between beneficial and harmful combinations, permitting railroad agreements sanctioned and published by the Interstate Commerce Commission. The speaker cites the Commission's view that Supreme Court interpretations make lawful railway operation impossible, and urges legislative amendment. While some taxes should remain local, the national government should adopt graduated inheritance and income taxes to ensure equitable burden-sharing, but with absolute justice and moderation toward both rich and poor.

Apple Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended March 31, 2018. For the second quarter of 2018, net sales were $61.1 billion, up 16% year-over-year, with net income of $13.8 billion and diluted earnings per share of $2.73. For the six months ended March 31, 2018, net sales were $149.4 billion and net income was $33.9 billion. Total assets were $367.5 billion, including $45.1 billion in cash and cash equivalents, while long-term debt was $101.4 billion and total shareholders’ equity was $126.9 billion.

Net sales increased across all geographic segments, driven primarily by higher sales of iPhone, Services, and Other Products. iPhone net sales rose 14% to $38.0 billion on a 3% increase in unit sales. Services net sales grew 31% to $9.2 billion, and Other Products net sales increased 38% to $4.0 billion.

The U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, enacted December 22, 2017, lowered the federal statutory rate from 35% to 21%. The Company recognized a provisional tax expense of $2.6 billion in the first six months and reported an effective tax rate of 14.5% for the quarter and 21.6% for the six months.

During the quarter, the Company spent $23.5 billion on share repurchases and paid $3.2 billion in dividends. The Board authorized a new $100 billion share repurchase program on May 1, 2018. The Company had $111.1 billion in aggregate term debt principal outstanding and $12.0 billion in commercial paper outstanding as of March 31, 2018.

The Company is appealing the European Commission’s State Aid Decision regarding Ireland and expects a recovery amount of approximately €13 billion plus interest. It is also appealing two patent infringement verdicts in VirnetX lawsuits totaling $943 million. The Company adopted ASU 2016-09 for share-based compensation and ASU 2018-02, reclassifying $278 million from accumulated other comprehensive income to retained earnings.

Solar is now the cheapest power source worldwide, costing £0.02 per unit in sunny regions and cheaper than coal, gas, and wind, per researchers at Surrey. Global capacity surpassed 1.5 terawatts in 2024, while battery prices fell 89% since 2010, making hybrid systems competitive with gas. Grid congestion in California and China remains challenging. Smart grids, AI forecasting, and policy support are vital to stabilize networks and accelerate transition.

An internal Enron email from May 18, 2001, compiles press mentions of the company. A Dow Jones column reports that California’s long-term power contracts are jeopardized and notes that Enron, which has been selling aggressively, is looking “like a genius” as western U.S. power prices decline. An options report describes active trading in Enron June options, including an institutional investor buying June 55 calls and selling June 50 puts. Multiple news services report that Saudi Arabia selected international oil companies for three natural gas core ventures requiring combined investment of about $25 billion, reopening its energy sector to foreign investors. Enron and Occidental Petroleum received a stake in Core Venture 2, the Red Sea project led by ExxonMobil. Core Venture 1 (South Ghawar) was awarded to ExxonMobil, Shell, BP, and Phillips, while Core Venture 3 (Shaybah) was awarded to Shell, TotalFinaElf, and Conoco. Leaders for ventures 1 and 3 are expected by June 5, with memoranda of understanding to be signed by early June. The U.S. Energy Department welcomed the selection of American firms and said the decision aligns with the Bush administration’s energy plan.

Sam Bankman-Fried (SBF) founded the crypto trading firm Alameda Research in 2017 and the crypto exchange FTX in 2019 with Gary Wang; Nishad Singh and Caroline Ellison held key roles. FTX grew to become the world’s second-largest crypto exchange by early 2022, valued at $32 billion, and issued the FTT token. Alameda held a majority of FTT and received special privileges on the FTX platform, including a massive line of credit funded by customer assets and an “allow negative” code feature written by Wang and Singh that exempted it from automatic liquidation.

In November 2022, a leaked Alameda balance sheet revealed heavy reliance on illiquid FTT tokens, triggering a loss of confidence, a run on FTX, and a collapse in FTT’s price. FTX paused withdrawals and filed for bankruptcy on November 11, 2022. It was revealed that billions in customer funds had been diverted to Alameda for trading, venture investments, real estate, and political donations.

SBF was arrested and charged with fraud and money laundering; he pled not guilty. Wang, Ellison, and Singh pled guilty to various charges, including conspiracy and campaign finance violations, and admitted to enabling the diversion of funds and inflating revenues. Post-collapse scrutiny fell on investors, auditors, regulators, and celebrities for failing to detect or prevent the lack of corporate controls and misuse of customer assets.

After ignoring risks for a year, investors are skittish. Stocks fell over 2% Friday, capping the worst week in two years, after a jobs report signaled rising wages and potential inflation. The deeper concern is that cheap money from global central banks, which fueled the nine-year stock boom since 2009, may disappear sooner than expected. Stocks sold off, Treasury yields surged, and investors are nervous the global economy is doing too well.

Penn State has banned three student-led outdoor clubs from organizing trips next semester, citing high risk in remote areas with limited emergency access. The decision followed a two-month review without student leader consultation. Officials said the proactive assessment was not based on prior injuries and that a more expensive university-operated program will continue. Student leaders criticized the lack of dialogue and questioned the reasoning.

Android 8.0 Oreo includes Picture-in-Picture (PiP) Mode, which allows supported apps to play video or navigation content in a movable floating window while the user operates other apps. Supported apps include Google Chrome, Google Duo, Google Play Movies & TV, Google Maps, WhatsApp, YouTube, and VLC, though PiP in the YouTube app requires a YouTube Red subscription. As a workaround, users can play a YouTube video in Google Chrome desktop mode, enter full-screen, and tap the home button to generate the floating window. The window can be dragged around the screen, paused, closed via an “X” icon, returned to full-screen, or dragged to the bottom to dismiss. If PiP does not function, it can be enabled in Settings > Apps & notifications > Advanced > Special app access > Picture-in-picture.
Two teens arrested, one on the run after Frankston police pursuit. Subaru with stolen plates sped through road works, dumped in Bayswater. An 18-year-old man taken to hospital after police dog bite.

In *Thomas Henderson v. Alex. Beaton et als.*, the Texas Supreme Court reversed a judgment for defendants in a trespass-to-try-title action over an undivided half interest in a Navarro County league of land. The court held that an 1839 instrument from Mastín Latham to William F. Henderson—through whom the plaintiff claimed—was an absolute, unconditional deed, not an executory contract; the consideration recited past services already rendered, and the clause requiring equal division and Latham’s choice of halves did not create a condition defeating title. Because the instrument was an executed deed, the defenses of stale demand and abandonment were inapplicable. The court also rejected the statute-of-limitations defenses: the ten-year bar was incomplete, as the period from March 1861 to March 1870 was excluded by constitutional provision; the five-year bar failed for lack of evidence that defendants paid taxes; and the three-year bar failed because the occupants held the land as tenants of Latham, giving defendants no title or color of title, while the ten-year defense failed for want of privity. The cause was remanded for further proceedings to ascertain the rights necessary for partition.

The President reports that efforts to persuade Britain and France to revoke their edicts against U.S. commerce have failed; Britain rejected the proposed arrangement, and France has not responded. Consequently, the embargo remains in effect, having preserved maritime property and allowed time for defensive preparations, and Congress must now determine the nation’s course. Documents regarding correspondence with the belligerents and instructions to ministers are submitted. The British government has taken no steps to redress the attack on the frigate Chesapeake. Relations with other European powers are unchanged, though negotiations with Spain are paused. Harmony continues with the Barbary powers, except for a proceeding by the Dey of Algiers against the U.S. consul. Peace with Indian tribes is maintained; some tribes have surrendered accused murderers for trial, and one Cherokee division is considering seeking U.S. citizenship. Coastal defenses and gunboat construction have advanced; militia readiness and domestic arms production have been emphasized. The suspension of foreign commerce has spurred internal manufacturing. Treasury receipts totaled nearly eighteen million dollars, allowing payment of over two million dollars in debt principal and leaving a surplus that Congress may consider applying to internal improvements, education, or other national foundations. The address concludes with gratitude to Congress and citizens, and confidence in the republic’s permanence.

Ukraine partnered with Bitfury Group to place government electronic data on a blockchain platform, which Bitfury's CEO called the largest government blockchain project. A memorandum signed Thursday begins with a pilot launching late this year covering state registers, public services, social security, public health, and energy, before expanding to all areas including cyber security. Sweden, Estonia, and Georgia have smaller programs. Bitfury previously signed a land-titling agreement with Georgia.

Investors face five themes: The Bank of England's "Super Thursday" is expected to bring no rate change but scrutiny of its inflation and growth outlook amid a resurgent pound. Australian and New Zealand central banks meet as cooling housing and strong currencies delay hike expectations, while China data may show slowing inflation and its U.S. trade surplus is watched. The U.S. trade deficit is seen widening on record imports despite a weak dollar, with strong retail sales and a possible government shutdown also in focus. A gap has opened between U.S. and European earnings growth expectations, making European shares potentially vulnerable despite cheaper valuations. Emerging market central banks are active, with Russia expected to cut rates, Mexico and Romania likely to hike, and India expected to hold.

The Seventh Circuit affirmed the district court’s grant of summary judgment to the Village of Orland Park and three police officials in a lawsuit by former police officer Joseph McGreal. McGreal claimed his June 28, 2010 firing was retaliation for protected speech at a November 2, 2009 village board meeting, where he proposed alternatives to police layoffs, and he asserted a state-law intentional-infliction-of-emotional-distress claim. The court held that McGreal provided no admissible evidence that the defendants knew of his speech or that it motivated his termination, and he failed to show that the defendants’ alternative explanations—lying under oath, insubordination, and reckless conduct—were pretextual. The court also held that suspicious timing alone was insufficient to establish pretext. Regarding the emotional-distress claim, the court found McGreal offered no evidence of extreme or outrageous conduct or severe distress, and his admission that his distress was “garden variety” was legally insufficient under Illinois law.

Maddie Sabourin, an 18-year-old Georgia high school senior, is a kidney match for her grandfather, Sam Senseney, who has spent six years on dialysis awaiting a transplant. Despite doctors initially refusing due to her age, she convinced them to approve the donation. Sabourin promoted organ donation awareness through the Miss Georgia Outstanding Teen Pageant and raised $7,500 for the American Kidney Fund. They will meet doctors next week to schedule surgery within the month. Sabourin will miss three weeks of school but said saving her grandfather's life is worth it.

The passage describes example embodiments for 5G systems and core networks, particularly mechanisms for AMF selection supporting isolated network slices. It outlines 5G architecture and network functions (e.g., AMF, SMF, UPF, PCF, NRF, NSSF, UDM), registration management states (RM-DEREGISTERED, RM-REGISTERED), connection management states (CM-IDLE, CM-CONNECTED), and network slice selection assistance information (S-NSSAI, NSSAI). The document defines three network slice isolation levels: fully isolated; partly isolated with shared (R)AN; and partly isolated with shared (R)AN and AMF. During registration, a UE may include network slice isolation information in its request. Based on this information, the UE's subscription data, and operator policies, an NRF, NSSF, or UDM selects an AMF that supports the requested isolation level. The (R)AN then routes the registration to the selected AMF. The embodiments also address PDU session establishment, QoS flows, and user plane connectivity via network slice instances.
Gifts to the Annual Fund support protecting the rule of law, building independent courts, and advancing representation. Donors receive a sticker and magnet set.

In an action by E. F. Joy, assignee of W. W. Montague & Co., to set aside 1893 deeds of gift from Louis Helbing to his wife Louise, the trial court found no intent to defraud creditors. The appellate court affirmed, holding the plaintiff bore the burden to prove fraudulent intent at execution. Although Helbing was solvent when the deeds were made, they were not recorded until December 1895, and he obtained credit before recordation by representing the property as his own; however, this unrecorded status alone was insufficient to show fraudulent intent. There was also no evidence that Louise knew of his representations. The court further held that excluding testimony about personal property events occurring nearly four years after execution was harmless error. The judgment and order denying a new trial were affirmed.

Tropical Storm Nate is expected to strike the U.S. Gulf Coast as a hurricane this weekend, prompting Louisiana to declare a state of emergency and order evacuations from coastal areas ahead of a projected Sunday landfall. The storm, the 15th Atlantic system this year, has killed 22 people in Latin America. Forecasters predict it will strengthen to a Category 1 hurricane. Governor John Bel Edwards mobilized 1,300 National Guard troops and urged residents to prepare by Saturday night. Officials hope the storm’s fast movement will limit rainfall and strain on New Orleans’ fragile pumping system, though the city is taking steps to bolster drainage.

Astronomers from Trinity College Dublin used the James Webb Space Telescope to study rogue planet SIMP-0136, revealing strong auroras, storms, and constant silicate clouds. Led by Dr. Evert Nasedkin and Prof. Johanna Vos's 'Exo-Aimsir' group, the team detected temperature changes smaller than 5°C on the 1,500°C planet and storms similar to Jupiter’s Great Red Spot. Building on Boston University data, the findings represent precise extrasolar atmospheric measurements and may inform future studies of exoplanet weather.

The article examines a pair trading strategy in SPY and TLT following significant opposite-direction moves, such as those on June 18, 2021, when SPY rose 1.43% and TLT fell 1.67%. The strategy goes long SPY and short TLT when both move beyond 1.25 times their 50-day average high-minus-low on the same day. Backtesting from 2003 to June 2021 showed erratic, inconsistent results with a 1.93% CAGR, 60% win ratio, and 0.18% average gain per trade. Adjusting holding periods or movement criteria did not meaningfully improve performance, leading to the conclusion that the strategy is not tradeable.

This retrospective cross-sectional study analyzed factors delaying discharge from a 23-bed subacute Complex Discharge Unit at St James's Hospital, Dublin, during the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic (March 2020–February 2021). Among 390 patients admitted, 83.6% were over 65 years old (median age 79), 59.7% were female, and 48.2% had more than four comorbidities. Prolonged length of stay was defined as exceeding 15 days, and the median unit length of stay was 19.4 days. Kaplan-Meier and stratified Cox regression analyses found that patient-centred needs and complications arising from primary diagnoses or multimorbidity were statistically significant factors prolonging length of stay across age groups (65–85 years), both genders, and multimorbidity strata. Patients aged 65–75, females, and those with more than four comorbidities were more likely to experience prolonged stays. Conversely, complications arising directly from comorbidities, healthcare-associated infections, frailty or falls requiring integrated rehabilitation, and community services were not significant factors for prolonged length of stay. The authors conclude that reducing delays requires addressing complexities from primary diagnoses and patient-centred needs, and these findings can inform future pandemic contingency planning.
OpenAI is preparing a stand-alone app powered by Sora 2 that resembles TikTok, featuring a vertical feed of AI-generated videos, a recommendation algorithm, and options to like, comment, or remix.

The Warren Buffett ETF Portfolio (90/10) originates from a 2013 letter in which Buffett instructed that 90% of his wife's inheritance be invested in a very low-fee stock index fund and 10% in short-term government bonds. The strategy allocates 90% to low-cost, passively managed S&P 500 index ETFs and 10% to government bonds, aiming for long-term growth with reduced risk and lower fees than actively managed funds. The S&P 500 component provides exposure to large U.S. companies with historically strong returns, while government bonds offer a cushion against volatility. The approach emphasizes passive investing and avoiding market timing. Backtests of portfolios combining SPY with SHY, IEI, and TLT indicated that longer-maturity bonds generally produced better returns, with the SPY/TLT allocation performing nearly on par with a 100% SPY holding, though the strategy underperformed during the 2022 bond market decline. Past performance is not indicative of future results.

Bank of England research suggests a central bank digital currency (CBDC) could strengthen monetary policy transmission by forcing commercial banks to adjust interest rates more quickly to match the central bank rate. A CBDC would also improve quantitative easing by allowing the central bank to purchase government bonds directly from non-banks. The Bank is not currently planning to issue a digital currency but has conducted significant research on practical implementation, including designs to prevent bank runs.

In People v Schaub, the Michigan Court of Appeals reversed a circuit court order reinstating a child abandonment charge against Lawrence B. Schaub, who was accused of selling his ten-month-old daughter to an undercover police officer for $60,000. The district court had dismissed the charge, finding the child was never without care. The Court of Appeals held that while sufficient evidence supported the element of intent to wholly abandon the child, the prosecution failed to establish the element of “exposure” under MCL 750.135 because the child was transferred directly to a person to care for her and was never left unattended or at risk of personal injury. Judge O’Connell dissented, arguing that delivering an infant to a total stranger created a jury question as to whether the child was exposed to the hazard of injury. The majority noted that the Legislature subsequently enacted MCL 750.136c to prohibit the sale of a child, but ex post facto protections barred its application to Schaub.

Many American citizens in Cuba are destitute and lack food and medicine. Congress is recommended to appropriate at least $50,000, under the Secretary of State, for their relief and transportation to the United States.

Kyle Freeland pitched 5 1/3 innings and doubled in the Rockies' 11-4 win over the Giants. Every Rockies starter had a hit, including David Dahl's pinch-hit two-run homer, Trevor Story's triple, and RBI doubles by Nolan Arenado, Gerardo Parra and Ian Desmond. The Giants lost starter Jeff Samardzija to shoulder tightness after one inning and reliever Dereck Rodriguez to a line drive off his shin in his debut. Four San Francisco errors led to three unearned runs. Evan Longoria hit two solo home runs and Buster Posey one. Madison Bumgarner has a second rehab start Thursday; Dahl was held out of the starting lineup with a sore shin. Derek Holland faces Jon Gray Wednesday.

Walmart senior vice president Greg Cathey said the company plans to scale drone deliveries to most areas where it operates, moving beyond small-scale tests. The retailer has tested drones for over five years and surpassed 300,000 deliveries. Currently available at limited U.S. locations through partnerships with Alphabet’s Wing and Zipline, Walmart recently expanded Wing service to 100 stores in five cities and added Northwest Arkansas locations, with Cathey stating that "100 stores is just the start" and that drone delivery is a key part of its last-mile strategy. While widespread deployment remains years away due to regulatory and infrastructure hurdles, Cathey said the evolving regulatory environment has made drone delivery a viable business.

The Golden Cross Trading Strategy uses 50-day and 200-day moving averages, generating a buy signal when the short-term average crosses above the long-term average and a sell signal when it crosses below. Backtested on the S&P 500 since 1960, the strategy produced a 6.8% annual return with 79% winning trades and a 33% maximum drawdown, compared to buy-and-hold's 7.2% return and 56% drawdown. While invested only 70% of the time, its risk-adjusted return is 9.6%. The strategy aims to capture bullish market trends while minimizing losses during bear markets by reducing time spent in the market.

A cross-sectional study of 424 HIV patients receiving ART at Kibungo Referral Hospital, Rwanda, found a 13% non-adherence rate and 87% adherence rate. Data were collected from March to April 2024 using stratified random sampling and structured questionnaires. Bivariate analysis showed significant associations between ART non-adherence and age, education level, household size, having multiple sexual partners, longer travel and waiting times, smoking, and HIV status disclosure to friends. Multivariate analysis identified younger age (under 31 years), lack of tertiary education, stigma, perceived ART ineffectiveness, and failure to integrate ART into daily routines as significant factors associated with non-adherence; setting alarms as reminders was not significantly associated. The 13% non-adherence rate was lower than rates reported in Ethiopia (22.9%), Nigeria (30.4%), Uganda (approximately 25%), and South Africa (approximately 28%), and favorable compared to typical rates of 15–25% in the United States and Europe. The study concluded that interventions targeting younger patients, improving education, reducing stigma, and supporting daily routine integration are needed to improve adherence.

In Richard A. Milan v. Jack R. Duckworth and Barry Nothstien (N.D. Ind. Oct. 2, 1989), the court granted summary judgment for the defendants. Plaintiff Milan, an Indiana State Prison inmate, filed a pro se § 1983 action regarding the denial of his July 10, 1988 visitation with Judy Ballard, claiming due process and Eighth Amendment violations. Although prison Administrative Procedure Number 02-00-104 required written notice of a visitation denial, which defendants admitted was not provided, the court applied *Hewitt v. Helms* and *Kentucky Department of Corrections v. Thompson* and found the procedure contained no specific substantive criteria limiting discretion, so no protected liberty interest existed. Because plaintiff did not dispute defendants' authority to deny the visit or that the denial was without good cause, the court held the procedural failure to give written notice could not support a substantive constitutional claim. The court denied plaintiff's summary judgment motion.

HoopTactics provides proven baseline, sideline, and full court out of bounds plays creating high-percentage shots with multiple options and continuity. Full court situations under four seconds require preparation; against pressure when leading, baseline plays can secure inbound using best player, inbounder, and shooters. Advancing the ball to midcourt for a timeout is preferable to full court inbounding. At game's end, use baseline plays with top free throw shooters present.

E-learning is essential for business competitiveness, requiring governance to provide strategic direction, manage risks, and allocate resources. This paper examines e-learning systems, which use networked ICT to enhance learning but face integration challenges; e-learning ecosystems comprising learning communities, enterprises, and LMS components; and governance frameworks. E-learning governance encompasses structures such as roles and steering committees; processes including strategic planning, regulations, and risk management; communications and relational mechanisms; and pedagogies and instructional designs. The authors adopt Darking’s six dimensions of digital ecosystem governance—constitution, communication culture, credibility and trust, organisation, licensing and regulation, and technological aspects—to enhance this framework. Information security governance is highlighted as critical, requiring risk assessment, policies, counter-measures, and monitoring, alongside trust in services, business activities, and knowledge. The paper concludes by identifying a comprehensive governance framework and calling for further research into e-learning governance practices within digital business ecosystems.

The editor acknowledges assistance from the Reagan Presidential Library, Library of Congress, CIA, and Office of the Historian, and permissions from the estates of Alexander Haig and Jeane Kirkpatrick. The editor conducted research and selected documentation under Adam M. Howard; Kathleen B. Rasmussen reviewed the volume, and Kerry Hite performed copy and technical editing. Sources include public records, declassified and classified Reagan Library files, White House Staff and Office Files, Executive Secretariat collections, George P. Shultz’s donated papers, and Department of State lot files, notably Policy Planning Staff files and Haig’s memoranda of conversation. The State Department’s Central Foreign Policy File microfilm reels provided additional background.

The study estimates the COVID-19 burden of disease in the Republic of Ireland from March 1, 2020, to February 28, 2021, using Disability-Adjusted Life Years (DALY). Following Ireland’s March 2020 lockdown, the analysis calculates Years of Life Lost (YLL) from Central Statistics Office mortality data and Global Burden of Disease 2019 life tables, and Years Lived with Disability (YLD) from DATA.GOV.IE morbidity data across five health states: asymptomatic, moderate, severe, critical, and post-acute consequences. YLD incorporates PCR testing criteria, a 3:1 asymptomatic ratio from seroprevalence studies, disability weights from GBD 2019 and the European Disability Weight study, and Irish hospital data for durations. DALYs equal YLL plus YLD. Ethical approval was obtained from University College Cork.

Explainable AI is essential for transparency, trust, resource efficiency, and mitigating safety risks in LLMs. Challenges include a lack of unified evaluation frameworks, computational scalability, and real-world deployment gaps. The authors propose a framework using Concept Activation Vectors (CAVs) to interpretably control LLM behavior. CAVs are trained via logistic regression on model layer activations to detect target concepts and are dynamically applied during inference to enhance or suppress them. This lightweight method maintains text fluency and handles multiple concepts simultaneously through optimization, enabling precise control.

The passage describes a cloud-integrated storage appliance that caches snapshots for cloud storage and arranges snapshot metadata into per-data-collection key-value stores using local snapshot identifiers. The metadata includes inode records, directory records, and data map records, while snapshot data files are maintained locally and migrated to cloud storage. The appliance performs snapshot ingestion, snapshot and file-level restoration by merging valid metadata and data ranges from preceding snapshots back to a baseline, and snapshot reclamation by implicitly transferring valid records and data from deleted snapshots to succeeding snapshots. To reduce eviction of stable data blocks in forever-incremental configurations, the appliance creates synthetic baseline snapshots and refreshes eviction state data. This includes an ownership-expansion approach that copies valid preceding snapshot metadata to the most recent snapshot and updates fingerprint and eviction metadata for cached blocks, and a reverse-incremental approach that maintains a synthetic baseline snapshot identifier, transfers overwritten data to a pre-baseline snapshot, and refreshes eviction state.

The speaker notes Martin was blamed too quickly during early-season struggles, while Ray Emery won games upon returning and became the starter, leaving Martin on the bench. He emphasizes respect for Anaheim and the need to start well despite days off. He praises Brian as a GM unafraid to take chances, and credits his team's leadership from Alfredsson, Phillips, and Redden, depth, and matchup play against New Jersey and Buffalo. He highlights an improved, versatile player; J.S. as a matured, adjusted goaltender; a traded young player who became a strong two-way player; and Mike Comrie, who adapted to right wing and became a solid two-way player. He reflects that leaving his previous organization was difficult but that he left it in good shape with young talent. He notes playing four lines and six defensemen, credits Anton with leading in shot blocking, and observes that filled lanes and defensive positioning now force offenses to seek redirections.

In *Shumye v. Felleke*, the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California granted in part and denied in part Defendant Samuel Felleke’s motion for summary judgment and denied Plaintiff Rebecca Shumye’s motion. Shumye, an Ethiopian immigrant, sued her former spouse and Form I-864 sponsor to enforce his financial support obligation. The court held that a Form I-864 is an enforceable contract requiring annual income at 125% of the federal poverty level and that divorce does not terminate the obligation. It rejected Defendant’s aggregate-income approach, ruling that each calendar year must be analyzed separately. The court found the $49,000 divorce settlement and student loans were not income, but student grants and housing subsidies were. For 2000, 2001, 2002, 2004, and 2005, the court granted partial summary judgment to Defendant because Plaintiff conceded her income exceeded the threshold. For 2003, 2006, and 2007, Defendant failed to prove Plaintiff’s income exceeded the threshold, so summary judgment was denied. Plaintiff’s motion was denied because she did not present undisputed evidence that her income fell below the threshold in those years.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2016. Net sales for the second quarter of 2016 were $30.404 billion, up 31% year-over-year, and $59.532 billion for the six months ended June 30, 2016, up 30%. Net income was $857 million in Q2 2016 compared to $92 million in Q2 2015, and $1.370 billion for the six months compared to $35 million in the prior year period. Diluted earnings per share were $1.78 for Q2 2016. Operating income increased to $1.285 billion in Q2 2016 from $464 million in Q2 2015.

By segment, North America net sales grew 28% to $17.674 billion with operating income of $702 million. International net sales grew 30% to $9.844 billion, with an operating loss of $135 million. AWS net sales increased 58% to $2.886 billion, with operating income of $718 million.

As of June 30, 2016, cash and cash equivalents were $12.521 billion, total assets were $65.076 billion, long-term debt was $8.212 billion, and stockholders' equity was $16.538 billion. Net cash provided by operating activities was $3.465 billion in Q2 2016, while investing activities used $2.439 billion and financing activities used $1.039 billion. Capital expenditures were $1.711 billion in Q2.

The company disclosed legal proceedings including patent infringement complaints related to Amazon Web Services and a voluntary disclosure to U.S. agencies regarding sales to sanctioned individuals and entities in Iran. Tax contingencies totaled $1.6 billion, including ongoing disputes with the IRS regarding transfer pricing, a €196 million assessment from French tax authorities, and a European Commission investigation into Luxembourg tax rulings. This section provides mechanical, packaging, and orderable information for Texas Instruments' MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 devices. This study examines how time-delayed feedback affects optimistic multi-agent learning algorithms in normal-form games. While optimistic FTRL (OFTRL) achieves O(1) regret and converges to Nash equilibrium in poly-matrix zero-sum games without delay, even small delays severely degrade performance. In an unconstrained Matching Pennies game with a Euclidean regularizer, OFTRL suffers Ω(√T) regret and diverges from equilibrium for any delay m ≥ 1 (Theorems 6 and 7). To address this, the authors propose Weighted OFTRL (WOFTRL), which weights optimistic predictions by n ∈ N. A Taylor expansion analysis shows that the optimistic weight n and time delay m effectively cancel each other. When the weight slightly exceeds the delay (n = m + 1), WOFTRL achieves O(1) total regret with learning rate η = 1/(√8λL) where λ = (m+1)(m+2)/2 (Corollary 11), and best-iterate convergence to the Nash equilibrium in poly-matrix zero-sum games when η < 1/(√8λL) (Corollary 13). Experiments on Matching Pennies, Sato’s game, and Rock-Paper-Scissors confirm O(1) regret and convergence when n > m, and failure when n ≤ m.

The NVIDIA GA10x Ampere architecture introduces third-generation Tensor Cores that support new data types including TF32 and BF16, along with a Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity feature that doubles effective throughput for deep learning operations. These Tensor Cores accelerate AI denoising, DLSS (now supporting up to 8K), and other AI-based graphics applications. The architecture utilizes GDDR6X memory with PAM4 signaling to achieve speeds up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth up to 936 GB/sec, while professional GPUs including the NVIDIA A40 and RTX A6000 use 48GB of GDDR6 memory scalable to 96GB via third-generation NVLink, which provides 112.5 GB/sec total bandwidth between two GPUs.

The GA102 GPU is composed of seven Graphics Processing Clusters, 42 Texture Processing Clusters, and 84 Streaming Multiprocessors. Each SM contains 128 CUDA Cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, and one second-generation Ray Tracing Core. The second-generation RT Core doubles the ray/triangle intersection testing rate over Turing and adds a new Interpolate Triangle Position unit to accelerate ray-traced motion blur. The GA10x SM doubles peak FP32 throughput by enabling FP32 processing on both datapaths, increases combined L1 data cache and shared memory capacity by 33% to 128 KB per SM, and doubles shared memory bandwidth. Additionally, Raster Operators are now integrated into the GPCs rather than tied to the memory controller, increasing the total ROP count to 112 in the full GA102 and improving raster operation performance.

Other key features include a PCI Express 4.0 host interface providing up to 64 GB/sec peak bandwidth, up to 1.9x greater power efficiency compared to Turing, and NVIDIA RTX IO technology that enables GPU-based loading and decompression of game assets via Microsoft DirectStorage, offloading CPU work and improving I/O performance by up to 100x over traditional storage. The NVIDIA A40 data center GPU delivers up to 2x FP32 throughput, 2x ray-tracing throughput, and up to 5x AI and data science throughput compared to the previous-generation Quadro RTX 6000. The GeForce RTX 3090 and 3080 leverage these architectural improvements for high-resolution gaming and content creation, with the RTX 3090 capable of 8K60 gaming with DLSS. The architecture also supports HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4a with Display Stream Compression, seventh-generation NVENC hardware encoding, and fifth-generation NVDEC hardware decoding including AV1 support.

The passage distinguishes between investing and speculation based on Benjamin Graham's definition: investing requires selecting securities that protect capital and promise adequate returns. The author recounts purchasing Ask Jeeves shares for price appreciation without considering principal safety, which Graham would classify as speculation. To protect capital, investors should buy stocks at significant discounts to intrinsic value, creating a margin of safety against business deterioration and valuation errors. Financially solid companies with clean balance sheets—low long-term debt, strong current assets relative to liabilities, and high-quality liquid assets—are preferred. Buying companies at steep discounts due to negative sentiment or temporary problems allows investors to protect downside risk while positioning for upside as prices return to intrinsic value. Whether one is an investor depends on the selection process rather than the assets purchased.

This document provides a user-level description of AMD AGESA software procedures and interfaces for host environment wrapper implementers. It defines procedure call interfaces, a recommended wrapper implementation, build options, and terminology. The AGESA software uses a three-level code version scheme (X.Y.Z) and a two-level specification version (X.Y). Public call-in entry points use an “Amd” prefix, while call-out procedures use an “Agesa” prefix. The interface uses initializer functions to allocate and pre-fill parameter structures with defaults from build-time tables generated via the platform-specific “<Plat>Options.c” file; the host environment modifies parameters as needed before calling the main function and releasing the structure. The software operates in 32-bit protected flat-address mode and supports binary image builds with headers identified by “$AMD” and “$MOD” signatures, as well as full source integration. Call entry points align with a boot timeline (reset, early, post, late) to perform processor, memory, and platform initialization, generate system tables, and handle S3 resume. Error reporting is provided through return codes (e.g., AGESA_SUCCESS, AGESA_WARNING, AGESA_FATAL) and a circular event log. The document also covers UEFI integration, including SEC, PEI, and DXE phases, required PEIM modules, PPIs, environment variables, stack establishment macros, and numerous platform configuration structures for memory, VRM, PCIe, and processor features.

This study compared a Fast Track Diagnostic PCR panel and a hybridization capture-based metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) workflow using an Illumina/IDbyDNA Respiratory Pathogen ID/AMR enrichment panel on 29 nasopharyngeal samples from individuals suspected of acute upper respiratory infection. Results were analyzed with the IDbyDNA Explify Platform and phenotypically classified by infectivity potential. PCR detected 15 microorganisms in 28 samples, while mNGS identified 44 microorganisms (27 bacteria, 2 fungi, 15 viruses), including 29 not probed by PCR. Concordance for shared targets was high (98.33% positive percent agreement, 100% negative percent agreement). The mNGS approach exclusively detected 12 of 15 phenotypic group 2 microorganisms (frequently associated with disease) and 3 phenotypic group 3 pathogens (Coxsackievirus A, SARS-CoV-2, and human rhinovirus C), which are generally considered pathogenic. Co-infection was identified in 26 of 29 samples by mNGS. The authors conclude that hybridization capture-based mNGS offers broader pathogen discovery and genotypic differentiation than syndromic PCR, with potential clinical utility for assessing upper-to-lower respiratory trafficking risk, while remaining more feasible for clinical laboratories than target-agnostic mNGS due to lower sequencing requirements and adaptability to benchtop instruments. Further investigation is needed to validate phenotypic classifications for clinical relevance.

This paper introduces an architecture for digitally structured information exchange between industrial enterprises, focusing on the lifecycle management of industrial plants and technical information (e.g., for investment projects and maintenance). Motivated by the shortcomings of current largely manual, labor-intensive, and error-prone communication practices, the proposed solution relies on an open consortium that agrees on common business practices and information formats. Information exchange is coordinated by a scalable network of mediators acting as multi-sided platforms, which route messages between enterprises. Business parties connect via adapters that map their heterogeneous back-end systems to common structures, enabling single-integration connectivity. The study reviews previous work, including EDI, B2B standards, and technical information standards, noting that none provide a sufficiently generic and scalable medium for this purpose. It details challenges such as the heterogeneity of technical information structures, the complexity of plant lifecycles, and the networked nature of modern business. A functional prototype was implemented to demonstrate equipment information delivery in maintenance and renewal project scenarios, using a web application platform with import/export mappings. Experiments with suppliers and plant operators validated the practical usefulness. The discussion highlights potential efficiency gains, the need for an open governance consortium, and limitations including the lack of an established consortium and real adapters. The conclusion emphasizes that while the necessary ICT technologies exist, the primary challenge is organizing the ecosystem.

In Hunter v. Bales, the Supreme Court affirmed a decree for specific performance prosecuted by Bales as assignee of Thompson. Moore orally agreed to sell land to Thompson through an agent, then orally agreed to sell the same land to Matthew R. Hunter, executed a title bond to Thompson, but deeded the land to Hunter, who knew of the prior bond. The Court held that where conflicting theories exist and evidence supports each, the appellate court adopts the theory sustaining the lower court's finding. As between Thompson and Hunter, Thompson had the prior equity and was entitled to specific performance. The Court ruled that in equity, a valid land sale contract makes the vendee the equitable owner, but equity only regards as done what ought to be done for those entitled to specific performance. In a suit for specific performance, the plaintiff need only offer by complaint to bring the purchase money into court when liquidated upon decree. After tendering the purchase money and accrued interest and demanding conveyance, the obligee is not chargeable with further interest unless the vendor proves the obligee used the money. The judgment below was affirmed with costs.

This qualitative case study examined Physical Education Teacher Education (PETE) students' development of 21st-century skills within a peer mentoring structure during a 14-week first-year movement education course at a Turkish university. Participants included three peer mentors, 25 first-year peer learners, and the course lecturer. The course employed storytelling and gamification linking fundamental movement skills to popular narratives, using Instagram and Discord for pre-lesson preparation and post-lesson reflection. Data from field notes, recordings, social media, and reflections were analyzed inductively. Results revealed three themes: peer learners exercised communication and teamwork by excluding non-contributing group members, while peer mentors managed conflicts through task division and rotating leadership; peer mentors demonstrated accountability and responsibility toward the instructor by consistently producing lesson content, and peer learners later taught peers using storytelling, fostering creativity and productivity; and narrative-based learning connected course content to daily life, increasing knowledge permanence and engagement beyond traditional classroom methods. The study concluded that interactive peer mentoring environments effectively embed 21st-century skills and professional awareness. It recommended sustainably integrating peer mentoring and storytelling across the entire undergraduate PETE curriculum and conducting long-term studies with prospective teachers.

In *Asa B. Meech v. The City of Buffalo*, property owners sought to enjoin a second assessment levied to pay for sewer construction. The City initially assessed $1,058.63 and contracted with Robert J. Randolph to construct the sewer for that amount. During construction, Randolph encountered an unforeseen body of quicksand that made completion impossible at the contract price or even twice that sum. He stopped work and, together with several plaintiffs, petitioned the Common Council for additional compensation. The Council agreed to pay Randolph an additional $588.13 to complete the sewer and directed a further assessment on benefited real estate. Plaintiffs argued the second assessment was illegal because the City had already fixed the expense, contracted for it, and taken security for performance. After a special term held for plaintiffs and the general term reversed, the Court of Appeals affirmed. It held that a municipal corporation empowered to make public improvements and contract for work may voluntarily increase the contract price where circumstances equitably justify it, unless prohibited by its charter. The court ruled that when an assessment proves insufficient to defray the actual expense of an improvement, the municipality has the power and duty to order a further assessment. It concluded the supplementary assessment was a “further assessment” authorized by the city charter to cover the deficiency, that the additional payment was supported by sufficient consideration because Randolph would have abandoned the work otherwise, and that the City had authority to modify or rescind the original contract to ensure completion.

The Korean diet emphasizes traditional whole, unprocessed foods including fresh vegetables, whole grains, lean proteins, and fermented foods like kimchi, while limiting processed foods, sugary drinks, unhealthy fats, and dairy. Offensive set pieces off free kicks restart play after fouls under Law 13. The non-offending team places the ball at the infraction spot while offending players must stand at least 10 yards away. The ball is in play once touched by an offensive player and visibly moves, and the original kicker may not touch it again immediately. Free kicks are direct, allowing a goal without another touch, or indirect, requiring the ball to touch another player first; the referee signals an indirect kick by raising one arm.

In the offensive third, set pieces are designed to defeat the defensive wall with minimal complexity for an effective shot. Coaches base designs on eight locations near or far from the penalty area, whether the kick is direct or indirect, and player skill. Tactics include direct shots, simple touches, crosses, misdirection, screening, decoys, passes, chips over the wall, crashing the goal, and rebound follow-ups.

Players must ensure the ball is stationary and the referee is ready before kicking; the ball may be repositioned slightly beforehand. A dead-ball specialist may take direct shots. One player is in charge, and the team may ask the referee for 10 yards if defenders encroach, waiting for the signal to proceed. At higher levels, referees may use vanishing spray to mark the ball and wall.

Free kicks may be Ceremonial, with a delay to set the play, or Quick, taken immediately to exploit a defensive lapse on a direct kick when the referee is ready, without waiting for defenders to reach 10 yards. Rarely, an indirect free kick is awarded less than 10 yards from the goal, requiring the defensive wall to stand on the goal line between the posts until the ball is touched.

Practice should progress from no defenders to mannequins, stationary defenders, active defenders, and scrimmage simulations enforcing rules and referee signals. Coaches should prepare contingencies, scout opponents for gaps, incorporate the mandatory touch into indirect kick designs, keep plays simple, and encourage player input.

Pumpkin is a nutritious fruit from the Cucurbitaceae family with versatile culinary uses beyond pie and decoration. It is rich in fibre, iron, potassium, vitamin E, and carotenoids such as beta-carotene, alpha-carotene, lutein, and zeaxanthin. One cup of cooked pumpkin provides significant amounts of these nutrients, including over 565 mg of potassium. Consuming pumpkin supports cardiovascular health, immune function, eye health by reducing cataract and macular degeneration risk, brain health and cognition, and healthy blood pressure through an improved potassium-to-sodium ratio. The article is by registered dietitian Doug Cook.

A PRISMA-compliant systematic review of 270 studies on large language models (LLMs) and social science applied unsupervised machine learning—Sentence-BERT embeddings, K-means clustering, and latent Dirichlet allocation—to derive a data-driven taxonomy of the literature. The analysis produced a stable three-cluster solution: LLM as Social Minds (mind-like attributions, theory of mind, moral reasoning, and bias), LLM Societies (multi-agent interaction, cooperation, collective epistemics, and institutional design), and LLM–Human Interactions (trust, reliance, learning, productivity, and dyadic risk). These machine-discovered partitions aligned strongly with an expert-coded taxonomy (Macro-F1 = 0.954 ± 0.018; NMI = 0.811; ARI = 0.867). The authors present these clusters as levels of analysis rather than mutually exclusive camps, offering an integrated, reproducible map intended to standardize constructs, bridge fragmented research streams, and support cumulative, cross-level social science of LLMs.

Version 2 of the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) specification introduces a 52-bit FEATURES bitmap for advertising mandatory and optional hypervisor capabilities. Communication occurs through MSR 0xc001_0130 and VMCB offset 0xa0, enabling protocol version negotiation, SEV page table encryption bit discovery, and CPUID requests before a 4K-aligned, shared GHCB page is established. SEV-SNP guests must register the GHCB guest physical address before first use; hypervisors may provide a preferred address.

Non-Automatic Exit (NAE) events trigger #VC exceptions, which the guest handles via VMGEXIT by setting GHCB fields and a VALID_BITMAP. Defined NAE events include IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, #NPF/MMIO access, Page State Change, SNP Guest Request, SNP Extended Guest Request, SNP TIO Guest Request, AP Creation, #HV Doorbell Page, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, Secure AVIC backing page management, and Termination Request. These events specify required SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO, and SW_SCRATCH values, with some using shared GHCB buffer areas for data, certificates, or page state entries.

SEV-SNP launch supplies a secrets page and CPUID page, with an EFI configuration table GUID for OS communication. SMP booting requires AP jump tables or SNP AP Creation via VMSA pages; vCPU hotplug is unsupported for SEV-ES but supported under SEV-SNP. Restricted Injection uses a shared #HV doorbell page containing PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields to deliver interrupts and non-maskable events with defined host presentation and guest acknowledgment semantics. NMI handling relies on a guest "NMI Complete" message. Debug register virtualization is supported contingent on hardware capability. System Management Mode and nested virtualization are not supported.

This document describes AMD's Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine, optional extensions to the Secure Encrypted Virtualization API (SEV) and Secure Nested Paging Firmware ABI Specification (SNP) to facilitate page migration. TMPM requires IOMMU enablement and allows software to migrate pages between physical memory tiers while maintaining the same guest physical address. It supports migration of pages under concurrent DMA and SNP-protected guest pages inaccessible to the hypervisor or operating system. Key commands include PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO for hypervisor state and DMA-mapped pages, and PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST for SNP guest pages, which can move up to 128 pages per command via a Page Migration List. A new Pre-Migration state facilitates SNP guest page migration. Performance is highest with 16 or more pages per command, ideally 128, and by keeping the ring buffer full. The engine cannot migrate IOMMU structures, vIOMMU buffers, or the ring buffer. TMPM may modify IOMMU host page table entries non-atomically. Firmware reload requires pausing operations, tearing down the ring buffer, and using a same-or-greater version; the EPYC family is identified via the FW_VER_Major field of PM_GET_CAPABILITIES. All system physical addresses must be 4KB aligned.

A year-long knowledge exchange project between University College London's Institute of Education and Diversity Role Models supported Citizenship student teachers in England from October 2023 to June 2024 in developing trans-inclusive classroom practices. Against a backdrop of increased media scrutiny and draft Department for Education guidance—including a December 2023 non-statutory consultation on "gender questioning children" criticized for potential safeguarding risks, and a May 2024 proposed ban on discussing gender identity in Relationships, Sex and Health Education—student teachers remained bound by existing statutory guidance requiring teaching of facts and law regarding gender identity. Through three workshops, Diversity Role Models and mentor teachers helped student teachers "actualize" LGBTQ+ identities by placing them in real-life contexts, though presentations revealed most integration focused on sexual orientation rather than transgender identities, which student teachers attributed to fear and reduced confidence amid public debates. Storytelling and counter-stories were used to build empathy and challenge prejudice. Participants utilized domestic legislation such as the Equality Act 2010 and international frameworks including the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child, the Yogyakarta Principles+10, and UNESCO and Plan International guidance to frame trans people as rights holders. The project found that effective trans inclusion requires whole-school approaches beyond discrete lessons, including visibility through school displays and Pride clubs, restorative behaviour management, clear anti-bullying policies referencing gender identity rights, and bystander intervention training. Participants concluded that despite risks from proposed draft guidance, existing human rights and equality frameworks can be leveraged across subject areas to promote trans inclusion when combined with personal narratives, and that partnerships between universities and civil society organizations are essential to building teacher confidence and capacity.

Tables 6–8 report problems within one month after lower-dose (5 or 10 µg), 30 µg, and additional 30 µg BNT162b2 boosters in Phases 3 and 2/3.
