Faith-based organisations are increasingly supporting the NHS, with over 3,500 churches and 200,000 volunteers working on health and social care initiatives that address gaps left by funding cuts and limited resources, according to the Cinnamon Network. Its report studied 32 church-led initiatives tackling mental health, obesity and social isolation. Parish nursing is highlighted as a key project, with more than 100 registered nurses currently working with 85 UK churches and another 100 expected within 18 months. These nurses provide preventative care, patient support and advocacy, allowing NHS staff to focus on clinical duties while serving patients of all faiths and none.

This IDC White Paper examines high-performance computing (HPC) in manufacturing based on a December 2021 survey of 200 IT and departmental decision makers from discrete and process manufacturing enterprises with over 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. Amid geopolitical uncertainties, rising energy prices, supply chain disruptions, and sustainability demands, digitalization is fundamentally transforming manufacturing value creation. IT-based simulation, modeling, and analysis are key to accelerating product development, improving quality, reducing costs, and enabling new digital products and business models. Currently used mainly in product development, production planning, and quality management, deployment is expected to rise to 90% within two years, with 64% of enterprises planning investments. However, data silos and the absence of a unified data strategy limit progress. Emerging usage scenarios include virtual prototyping, digital twins, IoT-enabled feedback loops, and high-performance data analytics, with 39% of respondents seeking to simulate as many physical processes as possible. While demand for high-performance calculations is projected to grow significantly, many enterprises face trade-offs between calculation time and quality due to hardware limitations. Four out of five decision makers agree HPC is a game changer for innovation because it enables complex calculations, increases simulation quality and iteration intensity, unlocks new scenarios, and improves agility. Over 25% already use professional HPC infrastructures, 39% are planning or piloting deployment, and 15% are not engaging due to high costs and limited awareness. IDC expects HPC-based simulation, modeling, and data analysis to become routine in many enterprises.

Columbiana defeated Lisbon 49-47 in a high school girls' basketball game. The ICC Board may discuss replacing the 2021 Champions Trophy in India with a World T20 at upcoming meetings in Kolkata. This paper proposes iMOOE, a physics-guided invariant learning framework for zero-shot out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization in spatiotemporal PDE dynamics forecasting. The authors identify a two-level PDE invariance principle comprising invariant spatial operators and fixed composition relationships between these operators, physical parameters, and forcing terms. To capture this invariance from limited training domains, iMOOE employs a Mixture of Operator Experts (MOOE) architecture—where parallel neural operator experts approximate distinct physical processes and a fusion network aggregates their outputs with exogenous conditions—alongside a frequency-enriched invariant learning objective. This objective combines maximal prediction loss, risk equality across environments, and a frequency enrichment regularization to mitigate spectral bias. Experiments on five simulated PDE systems (Diffusion-Reaction, Navier-Stokes, Burgers, Shallow-Water, Heat-Conduction) and real-world Sea Surface Temperature data demonstrate that iMOOE achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot OOD forecasting performance, improving upon existing meta-learning, parameter conditioning, and neural operator baselines. The framework is compatible with diverse neural operator backbones, and sensitivity analyses indicate that a moderate number of experts (e.g., three) optimizes performance.

The lecture focuses on interacting Bose gases and superfluidity. For homogeneous systems, the Bogoliubov approximation replaces the condensate operator with a c-number, diagonalizing the Hamiltonian into non-interacting quasiparticles with linear low-momentum dispersion (sound) and quadratic high-momentum dispersion. Interactions cause quantum depletion—admixing finite-momentum states into the condensate—which is small (~1%) for dilute atomic gases but large (~90%) for liquid helium. Sound is observed experimentally via laser-induced density perturbations, and quasiparticle spectra are mapped using stimulated Raman scattering to measure the dynamic structure factor.

For inhomogeneous trapped gases, the Gross-Pitaevskii equation describes the macroscopic wave function. The Thomas-Fermi approximation neglects kinetic energy, giving a density profile that follows the inverted trapping potential. The healing length is the scale over which the wave function adjusts to boundaries or vortices. Vortices carry quantized phase winding and zero density at their cores; multiply charged vortices are unstable and decay into singly charged vortices that arrange in lattices.

In optical lattices, the tight-binding limit yields the Bose-Hubbard model with tunneling matrix element J and on-site interaction U. When U dominates, the system is a Mott insulator with integer atoms per site; when J dominates, it is a superfluid. A mean-field decoupling approximation produces a phase diagram with Mott lobes. The transition is observed through time-of-flight interference patterns for the superfluid and structureless expansion for the insulator, or via quantum gas microscopy resolving site-by-site occupation.

Crude sulfate turpentine is a derivative obtained as a Kraft process byproduct, composed mainly of alpha-pinene and beta-pinene with smaller amounts of other terpenes. Researchers at UW Health present a protocol and alpha-phase findings for evaluating Ambient AI (Abridge), a generative AI clinical documentation tool embedded in the Epic electronic health record, via a pragmatic type 1 hybrid randomized controlled trial within a Learning Health System framework. The Pragmatic Trial Operations playbook spans five components—governance, user experience, technical integration, documentation sustainment, and analytics—and uses alpha and beta phases, Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles, and the SEIPS framework to align research with clinical operations.

The alpha phase (June–October 2024) included 20 providers across five specialties and 8,527 encounters. Iterative feedback and a real-time dashboard refined workflows, while interviews identified barriers such as organizational context, provider readiness, and patient privacy concerns. A note-template discrepancy temporarily reduced ICD-10 documentation accuracy from 79% to 35% before a template fix restored baseline levels. To reduce manual coder burden, the team developed a large language model–based automated ICD-10 review system that achieved a mean Jaccard score of 0.54 against certified coder reviews.

The beta phase is a 24-week, multisite, closed-cohort stepped-wedge trial randomizing 66 providers across eight specialties into three waves to assess Ambient AI’s effect on provider well-being using the Professional Fulfillment Index. The protocol monitors unexpected performance drift via a difference-in-differences analysis with rolling two-week windows and uses an integrated analytics dashboard for operational and research oversight. The authors conclude that this governance and evaluation model offers a scalable, rigorous playbook for bridging generative AI innovation with safe, effective clinical adoption.

The Utah Court of Appeals affirmed the district court’s grant of summary judgment against Kari L. Baumann in her healthcare malpractice action against The Kroger Company and Dr. Gregory P. Tayler. Baumann failed to timely disclose expert witnesses under Utah Rule of Civil Procedure 26 as required by a stipulated discovery schedule. The district court precluded her from using any undisclosed expert reports to contest summary judgment under Rule 26(d)(4), finding no good cause for the failure. The appellate court declined to review Baumann’s claim regarding an expert for Dr. Tayler because the issue was unpreserved. Regarding the Kroger expert report, the court rejected Baumann’s argument that Rule 16(d) should apply instead of Rule 26(d)(4), holding that Rule 26 governs expert disclosure and the district court did not abuse its discretion in excluding the late report. Because expert testimony was necessary to establish the malpractice claims, summary judgment was proper.

A bill to facilitate national debt refunding is returned to the House of Representatives with objections focused on Section 5. While the importance of refunding debt to reduce interest payments is acknowledged, Section 5 is opposed because it would make 3 percent bonds the sole security for national bank circulation after July 1, 1881. This change would prevent most new banks from organizing and bar existing banks from increasing capital, effectively creating a monopoly for current participants. The provision would deprive bill holders of the best security, threaten the free access that characterizes the current system, and risk financial disaster by withdrawing currency from circulation. The message argues that refunding should not be tied to changes in banking law and urges Congress to adopt a suitable refunding measure that does not endanger the national banking system.

The paper introduces DSCHECKER, an LLM-based approach to detect and fix API misuses in Python data science libraries such as NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn, Matplotlib, and seaborn. These libraries involve dynamic, data-dependent behaviors that complicate misuse detection. DSCHECKER prompts LLMs with API directives and dynamic variable information to identify misuses and generate fixes in unified diff format. Evaluated on the DSMISUSES dataset of 38 misuses and a sampled set of deep learning misuses, results show that combining API directives with data information yields the best detection F1-score (61.18% for Llama 3.1 405B) and fix rate (51.28%), outperforming the existing tool LLMAPIDET, which achieved 16.49% recall on the same dataset. Few-shot prompting improved GPT-4o but not Llama. DSCHECKER generalized to deep learning misuses, detecting one case missed by LLMAPIDET. An agentic variant, DSCHECKERagent, which autonomously retrieves documentation and data information via function calls, achieved a 48.65% F1-score and 39.47% fix rate with GPT-4o, demonstrating practical potential despite lower performance than the idealized setup. The study concludes that LLM-based detection and fixing benefit from API directives and dynamic data context, and suggests improving API documentation formats for machine readability.

The document describes the NVIDIA Ampere GA10x GPU architecture, focusing on GA102 and GA104. Fabricated on Samsung’s 8nm process, GA102 contains 28.3 billion transistors and up to 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, and 336 third-generation Tensor Cores. Each Streaming Multiprocessor (SM) includes 128 CUDA Cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, one second-generation RT Core, and 128 KB of L1/shared memory. The SM doubles peak FP32 throughput by adding FP32 processing to both datapaths. ROPs are now integrated into Graphics Processing Clusters (GPCs), yielding 112 ROPs in the full GA102.

Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection throughput and add an Interpolate Triangle Position unit for hardware-accelerated ray-traced motion blur, up to eight times faster than Turing. They support concurrent ray tracing with graphics or compute workloads. Third-generation Tensor Cores support TF32, BF16, and Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity, doubling throughput for sparse matrices and enabling DLSS up to 8K, AI denoising, and broadcast features.

A study by King's College London of 2,066 millennial twins found that lonely 18-year-olds have twice the risk of developing mental health problems such as depression and anxiety, and a 38% increased risk of unemployment. Overall, 7% of participants often felt lonely, while 23-31% felt left out or lacked companionship. Loneliness was also associated with risky behaviors including smoking and inactivity. Contrary to popular belief, loneliness is highest among teenagers and young adults, not older people. While social media is sometimes blamed, the causes are more nuanced; loneliness can be contagious and may cause individuals to withdraw or act hostile, further isolating them. Researchers stress the importance of early intervention to prevent persistent loneliness, noting that loneliness and mental health problems are strongly connected.

Rice University and the Houston Museum of Natural Science (HMNS) have collaborated on space science outreach since 1988, creating early programs including the NSF-funded Teacher Research Program and the Master of Science Teaching degree. Led by Dr. Carolyn Sumners and Prof. Patricia Reiff, the partnership developed NASA-funded eclipse animations for the 2017 total solar eclipse and, for the 2023–2024 Heliophysics “Big Year,” produced the free fulldome planetarium show “Totality,” distributed to 147 planetariums and 53 Texas sites with documented viewership exceeding 180,000. Updated eclipse animations released in 2021 were requested by 186 educators in 33 countries and 33 U.S. states and received over 19,000 YouTube views; one animation’s predicted “diamond ring” effect during a lunar eclipse as seen from the Moon was confirmed by the Blue Ghost lunar lander in March 2025. The partners reached 5,104 educators through formal courses and workshops, distributing over 35,000 eclipse glasses and 30,000 viewing cards—plus a Buc-ee’s–funded card version to over 8,800 Texas public schools—collectively reaching over one million viewers. Their eclipse website offered free resources including safe observing guides, classroom activities, and equipment recommendations. Reiff served as Southwest Regional Coordinator for Citizen CATE 2024, an NSF- and NASA-funded SwRI project that deployed 35 community-led polarimetric telescope sites for the April 8, 2024 total eclipse, with over 80% of teams successfully observing totality and data processed within 24 hours. The partners also hosted 2023 annular eclipse public events, made extensive media appearances, and operated a space weather forecasting service that accurately predicted the May 2024 geomagnetic storm. Documented reach for the Big Year exceeded 250,000 in leveraged venues, with total reach estimated at over 1.5 million people.

New research from the University of Eastern Finland found that high blood levels of linoleic acid, the most common omega-6 fatty acid, were associated with a 43 percent reduced risk of premature death over 22 years among 2,480 men. This MIT lecture covers inverse and ill-posed problems, where small noise in measurements can produce large errors in solutions, such as finding velocity from noisy position data. The professor lists examples including seismology, medical imaging (CT, MRI, PET), scattering, coefficient identification in PDEs, integral equations of the first kind (Fredholm/Volterra), GPS positioning and velocity estimation, and genomics. To handle ill-posedness, he discusses Tikhonov regularization, which adds a penalty term like alpha times x squared to the least squares problem, and notes that balancing the regularization parameter alpha with the noise level delta is key; choosing alpha equal to delta to the 2/3 power yields an error of order delta to the 2/3. Other approaches mentioned include iterative methods with early stopping. The lecture begins with a geometric identity related to optimization duality involving distances from a point to the corners of a rectangle, and ends with administrative notes on upcoming student presentations and a guest lecture by Professor Carl Wunsch on Wednesday, May 10 at 4 o'clock.

Rams Coach Sean McVay said Todd Gurley will receive increased carries and "progressive work" through the third preseason game to prepare him for the Sept. 10 opener against Indianapolis. Gurley had four carries for two yards and caught a 10-yard pass against Dallas. McVay said coaches will monitor Gurley's workload to balance reps in the new system with keeping him healthy, noting they must protect him from overworking.

Opioid misuse is a global epidemic involving the mu-opioid receptor (MOR), which is targeted by abused opioids and treatment medications. While [11C]carfentanil PET ([11C]CFN-PET) has advanced knowledge of MOR availability, prior studies were largely restricted to the brain. This study presents the first human whole-body neuroreceptor PET imaging using [11C]CFN and a long axial field-of-view (LAFOV) PET scanner (PennPET Explorer), investigating extra-CNS reference regions (aorta and muscle). Healthy adults aged 18–45 without psychiatric or substance use disorders underwent T1-weighted MRI and two 90-minute dynamic whole-body PET scans following intravenous [11C]CFN injection. Brain PET data were co-registered to MRI, normalized to MNI space, and analyzed using the Logan reference tissue model with the visual cortex as reference to compute distribution volume ratios in bilateral amygdala, caudate, putamen, thalamus, and ventral tegmentum. Percent receptor occupancy for naloxone pretreatment was also calculated.

Mitch Larkin is considering adding the 400m individual medley to his Commonwealth Games trials program after winning gold at the Queensland titles, but will maintain focus on backstroke. The dual backstroke world champion, who won silver in the 200m backstroke but missed the podium in the 100m at the Rio Olympics, is seeking redemption. The Canon EOS M6 is an entry-level mirrorless camera replacing the M3, using the same 24.2-megapixel sensor and Digic 7 processor as the M5 but with a redesigned body, optional viewfinder, and tilting touchscreen. The lecture defines additive energy between subsets $A$ and $B$ of an Abelian group as the number of quadruples $(a_1,a_2,b_1,b_2)\in A\times A\times B\times B$ such that $a_1+b_1=a_2+b_2$. Small doubling implies large additive energy—if $|A+A|\le k|A|$ then $E(A)\ge |A|^3/k$, proven using Cauchy-Schwarz—but the converse is false, as a set may combine a structured piece with unstructured elements. The Balog-Szemerédi-Gowers (BSG) theorem recovers a partial converse: if a set has large additive energy, it contains a large subset with small doubling, with only polynomial loss in the constants. A two-set version states that if $|A|,|B|\le n$ and $E(A,B)$ is large, there exist large subsets $A'\subseteq A$ and $B'\subseteq B$ with $|A'+B'|$ small; the one-set version follows via the Ruzsa triangle inequality.

The proof uses a graphical version of BSG. For a bipartite graph $G$ between $A$ and $B$ with at least $n^2/k$ edges and small restricted sumset $A+_G B$, there exist large subsets $A',B'$ with small unrestricted sumset $|A'+B'|$. This implies the additive version by defining $G$ via "popular sums" (sums represented in at least $n/2k$ ways); large energy ensures $G$ has many edges while its restricted sumset remains small.

The graphical BSG is proved via dependent random choice. A path-of-length-2 lemma yields a large subset $U\subseteq A$ where most pairs have many common neighbors. Upgrading to a path-of-length-3 lemma produces large $A'\subseteq A$ and $B'\subseteq B$ such that every pair $(a,b)\in A'\times B'$ has many length-3 paths $a$–$b_1$–$a_1$–$b$ in $G$. Setting $x=a+b_1$, $y=a_1+b_1$, and $z=a_1+b$, each lying in the restricted sumset, shows $a+b$ can be written as $x-y+z$ in many ways. Consequently, $|A'+B'|$ is bounded by $|A+_G B|^3$, completing the proof.

This IDC White Paper presents findings from a December 2021 survey of 200 IT and departmental decision makers in discrete and process manufacturing enterprises with over 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. Amid geopolitical uncertainties, rising energy prices, supply chain disruptions, and sustainability demands, digitalization and IT-based simulation, modeling, and data analysis are critical to accelerating product development, improving quality, reducing costs, and enabling new digital products and business models. Currently used primarily in product development, production planning, and quality management—with deployment expected to reach as high as 90% in these areas within two years—these tools remain hindered by data silos. Emerging usage scenarios include digital twins, virtual prototyping, IoT feedback loops, and high-performance data analytics, the latter already used by 42% of respondents.

High-performance computing (HPC) is viewed as a game changer by 81% of respondents (96% of current HPC users) because it enables complex calculations, improves result quality and speed, and unlocks new innovation scenarios. Over a quarter of enterprises already use professional HPC infrastructures, while 39% are planning or piloting deployment. Key challenges include security concerns (72%), high energy consumption and sustainability (58%), licensing and hardware costs, inadequate computing power, and lack of internal and external expertise (42%). Consequently, 87% of HPC users prefer or plan to use external infrastructures such as cloud providers, while only 6% operate their own on-premises datacenter. Public cloud and hybrid architectures are expected to become the most important future HPC models, offering superior scalability, flexibility, and operational expenditure advantages compared with in-house systems.

The President spoke in Pittsburgh to outline the American Jobs Plan, a roughly $2 trillion, eight-year investment to rebuild the economy from the middle out. He cited the pandemic’s toll of 547,296 American deaths and praised the administration’s vaccination progress, with 200 million shots in the first 100 days, while noting that the wealthiest one percent saw their net worth rise by $4 trillion as millions of others lost jobs. The plan proposes modernizing 20,000 miles of highways, replacing the nation’s ten most economically significant bridges, repairing 10,000 additional bridges, and expanding rail and transit. It also addresses climate change by building 500,000 electric vehicle charging stations, transitioning federal fleets to clean vehicles, capping orphan oil and gas wells, and modernizing the power grid. Other provisions include replacing all lead pipes and service lines, ensuring affordable high-speed internet access nationwide, weatherizing buildings, and extending home and community-based care for seniors and people with disabilities with better wages for caregivers. The plan includes the largest increase in non-defense research and development spending on record for sectors like semiconductors and clean energy, and it calls for passing the PRO Act to empower workers. The President proposed paying for the plan by raising the corporate tax rate to 28 percent, establishing a 21 percent global minimum tax for U.S. corporations, eliminating offshoring deductions, providing tax credits for domestic manufacturing, and increasing IRS enforcement on corporate tax compliance, while pledging no federal tax increases for those earning under $400,000. He framed the investment as necessary to compete with China, create millions of jobs, and demonstrate that democracies can deliver for their people, urging bipartisan support.

Scientists at Rockefeller University developed a device to keep a tiny sliver of gerbil cochlea alive and functional outside the body, enabling direct observation of its auditory biomechanics. The study confirmed that a Hopf bifurcation—a mechanical instability that amplifies weak signals—governs the active process of hearing in mammals, validating a universal principle across the animal kingdom. By observing hair cell bundles and electromotility in real time, the advance provides a tool to study how hearing works and breaks, potentially leading to targeted pharmacological therapies for sensorineural hearing loss. The work was led by A. James Hudspeth shortly before his death in August 2025 and published in PNAS.

This patent describes memory arrays comprising vertically-alternating tiers of insulative material and memory cells. Individual memory cells include a transistor having first and second source/drain regions with a horizontally-oriented channel region therebetween and a gate operatively proximate the channel region, and a capacitor having first and second electrodes with a capacitor insulator therebetween. The first capacitor electrode is electrically coupled to the first source/drain region. Second electrodes of multiple capacitors in the array are electrically coupled with one another, in some embodiments via an elevationally-extending capacitor-electrode structure. A sense-line structure extends elevationally through the tiers and electrically couples second source/drain regions of transistors in different memory cell tiers. Embodiments include variations such as two gates directly above one another in a tier, two memory cells stacked directly above one another within a single tier, and single-gate transistors. Staircase regions with staggered contact openings and conductive vias, along with manufacturing methods using selective etching and deposition of materials including carbon-doped silicon nitride, conductively-doped polysilicon, titanium nitride, silicon dioxide, and silicon nitride, are also described.

The present application is a continuation of prior U.S. patent applications and claims priority to a provisional application. The invention relates to automated storage and retrieval systems (AS/RS). Traditional AS/RS bring totes to people for manual picking, which has limitations in efficiency and cost. The disclosed system provides storage, retrieval, and processing of objects using storage bins, destination bins, a gantry retrieval conveyance system, and a processing programmable motion device with an end effector that grasps objects from storage bins and deposits them into destination bins. A perception system identifies grasp locations, favoring flat surfaces and surface normals to improve grasp quality, and learns from good and bad grasp attempts. Storage and destination bins may be mingled and accessed by common or separate gantry systems. The system may include multiple storage and destination sections, processing stations, and floors, controlled by a computer system that tracks bin locations and identities to distribute objects according to a manifest.

Bear markets, typically defined as declines of 20% or more, feature high volatility, sharp rallies, and faster declines than rises. They occur roughly 20% of the time and are shorter than bull markets, but recoveries take significantly longer; for example, the S&P 500 fell 45% during the 2000–2003 bear market and took 6.5 years to reach new highs, while the Nasdaq dropped over 80% and required 15 years to recover. Traders benefit from increased volatility, which improves performance for both long and short strategies, as demonstrated by a mean-reversion strategy on QQQ that produced positive results during the dot-com crash, the GFC, and COVID-19. Investors benefit from lower prices and reduced earnings multiples. Bear markets are viewed as necessary to clear economic excesses and encourage innovation, though central bank interventions may increase future risks. Long-term investors and automated traders generally should maintain their strategies, with concern warranted primarily for those nearing retirement or fund withdrawal.

This study investigates thermal transport in monoclinic β-Ga₂O₃ under uniform strain (ε) and strain gradients (η) using first-principles-based neuroevolution potentials combined with the Boltzmann transport equation. While β-Ga₂O₃ is promising for high-power electronics and flexible devices, its intrinsically low thermal conductivity creates thermal management challenges exacerbated by fabrication-induced nonuniform strains. The results demonstrate that uniaxial and biaxial η in 10 nm and 100 nm films suppress thermal conductivity more strongly than corresponding uniform ε at 300 K, with biaxial η producing reductions up to approximately 43%. Mode-resolved analysis reveals η activates previously forbidden phonon scattering channels and expands the scattering phase space by breaking translational symmetry, particularly affecting low-frequency acoustic and optical phonons. Notably, η decouples thermal conductivity suppression from anisotropy modulation, reducing thermal conductivity without substantially altering thermal anisotropy ratios—a contrast to uniform ε, which strongly modulates anisotropy. These findings establish strain gradients as a critical factor requiring explicit treatment in ultra-wide bandgap semiconductor device thermal modeling.

UCLA researchers discovered that hair follicle stem cell activation depends on lactate production, potentially leading to treatments for baldness and alopecia. Published in Nature Cell Biology, the study showed that genetically blocking lactate in mice prevented stem cell activation, while increasing lactate accelerated hair growth. The team identified two preclinical drugs—RCGD423, which increases lactate via the JAK-Stat pathway, and UK5099, which blocks pyruvate from entering mitochondria—that promoted hair growth when applied to mouse skin. Provisional patents were filed, but the drugs have not been tested in humans or approved by the FDA.

The MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 debug subsystem (DEBUGSS) provides an ARM Serial Wire Debug (SWD) two-wire interface for debugging processor execution and device state, with on-chip pullup and pulldown resistors, software-configurable peripheral behavior during debug halt, a mailbox (DSSM) for SWD communication, and security features including SWD lockout and password authenticated debugging.
