The lecture reviews that digital communication employs a binary interface between source and channel coding for standardization, conceptual layering, and because Shannon proved it incurs no performance loss. The course will first study source coding—beginning with discrete source coding, then quantization, then waveforms—before studying channels. The immediate objective of discrete source coding is to map a sequence of source symbols into a binary sequence with unique decodability, assuming a reliable binary channel.

Fixed-length codes assign each of m symbols a binary string of length l, requiring 2^l ≥ m; l is chosen as ceil(log₂ m). Generalized fixed-length coding segments the source into blocks of length n, yielding mⁿ possible blocks and requiring bits per symbol approaching log₂ m as n grows large. Symbols carry no inherent meaning; only the alphabet size matters.

Variable-length codes are motivated by assigning shorter strings to more probable symbols, but concatenation without delimiters requires careful construction. A prefix-free code, where no codeword is a prefix of another, can be represented by a binary tree and is uniquely decodable; in fact, it is instantaneously decodable because the end of each codeword is immediately recognizable. The Kraft inequality states that a prefix-free code exists for given lengths if and only if the sum of 2^(−length) over all codewords is ≤ 1; equality holds for full trees. All uniquely decodable codes also satisfy this inequality. Unique decodability means the binary concatenation of any source symbol sequence differs from that of any other sequence.

The lecture concludes by introducing the next topic: discrete memoryless sources, where outputs are independent, identically distributed chance variables from a finite alphabet. This probabilistic model will be used to determine optimal code lengths, leading to concepts of entropy and optimal coding.

The shallow cross concept pairs a basic route and shallow drag route from opposite directions to stress linebackers against man and zone coverage, providing quick blitz answers and triangle reads. It succeeds against Man, Tampa 2, and Cover 4, but struggles against Cover 3. Routes use landmarks of 10-12 yards for the basic route and 3-4 yards for the drag, adjusting slightly for man or zone. Quarterbacks read downfield routes first before progressing to Post, Drag, Basic, and RB Checkdown. Variations include Bunch X Shallow Cross and Empty Shallow Cross Post-Wheel. Coach Shawn Liotta provides a video installation.

This lecture examines the economics and business case for green buildings, emphasizing that private-sector incentives are essential since over 80% of building stock is privately supplied. Using Millennium Partners as a case study, the speaker illustrates how developer priorities shift based on market context and profit motives across projects, moving from luxury condos and job creation to wellness and, most recently, high-level sustainability certifications like LEED Platinum and Passive House.

The lecture presents a market mechanism framework linking three stakeholders in a chain: tenants, owners, and developers. If tenants value green features and have a higher willingness to pay, owners can charge higher rents and experience lower vacancy, leading to higher net operating income, lower risk, and greater net present value. This increased owner willingness to pay translates into higher sale prices for developers. Potential benefits discussed include lower operational and financing costs, easier permitting, health and productivity gains, talent retention, and higher asset values. Empirical studies cited show average rent premiums of about 6% for residential and 5% for commercial, and sales price premiums around 7.6%, though results vary widely. Green construction can carry a cost premium (0–12.5% for new buildings), but this may decline with improved skills, technology, and supply chains.

The lecture also addresses market failures, focusing on information asymmetry. When buyers cannot verify green claims, adverse selection and greenwashing occur, disincentivizing quality construction. Certification systems like LEED are presented as tools to solve this information problem by credibly signaling building quality to the market.
WIS News 10 will air a 7:30 p.m. special on the August 21 total solar eclipse, when the moon will fully cover the sun over Columbia, drawing hundreds of thousands to the Midlands.

Brea Police deployed a $21,000 Polaris Gem Global Electric Motorcar, funded by the Air Quality Management District, to patrol The Tracks at Brea trail and downtown. Introduced at the Centennial Parade, it reaches 25 mph with a 98-mile range. Officials say it allows quicker patrols of linear parks than foot or bicycle.

While higher education institutions have established learning assessment processes for credit-bearing programs, noncredit continuing education—which includes professional competency training, career advancement, and personal enrichment—has historically lacked similar attention. The authors argue that despite shorter durations, varying learner motivations, and limited resources, assessment is needed to guide curriculum and improve student learning outcomes. They recommend developing clear, measurable, and realistic learning outcomes suited to the course length and learners’ prior knowledge, using frameworks such as Bloom’s taxonomy. For assessment, they propose learning outcome-focused surveys in which learners self-report their achievement, including retrospective pre-post designs for brief courses. For direct assessment, they suggest adding one to three quiz questions to end-of-course surveys or having learners produce work—such as projects, presentations, or role-plays—that instructors evaluate using a simple two-point scale. They emphasize ensuring validity, fairness, and learner benefit. The authors conclude that such assessments are feasible in noncredit settings and suggest leveraging digital micro-credentials to motivate learners and verify competencies.

BG Group agreed to buy Enron's offshore oil and gas assets in India for $388 million, a price analysts considered inexpensive. The assets include Enron's stakes in the Tapti, Panna/Mukta, and CB-OS/1 fields off western India. The deal is conditional on BG securing operatorship and Indian government approval; partner ONGC, which holds 40 percent and had previously bid for the assets, is seeking operatorship and could block the transfer. Enron is separately attempting to sell its 65 percent stake in the Dabhol Power Project, which is stalled by payment disputes and a $24 million interest default by its Indian unit. Former Enron executive and Army Secretary Thomas White was also named the Defense Department's top official for homeland security.

The lecture reviews Markov chains and eigenvalues, explaining that for a block upper diagonal transition matrix, the eigenvalues are the union of those of the transient and recurrent submatrices, and left eigenvectors of the recurrent submatrix extend to the full matrix. It then introduces state rewards, defining expected aggregate rewards over n steps and steady-state gain. The expected first passage time to a state is formulated as a reward problem by making the target state a trapping state and solving the linear equations v = r + Pv. The lecture concludes with dynamic programming, where a decision maker at each state selects an alternative yielding an immediate reward and transition probabilities; Bellman's algorithm finds the optimal policy and expected aggregate reward for a finite horizon by working backward from a final reward, with each optimal decision depending only on the current state.

This application, a continuation of International Patent Application No. PCT/CN2020/108808, discloses methods and apparatuses for information transmission and reception in communication systems, particularly for managing Maximum Power Exposure (MPE) in high-frequency bands. An information sending method involves a first communication node sending report information to a second communication node; the report includes at least one of first type power parameter information (e.g., maximum power reduction, remaining or accumulated energy value, uplink duty cycle, alert identification, power backoff, or power headroom) or uplink channel state information (e.g., reference signal information, antenna group information, uplink path loss, or quasi co-location information). A corresponding reception method involves the second communication node receiving the report and scheduling the first communication node to determine maximum power reduction and mitigate MPE effects. The application also describes information sending and reception apparatuses, first and second communication nodes comprising processors and storage, and a storage medium storing programs to execute these methods.

The Power play is a versatile gap run scheme featuring a pulling backside guard, kick out block, and back blocks to create angles at the point of attack. Its strengths include outnumbering the defense with concentrated blockers and double teams—taught as vertical or horizontal combinations to fit different line sizes—making it effective for gaining yardage. Its primary weakness is backside pursuit and penetration through the vacated guard gap, especially against even and odd fronts if protection calls or tackle hinges fail. The passage details player-by-player blocking assignments against 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts, and describes variations including the Diamond Fullhouse and Gun Same-Side Power RPO.

European Commission President Jean-Claude Juncker stated that India's 5.7% GDP growth is not considered a slowdown outside India, contrasting with domestic criticism. World Bank President Jim Yong Kim attributed the slowdown to temporary GST disruptions, while BJP leader Yashwant Sinha described the economy as a "mess" and called for course correction.

Bill Purswell was convicted of transporting intoxicating liquor and sentenced to one year in prison. Officers hiding in a field observed him carrying a jug of whiskey on another person’s property and arrested him without a warrant. The court affirmed the conviction, holding that objections to illegal search and seizure are personal to the property owner or possessor and unavailable to Purswell; that the arrest was lawful because officers witnessed a felony in progress, making the evidence admissible; and that general objections to the jury charge are insufficient. On rehearing, the court rejected his claim of jury misconduct based solely on his own affidavit alleging the jury considered his failure to testify, citing insufficient proof. The judgment was affirmed and rehearing overruled.

The court affirmed an order denying Dairylea Cooperative's motion to quash a subpoena duces tecum issued by the New York Attorney-General for a grand jury investigation. The court rejected the State's claim that no appeal lay from the order, finding older precedents no longer controlling. It held the Attorney-General had authority under Executive Law § 63(3) because the Commissioner of Agriculture and Markets had requested the investigation.

The passage is a November 2001 *Texas Monthly* article, "How Enron Blew It," by Mimi Swartz, forwarded among Enron employees via email. It recounts Enron’s rise from a 1985 pipeline company to a dominant energy-trading giant under Ken Lay and Jeff Skilling, with its stock increasing 1,700 percent over sixteen years. The firm fostered an aggressive, "knowledge-based" culture that prized risk-taking, recruited elite talent, and used a harsh forced-ranking performance review system. Enron expanded into electricity, water through Azurix, and telecommunications, while employing mark-to-market accounting to book profits upfront. The article notes subsequent setbacks: a stock price decline from $80 to roughly $35, backlash during the California energy crisis, costly international projects including a troubled Indian power plant, failed broadband and video-on-demand ventures, and growing Wall Street scrutiny of its finances. After six months as CEO, Skilling resigned in 2001, citing personal sacrifices, while Lay returned to leadership and acknowledged the need to refocus on core energy businesses and address morale issues.

Firefly Aerospace's stock fell nearly 21% after its Alpha Flight 7 rocket exploded during a test flight at its Texas facility on Monday. The company said all personnel were safe and it is assessing damage to the stage test stand. Firefly, which makes rockets, space tugs and lunar landers, debuted on the Nasdaq last month, raising $868 million at a $6.3 billion valuation, but shares have since pulled back over 50%. Earlier this year, its lunar lander successfully landed on the moon, and the company stated it learns from each test to improve reliability.

South Dakota's Board of Regents directed staff to prepare a plan to close Pierre's Capital University Center for the Oct. 3-5 meeting. Kevin Schieffer pushed for action. John Bastian said a wind-down is needed.

The disclosure provides transmitting devices and methods for improved UE-autonomous radio resource allocation for sidelink data and scheduling assignment transmission, particularly for vehicular (V2X) communication. A transmitting device continuously performs a resource sensing procedure to acquire information about future radio resources, including monitoring other devices' scheduling assignments to identify reserved resources and measuring received signal energy. Upon data arrival, the device performs autonomous resource allocation to select radio resources within a transmission window based on information gathered during a preceding sensing window. The allocation distinguishes primary subframes—where sensing was fully performed in all corresponding subframes of the sensing window—from secondary subframes, where sensing information is incomplete because the device could not sense during corresponding subframes due to its own half-duplex transmissions. The device preferentially selects resources in primary subframes over secondary subframes. Resource candidates are ranked separately within each category based on time delay and predicted energy, favoring candidates with shorter delay and lower predicted energy. The procedure also applies to scheduling assignments, which may reserve resources for future transmissions. This improves upon existing methods by addressing inaccurate energy predictions and latency issues.

The passage argues that the Arctic is a complex, interconnected system of environmental, geopolitical, economic, and sociocultural factors where decisions produce cascading, cross-domain effects. Traditional linear, siloed security education is inadequate for this environment. It advocates a systems thinking framework emphasizing holistic, interdisciplinary analysis, pattern recognition, and leverage points for educational intervention. The proposed Systems Thinking Education Model consists of three components: core principles (interdisciplinary learning and interconnected analysis), leverage points (mental model shifts, information flows, governance, behavioral changes, and technology), and learning/assessment strategies. Recommended instructional methods include concept mapping, simulations and wargaming, role-playing, and interactive case studies. Assessment should shift to scenario-based problem-solving, reflective analysis, and competency-based metrics measuring interdisciplinary analysis and strategic foresight. This approach bridges the gap between policy theory and operational reality, preparing professionals to anticipate unintended consequences and adapt to dynamic challenges. The framework is especially applicable to online graduate education through asynchronous scenarios, digital simulations, and collaborative, cross-disciplinary exercises.

Officials declared Code Red Dangerous for the AJC Peachtree Road Race shortly after 9 a.m.; runners should slow down. 11Alive broadcasts the 49th race, offering $70,000 exclusively to American athletes in upper 80s weather.

On October 29, 2001, Moody's Investors Service downgraded Enron Corp.'s senior unsecured long-term debt rating to Baa2, two notches above junk status, and placed its commercial paper rating on review for further downgrade. Enron's stock price fell to around $14, a multi-year low, after losing more than half its value in two weeks and over $14 billion in market capitalization. The company, which drew down approximately $3 billion in bank credit lines last week, said it was negotiating with banks for an additional $1 billion to $2 billion in credit to restore confidence. Analysts characterized the drawdown as a sign of desperation and predicted lenders would demand collateral and stricter terms. The crisis followed disclosures of off-balance-sheet transactions with partnerships run by former CFO Andrew Fastow, which led to a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity, Fastow's replacement, and a U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission inquiry. European energy firms were freezing or restricting trade with Enron over credit worries, while shareholders filed at least five lawsuits against Enron and executives including Fastow, former CEO Jeff Skilling, and Chairman Ken Lay alleging conflicts of interest. Standard & Poor's also revised its outlook on Enron to negative.

This MIT OpenCourseWare lecture by Lorna Gibson introduces a course on cellular solids—porous materials with low solid volume fractions—covering honeycombs, foams, and natural and medical materials including trabecular bone, tissue engineering scaffolds, wood, cork, and bamboo. The course addresses modeling of stiffness and strength, applications such as lightweight sandwich panels, energy absorption, thermal insulation, and catalyst carriers, and open-ended student projects. Gibson displays samples including aluminum and ceramic honeycombs, metal and polymer foams, bone, and wood, and discusses processing techniques: honeycombs are produced by expansion, corrugation, extrusion, rapid prototyping, casting, and bio-carbon templating from wood; polymer foams are made by mechanical stirring, physical or chemical blowing agents, syntactic foams, and structural foams; and metal foams are fabricated via molten metal stirring, titanium hydride decomposition, replication of polymer foams, vapor deposition, entrapped gas expansion, hollow sphere bonding, and fugitive phase methods. She ends with a brief account of her education and career path from civil engineering to materials science at MIT.

Goals are scored more frequently during specific approximately five-minute segments in soccer, including the starts and ends of halves, periods following goals, saved or missed penalty kicks, bad fouls, and extra time. The phenomenon stems from team psychology, including excitement, mental unpreparedness, complacency after scoring, emotional reactions to conceding, and urgency near halftime or the final whistle. Coaches must prepare players to avoid let-downs after goals, preventing over-confidence or depression, and commonly remind teams, "No letdown!"

Q3 2025 credit commentary notes that municipal bonds are an extremely safe, flight-to-quality asset class, but anticipated challenges are now present and highlighted by a government shutdown, and muni credit quality may begin to turn this quarter. The Federal Reserve lowered short-term interest rates in September amid a slowdown in job growth and mixed inflation readings, while many municipalities have received upgrades for better-funded reserves. The passage also provides biographical details on David Kotok, co-founder and former Chief Investment Officer of Cumberland Advisors, including his publications, media contributions, education, and service on various economic and governmental boards.

Ivy Chiu of RBC advises newcomers to Canada to build networks before job searching. Tips include starting online job searches before arriving, using free newcomer workshops for resumes and interviews, pursuing internships and volunteering, updating credentials for the Canadian market, and improving English or French proficiency. Preparation helps manage job hunting emotions.

Supreme Court justices debated whether Delaware’s procedural requirements for medical malpractice litigation should apply in federal court. Justices Kagan, Jackson, and Sotomayor suggested the state rules conflict with the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure by forcing plaintiffs to effectively prove their case at the outset, requiring an affidavit to initiate suit, and delaying answers. Counsel for the defendants argued federal courts need not reject entire state statutes over partial conflicts, but Justice Gorsuch questioned the authority to selectively rewrite state law. Chief Justice Roberts and Justices Thomas and Alito revealed little of their positions, leaving the outcome uncertain.

An American Soccer Player's Creed, copyrighted by John C. Harves and presented by CoachingAmericanSoccer.com, establishes tactical and ethical guidelines for soccer players. It requires maintaining constant ball awareness, communicating with teammates and coaches, playing hard without committing stupid fouls, knowing the Laws of the Game, and demonstrating fair play and sportsmanlike behavior both on and off the field.

Trump and Trudeau's meeting clarified US-Canada trade relations, with Trump calling issues less severe than with Mexico and signaling tweaks rather than an overhaul, pushing USD/CAD to 1.3060. The pound outperformed while the euro lagged. A short EURUSD trade closed for a 130-pip gain. Markets await Yellen's testimony, China CPI and PPI data, and a Kuroda speech.

The DAWN-PLASMA study was a randomized, open-label, phase 2, multicenter trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of convalescent plasma plus standard of care versus standard of care alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. The primary objective was to assess whether early administration of high-volume, high-titer convalescent plasma reduced the need for mechanical ventilation. The primary endpoint was the percentage of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Secondary endpoints included clinical status, time to sustained improvement, incidence of mechanical ventilation or death, safety outcomes, and quality of life. Participants were randomized 2:1 to receive 800–1000 mL of convalescent plasma in four doses, with the first dose within 12 hours of randomization, or to standard of care. The study followed the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH GCP guidelines, required IEC approval and informed consent, and used a computerized randomization system with a blinded statistician until database lock. Six patients were substituted after consent withdrawal or screen failure, and no patients were lost to follow-up.

This study evaluates the usability of e-business portals in Saudi Arabia, an emerging online market. Using a cross-sectional design, 65 students trained in user interface evaluation assessed eight popular websites—four retail and four booking—via a questionnaire measuring navigation, design, and content on a Likert scale. Findings revealed generally positive ratings but notable usability weaknesses across both groups. Navigation issues included orphan pages, links causing menus to disappear, poor internal navigation, and incorrect sitemap links. Design problems featured inconsistent Arabic-English language interfaces, inconsistent font sizes, overly complex layouts, and insufficient icon labeling. Content deficiencies included missing contact information, absent last update dates, missing sitemaps, spelling and grammatical errors, empty pages, and poor alphabetical ordering. Cronbach’s Alpha values were 0.66 for Group 1 and 0.79 for Group 2, indicating converging but weaker internal validity for the smaller group. The authors note the small sample size and number of websites limit generalizability. They recommend user-centered and participatory design approaches, ethnographic studies, and technical writing improvements to address these issues. Enhancing website usability in these areas is deemed critical for customer satisfaction, engagement, retention, and revenue growth in Saudi Arabia’s e-business sector.

Bank of Canada official Carolyn Wilkins expects Canada's household debt-to-income ratio (170.4% in Q4 2017) to gradually decline as credit growth slows and labour income rises, though winding down will take time. She noted debt funded asset purchases, boosting net worth. The Bank, which has raised rates three times since July, views debt as a top concern; Poloz said high debt makes households 50% more sensitive to interest rate movements.
It is the team's responsibility to battle to the net; the opposing goalie is large and plays back; after regrouping during two days off following a loss, they are ready to get the first goal tonight.

To attack full-court pressure, teams must anticipate presses, analyze their weaknesses, and employ a five-player approach using offensive formations rather than relying on one ball handler. Key principles include spreading the floor, taking maximum distance up court, and using a slow-to-quick tempo while working the ball to the middle. Advance the ball with short, crisp passes, use the dribble sparingly and always end with a shot or pass, and avoid one-handed or lob passes. Receivers must create leads, meet passes, and catch in a triple-threat stance with their back to the sideline. After made shots or rebounds, the first look is a long outlet pass, followed by short and middle options, while the trailer maintains defensive balance. Teams should practice attacking outnumbered situations like 2-on-1 and 3-on-2 breaks, and reverse the ball to the inbounder trailer against double teams to create 4-on-3 advantages. Coaches should install press breaks using the "Whole-Part-Whole" teaching method, emphasizing precise execution, spacing, and timing through progressive breakdown drills and live defense. Always run the press break after made field goals and free throws to eliminate surprise, and flow directly into early offense if the break does not produce a good shot.

The negatively charged boron vacancy (V$_{\rm B}^-$) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) offers an alternative to diamond nitrogen-vacancy centers for near-surface quantum sensing. This study demonstrates coherent control of the three nearest-neighbor $^{15}$N nuclear spins in isotopically enriched h$^{10}$B$^{15}$N using electron-nuclear double resonance (ENDOR). Hyperfine coupling induces electron-nuclear spin mixing, enabling selective addressing of four hyperfine states (P1–P4) with distinct transition energies ($\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$) and lifting degeneracies. This mixing enhances the nuclear g-factor by approximately 116-fold compared to isolated $^{15}$N nuclei, allowing rapid nuclear Rabi driving. The nuclear spin Rabi coherence time exceeds 10 µs, orders of magnitude longer than the electron spin coherence time. However, optical repumping causes rapid nuclear spin depolarization within approximately 1 µs, tentatively attributed to the optically excited 3E$''$ state. These results establish the strongly coupled nuclear spins of V$_{\rm B}^-$ as a controllable quantum resource with potential for quantum memories, nuclear-assisted dynamics, and nanoscale quantum sensing in van der Waals heterostructures.

Treetops, built in 1992 near Keynsham town centre, accommodates elderly people with dementia in three units with lounges and dining rooms. It offers named carers, individual support, family care planning, and activities. It advises checking suitability and disclaims responsibility for inaccuracies.

The Supreme Court of Pennsylvania affirmed the Commonwealth Court order holding that the Nonpublic Elementary and Secondary Education Act (Act 109) is constitutional and enforceable as applied to nonsectarian nonpublic schools. The court rejected the Department of Education’s contention that *Lemon v. Kurtzman* had declared the Act unconstitutional in its entirety, ruling that *Lemon* invalidated it only as applied to sectarian schools. The court held that Act 109 is severable under Pennsylvania’s Statutory Construction Act and the Act’s own severability clause, and that the legislative purpose of enhancing secular education is effectuated by its application to nonsectarian schools. It further held that subsequent legislation did not impliedly repeal Act 109 because those statutes did not cover the Act’s entire subject matter and were not irreconcilable. Finally, the court ruled that requiring the Department to determine whether a school is sectarian or nonsectarian does not create excessive entanglement in violation of the First Amendment. Justice Eagen dissented.

Blair school district voters failed to approve a $250,000 transportation bond issue, with 58.76 percent approval falling short of the required 60 percent super-majority. The bond would have purchased three buses to replace leased vehicles. Other area municipal and school board election results are included.

Tesla, Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2018, includes unaudited consolidated financial statements. Total revenues were $3.41 billion compared to $2.70 billion in the prior-year quarter. Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $709.6 million, or $4.19 per share, compared to $330.3 million, or $2.04 per share. Total assets were $27.27 billion, total liabilities were $21.55 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $4.45 billion. Cash and cash equivalents and restricted cash decreased by $745.3 million to $3.22 billion; net cash used in operating activities was $398.4 million, net cash used in investing activities was $728.6 million, and net cash provided by financing activities was $371.7 million. The company adopted ASC 606 on January 1, 2018, using the modified retrospective method, changing revenue recognition for certain vehicle sales with resale value guarantees to sales with a right of return and reducing the opening accumulated deficit by $623.2 million. Tesla operates automotive and energy generation and storage segments. As of March 31, 2018, total debt was $10.47 billion, customer deposits were $984.8 million, and the company was in compliance with debt covenants. The filing also describes a 2018 CEO Performance Award of 20.3 million stock options, with $766.2 million of unrecognized stock-based compensation expense for milestones considered probable of achievement and $1.51 billion for those not probable.

Tesla Motors, Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2016, reports total revenues of $1.27 billion, up from $955.0 million in the prior-year quarter, and a net loss of $293.2 million. Automotive revenue rose to $1.18 billion, driven by higher vehicle deliveries including Model X, while gross margin was 21.6%. Total assets grew to $11.87 billion and cash and equivalents reached $3.25 billion, boosted by a $1.7 billion public stock offering and $1.1 billion in debt proceeds. The company produced 18,345 vehicles in Q2 and targets 50,000 deliveries in the second half of 2016 and 500,000 total vehicles in 2018. Tesla plans to invest approximately $2.25 billion in capital expenditures in 2016 and expects Gigafactory cell production to begin in Q4 2016. On July 31, 2016, Tesla entered into an agreement to acquire SolarCity Corporation, subject to shareholder and regulatory approval. Subsequent to the quarter, Tesla received conversion notices for approximately $411 million of its 2018 convertible notes. The filing notes risks including supplier concentration, production ramp challenges, and the need for additional capital to support growth.

This ebook edition of *Papers Relating to the Foreign Relations of the United States, 1906, Part I*, generated by the Office of the Historian in May 2018, offers the full volume content for offline reading with search and bookmarking; readers should cite document numbers rather than page numbers. The included presidential annual message urges Congress to prohibit corporate campaign contributions and to pass a bill granting the Government the right to appeal criminal cases on questions of law, arguing that the absence of such appeal authority allows conflicting lower court decisions to block justice and prevents the Supreme Court from deciding constitutional questions.

Former Bengals quarterback Andy Dalton has been floated as a potential option amid Jake Browning's struggles. Dalton started in Cincinnati in 2011 and played 13 games under coach Zac Taylor in 2019. Now with the Panthers through 2026, a trade would cost the Bengals about $3 million. Browning has 506 passing yards, three touchdowns, and five interceptions through three games.

The device operates on independent AVDD and DVDD supplies. Decouple AVDD with a minimum 10µF and 1µF capacitor and DVDD with a minimum 10µF capacitor placed close to the pins; decoupling improves PSRR. The device offers NAP and power-down modes to reduce consumption at lower throughput. Enter NAP by writing 69h to address 05h, setting NAP_EN, and holding CONVST/CS high after conversion; exit via a falling edge after tNAP_WKUP. Enter power-down by unlocking the register and setting PWRDN to 1b on the CONVST/CS rising edge; exit by clearing PWRDN and waiting tPWRUP, with analog blocks off but the interface and registers active. For layout, partition analog and digital sections, place 1µF X7R 0603 10V-rated ceramic capacitors near AVDD and DVDD without vias, connect a 1µF and a 10µF (<0.2Ω ESR) capacitor directly to REFCAP, and decouple REFIO with a minimum 4.7µF ceramic if using the internal reference. The May 2025 revision changed ADS8685W and ADS8689W to Production Data, and the IC requires ESD precautions.

Moscow denies poisoning the Skripals, but Britain accuses Russia of stockpiling Novichok and using it on British soil. Russian officials deflected blame toward a UK facility and Putin offered conditional cooperation. The author urges the West to impose tougher sanctions and pursue legal changes to target billions in hidden assets held by Putin's allies in Britain and America.

In a May 1980 interview, Ronald Reagan criticized the President's remarks on a failed mission and expressed concern that Iran was moving into the Soviet camp, noting Soviet influence through cross-border propaganda and the Communist Party; he warned this would seriously threaten the Middle East, US security, and allies. In his July 1980 Republican nomination acceptance speech, Reagan emphasized peace through strength, pledged to protect Americans from hostile foreign powers, and vowed to negotiate in good faith while ensuring enemies of freedom do not dictate humanity's future. In an address to veterans, he stated peace is not preserved by weakness, noted the disappearing margin of safety in defense capability, defended military preparedness, and cited Will Rogers on strength not inviting war.

The article investigates non-Abelian quantum interference and entanglement generation via braiding of topological edge states in periodically modulated one-dimensional multi-chain Su-Schrieffer-Heeger systems. The platform is protected by time-dependent interchain symmetry, which forms multiple edge-state branches and enables their temporal braiding and robust adiabatic evolution even when energy gaps close transiently, and by time-independent inversion symmetry, which conserves parity and allows phase-controlled partitioning of particle transfer. In a double-coupled chain, two pairs of edge states undergo Abelian braiding and symmetry-protected transport between chains at a tunable ratio governed by an accumulated dynamical phase. In a triple-coupled chain, three pairs of edge states exhibit non-Abelian braiding, where the sequence of operations determines the recipient chain for topological transport. For two-particle injection, the system realizes non-Abelian Hong-Ou-Mandel interference, generating spatially entangled two-particle NOON states on different chains depending on the braiding order. The authors identify these effects as key signatures of non-Abelian topology and propose photonic waveguide arrays as a viable experimental platform.

Speedy, which floated on the stock market in March 1999, faced operational and financial difficulties when Russell Down became chief executive in the summer of 2015 following a profit warning. Down found the business amid issues including unreliable IT data on asset hire status, declining revenue from smaller customers, and equipment testing backlogs at regional depots that left over 50% of products unavailable in September 2015. He transformed the inward-looking culture, instilled a rigorous customer focus, kept a tight rein on operating costs, and improved product availability and asset utilisation. Results for the six months to September showed profits surging 58.8% to £10.8m, reduced net debt, and improved Return on Capital Employed. The company reintroduced annual staff surveys and has acquired Prolift Access Limited and Platform Sales & Hire Limited to expand its powered access product reach, positioning it to deliver sustainable profitable growth.

Clark County schools are deciding at the school level how to spend their share of Nevada’s new $36 million weighted funding formula. The program allocates $1,200 per student who scores in the bottom 25 percent on state tests, is either learning English or living in poverty, and does not attend a school receiving Zoom or Victory funding. Clark County received over $34 million. Unlike schoolwide Zoom and Victory funds, weighted funding targets specific students. Schools are finalizing spending plans; Garside Junior High is receiving over $450,000 and considering expanded after-school tutoring and technology. Spending will be tracked separately and analyzed for impact on student achievement.

Mastitis is the dairy industry's costliest disease, typically treated with antibiotics that kill bacteria but cannot regenerate damaged mammary tissue. Cornell researchers Van de Walle and Nydam published findings in *Scientific Reports* on bovine mammary stem cell secretions as an alternative therapy. Their study, the first to detail these secretions, found they promote tissue healing through blood vessel formation and cell migration, protect epithelial cells from bacterial toxins, and contain antimicrobial peptides effective against gram-negative bacteria. This could complement existing antibiotics, which work better on gram-positive bacteria. The researchers plan to test the therapy in cows with mastitis.

Hyundai and Kia have installed a vehicle-to-everything (V2X) system on a 14-kilometer road in Hwaseong, South Korea, to advance autonomous driving. The system allows real-time communication between vehicles, road infrastructure, and pedestrians to overcome sensor limitations. The companies will gather data through year-end to refine the system for a 2020 highway infrastructure project.

A treaty of annexation concluded on February 14, 1893, between the United States and Hawaiian commissioners is transmitted for Senate ratification, deferring detailed questions to future U.S. adjustment. The overthrow of Queen Liliuokalani is attributed to her own policies rather than U.S. promotion, and her restoration is deemed undesirable. Annexation is presented as preferable to a protectorate to secure U.S. interests and prevent other powers from gaining the islands. Prompt ratification is urged to maintain peace until Congress establishes permanent government.

Caitlin Bassett says the build-up to Saturday's Super Netball grand final between Sunshine Coast Lightning and Greater Western Sydney is unlike anything she has experienced. Despite being an international star, she has never played in a national grand final. Lightning captain Geva Mentor has prepared to face Giants shooter Kristina Brice by training against 215cm Junior Levi.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI), developed by Welles Wilder in 1978, is an oscillator measuring price momentum on a 0–100 scale to identify overbought and oversold conditions. Backtesting indicates RSI works best for mean-reverting strategies on stocks and stock indices, particularly with short lookback periods of two to five days using daily bars. While simple strategies can perform well, adding filters or additional indicators improves effectiveness. Typical thresholds vary by timeframe; for example, a two-day RSI may use 15 for oversold and 85 for overbought. Variations include Connors RSI and Cutler’s RSI. The indicator performs poorly on commodities and forex, and divergence signals offer little practical value. Research emphasizes that backtesting is essential to optimize settings and confirm predictive value for specific assets.

The Supreme Court case *Landor v. Louisiana Department of Corrections and Public Safety* will consider whether the Religious Land Use and Institutionalized Persons Act (RLUIPA) permits money damages against government employees who violate prisoners’ religious rights. The case involves Damon Landor, a Rastafarian inmate whose dreadlocks were forcibly shaved by Louisiana prison officials. The author contends Landor should win, citing the analogous Religious Freedom Restoration Act’s authorization of money damages. The piece challenges three common narratives: that religious-freedom cases are polarized and partisan, that protections chiefly benefit majority faiths, and that claimants are merely conservative culture-war actors. It notes that many such decisions are unanimous, often protect minority religions, and typically involve practical accommodations rather than high-profile social disputes. The case underscores that religious freedom is a foundational human right for all persons.

A retrospective study of 671 traumatic brain injury (TBI) patients (212 women and 459 men) from July 2017 to December 2018 examined gender-dependent risk factors. Domestic accidents were the most frequently reported cause of TBI overall (43.81%) and in both sexes (57.54% of women; 37.47% of men), followed by alcohol-related injury (20.71%), motor vehicle injury (16.54%), and criminal injury (11.17%). Patients living in villages had a significantly higher risk of TBI than those in cities, though city patients were older on average. Men were affected at a significantly younger mean age than women (44.41 versus 49.50 years) and had longer hospitalizations; total hospitalization days correlated with age in both groups. The majority of patients received conservative therapy, while 198 required surgical treatment. The authors concluded that gender plays a crucial role in TBI incidence, severity, and post-TBI outcomes, and that alcohol consumption and poor healthcare practice are avoidable risk factors. The study was limited by the absence of a control group.

This passage outlines a coaching progression for teaching young soccer players offensive corner kicks under Law 17. Awarded when defenders send the ball over their own end line, corner kicks offer scoring opportunities through set plays. The initial sequence involves explaining the rule, demonstrating ball placement in the corner arc, and teaching the correct 45-degree run-up and instep drive kick. Coaches first demonstrate right-footed kicks from the right corner, then introduce a three-position play with a corner taker, a receiver five yards into the field, and a cover man near the end line. After rotating all players through these positions, coaches demonstrate left-footed and left-side options. For games, specific players are assigned, passive and active defenders are added, and additional passing options and offside rules are introduced. Coaching tips note that the referee indicates the correct corner and that the taker must wait for the signal before kicking; stronger players may eventually execute longer, lofted balls.

UNC coach Bill Belichick accepted blame for a 38–10 loss to Clemson, citing defensive lapses allowing 399 passing yards and three illegal formation penalties. The offense managed 213 passing yards with no touchdowns and converted 2-of-11 third downs. Belichick praised his team’s effort but refused to evaluate the rebuild. Deion Sanders said he is trying to find light in a dark tunnel.

U.S. stocks fell about 2 percent on Monday as Facebook shares tumbled 7.1 percent on reports that a political consultancy gained inappropriate access to data on more than 50 million users, sparking a broader technology selloff. The Nasdaq Composite slid 2.09 percent and the S&P technology index dropped 2.5 percent. All 11 major S&P sectors declined amid concerns about data privacy, global trade tensions, and an upcoming Federal Reserve interest rate decision.

Blackwell features advanced power management including reduced latencies for power states, fine-grain clock and rail gating, GDDR7 fast-wakeup support, separate voltage rails for GPU cores and memory, and accelerated frequency switching that adjusts clocks 1000x faster than previous architectures. It enters its deepest sleep state 10x faster than Ada, enabling up to 50% power savings. DLSS 4 leverages fifth-generation Tensor Cores to introduce Multi Frame Generation, creating up to three additional frames per rendered frame via a 40% faster AI model that uses 30% less VRAM, alongside enhanced Flip Metering. DLSS 4 also replaces CNNs with transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, doubling parameter ingestion to improve temporal stability, motion detail, and lighting quality. Blackwell enables neural shaders through the Cooperative Vectors API, supporting neural texture compression, RTX Neural Materials, Neural Radiance Cache for global illumination, RTX Skin for subsurface scattering, and RTX Neural Faces. The GPU family includes the flagship GB202 (RTX 5090) with 92.2 billion transistors and 24,576 CUDA cores; the high-end GB203 (RTX 5080/5070 Ti) with 45.6 billion transistors and 10,752 CUDA cores; and the performance-segment GB205 (RTX 5070) with 31 billion transistors and 6,400 CUDA cores.

Sodium cumenesulfonate is a water-soluble hydrotope compound available in powder and liquid forms. It increases solubility, lowers cloud points, promotes compatibility, and moderates viscosity. Applications include cleaners, drilling fluids, detergents, and oilfield uses. Raw material price volatility, health hazards, and declining R&D may hamper the market, while industrialization and household detergent demand in emerging economies drive growth. The liquid form and household application segments dominated the 2015 market and are expected to remain leading.

San Diego police pursued a wanted shooting suspect from Fairmont Avenue in City Heights at 12:30 Sunday. Suspect crashed into school and fire station fences, fled with a gun, was arrested near 41st Street, University Avenue.

A treaty for Hawaii's admission as a US state failed in 1855 after King Kamehameha III died and his successor opposed it. A reciprocity treaty that July also failed ratification. Diplomatic rank was raised in 1863, but the Civil War deferred further reciprocity talks. In 1867, Minister McCook negotiated a new reciprocity treaty, approved by the President but rejected by the Senate in 1870. Secretary Seward instructed McCook to explore annexation, later advising that annexation should be preferred over reciprocity if the two policies conflicted. Hawaiian ratification of the 1867 treaty was delayed by apprehension over the USS Lackawanna's presence.

The speaker takes the presidential oath, invoking divine guidance to restore harmony among the states and preserve free institutions. Citing a duty to serve without seeking reelection, the speaker addresses the settlement of the slavery question in the Territories through popular sovereignty, leaving the decision to residents subject to the Constitution, and notes a pending Supreme Court case on the timing of such decisions. The speaker urges suppression of sectional agitation to preserve the Union, warns that disunion would cause universal ruin, and condemns calculations of the Union’s material value. The address highlights the danger of a large treasury surplus and public land squandering, advocating strict construction of the Constitution, using surplus funds for national objects like debt reduction and naval expansion, and reserving public lands for settlers. It defends federal military road construction for national defense, and outlines a foreign policy of peace, commerce, non-interference, and avoidance of entangling alliances, while asserting that territorial expansion must occur only through just purchase or voluntary union. The speaker concludes by taking the oath.

Stephen Hawking, the theoretical physicist and author of the bestseller "A Brief History of Time," has died, his family announced. Diagnosed with ALS at 21, he lived with the disease for over 50 years, communicating through a voice synthesizer after 1985. As Lucasian Professor at Cambridge, he pursued a "unified theory" reconciling relativity and quantum mechanics. He called belief in an intervening God wishful thinking. Despite near-total paralysis, he became a scientific celebrity through books, cameos on "The Simpsons" and "Star Trek," and the film "The Theory of Everything." His celebrity generated enthusiasm for science, and his achievements demonstrated that severe disabilities need not stop patients from living.

Frost Brown Todd and Gibbons plan to merge in January to form FBT Gibbons, with 800 lawyers in 25 offices. The merger adds Northeast offices. Robert Sartin will be chairman, while Adam Hall and Peter Torcicollo will be co-managing partners. Frost Brown Todd had $336.5 million in revenue and Gibbons had $115 million. Talks began after a Zeughauser Group retreat.

Synaptics announced plans to mass produce "Clear ID," an optical in-display fingerprint sensor for bezel-less smartphones. The company claims it is twice as fast as 3D facial recognition, requires one touch, and works from any angle. Despite Apple adopting facial recognition, Synaptics states consumers prefer front-facing fingerprint authentication, ensuring the technology remains a security option.

The passage describes design patterns for containerized and distributed systems. It begins with single-node container patterns: the sidecar pattern augments an application container with additional functionality, requiring a stable, well-documented API and parameterization via environment variables; documentation should be embedded in the container image using Dockerfile directives like EXPOSE, ENV, and LABEL. The ambassador pattern brokers communication between an application and external services, with examples including client-side sharding for Redis using twemproxy, service brokering for dynamic discovery, and request splitting for experimentation using nginx. The adapter pattern standardizes application interfaces for monitoring, logging, or health checks without modifying the main container, exemplified by Prometheus exporters, Fluentd log normalization, and MySQL health-check adapters.

The text then covers multi-node distributed patterns. Microservices architectures decouple functionality into independent services with defined APIs, improving scalability and team autonomy over monolithic designs. The replicated load-balanced service pattern uses stateless replicas behind a load balancer, employing readiness probes, session tracking, and layered caching (Varnish) and SSL termination (nginx) for performance and security. Sharded services partition data across nodes using sharding functions such as hashing and modulo operations; consistent hashing minimizes re-sharding disruption, while hot sharding and replicated shards improve resilience. The scatter/gather pattern parallelizes requests across leaf nodes to reduce latency, though overhead and straggler effects limit excessive parallelization; reliability is improved by replicating shards. Finally, the passage introduces function-as-a-service (FaaS) or serverless computing for event-driven, ephemeral workloads.

Florida State University President John Thrasher appointed a 15-member committee, chaired by Renisha Gibbs and the chief diversity officer, to review campus policies on building names, markers, and statues. The panel was formed amid national debates over Confederate symbols and will seek community input on naming criteria and recommendations. The committee meets next week and will hold public meetings, following calls by the campus chapter of Students for a Democratic Society to remove the statue of Francis Eppes.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU is an 8th-generation data center accelerator based on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture (GA100) fabricated on TSMC’s 7nm process. Designed for AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads, it features third-generation Tensor Cores that support TF32, BF16, FP64, INT8, and other data types, delivering dense FP16/FP32 mixed-precision performance 2.5× that of the Tesla V100, and up to 5× with Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity; TF32 operations run 10× faster than V100 FP32 (20× with sparsity), while FP64 performance is 2.5× higher. The GPU includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/s of bandwidth and a 40 MB L2 cache. Its Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) capability securely partitions a single A100 into up to seven isolated GPU instances for multi-tenant cloud environments. Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/s of multi-GPU bandwidth, and CUDA 11 adds asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, task graph acceleration, and L2 cache residency controls. The A100 powers systems such as the DGX A100 and scales from workstations to supercomputers.

A government shutdown has left essential federal aviation employees, including air traffic controllers and TSA agents, working without pay, increasing workplace stress and reducing efficiency. While workers believe air travel remains safe, they report that furloughs of roughly 11,300 FAA colleagues and halted projects are straining operations and will likely cause more delays and cancellations. Employees describe anxiety over missing paychecks and fear that officials may use the shutdown to execute mass firings or weaken unions. The FAA states it will not compromise safety and that critical positions are exempt from reductions, while Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy threatened to fire workers who do not report. Unions disavow coordinated sick-outs but note some workers may be unable to commute without pay.

The 23rd BMO Okanagan Marathon in Kelowna expects nearly 3,000 participants. Events include a Boston-qualifying marathon, half marathon, 10K, newly timed 5K, and kids’ 1K fun run along Okanagan Lake. Saturday features a 3K friendship run, the 5K, and kids’ activities; Sunday holds the marathon, half marathon, and 10K. The event supports the Sunshine Foundation of Canada. Walk-up registration and race package pickup are available at City Park.

Truman issued December 1945 statements on China, a Department of National Defense, and displaced persons immigration. State Department leadership changed in 1945: Edward R. Stettinius, Jr. resigned June 27; James F. Byrnes was commissioned July 2. Joseph C. Grew resigned August 16; Dean G. Acheson was commissioned the same day. Patrick J. Hurley resigned November 27; General George C. Marshall was appointed personal envoy to China. Former Secretary Cordell Hull received the Nobel Peace Prize December 10. Executive Order 9608 (August 31) transferred international information functions from the Office of War Information and Office of Inter-American Affairs to the Department. Executive Order 9621 (September 20) transferred the Research and Analysis Branch and Presentation Branch of the Office of Strategic Services to the Department, directing it to lead development of a coordinated foreign intelligence program.

The passage describes robotic and navigation-assisted surgical systems, tool assemblies, and methods for spinal procedures, particularly pedicle screw and tap marker placement. It identifies challenges with manual K-wire placement, incompatible robotic interfaces, multiple instrument changes, and navigation errors caused by relative vertebral movement during discectomy and cage placement. Disclosed systems include a robotic manipulator with interchangeable drive couplers that adapt various working tools—such as scalpels, drills, burs, dilators, and tap inserters—to a common input device without requiring its decoupling. An elongate sleeve retracts soft tissue to form a working channel and includes a distal movable feature that remains closed during advancement to prevent tissue ingress and opens upon tool passage; it may also feature bone-penetrating spikes for fixation. Methods involve controlling a manipulator to position and advance a screw and coaxial sleeve along a planned insertion trajectory through soft tissue, then advancing the screw into bone relative to the sleeve. To address navigation drift, a tracking device with optical markers and a ratcheting mechanism can be removably attached to a working tool or tap marker secured in bone, enabling relocalization of the vertebra. A navigation feature on the tool permits positional verification with a trackable digitizing probe.

Bemidji (14-6) beat Thief River Falls (9-12) 77-45 with four players in double figures, Caden Rolfes (18) and Linaes Whiting (17). Peterson praised the effort, noting the 32-point win improved on a 56-51 win three weeks ago. Bemidji plays Feb. 18 at Fergus Falls against Section 8AAA's top team.

Socket 940 base and cover are LCP (94 V-0 UL); base is black, cover natural or ivory. Cover thickness ≤1.17 mm; flatness <0.25 mm after reflow and testing. A removable overlay facilitates vacuum pick-and-place without outgassing or residue. Molded markings: "SOCKET 940," directional indicators, A01 triangle, UL symbol. Lot traceability marked. Contacts: high-strength copper alloy, 1.27 µm nickel, 0.76 µm gold plating. SMT solder balls: 0.76 mm tin/lead (63/37 ±5%) on 0.64 mm pads; solder barrier required; 0.20 mm co-planarity. Stainless steel lever for toolless actuation; open insertion/extraction <2 kgf, closed extraction ≥0.013 kgf/pin, actuation <3.6 kgf. Pin displacement <1.0 mm. Socket must survive 50 cycles with no visual defects. Electrical specs: 1.5 A/contact, <30°C rise; LLCR <25 mΩ; inductance <4 nH and 3 nH ±10%; capacitance <1 pF; differential impedance 100 Ω ±10%; propagation delay skew <10 ps + 3 ps; crosstalk measured; 650 Vac dielectric; 1000 MΩ insulation.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K on January 27, 2022, disclosing under Item 2.02 the issuance of a press release reporting financial results for the first fiscal quarter ended December 25, 2021. The press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1. The report was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. The passage reports a qualitative case study of 20 Turkish teachers in Hazro, Diyarbakır, regarding distance education during the COVID-19 pandemic. While 45% of teachers believed education progressed, 70% found distance education insufficiently efficient, and none considered it fully efficient. Target behaviors and achievements were partially achieved, primarily due to students lacking technological materials and internet infrastructure. Key problems included student equipment shortages, parental difficulties managing multiple school-age children, infrastructure deficiencies, and student absenteeism. For Turkish lessons, teachers identified needs including reading books and dictionaries (35%), technological materials (25%), both (20%), and practice activities (20%). Phones (65%) and WhatsApp were the most used communication tools and applications, followed by Zoom and EBA. Teachers emphasized qualifications such as subject knowledge, technological competency, communication skills, and activity-oriented instruction. Suggestions included resolving infrastructure problems, providing materials and internet access, updating EBA content, implementing hybrid education models, offering professional development, and rearranging post-pandemic target behaviors.

Diana Beresford-Kroeger and her husband Christian own 160 acres near Merrickville, where they built a home and arboretum called Carrigliath beginning in the 1970s. Born in Ireland, Beresford-Kroeger lost her family at age 11 and was raised by guardians who taught her nature and Irish traditions. She earned degrees in botany, medical biochemistry, and experimental surgery from University College Cork, Carleton University, and the University of Ottawa. The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, powered by the NVIDIA Ampere architecture-based GA100 GPU fabricated on TSMC’s 7nm process, is designed to accelerate AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads in cloud data centers. It features 108 Streaming Multiprocessors with 6912 FP32 CUDA cores and 432 third-generation Tensor Cores supporting FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary data types. A100 introduces Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity, which doubles Tensor Core throughput for deep learning by skipping zero values in a 2:4 sparse pattern. Compared to the NVIDIA Tesla V100, A100 delivers up to 10x faster TF32 performance (20x with sparsity), 2.5x faster FP16/FP32 mixed-precision (5x with sparsity), 2.5x faster FP64, and up to 20x faster sparse INT8 inference.

The GPU includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth and a 40 MB L2 cache with residency controls and Compute Data Compression. Its Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology securely partitions the GPU into up to seven isolated GPU Instances for multi-tenant environments. Other features include third-generation NVLink providing 600 GB/sec total bandwidth, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, asynchronous copy and barrier instructions, Task Graph acceleration, and improved error/fault detection, isolation, and containment. The NVIDIA DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs with NVSwitch and Mellanox networking, delivering 5 PFLOPS of AI performance for scalable infrastructure.

The lecture explains binary detection by simplifying the communication system to a single bit transmission observed as a scalar value corrupted by Gaussian noise, emphasizing that solving such simplified "toy" problems first provides the theoretical foundation for practical engineering. It defines Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) detection, where the receiver minimizes error probability by comparing the likelihood ratio to a threshold based on a priori probabilities. For antipodal signaling in Gaussian noise, the log-likelihood ratio reduces the decision to comparing the observation against a threshold, with error probability determined by the Q-function of the signal-to-noise ratio. The framework extends to vector signals, where forming the inner product—equivalently using a matched filter—yields a sufficient statistic that projects the problem onto one dimension, preserving the same scalar error probability analysis.

The NVIDIA Ampere GA102 GPU is fabricated on Samsung’s 8nm process with 28.3 billion transistors and a 628.4 mm² die. Its full configuration includes 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, and 336 third-generation Tensor Cores across seven Graphics Processing Clusters, 42 Texture Processing Clusters, and 84 Streaming Multiprocessors. The GA10x SM doubles peak FP32 processing over Turing by enabling FP32 operations on both datapaths, and increases combined L1 data cache and shared memory capacity by 33 percent. Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection throughput, support concurrent ray tracing with graphics or compute workloads, and add hardware-accelerated ray-traced motion blur. Third-generation Tensor Cores introduce fine-grained structured sparsity for up to 2x throughput, TF32 and BF16 precision modes, and accelerate AI features including DLSS up to 8K. The architecture supports GDDR6X memory up to 19.5 Gbps using PAM4 signaling for up to 936 GB/s bandwidth, as well as GDDR6. It utilizes PCIe Gen 4 and third-generation NVLink providing 112.5 GB/s total bandwidth between two GPUs. RTX IO enables GPU-based loading and decompression via Microsoft DirectStorage, reducing CPU utilization. The RTX A6000 and A40 professional GPUs include 48 GB of GDDR6 scalable to 96 GB via NVLink; the A40 offers up to 2x FP32, 2x ray-tracing, and 5x (10x with sparsity) AI throughput compared to the Quadro RTX 6000. Additional features include 112 ROPs integrated into GPCs, fifth-generation NVDEC with AV1 hardware decode, seventh-generation NVENC, HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC supporting 8K60 and 4K120, and Error Detection and Replay (EDR) for GDDR6X memory overclocking.

The passage discloses systems and methods for plasma processing substrates to create arbitrarily-shaped ion energy distribution functions (IEDF) using shaped-pulse bias. A shaped-pulse bias waveform—comprising a positive jump, a negative jump (V_OUT), and a negative voltage ramp that compensates for ion current—maintains a nearly constant sheath voltage for approximately 90% of each cycle, producing a mono-energetic IEDF. To achieve arbitrary IEDF shapes, embodiments modulate the amplitude of the negative voltage jump and resulting sheath voltage, using a predetermined relative number of pulses or bursts at each amplitude to determine the relative ion fraction at the corresponding energy. In other embodiments, the negative voltage ramp overcompensates for ion current, causing the substrate voltage to increase during the compensation phase and yielding a wider, double-peaked IEDF; or it undercompensates, causing the substrate voltage to decrease and yielding a wider, single-peaked IEDF. A substrate processing system includes a bias supply with a processor and memory to control these waveforms applied to a power electrode.

The Princeton Offense is an unstructured, motion-based basketball style popularized by Pete Carril that relies on constant movement, defensive reads, and counter actions rather than set plays, with the back door cut as its signature option. All five players must possess outside shooting, passing, driving ability, court savvy, unselfishness, and superior conditioning, while coaches must adhere to an "All or None" commitment to the system.

The offense emphasizes precise 12- to 15-foot spacing to spread defenses and prevent help. It operates through adaptable entries—such as off-guard rubs, mid screens, and dribble clears—flowing into exchanges and down screens that drive continuous ball movement, followed by post actions including high-post basket cuts and flash back doors. If no shot emerges, it cycles back into entries.

Tempo control and patience are vital, often involving 15 to 20 passes per possession to minimize opponent opportunities. Dribble penetration is used sparingly to maintain spacing and counter overplays. Post-ups frequently serve to collapse defenses for kick-out passes to outside shooters. The offense also includes quick-hitting specials for late shot-clock situations and press breaks to exploit extended defenses.

Psychologically, the system creates pressure by reducing possessions, demoralizing opponents with easy back-cut baskets, exposing weak defenders, and forcing rushed shots and turnovers. Its unpredictability makes it difficult to scout, and its stability ensures steady performance regardless of shooting fluctuations.

The lecture reviews Wald’s identity and sequential hypothesis testing, then introduces martingales and Jensen’s Inequality. Wald’s identity states that for a random walk stopped at a threshold-crossing time J, the moment-generating-function equality that holds for a fixed number of steps also holds for the stopping time J. From this, Wald’s equality follows by differentiation at r = 0, and a second derivative yields a relation between the expected value of the stopped sum squared and the expected stopping time, which is useful for zero-mean random walks. The professor corrects a prior interchange of hypothesis 0 and hypothesis 1 in the slides. In sequential hypothesis testing, the likelihood ratio is a sufficient statistic and its logarithm forms a random walk; under hypothesis 1, the key parameter r* equals 1. Fixed-n tests rely on Chernoff bounds, whereas sequential tests use upper and lower thresholds, trading error probability under one hypothesis for the expected number of observations under the other. Martingales are defined as sequences where the conditional expectation of the next term given all previous terms equals the current term. Examples include zero-mean random walks, sums of variables with zero conditional mean, and products of independent unit-mean variables. A “double or nothing” product martingale illustrates that the limit of expectations need not equal the expectation of the limit. Submartingales and supermartingales are defined using inequalities. Finally, Jensen’s Inequality states that for a convex function H, H of the expected value of Z is less than or equal to the expected value of H of Z.

In Bertie Secor, Administrator v. James E. Siver et al., the Iowa Supreme Court affirmed the district court’s dismissal of the plaintiffs’ petition to recover on a foreign judgment and its ruling in favor of the defendants on their fraud counterclaim. The plaintiffs had sought to enjoin the defendants from conveying property to their sons to avoid the judgment. The defendants counterclaimed that the deceased John S. Secor had fraudulently induced them into a land exchange that left them with a deficiency judgment and worthless property.

The court held that an objection to a witness’s competency must specifically state the grounds; a general objection that a witness is “incompetent and unqualified” is insufficient. It also held that an objection to testimony about “personal transactions” with a deceased does not necessarily cover “personal communications,” as the terms are distinct. Applying these rules, the majority found James E. Siver and Elizabeth Siver competent to testify about the property’s description, quality, value, their reliance on Secor’s representations, the condition of the property received, and certain conversations, and concluded that admissible evidence supported the trial court’s decree for the defendants. The court further held that costs taxed against an administrator in an official capacity would not be retaxed to the administrator in an individual capacity merely because the action was allegedly brought officiously.

Justices Ladd, Salinger, and Stevens dissented, arguing that the objection was sufficient because a consummated “transaction” necessarily includes the communications and negotiations leading to it, and that the testimony concerned continuous conversations in which both spouses participated, rendering the witnesses incompetent under the statute.

The NPD Group identified five trends shaping Britain's £57 billion foodservice industry in 2018: (1) smartphone click & collect to reduce wait times, increase sales and profits, and improve customer data, requiring operational changes and staff training; (2) investing in staff hiring, training, and retention to foster emotional connections, loyalty, and profits; (3) tiered, personalized VIP loyalty schemes replacing traditional discounts to target valuable customers; (4) ensuring product quality, service, support, and marketing deliver on brand promises to avoid social media complaints; and (5) using staff and customer data to offer authentic, personalized recommendations. Foodservice Director Cyril Lavenant stated that success requires innovation and effective responses to these opportunities.

Socket 940 specifications cover markings, materials, mechanical operation, durability, visual inspection, and electrical performance. Markings include the socket identifier, directional indicators, orientation symbol, UL symbol, and lot traceability number on the cover. Contacts use high-strength copper alloy plated with nickel and gold and must be lubricant-free; tin/lead solder balls (0.76 mm diameter) mount the socket to the PCB with a 0.20 mm co-planarity requirement and a solder barrier. A stainless steel lever enables toolless actuation; insertion/extraction forces are limited, and pin displacement must be under 1.0 mm. The socket must endure 50 cycles and pass visual inspections for defects. Electrical requirements include a 1.5 A current rating, contact resistance under 25 mΩ, inductance and capacitance limits, 100 Ω ±10% differential impedance, propagation skew under 10 ps, minimum 650 Vac dielectric withstanding voltage, and minimum 1000 MΩ insulation resistance.

Volunteers in southern New South Wales and the ACT are conducting late winter platypus surveys to gather baseline data on the near-threatened species. Cooma Waterwatch coordinator Antia Brademann said it was the fourth year surveying the Upper Murrumbidgee River, where numbers appear stable, though none were sighted on this occasion. Platypus populations have declined across eastern Australia due to habitat change, reduced river flows, and waste. Citizen science provides valuable monitoring. Brademann encourages year-round sightings reports and advises scanning waterways in early morning or late evening during August and September for ripples, bubbles, and a rounded back.

Adding four live ants to warmed cow’s milk and burying the jar in an ant mound overnight is a traditional yogurt-making method once popular in Bulgaria and Turkey. A new study shows that bacteria living on ants, along with ant-derived formic acid and enzymes, acidify and thicken the milk. Frozen or dehydrated ants are less effective because their microbes do not ferment milk as well. Researchers caution that live ants can carry parasites capable of causing liver or gastrointestinal disease and do not recommend attempting this at home.

This command moves SNP guest pages within physical address space as a faster PAGE_MOVE alternative. It requires 2M pages to be contiguous and aligned, prohibits DMA and CPU access, and mandates source pages be Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid and destinations be Pre-Migration; after migration, destinations take the source state and sources return to Pre-Migration. Firmware validates platform state, addresses, and RMP access; invalidates TLBs; copies data; and updates RMPs. A separate command marks sequence completion. Command and list errors return status codes, ring buffer errors use PM_STATUS, and hardware errors use command status or MCA. Up to 128 pages per batch may become unrecoverable on hardware errors, potentially requiring reboot after saving state.

Action on Smoking and Health (ASH) advocates for zero tobacco deaths, asserting that smokers are victims of an industry that markets an addictive, deadly product. Citing the Danish Institute for Human Rights and the Cape Town Declaration on Human Rights and a Tobacco-Free World—endorsed by over 150 organizations—ASH argues that tobacco production violates the human right to health and calls for bold action to achieve a tobacco-free world.

Jara, previously deputy superintendent of Orange County Public Schools and former superintendent at Monroe County Public Schools in Florida, was chosen from six finalists including internal candidate Dr. Mike Barton. The article discusses the application of gamification in academic education at the University of Wrocław's Institute of Pedagogy, presenting four projects. Gamification is defined as applying game mechanics to increase motivation and modify behavior, offering an alternative to traditional teaching in a knowledge-based society.

The first project, "Kulturalny Wrocław," used a location-based game for cultural education in which students located sites, solved riddles, and completed crosswords outdoors. Participants rated it highly for socialization and experiential learning, and it was later incorporated into the curriculum with minimal cost.

The second project was a five-day gamified career management seminar featuring a science-fiction plot, point systems, and badges. Though highly effective in increasing engagement and exam results, instructors noted it required substantial preparation, making it suitable primarily for repeated or externally funded courses.

The third project, "Zostań przedsiębiorcą," employed a location-based game to diagnose entrepreneurship competences. Students praised its social and dynamic nature and soft-skills development, though they noted drawbacks including weather dependence and ambivalence toward competition.

The fourth project used a LARP game, "Spell of the Black Magic Master," to develop soft skills through role-play. While educational goals were met, students without prior role-playing experience reported lower satisfaction due to the game's complexity.

The article concludes that simple location-based games with clear rules integrate well into academic curricula, while longer, complex games better serve as supplementary, funded programs. Successful implementation requires aligning game design with students' prior experience, the subject matter, available time, and organizational resources, often necessitating preparatory socialization activities.
