He noted the team's depth throughout the playoffs, with various players stepping up, and said Marty and the team came through huge. He was inspired by a veteran leader whose locker room presence was valuable, and he described the tense, exciting final moments on the bench as the clock ran down.

The New Jersey Supreme Court affirmed denials of costs and counsel fees in two consolidated cases under N.J.S. 2A:15-53 of the Anti-Injunction Act. In the arbitration case, the court held that the employer’s suit—seeking a declaratory judgment on the arbitrability of a discharged employee’s grievance and an ancillary stay of arbitration—did not fall within the Act’s scope because it was not a suit to enjoin unlawful coercive labor activity. In the strike case, where the employer sought an injunction against illegal picketing, the Appellate Division had reversed the interlocutory injunction solely for procedural deficiencies and not on the merits, finding a substantive basis for injunctive relief existed. The court held that because the suit was not “wrongfully brought,” the employer was entitled to relief on the merits, and the procedural errors were not the basis of the defense, mandatory costs and counsel fees were not warranted under the statute’s purpose of protecting labor from meritless suits. The court granted leave for appellants to reapply for statutory trial court costs if desired and awarded costs to the respondent in the arbitration case only.

The SanDisk Sansa Fuze manual describes a portable digital audio/video player with a 1.9" color screen, FM tuner, built-in microphone, microSDHC card slot, and non-replaceable rechargeable battery providing up to 24 hours of audio or 5 hours of video playback. It supports MP3, WMA, WAV, secure WMA, Audible, podcasts, MPEG4 video, and JPEG photos, with additional video and photo formats supported via the Sansa Media Converter software.

Controls include a power switch for on, off, and reset functions; a Hold/Lock switch that disables all buttons when engaged; and a thumbwheel for menu navigation and volume adjustment. The player charges via USB, AC, or car adapter, though playback is unavailable during USB charging. It connects to computers via USB 2.0 for drag-and-drop file transfers, Windows Media Player synchronization, firmware updates, or formatting, which erases all content.

Users can play music with repeat, shuffle, equalizer, and Go List options; watch videos with bookmarks, ratings, and brightness adjustment; and view photo slideshows with configurable duration, looping, shuffle, and background music. The FM radio supports live broadcast listening, up to 30 presets, auto-scanning, station recording, and region and mode settings. The built-in microphone allows voice recording. The manual states the product is intended solely for home and personal use and warns against unauthorized commercial copying of copyrighted material.
An order sustaining a demurrer to an amended petition but making no disposition of the action is not final, and the appeal was dismissed.

Meighan Wark of Huron County presented to Central Huron Council a proposal to renovate Clinton Library to achieve Ontario Public Library accreditation and improve services. In 2015, 11 county branches received accreditation, but Clinton failed due to accessibility issues and inadequate square footage. Under the county-municipality partnership, the county provides staff, materials, and services while the municipality maintains the building. Wark explained that standards require specific square footage based on population, accessible layouts, and flexible spaces for technology and circulation. The next steps involve both parties agreeing on required components and space needs before engaging an architect for draft drawings to present to council and the community. Wark noted provincial funding is possible but requires a shovel-ready project, and the county would invest in the interior if the municipality commits to building improvements. Mayor Jim Ginn and council will continue discussions.

Charlie Alliston, 18, knocked down and killed Kim Briggs, 44, on Old Street in east London while riding a fixed-wheel "Planet X" track bike with no front brake at about 20mph. Mrs Briggs, a mother of two, was crossing the road on her lunch break on February 12 and died a week later from catastrophic injuries including two skull fractures and bleeding on the brain. At the Old Bailey, prosecutor Duncan Penny QC stated that riding such a bike without a front brake on public roads is unlawful, and crash reconstructions showed a front brake would have enabled Alliston to stop in time. Alliston had posted online comments blaming Mrs Briggs, claiming she stepped into the road while looking at her phone and ignored his warnings. He had reportedly removed the front brake from a previous bike and bought the Planet X bike a month before the collision. He denies manslaughter and causing bodily harm by wanton or furious driving.

Elijah Brown scored 27 points, including 17 of New Mexico’s final 19, to lead the Lobos to a 78-73 victory over Boise State. New Mexico (16-10, 9-5 Mountain West) seized control with a late first-half 11-0 run and withstood a late rally. Chandler Hutchison had a career-high 31 points for Boise State (16-8, 9-4), which never led. The win leaves New Mexico one game behind Boise State, Colorado State and Nevada in the conference standings. New Mexico plays at Fresno State next, while Boise State hosts Wyoming.

The NVIDIA Turing architecture introduces a new Streaming Multiprocessor design with 64 FP32 and 64 INT32 cores per SM, enabling concurrent floating-point and integer execution, plus eight mixed-precision Tensor Cores and one RT Core per SM. Each SM is partitioned into four processing blocks with a new L0 instruction cache and a 96 KB configurable L1 data cache/shared memory. Turing achieves roughly 50% better delivered performance per CUDA core than Pascal. It is the first GPU architecture to utilize GDDR6 memory, features larger L2 caches, and improves lossless compression, increasing effective memory bandwidth by about 50% over Pascal. The display engine supports 8K resolutions, HDR, and VirtualLink/USB-C for VR, while the enhanced video engine adds new decode formats and improved encoding quality.

Turing Tensor Cores support FP16, INT8, and INT4 precision, accelerating deep learning inference and training. The Tesla T4 data center GPU leverages these to provide up to 40× higher inference performance and over 50× the energy efficiency of CPU-based servers. NVIDIA NGX uses Tensor Cores for AI-driven graphics features, including Deep Learning Super Sampling (DLSS), which infers high-quality images from lower-resolution inputs to improve performance; other NGX capabilities include AI InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez.

Dedicated RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection, enabling real-time ray tracing on a single GPU and making Turing approximately 10× faster at ray tracing than Pascal. A hybrid rendering model combines rasterization with ray-traced shadows, reflections, and ambient occlusion. Additional features include Mesh Shading to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks, Variable Rate Shading to dynamically adjust per-region shading rates, Texture Space Shading to decouple shading from screen-space sampling, and Multi-View Rendering to process multiple viewpoints in one pass. Turing TU102 and TU104 use NVLink for multi-GPU data transfers, while TU106 does not support NVLink or SLI. The architecture also introduces RTX-OPS, a workload-based metric for quantifying hybrid rendering performance.

This retrospective cohort study using the HCUP-NIS database (2017–2019) examined whether perinatal mood disorders are associated with peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) and cardiac events in over 2.2 million pregnant and postpartum hospitalizations. Among the cohort, 7.4% had a mood disorder diagnosis. Patients with mood disorders had higher unadjusted rates of PPCM (0.12% versus 0.05%) and composite adverse cardiac events (0.36% versus 0.14%). After multivariable adjustment for demographic and clinical confounders, mood disorders remained independently associated with PPCM (adjusted odds ratio 1.36, 95% CI 1.03–1.80), the composite cardiac outcome (aOR 1.57, 95% CI 1.37–1.81), and pulmonary edema (aOR 1.62, 95% CI 1.39–1.89). Maternal death was not significantly associated with mood disorders. The authors conclude that perinatal mood disorders are associated with increased rates of PPCM and adverse cardiac events, representing a modifiable risk factor with implications for mental health care and prevention during pregnancy and postpartum. Limitations include reliance on ICD-10 codes and inpatient data without post-discharge outcomes.

In card identification mode, the host resets cards, validates voltage, and requests RCA via CMD line only. CMD0 sets cards to Idle State with default RCA=0x0000; UHS-II retains its Device ID. CMD8 verifies interface operating condition via the VHS field and check pattern; cards echo valid conditions or remain idle. CMD8 is mandatory before ACMD41 for SDHC/SDXC cards and indicates host support for Physical Layer Version 2.00 or later.

Modern defensive multiplicity against spread offenses has made run fits a vital, often overlooked focus. Run fits are categorized by post-snap front spacing and box count. Even spacing leaves the B gap open, while odd spacing leaves the C gaps open. The terms 7, 8, and 9 man spacing refer to defenders in the box versus 12/21 personnel. Seven-man spacing is a "light box" with one fewer defender, often using middle-of-the-field-open coverage and tools like two-gapping, stunts, "stack-track-fallback" versus zone, and "spill-overlap" versus gap schemes. Eight-man spacing is "gapped-out" with equal numbers, typically in middle-of-the-field-closed coverage and one-gap fits, using "indicator fitting" versus zone and "lever-spill-lever" versus power. Nine-man spacing is "maxed out" with an extra defender, often in Cover 0/blitz fits for aggressive gap play. Coaches must translate these varied concepts into executable schemes tailored to their talent and philosophy, including within 3-4 defenses.

A University of Rochester study in Scientific Reports found that low doses of alcohol improved glymphatic function in mice, enhancing brain waste clearance including proteins linked to Alzheimer’s disease. Mice consuming approximately 2.5 drinks daily (0.5g/kg) showed reduced brain inflammation and more efficient cerebral spinal fluid movement compared to control mice, with identical cognitive and motor performance. Intermediate (1.5g/kg, ~7.9 drinks) and high (4g/kg, ~21 drinks) doses impaired glymphatic function and increased inflammation, with high doses also impairing cognitive and motor skills; intermediate dose suppression reversed 24 hours after cessation. Researchers stated the results support a J-shaped model, where low alcohol doses benefit brain health while excessive intake is detrimental.

Andrew Lo discusses financial market conditions, noting the stock market is down while short-term rates are up, and states that the Fed is working to maintain liquid markets amid significant fear. An audience member compares the situation to Argentina’s past crisis and suggests surviving creates opportunities. Lo links this to psychological biases that paralyze decision-making under fear and proposes a transparent pricing platform for complex securities. He argues against suspending mark-to-market accounting, calling it a dangerous idea. Lo defines forward contracts as customized, over-the-counter agreements to buy or sell assets at a future date for a price set today; he notes they have zero initial value, carry counterparty risk, and are illiquid. He discusses hedging strategies and debates among companies about hedging outputs versus inputs. He then explains futures contracts as standardized, exchange-traded instruments that are marked to market daily and use a clearing corporation to reduce counterparty risk. He provides an example of NYMEX crude oil futures and explains initial and maintenance margin requirements, concluding that while some industries prefer forwards for customization, futures offer greater liquidity and safety.

The lecture explains stimulated light forces using the dressed atom picture, in which the atom-laser interaction is diagonalized before spontaneous emission is introduced. In the strong Rabi limit, the Optical Bloch Equations decouple into separate equations for populations and coherences in the dressed-state basis. Atoms in the two dressed states experience opposite dipole forces, so the net force depends on population imbalance: red-detuned light produces an attractive force, while blue-detuned light is repulsive. On resonance, the forces average to zero but fluctuations cause heating. When an atom moves through a laser field, a time lag in adjusting its dressed-state population creates a friction force, leading to blue-detuned cooling known as blue molasses or Sisyphus cooling. In a blue-detuned standing wave, atoms tend to emit photons at potential maxima and drop to minima, repeatedly climbing hills and losing kinetic energy. Heating arises from force fluctuations as atoms switch dressed levels. In the perturbative limit of large detuning, the friction and momentum diffusion coefficients are derived; the minimum achievable temperature is limited by the lattice depth, making it impossible to localize two-level atoms in a standing wave via laser cooling alone. The dipole potential is also discussed in terms of induced dipoles and the analogous macroscopic physics of optical tweezers. The lecture concludes with an outlook on magnetic trapping, evaporative cooling, Bose gases, Fermi gases, and quantum logic with ions.

The TPS7H500x-SP series are radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters up to 2 MHz, designed for use with external gate drivers. They support buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies.

Oscillator modes include internal (RT populated), external synchronization (RT floating with a 200 kHz–4 MHz clock at twice the desired switching frequency applied to SYNC), and primary-secondary (primary RT populated outputs a clock to a secondary device with RT floating), which produces a 90° or 270° phase shift. In external synchronization mode, the applied clock must be present before OUTA and OUTB become active.

Primary switching outputs (OUTA/OUTB) and synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA/SRB) provide roughly 150 mA peak current. OUTB and SRB are only available on the TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP and are active only when the duty cycle limit is set to 50% by connecting DCL to AVSS. Configurable duty cycle limits are 100% (DCL to VLDO), 75% (floating), or 50% (AVSS). SRA and SRB are disabled during soft-start until the SS pin voltage exceeds 1 V.

Dead time is programmable via resistors from the PS and SP pins to AVSS (10 kΩ–300 kΩ) on the TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5002-SP, while the TPS7H5003-SP has a fixed 50 ns typical dead time. Leading edge blank time is programmable via a resistor from the LEB pin to AVSS (10 kΩ–300 kΩ) for all devices except the TPS7H5003-SP, which has a fixed 50 ns blank time. Pulse skipping occurs when the COMP pin voltage is below 0.3 V at the clock rising edge and the previous duty cycle was less than 25%.

Current is sensed at the CS_ILIM pin; the sensed peak current is compared to COMP/2 with a 150 mV offset. The current limit threshold is 1.05 V, triggering cycle-by-cycle limiting followed by hiccup mode after a delay set by the HICC pin capacitor (minimum 3.3 nF recommended). The FAULT pin triggers shutdown if its voltage exceeds 0.6 V for longer than 0.4–1.4 µs, followed by a delay of approximately 15 switching cycles and a soft-start restart. Slope compensation is set via the RSC pin resistor. Frequency compensation uses a transconductance error amplifier with Type 2A or 2B networks. Thermal shutdown occurs at 175°C typical, with restart at 160°C.

The controllers operate from a 4 V to 14 V supply with a minimum 0.1 µF bypass capacitor from VIN to AVSS. Layout guidelines require separating analog ground (AVSS) from power ground at a single point, minimizing high di/dt and dv/dt loops, keeping bypass and compensation components close to the controller, routing noisy output and SYNC traces away from sensitive pins (VSENSE, COMP, CS_ILIM, HICC), and connecting the CFP package backside metalization to the AVSS plane with multiple vias.

North Carolina child care academies in at least 11 counties fast-track early childhood educators into classrooms in two to six weeks with little to no cost, addressing staffing shortages affecting 60% of licensed providers. Two models exist: a classroom-ready model requiring at least 20 hours and qualifying graduates to work in licensed facilities, and a teaching credential model that adds EDU 119 curriculum, awarding transferable continuing education credit (EDU 3119) that qualifies graduates as lead teachers. Programs are typically collaborations among Smart Start partnerships, community colleges, and Child Care Resource and Referral organizations. A $1.476 million state pilot to expand academies passed the House but was not included in the final budget; however, the Division of Child Development and Early Education is offering up to $50,000 grants for up to 10 institutions to run academies between October 2025 and July 2026. Current programs operate in counties including Buncombe, Cabarrus, Catawba, Davidson, Davie, Durham, Johnston, McDowell, Rowan, Stanly, and Wayne, funded by various grants such as the Camber Foundation, Dogwood Health Trust, and Duke Community Affairs.

Lecture 9 covers trajectory optimization through policy search, focusing on open-loop control policies parameterized by a vector alpha. The instructor introduces shooting methods, which simulate the system forward and adjust parameters to optimize a cost or reach a target. Gradients for these methods can be computed via the adjoint method—simulating forward, then backward through time—or via real-time recurrent learning (RTRL), which computes gradients in a single forward pass by maintaining a sensitivity matrix, trading memory for the absence of a backward pass. Sequential quadratic programming tools like SNOPT are recommended over simple gradient descent because they do not require tuning a learning rate, converge faster, and handle constraints easily. The lecture then presents direct collocation (DIRCOL), which parameterizes both states and controls and enforces system dynamics through explicit constraints rather than simulation. This formulation allows cost evaluation without explicit simulation and can help escape local minima depending on initialization. Demonstrations include pendulum and acrobot swing-up. The instructor notes that these methods find local optima, which are often acceptable in practice if the goal is achieved. The next lecture will cover stabilizing these trajectories using LQR methods.

A Warren County, Iowa family has been without clean water for two months after a DOT highway project affected their 68-year-old well, despite promises not to dig near it. The family of four hauls water daily for basic needs. After getting nowhere with officials, Mark Paschell and a contractor dug a 300-yard trench to connect to rural water. This study reports on 377 percutaneous tracheostomies performed between March 2020 and March 2022 at Jaber Al Ahmad Al Sabah Hospital in Kuwait on intubated, mechanically ventilated COVID-19 ICU patients, representing the largest reported single-center series. The bedside percutaneous technique was preferred over open tracheostomy after a minimum of seven days of intubation to reduce staff exposure and viral cross-contamination. The mean patient age was 56.2 years, 59% were male, and common comorbidities included diabetes mellitus (50%) and hypertension (48%); 29% were on ECMO and 23% on dialysis. Complications occurred in 23% of cases, with minor bleeding being the most common at 14%; other complications included nine tracheo-esophageal fistulae (2%) and one tracheo-innominate fistula (0.2%). Following tracheostomy, 54% of patients were weaned from sedation and 41% from mechanical ventilation. The overall mortality rate was 63%, with all deaths attributed to COVID-19 complications rather than the procedure. The authors conclude that percutaneous tracheostomy can be safely performed in COVID-19 patients and should ideally be done as soon as possible after the seventh day of intubation, though optimal timing remains debated. Study limitations include the absence of an open tracheostomy comparison arm and lack of long-term follow-up data on speech, swallowing, or tracheostomy status after discharge.

Backtests using Yahoo! Finance data from 2014 indicate a positive end-of-month effect in Bitcoin usable as a turn-of-the-month strategy. Optimizing entry and exit points around month-end yielded an average gain of 3.3% per trade, a 41.8% CAGR, and a 25% max drawdown with 16% market exposure. While somewhat curve-fitted, turn-of-the-month returns exceed random period returns. Adjusting entry timing and adding variables reduces drawdowns and smooths the equity curve, though CAGR drops. Recent performance was flat during Bitcoin declines. The complete strategy is withheld for potential future use, but free trading strategy resources are available.

Bed Bath & Beyond (BBBY) is a major U.S. home goods retailer that operated 1,541 stores across North America and Mexico as of November 2016, including banners such as buybuy BABY and World Market. Its stock traded near $80 in early 2014 and 2015, then declined to roughly $39 by November 2016; it briefly rallied after the U.S. election but fell following weak Q3 earnings and lost its NASDAQ-100 listing in December 2016.

The company faces challenges including recently issued bonds, stagnating revenue between $11.5 billion and $12 billion, declining gross margins from 42.8% in 2007 to 38.2%, shrinking net income, and competitive pressure from Amazon without a strong structural moat.

Four arguments support a bullish view: BBBY pays a dividend with a low payout ratio and has reduced shares outstanding from 260 million to 150 million since 2010 through aggressive buybacks; it acquired One Kings Lane and PersonalizationMall.com to grow its online business; it is testing a “Beyond+” loyalty program to improve customer retention; and the stock appears undervalued, with an estimated intrinsic value of $54.17 and a suggested entry point of $32.50 using a 40% margin of safety. The author believes the company can achieve single-digit growth and reasonable returns despite macroeconomic sensitivity.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition system. It is reset by a logic 0 on the RESET pin or by writing 1b to the RESET field of address 0x00 in register bank 0, and powered down by a logic 0 on the PWDN pin or by writing 11b to the PD_CH field of address 0xC0 in register bank 1. After reset or power-up, registers return to default values and the device requires an initialization sequence of register writes with a free-running sampling clock applied. Configuration options include analog input range, bandwidth, common-mode voltage, and data interface output lanes. A speed-boost mode allows up to 8MSPS for a user-selected channel pair. The device uses three register banks accessed via SPI; bank 0 is always accessible, while banks 1 and 2 are selected through register 0x03. Register writes require two frames (bank selection, then data), and reads require four frames including read-enable and read-disable steps. Multiple devices can be connected in a daisy-chain topology, where N devices require N × 24 SCLKs per write and specific frame sequences for reads. In ATE applications, the ADS9803 achieves a post-calibration TUE of 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C and offers wide-bandwidth mode settling to 99.95% in 7.5µs. The device uses AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD with no required power-up sequence, and layout recommendations include keeping analog signals isolated from digital lines and placing bypass capacitors close to supply pins.

In three cases decided on June 22, 1995, Yale-New Haven Hospital, Inc. sued Clifford Mitchell and Laureen Wilczynski in New Haven Superior Court to recover payment for medical services. The defendants filed special defenses alleging the hospital violated the Hill-Burton Act and Connecticut’s hospital bed funds statute, and they filed counterclaims under the Connecticut Unfair Trade Practices Act (CUTPA). The hospital moved for summary judgment, arguing that no genuine issue of material fact existed and that the defendants lacked a private right of action under the federal and state statutes. The court denied the motions, holding that indigent patients are intended beneficiaries who may raise noncompliance with the Hill-Burton Act and the hospital bed funds statute as a valid special defense to a collection suit. The court further held that alleged violations of those statutes could form the basis of a CUTPA claim even if no private cause of action exists under them, and that factual issues regarding the counterclaims required trial. The court also rejected the hospital’s argument that the Hill-Burton Act preempts CUTPA.

Alan Oppenheim discusses the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) algorithm for computing the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT). He notes that the FFT is far more efficient than direct DFT computation, which requires roughly N squared complex multiplies and adds, whereas for N equal to a power of 2, the FFT requires computation proportional to N times log base 2 of N. The lecture presents the decimation-in-time form, which recursively decomposes the DFT into smaller DFTs: first into two N/2-point DFTs of even and odd samples, then into N/4-point DFTs, continuing down to 2-point DFTs. The basic operation is the butterfly, where the bottom branch is multiplied by powers of W sub N before combining with the top branch. A key simplification exploits the fact that W sub N to the N/2 equals minus 1, allowing each butterfly to be performed with one multiplication by a power of W sub N followed by an addition and subtraction, reducing multiplications. The resulting flow graph produces sequential output but requires the input in bit-reversed order. Oppenheim mentions that FFT algorithms were a major landmark in digital signal processing, with a form disclosed by Cooley and Tukey in 1965, and that the algorithm is important for spectral analysis and implementing convolution. He indicates the next lecture will cover memory arrangements and modifications.

Szemerédi's graph regularity lemma states that for every epsilon > 0, there exists a constant M depending only on epsilon such that every graph has an epsilon-regular partition into at most M parts, independent of the graph's size. An epsilon-regular pair of vertex sets (X,Y) is defined by the property that for all sufficiently large subsets A of X and B of Y, the edge density between A and B differs from the edge density between X and Y by at most epsilon. An epsilon-regular partition is one in which the sum of products of sizes over all non-epsilon-regular pairs is at most epsilon times the total number of vertex pairs.

The proof uses an energy increment argument. Energy is defined as a weighted mean of squared edge densities between pairs of parts in a partition, and it always lies between 0 and 1. Starting from a trivial partition, if the current partition is not epsilon-regular, one simultaneously refines it using witnessing subsets for each irregular pair. Lemmas show that energy never decreases under refinement and increases by at least epsilon^5 when refining a non-epsilon-regular partition. Because energy is bounded above by 1, the iteration must terminate after at most epsilon^{-5} steps, producing an epsilon-regular partition.

The resulting bound is a tower of exponentials in 1/epsilon, and Gowers proved that such tower-type bounds are necessary. The lemma can be extended to guarantee an equitable partition, where part sizes differ by at most 1, by further refining and rebalancing at each iteration; simply modifying a regular partition at the end does not work because epsilon-regularity is not preserved under arbitrary refinement. The lemma is trivial for sparse graphs but meaningful for dense graphs. The next lecture will cover applications, including Roth's theorem.

Digital piracy, which emerged globally with Napster in 1999, remains resilient despite decades of legal, technical, and educational countermeasures, significantly reducing revenues for content industries. This study investigates how firms can design business models to minimize piracy's negative impact through qualitative case studies of Spotify and Netflix, drawing on archival sources, industry reports, and executive interviews.

The research identifies digital piracy as most attractive in audio and film categories because unlicensed copies are easier to produce, access, and consume than in written or interactive media. Traditional responses focused on pricing, DRM, and enforcement have failed to suppress piracy, suggesting the need for holistic business model innovation.

Applying a framework of four business model elements—customer identification, customer engagement, monetization, and value chain linkages—the authors find that Spotify and Netflix compete by offering subscription streaming services that match piracy's perceived "free" benefit through ad-supported free tiers or trials while outperforming piracy on convenience, quality, and user experience. Their models feature intuitive interfaces, broad multi-device accessibility including offline consumption, extensive content catalogs, consistent streaming quality, social media integration, and proprietary personalized recommendation systems. They also address piracy drivers by reducing geographical restrictions and release windows.

A causal loop analysis shows how free tiers attract users, building a larger userbase that increases bargaining power for licensing agreements, expands the content catalog, and enables community and personalization features. These elements increase willingness to pay, driving subscription revenues that fund further growth, creating a virtuous cycle.

The article concludes that business model innovation centered on consumption experience—rather than price or content protection alone—offers sustainable competitive advantage against piracy. The findings are primarily applicable to digital distribution in music and film but may inform other content sectors, with implications for technology strategy, firm diversification, and network competition.

The paper extends Uustalu’s characterization of monoids in non-indexed containers to indexed containers. Indexed containers, introduced by Altenkirch et al. as a generalization of Abbott et al.’s containers, represent strictly positive types and correspond to generalized polynomials between families of sets. The authors outline the monoidal structure on the category of indexed containers ICI corresponding to composition of their extents, generalize Uustalu’s characterization to account for indexing, and prove that monoids in ICI correspond precisely to monad structures on the associated endofunctors. Examples include the product of indexed container monads, indexed variants of the state and writer monads, and a free monad on Fin yielding well-scoped untyped λ-terms. The development is formalized in Cubical Agda, motivated by its support for functional extensionality. The paper reviews related work on polynomial monads and prior formalizations, describes the paper’s structure, fixes notational conventions, and begins Section 2 by defining indexed containers, their extent functors, morphisms, and the category ICI, noting that the extent functor is full and faithful.

This study examines the relative role of different age groups in propagating four Omicron waves in France between March 1 and December 29, 2022, using a relative risk (RR) statistic calculated from ICU admissions. During the Spring, Summer, and Autumn waves, children aged 10-19 years and 0-9 years showed the highest RR estimates, indicating a disproportionate role in transmission, particularly when schools were open. For the Autumn-Winter wave, the highest RR estimates shifted to adults aged 30-39 years, followed by adults aged 40-49 years and persons over 80 years, a change the authors suggest may relate to built-up immunity in children and younger adults during previous waves. The authors conclude that the leading role in Omicron transmission in France shifted from children and younger adults to adults aged 30-49 years and those over 80 years as time progressed. They recommend increasing booster vaccination coverage for all adults and possibly children to limit community spread, and undertaking further efforts to prevent transmission among elderly individuals, including in Long-Term Care facilities.

The TPS7H500x-SP series comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting topologies such as buck, flyback, forward, push-pull, and full-bridge with switching frequencies from 100 kHz to 2 MHz. Each device generates an internal 1.23-V bandgap reference, divided to 0.613 V for the transconductance error amplifier, which regulates the output set by a resistor divider. A soft-start sequence ramps the SS pin voltage, with synchronous rectifier outputs activating once SS exceeds 1 V. Switching frequency is configurable via an RT resistor, an external SYNC clock, or primary-secondary synchronization. Primary outputs (OUTA/OUTB) and synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA/SRB) provide roughly 150-mA peak current and require external gate drivers. Dead time (PS/SP pins) and leading edge blank time (LEB pin) are resistor-programmable on most variants, while pulse skipping prevents issues during high-frequency operation. Duty cycle limits are set via the DCL pin. Current sensing at CS_ILIM drives PWM generation; exceeding 1.05 V triggers hiccup mode, controlled by a capacitor on HICC. An external FAULT pin above 0.6 V forces shutdown and restart after a delay. Slope compensation is set via RSC, and frequency compensation uses Type 2A or 2B networks. Thermal shutdown occurs at 175°C with restart at 160°C. The document provides a detailed 500-kHz synchronous push-pull design example, including component calculations for the feedback divider, dead time, blanking, soft-start, transformer, GaN FET selection, output filter, current sense, hiccup, compensation, and slope compensation. Layout guidelines recommend minimizing noise coupling, separating analog and power grounds, placing bypass capacitors close to the controller, and routing sensitive traces away from high dv/dt and di/dt nodes.

Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) is an opt-in BIOS feature for firmware updates with optional customer co-signing. The security processor authenticates packages against customer and AMD keys; the customer public key is set during early boot and cannot be updated later. Patches verify system patch levels and firmware versions for applicability, and can update registers, images, or firmware portions. SEV updates auto-commit without rollback, while SNP requires HV-FIXED pages. SFS supplies attestation data but will not modify firmware protected by attestation schemes. Packages verify dependencies for resiliency and are non-persistent across reboots. Commands require 2MB-aligned memory and a customer deployment agent using the TEE mailbox. The ASP verifies signatures, executes validated patches, and returns status. Interfaces provide firmware and patch level information. Packages follow a fam_<family>-<AGESA-Release>-SFS-<n>.pkg naming convention and apply only to matching firmware versions. Updates run parallel to x86 and DMA traffic with minimal performance impact, though SEV/ES VMs may require brief stops for SEV firmware updates.

The UC1825B-SP is a dual-output controller with a sawtooth oscillator whose frequency and maximum duty cycle are set by external RT (recommended 1 kΩ to 100 kΩ) and CT components; controlling DMAX below 70% is not recommended. It has integrated push-pull drivers and, with external components, can support half-bridge, full-bridge, forward, and current-mode topologies. A design example uses a 215 kHz switching frequency with RT = 10 kΩ and CT = 680 pF, a transformer turns ratio of 2.2 based on a 30% target duty cycle (which must remain below 50% for dual-output operation), a primary inductance of 120 µH based on 6% magnetizing current, and an auxiliary winding turns ratio of 1.5. The output inductor is 2.2 µH. An RCD clamp is designed with Kclamp = 1.5. The output diode requires a voltage rating above the calculated stress (60 V used), and main push-pull MOSFETs should have voltage ratings 2.5–3 times the input voltage. Output filtering uses approximately 1145 µF with a 500 nH filter inductor and a 0.5 Ω damping resistor. Type IIB compensation targets a 5 kHz crossover frequency. The sense resistor is sized to the approximately 1 V CS pin threshold. The device operates from a 10 V to 30 V input and requires careful PCB layout, including short, thick power traces; separated power and signal grounds; and placement of bypass, filter, and compensation components close to the IC.
