He reflected on moving past a Game 7 loss and focusing on dressing the best lineup to win. He recalled telling Dean Lombardi he had a good coach.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2022, reports second quarter fiscal year 2023 revenue of $52.7 billion, operating income of $20.4 billion, net income of $16.4 billion, and diluted earnings per share of $2.20. Total revenue for the six months ended December 31, 2022, was $102.9 billion with net income of $34.0 billion. The Intelligent Cloud segment generated $21.5 billion in quarterly revenue, followed by Productivity and Business Processes at $17.0 billion and More Personal Computing at $14.2 billion. Microsoft Cloud revenue grew 22% to $27.1 billion, driven by 31% growth in Azure and other cloud services, while Windows OEM and Devices revenue each declined 39%, and Xbox content and services revenue fell 12%. The company completed its $18.8 billion acquisition of Nuance Communications in March 2022 and has a pending $68.7 billion agreement to acquire Activision Blizzard, expected to close in fiscal year 2023 pending regulatory approvals. On January 18, 2023, Microsoft announced a workforce reduction of approximately 10,000 jobs and recorded a $1.2 billion charge in the quarter, including $800 million in severance. A change in accounting estimate increased the useful lives of server and network equipment from four to six years, boosting quarterly operating income by $945 million and net income by $768 million. As of December 31, 2022, total assets were $364.6 billion, cash and cash equivalents were $15.6 billion, total debt was $48.1 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $183.1 billion. Unearned revenue totaled $39.6 billion, with $193 billion in revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations. The effective tax rate was 19% for the quarter. The company declared a $0.68 per share dividend and had $31.5 billion remaining under its $60 billion share repurchase program.

The Bollinger Band Squeeze strategy seeks to trade in the direction of a breakout after a period of low volatility, identified when the bands contract. According to the article’s backtesting, the strategy performed poorly across most assets and generally failed to beat buy-and-hold, even for consumer staples such as Pepsi; the authors concluded that anecdotal evidence for the strategy is untrustworthy and better indicators exist. The tool was developed in the 1980s by John A. Bollinger, an author and financial analyst born in 1950, who named the bands during a television interview. The article states that, as a breakout strategy, it behaves differently from mean reversion, has a lower win rate, and requires backtesting to confirm positive expectancy. Common mistakes include trading without positive expectancy and failing to follow the strategy due to biases, which mechanical trading may mitigate. The authors note that strategies are asset-specific and do not work universally.

Pedro Russell, following an unconventional education and careers in consulting and education, earned an MBA from MIT Sloan and co-founded GPS Partners, a search fund focused on for-profit medical technical schools. GPS targeted MedPro Institute, a Boston-area vocational school established in 1998 by Dr. Samantha Hill that offered certificate programs in medical assisting, phlebotomy, medical billing and coding, and dental assisting. The school had strong graduation and placement rates and relied primarily on word-of-mouth recruitment. With Hill open to selling, GPS signed a letter of intent and began due diligence. Russell identified an opportunity to grow enrollment through increased visibility but needed to assess how additional students would affect specific costs—including rent, cleaning, instructor and career services salaries, accreditation, supplies, insurance, internet, and electricity—which differed in their links to student volume. Drawing on his MIT accounting coursework regarding cost-volume relationships, Russell aimed to evaluate whether the acquisition could balance growth with financial sustainability before responding to Hill.

Augustine Heard reports interrupted communications to Fusan and speculation that the Tong Hâk may be preparing action against Tai Wen-kun, causing alarm. The King is believed to have requested U.S. naval aid, prompting the State Department to order Admiral Harmony to send the U.S.S. Petrel, which arrived at Chemulpo on April 19; Commander Dayton proceeded to Seoul. Chinese ironclads and Japanese warships also arrived. Heard requested rifle ammunition from Dayton. The passage includes an official order condemning heterodox teachings, directing authorities to arrest movement leaders and enforce obedience, while urging subjects to practice loyalty, filial piety, and willingness to sacrifice their lives for the King.

New Jersey Senator Cory Booker campaigned for Democratic Senate nominee Doug Jones in Alabama, a visit viewed as groundwork for a potential 2020 presidential bid. While Jones' campaign largely discouraged national Democrats from appearing in the state, Congressional Black Caucus members were welcomed to help mobilize black voters, who are pivotal in Democratic primaries. Booker, one of three prominent black Democrats considered potential 2020 contenders, stressed his family roots in Alabama. The state's African-American voters have historically played a decisive role in Democratic primaries, as seen in Barack Obama and Hillary Clinton's victories. Other potential candidates Deval Patrick and Kamala Harris also supported Jones.

The Second Circuit reversed a Board of Tax Appeals decision upholding a 1931 income tax deficiency against petitioner Pfeiffer. The Commissioner had asserted that Pfeiffer should have included in income the fair market value of preferred stock received as a 1931 dividend on common stock, and $200,000 from the 1931 redemption of preferred shares received in a 1928 dividend. The majority held that Section 115(f) of the Revenue Act of 1928, which exempts “stock dividends” without qualification, applies to preferred stock dividends on common stock, and that statutory history, administrative practice, and precedent supported this broad exemption. The court declined to address the Commissioner’s alternative argument that the redemption proceeds were taxable under Section 115(g) or as capital gain, because the issue was not raised or decided below and the Commissioner did not cross-appeal. Judge Hand dissented, arguing that Congress intended the exemption to apply only to dividends not constitutionally taxable as income under *Eisner v. Macomber*, that preferred stock on common is income, and that the Supreme Court’s rejection of related basis-reduction regulations in *Koshland v. Helvering* undermined the administrative interpretation of the exemption.

The Bank of N.T. Butterfield & Son Limited reported first quarter 2018 results on its April 24 earnings call, noting core return on average tangible common equity of 24.3% and a net interest margin of 3.05%. The bank completed its acquisition of Deutsche Bank’s Global Trust Solutions, integrating operations in Cayman, Guernsey, and Switzerland and opening a Singapore office. It expects to close the acquisition of Deutsche Bank’s banking operations in Cayman and the Channel Islands by year-end, adding a Jersey location and increasing total deposits by approximately 20%. Net interest income rose $3.8 million sequentially to $79.9 million, while non-interest income declined 6.1% due to seasonality. Core non-interest expense was $76 million, with a core efficiency ratio of 62.3% as the bank targets 60%. The Basel III total capital ratio was 19.2%, and common equity to total assets was 6.7%. The board authorized a $0.38 quarterly dividend, an 18% increase, and the company filed an S-3 shelf registration. Total assets were approximately $11 billion, loans were $4.0 billion, and the investment portfolio was $4.5 billion, with 94.6% rated AAA. Management described benign credit conditions, a 2 basis point net charge-off ratio, and an asset-sensitive balance sheet. They indicated that fee income is stable and that expense growth includes some non-recurring items, while the Global Trust Solutions acquisition is expected to add approximately $2 million in quarterly core expenses. The bank continues to evaluate opportunistic acquisitions and noted that the pending banking deal will increase asset sensitivity due to roughly $2 billion in additional deposits.

A player expressed regret over teammate Roli's injury during the Stanley Cup Finals but viewed the resulting opportunity to play as one to embrace. He stated that while circumstances were imperfect, he and the team maintained confidence in each other, and dwelling on the incident was unproductive. He noted that Finals intensity would provide motivation, that Roli would continue contributing hints on shooters' tendencies, and that maintaining normal preparation and confidence was essential. He acknowledged a rocky season but emphasized seizing the opportunity to finish what they started.

Andy overcame injuries to become a key physical playoff player. The team must control emotions against the Canucks and maintain its Boston mindset. Newfoundland fans are passionate, and a new team will boost the economy despite the previous junior team's struggles.

Dan Le Batard reported that the Miami Heat organization believed LeBron James "checked out" during the 2014 NBA Finals because he knew he was leaving, despite his strong statistics. This raises questions about whether James might similarly disengage in the 2018 Finals if he opts out of his Cavaliers contract and believes the team cannot win.

Hammerson confirmed receiving a highly preliminary, non-binding £4.88bn cash and share proposal from Klépierre SA on 8 March, valuing it at 615p per share, a 41% premium. Directors rejected the unsolicited approach as opportunistic and significantly undervaluing the company. Hammerson's shares rose 25% to 545p. The firm remains committed to acquiring Intu Properties, announced on 6 December, expecting £25m in annual synergy savings. Chairman David Tyler criticized the offer as below book value and involving shares in a lower-quality company. Hammerson trades at a 28% discount to book value with a forward dividend yield near 5%.

Bitcoin rallied to within 1% of its all-time high, trading up roughly 2% at $123,874 as the U.S. government shutdown entered its third day. The cryptocurrency has gained 12% this week as investors seek safe haven assets after lawmakers failed to reach a federal funding deal. Standard Chartered expects Bitcoin to hit a new high soon and ultimately reach $135,000. Traders are also hedging with spot gold, which rose 0.5% to $3,876.55 per ounce, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite rose 0.5% and 0.27%, respectively.

Google canceled Daily Stormer's website registration for violating policies against inciting violence, hours after GoDaddy told the neo-Nazi site to find a new host following its ridicule of Heather Heyer, killed while protesting the Charlottesville white nationalist rally. YouTube terminated the site's channel for hate-speech violations, and Facebook said it removes links to the site unless posts clearly condemn the content. Daily Stormer had briefly registered with Google via an automated process. Tucows denied hosting the site but stopped providing contact-privacy services to it, while Cloudflare denied being the host though it may mask the true host's identity. The moves follow the Charlottesville violence and were spurred by an online campaign led by activist Amy Siskind, and could signal increasing hurdles for extremist websites to maintain an online presence.

Matthew James Phelps, 29, called 911 on September 1 claiming he killed his wife Lauren, 29, after taking Coricidin cough medicine. Investigators found red-stained bedding and an empty box of the medicine in their North Carolina home. Lauren died at the hospital. Phelps, who has no criminal record, is held without bail on first-degree murder charges. The couple had been married less than a year.

The passage describes bonded optical devices for wearable electronics and other displays, such as augmented reality glasses, heads-up displays, and cell phones. To address challenges in producing high-resolution, multi-colored images from monochromatic micro light-emitting diode (microLED) wafers or chips, embodiments involve directly bonding separate optical elements—such as red, green, and blue LED chips—to carrier or processor elements (e.g., silicon or CMOS backplanes) without an intervening adhesive, using dielectric-to-dielectric and/or conductor-to-conductor bonding techniques (e.g., ZiBond, DBI). This enables fine pixel pitches of less than 50 microns, and in some cases less than 1 micron. The monochromatic optical elements are optically coupled to a common optical pathway, such as a waveguide with redirection elements and combiner optics, which superimposes the light to create a multi-colored image. The processor elements include active circuitry to independently control the optical emitters. Pixel isolation structures, such as deep trench isolation, may be included to limit crosstalk between adjacent emitters or matrices of pixels.

In Edwin P. Whitmore et al., Executors of the Will of Horace M. Whitmore, Deceased, v. The San Francisco Savings Union and James De Fremery et al., the court held that a creditor’s failure to present a claim against a decedent’s estate within the statutory time does not extinguish the underlying debt, but only bars the remedy against the estate. Horace M. Whitmore died owing a promissory note secured by a deed of trust on land. The creditor failed to present its claim within ten months after publication of notice. The executors sued to enjoin the trustees’ sale of the land and compel surrender of the security. The majority reversed the lower court’s judgment and directed that the demurrer be sustained, ruling that because the debt remained unpaid, equity would not compel the creditor to surrender its security or enjoin the sale, as one who seeks equity must do equity. The dissent argued that failure to present the claim abrogates the lien on estate property, and equity should compel the creditor to release the legal title so the property may be administered for estate purposes.

Transport Cabinet Secretary James Macharia told the National Assembly Transport Committee that poor enforcement of existing regulations by bodies like NTSA has caused disorganization in the boda boda sector. He said the ministry is working with county committees and the traffic department to improve implementation. Ruiru MP Simon King'ara called for a separate motorbike safety authority to replace NTSA and dismissed calls to ban boda boda riders from city centres, suggesting benchmarking Rwanda instead. Nairobi County recently banned boda boda riders from the CBD.

The IRS is furloughing about 34,000 workers due to a government shutdown beginning October 8, 2025, while 39,870 excepted and exempt employees remain on the job. Most operations are closed, and furloughed staff are in non-pay status but must report for their next tour of duty.

A speaker addresses a meeting in the national capital regarding relief for the Johnstown, Pennsylvania, flood disaster and neighboring areas. He notes a $2,000 contribution from Jacksonville, Florida. Citing a dispatch from Pennsylvania's governor, he reports appalling losses at Williamsport, with thousands hungry, homeless, and in urgent need of food. He proposes appointing three committees: one to collect food for immediate shipment to Williamsport, one to gather clothing and bedclothing, and one of business people and bankers to raise money for rebuilding and furnishing demolished homes. He states he already sent his own subscription and urges Washington to respond generously.

The Louisiana Fourth Circuit Court of Appeal affirmed William Brock’s conviction for molestation of a juvenile and his ten-year hard labor sentence. Brock, who lived with the victim’s mother, was found guilty of digitally manipulating the three-year-old victim. On appeal, he argued insufficient evidence and an excessive sentence. The court rejected both claims, holding that medical testimony, the child’s statements, and Brock’s supervisory role provided sufficient evidence for a rational trier of fact to find all elements of the offense under R.S. 14:81.2 beyond a reasonable doubt. The court also held that the trial court properly considered aggravating and mitigating factors under C.Cr.P. Art. 894.1 and that the ten-year sentence, five years below the statutory maximum, was not an abuse of discretion.

This study analyzes public financing instruments for European cleantech start-ups and SMEs, many under Horizon 2020. Funding includes loans, equity, grants, and guarantees for energy efficiency, smart cities, ICT, renewable energy, and healthcare. Managed by the EIB, EIF, EBRD, EUREKA, and the European Commission, some instruments provide direct funding while others use intermediaries. Instruments are benchmarked on metrics such as portfolio size, success rates, and technology readiness levels. Most target SMEs, some include research institutions, and many offer business coaching, advisory services, and R&D support.

At his final press conference, President Bush thanked the press corps and reflected on his tenure. He stated he would request the remaining $350 billion in bailout funds for President-elect Obama only if specifically asked. On Gaza, he supported Israel’s right to defend itself and called for a sustainable cease-fire contingent on Hamas halting rocket fire and arms smuggling. He identified an attack on the U.S. homeland as the most urgent threat facing the incoming administration, noting North Korea and Iran remained dangerous. Bush urged the Republican Party to be more inclusive and compassionate. He defended his economic and Iraq policies, including the surge and TARP, admitting he set aside free-market principles when advised of a potential depression, and acknowledged mistakes such as the “Mission Accomplished” banner, Abu Ghraib, and the absence of WMDs in Iraq. He declined to discuss preemptive pardons, strongly disagreed that America’s moral standing had been damaged, and expressed hope that Washington’s tone would improve for Obama. He also discussed New Orleans reconstruction, his opposition to protectionism, and his plans to remain active after leaving office.

The NVIDIA GA10x SM architecture improves upon Turing and Volta with four processing partitions, each containing a 64 KB register file, L0 cache, warp scheduler, dispatch unit, and math units, sharing a 128 KB L1 data cache/shared memory subsystem. The GA10x SM doubles peak FP32 throughput by adding FP32 capability to both datapaths per partition, enabling 128 FP32 operations per clock across four partitions, or 64 FP32 and 64 INT32 operations. It includes one third-generation Tensor Core per partition—four total—each twice as powerful as Turing’s, supporting TF32, BF16, and Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity for up to 2x matrix multiplication speedup. The L1 cache is 33% larger than Turing’s with double the shared memory bandwidth.

GA10x GPUs feature second-generation RT Cores that double the ray/triangle intersection rate over Turing and add an Interpolate Triangle Position unit to accelerate ray-traced motion blur by up to 8x. Enhanced Async Compute allows concurrent RT Core and graphics or compute workloads within an SM. The architecture introduces GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling, achieving up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth, over 52% more than the RTX 2080 Ti. NVIDIA RTX IO integrates with Microsoft DirectStorage for GPU-based lossless decompression and rapid asset loading, offloading CPU work and improving I/O performance by up to 100x compared to traditional storage.

The NVIDIA A40 data center GPU delivers up to 2x FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to 5x (10x with Sparsity) AI throughput versus the Quadro RTX 6000, with 48 GB of memory scalable to 96 GB via NVLink and PCIe Gen4. The RTX A6000 workstation GPU includes 10,752 CUDA Cores and 48 GB of GDDR6. Consumer cards include the RTX 3090 (GA102, 24 GB GDDR6X, 82 SMs), RTX 3080 (68 SMs, 2.7x tensor throughput with Sparsity), and RTX 3070 (GA104, faster than RTX 2080 Ti, GDDR6).

Display support includes HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a for 8K60/4K120. The fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware AV1 decode, and the seventh-generation NVENC supports encoding up to 8K HEVC. Ampere GPUs also feature Error Detection and Replay (EDR) for GDDR6X stability and are up to 1.9x more power efficient than Turing.

Tennessee National Wildlife Refuge closes August 21. Cross Creeks National Wildlife Refuge in Dover offers total eclipse viewing with staff assistance. Visitors may watch from the Visitor Center, patio, or 9-mile road. Partial eclipse begins 11:56 am CDT, totality 1:25 am CDT, lasting 55 seconds. Glasses and water sold; bring picnics. Call 731-642-2091.

This study examines the need for culturally sensitive mentorship for entry-level occupational therapy students from historically underrepresented groups. Using a cross-sectional survey of 133 students at a large urban private university, including 59 who identified as BIPOC, Hispanic/Latinx, or biracial, researchers found current mentorship programming insufficient for underrepresented students. While 89.5% of students had past formal or informal mentors, only 34% had current mentors. BIPOC students were significantly more likely than white students to rate mentor awareness of biases and prejudices as important. Hispanic/Latinx students reported significantly lower agreement that their mentors worked effectively across cultural differences or helped integrate their personal life with academic responsibilities. Students prioritized mentor personality, expertise, availability, and shared interests, with over one-third preferring mentors with similar ethnic or cultural backgrounds. Respondents desired mentors who demonstrated cultural humility, empathy, anti-racism allyship, and support for navigating workplace discrimination, microaggressions, and the transition from academia to clinical practice. They also sought guidance on networking, certification exam preparation, job searching, and work-life balance, preferring monthly or biweekly communication. The authors recommend hybrid formal and informal mentorship models, virtual platforms to expand diverse mentor access, cultural sensitivity and anti-racism training for mentors, and institutional policies supporting diversity, equity, inclusion, justice, and accessibility. Limitations include the single-institution setting, cross-sectional design, and primary focus on race and ethnicity rather than intersecting identities such as gender, LGBTQ+ status, or disability.

In Kellner v. District Court (decided February 16, 1953), the Colorado Supreme Court made absolute a rule to show cause in prohibition against the Denver District Court. The underlying action involved plaintiffs suing defendants for fraud and rescission of a home sale. Defendants, who had sold their Colorado home and moved to Ventura, California in September 1951, were personally served in California under Rule 4(f)(1), which permits service outside the state on Colorado residents. Defendants moved to quash, asserting they were California residents, but the trial court denied the motion and ordered them to answer. The Supreme Court held that the uncontroverted facts—including California voter registration, employment, driver's licenses, and property purchase—established defendants had abandoned Colorado residence before the action commenced in May 1952. Because plaintiffs failed to carry the burden of proving defendants remained Colorado residents, the California service was invalid, and the trial court lacked personal jurisdiction. The Court further held that an inferior tribunal proceeding without jurisdiction over the person presents a matter of great public importance warranting the exercise of original jurisdiction.

The Sensex and Nifty closed marginally lower on Tuesday at 28,339.31 and 8,792, respectively. Five stocks hit new 52-week highs: AIA Engineering closed 2.02 percent higher after reporting 17.6 percent profit growth and an interim dividend; Alkem Laboratories closed 2.03 percent higher on a 24.9 percent Q3 profit rise; KEC International, Exide Industries, and Kalpataru Power Transmission hit early trade highs but closed lower.

European markets reached record highs, with the STOXX 600 gaining about 0.5 percent, led by steelmakers and banks, while auto stocks declined. Gold surpassed $4,000 per ounce amid expectations of U.S. Federal Reserve easing. Other reported items include: the Bank of England warning of AI bubble risk; Germany opening an antitrust probe into Temu; Fifth Third acquiring Comerica for $10.9 billion; the World Bank raising China’s 2025 growth forecast to 4.8 percent; and OpenAI reaching a $500 billion valuation. Pan Finance is described as a global financial intelligence source.

This study by Çelen (2023) examined education faculty students' attitudes toward the Research Methods in Education (RME) course and their views on its instruction. Using a mixed-methods sequential explanatory design, the quantitative phase surveyed 190 students from Turkish Teaching, English Teaching, and Pre-School Teaching departments at Bayburt University with a 21-item attitude scale measuring contribution to the profession, confidence, and contribution to daily life. The qualitative phase conducted focus group interviews with 10 pre-service teachers. Quantitative findings showed no significant difference in attitudes by department, but a significant difference by grade level between first and fourth-year students. The contribution to daily life sub-dimension had the highest mean score. Qualitative findings indicated that 90% of participants found the course necessary, 50% reported personal gains, and 60% viewed the lesson duration as insufficient. The study recommends offering prerequisite courses before RME, scheduling it in the third or fourth year, making it compulsory, and extending its duration or credits, potentially splitting it into two courses.

Bath Rugby fans remain stranded across Europe three days after their team's 24-20 Champions Cup loss to Toulon, as snow, ice and wind caused mass flight cancellations from Marseille, Nice and Amsterdam, with Heathrow and other London airports also affected. With no direct flights to Bristol available, supporters have faced disrupted journeys via connections through cities including Munich, Brussels and Madrid, or alternative train routes, while some remain stuck in France hoping to return Tuesday or Wednesday. The chaos has forced fans to take extra days off work, arrange extended pet care, and miss important events such as a funeral. The Bath team returned Sunday via a chartered flight. While some travellers reported airport confusion, diversions and long delays, others attempted to make the best of their extended stays.

China tightened export restrictions on rare earths and related technology ahead of an expected meeting between Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump, causing U.S. rare earth miner stocks to surge Thursday. The new rules require export licenses for products containing rare earths worth 0.1% or more of their value and for using Chinese extraction, refining, or recycling technology. The White House is assessing the impact and has accused Beijing of manipulating markets to control global technology supply chains. The Trump administration has taken equity stakes in domestic miners, including MP Materials, to build a supply chain and reduce U.S. dependence on China. Industry executives say they are in close contact with the administration, and analysts believe the restrictions strengthen Beijing's position ahead of the expected summit.

On October 29, 2018, and March 10, 2019, Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft operated by Lion Air and Ethiopian Airlines crashed, killing all 346 people aboard. The cause was the Maneuvering Characteristics Augmentation System (MCAS), software intended to prevent stalls by automatically pushing the aircraft’s nose down when a high angle of attack was detected. MCAS relied on data from a single angle-of-attack sensor, and Boeing had significantly increased its stabilizer authority and removed an initial G-force trigger without fully reporting these changes to the FAA or airlines. Boeing developed the 737 MAX under intense pressure to compete with Airbus’s A320neo, compressing the design schedule and seeking to avoid simulator training to reduce costs. Internal communications showed employees raised safety concerns, but a corporate culture shift following the McDonnell Douglas merger prioritized business metrics over engineering rigor, and dissent was discouraged. The FAA certified the aircraft based on limited differences from prior 737 models and did not adequately review MCAS. After the second crash, the global fleet was grounded for 21 months. Boeing lost over 1,000 orders, faced billions of dollars in direct costs and lost sales, and replaced senior leadership, while regulators later mandated simulator training and new oversight procedures.

Centrica's stock price fell 35% in the last year, giving it an 8.6% dividend yield. It faces regulatory uncertainty and business model challenges but trades at a P/E ratio of around 10, with expected earnings growth of 7% this year. Volution reported interim revenue growth of 11.6% and a 6.7% rise in adjusted operating profit, and announced the acquisition of Simx Limited. With earnings expected to rise 6% this year and 7% next year, and dividends covered 3.3 times by profit, Volution could offer dividend growth despite its current 2.2% yield.

The speaker recounts being inactive for roughly seven months during contract negotiations before being selected for the Russian Olympic team and working out with junior whalers. After a team from North Carolina made an offer, the Detroit Red Wings matched it within seven days, enabling his return. Despite mental exhaustion and jet lag after returning from Japan, he played Friday night. He notes that Detroit has been his second home since he defected from Russia to join the Red Wings. He recounts seeing Vladi in the building before game three following an inspirational speech by Scotty Bowman, winning the Stanley Cup, and spending time with Vladi on the ice speaking Russian to help him feel comfortable and celebrate.

Constraint Programming faces a modeling bottleneck that Constraint Acquisition (CA) seeks to automate, yet hybrid CA methods lack dedicated mechanisms to address over-fitting of global constraints from passive learning. This study proposes a three-phase hybrid framework (HCAR) to systematically identify and refine such over-fitted constraints. Phase 1 applies passive learning to a small set of positive examples to generate candidate global constraints—such as AllDifferent, Sum, and Count—and a pruned bias of fixed-arity constraints. Phase 2, the core contribution, conducts Query-Driven Interactive Refinement: it assigns machine learning-based prior confidence scores to global candidates, posts targeted oracle queries, updates beliefs using a Bayesian framework, and accepts or rejects constraints based on predefined thresholds. Rejected constraints trigger a Subset Exploration mechanism that recovers valid sub-constraints by reducing variable scope while preserving parameters. Phase 3 uses active learning (MQuAcq-2) to acquire any remaining fixed-arity constraints. The framework features adaptive query budget allocation, and empirical validation demonstrates high accuracy and target model coverage with manageable query complexity.

Research expectations for U.S. mathematics education faculty vary by institution type, department type, and research time commitment. A survey of 404 faculty found that R1 faculty typically spend 40% of their time on research and are expected to publish about 2.25 papers per year, with research journal articles most valued; they are less likely to have written expectations but more likely to be required to pursue external funding, give presentations, and value sole authorship. R2 faculty average 1.5 papers per year, are more likely to have explicit written expectations, and fall between R1 and Other institutions on funding and authorship importance. Faculty at Other institutions typically devote 20% of time to research and publish about one paper per year, valuing presentations and professional development more while requiring external funding less. A 10% increase in research time corresponds to 0.184 more expected papers. Faculty in mathematics departments are expected to publish approximately 0.31 fewer papers than those in education departments but value conference proceedings and funding more. The authors recommend that departments explicitly document expectations regarding publication quantity, publication types, and scholarly activities.

This work investigates the orbital Edelstein effect (OEE) and spin Edelstein effect (SEE) in gated, doped monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) such as MoS₂. Breaking the mirror symmetry via a perpendicular electric field or substrate lowers the point group symmetry to C₃ᵥ, inducing Rashba-type chiral in-plane orbital and spin textures. Using a minimal five-band tight-binding Hamiltonian for metal d orbitals fitted to density functional theory, the authors compute the Edelstein susceptibilities. For electron-doped TMDs, the OEE is several times larger than the SEE and increases linearly with carrier concentration, because the spin contributions from the two conduction bands largely cancel while the orbital contributions do not. For hole-doped TMDs, both effects are comparable in magnitude but become strongly enhanced when holes occupy the Γ valley; this can be achieved either by high doping or by small compressive strain, which raises the Γ valley above the K/K′ valleys. The orbital contributions from the two valence bands add constructively, whereas the spin contributions tend to cancel, further enhancing the OEE. The predicted orbital Edelstein susceptibilities (~10⁻⁸ to 10⁻⁷ µB V⁻¹ m) exceed those reported for other material systems by one to two orders of magnitude, suggesting that gated monolayer TMDs provide an ideal platform for studying the OEE and related spintronics phenomena.

Royal Rumble 2017 at the Alamodome targets 60,000 tickets. Confirmed names include Goldberg, Brock Lesnar, and John Cena; The Undertaker is expected and Shawn Michaels is rumored for a non-wrestling role. The card features AJ Styles vs John Cena for the WWE Championship, Kevin Owens vs Roman Reigns for the Universal Championship with Chris Jericho in a shark cage, and a 30-Man Royal Rumble Match featuring Goldberg, the first entrant, and Brock Lesnar, who are expected to cost each other the match and set up a Wrestlemania 33 match.

On December 12, 2016, NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K reporting a Termination Agreement with Goldman, Sachs & Co. to terminate 63,259,180.62 outstanding warrants issued in November 2013. In consideration, NVIDIA will deliver common stock based on the daily volume-weighted average price during an observation period from December 13, 2016, to January 31, 2017, relying on an exemption from registration under Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act of 1933.

While government shutdowns historically have had minimal economic impact, with markets recovering quickly and GDP effects around 0.1 percentage point per week, analysts warn the current situation could differ. President Trump has threatened to make some federal furloughs permanent, which would depart from past practice and create uncertainty. A prolonged shutdown could also delay key economic data releases, including jobs reports and inflation readings, potentially affecting Social Security cost-of-living adjustments and forcing the Federal Reserve to rely on private data. Most analysts still expect a relatively mild overall impact, though furloughed employees and contractors face immediate financial instability.

A column by criminal defense attorney Adam R. Banner discusses the Netflix documentary “Unknown Number: The High School Catfish,” which follows Michigan teens Lauryn Licari and Owen McKenny as they receive harassing, graphic, and threatening text messages from an unknown sender who appears to know them personally. After 18 months, local investigators in Beal City enlisted the FBI, which examined 720 pages of messages and conducted a forensic phone dump. Banner notes the documentary briefly addresses cellphone forensics but could have explored it further, and he connects the case to broader dangers of student cellphone use, referencing Oklahoma’s upcoming “bell to bell” school cellphone ban.

Keltner Channels, developed by Chester W. Keltner in the 1960s, are a technical analysis tool used to assess volatility and identify potential price trends. The indicator consists of three lines: a middle line typically based on a moving average of the typical price (the average of high, low, and close), and upper and lower bands set at a multiple of the Average True Range (ATR) above and below the middle line. The bands expand and contract as volatility changes. Older and less famous than Bollinger Bands—which rely on standard deviation and closing prices—Keltner Channels are generally viewed as leading indicators because they use volatility to anticipate price movements. Traders use them for mean reversion, momentum, swing trading, and scalping, often treating price moves outside the bands as signals for entry, exit, or potential reversals. While there is no universal optimal setting, a common default is a 20-period exponential moving average with an ATR multiplier of 2.0. Backtests described in the passage show a mean reversion strategy on the S&P 500 yielded 288 trades, a 77% win rate, a 6.3% CAGR, and a profit factor of 2, while a momentum strategy using a 30-day period and a 1.3 ATR multiplier produced 143 trades and a 3.6% CAGR. The Keltner Channel does not repaint. A Bollinger squeeze within the Keltner Channel occurs when Bollinger Bands narrow inside the Keltner boundaries, suggesting consolidation and a potential breakout. Traders should avoid over-reliance on the indicator and consider broader market context.

The Bank of England allotted £5.085 billion in its six-month indexed long-term repo operation, the highest amount since March 2020 and more than double the previous week’s £2.352 billion, indicating a sharp rise in bank demand for central bank liquidity. The BoE is encouraging use of the facility as it unwinds quantitative easing and shifts away from excess reserves toward a framework where banks actively borrow funds. Demand for six-month repos remains modest compared with short-term facilities, evidenced by a record £87.149 billion seven-day repo allotment last week. The central bank aims to normalize funding conditions while maintaining market stability, and persistent high demand could reshape liquidity management in a post-QE environment.

The Fabian Market Timing Model is a quantitative long-term trend-following strategy developed by Richard Fabian in the 1960s. It generates weekly buy and sell signals based on the 39-week moving averages of the S&P 500, Dow Jones Industrial Average, and utilities sector to reduce false signals. The model emphasizes mechanical, rule-based trading over discretionary decisions. Backtesting indicates long-term returns approach buy-and-hold levels with lower volatility and drawdown. Discipline in following the system is considered more important than the model itself.

A House panel advanced a bill to fix South Carolina's $24 billion pension gap by raising employee contributions to 9 percent and employer contributions to 18.56 percent by 2023; local governments oppose the 60 percent increase. The full committee debates it Thursday. A bill recognizing out-of-state concealed weapons permits advanced to the House floor. The Senate passed a measure for Coastal Carolina University championship license plates costing $70 extra, with profits funding scholarships; a similar Clemson bill is pending.

Chelsea will face Barcelona in the Champions League last-16 after finishing second in Group C. First leg: February 13/14 or 20/21; second: March 6/7 or 13/14. Barcelona topped Group D with 14 points. They last met in the 2012 semi-final; Chelsea won 3-2 on aggregate. Lionel Messi has 363 goals in 397 Barcelona appearances since 2004. Odds: Chelsea 9/4, draw 23/10, Barcelona 6/5.

Hanne Rinholm, Ida Heiberg Solem, and Inger Ulleberg of Oslo Metropolitan University explore dialogic classroom practices in music and mathematics education to bridge the gap between educational rhetoric and practice. Drawing on dialogism, Bildung, and Biesta’s dimensions of education, they analyze two qualitative cases—a pre-service teacher choir project and an upper-primary mathematics lesson—using narrative, hermeneutic methods. The study employs theoretical lenses including epistemological and ontological dialogue, musicking, mathematizing, and the didactic contract. In the music case, the teacher’s openness about personal loss and inclusion of student song choices fostered existential engagement and musicking. In the mathematics case, the teacher’s admission of uncertainty and uptake of student discoveries about fractions promoted collective mathematizing. Both cases demonstrate that genuine dialogic pedagogy requires teachers to listen, take risks, show vulnerability, and establish a didactic contract that values student voices. The authors argue that integrating epistemological and ontological dialogue supports Bildung, participation, and democratic citizenship, though they acknowledge paradoxes regarding teacher power and the unpredictability of educational outcomes.

The speaker addresses the council on America's duty to help establish a new international peace. The United States must join other nations to guarantee a just and lasting peace, but only if the terms satisfy American principles and serve mankind's interests, not merely immediate national aims. The war must end, but peace requires more than agreements between belligerents; it needs an organized common peace secured by a superior collective force, not a balance of power. The speaker interprets assurances from warring nations as implying "peace without victory," since imposed terms would breed resentment and instability. Only a peace of equals, based on equality and mutual benefit, can endure.

Lorna Gibson discusses modeling osteoporosis in trabecular bone using Voronoi honeycombs. She describes obtaining a whale vertebra for a student project and plans to cut it for compression testing. Finite element analysis of 2D Voronoi honeycombs shows elastic moduli agree with analytical models, but compressive strength is lower than regular hexagonal honeycombs due to broader strain distributions, reaching a minimum around 5% relative density near the crossover between elastic buckling and plastic yielding. Modeling bone loss by thinning struts versus removing them reveals that strut removal causes significantly greater reductions in modulus and strength. In 2D, the percolation threshold—where the structure separates into pieces and properties drop to zero—occurs at about 30–35% density reduction, while in 3D it occurs near 50%. More realistic models using perturbed square Voronoi patterns matched to vertebral bone orientation confirm these trends, with 3D structures requiring more material removal than 2D for equivalent modulus loss.

Gibson then covers metal foams as bone substitutes and implant coatings, noting biocompatible metals such as titanium and tantalum and manufacturing methods including replica processes, fugitive phase processing, foaming agents, gas expansion, freeze casting, and selective laser sintering. Data show scatter but generally follow expected scaling for modulus and strength.

Finally, she discusses evolutionary studies linking trabecular architecture to locomotion. A phylogenetic overview notes calcium carbonate mineralization in early organisms and calcium phosphate bone appearing in vertebrates around 450 million years ago. A study of the 8-million-year-old hominid *Oreopithecus bambolii* compared ilium trabecular structure to humans and non-human primates, concluding the species was likely bipedal based on density patterns and architectural similarities. She briefly notes that bone quality, including microcracks in the solid material, also affects strength, and previews the next lecture on tissue engineering scaffolds.

The lecture recaps linearizing Einstein's equations, decomposing perturbations into six gauge-invariant functions and four gauge degrees of freedom, and identifies the transverse, traceless spatial perturbation $h_{ij}^{TT}$ as the radiative degree of freedom possessing two polarizations. Because a single freely falling body experiences no coordinate acceleration, observing gravitational waves requires measuring relative effects across a finite region. The lecturer describes two approaches: the varying round-trip light travel time between separated bodies, which underlies interferometric detectors like LIGO; and geodesic deviation, which shows that $h_{xx}$ and $h_{xy}$ induce orthogonal "plus" and "cross" tidal stretch-and-squeeze polarizations on a ring of test masses. To compute the radiation from a source, one uses the linearized Einstein equation in Lorentz gauge. In the far-field limit, the trace-reversed spatial metric perturbation is proportional to the second time derivative of the source's quadrupole moment $I_{ij}$. Projecting out the transverse components and removing the trace yields the quadrupole formula, giving the gauge-invariant $h_{ij}^{TT}$ as $2G/r$ times the transverse-traceless projection of $\ddot{I}_{ij}$, describing the observable gravitational wave field.

Research published in The FASEB Journal identified TRPM8 and TRPP3 receptors as therapeutic targets to increase brown adipose tissue. Using human bone marrow stem cells and subcutaneous fat cells, scientists found these receptors were highly present in differentiated brown fat but absent in progenitor cells. Stimulating TRPM8 supported browning, while eliminating TRPP3 prevented brown fat formation, suggesting potential new treatments for obesity, diabetes, and related metabolic disorders.

Tesla, Inc. filed its Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the period ended September 30, 2021. The company reported total revenues of $13.757 billion for the three months ended September 30, 2021, and $36.104 billion for the nine months ended September 30, 2021, compared to $8.771 billion and $20.792 billion in the prior year periods. Net income attributable to common stockholders was $1.618 billion for the quarter and $3.198 billion for the nine-month period, up from $331 million and $451 million in the prior year periods. As of September 30, 2021, total assets were $57.834 billion, including $16.065 billion in cash and cash equivalents, and total stockholders' equity was $27.053 billion.

The report notes Tesla operates in two segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. It discusses ongoing global impacts from COVID-19, including supply chain and semiconductor challenges. During the nine months ended September 30, 2021, Tesla purchased $1.50 billion in bitcoin, recorded impairment losses of $101 million, and held digital assets with a carrying value of $1.26 billion and fair market value of $1.83 billion as of September 30, 2021. The company adopted ASU 2020-06 on January 1, 2021, using the modified retrospective method, which changed accounting for convertible instruments and diluted EPS calculations. Debt activities included full repayment of the 2025 Notes and China loan agreements, issuance of Automotive Asset-backed Notes, and conversions of convertible senior notes. The filing details the 2018 CEO Performance Award, noting achieved and probable operational milestones and associated stock-based compensation expenses. Tesla also outlines commitments under its Buffalo, New York operating lease arrangement, including investment and job creation targets.

Lyminster Primary School received an Ofsted rating of requiring improvement after a May inspection. Inspector Marcia Goodwin noted positive changes under headteacher Steven McGinley but said they had not yet had sufficient impact. The report cited a legacy of weak teaching that led to last year’s Year 6 pupils under-achieving in SATs, and inconsistent teaching quality. McGinley welcomed the clear focus, noted pupils’ good conduct, and expressed confidence the school would rapidly bounce back.

Apple Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended April 1, 2023. Second-quarter net sales were $94.8 billion, down 3% year-over-year, with net income of $24.2 billion and diluted earnings per share of $1.52. Six-month net sales were $212.0 billion and net income was $54.2 billion. iPhone net sales were relatively flat, Mac net sales fell 31%, and Services net sales rose 5% compared to the prior-year quarter. By segment, Americas net sales decreased 8% while Rest of Asia Pacific increased 15%. As of April 1, 2023, total assets were $332.2 billion, total current liabilities were $120.1 billion, and total shareholders’ equity was $62.2 billion. The company generated $62.6 billion in cash from operating activities during the six months. It repurchased $19.1 billion of common stock and paid $3.7 billion in dividends during the quarter. On May 4, 2023, the Board authorized an additional $90 billion share repurchase program and raised the quarterly dividend to $0.24 per share. The Ninth Circuit affirmed the district court ruling in the Epic Games lawsuit on April 24, 2023, and a hearing for the European Commission’s appeal of the State Aid Decision is scheduled for May 23, 2023.

In *Mary Lee Geesbreght v. John Geesbreght* (Tex. Civ. App.—Fort Worth, July 13, 1978), the court affirmed the trial judgment granting a divorce and awarding custody of the parties’ minor children to the father, but reversed and remanded the property division for a new trial. The appellate court rejected Mary Lee’s jurisdictional challenges, holding she had waived her right to complain and that the children’s domicile remained in Texas. The court also found no reversible error in the jury trial on custody or in the supplemental charge regarding possessory conservator rights. However, the trial court erred by valuing John’s stock in Emergency Medicine Consultants solely at its $16,000 book value without considering corporate goodwill that existed apart from his personal services, rendering the property division grossly inadequate. Appeal costs were taxed equally to both parties.

Whangarei District Council advises drivers using Kensington Park during winter congestion that rule-breaking vehicles will be ticketed after initial warnings. Drivers should plan ahead, car pool, leave earlier, or park farther away and walk.

Bluehole launched PUBG Xbox One event Snipe City, requiring 400,000 M24 and Kar98 kills by July 10. Eligible players receive Bloody Tank Top, Padded Jacket, and two Militia Crates. Results announced July 11.

State Bank Financial Corporation (NASDAQ:STBZ) was upgraded to "buy" by Zacks Investment Research with a $30.00 price target, while Hovde Group downgraded it to "market perform" with a $24.50 target. Analysts average a "Hold" rating and $25.25 target. The stock opened at $26.86 with a market cap of $963.28 million. The company reported Q3 EPS of $0.34, beating estimates by $0.03, with analysts forecasting $1.33 for the current fiscal year. It declared a $0.14 quarterly dividend yielding 2.08%. Directors Robert H. McMahon and John D. Houser recently sold shares. Insiders own 6.31% and institutional investors own 81.81% after several funds increased stakes. The Georgia-based bank holding company provides community banking services.

Police appeal for information after a teenager was sexually assaulted on a train on April 8. A man fell into her when the train jolted, touched her inappropriately until passengers intervened. Call 0800 40 50 40 or text 61016, quoting 148 18/04/17.

Jammu and Kashmir Public Service Commission has kept in abeyance the April 23, 2017 result of the Combined Competitive (Preliminary) Examination, 2016 and withdrawn the main examination notification after detecting discrepancies in question papers and answer keys. It will refer all 23 subjects' papers and keys to independent experts for re-evaluation following post-result representations. Next main exam date will be notified after the experts' report. NVIDIA Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 29, 2018, reported quarterly revenue of $3.123 billion and six-month revenue of $6.330 billion, increases of 40% and 52% year over year, respectively. Net income was $1.101 billion for the quarter and $2.345 billion for the six months, with diluted earnings per share of $1.76 and $3.74. The GPU business generated $2.656 billion in quarterly revenue and the Tegra Processor business generated $467 million. Construction began on a 750,000 square foot building on its Santa Clara campus, targeted for completion in fiscal year 2022.

Microsoft Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2022, reports total revenue of $49.36 billion, net income of $16.73 billion, and diluted earnings per share of $2.22. Total assets were $344.61 billion as of March 31, 2022. Asian shares fell Tuesday as U.S. tech shares dropped on fears of tighter regulation after Facebook tumbled 6.8% over improper access to 50 million users' data. Cleveland Central High School students presented the Purple Christmas Showcase at the Delta Art Alliance Friday, featuring photos and biographies from interviews for the Cleveland Yearbook. Lagos and Ogun health workers are on high alert for Lassa fever. Ogun confirmed one case; patient isolated, responding to treatment, with 66 contacts under surveillance. LUTH cases are responding. Last week, Lagos had five cases, two deaths, and 150 under surveillance.

This study externally validated a longitudinal Grade of Membership (L-GoM) model of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) progression—previously developed in clinic-based, high-socioeconomic-status, non-Hispanic white Predictors 2 patients and validated in Predictors 1—using the community-based, multiethnic Predictors 3 cohort (N=273) from the Washington Heights Inwood Columbia Aging Project. Participants included older adults with mild cognitive impairment (MCI; 83 nonconverters, 40 converters) and AD dementia (118 nonreverters, 32 reverters). The L-GoM model uses four latent subtypes derived from 11 clinical domains to generate individual-specific predictions. Investigators applied the model to initial-visit data to predict survival and need for full-time care (FTC) over 7.5 years, aggregating individual predictions to compare against group-specific observed proportions. Results showed that the model fit well for AD nonreverters and for the MCI group overall, accurately predicting mortality and FTC prevalence. However, the 32 AD reverters survived substantially longer and had lower FTC needs than predicted, suggesting they were likely misdiagnosed. MCI converters survived longer than predicted but remained within confidence bands. Baseline L-GoM subtype scores differed significantly by diagnosis, sex, ethnicity, and ApoE status. Compared with Predictors 2, Predictors 3 participants were older, more often female and Hispanic, and had lower educational attainment. The authors concluded that the L-GoM model is valid for predicting outcomes in community-dwelling, diverse older adults with AD or MCI, and that the associated web-based calculator produces informative individual-level predictions, though it is vulnerable to misdiagnosis.

Fibonacci trading employs tools such as retracement, expansion, and fan to identify potential support and resistance levels and plan trade entries, exits, stops, and limits. The retracement tool marks levels at 23.6%, 38.2%, 50%, 61.8%, and 100% of a preceding swing; the expansion tool estimates profit targets; and the fan plots dynamic trendlines. The optimal timeframe and levels depend on trading style and volatility, requiring backtesting to determine effectiveness. The authors are skeptical because there is no scientific evidence that prices follow Fibonacci numbers, and the strategy’s subjectivity makes backtesting difficult. They cite Clarissa Gunawan’s study on Vanguard ETFs, which found passive buy-and-hold outperformed active Fibonacci strategies, suggesting the tools may mark support and resistance but should be used cautiously alongside other indicators rather than as standalone strategies.

Day trading involves buying and selling financial instruments within a single trading day to profit from short-term price movements. The article outlines numerous strategies—including momentum, range, scalping, breakout, pullback, reversal, gap, news, pattern, seasonal, dark pool, statistical arbitrage, pairs, order flow, market making, short squeeze, statistical volatility, market profile, regime switching, volatility targeting, and phase analysis trading—each utilizing technical indicators and carrying distinct risks. Unlike swing trading, which holds positions for days or weeks, day trading avoids overnight exposure but demands rapid decision-making and substantial capital; in the U.S., FINRA requires a minimum of $25,000 for pattern day traders. Significant risks include market volatility and leverage, which magnifies both profits and losses, and the passage notes that most day traders lose money. Success requires strict discipline, emotional control, backtesting with historical data, and adapting strategies to specific market dynamics, time-of-day fluctuations, seasonal patterns, and holidays.

Yale and Brookings researchers argue that AI’s impact on the U.S. labor market consists of isolated “lightning strikes” rather than a widespread “house fire.” Despite studies showing declines in entry-level roles in software development and customer service, and comments by Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell about young workers struggling, the researchers say labor market data reveals no broad, AI-driven disruption. Lead author Martha Gimbel states that employment shifts remain within historical norms and are driven by macroeconomic factors—a slowing economy, an aging population, and declining immigration—rather than by technology. While recent graduates face a tough “low hire, low-fire” environment and youth unemployment has risen to 10.5%, older workers are also experiencing elevated long-term joblessness. The researchers stress that exposure to AI does not equal displacement; jobs may change rather than disappear, as seen with radiologists. They note generative AI primarily affects big cities with knowledge-sector clusters, not the industrial heartland. Real systemic displacement, they contend, will only emerge when companies redesign enterprise workflows around embedded AI—a slow, uneven process expected to take years.

Dallas Stars and Vegas Golden Knights stood together before the Golden Knights' debut to honor Las Vegas shooting victims, a deceased staff member, and announcer Dave Strader, with moments of silence.

Newcastle are set to renew interest in Besiktas midfielder Tolgay Arslan this summer, alongside Chelsea, Borussia Dortmund and Bayer Leverkusen. Jose Mourinho told Real Madrid to abandon pursuit of Manchester United goalkeeper David de Gea, contracted until 2019 with an option for another year. Shakhtar Donetsk chief executive Sergei Palkin claims midfielder Fred will leave in June for either Manchester United or Manchester City.

The passage examines Education Savings Accounts (ESAs) as a turning point in school choice, comparing the 2023 universal ESA wave in red states to the 1993 charter school expansion in primarily blue states. It traces ESAs to Milton Friedman’s voucher theories, noting they provide publicly funded parental allocations for private school tuition, homeschooling, or educational services with minimal regulation. The brief contends that ESAs are designed to reduce government’s role in education and lower taxpayer costs, reflected in per-pupil allocations that are fractions of public school spending across states. This gap requires families to supplement tuition, which has increased private school costs in some states. Despite lower per-pupil amounts, state spending on vouchers and ESAs has risen substantially. The passage identifies accountability gaps in spending and pedagogy, noting that some programs have approved non-educational purchases and often lack requirements for certified teachers, standardized testing, or curriculum standards. It argues ESAs strain public school budgets—particularly in rural areas where enrollment declines threaten school closures and community institutions—and facilitate discrimination against students with disabilities, underperforming students, and LGBTQ+ faculty and staff. The brief recommends repealing ESAs or, alternatively, imposing strict oversight, spending limits, anti-discrimination protections, and public referenda, while noting that state referenda in Colorado, Kentucky, and Nebraska have rejected private school choice programs.

Impact venture capital firms have raised $13 billion since 2001 ($10 billion since 2010) to invest in early- and mid-stage "GoodBusiness" startups—for-large-profit companies delivering social or environmental benefits. Unlike general impact investors who accept near-market or sub-market returns, impact VCs target top-quartile financial returns because of their impact-oriented theses. The author categorizes these funds by scale and structure: multi-billion-dollar broad-focus firms such as Capricorn Investment Group and Generation Investment Management; traditional VC-style firms raising $100–$900 million like Elevar Equity and Obvious Ventures; sub-$100 million funds; and founder/LP funds including Omidyar Network and the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative. Major sub-sectors include environmental protection, emerging-market services for the growing middle class, ethical consumer products, and support for underrepresented founders. While dedicated impact VC funds are currently expanding, the author predicts the distinction will fade within 10–15 years as traditional VCs incorporate GoodBusiness into their standard investment theses, driven by unstoppable global technological, demographic, and climate trends.

Ukrainian startup Dropla, founded by V'yacheslav Shvaydak, has developed an AI software called Blue Eyes to detect Russian ambush drones and landmines along Ukrainian supply routes. Russian forces have increasingly deployed explosive-laden quadcopters that lie in wait to attack logistics vehicles behind the front lines. Blue Eyes processes real-time thermal and optical video feeds from cheap quadcopters flying over supply roads, rapidly identifying threats and sending coordinates to Ukraine's battle management system. The system includes a 2.1-kg hardware box and can process up to 130 frames per second. Dropla's team of Ukrainian engineers has trained the AI to recognize over 170 types of explosive threats. Multiple frontline units have tested Blue Eyes in combat since early summer, and the company plans to scale deployment near the zero line fivefold. Experts note that ambush drones pose a severe threat to logistical chains, requiring constant situational awareness and rapid technological adaptation.

U.S. wheat futures fell to a nearly three-week low on light export demand and Plains rain forecasts. Soybean futures declined for a fifth day on expectations of quickening Midwest planting, while Chinese export concerns persisted. Corn futures were little changed. The USDA reported corn planting at 5 percent and soybeans at 2 percent, behind average, and wheat condition at 31 percent good-to-excellent, below forecasts.

Aldwick councillor Jacqui Maconachie died at home after battling cancer. The 22-year Arun District Council veteran, who served as chairman from 2001-2002, leaves behind husband and fellow councillor Dougal. MP Nick Gibb and chief executive Nigel Lynn paid tribute and offered condolences.

This application is a continuation of multiple prior U.S. patents and claims benefit of numerous provisional patent applications. The background describes hydraulic fracturing operations in which fluid ends attached to power ends pressurize fluid for injection into wellbores. Traditional fluid ends are machined from high-strength alloy steel as a single housing with intersecting vertical and horizontal bores, creating stress points prone to fatigue cracks and corrosion, often requiring replacement after only a few jobs. The disclosed fluid end comprises a plurality of side-by-side fluid end sections, each having a housing with only a single horizontal bore and no intersecting vertical bore, removing common stress points and reducing manufacturing time and material costs. Each housing is attached to a connect plate and supported by stay rods. Fluid is delivered through upper and lower intake manifolds into a fluid routing plug installed within the horizontal bore, which routes fluid to a suction valve, and pressurized fluid exits through a discharge bore and conduit. The fluid routing plug features tapered walls, offset fluid passages, and beveled sealing surfaces that engage corresponding housing surfaces and seals to manage operational loads and expansion. Seals are installed in housing grooves and sized to occupy nearly all groove volume to prevent proppant erosion. The modular design allows individual section replacement without replacing the entire fluid end.

The Side Screen Offense is a common NBA two-player, on-ball screen-and-roll isolation typically run on the left for right-handed players and right for left-handed players to allow strong-hand dribble penetration to the middle. The ballhandler can drive, pull up, pass to the rolling screener, or kick out to a shooter. Success requires execution, coordination, timing, and non-verbal communication. The offense includes eight basic reads and counters, such as turning the corner on a chase, a drop pass against baseline help, a kick-out on a sag, a pull-up when the defender goes under, driving opposite on an early cheat, a crossover when the defender fights through, a pop-out when the defense shows and recovers, and post rolls, isolations, slips, lobs, or a 2-1-2 alignment against switches, denials, or traps. Entries include the High Post Rub, Power, and Horns sets, and the action can flow into Flex, Triangle, or Motion continuities. Teaching employs the whole-part-whole method and progressive drills. Strategically, teams should scout opponents, vary alignments, attack weak defenders, use the set as a late-clock continuity, and know how to defend it.

A collection of news articles dated April 10–11, 2001, covers California’s energy crisis. A confidential California Independent System Operator study identified government-run utilities—including the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power, the Bonneville Power Administration, and Canada’s BC Hydro (Powerex)—as among the top entities earning alleged excess profits in the spot market from May to November 2000. Powerex led with $176.2 million, followed by Mirant with $96.8 million; the public agencies denied manipulating prices, stating they followed market rules. California lawmakers traveled to Idaho to urge the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to impose cost-based wholesale price caps, facing opposition from FERC Chairman Curt Hebert and Vice President Dick Cheney, who argued caps worsen supply problems, while some commissioners and Western states supported temporary controls. In the utilities’ divergent paths, Pacific Gas & Electric filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, while Southern California Edison reached a tentative $2.76 billion deal to sell its transmission lines to the state and supply low-cost power for 10 years to avoid bankruptcy. Other reports noted warnings from PUC President Loretta Lynch that further consumer rate hikes may be necessary, Governor Gray Davis’s executive order demanding business energy efficiency, and Spain drafting new electricity tariffs to avoid a “California experience.”
Takes advantage of opportunities, claims a better beard than Marshy, feels better after first Stanley Cup Finals experience, views every game as must win, wants to go back with a split.

A study published in the Journal of the American College of Cardiology found that over 99% of people who experienced first-time heart attacks, strokes, or heart failure had at least one nonoptimal cardiovascular risk factor—specifically high blood pressure, cholesterol, blood glucose, or a smoking history—and more than 93% had multiple risk factors. Researchers attribute the previously underreported prevalence of warning signs to doctors using higher “clinical” treatment thresholds rather than “optimal” health levels, which causes them to overlook modest but dangerous elevations. The findings were based on over 9.3 million people in South Korean cohorts and nearly 7,000 U.S. participants followed for 20 years. Experts note that the U.S. healthcare system invests far more in treatment than prevention, and addressing these common, nonoptimal risk factors earlier could prevent many serious cardiovascular events.
Admiral Harry Harris, the proposed ambassador to Australia, will instead become ambassador to South Korea amid critical negotiations over North Korea's nuclear weapons and the Korean War.

The Triangle and Two defense uses three players in a triangle zone and two chasers in full pass denial to stop two outstanding scorers or disrupt offenses. The triangle provides backside support against cuts and dribble penetration. Variations include double-teaming baseline and middle drives, combining with a chaser to defend strong post and outside players, and inverting the triangle against two-guard fronts. The chasers' pass denial is key to keeping the ball from the opponent's best scorers and disrupting set plays.

Former Oklahoma state schools superintendent Ryan Walters resigned to lead the national anti-union Teacher Freedom Alliance after a turbulent tenure that critics describe as a “microcosm” of the Trump administration’s education overhaul. From 2023 to 2025, Walters pursued aggressive culture-war policies, including mandating Bibles and Christian prayer in schools, targeting transgender student rights, partnering with conservative figures to rewrite social studies standards, monitoring teachers’ social media, and pushing immigration enforcement in schools. Though praised by right-wing groups for fighting “woke indoctrination,” his top-down edicts drew lawsuits, court blocks, bipartisan opposition, and fear among educators. Observers note that Education Secretary Linda McMahon is now applying similar tactics federally—targeting teachers, equity programs, and LGBTQ protections—while Walters, despite his vocal Trump loyalty, never secured a cabinet post. Critics argue his Oklahoma administration prioritized relentless ideological conflict over improving schools, previewing the federal “Project 2025” approach to education.

Hunter Greene, 17, was selected second overall by the Cincinnati Reds in the June 12, 2017 amateur draft. He is considered one of the most intriguing and marketable prospects in years, compared to Bryce Harper for his talent and charisma. As an African American who trained at MLB's Urban Youth Academy in Compton, he arrives as baseball faces declining African-American participation. Greene is a rare two-way prospect: a right-handed pitcher with a 102 mph fastball and a slugging shortstop. While the Reds drafted him primarily as a pitcher and plan to develop him slowly, they will allow him to take at-bats and keep open the possibility of field play. It may be years before he reaches the majors, but his unique combination of skills and cultural significance could give him an immediate impact on the sport.

The present disclosure describes methods and apparatuses for applying scheduling offsets and managing hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ) feedback and beam operations in next-generation wireless networks when a user equipment (UE) enters a power saving state. The UE receives a power saving signal, such as downlink control information (DCI) or radio resource control (RRC) signaling, indicating a minimum applicable scheduling offset (K0min) between a physical downlink control channel (PDCCH) and a physical downlink shared channel (PDSCH). The UE determines an application delay based on a predefined value and applies the minimum scheduling offset restriction after that delay; during the delay, a different offset configured by RRC may be used. After the delay, if a subsequent DCI provides an applicable offset larger than the minimum, the UE applies that offset; otherwise, it forgoes the minimum restriction. The UE sends HARQ feedback for the power saving signal after a time offset specified in the signal or via RRC. To prevent misalignment, the HARQ feedback bit for the power saving signal can be appended to the HARQ codebook for PDSCH receptions as the least or most significant bit, or transmitted on a dedicated physical uplink control channel (PUCCH) resource with independent codebook generation. For default beam operations, when the UE deactivates antenna panels in the power saving state, it selects spatial domain filters, sounding reference signal (SRS) resource sets, or transmission configuration indication (TCI) states associated with active panels for uplink transmissions. For a physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) scheduled by fallback DCI, the UE may use the spatial relation of an active PUCCH resource, the TCI state of the CORESET containing the DCI, or an SRS resource indicator in the DCI. If no dedicated PUCCH resource is configured, the UE uses the spatial domain information of the lowest-ID CORESET associated with an active panel. The base station ensures that scheduled offsets are larger than the indicated minimum values after the application delay.

Ohio State linebacker Arvell Reese is emerging as a potential top-10 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, a rare projection for an off-ball linebacker. The 6'3", 243-pound Reese is deployed across the front seven and possesses elite athleticism, play strength, and downhill burst, excelling as a run defender and quarterback spy. The longest woolly rhino horn ever found was recovered from Siberian permafrost and dated to roughly 19,600 years ago. At nearly the size of a small adult human and 30 centimeters longer than the previous record, it exceeds the horn length of any modern rhino species. Researchers believe it belonged to a female with a proportionally small skull. Counting seasonal keratin layers in the horn revealed the rhino lived at least 40 years—the oldest woolly rhino yet found—surpassing the maximum age of modern wild rhinos and matching the oldest captive individuals. The species' flattened, saberlike horns were likely used to brush away snow while feeding.

The lecture describes fusion trees, a static integer data structure for the word RAM that achieves O(log_w n) time for predecessor and successor queries. Combined with van Emde Boas trees, the two yield min(log w, log_w n) ≤ √log n. Invented by Fredman and Willard in 1990, the structure uses a B-tree-like node with branching factor w^(1/5). Because a node stores k = w^(1/5) keys of w bits each, the total bits exceed a single word, preventing standard constant-time comparisons. Instead, fusion trees use “sketching”: extracting at most k−1 “important bits” per key that preserve the order of the stored keys. A query proceeds by first comparing a sketch of the query against all stored sketches in parallel via word-level subtraction and borrow-bit analysis. Because an arbitrary query may diverge from the stored set, the algorithm finds the longest common prefix to locate the first mismatch, constructs a corrected query sketch, and searches again to find the true predecessor or successor. The lecture explains how to compute these approximate sketches in constant time using integer multiplication by a specially chosen multiplier to spread important bits into a small window without collisions. It also covers how to find the most significant set bit in constant time by splitting the word into √w clusters, identifying non-empty clusters, perfectly sketching the summary, and applying parallel comparison. Other variants discussed include AC0 RAM versions that avoid multiplication, dynamic versions using exponential search trees or hashing, and the open problem of achieving dynamic update bounds with high probability.

The Supreme Court relisted numerous cert petitions for its upcoming conference after a summer break, covering a wide array of legal issues. The cases include disputes over parental rights regarding gender identity in schools, religious accommodations under Title VII for COVID-19 vaccine mandates, Section 230 immunity for internet platforms, Seventh Amendment jury-trial rights in state administrative proceedings, termination of prospective prison relief under the Prison Litigation Reform Act, Federal Arbitration Act exemptions for local delivery workers transporting interstate goods, exceptions to criminal appeal waivers, Confrontation Clause limits on shielding child witnesses, public trial rights and tribal jurisdiction, the effect of presidential pardons on Jan. 6 prosecutions, FDA authority over stem cell procedures, unclaimed property and due process, qualified immunity for police, Brady violations in habeas cases, the Feres doctrine barring military tort claims, and Batson challenges to racially motivated jury strikes.
