This MIT lecture explains Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) methodology using a hand dryer study comparing the Dyson Airblade, the Xlerator, and paper towels. LCA evaluates environmental impacts of a product across its entire life cycle, differing from corporate-level carbon footprinting. The lecture details the four ISO-standardized LCA stages: goal and scope definition, inventory analysis, impact assessment, and interpretation. The study’s functional unit was one pair of dried hands, analyzed cradle-to-grave with system boundaries excluding capital goods and using cut-off rules for minor impacts. Because Dyson commissioned the study, it provided proprietary data, while competitor data came from public sources, requiring standardized assumptions—such as manufacturing location and five-year product lifetime based on warranty—that students critiqued. The inventory analysis used bills of materials and databases like ecoinvent, substituting proxy data where specific information was unavailable. Impact assessment included Global Warming Potential, water use, Cumulative Energy Demand, and the broader IMPACT 2002+ framework, which aggregates midpoint categories into indicators like human health and ecosystem quality. The interpretation phase involved extensive sensitivity and uncertainty analyses, including Monte Carlo simulations, to test assumptions such as electricity grid mix and hand-drying time. Despite some scenario overlap with the Xlerator, the analysis found the Dyson Airblade generally had the lowest environmental impact. The lecture emphasizes that LCA requires numerous value judgments and assumptions, particularly when used for comparative assertions or external marketing claims.

A Children's Rights Alliance report by DCU researchers examines homelessness's impact on children's education in the greater Dublin area. Parents choose between food and school travel costs. Children arrive hungry and in dirty clothes, rise early for long journeys, and fall asleep in class, with frequent absences. Homelessness affects mental health and behavior. The report recommends free school travel, ring-fenced school funding for meals, psychological assessments and homework clubs, accommodation near schools for families, and a six-month limit on emergency stays.

Andrew & Andrew family solicitors explain the legal process for terminating marriage or civil partnership in the UK, which requires a court order. Grounds include adultery (heterosexual only), unreasonable behaviour, desertion, and two- or five-year separation. Proceedings begin with a petition and a Statement of Arrangements for children. Uncomplicated cases may conclude within six months. They strive to resolve disputes in the best interest of children and follow the Resolution Code of Practice.

A study analyzed secondary data from a cross-sectional baseline survey and a randomized controlled open-label trial in Muheza, Tanzania, to determine malnutrition risk factors and evaluate the impact of intermittent preventive therapy for malaria (IPTsc) on the nutritional status of school-age children. Among 1,566 children aged 5–15 years randomized to dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (DP), artesunate-amodiaquine (ASAQ), or standard care and followed for 20 months, baseline malaria prevalence was 27%. In children aged ≤10 years, 23% were underweight, 21% were stunted, and 28% were thin or severely thin. Malaria infection was associated with 78% higher odds of stunting (adjusted odds ratio 1.78, 95% confidence interval 1.36–2.33, p<0.001), and low socioeconomic status was associated with higher odds of being underweight (AOR 1.50, 95% CI 1.13–2.01, p=0.006). Over the intervention period, changes in mean weight, height, and BMI did not differ significantly between the DP or ASAQ groups and the control group. The authors conclude that malaria and malnutrition represent a substantial double burden in this setting and recommend reinforcing nutritional programs alongside malaria control, as IPTsc alone did not improve nutritional status.

The NVIDIA Tesla T4 is a Turing-based inference accelerator for hyperscale data centers, enterprise solutions, and edge devices. It features 2,560 CUDA Cores and 320 Tensor Cores, delivering up to 130 TOPS (INT8) and 260 TOPS (INT4) inference performance. Compared to CPU-based inferencing, it offers up to 40X higher performance and over 50X greater energy efficiency, and up to twice the energy efficiency of the prior-generation Tesla P4.

The Turing architecture introduces multiple advancements, including an enhanced video engine supporting additional decode formats and significantly more concurrent streams than Pascal; improved Multi-Process Service for better small-batch inference performance and reduced latency; GDDR6 memory and larger L2 caches that provide approximately 50% higher effective bandwidth over Pascal; and a new display engine supporting 8K resolution, HDR, and VirtualLink for VR. Turing GPUs also include dedicated RT Cores that enable real-time ray tracing via hybrid rendering, and Tensor Cores that power AI-based features such as DLSS and NGX. Other new capabilities include Mesh Shading, Variable Rate Shading, Texture Space Shading, and Multi-View Rendering. The TU104 GPU—used in the Tesla T4, GeForce RTX 2080, and Quadro RTX 5000—contains 48 SMs, 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores. The TU106 (GeForce RTX 2070) has 36 SMs, 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, but does not support NVLink or SLI.

The Yankee concept is a pro-style shot play using a post-dig combination from opposite sides to attack 1-high safeties. Run primarily from heavier personnel sets to draw single-safety looks, it works well against Cover 1 and Cover 3 by high-low reading the free safety, but struggles against Cover 2 and Cover 4. Key routes include a Z-receiver post, an X-receiver dig at 15 yards, a tight end crossing at 5-6 yards, a fullback arrow at 3-4 yards, and a tailback flare. The quarterback reads post to dig to crosser to check-down, transitioning quickly to underneath routes against two-high shells. Variations include 2x2 formations with shallow crossers and whip routes underneath to clear throwing lanes.

A study in Science Advances suggests a worst-case "pulse" scenario—where warm water collapses Antarctic glaciers, raising seas 10–30 feet by 2100—may already be starting. Normally, holes in Antarctic ice cool and sink surface water, preventing glacier melt. But researchers found that in the Amundsen Sea and Sabrina Coast, melting glaciers are creating warm subsurface water pools that accelerate melting through a positive feedback loop. Reduced Antarctic bottom water could slow ocean currents, potentially causing superstorms and faster atmospheric warming. Scientists stress that stopping global temperature rise is critical to prevent ice shelf collapse.

A longitudinal study compared humoral and cellular immune responses to Covishield (ChAdOx-1 nCoV-19) and Covaxin (inactivated vaccine) in 691 Indian adults aged 18–45, stratified by baseline serostatus. Covishield induced significantly higher seroconversion rates than Covaxin in both seronegative (98.3% vs. 74.4% after two doses) and seropositive (91.7% vs. 66.9%) participants. Geometric mean titers of anti-spike and neutralizing antibodies were substantially higher following Covishield, and the vaccine elicited significant spike-specific CD4 and CD8 T cell responses in seronegative individuals, whereas Covaxin primarily induced CD4 responses and lacked significant CD8 T cell expansion. In seropositive participants, neither vaccine significantly increased T cell frequencies. Covishield demonstrated greater breadth against SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern, including Wild-Type and Delta, than Covaxin; neither vaccine elicited Omicron-specific responses in seronegative individuals, though a single Covishield dose in seropositive individuals did. The Omicron wave confounded durability assessments and likely caused asymptomatic breakthrough infections. Non-responsiveness in seropositive participants correlated with higher pre-vaccination antibody titers. The authors conclude that vectored vaccines elicit stronger and broader anti-spike responses than inactivated vaccines and suggest heterologous boosters and population immune history should inform future vaccine policy.

Pre-apprenticeship programs are proposed as a way to make selective construction apprenticeships more accessible to workers who lack pre-existing skills or need extra support. These short-term programs provide career exposure, skill-building, mentorship and industry credentials, but they remain limited due to insufficient funding and a lack of required outcomes tracking. To expand them, the author recommends financing wraparound supports such as childcare and transportation through income-contingent loans or credit, improving data collection on graduation and job placement, and using that evidence to attract grants and philanthropic investment. Partnerships among employers, unions, government and philanthropy are needed to strengthen construction career pathways, fill in-demand jobs and create best practices for other industries.

An AI tool called Waldo scanned over 430,000 Reddit posts about cannabis use and flagged more than 28,000 as potentially describing unexpected or harmful side effects. The tool could help public health workers monitor social media for adverse effects, supplementing traditional government surveillance. It remains unclear whether it would work as well for other drugs or products. Researchers suggest ethical future applications could flag rare side effects for health officials, especially in countries lacking robust drug monitoring systems.

Jorge Guerra Pires presents Robodoc, a prototype medical chatbot that integrates OpenAI large language models with specialized diagnostic models through API function calling. Built using Angular and TypeScript, the system processes user text or image inputs and intelligently routes them to the appropriate model: a TensorFlow.js model for diabetes detection from numerical data, and Teachable Machine transfer-learning models for chest X-ray (viral and bacterial pneumonia) and optical coherence tomography (Drusen, CNV, and DME) analysis. Results indicate good overall integration, with the diabetes and retinal models achieving high accuracy on most classes and the chatbot generally selecting the correct model and generating human-friendly responses. However, minor deviations occurred, including misclassification of normal lungs as pneumonia, lower accuracy for viral pneumonia, and occasional errors in urgency-based appointment scheduling for retinal conditions. The author concludes that combining public LLM APIs with transfer learning tools enables the construction of complex, low-cost medical chatbots without extensive research infrastructure, offering a user-friendly interface alternative for bioinformatics while emphasizing that such systems should assist rather than replace human clinicians.

The article backtests six swing trading indicators—Relative Strength Index (RSI), Internal Bar Strength (IBS), Stochastics, Bollinger Bands, WilliamsVixFix, and Williams %R—using the S&P 500 ETF (SPY). Swing trading involves holding positions from one day to a few weeks, with 1–15 days identified as the best time frame. The evaluation focuses on risk-adjusted return compared to maximum drawdown. The RSI strategy performed poorly since 2015 with a 30% drawdown in 2020. IBS showed reasonable results, Stochastic performed very well but may be curve fitted, Bollinger Bands had good returns with significant drawdowns, and WilliamsVixFix returned about 8.5% annually with high drawdowns. Williams %R is identified as the best indicator, particularly with a 10-day lookback, entry at -90, and exit at -80, yielding about a three-day holding time, the lowest average maximum drawdown, and only two negative years since 1993.

This continuation application of U.S. application Ser. No. 17/684,607 and prior Korean applications discloses methods and apparatus for video signal encoding and decoding. The invention aims to improve intra-prediction and inter-prediction efficiency and reduce overhead during brightness changes such as fade-in or fade-out. Solutions include determining whether a current block merges with a neighbor block to use identical motion information and a weight prediction parameter; if not merged, the parameter is obtained from or encoded into a bitstream. Motion vector precision may be upwardly adjusted based on reconstructed pixels adjacent to the current block. For intra-prediction, an apparatus decodes mode information, generates prediction samples, and determines whether to correct them using correction coefficients derived from similar previously encoded blocks based on standard deviations of reconstructed pixel areas. Intra-prediction modes may be determined from candidate modes based on usage frequency in upper or left neighbor blocks, or from a difference value relative to a previous block. The encoding apparatus includes a video dividing unit, prediction, transform, quantization, rearrange, entropy encoding, dequantization, inverse-transform, filter, and memory units; the decoding apparatus reverses these processes. Weight prediction parameters may also be derived via regression analysis of reconstructed pixels, and prediction may be performed on sub-blocks divided from the current block.

NVIDIA’s Turing architecture introduces RT Cores and enhanced Tensor Cores, enabling real-time hybrid rendering that combines ray tracing, rasterization, and AI. The enhanced Tensor Cores support FP16, INT8, and INT4 precision, accelerating deep learning inference and training as well as NVIDIA NGX neural graphics features including Deep Learning Super Sampling (DLSS), AI InPainting, AI Super Rez, and AI Slow-Mo. The Tesla T4 data center GPU, featuring an enhanced video engine and Multi-Process Service (MPS), delivers up to 130 TOPS of INT8 and 260 TOPS of INT4 performance, providing up to 40× higher inference throughput and 50× greater energy efficiency than CPU-based inferencing.

Turing is the first GPU architecture to use GDDR6 memory, offering 14 Gbps signaling with 20% better power efficiency than GDDR5X, alongside larger L2 caches—6 MB in the TU102—and improved lossless compression that yields roughly 50% higher effective memory bandwidth over Pascal. The architecture includes an enhanced display engine supporting 8K at 60 Hz, DisplayPort 1.4a with VESA DSC 1.2, native HDR tone mapping, and an NVENC encoder that supports H.265 8K encode at 30 fps with bitrate savings while exceeding software x264 fast-preset quality at lower CPU utilization; the NVDEC decoder adds HEVC 4:4:4 and VP9 10/12-bit support. For VR, Turing offers hardware support for USB-C and VirtualLink, Multi-View Rendering (MVR), and foveated rendering via Variable Rate Shading.

New programmable shading technologies include Mesh Shading with Task and Mesh Shaders to eliminate CPU draw-call bottlenecks, Variable Rate Shading (VRS) for dynamic per-region shading-rate control, and Texture Space Shading to decouple visibility and appearance sampling. RT Cores in the TU102, TU104, and TU106 accelerate bounding volume hierarchy traversal and ray/triangle intersection, making real-time ray tracing approximately 10× faster than Pascal and enabling physically correct shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections through hybrid rendering and denoising.

The TU104 GPU incorporates 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores with second-generation NVLink, while the TU106 (GeForce RTX 2070) includes 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores but no NVLink or SLI. NVIDIA defines RTX-OPS as a workload-based metric that blends peak tensor, CUDA, ray-tracing, and integer operations to measure hybrid rendering performance.

This paper introduces 3DPCNet, a pose-only, estimator-agnostic rectification module that maps camera-centered 3D human poses to a fixed body-centered canonical frame. The architecture employs a hybrid encoder with parallel graph convolutional and transformer branches fused via gated cross-attention, predicting a continuous 6D global rotation converted to SO(3) via Gram-Schmidt orthonormalization and an optional residual joint correction. Trained using self-supervised synthetic pose rotation with a composite loss, the module reduces MM-Fi rotation error from 20–22° to 3–4° and MPJPE by approximately 27%, generalizing across subjects and environments. On TotalCapture, canonicalized poses yield wrist acceleration signals that closely match synchronized IMU ground truth, outperforming a geometric baseline. The results demonstrate that pose-only canonicalization substantially diminishes viewpoint-induced variability and produces kinematic trajectories suitable for longitudinal analysis in rehabilitation, sports science, and VR training.

New federal tax law changes to payroll withholding tables will result in extra cash in paychecks for about 90% of workers beginning in February, with amounts varying based on income, filing status, dependents, and W-4 allowances. A married couple earning $90,000 with two children could see approximately $61 more per semi-monthly paycheck, while a single person earning $35,000 with no children could see about $32 more. The child tax credit doubled to $2,000 per qualifying child under 17. Employers must adopt new tables by February 15. A revised W-4 form is expected by early spring, and taxpayers may need to adjust withholding due to increased standard deductions and changes to itemized deductions, including a $10,000 cap on state and local taxes and the elimination of home equity loan interest deductions. The IRS will release an updated withholding calculator by February's end. Withholding on supplemental wages, including bonuses, dropped from 25% to 22%.

Christian Brothers four-star defensive lineman Bill Norton committed to Georgia. The 6-foot-6, 270-pound TSSAA Mr. Football is ranked 11th among strong-side defensive ends by 247Sports and chose Georgia over Alabama, LSU, Tennessee, and others.

The growth of online education in African universities since the 1990s, driven by ICT adoption and flexible higher education policies, faces challenges including low internet penetration (47%), weak infrastructure, limited affordability, inadequate faculty digital skills, and a rural-urban digital divide. Over three-quarters of African nations have experienced warfare in the last three decades, disrupting higher education through infrastructure destruction, casualties, brain drain, and displacement. While online education could sustain learning during conflicts, African universities struggle with ICT deployment in wartime.

This study conducted a bibliometric analysis of Scopus publications from 2000 to 2024 on wartime and online education. From 90 initial documents, 53 were analyzed. Publications originated from ten countries, led by the United States (21) and Ukraine (10), with no African countries represented. Further screening for wartime, education, and online learning yielded only five publications across three countries (Ukraine, Austria, and the United States). Publication trends increased over time, peaking at 12 in 2023. Most documents were articles (76.9%) in social sciences (55%). Keyword co-occurrence analysis identified two clusters: learning (e-learning, online teaching, university teachers) and warfare (students, teachers, Ukraine, war).

The findings highlight a significant research gap regarding wartime online education in Africa. The study concludes that urgent research is needed to develop strategies for conflict-affected African higher education institutions, support organizational sustainability, and align with Sustainable Development Goals. A limitation is the exclusive use of the Scopus database. Future research should investigate conflict-related brain drain, psychological trauma, and inclusive online learning for people with disabilities in African universities.

Dick Tuck, a Democratic operative who made a career of political pranks targeting Richard Nixon, has died at 94 in Tucson, Arizona. Tuck, who began pranking Nixon as a college student in 1950 by sabotaging a campaign appearance, specialized in stunts including posing as a fire marshal to deflate crowd estimates, planting a supporter to console Nixon after a 1960 debate, and infiltrating a 1962 Chinatown rally with a Chinese-language sign questioning a Howard Hughes loan to Nixon's brother. He also worked on Robert F. Kennedy's 1968 campaign and ran unsuccessfully for California Senate in 1966. Tuck maintained his Nixon animus into his 90s, proposing that the date of Nixon's resignation be declared a national holiday.

Mathieu Henderson capped his four-year OHL career with a breakout season, finishing ninth among defencemen with 10 goals and 44 assists for the Flint Firebirds. The 21-year-old Brantford native began his career in Plymouth before the team relocated to Flint, and in his final season improved his plus/minus from minus-45 to minus-7 while focusing on defence. After the Firebirds were eliminated from the opening playoff round, he played three games with the ECHL's South Carolina Stingrays. Henderson is considering professional hockey in North America or Europe, or attending school, and credited his parents, Randy and Brenda, for their support.

Glenn Ellison begins by reviewing VCG mechanisms, noting they implement utilitarian social choice solutions in dominant strategies but are not budget balanced and can be computationally infeasible for large action spaces. He then turns to Google’s dominance in online search and its highly profitable advertising system. For each query, Google runs a generalized second-price auction: advertisers submit per-click bids, which are multiplied by quality scores; ads are ranked by this product, and winners pay the lowest bid needed to maintain their position. Quality scores are essential to prevent irrelevant but high-profit ads from winning unrelated queries.

Citing Edelman, Ostrovsky, and Schwarz, Ellison explains that although Google’s auction is not a VCG mechanism and truth-telling is not an equilibrium, strategic bid shading results in equilibrium payments that exactly replicate VCG payments. This yields an ex-post equilibrium, ensures efficiency, and means Google cannot be undercut on price without selecting worse ads. He next summarizes Athey-Ellison, which incorporates consumer search costs into the model. Reserve prices can signal ad quality and improve welfare rather than reduce it; under uniform search costs, consumer surplus and social welfare are maximized at the same reserve price, and any departure from it harms both consumers and advertisers. Finally, he briefly notes Anderson and Renault’s work on endogenous pricing in position auctions, which can produce multiple equilibria, and Armstrong and Zhou’s analysis of platform information design, where revealing too much information about consumer-product matches reduces price competition and makes the fully consumer-optimal outcome unattainable.

The civil aviation ministry has requested a two-month deferral of the July 1 GST rollout, stating that airlines need more time to update their systems and citing concerns over unclear tax rules and higher operational costs. The finance ministry has rejected rumors of a delay, affirming that the implementation remains on track.

The passage describes embodiments for managing indexed data and optimizing index file sizes based on storage conditions. It details a data intake and query system, exemplified by the SPLUNK® ENTERPRISE system, that collects, indexes, and searches machine-generated data stored as timestamped events. The system architecture includes forwarders that receive and forward data, indexers that parse, timestamp, and index events, and search heads that process queries using a late-binding schema with extraction rules applied at search time. The document outlines data ingestion, distributed query processing, field extraction from disparate sources, hierarchical data models for report generation, and acceleration techniques such as keyword indexes, summarization tables, and intermediate report summaries. It further describes security features for detecting notable events, data center monitoring for virtualized environments, and cloud-based system deployments.

The IRS announced higher federal income tax brackets for 2026 to adjust for inflation. The standard deduction will rise to $32,200 for married couples filing jointly and $16,100 for single taxpayers. The top 37% rate applies to individuals above $640,600 and joint filers above $768,700. Changes also affect capital gains, estate tax, and tax credits. The announcement followed news that the IRS would furlough nearly half its workforce due to a government shutdown.

Egyptian archaeologists unveiled the tomb of Hetpet, a Fifth Dynasty priestess to Hathor, on the Giza plateau. The tomb features an L-shaped shrine and rare wall paintings depicting hunting, fishing, musical, and monkey scenes, plus a basin engraved with her name. Antiquities Minister Khaled al-Enany noted a 1909 German expedition found antiquities bearing her name. Excavations continue.

This study examined hippocampal perineuronal nets (PNNs) and related gene expression in postmortem samples from subjects with substance use disorder (SUD), major depressive disorder (MDD), comorbid SUD/MDD, and psychiatrically normal controls, as well as in rhesus monkeys with chronic alcohol self-administration. Subjects with SUD showed significantly increased numerical densities of PNNs in hippocampal CA1 stratum oriens and other subregions, alongside increased parvalbumin and VAMP2 mRNA, decreased matrix metalloproteinase 9 and cathepsin S expression, and increased WFA-labeled glial cells. Rhesus monkeys with chronic alcohol use also displayed increased hippocampal PNNs and WFA-glia. In contrast, subjects with MDD generally showed decreased PNN densities and opposing molecular changes, while subjects with comorbid SUD/MDD often lacked the SUD-specific differences or showed altered patterns, suggesting MDD modifies extracellular matrix pathology in SUD. The authors conclude that increased hippocampal PNNs may stabilize contextual reward memories in SUD, representing potential therapeutic targets for cue-induced relapse, and emphasize the importance of considering comorbid MDD in SUD neuropathology and treatment strategies.

The passage defines the SEV-ES and SEV-SNP Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol. It specifies GHCBData fields for the GHCB guest physical address, which must be 4K aligned, maximum and minimum GHCB protocol versions, the SEV page table encryption bit number, and CPUID request and response values. The hypervisor writes initial SEV information and capabilities before the GHCB address is established; the guest selects a protocol version, determines the encryption bit position to build page tables, allocates a GHCB page, and registers its guest physical address via MSR protocol before using VMGEXIT.

The document details standard and exception-based Non-Automatic Exit (NAE) event processing. Guests copy register state to the GHCB, set the VALID_BITMAP, and invoke VMGEXIT; hypervisors return results or errors in SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2. Supported NAE events include IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, MMIO access using a shared buffer, Page State Change operations, SNP Guest Request, SNP Extended Guest Request for certificates, SNP TIO Guest Request for trusted devices, AP Creation using VMSA pages, #HV Doorbell Page registration and management, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer configuration, APIC ID List retrieval, SNP Run VMPL, Secure AVIC backing page registration, and Termination Request.

For SMP booting, SEV-ES uses AP Reset Hold and AP Jump Tables; SEV-SNP adds SNP AP Creation via VMSA pages, which also enables vCPU hotplug. The hypervisor must not update AP registers after their initial measured state. NMI handling requires the guest to issue an NMI Complete message; full hardware debug register virtualization is supported where available. System Management Mode and nested virtualization are unsupported.

For SEV-SNP with Restricted Injection, the hypervisor signals events through a shared #HV doorbell page. The PendingEvent field indicates interrupt vectors, NMI, and machine check events, while NoEoiRequired allows optimized end-of-interrupt processing without exiting the guest. Hosts present the highest-priority ready interrupt and manage non-maskable events; guests atomically exchange PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired to acknowledge interrupts and perform end-of-interrupt cycles.

The passage describes systems and methods for analyzing medical images to localize, classify, and detect abnormalities. In one aspect, a multi-task network jointly trains a localization network and a classification network in multiple phases to localize and classify lesions, with variants including a multi-modality fusion network for multi-parametric MRI and a regression network to score lesions. In another aspect, abnormalities are detected by deleting portions of an input image to generate incomplete images, synthesizing replacement portions via a trained generative adversarial network to create synthesized images, determining a normal image from the synthesized images, and detecting the abnormality by comparing the input image and the normal image. In a further aspect, deep learning models are trained on multi-site datasets by iteratively updating a pretrained model with sub-datasets reordered by similarity to a primary dataset, then optimized for a deployment site using deployment data reordered by uncertainty.

Two TPS7H500x-SP controllers can operate in primary-secondary mode via the SYNC pin. The primary outputs a clock at twice the switching frequency to the secondary via its SYNC pin, while its RT pin is populated and the secondary's RT pin left floating. This synchronizes two independent converters with no other connections, or creates an interleaved parallel converter by connecting VSENSE, COMP, SS, and HICC. The secondary inverts the clock, causing a 90° or 270° phase shift between corresponding outputs.

The speaker noted little difference from Anaheim but said the team failed to play its game while the opponent executed its plan and capitalized on a power play. A reviewed goal was disallowed by Toronto, which the team must accept, and they must move on.

SOS full court pressures include primary "shadow" scenarios (Back, Up, Face), where a second defender shadows the on-ball defender, and secondary "Blitz" pressures that deny first passing lanes and trap deep. They aim to create turnovers, rushed shots, fatigue, and tempo changes while removing the ball from playmakers. Execution requires forcing the ball to the sidelines, denying middle penetration, and applying basic SOS fundamentals. All scenarios except "hold" end in Base Go Red. Pressure is abandoned if the shadow player is out of position or a deep or middle outlet pass occurs, reverting to half-court defense.

The University of Virginia Health System's thoracic Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) program, launched in early 2016, reduced morphine use by 59-74 percent without compromising pain control, decreased median hospital stays by two days for thoracotomy patients, and saved over $1.3 million in its first year while freeing beds for approximately 28 additional patients. The program enrolled 139 patients and compared them to over 220 previous patients, showing benefits without increasing complications or readmissions. The initiative incorporates preoperative preparation, nutritional optimization, avoidance of excessive intravenous fluids, and minimized opioid use. Researchers published findings in the Annals of Thoracic Surgery and plan continued evaluation.

AMD shares surged on an AI chip deal with OpenAI, while gold rallied above $3,900/oz amid a weaker yen and U.S. rate cut bets. Evercore’s Emanuel projected a bubble scenario could lift the S&P 500 to 9,000 by 2026. Culpeper defeated Courtland 2-1 in a nondistrict baseball game defined by defensive miscues. The Department of Education will delay two Obama-era rules set to take effect July 1 that would have held for-profit colleges accountable and protected borrowers through gainful employment standards and loan forgiveness for defrauded students. Critics argue the rules burden colleges; a California for-profit group sued to block one rule, while Democratic attorneys general and senators opposed the delay. Hearings will occur in July.

The primary objective of an offensive goal kick is to retain possession and create an attack. A goal kick is taken from the Goal Area when the ball crosses the end line last touched by an attacker; opponents must stay outside the Penalty Area until the kick, and the ball is live once kicked and visibly moves (Law 16). For youth aged 10 and under, build-out lines require defenders to retreat, and teams are often forced to build up from the back; the simplest approaches involve a designated kicker at the outermost goal area corner passing to a dribbler or target receiver up the sideline, while emphasizing keeping the ball wide and never sending it across the own goal. For players 11 and older, progressions add secondary and midfielder targets, with the kicker selecting the open receiver or kicking short to covered targets to create space. At adult levels, the goalkeeper usually takes the kick, using short passes or deep kicks to targets. A goal kick is a direct restart, and field conditions like wind can dramatically affect the outcome.

A JRF study states a UK working couple with two children needs £40,000 annually for a decent living, requiring each parent to earn £20,000, up from £13,900 in 2008, while a single person needs £18,400, up from £13,400 a decade ago. The author argues redistribution is unworkable as only about 30% of households earn above £40,000. The author instead proposes raising the personal allowance to £18,400, taxing couples separately, reducing childcare and housing regulation, and pursuing economic growth through lower taxation and less government.
Researchers are testing whether supplemental income for new mothers improves babies' brain and emotional development in the first three years, potentially changing views on poverty's effects.

This prospective, descriptive cross-sectional study examined 165 scorpion sting patients admitted to Tesseney Community Hospital in Eritrea’s western lowlands from June 2019 to May 2020. The cohort had an almost equal male-to-female ratio, with 61.2% older than 15 years and 57% from urban areas. Most stings occurred at night (62.4%), indoors (56.4%), on the foot (64.8%), during summer (93%), and involved black scorpions (38.8%). The case fatality rate was 4.8%. Common manifestations included localized pain (70.3%), sweating (56.4%), and vomiting (33.9%). Using Abroug’s classification, 43.6% of cases were class III (severe), 35.8% class II, and 20.6% class I. Children under 15 years and patients with no formal education showed possible predisposing factors for severe symptoms or death. The high proportion of class III cases was attributed to delayed hospital presentation among adults who initially relied on home remedies. Management included local anesthesia, oral analgesics, diazepam, and nifedipine and/or scorpion antivenom for moderate-to-severe cases. The study was limited to a single hospital without post-discharge follow-up, and essential medications were sometimes unavailable. The authors conclude that while adults bear a higher burden, envenomation severity is greater in children. They recommend preventive education, improved care-seeking behavior, equipping facilities with essential drugs such as prazosin, and further research on scorpion habitats and species.

Project Sashakat, a Finance Ministry-endorsed five-pronged strategy for faster NPA resolution, recommends asset management companies and steering committees to resolve bad loans. Accounts over Rs 500 crore would use an AMC/AIF-led approach, while loans up to Rs 50 crore would use a templatised SME Resolution Approach within 90 days. The strategy includes inter-creditor arrangements requiring 66 percent lender approval, aims to attract foreign capital, proposes an asset trading platform, and does not recommend a bad bank.

The random walk trading strategy, popularized by Burton Malkiel in *A Random Walk Down Wall Street*, is based on the theory that stock prices move unpredictably and independently of historical data, rendering traditional analysis futile. The strategy assumes a 50% probability of prices rising or falling and emphasizes risk diversification through broad market index funds or varied stock portfolios rather than attempting to time the market. Like the Efficient Market Hypothesis, it suggests consistently outperforming the market is nearly impossible, though the two differ in that EMH assumes market efficiency while random walk assumes irrational randomness. Backtests showed random entries in the S&P 500 produced positive results due to long-term market drift, while a gold ETF backtest yielded negative returns. The approach ultimately supports passive investing to mitigate risk.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced an agreement to build a Qatari Emiri Air Force facility at Mountain Home Air Force Base in Idaho, where Qatari F-15 pilots will train with American personnel. The base currently hosts Singaporean F-15s for training. Qatari Defense Minister Sheikh Saoud bin Abdulrahman al-Thani met with Hegseth at the Pentagon on October 10, 2025, reflecting deepening Trump administration-Qatar ties.

Official car mpg figures based on the outdated NEDC test are unreliable due to loopholes allowing unrealistic conditions, such as disabled ancillaries, removed parts, eco modes, and arbitrary result reductions. From September 2017, the tougher WLTP replaced NEDC, with full compliance required by September 2018. Which? conducts lab tests using WLTP with cold and hot cycles, plus a sustained motorway cycle, while maintaining realistic conditions including default driving modes, air conditioning and lights on, and unmodified vehicles. Which? also measures emissions and verifies suspicious NOx results using Portable Emissions Measuring Systems on real roads. The organisation has published real mpg data for over 700 cars.

The report, submitted February 15, 1893, details United States policy toward Hawaii from 1820 onward, documenting consistent opposition to foreign aggression and protection of American interests. It records repeated contemplation of annexation, including a proposed protectorate in 1850, a contingent deed of cession in 1851, a draft treaty in 1854, and advocacy by Secretaries Seward and Fish and Presidents Johnson and Grant from 1867 to 1873. After the 1875 reciprocity treaty, the United States asserted exclusive commercial rights and supported the Hawaiian government. In 1881, Secretary Blaine called the islands key to the American Pacific and stated the United States would seek an avowedly American solution if benevolent neutrality failed.

This study examines how U.S. college teaching modalities—in-person, hybrid, and online—affected county-level COVID-19 cases and deaths. Using a quasi-experimental design that matches comparable colleges and addresses endogeneity in reopening decisions, the authors find that college reopening, especially in-person instruction, increased infections and deaths in surrounding communities relative to remote options. The methodology incorporates staggered reopening dates, cellphone mobility data, and re-weighting based on modality selection likelihood. County-level outcomes are used to assess community transmission risks from students to non-students.

Anthurium, a South American plant with red, pink, or white flowers, filters indoor ammonia and xylene. It needs indirect light, dampness, 18°C–21°C temperatures, winter leaf spraying, and regular repotting; its sap may cause allergies.

French President Macron visited Nigeria to discuss the G-5 Sahel, intelligence sharing against Boko Haram, and witness an MoU for a French agricultural project creating about 150,000 jobs. Global genomic sequencing is highly uneven, with 90% of SARS-CoV-2 sequences originating from 10% of countries as of July 2022, rendering standard country-specific regression methods unreliable where data are sparse. The authors present a hierarchical Bayesian multinomial model that jointly estimates variant dynamics by partially pooling information across countries and variants. This approach yields country-specific variant proportions, growth rates, and global relative fitness advantages while shrinking extreme estimates toward shared means to reduce overfitting. Applied to SARS-CoV-2 variants including BA.4 and BA.5, the model captured heterogeneous invasion dynamics across nations. Retrospective validation against single-country multinomial models demonstrated that the multicountry approach provides more stable fitness estimates, better calibrated uncertainty, and lower Brier scores during early emergence, even generating estimates for countries before local observation of a variant. The framework is generalizable to other pathogens and subnational scales and is intended to support low- and middle-income countries with limited sequencing capacity, complementing investments in global surveillance infrastructure. Key assumptions include random sampling, correct lineage assignment, and constant generation intervals across variants.

An IDC survey of 200 industrial enterprises in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland found that advances in IT have expanded usage scenarios for manufacturing, with more than half of decision makers already using simulation, modeling, and virtual prototyping, and 42% using high-performance data analytics. High-performance computing is viewed as a game changer for product and process innovation by 81% of respondents, rising to 96% among those that have already implemented it, because it enables complex calculations, improves quality and intensity of use, unlocks new scenarios, and increases innovation and agility. Currently, over a quarter of enterprises use professional HPC infrastructures and 39% plan or are piloting deployment, while 15% are not engaging with it. Most prefer external solutions: 87% favor cloud or other external HPC infrastructures, and 74% operate or plan to use colocation datacenters, whereas only 6% have on-premises HPC. Major challenges include security concerns cited by 72%, high energy consumption and sustainability cited by 58%, and lack of internal and external expertise cited by 42%. Cloud-based and hybrid HPC architectures are expected to become the most important models, offering scalability, flexibility, and cost optimization. HPC as a Service is seen as beneficial for accessing modern hardware, supporting global collaboration, and enabling new data-based business models without large upfront investments. IDC recommends establishing virtual product development, devising a holistic data strategy centered on a single source of truth, evaluating suitable HPC operating models, selecting scalable and energy-efficient solutions, and leveraging external expertise.

WIRED's Zoë Schiffer and Manisha Krishnan review recent stories, including the US government shutdown, during which federal agencies distributed politicized messaging—such as out-of-office templates and website banners—blaming Democrats for the closure, a move that may violate the Hatch Act. They discuss a report on Peter Thiel’s lectures about the Antichrist and doomsday theory, influenced by the writings of Carl Schmitt, and an awkward interview where journalist Ross Douthat questioned the irony of Thiel’s surveillance technology investments given those fears. Additionally, they note that scientists created human eggs from skin cells and used them to form embryos, a development that could offer alternatives to IVF but raises ethical concerns. Finally, they discuss OpenAI’s launch of Sora 2, a standalone social app for AI-generated videos that resembles TikTok, where identity verification creates user avatars; the app has content guardrails and inconsistent copyright blocks, and its current feed largely features OpenAI employees and CEO Sam Altman.

Nick Kyrgios will play John Isner in Friday's second singles rubber of Australia's Davis Cup quarter-final against the United States in Brisbane; both are among the season's ace leaders. Jack Sock faces Jordan Thompson in the opener. Sam Groth and John Peers meet Sam Querrey and Steve Johnson in Saturday's doubles ahead of Sunday's reverse singles. Isner leads Kyrgios 2-1; Sock has never played Kyrgios. Thompson replaces Bernard Tomic, who declined to play. Lleyton Hewitt was confident in Thompson.

On January 25, 2022, Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K furnishing a press release as Exhibit 99.1 that announced financial results for the fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2021. The information is not deemed filed under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. Alice L. Jolla, Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer, signed the report.

John Clarke, Michel Devoret, and John Martinis won the 2025 Nobel Prize in physics for demonstrating quantum tunneling and energy quantization in an electric circuit during the 1980s. Their experiments with Josephson junctions showed quantum effects at a macroscopic scale, laying the foundation for superconducting qubits used in quantum computers. The three researchers will share the 11 million Swedish kronor prize.

On October 30, 2001, Enron Corp. shares fell to eight-year lows, dropping as much as 20 percent to around $11, after Moody's Investors Service lowered the company's long-term debt rating to Baa2, two notches above junk status, and placed its commercial paper rating on review for downgrade. The company, which lost approximately $15 billion in market capitalization over two weeks, was lobbying banks for new credit lines after tapping existing facilities and being shut out of the commercial paper market. Bond default insurance premiums doubled, while Enron's 6.4 percent bonds due in 2006 fell to 74 cents on the dollar. The declines followed disclosures of $1.01 billion in third-quarter losses, a $1.2 billion reduction in stockholders' equity, and concerns over $3.3 billion in liabilities from off-balance-sheet partnerships managed by dismissed CFO Andrew Fastow, which are under SEC investigation. Major utility trading partners including AEP, Exelon, and Northeast Utilities stated they continued trading with Enron while closely monitoring credit exposure. The NYMEX board approved a new over-the-counter clearing service for natural gas contracts to mitigate counterparty credit concerns. Separately, new Enron CFO Jeff McMahon said the company's industrial markets forest products unit expected monthly newsprint trading volumes to reach 120,000 metric tons by year-end and would maintain capital despite the parent company's struggles. Germany's cartel office also said it may sue four utilities over balancing energy charges affecting new market entrants including Enron Capital & Resources.

The passage describes the MSPM0 G-Series 80MHz microcontrollers (MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, MSPM0G1518). It details the Power Management Unit (PMU) with brown-out reset and core regulator modes; the Clock Module (CKM) with multiple internal and external oscillators and distributed system clocks; a DMA controller supporting 12 channels and various transfer sizes; an event manager routing peripheral events to the CPU, DMA, or other peripherals; non-volatile flash memory up to 512kB with ECC and 1kB sectors; up to 128kB dual-bank SRAM with ECC and write-execute partitioning; up to 93 GPIOs with wake and FastWake features; IOMUX pad configuration; two 12-bit ADCs with 4Msps and hardware averaging; an internal temperature sensor; a configurable VREF; comparators; a 12-bit DAC with FIFO and DMA; security features including AES-128/256, firewalls, secure key storage, CRC, TRNG, and an AESADV accelerator; a MATHACL hardware accelerator; UART, I2C, SPI, and CAN-FD interfaces; a Low-Frequency Sub System with RTC and independent watchdog; a windowed watchdog; general-purpose and advanced timers; serial wire debug; a boot strap loader with password protection; factory constants; and recommended application schematics. It also lists development tools, documentation support, a revision history updating specifications and adding package variants, and mechanical packaging information.

Scotiabank's 1832 Asset Management LP will pay an $800,000 fine and $150,000 in costs under an Ontario Securities Commission settlement for improperly providing lavish promotional benefits to financial advisers from 2012 to 2017. The firm has begun improving its compliance practices.

The Open Source Definition was published in early February 1998, when Christine Peterson proposed "open source" as a business-friendly alternative to "free software." Though founders cite different dates, the movement promoted the same principles of accessible source code and user freedom with more moderate messaging. Major technology companies and platforms now rely on open source. Microsoft notably reversed its former hostility, when CEO Steve Ballmer likened Linux to cancer in 2001. Red Hat's Tim Burke notes open source has shifted from cloning proprietary products to leading innovation.

The document specifies design parameters and layout guidelines for the TPS7H500x-SP controller. An 80-V GaN FET was selected for synchronous rectification despite an approximate 20-V maximum expected stress, with a parallel Schottky diode to reduce soft-start current and reverse conduction losses. An RCD clamp limits switch node overshoot based on KCLAMP, leakage inductance, and peak primary current. The output inductor is 0.47 µH with 40% ripple current. Output capacitance requires at least 1.3 mF, but 2.3 mF was implemented using seven 330-µF polymer tantalum capacitors to mitigate radiation-induced single event transients; an additional LC filter reduces output ripple, with a damping resistor for high-frequency peaking. Cycle-by-cycle limiting activates at approximately 35 A, using a 7.5-Ω current sense resistor. A 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor and a 102-kΩ slope compensation resistor are used. Frequency compensation employs Type 2A components (40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, 47 pF) targeting a 10 kHz crossover. The controller accepts a 4-V to 14-V input and requires a minimum 0.1-µF bypass capacitor. Layout guidelines recommend routing feedback away from power magnetics, minimizing switch node area, separating analog and power grounds at a single point, placing bypass capacitors close to the controller, routing high dv/dt signals away from sensitive pins, and connecting the CFP backside metallization to AVSS. The package is hermetically sealed with a metal lid and gold-plated leads.

Energy storage is widely promoted as a solution for integrating renewable energy, but it carries capital and running costs that must be outweighed by savings. Different technologies suit different scales: lithium ion batteries work well for small-scale distributed applications but are currently expensive, while pumped hydro is inexpensive and efficient for large-scale grid management. Lithium ion costs are falling, yet a home battery needs to cost roughly A$1,000 per kWh installed to break even under current variable retail rates; if retailers switch to flat rates, the required cost drops to about A$300 per kWh. Reducing peak demand with batteries only avoids network infrastructure costs if overall electricity demand is growing, which has not been true since 2009 despite a recent rebound. Although pumped hydro is already cost-effective and easier for market operators to control, distributed lithium ion batteries may ultimately prevail due to consumer behavior, similar to rooftop solar.

On August 3, 2020, Apple Inc. filed an amendment to its Restated Articles of Incorporation with the California Secretary of State, increasing authorized common stock from 12,600,000,000 to 50,400,000,000 shares and effecting a 4-for-1 automatic stock split at 5 p.m. PDT on August 28, 2020.

Bitcoin futures began trading on Cboe Global Markets' exchange, adding momentum to a recent price surge but drawing mixed reactions from financial institutions. The cash-settled contracts, based on Gemini Exchange prices, offer a regulated alternative to the spot market, though Interactive Brokers is limiting short positions and margin, while Charles Schwab, TD Ameritrade, JPMorgan Chase, and Citigroup are restricting or delaying participation; Goldman Sachs will clear trades for certain clients. Proponents suggest futures may eventually reduce volatility and improve price discovery, but analysts warn of significant risks, including inaccurate pricing, systemic threats to clearing houses, margin call failures, and potential manipulation of the underlying spot market.

Bernstorff wrote that the blockade would end if a conference could be arranged, and transmitted German and Austro-Hungarian notes of January 31, 1917, on new naval warfare zones. Ambassador Gerard reported Zimmermann delivered submarine documents and said Bernstorff would confidentially urge the President to make peace, claiming Germany could compel England to terms within two months and warning of confrontation by Japan and other yellow races. The Greek Government announced an Entente concession allowing indispensable victuals pending the blockade's end. The German Chancellor reportedly demanded Belgian guarantees, French territory, limited Serbian restoration, and indemnities. Austria-Hungary's Foreign Minister expressed desire to maintain U.S. relations, stated submarine warfare could not be modified, and urged Wilson to influence the Entente to accept "peace without victory" rather than pursue Austria-Hungary's dismemberment.

The paper studies Gorenstein-projective modules over Z[ε] = Z[T]/(T²), where the category G-proj Z[ε] is equivalent to torsionless modules, perfect differential structures, and orbits of bounded complexes of free abelian groups, but lacks the Krull-Remak-Schmidt property. The main theorem proves that the stable category modulo projectives is equivalent to the stable category of submodules of free modules, the orbit category D^b(Z)/[1], and homotopy and stable categories of perfect differential structures. It also presents a chain from bounded complexes of free abelian groups to finite abelian groups and a commutative cube.

An Irish Times article features Ernest Walton, 1951 Nobel winner, in a Trinity College Dublin lab. It describes him as quiet and shy, noting his refusal to leave Ireland and his 1930s work smashing the atom nucleus at Cambridge. Its downbeat tone contrasts with scientific hype. Jack McManus's photograph gives equal visual status to Walton and his machine. It promotes Irish Times images and a book by Arminta Wallace.

The Korean diet is based on traditional Korean eating habits, emphasizing whole, unprocessed foods such as fresh vegetables, whole grains, lean proteins, and fermented foods including kimchi and doenjang. It limits processed foods, sugary drinks, unhealthy fats, and dairy. The diet is high in fiber and low in calories and saturated fat, offering benefits such as improved gut health from fermented foods and antioxidants from fresh ingredients. It also emphasizes smaller portions and regular physical activity. Drawbacks include high sodium content, low calcium due to limited dairy, and high carbohydrates from rice and noodles, requiring portion control. The diet can be adapted for vegan, low-carb, and gluten-free needs.

The manual provides instructions for the Sansa Fuze player, covering how to transfer music, photos, and videos using drag-and-drop, Windows Media Player, or Sansa Media Converter; play music, audiobooks, and videos and view photos with playback controls and options; use the FM radio, program presets, and record broadcasts; perform voice recordings; delete content from the player or a computer; adjust system settings such as wallpaper, backlight, power saver, language, date and time, brightness, USB mode, and factory reset; and includes troubleshooting tips, supported file formats and bit rates, customer support contact information, a one-year limited warranty policy, and end-user software license agreement terms.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition system with a built-in analog front-end. Its speed-boost mode supports up to 8MSPS for a user-selected analog input channel pair while the remaining six channels idle. The device uses 16-bit configuration registers in three banks; bank 0 is always accessible, while banks 1 and 2 require selection via REG_BANK_SEL. Register writes involve selecting the bank via address 0x03 in bank 0, then writing the target register. Register reads require bank selection, setting SPI_RD_EN and SPI_MODE in register 0x00, issuing the register address, then disabling read access. Daisy-chain mode connects multiple devices with shared CS and SCLK, sequential SDO-to-SDI linking, and requires N × 24 SCLKs for writes; reads use frames with 0xFE and 0xFF commands after enabling read access. Registers configure SPI mode, daisy-chain length, data format, averaging, XOR operation, test patterns, speed-boost mode, gain error correction, analog input bandwidth, power-down, reference, output data lanes, and common-mode range. For ATE applications, post-calibration TUE is 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C. The device offers low-noise (22.7kHz) and wide-bandwidth (700kHz) modes, settling to 99.95% full-scale in 7.5µs in wide-bandwidth mode. It operates from AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD with no required power-up sequence, and layout guidelines recommend placing bypass capacitors near power pins and isolating analog and digital signals.

This retrospective study developed a predictive nomogram for shunt-dependent hydrocephalus (SDHC) following aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH). Reviewing 109 patients treated between 2013 and 2021, researchers analyzed demographics, laboratory values, aneurysm characteristics, and treatment modality. All patients received external ventricular drainage and underwent an EVD challenge; those with failed challenges or hydrocephalus after removal received ventriculoperitoneal shunts. Multivariate logistic regression identified three independent risk factors for SDHC: age ≥65 years (OR 3.94), surgical clipping versus endovascular coiling (OR 4.36), and Hunt and Hess scale ≥3 (OR 3.59). The model demonstrated an area under the curve of 0.753. A nomogram assigning one point to each factor was constructed to estimate SDHC probability. Unlike prior studies, Fisher grade, aneurysm location, and inflammatory markers (NLR, PLR, PNR) were not significant predictors, possibly due to universal EVD placement and a high rate of endovascular coiling. The authors noted the study's retrospective design and limited sample size as limitations requiring prospective validation.

Nike reported fiscal first-quarter revenue of $11.72 billion, up 1% year-over-year and exceeding Wall Street expectations, though net income fell 31% to $727 million and gross margin declined to 42.2% as the company clears stale inventory through discounting under CEO Elliott Hill's turnaround strategy. Wholesale revenue rose 7% and North America sales increased 4%, but direct sales fell 4% and China revenue dropped 9%. The company is restructuring teams by sport rather than gender and age, recently launched NikeSKIMS to grow its female customer base, and finance chief Matt Friend warned that progress will not be linear.

An international team has obtained live specimens of Kuphus polythalamia, a giant sulfur-feeding shipworm found in a Philippine lagoon. Unlike wood-eating relatives, the mud-dwelling mollusk uses microbes to convert hydrogen sulfide into carbon. Researchers hope to discover new antimicrobial substances from microbes in its gill. The findings were published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. The animal's tusk-like shells reach five feet, but its life cycle and age are unknown.
Team hopes Horton recovers; Aaron cannot continue in playoffs. After a tough loss with lucky bounces, they will focus on next game. Three series were hard fought, nothing unusual.

The article presents a seasonal trading strategy for the German stock market using the iShares MSCI Germany ETF (EWG). The DAX 40, Germany's main index of 40 blue-chip companies founded in July 1988, has a $1,250 billion market capitalization and a 5.36% annual return since inception. EWG invests in large and mid-size German companies, charges a 0.50% expense ratio, and offers U.S. investors access to the German market. Historical EWG returns since 1996 show the strongest performance in the fourth quarter. The strategy invests only during the final quarter of each year. Backtesting since inception, adjusted for dividends and splits, indicates this approach has outperformed buy and hold.

Climate change in the northern Rocky Mountains is warming streams and reducing water flow, allowing introduced rainbow trout to invade habitat native to cutthroat trout. The two species are hybridizing, producing less fit offspring and threatening permanent loss of the native species. A study in *Global Change Biology* found widespread hybridization, especially where rainbow trout were historically introduced. Some states are now removing rainbow trout to prevent the cutthroat trout's extinction.

Former INEC official Christian Nwosu testified before Justice Mohammed Idris at a Lagos Federal High Court that EFCC operatives coerced him into admitting he collected N30 million from former Petroleum Minister Dieziani Alison-Madueke. Nwosu alleged that operative Usman Zakari threatened detention unless he wrote dictated statements, and that prosecutor Rotimi Oyedepo ordered his detention. He claimed he was forced to surrender N5 million in cash drafts and property worth N30 million after being escorted to a bank by armed police.
CoachingAmericanSoccer.com offers Rules of the Road for new players and coaches, covering tactics and positioning.

A nationwide study of over 1.1 million older adults linked long-term exposure to outdoor trichloroethylene (TCE), an industrial solvent used in metal degreasing and dry cleaning, to a 10% increased risk of Parkinson's disease. Researchers analyzed Medicare beneficiaries over age 67 diagnosed between 2016 and 2018, mapping TCE exposure using ZIP+4 codes and EPA data. The study identified hot spots in the Rust Belt and near major emitting facilities, with higher risk closer to two of the top three facilities. Published in the American Academy of Neurology's journal, the study shows an association, not causation. Limitations include that findings may not apply to younger people and exposure estimates were based on 2002 outdoor air levels.

State Street Corporation, which commissioned the "Fearless Girl" statue in New York City, agreed to pay $5 million to settle U.S. Department of Labor claims alleging it paid 305 top female employees and 15 black vice presidents less than male and white employees in the same positions. Clarke, Devoret and Martinis won the 2025 Nobel Prize in physics for quantum effects in an electric circuit.

Miami Dolphins wide receiver Tyreek Hill dislocated his knee in the third quarter of the team's first win of the season over the Jets, suffering the injury when his left leg twisted under him during a tackle out of bounds after a 10-yard catch. He was carted off with an air cast, waved to the crowd, and remained hospitalized overnight for further tests. Hill had 67 receiving yards on six catches before exiting and was in good spirits. The team will need other players, including Waller and running backs, to step up in the passing game.

Sir John Deane's sixth form college held its fourth annual Evening of Jazz and Soul at the Macdonald Portal Hotel in Tarporley. Researchers at Chalmers University of Technology in Sweden used machine learning and advanced computer simulations to reveal the previously unknown low-temperature phase structure of formamidinium lead iodide, a promising halide perovskite for solar cells. Collaborators at the University of Birmingham confirmed the findings experimentally by cooling the material to −200°C. The breakthrough enables simulations thousands of times longer with millions of atoms, providing essential knowledge to engineer stable, ultra-efficient, flexible solar cells thin enough to encase devices and buildings. The study was published in the *Journal of the American Chemical Society*.

Wafa Yahia, the Syrian grandmother central to Hawaii's lawsuit against President Trump's travel ban, arrived in Honolulu after U.S. approval. Her son-in-law, plaintiff Ismail Elshikh, credited the lawsuit for her visa. Hawaii Attorney General Doug Chin said the legal challenge will continue because the executive order remains harmful.

A study in the Journal of Experimental Psychology suggests general distraction, such as hobbies or exercise, is the best short-term option for recovering from a breakup, though it should be used sparingly. Focusing on an ex's negative qualities is another recommended technique.

The author describes struggling to sleep comfortably during pregnancy due to physical changes and medical advice against lying on the back or stomach, leaving side-sleeping as the only option. After discovering the Leachco U-shaped pregnancy pillow through a friend's social media post, she purchased it and found it significantly improved her sleep and comfort, allowing her to rest on her side and flip over easily. She notes downsides including its large size, a scratchy default cover, and its effect on bed blankets, but considers it worthwhile. She recommends the pillow for pregnant individuals and anyone seeking comfort, planning to continue using it after giving birth.

Vale SA's stock conversion plan drew 84.4 percent of preferred shares, exceeding the minimum threshold and prompting the company to potentially accelerate its Novo Mercado listing to this year from 2020. Common shares rose 2 percent to 31.40 reais, preferred shares gained 1 percent to 29.02 reais, and American depositary receipts added 0.9 percent to $9.775.

A swimming advisory was issued for Little Beach in Port Stanley due to high bacteria levels, warning of health risks, but the beach remained open. Cathie Walker said an advisory differs from a closure. Beachgoer Terrie Vergiris brought children to swim and said she did not notice the signs, believing the beach was safe. This study examines primary school teachers' perspectives on the virtual education experiences of students with disabilities in inclusive education settings in Turkey during the COVID-19 pandemic. Using a phenomenological design, researchers conducted semi-structured interviews with 10 general education primary school teachers after the return to in-person instruction. Findings indicate that participation in virtual classes varied: students with parental support and adequate technology attended regularly, while others could not participate due to family illiteracy, low socioeconomic status, internet and device problems, or preference for rehabilitation center services. Teachers reported challenges including large class sizes that prevented individual attention, lack of socialization, students keeping cameras off, behavioral issues, difficulty tracking homework, and insufficient home learning environments. While some teachers maintained effective cooperation with families through daily communication and guidance, others faced difficulties due to unresponsive parents or limited time. Teachers applied diverse solutions such as hybrid in-person and virtual schedules, WhatsApp support, video feedback from families, and flexible lesson delivery. They suggested keeping schools open for students with disabilities, providing financial and technological support to disadvantaged families, developing more engaging and social content, utilizing Education Informatics Network support points for motivation, and coordinating with rehabilitation centers. The study concludes that parental involvement and support are critical factors in the success of virtual inclusive education.

The paper defines youth as persons aged 15–24 (UN definition) and distinguishes hard skills (technical) from soft skills (generic workplace skills). Experiential learning, or work-integrated learning (WIL), includes co-op, which fully integrates work experience into academic curricula. Nigeria’s youth unemployment rate, historically lower than most regions, exceeded most areas by 2021 and is at least double the total unemployment rate; youth also show lower employment-to-population ratios and high NEET rates (28% in 2019), with significant gender, regional, and educational disparities. Co-op programs, originating in industrialized nations and implemented in some sub-Saharan African institutions, alternate academic study with paid work terms, requiring collaboration among universities, industry, and government. Evidence from developed countries indicates co-op improves graduate employment rates, earnings, field-of-study alignment, and skill development. The paper examines Nigerian government interventions—SIWES, SURE-P, and N-SIP—noting that SIWES lacks full curricular integration and close institutional-employer collaboration. It argues for a federally driven co-op initiative in Nigeria, adopting the alternating model and leveraging existing program infrastructure to align post-secondary education with labor market demands. The authors recommend cost-sharing mechanisms, tax credits, and public-sector role modeling to encourage private-sector participation. They conclude that while co-op alone cannot resolve unemployment, it is a critical component of a multipronged strategy, and future research should address management structures, program templates for diverse institutions, and applicability to non-tertiary systems.

A study of the Omicron BA.1 wave in England from November 2021 to January 2022 analyzed 48,615 BA.1 genomes and human mobility data to investigate spatial dissemination. The variant, designated a WHO Variant of Concern on 26 November 2021, was first confirmed in England on 27 November 2021. Phylogenetic analysis identified at least 6,455 independent introduction events, with 69.9% being singletons. Early importations before and during travel restrictions on southern African countries (26 November–15 December 2021) comprised roughly 6% of introductions but caused approximately 80% of reported infections through end-January. The restrictions were largely ineffective because importation sources shifted to the United States, where Estimated Importation Intensity was about four times that of South Africa during the restriction period.

Spatial expansion centered initially on Greater London, which acted as the primary source for local and long-distance viral lineage movements, contrasting with the Delta variant's initial spread from England's North West. The eight largest transmission lineages accounted for over 60% of sampled English genomes, with six imported before travel restrictions. Spread occurred in stages: initial concentration in Greater London, long-distance dispersal (>300 km) in early December, and increased mid-to-long range (50–300 km) movements during the New Year period. A phylogeographic generalised linear model supported a gravity model during the expansion phase, with dissemination driven by population size, distance, and Greater London origin. Post-expansion dynamics showed increased importance of aggregated mobility and dissemination toward areas with later epidemic peaks.

Human mobility between home and hub local authorities decreased by an estimated 11.97% per unit increase in weekly COVID-19 cases per 100 people at the hub, with greater reductions for shorter-distance travel. This behavioural response, alongside "Plan B" restrictions and holiday mixing, contributed to spatial heterogeneity in epidemic peaks. The study concludes that targeted travel restrictions implemented after local transmission is established have limited practical value, and characterising the interplay between transmission intensity, perceived risk, and human mobility is critical for future intervention strategies.

The TLV321/2x comparators consume 40µA per channel with 40ns propagation delay. The TLV321x has a push-pull output, while the TLV322x has an open-drain output that can be pulled up to 5.5V independent of the supply voltage. The input range extends from 200mV below V- to 200mV above V+; no phase inversion occurs within this range, and input current must be limited to 10mA or less. Unused inputs must not be tied together, but instead tied to available voltages within the specified range with at least 50mV differential. The family includes 1.8mV of internal hysteresis. Push-pull outputs must not be connected to another output or shorted to the opposite supply; unused push-pull outputs must be left floating. Open-drain outputs allow logical OR'ing and level translation, with recommended pull-up resistor current between 100µA and 1mA; unused open-drain outputs may be left floating or tied to V-. Inputs and outputs incorporate internal ESD protection. The TLV321x has an internal Power-On Reset circuit that holds the output low for up to 32µs after the supply crosses 1.65V, after which the output reflects the differential input when the supply is at or above the minimum voltage. Propagation delay is influenced by overdrive voltage, with smaller overdrive increasing delay. External hysteresis can be added via positive feedback using resistor networks. A typical low-side current sensing application triggers when the amplified shunt voltage exceeds 1.1V. Layout requires 0.1µF low-ESR bypass capacitors directly between V+ and ground, and series resistors are recommended to limit current during possible output shorts.

The NVIDIA GA10x Ampere architecture delivers up to 2x improvements in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI over Turing. Each Streaming Multiprocessor (SM) contains 128 CUDA Cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, one second-generation Ray Tracing Core, and 128 KB of configurable L1/Shared Memory. GA10x doubles peak FP32 throughput per SM by enabling FP32 processing on both datapaths, allowing 128 FP32 operations per clock. Combined L1 data cache and shared memory capacity is 33% larger, with double the shared memory bandwidth compared to Turing.

The GA102 GPU features twelve 32-bit memory controllers (384-bit total) with 6144 KB of L2 cache. It utilizes GDDR6X memory with PAM4 signaling and MTA encoding, delivering up to 936 GB/sec of peak memory bandwidth, a 52% increase over the prior generation. Error Detection and Replay (EDR) technology improves memory overclocking stability by retrying failed transmissions. ROPs are now integrated into Graphics Processing Clusters (GPCs), increasing the GA102 total to 112 ROPs and improving raster operation performance.

Second-generation RT Cores double the ray/triangle intersection testing rate and add an Interpolate Triangle Position unit that accelerates ray-traced motion blur rendering by up to 8x over Turing. The architecture also supports concurrent ray tracing with graphics or compute workloads within each SM. Third-generation Tensor Cores are twice as powerful as Turing's, support new data types including TF32 and BF16, and implement Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity for up to 2x throughput on sparse matrices.

NVIDIA RTX IO leverages Microsoft DirectStorage to enable GPU-based lossless decompression, significantly reducing CPU utilization and improving I/O performance. The architecture supports HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a, and 8K60/4K120 displays. Hardware video capabilities include fifth-generation NVDEC with AV1 hardware decode support and seventh-generation NVENC encoding.

The GeForce RTX 3090 incorporates the GA102 GPU with 10,496 CUDA Cores and 24 GB of GDDR6X memory, delivering 1.5x the performance of TITAN RTX. The RTX 3070 uses the GA104 GPU and exceeds the RTX 2080 Ti in performance. For data centers, the NVIDIA A40 offers up to 2x FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to 5x (10x with Sparsity) AI throughput over the Quadro RTX 6000, with 48 GB of memory scalable to 96 GB via NVLink. The RTX A6000 features 10,752 CUDA Cores and 48 GB of GDDR6 for professional workstations.

This November 22, 2001 email from Commissioner.COM to Paul Lucci at Enron contains advertisements for various products and services, including an Anna Kournikova calendar, a Lara Croft DVD, magazine subscriptions, gas discounts, a Vegas vacation, a satellite dish, Fantasy Football Guides, and an Xbox giveaway. Cuba held a January 2 parade honoring Fidel Castro and marking the revolution's 58th anniversary, with soldiers marching without equipment. Tens of thousands marched despite Castro's ban on monuments in Raúl Castro's final full year, amid economic decline from Venezuela's crisis and threatened US rapprochement under Donald Trump. Jennifer Bello affirmed Cuba would not renounce principles.

The Investors Intelligence Sentiment Index, created by AW Cohen in 1963 and published by Chartcraft, is a contrarian indicator based on weekly surveys of over 100 market newsletters. It measures percentages of advisors who are bullish, bearish, or expecting correction, and tracks stocks above 10-week and 30-week moving averages. Because advisors are often wrong at turning points, extreme readings signal opposite positions: above 55% bullish indicates excessive optimism (negative), while below 35% indicates excessive pessimism (positive). Weekly figures above 70% indicate overbought conditions and below 30% indicate oversold. Unlike the AAII Sentiment Survey, which polls individual investors since 1987, Investors Intelligence surveys professional advisors. The index is available by subscription on Chartcraft's website.

TI provides resources "as is" without warranties for skilled developers solely responsible for product selection, application design, and compliance. Resources may change without notice; use is limited to development with described TI products, with no IP licenses granted. Users indemnify TI. Product terms and warranties remain unchanged.

The article argues that the Shaw v. Reno doctrine, which subjects race-predominant congressional districting to strict scrutiny, lacks originalist support and should be rejected in the Louisiana redistricting case. The author contends the Fourteenth Amendment’s original public meaning did not constrain election regulation, as evidenced by the subsequent Fifteenth and Nineteenth Amendments, and that the Fifteenth Amendment’s prohibition on denying or abridging the right to vote does not encompass Shaw claims, which involve racial separation rather than vote dilution. While stare decisis generally preserves precedent, the author asserts Shaw is unworkable and irreconcilable with Voting Rights Act Section 2 vote-dilution jurisprudence; a consistent originalist should therefore jettison Shaw to resolve this tension and preserve Congress’s statutory enforcement authority. The author urges Justice Barrett to apply this originalist analysis with intellectual honesty.
