In G. M. Cox v. George W. Burnham, the plaintiff challenged the defendant judge’s jurisdiction to hear a pharmacist’s application for a permit to sell intoxicating liquors at a term subsequent to the one at which it was filed. The court held that the applicable Code sections are not mandatory and do not abridge the court’s general power to control the business of the term; an adjournment without a hearing does not automatically dismiss the application or deprive the court of jurisdiction. In the absence of a showing to the contrary, it is presumed that cause existed for continuing the matter. Finding the hearing at the later term regular and not evasive of the liquor laws, the court concluded the defendant acted within jurisdiction and dismissed the certiorari proceedings.

Current European Respiratory Society/American Thoracic Society guidelines recommend using a forced vital capacity (FVC) below the lower limit of normal (LLN) to exclude pulmonary restriction, but recent reassessment in diverse cohorts using race-neutral reference equations found this approach has a negative predictive value (NPV) of only 80.5% overall and 65.2% among non-Hispanic Black patients, resulting in under-recognition. This study developed and externally validated three machine learning models—logistic regression, random forest, and boosted tree—using demographic, anthropometric, and spirometric data from two academic health systems to predict restriction without static lung volume measurements. In the external validation dataset of 24,524 pulmonary function tests, the random forest model achieved an NPV of 88.3% and sensitivity of 83.3%, compared to 72.7% and 46.0% for the FVC LLN, though it excluded the need for static lung volume measurements in fewer tests (56.7% versus 78.4%). Among non-Hispanic Black patients, the random forest model improved the NPV to 74.6% versus 49.5% for the FVC LLN, reducing but not eliminating performance disparities. The models demonstrated excellent discrimination but poor calibration upon external validation. The authors conclude that machine learning models improve both accuracy and equity in excluding restriction from spirometry.

Asian stocks were shaky and the Chinese yuan near 11-month lows on Wednesday amid fears of a Sino-U.S. trade war ahead of an end-of-week tariff deadline. MSCI's Asia-Pacific index edged up 0.1 percent after hitting a nine-month low, while Japan's Nikkei lost 0.5 percent. Wall Street fell Tuesday, with the S&P 500 down 0.49 percent and the Nasdaq dropping 0.86 percent, pressured by declines in Facebook, Tesla, and Micron Technology. China's central bank moved to calm markets and stabilize the yuan. The Mexican peso surged 2.6 percent on comments from its newly elected president. Oil prices rose on lower U.S. stockpiles, while copper hit nine-month lows on trade worries.

Late-breaking news and upcoming events include calls for Russia investigations after Flynn's exit, a possible shift in Israeli-Palestinian policy, the arrest of a Vietnamese woman in Kim Jong Nam's death, NATO talks in Brussels, cracks in California's Oroville Dam, a study on risky driving, a Boeing union vote, laser labeling in Sweden, Kate Upton's third Sports Illustrated cover, and Rumor the German shepherd's Westminster win.

The Care Quality Commission rated East of England Ambulance Service NHS Trust as "Requires Improvement" overall following a March inspection, though "Outstanding" for caring. While progress was noted in safeguarding and incident reporting, the trust still fails to meet national response standards and experienced serious winter delays. Inspectors found low staff morale and disengagement from management, though staff remained dedicated. The trust must improve response times, apply procedures consistently, and better support staff. The CEO acknowledged challenges but highlighted improvements in Patient Transport Services and Emergency Operations Centres, and £11.5 million in additional funding.

The author selects best all-around January 2017 CCC stocks from David Fish's list by applying the Dugan Stock Scoring System, which evaluates Risk, Value, Past Performance, and Future Performance Expectations, to non-REIT and non-MLP companies, then filtering for minimum yield of 2.25%, $5B market cap, 5% recent dividend increase, 5% estimated EPS growth next year and for five years, and Dugan Score of 50, plus maximum relative Graham number of 70, payout ratio of 70, and debt/equity ratio of 1. The system assesses current conditions and expected future performance, with broker sector weighting adjustments. This yielded 21 highest-scoring companies.

Coach DeBoer said the team, though down in the series, will not make panic lineup changes. He expressed confidence from past comebacks, stating the team can win consecutive games once it gets the first victory. He noted they created quality scoring chances but credited the opposing goaltender and team for shutting them down. DeBoer discussed adjusting to travel and time changes in Los Angeles, praised the series officiating and disciplined play, and stressed the need to score more goals and capitalize on power plays. He also questioned a referee's call on a dead puck but was not disappointed in the team's effort to the final buzzer.

Tesla, Inc.’s 2018 Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2018, describes the company as a vertically integrated sustainable energy company operating in two reportable segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. It designs, develops, manufactures, and sells fully electric vehicles, including the Model S, Model X, and Model 3, with future products planned such as the Model Y, Tesla Semi, a pickup truck, and a new Roadster. It also manufactures and sells energy storage products—Powerwall 2 and Powerpack 2—and solar energy systems, including Solar Roof. Vehicles are sold directly to consumers through company-owned stores, galleries, and service centers, supported by a global Supercharger and Destination Charging network and mobile service technicians. Manufacturing facilities are located in Fremont and Lathrop, California; Tilburg, Netherlands; Gigafactory 1 in Nevada; and Gigafactory 2 in Buffalo, New York. Construction of Gigafactory Shanghai began in January 2019, with the goal of producing certain Model 3 trims for the local market by the end of 2019. The company relies on proprietary powertrain, battery pack, power electronics, and self-driving technologies, and has pledged not to initiate patent lawsuits against good-faith parties in the electric vehicle field. It offers various financing options, warranties, and service plans for its vehicles, energy storage, and solar products. As of December 31, 2018, Tesla had 48,817 full-time employees. The report outlines risks, including potential delays in production ramps for Model 3 and future products, dependence on single-source and key suppliers such as Panasonic, the need to scale global sales, delivery, and servicing, fluctuations in raw material costs, challenges in achieving cost targets, and uncertainties related to international expansion and regulatory environments.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 30, 2019 reports total net sales of $58.0 billion, a 5% decrease from the prior year, net income of $11.6 billion, and diluted earnings per share of $2.46. The decline was driven by lower iPhone net sales, partially offset by higher Services and Wearables, Home and Accessories net sales. The Company released updated iPad Air, iPad mini, iMac and AirPods models, and announced new services including Apple News+, Apple Card, Apple Arcade, and Apple TV+. Apple repurchased $24.0 billion of common stock and paid $3.4 billion in dividends during the quarter. On April 16, 2019, Apple and Qualcomm reached a settlement agreement to dismiss all litigation. The filing also details adoption of new accounting standards and provides condensed consolidated financial statements.

Israel and Canada signed a modernized free trade agreement in Montreal to replace their 1997 pact. Canadian International Trade Minister Francois-Phillippe Champagne and Israeli Economy Minister Eli Cohen signed the deal, which eliminates duties on thousands of additional products and includes new chapters on labor, the environment, trade and gender, and small and medium-sized enterprises, as well as improved dispute-settlement provisions. The agreement requires ratification by both parliaments and aims to double bilateral trade.

This study presents a PRISMA-guided meta-analysis of 13 peer-reviewed studies from eight countries examining AI-related technologies in education between January 2015 and July 2024. The analysis found a large, statistically significant overall positive effect size of 0.86 (95% CI [0.45, 1.27], p < 0.0001) for AI applications in education. Chatbots and generative AI demonstrated the highest effect size at 1.02 (95% CI [0.45, 1.59], p < 0.0001), while online learning and virtual reality showed an effect size of 0.79 (95% CI [-0.04, 1.62], p < 0.07), and learning management systems with AI platforms showed 0.62 (95% CI [0.03, 1.21], p < 0.05). The researchers also applied novel algorithms based on Naive Bayes, TF-IDF/BM25, and BERT, yielding positive overall effect sizes of 0.86, 0.84, and 0.88 respectively via a mixed weighted model. Substantial heterogeneity was observed across studies (I² ranging from 54.03% to 93.23%), and publication bias was detected. The authors conclude that AI technologies significantly enhance educational outcomes, though effectiveness varies considerably depending on implementation context, educational level, and specific technology.

A Danish study found children of older mothers had fewer behavioural, social and emotional difficulties at ages seven and 11, but not at 15. Researchers linked this to older mothers' "psychological maturity"—greater tolerance, emotional stability and less discipline—along with stable relationships, education and wealth. However, older mothers face greater risks of miscarriage, premature birth and deformities. The average pregnancy age in Denmark is 30.9.

Temple Grandin will present "Livestock Handling and Animal Behavior" at 7-9 a.m. Feb. 23 at Tyler Jelly Building, Tehama District Fairground. Sponsored by Shasta College and University of California Cooperative Extension. Breakfast: $15. Call Josh Davy 527-3101 or write to jdavy@ucdavis.edu.
Scientists created human eggs from skin cells through meiosis, potentially treating infertility.

Niu Technologies, a manufacturer of electric bicycles and scooters, has posted major stock gains in 2025 driven by strong recent growth. The author believes future growth may not continue or justify current valuations and assigns a neutral hold rating, noting that factors could disrupt the expected growth priced into the stock.

Russian math, an after-school enrichment approach emphasizing reasoning and deep understanding over rote memorization, is spreading rapidly in the U.S. through programs like the Russian School of Mathematics, which enrolls 22,000 students nationwide. Founded by Russian immigrants who adapted Soviet teaching traditions, the curriculum introduces abstract concepts early and uses engaging, hands-on problems. Parents enroll children—at about $2,000 a year—due to dissatisfaction with public school math or to help them reach their potential. The trend raises concerns among American educators about uneven student preparation, overconfidence, and widening achievement gaps between families who can afford it and those who cannot. Supporters note it expands the pool of students comfortable with math, and honors class enrollment has grown in towns where it operates. Critics warn it fuels a competitive "arms race" in after-school instruction that pressures families.

Enron Corp. disclosed in late October 2001 that the Securities and Exchange Commission requested information regarding its related-party transactions with partnerships formerly run by Chief Financial Officer Andrew Fastow, including LJM Cayman and LJM2. The announcement caused Enron’s stock to fall more than 20 percent to $20.65, a 52-week low, following the company’s prior disclosure of a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity and $1.01 billion in third-quarter charges tied to unwinding those partnerships, which produced a $618 million quarterly loss. Analysts and investors raised concerns about the company’s transparency, complex off-balance sheet financing vehicles such as Whitewing and Marlin, potential dilution of shareholders if debt ratings fell below investment grade, and a Moody's review of Enron’s debt for possible downgrade. Multiple class-action lawsuits were filed against Enron and executives including Kenneth Lay, Jeffrey Skilling, and Andrew Fastow, alleging securities law violations and failure to timely disclose financial problems. Lay stated the company would cooperate fully with the SEC and welcomed the opportunity to address concerns about the transactions.

Fredrik underwent X-rays and will have a report by day's end; he missed shifts but finished the game. The team had a poor start and struggled with passing, causing numerous turnovers that stalled the offense. One line has remained productive since the Colorado series. The power play failed to generate quality shots. The coach dismissed historical comparisons as irrelevant, emphasizing focus on evening the series. Shanahan had a poor game and line adjustments are possible. Penalty minutes taxed key players, reducing ice time for others and creating imbalance that must be corrected. The team failed to get the puck deep enough in the offensive zone, requiring changes to forechecking and zone entries against Carolina's quick breakouts.

This divisional patent application describes compositions and methods for enhancing CAR T cell efficacy by reducing or eliminating expression and/or function of Tet1, Tet2, and/or Tet3—particularly Tet2—in immune effector cells engineered to express a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR). Disruption of Tet decreases 5-hydroxymethylcytosine levels and enhances CAR T cell proliferation, effector cytokine production, degranulation, and stem cell memory T cell (Tscm) populations. The CAR comprises an antigen-binding domain (e.g., targeting CD19), a transmembrane domain, a hinge region, and intracellular signaling domains. Tet disruption is achieved using gene-editing systems (e.g., CRISPR/Cas9, ZFN, TALEN, meganuclease), siRNA/shRNA, small molecules, or dominant negative proteins. The application provides vectors co-encoding a CAR and a Tet inhibitor, methods for ex vivo and in vivo manufacture and treatment of hematologic and solid cancers, and clinical data from a CLL patient showing that CAR19 insertion into the Tet2 locus disrupted Tet2 function and correlated with favorable clonal expansion.

This first Mendelian randomization study evaluated the causal effect of genetically determined pericardial adipose tissue (PAT) on multiple cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) using 11 single-nucleotide polymorphisms as instrumental variables. Genetically determined PAT was significantly associated with increased risks of CVD, heart failure, hypertension, coronary heart disease, ischemic heart disease, ischemic stroke, and venous thromboembolism, but not with cardiac arrhythmias, atrial fibrillation, aortic aneurysm, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, myocardial infarction, cardioembolic stroke, small vessel stroke, large artery stroke, or subarachnoid hemorrhage. Two-step mediation analysis indicated hypertension mediated the associations for several CVDs, with mediated proportions of 13.23% for heart failure, 13.51% for coronary heart disease, 19.18% for ischemic heart disease, and 14.51% for ischemic stroke. The study suggests PAT may be a potential therapeutic target for CVDs, particularly in people with obesity, and that antihypertensive drugs could be used conjunctively. Limitations include a solely European population, sample overlap, and small case numbers for certain outcomes.

The passage highlights sexual harassment in higher institutions, citing OAU professor Richard Akindele's dismissal for soliciting sex from a student. It praises OAU's swift action, urges other institutions to emulate it, enforce moral standards, protect female students, punish offending lecturers, and advises female students not to lure lecturers.

Tom Evans, father of terminally ill toddler Alfie Evans, stated that his 23-month-old son's life support was turned off at Alder Hey Children's Hospital but that Alfie has been breathing unassisted for nine hours. Evans said doctors, who had initially refused oxygen, re-intervened and provided oxygen and water after he argued the situation was becoming unlawful. Alfie's mother, Kate James, is with him. Evans believes Alfie will need life support again within hours.

Indian troops killed three youth in Shopian, damaging a mosque and houses and sparking protests where civilians were injured. Two soldiers died and others were wounded in attacks in Shopian and Bandipora. Train services were suspended. Resistance leaders opposed attempts to alter Kashmir's disputed status and cited moves to challenge Article 35A. A civilian injured in a Srinagar explosion died.

An internal Enron news digest dated June 4, 2001, compiles articles mentioning the company. Key stories include: President Bush adviser Karl Rove’s financial disclosure of $100,000–$250,000 in Enron stock while awaiting government ethics approval to divest; Saudi Arabia signing agreements worth at least $25 billion with nine global oil and energy firms, including Enron, to develop natural gas fields and related infrastructure; opinion pieces on energy market cycles and Enron’s corporate influence; and extensive coverage of the troubled Dabhol Power project in India, where lenders met in Singapore to address a dispute after the Maharashtra State Electricity Board halted power purchases and defaulted on payments, prompting arbitration threats and raising concerns from Fitch and Moody’s about India’s investment climate and contract sanctity. Other articles report Nigerian President Obasanjo criticizing Enron for poor performance and exorbitant prices on a Lagos power project; an analysis of U.S.-India relations highlighting the Enron dispute and ties between Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay and President Bush; and Enron Japan chief Joseph Hirl commenting on Japan’s electricity deregulation, lack of competition, and high energy costs relative to the United States.

The speakers addressed preparing for an upcoming road playoff game, noting the need to match their road mindset, establish their game early, and expect a desperate opponent. They valued the rare practice day to rest and adjust, acknowledged both teams are banged up, and emphasized winning faceoffs and executing under pressure. One praised a teammate’s versatility and recent scoring success, while another cited experience helping them focus only on the present game. They also noted playing more aggressively in the previous third period and credited a former player for providing relatable guidance and subtle details.

Researchers developed a metagenomic next-generation sequencing workflow using HostEL host background depletion and AmpRE single-tube DNA/RNA library preparation for infectious disease diagnosis. HostEL uses magnetic bead-immobilized nucleases after selective lysis to deplete human nucleic acids while enriching pathogen DNA and RNA, including bacteria, fungi, and viruses. AmpRE enables rapid library generation with minimal clean-up for shallow sequencing. Analytical validation using spiked plasma samples detected all 10 species down to 70,000 cells/mL, achieving 96% sensitivity and 96% specificity on both iSeq 100 and MiniSeq platforms. Clinical validation with 42 plasma samples demonstrated 93% agreement with clinical molecular diagnosis for samples with Ct values below 33, detecting both DNA and RNA viruses. Depending on the platform, turnaround times ranged from 13 to 27 hours. The workflow is not applicable to parasites and was limited to plasma samples in this study.

Cruzin' for Life, a Santa Maria nonprofit, operates a retrofitted van transporting Mission Hope Cancer Center patients. In its first year, the wheelchair-accessible van served more than 2,600 patients across seven local areas, logging more than 34,000 miles. The service was created after a board member's relative was diagnosed with cancer and is funded through events including an annual crab feed and car show, plus a $36,000 donation from Santa Maria Energy. Patients call directly or are referred by staff. The organization may add a second van if need and funding allow.

A woman declared dead by paramedics after a June 24 car crash in Carletonville, South Africa, was found alive hours later in a mortuary refrigerator. Two others died in the crash. Distress Alert said all proper checks were done and has launched an investigation.

The 2025–26 season marks Jim Montgomery’s first full year as St. Louis Blues head coach after a mid-season takeover. Known for structured systems and strong special teams, Montgomery aims to return the team to playoff contention. The Blues open at home on Oct. 9, with seven of their first 11 games at home. Key matchups include early rivalries, Chicago games, and a late April divisional stretch. A Winter Olympics break from Feb. 5–25, 2026 offers a midseason checkpoint before a packed March and April. Montgomery must blend veterans with young talent, tighten defense, and navigate 26 division games to secure a playoff berth.

Backtests of NIFTY 50 using Yahoo Finance data from 2007 indicate a positive end-of-month effect comparable to the US turn-of-the-month effect. An optimized trading strategy enters at the close of the fifth-to-last trading day of the month and exits at the close of the second trading day of the new month. The backtest produced a 10.5% CAGR with 30% market exposure and a 26% maximum drawdown, outperforming buy and hold. While somewhat curve-fitted, the results remained reasonably robust when entry and exit dates were adjusted slightly.

The passage describes an autonomous vehicle control architecture comprising an autonomous vehicle (AV) control sub-system for normal operation and multiple independent auxiliary control units that provide redundancy for critical safety situations. The AV control sub-system uses multiple sensors and processing resources to operate vehicle interfaces for propulsion, braking, steering, and other functions, and includes event determination logic with confidence scoring, route planning, and remote assistance capabilities. The auxiliary control units operate independently of the AV control sub-system and each other, using dedicated sensors, separate communication busses, and hardware or firmware architectures optimized for reliability. These units can function in a trajectory verification mode, receiving planned trajectory data from the AV control sub-system and communicating vehicle response outputs to verify or alter trajectories, or in a failsafe and bypass mode. In failsafe and bypass mode, the units detect predefined safety-critical conditions or events—including AV control sub-system malfunction—and directly signal predetermined vehicle response actions, such as braking, steering, or stopping, to vehicle interfaces, superseding commands from the AV control sub-system. The vehicle response outputs may correspond to fixed actions, actions conditioned on duration or magnitude, or selected actions based on sensor input, and can be sustained until the triggering condition clears or the vehicle reaches a desired safe state.

Celtic's 2-1 victory over Rangers at Ibrox leaves a 19-point gap with a game in hand, the largest since 1925-26. That year, John Logie Baird first demonstrated television at Selfridges. Celtic are set to break the 20-point margin from that season. In 1985-86, Rangers finished 22 points behind after a second-half collapse.

This pilot study examines the integration of drama-based pedagogy in STEAM education through a literature review and qualitative observation of two classroom activities. The research investigated how university students view dramatic activities in science and history (RQ1) and what they achieve in STEAM classrooms through drama (RQ2). Using participant observation and detailed field notes, the authors studied 19 first-year female students at ELTE University in Budapest during an art-based methods course. The two activities were "The Life Cycle of a Butterfly," in which groups choreographed movements after a presentation, and the "Indian Caste System," in which groups created short scenes about caste life. The literature review establishes that drama-based pedagogy positively affects academic achievement, 21st-century skills, motivation, creativity, communication, and collaboration, while noting implementation challenges such as classroom management, noise, time limitations, curriculum regulations, and lack of qualified teachers. Findings from the pilot study identified four key observations: students demonstrated increased creativity and diverse artistic interpretations; engaged in collaborative group work and supportive interaction; exercised problem-solving and thinking skills; and showed strong motivation and involvement in the learning process. Students expressed appreciation for interactive, creative activities over passive instruction. The study concludes that drama is a valuable STEAM tool that enhances enjoyment, motivation, and competence development. However, significant limitations include the small sample size, homogeneous demographic (all female, first-year, limited prior STEAM/drama experience), and narrow age and educational background, meaning the results offer only preliminary insights requiring future validation.

TrackR unveiled three Bluetooth tracking devices ahead of CES: the cheaper, colorful TrackR pixel; the slim, credit card-sized TrackR wallet 2.0; and the TrackR atlas smart plug that maps homes and supports Amazon Alexa. The pixel and wallet offer Bluetooth and crowd-sourced tracking via smartphone apps. All devices have replaceable batteries. Prices range from $24.99 to $39.99, with pre-orders starting today and a Spring launch expected.

Turing architecture enables real-time ray tracing via RT Cores, RTX software, and filtering algorithms, delivering photorealistic objects with shadows, reflections, and refractions. With Microsoft's DirectML and DXR APIs, it supports real-time AI and ray tracing. The paper examines TU102 GPU in GeForce RTX 2080 Ti and Quadro RTX 6000, featuring advanced shading and Volta CUDA enhancements and combining programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI.

NVIDIA Corporation announced on May 2, 2016, that it and Samsung agreed to settle all pending intellectual property litigation, leading to immediate dismissal of cases in U.S. courts, the ITC, and the U.S. Patent Office. The settlement includes licensing a small number of patents to each other but no broad cross-licensing or other compensation.

Thinking Machines Lab, cofounded by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati and prominent ex-OpenAI researchers, has launched Tinker, a tool that automates the fine-tuning of frontier AI models. Tinker allows users to customize open-source models such as Meta’s Llama and Alibaba’s Qwen via an API using supervised and reinforcement learning, without managing complex infrastructure. The startup, valued at $12 billion after raising $2 billion in seed funding, aims to make advanced AI capabilities more accessible and reverse the trend toward closed commercial models. Beta testers praise Tinker for combining user-friendliness with granular control. The company is currently offering free API access to vetted applicants while planning automated misuse safeguards and eventual monetization.

San Juan Mayor Yulin Cruz called a Harvard study estimating 4,645 excess deaths after Hurricane Maria "a day of collective mourning," criticizing the official toll of 64. The study suggested the toll could be 70 times higher, with a likely figure near 5,000. She criticized Trump for not apologizing, said Puerto Rico is unprepared for the upcoming hurricane season, and keeps reminders including a hat and "NEVER AGAIN" on her wall.

Michael Flynn resigned as national security adviser after the Washington Post reported he discussed U.S. sanctions with Russia’s ambassador before President Trump’s inauguration. Government officials had reportedly known of the discussions, and acting Attorney General Sally Yates had warned White House Counsel Donald McGahn that Flynn was vulnerable to Russian blackmail. President Trump was allegedly aware of Flynn’s actions weeks before Vice President Pence, who had publicly defended Flynn. Trump has responded by criticizing illegal leaks and “fake news” rather than addressing the matter directly. Pundits and a Politico source suggest Flynn, who lacked diplomatic experience but was loyal to Trump, could not have acted alone. Lawmakers including Senator John McCain are pushing for investigations into Russian interference and alleged ties to the Trump administration. Because Flynn’s conversations occurred before inauguration and he has resigned, he could testify without executive privilege protection. If he implicates Trump, the President could face allegations of complicity in pre-inauguration communications and knowingly allowing aides to make false statements. McGahn may also face scrutiny regarding what he relayed to Trump.

The passage provides technical specifications for the TMS320DM814x processor, covering reset types such as Software Global Warm Reset, Test Reset, and Local Reset, plus reset isolation for PCI Express and EMAC Switch, RSTOUT_WD_OUT behavior, power-domain switching, and reset timing. It details the clocking architecture, including DEV and AUX clock sources, PLL configurations, frequency limits, SYSCLKs, and module clocks. The text also describes ARM Cortex-A8 and C674x DSP interrupt controllers, and provides peripheral information, timing requirements, and register descriptions for DCAN, EDMA, JTAG, EMAC Switch, GPIO, GPMC/ELM, HDMI, HDVPSS, video DAC, I2C, Imaging Subsystem, and DDR2/3 memory interfaces.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2015, describes its mission to empower every person and organization and its mobile-first, cloud-first strategy centered on three ambitions: reinventing productivity and business processes, building the intelligent cloud platform, and creating more personal computing. The company develops, licenses, and supports software, services, and devices—including Windows, Office, Azure, Xbox, Surface, Lumia phones, and Bing—and operates six segments: Devices and Consumer (D&C Licensing, Computing and Gaming Hardware, Phone Hardware, and D&C Other) and Commercial (Commercial Licensing and Commercial Other). The April 2014 acquisition of Nokia’s Devices and Services Business is reported in Phone Hardware, and Mojang was acquired in November 2014. Research and development expense was $12.0 billion in fiscal 2015, representing 13% of revenue. As of June 30, 2015, Microsoft employed approximately 118,000 people, and in June 2015 it approved a restructuring plan to eliminate up to 7,800 positions in fiscal 2016, primarily in Phone Hardware. Products are distributed through OEMs, distributors, resellers, online channels, and retail stores under various licensing and subscription programs. Risk factors include intense competition from firms such as Apple and Google; margin pressure from the shift to cloud services and vertically integrated hardware; execution risks related to Windows 10; potential impairment of goodwill and intangible assets, including $5.1 billion and $2.2 billion charges recorded in the Phone Hardware segment in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2015; intellectual property and piracy risks; cyber-attacks and data security vulnerabilities; government litigation and regulatory scrutiny; and global operational, tax, and supply chain risks.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s 2021 Form 10-K reports the fiscal year ended December 31, 2021. The company is a large accelerated filer, and its common stock trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol AMZN. Operations are organized into three segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS). The company serves consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, content creators, advertisers, and employees through online and physical stores, electronic devices, subscriptions including Amazon Prime, cloud services, advertising, and publishing. As of December 31, 2021, Amazon employed approximately 1,608,000 full-time and part-time employees. Executive officers include Jeffrey P. Bezos as Executive Chair and Andrew R. Jassy as President and Chief Executive Officer. Significant risk factors include intense competition; expansion into new products, services, and geographies; international regulatory restrictions, particularly in China and India; seasonality with higher sales in the fourth quarter; fulfillment network and data center strain; data security and system interruption risks; inventory and payments risks; foreign exchange exposure; evolving government regulation and legal proceedings; tax liabilities; and acquisition-related risks. As of year-end, the company operated leased and owned facilities for offices, physical stores, and fulfillment and data centers. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $96.0 billion at December 31, 2021, compared to $84.4 billion at December 31, 2020. Net cash provided by operating activities was $46.3 billion in 2021, down from $66.1 billion in 2020, while cash capital expenditures increased to $55.4 billion from $35.0 billion, primarily for fulfillment and technology infrastructure supporting AWS. Financing activities provided $6.3 billion. Critical accounting judgments relate to inventories and income taxes, and effective January 1, 2022, U.S. tax rules require research and development expenses to be capitalized and amortized.

This study developed and externally validated deep learning MRI biomarkers for extra-prostatic extension (EPE) and seminal vesicle invasion (SVI) in localized prostate cancer. Using 820 patients for training and internal testing, plus two external cohorts, the EPE and SVI classifiers achieved AUCs ranging from 0.611 to 0.743 and 0.678 to 0.775, respectively, across test sets. Both biomarkers were significantly associated with biochemical recurrence (BCR). The combined biomarker improved prognostic discrimination (C-index 0.73) and stratified risk within identical Gleason scores. Integrating the biomarkers into NCCN and UCSF-CAPRA risk groups reclassified 26.4% of patients and improved discriminatory ability (NCCN C-index: 0.592 to 0.617; UCSF-CAPRA C-index: 0.592 to 0.614). Interpretability analyses confirmed the models focused on relevant anatomical regions. Limitations include the lack of overall survival endpoints and underrepresentation of African American patients.

Lightning is random and not attracted to metal or water. It can strike from clear skies up to 10 miles away. The passage debunks five myths: metal attracts strikes; car tires insulate; clear skies are safe; lightning never strikes the same place twice; and sheltering under trees is safe. Cars are safe due to metal frames, while trees are dangerous. Most leisure deaths occur on or near water.

The "Power" Offense is a basketball set offense used by almost every NBA team to free up outstanding shooters by running them off baseline and down screens. It is initiated with wings crossing under the basket and curling off down screens set by posts, while the point guard looks to pass to the shooters or feed the posts rolling to the basket. The offense includes specific reads and counters based on defensive actions: shooters curl when defenders chase out, fade when defenders cheat over the screen, back cut on early anticipation, and execute screen-and-roll or isolations when defenders switch. Automatic counters address defensive overplays through fake cross entries, misdirection, back cuts, direct post entries, and dribble drives. If the initial action does not produce a shot, continuity options—Motion, Side Screen, Drive & Kick, and Triangle Post—provide continuous player movement. A "Single/Double" variation sets double and single baseline screens for a great shooter. The offense emphasizes offensive rebounding, precise execution, non-verbal communication, timing, and defensive recognition. Game strategies include scouting opponents, deploying various alignments, attacking the weakest defenders, and using Side Screens as the shot clock winds down. Even teams that do not run the offense must know how to defend against it.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2015. Net sales for the second quarter of 2015 were $23.2 billion, up 20% from the prior year, and $45.9 billion for the six-month period. The company reported net income of $92 million in Q2 2015 compared to a net loss of $126 million in Q2 2014, and net income of $35 million for the six months ended June 30, 2015 versus an $18 million net loss in the prior year period. Operating income increased to $464 million in Q2 from a $15 million loss. Segment net sales were North America $13.8 billion, International $7.6 billion, and AWS $1.8 billion, with AWS sales increasing 81% year-over-year. Cash and cash equivalents totaled $10.3 billion at quarter end. Operating cash flow was $2.0 billion in Q2, and trailing twelve-month free cash flow was $4.4 billion. The company changed its reportable segments to North America, International, and AWS, and acquired certain companies for $349 million. It disclosed long-term debt with a face value of $8.3 billion and total contractual commitments of $32.8 billion. Legal proceedings include patent infringement complaints and a European Commission competition investigation. Tax contingencies totaled $854 million, including disputes with the IRS over approximately $1.5 billion in additional federal tax for 2005–2006 transfer pricing, a €196 million French tax assessment for 2006–2010, and a European Commission state aid investigation in Luxembourg.

Ruston (La.) faces Stephenville (Texas) in a top ranked interstate high school football game in Stephenville. Ruston enters 4-0 and ranked No. 2 in Louisiana and No. 25 in Texas, while Stephenville is 5-0. After both teams traded three-and-outs, Ruston running back Dalen Powell fumbled on the Bearcat 19, and Stephenville quarterback Trot Jordan threw a 19-yard touchdown pass to Jhett Banuelos. Last year, Ruston defeated Stephenville 63-17.

The United States proposed arbitration to settle the boundary dispute between Great Britain and Venezuela, but Britain refused. Britain argued the Monroe Doctrine was inapplicable to modern conditions and not part of international law. The U.S. defended the doctrine as essential to national safety and applicable to the dispute, asserting that any European territorial extension in the Americas threatens its interests. The U.S. now intends to determine the true boundary itself and requests that Congress fund a commission to investigate the divisional line between Venezuela and British Guiana. Upon the commission's report, the U.S. will resist any British appropriation or jurisdiction over territory found to belong to Venezuela. The message acknowledges the gravity of this course but maintains that submitting to injustice would compromise national honor and safety.

The U.S. Supreme Court’s October 2025 term, beginning October 6, includes major cases on presidential power, civil rights, and social issues. Over the summer, the Court issued 6-3 shadow docket rulings allowing the Trump administration to fire Consumer Product Safety Commission and Federal Trade Commission commissioners, terminate National Institutes of Health grants, and permit Immigration and Customs Enforcement racial profiling in Los Angeles. This term, the Court will hear challenges to President Trump’s authority to impose tariffs, to Congress’s power to limit the president’s ability to fire agency heads—potentially overruling a 1935 precedent—and to an executive order restricting birthright citizenship. The Court will also rehear a Louisiana redistricting case that could affect the constitutionality of Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act and disparate impact liability under laws such as Title VII and the Fair Housing Act. Additional cases involve a Colorado law banning conversion therapy, Idaho and West Virginia laws limiting transgender athletes, and whether the Fourth Amendment’s emergency aid exception requires probable cause for police to enter a home. Author Erwin Chemerinsky predicts the term will produce blockbuster rulings profoundly affecting law and American society.

The Department of Homeland Security proposed replacing the "duration of status" policy with a four-year cap on how long international students can remain in the U.S., requiring USCIS extensions to stay longer and barring students from changing majors or transferring institutions. Higher education institutions, hospitals, and private sector leaders opposed the rule, submitting comments before the September 29 deadline arguing it would unnecessarily restrict already closely monitored students, disrupt healthcare systems relying on roughly 17,000 J-1 visa physicians, harm research and industry, and burden schools with costly, uncertain extension processes. Commenters noted many programs require more than four years. DHS stated the rule aims to reduce F and J visa overstays, though critics say overstay rates are overestimated. Few comments supported the change, some claiming international students displace Americans; one association suggested limiting the rule to colleges with admission rates under 30 percent.

Apple Inc.’s Form 8-K dated June 3, 2015, reports an underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs International and Mitsubishi UFJ Securities International plc for ¥250 billion of 0.350% senior unsecured Notes due 2020. The notes mature June 10, 2020, pay interest semi-annually beginning December 10, 2015, and will be issued under an indenture dated April 29, 2013. The report was signed June 10, 2015, by CFO Luca Maestri and includes related exhibits.

Diet can provide protection as temperatures fall and colds and flu spread. Rest and hydration are vital, yet food provides nutrients and energy. Poor nutritional choices slow recovery. Fruit and vegetables probably have the most impact in fighting infection; variety including different coloured fruits is beneficial. Beta carotene is the primary source of vitamin A; carrots and orange, yellow, or red vegetables are ideal sources. Fruit and vegetables supply fibres helping beneficial bacteria regulate immune activity, and provide vitamins A and C and minerals such as magnesium and zinc. Protein helps the body grow, repair, and regulate hormones; a lack of protein disrupts T cell and antibody production and reduces the ability to repair itself. Herbs and spices boost immunity through anti-inflammatory and anti-bacterial compounds; ginger is an antioxidant and turmeric has anti-bacterial properties. Coriander, mint, and basil contain antioxidants. Probiotics stimulate the immune system. Nuts and seeds provide minerals, fatty acids, and vitamin E for cell repair. These food groups can be easily included in a diet.

This qualitative phenomenological study examined the perspectives of 16 early childhood teachers in Ankara—eight bilingual teachers in private preschools offering foreign-language instruction and eight monolingual teachers in state preschools—on bilingualism and bilingual education. Through semi-structured interviews and content analysis, five themes emerged: benefits of bilingual education, bilingual children attending monolingual schools, bilingual education programs, issues in bilingual education, and the impact of bilingualism on children’s development. Both groups agreed that bilingualism offers advantages for children’s future careers, self-confidence, cognitive development, and communication skills, and they supported the expansion of bilingual schools in Türkiye. However, perspectives diverged regarding bilingual children in monolingual schools; most bilingual teachers viewed it as a disadvantage due to the risk of losing the second language, while some monolingual teachers considered it beneficial for strengthening the native language. Teachers generally lacked sufficient knowledge about specific bilingual program models, though both groups emphasized that school staff should be proficient in both languages. Identified challenges included ineffective use of both languages by teachers, shortages of qualified personnel and resources, children’s language deficiencies, and insufficient parental familiarity with the second language. Monolingual teachers more frequently noted negative developmental impacts, such as difficulties arising from not knowing the dominant community language, whereas bilingual teachers highlighted positive outcomes like enhanced self-confidence and cultural awareness. The study concludes that despite gaps in their knowledge of program implementation, teachers recognize bilingualism as an advantage and recommend improved professional development, better-qualified personnel, adequate resources, and parental support to advance bilingual early childhood education.

Losing a long overtime finals game was difficult, but they must regroup and give their best shot tomorrow night; they have been here before. Both goalies played tremendously well, with only one goal in six periods. They remain excited, will adjust their approach, and will not dwell on missed opportunities.

Artificial intelligence is changing the intellectual property landscape and raising unresolved questions about whether AI can be an inventor or hold a patent and what "a person skilled in the art" might reasonably know. Foley Hoag biotech patent lawyer DeAnn Smith expects these issues to be worked out in future litigation. The U.S. patent office required physical models of inventions until 1880, when it switched to requiring diagrams.

This study compared three surveys regarding primary care physicians’ experiences with EHR interoperability: the 2021 National Electronic Health Records Survey (NEHRS), a voluntary survey with an 18.2% response rate; the 2022 American Board of Family Medicine Continuous Certification Questionnaire (CCQ), a mandatory recertification component with a 100% response rate; and the 2022 University of California, San Francisco Physician Health IT Survey, a voluntary survey with a 3.6% response rate. While all three surveys indicated substantial room for improvement in health information technology interoperability, physician satisfaction, and after-hours documentation, they differed significantly in respondent demographics and granular findings. CCQ respondents skewed younger and were more likely to work in health systems, NEHRS respondents were disproportionately in private practice, and UCSF respondents were more often in academic or faculty practices. CCQ and NEHRS results were relatively similar on some interoperability measures, whereas UCSF respondents reported substantially less positive experiences. Stratified analyses showed these cross-survey differences persisted across age groups, EHR platforms, and practice types. The authors conclude that high-level findings were consistent across sources, but differences in response rates and respondent composition affect granular, policy-relevant results. They suggest that supplementing NEHRS with mandatory data from medical certifying boards could improve reliability, though such surveys are limited to specific specialties.

A multi-centre randomised controlled trial across five English sites evaluated the 12-month PrAISED intervention, an intensive, tailored exercise and functional activity rehabilitation programme for people with mild dementia or mild cognitive impairment. Three hundred and sixty-five patient-carer dyads were randomised to the intervention (up to 50 home therapy sessions over 12 months) or a control condition (falls prevention assessment and advice). The primary outcome was carer-rated disability in activities of daily living at 12 months. Despite high adherence, reasonable fidelity, and positive reception from participants and therapists, the intervention showed no significant effect on activities of daily living, physical activity, quality of life, cognition, or most secondary health status outcomes. A possible but statistically uncertain 22% relative reduction in fall rate and some cognitive domain improvements in underpowered analyses did not translate into functional gains. Delivery and follow-up were disrupted by the COVID-19 pandemic. The authors conclude that exercise and functionally orientated rehabilitation are unlikely to change the rate of functional decline in dementia, and that post-diagnostic support should instead emphasise adapted or supported functioning, psycho-social wellbeing, and therapeutic relationships.

Karmel Davis was named Tupelo Public School District 2017 Parent of the Year. Corey Crayton received a Northeast Mississippi Habitat for Humanity home funded by HomeStretch Furniture after completing sweat equity hours. Millsaps junior Noah Barbieri was named a Truman Scholar, receiving $30,000 for graduate school; he is the second Millsaps student to receive the award and plans to pursue an economics doctorate.

In this October 2, 1998 decision from the United States District Court for the Western District of New York, Chief Judge Larimer granted defendant Garlock Sealing Technologies’ motion for summary judgment and dismissed pro se plaintiff Steven C. Gittens, Sr.’s Americans with Disabilities Act complaint with prejudice. The court held that dismissal was warranted under Federal Rules of Civil Procedure 41(b), 16(f), and 56 because the plaintiff failed to respond to the motion or obey court orders for over six months despite explicit warnings, demonstrating willfulness and bad faith. On the merits, the court found the plaintiff failed to establish a prima facie case of disability discrimination because his 25-to-30-pound lifting restriction and inability to perform a specific punch press operation did not substantially limit the major life activity of working as required by the ADA; he had remained employed in other positions and presented no evidence that defendant’s legitimate, non-discriminatory reasons for reassignment were pretextual.

This review examines lung cancer screening biomarkers to address high mortality resulting from late-stage diagnosis and inadequate early detection. Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer death globally, with 2.1 million new cases and 1.8 million deaths reported in 2018. The study analyzed U.S. clinical research from the past 10 years to evaluate the sensitivity and specificity of various screening methods. Biomarkers assessed included volatile organic compounds (80% sensitivity and specificity); circulating tumor DNA (80% sensitivity, 96% specificity); four miRNA molecules (93–96% sensitivity, 23–33% specificity); six methylated genes in sputum and serum (varying sensitivities and specificities); Ga-Alfatide II scans (86% sensitivity, 85% specificity); combined score analysis (78% sensitivity, 50% specificity); and WT-IDH (63% sensitivity, 93% specificity). Circulating tumor DNA and Ga-Alfatide II PET/CT scans were identified as the most promising screening tools due to high sensitivity and specificity. Other biomarkers require further refinement to be viable. The review notes that small cell lung carcinoma carries a poor prognosis, while adenocarcinoma has a better prognosis with early surgical resection. Current standard screening involves low-dose CT for patients aged 50–80. The authors recommend advancing biomarker-targeted screening, minimizing modifiable risk factors, and exploring immunotherapy and chemotherapy to reduce mortality.

The passage argues that justice must be swift but lawful, condemning mob lynching. It asserts that education, particularly industrial schools like Hampton and Tuskegee, benefits both Black and white citizens by reducing criminality and improving race relations. It warns that inflammatory rhetoric from demagogues incites mob violence and, through “suggestion,” increases the very crimes denounced. The text further criticizes agitators who preach class hatred against the wealthy, stating they corrupt genuine reform, foster anarchy, and provoke destructive backlash. It concludes that progress requires rejecting both demagogues who exploit base passions and wealthy exploiters who disregard public welfare, advocating instead for a sane, resolute advance along the path set by Congress.

Pocatello-Chubbuck School District will finalize high school boundary changes using three focus groups. Trustees tabled the decision last month seeking more feedback. It ended open enrollment after 20 years due to enrollment and socioeconomic disparities among three high schools.

In In re Jeffery Wayne Smith and Paulette Monee Smith (Bankr. N.D. Ind. May 29, 1998), the bankruptcy court partially granted and partially denied the Standing Chapter 13 Trustee’s objection to the debtors’ amended Chapter 13 plan. The debtors proposed to pay Chrysler Financial Corporation in full for a 1997 vehicle purchased shortly before bankruptcy, pay NBD Bank the replacement value of a 1996 vehicle, and pay a limited dividend to unsecured creditors. The Trustee objected, arguing unfair discrimination under 11 U.S.C. § 1322, lack of good faith under § 1325(a)(3), and failure to apply all disposable income under § 1325(b)(1)(B). The court held that the disparate treatment of Chrysler was permissible because the debtors had bought the vehicle five months before filing and made no payments, making full payment equitable, but reduced Chrysler’s interest rate from 8% to the 3.9% contract rate. The court found the plan was filed in good faith, accepting the debtors’ explanations for scheduling oversights and for deferring ERISA-qualified profit sharing benefits into a 401(k) to avoid taxes and penalties. Regarding disposable income, the court ordered the debtors to furnish paycheck stubs every six months and remit net overtime exceeding projections; increased the monthly plan payment by $75 to $1,808.33; held that undistributed ERISA profit sharing benefits were not disposable income but required any cash distributions received during the plan to be paid to creditors; and mandated that voluntary retirement or 401(k) contributions from income cease and be devoted to plan payments. The court confirmed the amended plan as modified, finding it satisfied the requirements of 11 U.S.C. §§ 1322 and 1325.

Snap faces significant competition from Facebook's Instagram and Microsoft Skype, which have replicated its features, contributing to a 22% year-over-year decline in app downloads and 166 million daily active users. Only 7% of marketers used Snapchat in the first quarter of 2017. Snap reported first-quarter revenue of $150 million and a loss of $2.31 per share, missing consensus estimates. A lock-up expiration by the end of July will release 1.2 billion shares, representing an estimated 84% dilution of outstanding stock and potential downward price pressure if insiders sell. With 28% of the float in short positions, the author views shorting as risky and plans to watch from the sidelines, seeing no short-term value in owning the stock.

Safety endpoints at 24 and 48 weeks were similar across study groups, with comparable rates of adverse events, serious events, bleeding, and deaths. Twenty-four deaths were reported overall, and no pregnancies occurred. Laboratory data revealed no clinically concerning hepatic or renal signals. The AEGEAN study concluded that apixaban therapy for atrial fibrillation yielded high adherence and persistence through 48 weeks, but the proactive educational program provided no additional adherence or persistence benefits.

Cosmonauts Fyodor Yurchikhin and Sergey Ryazanskiy will conduct an ISS spacewalk on August 17, exiting Pirs airlock at 10:45 am EDT. Ryazanskiy will deploy five nanosatellites; both will collect samples and install handrails. Yurchikhin, EV1 on his ninth spacewalk, and Ryazanskiy, EV2 on his fourth, will wear Orlan spacesuits with blue stripes. NASA will telecast the 202nd spacewalk live.

Stenabolic (SR9009) is an oral synthetic Rev-Erb ligand developed by Scripps Investigation Institute. By activating the Rev-Erb protein, it increases muscle mitochondria and metabolism, improving endurance and strength. Mice studies showed 50% greater running capacity. It increases resting energy expenditure by 5%, burns fat and glucose, and reduces liver cholesterol. It lowers triglycerides by 12%, total cholesterol by 47%, fatty acids by 23%, glucose by 19%, insulin by 35%, and IL-6 by 72%. It is gaining popularity among athletes.

Zemlin cited Linux dominance in high performance computing, stock exchanges, and mobile devices, plus $14.5 billion in value. Hart joined as Gold Member with healthcare API HartOS. The Linux Foundation released free open source basics publication; Cloud Native Computing Foundation added 11 members.

The "Single/Double" offense attacks the Triangle & Two defense by using screens to free shooters from the chasers' pass denial. Screens can be run from either side, creating options including left and right entries, double screens, single screens, pop outs, base screens, and side screens with rolls, drop passes, and kick out passes. Success requires execution, coordination, defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, timing, and experience, developed through breakdown drills and scrimmaging. Game strategies include scouting opponents, using varied alignments and entries, and attacking weak defenders. In the Triangle & Two defense, three players guard a zone triangle while two chasers aggressively deny passes and rebounds to specific opponents.

This study examines 114 Greek primary teachers’ views on STEM education and conditions for its effective implementation, using a digital questionnaire and structured interviews from March to May 2022. Teachers highly value STEM for developing students’ scientific thinking, problem-solving, critical thinking, collaboration, and connections to everyday life, and many perceive it as a means to reduce educational inequalities. However, they identify a major gap between the importance they assign to core STEM practices and the minimal frequency with which students actually perform them. Teachers report low self-efficacy in teaching science and mathematics—especially science—and attribute STEM implementation weaknesses to insufficient training and materials (58%), inadequate infrastructure and equipment (42%), and limited time with unclear curriculum placement (31%). To support implementation, 71% request additional training, while others cite needs for equipment, teaching materials, ongoing guidance, sample lessons, and timetable adjustments. The authors note that Greece introduced STEM in 2021–2022 as under-resourced “skills workshops” without adequate funding or materials, leaving willing teachers underprepared. They conclude that effective STEM integration requires systemic institutional support rather than blaming educators for implementation failures.

The passage includes a blank U.S. passport application template and a May 10, 1902, letter from the U.S. Legation in Buenos Aires regarding Argentine President Julio A. Roca’s message to Congress. The message was optimistic but disappointed expectations by treating vaguely the British-mediated negotiations with Chile to limit armaments, a generality the letter attributes to the recent death of Foreign Minister Dr. Alcorta. Both nations had incurred heavy military expenditures, causing debt, deficits, appropriated conversion funds, high loan interest, heavy taxation, and poor economic conditions, leading to recognition that costly arms spending must cease.

South Korea's fertility rate fell from 2.1 in 1984 to 1.6 in 1987 as married women's education levels increased. By 2012, nearly 95% of married women held high school or university degrees, while labor force participation rose from 39% to 53%. The fertility rate stood at 1.24 in 2015.
Newly analyzed microstructures explain why dandelion seeds are difficult to dislodge.

Archaeologists excavating Amsterdam's Amstel riverbed for a subway line discovered 700,000 discarded objects spanning from Neolithic stone axes to modern cellphones as part of the "Below the Surface" project. The finds, recovered from 12 meters below two construction sites, include everyday items like pots, coins, weapons, and personal objects, many preserved intact. A selection of 10,000 objects will be displayed at the new Rokin subway station, opening July 22 with the North/South line. The project features an interactive website with about 30,000 objects attracting 40,000 to 60,000 daily visitors, and a book-catalog called "Stuff" distributed to schools. The project cost 6 million Euros.

This document outlines the statistical analysis plan for a clinical trial evaluating dasiglucagon, GlucaGen, and placebo. Concomitant medications and current diabetes treatment will be coded with WHODrug/ATC and summarized by treatment. The primary efficacy endpoint, time to plasma glucose recovery within 45 minutes, will be analyzed on the Full Analysis Set using Kaplan-Meier methods, a stratified log-rank test, and a Cox proportional hazards model adjusted for age group and injection site; sensitivity analyses include alternative censoring rules for rescue IV glucose. A hierarchical procedure controls type I error for confirmatory dasiglucagon versus placebo comparisons. Secondary endpoints include plasma glucose recovery rates and changes from baseline at 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes, analyzed via Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel tests and analysis of variance. Pharmacokinetic parameters will be derived by non-compartmental analysis, and the pharmacodynamic endpoint is the plasma glucose area under the effect curve from 0 to 30 minutes. Safety analyses, based on the safety set, will summarize treatment-emergent adverse events, local tolerability, laboratory results, vital signs, ECG parameters, QTc intervals, and immunogenicity. No interim analyses are planned, missing data will not be imputed, and appendices provide programming specifications, QC requirements, and a list of planned tables, figures, and listings.

A goaltender described making key saves during finals games, including an initial breakaway save and a "soccer goalie save." He noted he was not happy with his game in the first two games but said recent timely saves boosted his confidence. He expressed pride in playing in Nashville, citing the city's and hockey's growth, and described the special feeling of playing before the home crowd.

Before COVID-19, Japanese universities lagged in educational ICT use due to traditional in-person education norms and structural barriers such as credit limits on distance learning. The pandemic forced an immediate shift to full-time online classes, prompting examination of MEXT policy, academic staff, students, and lifelong learning. Japan’s 788 mostly private universities enroll young, digitally native undergraduates, while faculty—traditionally research-oriented—have increased teaching hours since 2008 credit-system reforms.

MEXT had planned digitalization pre-pandemic, capping remote credits at 60 until COVID-19 prompted emergency relaxation and later hybrid policies. The 2022 revision of university establishment standards maintained credit limits but allowed exceptions for institutions with strong internal quality assurance. MEXT launched projects such as Scheem-D and Plus-DX to support digitalization. Cabinet-level initiatives under “Society 5.0” and Prime Minister Kishida promoted inter-university online collaboration and integration of student data with “My Number,” raising concerns about personal information protection.

Faculty ICT use was previously limited largely to PowerPoint, with low adoption of LMS and file-sharing tools. The pandemic forced widespread use of hybrid and high-flex formats, revealing challenges in student communication, practical instruction, and faculty digital literacy. Sharing online best practices and preserving face-to-face interaction are viewed as important responses, though transforming educational culture remains slow.

Japan’s credit system lacks “substantiation”: students average only five weekly self-study hours against a 30-hour standard, burdened by heavy course loads, early job hunting, and cultural views emphasizing leisure and social activities. The pandemic increased out-of-class learning through LMS-based assignments, but also created burdens. Experts recommend combining ICT tools with reduced course loads and improved curriculum management.

Lifelong learning is weakly institutionalized. Degree-oriented university distance learning serves most adult learners and was gradually digitalizing, yet remained marginal during the pandemic and largely separate from commuter programs. Traditional non-degree public lectures (Kokaikoza) saw minimal digitalization due to resource constraints, while newer vocational certificate programs targeting working adults advanced further online, accelerated by COVID-19.

In conclusion, while the pandemic rapidly advanced university digitalization and created opportunities for adult learners, persistent challenges include university culture, credit-system reform, the peripheral status of lifelong learning, and risks of sharing digitized student data across government and private sectors. Addressing these requires sector-wide infrastructure development and careful multi-stakeholder dialogue.

The lecture advances the proof of Freiman’s theorem for sets of small doubling. Recalling Ruzsa’s modeling lemma, a set with small doubling contains a large subset (at least 1/8 of its size) that is Freiman 8-isomorphic to a subset of a small cyclic group. The aim is to extract additive structure from such a dense subset.

In the finite field model \( \mathbb{F}_2^m \), a subset \( A \) of constant density \( \alpha \) need not have \( A+A \) contain a large subspace, as illustrated by a Niveo set. However, Bogolyubov’s lemma states that \( 2A - 2A \) contains a subspace of codimension less than \( 1/\alpha^2 \). The proof uses Fourier analysis on the convolution of indicator functions for \( A \) and \( -A \); the support of this convolution is \( 2A - 2A \). Letting \( R \) be the set of characters with large Fourier coefficients (at least \( \alpha^{3/2} \)), Parseval’s identity bounds \( |R| < 1/\alpha^2 \). The orthogonal complement of \( R \) is contained in the support of the convolution, yielding the subspace.

For the cyclic group \( \mathbb{Z} \mod n \), subspaces are replaced by Bohr sets. A Bohr set \( \text{Bohr}(R, \epsilon) \) consists of elements \( x \) such that \( rx/n \) is within \( \epsilon \) of an integer for all \( r \in R \); \( |R| \) is its dimension and \( \epsilon \) its width. Bogolyubov’s lemma in this setting says \( 2A - 2A \) contains a Bohr set of dimension less than \( 1/\alpha^2 \) and width \( 1/4 \). The proof follows the same Fourier-analytic argument with modified notation.

To locate a generalized arithmetic progression (GAP), the lecture turns to the geometry of numbers. A lattice in \( \mathbb{R}^d \) is the integer span of \( d \) independent vectors, and its determinant is the volume of its fundamental parallelepiped. For a centrally symmetric convex body \( K \), the \( i \)-th successive minimum \( \lambda_i \) is the smallest scale such that \( \lambda_i K \) contains \( i \) linearly independent lattice vectors. Minkowski’s second theorem states that the product of the \( d \) successive minima times \( \text{vol}(K) \) is at most \( 2^d \) times the lattice determinant.

This is applied to show that a Bohr set of dimension \( d \) and width \( \epsilon \) contains a proper GAP of dimension at most \( d \) and size at least \( (\epsilon/d)^d \) fraction of the cyclic group. The proof constructs a \( d \)-dimensional lattice from the Bohr set’s frequencies and applies Minkowski’s theorem to a box of width \( 2\epsilon \), yielding directional basis vectors that project to a proper GAP. These results provide the necessary ingredients to conclude the proof of Freiman’s theorem.

The ScottishPower Foundation donated £95,220 to the Sussex Wildlife Trust for its 50th anniversary celebrations at Woods Mill in Henfield. The funding will enable 1,300 additional people to participate in events, deliver ten wildlife identification courses, train 250 wildlife champions, establish a young naturalists club, and fund habitat improvements including reed bed restoration and improved path access. Foundation trustees visited the site this week and joined a pond-dipping session with local primary school students.

The NVIDIA A100 GPU, based on the Ampere architecture, delivers significant improvements over the V100. Its third-generation Tensor Cores increase thread sharing by 4x, issuing 8x fewer instructions and performing 2.9x fewer register file accesses for matrix multiplies. A new asynchronous copy instruction loads data directly from global memory into shared memory, bypassing L1 cache and registers, while maximum shared memory per SM increases 1.7x to 164 KB. The GPU provides 1555 GB/sec HBM2 memory bandwidth, 2.3x L2 read bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache with residency controls, and Compute Data Compression to reduce DRAM traffic.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) can partition each A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute and memory paths, enabling multi-tenant deployment with defined quality of service and fault isolation. Instances can be subdivided into Compute Instances, and vGPUs can be migrated to balance loads.

Third-generation NVLink delivers 600 GB/sec total bandwidth via 12 links, while PCIe Gen 4 provides 31.5 GB/sec per direction and SR-IOV support. The architecture improves error attribution, isolation, and containment.

Additional hardware includes five NVJPG and five NVDEC decode engines, an Optical Flow Accelerator, and 11x/2.7x improved FP16/FP32 atomic throughput. CUDA 11 introduces Task Graphs, asynchronous copy and barriers, L2 residency controls, and Cooperative Groups enhancements. The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs via NVSwitch to deliver 5 PFLOPS, scaling via MIG. The A100 also supports fine-grained structured 2:4 sparsity to accelerate sparse neural networks with virtually no accuracy loss.

The SUSHI study developed and evaluated an online version of the Social Inclusion Questionnaire User Experience (SInQUE) for mental health supported accommodation services in an inner London borough. Through lab-testing with six staff members and field-testing with twelve staff and twelve service users, researchers refined the 46-item tool, which assesses social inclusion across nine areas and generates reports to inform collaborative care planning. Participants generally found the tool user-friendly and relevant, though some staff raised concerns about intrusive questions that service users did not share. An implementation strategy was essential for uptake: in the borough with support, 27 staff registered and 30 assessments were completed with 28 service users, while no assessments were completed in two other areas offered the tool without implementation support. Using the ICAMO framework, the team developed a logic model mapping intervention characteristics, context, actors, mechanisms, and outcomes. The findings indicate the online SInQUE is acceptable and potentially useful, particularly in supported housing, but achieving broader use requires active leadership endorsement. Limitations include approximately 10% uptake, no female service user participants, testing in a single borough, and a short study period.

The Dark Cloud Cover is a bearish reversal candlestick pattern occurring after an uptrend or rally within a downtrend. It forms when a bearish candlestick opens above the previous bullish candlestick’s close but closes below its midpoint, suggesting a shift from bullish to bearish sentiment. Traders may use the pattern as a signal for short selling or closing long positions, but it is not a guarantee of reversal. Confirmation should be sought through subsequent price action, technical indicators such as Moving Averages, MACD, or RSI, and resistance levels. The strategy is best suited for bearish trends and can be applied across various assets and timeframes, though shorter timeframes carry a higher risk of false signals. Effective risk management, including stop-loss orders and integration with broader technical and fundamental analysis, is essential. Backtesting can provide performance insights, but results vary by market and parameters and do not predict future performance. Common mistakes include trading without confirmation, ignoring risk management, and using the pattern in inappropriate market conditions.

This document standardizes the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) to enable interoperability between guest operating systems and hypervisors supporting SEV-ES or SEV-SNP. The GHCB is defined as a 4KB decrypted page that mirrors the SEV-ES VMCB save state area; its guest physical address is established via MSR 0xc001_0130 and VMCB offset 0x00a0. The specification introduces protocol versioning, including Version 2 with a 52-bit hypervisor FEATURES bitmap for advertising capabilities, and subsequent revisions that add SEV-SNP support, 64-bit guest request sequence numbers, multiple VMPL levels, APIC ID lists, page state change notifications, SEV-TIO trusted device pass-through, Secure AVIC, and expanded error codes. A GHCB MSR protocol facilitates early negotiation of versions, SEV information, CPUID values, and GHCB GPA registration, which is required for SEV-SNP guests. Non-Automatic Exit (NAE) events are handled via #VC exceptions and VMGEXIT, using a VALID_BITMAP to track required guest and hypervisor state. Supported NAE events include IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, MMIO access, page state changes, SNP Guest and Extended Guest Requests, AP creation, #HV doorbell page management, IPI and timer emulation, APIC ID retrieval, SNP Run VMPL, SEV-TIO attestation, Secure AVIC backing page registration, and termination requests. The document details SMP booting through AP reset hold and jump tables, with SEV-SNP adding AP creation via VMSA pages. Under Restricted Injection, the hypervisor delivers events through a shared #HV doorbell page containing PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields. System Management Mode and nested virtualization are explicitly unsupported.
