This paper analyzes South Australia’s 2018 “World Class” public education policy using Bacchi’s “What’s the Problem Represented to be?” (WPR) framework. Situated within the Global Education Reform Movement (GERM) and informed by McKinsey and Company’s “Universal Scale” and “roadmap,” the policy aimed to achieve “World Class” status by 2028 by ranking schools on standardised measures including NAPLAN. The Department for Education represented the problem as competing educator voices and insufficient clarity, proposing centralised control as the solution. Through document analysis of publicly available and freedom-of-information materials, the authors find the policy relied on a “single source of truth” School Improvement Dashboard, scripted curriculum, and a 50 percent increase in Education Directors to enforce compliance. Schools were differentiated into five performance tiers, with low-NAPLAN (typically disadvantaged) schools subjected to greater bureaucratic scrutiny and reduced autonomy. The paper argues this “managerially enforced” complexity reduction eroded professional trust, marginalised the social and democratic purposes of schooling, and narrowed educational focus to standardised test scores. After four years, outcomes included declining PIRLS results, a widening PISA equity gap, increased absenteeism, and reduced retention and certification rates. The authors propose a “Beyond World Class” alternative that prioritises equity, inclusion, democratic policy partnerships, and professional trust in educators, aligned with the Alice Springs (Mparntwe) Education Declaration.

Non-centrosymmetric crystals lacking inversion symmetry can exhibit polar properties. Polar metals combine a polar crystal structure with intrinsic metallic conductivity; because itinerant electrons screen electric fields, the polarization direction cannot be reversed by an applied field. Distortive polar metals (DPMs) undergo a centrosymmetry-lifting structural transformation. This study investigates the metallic DPM Mn5Al8, which undergoes a first-order martensitic transformation from cubic γ-brass (I¯43m) to polar rhombohedral γ2 (R3m) at approximately 880°C, as confirmed by X-ray diffraction, differential scanning calorimetry, resistivity measurements, and density functional theory calculations indicating metallic behavior. The symmetry reduction creates a herringbone microstructure of rank-2 laminate twins with four polar variants. Advanced electron microscopy, including four-dimensional STEM differential phase contrast, reveals head-to-head (H-H) and tail-to-tail (T-T) domain boundaries exhibiting "bound charge" configurations. Despite the absence of net free charge in a metal, surface characterization via low-voltage SEM, electrostatic force microscopy, copper deposition, and oxidation patterns indicates variable surface reactivity correlated with boundary type: H-H boundaries show lower work function and higher local electron concentration, while T-T boundaries appear depleted. A chemical sorting of the Inorganic Crystal Structure Database identified roughly 134 metallic polar metals, about 20% of which are DPMs, highlighting a broad chemical space. The results suggest that geometric polarization discontinuities in metallic DPMs can locally influence the density of states and free carrier concentrations at domain boundaries.

Active galactic nuclei (AGN) variability challenges the standard Shakura-Sunyaev disc model, which predicts changes on thousands of years rather than the observed months-to-years timescales. The Seyfert 1 galaxy Fairall 9, monitored for roughly 1000 days by Swift, NICER, and LCO, provides a detailed test case. Its spectral energy distribution (SED) evolves across three segments, showing a 40–50% increase in the global mass-accretion rate and a brighter optical/UV disc, while the integrated X-ray coronal power remains nearly constant, softening due to increased seed-photon Compton cooling. Fourier analysis using Gaussian Process regression reveals that UV and X-ray power spectra differ, suggesting separate intrinsic origins. Frequency-resolved lags and coherence vary between segments: early data show long, semi-coherent lags inconsistent with simple disc reverberation, while later data show reduced coherence. An analytic model treating observed emission as combinations of intrinsic disc and coronal light-curves—linked by seed-photon modulation, X-ray reverberation, and wind reprocessing—can explain the weak correlation and stochastic lag variations as interference between intrinsic disc and coronal power at low frequencies. The sharp rising phase, however, requires an additional long inward-propagating component, likely driven by the global mass-accretion rate increase altering the inner flow structure. These results indicate that Fairall 9’s inner accretion geometry evolves on observable timescales, contradicting static standard disc theory and complicating reverberation interpretations.

Jane Goodall, the pioneering primatologist and conservationist, died at 91 on October 1 while on tour in California; the Jane Goodall Institute stated she died in her sleep of natural causes. Without formal training, Goodall was hired by archaeologist Louis Leakey and began observing chimpanzees in Tanzania's Gombe Stream Game Reserve in 1960. She discovered that chimpanzees make and use tools, engage in warfare, and have personalities. She earned a PhD in ethology from Cambridge in 1965 without obtaining a bachelor's degree. Goodall married wildlife photographer Hugo Van Lawick in 1964; they had a son and divorced in 1974. She married Derek Bryceson in 1975, who died in 1980. In 1977, she founded the Jane Goodall Institute, adding the Roots & Shoots youth program in 1991. She advocated for ending invasive chimpanzee research, and in 2015 the last federally owned lab chimps retired. She was named a UN Messenger of Peace in 2002, a Dame of the British Empire in 2004, and received the French Legion of Honor in 2006.

This randomized controlled trial (NCT05557643) compared Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) alone versus MBSR combined with group psilocybin-assisted psychotherapy (PAP) for frontline physicians and nurses experiencing depression and burnout related to COVID-19. Twenty-five participants were randomized to an 8-week MBSR course or to MBSR plus a group psilocybin dosing session (25 mg) with preparatory and integration sessions. The primary outcome was change in Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology (QIDS-SR-16) scores at two weeks post-intervention. The MBSR+PAP group showed a significantly greater reduction in depressive symptoms at two weeks compared with MBSR alone (between-groups effect=4.6, p=0.004, d=1.04), with mean scores indicating remission. The combined intervention also significantly reduced depersonalization at two weeks, emotional exhaustion at six months, demoralization, and increased connectedness to self and others. All adverse events were mild or moderate; there were no serious adverse events, emergent suicidality, or self-injurious behaviors. Attendance was high in both arms. Post-randomization expectancy was higher for MBSR+PAP but was not associated with symptom improvement in that arm, whereas it was in the MBSR-only arm. Mystical experience scores correlated with clinical improvements across the entire sample. The authors conclude that group MBSR+PAP is safe, feasible, and potentially efficacious for this population, though the small, homogeneous, unblinded sample limits generalizability, and larger placebo-controlled trials are needed.

In July 1889, an insurrection by Robert Wilcox and Robert Boyd was defeated, and U.S. sailors from the U.S.S. Adams landed to protect the city. Stock trading strategies are defined rules and methods for short-term buying and selling of stocks and ETFs, distinct from long-term investing. Approaches include day trading, swing trading, momentum trading, scalping, trend following, arbitrage, high-frequency trading, event-driven trading, sector rotation, pair trading, market-neutral trading, statistical arbitrage, technical analysis, seasonality, long-short equity, S&P 500 trading, Nasdaq 100 trading, overnight trading, mean reversion, and oscillator trading. Successful application requires discipline, quantified and backtested rules, risk management, and accounting for costs such as commissions and slippage. Diversification across assets, sectors, strategies, and timeframes is recommended to mitigate risk, while trading a single stock is discouraged for retail traders due to the danger of severe losses. Emotions like fear and greed can lead to irrational decisions. Strategies may be automated with algorithms to enable faster execution and reduce human error. The 3 5 7 Rule posits that price movements often follow three initial pushes in one direction, five counter moves, and seven pushes reaffirming the original trend. The best strategy depends on an individual’s requirements, mindset, and ambitions.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit simultaneous-sampling data acquisition system. Each analog input channel features ±18V clamp protection, a programmable gain amplifier with user-selectable bandwidth and low-pass filter, and a 20-bit SAR ADC, supporting single-ended or differential true bipolar inputs with a constant 1MΩ impedance and common-mode rejection up to ±12V. The system achieves 2MSPS per channel for all channels simultaneously, or up to 8MSPS in speed-boost mode for a selected channel pair. It operates from 5V and 1.8V analog supplies, includes a 4.096V internal reference with external reference support, and provides 20-bit output data in straight-binary or two’s-complement formats. A source-synchronous interface supports 2-lane and 4-lane SDR and DDR modes. Additional features include a data randomizer, programmable digital averaging, test patterns for interface debugging, multi-device synchronization via SMPL_SYNC, and SPI-based configuration with daisy-chain capability. In ATE applications, the device offers 0.0015% post-calibration TUE and wide-bandwidth settling to 99.95% of full scale in 7.5µs.

The 3-2 zone is a 1-2-2 variation where the point defender drops to the free throw line, allowing wings to deny wing entry passes and protect the high post. It can be adjusted to a 1-2-2 or 1-3-1 against an excellent outside-shooting point guard. A taller, athletic wing can interchange with the point to limit high post passes and help weakside rebounding. The alignment supports fast breaks. Basic defensive shifts cover ball positions in the middle, wings, and corners, with alternate shifts using a point/wing interchange.

Mineral companies owe over $42 million in delinquent taxes to 12 Wyoming counties, primarily due to bankruptcies that leave counties as low-priority unsecured lenders, according to a Powder River Basin Resource Council report. Campbell County is owed the most at over $26 million, followed by Sheridan County at about $7.46 million. The county tax payment schedule’s 18-month delay contributes to the problem, compared to the state’s two-month severance tax turnaround. The unpaid taxes affect school districts and public services. The report recommends four policy changes: monthly ad valorem tax collection, perpetual liens, a state funding pool for bankruptcies, and legislation requiring tax debt checks before asset transfers. Previous legislative efforts have failed, but a new bill will be presented this year.

UNMC College of Dentistry provided free dental care to Nebraska children during Children's Dental Day. Since 2001, the program has served 159 to 200 children annually, providing over $3 million in dental services and education.

This patent application is a continuation of U.S. application Ser. No. 16/725,043, claiming priority from multiple UK and PCT applications, and relates to storage systems. It describes a system where stacks of storage containers are arranged within a framework beneath a grid of rails. Robotic load handling devices move on the rails to lift containers. The framework uprights and grid integrate service means—such as power, data communications, lighting, fluid pipes, and sensors—to enable interaction, control, and monitoring of the system and individual containers from within the framework. Services may be routed to containers via releasable connectors or non-contact methods like induction. Sensors and data loggers monitor structural integrity, environmental conditions, fire, smoke, heat, gas, and container identity, communicating data to a central system. The system supports condition monitoring without operational shutdown, targeted fluid or gas delivery (e.g., fire suppression), and partitioning into subsections. Containers may include transparent or no sides and internal service means. This configuration aims to increase reliability and reduce costs compared to prior art systems lacking integrated framework services.

US stock options expire on the third Friday of each month, shifting to Thursday if Friday is a holiday. Backtests since 1990 show the S&P 500 produces above-average returns during options expiration (OPEX) week, with March the strongest month and July and January the weakest. A strategy buying at the open of OPEX week and selling at the close of expiration day yielded an average gain of 0.2% per week for SPY, increasing to 0.3% when entering at the close of the preceding Friday. By contrast, holding only on the expiration day produced negative average returns. The week after OPEX week historically underperforms a random week, with August showing positive returns and September showing the worst performance. The day before OPEX also shows poor S&P 500 returns, while the day after averages a negative return. Four times per year—in March, June, September, and December—stock index futures, stock index options, single stock options, and single stock futures expire simultaneously on "quadruple witching" days, which can increase volatility due to hedging and "pin risk." Calendar-based trading strategies seek to exploit such recurring date-specific market patterns.

The elected Chief Magistrate takes the constitutional oath, expressing gratitude while acknowledging weighty responsibilities. He pledges cooperation with the legislative and judicial branches and appointing able, honorable officials. Guided by the Constitution, judicial decisions, and earlier Presidents, especially Washington, he will execute duties including commanding the military, conducting foreign relations, and enforcing laws. The lecture explains the mechanics of corporate carbon footprints using a WidgetCo case study, a chair manufacturer with owned and joint-venture plants in Michigan and Shanghai, U.S. distribution centers, and multiple transportation modes. The professor describes calculating emissions by multiplying activity data by published emissions factors, preferring fuel consumption data when possible and cautioning against mathematical aggregation errors when using ton-miles. The discussion defines the three emission scopes: Scope 1 (direct emissions from owned sources), Scope 2 (indirect emissions from purchased electricity), and Scope 3 (all other indirect emissions), noting that organizational boundaries determined by equity share or control approaches heavily influence results. Student calculations for WidgetCo varied significantly, largely depending on whether the Shanghai joint venture was included and under what boundary assumption. The lecture also covers practical data-gathering challenges, the need for consistent units and emissions factors, and the importance of both absolute and relative metrics. It examines disclosure drivers such as the Carbon Disclosure Project and investor pressure, and highlights the difficulty of comparing competitors like FerretCo, whose lower disclosed emissions partly reflect a different supply chain model using contract manufacturers outside its direct organizational boundary. The session concludes by distinguishing corporate footprints from supply chain and product-level assessments, previewing life cycle assessment as the methodology for product-level analysis.

This retrospective study of 1,383 patients at Nigeria's only dedicated noma hospital in Sokoto (1999–2024) estimated noma incidence across northern Nigeria using the WHO Delphi method. The overall incidence was 114.5 cases per 100,000 population, with an annual average of 4.4 and median of 2.2 cases per 100,000. Incidence was higher among males (120.7) than females (108.1) and highest in children under ten years. Sokoto state had the highest incidence overall (921.9) and among those under 18, while Kebbi had the highest incidence among young and middle-aged adults; Adamawa had the lowest incidence (6.3). Most patients presented with active disease (67.3%), and gangrene (stage 3) was the most common stage (59.7% of cases; incidence 101.5 per 100,000), exceeding oedema and acute necrotizing ulcerative gingivitis. The study noted increased incidence between 2020 and 2024 and highlighted the need for early detection programs. Data from six northern states or territories were unavailable.

This study examines barriers to distance education in Turkish university mathematics education following the COVID-19 pandemic and the February 2023 earthquake, which forced a return to online learning. Using Q methodology, 13 faculty members ranked 50 statements about online teaching obstacles. Three factors emerged: six faculty emphasized student-related barriers, such as disengagement, reluctance to participate, and distraction; five highlighted technology and facility deficiencies, including inadequate digital library access and equipment; and two identified pedagogical barriers specific to mathematics, such as unreliable online assessment, limited usefulness of graphic tablets compared to chalkboards, and difficulty representing mathematical concepts digitally. Overall analysis indicated curriculum-pedagogy barriers had the highest average impact, followed by teacher, technology, and student barriers. Notably, teacher-related barriers did not form a distinct factor, as participants felt experienced from pandemic-era teaching. All faculty agreed that pure distance education is unsuitable for mathematics and preferred blended or hybrid models. The study concludes that mathematics education faces unique field-specific obstacles in online environments.

Natural bacteria identified on grape plant leaves can degrade guaiacol, a primary compound causing smoke taint in wine from wildfire smoke. In laboratory tests, two bacterial strains nearly eliminated guaiacol within 96 hours but did not consume similar smoky compounds, indicating specificity. Researchers also identified the gene responsible for this degradation. Unlike activated charcoal filtering, which can remove desirable wine components, this microbial approach may offer a more targeted solution. However, additional research is needed to find bacteria capable of degrading other volatile phenols that contribute to smoke taint, a problem that cost California and Oregon winemakers over $3 billion in 2020.

The passage describes systems and methods for secure, zero-knowledge sharing of encrypted user data—particularly sensitive personal health information—between multiple users, such as healthcare providers and patients. To mitigate risks of server-side attacks, cloud provider liability, and burdensome electronic medical record requirements, embodiments employ a client-side Key Hierarchy Structure (KHS) with layered encryption. User credentials, including a password and answers to security questions, derive a Password-Derived Key (PDK) and a Questions-Derived Key (QDK), which encrypt a Master Encryption Key (MEK). The MEK encrypts one or more Data Encryption Keys (DEKs) that encrypt the actual user data. Plaintext keys and credentials are discarded and not stored in non-volatile memory, ensuring the server and cloud provider cannot access the data. For sharing, embodiments use public-key infrastructure or a Shared Data Key Hierarchy Structure (SD-KHS), in which a Shared DEK (SDEK) is encrypted for each authorized recipient’s public key; recipients decrypt the SDEK to access a shared copy. Modifications are proposed via encrypted messages to the data owner for approval. The system supports various client devices and uses key derivation functions, random salts, initialization vectors, and obfuscated KHS entry names.

This paper investigates whether highly impactful medical journals lead in disseminating interdisciplinary research (IDR) compared to less impactful journals. Using PubMed articles indexed with second-level MeSH "Disease" terms, the authors constructed correlation networks for articles published in the top 10% SCImago Journal Rank journals (I) and less impactful journals (NI) for 1999, 2010, and 2022, controlling for sample size with a June subset of NI articles. Results showed that NI journals consistently had higher average node strength and network density, indicating greater interdisciplinarity, whereas I journals exhibited higher modularity, reflecting more compartmentalized knowledge structures. Both tiers shared a stable inner core of concepts including sexually transmitted diseases, immunologic deficiency syndromes, and urogenital neoplasms. Neoplasms by site showed the highest node strength and betweenness centrality, highlighting cancer research as a major IDR driver. Analysis of positive and negative difference networks revealed that discrepancies between I and NI clustered around evolving topic areas over time, despite a universal stable core. The authors conclude that high-impact journals tend to publish more disciplinary-based research, potentially due to peer-review biases and clinical translation infrastructures—such as trial registration and reporting guidelines—that favor tightly pre-specified, single-discipline studies, and suggest integrating IDR evaluation within these compliance frameworks.

Archaeologists have identified a mass grave in Repton, Derbyshire, as the burial site of over 250 members of the Viking Great Heathen Army from 874. The lecture discusses plasma spectroscopy diagnostics and simplified equilibria used to model ionization and excitation states. Complete thermodynamic equilibrium features Boltzmann occupation, balanced microscopic processes, and a single shared temperature for electrons, ions, and radiation, but it is rare in practice because plasmas are seldom optically thick. Local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) assumes an optically thin plasma where collisional excitation and de-excitation dominate the population balance while radiative processes are ignored for setting state populations; this yields the Saha equation, which relates ionization state densities to temperature and ionization potential. Corona equilibrium, also called collisional-radiative equilibrium, applies to low-density, optically thin plasmas where excitation is collisional but de-excitation occurs through spontaneous emission before a subsequent collision can take place. Non-LTE (nLTE) modeling requires identifying and explicitly solving the specific set of relevant atomic rate equations for a given plasma, such as neglecting collisional processes in a strongly photo-ionized plasma.

A general spectroscopic workflow begins with modeling a plasma element’s mass density and temperature, determining the appropriate equilibrium, calculating ionization and excited state populations, computing transition line strengths, and predicting the emitted spectrum. If the plasma is not optically thin, radiation transport must be included, along with wall reflections and the detector’s frequency-dependent response, before comparing the synthetic spectrum to experimental data and iterating.

The line ratio technique offers a simpler diagnostic: measuring the intensity ratio of strong, isolated, identified spectral lines from different ionization states allows inference of the relative population of those states, which can be combined with an equilibrium like Saha to estimate temperature.

In X-ray spectroscopy, characteristic lines from transitions to the lowest energy levels are strong and narrow; for example, the K-alpha transition (n=2 to n=1) is typically the brightest. Highly ionized atoms are often described as helium-like or lithium-like. X-ray filters exploit sharp absorption edges (K-edge, L-edge) in solid foils to block selected energy ranges. Because refractive indices are near unity for X-rays, imaging typically uses pinholes, producing inverted, magnified images limited by geometric and diffractive blur, or bent crystals for monochromatic imaging. Common detectors include time-integrated film and reusable image plates read by laser, expensive time-gated electronic cameras, and streak cameras that record one spatial dimension versus time with extremely high temporal resolution.

The author draws parallels between dating and hiring a content marketing partner, offering five tips. First, choose a provider whose strategic interests align with your vision. Resolute Marine Energy (RME), led by CEO Bill Staby and COO Olivier Ceberio, developed the Wave O₂™, a wave-driven desalination system designed to provide cheaper fresh water to coastal communities with weak electric grids, such as Ugu in South Africa, where high potable water costs resulted from reliance on diesel generators. By 2012, the Development Bank of South Africa expressed interest in funding the local portion of a Ugu pilot, but RME still needed $6 million to complete system testing.

The company faced a strategic choice among three approaches: developing a wave-energy converter (WEC) that produces electricity to power a standard desalination plant, which offered access to U.S. government grants but lower profit margins and significant competition; using hydraulic power to directly operate desalination, which aligned with RME’s business plan and offered higher water margins with fewer direct competitors but required difficult-to-obtain private investment; or creating a vertically integrated “black box” that owns both the WEC and the desalination plant to produce water and electricity, which was potentially the most financially rewarding but the most capital-intensive and technically challenging.

RME had filed 10 provisional patents and three Patent Cooperation Treaties and had relied largely on U.S. government funding. The decision would determine whether RME defined itself as an energy company, a water company, or a hybrid.

The Federal Circuit affirmed a Court of Federal Claims judgment awarding $250,000 in Public Safety Officers’ Benefits Act death benefits to the estate of Christine H. Roberts, mother of a sheriff killed in the line of duty in 2001, who filed a claim but died before payment. The majority held that 42 U.S.C. § 3796(a) unambiguously requires beneficiaries to survive only the officer’s death, not the claims process, rejecting the Bureau of Justice Assistance’s argument that beneficiaries must survive until payment and denying Chevron deference to the agency’s contrary interpretation. Judge Prost dissented, arguing the statute is ambiguous on whether estates may receive benefits and that the agency’s interpretation limiting payment to living payees warrants deference.

Play action is a pass play designed to look like a run to deceive the defense, creating space for downfield passes. The quarterback fakes a handoff before dropping back, while the offensive line shows run blocking then switches to pass protection. It works best when a team has established a run game or in run situations like short yardage, goal line, or red zone, with some teams using it on 30 to 40 percent of passes. Common concepts include the Double Post, with two deep post routes, and the Bubble Y Over, a spread formation offering at least four passing options. Unlike a Run Pass Option (RPO), which can become a run or pass based on the quarterback's read, a play action pass is always a pass.

Industry 4.0 increases technology dependence, but Indonesian digital startups often struggle due to weak business model exploitation, leading to losses and bankruptcy. This research develops a profitable digital startup business model using the Lean Canvas framework. Through descriptive qualitative methods, including semi-structured interviews with 120 respondents and data source triangulation, the study applies nine Lean Canvas components: customer segments, value propositions, channels, customer relationships, revenue streams, key resources, key activities, key partnerships, and cost structure. The model was implemented for a digital startup called "Beautiful Memories," which solves limited vendor package offerings by connecting customers with photographers, video editors, decoration services, and souvenir providers based on user needs. Its unique value proposition includes customized services and vendor certifications; revenue streams include 10% commissions per order; and key metrics track certification quality. Social media is the primary channel. The Lean Canvas helps startups systematically map strategies, reach broader markets, and calculate costs and revenues.

Apple's stock has underperformed the S&P 500, falling 6% on June 9–12, 2017, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq reached new highs. Forward EPS estimates for fiscal 2017–2019 have risen since May 31, while revenue estimates have fallen slightly. The stock stalled after breaking above February 2015 highs of $133–$134. The author compares current trends to 2012 and 2015 corrections, noting estimates lack the warning seen in 2012, but worries Apple may be entering a period of lagging relative performance after a 17-year run. Concerns include high price points for new iPhone and iPad models, a $765 billion market cap, and whether fiscal 2018 "supercycle" expectations are met. A drop through $133–$134 on volume would signal a bigger issue, and failure to trade above the mid-May 2017 high of $156 while the S&P 500 rises would confirm underperformance. Potential positives include a tax bill and cash repatriation. The author sold some shares June 12 but remains long AAPL and QQQ.

The US Department of Transportation issued an order to prohibit seven Chinese airlines from flying over Russia on US routes, forcing them to use longer, less efficient flight paths. The measure aims to address a "competitive disparity" for US carriers, which are barred from Russian airspace due to sanctions over Ukraine. Targeted airlines include Air China, Beijing Capital Airlines, China Eastern, China Southern, Hainan, Sichuan, and Xiamen Airlines; cargo carriers and Cathay Pacific are excluded. Some routes, such as China Eastern's New York-Shanghai and China Southern's New York-Guangzhou flights, currently traverse Russia and could face additional hours. US airlines and their trade group support the order, while China's Foreign Ministry criticized it for hindering travel and people-to-people exchanges. US-China flights remain below pre-pandemic levels, and security concerns exist regarding potential diversions to Russia.

The AEGEAN study found high and comparable apixaban compliance (>95% at Weeks 4, 12, and 24; >94% at Week 48) across all study groups. Mean adherence at 24 weeks was approximately 91.6% in both the Primary SOC and Additional Educational Program groups, with no significant difference, and remained comparable through 48 weeks, though adherence significantly declined between later assessment periods. Persistence and percentages of fully adherent subjects were similar across groups at 24 and 48 weeks. In the Primary SOC group, non-adherence was associated with lower MMSE scores, alcohol consumption, and permanent atrial fibrillation. Safety endpoints, including adverse events, bleeding events, and deaths, were similar between groups. The study concluded that adherence and persistence were sustained up to 48 weeks, and the proactive educational program provided no additional benefit.

Investigations of the intermetallic compound CoSn₂ reveal a symmetry-broken state emerging below approximately 25 K. Resistivity exhibits a slope change at this temperature, yet no anomalies appear in specific heat or magnetic susceptibility, and the material remains paramagnetic. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction at 22 K detects weak superlattice reflections indicating a structural transition from tetragonal I4/mcm to acentric monoclinic C2 symmetry with doubled a and c axes, though the lattice distortion is minimal. Angle-dependent magnetoresistance confirms a breaking of four-fold rotational symmetry to two-fold below 20 K. Phonon calculations show dynamic stability, ruling out a purely structural origin, while electronic susceptibility calculations reveal nesting-driven instabilities capable of breaking rotational symmetry. ARPES measurements identify a flower-like Fermi surface and orbital-selective anisotropy—particularly from Co-dxy orbitals under linear vertical polarization—suggestive of orbital-driven electronic nematicity. The band structure also contains a nodal loop with Dirac-like carriers near the Fermi level. These findings establish CoSn₂ as a three-dimensional, nonmagnetic nodal line semimetal platform for studying electronically driven symmetry breaking without strong correlations or magnetic ordering.

This preprint presents a causal Bayesian Network (BN) to improve clinical diagnosis of Alzheimer’s Disease (AD). AD, characterized by amyloid beta plaques and tau tangles, is the leading cause of dementia, yet clinical diagnosis is challenging, with significant physician discomfort and misdiagnosis rates. Unlike black-box machine learning models, the proposed BN is interpretable and distinguishes between the probability of having AD (“Suspected AD”) and receiving a formal diagnosis (“Diagnosed AD”), incorporating a “Formal Testing” node to account for undiagnosed cases.

The model structure follows medical idioms (condition, manifestation, risk factor, comorbidity, complication, treatment) and aligns with NIA-AA diagnostic criteria for AD MCI and AD dementia. It includes clinically relevant variables such as age, family history, traumatic brain injury, and genetic mutations (APP, PSEN1, PSEN2) as risk factors; signs/symptoms (e.g., memory impairment); medical tests (cognitive and biomarker); other dementia and reversible conditions as alternative causes; and complications/treatments. Parameters are derived from the NACC Uniform Data Set, literature, and expert judgment, calibrated so the prior probability of suspected AD matches the estimated general population prevalence of 3.336%.

Validation demonstrates internal consistency via prior marginals and external consistency through clinical scenarios. Examples show the model’s ability to update probabilities with new evidence, exhibit “explaining away” when alternative conditions are observed, use biomarkers to increase diagnostic certainty, perform backward reasoning (e.g., inferring genetic mutation probability from early-onset symptoms), and differentiate AD MCI from AD dementia based on independence levels.

Limitations include the coarse aggregation of non-AD conditions into broad categories, reliance on data from diagnosed patients that may miss undiagnosed cases, manually set parameters, and simplified age modeling. Future work aims to model individual alternative dementias and reversible conditions separately, incorporate autopsy data for definitive AD, expand early-onset variables, and potentially extend the tool to research settings including preclinical AD.

In *Vansickle v. Brown*, the court affirmed the judgment for the defendant in a malicious prosecution action brought after the plaintiff was arrested for obstructing a highway, indicted, and then released by a nolle prosequi. The court held that evidence of an arresting officer’s uncivil conduct is inadmissible unless instigated by the defendant; a later trespass judgment and a subsequent county court order were properly excluded; and verbal county court directions were admissible only to show the defendant’s good faith. The defendant could testify to his own good faith. The court overruled *Hickman v. Griffin*, holding that probable cause requires the prosecutor to actually believe in the accused’s guilt based on reasonable grounds. It also held that waiving a preliminary examination and entering a recognizance is prima facie evidence of probable cause, and that malice is not inferred as a matter of law from want of probable cause. The defendant’s jury instructions on malice, probable cause, and good faith were upheld, while the plaintiff’s requested instruction was refused. Judges Napton and Henry dissented in part.

This document describes AMD's Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine, optional extensions to SEV and SNP that offload page migration between memory tiers while maintaining guest physical addresses. TMPM requires IOMMU enablement; support is indicated by the ENGINE_READY bit. The engine migrates Hypervisor-owned pages using PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO, which coordinates with IOMMUs to move pages under active DMA by updating host page table entries, and migrates SNP Guest pages using PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST, which requires source pages in Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid state and destination pages in Pre-Migration state. Commands support up to 128 pages per list via a dedicated ring buffer with defined initialization, shutdown, pause, resume, and interrupt mechanisms. System Physical Addresses must be 4K aligned and include encryption bits when SMEE or SME-MK is enabled. TMPM firmware can be reloaded when idle via a BIOS-to-PSP mailbox, with EPYC Family 19h identified by FW_VER_Major 71. IOMMU structures, ring buffer pages, and vIOMMU buffers are non-migratable. Performance is optimized by batching 16 to 128 pages and keeping the command ring buffer full. Errors are reported in command statuses or the PM_STATUS register, and severe hardware errors may require system reboot.

The article investigates pedagogical approaches for integrating Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) into South Africa’s Curriculum Assessment Policy Statement (CAPS) Technology curriculum. Grounded in Kolb’s experiential learning theory, the qualitative descriptive case study used semi-structured interviews and classroom observations with eight Senior Phase Technology teachers in Mpumalanga’s Ehlanzeni District. Findings reveal that teachers possess theoretical knowledge of ESD, including resource preservation, renewable energy, and indigenous knowledge, and identify curriculum opportunities such as the design process, investigative teaching, and technology-driven solutions for recycling and environmental conservation. Collaborative learning was viewed as a promising approach to foster creativity, cross-cultural collaboration, and environmental stewardship. However, classroom practices largely failed to emphasize ESD, with teachers relying primarily on demonstrations rather than collaborative or experiential methods. The study concludes that Technology Education offers substantial potential for ESD, but effective integration requires practical, collaborative pedagogical strategies. Limitations include the focus on a single district, exclusive use of qualitative methods, and restriction to the Senior Phase. Recommendations include holistic ESD integration, value transformation, and collaborative, hands-on projects.

This preprint outlines the protocol for the CBC2 study, a prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 4 trial of Thai cannabis oil in 90 women with metastatic breast cancer undergoing chemotherapy at King Chulalongkorn Memorial Hospital, Thailand. Participants will be randomized 1:1:1 to receive Ganja Oil (low-dose THC/CBD), Metta Osot (high-dose THC), or placebo for 90 days. The study aims to evaluate efficacy on quality of life and chemotherapy-related symptoms using the Edmonton Symptom Assessment System, and to assess adverse effects, pharmacokinetic parameters (Tmax, Cmax), pharmacogenetic profiles, and alterations in microbiome profiles, cytokines (IL-17, IFN-γ, IL-10, TGF-β), and bacterial metabolites (SCFAs, iso-SCFAs, equol, bile acids) from blood, saliva, stool, and skin samples. It will also examine bacterial translocation markers (LBP, sCD14) to explore a gut-breast cancer microbiota axis. Approved in December 2022, the trial is anticipated to launch in January 2023.

The use of position numbers in soccer, recently revived to reduce confusion, originated in 1920s England with a 2-3-5 formation assigning numbers 1–11 from back-to-front and right-to-left. The 1950s “W-M” formation maintained these numbers while shifting roles, establishing the “Number 9” as a central striker and “Number 10” as a set-back playmaker. From the 1960s, “Total Football” and tactical experimentation led to flexible numbering and position merging. In 2012, U.S. Soccer standardized a 4-3-3 numbering system and position profiles based on Technical, Tactical, Physical, and Mental attributes. Modern terminology includes “False 9,” a striker dropping into midfield, and “Double-9s,” or paired central strikers.

A punter flips field position by kicking the ball after a failed offensive possession, using hang-time, accuracy, and touch to pin opponents deep and assist coverage teams. The role requires leg strength, flexibility, and creativity to execute varied trajectories, along with occasional participation in fake punts. Many punters also serve as holders for kicks. Typically abbreviated as "P," the position favors slimmer athletes around 5'10"–6'2" and 180–210 pounds. Notable punters include Shane Lechler, who holds the NFL record for highest career average yards per punt at 47.6, and Ray Guy, a first-round draft pick who won three Super Bowls and for whom the collegiate Ray Guy Award is named. The position remains critical because punting forces opponents into longer drives, directly influencing scoring probability, defensive confidence, and game momentum.

This patent application, a continuation of prior U.S. patent applications, discloses systems and methods for a microservices architecture in cloud computing data centers. To relieve system designers from needing to know implementation details at design time and to improve portability, the specification describes a framework that encapsulates functionality behind a standardized microservices API. Microservice accelerators—including local software, resource pools, FPGAs, ASICs, and hardware accelerators—register their capabilities and microservice connection capabilities with a Service Discovery Function (SDF), which maintains an ontological catalog. A microservices driver queries the SDF to dynamically discover, select, and provision the best available instance, translating generic API calls into native invocations. The architecture supports dynamic service chaining via message forwarders, allowing data to flow directly between provisioned microservice instances without returning to the host, thereby reducing latency and request/response overhead. The disclosure also details data center infrastructure including switching fabrics, virtualized nodes, orchestrators, platform logic with telemetry and manageability engines, and load-balancing engines. Example implementations include computing apparatus and tangible, non-transitory computer-readable mediums configured to receive microservice registrations, log them in a registration database, publish them to a microservices driver, and store information for spawning and programming new instances.

Micro E-mini S&P 500 Index futures (MES) are 1/10th the size of E-mini contracts, launched by CME Group in 2019 to make the S&P 500 futures market accessible to retail traders with small accounts. Traded on the CME Globex electronic platform and financially settled, each contract unit equals the index value multiplied by $5, with a minimum price fluctuation of 0.25 index point ($1.25). Quarterly contracts (March, June, September, December) are listed for five consecutive quarters and terminate at 9:30 a.m. ET on the third Friday of the contract month. Trading hours are Sunday 6:00 p.m. to Friday 5:00 p.m. ET, with a daily maintenance period from 5:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. ET. A trading strategy typically involves technical or fundamental analysis, position sizing, and risk management; a mean reversion strategy backtested on E-mini data (due to the Micro contract’s limited history) showed performance metrics without risk management parameters. Historically, the contract performs better in winter and spring than in summer. As of December 9, 2022, the contract traded at $3959.50, with an all-time high of 4808.25 (January 2022) and an all-time low of 2174.00 (March 2020). Traders access the market through futures brokers using margin (about $1,060), though CFDs are also available. The biggest risk is adverse price movement magnified by leverage.

The MOVE Index measures U.S. interest rate volatility via 1-month OTC options and is known as the "VIX of the bond market." Created by Merrill Lynch in 1998 and acquired by ICE in 2019, it spiked to 199 in March 2023 amid Federal Reserve rate hikes and banking concerns, above its historical average near 85 since 2000. Unlike the VIX, high MOVE levels do not signal good bond entry points. A backtested strategy from 2002 held TLT when the MOVE Index was below its historical mean near 86 and sold when above, producing somewhat linear growth and roughly half the maximum drawdown of buy-and-hold, but was not highly profitable, harming 2008 returns while helping in 2022. The MOVE Index indicates bond volatility, but avoiding high volatility does not appear to be a good trading strategy.

Vision is critical in soccer for passing, defending, and quick decision-making. Pelé, who had peripheral vision 30 percent greater than average and studied geometry and chess, exemplifies its value. Successful coaches stress four fundamentals: maintaining awareness of all players through constant scanning; raising the head immediately after controlling the ball while keeping the eyes and body moving to see the full field; analyzing and anticipating play to position oneself effectively; and developing peripheral vision to identify options and threats on both offense and defense. Communication, particularly from players with the best overall view, is essential. Coaching tips include taking the first touch away from the body and receiving passes with the far foot to maximize vision. A recommended drill involves two-touch passing between distinct jersey colors in a grid, requiring players to scan the field and keep their heads up without shouting for the ball.

The DAWN-PLASMA study was a randomized, open-label, phase 2, multicenter trial evaluating convalescent plasma plus standard of care versus standard of care alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. Between May 2020 and January 2021, 489 patients were randomized 2:1 (326 to plasma, 163 to control). The primary endpoint was the percentage of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Secondary endpoints included clinical severity, oxygenation, ventilation status, time to sustained improvement, mortality, safety, and correlation of outcomes with donor antibody titers. Eligible participants were adults with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and pulmonary involvement, not on mechanical ventilation at randomization. The intervention consisted of 800–1000 mL of convalescent plasma in four units, initiated within 12 hours of randomization, with a minimum neutralizing antibody titer of 1/160. The study was conducted in accordance with GCP and the Declaration of Helsinki, using computerized randomization with a blinded statistician until database lock. Analysis sets included a Full Analysis Set, excluding seven randomized patients, and a Per Protocol Set, excluding 29 patients with major protocol violations. Baseline characteristics were well matched. In the plasma group, the median time to first transfusion was 5 hours, median volume administered was 884 mL, 80.7% of units had neutralizing antibody titers of at least 1/320, and 91.9% of patients received all four units.

The COVID-19 pandemic forced higher education institutions to adopt online learning, but many lacked adequate infrastructure and faced data privacy and suitability issues with public cloud platforms. This study presents UZEP, an Education as a Service (EaaS) cloud-based distance education platform designed for emergency use without requiring client infrastructure. UZEP features modules for learning management, virtual classrooms via BigBlueButton, online exams for up to 10,000 concurrent students, homework, digital material sharing, announcements, surveys, and reporting, with integration capabilities for university management systems and compliance with personal data protection laws. Tested by 12 universities during Fall 2020, UZEP was evaluated by experts, administrators, lecturers, and students. Experts found it easy to use and rapidly deployable but noted deficiencies in communication tools and learning analytics compared to Moodle, edX, and Google Suite. Administrators rated ease of use and openness to development highest, while lecturers most valued the virtual classroom module. Students reported moderate satisfaction and requested improved social tools and exam module functionality. The study concludes that UZEP's integrated, scalable structure supports effective emergency transitions to distance education, though future enhancements should address communication, assessment security, and analytics.

Diversification reduces portfolio risk by combining investments with returns that respond differently to market conditions. To be effective, investors must avoid common mistakes: failing to account for all holdings, including EPF and stock options; holding too many investments, which dilutes benefits and increases costs; purchasing assets without understanding them; selecting an asset allocation misaligned with financial goals and liquidity needs; and neglecting periodic rebalancing. Investors lacking expertise may use financial advisors or mutual funds. Diversification within asset classes, such as varying market capitalizations and sectors in equity or credit profiles and tenors in debt, can also improve risk and returns.

The disclosure provides apparatus and methods for assessing tissue viability around burns and other wounds by measuring tissue capacitance and deriving sub-epidermal moisture (SEM) values. Electrodes on a substrate form virtual capacitive sensors that measure capacitance of proximate tissue. A processor compares measured capacitance or SEM values against thresholds or data arrays to determine burn depth and map boundaries between viable and non-viable tissue, including necrotic tissue, zones of stasis, and zones of hyperaemia. The apparatus may include visual indicators, projectors, or perforations to mark boundaries on the tissue. The methods are also applicable to monitoring healing of various wounds and evaluating wound-healing therapies.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated December 29, 2020, reporting that its Board appointed Monica Lozano to the Board, effective January 4, 2021. Wound Care Advantage, Dr. David G. Armstrong, the Southwestern Academic Limb Salvage Alliance, and Gen1 Research launched Advanced Discovery, a research alliance to improve wound care outcomes and reduce treatment costs through evidence-based science. The alliance offers access to an international network of advanced wound and hyperbaric treatment centers and de-identified clinical data from more than 42,000 patients and 880,000 wound assessments collected over 16 years, supplemented by data from SALSA’s academic affiliations including Keck School of Medicine at USC. From 2010 to August 2012, buying on weakness and selling on strength in SPY worked well. Day trades entered at next open and exited at 11:30 based on prior day's last hour high or low. Buying on the close had similar returns but larger drawdowns, while stop-losses and targets hurt performance. Results include returns, fills, and averages.

The passage discloses systems, methods, and WTRU instrumentalities for low-latency MAC PDU assembly in 5G flexible radio access technology (5gFLEX). Latency is reduced by having a WTRU determine network transmission parameters—such as a modulation and coding scheme, resource range, and transport block size—prior to receiving a transmission grant, allowing incremental creation, segmentation, assembly, multiplexing, and physical layer encoding of fixed-size data blocks before the grant arrives. The WTRU monitors and decodes downlink control information, determines decoding parameters (e.g., CRC length, aggregation level, DCI format, robustness level), and derives transmission or reception parameters (e.g., QoS level, spectrum operating mode, HARQ feedback timing, MCS, resource blocks, power, TTI) therefrom, potentially using a network-configured mapping. The detailed description illustrates communications system architectures, WTRU and base station components, various radio access networks and core networks, 5gFLEX air interface capabilities supporting ultra-low latency and ultra-reliable transmission, flexible waveforms, spectrum operation modes, variable timing and bandwidth, scheduling modes, transport channels for specific services, and procedures for autonomous parameter selection, incremental transport block generation, MAC multiplexing, and aggregated data block HARQ status reporting.

NVIDIA Corporation’s fiscal year 2022 Form 10-K annual report covers the period ended January 30, 2022. The Delaware corporation, headquartered in Santa Clara, California, trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol NVDA. Its platforms address the Gaming, Data Center, Professional Visualization, and Automotive markets.

On February 8, 2022, NVIDIA and SoftBank terminated the Share Purchase Agreement for Arm Limited due to significant regulatory challenges, and NVIDIA expects to record a $1.36 billion charge in the first quarter of fiscal year 2023. The company utilizes a fabless manufacturing strategy, relying on foundries such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company and Samsung Electronics for wafer fabrication and independent subcontractors for assembly, testing, and packaging.

As of January 30, 2022, NVIDIA had 22,473 employees in 32 countries, with 16,242 in research and development, and its overall turnover rate for fiscal year 2022 was 4.9%. The company faces risks including intense competition from firms such as AMD and Intel, difficulty forecasting demand due to cryptocurrency mining and gray-market resale, dependence on third-party manufacturing and supply chain partners, international operations that generated 84% of fiscal year 2022 revenue, climate change impacts, and a February 23, 2022 security incident in which unauthorized threat actors accessed the company’s network and misappropriated proprietary information, including source code.

Judge Elaine E. Bucklo of the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois denied cross-motions for summary judgment in a December 20, 2007 ERISA action by Plumbers Local Union No. 93 funds against Waterworks, Inc. to compel an audit. The court found genuine issues of material fact regarding whether a collective bargaining agreement was formed at a disputed 2004 meeting or through Waterworks’ subsequent conduct, which included submitting contribution reports and benefit payments consistent with the agreement without signing the “Warranty and Acceptance” clauses. The manual excerpt explains that missing ID3 tags or WMA metadata cause "unknown artist/album" display, which can be fixed by editing file properties. Options trading in EEM offers exposure to rising and falling markets but carries significant risks, including potential losses from adverse price movements, time decay, liquidity constraints, and volatility. Common strategies include long calls and puts, covered calls and puts, straddles, strangles, collars, and butterfly spreads. Traders can analyze pricing using the Black-Scholes model and technical analysis tools, though backtesting is recommended to verify a statistical edge. Leverage is available but highly risky and not recommended for beginners. Trading costs, minimum deposit requirements (typically $500–$2,000), and margin requirements (generally 10%–50%) vary by broker and contract type. Effective risk management requires understanding option delta, employing hedging strategies, maintaining appropriate position sizing and margin levels, and using stop losses, which may be less effective in practice than in theory. Expiration dates typically fall on the third Friday of the expiration month, while tax implications depend on the trader’s jurisdiction. Best practices include selecting a reputable broker, monitoring liquidity and bid-ask spreads, reading the options chain, and ensuring a thorough understanding of option pricing before trading.

Hucknall and Linby Dolphins finished fifth at Matlock gala. Katie Hill took three second places and several swimmers placed second or third. Lewis Kemp, Joel Gospel, Ben Staniforth and Tyler Dennis won the U10 boys medley relay.

Sungi Cho, a former Army Black Hawk pilot and West Point mechanical engineering graduate, founded P6 Gear to address military equipment deficiencies. Using 3D printers, he developed the Warbelt Hanger for barracks gear organization, selling to military and law enforcement, and later created the MOLLE Backer, a universal base mount for MOLLE systems. He is evaluating whether to continue in-house 3D printing or switch to outsourced injection molding, which yields stronger parts with lower material and scrap costs but requires an $11,487 mold and third-party manufacturing, versus his current $1,716 printer cost. The ADS868xW includes high and low input alarms with independently programmable thresholds and common hysteresis, plus fixed AVDD alarms at 5.3V and 4.7V. It communicates via a multiSPI interface supporting legacy SPI and source-synchronous protocols with single or dual SDO outputs, and supports single-device or daisy-chain host topologies. The device operates in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states, with an active-low RST pin configurable for application or power-on reset. Programming uses 32-bit data transfer frames controlled by CONVST/CS and SCLK, supporting read, write, set, and clear commands. Nine configuration registers manage device ID, reset and power control, SPI and SDO modes, output data flags, input range, and alarm settings. For industrial applications such as PLC analog input modules, the device offers fast-settling 16-bit conversion with an integrated analog front end, reference, and safety features. Power supply recommendations include AVDD and DVDD decoupling, and the device supports NAP and power-down modes to reduce consumption.

This study evaluated diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps for preoperative prediction of pTERT mutation status in glioblastoma (GBM) using a residual convolutional neural network (ResNet). In a retrospective cohort of 266 GBM patients, conventional structural MRI modalities (T1WI, T2WI, CE-T1) showed poor predictive accuracy (approximately 50–52%, AUC ~0.53–0.57). In contrast, ResNet using DWI combined with ADC maps (DWI*) achieved 85.20% slice-level accuracy (AUC 0.934) and 86.6% patient-level accuracy. ADC maps alone significantly outperformed DWI alone (78.63% vs. 54.58% accuracy). Using the entire tumor as the region of interest yielded the best results, though enhanced tumor ROI also performed well (81.70% accuracy, AUC 0.869). Clinical characteristics including age, necrosis volume, and tumor location showed moderate predictive value individually but did not improve performance when integrated into the DWI* model. The authors conclude that DWI combined with ADC maps using ResNet effectively predicts pTERT mutation status in GBM and outperforms conventional structural MRI, supporting the inclusion of DWI in clinical management.

This scoping review protocol aims to map evidence on modifiable and non-modifiable determinants of antipsychotic-induced metabolic syndrome (MS) and non-pharmacological interventions for community-dwelling adults prescribed antipsychotics. Antipsychotics cause MS in approximately 40–80% of patients, increasing risks of hypertension, cardiovascular disease, and type 2 diabetes. Non-modifiable determinants include gender, ethnic background, age, and family history; modifiable determinants include diet and physical activity. Previous non-pharmacological interventions show limited clinical efficacy, and the preferred context for delivery is unclear. Following Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and PRISMA-ScR, the review will search electronic databases and grey literature for qualitative, quantitative, and mixed-method studies. Two reviewers will independently screen titles and abstracts; one reviewer will conduct full-text screening with a second checking 10%. Data will be extracted and synthesised narratively, with JBI evidence levels assigned. Ethical approval is not required. Experts by experience and personal consultees contributed to the research design, and stakeholder consultation will follow the review. Findings will be disseminated via peer-reviewed publications and conferences.

The Colorado Court of Appeals affirmed summary judgment for Shelter Mutual Insurance Company, ruling it had no duty to pay Samuel and Mary Breit uninsured motorist benefits beyond $100,000 despite Breit holding two policies with $100,000 coverage each. The court held the policies' anti-stacking provisions unambiguously barred aggregating limits for multiple policies issued by the same insurer, consistent with *Thompson v. Shelter Mutual Insurance Co.* It rejected the argument that an "Other Insurance" clause created ambiguity or conflicted with the anti-stacking provision, distinguishing *Compton v. State Farm Mutual Insurance Co.*, which involved multiple insurers and conflicting language. The court found the doctrine of reasonable expectations inapplicable because the policy language was clear and not unconscionable, and it declined to award fees, finding the appeal not frivolous.

The Trump administration moved career and technical education (CTE) programs from the Education Department to the Labor Department to better align high school training with workforce needs. Officials say the change will reduce administrative burdens, boost youth labor force participation, and help states centralize workforce development. Supporters argue it will improve accountability and connect education with employer demands. However, critics, including congressional Democrats and education advocates, contend the transfer is illegal, strains already limited federal staffing, and risks steering students toward short-term job training rather than long-term educational pathways. They worry it could revive stigma tracking low-income and minority students into lower-wage vocational roles and reduce specialized support for vulnerable populations, though proponents say the Labor Department is better positioned to ensure programs match employer needs and workforce outcomes.

Cervical cancer disproportionately affects low- and middle-income countries, particularly sub-Saharan Africa, where access to precancer treatment is limited. This mixed-methods study evaluated the experiences and acceptability of self-administered intravaginal 5-Fluorouracil (5FU) among 12 women living with HIV in Kisumu, Kenya, following a Phase I pilot trial (March 2023–February 2024) testing 5FU as adjuvant therapy after primary ablation or excision for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2/3. Participants self-administered 2g of 5FU every other week for eight applications at home using an applicator and tampon after receiving education sessions.

Quantitative questionnaires and in-depth interviews revealed high acceptability. Although some participants initially reported anxiety or uncertainty, all 12 ultimately strongly agreed the cream was safe, felt confident they used it correctly, and preferred 5FU over prior ablation or excision. Participants valued reduced pain, less fear, minimal disruption to daily work, and the privacy and convenience of home administration. Challenges included difficulty measuring the correct dose, limited knowledge of female anatomy, initial tampon-use difficulties, mild side effects such as vaginal itching and discharge, privacy constraints in single-room households, and partner tensions over required condom use. Confidence improved with repeated nurse education and clinic follow-up.

The authors conclude this is the first study of African women’s actual experiences with self-administered 5FU for cervical precancer, demonstrating high acceptability and adherence that support continued feasibility and efficacy research in low- and middle-income countries. They recommend pre-filled applicators, enhanced patient education, and strategies to mitigate home privacy barriers. Limitations include the small, single-site sample. Randomized trials are ongoing in South Africa and planned in other settings to evaluate 5FU as adjuvant and primary treatment.

This withdrawn medRxiv preprint evaluates six machine learning models for pancreatic cancer diagnosis using a synthetic dataset of demographic, clinical, and symptom data. The study notes that traditional diagnostic methods have limitations and that machine learning faces challenges with data imbalance and interpretability. After preprocessing and splitting data into 80% training and 20% test sets without resampling, all six models—Logistic Regression, Random Forest, SVM, Neural Network, Decision Tree, and SuperLearner—achieved similar accuracy between 76.05% and 76.35%. However, sensitivity was very low: Random Forest and Decision Tree had 0%, SVM had the highest at 1.90%, Logistic Regression and Neural Networks had 1.47%, and SuperLearner had 0.42%. SuperLearner achieved the highest precision at 66.67%. The analysis attributes the poor sensitivity to class imbalance and suggests that distinct clustering patterns observed in gene expression heatmaps, PCA, and correlation analyses of metastasized cancer and normal colon tissues could inform future feature engineering. The discussion recommends resampling techniques, cost-sensitive learning, threshold tuning, and ensemble methods to improve sensitivity, alongside interpretability tools like SHAP and LIME. It also calls for integrating real-world clinical data and fostering collaboration between data scientists and clinicians. The conclusion emphasizes that while models show reasonable accuracy, their low sensitivity limits clinical utility, and future work must address class imbalance, employ explainable AI, integrate diverse data modalities, and undergo real-world validation.

In Horejs v. Milford, the Indiana Supreme Court reversed a trial court’s grant of partial summary judgment in a wrongful death suit. David Shaner sued for final-expense and survivor damages after his wife Laura died from complications related to dialysis. While the case was pending, David died intestate with no known heirs. Laura’s estate administrators continued pursuing both categories of damages, but the trial court and Court of Appeals granted partial summary judgment on the survivor damages claim, concluding that without heirs, such damages would be punitive. The Supreme Court held that Indiana’s wrongful death and survival statutes do not require an heir for a survivor-damages claim to survive the death of the statutory beneficiary, and that its prior decision in Bemenderfer v. Williams does not impose such a requirement. Therefore, David’s claim did not abate. However, because the proper party to continue David’s individual claim was unclear, the Court remanded for the trial court to determine whether a legal representative or successor in interest of David exists to continue the action.

The lecture distinguishes poker tournaments from cash games, noting tournaments have increasing blinds, no rebuys, less metagame, frequent but fixed losses, and a wider range of situations, which is why the class focuses on them. It then reviews preflop hand equities, categorizing matchups: bigger pair versus smaller pair (~80/20), dominating hands (~70/30), two overcards versus a pair (~50/50), and unrelated cards (~60/40), noting suitedness helps more when behind. The core strategic advice is to not fear preflop all-ins, especially with under 12 big blinds with antes; from the small blind, all-in ranges can be wider than from the button because position is irrelevant once all-in. The instructor explains exploitative thinking versus Nash equilibrium through an iterative best-response example, yielding approximate Nash ranges for a 15 big blind small-blind scenario. He emphasizes either shoving or folding short-stacked, as small raises give opponents free options. Additional topics include adjusting raise sizes for limpers (+1 big blind per limper), calling all-ins with sufficient odds based on effective stack size, re-raising to about 2.5 times the open, and avoiding "sucker bets" that grant opponents extra profitable options unless they are prone to errors.

The S&P 400 Midcap index, formed in 1991, tracks 400 U.S. mid-sized companies with market caps between $3.6 billion and $13.1 billion. It is market-cap weighted and rebalanced quarterly. The E-mini S&P MidCap 400 futures (ticker EMD) trade on the CME Globex platform Sundays through Fridays from 6:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. ET with a one-hour daily break. One contract unit equals $100 times the index value, with minimum price fluctuations of 0.1 index points ($10) for outright trading and 0.05 points ($5) for BTIC and calendar spreads. Quarterly contracts (March, June, September, December) are listed for five consecutive quarters, are financially settled by cash on the third Friday of the contract month, and have a 50-contract block minimum for BTIC. As of December 1, 2022, the futures traded at $2585.8. The all-time high was 2924.2 (futures) or 2925.93 (index) in November 2021, and the all-time low was 119.43 in June 1991. The index tends to perform better in winter and spring. ETFs tracking the index include IJH, SPMD, and EWMC. Backtested strategies generally underperformed on mid-caps compared to large-cap indices like SPY and QQQ, and the authors note difficulty finding uncorrelated mid-cap strategies. Prices are affected by component stock movements, interest rates, economic news, and the U.S. dollar. Trading requires a CME-access futures broker, though CFDs are an alternative.

The lecture covers empirical demand and supply models in industrial organization. It explains how supply-side first-order conditions, using an ownership matrix and demand derivatives, allow researchers to recover marginal costs and impose restrictions that improve the precision of demand estimates, particularly for random coefficient models. The BLP paper on the 1971–1990 U.S. automobile market is presented as a key example, showing that random coefficients better capture heterogeneous substitution patterns—such as high-end consumers being less price-sensitive and less likely to choose an outside option—than simple logit models. The lecture then discusses Nevo’s cereal market paper, which tests whether high margins result from collusion or from multi-product differentiation with heterogeneous tastes by comparing demand-recovered markups under different conduct assumptions to observed accounting markups; the findings reject collusion but not own-profit maximization. Finally, the lecture addresses the common ownership hypothesis—whether diversified institutional investors soften competition—and summarizes Backus, Conlon, and Sinkinson’s structural test in cereals. Using supply-side overidentifying restrictions and a Rivers-Vuong test, they reject common ownership, perfect competition, and monopoly in favor of own-profit maximization, though a plausible mechanism for common ownership remains elusive.

Rick Langenberg introduces Super Bowl 52 predictions from TMJ contributors and local figures, noting the Denver Broncos' absence. Most predict the New England Patriots will defeat the Philadelphia Eagles with scores ranging from close contests to blowouts, while several contributors predict an Eagles victory. The Ichimoku trading strategy is a technical analysis system developed by Japanese journalist Goichi Hosoda that uses multiple plotted averages to identify support and resistance levels, trend direction, and momentum. Its components—the Tenkan-Sen, Kijun-Sen, Senkou Span A, Senkou Span B, and Chikou Span—form a “cloud” that forecasts future price barriers and generates trading signals. Price above the cloud indicates an uptrend, while price below indicates a downtrend; Tekan/Kiju crossovers and Chikou Span price crosses provide additional confirmation. While the strategy can reduce market exposure and drawdowns compared to buy-and-hold, backtesting across various assets suggests it often underperforms risk-adjusted buy-and-hold returns. Traders should backtest and forward-test any Ichimoku-based strategy before use, as the system can produce false signals.

The 2007–09 Great Recession and lingering financial concerns weakened U.S. casual dining, yet by mid-2016 investors expected consistent economic growth to make consumers more inclined to eat out. In 2016, the U.S. restaurant industry was projected to reach nearly $800 billion in sales. Bloomin’ Brands, which opened the first Outback Steakhouse in 1988 and went public in 2012, owned 1,335 restaurants and franchised 166 across four casual dining brands—Outback, Fleming’s Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar, Bonefish Grill, and Carrabba’s Italian Grill—as of June 2016; approximately 85% were in the U.S., and almost two-thirds were Outback locations. The case describes 13 publicly traded restaurant comparables as of June 2016 and includes Exhibits 1–3 with price-earnings multiples, income statement data, and balance sheet data for Bloomin’ Brands and the comparable companies.

Microsoft Corporation filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2022.  Revenue by segment included $16.5 billion from Productivity and Business Processes, $20.3 billion from Intelligent Cloud (up 20%), and $13.3 billion from More Personal Computing. Microsoft Cloud revenue grew 24% to $25.7 billion, driven by a 35% increase in Azure and other cloud services.

 During the period, the company completed its $18.8 billion acquisition of Nuance Communications and maintained its agreement to acquire Activision Blizzard for $68.7 billion, expected to close in fiscal year 2023. Microsoft also changed the estimated useful lives of server and network equipment from four to six years, which increased operating income by $1.1 billion and net income by $859 million for the quarter.

 As of September 30, 2022, total assets were $359.8 billion, cash and cash equivalents were $22.9 billion, and total debt was $48.6 billion. Unearned revenue stood at $43.9 billion, with remaining performance obligations of $183 billion. The 60/40 portfolio strategy allocates 60% of capital to equities and 40% to bonds, historically favored for its simplicity and favorable risk-adjusted returns based on the typically low or negative correlation between stocks and bonds. In times of economic stress, bonds often appreciate as investors seek safety, cushioning equity declines. However, in 2022, rising inflation caused both asset classes to fall simultaneously, with the portfolio declining 16.1% in the first half of the year and returning -17.77% year-to-date as of September 17, 2022. Historically, since 1926, the portfolio has averaged an 8.8% annual return, and intra-year declines exceeding 10% have often been followed by rebounds. The maximum drawdown since January 2010 was 21.85% in March 2020, with recovery in 79 sessions. Despite 2022's challenges, the article argues the strategy is not obsolete, noting that bonds diversify effectively during slowing growth but not necessarily during rising inflation, and lower current valuations may support higher future returns. Investors can construct the portfolio using low-cost ETFs such as SPY and TLT or funds like BlackRock Target Allocation Funds. Alternatives include the 80/20 portfolio, Ray Dalio’s All-Weather Portfolio, trend-following CTA strategies, gold, crypto, international equities, tail risk strategies, and Thomas Carlson’s "Defense First" strategy. The article concludes that market timing is futile and diversification principles remain sound.

The Supreme Court of Rhode Island affirmed Andrew A. Bucci’s conviction for furnishing legal advice to Robert Oliva while suspended from the practice of law, in violation of General Laws § 11-27-10. Bucci was initially convicted in District Court and fined $500; after a trial de novo in Superior Court, a jury again found him guilty and sentenced him to six months imprisonment. The court rejected Bucci’s argument that a variance existed between the charge of giving legal advice and the proof, noting that recorded conversations demonstrated he provided extensive legal advice and litigation management to Oliva, even though he also retained another attorney to appear in court. The court also held that the statute does not require proof of pecuniary benefit. Finally, the court rejected the claim that the Superior Court could not impose a harsher sentence after a trial de novo, citing precedent that permits greater sentences in two-tier court systems, and noted that sentence challenges must first be raised in the Superior Court under Rule 35. Justice Shea did not participate.
