University of Liverpool research found that among 38 healthy adults, higher musical aptitude correlated with lower hallucination proneness, both linked to corpus callosum integrity. Musical aptitude associated with higher white matter integrity, hallucination proneness with lower integrity, mediated by corpus callosum. Researchers suggest musical training may counteract hallucination predisposition in psychosis.

The study investigated whether group-based brain parcellation atlases inflate functional connectivity (FC) differences between early psychosis patients and healthy controls compared to individualized parcellations. Using resting-state fMRI data from the Human Connectome Project – Early Psychosis (HCP-EP) and a Group Prior Individualized Parcellation (GPIP) algorithm based on the Schaefer atlas, the researchers found that individualized parcellations reallocated over 42% of vertices and produced more functionally homogeneous regions. While both methods revealed widespread hypoconnectivity in patients, the group-based approach detected larger case-control differences and identified approximately 9% more dysconnected edges in thresholded network-based statistic (NBS) analyses. The specific edges and regions implicated differed considerably between methods, with only moderate correlation in edge-level t-statistics and 643 divergent edges in NBS components. However, network-level inferences were largely consistent across approaches, with the control network most affected. Parcel size changes did not differ significantly between groups. The authors conclude that group-based parcellations may overestimate FC disruptions, whereas individualized parcellations provide more conservative and refined estimates of dysconnectivity in psychosis.

Pupils from Richardson Dees Primary School tend a roof-top garden at The Forum. Centre manager Nick Lambert created the project to partner with the school. The eight to ten-year-olds grow flowers, fruit, vegetables, and herbs to share. Teaching assistant Laura Wilson said the project teaches gardening, promotes healthy eating, and builds confidence. Lambert said pupils have taken ownership of the space, featuring a greenhouse and beds.

Regional indexes and Wall Street advanced, while a New York explosion had no lasting market impact. Coach Quenneville discussed the team's inconsistent energy and the grueling playoff demands. He said top players sometimes endure scoring slumps but contribute in other ways and eventually score. Rob Hanna's study of Russell 2000 Death Crosses since 1988 found the S&P 500 rose 84% of the time in the following year, with the largest gain over 60% in 2020, though sizable drawdowns occurred. The most recent cross was in 2022; the S&P 500 has fallen since. Because the Russell 2000 represents volatile small-cap stocks, the signal may be less reliable for the S&P 500. South Sudan nonprofit GAIS wants the government to restrict international seed imports after FAO imported 100 metric tons of seeds despite GAIS's local application. GAIS Director Mike Gaga appealed to promote local suppliers, while Gbudue agriculture official Mariano Erneo said he would investigate. The lecture reviews solving linear systems using backslash, which requires n³ operations and achieves machine accuracy, though ill-conditioning can yield multiple valid solutions. For nonlinear systems, Newton-Raphson requires iterations costing iterations×n³, and fsolve converts root-finding into minimizing the norm of f. Implicit ODE solvers require solving nonlinear equations at each timestep, with cost scaling as timesteps×iterations×n². The professor defines functionals as objects taking function names as inputs and notes that molecular energy is a functional of electron density, the basis of density functional theory. He then discusses numerical integration and interpolation: integration rules approximate functions using basis functions fit to sampled points, but different rules can agree while still being incorrect, as illustrated with a specific function. Using k=n basis functions produces interpolation; fewer produces approximation. Orthogonal basis functions prevent singular matrices. Polynomials are common, but monomials create exponentially growing condition numbers. Lagrange polynomials set coefficients equal to function values, while Newton polynomials allow adding points without changing prior coefficients. Gaussian quadrature chooses weights and points to exactly integrate monomials up to order 2n−1, yielding higher-order error scaling than Simpson’s rule. A related 15-point method provides an error estimate by comparison. Finally, multidimensional integrals require nested quadrature loops, causing effort to grow exponentially with dimension—a challenge called the curse of dimensionality.

Schools should develop drills beyond lockdowns—including unscheduled closures and serious disaster simulations—to prepare for emergencies when standard systems fail.

Stress and "broken heart" syndrome are discussed following George H.W. Bush's hospitalization for sepsis after his wife's funeral. Stress weakens the immune system and Bush may have ignored early infection signs, but at 94 his hospitalization likely stems from underlying health issues including Parkinson's disease. While sudden shock can trigger broken heart syndrome, experts caution that death soon after losing a spouse is often coincidence in older people with health problems, as with Johnny Cash and Debbie Reynolds, whose deaths were attributed to underlying medical issues.

The lecture begins with questions on the Hawking-Page transition, clarifying that it is a first-order phase transition in a single CFT and that describing it as "deconfinement" is heuristic, based on scaling behavior rather than actual confinement. The main topic is entanglement entropy (EE). For a quantum system partitioned into subsystems A and B, EE is defined as the von Neumann entropy of the reduced density matrix rho_A obtained by tracing out B. For a pure state, the EE of A equals that of B, and zero EE indicates an unentangled product state; for mixed states, EE also contains classical statistical correlations. A two-spin example illustrates how EE quantifies entanglement. Key properties discussed include subadditivity and strong subadditivity.

In local many-body systems and QFTs, interactions between A and B are supported near their shared boundary. Consequently, the ground state of a local Hamiltonian generally obeys an area law, where the leading term of EE is proportional to the area of the boundary of A divided by a short-distance cutoff. Subleading terms capture long-range effects. In 2+1 dimensional gapped systems with topological order, a constant subleading term independent of the region's shape or size characterizes the phase. In 1+1 dimensional CFTs, EE is given by (c/3) log(L/epsilon), where c is the central charge, linking EE to the number of degrees of freedom.

The lecture then presents the Ryu-Takayanagi holographic proposal: for a CFT with a gravity dual, the EE of region A equals the area of the minimal bulk surface gamma_A anchored to the boundary of A, divided by 4G_N. This applies to time-independent states and satisfies strong subadditivity, as shown geometrically. For a 1+1 dimensional CFT dual to AdS3, the minimal surface is a semicircle, reproducing the CFT result. At finite temperature, dual to a black hole, a small region yields a vacuum-like result, while for a large region the minimal surface hugs the horizon; when A comprises the entire space, the formula reduces to the black hole entropy. In higher dimensions, the near-boundary behavior of minimal surfaces ensures the area law. The lecture concludes that this formula conceptually links spacetime geometry to quantum entanglement, unifying quantum information, many-body physics, and gravity.

This study examines software engineering challenges in integrating large language models (LLMs) into financial report analysis and compares open-source and commercial approaches. Through a Design Science Research field study at Getinge AB, the authors developed and evaluated two solutions for automating narrative financial commentary: a local multi-agent system using open-source models (e.g., LLaMA 3.1 via Ollama) and a cloud-based system using OpenAI’s GPT-4o. The research identifies primary engineering challenges in task-specific prompt and system design—where strict formatting, tone, and conditional logic are difficult to enforce—variability in preparing heterogeneous financial data from disparate sources, and constraints arising from sensitive data requiring on-premises or compliant deployment. The local solution ensured data privacy and control but suffered from hardware limitations, poor instruction adherence, and hallucinations, necessitating complex prompt engineering and chained agent architectures. GPT-4o delivered more professional, concise outputs with simpler integration but raised concerns regarding data exposure, vendor lock-in, and occasional logical or structural inconsistencies. Evaluation by financial domain experts indicated that both approaches generated draft-quality summaries requiring manual refinement, with neither producing report-ready outputs suitable for formal reporting without human validation. The findings underscore the need for architectural mechanisms such as verification modules, prompt chaining, and hybrid deployment strategies to balance control, compliance, and reliability in precision-critical financial workflows.

Syrian state media reported government forces seized al-Sukhna, the last major Islamic State-held town in Homs province, as the army advances into Deir al-Zor, the jihadist group's last major Syrian foothold. The U.S.-backed Syrian Democratic Forces are separately capturing Raqqa.

Four challenges in QED of strong-field attoscience are identified: generating massively quantum states of light; creating entangled light-matter states in complex materials; characterizing these states using ultrafast quantum-optical methods; and simulating strong-field dynamics with cold-atom and ion quantum platforms. Advances in quantized theoretical descriptions, attosecond metrology, structured and squeezed light sources, 2D and topological materials, quantum simulators, and ultrafast measurement protocols are driving the field. The convergence of attosecond physics and quantum optics aims to engineer non-classical states for scalable quantum light sources, quantum simulators, and ultrafast quantum processors.

The DAWN-PLASMA trial was a randomized, multicenter, open-label phase II study evaluating the efficacy and safety of best supportive care plus convalescent plasma versus best supportive care alone in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. Between May 2020 and January 2021, 489 patients were randomized 2:1 to receive four units (800–1000 mL) of high-titer convalescent plasma or standard of care. The primary endpoint—proportion of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at day 15—was similar between the plasma (83.7%) and control (84.1%) groups. No statistically significant differences were found in mortality, clinical severity, or other secondary endpoints at days 15 or 30. The incidence of adverse events, serious adverse events, and fatal adverse events was comparable between groups. Transfusion-related side effects occurred in 6% of the intervention group. Higher neutralizing antibody titers at baseline and day 6 correlated with better clinical outcomes, but the intervention did not significantly increase titers. The study concluded that early administration of a high volume of high-titer convalescent plasma did not alter the natural course of hospitalized COVID-19.

Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) can arise from oral potentially malignant lesions (OPMLs) such as leukoplakias. Fanconi anemia (FA) patients have a markedly increased risk of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) and frequently develop OPMLs at younger ages than the general population. This proof-of-principle prospective longitudinal study evaluated whether next-generation sequencing (NGS) of liquid biopsies (saliva and plasma) could detect cancer gene mutations in 16 FA patients before clinical diagnosis. Over approximately two years, 50 liquid biopsies were collected. DNA was extracted and sequenced using the Oncomine Pan-Cancer Cell-Free Assay. Mutations were found in 15 samples from 9 patients, most frequently in TP53, with limits of detection down to 0.07% in saliva. Among 14 patients with clinical follow-up, mutations were detected in 6 of 7 patients who later developed oral lesions or carcinomas, with lead times of 23 to 630 days (median 205 days) before clinical diagnosis. No mutations were found in 5 of 7 patients who remained lesion-free. The approach showed 92% accuracy, 86% sensitivity, and 100% specificity. Kaplan-Meier analysis indicated a significant difference in oral lesion/tumor-free survival between patients with and without mutations. The authors conclude that deep-sequencing of saliva and plasma can stratify FA patients into risk groups and may enable earlier detection of OPMLs and OSCC.

The passage explains terminology for offensive line blocks in football, aiming to inform readers about block types and increase appreciation for linemen. It defines a Trap block as leaving a defensive lineman unblocked at the snap and kicking him out to maintain inside leverage. A Base block is a one-on-one block requiring inside leverage in run or pass plays. A Reach block establishes outside leverage on the front side of a run play. A Down block is an angle block on an inside defender on the front side. A Log block pulls and seals a defender inside. A Pull involves a blocker running around another player to block elsewhere. A Veer block uses a drop step to climb to the second level in triple option offenses. A Combo block involves two players blocking a first-level defender to a second-level defender. A Drive block is a one-on-one run block driving a defender off the line. A Double Team block is the first-level part of a combo block. A Scoop block is a backside combo block. A Cut block dives at a defender’s legs. A Crack block sends a perimeter player to block an interior defender. A Kick Out block occurs outside the tackle on an edge defender to create a wider running lane.

The team faces elimination and must win the next game. A young player responded well to adversity and must continue playing physical. The speaker trains year-round for heavy ice time and conserves energy through smart positional play. The team must not look ahead or get overhyped at home, but maintain desire and physical play. Two backup goalies handled a difficult rotation with class. The club must stay out of the penalty box, get pucks deep, and wear the opponent down. The study lasted approximately 33 months and ended in February 2023, with participants enrolled for up to 26 months. BNT162b2 was 95% effective in preventing COVID-19 from 7 days after Dose 2 compared to placebo in participants aged 16 years and older, regardless of past infection. BNT162b2 and BNT162b2SA produced immune responses comparable to those against the original strain seen after Dose 2. In Phase 1, some participants had a temporary drop in lymphocytes 1 to 3 days after Dose 1 that resolved by 6 to 8 days. Injection site reactions and systemic events were mostly mild or moderate, well tolerated, and short-lived. Few participants left Phase 2/3 due to medical problems (less than 1% in both the BNT162b2 and placebo groups). Serious medical problems were rare, and no single serious event occurred in at least 1% of participants in any group; researchers generally did not believe these were related to the study vaccine. Deaths during Phase 2/3 were not believed to be caused by BNT162b2.

This ebook edition of Foreign Relations of the United States Volume IV (Soviet Union, January 1983–March 1985) was generated in January 2025 by the Office of the Historian, U.S. Department of State. Researchers led by Dr. Daniel May found that pollen gathered by honeybees contains beneficial endophytic actinobacteria, primarily Streptomyces, which produce antimicrobial compounds that protect hives against pathogens such as the mold causing stonebrood and other bacterial pathogens. DNA analysis of pollen from native plants and nearby hive stores confirmed that bees transport these bacteria back to colonies. The findings suggest that landscapes rich in diverse plant species provide bees with a greater variety of these protective microbes, and that introducing specific beneficial bacteria into hives could offer sustainable new treatments for bee and crop diseases.

Yankees shortstop Anthony Volpe played through a partially torn shoulder labrum in early May during the 2025 season. After poor regular and postseason performances, Volpe said no decision has been made on offseason shoulder surgery. He needs to be fully healthy next season.

Value investing involves buying undervalued stocks with strong fundamentals for long-term appreciation and stability, while growth investing focuses on companies with high future growth potential regardless of current valuation, seeking short-term appreciation but carrying higher risk and volatility. Historically, value has outperformed growth since 1926, but growth has led since approximately 2007, particularly in small-caps, though volatile small-caps are the riskiest stocks. The passage presents a weekly rotation strategy, backtested from 2000, that switches between value and growth based on short-term momentum using a simple ratio and two moving averages. This approach achieved higher returns with lower volatility and drawdown than either factor independently. Performance varies by market cycle: value typically outperforms after market crashes and during periods of rising rates, while growth leads during bubbles and low interest rate environments. The conclusion is that rotating between factors based on momentum is superior to holding either strategy alone.

The passage details the NVIDIA Ampere GA10x GPU architecture (GA102 and GA104), which powers the GeForce RTX 3090, 3080, 3070, RTX A6000, and A40. It offers up to 1.7x faster raster and 2x faster ray tracing performance than Turing. Key features include 2x FP32 processing in the Streaming Multiprocessor (SM), second-generation RT Cores with concurrent workload support and hardware-accelerated motion blur, and third-generation Tensor Cores with structured sparsity, TF32, and BF16 support. GA102 includes 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 RT Cores, and 336 Tensor Cores. Memory options include GDDR6X with PAM4 signaling and GDDR6. The architecture also supports third-generation NVLink, PCIe Gen 4, RTX IO for GPU-based loading and decompression, HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4a with 8K support, fifth-generation NVDEC with AV1 decode, seventh-generation NVENC, and Error Detection and Replay (EDR) for overclocking. The RTX A6000 and A40 are positioned for professional and data center visual computing.

In *Kitrosser v. The CIT Group/Factoring, Inc.*, the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York granted in part CIT’s motion for summary judgment in a dispute over the liquidation of collateral. The Kays had guaranteed the debts of their corporations, Top Form Mills, Inc. and Top Blush Corporation, which filed for bankruptcy in 1988; CIT liquidated the Kays’ collateral in 1992 to satisfy outstanding obligations. The court held that because the bankruptcy petitions were dismissed without discharge under Section 1112(b), postpetition interest continued to accrue on the debt, and the Kays remained liable as guarantors for the full amount, including such interest. The court further held that CIT’s settlement with the Economic Development Administration for less than the full guarantee did not reduce Mr. Kay’s liability, as the guarantee unambiguously permitted CIT to compromise with other parties without releasing co-guarantors. Finally, the court dismissed with prejudice the Kays’ fifth and sixth causes of action in their amended complaint—which alleged CIT breached duties by reducing Top Blush’s advance rate in 1988—because the claims did not relate back to the original 1993 complaint under Rule 15(c)(2) and were time-barred under New York’s six-year statute of limitations.

The speaker accepts a nomination and thanks the convention for nominating Senator Barkley. He argues that the Democratic Party serves the people while the Republican Party serves special interests, citing economic gains and foreign policy achievements like the United Nations and aid to Europe and the Far East over the past 16 years. The paper proposes an AI-based Computer Science Laboratory management system to address cheating, disengagement, and lack of practical skills in CS education. It generates unique programming questions for each student based on faculty-specified keywords and difficulty levels using a fine-tuned CodeLlama model trained on a synthetic dataset of 10,000 ML/AI questions. The system supports proctored and non-proctored lab modes, assessing students holistically through gamified conceptual quizzes, coding tasks, and an interactive AI viva that uses automatic speech recognition to evaluate reasoning. Faculty and student dashboards provide lab management, progress tracking, analytics, and faculty override of automated scores. A fine-tuned XGBoost evaluator on SBERT embeddings performs automated grading. Experiments demonstrate strong agreement between AI and faculty scores (Pearson r = 0.914, Spearman ρ = 0.892, Cohen’s κ = 0.69), with the evaluator achieving RMSE = 3.37 and R² = 0.861. The system discourages cheating, improves engagement, and provides detailed performance feedback.

The study uses a DFT+DMFT approach incorporating non-local self-energy corrections to investigate the electronic spectra of α-iron, CrO2, CrTe2, and altermagnet CrSb in the paramagnetic phase. For iron and CrO2, which have d-state fillings far from half-filling, non-local magnetic correlations near the Curie temperature produce pronounced band splitting that qualitatively resembles ferromagnetic DFT band structures. For CrTe2 and CrSb, which are close to half-filling, strong band splitting originates primarily from local spin correlations and persists over a wider temperature range. The resulting split bands carry partial spectral weight of the non-magnetic bands without definite spin polarization, combining itinerant and local-moment characteristics. These states may influence transport properties and permit control of spin polarization via weak magnetic fields, with potential spintronics applications. The authors note that the density-density approximation overestimates magnetic transition temperatures and propose future extension to SU(2) symmetric Hund interactions.

The Triangle Game is a basketball offense built on inside screening and wing shooting, best executed by physically strong players proficient in setting and using screens. Wing shooters spread the defense, while smaller inside players can create mismatches. The offense features continuity actions including base screens, back screens, skip passes, and back-door cuts, with success dependent on precise execution and reading defensive positioning. Counters address defenders playing high, low, behind, fronting, switching, or double-teaming, utilizing moves such as power lay-ups, baby hooks, face-ups, lobs, and trap releases. Tex Winter’s “line of deployment” aids in reading post defense. The system also includes late-game “crunch time” options like staggered screens, isolations, and side screens.

The authors introduce GEM, a cryo-electron microscopy reconstruction framework that uses 3D Gaussian Splatting to explicitly model protein density with sparse 3D Gaussians, each parameterized by 11 values. By localizing gradient computation to only the Gaussians influencing each pixel and enabling parallel rasterization, GEM eliminates the cubic memory and computational overhead of NeRF-based real-space methods while avoiding the information loss of traditional Fourier-space approaches. The framework achieves up to 48× faster training speed and substantially lower memory usage than existing methods. Validated on four standard cryo-EM datasets, GEM consistently attains gold-standard Fourier shell correlation resolutions better than 3 Å, outperforming both the Fourier-space baseline CryoDRGN and the real-space baseline CryoNeRF in reconstruction quality and efficiency.

This computational study examines the reaction 2 CH₂ → C₂H₄ on a 2D-periodic gold (111) monolayer and on three gold layers using DFT with the PBE functional and Grimme dispersion correction. Adsorption energies, reaction energies, and activation energies were calculated with the counterpoise correction. Both reactants and products adsorb more strongly on the monolayer (−137.70 and −46.00 kJ mol⁻¹) than on three layers (−115.49 and −5.04 kJ mol⁻¹). The overall reaction is more exothermic on the monolayer (−432.06 vs. −335.50 kJ mol⁻¹) and proceeds with a substantially lower activation energy (4.78 vs. 52.10 kJ mol⁻¹). On the monolayer, the reaction path involves diffusion of fragments, association over a shared proton, and C=C bond formation, yielding a flat product. On three layers, greater rotational motion dominates, the intermediate is less stable at larger fragment separation, and the product orients perpendicular to the surface. The stronger monolayer interactions are attributed to greater availability of gold valence electrons at the surface, whereas in thicker layers these electrons are bound in the conduction band. The findings highlight that layer thickness and surface morphology significantly influence adsorption and reaction energetics relevant to carbon upconversion.

AMD's Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine processes memory migration commands through a ring buffer interface capable of parallel execution. Performance is optimized with commands moving 128 pages at once, though system activity involving the data fabric, DMA, and IOMMU may reduce throughput. The ring buffer should be kept sufficiently full, and interrupts should be requested at the end of command sequences rather than per command.

TMPM commands include PM_GET_CAPABILITIES, PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO for hypervisor-owned pages, and PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST for SNP guest pages. Each command uses a parameter page containing 1–128 Migration Entries. All system physical addresses must be 4KB-aligned; 2MB pages must be split into physically contiguous 4KB pages prior to migration. Migration is prohibited for IOMMU data structures, the ring buffer itself, and argument pages.

Device initialization requires verifying ENGINE_READY, configuring a 4KB-aligned ring buffer of 1–255 contiguous pages, and setting the DRIVER_INITIALIZED bit. The OS binds to the device via ACPI identifier AMDI0095, and the PAGEMIGRATION_EN bit must be set in all IOMMUs. The engine may modify IOMMU host page table entries and set Access and Dirty bits, so software must avoid concurrent modifications. Firmware reloads require halting operations and tearing down the ring buffer. Errors are reported via command status fields, ring buffer status registers, and the Machine Check Architecture.

This paper presents new results on boundedness of Bergman type projections in tubular domains over symmetric cones and their products, with applications in complex function theory. It defines tube domains over irreducible symmetric cones, mixed-norm weighted Bergman spaces, and the weighted Bergman projection with its integral kernel representation. The second part presents a new sharp decomposition theorem for Bergman A^1_α spaces in tube domains and poses problems for harmonic function spaces, indicating similar results may hold in Siegel domains of second type, bounded symmetric domains, and minimal bounded homogeneous domains. Proofs use special integral representations, uniform estimates, and Forelly-Rudin estimates. Preliminaries on symmetric cones, determinant functions, and simple Euclidean Jordan algebras are reviewed.

The On-Balance Volume (OBV) indicator, published by Joseph Granville in 1963, measures buying and selling pressure by adding volume when the market closes higher and subtracting volume when it closes lower. It typically follows price trends, confirming market direction. Non-confirmation occurs when price makes new highs or lows but OBV fails to do so, indicating potential weakness, while advanced breakouts or breakdowns—where OBV reaches new extremes without price confirmation—suggest trend continuation but are difficult to backtest. Granville created OBV to track institutional investor activity; a downward-sloping OBV with rising price may indicate smart money exiting, while rising OBV with falling price suggests institutional buying. A backtest using RSI on the OBV indicator for the S&P 500 (SPY) tested multiple settings. One selected strategy using a 5-day RSI and a buy threshold of 30 yielded 337 trades, a 0.55% average gain per trade, a 73% win rate, a 24% maximum drawdown, and a 2.09 profit factor. The article concludes that volume is of limited value as a standalone parameter and that better indicators may be available.

The lecture transitions from linear algebra to solving systems of nonlinear equations f(x)=0 and optimization. It recaps that any matrix has a condition number defined as the square root of the ratio of its largest and smallest singular values from the singular value decomposition. Because exact solutions to nonlinear systems are generally unavailable, iterative methods are required, and results must be validated against experiments, analytical limits, or multiple solution attempts. Two stopping criteria are defined: the step norm criteria, which checks if successive iterations are sufficiently close using absolute and relative tolerances, and the function norm criteria, which checks if the residual f(x) is sufficiently near zero. A root is locally unique if it is isolated in a surrounding ball of nonsolutions; the inverse function theorem states that a nonzero Jacobian determinant at a root guarantees local uniqueness. The lecture explains linearization via the Jacobian, f(x+δx) ≈ f(x) + Jδx, and defines convergence rates: linear (q=1), superlinear (q>1), and quadratic (q=2). The Newton-Raphson method, x_{i+1} = x_i − J⁻¹f(x_i), is presented for multidimensional systems; it possesses a local convergence property and converges quadratically near a locally unique root, but can fail if the Jacobian is singular or the initial guess is poor. Examples include vapor-liquid coexistence with the Van der Waals equation and the geometric intersection of two circles.

In *Bost v. Illinois State Board of Elections*, the Supreme Court is considering whether a candidate has standing to challenge election rules in federal court. Republican Congressman Michael Bost sued to block an Illinois rule counting mail-in ballots received up to 14 days after Election Day. Lower courts dismissed the suit for lack of standing, rejecting his claims of vote dilution and extra campaign costs as generalized or speculative harms. Before the Supreme Court, Bost argues that extended observer costs constitute a concrete “pocketbook injury” and that the rule harms his electoral chances and margin of victory, affecting future fundraising and opposition challenges. He also proposes a broad rule that candidates have standing to challenge election rules governing their races. The United States supports Bost’s narrow argument that he has standing to challenge this specific rule but opposes a blanket rule of candidate standing.

The study evaluates the Happy Ring, a novel finger-worn wearable using electrodermal activity, accelerometry, photoplethysmography, and skin temperature, for assessing sleep against in-lab polysomnography (PSG), the Dreem headband, and other devices (Oura, Fitbit, Whoop, Actiwatch). In 36 healthy adults across 77 nights (one laboratory, two at-home), the device employed two scoring approaches: Happy Generalized, a static population-level algorithm, and Happy Personalized, a dynamic algorithm adapted to individual user data. Both approaches demonstrated good sleep-wake detection accuracy (0.91–0.92) in lab and home settings, with sensitivity comparable to other devices (93–94%). However, Happy Personalized showed significantly improved specificity (83% in-lab) compared to Happy Generalized (70%) and other devices (19–54%). Sleep stage classification agreement with PSG was moderate and comparable to other wearables, with the personalized approach again performing better. The authors conclude that the personalized approach represents a significant innovation for improving specificity, though findings are limited by a small, healthy sample and the use of a commercial headband for at-home assessment.

inferring Cardio-Vascular States (iCVS) is a mechanistic model that estimates hidden cardiovascular states in real time at the bedside using only routinely available arterial and venous blood pressure waveforms, plus patient age and weight. The model uses ordinary differential equations linking 15 hidden parameters to five observables, incorporating autonomic regulation (baroreflex and independent components) and non-autonomic vascular resistance modulation. By exploiting both slow-scale mean pressures and fast-scale pulse contour features, it balances explanatory power with estimability without requiring invasive measurements beyond standard catheters. Demonstrated on 10 critically-ill children in a pediatric intensive care unit, iCVS correctly identified hypovolemic shock (negative intravascular volume change), distributive shock (negative non-autonomic vascular resistance), and cardiogenic shock (reduced contractility), matching expert clinician assessments despite noisy data. Reconstructed observables correlated with measurements at 0.71–0.94. The authors state the model requires minimal a priori assumptions and warrants prospective validation on larger cohorts to define diagnostic thresholds, with future potential for hybrid machine-learning integration.

China faces two debt problems. Internally, debt has risen to an estimated 328% of GDP due to post-crisis stimulus, loose credit, and shadow banking. Because this debt is largely internal and shielded by a closed capital account, crisis has been averted, but the burden will persist and require drastic policy intervention. Externally, China has become a major creditor through overseas infrastructure loans and bailouts to Venezuela, Argentina, and Belt and Road Initiative participants including Kenya, Laos, Sri Lanka, and Pakistan. Many loans are of questionable value to borrowers with limited repayment capacity, creating political resentment and default risks. The situation parallels the 1980s Latin American debt crisis, where supply shock windfalls funded unserviceable loans. If China's overseas loans fail to generate returns and political changes lead to non-payment, China may find itself holding large amounts of unserviceable debt, unable to enforce claims.

A pragmatic two-stage adaptive randomized trial in a U.S. academic emergency department compared auricular acupuncture (AA), peripheral acupuncture (PA), and usual care (UC) for acute musculoskeletal pain. Of 236 randomized patients, both acupuncture groups showed significantly greater pain reduction at one hour post-treatment than the control group (mean reductions of 2.1 and 1.6 points versus 0.5 on a 0–10 numeric rating scale), with no significant difference between AA and PA. Acupuncture groups demonstrated non-significant trends toward fewer opioid orders and discharge prescriptions and reported high treatment satisfaction (mean 4.4 on a 1–5 scale). Adverse events were minimal, with no serious events reported. The study population was diverse, with 53.6% of participants identifying as Black. The authors conclude that both acupuncture styles are feasible, acceptable, and effective for acute musculoskeletal pain in the emergency department.

Closed cell foams are widely used for thermal insulation because their low thermal conductivity results mainly from a high volume fraction of gas and a low volume fraction of solid, while small cell sizes suppress convection and radiation. The total thermal conductivity equals the sum of contributions from conduction through the solid and gas, convection within cells, and radiation; conduction through the gas dominates, whereas convection is negligible in most foams because cell sizes are much smaller than the roughly 20 mm required for a significant Rayleigh number. As relative density decreases, radiation contributes more, creating a trade-off with solid conduction that produces a minimum overall thermal conductivity. Foams possess the same specific heat and thermal expansion coefficient as the parent solid, but their much lower modulus gives them better thermal shock resistance, allowing them to endure larger temperature changes before cracking.

The ADS9803 has three power supplies—AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD—with no required power-up sequence; a common 1.8V supply can power VDD_1V8 and IOVDD, and IOVDD powers the digital interfaces. Layout should avoid crossing digital lines with the analog signal path; keep analog input and reference signals away from noise. Use 0.1μF ceramic bypass capacitors close to each power-supply pin without vias, and place reference decoupling capacitors near the REFIO and REFM pins, avoiding vias between REFIO and the capacitors; connect GND and REFM pins to a ground plane. TI provides development tools, documentation notifications via ti.com, and E2E support forums. The device requires ESD precautions. The document includes mechanical, packaging, and orderable information subject to change, along with accuracy and liability disclaimers.

The invention provides systems and methods for offering, purchasing, and reselling tokenized securities—termed Blockchain Instruments for Transferrable Equity (BITE) tokens—on an immutable blockchain platform (e.g., Ethereum). The platform facilitates investor registration, accreditation verification via third-party agencies or self-accreditation, and maintenance of whitelists and blacklists. Accredited investors review mandatory disclosure documents (e.g., Private Placement Memorandums, subscription agreements) and accept terms via a graphical user interface before purchasing tokens with cryptocurrency or fiat, typically through an escrow account governed by smart contracts. The token lifecycle includes presale, offering, rest, and trading periods; a rest period restricts resale to comply with securities regulations (e.g., SEC Rule 144). BITE tokens represent equity instruments and may include conversion, dividend, financing, and liquidity-event rights. The system supports secondary market transfers, enforces compliance (e.g., OFAC, AML/KYC, accredited-investor status), and utilizes transferable proxy contracts and encrypted escrow contracts to manage ownership and data visibility. Various graphical user interfaces support company management, shareholder administration, transfer windows, document handling, and broker/advisor workflows.

El artículo analiza la expresión de emociones en 798 tuits de las cuentas corporativas de Twitter de Acciona e Iberdrola (Ibex 35) publicados entre abril y junio de 2016. Mediante análisis del discurso y lingüística cognitiva, examina qué sistemas léxicos y estructuras lingüísticas (metáforas) conceptualizan, describen o evocan emociones, y su relación con la misión, visión y valores de las empresas. Se clasificaron 14 categorías emocionales con valencia positiva o negativa. Los resultados muestran que la mayoría de los tuits son emocionales (Acciona: 66,5 %; Iberdrola: 73,62 %), predominando las emociones positivas como el orgullo (27 % en ambas), el interés, la alegría y la confianza, mientras que las negativas son escasas (4,7 % y 3,7 %). Las metáforas detectadas vinculan dominios fuente específicos de cada empresa con emociones destino: en Iberdrola, la luz, la energía y el sol conceptualizan la alegría-felicidad, y el color verde (metonimia) transmite orgullo; en Acciona, la sostenibilidad evoca confianza y el orgullo se asocia a la innovación y la sostenibilidad. Se concluye que los mapas conceptuales parten de la identidad corporativa para reforzarla, y se sugieren implicaciones pedagógicas para la enseñanza del español de los negocios.

Researchers developed a fully automatic machine learning tool to predict one-year overall survival in pediatric diffuse midline glioma from multisequence MRI. Using transfer learning with nnU-Net pretrained on glioblastoma data, the tool automatically segments tumor core and whole tumor volumes, extracts radiomic features, and applies support vector machine classification. The method was trained and validated on an internal cohort of 53 patients from Children's National Hospital and tested on an external cohort of 16 patients from Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, achieving 77–85% accuracy for survival prediction. Homogeneous whole tumor intensity on baseline T2 FLAIR and a larger post-radiation therapy tumor core-to-whole-tumor volume ratio were identified as indicators of worse prognosis. The automatic segmentation achieved mean Dice scores of 0.91 for tumor core and 0.88 for whole tumor on the internal cohort, with similar whole tumor performance on the external cohort. The tool is intended to provide consistent, repeatable, and noninvasive prognostic assessment to support risk stratification, clinical trial evaluation, and therapeutic management.

Investors worried about U.S.-North Korea tensions will find few reliable historical comparisons for stock market reactions. While a major war would devastate markets, there is generally little connection between conflict levels and stock valuations. The early 1990s "peace dividend" appears coincidental, as valuations rose during some wars and fell during others; the 1990s bull market most likely had more to do with the internet and falling interest rates. Last week's drop may have more to do with President Trump's unpredictability and a reversal of the post-election "Trump trade" than with imminent military conflict, and investors will focus on the president's mindset.

The "Pound Cake" offense attacks a Box & One defense by isolating the star player in the post against the chaser, who is typically proficient in pass denial but ill-prepared for post defense, while a 2-1-2 alignment limits defensive help. If no shot is available, the star can roll to the basket for base screens set by O4 and O5, executing reads such as curl, fade, back cut, or screen & roll, or pop out to the perimeter for 1-on-1 isolation with posts in the short corners and guards on the wings. Additional options include ball reversal, post flashes, screener pops, guard basket cuts, and double mid-screens. Success requires precise execution, coordination, defensive recognition, timing, scouting to identify opponent tendencies and weakest defenders, and utilizing multiple alignments to prevent defensive focus.

Dietitians Barbara Kovalenko and Yelena Wheeler advise planning ahead and setting realistic targets, such as not gaining more than two pounds, to enjoy a healthy Diwali while managing diabetes, heart health, or weight. They recommend using smaller plates, stopping once full, and swapping fatty or sugary ingredients for healthier options: unsaturated oils instead of ghee, butter, or coconut oil; wholegrain rice and bread instead of white; tofu instead of paneer; and baking rather than deep-frying. Include high-fibre foods like lentils, wholegrains, and vegetables, and choose lean proteins such as grilled chicken or fish. Limit sweets and replace refined sugars with fresh fruit, dates, or dried fruit; use semi-skimmed milk and whole wheat flour in desserts. Eat simple carbohydrates alongside protein and fibre to prevent blood sugar spikes. Limit alcohol and sugary drinks, drink water, stay active with walking or dancing, monitor blood sugar levels, avoid skipping meals, and ask family for support.

The bark Cape Horn Pigeon was seized by the Imperial Russian Government and detained at Vladivostok until after the Okhotsk Sea whaling season had closed, causing severe damages to its owners, officers, and crew. The captain estimated damages at $49,500 and presented a claim in September 1892. In May 1893, the United States envoy requested an investigation. Russia’s Foreign Ministry replied in June 1893 that the arrest resulted from a misunderstanding, ordered the vessel’s release, and admitted indemnity was due, though it deemed $2,500 sufficient rather than the $45,000 claimed for lost whales. In June 1894, the United States formally presented indemnity claims, and Russia finally responded in October 1895 requesting vouchers for $3,400 in expenses.

The Supreme Court will decide whether trial courts may bar defense lawyers from discussing a client’s ongoing testimony with the client during an overnight recess. The case involves David Villarreal, convicted of murder after a judge barred such consultation while he was mid-testimony. The Texas Court of Criminal Appeals rejected Villarreal’s argument, explaining that the order balanced the Sixth Amendment right to counsel against preventing improper management. Two Supreme Court decisions set boundaries: a 1976 ruling held that an overnight ban on any discussion with a testifying client violated the Sixth Amendment, while a 1989 ruling held that a brief midday recess contact ban did not. State and federal courts are split on overnight testimony-specific bans. Villarreal argues the restriction is unworkable because trial strategy and testimony are inseparable. Texas contends the order is workable and distinguishes overnight recesses from brief ones. The United States filed a brief supporting Texas, arguing limited conferral orders are historically consistent and necessary for truth-finding.

This study employed a single-group posttest design to examine an eight-week activity-based lesson plan for five volunteer beginner guitar students aged 18–33 with no prior instruction. Delivered as online one-on-one lessons totaling sixteen hours, the curriculum addressed scales, chords, and arpeggios using a 3E instructional model. Three field experts evaluated theoretical knowledge tests and performance tests using a Likert scale adapted from Albuz (2001). Students scored 90, 80, 100, 90, and 100 on theoretical tests (mean 92), and chapter achievement scores were 91, 89.2, 95.5, 93.6, and 98.8, resulting in a class average of 93.6, rated "very good." The findings demonstrate that activity-based lesson plans effectively supported learning and achievement in amateur guitar education during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Early Offense consists of three phases: an initial early push before the defense gets organized, a continuous flow into an early set, and a continuity offense as the shot clock winds down. Success requires moving from push to flow to continuity without hesitation, playing disruptive defense to force bad shots and turnovers, rebounding with authority, executing effective outlet passes, and advancing the ball into the front court within three to five seconds. Wings run wide lanes, the point advances with a hard speed dribble while analyzing defensive deployment, and players should pass ahead and minimize dribble. If the flow does not produce a good shot, the offense moves directly into continuity while maintaining poise and going to the offensive boards with determined aggressiveness.

The Digital Business Ecosystem (DBE) is the co-evolution of the Business Ecosystem and the Digital Ecosystem, with a lifecycle comprising formation, evolution, and dissipation. The formation phase is critical and relies heavily on negotiation among entities. Existing approaches such as Electronic Institutions and Contractual Agent Societies use norms to coordinate activities, while the Contract Net Protocol (CNP) facilitates negotiation through steps including task announcement, bidding, bid evaluation, and contract award. The authors propose the Contract Net with Quality Protocol (CNQP), an extension of the FIPA CNP that adds quality evaluation steps to the negotiation process. In CNQP, participants evaluate the quality of the initiator during task announcement processing, and the initiator evaluates participant quality during bid processing, utilizing a Quality Backbone Engine. This introduces additional time but reduces risk, improves transaction performance, and increases confidence among business entities. Quality encompasses reliability, trust, and reputation. The authors conclude that quality evaluation is necessary for successful contract execution despite the efficiency trade-off, and future work will apply the protocol to service-level parameter negotiation.

Offensive tackles are essential but rarely glorified linemen at the outermost spots on both sides of the offensive line. They execute run and pass blocking, often in isolation against opposing pass rushers while diagnosing pre-snap looks and blitzes. Success is measured by winning one-on-one blocks to protect the quarterback—particularly the left tackle shielding the blind side—and open running lanes. The role requires elite functional athleticism, footwork, agility, strength, and football IQ. Players are typically tall, lengthy, and thick, generally 6'3" to 6'8" and 300 to 340 pounds. The position name originated from early football, when edge defenders tackled ball carriers. Notable players include Jonathan Ogden, Anthony Munoz, and Joe Thomas.

The passage describes container and distributed system design patterns. Single-node patterns include the ambassador pattern, which routes traffic between main applications and experiments using IP hashing and weighted splitting, and the adapter pattern, which standardizes monitoring, logging, and health-check interfaces without modifying application containers. Examples include Prometheus exporters, Fluentd log normalization, and MySQL health-check adapters. Multi-node patterns cover microservices, which improve reliability, agility, and independent scaling but complicate debugging and design. The replicated load-balanced service pattern deploys stateless replicas behind load balancers with readiness probes, and can incorporate session tracking, caching layers such as Varnish, rate limiting, and SSL termination via nginx. Sharded services partition large datasets across shards using sharding functions and consistent hashing to limit disruption during scaling; replicated and hot-sharded caches enhance resilience and dynamic load handling. The scatter/gather pattern parallelizes computation across nodes to reduce latency, though overhead and straggler effects limit benefits, and reliability requires shard replication. Finally, event-driven and function-as-a-service architectures simplify deployment and scaling but are ill-suited for long-running background tasks or large in-memory datasets, may become costly under sustained load, and support patterns such as decorators for API transformation and event handlers for asynchronous tasks like two-factor authentication.

Researchers from the University of Exeter claim to have refined James Lovelock's 1970s 'Gaia' hypothesis, which proposed that Earth is a self-regulating living organism. They say the key is 'sequential selection,' where destabilizing situations are short-lived and lead to stable situations that persist, allowing the system to acquire further stabilizing traits through 'selection by survival alone.' Professor Tim Lenton states this explains how Earth accumulated stabilizing mechanisms over 3.5 billion years, addressing the original problem that natural selection could not explain planetary stabilizing properties over geologic timescales. The paper, published in Trends in Ecology and Evolution, may help estimate the probability of complex life elsewhere and understand Earth's response to human-produced climate change and extinction events.

Verdad Research found that US hard-to-borrow stocks underperform over 3-, 6-, and 12-month periods, while general collateral stocks yield positive returns; this pattern is not systematic in Japan and Europe. Small-cap hard-to-borrow stocks perform particularly poorly. However, the negative edge is likely insufficient for a profitable short-selling strategy because traders often cannot secure a short locate. Stocks become hard to borrow due to limited supply, high demand, regulatory restrictions like Regulation SHO, high stock loan fees ranging from 1% to 50%, and locate requirements. Borrowing costs vary by stock characteristics: large, stable, and liquid stocks are cheaper to borrow, while smaller, volatile, illiquid stocks are more expensive. For example, GameStop’s short-borrow fee surged from approximately 1% in January 2019 to 34% in January 2021 during a short squeeze. Short selling carries unlimited potential losses.

A time frame in trading refers to the time horizon of a trade and the bars used in a strategy, such as tick, minute, daily, weekly, or yearly data. The authors believe daily bars are the best starting point for trading and swing trading because they offer simplicity in backtesting and help identify market inefficiencies. However, they recommend being agnostic and using multiple time frames as a diversification tool. Different participants use different horizons: day traders focus on minutes or hours, swing traders on days, trend followers on days to months, and investors on years or decades. Mixing time frames within a single strategy is possible, and diversifying across time frames can spread risk, reduce correlations, optimize capital use, and minimize drawdowns by offsetting losses in one area with gains in another. The right time frame depends on individual goals, preferences, and strategy.

James Swan continues a lecture on numerical optimization, reviewing steepest descent for finding local minima via negative gradient directions and quadratic step-size estimates. He explains that systems of linear equations Ax=b can be posed as minimizing a quadratic functional when A is symmetric and positive definite, but steepest descent can be inefficient due to eigenvalue-dependent step-size oscillations. The conjugate gradient method improves this by selecting A-conjugate directions that preserve minimization along previous steps, converging in at most n steps for n unknowns while only requiring matrix-vector products. Newton-Raphson solves grad f = 0 using the Hessian, yielding quadratic convergence and exact solutions for quadratic functions, but it may converge to saddle points or maxima if the Hessian lacks positive eigenvalues and requires expensive linear solves. Trust-region methods combine both approaches heuristically: an adaptive radius determines whether to take a Newton-Raphson step (if it lies within the trust region and reduces the objective) or a steepest descent step, adjusting the radius based on how well the quadratic approximation predicts the actual function decrease. MATLAB uses such trust-region and dogleg strategies in its solvers.

This study used a 7 Tesla sparsely-sampled dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI protocol to investigate the relationship between hypertension, blood pressure, and blood-brain barrier (BBB) leakage in 23 patients with essential hypertension and 20 normotensive controls matched for age and sex. No significant difference in BBB leakage rates (Ki) was observed between hypertensive patients and controls based on dichotomous hypertension status. However, higher current systolic, diastolic, and mean arterial blood pressure were significantly and positively associated with increased BBB leakage in cortical and total grey matter, but not in white matter or deep grey matter, after adjusting for age, sex, cardiovascular risk factors, and cerebral small vessel disease score. Blood plasma volume fraction (vp) was significantly higher in hypertensive patients across grey matter regions but showed no significant relation with continuous blood pressure measures. Post-hoc subgroup analysis revealed that hypertensive patients with normal blood pressure on antihypertensive medication had lower leakage rates than patients with current high blood pressure, suggesting a protective effect of effective medication. The authors conclude that current blood pressure, rather than hypertension status alone, is associated with BBB integrity in grey matter, and that subtle BBB changes may be detectable prior to overt neurovascular damage.

Andrew Lo reviews the risk-return trade-off, explaining that combining imperfectly correlated securities produces a bullet-shaped efficient frontier where rational, risk-averse investors prefer the upper branch. He notes that adding more assets improves this frontier because investors can always choose zero weight in unwanted assets, shifting opportunities northwest. Introducing a risk-free asset creates linear combinations with any risky portfolio; the optimal combination lies on the line tangent to the efficient frontier. This tangency portfolio—called M—maximizes the Sharpe ratio, which measures expected excess return per unit of volatility. Because all mean-variance investors will hold some mix of the risk-free asset and this single tangency portfolio, equilibrium implies that portfolio M must be the market portfolio, with weights proportional to market capitalizations. This yields a linear relationship for efficient portfolios. Extending this, Sharpe showed that any individual asset’s expected return equals the risk-free rate plus its beta—defined as the covariance of the asset with the market divided by the variance of the market—times the market risk premium. This provides the appropriate discount rate for capital budgeting and establishes a benchmark for evaluating manager performance (Alpha).

This study examines dropout tendencies among 1,061 undergraduate and preparatory students at Turkish public universities during the 2023–2024 academic year, using a descriptive correlational design grounded in Tinto’s Theoretical Dropout Model. Utilizing the 32-item School Dropout Scale in Higher Education (Cronbach’s α = .911), the research found a moderate overall dropout tendency (mean = 2.67). No significant gender difference was observed. However, significant differences emerged by year of study, location, employment status, and peer influence: students in their third year or above, those studying outside metropolitan cities, those working while studying, and those with close friends who had dropped out all showed significantly higher tendencies. Spearman correlations revealed that lower school attendance, lower parental education (particularly maternal), lower GPA, lower family income, and a higher number of siblings were significantly associated with greater dropout tendency. Pearson analysis showed all six subdimensions—Health and Wellbeing, Institutional Factors, Faculty Members, Academic Factors, Social Factors, and Financial Factors—were positively correlated with overall dropout tendency, with Health and Wellbeing showing the strongest relationship. The findings support Tinto’s model and highlight the need for institution-level interventions, particularly academic mentoring, financial aid, and mental health services in non-metropolitan universities, alongside early monitoring of attendance and at-risk students.

ZnSe-WSe2 and ZnSe-MoSe2 core-shell nanowires were fabricated by depositing MoO3 and WO3 precursor layers onto ZnSe nanowires via DC magnetron sputtering, followed by selenization at controlled temperatures. TEM, XRD, XPS, Raman, and photoluminescence characterization confirmed complete conversion of the oxide precursors to TMD shells and verified the intact ZnSe core. At lower selenization temperatures, conformal layered shells formed, while at higher temperatures the shells became discontinuous with protruding TMD crystals. This morphological transition results from a shift from solid-state interfacial reaction at lower temperatures to gas-phase reaction and island growth driven by precursor evaporation at higher temperatures. These findings provide a basis for optimizing core-shell nanowire morphology for optoelectronic and catalytic applications.

The paper introduces EduVidQA, a dataset and benchmarking study for question answering over educational lecture videos. Motivated by a survey of 52 STEM students showing high demand for interactive learning but low rates of asking questions in video comments, the work explores how well Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can automatically answer student questions and whether finetuning with synthetic data improves performance. The authors contribute: (1) a dataset of 270 real-world, expert-verified QA pairs collected from YouTube Computer Science and AI lecture comments, alongside 4,982 synthetic QA pairs generated from NPTEL lecture transcripts using GPT-4o, with adversarial refinement and Bloom’s taxonomy difficulty tagging; (2) a qualitative preference study identifying Clarity, Encouraging Critical Thinking, and Uses Pedagogical Techniques as key answer qualities; (3) novel LLM-based qualitative evaluation metrics using Likert scales validated against human annotations; and (4) benchmarking of six state-of-the-art MLLMs across open-source and closed models. Results demonstrate that supervised finetuning on synthetic data enables smaller open-source models to achieve comparable or better performance than larger closed models on both text-based and qualitative metrics for real-world and synthetic test sets. The authors note limitations regarding demographic scope, real-world dataset size, and compute constraints.

This paper proposes a hybrid memory system for long-running Low-Code/No-Code (LCNC) agents to address context window limitations causing memory inflation and contextual degradation. The architecture comprises Working Memory (immediate context), Episodic Memory (time-indexed interaction records in a vector database), and Semantic Memory (generalized knowledge). The core "Intelligent Decay" mechanism assigns each memory entry a utility score based on recency, semantic relevance to the current task, and user-assigned importance, proactively pruning low-utility memories or consolidating them into semantic memory. A user-centric timeline interface enables non-technical users to act as Human-in-the-Loop evaluators by pinning, forgetting, or consolidating memories. Experiments on a 500-turn project planning task compared the hybrid system against a sliding window baseline and a basic RAG baseline. The hybrid system achieved a 92.5% task completion rate, reduced token costs by 22% compared to basic RAG, and maintained higher consistency (0.94) with a 1.2% contradiction rate, while naive "All-Add" strategies exhibited performance degradation over time. Limitations include the need for hyperparameter tuning and consistent user feedback.

As of September 10, 1892, the bark Cape Horn Pigeon was owned by multiple American citizens, with managing owners J. & W. R. Wing of New Bedford holding twenty sixty-fourths and other fractional owners including Edward F. Potter and Louisa B. Haskell, who held ten sixty-fourths conveyed from the estate of Alexander H. Seabury. Built in Dartmouth, Massachusetts in 1854 for whaling and measuring 201 42/100 tons, the vessel was fitted out in San Francisco in December 1891 for a whaling voyage in the Japan and Okhotsk seas. Its crew of thirty plus captain were compensated by shares of net proceeds, though most were in debt to the ship due to low oil yields. The bark was not equipped or intended for sealing. Supporting documents were annexed as exhibits.

Apple Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the second quarter of fiscal 2020 ended March 28, 2020. For the quarter, the Company reported net sales of $58.3 billion, up 1% year-over-year, net income of $11.2 billion, and diluted earnings per share of $2.55. For the six months ended March 28, 2020, net sales were $150.1 billion and net income was $33.5 billion. Total assets as of March 28, 2020 were $320.4 billion.

 Net sales growth was driven by a 17% increase in Services and a 23% increase in Wearables, Home and Accessories, while iPhone net sales declined 7% in the quarter. Mac and iPad sales also decreased. The COVID-19 pandemic caused manufacturing and supply chain disruptions beginning in February 2020, temporary closure of all retail stores outside China effective March 13, 2020, and weakened demand in the final weeks of the quarter.

 During the quarter, the Company repurchased $18.5 billion of common stock and paid $3.4 billion in dividends. As of March 28, 2020, the Company held $40.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $152.7 billion in total marketable securities. Total term debt outstanding was $98.0 billion. The Company adopted new accounting standards for leases and hedging, recording right-of-use assets of $7.5 billion and lease liabilities of $8.1 billion upon adoption, and adjusted accumulated other comprehensive income by $136 million. Notable contingencies include a settlement of up to $500 million related to iOS performance management, a €1.1 billion fine from the French Competition Authority, and an escrowed recovery amount of €12.9 billion related to the European Commission State Aid Decision.

Peru’s fragmented, decentralized health system and a regulatory mandate for >99% medical oxygen purity created a pre-pandemic “policy trap” that concentrated supply among a few large companies and blocked smaller competitors. During COVID-19, these structural failures caused acute shortages, particularly in rural Andean and jungle regions, worsened by bureaucratic delays in authorizing 93% purity, fragmented procurement that bypassed centralized purchasing, and the absence of a national oxygen tracking system. Civil society and private sector groups, notably the Catholic Church’s Respira Perú, donated oxygen plants and supplies to fill government gaps, but bureaucratic obstacles stalled many installations. By the end of the pandemic, 496 oxygen plants had been installed, yet nearly 200 are now unused or broken due to lack of maintenance plans, legal ambiguities over donated assets, staff turnover, and poor training, leading facilities to revert to expensive cylinder purchases from dominant suppliers. Stakeholders warn that Peru has not learned from the crisis and urge creation of a National Oxygen System to centrally manage supply chains, demand forecasting, equipment inventories, maintenance, quality control, and equitable distribution to ensure sustainable local supply and future preparedness.

Turing GPUs improve video encoding quality over Pascal and software-based x264 encoders while reducing CPU utilization, enabling 4K streaming. They include hardware support for USB Type-C and VirtualLink, allowing VR headsets to operate over a single connector for power, display, and data, simplifying setup and supporting small-form-factor devices.

For multi-GPU setups, Turing TU102 and TU104 use NVLink instead of traditional SLI bridges, delivering up to 100 GB/sec bidirectional bandwidth in TU102 and 50 GB/sec in TU104, with support for two-way SLI and advanced display topologies.

Turing introduces RT Cores to accelerate real-time ray tracing through hybrid rendering that combines ray tracing with rasterization. RT Cores perform BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing, making ray tracing approximately 10 times faster than on Pascal. The GPUs also feature Tensor Cores that power NVIDIA NGX AI technologies, including Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS) for improved performance and image quality over TAA, as well as AI InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez.

Mesh Shading adds Task and Mesh Shader stages to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks and increase real-time object counts. Variable Rate Shading (VRS) enables dynamic, region-based shading-rate adjustments for applications such as Content Adaptive, Motion Adaptive, and Foveated Rendering. Texture Space Shading (TSS) decouples shading from screen space to improve efficiency and temporal stability, particularly for VR stereo rendering. Multi-View Rendering (MVR) expands on Pascal’s Simultaneous Multi-Projection to support up to four views per pass, improving VR and shadow-map rendering efficiency.

Turing supports DirectX 12 Tier 3 bindless resource views and Tier 2 resource heaps. The architecture is implemented in the TU102, TU104, and TU106 GPUs, which power products such as the GeForce RTX 2080 Ti, RTX 2080, RTX 2070, and corresponding Quadro and Tesla cards; TU106 does not support NVLink or SLI. NVIDIA also introduced RTX-OPS as a workload-based performance metric for hybrid rendering workloads.

The speaker contends that the nation's moral and spiritual welfare depends on religion, which government and education alone cannot provide. Modern society faces increased crime, lawlessness, and complex temptations, particularly following war, but government’s role is limited to maintaining order and justice. Effective law observance requires public sentiment derived from religious conviction, and intellectual development without moral growth increases capacity for evil. The foundations of American government—freedom, equality, and self-government—rest on religious principles of divine fatherhood and human brotherhood. Historical clergy shaped education and governance through spiritual leadership. Because government reflects the virtue of its people and cannot create virtue itself, lasting reform requires religious influence through clergy, home piety, and personal sacrifice. The speaker concludes that despite modern challenges, national faith endures, and expanding it is essential to preserving and improving the country's moral life.

This scoping review mapped approaches to measuring socioeconomic status (SES) in sub-Saharan African health research, analyzing 65 articles published between 2012 and 2024 across 22 countries, with South Africa, Kenya, and Ghana most frequently represented. Cross-sectional designs and themes related to maternal and child health and SES assessment dominated the included studies. The review identified 41 SES measures categorized into 11 groups. The asset-based Wealth Index was the most frequently used measure, accounting for 61.9% of applications, including variations such as the standard Wealth Index (28.6%), Household Wealth Index, and Harmonized Wealth Index. Principal Component Analysis was the predominant calculation method for asset-based indices, used independently in 57.7% of cases and combined with other methods in 9.6%. Other measures included the Multidimensional Poverty Index (16.7%), indices based on education, health, and living standards, and subjective social status measures. Asset-based indices were commonly employed in contexts where income data were unreliable, while multidimensional measures tended to reveal more pronounced health disparities. The review noted that the lack of standardized SES measures complicates comparison across studies and may hinder effective targeting of vulnerable groups. Limitations included the absence of critical quality appraisal and significant methodological heterogeneity. The authors concluded that selecting context-appropriate SES measures is essential and recommended moving toward standardized methods that allow for local adjustments.

Researchers including Binghamton University's Carl Lipo confirmed via 3D modeling and field experiments that Rapa Nui's moai statues were moved upright through a rocking, zig-zag "walking" motion using rope and few people. Distinctive design features, including wide D-shaped bases and a forward lean, enabled this movement. The team transported a 4.35-ton replica 100 meters in 40 minutes using 18 people. Concave roads across the island further supported this method. The findings challenge the theory that the statues were moved lying prone on wooden devices and celebrate the innovation and intelligence of the ancient Rapa Nui people.

Sudan, the world's last male northern white rhino, died in Kenya at age 45 after a severe leg infection led his veterinary team to euthanize him. Captured in 1975 and moved to the Ol Pejeta Conservancy in 2009 with two females, Najin and Fatu, he never reproduced. War and poaching had driven the subspecies to extinction in the wild. Only the two females remain; one is sterile and the other cannot carry a calf to term, preventing natural reproduction. Scientists collected sperm from Sudan and plan to attempt ovum pick-up from the females to fertilize eggs and implant them in a southern white rhino, though the procedure is unprecedented and risky.

This study developed and tested maternal vulnerability segmentation tools (MVST) to identify pregnant women in Oromia, Ethiopia, at risk of underutilizing essential maternal services. Using baseline data from 1,189 pregnant women identified through household visits, researchers developed a 20-item questionnaire covering economic, social, and service-access drivers. Factor analyses yielded a four-item tool for urban-rural settings (rural residence, houses not made of corrugated iron, women without a mobile phone, and far distance from a health facility) and a six-item tool for rural settings (adding women and husband education, and household mobile phone ownership), both with acceptable reliability and model fit. Higher composite vulnerability scores were significantly associated with lower antenatal care visits and lower health facility delivery; scores above three indicated greater risk of home delivery, while scores of one or more indicated greater vulnerability for antenatal care. The study concludes that these tools enable community health workers to classify pregnant women by degree of vulnerability for targeted interventions, and calls for further research to validate such tools across different low- and middle-income contexts.

This document specifies the statistical analysis plan for a clinical trial evaluating dasiglucagon, GlucaGen, and placebo. Statistical testing will be two-sided at the 0.05 significance level, using SAS and Phoenix WinNonlin. Analysis populations include the safety set, full analysis set (FAS), and per protocol set (PPS). The primary efficacy endpoint, time to plasma glucose recovery within 45 minutes without rescue intravenous glucose, will be analyzed on the FAS using Kaplan-Meier estimates and a stratified log-rank test, with a hierarchical testing procedure for secondary endpoints including recovery rates at 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes and plasma glucose changes from baseline. Pharmacokinetic parameters will be calculated by non-compartmental analysis, and pharmacodynamic metrics include the plasma glucose area under the effect curve. Safety analyses comprise adverse events, local tolerability, laboratory assessments, vital signs, electrocardiograms, and immunogenicity. Post-hoc analyses will be labeled exploratory. The plan adds sensitivity analyses and updates terminology from the protocol.

Labor force participation among young Americans without college degrees has declined, with roughly 12% of 18- to 24-year-olds now disconnected from work and school. Goldman Sachs data shows the share of non-graduates citing unspecified reasons for being unable to work has doubled to nearly 5% over 30 years. Experts attribute the trend to available jobs lacking family-sustaining wages, a cultural stigma against blue-collar roles, rising mental health challenges, increased reliance on family support, and gig workers potentially being undercounted in surveys. Proposed solutions include expanding apprenticeships and work-embedded education while reducing stigma around non-degree careers, though experts say helping those already in their late 20s will be difficult.

Research from Ben-Gurion University published in *Social Psychological and Personality Science* found that using smiley face emojis in formal work emails decreases perceptions of competence without increasing perceptions of warmth, unlike face-to-face smiles. Experiments with 549 participants from 29 countries showed that responses to formal emails without smileys contained more detailed, content-related information. When the sender's gender was unknown, participants were more likely to assume a smiley sender was a woman. The researchers concluded that smileys should be avoided in initial workplace interactions.

A qualitative study explored perspectives on regional teaching for Stage 1 anaesthetic trainees across a UK deanery with five hospital trusts. Semi-structured focus group interviews with six trainees and eight trainers identified themes including the complexity of the new three-year Stage 1 curriculum, pressure of the primary FRCA examination, heterogeneous trainee needs, and disparities between hospital sites operating in silos with variable teaching quality and trainer compensation. Participants identified logistical challenges for a regional programme, including location, funding, rota organisation, group dynamics, and quality control. Despite these barriers, both trainers and trainees supported developing a regional teaching programme to improve fairness, standardise exam-focused teaching, share resources, and enhance social networking. Trainers expressed willingness to collaborate, while trainees suggested mechanisms for feedback and continuity. The study, part of a quality improvement project, informed subsequent actions including a deanery-wide trainee survey. Limitations included a small trainee sample and potential interviewer bias. The authors conclude that a well-executed regional programme could address training disparities but requires sustained engagement and investment.

Researchers performed the first genome-wide association study of neonatal jaundice in 27,384 Norwegian newborns, replicating findings in 6,902 Danish neonates. Two loci reached genome-wide significance: a missense variant in UGT1A4 (rs6755571) associated with a five-fold lower risk of jaundice, and a locus near CHRDL1 on the X chromosome. Parental origin analysis indicated these effects were driven by transmitted alleles, reflecting neonate-specific effects. A maternal GWAS identified associations at the UGT1A* and CHRDL1 regions, plus an ABO gene variant explained by maternal-fetal ABO blood group incompatibility. The protective UGT1A4 effect was not modified by ABO incompatibility but was stronger in full-term and post-term neonates. The study found marked differences between neonatal and adult bilirubin genetics: the lead adult UGT1A* variant was distinct from the neonatal lead variant, SLCO1B1 variants were not associated with neonatal jaundice, and a polygenic score for adult bilirubin only predicted neonatal jaundice when the UGT1A* region on chromosome 2 was included. Colocalization analysis linked the neonatal UGT1A* signal to UGT1A1 expression in the colon but not the liver, suggesting context-specific genetic regulation of bilirubin clearance in neonates.

The SPREAD Offense is a 3-2 no-post motion offense requiring all five players to pass and handle the ball. Success depends on reading and countering defensive overplays through basic cuts and continuity. Overplayed players back cut immediately. Ball handlers assume triple threat, drive when overplayed, and kick out if defenders help. Corners can break to the middle for back door passes to cutting teammates when wings are overplayed or the shot clock is low.
