Intercontinental Exchange, parent of the New York Stock Exchange, will invest $2 billion in cash in Polymarket at a $9 billion valuation. The companies will partner on tokenization initiatives and ICE will distribute Polymarket’s data. Founded in 2020, the blockchain-based prediction market platform surged during the 2024 U.S. presidential election, with trading volume peaking at nearly $400 million the day after the election. The deal comes amid growing investor enthusiasm for prediction markets. Competitor Kalshi announced it raised $185 million at a $2 billion valuation and is now in talks to raise capital at nearly a $5 billion valuation.

Investors sold PPL Corporation (NYSE:PPL) shares on strength Wednesday, resulting in a $29.88 million net money flow out of the stock, though shares still rose $0.19 to close at $37.65. Analysts maintain a consensus "Hold" rating with a $38.94 price target following mixed recent rating changes. The company reported Q2 EPS of $0.52, beating estimates by $0.02, but revenue of $1.73 billion missed expectations and fell 3.4% year-over-year. PPL pays an annualized dividend of $1.58, yielding 4.24%, with a 66.11% payout ratio. Insiders sold 47,163 shares worth $1.86 million in the last three months, while several hedge funds and institutions increased Q1 holdings, bringing institutional ownership to 71.01%. The firm has a market capitalization of $25.58 billion and a PE ratio of 15.61.

Europe faces challenges from an ageing population that strain tax-funded health and social care systems, particularly for citizens aged 75+. The authors propose proactive digital wellness services for the “young elderly” (60–75), delivered via mobile omnivore platforms, to maintain health, activity, and independence and thereby reduce future care costs. A three-step approach is outlined: prevention programs for the 60–75 group; smartphone-based intervention tools; and commercially driven ecosystems to sustain ICT services. The young elderly represent 18–23% of the EU population, estimated at 97 million by 2020. The Finnish BeWell program (2014–2016) develops these services using the Wellmo platform and Tieto cloud analytics, designing them with users through multi-disciplinary action design research. Survey results from 101 young elderly respondents indicate that this group uses smartphones, finds mobile apps useful, and regards intellectual and physical wellness as important. The study concludes that such digitally supported wellness routines can form a disruptive, scalable intervention to lower public health costs and serve a large consumer market.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on April 26, 2018, announcing its first quarter 2018 financial results. The filing incorporates by reference the press release as Exhibit 99.1 and information on non-GAAP financial measures as Exhibit 99.2. Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, signed the report.

The device supports an external 4.096V reference at the REFIO pin when the INTREF_DIS bit in the RANGE_SEL_REG register is set to 1, using an internal buffer to drive the ADC reference pin. A 10µF capacitor is required between REFCAP and REFGND, and a 1µF capacitor must be placed close to REFCAP for decoupling; the buffer must not drive external loads. The buffer output is stable across –40°C to +125°C with typical drift of 0.5ppm/°C and maximum drift of 2ppm/°C. The ADC supports single-ended and differential inputs in bipolar and unipolar ranges with straight-binary output, and the LSB size equals the full-scale range divided by 2^16.

Alarm features include an input alarm with user-programmable high and low thresholds and common hysteresis, and an AVDD alarm with fixed thresholds of 4.7V and 5.3V. Both alarms are enabled by default and can be disabled via the RST_PWRCTL_REG register. Each alarm has active and tripped flags in the ALARM_REG register; active flags clear at the end of conversion, while tripped flags clear only after the register is read. Flags are updated at the end of each conversion and can be read via the ALARM pin, internal registers, or appended to the data output.

The device uses a multiSPI interface supporting standard SPI and daisy-chain topologies. In daisy-chain mode, optimal data frames require 32 × N SCLK edges for N devices. The device operates in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states controlled by the RST and CONVST/CS pins. Data transfer frames begin at the falling edge of CONVST/CS and end at the rising edge; valid write commands require 32 SCLK cycles. The device supports legacy SPI-compatible protocols and source-synchronous protocols, with single or dual SDO-x output modes.

Nine configuration registers control device ID, reset and power control, SDI and SDO protocols, data output content, input range and reference, and alarm thresholds and flags. Writes to the RST_PWRCTL_REG require a preceding write of 69h to address 05h as a protection key.

The ADS868xW is a 16-bit SAR ADC with an integrated analog front end, programmable gain amplifier, ADC driver, and reference, suitable for industrial analog input modules when paired with an external multiplexer. AVDD and DVDD must be decoupled with 10µF and 1µF capacitors placed close to the pins. The device offers NAP and power-down modes to reduce power consumption, controlled through the RST_PWRCTL_REG. For PCB layout, analog and digital sections should be separated, decoupling capacitors should be placed directly next to supply pins without vias, and the REFCAP pin should have a 1µF capacitor close to the device plus a 10µF capacitor with ESR less than 0.2Ω.

FreeNAS released Version 11, based on FreeBSD 11-STABLE, following Version 10’s failure and demotion to a tech preview. It includes the bhyve hypervisor, AWS S3 compatibility, messaging tool integrations, configurable boot services, and FreeBSD jails. Docker support is postponed. A new Angular GUI is included but remains in beta. Testers reportedly found few issues.

JPMorgan Chase reduced its DeVry Education Group position by 9.6% in the third quarter, while UBS, PNC Financial Services, KBC Group, and Retirement Systems of Alabama increased their stakes. DeVry shares traded at $31.20 with a $1.95 billion market cap. The company reported quarterly EPS of $0.39, missing the $0.41 estimate, but revenue of $449.90 million beat expectations, up 1.9% year-over-year. Analysts assign a consensus "Hold" rating with a $26.11 average price target. DeVry pays a semiannual dividend of $0.18, representing a 1.29% yield. The company is a global provider of educational services in healthcare, technology, business, and law.

Ostersunds drew Arsenal in the Europa League last 32, Arsenal's first Swedish tie since 1999-2000. Dortmund, Atletico Madrid, Celtic and Napoli dropped from the Champions League to face Atalanta, Copenhagen, Zenit and RB Leipzig.

This study examines the spatiotemporal evolution of SARS-CoV-2 Alpha and Delta variants during Vietnam's 2021 COVID-19 outbreak. After controlling transmission in 2020, Vietnam reported over 1.7 million infections and 32,000 deaths in 2021 following Alpha and Delta importations. Analysis of 1,303 genome sequences showed Delta (93.8%, predominantly AY.57 lineage) dominated, while Alpha comprised 5.7%. Alpha was introduced via multiple events between January and May but was contained by strict public health measures, resulting in only sporadic clusters. Delta AY.57, with an estimated most recent common ancestor of March 14, 2021, caused an explosive nationwide outbreak from May onward. Phylogeographic analysis indicated the Northeast and Red River Delta initially seeded spread, with the Southeast later seeding the north; strict in-country travel restrictions limited inter-provincial viral dispersal and fostered distinct localized clusters. Genetic diversity increased sharply from April to August 2021 as the virus spread through a largely unvaccinated population. The AY.57 lineage evolved under weak purifying selection with an evolutionary rate of 5.29×10⁻⁴ substitutions per site per year. The findings highlight that while rigorous containment suppressed Alpha, the highly transmissible Delta variant overcame these measures in an immunologically naïve population, underscoring the importance of genomic surveillance to inform pandemic response.

This systematic review, registered on PROSPERO, evaluated human studies on marijuana and cannabinoid effects on the microbiome. Of 4,022 identified articles, nine studies—one case-control, six cohorts, and two clinical trials comprising 2,526 participants—were included. Cannabis use and endocannabinoid supplements were associated with alterations in gut and oral microbiota across conditions including HIV infection, inflammation, obesity, cognitive deficits, and musculoskeletal pain. Key findings included increased *Akkermansia muciniphila* following oleoylethanolamide supplementation in obese participants, positive correlations between AEA and butyrate, and shifts in oral bacteria such as *Streptococcus mutans* and *Lactobacilli*. Reported adverse events included coughing, wheezing, drowsiness, night sweats, and systemic aspergillosis. Due to limited data and diverse pathological conditions, a meta-analysis could not be conducted. The authors conclude that marijuana use and endocannabinoid supplements may interact with gastrointestinal microbiota to contribute to pain manifestation, though further research is necessary.

Patrick Kane, Brent Seabrook, and Bryan Bickell discussed tying their playoff series against Boston and returning to Chicago with home games ahead. Seabrook scored the overtime winner and credited simply putting pucks on net while praising his team’s resilience. Bickell emphasized physical play, finishing checks, and creating space for teammates. Kane praised the team’s depth, highlighted contributions from players like Krüger and Seabrook, and expressed confidence in Crawford despite recent tough breaks. Seabrook said he encouraged Toews to focus on scoring rather than only doing little things right, and told Leddy to keep his head up after a coaching decision. The players acknowledged the series has been unusual with close games and overtimes, stressed the need to improve defensively and play as a five-man unit with speed, and described their game plan against a large opposing defenseman: getting pucks behind him, getting to the net, and finishing checks. They also expressed pride in the franchise’s history and logo.

Cboe CEO Tilly said the smooth launch of bitcoin futures could lead to cryptocurrency options and ETFs, though regulators may take time. The first U.S. traditional exchange to offer them, Cboe saw nearly 3,700 contracts trade by Monday with nearly 20 firms participating. Contracts were volatile, surging 20 percent and triggering a halt, but operations worked. Three fund managers asked the SEC to approve bitcoin ETFs following debut. Cboe will wait for a couple of settlements on one-month contracts before introducing new crypto-derivatives and has appealed an SEC ruling blocking a Cboe-listed bitcoin ETF. Tilly expects futures on other digital currencies to follow.

Chinese textile firms increasingly use North Korean factories and workers to cut labor costs, with garments labeled "Made in China" and exported worldwide, traders in the border city of Dandong told Reuters. UN sanctions targeting North Korea's nuclear and missile programs do not ban textile exports, which totaled $752 million in 2016. Manufacturers save up to 75 percent using North Korean workers, who traders say are more productive but earn significantly less than Chinese workers. Chinese firms also employ North Korean workers in China, though new UN sanctions prohibit increasing their numbers overseas. Much of workers' wages are remitted to the state, helping fund Pyongyang's weapons programs. The practice highlights North Korea's adaptation to sanctions and continued reliance on China.

Glenner Town Square is an 8,500-square-foot 1950s-themed miniature downtown in Chula Vista designed to spark long-term memories in Alzheimer’s and dementia patients; it opened in April 2018 with 13 interactive storefronts. Glenner also owns adult day-care centers in Hillcrest and Encinitas that will eventually be transitioned into Town Square projects. It also catalogs other licensed adult day programs for the cognitively impaired across San Diego County, describing their services, locations, and contact details.

Having reached the finals three times with three different teams, the speaker is determined to win the trophy this time. They credit hard work for the team's success, praise the sold-out games and enthusiastic fans, and expect a tight series against the Flyers, stating that winning is most important.

The speaker reports to Congress that America has improved after a period of decline, citing bipartisan cooperation, reduced inflation and interest rates, across-the-board tax cuts, deregulation, and job growth. The address sets four national goals for the decade: vigorous economic growth through reduced federal spending, deficit reduction, a line-item veto, a balanced budget amendment, and tax code simplification; developing the next frontier by building a permanently manned space station within ten years and preserving the environment; strengthening traditional values through education reform, restoring discipline, combating crime and abortion, and creating enterprise zones; and securing meaningful peace through restored military credibility, alliances, nuclear arms reduction, and diplomatic efforts in Lebanon, Central America, and with the Soviet Union. The speaker urges continued bipartisan progress, warns against tax increases, and honors military and civilian heroes.

This study evaluates a screening-isolation strategy for epidemic control in semi-isolated communities without vaccines or medications using a mathematical model based on SIR/SEIR frameworks. The model incorporates external infection influx, screening efficiency, and time lag. Results indicate that the strategy effectively controls diseases with a basic reproduction number up to 6.0 but fails at 8.0 without additional measures. Successful control requires a time lag below a calculated constraint and screening at least every three days; weekly screening yields significantly worse outcomes, and biweekly screening fails. Higher screening efficiency substantially reduces cumulative infections. Infection size increases proportionally with external influx, necessitating strict border control. The authors conclude that periodic community-wide screening combined with limited migration can effectively limit epidemic spread in semi-isolated communities when pharmaceutical interventions are unavailable.

MultiChoice is losing DStv Premium subscribers to Netflix in South Africa, with numbers dropping by 41,000 and average revenue falling to R344. CEO Calvo Mawela cites Netflix's unfair advantage and plans a standalone streaming service after securing channel rights. MultiChoice urges ICASA not to over-regulate pay-TV, warning of job losses to international streaming giants.

The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate to between 1 and 1.25 percent for the third consecutive quarter, citing strong job growth and moderate economic growth while acknowledging weaker inflation and lowering this year's forecast to 1.6 percent. Some officials predict unemployment could fall below 4 percent.

Ben Rice is a Yankees player born in Cohasset, Massachusetts, who hit 26 home runs in 138 games in 2025 while playing first base, catcher, and designated hitter. Despite growing up near Boston, he was a Yankees fan. Rice attended Dartmouth but had limited college playing time due to COVID-19 before the Yankees drafted him in the 12th round of the 2021 MLB Draft. He is 26 and not a free agent until after 2030. He hit a two-run home run in his 2025 playoff debut against the Red Sox.

Tom Brady's agent Don Yee confirmed he will return to the Patriots in 2018 and play into his mid-40s. Brady has two seasons remaining on his contract worth $14 million plus a $1 million roster bonus annually. Patriots owner Robert Kraft said there is no issue with his current contract.

The speaker refuses to analyze the previous game with the media, stating the team will review it internally. He notes players wanted to move after a long flight and will feel better tomorrow. He asserts the pressure is on Calgary, as the Cup is in the building, all of Canada is watching, and Calgary is expected to win, while Tampa's only focus is extending the series one game at a time. He emphasizes playoff battles over tactical analysis, outlines the team's post-game itinerary to stay Sunday for rest, and praises a Calgary player while stressing the importance of big plays at key moments. He expresses confidence in his team's chances and curiosity about how Calgary will handle elimination-game pressure at home, acknowledging his own team struggled mentally last night by anticipating a potential victory.

Exact diagonalization of a continuum model for approximately 2°-twisted bilayer MoTe₂ at hole filling νₕ = 3 reveals an intermediate intervalley superconducting phase between a ferromagnetic Chern insulator and a non-Abelian fractional spin Hall insulator as the intervalley screening length d is tuned. The superconducting state, stabilized by screened short-range intervalley interactions, displays time-reversal symmetry, extended nodal s-wave pairing, negative binding energy, a dominant eigenvalue in the pair density matrix, and finite superfluid stiffness. The transition to the fractional spin Hall insulator is continuous, with the two ground states adiabatically connected, and is described by an effective Chern-Simons field theory in which topology and symmetry change simultaneously. The study emphasizes that realistic moiré band geometry and non-uniform quantum geometry are crucial for this superconductivity, and suggests that experimentally tuning d via gating or substrate engineering could realize the phase.

Joppatowne High School held its 45th commencement for over 130 graduates at Harford Community College. About 95% of the 138-member class will attend college, technical school, or enter the military or law enforcement. Graduate Amya Hill plans to study nursing at Albany State University, while Zachary Wagmun will pursue an electrician’s apprenticeship at Harford Community College. Valedictorian Kacey Lebrun and class president Breea Stevenson delivered student speeches; Stevenson shared life lessons about comfort zones, separating from negative influences, and focusing on the present. Remarks were also given by local officials, including state Sen. Robert Cassilly, who honored fallen officer Amy Caprio and Sgt. Eddison Hermond.

Over-the-counter (OTC) trading involves direct transactions between two parties outside centralized exchanges, conducted electronically via decentralized networks of market makers and dealers. It facilitates trading in stocks, bonds, derivatives, and commodities, particularly for small companies that do not meet formal exchange requirements, as well as foreign companies through American Depository Receipts (ADRs).

While OTC markets offer flexibility through customized contracts and allow smaller firms to access capital, they are generally less transparent, subject to lighter FINRA regulation, and lack standardized contracts. This results in higher counterparty risk, lower liquidity, higher transaction costs from slippage, and greater susceptibility to fraud and market manipulation, such as pump-and-dump schemes. OTC stocks, especially penny stocks, historically exhibit high failure rates and negative average returns.

Both long-term investment and short-term trading in OTC stocks are considered inadvisable due to poor performance and unfavorable odds. Although cryptocurrency can be traded OTC via exchange desks or peer-to-peer platforms, most crypto trading occurs on public exchanges. Regulated stock exchanges are presented as preferable to OTC markets for investors.

CoreWeave has surged on major AI deal wins and bullish sentiment but faces rising competition, valuation concerns, and revenue concentration risk from Microsoft. Recent $22.4B OpenAI and $14.2B Meta deals diversify its customer base, while aggressive capex and debt-funded growth raise sustainability questions given its high forward revenue multiple. Despite strong momentum, shares may face a cooling-off period as optimism appears fully priced in and risks remain elevated.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Michael Ben’Ary was abruptly fired from the Eastern District of Virginia amid a terrorism prosecution. A letter with his signature claimed a false social media post by pro-Trump commentator Julie Kelly led to his termination; Kelly had linked him to former Biden official Lisa Monaco and resistance to indicting former FBI Director James Comey. The letter warned that Department of Justice leadership is more concerned with punishing the president’s perceived enemies than protecting national security.

OptumCare offers "Brainsaver" classes in the Valley, a 12-week course focusing on brain health through physical exercise, stress reduction, cognitive exercises, education, socialization, and nutrition to help keep Alzheimer's Disease at bay. Classes meet at three locations: Deer Valley on Mondays and Wednesdays, and Goodyear and Chandler on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

A federal government shutdown appeared more likely after President Donald Trump met with congressional leaders on September 29, 2025. Vice President JD Vance said a shutdown is likely because Democrats refuse to cooperate, while Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer cited “very large differences” but noted Trump heard Democratic objections. Republicans want a “clean” continuing resolution to maintain funding until late November, while Democrats demand it include an extension of enhanced Obamacare tax credits due to expire. Both sides blame each other as the deadline nears.

Moina Shaiq launched the "Meet a Muslim" program in Fremont, California, after placing a newspaper ad inviting questions about Islam. Following strong initial attendance, she now holds voluntary sessions across the Bay Area and beyond to educate the public and break down stereotypes regarding topics like the hijab, Sunni-Shia differences, and women's rights. The initiative reflects a resurgence of Muslim outreach programs that emerged after 9/11 and have increased amid recent anti-Muslim crimes and political rhetoric. Though Shaiq has faced threats, she continues to foster understanding. Muslim advocacy groups support such local engagement, while some activists argue the focus should be on policy change rather than individual outreach.

The disclosure relates to methods and devices for sounding reference signal (SRS) transmission and reception in a wireless communication system. A user equipment (UE) receives, from a base station (BS), configuration information including one or more SRS resources and usage information, and performs SRS transmission using those resources. A guard period (Y symbols) related to the SRS resources is configured for antenna switching. When the guard period overlaps with transmission of a specific uplink channel—such as a physical uplink control channel (PUCCH) for channel state information reporting or beam failure recovery, or a physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH)—the priority between the guard period and that uplink channel is configured identically to the priority between the SRS and that channel. The number of guard period symbols is determined based on subcarrier spacing, and configuration information including a starting position index, the number of symbols, and whether the guard period is configured between SRS and an adjacent uplink channel may be provided per SRS resource set via higher layer signaling. If no guard period is configured, the UE may perform uplink transmissions before and after it using the same transmission beam indicated by an SRS resource indicator and/or transmit precoder matrix indicator. The disclosure further describes handling collisions between the guard period and PUSCH/PUCCH by dropping, puncturing, rate matching, or shifting symbols, and addressing collisions between guard periods and SRS resource sets by dropping lower-priority sets or transmitting them in a later slot, thereby enabling efficient uplink transmission and preventing antenna switching distortion.
Turing Tensor Cores accelerate deep learning with INT8 and INT4 modes, bring AI to GeForce and Quadro, and power DLSS for high-quality images from fewer samples.

Zsolt Lakatos, 31, was sentenced to 13 years in prison for violently shaking his four-month-old son, causing catastrophic brain injuries. He failed to appear for the end of his trial on February 6 and was arrested eight days later in Litherland. At Liverpool Crown Court, he admitted breaching bail and received an additional 10 days, stating he had panicked at the prospect of imprisonment. The child, now 22 months old and in foster care, requires lifelong nursing care. Lakatos admitted shaking the baby twice but denied intending serious harm, claiming the second incident occurred out of frustration. He has a previous conviction for assaulting a partner.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated January 3, 2016, furnishing a press release under Items 2.02 and 7.01 as Exhibit 99.1, not deemed "filed" under Section 18 of the Exchange Act. General Counsel Todd A. Maron signed the report on January 4, 2016.

Coach Quenneville reflects on his years with the Blackhawks, citing familiarity with the core group, their all-out commitment, and consistent leadership. He describes his coaching approach as challenging players while maintaining open communication and accountability. Regarding goaltending, he clarifies that rotating Corey and Scottie provided opportunity rather than benching, highlighting healthy competition and Corey’s solid return. He notes line adjustments, improved play and timely goals from advancing players, and trust earned through defensive reliability and recent performance. He stresses treating every game as a must-win, praises players for developing a shot mentality and imaginative play under pressure, and acknowledges that controlling matchups against defensive pairings is especially difficult on the road.

Cover 0 is a man-to-man defense with no deep safeties helping underneath defenders, designed to bring maximum blitz pressure—typically six players to the line of scrimmage—while covering all eligible receivers. Its strengths include simple, concrete assignments, easy adjustment to motion, effectiveness against the run and Run-Pass Options, and success against short, quick, and long passing routes due to heavy pressure. It can also be disguised pre-snap. Weaknesses include vulnerability to deep routes if a defender is beaten with no help over the top, draw plays, quarterback scrambles, pick plays, and an open middle of the field. General rules assign defensive backs to man coverage on receivers and tight ends, while linebackers blitz. Variations include Cover 0 "Rat," where one linebacker drops to defend crossing routes and QB runs while five rush, and schemes where a hybrid defensive lineman drops into coverage on a running back.

This article examines holistic education within Indian higher education, tracing its conceptual roots to the Latin terms *educere* and *educare* and to Indian sages—Tagore, Osho, Vivekananda, and Sri Aurobindo—who advocated the integrated development of mind, matter, and spirit. It contrasts these philosophies with contemporary materialist education and aligns them with modern policies including India’s NEP 2020, UN SDG 4.7, and the ISEE Assessment. Employing a twofold methodology comprising a comprehensive review and a PRISMA-guided systematic literature review of Scopus and Semantic Scholar, the researchers screened 472 pre-2021 English articles to finalize eight for qualitative thematic analysis. The study validates the LIBRE/EMC² framework—encompassing empathy, mindfulness, compassion, and critical inquiry—as core dimensions of holistic education. Foundational themes emphasize whole-person development, holistic pedagogy, active and critical learning, competency-based approaches, institutional clarity, and lifelong global citizenship. The four dimensions are substantiated through the literature: empathy through interpersonal sensitivity and cultural awareness; critical inquiry through analytical thinking and reflective practice; mindfulness through self-awareness, emotional regulation, and spiritual attunement; and compassion through caring, integrity, and social responsibility. The discussion links these dimensions to Indian philosophical ideals and proposes classroom-level assessment feedback loops to inform institutional policy. The authors conclude that the LIBRE/EMC² model offers a culturally grounded foundation for curriculum design and evaluation, while acknowledging limited database coverage and calling for future development of culturally sensitive assessment instruments.

University of Maryland researchers found sustained energy drink consumption among 1,099 students increased risk of cocaine use, non-medical prescription stimulant use, and alcohol use disorder by age 25. Over half (51.4%) maintained consumption; 17.4% had intermediate use, both at higher risk than 20.6% non-users. Those with declining use were not at higher risk.

Consumer advocates reported glitches in the final days of Affordable Care Act enrollment, including incorrect messages telling some applicants no plans were available in their area. Friday is the deadline for 39 states using HealthCare.gov, though the administration cut the sign-up period to 45 days. The administration claims the issue is resolved and is contacting affected consumers, but advocates say the problem persisted. People in hurricane-affected areas can enroll through Dec. 31. Despite sharp premium increases, higher subsidies mean many eligible for financial help may pay less in 2018, with some bronze plans available at no premium. States running their own exchanges, including California and New York, have extended deadlines through January.

President Woodrow Wilson’s April 6, 1917 proclamation declares that a state of war exists between the United States and the Imperial German Government under a Congressional joint resolution and Sections 4067–4070 of the Revised Statutes. It directs all United States officers to exercise vigilance and appeals to American citizens to uphold the law. The proclamation establishes regulations for male German alien enemies aged fourteen and older within the United States who are not naturalized, requiring them to preserve the peace, refrain from hostility, and comply with presidential regulations. Law-abiding alien enemies may continue their occupations undisturbed, but are subject to restrictions including prohibitions on possessing weapons, explosives, aircraft, wireless apparatus, or ciphers; approaching military installations; attacking the government or its personnel; aiding enemies; residing in prohibited areas; or entering or leaving the United States without permits. Violators face property seizure, summary arrest, confinement, restraint, or removal. The proclamation applies to all land and water under United States jurisdiction.

The Nationals signed Jeremy Hellickson to compete with A.J. Cole and Erick Fedde for the fifth starter spot, though it may extend past opening day. Hellickson might stay behind to build arm strength, while Cole will make the team as starter or reliever. Dave Martinez named Max Scherzer opening day starter, followed by Strasburg, Gonzalez, and Roark; Fedde likely heads to the minors. Hellickson struggled with Baltimore last season, but the Nationals identified delivery fixes. Trea Turner left camp Monday for an ingrown toenail and could return Tuesday.

The November 14, 2000 issue of VentureWire, published by Technologic Partners, reports private company business news. Top stories include Apax Partners merging its European and Israeli units and pledging $600 million in Israeli investments; New Edge Networks laying off 135 employees; KSolutions receiving a $50 million first funding round; and Cisco Systems acquiring Radiata for $295 million. The issue also covers numerous venture capital funding rounds, including $80 million for PhotonEx, $50 million for StorageApps, $40 million each for Blaze and Equator, and smaller rounds for companies such as SmartEnergy, Cablesoft, and Nitronex. Bad news includes executive departures at Buzz MSP, the closure of eSociety, and layoffs at iExplore. The newsletter details several mergers and acquisitions, such as iKnowMed acquiring CancerSource.com and USBX acquiring BizQuest, along with company name changes, a new product launch by Venture Studio, multiple board and executive appointments, venture capital firm personnel changes, and corrections to previous stories.

In *The People v. John Ortiz* (1924), the defendant appealed his simple assault conviction for breaking into his home and cutting Albert Donaso with a pocket-knife during a struggle. The defendant claimed self-defense, testifying that he drew and opened his pocket-knife only after Donaso rushed at him with a knife. The appellate court affirmed the judgment, ruling that the district attorney properly asked the defendant to demonstrate retrieving and opening the knife during cross-examination to test his account. The court also held that evidence regarding alleged threatening letters was a collateral issue, and its exclusion did not warrant reversal because the central question for the jury was whether the stabbing was in self-defense.

NVIDIA's Blackwell architecture introduces neural shaders that integrate AI into the graphics rendering pipeline, enabling Tensor Core access through any shader type via the new Cooperative Vectors API for DX12 and Vulkan. Ray Reconstruction (RR) uses transformer models to enhance image quality in ray-traced scenes and reduce common denoising artifacts, while Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing (DLAA) applies AI-based anti-aliasing at native resolution for improved temporal stability and detail. Key neural shader technologies include RTX Neural Materials for film-quality rendering, RTX Neural Texture Compression reducing VRAM usage by over 3×, Neural Radiance Cache (NRC) for approximating complex indirect lighting, RTX Skin for real-time subsurface scattering, and RTX Neural Faces using generative AI to infer more natural-looking faces. The architecture spans multiple GPUs: the flagship GB202 powers the GeForce RTX 5090 with 92.2 billion transistors, 24,576 CUDA cores, and a 512-bit memory interface; the high-end GB203 powers the RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti with 45.6 billion transistors, 10,752 CUDA cores, and a 256-bit interface; and the performance-segment GB205 powers the RTX 5070 with 31 billion transistors, 6,400 CUDA cores, and a 192-bit interface.

Soybean futures rose on diminishing supplies and intact demand. Apr 1-15 arrivals: 97,040 tonnes vs 1,64,286 in Mar. Prices expected higher; Ref Soy oil and CPO may rise, but imports may pressure prices further.

In *Juan Archibeque v. Jose Maria Miera*, the court affirmed a district court judgment for the defendant. It held that under the organic act, only the supreme court has appellate jurisdiction, and district courts hearing appeals from justices of the peace act as courts of original jurisdiction, trying cases *de novo* without regard to prior proceedings. The transcript from the justice’s court serves only to verify that the case originated there, was decided, and was properly appealed. The court further held that weighing testimony discrepancies is the jury’s province, and motions for a new trial based on a verdict against the evidence are discretionary, to be granted only if the verdict is clearly against the weight of evidence. Here, testimony differed regarding the number of cattle, the timing of the incident, and the presence of fresh tracks from multiple animals in a wet field, leaving it to the jury to determine whether the defendant’s cattle caused the wheat damage. Finding no clear preponderance of evidence against the verdict, the court affirmed the judgment.

Astronomers say Oumuamua, the first known interstellar visitor, likely came from a binary star system. Discovered in October by a Hawaiian observatory, the 1,300-foot asteroid is traveling away from Earth at over 16 miles per second. Researchers believe it was ejected during planet formation and is tumbling through space after a collision knocked it from its home system, and will tumble for billions of years. Originally thought to be a comet, it is now classified as an asteroid. Researchers suggest binary star systems may produce most interstellar objects.

Tesla announced the $36,990 Model 3 Standard and $39,990 Model Y Standard, budget variants lacking Autosteer, LED lightbars, and FM/AM radio. Buyers save $5,500 and $5,000 over premium versions. Tesla stock fell as investors wanted lower prices. The Model Y Standard arrives November–December and the Model 3 Standard December–January. After the federal $7,500 EV tax credit ended, New York incentives may cut prices by $2,000. Musk, who once teased a $25,000 EV, recently called the endeavor "pointless."

This study used machine learning to predict depressive symptom severity (DSS) from sleep quality, anxiety, and brain gray matter volume (GMV) in the HCP-Young cohort, validating models out-of-cohort in HCP-Aging and eNKI datasets and assessing longitudinal prediction in eNKI. Sleep quality robustly predicted DSS across all three independent cohorts. Adding anxiety scores improved prediction, and anxiety mediated the link between sleep quality and DSS. GMV and functional brain measures did not predict DSS or improve model performance. The reverse prediction of sleep quality from depressive symptoms was weaker. Longitudinal analyses showed baseline sleep and anxiety predicted future DSS, except in participants who received neurofeedback between visits. The authors conclude that poor sleep and anxiety are robust individual-level predictors of depressive symptoms, whereas structural and functional brain features did not play an important predictive or mediatory role.

Chapter I covers January 1–March 8, 1945, documenting United States consultations with the United Kingdom, the Soviet Union, China, and France on questions not settled at Dumbarton Oaks and decisions taken at the Yalta Conference. It includes consideration of views on the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals submitted by the American Republics, other Governments, members of the United States Congress, and the general public, and the extension of Conference invitations to Governments of 39 United Nations. The chapter contains telegrams and radiograms between Washington and various foreign capitals. Document 1 describes a December 29 meeting where the Secretary of State and Heads of Mission of American Republics discussed memoranda regarding Dumbarton Oaks proposals submitted by nine governments and progress toward a Conference of American Republics associated in the war.

The Base Cross Offense is a basketball strategy designed to isolate low post players by using smaller perimeter players to set baseline screens for bigger posts, creating size mismatches. The core action begins with a point guard entry pass to a wing, followed by a give-and-go cut; if not open, the guard sets a baseline screen for the post player, who comes off the screen for a shot or strong post-up. Variations include pass, dribble, UCLA, and Hawk entries. Success depends on precise execution of screens and reads based on defensive positioning, with specific counters for defenders who trail, switch, front, or overplay. If the initial post option is unavailable, the offense flows into ball reversal and weakside down, mid, or side screens. Teaching the offense requires a focus on fundamental post moves, screening, and coordinated team execution through breakdown drills and scrimmaging. Game strategies include scouting opponents, varying alignments and entries, and attacking weak defenders. Even teams that do not run the offense must be prepared to defend against it.

The passage contends that the Carter administration suffered major strategic setbacks in Iran and Nicaragua by facilitating the replacement of U.S.-friendly moderate autocrats with hostile extremists, while failing to address similar risks elsewhere. It argues that this failure stemmed from an unrealistic, intellectually fashionable preference for leftist challenges over rightist autocracies. The author, Kirkpatrick, asserts that traditional authoritarian regimes are less repressive, more amenable to liberalization, and more compatible with U.S. interests than revolutionary autocracies, citing Vietnam, Cambodia, China, Taiwan, and Korea as evidence. Traditional autocrats tolerate existing inequities without creating refugees, whereas revolutionary autocracies create systemic brutality and poverty.

Des Moines Public Schools Superintendent Ian Roberts resigned effective immediately after ICE arrested him during a targeted enforcement operation. Born in Guyana, Roberts allegedly evaded arrest; ICE stated he was in the U.S. unlawfully since entering in 1999 on a student visa and had a final removal order from May 2024. His attorney, Alfredo Parrish, said Roberts believed his immigration case had been closed successfully and is filing a motion to reopen it. Roberts is currently held at Woodbury County Jail. The arrest raised questions about the district’s hiring vetting process, though officials said Roberts completed an I-9 form. The school board had planned to meet to discuss ending his contract before he resigned.

Devanna Cornitcher, 25, was stabbed to death in Chester, Pennsylvania. Boyfriend Alonzo Carter, 25, was arrested after her daughter witnessed the killing. Carter allegedly confessed, claiming self-defense. Both children were present. Carter was denied bail.

The NHS Patient Charter (Constitution) sets out patients' legal rights, NHS pledges, and patient responsibilities. Rights include care free at the point of use, with exceptions such as prescriptions in England, dentistry and eye care; equal access regardless of age, disability, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender reassignment, pregnancy, or marital status; waiting time standards with alternatives if unmet; safe settings with qualified staff; access to NICE-recommended treatments; fair local decisions; routine vaccinations; consent; privacy; choice of GP; involvement in decisions including end-of-life care; a duty of candour if something goes wrong; and the right to complain, seek judicial review, and receive compensation for negligence. Responsibilities include looking after your own health, treating staff and patients with respect, following treatment plans or discussing difficulties, and taking part in vaccination and screening programmes. The Charter is presented as a tool for empowerment and accountability, stressing that the NHS is a partnership based on shared responsibility, especially during times of strain.

A study found that expensive-looking fake creams produced stronger nocebo effects than cheaper-looking ones. Participants told the creams increased pain sensitivity reported nearly 30 percent more pain with the expensive cream versus about 3 percent with the generic. fMRI scans showed corresponding changes in neural pain pathway activity. Researchers suggest medical professionals could minimize nocebo effects by considering how they discuss medication prices with patients.

Speakers said early powerplay and penalty kill are difficult when not warmed up, credited home crowd as a season strength, acknowledged opponent's talent and scoring, cited frustration with effort and play, and expect to turn things around in two home games.

In soccer, "goal side" positioning places defenders between their goal and opponents. Youth are taught to "get in their way" or keep opponents in front of them. Defenders move out from the goal, adjust to opponent movement, and sprint past opponents to turn into position. Training progresses from half-speed drills without a ball to full-speed play. Coaches should provide one-on-one instruction, using analogies from basketball and football while noting that blocking or extending arms is illegal.

U.S. markets shifted to a risk-off tone last week, recording a bearish engulfing pattern amid a flood of clouded market-moving events. GDP grew 3%, beating expectations, but data remained distorted by tariff policies that skewed trade deficits and masked underlying demand softness, including low personal spending. The FOMC meeting saw two dissenting votes for the first time since the 1990s, while Chair Powell maintained a patient, data-dependent stance citing uncertain impacts of tariffs and immigration policies on inflation and labor force structure. The nonfarm payrolls report showed only 73,000 jobs added versus 100,000 expected, with the largest two-month downward revision on record since 1979 excluding the pandemic; the unemployment rate rose to 4.2%. President Trump fired the Bureau of Labor Statistics commissioner after the report, announced nuclear submarine deployments toward Russia, and advanced tariff negotiations, while Fed Governor Adriana Kugler announced an early resignation. Despite strong Q2 earnings—82% of S&P 500 companies beat EPS estimates and 79% beat revenue estimates, with earnings revision ratios hitting multi-month highs—markets sold into the news due to elevated doubts about economic growth and a lack of new buyers. Interest rate markets priced in over 75% odds of a September Fed rate cut and three cuts by January, with bond ETFs breaking above key resistance levels. Market internals deteriorated, with all sectors except Utilities declining, transports and retail entering a distribution phase, and volatility confirming a shift to risk-off conditions.

NVIDIA Corporation's fiscal year 2018 Form 10-K annual report covers the period ended January 28, 2018. The Santa Clara, California-based company operates a fabless manufacturing business with two reportable segments, GPU and Tegra Processor, serving the Gaming, Professional Visualization, Datacenter, and Automotive markets. Its unified platform strategy leverages GPUs and CUDA, with product brands including GeForce, Quadro, Tesla, DGX, GRID, and Tegra-based DRIVE and SHIELD. Manufacturing is outsourced to suppliers including Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company and Samsung Electronics. As of January 28, 2018, NVIDIA had 11,528 employees, including 8,191 in research and development, and held $7.11 billion in cash and marketable securities. FY2018 research and development expenses were $1.80 billion. Revenue from sales outside the United States and Other Americas accounted for 79% of total revenue. The report outlines risks such as rapid technological change, intense competition from companies including AMD and Intel, dependence on third-party manufacturers and assemblers, cybersecurity breaches, product defects, and international operational uncertainties. NVIDIA's common stock trades on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under the symbol NVDA. In November 2017, the company increased its quarterly cash dividend to $0.15 per share. As of January 28, 2018, it had repurchased 251 million shares for $5.5 billion under its share repurchase program and was authorized to repurchase up to an additional $1.82 billion through December 2020, with an intent to return $1.25 billion to shareholders in fiscal year 2019.

A suspect led a two-hour police chase through Kansas and Missouri, crashing in Savannah after police used a spike strip. Officers found drugs and weapons and hospitalized him for suspected methamphetamine ingestion.

The Alabama Court of Civil Appeals denied James F. Robertson III’s petition for a writ of mandamus to compel a default judgment in his divorce from Cynthia D. Robertson. Robertson, an inmate acting pro se, published notice of the divorce after he could not locate his wife, but he did not file the proof-of-publication affidavit required by Rule 4.3(d)(5), Ala. R. Civ. P. The trial court denied his default-judgment motions for that reason. Because mandamus requires a clear legal right to the order sought, the court denied the petition.

In a reappraisement appeal of fishing equipment at Seattle, the defendant conceded packing charges of 50 yen and 4 yen were dutiable. The Government's challenge to a 26.557 yen deduction lacked evidence. The court found the value to be the appraised value less shipping, consular fees, insurance, petties, and the 26.557 yen deduction.

BSE Sensex rose 270 points to 29,683.87 and Nifty reached 9,214.15. Metal, energy, FMCG, and banking stocks gained, while TCS traded flat. Asian stocks recovered after US comments on the dollar, but North Korea tensions limited gains. The rupee was at 64.40 per dollar.

In *Pacific Gamble Robinson Co. v. Lapp*, the Washington Supreme Court reversed the lower courts' dismissal of a creditor's claim against the Lapp marital community. Conrad Lapp signed a promissory note in Colorado for a debt owed to Pacific Gamble Robinson Co. by his Colorado corporation, without his wife's signature. After defaulting in 1977, the Lapps moved to Washington. The Court held that Colorado law applied to the debt under the "most significant relationship" test because the contract was made, negotiated, and intended for performance in Colorado while the Lapps were domiciled there. Under Colorado law, a husband's earnings and property are subject to his separate debts, so Mr. Lapp's earnings—characterized as community property in Washington—could be reached to satisfy the debt. Justice Horowitz dissented, contending that Washington law should govern the source of funds available to satisfy the judgment; under Washington community property law, a separate debt incurred for a husband's noncommunity business cannot be collected from community property, and the majority improperly subjected Washington domiciliaries' community assets to an out-of-state creditor.

The WMCC vocational class built cabinets and countertops for the Kidder United Methodist Church kitchen. The church, city of Kidder, and Caldwell County Emergency Management are partnering to establish the church as a disaster relief center. The church paid for materials while the prison provided offender labor. The project provided real-world experience for offenders, who typically dismantle class projects, and benefited the community.

Cryptocurrency trading involves exchanging digital assets like Bitcoin and Ethereum for profit using various strategies, including day trading, swing trading, trend following, arbitrage, range trading, and sentiment analysis. Unlike traditional stocks, cryptocurrencies are purely digital, decentralized, and facilitate peer-to-peer exchanges without intermediaries while concealing user identities. Prices are influenced by market demand, investor sentiment, regulation, technology, and macroeconomic trends. Trading fees vary by platform and may include maker/taker, deposit/withdrawal, and spread costs. Risks include extreme volatility, scams, cybercrime, lost private keys, and lack of centralized regulation. Halving events reduce mining rewards by half, potentially increasing scarcity and prices. Hard forks split blockchains into separate chains, creating new coins and market volatility. Decentralized finance projects enable direct peer-to-peer trading without intermediaries, potentially lowering costs. Tether (USDT) provides a stable hedge against volatility, though its peg could fail and destabilize markets. Backtesting from late 2014 showed a Bitcoin strategy with an 87% annual return and 42% win rate, and the text indicates trend following has historically outperformed mean reversion. The article recommends selecting strategies based on individual goals and risk tolerance and emphasizes backtesting before committing capital.

This MIT OpenCourseWare transcript records a panel discussion on financing sources for entrepreneurs, part of a course covering business plans, pitching, customer discovery, business models, and financial projections. The professor introduces panelists Axel Bichara, Julianne Zimmerman, and Amir Nashat, who represent venture capital, angel investing, and seed-stage funding.

The discussion addresses diverse funding sources, including venture capital, angel and friends-and-family investment, customer revenue, government grants such as SBIR, crowdfunding, credit cards, and business plan competitions. Panelists emphasize selecting capital appropriate to the company’s stage, market potential, and goals, noting that only a minority of successful companies require venture funding.

Bichara describes his experience as a venture capitalist, angel investor, and co-founder of the hardware accelerator Bolt, which provides intensive hands-on product and team development. Zimmerman, a former entrepreneur and founder of seed-stage firm Vodia Ventures, stresses that every capital type has distinct uses, benefits, and costs, and that alignment of interests between founders and investors is essential. Nashat, a managing partner at Polaris, outlines his firm’s traditional early-stage VC focus on backing strong entrepreneurs.

The panel explains convertible notes as short-term debt that converts to equity under specified conditions, offering a quick, inexpensive interim instrument but carrying risks if overused or if the company fails. They contrast this with equity financing, where interests are more directly aligned.

Additional topics include evaluating incubators and accelerators based on their level of hands-on support and peer environment; the necessity of reference-checking potential investors; the risks of strategic investors whose corporate priorities may conflict with the startup’s long-term interests; and the operational difficulties created by numerous small investors with unanimous voting rights. The panelists advise entrepreneurs to address their largest risks with minimal capital early, to pursue warm introductions rather than cold submissions, and to ensure that all stakeholders share a common definition of success.

The paper proposes Flow Matching for Corrected Posterior Estimation (FMCPE) to address model misspecification in Simulation-Based Inference (SBI). When simulators are imperfect, standard neural posterior estimation yields biased or overconfident posteriors. FMCPE corrects these estimators by learning two complementary flow matching transport maps using a small set of high-fidelity calibration parameter-observation pairs alongside abundant low-fidelity simulations. The first map couples real observations with surrogate simulator outputs, while the second refines the simulation-based posterior toward the true posterior. The method jointly trains the vector fields, enabling robust correction without requiring explicit knowledge of the misspecification form or relying on conditional independence assumptions. Experiments on Gaussian, Pendulum, WindTunnel, and LightTunnel tasks demonstrate that FMCPE consistently outperforms NPE and MFNPE baselines, particularly with limited calibration data, as measured by jC2ST, Wasserstein distance, and mean squared error. The approach is computationally efficient, amortized, and applicable as post-processing to any SBI model.

The Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00 defines the SD memory card physical interface, including the Mc-EX extension. It specifies three capacity types: SDSC (up to 2 GB), SDHC (>2 GB to 32 GB), and SDXC (>32 GB to 2 TB). Operating voltages include High Voltage (2.7–3.6 V), UHS-II (VDD1: 2.7–3.6 V, VDD2: 1.70–1.95 V), and Low Voltage Signaling. Cards are categorized as Read/Write or Read Only Memory (ROM). Bus speed modes encompass Default Speed, High Speed, UHS-I modes (SDR12, SDR25, SDR50, SDR104, DDR50), and UHS-II modes (FD156, HD312, FD312, FD624), with UHS-II supporting up to 6.24 Gbps per lane. Form factors include Standard Size, miniSD, and microSD. Communication uses command and response tokens on the CMD line and block-oriented data transfer on DAT lines with CRC protection, supporting 1-bit and 4-bit widths. Key registers include CID, RCA, CSD, SCR, OCR, SSR, and CSR. Initialization proceeds through card identification (CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41) to data transfer mode, with UHS-I requiring a 1.8 V voltage switch sequence (CMD11) and tuning (CMD19), and UHS-II requiring PHY initialization and SD-TRAN emulation. The specification defines write protection via mechanical switches, internal settings, and password lock/unlock commands (CMD42), along with Card Ownership Protection (COP) using Force Erase Password (FEP). Erase operations include ERASE, DISCARD, and FULE. Performance is classified by Speed Class and Application Performance Class, with additional features including Command Queue, Cache, Self Maintenance, and Low Voltage Interface support.
St. Louis Court of Appeals affirmed circuit court judgment in Century Realty v. Travelers Insurance based on same facts and principles as prior case.

Apple offers free battery replacements for 13-inch MacBook Pros without Touch Bar built October 2016–October 2017 due to swelling. Owners can check eligibility on Apple Support with the serial number.

Items include South Carolina's 2018 governor race, Joe Wilson's office move, archivists seeking $200,000, a $38 million port sale, Charleston cardiac care, Tecklenburg's first year, and new state laws.

DS-STAR is a novel autonomous data science agent that leverages large language models to solve complex tasks across heterogeneous data formats, including JSON, Markdown, and unstructured text. The framework first employs an analyzer agent to automatically generate descriptions of input data files. It then iteratively generates and refines solution plans through a core loop involving a planner agent, a coder agent, an LLM-based verifier agent that judges plan sufficiency, and a router agent that decides whether to append new steps or backtrack to remove erroneous ones. Additional modules include a debugging agent and a retriever for handling large-scale data lakes. Evaluated on the DABStep, KramaBench, and DA-Code benchmarks, DS-STAR significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on data analysis, machine learning, visualization, and data wrangling tasks. Ablation studies demonstrate that both the analyzer and router agents are critical components, and hard-level tasks require more refinement iterations than easy tasks. The authors identify human-in-the-loop integration as a key direction for future work.

"Sell the rip" is a trading strategy where investors sell an asset—closing a long position or opening a short—when its price is considered overvalued, based on mean reversion principles. It focuses on selling before a market correction and is typically used by short-term traders for short-selling stocks with weak fundamentals overpriced by market sentiment; it is generally unsuitable for long-term investments or assets with strong growth potential. The strategy is one half of "buy the dip, sell the rip" and is technically similar to "sell the rally," though a "rip" specifically indicates an overbought, overvalued condition. Traders commonly use oscillating indicators such as RSI, Stochastic, Williams %R, IBS, Bollinger Bands, and moving averages. A backtest on the S&P 500 (SPY) using a 3-day RSI strategy showed a 75% win rate and 1.6 profit factor, but large drawdowns. Tightening exit criteria to sell sooner on smaller, more frequent rips reduced drawdowns and improved the equity curve, though average gains per trade fell to 0.48%. The approach has performed well on the S&P 500 in recent decades but is less effective in trend-following markets like commodities.

The passage argues that despite technological advances including AI, modern education remains anchored by prescribed curriculum inherited from the Prussian model, leaving minimal room for student autonomy. While AI promises personalized learning, implementing it requires reducing state curriculum control so students can self-determine their learning. The curriculum reflects societal will and functions as the system's anchor, connecting policies, teaching methods, assessments, and standards. Over 200 years, reforms have strengthened prescription through standardized testing, age-based grouping, and accountability, creating a mindset that all students must learn identical content. This creates a conflict: curriculum reflects current societal needs but may become irrelevant by graduation, yet students lack autonomy to explore beyond mandated content.

The authors propose a "balanced curriculum" where part remains system-controlled while part grants students autonomy, with proportions varying by age, experience, and support. Drawing on panarchy theory, they describe education as a hierarchical, multi-layered system with adaptive cycles (growth, conservation, release, reorganization). The system exhibits resilience and adaptability by absorbing innovations that reinforce existing structures while rejecting transformational changes that threaten curriculum control. Categorized by impact, tiny, small, and large innovations strengthen the system, whereas transformational innovations granting significant student autonomy are marginalized.

The authors argue transformation must begin with small subsystems within existing schools rather than whole-school reforms. These autonomous environments allow personalized, product-oriented learning with teachers as facilitators. If successful, subsystems can spread upward through the hierarchy. Examples include Chongqing's ICEE program and Australian initiatives (Studio School, ScotsX), which began as small programs or school-within-a-school models and gradually expanded, demonstrating a pathway for systemic transformation.

The passage provides a chronological list of major public statements of American foreign policy from January through December 1945, identifying each speaker—President Roosevelt, President Truman, Under Secretary Grew, Secretaries Stettinius and Byrnes, and adviser Cordell Hull—along with dates, topics, and publication sources. The statements address the Yalta, San Francisco, and Potsdam conferences; the founding of the United Nations; the surrenders of Germany and Japan; the use of atomic weapons; atomic energy policy; and relations with China, and were published primarily in the Department of State Bulletin and Public Papers of the Presidents.

The speaker praises the defense, crediting Yannick Weber and Matt Irwin alongside the top four for handling tough minutes against teams with two top centermen. The ADS868xW supports four legacy SPI-compatible protocols (SPI-00-S, SPI-01-S, SPI-10-S, SPI-11-S) for device configuration and data transfer, defaulting to SPI-00-S on power-up, with protocol selection set via the SDI_MODE[1:0] bits in the SDI_CTL_REG register; write operations require at least 32 SCLKs. Read protocols include legacy SPI with single or dual SDO-x, and source-synchronous (SRC) modes; single SDO is selected by SDO_MODE[1:0] = 00b, dual SDO by SDO1_CONFIG[1:0] = 11b in the SDO_CTL_REG, and SRC uses the RVS pin as a synchronous output clock with clock source selected by the SSYNC_CLK bit. The device contains nine configuration registers, including DEVICE_ID_REG, RST_PWRCTL_REG (write-protected and requiring 69h written to address 05h for access), SDI_CTL_REG, SDO_CTL_REG, DATAOUT_CTL_REG, RANGE_SEL_REG, and alarm threshold registers. As a 16-bit SAR ADC with an integrated analog front-end and reference, it is designed for industrial data acquisition up to ±10V, settles to 1% accuracy in under 5µs, and offers programmable input and AVDD alarms with hysteresis. It operates with separate AVDD and DVDD supplies that require decoupling capacitors, and provides NAP and power-down modes via the RST_PWRCTL_REG. Layout guidelines recommend isolating analog and digital signals and placing bypass capacitors close to supply pins without vias. In the latest revision, the ADS8685W and ADS8689W changed from Advance Information to Production Data.

Arthur James Balfour states that the Central Powers employ brutal methods to terrorize neutrals; that durable peace requires Allied success, removal of international unrest, discrediting of Central Powers' aggressive methods among their own peoples, and international sanctions; and that the country is making great sacrifices believing Allied victory is necessary for peaceful civilization and reform. The Martingale trading strategy involves doubling trade size after each losing trade to recover all previous losses and achieve a net profit equal to the initial bet. Originating in 18th-century gambling from French mathematician Paul Pierre Levy, it relies on the theory of mean reversion and statistical outcomes with 50% probability. Unlike the anti-Martingale system, which reduces bets after losses, or averaging down, which is a planned entry method, the Martingale strategy aggressively increases risk exposure to avoid accepting losses. While it theoretically offers a near-100% win rate given infinite capital, a sustained losing streak can cause devastating drawdowns or total loss of capital, especially since individual stocks can fall to zero. The strategy may be less dangerous when applied long-only to broad market index ETFs such as SPY, IVV, or VOO, or in forex trades with positive carry interest. A backtest example applying a Martingale position-sizing method to SPY based on RSI levels produced undesirable results compared to a benchmark strategy. The authors do not recommend using the Martingale method for trading and instead advocate for diversified, uncorrelated, data-driven strategies to reduce risk.

Rev. Brian Sietsema handled pronouncer duties for two groups of spellers—about 180 children—at the Scripps National Spelling Bee on Wednesday, marking the first time in 15 years that longtime pronouncer Jacques Bailly took breaks to preserve his voice during an expanded bee. Sietsema, a Greek Orthodox priest and former Merriam-Webster pronunciation editor, stepped in as the bee nearly doubled in size. More than 500 spellers competed in preliminary rounds, with 41 advancing to the semifinals based on a written test. Among the notable spellers were 13-year-old Rebekah Zeigler, who advanced past Round 3 for the first time; Reagan Remmers, who was reinstated after judges determined her misspelling of "balaclava" matched a Ukrainian city name; and 14-year-old Alaskan Daniel Doudna, who spells deliberately after past mistakes.

A New York Times survey of federal judges found dozens expressing concern about the Supreme Court’s emergency docket decisions in cases related to President Trump since his second term. Only 12 of 65 respondents said the docket was used appropriately, and only 12 said lower courts had sufficient guidance. Anonymous judges called the orders demoralizing, while a Trump appointee praised them. Critics argued the survey may overrepresent dissatisfied judges, and many orders lacked reasoning while benefiting Trump.

Scientists at Children's Hospital Oakland Research Institute found adding half a litre of water to breakfast promoted weight loss in 173 women aged 25 to 50. Other studies indicate drinking half a litre of water burns an extra 23 calories. While low-carb, high-protein diets aid weight loss by increasing satiety, gorging on steaks and bacon is not the best method.

Susan R. Koff examines the integration of dance education and social studies education within United States formal schooling. International testing regimes such as PISA and NAEP exclude arts education and emphasize reading, mathematics, and science, which narrows curricular focus and discourages interdisciplinary approaches. Social studies, defined by the National Council for the Social Studies as the integrated study of social sciences and humanities to promote civic competence, is not tested in PISA. A survey of 91 graduates of US dance education programmes found that most incorporate social studies concepts into their teaching: 94% reported attention to people, places, and environments; 97% reported a focus on individual development and identity; and majorities covered culture, time/continuity/change, individuals/groups/institutions, and global connections. Fewer respondents addressed power, authority, and governance (44%) and civic ideals and practices (44%). Open-ended responses indicated that teachers interpreted these concepts either literally, such as by teaching specific cultural dance forms and their geographic origins, or implicitly, such as by using classroom dynamics to mirror civic society and governance. The study concludes that although commonalities between dance and social studies exist, dance educators often work in isolation with limited guidance, and prescriptive curricula may obscure implicit interdisciplinary connections. The author suggests overhauling dance curricula, increasing professional development, and aligning educational policy with the UNESCO Framework for Culture and Arts Education to support holistic, integrated education. The research was limited by a US-only subject pool and restricted survey questions imposed by the Institutional Review Board.

The Yankees and Red Sox will play a best-of-three AL Wild Card series in New York beginning September 30. Boston is the No. 5 seed after trading Rafael Devers, while New York is the No. 4 seed despite the AL's second-best record, as the Blue Jays won the division via tiebreaker. The series airs on ESPN and streams on the ESPN app. It is the sixth postseason meeting, with Boston leading 3-2.

The Colorado Prescription Drug Affordability Board voted to set a first-in-the-nation payment limit on Amgen’s arthritis drug Enbrel for state government agencies and commercial health plans. The ceiling is $600 per unit, or about $30,350 annually per person, down from roughly $53,000 paid in 2023. The limit matches a Medicare maximum fair price taking effect in January and may prompt other states to pursue similar strategies.

Astronomer Hector Socas-Navarro proposes detecting alien civilizations by searching for massive swarms of geostationary satellites around exoplanets. Unlike radio or laser searches, this method does not require synchronicity between sender and receiver. These satellite belts, or "Clarke exobelts," could be detected during planetary transits when they cause slight additional starlight dimming. The approach uses existing exoplanet data and requires no new telescopes. Even extinct civilizations might leave detectable satellites. SETI astronomer Seth Shostak calls the idea clever and easy to attempt, though its success is uncertain.

The Miami Dolphins defeated the New York Jets on Monday Night Football for their first win of the season, but wide receiver Tyreek Hill suffered a feared dislocated left knee early in the third quarter and was carted off, expected to miss the remainder of the season. Tight end Darren Waller, in his first game since January 2024, caught two touchdown passes and may play a major role in Hill's absence. The Jets fell to 0-4 under coach Aaron Glenn, committing three turnovers and 12 penalties for 101 yards while being outscored 50-12 in first halves over the past three games. Quarterback Fields had a 43-yard rushing touchdown but more rushing yards than passing yards through three quarters, and a Jets running back gained 81 yards and scored on a 43-yard carry. The passage also lists numerous other NFL headlines regarding injuries, trades, fantasy football, and Week 4/5 matchups.
