The lecture concludes the discussion of conjugate gradients (CG) and related Krylov subspace methods. The Arnoldi algorithm generates an orthogonal basis for the Krylov subspace via a Gram-Schmidt-like process, producing the matrix relation AQ=QH. For symmetric matrices, H becomes symmetric tridiagonal (the Lanczos case), which allows efficient approximation of low eigenvalues—called Ritz values—of large matrices via a small submatrix.

CG applies to symmetric positive definite matrices, with each iterate x_k in the Krylov subspace. The method yields orthogonal residuals and A-orthogonal (conjugate) search directions, requiring one matrix-vector multiplication, two inner products, and a few vector updates per cycle. Its convergence rate depends on the square root of the condition number. CG is equivalent to minimizing the energy 1/2 x^T A x - b^T x, contrasting with steepest descent, which follows the residual direction directly and converges slowly. CG instead uses A-orthogonal search directions for faster progress.

For non-symmetric or indefinite problems, the MINRES (minimum residual) method is safer but more expensive. It uses the Arnoldi basis to minimize ||b - Ax_k||, resulting in a least squares problem where H is not tridiagonal, eliminating short recurrences.

The lecturer notes that choosing between direct elimination and iterative Krylov methods like CG for large systems requires experimental comparison.

China cut the dollar's share in its trade-weighted currency basket from 26.4 to 22.4 percent and expanded the basket from 13 to 24 currencies. Effective January 2017, this first adjustment since December 2015 aims to reduce focus on the yuan-dollar rate after the yuan fell seven percent against the dollar in 2016. The move precedes U.S. President Trump taking office; he accused China of currency manipulation and appointed a Beijing critic to a trade post. Officials maintain the yuan is stable.

GSK announced that chief commercial officer Luke Miels will become CEO on Jan. 1, replacing Emma Walmsley. Walmsley’s tenure included spinning off GSK’s consumer health business into Haleon and focusing on specialty drugs and vaccines, but investors questioned the strategy and the company’s shares have flattened. AstraZeneca plans to list ordinary shares on the New York Stock Exchange while maintaining its London listing, a move to give U.S. investors easier access but seen as a blow to the U.K., where drugmakers criticize drug-pricing policies and the commercial environment. AstraZeneca and Novartis are also opening direct-to-consumer sales channels in the U.S.

Turkey will extend its state of emergency for three months from April 19, pending parliament's approval. Deputy Prime Minister Numan Kurtulmus cited the fight against FETO, blamed for the July 15, 2016 coup. Emergency rule since July 20, 2016 lets government bypass parliament and limit or suspend rights.

Cheltenham Town faces a second successive summer battle to retain midfielder Harry Pell, 26, after a rival League Two club made an approach. Pell nearly joined Blackpool for £200,000 last August but failed to agree terms. He signed a contract extension in January 2017 and has made over 120 starts, scoring three goals in his last five games.

Zimbabwe's livestock department faces Foot and Mouth Disease vaccine shortages, causing unchecked spread in Midlands, Manicaland, Masvingo, Matabeleland North, and Matabeleland South, with active infections in Chipinge South, Mwenezi, Chivi, and Chiredzi. Dr Unesu Ushewokunze-Obatolu cited staff below 30 percent, weak logistics, funding, fence vandalism, and livestock movement across former control zones. Without zonal controls, cattle requiring vaccination exceed two million, needing more frequent doses.

This September 19, 2000, VentureWire newsletter reports private company business news. Top stories include Pseudo.com shutting down and laying off 175 employees after funding and sale efforts failed; Broadbase Software acquiring Servicesoft in a stock deal worth approximately $645 million; infrastructure provider Enfrastructure raising over $100 million in its first round; former Baan CEO Mary Coleman becoming CEO of RightWorks; Interregnum launching a $105 million IT fund; and Q9 Networks completing a $26.5 million Series A. The issue also lists dozens of venture funding rounds, including Darwin Networks ($91 million), IPG Photonics ($75 million), Wheelhouse ($52 million), Everdream ($50 million), and Nishan Systems ($50 million). Additional sections detail company launches and name changes, mergers and acquisitions, new directors and executives, venture fund and personnel updates, and corrections to prior reports on Global Factory, NewsMarket, and Screen4Me.com.

Stone tools at Attirampakkam, India, dated to 385,000–172,000 years ago, suggest earlier human migration from Africa than previously believed. Published in Nature by Shanti Pappu's team, the study found no human remains, but the artifacts are crucial for understanding ancient cultural origins and human evolution.

IMI plc (LON:IMI) has a consensus "Hold" from eighteen analysts (two sell, twelve hold, four buy) and an average 12-month target of GBX 1,027.29. BNP Paribas raised target to GBX 1,400 ("outperform"); Barclays maintained "overweight" at GBX 1,190; Goldman Sachs, Credit Suisse, and JPMorgan reaffirmed "neutral" at GBX 1,000, GBX 1,020, and GBX 990. Stock opened at GBX 1,216.00, with market cap of GBX 3.29 billion, 50-day and 200-day moving averages of GBX 1,104.16 and GBX 1,051.38, and 52-week range of GBX 751.00–1,223.00. UK-based IMI specializes in fluid control engineering.

This disclosure describes systems and methods for contextualizing industrial automation data via a cloud-based industrial data services platform. Industrial devices support structured Basic Information Data Types (BIDTs)—State, Rate, Odometer, and Event—supplemented with user-configurable metadata. Gateway devices discover BIDTs on industrial devices and apply user-defined hierarchical asset models to group and contextualize the data. An application server system aggregates these asset models into plant or enterprise models and generates graphical data presentations using BIDT-specific widgets for client devices. The platform includes an Industrial Data Services system that registers assets and owners, brokers data services, and manages secure gateway-to-cloud connectivity through a registry that authenticates gateway devices by physical address and grants temporary communication certificates. The architecture supports multiple asset views—such as production and design models—role-based access, and integration of data from geographically distributed facilities.

The University of Nebraska-Lincoln is investing in agricultural and environmental programs, which account for 48.5 percent of campus research expenditures and saw 78 percent undergraduate enrollment growth from 2006 to 2016. New facilities include the Massengale Residential Center, East Campus Recreation and Wellness Center, Veterinary Diagnostic Center, and the relocated Department of Food Science and Technology at Innovation Campus. UNL received a $20 million National Science Foundation grant for root and soil microbe research and launched the INFEWS cross-disciplinary initiative.

The Buffalo County Historical Society opened the climate-controlled, 6,000-square-foot Family History Center at Trails & Rails Museum, which recorded 2,000 summer visitors and a 25 percent tour increase. Supporters seek $660,000 for a phase-two west wing.

Lincoln Public Schools maintains the smallest student-teacher ratios among Nebraska’s ten largest districts, with 13.14 elementary pupils per teacher and 14.14 at the secondary level. The district aims to preserve small class sizes to improve achievement, especially for low-income, minority, and refugee students.

Alliance’s Carhenge, a 1987 automobile replica of Stonehenge built by Jim Reinders and now city-owned, will host visitors for the August 21 total eclipse. The monument was built without tax dollars.

Joe Hadzima delivers an educational overview of startup legal issues, organized around intellectual property, legal entities, people, and financing. On IP, he explains trademarks, copyrights, trade secrets, and patents, noting that patents grant a right to exclude for 20 years and require novelty and non-obviousness; provisional applications provide an inexpensive filing placeholder. He cites a study linking strong patent strategy to venture success and describes MIT’s Technology Licensing Office, which licenses university-owned research under terms including royalties and equity. For legal entities, he advises forming a Delaware corporation early and electing S-corporation status to avoid double taxation, while warning that Internal Revenue Code Section 83 can impose ordinary income tax on founders who receive stock concurrently with investment; founders should incorporate early and file an 83(b) election. Regarding people, he recommends using a “Founder’s Memo” to address equity splits, vesting, board seats, and stock restrictions, and notes that first-round venture financing typically reserves 12–18% of equity for employees through restricted stock, incentive stock options, or non-qualified options. On financing, he cautions that securities offers must be registered or qualify for an exemption, reviews convertible notes, and outlines venture term sheet elements such as liquidation preferences, anti-dilution protections, and preferred returns. He concludes by directing viewers to the lecture deck for further guidance.

Researchers used finite element simulations of aortic growth and remodeling to generate synthetic training data representing thoracic aortic aneurysms (TAAs) resulting from combined mechanobiological insults—compromised elastic fiber integrity and dysfunctional mechanosensing. They trained four neural operator architectures (CNN-DeepONet, FNN-DeepONet, UNet, and Laplace Neural Operator) to predict underlying insult profiles from image-derived dilatation and distensibility maps. Predictions based on both dilatation and distensibility were significantly more accurate than those using dilatation alone, reducing errors roughly by half across all networks. UNet achieved the best overall accuracy. The findings suggest that full-field measurement of aortic shape and mechanics, rather than maximum size alone, could improve personalized TAA diagnosis and treatment planning.

This cross-sectional study investigated antimicrobial resistance (AMR) among 346 patients at ACS Medical College and Hospital in Chennai from November 2023 to May 2024. Amidst India's alarming AMR situation—driven by over-the-counter antibiotic availability, weak regulation, and lack of awareness—the study aimed to identify common resistant organisms and propose antimicrobial stewardship strategies. Of 346 samples, 264 (76.3%) cultures were positive, with Gram-negative bacteria comprising 75.4%. Escherichia coli was most prevalent (28.8% of positive cultures), especially in urine, followed by Klebsiella species (26.9%), prominent in sputum. High resistance rates were observed for Cefoperazone/sulbactam (97.4%), Cefotaxime (92.1%), Cefuroxime (93.4%), and Polymyxin B (98.7%), while Amikacin (71.1%) and Gentamycin (63.2%) showed greater sensitivity. Limitations included the six-month duration, small sample size, cross-sectional design, urban focus, and absence of clinical outcome data. The authors recommend multidisciplinary stewardship teams, regular resistance surveillance, clinician education, evidence-based guidelines, diagnostic testing promotion, and restrictions on over-the-counter sales and self-medication. Future research should explore resistance mechanisms, stewardship program effectiveness, host factors, alternative therapies, and enhanced surveillance.

The SanDisk Sansa Fuze is a portable digital audio/video player with a 1.9-inch color TFT screen, integrated FM tuner, built-in microphone, and microSDHC card slot. It supports MP3, WAV, WMA, secure WMA, and Audible audio formats; MPEG4 video; and JPEG photos, with additional video and photo formats supported through the Sansa Media Converter. The device has a non-replaceable rechargeable battery offering up to 24 hours of audio or 5 hours of video playback, and charges via USB, AC adapter, or car adapter.

Users operate the player with a thumbwheel and switches for power, reset, and hold/lock. Media can be transferred via USB using drag-and-drop, Windows Media Player, Audible Manager, or the Sansa Media Converter. The player provides music playback controls including repeat, shuffle, equalizer settings, and Go Lists; video playback with bookmarks and brightness adjustment; and photo slideshow options. It also offers FM radio listening with up to 30 presets and recording, along with voice recording.

System settings include wallpaper, backlight, power saver, language, date and time, brightness, and USB mode. The player can be formatted or reset to factory settings, which deletes content. SanDisk offers a one-year limited warranty to the original purchaser, firmware updates via its support site, and technical support. The manual notes copyright restrictions and includes an End User License Agreement for the device software.

This paper examines whether digitalization affects sustainable development and whether cultural characteristics influence digitalization levels across 28 EU countries. Using Digital Economy and Society Index (DESI) data from 2014–2017, the authors analyze correlations with indices measuring sustainability components—Global Competitiveness Index, Global Innovation Index, GDP, Global Entrepreneurship Index, Good Country Index, Sustainable Development Goals Index, and Sustainable Society Index—alongside Hofstede’s cultural dimensions.

Results confirm significant positive correlations between DESI and economic and social indicators, including competitiveness, innovation, entrepreneurship, GDP, human wellbeing, and the Sustainable Development Goals Index. However, digitalization correlates negatively with environmental wellbeing and shows no significant correlation with the Planet & Climate component.

Regarding culture, power distance and uncertainty avoidance negatively correlate with digitalization, while individualism and indulgence positively correlate. Long-term orientation shows no significant relationship. The authors conclude that digitalization positively impacts economic and social sustainability but negatively affects the environment. Cultural differences significantly influence digitalization levels, suggesting macromarketing tools should be shaped by national cultural characteristics to facilitate technological change. Limitations include the EU-only sample and underdeveloped sustainability measurement methodologies.

Ari Ne’eman draws parallels between the Trump administration’s autism policy and the Soviet Union’s politically constrained approach to intellectual disability research in 1963. He notes that while the Kennedy family historically advanced disability rights through initiatives like the President’s Panel on Mental Retardation and the Developmental Disabilities Act, Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. recently stood with President Trump promoting unproven theories linking autism to vaccines and acetaminophen. Ne’eman argues that rising autism rates reflect diagnostic substitution, broadened diagnostic criteria, and improved access to diagnosis—factors the administration ignores in favor of pseudo-scientific epidemic claims. He compares this to Soviet researchers who, bound by Communist ideology, artificially suppressed intellectual disability prevalence by rejecting certain causes and manipulating diagnoses. Ne’eman concludes that the administration is subordinating scientific evidence to political ideology while simultaneously proposing cuts to the Developmental Disabilities Act and Medicaid, which fund essential services for autistic people.

The Houston Astros beat the Chicago White Sox 7-1 on Sunday, April 22, 2018, winning their sixth straight and completing a three-game sweep in which they outscored Chicago 27-2. Jose Altuve hit a go-ahead single in a five-run seventh inning, Lance McCullers Jr. allowed one run over six innings, and Evan Gattis hit his first home run of the season. The White Sox lost their seventh straight, falling to 4-14. Reliever Danny Farquhar remained in critical but stable condition after collapsing in the dugout Friday. The Astros next face the Los Angeles Angels, while the White Sox play Seattle.

A message to the Senate communicates approval of an act regulating electoral vote counting for the 1877 election, citing an unprecedented dispute and imminent peril. While the President of the Senate historically counted votes and Congress resolved doubts, the dispute now affects the outcome. The act provides an orderly method: Congress decides single returns, and a tribunal decides double returns unless both Houses concur otherwise. The agitated country needs peace and assurance that the result will be accepted and the highest officer will hold office without a questioned title, and the bill is signed as a definite resolution, though permanent legislation may be needed.

Police and Crimestoppers warn the public about counterfeit banknotes during the festive season. Over 237,000 fake notes worth over £4.88 million were removed from UK streets in the first half of 2017. Retailers, businesses, charities and the elderly have been conned; the crime is linked to organised gangs. Crimestoppers and the Bank of England launched the Banknote Checking Scheme for businesses in October. Report information on those making, buying or selling counterfeit notes to Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111 or via their online form.

The passage specifies SD Memory Card Physical Layer Specification Version 6.00 requirements for Card Ownership Protection (COP) and Force Erase Protection (FEP) using CMD42, detailing password setting, replacement, and clearing procedures, lock/unlock state handling, and force erase operations for COP and non-COP cards. It defines CMD42 parameter behaviors, error handling through status bits, and differences between card types. The text further explains the Switch Function command (CMD6) for querying and configuring function groups such as bus speed mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit, including status data structures and busy indications. It covers command and response formats, Card Command Classes (CCC), application-specific commands (CMD55/ACMD), Card Status and SD Status registers, initialization commands (CMD8), capacity-based differences between SDSC and SDHC/SDXC cards, clock control, CRC protection, read/write/erase timeout conditions, and Speed Class performance definitions based on Allocation Units and Recording Units.

Toronto's housing market, which saw average GTA sale prices reach $916,567 last month (up 33.2 per cent year-over-year), appears to be cooling as buyers delay purchases awaiting potential government affordability measures and sellers rush to list properties. Many homeowners, such as Sarah Blakely, who sold her Toronto home for over $1 million after buying it for $300,000 seven years ago, are cashing out and relocating to less expensive cities like Ottawa, Burlington, Hamilton, or Nova Scotia to live mortgage-free, gain space, and be closer to family. Real estate agents note that while some segments remain strong, bidding wars have eased and high bids are less common. Agents advise Toronto homeowners to sell before a market correction, though they caution that cashing out carries risks if prices continue to rise.

Defending champions India will face Bangladesh in the Champions Trophy semi-final at Edgbaston on June 15. Bangladesh enters after defeating New Zealand, while India aims to continue its strong batting and balanced bowling. The match airs on Star Sports Network at 3 PM IST and streams on Hotstar.
Fire broke out at Scope Hospital in Lucknow after a UPS burst into flames. Over 50 patients and attendants escaped; ICU patients shifted to neighbouring hospitals and a fire probe was ordered.

LeBron James, a four-time NBA champion, four-time MVP, 19-time All-Star, and the highest-paid player in league history, has a net worth of $1 billion as of 2022. Over 21 years, he has earned $479.5 million in NBA salary, with a $97.1 million extension pushing his career total to $532 million. In 2022, he led all athletes with $126.9 million in combined on- and off-court earnings through endorsements with Nike, Beats by Dre, AT&T, Walmart, Kia, and PepsiCo, among others. He has invested in Blaze Pizza, Liverpool FC, Fenway Sports Group, SpringHill Company, Uninterrupted, Canyon Bicycles, and a Manhattan office building. Despite his wealth, he is known for frugal habits such as refusing to pay for phone data roaming, yet he spends approximately $1.5 million annually on body maintenance and owns luxury homes in Akron and Los Angeles along with high-end vehicles. He is married to Savannah James, and they have three children; his son Bronny became the highest-paid college athlete via NIL at USC, and in October 2024 they became the first father-son duo to play together in the NBA. James is active in philanthropy through the I Promise School, the LeBron James Family Foundation, and the "More Than a Vote" campaign. After hinting at retirement following the Lakers' 2023 Western Conference Finals loss, he teased a major announcement in October 2025 that was revealed to be a Hennessy advertisement, causing a 20-fold jump in Lakers ticket sales.

Sixth Circuit affirmed the judgment in Co-operative Transit Co. v. Dayoub, finding no error in instructing the jury on inconsistency between an interrogatory and the verdict and substantial evidence supported it.

The passage examines the Baku Declaration of the 18th NAM Mid-Term Ministerial Meeting and the April 2018 CHOGM Communiqué regarding the Global South and Indian foreign policy. Sushma Swaraj represented India at Baku, while Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended CHOGM to advance post-Brexit UK relations; Modi notably skipped the 2016 NAM summit. The Baku Declaration criticized protectionism in developed nations, called for concluding the Doha Development Round to address trade inequities, and reaffirmed South-South cooperation as a complement—not substitute—to North-South cooperation. It condemned Israeli occupation of Palestinian territories and the Syrian Golan, and emphasized tolerance and diversity. The CHOGM Communiqué also rejected protectionism, endorsed a rules-based multilateral trading system, and set a goal of $2 trillion in intra-Commonwealth trade by 2030. It recognized vulnerabilities facing small states, including climate shocks, unsustainable debt, and financial “de-risking,” and expressed solidarity with Bangladesh over Rohingya refugees, urging their safe return under UNHCR oversight. The author contends that despite rhetorical support for policy autonomy, India has largely abandoned traditional non-alignment and NIEO agendas, maintains a negative stance on Rohingya refugees, and that both documents ultimately fail to challenge the structural economic imbalances, market access barriers, and neoliberal constraints facing the Global South.

In *Jean Melchior v. Hilite International, Inc.* (Fed. Cir. Dec. 12, 2016), the Federal Circuit reversed the district court’s denial of Hilite’s motion for judgment as a matter of law after a jury found Hilite infringed Melchior’s cam phaser patents and that the claims were not invalid. The patents cover hydraulic cam phasers that use torque reversals to transfer fluid between chambers without a pump. The court held that claim 22 of the ’017 patent, treated as representative, was anticipated by the prior art Danckert reference because Melchior’s expert conceded Danckert satisfied all claim limitations except “direct transfer in a closed line,” which the court concluded was not a claim limitation. The court further held the remaining asserted claims of the ’506 and ’254 patents would have been obvious over Danckert in view of Shirai, as Melchior did not challenge Hilite’s obviousness rationale. Judge Newman concurred in the judgment of no liability on the alternative ground that infringement was not supported by substantial evidence, noting the parties stipulated there was no infringement when the pump was operational and Melchior failed to show the accused devices operated contrary to design during transition modes.

This study examines Norwegian Physical Education Teacher Education (PETE) students' perceptions of a flipped learning (FL) framework applied in two units—dance and motor learning—over two semesters. Using a qualitative constructivist grounded theory approach, the researchers interviewed 22 PETE students. The analysis produced five empirical themes: expectations, including peer pressure to prepare; simple input, with students perceiving video preparation as more accessible and efficient than reading; deep learning, through repeated viewing and in-class application of concepts; a supportive learning environment, particularly for practical activities; and challenges, such as the inability to ask questions during preparation, technical problems, and time demands. The authors conclude that FL positively promotes student learning and motivation in PETE. Students regarded the digitally enriched approach as a useful tool for their future professional practice, and the perceived advantages outweighed the reported challenges.

St. Jude researchers identified kinases Mst1 and Mst2 as key regulators of dendritic cell function and T cell responses, in a study published in Nature. Using the NetBID systems biology algorithm, the team found that the Hippo signaling pathway governs distinct dendritic cell subsets. CD8α+ dendritic cells, which prime anti-tumor CD8 T cells, are more metabolically active than CD8α- dendritic cells. Mst1/2 integrate metabolic activity and unconventional NF-κB cytokine signaling to drive interleukin-12 production and selectively regulate CD8α+ dendritic cell function. The findings suggest potential treatment strategies for cancer and immune disorders by modulating dendritic cell activity.

On January 27, 2021, Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC regarding a press release announcing financial results for the quarter ended December 26, 2020. The report states this information is not deemed "filed" under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, signed the filing.

A Roman pottery fragment found on Chapel St Leonards' beach is the third Roman artefact discovered there recently, suggesting a lost Roman settlement may be located there rather than Skegness. Other archaeological finds have also been unearthed, and Lincolnshire County Council is urging residents to report discoveries.

The Supreme Court of Alabama answered a certified question from the Eleventh Circuit in the negative. The question asked whether a provision in an Employers Mutual Casualty Company “linebacker” policy limiting the definition of “insured” to employees acting “within the scope of duties” conflicted with a separate provision covering “violations of constitutional/civil rights,” thereby creating an ambiguity to be construed against the insurer. The case arose from underlying 42 U.S.C. § 1983 actions by Janice Shrader and Debra Lynn Minnix Livingston against City of Attalla police officers for sexual abuse; the plaintiffs sought coverage under the policy after settling with the officers. The district court had held the policy unambiguously excluded coverage because the assaults were outside the officers’ scope of duties. The Alabama Supreme Court held that the Titan I and Titan II cases, which involved different policy language and were based on law-of-the-case and ambiguity between intentional-act and personal-injury provisions, were not controlling. The Court concluded that because civil rights violations under “color of law” can overlap with acts “within the scope of duties,” the coverage was not illusory, the provisions were not inherently ambiguous, and the policy must be enforced as written.

This preprint examines whether outdoor temperature drops worsen COVID-19 symptoms during the Omicron wave in Tomsk, Russia (January–March 2022). The authors hypothesize that infected individuals have a "compromised airway epithelium" whose protective functions are easily disturbed by external triggers like temperature declines, leading to increased severity. Using daily weather data and COVID-19 hospitalizations as a severity proxy in a case-crossover design, they analyzed temperature fluctuations against hospitalization spikes. They identified a main pandemic "carrier wave" and found that drops in daily temperature greater than 3°C were associated with characteristic bursts in daily hospitalizations, with an average time lag of 1–2 days. Of 17 hospitalization surges, 14 were associated with temperature drops (8 as primary triggers, 6 as additional factors), while 3 were unrelated to temperature changes. The study advocates a mechanistic approach, suggesting that predictable temperature drops can help forecast hospitalization increases and improve healthcare system preparedness. Future research should explore humidity, air pollution, and airway supersaturation effects.

Historical evidence indicates US stock markets often exhibit lower volatility and reasonable returns during foreign wars, supporting Nathan Rothschild’s maxim to "buy to the sound of cannons." The Dow Jones dropped nearly 20% after Pearl Harbor but rose over 60% before World War II ended, and the market had fully discounted the 1990 Kuwait invasion by October before rising sharply after the US victory. A study from 1890 to 2017 found war periods had less volatility than peaceful periods, attributed to increased government defense spending. Conversely, wars on home soil devastate markets, as seen in post-WWII Germany and Russia in 1917 and 2022. Gold and commodities frequently rise during conflicts due to uncertainty, anticipated money printing, and supply disruptions. Markets typically discount wars early and look ahead, sometimes rallying despite negative news.

The study demonstrates chirality-selective heat transfer and a nanoscale thermal switch in heterostructures of ferromagnetic [Co/Pt] multilayers and chiral α-SiO2. Time-resolved magneto-optic Kerr effect measurements revealed that reversing the magnetization direction in [Co/Pt] changes the apparent thermal conductivity of α-SiO2 by approximately 7%, with opposite trends for left-handed and right-handed α-SiO2, while non-chiral SiO2 shows no dependence. Ultrafast optical demagnetization in the ferromagnet transfers spin angular momentum to the lattice, generating chiral phonons that carry energy and angular momentum into the adjacent chiral material. Molecular dynamics simulations based on first-principles calculations confirm that angular momentum conservation in chiral phonons produces distinct spatiotemporal temperature profiles and a chiral phonon diode effect, where heat transfer is more efficient when the phonon chirality matches the material chirality. The thermal on/off ratio is approximately 1.07 at room temperature and enhances to about 1.2 at 50 K due to reduced phonon-phonon scattering. These results provide a basis for nanoscale chiral thermal switches and diodes in insulating materials.

Digital media brand The Debrief has announced it is closing after four years, stating it could not see a viable future despite recent success at the British Media Awards. Launched in 2014 to reflect issues facing young women, the site conducted investigations including "Mad About The Pill" on hormone contraceptives and mental health, and its "Make Renting Fair" campaign helped enforce a ban on letting agency fees. Many writers will likely contribute to sister publication Grazia, and readers reacted with sadness.

Gold prices firmed but spot gold was mostly unchanged on Feb 14 as investors awaited Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen's testimony for interest rate hints. The dollar held near recent highs and gold ETF holdings rose. Dallas Fed President Robert Kaplan urged prompt rate hikes, U.S. inflation expectations increased, and Venezuela's gold holdings fell 23 percent in 2016.

Nancy Lever, executive director at the University of Maryland, states that successful school-based mental health programs require family-school-community collaboration and recognize existing school staff and teachers as central to identifying student needs and building buy-in. While approaches should be tailored to local needs, effective programs integrate community-based mental health providers into schools rather than relying solely on outside referrals. Minnesota adapted the University of Maryland model, developed in the late 1980s by Mark Weist, into a nationally regarded program; Mark Sander established a funding model capturing health insurance and compensating clinicians for non-counseling school time. Similarly, Baltimore providers emphasize visibility and integration to reduce stigma and improve access. Minnesota’s program grew through legislative support driven by constituent demand and is funded by insurance and $20 million in state funding.

Nobel-winning biochemist Peter Agre will lecture on science and diplomacy at the University of Louisville May 9 at 12:30 p.m., sponsored by UofL's Chemistry Graduate Student Association and Clariant. Agre, a 2003 Nobel laureate for discovering aquaporins, led visits to Iran, Myanmar, Cuba and North Korea.

Peter Joseph Saville, a Worthing dentist who treated patients for over 40 years at his West Park Lane practice, died at home on June 27 aged 90. Born in 1928, he studied at Guy's Hospital, served as an army dental surgeon in Cyprus and Egypt, and married Josephine in 1954 before moving to Worthing. An avid sportsman, he played cricket, hockey, golf, tennis and squash, and was president of Worthing Hockey Club. A devoted Catholic and Eucharistic minister, he visited Lourdes, supported charities including Worthing Churches Homeless project, and was a member of the Catenian Association. He is survived by his wife, six children and eight grandchildren. His funeral mass is on July 12 at Saint Mary of the Angels, followed by burial at Durrington Cemetery; donations may be made to CAFOD or St Barnabas House.

This week’s episode of STAT’s biotech podcast, “The Readout LOUD,” features Mizuho strategist Jared Holz discussing the rebound in biotech stocks and sentiment. The episode also covers former FDA vaccine regulator Peter Marks joining Eli Lilly, a math error that cost AstraZeneca a rare disease candidate and a biotech’s attempt to revive it, and new funds raised by China-focused Expedition Therapeutics.

Jaime Smith’s new book offers a practical how-to guide for community college students seeking to transfer to four-year institutions. Clearly written and logically organized, it includes diverse case studies and tips on keeping syllabi, prioritizing fit over prestige, understanding housing costs, and distinguishing institutional from major admission. The reviewer praises the book but adds that students should consult local transfer advisers for nuances in articulation agreements, credit limits, and scholarships that websites often omit. The reviewer objects to Smith’s vague guidance on completing associate degrees, noting that many transfer agreements require them to prevent credit loss and provide academic insurance. Despite this omission, the reviewer finds the book accessible and useful for its target audience.

Call to the Pen announced weekly minor league coverage including top performers Mondays and scouting videos Fridays. In week one, Atlanta's Mike Soroka went 2-0 with a 0.77 ERA in two AA starts at age 19. Highlights included Kyle Tucker's seven-RBI game, Jose Medina's three home runs, Dane Dunning's eight-inning shutout with 13 strikeouts, Josh Staumont's six shutout innings with 12 strikeouts, Visalia's nine perfect innings, Kane County's combined no-hitter, and defensive plays by Johnny Davis, Connor Myers, Daniel Spingola, and Jordan Luplow. Leaders: Ian Happ (6 HR), Jorge Mateo (9 SB), Mike Clevinger (25 K). Manager Phillip Wellman won his 1,000th game with San Antonio.

The Steelers lead the AFC North entering Week 5 after being the only division team to win in Week 4. They are in the best position to win the division as the Browns, Ravens, and Bengals struggle with poor play, injuries, and ineffective quarterbacking. Pittsburgh has a Week 5 bye while Cincinnati hosts Detroit and Cleveland plays Minnesota overseas, with all three potentially losing again.

The team maintained its approach despite recent losses and secured a win. Martin Brodeur discussed making key saves, including on a breakaway by Gagne who missed the net, and noted fortunate bounces as Brown and Kopitar hit goalposts. Scoring the first goal was a priority. Brodeur praised a young teammate's growth, important playoff goals, and puck protection. The team looks forward to the next game in New Jersey, hoping for improved home offense. Despite a disputed penalty on Clarkson, they remained calm, made passes instead of dumping the puck, and scored in the third period. Brodeur emphasized focusing on winning and living in the moment.

Students at several universities received honors. Molly Noon was inducted into Pi Theta Epsilon at Misericordia. Abigail Kauffman received Immaculata's senior leadership award. Geisinger graduates Roni Dermo, Cassandra Graeff, and Elizabeth Helwig matched to residencies. King's College students earned honors and completed internships. Gregory Schuettler joined a graduate honor society at Kutztown. Susquehanna's Ashley Machamer presented research and Kelsey Miller became sorority president. Shelby Weikel was recognized at University of the Sciences. Wilkes students Rachael Krell and Shana Noon completed service trips to Costa Rica and the Dominican Republic.

A study of voluntary medical male circumcision (VMMC) in Rakai, Uganda, found that early sex resumption (ESR) before the recommended 42-day wound-healing period declined from 45.1% in 2013–2015 to 14.9% in 2018–2020. Using cross-sectional data from the Rakai Community Cohort Study, researchers analyzed risk factors among recently circumcised men aged 15–49. ESR was significantly more common among currently married men compared to never-married men across most periods, among men reporting multiple sexual partners in 2016–2018 and overall, and among men with primary versus post-primary education in 2018–2020 and overall. After adjustment, occupation and HIV status were not consistently associated with ESR. The authors attribute the decline to strengthened post-VMMC counseling beginning in 2016 and recommend involving female partners in counseling and targeting men with lower education to further reduce ESR and associated HIV risks.

CVS Health's stock fell 23.4% during a 12-week period in late 2016, driven by Walgreens' merger with Prime Therapeutics and CVS's removal from the Tricare network. The author argues these events will not significantly impact revenue, as CVS Caremark remains the nation's largest specialty pharmacy with 90 million members, while the Tricare loss is not materially catastrophic. Despite the decline, CVS has outperformed competitors, producing 58% more consolidated revenue over a three-year period. Growth is expected from 2015 acquisitions of Omnicare and Target's 1,700 pharmacies and 80 MinuteClinics, which saw 8% sales growth in Q2 2017. Using a discounted cash flow model, the author estimates CVS's intrinsic value at $116.32, indicating 45.3% upside from $80.07, and projects net income growth of 2.5%–6.2% annually through 2023. The author concludes that the market has unfairly punished CVS, which remains a leader in drug stores, specialty pharmacy, and long-term care, and is well-positioned for long-term success.

This Phase 1/2, outpatient, crossover, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled human laboratory study translated a preclinical yohimbine-induced reinstatement model to individuals with alcohol use disorder (AUD; N=32). It tested the safety of oral mifepristone (600 mg/day for 7 days) versus placebo, co-administered with yohimbine (32.4 mg), cue-reactivity, priming alcohol, and alcohol self-administration. Primary outcomes were safety and tolerability; secondary outcomes were alcohol craving, consumption, and mediation/moderation analyses.

Mifepristone was safe and well-tolerated with no serious adverse events, no effect on alcohol pharmacokinetics, and no difference in subjective alcohol effects versus placebo. Mifepristone reduced self-reported alcohol craving (ACQ, AUQ) and cue-elicited salivary output compared with placebo, but did not significantly reduce alcohol consumption in the laboratory or outpatient settings. Cortisol levels increased with mifepristone but did not mediate its effects on craving or salivary output. Family history density of alcoholism (FHDA) moderated drug effects: mifepristone significantly reduced craving and urge only in participants with low FHDA, though it reduced salivary output in both low and high FHDA groups. The findings support the safety of mifepristone in AUD and indicate it attenuates stress-induced alcohol craving independent of cortisol, with potentially greater efficacy in individuals with low familial risk for AUD.

Seagate released new 12TB Barracuda Pro and IronWolf/IronWolf Pro 3.5-inch hard drives, with additional capacities from 1TB to 10TB. The Barracuda Pro targets internal builds, offering 250MBps write speeds, 256MB cache, 7.8W power draw, and a five-year warranty. The NAS-focused IronWolf offers 210MBps transfers and a three-year warranty, while the IronWolf Pro reaches 250MBps with greater reliability and a five-year warranty. The 12TB models are priced at $390, $430, and $440, and are now shipping worldwide.

Ronald E. Gabler was convicted by a jury of aggravated assault for attacking Thomas R. Duff and was denied a motion for new trial. Gabler claimed ineffective assistance of counsel, arguing that trial counsel failed to investigate Duff’s medical records and failed to object to testimony attacking his character. Applying the two-prong test from *Strickland v. Washington*, the court found that counsel’s decisions were reasonable trial tactics and that Gabler failed to show a reasonable probability of a different outcome. The court noted that Gabler had insisted on calling a character witness against counsel’s advice and that any deficiency regarding medical evidence or character testimony was not prejudicial. The denial of the motion for new trial was affirmed.

The lecture transitions from tree-level QED diagrams, which contain no loops and have fully determined intermediate momenta, to loop diagrams that represent quantum vacuum fluctuations. Loop diagrams require integration over free internal momenta, leading to mathematical divergences arising from extrapolating the theory to arbitrarily high energies. In the late 1940s, Schwinger, Feynman, and Tomonaga developed renormalization methods to systematically remove these divergences and obtain physically sensible results; Dyson subsequently simplified these techniques using Feynman diagrams. Loop effects introduce key conceptual differences: tree-level diagrams can be obtained from solving classical equations of motion perturbatively, whereas loops capture genuine quantum physics and vacuum fluctuations from the path integral. Consequently, the bare mass, charge, and fields in the Lagrangian differ from measured physical quantities. Loop corrections shift the electron propagator's pole (mass renormalization) and its residue (field renormalization by a factor Z), while photon propagator corrections renormalize the field strength (by Z3) but preserve masslessness due to gauge symmetry. The vertex correction renormalizes the electric charge and generates an anomalous magnetic moment. The Dirac equation predicts a g-factor of exactly 2, but experiments showed a slight deviation; Schwinger's 1948 first-order loop calculation yielded a correction of alpha over 2π, agreeing with observation. Subsequent higher-order calculations—involving up to 891 diagrams—have been performed, and the anomalous magnetic moment remains one of the most precisely measured quantities in physics, confirming QED's accuracy.

This study defines the transcriptomic profile of granulomatous myositis (GM) by analyzing muscle biopsies from 38 patients compared to other inflammatory myopathies and controls. GM biopsies showed marked upregulation of IFNγ and IFNγ-inducible genes, proinflammatory cytokines (IL1B, TNF, TGFB1), chemokines, and TNF family molecules. CD4+ T-cell, B-cell, plasma cell, and macrophage markers were elevated, with HLA type II expression higher than in other inflammatory myopathies. Spatial transcriptomics localized these features to non-caseating granulomas. Analysis identified 1,293 specifically upregulated and 256 downregulated GM genes, predominantly expressed by granuloma macrophages, that correlated with disease activity markers. CHIT1 was the most significantly upregulated gene and was confirmed at the protein level in granulomas and giant cells. A support vector machine model using these gene sets achieved an AUC of 99.6% and accuracy of 98.6%. The findings suggest GM shares inflammatory pathways with sarcoidosis, indicating potential therapeutic targets including TNF, IL1, and JAK/STAT inhibitors, and provide biomarkers for GM diagnosis and disease monitoring.

This study compared REM sleep microstructure among patients with isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD), Parkinson’s disease with RBD (PD+RBD), and controls. iRBD patients showed increased phasic REM sleep proportion and higher REM arousal indices versus controls and PD+RBD. PD+RBD patients exhibited reduced REM sleep duration and percentage, longer REM latency, shorter REM bout durations, and a higher normalized REM bout index compared to the other groups. RSWA percentage was highest in iRBD, intermediate in PD+RBD, and lowest in controls. Both patient groups displayed altered sawtooth wave (STW) spectral characteristics with a shift toward higher frequencies, while PD+RBD specifically showed reduced STW density and duration. NREM/REM sleep transition duration increased from controls to iRBD and peaked in PD+RBD; controls predominantly exhibited "atonia-first" transition sequences, whereas "STW-first" sequences were more common in both patient groups. These findings demonstrate that REM sleep anomalies in RBD extend beyond muscle atonia loss to encompass broader microstructural changes that may serve as accessible biomarkers.

The lecture recaps optimal control for the double integrator system, comparing manual linear feedback design with minimum-time bang-bang control and Pontryagin's minimum principle. It then introduces dynamic programming as a second analytical solution technique. Starting from discrete-time recursive cost-to-go and the principle of optimality, the lecture derives the continuous-time Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation and a sufficiency theorem stating that a policy minimizing the HJB equation is optimal. This is applied to the Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR), where assuming a quadratic cost-to-go function yields the optimal linear feedback law and the Riccati differential equation for the matrix S(t). The infinite-horizon steady-state solution corresponds to the standard LQR result. The lecture contrasts Pontryagin's principle—a necessary condition valid along individual trajectories even with non-smooth value functions—with the HJB sufficiency theorem, which requires smoothness. LQR is presented as a foundational tool for designing optimal linear controllers for more complex systems, while noting that analytical methods break down for nonlinear dynamics, motivating future algorithmic approaches.

Hedge funds are private investment pools for accredited investors and institutions, professionally managed to maximize returns and minimize risk. They trade relatively liquid assets using complex techniques like leverage, short selling, and derivatives, generally aiming for market-neutral returns. Strategies vary widely and may be systematic or discretionary; common approaches include long/short equity, event-driven, global macro, and merger arbitrage, while niche funds target specific markets like real estate or cryptocurrency. Achieving smooth returns depends heavily on combining uncorrelated strategies. Minimum investments typically range from $100,000 to $500,000. Unlike publicly offered mutual funds, hedge funds employ aggressive tactics, charge higher fees, and carry risks including liquidity, leverage, counterparty, and strategy failure. They typically report performance quarterly, and investors should consult tax advisors regarding tax implications.

The study introduces PHIVE, a physics-informed variational autoencoder framework for rapid, unsupervised metabolite quantification in whole-brain magnetic resonance spectroscopic imaging (MRSI) with simultaneous uncertainty estimation. Traditional parametric fitting methods such as LCModel are computationally demanding for high-resolution whole-brain MRSI data. PHIVE incorporates a convolutional encoder and a physics-based decoder, using variational inference to model latent representations probabilistically and estimate aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties, which are propagated to final metabolite concentration estimates and CRLB maps. A conditional baseline approach allows dynamic adjustment of spline baseline flexibility across stiffness levels (0–3, corresponding to 3, 6, 9, and 12 knots) without retraining multiple networks.

The model was evaluated using 7T MRSI data from 12 healthy volunteers, with eight subjects used for training and four for testing, and results were compared against LCModel. PHIVE processed whole-brain datasets in 6 milliseconds per subject, reducing computational time by six orders of magnitude compared to LCModel’s approximately 2 hours. Metabolite maps produced by PHIVE showed high visual similarity to LCModel outputs, with strong positive correlations (R² up to 0.86) for metabolites such as NAA and Glx, though lower correlations were observed for tCho and mIns. PHIVE generally demonstrated lower coefficients of variation than LCModel, particularly for Glx and mIns, indicating improved precision. A paired t-test showed significantly higher relative mIns concentrations with PHIVE compared to LCModel, while no statistically significant differences were observed for tNAA, Glx, tCho, Tau, or GSH.

PHIVE generates spatial maps of metabolite relative concentrations normalized by total creatine, alongside corresponding CRLB, epistemic, and aleatoric uncertainty maps, with higher uncertainty observed in low-SNR regions such as the brain periphery and ventricles. The conditional baseline analysis revealed varying spatial differences across stiffness levels, notably for mIns. Limitations include the absence of an in vivo ground truth, a limited sample size, lack of automated frequency correction preprocessing, reduced specificity for certain metabolites, and the need for enhanced interpretability and longitudinal validation. The authors conclude that PHIVE represents a significant advancement for rapid, accurate, and uncertainty-aware MRSI analysis with potential for clinical integration.

This study investigates the effects of femtosecond pulsed-laser irradiation on niobium thin films (~190 nm) to create laser-induced periodic surface structures (LIPSS). Using varying pulse energies, the researchers generated quasi-1D periodic corrugations with a periodicity of approximately 260 nm and characterized the samples via SEM, TEM, XRD, SQUID magnetometry, magneto-optical imaging, transport measurements, and time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau (TDGL) simulations.

Results show that increasing laser pulse energy gradually produces LIPSS, reduces film thickness, increases grain size at ripple peaks, and decreases the niobium lattice parameter by up to approximately 1.05%, indicating compressive stress. These microstructural changes correlate with isotropic reductions in intrinsic superconducting properties: the critical temperature decreases from 8.93 K in pristine films to 8.53 K in fully patterned films, and the upper critical field is slightly depressed.

The flux-pinning landscape becomes strongly anisotropic. Magnetization, transport, and magneto-optical experiments demonstrate that the critical current density is enhanced when current flows parallel to the LIPSS compared to the perpendicular orientation, particularly at lower magnetic fields and intermediate temperatures. The anisotropy ratio saturates at low fields and collapses to unity near the upper critical field. TDGL simulations confirm that thickness undulations pin vortices, favoring motion along the grooves and explaining the non-monotonic field dependence of the parallel critical current density through collective and individual vortex dynamics.

The authors conclude that laser processing enables tailored modification of niobium film properties, offering a route to fabricate anisotropic superconducting circuit elements, though the technique induces compressive stress that slightly degrades intrinsic reversible properties.

Knees undergo lifelong wear and tear, leading many people over 50 to require surgery, but injury risk can be reduced through healthy lifestyle choices. If injury occurs, physiotherapy can aid recovery and may delay or prevent surgery. This preprint investigates behavioural changes in frontotemporal dementia (FTD), comparing behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) and semantic dementia (SD) to determine whether their behavioural profiles differ qualitatively or quantitatively and to clarify the roles of the prefrontal cortex and anterior temporal lobes (ATL). Using a transdiagnostic approach with 47 patients and 18 controls, the study employed informant questionnaires (CBI-R, AMI-CG, CamQUAIT), neuropsychological assessments, and structural MRI. Results showed both bvFTD and SD exhibited widespread behavioural impairments, with bvFTD generally more severe, but no qualitative double dissociations or SD-specific behaviours were found. Principal component analysis extracted three behavioural dimensions: apathy, challenging behaviours, and activities of daily living. Apathy was more severe in bvFTD and associated with executive dysfunction and anterior cingulate cortex atrophy across the FTD spectrum, not with ATL volume or social-semantic knowledge. Neuropsychological measures of semantic memory and executive function discriminated bvFTD from SD more accurately than behavioural measures (combined AUC = 95.1%). The authors conclude that behavioural changes represent quantitative differences along a continuum rather than distinct syndromic profiles, that neuropsychological assessment is the preferred diagnostic discriminator, and that SD—including left- and right-dominant ATL atrophy—is best conceptualised as a unitary-yet-graded disorder underpinned by bilateral ATL rather than a separate right temporal variant.

The 4-Vertical concept sends four receivers downfield to stretch defenses vertically and horizontally, creating one-on-one matchups. It is effective against man coverage and Cover 3 by exploiting seams and voids over linebackers, but struggles against Cover 4 and soft zones, where horizontal routes are preferable. Against two-high safeties, the tight end occupies the boundary, the slot works the field hash, and outside receivers run go routes; against one-high, the slot occupies the field seam and outside receivers convert to comebacks if not open at 15 yards. The quarterback must look off safeties, identify coverages pre-snap, find favorable matchups or zone voids, and check down to the running back. Variations from 3x1 and empty sets maintain landmarks, using the tight end and slot to isolate receivers or adding a shallow cross for the running back against blitzes.

Seeking additional competitive advantages beyond its low-cost model, Lucky Air considered expanding its e-commerce capabilities. While China's online travel market remained underdeveloped—with low Internet penetration in Yunnan, poor payment infrastructure, and dominant offline travel agents—the airline's website, luckyair.net, offered discounted fares and community features, though only 1% of total tickets were sold directly to consumers online. The case examines whether Lucky Air should invest significantly in e-commerce to build customer loyalty and reduce distribution costs, bundle tour packages like competitor Spring Airlines, or pursue other strategies to differentiate itself in a crowded, regulated market.

The President addresses the American people on the situation in Vietnam, noting that when he took office there were 540,000 American troops in Vietnam and no plan to end U.S. involvement. He states his administration implemented a plan to train and equip South Vietnamese forces and withdraw American troops as South Vietnamese capacity increased. Over 265,000 troops have already been brought home, and casualties have fallen significantly. He credits the Cambodian operation and the Laotian operation—where South Vietnamese ground forces fought with American air support—with disrupting enemy supply lines and enabling further withdrawals. He announces an accelerated withdrawal of 100,000 additional troops between May 1 and December 1, 1971, for a total of 365,000 withdrawn. He states the ultimate goal is total American withdrawal and a lasting peace, preferably through negotiations including a cease-fire and prisoner release, and he calls on Hanoi to agree to the unconditional release of all prisoners of war. He rejects setting a fixed withdrawal date, arguing it would aid the enemy and endanger remaining forces. He defends the conduct of American soldiers, pledges to end involvement in a way that gives South Vietnam a chance to survive as a free people, and asks to be held accountable if he fails to achieve this goal.

Tesla sells directly through company-owned stores, galleries, and service centers, operating 208 total locations globally and 118 service centers as of December 31, 2015. It also maintains 584 Supercharger stations and a destination charging network. Manufacturing occurs at facilities in Fremont, California; Lathrop, California; Tilburg, Netherlands; and the Gigafactory near Reno, Nevada, which is being developed with Panasonic and is expected to reach full production capacity in 2020. The company relies on many single-source suppliers, including one fully qualified battery cell supplier for production vehicles. It earns tradable regulatory credits and has received tax incentives from California and Nevada. The filing details extensive risk factors, including potential production delays, supplier dependence, competition, international expansion challenges, and reliance on key employees including Elon Musk and JB Straubel. As of December 31, 2015, Tesla had 13,058 full-time employees.

Final exams run Dec. 12–20. Campus libraries fill quickly, prompting students to seek alternative study spaces in academic buildings, cafes, and online-reserved rooms through the Center for Career and Professional Development, which provides private space and refreshments. Lehigh extends building hours during this period, including 24-hour access to Fairchild-Martindale Library. Students report that overcrowding, distractions, and unfair seat-saving in libraries add to finals stress, with some waking early to secure preferred spots.

Daisy McCrackin and Capone were kidnapped by Stewart, Jones, and Neal for almost three days. The trio entered McCrackin’s home on May 3, assaulted them, drove them to Compton, and held Capone in a bathtub for 30 hours. McCrackin was forced to provide $10,000 before escaping on May 4.
