Lattice Semiconductor (LSCC) shows early signs of revenue rebound, driven by data center strength but offset by weak automotive and industrial markets. Management highlights opportunities in high-end data center chips and emerging markets including robotics, vision systems, and security. Inventories are normalizing, financials are solid with strong cash generation and no debt, and Q3 guidance implies further growth. The target price was raised to $70, but a HOLD rating is maintained due to expensive valuation and thin margin of safety. The article discusses LSCC’s latest quarterly results and an updated DCF valuation. LSCC designs low-power programmable chips, including FPGAs.

Trust Co. of Vermont raised its UTX stake 2.3% in Q3 to 115,963 shares worth $11.78 million. Several institutions also increased stakes; institutions own 78.26% of shares. UTX traded at $109.62. Q3 EPS was $1.76 on $14.40 billion revenue, beating estimates. Analysts forecast $6.60 EPS, rate it "Hold," and set a $112.82 target. Director Brian Rogers bought 5,000 shares in December, while VP Robert Bailey sold 967 in November. Insiders own 0.15%. United Technologies provides high-technology products to building systems and aerospace industries.

This document is a Statistical Analysis Plan for clinical trial ZP4207-17086. It specifies that electrocardiogram data will be tabulated by investigator assessments and descriptive measures presented by treatment group and visit, with categorical summaries of QTcF values (>450, >480, >500 ms) and changes from baseline (>30, >60 ms). Anti-drug antibody occurrence will be analyzed descriptively per treatment group without statistical tests, defining treatment-induced and treatment-boosted antibodies, with overall incidence based on evaluable patients having at least one post-drug sample. Changes from the protocol include rewording the primary efficacy analysis and adding sensitivity and supportive analyses, and changing secondary efficacy terminology from "within" to "at" specific time points. Appendices detail presentation and programming specifications for tables, figures, and listings; SAS programming quality control requirements covering program structure, log review, output verification, dataset validation, and documentation; and a comprehensive list of planned tables, figures, and listings for efficacy, safety, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic, and demographic analyses.

Scientists increasingly believe ultraprocessed foods may have addictive properties similar to alcohol, nicotine, and opioids. These foods, which account for over half of the average U.S. diet, are engineered with concentrated salts, fats, sugars, and additives that activate the brain's reward system, triggering cravings, tolerance, withdrawal, and loss of control. Using the Yale Food Addiction Scale, approximately 14 percent of adults and 12 percent of children meet criteria for food addiction. Research shows neurochemical and structural brain changes in response to these foods that mirror those seen with addictive substances, and young adults on ultraprocessed diets eat more even when not hungry. Experts argue these products are designed to maximize consumption and corporate profit. Efforts to regulate them include school bans, improved labeling, taxation, and restrictions on marketing, with some progress seen in countries like Chile. Researchers emphasize that systemic policy changes, rather than individual responsibility alone, are needed to address the public health impact.

The Trump administration's 2018 Nuclear Posture Review outlines plans to modernize the US nuclear arsenal with smaller, low-yield atomic bombs and a nuclear-armed sea-launched cruise missile to enhance deterrence against threats from Russia, China, North Korea, and Iran. President Trump and Defence Secretary Jim Mattis said the strategy modernizes the nuclear triad, command systems, and dual-capable aircraft while reaffirming commitments to arms control, the Non-Proliferation Treaty, and the nuclear testing moratorium. Mattis noted Russia and China are pursuing new nuclear capabilities and modernizing conventional forces, while Russia relies on nuclear escalation strategies. The report omits Pakistan. It states the US will not use nuclear weapons against compliant non-nuclear NPT states and emphasizes strengthening extended deterrence for allies through tailored strategies and collaboration. Officials said the policy ensures flexibility amid a dangerous threat environment.

The federal government and all 14 provincial and territorial jurisdictions reached a two-year agreement under which provinces and territories will receive 75 per cent of tax revenues from legalized marijuana, with a portion allocated to municipalities for costs such as law enforcement. Ottawa will retain 25 per cent up to $100 million per year, with additional revenue going to provinces. Legalized marijuana is expected to generate approximately $400 million in tax revenue over the first two years, and ministers will meet in December 2018 to review the framework. Provinces may apply markups beyond existing taxation levels. Ministers also discussed equalization payments, the Canada Pension Plan, and a national strategy to improve corporate ownership information sharing to combat tax evasion, money laundering, and terrorist financing.

South Africa will likely avoid a junk rating from Moody's this week, with all 15 respondents in a Bloomberg survey predicting it will retain its sole remaining investment-grade rating following President Cyril Ramaphosa's replacement of Jacob Zuma, which has boosted the rand and business confidence. However, risks including missed budget targets, weak economic growth, and the ANC's push for land expropriation without compensation could still jeopardize ratings. Moody's, which rates the country one step above speculative grade, will announce its decision Friday. A junk rating would exclude South Africa from key bond indices, risking significant capital outflows and higher borrowing costs.

Scientists from the University of Washington, Texas A&M, and the Western Australian Museum discovered a new clingfish genus and species, the duckbilled clingfish (Nettorhamphos radula), from two specimens in a jar from 1977. The finger-sized fish has a broad, flat snout and 1,800 to 2,300 tiny conical teeth—about ten times more than other clingfish. Using CT scanning, researchers digitally examined its skeleton and 3-D printed parts for analysis rather than dissect the rare specimens. Published April 14 in Copeia, the finding highlights the value of museum collections. Scientists study clingfish for their ability to stick to rough surfaces with suction forces up to 150 times their body weight, which could inform surgical devices and whale tracking.

Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) poses a critical global health threat, and traditional culture-based diagnostics are too slow to guide treatment. While Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) can rapidly capture genetic variation, translating this data into clinically actionable predictions remains challenging. Standard machine learning models like Random Forest and XGBoost treat the genome as an unordered set of features, ignoring the sequential context of Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms (SNPs), whereas data-intensive architectures like Transformers are impractical for moderately sized genomic datasets.

To address this, the authors developed AMR-EnsembleNet, a soft voting ensemble that combines a lightweight 1D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)—which learns local SNP motifs from ordered sequence data—with an XGBoost model that captures complex, non-local feature interactions. Evaluated on the GieSSen benchmark dataset of 809 *E. coli* isolates across four antibiotics (Ciprofloxacin, Cefotaxime, Ceftazidime, and Gentamicin), the ensemble consistently outperformed or matched individual baseline models. It demonstrated particular strength on imbalanced datasets, achieving superior recall for resistant isolates and more balanced overall performance.

Using SHAP interpretability analysis, the authors mapped the most predictive SNPs to well-established AMR-associated genes, including *gyrB*, *marR*, *rpsL*, *parC*, *fusA*, *ampC*, *acrD*, and *ftsI*, confirming that the model learns biologically meaningful signals rather than statistical noise. The framework offers a robust, computationally efficient, and interpretable approach to genomic AMR prediction.

The dollar rose broadly Monday as traders unwound bearish bets following a weekend without new abrasive U.S.-North Korea rhetoric. The dollar index gained 0.3 percent against major currencies and advanced against the yen and Swiss franc. U.S. and world stocks rose, easing last week's geopolitical fears. Investors await Tuesday's U.S. retail sales report for inflation clues.

Saskatoon proposes a $1.2-million, two-year plan to remove and replace approximately 1,000 black ash trees infested with cottony ash psyllids, invasive European tree lice. Insecticides proved ineffective. The city has removed 121 trees so far this year. Year-one funding of $757,000 is secured from reserves, but year-two funding of $423,000 is not yet identified. About 27 per cent of Saskatoon’s 105,000 trees are ash species.

This study investigates water- and ethanol-assisted capillary densification as a scalable post-processing method to enhance the mechanical properties of electrospun polyacrylonitrile (PAN) nanofiber yarns. Using a simple liquid-assisted rolling and drying approach, capillary forces generated during solvent evaporation drive fiber compaction and alignment, significantly improving tensile modulus, strength, and interfiber load transfer compared with as-spun yarns. Water treatment outperforms ethanol due to slower evaporation kinetics and stronger capillary driving forces, while subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C further increases stiffness but reduces ductility by promoting localized fusion at fiber junctions. Yarns with diameters smaller than 10 μm approach the mechanical performance of individual nanofibers. Quantitative SEM image analysis showed that both fiber alignment (coherency factor) and in-plane packing density are strong individual predictors of peak load, and together they explain 80% of the variance in a multiple regression model, demonstrating synergistic, non-redundant contributions to yarn strength. A stochastic mean-field constitutive model incorporating Weibull-distributed fiber recruitment and failure, orientation averaging, and a packing efficiency factor successfully reproduces the experimentally observed five-regime stress–strain behavior. The model parameters quantitatively map onto image-derived microstructural descriptors, closing the structure–mechanics loop and providing a predictive framework for designing high-performance nanofiber assemblies.

Gary Gensler lectures on financial system challenges and opportunities, beginning with class logistics: he reviews paper submissions, emphasizes critical reasoning over summarizing prior readings, and announces upcoming guests including Intercontinental Exchange CEO Jeff Sprecher, Bakkt CEO Kelly Loeffler, and a surprise guest on October 16.

Students discuss financial sector consolidation linked to the Riegle-Neal Act of 1994 and the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act of 1999, resulting income disparities, and too-big-to-fail moral hazard exemplified by Citigroup and former FDIC chair Sheila Bair’s view that restructuring would have been preferable to bailouts. They also observe that innovation often outpaces regulation, complicating oversight.

Gensler defines finance’s core role as intermediating and pricing money and risk. Key functions include investments, store of value, credit, payment, liquidity, and market making. Major sectors are commercial banking, investment banking and brokerage, insurance, asset management, and market infrastructure. He distinguishes primary markets (first issuance) from secondary markets (subsequent trading), notes that secondary markets generally have higher volume, and stresses that ledgers and payment/settlement systems are foundational to finance and to blockchain applications.

Regulation has existed for millennia; contemporary priorities include financial stability, consumer and investor protection, and illicit activity prevention. Regulatory intensity follows an ebb and flow, such as post-crisis Dodd-Frank reforms eventually facing pressure for easing.

Finance and technology are symbiotic; current fintech trends include AI, machine learning, biometrics, open banking, big data, robotic process automation, cloud computing, and chat bots. Incumbents’ legacy systems may create opportunities for blockchain disruption.

The US total credit market debt is roughly 350% of GDP, with significant bond and equity markets. Household debt is dominated by mortgages and student loans. Major financial risks include market, credit, operational, counterparty, liquidity, funding, settlement, and model or correlation risks.

Gensler attributes the 2008 subprime mortgage crisis to weak underwriting, predatory lending, easy credit, derivatives-driven leverage, poor risk management, and asymmetric incentives. Major failures included Bear Stearns, Northern Rock, Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, and Lehman Brothers, requiring government intervention to prevent systemic collapse.

Currently, the banking sector is stronger and better capitalized but more concentrated, while high asset valuations and uneven economic well-being persist. Blockchain opportunities in finance may address legacy customer interfaces, data intensity, economic rents, concentrated risk, and infrastructure costs.

NYU physicists developed a method to generate self-organizing patterns from immiscible liquids in confined geometries, described in PNAS. Droplets de-mix into multiple layers at speeds that determine stripe patterns independent of droplet size, enabling step-wise release of inner droplets. The advance offers potential for sophisticated pharmaceuticals and consumer products.

The Fifth Circuit affirmed Jose Verastegui’s convictions and sentences for felon in possession of a firearm and unlawful reentry. The court rejected his arguments that his above-guideline 120-month sentence was unreasonable and that the district court abused its discretion in upwardly departing and varying from the advisory range. It also rejected his constitutional challenges to the statutes and guideline adjustments, noting they were foreclosed by binding precedent, though raised to preserve issues for potential Supreme Court review. The opinion was designated unpublished and non-precedential.

This lecture defines the nuclear force as the residual interaction between quarks localized in different hadrons, distinct from the strong force that binds quarks within a single hadron. Experimental understanding derives from nucleon-nucleon scattering, nuclear binding energies, and nuclear structure data such as energy levels and moments, especially for light nuclei. The force depends on the distance between nucleons and on their spin and angular momentum, exhibiting spin-orbit and tensor components. It is short-range, vanishing beyond about 2 femtometers and becoming strongly repulsive below about 0.5 femtometers. The force is charge independent, meaning it does not depend on whether the interacting nucleons are protons or neutrons. This property enables the study of mirror nuclei—pairs with the same mass number but reversed proton and neutron numbers—which helps isolate electromagnetic effects and allows investigation of unstable nuclei through their stable counterparts. Comparisons show that mirror nuclei have nearly identical binding energies and excitation levels once Coulomb contributions are removed.

The Enjifit workout partner app launched July 3, 2018, for iOS in New York City. Founded by Nicole Garcia, it connects users with nearby workout partners and personal trainers based on goals and interests. Features include filtering, messaging, workout reminders, and session posting. The app is free with a PRO subscription for trainers. An Android version is coming soon.

ANU and the Institut de Physique du Globe de Paris studied alumino-silicate glass used in mobile screens. Researchers found that sodium and potassium atoms form clusters and percolation channels at the nanometre scale rather than distributing randomly, and calcium and magnesium influence glass flexibility and fracture resistance. The findings could help develop fracture-proof glass, and ANU will seek manufacturing partners. Samsung and LG are developing foldable displays.

Milky Tea announced HyperBrawl Tournament will come to Steam Early Access in June 2017. The combat sports arena game combines handball with PvP combat, featuring 10 warriors, 10 weapons, 6 arenas, and 1-4 player local and online multiplayer.

This application, a continuation of prior U.S. patent applications, describes systems and methods for estimating a depth map from a single color input image using a machine-learned model. The depth estimation model trains on monocular video and/or stereoscopic image pairs by extracting depth maps and poses from images, generating synthetic frames through projection, and computing an input scale occlusion and motion aware loss function. The loss function evaluates per-pixel photometric reconstruction error, uses a minimum error between synthetic frames from temporally adjacent images to mitigate occlusion artifacts, incorporates upsampled depth features to avoid texture-copy artifacts, and applies a mask to discount static features. A depth estimation training system on a game server refines model parameters to minimize this loss. The trained model is provided to client devices in a parallel reality game system, where it generates depth maps from captured scenes to enable depth-aware augmentation of real-world imagery with virtual content.

Nougat updates for OnePlus 3 and 3T roll out with identical builds, featuring redesigned notifications, settings, multi-window, direct-reply, doze, and OxygenOS 4.0 tweaks. Users can manually check in Settings.

The address outlines the administration's intent to maintain and enforce the preceding administration's reforms against lawlessness and abuses by capital combinations in railroads and interstate commerce, while pursuing further legislation to make these reforms lasting. This includes amending antitrust and interstate commerce laws, relieving railroads from certain antitrust restrictions, imposing federal supervision on securities issued by interstate railroads, and reorganizing the Department of Justice, Bureau of Corporations, and Interstate Commerce Commission. The most pressing matter is tariff revision; Congress will be called into extra session on March 15 to revise the Dingley Act to secure adequate revenue, protect domestic labor and industries, and apply maximum tariffs against countries with inequitable trade policies. Because expenditures currently exceed receipts by $100,000,000, a graduated inheritance tax is recommended if import duties cannot eliminate the deficit. Necessary government expenditures include scientific agriculture, conservation of resources, improvement of forests and waterways, and bond-financed construction of the Panama Canal as a lock canal, which will proceed under its current organization and aid domestic and South American trade. The administration also deems essential the maintenance of a proper army, navy, and fortifications to defend national interests, uphold the policy bearing President Monroe's name, and preserve peace through preparedness, while favoring arbitration. The government will seek respect for its citizens abroad, minimize evils from Asiatic immigration through treaty and regulation, and remedy a defect in federal jurisdiction by empowering federal courts to enforce treaty rights for aliens. Reforms to monetary and banking laws and passage of a postal savings bank bill are urged, along with encouragement of foreign trade, direct steamship lines to South America, and the use of tariff provisions to combat foreign discrimination. Prosperity in Porto Rico continues, while Philippine business is expected to improve under revised tariff terms. The speaker hopes for better relations with the South, increased political tolerance, and compliance with the Fifteenth Amendment through electoral qualifications applied to both races, with the federal government not interfering in Southern domestic affairs that meet this standard. He encourages negro industrial progress and advises careful executive discretion in appointments to avoid exacerbating race feeling. On labor, he supports additional laws for employee liability, safety devices, and government employee compensation; affirms federal court authority to issue injunctions in industrial disputes and opposes legalizing secondary boycotts; and recommends statutory conditions for temporary restraining orders to prevent abuse while preserving judicial power.

Pepsi Nigeria announced the "No Shakin' Carry Go" campaign will send 10 fans on an all-expense paid trip to a VVIP experience at the One Africa Music Fest in Dubai in November, meeting Wizkid, Tiwa Savage, Davido, and Tekno. Follow Pepsi's social media.

Nvidia, Amazon and Tesla each fell about 5%, with Nvidia losing nearly $229 billion in market cap, Microsoft dropping $85 billion, Amazon declining $121 billion, and Tesla sinking $71 billion. An Accenture study of 1,300 investors found clients across ages and economic brackets prefer hybrid wealth management combining robo-advisers with human expertise rather than one replacing the other. Respondents ranked hybrid firms higher for offering low-cost access to robo-advisers along with human expertise for complex situations.

Kennesaw State won the 2017 ASUN Championship at The Legends at Chateau Elan in Braselton, Ga., at 1-under 863, beating Lipscomb by one shot for a second straight title and seventh consecutive NCAA Regional berth. Pupils appealed to President Mnangagwa to suspend November 2018 public examinations, citing inadequate preparation due to teachers conducting Zimbabwe Electoral Commission duties. Permanent Secretary Dr Sylvia Utete-Masango revealed the appeal, noting the President's response was undisclosed. To compensate for the shortened second term ending July 26 for July 30 elections, with the third term opening September 4, schools should organize holiday lessons in liaison with district and provincial officials.

NASA's New Horizons spacecraft, following its 2015 Pluto flyby, will reach Kuiper Belt Object 2014 MU69 by January 1, 2019. Nicknamed "Ultima Thule" via a public SETI Institute-hosted campaign, the object orbits 1.6 billion kilometers beyond Pluto and will be the most primitive object observed and farthest encounter achieved by a spacecraft. Selected for research value and lower fuel requirements, MU69 may be an extreme prolate spheroid or close/contact binary based on 2017 observations. The temporary nickname, meaning "beyond the borders of the known world," was chosen from 34,000 public nominations. NASA will submit a formal name to the International Astronomical Union after the flyby, depending on whether MU69 is a single body, binary pair, or multiple objects.

This study characterized clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) using exome sequencing from 454,803 UK Biobank and 173,585 Geisinger participants, identifying 27,331 and 12,877 carriers, respectively. Genome-wide and exome-wide association studies identified 27 common variant loci and rare variant associations in genes including ATM, CHEK2, CTC1, CLPTM1L, and KDELC2. Analyses of individual CHIP genes revealed subtype-specific risk architectures, including opposing effects at the TCL1A locus, which increased DNMT3A-CHIP risk but decreased TET2-CHIP and ASXL1-CHIP risk, and protective associations for PARP1 and LY75 missense variants with DNMT3A-CHIP. While CHIP was largely distinct from mosaic chromosomal alterations (mCA), it shared germline genetic risk factors with mosaic loss of Y (mLOY) and X (mLOX), and novel rare variant associations were identified for mCA, mLOY, and telomere length. Cross-sectional phenome-wide analyses associated CHIP mutations with hematologic, cardiovascular, oncologic, and infectious traits, including a significant association between high variant allele fraction CHIP and severe COVID-19. Longitudinal analyses showed that high VAF CHIP carriers had elevated risks of blood cancers (especially myeloid), lung cancer, prostate cancer, and all-cause mortality, but the association with cardiovascular disease was more modest than previously reported, and a reported protective IL6R effect was not replicated in the full cohort. A polygenic risk score for DNMT3A-CHIP predicted myeloid and lung cancers, as well as other CHIP subtypes, but not cardiovascular disease. The findings emphasize that CHIP is a heterogeneous composite of subtypes with distinct genetic drivers and clinical consequences.

Attacking runs in soccer are off-the-ball movements by offensive players into open space among, between, or behind defenders to receive a pass. The two keys are recognizing or creating open space and ensuring the ball carrier sees the run and delivers a proper pass. Seven main components are: recognizing open space, choosing an appropriate run (such as diagonal, through, or checking runs), breaking away from a defender, moving into open space, timing the run to avoid offside, receiving an optimal pass, and communicating with the ball carrier through oral, visual, or eye contact. A successful run requires exploiting a brief head start, maintaining separation, and completing the run without unexpectedly changing direction. Coaching tips emphasize rewarding good runs with passes, avoiding ball-hogging, having passers continue attacking runs after passing, and keeping all players active.

The Clock (1-3-1) Offense attacks the Diamond & One combination defense by placing the Star player in the middle to isolate them against the pass-denial chaser, creating layups, putbacks, and open shots. The offense employs schematic sequences including corner pass-and-cut actions, ball reversals, post isolations, dribble clears, and high post triangle actions with drop passes, kick outs, and post flashes. It creates a three-on-two offensive rebounding advantage on missed outside shots. Successful implementation requires coordinated execution of screens, post ups, defensive recognition, and non-verbal communication. Game strategies emphasize scouting opponents, varying alignments and entries, and attacking weak defenders. The Diamond & One defense uses four zone defenders and one pass-denial player against the opponent's top scorer.

Education leaders Uncapher and Kendall-Taylor argue that the education sector invests heavily in programs, products, and policies but neglects the narratives needed to help communities understand them, causing good ideas to stall when they encounter default public skepticism about top-down control, data danger, and technology replacing teachers. They propose treating narrative as a design problem from the start through a rigorous “Frame → Test → Iterate → Scale” process: clarify the core story and audience mindsets, develop values-based metaphors and explanations, pressure-test through interviews and surveys, refine with stakeholders, and package strategies for broader use. Examples include reframing standards and testing as “clear signposts” and AI as a “teaching assistant” rather than surveillance. Key recommendations include leading with shared values, explaining mechanisms, centering human roles, naming risks plainly, and avoiding “silver bullet” or “us vs. them” framing. They conclude that building narrative infrastructure alongside products and policies rebuilds trust and allows innovations to succeed.

A speaker interviews hockey prospects James van Riemsdyk, Kyle Turris, Patrick Kane, Sam Gagner, Keaton Ellerby, and Karl Alzner in Columbus. Questions address their college choices, NHL team interests, family influences, youth hockey backgrounds, memories from Sweden, and influences from various coaches and players. The session concludes with congratulations and wishes for luck on draft day and in upcoming media interviews.
Akure-based lawyer Morakinyo Ogele issued a seven-day ultimatum to the EFCC to apologize to the Sun Newspaper for invading its premises and to pay N1 billion compensation.

Guilford and Milford police warned residents to lock vehicles after juveniles broke into dozens of shoreline cars, stealing property and vehicles when keys were left inside. Thieves drive recklessly when fleeing, endangering public safety. Milford police seek two suspects who used stolen credit cards. Authorities advise locking doors, keeping lights on, and calling 911 about suspicious activity, noting arrests were made.

North Wales Police are appealing for witnesses after a man in his 40s of oriental appearance attempted to get a woman in her 30s into a car on Sisson Street, Rhyl, at 8:25am. She escaped unharmed and he left in a silver vehicle. Police say it appears isolated. Denbighshire council warned schools and parents after initial reports of a child being involved, but police confirmed none was. Witnesses should contact police or Crimestoppers quoting V151756.

The Las Vegas Aces lead the Phoenix Mercury 3-0 in the WNBA Finals after a 90-88 Game 3 win on A'ja Wilson's last-second shot. The Aces can clinch their third championship and first Finals sweep since 2020 in Game 4 on Friday. Coach Becky Hammon's defensive schemes, bench contributions from Jewell Loyd and Evans, and the core trio of Wilson, Jackie Young, and Gray have kept the Mercury on their heels. After hovering around .500 early this season, Las Vegas won 16 straight games to reach the playoffs. Mercury guard Sabally is out for Game 4 with a concussion.

Trump threatened 100% tariffs on China from November 1 and secondary tariffs on buyers of Russian crude, reigniting trade war fears. The S&P 500 fell 2.36% last week, dropping over 3% from Thursday's record high to close at its lowest level since early July, while the VIX rose to 21.90. Crude oil declined sharply amid the stock sell-off and after OPEC+ agreed to raise September output by 547,000 bpd. Weaker U.S. jobs and PMI data fueled demand concerns. Analysts warn the correction may not be short-lived, citing potential topping patterns and suggesting defensive positioning as earnings season continues.

The Texas Supreme Court tentatively opined that the American Bar Association should no longer have final say over Texas bar exam eligibility, undercutting the ABA as an accreditor. The court invited public comments by Dec. 1 on changes effective January, noted it may consider alternative accreditors, and said it would not impose additional burdens. The ABA is reviewing the order and will comment.

Output capacitance is set to the greater of two values for load transient deviation and ripple, requiring at least 1.3 mF with derating for aging, temperature, DC bias. Space-grade designs need additional capacitance for single event transient mitigation; the example uses 2.3 mF. An optional LC filter reduces ripple with resonant frequency between the crossover frequency and switching frequency/ESR zero. Cycle-by-cycle limiting begins at roughly 35 A, providing 45% margin over 24.25 A peak inductor current.

The speaker said his team played well in a loss to the Penguins despite tough goals against, including a deflection off a defenseman and a five-on-three. He praised the goaltender as the team's backbone and complimented an inexperienced player for stepping in and playing well on the road against the defending champions. He noted the loss reduces opportunities to win four games, making the next contest important. He expressed trust in all defensemen, including the top four against top lines and a less-discussed pair capable of handling top opponents. He acknowledged the team lacks finals experience but has grown from past playoffs, and said preparation has remained consistent. He cited the opponent's speed as a key factor and praised Filip as a mature leader and difference-maker.

The passage compiles July 16–17, 2001 news articles mentioning Enron and related energy developments. California Secretary of State Bill Jones urged the attorney general to investigate state energy consultants for conflicts of interest after disclosures revealed several purchased stock in power companies—including Edison, Dynegy, Calpine, and Enron—before or during their state contracts. The London Metal Exchange fined Enron Metals Ltd £190,000 ($264,000) for persistent late delivery of warrants and failure to input trades into the matching system, which Enron admitted and settled. A California Senate committee indicated it would likely drop a contempt charge against Enron after the company moved toward complying with a subpoena for documents related to wholesale electricity price investigations. Terremark Worldwide reported a $103.9 million annual loss and auditor concerns about its ability to continue as a going concern; Enron is among its customers. The Alliance for Retail Energy Markets, which includes Enron Energy Services, opposed California legislation bailing out Southern California Edison, arguing it would eliminate competition and restore utility monopolies. In the Netherlands, electricity traders including Enron pressed regulators to force generators to disclose plant outage information amid extreme spot price spikes. In the U.S. Northwest, Enron’s Portland General Electric faces claims along with other utilities that they overcharged regional providers by $611 million. India rejected Enron’s proposal to sell its stake in the Dabhol Power Co. to a state-run utility. Separately, a SmartMoney.com article noted investors shifting toward diversified portfolios including energy stocks such as Enron after technology sector losses.

Since a 2023 state takeover led by Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, New College of Florida has experienced sharply increased spending—about $134,000 per student, more than ten times the state system average—alongside declining graduation and retention rates and a drop of nearly 60 spots in national liberal arts rankings. Critics, including a faculty member and former vice president Nathan Allen, describe the overhaul as a costly personal project with little return, comparing recruitment efforts to a Ponzi scheme due to high attrition. President Richard Corcoran has disputed ranking criteria and referenced possible closure if the college fails to differentiate itself, while critics argue administrative changes are erasing the school’s unique identity. Amid fears the institution could close within one to three years, Allen and some faculty and alumni have increasingly discussed privatization as a potential alternative.

The team expressed disappointment at losing the Stanley Cup Finals but pride in reaching them, praised a teammate's playoff performance, noted offensive struggles and failing to achieve a needed win, credited Bryan and Mike, and stated they will return.

The speaker reports that Congress may safely assemble in Philadelphia despite recent sickness, but suggests amending the 1794 law to allow postponing its meeting. Quantum-correlated pairs are crucial for quantum information, but optical generation of nonclassical phonon pairs is challenging due to limited optomechanical coupling and underdeveloped high-order nonlinearity. This work presents a method to generate quantum-correlated phonon pairs from an optomechanical crystal nanobeam cavity using effective high-order optomechanical nonlinearity, with simultaneous Stokes and anti-Stokes interactions in one pulse. The effective spontaneous four-wave mixing process creates a degenerate correlated phonon pair, retrieved by a red-detuned pulse and verified via the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality. The protocol demonstrates pulse-scheme engineering of high-order optomechanical nonlinearity for mechanical quantum computing, driving the cavity at ωa ± ωm to produce two-mode squeezing and beam-splitter interactions.

The TPS7H500x-SP series consists of radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency peak current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting switching frequencies up to 2 MHz and topologies including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge. The document details a 500 kHz synchronous push-pull converter design example using GaN devices with a 5 V output, specifying a 205 kΩ RT resistor, 10 kΩ and 1.4 kΩ feedback divider resistors, 20.5 kΩ dead-time resistors, 49.9 kΩ leading-edge blanking resistor, 33 nF soft-start capacitor (~7.5 ms), transformer turns ratio of 2.5 with 40 µH primary inductance, 170 V primary GaN FETs, 80 V secondary GaN FETs with parallel Schottky diodes, 0.47 µH output inductor, 2.3 mF output capacitance for single-event transient mitigation, 7.5 Ω current-sense resistor, 3.3 nF hiccup capacitor, Type 2A compensation components (40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, 47 pF), and 102 kΩ slope compensation. Layout guidelines require routing feedback away from power magnetics and switch nodes, minimizing switch-node copper, separating analog and power grounds, placing bypass and compensation components near the controller, and routing high-dv/dt output traces away from sensitive pins.

Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) patterns from direct electron detectors (DEDs) such as Timepix-based hybrid pixel detectors (HPDs) provide high detection quantum efficiency and modulation transfer function, but their coarse pixel pitch limits angular resolution. This study applies a sub-pixel shift-and-add algorithm to multiple high-quality DED patterns, collected with sub-pixel spatial offsets from a silicon single crystal using a Thermo Fisher Scientific Apreo 2 with a TruePix detector (256×256 pixels, 55 µm pitch), to reconstruct a super-resolution pattern. The method increased the pattern signal-to-noise ratio by more than a factor of two compared to long-exposure single-frame or frame-integrated patterns of equivalent dose. The super-resolution pattern recovered fine features comparable to those in camera-retracted and simulated patterns, including higher-order Laue zone rings and fine band structure. The approach requires no hardware modifications and can improve pattern analysis for applications such as high-resolution strain measurement and indexing.

This report examines newcomer education in California, where newcomers—students recently arrived in U.S. schools with limited English proficiency, often socioeconomically disadvantaged and experiencing trauma—are largely absent from policy, data systems, and curricula. No statewide data exists for Students with Interrupted Formal Education (SIFEs). While federal court rulings guarantee educational rights, many districts lack resources to meet legal adequacy standards. California’s per-pupil funding is below average, and although the Local Control Funding Formula, CalNEW, and Opportunities for Youth pilot provide some support, federal Title III Immigrant Student funding reaches only a fraction of students due to growth requirements. The report finds that effective newcomer education requires specialized instructional programs, integration of language and content, translanguaging, educator training, welcoming environments, robust intake, and wraparound social services including legal, housing, and mental health support. Recommendations include building state leadership capacity, incorporating newcomers and SIFEs into state data systems, codifying the OFY initiative, adjusting LCFF for late-arriving students, addressing newcomers in instructional frameworks, investing in open curriculum and research, and advocating for federal policy changes such as removing the Title III growth requirement.

Backtesting is the process of simulating trading strategies against historical market data to evaluate performance, risk, and profitability without risking real capital. It requires accurate, comprehensive historical data—including delisted or failed assets—to avoid survivorship bias and ensure reliability. The practice helps traders define strategy parameters, refine risk management, and account for trading costs such as transaction fees and slippage. However, backtesting has limitations: it cannot guarantee future success, may suffer from overfitting if not validated properly, and often overlooks psychological factors. To ensure robustness, traders should use diverse datasets, conduct out-of-sample and forward testing, employ paper trading, and incorporate realistic costs and market conditions. Backtesting applies across multiple asset classes—including equities, forex, cryptocurrency, futures, options, and CFDs—each presenting unique challenges such as volatility, leverage, and data quality. Various software tools are available, and selection depends on user-friendliness, customization, data integration, and analytical capabilities. Advanced techniques like machine learning, walk-forward testing, and statistical analysis can further enhance strategy evaluation and portfolio optimization.

In *William Skrainka et al. v. Gerard B. Allen*, decided June 24, 1879, the court reversed and remanded the St. Louis Circuit Court judgment. The court held that creditors must be preferred to stockholders regarding corporate assets, and personal profits of members that diminish the common fund must be held for the corporation until creditors are paid. It ruled that stockholders who received bonus stock or second-mortgage bonds without valuable consideration are liable to creditors for unpaid stock to the amount realized from the bonds. Finally, in a statutory proceeding against a stockholder, liability is measured by shares owned at the date of the motion after notice, not at the return of execution against the corporation. Thus, Allen was liable for unpaid stock and bond sale proceeds, but only for shares held at the motion filing.

The 3-3-5 defense, also called the 3-3 stack, employs three defensive linemen, three linebackers, and five defensive backs. It is a high-risk, high-reward scheme relying on pressure, speed, and athleticism, often using smaller, faster players and shifting bigger linebackers to the line or bigger defensive backs to linebacker. Its strengths include flexibility, disguised coverages such as Cover 1 and Cover 3 from the same pre-snap shell, and multiple blitz variations. However, it is vulnerable on the edges to runs like Buck Sweep and outside zone, as well as to seam routes and Trips formations that reduce box defenders. Common blitzes include the Sam Blitz and the SAW Blitz, which create different fronts. Notable users include inventor Joe Lee Dunn, Matt Campbell at Iowa State, Tony Gibson at NC State, and high school coach Tim Racki, who won eight state titles using the defense.

The passage describes dry, free-standing electrode films for energy storage devices, including lithium-ion batteries, that incorporate a microparticulate non-fibrillizable binder having a particle size of about 0.5 to about 40 μm, such as cellulose, carboxymethylcellulose (CMC), or polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), optionally with a fibrillizable binder such as polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE). The self-supporting film includes a dry active material such as graphite, is substantially free of holes, cracks, and surface pits, and has a tensile strength of at least about 1 N. Fabrication methods involve high-shear processing, such as jet milling, to reduce the non-fibrillizable binder to microparticulate size, combining it with a fibrillizable binder and active material, and calendering to form the film. An alternative parallel processing method separately mixes a bulk active material with the microparticulate non-fibrillizable binder and a structural fibrillizable binder with active material before combining them. Example 1 demonstrates that reducing CMC particle size from approximately 70 μm to approximately 10 μm via jet milling increases first-cycle efficiency, mitigates electrode defects, and improves tensile strength compared to as-received CMC. The disclosure further provides electrodes containing the film in contact with a current collector, energy storage devices incorporating such electrodes, and related active material and electrolyte compositions.

New York State’s early intervention providers have not received a substantive raise in three decades, with state-set reimbursement rates for many services now lower than in the 1990s. Extensive uncompensated work, including travel, reporting, and preparation, has contributed to widespread attrition, leaving many families, especially in rural areas, without timely access to critical therapies. In 2024, New York authorized a 5% rate increase for in-person services and an additional 4% for underserved areas, but full implementation remains pending federal approval, and advocates fear potential federal Medicaid cuts could further delay improvements. Similar pay crises and provider shortages are reported in other states, including Illinois, Texas, and Rhode Island.

Mounting evidence indicates that dietary guidelines falsely equate protein sources by quantity alone, ignoring quality differences in essential amino acid content and bioavailability. While U.S. adults consume excess total protein, many—especially those over 70—may lack adequate high-quality protein needed for muscle maintenance. Animal proteins generally contain all essential amino acids and are more digestible than most plant proteins. Research shows that when adults consume guideline-"equivalent" amounts of animal versus plant proteins, animal sources yield significantly greater muscle protein synthesis. Tools like the EAA-9 reveal that plant foods such as peanut butter and legumes require substantially larger serving sizes and calories to match the amino acid benefits of eggs or meat. Older adults may need up to 1.5 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight daily due to reduced synthesis efficiency. Experts recommend updating guidelines to focus on essential amino acids rather than total protein, combining complementary plant proteins, using processing methods like soaking or fermentation to improve digestibility, and personalizing recommendations by age and demographic to ensure adequate nutrition amid shifting toward plant-based diets.

The article recounts selected results from the FLaNN community on the expressivity of formal transformer models via logic, automata, and circuit complexity. Transformers define families of formal languages by mapping input strings to output tokens. Unique Hard Attention Transformers (UHAT) with positional encodings (PEs) are strictly contained in AC⁰, so they cannot express PARITY or MAJ, yet they can express FO[Mon], masked NoPE-UHAT coincides with FO/star-free languages, and PALINDROME is expressible by UHAT with PEs. Verification of masked UHAT without PEs is decidable. Average Hard Attention Transformers (AHAT) are upper-bounded by TC⁰; Counting LTL with unary numerical predicates is expressible by AHAT with PEs, and the fragment Kt[#] is expressible by masked NoPE-AHAT. NoPE-AHAT precisely recognizes permutation-invariant languages with semi-algebraic Parikh images, making their verification undecidable. The article highlights limitations: hard-attention models do not fully capture softmax transformers, though uniform-attention AHAT[U] languages are recognized by softmax transformers; and expressibility differs from trainability, since PARITY is expressible by softmax transformers but difficult to train, whereas MAJ is efficiently trainable. The authors note open problems and aim to motivate researchers in logic, automata, verification, and programming languages to engage with FLaNN.

This preprint reports a co-produced, community-based active case finding study (part of NIHR STIMULATE-ICP) that identified 23 adults with probable but undiagnosed Long Covid in Camden, Merton and Derbyshire through semi-structured interviews. Thematic analysis revealed four themes: limited Long Covid awareness and self-doubt about symptoms; barriers to healthcare engagement including reluctance to burden the NHS, non-help-seeking identities, and fluctuating multi-system symptoms complicating diagnosis and care; enacted, anticipated and internalised stigma and discrimination related to age, gender, employment and social exclusion; and use of non-NHS support alongside desires for easier primary care access, dedicated Long Covid services, and social/community support. The discussion frames these barriers as forms of epistemic injustice and intersectional stigma that exacerbate health inequalities. Recommendations include raising awareness, mitigating stigma, improving clinician listening and signposting, and developing an online help-seeking tool. The device enters CONV state on the CONVST/CS rising edge and ignores further transitions during the conversion interval tconv, returning to ACQ at conversion end. The host monitors the RVS pin or waits for tconv_max before initiating new operations.

A data transfer frame begins at the CONVST/CS falling edge and ends at the subsequent rising edge. On the falling edge, RVS goes low, the 32-bit output shift register is loaded, and the internal configuration register resets to 0000h (NOP). SCLK shifts data in via SDI and out via SDO-x. On the rising edge, the input shift register transfers to the command processor. An optimal frame contains 32 SCLKs; short frames (<32) invalidate writes but allow valid partial reads of MSBs, while long frames (>32) treat the last 32 bits received as the command.

The device features nine configuration registers. Commands include half-word (HWORD) and byte read/write operations; for HWORD commands, the LSB of the 9-bit address is ignored. Valid 32-bit configuration commands execute at the CONVST/CS rising edge. Output data for frame F+1 depends on the command issued in frame F and the DATA_VAL bits, yielding fixed patterns, 8-bit or 16-bit register data, or the latest 16-bit conversion result. The DATAOUT_CTL_REG optionally appends flags for device address, input range, AVDD alarm, input alarm, and parity.

The multiSPI interface supports four legacy SPI-compatible protocols (SPI-00-S through SPI-11-S), defaulting to SPI-00-S on power-up and selected via SDI_CTL_REG. Read options include legacy single or dual SDO-x modes and source-synchronous (SRC) protocols using RVS as the output clock; dual SDO mode is enabled in SDO_CTL_REG. Key registers include DEVICE_ID_REG for daisy-chain identification; RST_PWRCTL_REG for reset, NAP, and power-down modes, which requires writing 69h to address 05h to unlock; SDI_CTL_REG and SDO_CTL_REG for protocol configuration; DATAOUT_CTL_REG for output formatting; RANGE_SEL_REG for reference and input range selection; and ALARM, ALARM_H_TH_REG, and ALARM_L_TH_REG for alarm thresholds and hysteresis.

An example application pairs the ADS8681W with an eight-channel multiplexer for a PLC analog input module, achieving under 5µs settling to 1% accuracy with software-configurable voltage and current inputs. Programmable input alarm thresholds and hysteresis support applications such as NTC thermistor temperature monitoring.

The device uses separate AVDD and DVDD supplies, each requiring decoupling capacitors (minimum 1µF and 10µF for AVDD; 10µF for DVDD). NAP mode is enabled via RST_PWRCTL_REG with CONVST/CS held high, and PD mode is entered by setting PWRDN after unlocking. Layout recommendations include partitioning analog and digital sections, placing bypass capacitors close to pins without intervening vias, and using specified capacitors for REFCAP and REFIO.

Turing architecture introduces advancements in memory, display, video, ray tracing, AI-based graphics, and shading. Memory improvements include GDDR6 with 14 Gbps signaling and 20% better power efficiency than GDDR5X, larger L2 caches such as 6 MB in TU102, and enhanced lossless compression, together providing approximately 50% effective bandwidth improvements over Pascal. The display engine supports DisplayPort 1.4a for 8K resolution at 60 Hz, VESA Display Stream Compression 1.2, native HDR processing, and ITU-R BT.2100 tone mapping. Video features include an NVENC encoder supporting H.265 8K encode at 30 fps with up to 25% bitrate savings for HEVC and up to 15% for H.264, and an NVDEC decoder supporting HEVC 4:4:4 8/10/12-bit and VP9 10/12-bit HDR. For VR, Turing supports USB Type-C and VirtualLink, which delivers power, display, and data through a single connector. NVLink replaces previous SLI bridges in TU102 and TU104, providing up to 100 GB/sec bidirectional bandwidth in TU102 and 50 GB/sec in TU104, with support limited to two-way SLI.

Real-time ray tracing is enabled by RT Cores in TU102, TU104, and TU106, which accelerate BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection, making ray tracing roughly ten times faster than in Pascal. Turing uses a hybrid rendering model combining rasterization with ray tracing for effects like reflections, shadows, and ambient occlusion, and supports APIs including RTX, DXR, and Vulkan. NVIDIA NGX utilizes Tensor Cores for AI-based graphics enhancements, notably DLSS, which produces quality comparable to or better than TAA with roughly half the shading work, and a DLSS 2X mode approaching 64x supersampling quality. Additional NGX features include InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez.

Turing introduces new shading and rendering capabilities: Mesh Shading with Task and Mesh Shaders reduces CPU draw-call bottlenecks; Variable Rate Shading allows dynamic per-16x16-pixel shading-rate adjustment for algorithms such as Content Adaptive, Motion Adaptive, and Foveated Rendering; Texture Space Shading decouples visibility and appearance sampling to improve efficiency and temporal stability; and Multi-View Rendering supports up to four hardware views per pass. Turing also supports DX12 Tier 3 bindless resource views and Tier 2 resource heaps. The architecture is implemented in TU102 (e.g., RTX 2080 Ti), TU104 (e.g., RTX 2080, Tesla T4, Quadro RTX 5000), and TU106 (e.g., RTX 2070), the latter lacking NVLink and SLI. RTX-OPS is introduced as a workload-based metric weighting Tensor, FP32, RT, and integer operations. The document also illustrates ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections in games, highlighting advantages over rasterized techniques.

This lecture examines gender discrimination and identity, outlining reasons to study gender differences including fairness, economic efficiency through improved talent allocation, and understanding preference formation. Despite substantial labor market gains for women driven by increased education, technological innovations such as the pill and dishwasher, labor demand shifts toward services, and reduced discrimination, a significant wage gap persists. Research by Claudia Goldin indicates that women earn roughly 20% to 30% less than men for equal work, conditional on work time and education, with the gap widening between ages 30 and 45.

Technological solutions like blind auditions for orchestras, studied by Goldin and Rouse, increased the proportion of women hired by fostering impartiality, though women and minorities remain underrepresented in leadership roles. In academia, progress for women in economics has stalled at certain career stages. The lecture discusses how biased belief updating contributes to gaps: Sarsons (2019) finds that after adverse patient outcomes, physicians sharply reduce referrals to female surgeons and to other female surgeons generally, whereas male surgeons face less punishment; after good outcomes, referrals to male surgeons double, while referrals to female surgeons rise by only about 70%.

Algorithms trained on human decisions can replicate bias, though researchers suggest they may be easier to correct than human biases. Gender identity norms also constrain outcomes. Bertrand et al. (2015) document a missing mass in the distribution of relative income just above the 50% threshold where wives outearn husbands, consistent with the norm that men should earn more; this arises from fewer such couples forming, higher divorce rates, and women reducing labor supply. Kleven et al. show a nearly 20% long-run earnings penalty for women after the birth of a first child in Danish data, with effects transmitted across generations. Antecol finds that gender-neutral tenure clock stopping policies in academia reduced female tenure rates while increasing male ones.

Bursztyn et al. demonstrate that single female MBA students report lower career ambition when their responses are publicly observable, particularly to single male peers, to avoid signaling undesirable traits in the marriage market. Finally, Vesterlund et al. examine nonpromotable tasks: women are more likely to volunteer for them and more likely to be asked. In mixed-gender experiments, women invest more in group tasks because they are expected to, but this difference disappears in same-sex groups; when asked, women comply more often than men, amplifying disparities. The lecture concludes that persistent gender gaps stem from biased beliefs, identity norms, and task allocation dynamics, and that understanding these factors can help inform interventions.

The MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 documentation describes the independent watchdog timer (IWDT), a device-independent supervisor in the LFSS with its own power and clock source, featuring a 25-bit counter with closed and open window driven from a 32kHz LFOSC and eight selectable periods, which generates a POR reset if not serviced. The windowed watchdog timer (WWDT) supervises code execution with eight selectable periods, automatic sleep stopping, and interval timer mode, generating a reset or interrupt. The RTC_B real-time clock operates from a 32kHz source, providing calendar counters, customizable and interval alarms, periodic wake-up interrupts, and calibration up to ±240ppm for crystal offset and temperature drift. Timer peripherals include general-purpose (TIMGx) and advanced (TIMAx) 16-bit counters with programmable prescalers, quadrature encoder interface, synchronization, cross-triggering, asymmetric PWM with dead band, fault handling, and additional capture/compare channels. The IOMUX manages peripheral function selection, output driver, input path, and SHUTDOWN wake-up logic. A two-wire Serial Wire Debug (SWD) interface is provided through the DEBUGSS, which supports a mailbox, security features including SWD lockout and password-authenticated debugging, and configurable peripheral behavior during debug halt. A memory-mapped FACTORY region contains read-only DEVICEID and USERID factory constants. Application recommendations include 10µF and 0.1µF decoupling capacitors on VDD/VSS, a 47kΩ pullup and 1000pF pulldown on NRST, and pullup resistors for 5V-tolerant open-drain IOs. The September 2025 revision removed DGS32 package information and added the DEBUGSS section.

The double-down trading strategy involves adding an equal position size to a losing trade—typically as the price falls—to lower the average entry price and recover losses if the price reverses. While it may help reach breakeven faster, it risks greater losses if the decline continues and often reflects an anchoring bias rather than rational planning. Unlike the Martingale strategy, which increases position size after losses, double-down adds the same size, limiting—but not eliminating—additional risk. It differs from the repair strategy, which uses options to adjust a losing position. Backtests indicate the strategy tends to improve performance in mean-reverting assets like stocks but worsens results in trending assets such as junk bonds. Consequently, it is rarely part of a disciplined trading plan and requires careful assessment of market conditions and risk management.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture introduces significant advancements over Turing. The full GA102 GPU comprises seven Graphics Processing Clusters (GPCs), 42 Texture Processing Clusters (TPCs), and 84 Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs), with 112 Raster Operators (ROPs) now integrated into the GPCs rather than tied to memory controllers. Each SM contains 128 CUDA Cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, one second-generation Ray Tracing Core, and 128 KB of L1/Shared Memory. The SM design doubles peak FP32 throughput by enabling FP32 operations on both datapaths and increases L1 cache capacity by 33 percent compared to Turing.

The architecture supports a third-generation NVLink interface providing 112.5 GB/s total bandwidth between two GPUs, a PCIe Gen 4 host interface offering up to 64 GB/s peak bandwidth in a x16 slot, and GDDR6X memory delivering up to 936 GB/s via PAM4 signaling. GDDR6X also incorporates Error Detection and Replay (EDR) to improve stability when overclocking. Second-generation RT Cores double the ray/triangle intersection testing rate over Turing, add a new Interpolate Triangle Position unit to accelerate ray-traced motion blur, and enable concurrent ray tracing with compute or graphics workloads within each SM. Third-generation Tensor Cores support TF32, BF16, and Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity for up to 2x inferencing throughput, enhancing DLSS—including 8K gaming on the GeForce RTX 3090.

Other features include NVIDIA RTX IO for GPU-based lossless decompression via Microsoft DirectStorage, a fifth-generation NVDEC with AV1 hardware decode, a seventh-generation NVENC encoder, and HDMI 2.1 / DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a supporting 8K60 and 4K120 resolutions. The NVIDIA A40 data center GPU offers 48 GB of memory scalable to 96 GB via NVLink, while the RTX A6000 workstation GPU provides 48 GB of GDDR6 and professional certifications. Ampere delivers up to 1.9x the power efficiency of Turing and up to 2x performance in programmable shading, ray tracing, and artificial intelligence workloads.

In 1886, the U.S. opposed a Hawaiian loan handled by an English syndicate under reciprocity treaty privileges. In early 1887, the U.S. withheld approval of a proposed Hawaiian-Samoan political alliance. In December 1887, Britain proposed that the U.S., England, and Germany guarantee Hawaiian neutrality and equal harbor access. In February 1888, Bayard declined, citing existing U.S.-Hawaiian treaties that secured equal accessibility and prohibited territory cession without U.S. consent. Britain's proposal stemmed from Pacific rivalries with Germany and jealousy of U.S. influence. Meanwhile, the British commissioner protested U.S. exclusive use of Pearl River Harbor under a supplementary convention, warning it threatened independence, though Hawaii ratified it with assurances U.S. rights were limited and temporary.

In a December 31, 1842 message to Congress, the President addressed U.S. trade with the Sandwich Islands, diplomatic intercourse, and post-war affairs in China. He transmitted correspondence between Hawaiian agents and the Secretary of State, noted the islands’ importance as a Pacific refitting stop, their progress in civilization, and that American vessels constitute five-sixths of annual traffic. He declared U.S. support for Hawaii’s independent existence and prosperity without seeking exclusive control, warned of U.S. dissatisfaction should another power colonize or subvert the islands, and recommended Treasury funding for a consul there. Regarding China, he observed that a British treaty opened four ports—Amoy, Foo-Choo-Foo, Ningpo, and Chinghai—to British commerce but did not address other nations, leaving the United States to seek its own arrangements with the Chinese Empire.

This Texas Instruments document describes a low-side current sensing circuit using an amplifier and high-speed comparator that changes state when the amplified shunt resistor voltage reaches an over-current threshold. Design requirements specify a logic high alert when the amplifier output exceeds 1.1V, and require 0.1µF low ESR ceramic bypass capacitors directly between the V+ and ground pins to prevent ringing and false triggers. The device supports split or single supplies, with outputs swinging to V- on split supplies. Layout guidelines include minimizing input-output coupling, placing bypass capacitors close to supply pins, and treating the device as high-speed logic. The document also lists related reference designs, support resources, documentation update procedures, ESD warnings, mechanical packaging specifications, and legal disclaimers.

Christmas Bird Counts compile over a century of early-winter bird data across the Americas. Sheridan's count is Dec. 14; Story-Big Horn's is Dec. 23. All skill levels may participate and should bring lunch, water, warm clothing and footwear.

On September 10, 2015, Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting its underwriting agreement with Goldman, Sachs & Co. for the issuance and sale of €1 billion in 1.375% Notes due January 17, 2024, and €1 billion in 2.000% Notes due September 17, 2027. The passage examines the shift toward an Internet of Things (IoT) society and the emergence of a new productivity paradox, where technology investments may lag behind measured productivity gains. It traces this paradox from earlier computer and internet eras, noting that the internet and IoT generate significant uncaptured GDP—value such as free culture, consumer surplus, and new digital services that provide utility but are not reflected in traditional revenue-based GDP metrics. Through empirical analysis of 500 global ICT firms from 2005 to 2016, the authors find that high R&D-intensive firms face declining marginal productivity of ICT, while low R&D-intensive firms experience rising marginal productivity. To overcome this trap, leading firms are transitioning from traditional Product of Things (PoT) strategies to sophisticated digital business strategies that activate a self-propagating function. This is achieved by harnessing soft innovation resources—including sleeping resources, trust, past experiences, memory, and untapped human potential—to develop supra-functionality beyond pure economic value. Case analyses of seven leading global ICT firms—Samsung, Intel, Google, Microsoft, Huawei, Apple, and Amazon—illustrate transformative directions such as smart user experiences, information search platforms, connected ecosystems, and merging physical and digital retail. The paper concludes that global ICT firms must recognize the two-faced nature of ICT advancement, embrace digital business strategies, and adopt trust-based, ICT-driven disruptive business models with consolidated challenges to social demand in order to thrive in an IoT-based society.

The lecture introduces nuclear binding energies to explain solar system abundances, such as the high frequency of hydrogen and iron. Binding energy is defined by the mass difference between a nucleus’s constituent protons, neutrons, and electrons and the nucleus itself. A plot of average binding energy per nucleon versus mass number shows a fairly stable range of 7.5 to 9 MeV, with a maximum around iron; this peak means energy is released through both fission of heavier nuclei and fusion of lighter ones. The Weizsäcker semi-empirical mass formula, also called the liquid-drop model, parameterizes this curve with five terms: a volume term dominating at about 16 MeV per nucleon, indicating short-range nuclear forces and a high central density; a surface term reducing binding energy for surface nucleons; a Coulomb term accounting for proton repulsion; an asymmetry term based on the Pauli exclusion principle that favors equal numbers of protons and neutrons; and a pairing term giving lower energy for even numbers of protons or neutrons. Together these terms reproduce the binding energy curve with its peak near iron.

Tariff-induced monopolies are rare, but the anthracite coal tariff should be removed. The monetary system needs elasticity; banks should furnish adequate circulation, and legislation should ensure currency is interchangeable, meets commercial needs, and is convertible to gold. A proper immigration law is needed. Organized capital and labor are necessary factors that can benefit or harm society, and opposition should target bad conduct rather than the organizations themselves. Both must obey the law, respect individual freedom and justice, and serve the public interest. Class animosity is condemned; individuals should be judged by merit, and the National Government should exercise its powers accordingly.

In September 1945, Colonel Alfred McCormack was appointed Special Assistant to the Secretary of State for Research and Intelligence, and Executive Order 9630 terminated the Foreign Economic Administration, transferring some functions to the Department of State and others to the Reconstruction Finance Corporation, Commerce, and Agriculture. The passage documents 1945 Lend-Lease operations and discontinuance; the Bretton Woods proposals and December 27 signing of International Monetary Fund and International Bank agreements; and statements on international trade and commodity agreements.

Researchers warn that consuming more than one glass of wine nightly may indicate chronic alcoholism, with 27% of Australians aged 55–64 in New South Wales drinking at risky levels. Medical professionals recommend several alcohol-free days weekly and limiting intake to two standard drinks daily, noting that most alcoholic beverages exceed one standard drink. Daily drinking increases risks of pancreatitis, liver disease, obesity, alcoholic dementia, and cancer. Experts note rising substance misuse among aging populations, partly due to cheap supermarket alcohol, and emphasize that the daily limit cannot be averaged across a week.

The 3 Days Down Overnight Trading Strategy is a mean reversion strategy for SPY that enters at the close of three consecutive down days and exits at the next open. Backtesting from 1993 shows 661 trades, 0.13% average gain, 65% win rate, and 8% max drawdown. Exiting at the next close instead raises average gain to 0.24% and CAGR to 5%, but drops win rate to 61%, increases drawdown to 17%, with 8% time in market. A March 2022 modified version reduced exposure and drawdowns, yielding 0.35% average gain, 60% win ratio, and 10% max drawdown. In the 2022 bear market, it made 35 trades with 0.3% average gain. The strategy also works for QQQ and some stocks, but less effectively.

The overlap in soccer sends an unmarked back player, usually a wing fullback, into attack by sprinting past a midfielder along the sideline, creating space or freeing another attacker. The overlapping player typically receives the ball to cross, or passes to the midfielder if covered. An underlap sends the fullback inside the midfielder for a shot. Both require space, usually near sidelines, and the defender returns afterward. Unlike a vertical offensive switch, the midfielder stays in attack. Coaches should vary overlap and underlap runs, though adding overlaps to a crowded attack can cause congestion.

The court affirmed a judgment sustaining a demurrer in Ross Nelson v. Peter John, an action for specific performance of an 1892 contract by Puyallup Indians John and Chekudakai Salerhand to convey land patented in 1886 subject to restrictions on alienation. The court held that the restrictions were valid and necessary under the government’s policy making the Indians wards, and were not void as repugnant to the fee grant. It held that the 1887 citizenship act did not impliedly repeal the restrictions, and that the 1893 Act of Congress, passed after the contract, expressly withheld the power of alienation for ten years, rendering the 1892 contract void.

The United States has auctioned the seized Russian superyacht Amadea, which was apprehended in Fiji in 2022 by the Justice Department’s KleptoCapture task force. The new owner and sale price have not been disclosed following the September 10 sealed-bid auction. The 106-meter yacht, valued at approximately $230 million, was believed to be formerly owned by a sanctioned Russian oligarch. Ownership has been contested by Eduard Khudainatov, but a judge ruled he was a “straw owner” and could not block forfeiture; Khudainatov has appealed. This preprint presents a rigorous mathematical analysis of the direct and inverse problems associated with an SEIR-like model featuring a time-dependent transmission parameter for SARS-CoV-2. The proposed nine-compartment model divides the population into susceptible, exposed, vaccinated, asymptomatic infectious, mildly infectious, severely infectious, critically infectious, recovered, and deceased individuals. While most model parameters are sourced from the literature, the transmission rate is unknown and must be estimated from observed daily incidence. The authors prove that the direct problem has a unique, non-negative solution and analyze the parameter-to-solution map, establishing its well-posedness, continuity, injectivity, weak sequential closedness, and Fréchet differentiability. For the inverse problem, they employ Tikhonov-type regularization to estimate the time-dependent transmission parameter from reported daily infections and derive sufficient conditions for the existence, stability, and convergence of solutions. The article is organized to present the model, direct and inverse problem analyses, and a numerical example using real data.

Sudo Security Group found Apple granted Uber unique permission to record iPhone screens for iPhone-Apple Watch functionality. No other third-party developer had received such an entitlement. No evidence Uber misused this. Uber has removed it, stating Apple granted it years ago because Apple Watch could not handle map rendering, and it is no longer in their codebase. Uber is negotiating with TfL after losing its London licence.

Enron Corp. is eliminating about 250 jobs, or 20 percent, at its broadband unit after completing its fiber-optic network and facing slow demand for streaming media. President John Tyler's December 30, 1842 message to Congress reports large U.S. imports from China and growing exports, including $715,000 in domestic and $485,000 in foreign merchandise in 1841 direct trade, plus indirect trade via other countries. He notes China's historical exclusion of foreigners but states that events, including its treaty with England establishing equal terms, appear likely to break down that spirit of nonintercourse, and observes the U.S. market there has more than doubled in ten years. RTX Neural Texture Compression (NTC) uses neural shaders to compress textures more efficiently than traditional methods, reducing memory usage by over 3× while improving visual quality. Stochastic Texture Filtering (STF) reduces aliasing and moiré patterns and runs fast on Blackwell GPUs. Neural Radiance Cache (NRC) is a neural shader that caches radiance data to approximate global illumination after one bounce, improving performance and indirect lighting quality. RTX Skin applies real-time subsurface scattering for translucent materials like skin. RTX Neural Faces uses a real-time generative AI model trained on offline images to infer natural-looking faces from rasterized inputs. The Blackwell GPU architecture includes the flagship GB202 (RTX 5090) with 92.2 billion transistors and 24,576 CUDA cores; the high-end GB203 (RTX 5080, 5070 Ti) with 45.6 billion transistors and 10,752 CUDA cores; and the performance GB205 (RTX 5070) with 31 billion transistors and 6,400 CUDA cores.

Researchers at Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis discovered that brown fat contains a backup heat-generation system involving peroxisomes, which can compensate when mitochondria lack uncoupling protein 1. In mice, peroxisomes multiplied during cold exposure and generated heat through acyl-CoA oxidase 2 (ACOX2). Mice without ACOX2 in brown fat had poorer cold tolerance, lower body temperatures, reduced insulin sensitivity, and increased weight gain on high-fat diets, whereas mice with elevated ACOX2 showed improved heat production, cold tolerance, insulin sensitivity, and weight control. The findings suggest that dietary interventions using specific fatty acids—present in dairy, breast milk, and produced by gut microbes—or drugs activating ACOX2 could potentially enhance this pathway to improve metabolic health and weight management in humans.
