The S&P 500 Equal Weight Index (EWI), created in 2003, comprises the same 500 U.S. companies as the traditional S&P 500 but assigns each stock an equal 0.2% weight at quarterly rebalances, rather than weighting by market capitalization. Consequently, sector weights depend on the number of constituent companies. The Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF (RSP) tracks the EWI, while the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) tracks the market-cap-weighted index. Historically, the equal-weight index has outperformed the market-weighted index due to the small-cap effect, wherein smaller companies often achieve higher growth rates. For example, from 2004 over 18 years, $10,000 invested in RSP grew to $60,000 compared to $55,000 for SPY, despite RSP's higher expense ratio (0.2% versus 0.0945%). Equal-weighting also provides more protection during downturns in large-cap stocks, though the ETFs require periodic rebalancing and can exhibit large daily return differentials during market turbulence.

Choked gamma-ray bursts occur when relativistic jets launched during core-collapse supernovae fail to escape the hydrogen-rich envelopes of Blue and Red Supergiants. These events can generate shock breakouts producing brief X-ray, ultraviolet, and optical transients, and act as candidate sources of TeV–PeV neutrinos and ultra-high-energy cosmic rays, potentially explaining the lack of observed neutrino–GRB correlations and the diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux.

This work investigates jet propagation, shock formation, and cocoon dynamics using relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations performed with the PLUTO code. Continuous density profiles are adopted for the progenitors, and jet-head motion is numerically integrated across 39,000 one-dimensional models to estimate breakout and choking times, yielding linear scaling relations. Magnetized top-hat jets are injected with specified luminosity, opening angle, enthalpy, magnetization, and engine duration. A shock-finding algorithm identifies cells exhibiting converging flows, pressure jumps, aligned temperature and density gradients, and relativistic Mach numbers exceeding unity.

Preliminary results focus on a Blue Supergiant progenitor of 50 solar radii and 15 solar masses with a jet luminosity of 10^51 erg s^−1, initial Lorentz factor 7, and 5-second engine time. During injection, the jet head and cocoon produce external cocoon shocks, a termination shock, and an internal collimation shock. After engine shutdown, the collimation shock disappears, while the cocoon-driven forward shock accelerates into lower-density regions. For this configuration, the jet chokes approximately one minute after launch. Strong shocks develop in both the jet core and external cocoon, with dominant acceleration sites shifting outward following shutdown. Future work will extend the analysis to Red Supergiants and varied jet parameters to derive neutrino and electromagnetic spectra for multi-messenger observations.

The NVIDIA Turing architecture introduces significant advancements in memory, display, rendering, and AI. Its memory subsystem uses GDDR6 and larger L2 caches—TU102 features 6 MB, double that of Pascal’s GP102—along with improved lossless compression, yielding approximately 50% higher effective bandwidth than Pascal. Turing’s new display engine supports DisplayPort 1.4a for 8K at 60 Hz, HDR tone mapping, and USB-C/VirtualLink for simplified VR headset connectivity. Video engines include an enhanced NVENC supporting H.265 8K encode and an NVDEC supporting HEVC 4:4:4 and VP9 HDR.

For multi-GPU configurations, TU102 and TU104 use NVLink instead of older SLI bridges, providing up to 100 GB/s bidirectional bandwidth in TU102, though only two-way SLI is supported. Turing enables real-time ray tracing through dedicated RT Cores in TU102, TU104, and TU106, which accelerate BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection, making ray tracing roughly 10 times faster than Pascal. This supports a hybrid rendering model combining rasterization and ray tracing for reflections, shadows, and ambient occlusion.

Turing also introduces AI-based graphics enhancements via NGX and Tensor Cores, including Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS), which delivers quality comparable to or exceeding TAA with less shading work. Additional rendering features include Mesh Shading (Task and Mesh Shaders), Variable Rate Shading (VRS), Texture Space Shading (TSS), and Multi-View Rendering (MVR). The architecture is implemented across TU102 (e.g., RTX 2080 Ti), TU104 (e.g., RTX 2080, Tesla T4), and TU106 (e.g., RTX 2070), with TU106 lacking NVLink/SLI. A new RTX-OPS metric quantifies performance across the hybrid rendering workload.

Iain Stewart discusses the Sudakov form factor in SCET, noting that rapidity divergences require an additional regulator, nu, alongside dimensional regularization (mu). This necessitates a two-dimensional renormalization group in mu and nu space to sum large logarithms, as the hard, collinear, and soft modes live at different points in this space. Evolution kernels connect these modes, and the renormalization exhibits path independence in the mu-nu plane. Anomalous dimensions for mu and nu are derived from counter terms, with the nu anomalous dimension being finite after cancellations of poles. The framework is applied to Higgs production (gg to H) measuring the pT distribution, which involves rapidity divergences and SCET_2. The lecture then examines Drell-Yan production in three kinematic limits: inclusive (tau of order 1, yielding standard PDFs), endpoint (tau near 1, introducing a soft function), and isolated (constraining hemisphere momenta to be small, yielding beam functions). Beam functions are matrix elements of collinear operators measuring both large and small momentum components; they can be further factorized into perturbative matching coefficients and standard non-perturbative PDFs.

The lecture reviews that under AWGN and equiprobable signals, the minimum distance decoder is equivalent to the maximum likelihood and MAP decoders. Error probability is estimated by the union bound, $P_e \approx K_{\min} Q(d_{\min}/2\sigma)$. Effective coding gain ($\gamma_f$) is defined as the gap between a signal set and the baseline scheme (2-PAM for power-limited, M-PAM for bandwidth-limited) at a fixed probability of bit error of $10^{-5}$. It is approximated via the nominal coding gain $\gamma_c = d_{\min}^2/(4E_b)$ and the average nearest neighbors per information bit ($K_b$), using the rule of thumb $\gamma_f \approx \gamma_c - 0.2\log_2 K_b$ in dB. Examples show 4-QAM and a 2-point diagonal constellation have 0 dB effective gain, while a 4-point 3D constellation achieves roughly 1 dB. Orthogonal signal sets approach the Shannon limit as dimension $M$ increases, but their spectral efficiency vanishes and decoding complexity becomes exponential in the number of information bits, rendering them impractical. Simplex and bi-orthogonal sets are noted as related variants. For the bandwidth-limited regime, a similar framework applies using nearest neighbors per two dimensions ($K_s$). The lecture concludes with a preview of binary block codes, stating that separating binary coding from modulation incurs at most a 0.2 dB loss relative to the Shannon limit in the power-limited regime.

This study examined predictors of adherence to COVID-19 preventive behaviors among 15,131 Spanish residents during the first-wave lockdown (May–June 2020). Using data from the PSY-COVID survey, the study assessed sociodemographic, personality, cognitive, and social variables. Results indicated regional differences in post-confinement prevention intentions, with the Canary Islands showing the highest and Aragón and the Balearic Islands the lowest. A predictive linear mixed model identified self-efficacy, outcome expectations, and general adherence as the strongest predictors of future prevention behavior intention. Other significant factors included information level, prior experience, perceived vulnerability, proxy control in scientists, and social norms. Perceived severity moderated the effects of adherence to avoid infection and perceived vulnerability of others. Trust in scientists was high, whereas trust in the government was low. Region of residence exerted a small but statistically significant influence. The authors note limitations including online non-probabilistic sampling and some low internal consistency values. They recommend that public health authorities promote self-efficacy, maintain consistent communication, and address regional disparities to improve compliance.

Markov cohort-state-transition models depend on transition probability matrices (TPMs), which are challenging to estimate due to data limitations including multiple sources, unequal observation intervals, and missing transitions. Craig and Sendi’s uniform expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm for unequal intervals may increase within-state-transition variance and unnecessarily impact probabilistic sensitivity analysis. This paper proposes an optimized, weighted EM algorithm that assigns weights to estimated one-step transition count matrices to minimize output variance, drawing on best linear unbiased estimator theory. A computational grid search identifies optimal weights for a chosen function—such as the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER)—using bootstrapping to estimate uncertainty. In a proof-of-concept three-state model comparing a fictitious "SuperDrug" against placebo with 1-, 2-, and 3-month transition counts, the method reduced ICER variance by 15.2% and increased the probability of cost-effectiveness at £20,000/QALY by three percentage points, while maintaining similar means. The authors caution that the method is appropriate primarily for similar data sources to avoid bias, and they recommend further real-world validation.

The document describes AMD's Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine, an optional extension to SEV and SNP for page migration between memory tiers. TMPM requires IOMMU enablement and allows the hypervisor or operating system to migrate pages between system physical addresses while maintaining guest physical addresses. It supports migration of pages during concurrent DMA operations using the PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO command and migration of SNP-protected guest pages using the PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST command. The engine supports multi-page commands for up to 128 pages, defines a Pre-Migration state for SNP guest pages, and provides per-page status entries. Performance is optimized by processing groups of pages and managing ring buffer commands. IOMMU host page tables, ring buffers, and other specific data structures cannot be migrated, and host software must avoid concurrent modifications to referenced IOMMU host page table entries during TMPM operations.

Thailand's frozen food market is expected to register a 5.9% CAGR from 2017 to 2022, supported by an increasing number of trading partners and strong export demand for processed seafood and meat from Japan, Australia, China, Korea, the US, the EU, and the Middle East. Domestic growth is driven by rising demand from hotels, restaurants, hospitals, and quick service joints. The market is further driven by increasing usage of canned foods and online retailing, and covers frozen seafood and meat, ice cream and desserts, ready-to-eat meals, and processed fruits and vegetables.

CEZ will buy back nearly all its 2017 convertible bonds linked to MOL shares by selling most of its 7.5 percent stake in the Hungarian group, retaining about 0.1 percent. The paper presents a multi-criteria integer programming model for the Ambulance Location Problem to optimize station locations in a rural German region. The model maximizes population reachability within two response time thresholds (r1 = 5 and r2 = 10 minutes) while ensuring full coverage within a maximum allowed time (r3 = 15 minutes). It was applied to a real-world case study in Rhineland-Palatinate, optimizing four new stations among 17 potential sites across a study area of 70 municipalities and over 450,000 inhabitants, using a detailed road network with custom ambulance speed profiles. The analysis identified 16 Pareto-optimal solutions, revealing a trade-off: maximizing short-term (5-minute) coverage concentrates stations in urban centers, whereas maximizing longer-term (10-minute) coverage distributes stations more evenly into rural areas. The static model results served as an initial decision-support stage for political decision-makers, with promising locations subsequently evaluated through expert consultation and discrete-event simulation. The authors suggest future extensions incorporating investment costs and multiple vehicle coverage.

A short squeeze occurs when a heavily shorted stock's price rises unexpectedly, forcing short sellers to buy back shares at higher prices to cover their positions, further driving the price upward. These events are rare, typically last two to four weeks, and can inflict theoretically unlimited losses on short sellers. Notable historical examples include Volkswagen in 2008 and GameStop in 2021. While natural short squeezes are legal, manipulating prices or stock availability to cause one is illegal; naked short selling is also illegal. The opposite event is a long squeeze, where significant price declines force short sellers to cover. Predicting or backtesting short squeeze strategies is practically impossible, and stocks with high short interest generally underperform. An exit strategy involves monitoring price momentum and short interest while using stop-loss or trailing stop orders. Although short selling is difficult and risky, incorporating short strategies can add diversification to a trading portfolio.

The document outlines the statistical analysis plan for a clinical trial. Plasma glucose is measured at specified pre-dose and post-dose time points with defined allowable deviations. This study investigates resting-state directional connectivity in 43 drug-resistant focal epilepsy patients using stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) to localize the seizure onset zone (SOZ) and predict seizure outcomes without prolonged ictal recordings. The authors analyzed 10-minute interictal resting-state SEEG epochs using directed transfer function (DTF) for within-frequency connectivity, cross-frequency directionality (CFD) for cross-frequency interactions, 1/f power slope analysis for excitation-inhibition balance, and balanced random forest classifiers for prediction. Results showed dominant information flow from non-SOZ to SOZ across multiple frequencies. SOZ electrodes exhibited significantly higher inward but similar outward information flow compared to non-SOZ. Cross-frequency analysis revealed dominant flow from non-SOZ high-frequency activity to SOZ low-frequency activity. SOZ regions displayed significantly more negative 1/f power slopes than non-SOZ, probably reflecting higher excitability in non-SOZ. Larger within-frequency asymmetry—weaker SOZ-to-non-SOZ and stronger non-SOZ-to-SOZ flow—was associated with favorable Engel I seizure outcomes. The random forest classifier achieved an AUC of 0.94 and accuracy of 0.85 for SOZ prediction, and an AUC of 0.78 with 77% accuracy for seizure outcome prediction. The authors conclude that resting-state connectivity analysis combined with machine learning can identify SOZ and predict outcomes from brief recordings, supplementing traditional SEEG interpretation and potentially reducing hospitalization time. Limitations include using clinical SOZ as a proxy for the epileptogenic zone, reliance on short artifact-free epochs, and exclusion of clinical variables from outcome models.

The professor states he will not repeat discrete coding and invites questions. He announces a problem set due October 14 comprising problems 1 through 7, material from the end of lectures 8 to 10, and problem 26.

He then discusses Riemann versus Lebesgue integration. Riemann integration partitions the independent variable axis into intervals and approximates the function within each, which fails for irregular functions. Lebesgue integration partitions the dependent axis into slices and uses the "measure" (size) of the set of points where the function falls into each slice. When a Riemann integral exists, the Lebesgue integral gives the same result, but Lebesgue also applies to functions for which Riemann integration fails. This is necessary because transformations between time and frequency domains in communication theory can yield irregular functions, and random processes inherently involve such functions.

The lecture covers measure theory: the measure of an interval [a,b] is b minus a; the measure of a countable union of disjoint intervals is the sum of their measures; and subsets of zero-measure sets also have zero measure. The rational numbers between 0 and 1 are countable and have measure zero. An uncountable set with measure zero is also constructed by removing ternary expansions containing the digit 1.

A function is measurable if the set of times for which its value lies in any given interval is measurable. For non-negative measurable functions, the Lebesgue integral always exists as either a finite value or infinity. For example, a function that is 1 on rationals and 0 on irrationals has a Lebesgue integral of zero.

The professor defines L1 functions as measurable functions with a finite integral of absolute value, and L2 functions as measurable with a finite integral of squared magnitude. A time-limited L2 function is also L1. For time-limited L2 functions, Fourier coefficients exist, and the Fourier series converges in the "limit in the mean" (l.i.m.), meaning the energy of the approximation error goes to zero as more terms are added. Any set of coefficients with finite energy corresponds to an L2 function.

He concludes that arbitrary L2 functions can be segmented into time-limited intervals and expanded into Fourier series on each segment, which conceptually underlies voice compression algorithms. He contrasts this with the Fourier integral, which he will address next.

The paper presents a variadic nominal anti-unification (VNAU) algorithm that computes least general generalizations for variadic nominal terms, which combine binders with variadic expressions. Motivated by applications such as code clone detection, the technique addresses limitations of existing methods by handling bound variable renaming, scope, and structural differences like insertions and deletions. The rule-based algorithm operates on states containing anti-unification problems and applies transformation rules—including Tri-T, Tri-H, Dec-T, Dec-H, Abs-T, Sol-T, Sol-H, Mer, and Nar-T—to produce generalizations and difference information. It is parameterized by a finite set of atoms and a rigidity function to control the granularity of similarity. The authors prove that VNAU terminates, is sound, and complete. Examples demonstrate the encoding and analysis of type-2 and type-3 code clones, while the authors note limitations in efficiency due to high nondeterminism and exhaustive search.

This document describes AMD's Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine, which extends SEV and SNP to facilitate page migration between memory tiers. TMPM requires IOMMU enablement and is detected via the ENGINE_READY bit. It offloads page migration while pausing DMA during copy and IOMMU updates, and enables migration of SNP-protected guest pages. The PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO command migrates hypervisor pages with concurrent DMA, while PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST migrates SNP guest pages using a Pre-Migration state. Commands support up to 128 pages, with maximum performance at 128 pages per command. Non-migratable structures include IOMMU data structures, vIOMMU buffers, and the ring buffer. Source pages must be DMA-mapped via IOMMU host page tables. TMPM firmware can be reloaded via the BIOS-to-PSP mailbox when operations are paused, with EPYC family-specific procedures determined via PM_GET_CAPABILITIES. For debugging, software should not advance the ring buffer tail more than one command beyond the head.

The article examines artificial intelligence use in Hungarian education through interviews with 14 teachers and university lecturers and questionnaires from 53 university students. While 91% expressed positive attitudes toward AI integration in education, respondents noted risks including easier exam cheating, excessive reliance, impaired learning effectiveness, and undermined critical thinking. The study also evaluated ChatGPT, Bard/Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot on programming tasks. ChatGPT achieved the highest accuracy (92%) on beginner tasks requiring programming theorems and successfully completed all complex tasks after additional prompting, whereas Gemini and Copilot showed lower accuracy on basic tasks and failed to provide fully correct solutions for some complex assignments. The authors conclude that although AI tools are increasingly present in education and viewed favorably, their effectiveness remains limited by incorrect or incomplete responses, making them most useful for users who possess sufficient prior subject knowledge and critical thinking skills.

The ADS868xW device communicates via a multiSPI interface synchronous to the SCLK pin. Data writes require a minimum of 32 SCLK cycles and execute at the rising edge of CONVST/CS. The interface supports legacy SPI-compatible protocols (SPI-00-S through SPI-11-S, defaulting to SPI-00-S and selected via the SDI_CTL_REG register), dual SDO-x mode, and source-synchronous (SRC) protocols where the RVS pin provides the output clock. Input commands support byte and half-word (HWORD) read and write operations; for HWORD commands, the LSB of the 9-bit address is ignored. Output data for frame F+1 is determined by the command in frame F and the DATA_VAL bits, and can include appended flags controlled by the DATAOUT_CTL_REG register. The device contains nine configuration registers mapped across byte addresses, including registers for device ID, reset and power-down control (RST_PWRCTL_REG, which requires writing 69h to address 05h to unlock), SPI and SDO protocol configuration, output data flags, input range selection, and alarm thresholds with hysteresis. As a 16-bit SAR ADC with an integrated analog front-end and reference, it is designed for industrial data acquisition modules and supports programmable input and AVDD alarms. The device uses separate AVDD and DVDD supplies, requires specific decoupling capacitors on each supply and reference pins, and offers NAP and power-down modes for power savings. PCB layout requires separating analog and digital signals and placing bypass capacitors close to the supply pins.

This study investigates human-AI interactions in conversational information-seeking with ChatGPT, examining how users employ prompting strategies, how ChatGPT adapts its communication styles to issue controversy and user prompts, and how these responses shape user perceptions and attitudes. Using a 3 (issue: health, science, policy) × 2 (controversial, non-controversial) between-subjects experiment with 937 U.S. adults interacting with GPT-4o, the researchers extracted five communication styles (self-revealing, information-seeking, fact-oriented, action-seeking, cognitive complexity), citation and structure counts, and annotated eight prompting strategies using ChatGPT, validated by human coders (IRR = .814, weighted F1 = 0.903). Key findings indicate that 19.1% of users employed at least one prompting strategy, predicted by education level and party affiliation; issue controversy drove ChatGPT response styles and citation counts while user prompt styles remained consistent; and greater cognitive complexity in ChatGPT responses led to less favorable AI perceptions but more positive issue-relevant attitude changes.

The TPS7H500x-SP datasheet describes external fault protection via the FAULT pin, which triggers shutdown when the voltage exceeds 0.6 V (typical) for a pulse width between 0.4 µs and 1.4 µs, and recovers after the voltage falls below 0.5 V (typical) followed by a delay of approximately 15 switching cycles. Slope compensation, configured with a resistor on the RSC pin, prevents subharmonic oscillation; the recommended value equals the inductor falling current slope. Frequency compensation uses Type 2A or 2B networks connected to the COMP pin. Thermal shutdown halts switching above 175°C (typical) and resumes below 160°C (typical). The controllers use fixed-frequency peak current mode control and are radiation-hardness-assured for space-grade DC-DC converter designs up to 2 MHz, supporting topologies such as buck, flyback, forward, and push-pull when paired with external gate drivers. A detailed design example for a 500 kHz synchronous push-pull converter using GaN devices specifies a 5 V output, a 205 kΩ RT resistor, 20.5 kΩ dead-time resistors for approximately 25 ns, a 49.9 kΩ leading edge blank resistor for roughly 50 ns, a 33 nF soft-start capacitor yielding about 7.5 ms, a transformer turns ratio of 2.5 with 40 µH primary inductance, 170 V primary and 80 V secondary GaN FETs, a 0.47 µH output inductor, approximately 2.3 mF of output capacitance for single-event transient mitigation, a 7.5 Ω current sense resistor, a 3.3 nF hiccup capacitor, Type 2A compensation components of 40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, and 47 pF, and a 102 kΩ slope compensation resistor. The controller operates from a 4 V to 14 V input and requires a minimum 0.1 µF bypass capacitor. Layout guidelines recommend separating analog and power grounds at a single point, minimizing high di/dt and dv/dt loops, placing bypass and compensation capacitors close to the controller, routing the feedback trace away from noise sources, keeping the VSENSE divider near the device, isolating high dv/dt output traces from sensitive pins, and connecting the CFP package backside metallization to the AVSS plane.

The passage describes systems, methods, and computer-readable media for automatically generating orthodontic treatment plans using a database of user or user group preferences. The database is created by identifying reference key preference text statements corresponding to clinical behaviors and matching them to user-specific text instructions from historical treatment data using machine learning agents—such as Bag of Words—and/or similarity searching techniques like Damerau-Levenshtein distance. Alternatively, statistical preference analysis identifies consistently applied clinical behaviors over time via clustering models to determine recent stable preferences. Each database entry links a user-specific textual key preference, the associated user, and the corresponding clinical behavior. Upon receiving a digital model of a patient’s dentition and new treatment instructions, a treatment planning engine automatically generates a treatment plan by matching phrases in the instructions to the database and incorporating the relevant clinical behaviors. Monitoring tools track the performance of automatically applied preferences and facilitate updates to the database, reducing manual steps and iterative corrections in treatment planning.

Centana Growth Partners raised $250 million for its first fund to invest in financial services startups. Founded in 2015 by Eric Byunn, Steven Swain, and Ben Cukier, it has invested in four companies including One and Jumio, and expects to invest $5 million to $30 million in additional candidates.

The S&P 500 rose 2.2% in July and is up 7.8% year-to-date, but started August poorly. Medium- and long-term trends remain healthy, though short-term technicals look tenuous as volatility and credit spreads rise seasonally and 50-day breadth rolls over from overbought levels. Investors are increasing tech allocations, and U.S. electricity demand hit an all-time high. Gold climbed above $4,000/oz; Goldman Sachs says stocks are not yet in a bubble; the Bank of England warned of a sharp correction if AI or Fed confidence wanes; and an analyst expects the U.S. government shutdown to last into next week but not beyond.

The NVIDIA A100 GPU features third-generation Tensor Cores supporting FP16, FP32, TF32, BF16, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary formats, delivering up to 312 TFLOPS of dense mixed-precision FP16/FP32 performance and 19.5 TFLOPS of FP64—2.5× that of Tesla V100. It introduces TF32 to accelerate AI training without code changes, and Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity using a 2:4 pattern that doubles inferencing throughput by skipping zero values. The A100 includes 108 SMs, 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache, and combined L1 data cache/shared memory. Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) can partition the GPU into up to seven isolated instances for quality-of-service and fault isolation. The architecture also implements third-generation NVLink with 600 GB/sec total bandwidth, PCIe Gen 4, hardware-accelerated NVJPG decode and optical flow, and CUDA 11 advances including asynchronous copy, task graphs, asynchronous barriers, and L2 cache residency controls. The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs via NVSwitch to deliver 5 PFLOPS of AI performance.

Convalescent plasma plus best supportive care versus best supportive care; convalescent plasma versus SOC. Endpoints: WHO status at Days 15 and 30 and ventilation or death. Intent-to-treat Full Analysis Set excluded misdiagnosed or untreated patients withdrawing consent. Missing data imputed. Primary endpoint: logistic regression; mortality and MV/death: Cox regression; other outcomes: Fine and Gray models.

Obamacare affects nearly all Americans, including Medicare beneficiaries, workers with employer-sponsored insurance, individual market enrollees, and Medicaid recipients. President-elect Trump and Republicans have vowed to repeal most of the law, except possibly the provision allowing children under 26 to stay on parents' plans. Repeal would likely raise Medicare premiums, deductibles, and cost-sharing for 57 million enrollees, reinstate the prescription drug "donut hole," and eliminate free preventive benefits, though higher-income seniors might see reduced surcharges. The employer mandate would end, potentially causing some workers to lose coverage, while free preventive services, bans on annual and lifetime limits, and out-of-pocket spending caps would disappear. Employees at small companies could lose protections for pre-existing conditions and age-based premium limits. In the individual market, repeal would end exchange subsidies, essential benefit requirements, and limits on out-of-pocket costs and age rating. Medicaid expansion in 31 states and the District of Columbia, which added nearly 17 million people, would end, leaving millions uninsured. The individual mandate and its penalties would also be eliminated.

In this lecture, Hong Liu outlines course logistics: no textbook or recitation, office hours on Mondays, materials online, no exams, and grades determined by five problem sets (75%) and a final project (25%). He then introduces holographic duality, noting that while electromagnetism, weak, and strong interactions are understood as gauge theories in fixed spacetime, a quantum theory of gravity remains elusive. A 1997 proposal posits that quantum gravity is equivalent to ordinary quantum field theories on fixed spacetime—different descriptions of the same quantum system. Liu discusses earlier speculations about gravity emerging from other systems, such as Sakharov’s ideas and hydrodynamic analogies, and the hope of generating massless spin-2 particles from lower-spin theories. This was ruled out by the 1980 Weinberg-Witten theorem, which states that theories with a Lorentz-covariant conserved current or stress tensor cannot contain massless particles of spin greater than 1/2 or 1, respectively, in the same spacetime. Holographic duality circumvents this because the gravity lives in a higher-dimensional spacetime. Liu concludes by sketching the theorem’s proof using Lorentz symmetry, helicity, and rotation operators.

This protocol describes BioRecall, a pilot biobank-recall study inviting approximately 1,386 previously genotyped Central Finland Biobank donors with type 2 diabetes to complete an electronic questionnaire via the MyBiobank portal. The study collects data on lifestyles, environmental exposures, anthropometrics, health, symptoms, work characteristics, emotional state, sleep, and residential environment, which will be combined with existing genotype, biological sample, and clinical outcome data to investigate non-communicable disease risk and gene-environment interactions. Postcode information will allow linkage to spatial environmental data. Using pseudonymized IDs, survey data will be linked to biobank registry data without collecting directly identifiable information. The study is approved by the University of Jyväskylä Human Sciences Ethics Committee and Central Finland Biobank. Strengths include a low-cost, scalable, fully electronic design, automated participant feedback relative to national lifestyle recommendations, and innovative physical activity assessments. Limitations are the pilot's limited sample size, inclusion of only one biobank, and lack of wearable data. Data collection begins in February 2025; if successful, the study will expand to other donors and Finnish biobanks.

The Chicago Cubs defeated the Pittsburgh Pirates 7-0 on May 28, 2018. Anthony Rizzo hit his seventh home run and a two-run single, but his hard slide into catcher Elias Diaz in the eighth inning overshadowed the game. The slide upended Diaz, caused a wild throw that allowed two runs, and prompted debate over its legality. The call stood upon review, though Pirates manager Clint Hurdle was ejected for arguing. Cubs manager Joe Maddon defended the play as legal, while Diaz and Hurdle called it dangerous. Spot starter Mike Montgomery, replacing injured Yu Darvish, pitched 5 2/3 scoreless innings with five strikeouts. The Cubs arrived in Pittsburgh at 4 a.m. following a Sunday night game in Chicago.

In late 2006, Sony CEO Howard Stringer faced the imminent worldwide launch of the PlayStation 3 (PS3), priced at $599, while Microsoft’s Xbox 360 held a significant sales lead and Nintendo’s Wii, launching two days later at half the price, targeted a broader mainstream audience. The PS3 was also central to Sony’s effort to win the next-generation optical disc standards war for Blu-Ray against Toshiba’s HD-DVD, though Sony had previously failed to establish proprietary formats such as Betamax and UMD. The U.S. video game industry had grown to nearly $10.5 billion in 2005, evolving over three decades from Atari’s market collapse in 1983 to Nintendo’s resurgence with strict quality and licensing controls, and then to Sony’s dominance with the CD-based PlayStation in 1994 and the DVD-playing PS2 in 2000, which commanded a 55% market share by early 2006. Console manufacturers typically sold hardware at a loss and profited from software royalties; rising development costs, reaching over $5 million per title for the PS2, drove publishers to acquire independent development studios. The new console generation made Internet connectivity central, with Microsoft’s Xbox Live providing a unified broadband service, Sony’s PlayStation Network Platform offering an open ecosystem, and Nintendo’s Wii introducing motion controls and classic game downloads via its Virtual Console. While Sony and Microsoft pursued core gamers, Nintendo sought to expand the market with intuitive, casual-friendly games. The industry simultaneously confronted public and political pressure over violent game content, leading to the 1994 establishment of the ESRB and proposed federal legislation such as the Family Entertainment Protection Act in 2005. Despite competitive and pricing hurdles, some analysts forecast that the PS3 would account for over 50% of the next-generation console installed base by 2010.

DNA origami self-assembles nanostructures from a scaffold strand and shorter staple strands. A team led by Ralf Jungmann reports that DNA-PAINT super-resolution microscopy visualizes individual strands within these structures. The technique uses transiently binding, dye-linked imager strands that produce a blinking signal, enabling localization of staple strands and detection of unoccupied sites. While assembly is robust under varying conditions, staple strand incorporation efficiency depends on the precise position of its target sequence, so not all sites are occupied in every structure. The researchers recommend using excess components and selecting positions based on incorporation efficiency to optimize nanomachine assembly. The technology also has potential for quantitative structural biology.

The filing includes exhibits containing the press release and information on non-GAAP financial measures. Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, signed the report.

This paper studies modal extensions of lattice semantics, using lattices such as Łukasiewicz algebras, Belnap lattices, or Boolean algebras with more than two values as alternatives to the classical two-valued Boolean algebra for interpreting non-modal connectives. The necessity operator is interpreted as the greatest lower bound of values in accessible worlds. The authors define regular modal extensions, where necessity means truth in all accessible worlds, and normal modal valuations. They prove that for a complete lattice and designated values F, the normal modal valuation yields a unique regular modal extension if and only if the meet of F belongs to F and F is a filter; for finite lattices, regularity holds if and only if F is a filter. The paper then examines how modal formulas characterize lattice properties: a set of designated values F is implicative if and only if every frame validates (□ϕ ∨ □ψ) → □(ϕ ∨ ψ). For axiom K, if implication is strictly deductive, linearity of the lattice outside the filter is equivalent to every frame satisfying K. If implication is defined as −x+y, then anti-monotonicity, down-distribution, and the implicative property yield K, and with involutive negation this becomes an equivalence. An application to twist algebras shows that a filter contains all elements with first coordinate 1 if and only if every frame satisfies K. The authors conclude that lattice-based modal logics provide a natural foundation for cross-logical communication and identify the finite-model property as a direction for future computational applications.

South Carolina women's golfers Katelyn Dambaugh, Ainhoa Olarra, and Ana Pelaez earned Golfweek All-America honors, with Dambaugh named to the First Team and Olarra and Pelaez recognized as Honorable Mention. Dambaugh set a program record with five career All-America honors and finished as the school's all-time scoring average leader. Olarra posted five top-10 finishes and ranked second on the team in stroke average. Pelaez recorded a historic freshman season with a school-record 73.12 scoring average and medalist honors at the NCAA Columbus Regional. The MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 technical document details power, clock, memory, peripheral, and debug features. The Power Management Unit generates internally regulated core supplies, monitors the external VDD supply with a brown-out reset using programmable thresholds, and provides a core regulator supporting RUN, SLEEP, STOP, and STANDBY modes. The Clock Module provides internal and external oscillators ranging from 32kHz to 32MHz and distributes system clocks—including MCLK, CPUCLK, ULPCLK, MFCLK, LFCLK, ADCCLK, HFCLK, HSCLK, and CLK_OUT—each active in specific power modes.

The DMA_B controller supports two full-feature channels and one basic channel for data movement without CPU intervention, with direct triggers from ADC, UART, SPI, and timers. It supports 8-bit, 16-bit, and 32-bit transfers up to 64k blocks, configurable triggers, and advanced modes including stride and gather. An event manager routes static CPU interrupts, DMA triggers, and generic hardware events between peripherals via a fabric of static and programmable routes.

The devices include nonvolatile flash memory with 1KB sector sizes and up to 100,000 program/erase cycles on 32 selected sectors, or across the entire flash for 32kB devices. SRAM provides zero wait-state access, retains content in RUN, SLEEP, STOP, and STANDBY modes, and offers 1KB-resolution write protection. Up to 45 GPIO pins are supported with wake capabilities, managed by an IOMUX with programmable drive strength, speed, pullup/pulldown, and pin muxing.

Analog peripherals include a 12-bit ADC with up to 1.6-Msps conversion and 10.6-bit ENOB using an external reference, an internal temperature sensor with a factory single-point calibration value, a shared configurable 1.4V or 2.5V voltage reference, and a comparator supporting blanking from timers, wake from low-power modes, and an 8-bit reference DAC output. The Low-Frequency Sub-System contains a real-time clock with calendar, alarm, and calibration features, plus an independent watchdog timer with its own clock and power source.

Additional peripherals include UARTs with LIN mode, I2C supporting Standard, Fast, and Fast-mode Plus up to 1Mbps, SPI supporting up to 16Mbits/s, a windowed watchdog timer, and general-purpose and advanced timers with PWM, QEI, synchronization, and cross-trigger capabilities. Security features include flexible firewalls and a CRC-16 module. The debug subsystem provides an Arm-compatible two-wire SWD interface with on-chip termination, software-configurable peripheral behavior during debug halt, and a mailbox for software communication.

Factory constants memory provides read-only device identification and trim information. Application guidance recommends 10µF and 0.1µF low-ESR ceramic decoupling capacitors on VDD and VSS, a 47kΩ pullup resistor and 1000pF pulldown capacitor on the NRST pin, and pullup resistors for 5V-tolerant open-drain IOs. The September 2025 revision removed DGS32 package information and updated specifications for power modes, thermal characteristics, supply current, timing, clock, ADC, temperature sensor, VREF, SPI, TIMx, CPU features, and the DEBUGSS section.

MIT Professor Joe Hadzima introduces guest speaker Bob Jones, a serial entrepreneur, to discuss business planning and finding customers. The professor recaps prior lessons: planning is dynamic, goals are to create and harvest value, and investors ask “Why this? Why now? Why this team? Why won’t it work?” Jones argues that the only non-negotiable requirement for business success is having customers, and entrepreneurs must identify who will pay, what they truly want, and what motivates them.

Jones illustrates this with two product launches. His first, Regain—a nutrition bar for dialysis patients—failed because he surveyed clinicians rather than the actual purchasers (patients), who were often on public aid, unwilling to change habits, and unable to afford the product. He also underestimated retail slotting fees. His second, NiteBite—a timed-release glucose bar for diabetics to prevent nocturnal hypoglycemia—succeeded because he identified the true customer and emotional need (peace of mind), used a non-medical name to reduce stigma, leveraged Certified Diabetes Educators as influencers, built consumer demand first, and used that demand to enter retail and wholesale channels without paying slotting fees. The company achieved strong growth and was sold to a billion-dollar pharmaceutical firm.

Jones concludes that entrepreneurs must do “detective work” by talking directly to potential customers, testing bare-bones prototypes before formal branding, focusing on a motivated customer segment, and selling benefits rather than features.

The Relist Watch column reviews Supreme Court cert petitions relisted for conference. The court denied several petitions early in the term, including a death-penalty case on ineffective appellate counsel (over a Sotomayor dissent joined by Kagan and Jackson), a Seventh Amendment incorporation case (accompanied by a Gorsuch opinion), and a case on school districts concealing students’ transgender identity from parents (accompanied by an Alito opinion joined by Thomas and Gorsuch). Denials also included a Section 230 immunity petition and two “lost causes” involving FDA cell-processing rules and California unclaimed property law, both without recorded dissent.

New relists include multiple challenges to 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(3), which prohibits firearm possession by unlawful users of controlled substances; the Fifth and Eighth Circuits held the statute unconstitutional as applied, and the government is seeking review. In *Keathley v. Buddy Ayers Construction*, the Fifth Circuit applied a strict judicial estoppel rule to bar a debtor’s undisclosed personal injury claim, creating a split with circuits that use a flexible, intent-based approach; the author considers this a strong candidate for grant. Four additional new relists are pro se prisoner petitions raising procedural claims, including whether Elon Musk can be criminally prosecuted for drug transactions on Twitter. Numerous other relisted cases raise issues spanning the First Step Act, Title VII religious accommodations, the Feres doctrine, qualified immunity, Sixth Amendment confrontation and public-trial rights, tribal criminal jurisdiction, January 6 dismissals, Batson challenges, and AEDPA deference.

Modeling noisy, high-dimensional, nonlinear dynamical systems from data can be approached via transfer operator theory and reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHS). Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) discretizes the infinite-dimensional Koopman operator to globally linearize systems, enabling analysis of nonlinear and stochastic dynamics through linear regression and eigenvalue decomposition. Gaussian process (GP) regression provides a non-parametric, probabilistic kernel framework for function approximation. The authors combine GP regression with DMD by developing a Bayesian interpretation of the embedded Perron–Frobenius operator, yielding a modification of Extended DMD that constructs models from noisy measurement data and provides uncertainty estimates for multi-step predictions. To address the O(N³) cost of kernel-based DMD, they apply the variational free energy method, seeking a trade-off between generalization error and computational complexity through a unified Bayesian framework that simultaneously handles hyperparameter optimization, sparse dictionary learning, and measurement noise. The approach employs an operator-valued kernel to extend GP regression to an RKHS target space with infinite output channels, treating the embedded operator as a random variable.

The American Indian College Fund announced a two-year study funded by a $600,000 Strada Education Network grant to measure the economic and social impact of five North Dakota tribal colleges and universities on graduate well-being. Conducted with the North Dakota Association of Tribal Colleges and Gallup, the project will analyze graduate employment, survey 5,000 scholars on education rooted in Native American values, and pilot research on language and cultural preservation. The project concludes in September 2019, and results will be shared with state and federal policymakers.

An Atomic Cluster Expansion (ACE) machine learning potential was developed for YBa₂Cu₃O₇₋ₓ (YBCO) using density functional theory (DFT) data that includes defects, disordered configurations, and transition states. The potential predicts energies and forces with root-mean-square errors of approximately 10 meV/atom and 70 meV/Å, and it outperforms existing classical Buckingham+Coulomb potentials in describing the equation of state, lattice parameters far from equilibrium, and oxygen Frenkel pair migration barriers and formation energies. Molecular dynamics simulations with the ACE potential reproduced the orthorhombic-to-tetragonal transition at approximately 800 K, in reasonable agreement with the experimental transition near 1000 K. The transition is an entropy-driven order-disorder process in which oxygen atoms migrate from CuO chain (O1) and apical (O4) sites to interstitial O5 positions in the basal plane, rendering the a and b directions equivalent; this disordering is facilitated by a decrease in oxygen Frenkel pair formation energy at thermally expanded lattice parameters. The results demonstrate that machine learning potentials can capture complex defect physics and structural transitions in quaternary oxide superconductors, enabling predictive simulations of mass transport, degradation, and recovery in high-temperature superconducting materials under radiation-harsh conditions.

This non-empirical literature review examines the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on inclusive education, synthesizing literature from September 2023 to March 2024 following PRISMA guidelines. AI facilitates teaching, learning, and instructional design by personalizing learning, providing feedback, offering assistive features, and automating administrative tasks. Inclusive education seeks to provide equal opportunities for all students regardless of disability, ethnicity, or background, yet faces barriers including inadequate infrastructure, overcrowded classes, educator unpreparedness, incompatible digital materials, and labeling. AI enhances student engagement, adaptive learning, and equity but cannot replace human educators, as it lacks consciousness, emotions, and full creative capacity. Limitations include potential data bias, high implementation costs, privacy and security concerns, over-reliance on technology, and possible physical harm from devices. The discussion highlights inclusive syllabus design, Universal Design for Learning, assistive technology, and flexible access to materials. Acknowledging its non-empirical nature and general focus, the study recommends further empirical research. It concludes that AI supports inclusive education but requires careful implementation, and recommends integrating AI into child-centered teaching, providing continuous professional development for educators, and promoting inclusive policies and safe learning environments.

The lecture compares ion traps to neutral atom traps, noting that while much physics is similar, the Coulomb force enables far stronger confinement for ions using electric fields. Applications for both include atomic clocks, quantum simulation, and quantum information processing. Ions cannot be held in static electric potentials; instead, they are confined in dynamic traps such as Penning traps, which use magnetic fields for radial confinement, or RF (Paul) traps. Paul traps alternate rapidly between confining and anti-confining potentials; the resulting micromotion rectifies into a net restoring force for the slower secular motion, with the micromotion’s kinetic energy acting as the trap’s potential energy. The lecture details quantum computation with ions, focusing on the Cirac-Zoller two-qubit gate. In this scheme, the center-of-mass phonon mode serves as a data bus: the quantum state of a control ion is swapped onto the phonon, a controlled phase operation is performed on a target ion, and the state is swapped back. Although foundational, this gate requires extreme ground-state cooling and is difficult to scale, leading to the adoption of newer gate schemes such as geometric or Sørensen gates.

This study investigated race differences in the relationship between blood pressure (BP) and longitudinal cognitive performance using data from 2,284 Black and White participants aged 55 and older across three harmonized cohort studies (MARS, MAP, and Black Clinical Core). Participants were classified into normal, high, or variable BP groups based on mean systolic BP and variability, and were assessed across five cognitive domains plus global function. Linear mixed effects models revealed no racial differences in cognitive decline among individuals with normal BP. However, White adults with high BP exhibited significantly faster decline in global cognition, perceptual speed, semantic memory, and working memory compared to Black adults with high BP, with similar rates in episodic memory and visuospatial abilities. White adults with variable BP showed significantly faster decline in global cognition and all five cognitive domains compared to Black adults with variable BP. Secondary analyses indicated these differences were not attributable to lower baseline cognitive scores in Black participants. The authors suggest maintaining healthy BP may eliminate race-related cognitive disparities and propose that chronic stress, allostatic load, or autonomic nervous system factors may explain the reduced cognitive impact of BP fluctuations in Black adults. Limitations include the lack of data on medication adherence and comprehensive medication history.

Judges are imposing fines on attorneys for faulty AI-generated citations in legal briefs. In Puerto Rico, several law firms will share $24,492 in fees after opposing counsel filed motions with at least 55 defective citations. In California, lawyer Amir Mostafavi must pay $10,000 to the court for fake AI-generated content in appellate briefs; opposing counsel was denied fees because they failed to detect the errors, raising questions about lawyers' duty to identify fabricated citations in opponents' filings.

Charlie Javice, founder of the student financial aid startup Frank, was sentenced to 85 months in prison for defrauding JPMorgan Chase, which acquired Frank for $175 million in 2021. A jury found Javice and chief growth officer Olivier Amar guilty of three fraud counts and one conspiracy count for overstating customer numbers; Frank had fewer than 300,000 real customers, with the rest being synthetic identities. Judge Alvin Hellerstein imposed the sentence on September 29, 2025, also ordering three years of supervision, $22.36 million in forfeiture, and $287 million in restitution to JPMorgan. Javice, 33, expressed remorse and will remain on bail pending appeal. Prosecutors had sought 12 years, while her attorney requested a lighter sentence than Elizabeth Holmes’s. JPMorgan did not verify Frank’s customer count before the acquisition.

An ETF rotation strategy rotates monthly among SPY, TLT, and EEM, holding the previous month's top performer. Over two decades, it beat "buy and hold" with lower drawdowns and an 11% CAGR, but the portfolio fell 41% from its peak in 2022 and performance has declined over the last 5-6 years. Entry and exit occur at monthly closes without commissions or slippage, and the strategy is best suited for tax-deferred accounts.

A crack in the Forties Pipeline System has forced operator Ineos to shut down the 450,000-barrel-per-day pipeline for weeks to carry out repairs. The system underpins the Brent crude benchmark, carries nearly 40 percent of UK North Sea oil production, and connects 85 offshore fields. Brent prices spiked nearly 2 percent to above $64.50 per barrel, a two-year high. The outage could disrupt up to 10 million barrels over three weeks, force North Sea operators to reduce production, and require the UK to purchase crude elsewhere. The shutdown widened the Brent-WTI price disparity to nearly $7 per barrel, which is expected to increase demand for U.S. crude exports, accelerate inventory draws, and create ripple effects across global oil markets.

National Eat at a Black Coffee Shop Day, organized by The Black Star Project, occurs May 29, 2018, while Starbucks closes over 8,000 stores for diversity training. Over 400 Black-owned coffee shops expect higher sales and aim to keep and grow market share. The event is part of the "Circulate Black Dollars in the Black Community" campaign to re-circulate dollars in Black communities. One hundred thirteen returning spellers, including finalists Erin Howard, 13, Cameron Keith, 12, and Naysa Modi, 12, are competing in the Scripps National Spelling Bee. The students devote several hours on weekdays and weekends to studying words. Howard, who misspelled the trademarked word "Klydonograph" last year, prepared more thoroughly for such words this time. Repeat competitors say experience reduces stress but can create pressure to match past results. The Court of Appeals affirmed a Saginaw Circuit Court divorce judgment awarding Wesley Wiechmann physical custody of the couple’s two older children and Sylvia Wiechmann physical custody of the two younger children, with shared legal custody. A custody specialist had recommended that all four children be placed with the defendant, but the trial court concluded that separation was in the best interests of each child after reviewing the statutory factors under MCL 722.23. The Court of Appeals held that while keeping siblings together is generally in a child’s best interests, the best interests of each individual child control, and separation is permissible if keeping siblings together is contrary to those interests. The court found that the trial court did not abuse its discretion or commit legal error. It also rejected the argument that the appeal was moot, noting that no permanent custody modification order was on record despite subsequent proceedings.

The Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) Specification describes AMD’s secure method for applying non-persistent runtime updates to AMD-provided firmware components—such as ASP firmware, modules, and register settings—without requiring a BIOS reflash or system reset. SFS does not patch x86 or run-once boot code, and updates do not persist across reboots, serving as interim measures between BIOS releases.

SFS uses three monotonically increasing version identifiers—SFS Patch Level (SFSPL), Security Patch Level (SPL), and System Patch Level (SYSPL)—to ensure updates apply only to correct firmware levels. AMD cryptographically signs all update packages, and customers may optionally co-sign them; the ASP verifies signatures before application. Customers must opt-in via BIOS settings, test and validate patches, and may provide a public co-signing key during early boot.

Updates are applied at runtime by a customer-provided SFS Deployment Agent through a TEE Extended Command Buffer and ASP mailbox interface. Packages must be applied sequentially, verify existing firmware versions to maintain resiliency, and are designed to execute with minimal performance impact alongside x86 and DMA traffic.

The COVID-19 pandemic forced a global shift to distance education, revealing the need for alternative and improved education systems. This literature review examines artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted and AI-based training as forms of distance education. AI systems, such as IBM’s Watson and Google’s autonomous vehicles, utilize algorithms, machine learning, deep learning, and artificial neural networks to perform tasks, analyze data, and learn independently. In education, AI applications include personalized teaching, student affairs, data management, and Intelligent Education Systems (IES), which integrate domain, pedagogy, and learner models to adapt instruction to individual needs. The study identifies three AI education types: AI-supported face-to-face instruction, face-to-face instruction delivered by AI via robots or screens, and simulation-based education in virtual environments. These may employ supervised learning, where humans design algorithms and curricula, or unsupervised deep learning, where AI independently develops personalized educational programs. Simulation environments may use virtual reality tools or, potentially, direct neural integration. The discussion notes that AI education could increase efficiency, reduce costs, enable mass individualized instruction, and eliminate classroom discipline issues. However, it also raises concerns regarding the loss of human social interaction, privacy and cybersecurity risks, educator unemployment, psychological and developmental effects, and the potential blurring of real and virtual realities. The authors conclude that while computing power has not yet reached human mental capacity, AI-based education is becoming increasingly viable, and stakeholders must seriously consider and prepare for a future where education may be entrusted to machines.

The S&P 500 fell 2.36% last week, closing at its lowest level since early July after dropping over 3% from Thursday's high, though futures indicate a Monday rebound toward 6,300. The VIX rose to 21.90, its highest since June 23, while the AAII survey reported 40.3% bullish and 33.0% bearish sentiment. Crude oil fell 2.79% Friday and another 2.1% after OPEC+ agreed to raise September output by 547,000 bpd, and the U.S. threatened 100% secondary tariffs on India and China regarding Russian crude. Goldman Sachs forecasts oil at $64 in Q4 2025. Analysts suggest the decline may represent consolidation or a potential topping pattern, warranting defensive positioning. Bitcoin trades above $123,000 below record highs, and an analyst set a $7 trillion target for NVIDIA.

Trump threatened 100% tariffs on China from November 1, causing US stocks to tumble. July jobs data missed expectations with only 73K gains and sharp downward revisions for May and June, while consumer spending remains negative for 2025. However, June data was largely positive and Q2 earnings are strong, with S&P 500 earnings growth at 11.2% and sales at 5.6%. The S&P 500 hit its 9.1% average annual return but faced a negative reaction entering the historically weak August–October period. The US dollar rallied to 2024 lows but was rejected after the tariff news and weak data. Despite high valuations and a slowing economy, recession is not certain, and near-term weakness could create year-end opportunities.

The Seattle Mariners beat the Texas Rangers 2-1 on May 28 for their ninth win in ten games and 16th one-run victory. Marco Gonzales pitched 6 2/3 scoreless innings, extending his earned-run-free streak to 19 1/3. Texas scored in the third when Rougned Odor bunted for a single and later scored on a passed ball. Seattle took the lead in the sixth after Odor bobbled a potential double-play grounder; Nelson Cruz and Kyle Seager followed with RBI singles. Alex Colome and Edwin Diaz worked together for the first time, with Diaz earning his 19th save. Denard Span debuted, going 0 for 4. Jean Segura was scratched after a head injury but may return Tuesday; Dee Gordon could return Thursday. Felix Hernandez will start for Seattle against Austin Bibens-Dirkx.

Ride-sharing app Taxify, which claims to be Europe's fastest-growing, is launching in Sydney with half-priced fares for one month to compete with Uber. Founded in Estonia in 2013 by Markus Villig and backed by Didi Chuxing, the company has over 4000 registered drivers, takes 15% commission, operates in 20 countries, and caps surge pricing at 1.5 times the usual rate.

El texto analiza el estado del neuromarketing en el sector audiovisual español mediante una investigación cualitativa basada en 18 entrevistas a consultoras, representantes audiovisuales, neurocientíficos y académicos. El neuromarketing, definido como la aplicación de técnicas de neuroimagen para entender la conducta en mercados, es incipiente en España (H3), aunque factible para estudiar al consumidor audiovisual (H1). Requiere equipos multidisciplinares (H2) y enfrenta limitaciones en ética, interpretación de datos y tamaño muestral. Su uso se concentra en las cadenas privadas Atresmedia y Mediaset España, que testan contenidos de ficción y bloques publicitarios con técnicas como EEG y sensores biométricos. Las productoras cinematográficas y televisivas muestran interés pero no invierten por falta de recursos económicos y cultura de investigación (H5). La proyección futura se considera positiva (H6), dependiendo del abaratamiento, estandarización tecnológica, mejora en la interpretación de datos y demostración de retorno de inversión. Los principales retos son el avance en la interpretación neurocientífica y la monitorización de la emoción.

FCA data shows 70% of adults planning to access defined contribution pensions within two years were not asked by providers about their plans. Two-thirds lacked provider advice; 40% preferred independent decisions and 10% cited cost. One-third expect the state pension as their largest income source, versus 21% for their DC pot. Forty-four percent have a good idea of their annual retirement income, while 28% have little or no idea.

Research shows that improving school air quality through air filters and ventilation upgrades raises student test scores and attendance at low cost. Following a California gas leak, schools with air purifiers saw math and English gains comparable to Tennessee’s class-size reduction program for approximately $30 per student, less than 1% of that intervention’s cost. Additional evidence indicates reduced absenteeism, fewer illness-related absences, and direct cognitive benefits from reduced particulate matter. The intervention particularly benefits low-income students in polluted areas or aging buildings and requires minimal administrative effort. The author recommends schools install or maintain portable air purifiers with a Clean Air Delivery Rate of at least 30 cubic feet per minute per student and noise levels under 50 decibels, while urging philanthropists, advocates, and researchers to support implementation, standards, and further study.

Research published in *Nature Climate Change* documents recent sudden, catastrophic ecosystem shifts across Australia caused by the combined stress of gradual climate change (“press”) and extreme weather events (“pulse”). Case studies include kelp forest loss, Gondwanan refugia destruction, Murray River forest dieback, alpine forest conversion, arid zone boom-bust cycles, and mangrove dieback. Even near-pristine systems show limited resilience. These collapses threaten fisheries, water resources, carbon storage, and tourism. Because variables make prediction impossible, targeted interventions such as recolonisation and fire protection are costly and increasingly difficult as extreme events grow more frequent. The authors suggest that as ecosystems reach tipping points, the risks of inaction may outweigh those of active intervention.

The Cincinnati Bengals acquired quarterback Joe Flacco from the Cleveland Browns in exchange for a 2026 fifth-round draft pick, receiving Flacco and a 2026 sixth-round pick in return. Head coach Zac Taylor immediately named Flacco the starting quarterback for Sunday's game against the Green Bay Packers. The Bengals, who hold a 2-3 record and have lost three consecutive games, made the change after Jake Browning struggled while filling in for injured starter Joe Burrow, who remains on injured reserve recovering from turf toe surgery and has no timetable for return. Browning will revert to backup status. Flacco, who defeated the Packers 13-10 as the Browns' starter in Week 3, will take all practice reps as he prepares for his debut. The team hopes he can help end the losing streak and keep them in playoff contention.

U.S. stocks rallied sharply on October 22, 2001, despite widening anthrax concerns, as better-than-expected quarterly earnings from companies such as American Express, 3M, and U.S. Steel lifted the Dow Jones Industrial Average by 1.9% and the Nasdaq Composite by 2.2%. In contrast, Enron Corp. shares plunged approximately 20% to $20.65 after the company disclosed that the Securities and Exchange Commission requested information on certain related-party transactions involving limited partnerships organized and formerly run by Chief Financial Officer Andrew Fastow. Enron stated it would fully cooperate with the SEC and noted that its board had approved and been informed of the arrangements, which were disclosed in SEC filings. The partnerships led Enron to take a $35 million charge and repurchase 55 million shares, reducing shareholder equity by $1.2 billion. An Enron shareholder filed a derivative suit alleging the board breached fiduciary duties by allowing Fastow to run the partnerships, while Shapiro Haber & Urmy filed a class action suit alleging securities fraud on behalf of purchasers of Enron stock from July 13 to October 16, 2001. The developments followed Enron's report of a $618 million third-quarter loss—its first in over four years—which included $1.01 billion in charges and writedowns. AG Edwards downgraded Enron to "hold," and analysts raised concerns about the company's credibility, accounting practices, and potential costs of dismantling affiliated companies. Separately, UniPrime Capital Corporation announced it signed a Letter of Intent with Jessel Enterprises for a partial interest in a wind park ground lease owned by Enron Wind Development Corp. in the Tehachapi Valley, a project estimated to generate $96 million in annual revenue.

This retrospective cohort study used All of Us Research Program data (v7) to develop machine learning models predicting healthy aging among 99,935 adults aged 50 and older. Healthy aging was defined by a composite score of comorbidities, cognitive conditions, and mobility, with a secondary cohort applying an age threshold of 85. Using social determinants of health features, three algorithms—logistic regression, multi-layer perceptron, and XGBoost—were trained and evaluated. XGBoost with random oversampling achieved the best performance (AUROC 0.793) and predictive parity across race and sex. Feature importance analysis ranked health insurance type as the most predictive factor, followed by employment status, substance use, and health insurance coverage. The study concludes that machine learning can accurately predict healthy aging using SDOH data and underscores health insurance as a pivotal determinant of long-term health outcomes in older adults.

This study presents a multi-scenario simulation of replacing internal combustion engine vehicles with battery electric vehicles (BEVs) using one year of telematics data from 10,441 users in Asti, Italy. The authors replicate actual driving trips across four commercial BEV models and four charging policies—ranging from slow AC workplace or overnight charging to fast DC opportunistic charging—evaluating trip feasibility, monthly charging frequency, and post-trip state of charge. Results indicate that current BEV technology does not suit all users: workplace-only charging yields only 64–88% feasible trips, while fast DC charging when the battery state of charge is low performs best, achieving over 98% feasible trips for most models and allowing 72% of users to complete all trips with the largest battery vehicle. Overnight charging maintains the highest average post-trip state of charge but requires more frequent charges. Even under optimal conditions, 5% of users cannot meet their mobility needs without changing habits. The study acknowledges limitations including invariant energy consumption assumptions, universal charging availability, and omitted cost considerations.

Officials celebrated the groundbreaking of the Mauka Concourse at Daniel K. Inouye International Airport, a $220 million project finishing in 2020, adding gate capacity for larger aircraft and 260,000 square feet of passenger space. It is part of a $1.3 billion modernization including a five-level rental car structure by 2021.

On February 6, 2002, multiple news reports detailed the escalating fallout from Enron’s collapse. Former CEO Jeffrey Skilling was expected to testify before Congress without invoking the Fifth Amendment, while former CEO Kenneth Lay was subpoenaed by several committees after canceling a voluntary appearance and was widely expected to invoke his Fifth Amendment rights. Enron board member William Powers, who led an internal investigation, testified that Lay, Skilling, and other top executives knew or should have known about off-the-balance-sheet partnerships—such as the LJM entities run by former CFO Andrew Fastow—that were used to hide debt, inflate earnings by $1 billion, and enrich insiders by tens of millions of dollars. Powers stated that Enron knew the partnerships were causing losses by March 2001 and made the problem worse by continuing to feed stock into them.

Lawmakers and witnesses described a culture in which employees were threatened with firing or loss of bonuses if they resisted questionable partnership dealings, and a roughly three-week lockout prevented workers from selling Enron stock from their retirement accounts as the share price plummeted. Arthur Andersen and its chairman Joseph Berardino faced fierce criticism over the firm’s role in setting up partnerships and shredding documents. Labor Secretary Elaine Chao was scheduled to testify on strengthening retirement protections. Enron’s debtor-in-possession financing had shrunk from a projected $1.5 billion to between $250 million and $500 million, its broadband unit owed about $440,000 in back taxes, and the company was fighting the Houston Astros’ attempt to terminate the “Enron Field” naming rights deal. The scandal spawned terms like “Enronitis” and “Enronization” as investor confidence in corporate accounting and bonds plummeted, while Spain’s energy regulator announced an investigation into Enron’s local operations.

Former Maui County Councilmember Mike Victorino, a mayoral candidate, struck two teenage pedestrians on West Papa Avenue on April 13. The Bank of Canada and financial markets are in tension over the loonie’s value, with the bank preferring a weaker dollar to aid exporters while markets push it higher on economic strength, reaching nearly 75.50 U.S. cents. Board of Governors heard feedback on two on-campus gamedays. ASCSU plans to improve tailgating awareness through rebranding and pre-game programming after many used the lot only for parking. IES Holdings, a diversified U.S. infrastructure services provider with 130+ locations, has nearly doubled its share price year-to-date while outperforming infrastructure and Russell 2000 stocks. Its largest residential division faces challenges, but data center projects are boosting other divisions. The company’s backlog exceeds $2 billion and is growing over 20% year-over-year, alongside improved cash flow and record cash balances. This study tested whether role-taking and literacy interventions reduce demographic and appearance-based biases in trust and risk-taking related to social engineering. In an online experiment, 139 Arab participants were assigned to one of four groups—Persuader, Persuadee, Literacy, or Control—and evaluated 16 personas varying in age, gender, ethnicity, and attire before and one week after the intervention. Contrary to the hypothesis, repeated measures ANOVAs and Bayes Factors revealed no significant post-intervention changes in risk-taking, trust, or word-of-mouth across persona factors or roles. However, Issue of Involvement decreased significantly. The authors conclude that while participants found the interactive scenarios engaging and awareness-raising, short-term interventions were insufficient to alter deeply ingrained cognitive biases or behavioral susceptibility to social engineering. Limitations included the use of imagined scenarios, potential social desirability bias, and static comic-based simulations. The study suggests future research explore longer-term, immersive, or gamified approaches to achieve lasting debiasing effects.

The Great Southern Storm have named an initial 45-player colts squad under new head coach Glynn Verbruggen, who replaces Phil Gilbert. The squad will train on June 4 and 11 at Railways before final team selection for the Great Southern Colts Carnival in Kulin. It features league regulars, State 16 squad members Heath Spinks and Jacob Blight, and players with State Country colts experience. Linebackers require toughness, athleticism, and intelligence. Positioned 3–5 yards behind the defensive line, they relay calls, align teammates, and defend the run and pass. The name derives from their alignment behind the line. Roles include Sam, Mike, Will, and Jack. Skills include vision, agility, and tackling; typical builds are 5’10”–6’5” and 215–255 lbs. Notable players include Ray Lewis, Chuck Bednarik, and Lawrence Taylor. While NFL value on inside linebackers has declined amid passing offenses, versatile linebackers who rush, cover, and stop the run remain valuable.

The passage examines Germany's plan to organize Middle Europe under its control to serve imperialistic foreign policy, facing critical problems with the Poles, Czechs, South Slavs, and Bulgaria. The United States opposes not economic or cultural unification but the domination of Berlin, Vienna, and Budapest over subject peoples and resources. The alliance binding Berlin, Vienna, Budapest, Sofia, and Constantinople rests on subjugating the Poles, Czechs, and Croats, preserving German-Magyar ascendency, exploiting Bulgarian grievances, maintaining Turkish integrity, and post-war debts. America’s chief assets are the economic weapon of threatening commercial exclusion from raw materials and markets, and nationalist discontent within Austria-Hungary. The recommended policy is to encourage Czech and South Slav unrest while simultaneously offering Austria-Hungary’s ruling powers safety through a league of nations and disarmament, thereby reducing German-Magyar resistance and accelerating independence from Berlin.
