Texas administrators, parents, and experts worry that a new law replacing the STAAR test with three shorter annual exams could increase student stress and testing time rather than reduce it. Effective in 2027-28, the law bans practice tests and requires the Texas Education Agency to study reducing testing weight in school accountability ratings, but that report is not due until 2029-30 and the agency is not required to implement findings. Critics note that because the end-of-year exam will still heavily influence high-stakes A-F ratings, pressure may remain unchanged while adding more tests. Some advocates say many districts already administer multiple exams, so the law largely codifies existing practices. Skeptics want fewer restrictive testing-day protocols, more teacher input in designing the new end-of-year exam, and the option to use growth-based assessments like MAP for the first two tests. Supporters argue the changes will reduce overall testing time and better monitor student progress.

LAPIS is a performance-portable, high-productivity, extensible compiler framework built on MLIR that bridges C++ computational science and engineering (CSE) applications with Python-based artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) codes. It automatically compiles high-level MLIR—accepted from torch-mlir and MPACT frontends conforming to the linalg-on-tensors dialect—into Kokkos-based C++ source code via a custom Kokkos dialect. This dialect represents Kokkos execution and memory abstractions, including hierarchical parallel loops (range_parallel, team_parallel, thread_parallel), synchronization operations (single, team_barrier), and Kokkos Kernels linear algebra operations (gemm, gemv). LAPIS includes lowering passes that map parallel loops to Kokkos constructs, compute heuristics for team size and vector length, manage a Kokkos-inspired DualView memory model for heterogeneous systems, and emit parallel C++ code. The framework demonstrates portable performance for sparse and dense linear algebra kernels and coupled CSE-AI/ML use cases on AMD MI300A, NVIDIA H100, and Intel Granite Rapids CPUs.

District and Sessions Judge Nasir Khan Yousafzai sentenced four convicts in separate murder cases in Zhob. Shehzado was sentenced to death and fined Rs. 200,000. Ajab Khan, Fateh Khan, and Dilbar Khan received 25-year prison terms and fines.

This work proves the existence of strong pseudorandom unitaries (PRUs) in the quantum Haar random oracle model (QHROM), resolving the open question of whether PRUs exist when adversaries have access to both a Haar-random unitary and its inverse. The construction, $G_U(1^\lambda, k) = X^{k_3} \cdot U_\lambda \cdot X^{k_2} \cdot U_\lambda \cdot X^{k_1}$, makes two queries to the $\lambda$-qubit Haar random oracle $U_\lambda$ and uses a key $k = k_1||k_2||k_3$, requiring $O(\log^{1+\epsilon}(n))$ bits of randomness for security against adversaries making $\text{poly}(n)$ queries. The security proof employs the path-recording framework of Ma and Huang, introducing an approximate isometry $S$ that merges independent query databases and simulates keys, and uses a query-by-query hybrid analysis to show that the adversary’s view is statistically close to that of two independent Haar-random unitaries.

Chipotle released queso dip on September 12, but customers have complained on Twitter about its high price and taste. A spokesman said 63% of test market customers said it would increase visits, and the price will not drop because real ingredients cost more. In Sacramento, a large chips and queso ($6.25) costs nearly as much as a burrito ($6.70).

Peggy Mahoney forwarded an August 25, 2000 Energy Central Deregulation Public Forum message to Enron colleagues. The forum asked whether federal policy should change to encourage natural gas exploration and production on federal lands and the continental shelf to address anticipated supply shortages, noting that nearly 95% of planned power plants are gas-fired. It also included selected responses to a prior question about whether generators deliberately manipulated the San Diego market to raise profits and whether price caps should be imposed. Opinions were divided: some respondents claimed market manipulation or collusion occurred and supported price caps, while others blamed high prices on supply shortages, weather, reduced hydroelectric output, flawed deregulation structures, and normal market forces, arguing that price caps would create shortages, deter investment, and impede market solutions.

Mexico-based CEMEX grew from a domestic cement company into one of the world’s largest building materials suppliers between 1992 and 2007 through major acquisitions, including RMC in 2005 and Rinker in 2007. Its success was attributed to a post-merger integration process known as the CEMEX Way, which standardized business processes, technology, and organizational structure across all countries while granting local operational flexibility and fostering innovation. The CEMEX Way involved transferring CEMEX’s best practices to acquired firms and systematically identifying, cataloging, and adopting superior practices from acquired companies into corporate standards.

CEMEX’s internationalization occurred in four stages. During the 1980s, it laid groundwork by consolidating its Mexican market position and investing in information systems. In 1992, it stepped out by acquiring Spanish cement companies to respond to a European competitor’s growing share in Mexico and to access lower-cost capital; the integration transferred Mexican best practices that significantly improved Spanish operating margins and formalized its Post-Merger Integration (PMI) process. In the mid-to-late 1990s, it accelerated into Latin America, the Caribbean, and Asia, refining the CEMEX Way after integration challenges in Colombia revealed the need to learn from acquired firms. In the 2000s, it stepped up into large developed markets by redefining them into regions and shifting performance measurement to return on investment, leading to the acquisitions of Southdown in the United States, U.K.-based RMC, and Australia’s Rinker.

The PMI process deployed multinational teams of functional experts and middle managers to implement standards and identify acquirer capabilities for global adoption. By some estimates, 70 percent of CEMEX’s practices had been adopted from previous acquisitions, and the duration of PMI decreased from 25 months for Spain to less than five months for Southdown. The company also applied the PMI process to its Mexican operations to drive continuous improvement. By 2007, CEMEX operated in 50 countries with 65,000 employees and $21.7 billion in annual revenue, up from 6,500 employees and $275 million in revenue 25 years prior.

Paul Clement is set to be named Swansea manager after Bayern Munich granted him permission to speak with the club. The former assistant to Carlo Ancelotti is expected to sign a deal until 2019 and receive a £30 million transfer budget after replacing Bob Bradley. Swansea sit 19th in the Premier League and face relegation. Defender Neil Taylor said the squad would support Clement and work to turn the season around.

The 1956 Hungarian revolt was a nationwide uprising, unlike earlier localized riots in East Berlin and Poznán. Following Communist consolidation under Mátyás Rákosi after 1949, discontent grew due to economic failure, uncertain leadership, and encouragement from events in Poland and Yugoslavia. After a student rally on 22 October 1956, protests turned violent; revolutionary councils demanded nationalism, neutrality, and Soviet troop withdrawal. The Politburo reappointed Imre Nagy, and Soviet tanks briefly withdrew while leaders announced respect for Hungarian sovereignty, though this concealed an impending invasion. As the Suez Crisis diverted world attention, the USSR surrounded Budapest on 1 November and attacked on 3–4 November. Resistance ended by 30 November, with approximately 25,000 Hungarians and 7,000 Soviet soldiers killed.

U.S. District Judge Jeannette A. Vargas dismissed Drake's defamation lawsuit over Kendrick Lamar's 2024 song "Not Like Us," which called Drake a "certified pedophile." The judge ruled the lyrics were "nonactionable opinion" and "hyperbolic vituperations" made during a heated rap battle. Vargas also dismissed Drake's claims against Universal Music Group for defamation, harassment, and deceptive acts. Drake plans to appeal.

Springfield Police Officer Conrad Lariviere faces disciplinary action for writing "Hahahaha love this" on Facebook in response to the death of counter-protester Heather Heyer at a Charlottesville white supremacist rally. He later apologized for the "stupid comment." Police Commissioner John Barbieri launched an internal investigation, and Mayor Domenic Sarno denounced the remarks. Lariviere denied being racist.

The DAWN-plasma study is a randomized, open-label, phase 2, multicenter trial evaluating convalescent plasma plus standard of care (SOC) versus SOC alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. It hypothesizes that early, high-volume, high-titer convalescent plasma reduces the proportion of patients requiring mechanical ventilation. The primary endpoint is the percentage of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15; secondary endpoints include clinical status, time to sustained improvement, ventilation, death, and safety measures. Eligible participants are adults aged ≥18 with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, radiographic infiltrates or SpO2 ≤94%, and no mechanical ventilation at randomization. Exclusions include prior mechanical ventilation, grade 3 allergic reaction to fresh frozen plasma, and anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody therapy within the prior year. Patients receive 800–1000 mL of plasma in four 200–250 mL doses, with the first two units within 12 hours of randomization and the next two units 24–36 hours later; plasma must have neutralizing antibody titers of at least 1/160. Six patients withdrew or screened out before intervention and were substituted; no patients were lost to follow-up afterward. The study was approved by Independent Ethics Committees and conducted per the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH Good Clinical Practice guidelines, with required informed consent.

Coppin State University, a Maryland HBCU, has more than quadrupled out-of-state enrollment in two years through its Expand Eagle Nation program, which offers in-state tuition to students from qualifying states and territories without an HBCU. Students from these areas grew from 81 to 195 in 2024, then to 416 of 1,000 incoming students this fall, helping drive a 26 percent overall enrollment increase. The effort aims to counter the expected decline in high school graduates and raise the university’s profile. Coppin increased its presence through advertising, high school visits, and community college transfer partnerships, while preparing additional courses, faculty, and housing, including a new dorm. Officials said a key challenge is convincing prospective students that the tuition offer is legitimate.

The ACC Tournament ended its two-year Barclays Center run with Virginia's 71-63 win over North Carolina. Virginia, unranked and picked sixth, completed a remarkable season. North Carolina defeated Duke, while Duke's Marvin Bagley III showed why he's expected to be No. 1 NBA draft pick. Clemson beat BC to reach the NCAA Tournament for the first time in seven years. The ACC Tournament wants to return to Barclays Center.

The passage states that the Democratic Party has assumed full control of the United States government, reflecting a national shift in perspective rather than mere partisan victory. While acknowledging America's material and moral greatness, it criticizes the waste, human costs of industrialization, and government corruption that have accompanied progress. The speaker outlines a program of restoration to align national life with standards of justice, including reforming the tariff, banking and currency systems, industrial practices that exploit labor and natural resources, and inefficient agriculture. Government must safeguard public health, labor conditions, and individual rights through laws ensuring justice. The task requires non-partisan, deliberate, step-by-step reform of existing institutions rather than destruction. Describing the occasion as a day of dedication rather than triumph, the speaker calls upon honest and patriotic citizens for counsel and support in pursuing justice.

Williams & Connolly confirmed hackers accessed a small number of attorney emails via a zero-day attack but reported no evidence of further IT system access or extraction of confidential client data from databases. The firm believes the hackers are nation-state actors behind recent attacks on other law firms and companies and has blocked them. A prior warning linked Chinese government-tied hackers to targeting firms for U.S. national security and trade information.

The TPS7H500x-SP series comprises radiation-hardness-assured, peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters operating up to 2 MHz. The devices require external gate drivers and support topologies including buck, flyback, forward, push-pull, and full-bridge.

Enable and UVLO can be configured by tying EN to VLDO, using an external signal, or a resistor divider from VIN to set a start-up threshold; the UVLO threshold should be approximately 75% or less of the input voltage. An internal 1.23-V bandgap reference is divided to 0.613 V for the transconductance error amplifier, which regulates within +0.7%/-1%. Output voltage is programmed via a resistor divider to the VSENSE pin. Soft-start duration is set by a capacitor on the SS pin; synchronous rectifier outputs activate once SS exceeds 1 V.

Switching frequency is configurable in three modes: internal oscillator (RT resistor to AVSS, 100 kHz–2 MHz, SYNC outputs 2× frequency), external synchronization (RT floating, 2× clock applied to SYNC, 200 kHz–4 MHz), and primary-secondary (SYNC links two controllers with 90° or 270° phase shift). Primary outputs (OUTA/OUTB) and synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA/SRB) provide roughly 150-mA peak current; OUTB and SRB are active only when the duty cycle limit is set to 50% (DCL to AVSS) on supported models. Dead time and leading edge blank time are programmable via resistors on the PS, SP, and LEB pins (10 kΩ to 300 kΩ) for most variants, while the TPS7H5003-SP uses fixed values. Pulse skipping occurs when COMP is below 0.3 V and the previous duty cycle was under 25%. Maximum duty cycle is set via the DCL pin: 50% (AVSS), 75% (floating), or 100% (VLDO); the TPS7H5004-SP supports only 50%.

Peak current mode control turns off the primary outputs when the CS_ILIM pin voltage reaches the COMP/2 threshold plus a 150-mV offset. A 1.05-V threshold at CS_ILIM triggers hiccup mode, where the HICC capacitor controls the delay before switching stops and the subsequent restart delay. The FAULT pin shuts down the controller if its voltage exceeds 0.6 V for longer than the minimum pulse width, restarting after a delay. Slope compensation is set with an RSC resistor to prevent subharmonic oscillation. Frequency compensation (Type 2A or 2B) connects between COMP and AVSS. Thermal shutdown occurs above 175°C and resumes below 160°C.

A design example details a 500-kHz synchronous push-pull converter using GaN FETs, with a 2.5 transformer turns ratio, 40-µH primary inductance, 0.47-µH output inductor, approximately 2.3 mF of output capacitance for single-event transient mitigation, and specific component values for RT, feedback, dead time, leading edge blanking, soft-start, current sensing, frequency compensation, and slope compensation. The controllers operate from a 4-V to 14-V supply and require careful PCB layout: minimize high-di/dt loops, separate analog and power grounds at a single point, place bypass and compensation components close to the device, and route noisy switching traces away from sensitive pins such as VSENSE, COMP, and CS_ILIM.

This paper proposes the Language-Guided Change Detection (LG-CD) model for remote sensing change detection, integrating visual and textual information. It employs a pre-trained SAM2 encoder with multi-layer adapters to extract multi-scale features from bi-temporal images, and CLIP to encode textual prompts. A Text Fusion Attention Module uses cross-attention to align text with visual features and focus on key changing areas. A visual-semantic fusion decoder integrates both modalities to generate change detection masks. Combining visual and textual semantic information improves the model’s semantic understanding, detection accuracy, and generalization.

The passage defines Video Output 0 digital terminal functions, describing 8 MSB data signals for G/Y/YC, B/CB/C, and R/CR components and their roles in RGB, YUV444, Y/C, and BT.656 modes, plus pin abbreviations, internal pull defaults, and pullup/pulldown references.

In an MIT OpenCourseWare lecture, Will Ma discusses post-flop poker strategy. He explains that players often check to the preflop aggressor because that player’s range is stronger on average. Post-flop, a useful rule of thumb is to bet about half the pot on the flop, roughly 60 percent on the turn, and 70 to 100 percent on the river; betting extremely small is generally worse than checking because it grants opponents a free option. Ma presents the "Fundamental Theorem of Poker," advising players to bet their strongest hands for value, bluff with their weakest hands, and check middle-strength hands to avoid adverse selection. He recommends folding most hands that miss the flop when facing a half-pot bet, and notes that with deep effective stacks (around 40 big blinds or more), a raise should generally be reserved for two-pair or better, whereas shallower stacks permit committing with top pair. He also covers "leading" out of position when the flop favors one’s range over the preflop raiser’s, but cautions that it is an advanced, difficult-to-balance tactic. The lecture distinguishes between implied odds—calling with speculative hands like suited connectors to win large pots when they improve—and reverse implied odds, where weak hands lose additional chips post-flop despite adequate preflop equity. Finally, Ma argues that bluffs should be made with draws that have significant outs, and that players should abandon bluffs when the board runout weakens the range they are representing.

California lawmakers are considering competing proposals to prevent Southern California Edison from bankruptcy, including state purchase of transmission lines, ratepayer charges to pay off $3.5 billion in debts, and direct bailouts, ahead of an August 15 legislative deadline. Pacific Gas & Electric sued the state seeking compensation for long-term power contracts seized by Gov. Gray Davis in January from the defunct California Power Exchange. The state is selling surplus electricity at a loss after contracting to buy power at high prices. Duke Energy reported a 27% rise in second-quarter profit, boosted by wholesale power and trading growth. Consumer prices edged up 0.2% in June as energy costs moderated, and Contra Costa County approved $1.7 million for energy conservation upgrades to nine buildings.

Cervical cancer is a malignant condition of the cervix caused almost exclusively by sexually transmitted human papillomavirus (HPV), particularly types 16 and 18. A pre-cancer stage is asymptomatic but detectable through pap smears, recommended every three years for reproductive-age women. Symptoms of invasive cancer include post-coital bleeding, foul-smelling discharge, and abnormal vaginal bleeding; late-stage disease may involve weight loss, pelvic pain, and organ involvement. Diagnosis requires tissue biopsy and histology. Early-stage cancer can be cured via radical surgery or radiotherapy, while late-stage disease is managed with radiotherapy and chemotherapy to prolong life. In Nigeria, cervical cancer is the second most common cancer among women after breast cancer, with approximately 15,000 new cases and 10,000 deaths annually; most patients present late due to lack of structured screening. HPV vaccines are available for prevention, and precancerous lesions may be treated with cryosurgery, cauterization, or laser surgery.

U.S. District Judge Fernando Olguin dismissed Spencer Elden’s 2021 lawsuit over the 1991 Nirvana “Nevermind” album cover, which depicts Elden as a naked baby, ruling the image is not child pornography. Olguin found that except for nudity, no factors indicated lasciviousness, comparing the image to a family photo of a nude child bathing.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly present in higher education, a trend accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic. This position paper examines how AI shapes teaching-learning processes, research, organizational management, and external relations in higher education. Based on document analysis from the B-ON and SCILIT databases and author reflexivity, the study contrasts traditional and AI-oriented higher education, noting differences in institutional governance, training models, and research approaches. AI offers advantages such as personalized learning, automated grading, intelligent tutoring, predictive analytics, virtual assistants, and efficiencies in research and administrative tasks. However, integration faces challenges including equity and access, ethical and data privacy concerns, teacher training needs, financial costs, organizational resistance, and AI’s inherent limitations. The authors advocate for participatory implementation, AI literacy for all stakeholders, the reshaping of teacher roles, and action-research to improve educational quality. They conclude that higher education institutions must adapt to AI developments while maintaining academic freedom and encouraging continued research and discussion on its applications.

He stated his team is better than its performance in the first two games and must prove it. Chris Neil was given the day off because his wife is having a baby. He acknowledged the opponent outpositioned and outdefended them, capitalizing on mistakes, while his goaltender played well despite limited offensive testing of the opposing goalie. He cited poor faceoff performance, turnovers, and a lack of puck possession, patience, and speed as key issues, noting the opponent's centers and wingers have been more effective. He said adjustments are necessary, including attacking with more speed and avoiding stretch passes, and expects better play at home with crowd support. He praised Rob Niedermayer and planned to use his fourth line more for energy, while noting several forwards, including Mike Comrie, need to return to form.

San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan addressed the media before the team's final on-field practice before returning to training camp in late July. He said the previous day's practice was competitive, with the offense edging out the defense. He noted his father, Mike Shanahan, observes practices and offers input after watching tape, though he is not on staff. Shanahan said he values his father's insights because he has time to notice details Shanahan misses while managing head coaching duties. Shanahan plans to vacation in Mexico with his family before training camp. He also emphasized that play-action is critical to his offensive philosophy because it puts defenses in a bind, creates explosive plays, and reduces pressure on the offensive line and quarterbacks.

Indianapolis Public Schools is holding its first public meeting on closing three high schools by 2018-2019. A Taskforce report cites enrollment decline from 109,000 in 1967 to 30,000, with all seven high schools under capacity. It recommends operating four schools for flexibility. Meetings continue through April and May; recommendations by June, board vote in September.

The White House said it was not defending Roseanne Barr's racist tweet that led to the show's cancellation, but Trump and Sanders said ABC owed them an apology for derogatory comments about the administration. Trump tweeted that ABC's Bob Iger apologized to Valerie Jarrett but not to him for negative statements aired on the network. Sanders cited media examples to support Trump's claim of a double standard, saying he called out bias, not defending Barr.

The lecture reviews discrete symmetries—parity (P), time reversal (T), and charge conjugation (C)—in quantum mechanics and quantum field theory. In quantum mechanics, T must be implemented by an anti-unitary operator because it sends i to −i to preserve the Schrödinger equation under t → −t. For a complex scalar field, P, T, and C are implemented by unitary operators; parity gives η_P = ±1, distinguishing scalars from pseudoscalars, while charge conjugation exchanges particles and antiparticles. For a Dirac field, parity requires a spinor-space matrix D proportional to γ⁰ that commutes with γ⁰ and anticommutes with γⁱ; charge conjugation uses a matrix C satisfying Cγ^μC⁻¹ = −(γ^μ)^T; and time reversal uses a matrix D_T. The lecture then introduces path integrals for fermions via Berezin’s idea of Grassmann variables—anticommuting objects whose square is zero. Functions of a single Grassmann variable truncate after two terms. Integration is defined by linearity and the requirement that the integral of a total derivative vanish, which forces the integral of a constant to be zero and the integral of θ to be 1, making integration equivalent to differentiation. A change of variables θ′ = aθ yields dθ′ = (1/a)dθ, opposite to the standard bosonic case.

U.S. stock index futures were higher on April 20 as earnings season started strongly and oil prices rebounded on signals that OPEC-led supply cuts may be extended. However, North Korea-U.S. tensions and the French presidential election kept investors cautious. About 75% of reporting S&P 500 companies beat expectations, with overall profits estimated up 10.8%. Qualcomm rose after beating estimates, while eBay fell on a weak second-quarter profit forecast.
Estimation of m-qubit polynomial functionals underpins quantum information, statistical mechanics, many-body physics.

A player expressed surprise at coach Pat reinserting him after two weeks out, admitting he was nervous but grateful and wanted to contribute. He noted winning three cups in nine years was special despite a difficult season with roster changes, praising his teammates. He credited Pat's tough, no-nonsense approach and refusal to let the team become complacent for keeping them focused. He added he would sit with his family and could not think of a sweeter way to go out.

The passage describes systems and methods for synchronizing a rotating LIDAR sensor with one or more cameras. The LIDAR rotates about an axis, emitting light pulses toward an environment and detecting reflections. The cameras provide rows of sensing elements aligned with the LIDAR's axis of rotation and operate in a rolling shutter mode to obtain a sequence of image pixel rows. A controller determines the order and timing of image pixel capture based on the arrangement, emission order, and rotation characteristics of the LIDAR's light beams, aligning the cameras' fast and slow axes with those of the LIDAR. This improves temporal and spatial matching between image pixels and LIDAR reflections. The system associates LIDAR data with corresponding image pixels based on timing and viewing direction to generate a representation of the environment, such as a colored three-dimensional point cloud.

Quantbot Technologies LP increased its Zoe’s Kitchen holdings by 114.5% in the second quarter to 17,056 shares, while several other institutional investors including FMR LLC and California Public Employees Retirement System also modified their positions in the first quarter. Director A Alexander Taylor II purchased 3,100 shares in August. Analysts maintain a consensus “Hold” rating with a $17.55 target price. Shares opened at $12.39. Zoe’s Kitchen reported second-quarter earnings of $0.06 per share, beating estimates by $0.04, on revenue of $74.30 million, which missed estimates; revenue rose 12.1% year-over-year. The company develops and operates fast-casual Mediterranean-inspired restaurants.

Darren Osborne was sentenced to life in prison with a minimum term of 43 years at Woolwich Crown Court for driving a van into worshippers outside Finsbury Park mosque in London last June, killing Makram Ali and injuring nine others. Osborne, who shouted anti-Muslim statements and was described by prosecutors as having been radicalized by a BBC drama, was found guilty of murder and attempted murder. Police released footage showing he planned the attack in Wales before driving to London. The victim's family welcomed the verdict, while authorities noted the attack failed to divide the community.

Major hedge funds trimmed healthcare stakes in the second quarter as the sector rallied on dimming Republican efforts to repeal the Affordable Care Act, with Jana Partners exiting nine companies and Third Point reducing Humana and Baxter holdings. Funds also sold energy positions as the sector declined, with Third Point, Jana Partners, and Omega Advisors exiting multiple companies. Hedge funds gained 1 percent overall.

This application, a continuation of prior U.S. and international patent applications, relates to electronic cigarettes and similar devices. It discloses a coil-less atomizer using one or more woven fiber tubes within a housing, where the tubes function as both a heating element and a liquid wick. At least one tube includes an electrically conductive heating section connected to leads or contacts and end sections in contact with a liquid supply. Liquid is transported to the heating section through the tube's hollow interior and porous walls via capillary action. The tubes may be various shapes, diameters, and arrangements, and may include conductive sections with lower resistance than the heating section. Manufacturing methods involve selectively modifying tube sections, such as by masking and sputtering, to achieve desired electrical resistance properties. The design integrates liquid transport and heating into a single component.

The court denied Randall Fincke’s motion to reconsider its prior ruling that he violated Massachusetts General Laws ch. 110A, § 410(a)(2) by making a material misstatement in an October 2002 Business Plan falsely claiming Access Cardiosystems’ patent counsel had advised that its product infringed no known patents. The court found the statement objectively false and material regardless of whether investors understood it as a formal or informal opinion. On damages, the court rejected the investors’ testimony as not credible and found that only Joseph Zimmel’s October and November 2002 stock purchases, totaling $1.5 million, were made “by means of” the misstatement. The court entered judgment against Fincke in favor of Zimmel for $1.5 million plus six percent prejudgment interest from May 25, 2007, and in favor of Access for $281,534.62 plus twelve percent prejudgment interest from July 6, 2004, for Fincke’s prior breaches of fiduciary duty, with postjudgment interest on both awards.

The appellate court affirmed Bradford Washington's two second-degree murder convictions, one by jury verdict under indictment No. 999/05 for murder, weapon possession, reckless endangerment, and child endangerment, and one by guilty plea under indictment No. 1000/05. The court rejected his unpreserved and meritless claims regarding detective testimony about his evasion, the jury charge on consciousness of guilt, and the prosecution's summation theory. The second judgment was affirmed based on the first.

The BIRDS workshop aims to bridge digital library professionals and computational researchers to foster practical collaborations and innovative research systems. Domain experts often lack technical expertise or resources to implement modern computational solutions, while researchers are rarely aware of real-world library challenges. The interactive, full-day TPDL workshop will feature introductions, a keynote, scientific speed-dating, a panel discussion, and breakout groups; it does not require paper submissions. Goals include initiating a workshop series, identifying common challenges, discussing rough ideas and ongoing work, and producing a SIGIR Forum report. The target audience comprises practitioners and researchers interested in building digital library systems, with an emphasis on welcoming new community members. Organisers are Christin Katharina Kreutz and Hermann Kroll.

In Coleman v. Coleman, the Ohio Supreme Court affirmed the constitutionality of R.C. 3105.03, which requires plaintiffs in divorce and annulment actions to have been Ohio residents for at least one year before filing. The court rejected the argument that the durational residency requirement unconstitutionally penalized the right to interstate travel under the standards applied in Shapiro v. Thompson and Dunn v. Blumstein. It reasoned that divorce is a statutory privilege, not a basic need or fundamental constitutional right like welfare or voting. The court held that Ohio has a compelling interest in overseeing marriage and divorce laws exclusively for residents, preventing nonresidents from utilizing its courts, and encouraging marital stability. It concluded that the one-year requirement, which has existed since 1853 and exempts alimony-only actions, is the least restrictive means to ensure domiciliary intent. A concurring justice agreed based on the case's specific facts.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K on August 17, 2022. On that date, the Compensation Committee approved the Executive Cash Incentive Plan, which provides cash awards to eligible executives based on Committee-established performance goals and periods; participants forfeit awards if they terminate before payout unless the Committee decides otherwise. The Board also approved amended and restated bylaws effective the same day, modifying procedures for special Board meetings, shareholder nominations and proposals, proxy solicitation, special shareholder meetings, written consent, and emergency operations, and requiring non-white proxy cards for certain solicitations. The filing includes the amended bylaws and incentive plan as exhibits and was signed August 19, 2022.

Oliver Stone’s *Wall Street* opened in December 1987, shortly after Black Monday, and remains the definitive film on finance decades later. It succeeds not through realism but by blending a rags-to-riches fairy tale with immersive 1980s excess, following broker Bud Fox as Gordon Gekko makes his dreams come true at a cost. The film captures the era’s culture, junk bonds, corporate raiders, and unmatched excess. Michael Douglas’s Oscar-winning performance as the charismatic, corporate-targeting Gekko created an iconic symbol of greed that inspired real finance professionals. Memorable lines like “Greed is good” have cemented it as a lasting time capsule.

An analysis by Notre Dame Law School professor Derek Muller found that lawyers and staff at the nation's 100 top-grossing firms and 50 larger plaintiffs-side firms directed 92.45% of campaign contributions to Democrats in 2023-2024, up from a 6-1 Democratic to Republican ratio in 2017-2020. The group gave about $52 million to Democratic-affiliated groups and $4 million to Republican-affiliated groups. Among top-grossing firms, Cleary Gottlieb, Fried Frank, and Mintz Levin had the highest Democratic percentages, while Nelson Mullins, Lewis Brisbois, and Ogletree Deakins had the lowest.

A modified Google Camera app enables the Pixel's HDR+ mode on Android phones with Snapdragon 820, 821, or 835 processors. Amazon is refunding faulty solar-eclipse glasses. HBO refuses to pay hackers despite leaked episodes and emails, including new 'Curb Your Enthusiasm.' Waymo patented self-driving car technology to soften its body before a pedestrian collision to reduce injuries.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2016. The company operates through three segments—North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS)—serving consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, and content creators through retail websites, electronic devices, Amazon Prime, cloud computing, and other services. For 2016, consolidated net sales were $135.987 billion, operating income was $4.186 billion, and net income was $2.371 billion, with diluted earnings per share of $4.90. Segment net sales were $79.785 billion for North America, $43.983 billion for International, and $12.219 billion for AWS. Segment operating income was $2.361 billion for North America, a loss of $1.283 billion for International, and $3.108 billion for AWS. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $26.0 billion as of December 31, 2016, and capital expenditures were $6.7 billion, primarily to support fulfillment operations and AWS technology infrastructure. The company had approximately 341,400 full-time and part-time employees and listed its common stock on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under the symbol “AMZN,” having never declared or paid cash dividends. Key risks include intense competition; strain from rapid global expansion; seasonality; reliance on fulfillment network and data center optimization; international regulatory challenges, particularly in China and India; foreign exchange exposure; data security and system interruption risks; inventory management; and significant tax contingencies, including an IRS transfer pricing dispute and a European Commission state aid investigation in Luxembourg.

The Simons Observatory Large Aperture Telescope (LAT) employs SMuRF warm electronics and microwave frequency multiplexing to read out approximately 31,000 cryogenic transition-edge sensor detectors. Because the LAT receiver cabin is isothermal with the telescope structure, the room-temperature RF coaxial cables experience diurnal temperature swings that cause systematic phase drifts. Measurements using off-resonance tones show the drift correlates with ambient temperature but remains at the level of a few picoseconds over a day-night cycle. When converted to an inferred detector noise-equivalent current using measured SQUID response curves, the effect contributes minimally to on-sky detector noise and lies within the readout noise budget. The authors conclude that this warm-cable phase drift does not significantly affect LAT data quality or mapping speed.

Tesla, Inc. filed its 2022 Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2022. The Delaware-incorporated company, with principal executive offices in Austin, Texas, trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol TSLA. As of January 25, 2023, it had 3,164,102,701 shares of common stock outstanding, and the aggregate market value of voting stock held by non-affiliates was approximately $580.48 billion as of June 30, 2022.

Tesla designs, develops, manufactures, sells, and leases high-performance fully electric vehicles and energy generation and storage systems. It operates two reportable segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. Automotive products include the Model 3, Model Y, Model S, Model X, and the Tesla Semi, with planned vehicles including the Cybertruck and new Roadster. Energy products include the Powerwall and Megapack battery storage systems, retrofit solar energy systems, Solar Roof, and power purchase agreements.

The company sells directly to customers through its website and company-owned stores, and operates a global Tesla Supercharger network, which began opening to non-Tesla vehicles in certain locations in November 2021. It provides vehicle service through company-owned locations and mobile technicians, and offers limited warranties, extended service plans, and automotive insurance currently available in 12 states. Manufacturing facilities are located in California, Nevada, New York, Texas, Shanghai, and Berlin-Brandenburg.

The business is subject to various regulations, including NHTSA vehicle safety standards, state dealer licensing laws that challenge direct-to-consumer sales, and evolving self-driving vehicle laws. Government incentives such as the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 provide tax credits for electric vehicles and clean energy. Tesla also earns revenue from automotive regulatory credits.

Risk factors include macroeconomic conditions and COVID-19 impacts, supply chain constraints including semiconductor shortages, production ramp delays, reliance on key suppliers and raw material pricing, competition in the automotive and energy markets, managing international expansion, product liability and warranty claims, dependence on CEO Elon Musk, and cybersecurity threats. As of December 31, 2022, Tesla had 127,855 full-time employees worldwide, a year-over-year increase of 29,000, and emphasizes ESG initiatives and workforce training programs such as Tesla START.

Evelyn Montiel spent over 20 years working at her family’s ice cream truck and frozen fruit stand in Oakland while excelling as a high school student. After dropping out of an East Coast college due to depression, the nonprofit Students Rising Above helped her enroll at the University of Southern California, where she thrived and held internships. Though she graduated during the recession and returned to the family business, the organization connected her with a national investment firm that launched her finance career. She now works as a broker at a Silicon Valley startup while remaining in East Oakland, crediting the group for helping her succeed.

This Form 10-K is NVIDIA Corporation's annual report for the fiscal year ended January 29, 2017. Headquartered in Santa Clara, California, the company is incorporated in Delaware and its common stock trades on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under the symbol NVDA. As of February 24, 2017, 589 million shares were outstanding.

NVIDIA operates two reportable segments—GPU and Tegra Processor—addressing the Gaming, Professional Visualization, Datacenter, and Automotive markets. GPU brands include GeForce for PC gaming, Quadro for professional design, Tesla and DGX for AI and accelerated computing, and GRID for cloud-based visual computing. Tegra processors integrate computing for mobile gaming, entertainment, and autonomous systems. The company uses a fabless manufacturing model, relying on foundries such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company and Samsung for wafer fabrication and subcontractors for assembly and testing.

In fiscal year 2017, the company recorded $1.46 billion in research and development expenses and employed 10,299 people, including 7,282 in R&D. Sales to ASUSTeK Computer Inc. represented 12% of total revenue, while 80% of revenue came from customers outside the United States and Other Americas. Competitors include Advanced Micro Devices, Intel, Qualcomm, and others.

The filing outlines numerous risks, including dependence on third-party manufacturing and assembly, customer concentration, the conclusion of Intel licensing revenue, product defects, cybersecurity threats, international operational exposures, and competitive pressures. In September 2016, NVIDIA issued $2.00 billion in unsecured notes, and as of January 29, 2017, $827 million in convertible senior notes remained outstanding.

In November 2016, the quarterly cash dividend was raised to $0.14 per share, and fiscal year 2017 dividend payments totaled $261 million. As of January 29, 2017, the company was authorized to repurchase up to $2.73 billion in common stock through December 2020, following prior repurchases totaling 245 million shares for $4.59 billion. For fiscal year 2018, NVIDIA intends to return $1.25 billion to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

The September 26, 2000 VentureWire newsletter from Technologic Partners reports private company business news. Top stories include Chiaro Networks securing over $100 million in third-round funding, Bertelsmann and iSyndicate forming a joint European venture, Novalux raising $109 million in its third round, online jewelry retailer Miadora closing operations, Sun Microsystems launching a $50 million Asian investment program, and Mayfield Fund appointing Jennifer Jones as marketing partner. The issue also details numerous funding rounds under "New Money" for companies in sectors including optical networking, semiconductors, Internet infrastructure, healthcare, energy, and wireless. Additional sections cover new product launches, mergers and acquisitions, board appointments and executive hires, venture capital fund launches and restructurings, and corrections to previous reports regarding Sharing Technologies and epipeline.com.

On November 27, 2001, Enron Corp. faced a deepening financial crisis. The company struggled to find near-term gas and power sellers as trading partners reduced or halted transactions over credit concerns, with over-the-counter trading volume estimated at 25% of prior levels. Dynegy Inc. confirmed talks to restructure its proposed acquisition, potentially cutting the all-stock deal value by over 40% from roughly $9 billion to about $5 billion and lowering the exchange ratio below 0.15. Enron shares traded near $4, down sharply from prior highs around $84. Moody's stated Enron's Baa3 credit rating would remain unchanged for the day. Enron was turned down by investors including Prince Alwaleed, Carlyle Group, and Blackstone Group in efforts to raise up to $2 billion. The company faced a $690 million payment due, sought additional funding and debt maturity extensions, and shut down its equity trading unit. Multiple employee lawsuits were filed over 401(k) losses, and analysts warned that Enron's core trading business was deteriorating, with bankruptcy a risk if the Dynegy deal collapsed.

The DAWN-plasma trial was a randomized, multicenter, open-label phase II study evaluating the efficacy and safety of convalescent plasma combined with standard supportive care versus standard care alone in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. Between May 2020 and January 2021, 489 patients were randomized 2:1 to receive four units (800–1000 mL) of high-titer convalescent plasma (80.7% from donors with neutralizing antibody titers ≥1/320) plus standard care (n=326) or standard care alone (n=163). The primary endpoint, the proportion of patients alive and free of mechanical ventilation at day 15, showed no significant difference between groups (83.7% versus 84.1%; odds ratio 0.99; p=0.976). No statistically significant differences were found for secondary endpoints, including mortality or clinical status at days 15 and 30. Safety outcomes were similar between arms, with comparable rates of adverse events, serious adverse events, and fatal events; transfusion-related side effects occurred in 6.0% of the plasma group, and no TRALI cases were reported. Neutralizing antibody titers increased by day 6 but were not influenced by the intervention, though better clinical outcomes correlated with higher baseline and day 6 titers. The study concluded that early administration of a high volume of high-titer convalescent plasma did not change the natural course of hospitalized COVID-19.

This study analyzed NHANES 2009–2020 data to identify four empirical dietary patterns among 32,498 US adults: “American” (higher refined grains, meats, fats, and added sugars; HEI-2020 score 42.4), “Prudent” (higher vegetables, poultry, seafood, eggs, and oils; HEI 58.2), “Legume” (higher vegetables and legumes; HEI 55.0), and “Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy” (higher fruits, whole grains, soy, nuts, milk, and yogurt; HEI 62.0). The American pattern was most common overall (33.7%). Adults with prevalent cardiovascular disease were more likely to follow the American pattern (37.1%) than those without (33.3%). Higher social determinants of health (SDOH) scores, indicating greater socioeconomic vulnerability, were associated with higher alignment with the American and Legume patterns and lower alignment with the Prudent and Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy patterns. Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) participants (40.2%) and income-eligible non-participants (35.1%) were more likely to follow the American pattern than non-eligible adults (31.9%), and less likely to follow the Prudent and Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy patterns. The associations between SDOH score and dietary patterns, and between SNAP status and dietary patterns, differed significantly by race and ethnicity. The authors conclude that empirical dietary patterns vary by cardiovascular health and socioeconomic vulnerability, and interventions should consider these naturally occurring patterns to inform clinical care and public health efforts.

The State Bar of Michigan e-Journal for June 4, 2001, contains case summaries across multiple practice areas, including Business Law, Civil Rights, Contracts, Criminal Law, Employment & Labor Law, Family Law, Litigation, and Negligence & Intentional Tort, with special note of three Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals opinions. The issue also includes an editorial, classified advertisements, fields of practice listings, news and moves, and upcoming bar events. The email provides instructions for accessing the HTML or plain-text versions and managing subscriptions.
A study finds biased online images train AI to perceive women as younger and less experienced, providing evidence of discrimination against older women in the workforce.

The speaker praises a teammate's stable personality, skill, and playoff goal-scoring under pressure. He notes the team focused on getting pucks in and punishing their defense to win and gain a series advantage. As an eighth seed in the final, the team ignores historical statistics, stays focused on short-term goals, and built confidence through defensive adjustments. After dictating play in the recent game, they aim to repeat that performance.

Retired Justice Anthony Kennedy’s memoir, released October 14, discusses his judicial philosophy and career. He emphasizes judicial humility and integrity, admitting error regarding the execution of minors. Rejecting originalism and pragmatism, he argues constitutional interpretation improves through better perspective without changing the text. He defends opinions in Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission, the decision guaranteeing same-sex couples the right to marry, the case resolving the 2000 presidential election between Gore and Bush, and a First Amendment flag-desecration case, stressing focus on legal issues over politics. Kennedy recounts Justice Scalia’s personal attack in a marriage-case dissent, Scalia’s apology and their final reconciliation before Scalia’s death, and Kennedy’s dislike of the “swing justice” label. He notes his personal opposition to abortion while distinguishing moral from legal wrongs, his view that presidents must defer to Supreme Court rulings, a disturbing meeting with Vladimir Putin, opposition to courtroom cameras, a suspected retaliatory break-in after denying bail to a Manson family member, and his view of his children’s rock music as avant-garde.

The Wham play is a complementary run concept similar to Trap in which a Tight End or Fullback pulls to kick out a Defensive Lineman. It creates quick, unexpected favorable angles but is complex to teach and requires a powerful blocker. The passage details player assignments against 3-4 Odd and 4-3 Even fronts, including double teams, second-level climbs, and kickout blocks. It also describes two variations: Gun H-Back Wham RPO, where the Fullback blocks the Nose Tackle and the quarterback can throw a slant or bubble based on the flat defender; and Shotgun Influence Wham, which traps a widening 3-tech who reacts to a pulling Guard.

Facebook's new "Trending News" section in the Explore tab ranks stories by publication shares. Tapping a story shows headlines, videos, photos and posts. It follows May plans to redesign Trending Topics to show coverage and relevant discussions.

A descriptive cross-sectional study at CUSP in Huye district, Rwanda, assessed horizontal Hepatitis C virus (HCV) transmission among 148 household members of HCV-positive patients from 30 families. Using HCV antibody rapid tests and ELISA confirmation, the study found an HCV prevalence of 10.8% (16 participants). Risk factor analysis showed significant associations with HBV history (p=0.001), HIV history (p=0.001), and unprotected sex (p=0.016), while blood transfusion history (p=0.058) and awareness (p=0.079) were not statistically significant. Awareness was very low, with 93.9% of participants providing incorrect answers about transmission. The authors conclude that horizontal intra-familial transmission contributes to increased HCV prevalence, with unprotected sex as the primary risk factor. They recommend early screening of household members, improved patient follow-up, public education, and further countrywide or phylogenetic research to determine infection origins. The study was limited by its cross-sectional design and single-district scope.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated March 13, 2020, reporting that Bill Gates resigned from its Board of Directors effective March 13, 2020. The filing includes a press release announcing the resignation and lists registered securities including common stock, 2.125% notes due 2021, 3.125% notes due 2028, and 2.625% notes due 2033.

Iqaluit-Tasiluk MLA George Hickes told the Nunavut legislature on May 29, 2018, that Government of Nunavut civil servants are being intimidated by senior managers and told not to speak to their MLAs, reviving concerns he first raised in 2014. Hickes cited specific examples but kept details confidential, noting a culture of discomfort within the public service. He asked Minister David Akeeagok whether the Public Service Act prohibits such communication or if senior managers had issued directives against it. Akeeagok said no, confirming employees are free to speak with MLAs and are protected under the act and by an ethics officer. Hickes said constituents have a right to contact MLAs without fear of repercussions, particularly in small communities, and that such feedback is essential for elected members.

President Donald Trump nominated Travis Hill to chair the U.S. Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation. Hill, a former senior adviser at the Treasury Department, requires Senate confirmation. The nomination aligns with Trump’s deregulatory agenda, with Hill expected to balance financial stability and lighter regulatory burdens. If confirmed, he will oversee deposit insurance, set bank assessments, address sector failures, and influence debates on insurance limits and crisis intervention. The appointment is likely to draw Congressional scrutiny over potential regulatory leniency amid financial uncertainty.

The Mining Expo & Conference will be held on April 25 and 26 at the Windhoek Show Grounds under the theme “Maximising the multiplier effect from Namibia’s mining sector.” Nedbank Namibia CIB will showcase its mining finance capabilities, sharing insights on global positioning and foreign investment. Led by Dominic Shikola, the team provides complete funding solutions, including transaction structuring and capital access. Mining contributes about 11 percent of Namibia’s GDP, and Nedbank aims to maximise the sector’s multiplier effect while supporting Vision 2030.

The speaker declined to discuss specific penalties, physical altercations, or injuries, noting such incidents are part of playoff hockey. He identified the game's turning point as an offensive zone faceoff loss that led to a turnover, a penalty, and an opponent's power-play goal. He emphasized the need to win the next game, maintain momentum, and respond to setbacks within a series. He defended lineup decisions, including using seven defensemen for flexibility and keeping Nolan in the lineup for chemistry despite Pratt's strong play filling in for an injured Jason. He stated faceoffs and puck possession are critical, downplayed third-period fights as normal playoff hockey, discussed moving Rusty to a grinding role to increase involvement, and said Marty St. Louis is motivated by proving doubters wrong.

This October 18, 2001 email from Commissioner.COM to Paul Lucci at Enron provides fantasy football E-Reports for the team "Get Bad with Yourself." It opens with promotional offers for football games, NFL memorabilia, subscriptions, contests, and software. The bulk of the message consists of NFL player news updates dated October 14–18, 2001, detailing injuries, practice statuses, and fantasy football recommendations for numerous players and teams. It includes a dedicated section for the fantasy team "Luccis Losers." The email is copyrighted by Commissioner.COM Inc and SportsLine.com Inc.

The paper introduces the Construction Defining Functionality (CDF) framework for analyzing computational problems through three structural spaces: syntactic (Ssyn), defining formal generative rules; semantic (Ssem), encoding input-output interpretations and satisfying configurations; and logical (Slog), containing proof or computation trees. These spaces are linked by mappings αf : Ssyn → Ssem, βf : Ssem → Slog, and γf : Ssyn → Slog. CDF treats intensionality as internal generative structure and extensionality as observable behavior, classifying problems as ComCDF when they exhibit compositional coherence (γf = βf ◦ αf) and polynomially stable semantic growth, or as ExpCDF when recursive syntactic structure causes explosive, unstable semantic expansion. The framework is applied to distinguish 2-SAT and 3-SAT: 2-SAT’s binary clauses allow local implication graphs and stable, polynomial-time reasoning, whereas 3-SAT’s ternary clauses produce non-local, non-decomposable variable dependencies that make αf explosive and drive semantic space growth of O(2^n). The paper argues that 3-SAT’s intractability is an intrinsic structural consequence of this syntactic non-locality, not merely an algorithmic limitation.

Patents grant temporary monopolies; upon expiration, inventions become publicly available. Desktop FDM printers trace back to Scott Crump’s 1992 patent, while Stratasys still sells industrial systems up to $400,000. Industrial printers average $104,222 ($566,570 for metal), compared to $1,094 for desktop machines. Stereolithography and powder bed fusion also serve industrial and consumer markets at vastly different price points. Industrial additive manufacturing uses plastics, metals, and ceramics for high-volume, large-scale aerospace, automotive, and medical parts, such as NASA propulsion components and GE engine parts that reduce weight, cost, and part counts. Expiring patents spread industrial advances to broader markets. The Wohlers Report 2017 is a key industry resource.

European shares rose on March 23, 2017, as Britain formally began Brexit proceedings, with the STOXX 600 and German DAX each climbing 0.4 percent to multi-month highs. Auto stocks gained on Daimler's expected record sales, while banks fell on ECB policy signals. Deutsche Bank rose on its cash call. The London Stock Exchange and Deutsche Boerse advanced despite regulators blocking their merger. Engie and 3I Group rose on broker upgrades, Scout24 fell on weak results, and Aurelius plunged after investors rejected its rebuttal of a short-seller report.

At the UN Climate Summit, Xi Jinping reaffirmed China’s commitment to leading the global clean energy transition as other major economies retreat from climate priorities. China pledged to cut greenhouse gas emissions by 7 to 10 percent by 2035, its first target to reduce rather than merely slow emissions. Xi committed to 3,600 gigawatts of installed wind and solar capacity by 2035, an energy mix exceeding 30 percent renewables, mainstream electric vehicles, an expanded carbon trading market, and forest extent of 34 billion cubic meters. China invested $625 billion in clean energy last year, nearly one-third of the global total. Its large domestic market has driven down renewable technology prices, reshaped the global economy, and replaced coal domestically. While China’s annual emission reduction pace is slower than that of some industrialized nations, analysts suggest it may overdeliver, and its policies are not at risk of reversal each election cycle.

An open-label randomised controlled trial in Kampong Speu, Cambodia, compared the efficacy of 3·5 mg/kg and 7·0 mg/kg total doses of primaquine over 14 days versus no primaquine for preventing Plasmodium vivax recurrences. After seven days of artesunate, G6PD-normal patients were randomised to one of the three arms, while G6PD-deficient patients were assigned to the no-primaquine arm; participants were then relocated to a non-malarial area for 90 days. Among 156 patients, the 90-day recurrence rate was 81·4% with no primaquine, 24·4% with the 3·5 mg/kg regimen, and 4·7% with the 7·0 mg/kg regimen. The 7·0 mg/kg dose significantly reduced the risk of recurrence compared with the 3·5 mg/kg dose (hazard ratio 0·17, p=0·0229). Both primaquine regimens were well tolerated, with no serious adverse events; adverse events and anaemia were more common in the no-primaquine arm. The authors conclude that the 7·0 mg/kg primaquine regimen should be recommended in Cambodia and likely other Southeast Asian countries to reduce P. vivax relapses.

Sebi allowed debt issuers to request reviews of credit ratings by credit rating agencies to curb rating shopping. Reviews must be conducted by committees with a majority of independent members. Rating agencies must disclose non-accepted ratings for 12 months and upload half-yearly rating summary sheets within 15 days. Disclosures must be prepared separately for securities and other financial instruments. The decision follows stakeholder feedback on a consultation paper issued last year.

Paulo Dybala is fit to face Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-final return leg after training. He renewed his Juventus contract until 2022 by choice, expressing happiness, and his first-leg goals were crucial.

LG will release webOS-powered TVs later this month with Sky EPG compatibility from launch, enabling users to view and control Sky content seamlessly using LG's Magic Remote. The webOS "Today" menu aggregates viewing options from apps, online platforms, and live TV.

Pan Finance reports global financial news including JPMorgan Chase's AI integration, the Bank of England's largest six-month repo since 2020, Tesla's record Q3 deliveries, and U.S. and European stock movements. The U.S. froze $18 billion in New York City infrastructure funds over DEI contract concerns, suspending a $300 million DOT payment and delaying the Second Avenue Subway and Hudson River Tunnel. Coverage also includes Iran and Russia's $25 billion nuclear deal, Sempra's $10 billion stake sale and LNG expansion, OpenAI's $500 billion valuation and parental controls, a proposed 1:1 U.S. domestic chip rule, Singapore threatening Meta with fines, and Italy's business lobby cutting growth forecasts.

The Ministry of Justice admitted overcharging English councils by about £9m annually since 2013-14 for council tax summons fees after an administrative error added £2.50 per application. Councils are due full refunds, with fees cut. The error will cost £9m in revenue. Councils issued 3.5 million summons last year, while legal costs for arrears reached £292m in 2016-17, and over 4,800 people were taken to court for non-payment.

Melinda Rosetti-Spence was sentenced to 10 years for embezzling about $266,600 from cancer charity Pink Hearts Fund, where she was treasurer. A judge ordered repayment of about $181,000. She pleaded guilty to writing 132 checks to herself in 2016, citing a gambling problem. The charity's founder accused her of betrayal and stalking. She made no repayments since her arrest two years prior.

STAT's "Up and down the ladder" column tracks pharmaceutical industry personnel changes and invites readers to submit staffing updates. This week's feature notes that enGene hired Hussein Sweiti as chief medical officer; previously, he was global medical head of oncology clinical development at Johnson & Johnson. The full article is exclusive to STAT+ subscribers.

The Council of Regional Accrediting Commissions (CRAC), representing seven agencies overseeing 3,000 institutions, issued a statement supporting the use of artificial intelligence to streamline college credit transfer evaluations. The council emphasized that leveraging AI to assess course equivalencies and expand matches does not conflict with accreditation standards. Currently, manual credit evaluation is inconsistent and decentralized, resulting in significant credit loss, delays, and racial disparities that hinder degree completion. CRAC encourages institutions to adopt a default position of accepting transfer credits unless evidence shows required learning outcomes are unmet, using AI to analyze course data and reduce administrative burdens while maintaining human oversight. The statement is not a mandate but aims to spur innovation, address inequities, and free faculty to focus on student support. A pilot program involving 59 institutions is already testing an AI platform to identify course equivalencies.

A 2,100-year-old chalk bowl fragment engraved with "Hyrcanus" was unearthed in 2015 beneath a mikvah in Jerusalem's City of David and announced by the Israel Antiquities Authority. The name matches two Hasmonean kings but was common then, making ownership by royalty or a commoner uncertain. The fragment, one of Jerusalem's earliest chalk vessels, was found near remains of the Akra fortress.

Sheriff's detectives are investigating a Tuesday robbery at Summerland Antique Collective where a man bound female employees with duct tape, stole cash and merchandise. The suspect is a black male in late 20s or early 30s, muscular, wearing black. No serious injuries.

Bollinger Bands, created by John Bollinger, comprise a middle simple moving average band (default 20-day) and upper/lower bands calculated using standard deviations (default 2). The bands dynamically expand and contract to reflect market volatility. The article outlines numerous trading strategies, including the Squeeze (identifying low volatility periods preceding potential breakouts), Breakouts (trading price moves through upper or lower bands), %B (quantifying price position relative to the bands), Walks (following strong trends along the bands), and Bounce (mean reversion). Testing indicates the tool is somewhat profitable in mean-reverting stock markets and shows promise as a breakout indicator in commodities like gold, but strategies were not effective for stock indices. Traders can adjust settings such as the SMA period, standard deviation multiplier, and moving average type. Shorter timeframes increase signal frequency but also false positives, while longer timeframes improve reliability. Bollinger Bands have limitations, including delayed signals and false overbought/oversold readings during strong trends, and should be paired with other technical indicators and risk management techniques rather than used in isolation.

Apple Inc.'s March 1, 2019 Form 8-K reports Annual Meeting shareholder voting results. Directors were elected; Ernst & Young LLP was ratified as the 2019 independent accounting firm; and executive compensation was approved via advisory resolution. Shareholder proposals on proxy access amendments and a true diversity board policy were not approved. Katherine Adams signed the report on March 4, 2019.

Cryotherapy exposes users to sub-zero chamber temperatures and is gaining U.S. popularity, including at West Michigan's Polar Brrr Cryo. Invented in the 1970s by Japanese doctor Toshima Yamauchi for arthritis, claimed benefits include muscle recovery, reduced inflammation, and calorie burning. It is not FDA approved, with warnings against frostbite, burns, and eye injuries, and lacks substantial scientific backing. Supervised sessions last three minutes. Polar Brrr serves various clients, though those with heart problems or hypertension must consult a doctor. Introductory pricing is $25 for the first session or $90 for three; regular sessions cost $55.

The holiday effect is a stock market anomaly where stocks tend to generate increased returns around certain holidays. The article examines this seasonality in the S&P 500 across seven U.S. holidays: Martin Luther King Jr. Day, President’s Day, Easter, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas. Backtests show the effect is generally small and not a get-rich-quick strategy, but Independence Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas show significant patterns. The Independence Day strategy produced a 1.01% average gain and profit factor of 2.97; Thanksgiving produced 0.82% and 2.72; and the end-of-year Christmas rally produced a 1% average gain and profit factor of 4.8. Other holidays showed weak or negative results, including President’s Day (-0.24%) and Labor Day (0.11%). Potential causes cited include lower liquidity, holiday optimism, reduced macro news, and pre-holiday selling pressure creating a vacuum. Regarding post-holiday effects, holding over the holiday produced no gains, but the second trading day after showed stronger returns. A two-variable post-holiday strategy yielded a 0.56% average gain, 71% win ratio, and 3.5% annual return while invested only 1% of the time.

Scottish councils may raise basic council tax by up to 3% this year, ending the government freeze policy. However, about 700,000 households (26%) in bands E-H will see bills rise regardless due to multiplier increases approved by MSPs, raising £100m annually. Average band E households will pay roughly £2 more per week and band H about £10 more. The impact varies significantly by region, with over half of East Renfrewshire properties affected compared to 18% in East Ayrshire. Council tax bands remain based on 1991 property values; studies suggest 57% of homes would change band if revalued, though the government opposes this citing cost and disruption. Local authorities rely mainly on government grants, and the Scottish budget has sparked political dispute. Finance Secretary Derek Mackay's original plan cut core council grants while directing funds to specific services, but a deal with the Greens added £160m direct funding. Labour argues councils still face a £170m cut, while Greens say the deal takes allocations from "a severe cut" to "just about good enough".

Amazon is developing an AI chip for Alexa, which starred in the top Super Bowl YouTube ad. Strong Echo Dot sales and CES wins contrasted with price-war losses alongside Google. CES featured robot dogs and foldable TVs. Apple delayed its home speaker, a German Alexa went rogue, and Alexa will soon power Big Mouth Billy Bass.

On October 29, 2001, news reports detailed Enron Corp.'s severe financial crisis. Moody's Investors Service downgraded Enron's senior unsecured debt to Baa2 and placed all long-term ratings on review for further downgrade, while Standard & Poor's revised its outlook to negative. Enron's stock fell to near seven-year lows, losing roughly half its value in two weeks. The company, facing an SEC inquiry into off-balance-sheet partnerships run by recently ousted CFO Andrew Fastow, had reported a significant third-quarter loss and over $1 billion in charges and equity reductions. Enron drew down approximately $3 billion in credit lines and was negotiating with banks for $1 billion to $2 billion in additional financing to shore up liquidity. While some U.S. energy traders said dealings remained normal, European counterparts reportedly froze transactions amid credit concerns. Enron's bonds dropped sharply to around 80 cents on the dollar before recovering slightly, with yields near 12.1 percent. Analysts characterized the credit drawdown as an act of desperation, warned that lenders could demand harsher terms or collateral, and noted that a commercial paper downgrade could impede daily trading operations. One report speculated Royal Dutch/Shell might be a takeover target, while a research firm suggested a junk rating was unlikely despite poor disclosure.

This document is the AMD SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block Specification Agreement, a legal agreement between AMD and the recipient that governs access to and use of the attached technical Specification. It permits review solely as a reference for planning and designing products to interface with AMD products and for providing Feedback; it grants no intellectual property rights, prohibits duplication and redistribution, disclaims all warranties, provides the Specification entirely “AS IS,” limits AMD’s liability, imposes U.S. and other export control obligations, and is governed by California law.

The technical specification standardizes the GHCB, a 4KB decrypted memory page that enables a guest OS and hypervisor to communicate during Non-Automatic Exits (NAE) when SEV-ES or SEV-SNP is active. These features encrypt guest register state during world switches, preventing direct hypervisor access. Automatic Exits require no state exposure, while NAE events trigger a VMM Communication Exception (#VC), allowing the guest to selectively share state in the GHCB via VMGEXIT. Version 1 supports SEV-ES. Version 2 introduces SEV-SNP support, hypervisor feature advertisement through a FEATURES bitmap, and additions including XSS MSR values, Page State Change support for SEV-ES, APIC ID list retrieval, multi-VMPL execution, SEV-TIO trusted I/O, Secure AVIC, and updated secrets page and certificate request mechanisms. Revisions 2.01 through 2.04 added 64-bit guest request sequence numbers, VLEK GUID definitions, expanded error codes, and SEV-TIO/Secure AVIC documentation. The GHCB layout mirrors the SEV-ES VMCB save state area. The GHCB MSR protocol (MSR 0xc001_0130) facilitates early communication for protocol negotiation, CPUID requests, AP reset hold, GHCB GPA registration (required for SEV-SNP), page state changes, Run VMPL, and termination. Supported NAE events include IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, #NPF/MMIO, Page State Change, SNP Guest Request, SNP Extended Guest Request, SNP TIO Guest Request, SNP AP Creation, #HV Doorbell Page, #HV IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, Secure AVIC backing page registration, and Termination Request. The document defines standard VMGEXIT processing, error handling via SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2, and VALID_BITMAP requirements. SMP booting requires special handling because the hypervisor cannot modify encrypted AP register state after measurement; alternatives include AP Reset Hold, AP Jump Table set/get operations, and SNP AP Creation using VMSA pages. NMI handling requires the hypervisor to avoid intercepting IRET but to intercept #DB, relying on a guest “NMI Complete” message. Debug register virtualization is supported if hardware allows; otherwise DR7 accesses are intercepted and cached by the guest #VC handler. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported. Under SNP Restricted Injection, the hypervisor notifies the guest through a shared #HV doorbell page containing PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields.

Russia has marked Ukrainian drone pilots as high-priority targets, increasingly attacking suspected operator positions with missiles, bombs, and other weapons. Ukrainian soldiers and operators say pilots are targeted because drones are responsible for roughly 70% of battlefield casualties and are critical for intelligence, strikes, and artillery targeting. The death toll has risen sharply, prompting Ukrainian pilots to adopt protective measures such as operating underground and rotating positions frequently. Ukraine also targets Russian drone pilots, viewing them as high-value threats.

While the NHS commonly cites two liters, the recommended intake is 6-8 glasses (1.2 liters) daily, with some water obtained from food. Excessive consumption can cause rare but fatal water intoxication, and research suggests drinking according to thirst rather than a strict schedule. Studies indicate that drinking water before meals reduces calorie intake and increases weight loss. Overhydration has also caused deaths among marathon athletes.

The passage traces the history of software patterns from Donald Knuth’s general-purpose algorithms and object-oriented design patterns to open-source reusable components, establishing that patterns provide a shared vocabulary, enable learning from others’ experiences, and support the creation of reusable libraries.

The text introduces single-node container patterns. The sidecar pattern augments an application container to add functionality—such as proxying HTTPS, synchronizing dynamic configuration, or monitoring resources—without modifying the main application. Effective sidecars require parameterization, a stable API surface, and documentation. The ambassador pattern brokers interactions between an application and external systems, enabling client-side sharding, service brokering, and request splitting for experimentation. The adapter pattern standardizes interfaces across heterogeneous applications for monitoring, logging, and health checking.

The passage then addresses multi-node distributed patterns. Microservices architectures improve reliability, agility, and independent scaling but increase debugging and design complexity. The replicated load-balanced services pattern distributes traffic across identical stateless instances, with adaptations for session tracking, caching layers for performance, denial-of-service defense via rate limiting, and SSL termination. Sharded services partition state across multiple shards when data exceeds single-machine capacity; sharded caching improves memory utilization and throughput, though individual shard failures degrade performance. Replicated sharded caches combine sharding with replication to improve resilience.

Basketball teams must prepare for defensive, even, and offensive jump ball situations. Defensive situations require early rotation, watching the jumper’s eyes and hands to anticipate tip direction, and using Box, Diamond, and "Y" alignments to prevent easy scores if the opponent gains possession. Even jump balls require boxing out, establishing inside position, and executing coordinated clockwise or counter-clockwise rotations based on a predetermined signal. Offensive jump balls with a height advantage of 6 inches or more allow for set plays—including Ball Possession, Double Tap, Post Split, Jumper Fly, Forward Fly, Spread, Tandem, and Loop—with instructions to generally tip forward to the tallest player, maintain defensive balance, and flow into a set or motion offense if a quick shot is unavailable.

A U.S. official warned Mr. Toivola that an alleged Finnish Legation statement blaming Anglo-Americans for Soviet-Finnish peace rumors would harm Finnish interests. On January 20, 1942, Finnish Minister Procopé questioned U.S. travel restrictions on legation staff, noting Helsinki was in a war zone and restrictions applied equally to all foreign diplomats. The British Embassy reported that the USSR had secretly informed Finland via Swedish channels of readiness to discuss peace, with better terms available immediately. The U.S. and Britain agreed on a firm stance toward Finland to facilitate peace, and the Secretary of State instructed the U.S. Minister in Finland to convey this position to Witting regarding his optimistic remarks of January 20.

The speaker celebrates winning the Stanley Cup with the Pittsburgh Penguins.
