He recalls telling Fleury to make saves, jokes about his own stick-handling despite scoring two goals, and notes Geno won the Conn Smythe. He highlights the team's sacrifice for injured leader Sidney Crosby, praises Fleury as a winning goaltender, and credits Mario with keeping the team in Pittsburgh four years earlier.

Survivors and relatives of the 72 Grenfell Tower victims gave emotional tributes as a public inquiry began in London. Ahmed Elgwahry described being on the phone as his mother and sister died, while others criticized fire authorities for telling residents to remain in their apartments as flames spread. Inquiry chair Martin Moore-Bick agreed to start with victims' stories before examining technical causes like flammable cladding. Testimonies underscored anger at the local council, building managers, and government for failing to heed safety warnings. Families recounted specific losses, including Paulos Tekle's 5-year-old son, who died after the family was told to stay inside, and Marcio Gomes's son, born prematurely after his wife fell into a coma. Survivors insisted that keeping victims central to the inquiry also highlights concerns that social inequality contributed to the disaster.

Per Chancel and Piketty, India's income inequality rose rapidly from the 1980s, with the top 1% capturing 22% of national income, the highest since 1922. This followed pro-business policies from 1984. From the 1950s to 1970s, market regulations reduced inequality, benefiting the bottom 50% and middle 40%. Since the mid-1980s, growth concentrated among the top 10%, giving India one of the highest top 1% income share increases.

Systematic, data-driven identification of non-genetic direct risk factors remains uncommon compared to genetic studies, partly because mediation, confounding, and widespread correlation complicate the analysis of biobank-scale data. The authors propose Doublethink, a Bayesian model averaging method that tests whether a variable has a direct effect on an outcome while averaging over uncertainty in the inclusion of all other variables. Under a specific prior and large-sample assumption, Doublethink creates a correspondence between model-averaged posterior odds and frequentist p-values, allowing simultaneous control of the Bayesian false discovery rate and the frequentist familywise error rate. Applied to 1,912 pre-2020 variables in UK Biobank for COVID-19 hospitalization (1,917 cases and 200,000 controls), the analysis identified nine significant individual variables, including unspecified dementia, acute lower respiratory infection, tendency to fall, carer support, and history of psychoactive substance abuse, while educational qualifications were protective. Established factors such as age, sex, and deprivation were significant only when tested as groups of correlated variables. Compared with 127 published studies, commonly analyzed factors like obesity and smoking were supported, but frequently studied conditions such as diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and hypertension showed no significant direct effect, suggesting their effects may be mediated. Conversely, rarely studied categories—including psychiatric disorders, infection, dementia, and aging—showed strong direct effects. The method is limited to direct rather than total effects, is computationally intensive, and relies on large-sample approximations.

Pauli–Fierz Hamiltonian describes cavity electron–photon interactions yielding polaritonic states. Quantum chemistry fails for non-local coupling. Orthonormal, systematically improvable sinc basis on uniform real-space grid proposed; two-electron integrals scale as O(N^4), but sparse approximations enabled by decaying off-diagonal elements. Band-limited sinc suits delocalized interactions. Cavity photon fields are quantum harmonic oscillators.

Donald Trump initially offered vague condemnation of the Charlottesville white supremacist rally. After Merck CEO Ken Frazier resigned from the American Manufacturing Council to protest intolerance, Trump attacked him on Twitter over drug prices before denouncing white supremacists. Elon Musk and Disney's Robert Igor previously resigned from advisory councils over the Paris Climate Accord withdrawal.

ResearchAndMarkets.com added the "Global Industrial Hybrid Stepper Motors Market 2018-2022" report, projecting market revenue exceeding $1,000 million by 2022. The report identifies increasing focus on miniaturized stepper motors as a key trend, rising demand for automated industrial equipment as a primary driver, and competition from servo and conventional stepper motors as a major challenge. Key vendors include AMETEK, MinebeaMitsumi, Moons', Nidec, and Schneider Electric. The report covers market landscape, sizing, forecasts, application and regional segmentation, and vendor analysis.

Defending baseline out of bounds plays differs from standard defense because the defense has a numerical advantage (5 on 4), yet most coaches devote little attention to these situations. Unlike regular half-court sets where shooters move off screens away from the basket, baseline out of bounds shooters cut directly to the basket, leaving no room for defensive error. While some teams automatically play zone, zones struggle to adjust to the ball being behind the basket and remain susceptible to screens, rolls, and overloads. The passage details four strategies to exploit the numerical advantage. The "Jam" option employs aggressive, non-switching denial to disrupt plays and draw offensive fouls. "Jump Switching" aggressively switches and denies passing lanes to create turnovers, particularly viable with less than five seconds on the clock. The "Trap" option double-teams the inbounds pass receiver. "Combination Defenses"—including box-and-one, diamond-and-one, and triangle-and-two—seek to catch the offense off guard. Each strategy generally begins with sagging off to protect the middle, then smothering the inbounder, and transitioning to half-court pressure once the ball is inbounded.

This preprint reports a cross-sectional study using RNA sequencing and immunohistochemistry to identify the molecular signature of neuropathic pain in human nerves. Researchers compared 22 surgically excised Morton's neuroma samples against 11 control nerve samples. Differential expression analysis identified over 3,349 genes, with upregulation of immune and inflammatory response pathways and downregulation of nervous system development processes including myelination and axon guidance. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified modules related to defence response, neurogenesis, and muscle system processes that correlated with pain phenotypes. Deconvolution analysis revealed increased macrophage and memory B cell proportions in neuroma samples, with macrophage proportions correlating with paroxysmal pain severity. Genes specific to an M(GC) macrophage subset (MARCO, CD163, STAB1) were upregulated, and MARCO expression correlated with paroxysmal pain. Immunofluorescence confirmed demyelination, increased intraneural T-cell density, and elevated CD163+MARCO+ macrophage densities in neuroma samples, while CD68+ macrophage density correlated with burning pain. The findings suggest that persistent neuroinflammation involving specific macrophage subsets and impaired nervous system maintenance characterize chronic human neuropathic pain in Morton's neuroma.

Two stocks offer forecast dividend yields of 7.1%. Taylor Wimpey targets £1.3bn in shareholder returns from 2016-2018, with a £450m payout planned for 2017. The author considers this affordable and sustainable due to 2016 free cash flow of £511.6m and strong housing demand, though cyclical conditions mean payouts may not last indefinitely. Connect Group's expected 9.8p 2017 dividend is supported by strong cash generation, but the firm has £141.7m net debt and negative net tangible assets of £151.8m. The author warns that trading slowdowns or tighter lending could force a dividend cut, concluding risks outweigh rewards.

A 2017 RPS survey of 462 found 79% rated service very good to excellent, over 80% agreed RPS had integrity and honesty, but nearly 25% felt RPS was insensitive to Indigenous people. Reconciliation training will address this.

The Schrödinger bridge (SB) problem seeks stochastic dynamics between distributions, solved by iterative proportional fitting (IPF). Existing IPF requires samples from both marginals and fails for unnormalised densities. The authors propose data-to-energy and energy-to-energy IPF for unnormalised densities using off-policy RL techniques from diffusion samplers, as the first general method for such bridges. Contributions include learning low-cost bridges on synthetic data, improving data-to-data IPF via learned diffusion coefficients and drift, and data-free image-to-image translation via latent-space prior-to-posterior translation. The SB problem is formalized as KL divergence minimization to a reference process subject to marginal constraints, reducing to drift inference, with IPF recursing from the reference process.

Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay held a private meeting in Beverly Hills with prominent Californians including Arnold Schwarzenegger, Los Angeles Mayor Richard Riordan, and Michael Milken to pitch a deregulation plan to solve California’s energy crisis; attendees were reportedly noncommittal. The proposal called for consumers to pay public utility debt, an end to investigations, and opposed a state power authority. Senator Dianne Feinstein called for hearings into possible improprieties between FERC members and private energy interests, citing a report that Lay offered to support FERC Chairman Curtis Hebert’s continuation if he endorsed Enron’s deregulation views. The speaker discussed a one-goal hockey game decided by an early goal and a penalty call, noting missed second-period scoring chances. Overnight trading involves buying at the close and selling at the next day’s open or close. The passage presents multiple backtested S&P 500 strategies—such as Turnaround Tuesday, holiday seasonality, end-of-month effects, weekday effects, mean reversion, and options expiration—with trade counts ranging from 94 to 373 and average gains typically between 0.2% and 0.55%. A portfolio combining these strategies showed strong historical performance, but effective construction requires uncorrelated strategies across different asset classes, time frames, and styles to reduce overlapping signals and mitigate drawdowns. The authors emphasize that avoiding severe drawdowns aids compounding, that short-selling strategies are difficult but can provide downside risk reduction, and that mechanical execution is necessary. Out-of-sample testing from 2018 onward produced an average gain of 0.34% per trade.

The speaker emphasizes team depth, camaraderie, and defensive strength as keys to success. Against power forwards, he stresses positional play, respecting opponents' strengths, and avoiding unnecessary physical battles. He notes that learning from veterans like Ray Bourque and playing defined roles keeps players fresh. Reaching the finals again after a long absence reflects the team's determination and experience, but he insists they must ignore external pressure and media hype to focus on simple, fundamental play.

Soccer Small Sided Games (SSGs) involve teams of fewer than 11 players on reduced fields, used in both practice and competition to increase individual ball touches and player development. Practice SSGs, ranging from 3v3 to 9v9, target specific tactical themes in restricted spaces for ages U6 through U16. In August 2017, U.S. Soccer introduced Player Development Initiatives (PDIs) establishing national competitive standards for U6 to U12, featuring fewer players, smaller fields, goals, and balls, shorter game times, and modified rules. These include build-out lines at U9 to encourage possession, no offside before U9, and bans on headers and goalkeeper punts or drop kicks. Local youth organizations implement these standards nationwide.

Gonzalo Curiel, 20, was convicted in the 2015 killings of a 7-year-old boy and 3-year-old sister, and of torturing their older sister. Bodies were found in a storage unit. Tami Huntsman, 42, pleaded guilty to murder. The surviving sister testified. Both face sentencing next week.

The passage describes analyte monitoring systems and methods for sterilizing them while protecting sensitive electronics. It notes that radiation sterilization can damage electronic components, while gaseous chemical sterilization can damage sensor chemistry, making it difficult to sterilize integrated devices. The described system includes a sensor applicator, a cap, and a sensor control device with an electronics housing, a sensor, a sharp hub, and a sharp. A collimator is positioned within the cap or externally adjacent the applicator and defines a sterilization zone configured to receive the sensor and sharp. The collimator focuses radiation sterilization onto the sensor and sharp while preventing the radiation from damaging electronic components within the electronics housing. Seals may create a sealed region encompassing the sterilization zone and part of the housing interior. The passage also describes external sterilization assemblies with radiation shields and collimators for similar focused sterilization of medical devices. These approaches allow the system to be pre-assembled and terminally sterilized without requiring separate user assembly of individually sterilized components.

SpaceX will launch a Dragon spacecraft to the ISS at 12:31 pm ET from Kennedy Space Center, recovering the first stage. The mission carries 6,400 pounds of supplies, including scientific hardware and ice cream. It is the last new Dragon craft NASA will send to the ISS; future missions will use flight-proven hardware.

This patent application claims priority to prior U.S. applications and was developed with Department of Energy support, which retains certain rights. It relates to metal-assisted delayed fluorescent (MADF) emitters comprising cyclic platinum(II), palladium(II), and iridium(III) complexes employing benzo-imidazo-phenanthridine and analogues for organic light-emitting diodes and lighting applications. The complexes, defined by General Formulas I–XVII, feature small singlet-triplet energy gaps that enable emission through both thermally assisted delayed fluorescence and phosphorescence. The disclosure includes detailed chemical definitions, substituent options, synthetic examples preparing ligands L1–L31 and complexes MC1–MC31, and device implementations incorporating the emitters.

The Syrian opposition's High Negotiations Committee wants direct negotiations with the government in Geneva next week on political transition without Assad. Spokesman Salim al-Muslit said the group has not received an agenda and cited the 2012 Geneva communique on a transitional body. The HNC named a 22-member delegation for talks launched after government forces defeated rebels in Aleppo.

Tesla Motors, Inc.'s March 3, 2015 Form 8-K reports Board approval, effective March 3, 2015, of an amendment to the 2010 Equity Incentive Plan prohibiting repricing transactions, and an amendment to the bylaws adopting a majority vote standard for uncontested director elections while retaining plurality for contested elections. Neither amendment requires stockholder approval. The amended plan and bylaws are filed as Exhibits 10.1 and 3.1.

Global Fund.

Dr. Pasvolsky explained Chapter III's "peace-loving states" criterion emphasizes devotion to peace; new members would be admitted by the Assembly on Security Council recommendation. The Mexican Ambassador stressed cooperation for permanent peace. The lecture details the construction of Succinct Non-Interactive Arguments (SNARGs) from Batch Arguments (BARGs) and somewhere extractable hash functions, also referred to as somewhere statistically binding hash functions. The professor first recalls the definition of a BARG for an NP language, consisting of generation, prover, and verifier algorithms where the proof size is polylogarithmic in the number of batched instances k and polynomial in a single witness. Semi-adaptive soundness is defined, requiring a cheating prover to commit to its cheating index before seeing the common reference string. The lecture then defines somewhere extractable hash functions, comprising Gen, Eval, Open, Ver, and Extract algorithms, which satisfy completeness, index hiding, and somewhere statistical binding; repeating the construction l times yields binding on l locations while keeping unrevealed indices hidden. The construction uses fully homomorphic encryption with a chain of public keys and encrypted secret keys to ensure well-formed ciphertexts along the opening path. Finally, the SNARG construction is described: the prover computes all wires of the verification circuit, hashes the wire values using the somewhere extractable hash, and generates a BARG proving that every gate is satisfied and the output wire is 1. Because the BARG statements form an index language with a succinct description, the verifier runs efficiently without linear dependence on the number of gates.

The passage references an Irish Times report by Kitty Holland about a pregnant, suicidal girl detained under the Mental Health Act after being denied a requested abortion; she was later released when a second psychiatrist found no evidence of a mental health disorder. The author connects this case to broader concerns about psychiatry, recalling their grandmother’s forced detention and ECT treatment against family wishes, and their own depression diagnosis based on DSM symptoms. It argues that mental illness definitions are shaped by culture and politics, distinguishes brain illness from mental illness, questions the chemical imbalance theory, cites low reported efficacy for SSRIs, and states that psychiatry operates without the rigorous falsification standards of other medical fields and that mental illness remains poorly understood.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated June 28, 2021, reporting Andrew R. Jassy’s promotion to President and Chief Executive Officer effective July 5, 2021. The Board elected Jassy as a director effective the same date. The Company approved a restricted stock unit award of 61,000 shares vesting over ten years, security arrangements, and an indemnification agreement. Jassy joined Amazon in 1997 and has led Amazon Web Services since its inception.

Coupling an optical cavity directly to the quantum-critical order parameter of a magnetic system—exemplified by the transverse-field Ising model—allows a superradiant phase transition to occur at arbitrarily weak light-matter coupling, because the critical coupling strength vanishes at the matter quantum critical point. This direct coupling amplifies optical responses and generates intrinsic squeezing and light-matter entanglement that surpass those in the Dicke model. Coupling instead to a non-critical mode induces competition between magnetic order and superradiance, producing a tricritical point with distinct scaling behavior. Large-S analysis and density matrix renormalization group calculations support these conclusions, which remain robust in other models such as the ferromagnetic XY model and are experimentally accessible in cavity-magnonic systems.

The passage describes a Reconfigurable Power Station (RPS) that autonomously exchanges depleted power cartridges for energized ones to extend the range of unmanned systems, particularly Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). The RPS detects a UAV’s need for a new Swap Cartridge (SC) and uses identifiers to guide it to a landing zone equipped with visible or non-visible markers forming composite images for final approach. After landing, a retention system secures the UAV. Modular Power Bays (MPBs) within the RPS house multiple SC types, such as batteries, fuel cells, or fossil fuels, and an onboard processor selects the appropriate replacement. A swapping mechanism removes the depleted SC from the UAV’s Universal Integrated Swap (UIS) system and inserts a fully energized SC via an elevator. The system includes a Dynamic Terminal Landing system (DTL) with scalable markers, a Universal Swap Cartridge Processor (USP) for wireless communication, and a central processor coordinating landing, data transfer, environmental monitoring, and SC exchange. Though detailed for UAVs, the RPS is also applicable to ground, water, underground, and space vehicles.

JM Smucker sued Trader Joe's in US District Court in Northern Ohio, alleging its crustless peanut butter and jelly sandwich unfairly copies Smucker's Uncrustables. Smucker claims Trader Joe's infringed on trademarked design elements, including crimped edges and a specific shade of blue packaging, causing consumer confusion. The lawsuit demands Trader Joe's surrender all sandwiches and marketing materials for disposal and turn over all profits. Research projects for the Inquiry with completion targets of mid-January or February 1st include examinations of Central Powers newspapers for economic and political policy; a Who's Who for the Central Powers, Russia, Poland, the Balkans, and Scandinavia; a digest of treaty obligations; briefs on subject nationalities between the Baltic Sea and Persian Gulf; charts of international organization plans and events since 1870; and declarations on a new Poland. Experimental studies of orbitronics employ several approaches to detect orbital angular momentum, including torque measurements using conventional spin-orbit techniques, magnetoresistance, inverse orbital pumping, direct imaging via circular dichroism and electron energy-loss spectroscopy, and orbital Hanle magnetoresistance. Quantitative analysis is difficult because generation, transport across interfaces, conversion to spin, and transfer to magnetization are hard to disentangle. Key observations include CuOx as a strong orbital angular momentum source, longer orbital transport distances in ferromagnets than spin currents, material-dependent torque efficiency, and enhanced torque through crystal symmetry engineering. The orbital Hall effect and interfacial orbital Rashba-Edelstein effect are theoretically universal and can exist without spin-orbit coupling. However, open theoretical questions remain, particularly regarding orbital angular momentum relaxation: experiments indicate long relaxation lengths, but strong crystal field coupling suggests efficient dissipation, and first-principles calculations conflict on whether diffusion lengths are long in ferromagnets or short in normal metals. For applications such as MRAM, orbital torque could enable the use of low-resistivity light metals instead of heavy metals, but challenges include achieving higher torque efficiency than currently reported values around 0.3, generating substantial torque in high-tunneling-magnetoresistance systems like CoFeB, and reducing layer thicknesses by shortening orbital diffusion lengths. Recent demonstrations show reduced switching power compared to spin-orbit torque devices. The outlook emphasizes orbitronics' compatibility with abundant, non-hazardous materials, robustness against magnetic perturbations, and potential integration with photonics and phononics.

Ryan Dempster, now a Cubs special assistant, feels gratified watching Kyle Hendricks succeed. Dempster was traded from the Cubs to the Rangers in 2012 for Hendricks and Christian Villanueva. Dempster, who had no-trade rights, rejected a deal to Atlanta before consenting to the Texas trade. The email compiles November 19, 2001 news coverage of Enron's financial collapse and proposed rescue by Dynegy, a deal valued between approximately $9.8 billion and $15.6 billion that faces a lengthy, complex regulatory review by FERC and an SEC investigation into Enron's partnerships. Enron is selling noncore assets, including British utility Wessex Water to German bank WestLB for over £1 billion but less than the £1.4 billion paid in 1998, and its 65% stake in India's $2.9 billion Dabhol Power project to BSES, which expects due diligence by January 2002. Enron delayed its third-quarter SEC filing amid the crisis; it restated four years of earnings downward by a combined $586 million, and its stock has fallen about 67% to roughly $9. Trading partners are limiting exposure over fears Dynegy could withdraw, triggering a crisis in energy trading and financial markets. A Fortune feature warns that plunging stock prices are forcing companies to repay puttable zero-coupon convertible bonds, a $65 billion liability over three years that includes $1.33 billion from Enron due in 2004. Other articles note a corporate bond boom driven by refinancing of commercial paper as credit markets tighten, J.P. Morgan winning a stock-picking contest by declining only 8.6% in the third quarter, and an op-ed arguing Enron made enduring contributions to energy deregulation and risk management despite its current failures.

The Jammu and Kashmir Assembly saw opposition walkouts over alleged assaults on Kashmiri students in Haryana and other states, accusing the government of failing to check such incidents. MLB postseason headlines include roster decisions, managerial hires, and playoff previews. Boddie's application for habeas corpus against Emery denied.

Jason Ku, president of the MIT origami club OrigaMIT, guest lectures on the artistic and structural principles of representational origami design. American drug detainee Christian Beasley escaped from overcrowded Kerobokan prison by sawing through a ceiling and jumping a 6-meter wall. Fellow American Paul Anthony Hoffam was captured trying to escape. The prison, built for 300, holds nearly 1,600 inmates. Authorities investigating possible guard involvement. It was the second escape since June, when four foreign inmates fled; two recaptured, two remain at large.

The NVIDIA A100 GPU architecture advances HPC and AI performance through memory, compute, and multi-tenancy improvements. It includes 40 GB of HBM2 DRAM with 1555 GB/s bandwidth (over 1.7x Tesla V100), SECDED ECC, and a 40 MB L2 cache (6.7x V100) featuring 2.3x bandwidth, residency controls, and Compute Data Compression for up to 4x bandwidth gains. The GPU comprises 108 SMs with third-generation Tensor Cores delivering peak mixed-precision performance 16x standard FP32 FMA. Thread data sharing, larger matrix multiply dimensions, asynchronous global-to-shared memory copies, and 164 KB SMEM allocations improve SM efficiency.

A100 introduces Multi-Instance GPU (MIG), partitioning the GPU into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute, L2 cache, and memory bandwidth for QoS and fault isolation. Each GPU slice contains a Sys Pipe, GPC, L2 slice group, and frame buffer memory; Compute Instances allow further resource subdivision within a GPU Instance.

Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/s total bandwidth (double V100), while PCIe Gen 4 and SR-IOV enhance host and virtualization connectivity. Hardware additions include five NVJPG and five NVDEC units, an Optical Flow Accelerator, and improved atomic operation throughput. CUDA 11 adds Task Graphs, asynchronous copy and barriers, L2 residency controls, and Cooperative Groups. The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs via NVSwitch for 5 PFLOPS, supporting MIG and NGC software. A100 also implements fine-grained structured sparsity (2:4) to accelerate sparse networks with minimal accuracy loss.

President Rutherford B. Hayes issued a proclamation warning persons against settling in Indian Territory west of Arkansas without permission from the Indian Department. He stated that only designated persons may occupy the land and that those who settle without permission will be removed by agents according to law, with military aid if necessary.

Cosmetic tooth bleaching is a $3.2 billion industry with many over-the-counter products that confuse consumers. The FDA does not approve these cosmetic products, though the ADA offers a seal of acceptance for safety and effectiveness; only Crest 3D White Glamorous White Whitestrips currently holds it. OTC products take two to six weeks but may cause sensitivity. Custom dentist trays cost about $400 and take up to four weeks, while in-office bleaching exceeds $1,000, uses higher peroxide concentrations, and yields faster, more dramatic results, which insurance rarely covers. Dentists recommend examination first, as discoloration may signal cavities. Surface stains from food, drink, and tobacco may respond to cleaning, while deeper age-related stains can be bleached. However, trauma, tetracycline, or fluoride stains require crowns or veneers. All bleaching is temporary, and the ADA states there is no evidence supporting natural remedies like charcoal or lemon juice.

WHO reports Yemen's outbreak of a deadly waterborne disease has caused 503,484 suspected cases and 1,975 deaths since late April. While spread has slowed since July, about 5,000 people are affected daily. The epidemic stems from war-damaged infrastructure and poor sanitation. WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called for health workers to be paid and urged a political solution.

The Second Circuit reversed a district court order granting limitation of liability to Red Star Towing & Transportation Co. and Tug Ocean Prince, Inc. following a grounding and oil spill in the Hudson River involving the tug Ocean Prince and its tow, the barge New London. The court held that Red Star was not entitled to limitation because its management's negligence and the vessel's unseaworthiness—including the failure to designate a captain, the failure to inform the crew of one pilot's inexperience on the river, and the failure to post a lookout in hazardous conditions—were within Red Star's privity and knowledge. The court affirmed the dismissal of claims against the United States, holding that any negligence in maintaining navigation aids was not the proximate cause. It also held that Red Star's conduct constituted willful negligence and willful misconduct with respect to pollution cleanup costs, thereby denying the statutory $100-per-ton limitation under 33 U.S.C. § 1321 and exposing Red Star to full liability. The decision was reversed in part, affirmed in part, and remanded.

The "Single/Double" is a set basketball offense designed to free outstanding shooters through single and double baseline and down screens. The initial middle attack targets both sides of the defense simultaneously. The shooting guard cuts to the basket and can pop back out off a double screen or reverse off a single screen, while the opposite wing moves in the other direction. Once the ball reaches a wing, continuity continues through post ups, motion screening, or side screen action. The offense includes specific reads and counters for defensive responses such as chasing, cheating over, switching, and showing/recovering. Additional options include breaking double screens for screener scoring, strong post ups against smaller defenders, and offensive rebounding advantages. If initial screens fail, continuities like pass-and-screen-away motion, side screen and roll, and drive-and-kick actions maintain flow. Success requires precise execution, coordination, timing, and defensive recognition, taught through breakdown drills and whole-part-whole methods. Game strategies involve scouting opponents, varying alignments, attacking weak defenders, and using side screens as the shot clock winds down.

An internal Enron email dated December 13, 2000, circulated news summaries and Dow Jones Market Talk items to multiple employees. Key Enron-related mentions included Colombia setting a June 30, 2001 deadline to privatize state-run generator ISAGEN, where Enron had previously been a leading bidder, and Enron CEO Kenneth Lay stating categorically that he would not take a job in the Bush administration and planned to remain in Houston. The email also included market updates on topics such as investment bank liquidity, Bush tax cut prospects, HMO lawsuit rulings, bearish semiconductor and S&P outlooks, Toronto exchange technical levels, and various stock-specific analyst actions.

Cannabidiol (CBD) drug Epidiolex, developed by GW Pharmaceuticals, is being considered for FDA approval to treat seizures caused by Lennox-Gastaut syndrome and Dravet syndrome in patients aged 2 and older. Unlike widely available CBD products with unsubstantiated claims, Epidiolex is a 99% pure, THC-free, pharmaceutical-grade oral medicine manufactured under strict guidelines. FDA documents cite substantial evidence from three studies of its effectiveness, with acceptable risks given the serious, life-threatening nature of these rare epilepsy syndromes. While doctors may prescribe approved products as they see fit, the recommended use is very limited. Physicians and parents testified to its transformative effects for children with previously untreatable seizures, and doctors are interested in studying CBD for other conditions.

HHH defends excluding women from The Greatest Royal Rumble, stating cultures differ and WWE cannot dictate to a country or religion, but one cannot affect change by staying away. He cites the first women’s match in Abu Dhabi as cultural change and says he hopes women compete in Saudi Arabia within a few years.

The passage argues that Google's Pixel 2 and Pixel 2 XL are far more physically different than marketing suggests. The smaller Pixel 2, manufactured by HTC, has large bezels, chamfered edges, louder and tinnier speakers, and a less premium build quality. While specifications are mostly identical, the author views this design inconsistency as a step back from the unified design of the original Pixel and Pixel XL, and also notes the Pixelbook's design language is inconsistent with the new phones. The passage suggests the Pixel 2 XL is the design Google favored, while the Pixel 2 feels like a downgrade, but hopes Google's recent hiring of HTC engineers will improve consistency for future models.

Twelve-year-old Payton Leutner survived 19 stab wounds inflicted by friends Morgan Geyser and Anissa Weier near Milwaukee following a sleepover. After Payton crawled from the woods, a search located the two girls hours later on Interstate 94 with a 5-inch knife. During police questioning, the girls described a months-long plot to kill Payton, nicknamed Bella. Morgan stated her belief in the fictional internet character Slender Man motivated the attack, claiming they needed to kill someone to become his proxies and prove his existence. Payton, initially unable to speak, wrote to ask if her attackers were caught; her father confirmed they were in police custody.

Ion traps are limited by slow gate speeds due to ions' charge-to-mass ratio. Trapped electrons, being far lighter, could enable much faster quantum gates, but electron-only quantum computing faces cooling and scalability challenges. This work proposes a two-frequency planar Paul trap that simultaneously confines Ca+ ions and electrons in the same space, allowing laser cooling and optical manipulation of the electrons via the ion. The scheme involves laser-cooling Ca+, then photoionizing it to Ca2+ to produce a bound electron that can be excited into trap-induced states above the ionization threshold. The trap uses distinct high- and low-frequency radio-frequency drives to confine electrons and ions, respectively, in an overlapping potential without static fields. The authors analyze the resulting energy level structure, optical coupling schemes for state preparation and readout, and a planar ring trap design. Applications include high-speed quantum computing, radio-frequency to optical signal conversion, and multi-ion entanglement mediated by a shared electron.

AMD disclaims warranties and liability, grants no intellectual property licenses, reserves rights to change or discontinue specifications without notice, and states products are not intended for surgical implant, life support, or applications where failure could cause injury or damage.

This disclosure relates to ultrasonic fingerprint sensor systems positioned under displays, such as OLED and flexible OLED displays. The described apparatus includes a display with an underlying ultrasonic sensor system that transmits and receives ultrasonic waves through the display along an acoustic path. Between the sensor and display, the acoustic path may include a non-porous light-blocking layer, a grounded electrical shielding layer, a reworkable adhesive layer, and a mechanical stress isolation layer of plastic material. The sensor system includes a piezoelectric transceiver layer—using materials such as PVDF, PZT, or AlN—coupled to a substrate containing sensor pixel circuits. Implementations may incorporate high acoustic impedance layers, foam backing layers, or air cavities to enhance acoustic reflection and mechanical protection. The sensor can span the display’s active area, enabling continuous user authentication. Manufacturing methods involve bonding these intermediate layers to attach the sensor under the display. The systems may be arranged in “receiver up” or “receiver down” orientations, and the integration is intended to reduce electromagnetic interference, mechanical stress, and visible light transmission while preserving display performance.

The passage details NVIDIA's RTX Blackwell architecture and related technologies. AMP coordinates and schedules workloads to reduce response times for LLMs and prevent game stuttering. Blackwell adds hardware encode and decode support for 4:2:2 chroma sampling in H.264 and H.265, balancing color accuracy and file size. The ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC quality by 5%, adds 4:2:2 encoding, and introduces an AV1 Ultra High Quality mode for up to 15% total quality improvement; the RTX 5090 includes three encoders and two decoders for over 50% faster exports. An improved sixth-generation NVDEC offers 2x faster H.264 decoding and 4:2:2 support. DisplayPort 2.1b enables up to 80 Gbps bandwidth for 8K at 165Hz or 4K at 480Hz.

For power efficiency, Blackwell features Advanced Power Gating with faster state transitions, separate voltage rails for GPU cores and memory, and frame-granularity rail gating. Accelerated Frequency Switching adjusts clocks 1000x faster than prior architectures, while Low Latency Sleep enters the deepest sleep state 10x faster than Ada, yielding up to 50% power savings in scenarios like small language model inference.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, using fifth-generation Tensor Cores and an AI Management Processor to generate up to three additional frames per rendered frame with a 40% faster AI model and 30% less VRAM, alongside enhanced Flip Metering for smoother pacing. DLSS 4 also transitions to transformer-based neural networks from CNNs, doubling parameters and improving temporal stability, motion detail, and lighting for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing.

Blackwell introduces neural shaders via the Cooperative Vectors API, allowing Tensor Core access through any shader type. Applications include RTX Neural Materials for film-quality rendering, RTX Neural Texture Compression reducing VRAM usage by over 3x, Neural Radiance Cache for real-time global illumination, RTX Skin for ray-traced subsurface scattering, and RTX Neural Faces using generative AI for realistic facial rendering.

The architecture comprises the GB202 GPU (RTX 5090) with 92.2 billion transistors and 24,576 CUDA cores; the GB203 GPU (RTX 5080/5070 Ti) with 45.6 billion transistors and 10,752 CUDA cores; and the GB205 GPU (RTX 5070) with 31 billion transistors and 6,400 CUDA cores.

Zacks Investment Research downgraded Time Warner (NYSE:TWX) from buy to hold, citing digital growth and earnings strength but warning of advertising declines and currency headwinds. E-Book Derivative Litigation. The court approved the settlement notice form and scheduled a July 20, 2018 hearing to consider final approval, attorneys’ fees, and plaintiff service awards. The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition system. It outputs 20-bit conversion data in straight-binary or two's-complement formats, selectable via the DATA_FORMAT register, with LSB size dependent on the analog input range. The device operates with a differential or single-ended free-running sampling clock, and the SMPL_SYNC signal synchronizes multiple devices sharing the same clock and sync signals. An internal precision, low-drift voltage reference can be filtered with a 10µF ceramic bypass capacitor on the REFIO pin, or an external reference can be applied by disabling the internal reference through SPI or the SDI/EXTREF pin.

 The ADC supports 2-lane and 4-lane source-synchronous interfaces in SDR and DDR modes, outputting a 20-bit result MSB-first in a 24-bit data packet with DCLKOUT and FCLKOUT. A data output randomizer performs a bit-wise XOR operation with the LSB or a PRBS bit to randomize output and minimize ground bounce interference. Simple and moving data averaging modes improve SNR, while fixed, digital ramp, and alternating test patterns replace ADC data for interface debugging.

 The device is reset or powered down via dedicated pins or register writes, and it requires an initialization sequence of register writes after power-up or reset with a free-running sampling clock applied. A speed-boost mode enables up to 8MSPS sampling on a user-selected channel pair. Configuration uses 16-bit registers across three banks accessed via SPI, and multiple devices can be connected in a daisy-chain topology.

 In ATE applications, the ADS9803 achieves a post-calibration total unadjusted error of 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C and provides low-noise (22.7kHz) and wide-bandwidth (700kHz) modes for fast-settling multiplexed signals. It operates from AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD supplies, requiring specific decoupling capacitors and PCB layout practices to isolate analog and digital signals.

The study presents an ensemble of natural language processing classifiers to automatically detect goals-of-care (GOC) discussions documented in electronic health record (EHR) clinical notes for seriously ill patients. Because clinicians often document these conversations in general notes rather than dedicated Advance Care Planning notes, and because such documentation is rare and inconsistently recorded, the researchers addressed extreme class imbalance by comparing passive learning with active learning. Using 776 inpatient notes from the University of Pennsylvania Health System, they trained an ensemble of five classifiers—regular expressions, logistic regression, BERT-base, BioClinical BERT, and RoBERTa—aggregated via average, weighted average, and decision tree methods. The best performing system, a weighted-average ensemble trained with active learning, achieved F1 scores of 0.557 for utterance classification and 0.629 for note classification, correctly retrieving 72% of GOC discussion notes in the test set with a low false positive rate. Active learning improved precision and reduced annotation effort, requiring labels for only 30% of the unlabeled general-note utterances. The authors note that performance was moderated by the classifiers’ inability to incorporate broader paragraph-level context due to transformer token limits, and they plan future evaluation on a larger dataset and the MIMIC III database to improve generalizability and reproducibility.

The lecture covers matching, running, and power corrections in Heavy Quark Effective Theory (HQET). Wave function renormalization for heavy quark fields is performed using dimensional regularization, MS bar, and Feynman gauge, with a modified Feynman parameter trick used for integrals containing linear heavy-quark and quadratic gluon propagators. For heavy-to-light currents, the one-loop anomalous dimension is non-zero and independent of spin structure, unlike in full QCD, because treating the heavy quark mass as infinite converts QCD logarithms into UV divergences. For heavy-to-heavy currents with different velocities v and v′, the anomalous dimension depends non-trivially on w = v·v′ through a function r(w), and Wilson coefficients depend on scalar quantities including the heavy quark masses and w. A matching shortcut is described in which dimensional regularization regulates both UV and infrared divergences, rendering on-shell HQET loop graphs scaleless; thus, only full QCD graphs need be calculated to extract Wilson coefficients by matching infrared poles. The lecture then constructs 1/MQ power corrections by integrating out the small field component Bv from the full QCD Lagrangian, yielding a kinetic operator that breaks flavor symmetry and a magnetic operator that breaks both spin and flavor symmetry. Finally, reparameterization invariance (RPI)—a hidden symmetry arising from the arbitrariness in decomposing momentum into MQv + k—is introduced. RPI restores invariance under small boosts and constrains the kinetic operator’s Wilson coefficient to be exactly 1 to all orders in perturbation theory, whereas the magnetic operator’s coefficient is not constrained by RPI and acquires a non-Abelian anomalous dimension.

The professor begins by returning midterms and stating that the second half of the course will shift from block coding schemes to convolutional codes and codes on graphs. While random block codes can approach channel capacity, algebraic decoding methods cannot, and maximum likelihood decoding is exponentially complex. Convolutional codes, invented by Peter Elias, combine linear time-invariant structure with finite state dynamical structure, enabling lower-complexity decoding via algorithms like the Viterbi algorithm.

The lecture defines convolutional codes using Laurent sequences—semi-infinite binary sequences with a definite starting time—and D-transforms, which form a field allowing well-defined convolution and inverses. A rate 1/2 finite state encoder is introduced as a canonical example. The code is defined as the set of all output sequences y(D) = u(D)g(D), where u(D) ranges over all Laurent sequences and g(D) is the generator matrix of rational, causal impulse responses. Encoders are equivalent if they generate the same code, differing by a rational causal multiple; the canonical encoder is the minimal-degree polynomial form.

Using the example encoder's state transition diagram, the professor demonstrates that its free distance—the minimum Hamming distance between any two code sequences—is 5. The next lecture will cover trellis diagrams, catastrophic encoders, and the Viterbi algorithm.

This study examines the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into a university-level Digital Photography in Nature course through a qualitative case study involving 38 associate degree students and one instructor. Students noted advantages such as improved technical knowledge, time efficiency, objective feedback, and increased AI awareness, but also reported disadvantages including passivity, over-reliance on AI, diminished originality, and exposure to misinformation or contradictory outputs. The study concludes that AI-supported education offers significant pedagogical benefits but requires intentional integration within clear pedagogical frameworks, structured AI literacy training, promotion of critical thinking, and equitable access to digital resources. Limitations include the single-course setting, reliance on one instructor, exclusive use of qualitative methods, and absence of a control group.

The passage introduces Orochi, a versatile foundational model for low-level biomedical image processing tasks including restoration, super-resolution, fusion, and registration. The authors argue that existing specialist models are limited in real-world effectiveness and efficiency because biomedical applications often require sequential tasks, image degradations are interrelated, and biomedical data are large-scale and multi-channel. Orochi is designed with four key aspects: (1) Dataset Level: raw unlabeled data from over 100 publicly available studies totaling more than 100 terabytes across 2-5D modalities, converted via Random Multi-scale Sampling; (2) Pre-training Level: Task-related Joint-embedding Pre-training (TJP), inspired by JEPA, where the model jointly reconstructs various task-specific degradations to learn their interrelations; (3) Model Level: a hierarchical architecture using Mamba blocks for linear complexity and patch merging inspired by Swin-Transformer; and (4) Post-training Level: a three-tier fine-tuning framework (Full, Normal, and lightweight depth-wise separable convolution) enabling Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning. The authors state that Orochi is the first versatile foundational model addressing these domain-specific inefficiencies, and that even its lightweight tuning variant achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art specialist models.

The swinging gate formation is an unconventional special teams play typically used for two-point conversion attempts, where the offense lines up with kicking personnel in an unusual alignment—often with the offensive line shifted to one side and the kicker as an eligible receiver—allowing them to either execute a trick play or shift back into a kicking formation. It is uncommon in the NFL for post-touchdown attempts because extra points are snapped from the 15-yard line, though it has been used on field goals and two-point conversions. The objective is to force the defense to align quickly and exploit gaps, commonly through a side snap to a running back or a quick pass to the opposite side. Defensively, coaches emphasize matching personnel rather than just numbers, using safeties to protect the alley between the snapper and the formation, aligning box players to the heavy side, and having corners play pass-first.

This article provides generic names for football offensive formations, noting that coaches often use different terminology. It begins with basic formations: the I Formation stacks running backs behind the quarterback for power running; the Split Backs Formation places backs on either side but has declined in modern use; and the Twins Formation aligns two receivers on one side and tight end(s) on the other to create balanced run and pass threats. The article then covers spread offense formations: the balanced Ace Formation creates one-on-one matchups; the Trips Formation overloads one side with three eligible receivers; the Empty Formation spreads five receivers with no backs; the Quads Formation puts four receivers to one side; and the Bunch Formation groups three receivers to create picks and coverage confusion. Backfield sets include the Shotgun (quarterback 4–5 yards deep), the Pistol (running back directly behind the quarterback for downhill running, developed by Chris Ault at the University of Nevada), and the Single Back (one back with the quarterback under center). Old-school formations discussed are the Wishbone and Flexbone (option and misdirection), the Double Wing (tight splits and balanced attack), the T and Wing-T (motion and play action), the Power I (goal-line blocking), and the Single Wing (direct snap threats). Finally, gadget formations include the Wildcat (unbalanced line, non-quarterback snap), the Emory and Henry (widely spread pods), the Swinging Gate (post-touchdown trick play for two-point conversions), and Unbalanced formations (extra ineligible blockers to one side). Many older and unusual formations remain prevalent at the high school level.

The passage describes the NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture and its hybrid rendering model, which combines rasterization and ray tracing to achieve real-time, high-fidelity graphics. The passage details SEV-ES/SNP Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block protocols. The SEV-TIO extension enables guests to bind trusted devices via SNP TIO Guest Requests, which require unencrypted data such as Guest PCI ID, MMIO range, and TDISP status, and use shared data pages to return device measurements, certificates, and TDISP attestation reports. Secure AVIC requires guests to register or unregister backing pages for vCPU APIC state. Guests identify SEV-ES support through specific CPUID properties. The Passing Game is an unstructured, team-oriented basketball offense emphasizing continuous ball and player movement, off-ball screens, and unselfish play rather than set patterns. All five players are constantly involved, creating freedom and creativity while making it difficult to scout. It requires fundamental skills including sharp passing, proper spacing, triple threat positioning, purposeful cuts, setting and using screens, and offensive rebounding. Basic rules mandate moving with a purpose, meeting passes, maintaining 12–18 foot spacing, and eliminating unnecessary dribbling. Variations include three-out/two-in (Hi/Lo), four-out single or rotating post, and five-out motion alignments tailored to personnel. Against zones, it employs quicker passing, skip passes, gap penetration, and less screening. While strengths include effectiveness against all defenses and tempo control, weaknesses involve breakdowns from selfish play, rebounding challenges, and required patience. Coaches must commit to teaching fundamentals, but the system creates mental and physical pressure on opponents, exposes defensive weaknesses, and provides consistent stability regardless of shooting performance.

This systematic literature review of digital leadership in education, following PRISMA guidelines, analyzed 39 empirical articles. The study found that digital leadership lacks a comprehensive definition, with only 11 of 39 papers providing definitions that frequently omit leadership elements, organizational context, or environmental factors. Effects of digital leadership were identified across student, teacher, and school levels, though research predominantly addresses teacher technology integration and largely neglects student outcomes and digital security. Only 10 papers examined influencing factors, categorized as internal (individual characteristics, professional experience, digital literacy) and external (infrastructure, school culture, policies, training, COVID-19). The study proposes a technology-organization-environment (TOE) driven definition characterizing digital leadership as a dynamic, adaptive practice integrating technology and shaping organizational culture. It identifies future research directions including evolving definitions, student lifelong learning, digital security, follower involvement, and multicultural digital teams.

In NCAA football, targeting is forcible contact beyond a legal tackle or block, including helmet-to-helmet hits on defenseless players. It carries a 15-yard penalty and automatic disqualification: a first-half foul removes the player for the game, while a second-half foul also suspends them for the first half of the next game, extending to the postseason or next season if committed in the finale. Three targeting fouls in one season trigger an automatic one-game suspension. Unlike the NCAA, the NFL calls similar contact unnecessary roughness and only disqualifies for flagrant acts. The NCAA adopted the rule in 2008 to protect players and prevent brain injuries, added disqualifications and suspensions in 2013, and mandated video review for all calls in 2019. Notable examples include an unreviewed hit in the 2024 Peach Bowl and a disputed 2019 Fiesta Bowl call on Ohio State's Shaun Wade for a hit on Clemson's Trevor Lawrence.

Will Ma delivers his final lecture; Bill Chen will guest-lecture the final class on Friday. Ma presents an in-depth combinatorial analysis of a 100 big blind cash game hand where he holds eight-seven suited on the button. He discusses flop and turn bet sizing, the benefits of calling versus raising with medium-strength hands and draws, and the principle of structuring bets so the opponent goes all-in first when you have the nuts or a weak draw, while you get the last bet in with vulnerable good hands or stronger draws. After the opponent checks the river, Ma details a combinatorial range analysis to determine that a bluff is profitable because the opponent will fold more than half the time.

He then discusses general poker topics, including the "Moneymaker effect" and four unique reasons money can be made in poker: player overconfidence, poor gambling self-control, the game's rapid evolution, and the challenge of avoiding a results-oriented mindset. He recommends online learning resources such as CardRunners, Two Plus Two forums, and Twitch streams, and mentions several poker books. He concludes by emphasizing the importance of making good decisions and viewing one's poker career as a single long session. In a Q&A, he refers students to the MIT Poker Club, advises taking breaks to handle downswings, suggests playing tight against recreational casino players, and notes that online poker for money is illegal in Massachusetts.

The NVIDIA A100 GPU incorporates SECDED ECC across HBM2, L2 cache, L1 caches, and register files. It features 40 MB of L2 cache—6.7x larger than V100—with residency controls and Compute Data Compression for up to 4x bandwidth improvement. The GPU contains 108 SMs with third-generation Tensor Cores that deliver 16x peak mixed-precision performance over standard FP32, optimized for strong scaling through improved warp-level data sharing, asynchronous direct-to-shared memory copy, and 164 KB shared memory. A100 introduces Multi-Instance GPU (MIG), enabling partitioning into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute and memory paths for quality of service and fault isolation. The architecture includes third-generation NVLink providing 600 GB/s total bandwidth, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, and advanced error containment. Other additions include five NVDEC units, a five-core NVJPG decoder, an optical flow accelerator, and improved atomic operation throughput. CUDA 11 supports Task Graphs, asynchronous copy and barriers, and L2 residency management. The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs via NVSwitch to deliver 5 PFLOPS of AI performance, while A100 supports fine-grained structured 2:4 sparsity for deep learning efficiency.

Phase separation and coarsening in active fluids differ from equilibrium systems. This study examines DNA nanostar droplets in a 3D active self-stirring fluid composed of microtubules and kinesin motors, comparing it to passive fluids. In the active fluid, droplets coarsen primarily through collision-driven coalescence rather than Ostwald ripening. Experiments show that the mean droplet radius grows with a power-law exponent βR ≈ 1/3, similar to passive Brownian coarsening, but the droplet number decays with a steeper exponent γN ≈ −1.65 compared to −0.89 in passive fluids. Active coarsening is faster and lacks self-similarity: the droplet size distribution is log-normal and becomes increasingly asymmetric over time. Droplet effective diffusivity in the active fluid is independent of size, violating the Stokes–Einstein–Sutherland relation. Hydrodynamic and particle-based simulations confirm these exponents and reveal that they are robust across different active motility models. The study identifies a unifying control parameter, the collision kernel exponent k = 3 − (m+2)/α, linking anomalous diffusion exponent α and Stokes–Einstein–Sutherland exponent m. When k > 0, collisions favor large droplets, causing loss of self-similarity and a non-linear relationship between βR and γN. Probabilistic calculations validate this. The framework applies to biological condensates and other active or complex fluid systems. Limitations include finite system size and droplets remaining below the active length scale. Methods include protein purification, microscopy, particle image velocimetry, and custom MATLAB simulations of hydrodynamic and self-propelled particle dynamics.

President Trump accused large homebuilders of colluding and intentionally sitting on 2 million empty lots, claiming this is putting the American Dream on hold. Economist Bryan Caplan countered that U.S. homebuilders are not a cartel like OPEC but are instead constrained by restrictive zoning, local opposition, and permitting bottlenecks. According to NAHB data, nearly two-thirds of builders report a low supply of buildable lots, and construction remains limited by a lack of permitted land. Rare diseases affect approximately 300 million people globally, yet less than 50% of individuals receive a genetic diagnosis. This study investigated whether transcriptome-wide excess splicing outliers in RNA-sequencing data could identify causal variants in splicing machinery, rather than excluding such outliers as technical noise. Using FRASER and FRASER2 on whole blood RNA-seq from 390 individuals in the Undiagnosed Diseases Network and GREGoR cohorts, the authors identified individuals with excess intron retention outliers in minor intron containing genes (MIGs). This approach diagnosed four individuals with biallelic pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in RNU4ATAC (RNU4atac-opathy) and identified a fifth individual with rare, compound heterozygous variants in RNU6ATAC, suggesting a novel gene-disease candidate. Splicing outlier genes were significantly enriched for OMIM disease genes and genes implicated in developmental delay, and the MIG intron retention signature was robust across heterogeneous processing batches. These findings demonstrate that analyzing transcriptome-wide splicing patterns can serve as an unbiased diagnostic tool to diagnose known spliceopathies, provide variant-to-function evidence, and discover new gene-disease relationships.

The AMD Generic Encapsulated Software Architecture (AGESA) is a BIOS procedure library enabling AMD customers to implement AMD technology across multiple products. This document defines the user-level interface for host environment wrapper implementers, specifying procedure call interfaces, wrapper implementation guidelines, build options, and terminology. AGESA uses a version numbering scheme (X.Y.Z) and provides binary compilations, build control files, and tools in its release package. The architecture supports two primary build methods: binary module integration using a dispatcher and bridge model, and direct source integration. Interface calls use an initializer function to allocate and pre-fill parameter structures with defaults from build-time tables derived from a platform-specific <Plat>Options.c file. The software operates in 32-bit protected mode flat addressing and provides entry points aligned to a boot timeline, including AmdInitReset, AmdInitEarly, and AmdInitPost, which handle processor, memory, and platform initialization. Error reporting uses return codes and an event log. The library includes Integrated Debug Services macros, adheres to C coding standards, and supports UEFI environments through SEC, PEI, and DXE phase components with specific protocols and PPIs.

On November 1, 2001, news reports detailed escalating troubles at Enron Corp. The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission elevated its inquiry into partnerships involving former CFO Andrew Fastow to a formal investigation, fueling analyst concerns that the probe could spread into Enron’s core energy trading business. Enron’s stock price fell to $11.99, down about 14 percent for the day and roughly two-thirds over the preceding two weeks. Standard & Poor’s cut Enron’s long-term credit rating to “BBB,” two notches above junk status, and warned of further possible downgrades; Moody’s had also recently lowered its ratings. Enron secured $1 billion in credit lines from J.P. Morgan Chase and Salomon Smith Barney, backed by assets of its Northern Natural Gas and Transwestern Pipeline units, to supplement liquidity and support its investment-grade status. Key North American wholesale power and gas trading partners largely continued doing business with Enron, though some firms increased collateral requirements or reduced exposure amid credit concerns. EnronOnline transaction volumes remained above average, though competitors such as the IntercontinentalExchange and NYMEX stood to gain modestly. Enron retained former SEC enforcement chief William McLucas as counsel and formed a special committee headed by William Powers to address the SEC matter. Meanwhile, NYMEX natural gas futures edged lower on light profit-taking.

Public higher education funding in the United States remains deeply inequitable, with flagship institutions receiving roughly 40 percent more state funding per student than peer universities despite serving far fewer marginalized and low-income students. These disparities reflect a historical legacy of discrimination in which elite universities excluded women and minority students, while states begrudgingly created and underfunded alternatives such as HBCUs, women's colleges, and community colleges. Most states perpetuate these gaps through "base plus" appropriations based on prior funding cycles rather than institutional need, leaving open-access institutions that educate the majority of Black, Hispanic, Native American, and Pell-eligible students with dramatically fewer resources. The brief argues that policymakers must prioritize equity over adequacy by implementing funding formulas that direct additional resources based on student and institutional need—similar to K–12 systems—and by accounting for outside revenue sources such as endowments and tuition. It contends that universal free college and outcomes-based funding do not resolve systemic inequities, and that only after establishing an equitable distribution mechanism should states focus on increasing overall funding levels.

The passage critiques dominant climate education models for emphasizing scientific literacy, carbon reduction, and Western technological solutions while remaining ahistorical and erasing Black and Indigenous knowledge systems. It argues that frameworks such as Education for Sustainable Development and the UN Sustainable Development Goals perpetuate “climate coloniality” by imposing modernization, green extraction, and resilience narratives that disproportionately burden the Global South. Drawing on contrapuntal reading and decolonial theory, the authors propose “decolonial educational ecologies” as an alternative. This approach centers marginalized cosmologies, confronts colonial power imbalances and epistemic violence, rejects climate solutionism and anthropocentrism, and advances context-specific, justice-centered knowledge production grounded in reparations, distributive justice, and relational obligations with more-than-human kin.

The passage argues that the human brain does not function like a computer and that the dominant “information processing” (IP) metaphor is fundamentally flawed. It states that humans are born with senses, reflexes, and learning mechanisms, but not with data, rules, algorithms, or stored memories, and that the brain does not encode, store, or retrieve symbolic representations. Instead, experiences change the brain in orderly ways, allowing people to re-experience or perform tasks without retrieving stored copies. The author traces the IP metaphor as the latest in a historical series of flawed analogies, noting its faulty logical basis. Examples such as the difficulty of drawing a dollar bill from memory and a baseball player catching a fly ball through linear optical trajectory illustrate that intelligent behaviour does not require internal computation or representation. The passage also notes that every brain changes uniquely, making mind uploading and brain simulation impossible without the full biological and historical context. It concludes that the IP metaphor has hindered neuroscience, led to misguided funding, and should be discarded in favour of understanding humans as organisms.

The authors report an electrically driven polariton laser based on a solution-grown CsPbBr₃ perovskite microplate integrated within an optical microcavity with single-walled carbon nanotube electrodes. The device is fabricated as a metal-semiconductor-metal Schottky diode using a dry-transferred 435 nm-thick microplate on patterned electrodes between distributed Bragg reflectors. To optimize charge injection while preventing continuous ion migration, a two-stage cooling protocol is employed: cooling to 280 K followed by further cooling to 8 K at a constant current of 0.5 µA, which spatially freezes a rectifying p-i-n junction formed by redistribution of mobile ionic species. At 8 K, angularly resolved electroluminescence reveals strong coupling between excitons and cavity modes, with polarization-split lower and middle polariton branches. Under continuous electrical injection, the device exhibits a threshold current of 60 µA (~2.8 kA cm⁻²), marked by a superlinear increase in integrated emission intensity, linewidth narrowing, and energy blueshift, signifying the onset of polariton lasing while the carrier density remains below the Mott density.

The study investigates scientific knowledge advancement through conceptual recombination, proposing that papers creating "knowledge gaps"—structural voids in concept networks—possess superior generative capacity. Analyzing 34,363,623 papers from Microsoft Academic Graph (1900–2020) using persistent homology, the authors classify papers into gap openers (0.84%), non-gap openers with novel pairs (over 25%), and non-gap openers without novel pairs (over 70%). Gap openers connect newer, less established concepts; display higher novelty; use creation- and innovation-oriented language; and cite fewer prior works. Despite receiving fewer citations within five years, they achieve substantially greater long-term impact (31.39% more citations over 20 years), higher disruption scores, greater likelihood of reaching top citation percentiles, and associations with Nobel Prize-winning research, exhibiting delayed recognition ("sleeping beauty" patterns). Such papers emerge disproportionately from smaller, younger, fresher, and more geographically localized teams. The findings indicate that topological significance, not novelty alone, drives generative impact, and short-term evaluation metrics may undervalue gap-opening contributions.

A recent observational study published in Thorax found that individuals with asthma who consume high amounts of cured meats are more likely to experience worsening symptoms. Using data from 971 French EGEA participants tracked over two time periods, researchers classified weekly cured meat consumption as low (one or fewer servings), medium (one to four), or high (more than four). After controlling for smoking, physical activity, age, sex, and education, high consumers were 76 percent more likely to have experienced worsening asthma symptoms than low consumers. Body mass index accounted for only 14 percent of worsening symptoms, suggesting cured meat consumption has an independent influence beyond weight. Researchers believe nitrites and increased C-reactive protein may damage lung tissue through oxidative stress and inflammation. The authors note limitations, including that the study relied on participant memory and could not establish cause and effect.

The passage describes a patent application for instruments, systems, and methods that determine regional tissue material strength in real time and control penetration depth. The instrument houses rotational and axial drive motors that drive a working tool, such as a drill, saw, reamer, or driver, and includes a guide harp with rods for real-time depth measurement and plunge prevention. A torque sensor generates real-time signals, and a controller processes them into torque, energy, power, or accumulated energy to determine material strength, including identifying osteoporotic bone, and to provide feedback on tool passage through tissue. Axial force sensors measure forces on the working tool and guide harp. The system displays processed data and alerts to the user via an onboard or external wireless interface, enabling depth control and skive detection without fluoroscopy. The instrument can communicate with external computing devices and may include irrigation and battery power.

LLMs offer scalable, low-cost alternatives for synthesizing research data and simulating human behavior in computational social science tasks such as stance detection and sentiment analysis, but concerns persist regarding their accuracy, inherent biases, and ethical risks like misinformation. Techniques such as memory mechanisms and in-context learning can improve outputs, yet ensuring responsible use requires multidisciplinary expertise and broader societal engagement. LLMs may also assist in generating novel social theories, though questions about originality and validity mean they should serve as complementary tools within human-AI collaboration. The rapid advancement of generative AI necessitates updated regulatory frameworks to address challenges including misinformation, deepfakes, and discrimination while balancing innovation with risk mitigation. Although governments and companies have introduced AI principles and regulations, governance remains hindered by gaps between industry and policymakers, a lack of international consensus, and emergent risks—such as jailbreaking—that users discover in practice. The authors call for cross-sector partnerships, forward-looking regulations, and combined top-down and bottom-up governance that engages developers, users, and communities to ensure human-centered, trustworthy AI. This whitepaper is a joint effort by the Microsoft Research Asia Societal AI team and academic collaborators.

The President reports to Congress that reconstruction laws have failed, reducing states to military dependencies, excluding Virginia, Mississippi, and Texas from representation, and damaging relations between races, and he urges repeal of those laws, the tenure-of-office bill, and Army appropriations provisions interfering with the President’s authority and state militias. The passage describes container patterns and distributed system architectures. The ambassador pattern uses a proxy container to route application requests to sharded storage backends, broker services across different environments, and split traffic for experiments, with examples using twemproxy for Redis and nginx for request splitting. The adapter pattern modifies application container interfaces to standardize monitoring, logging, and health checks, exemplified by Prometheus exporters, Fluentd log normalization, and MySQL health check adapters. Microservices architectures improve reliability, agility, and independent scaling compared to monolithic systems, but complicate debugging and system design. Replicated load-balanced services deploy stateless replicas behind load balancers with readiness probes, session tracking, caching layers such as Varnish, rate limiting, and SSL termination via nginx. Sharded services partition large stateful datasets across shards using hashing and modulo functions; sharded caches improve memory utilization over replicated caches, consistent hashing minimizes remapping when scaling, and hot sharding addresses uneven traffic by replicating busy shards. The scatter/gather pattern parallelizes requests across leaf nodes that return partial results to a root node, though overhead and straggler latency limit benefits, and replicating shards improves reliability. Function-as-a-Service simplifies deployment and auto-scales but complicates debugging and monitoring, is poorly suited for long-running background processing or large in-memory datasets, and may become economically inefficient at high request volumes; the decorator pattern can transform requests or responses in FaaS.

Biological sex and gender identity are distinct. Sex is determined by genes such as SRY on the Y chromosome. Studies found SRY on X chromosomes in some anatomically male XX individuals, while SRY mutations caused XY individuals to develop as female. Gender identity is poorly understood, but evidence from cases such as David Reimer suggests it is more biological than social. While specific genes involved in transgender identity remain unknown, genes likely play a significant role, possibly including those on sex chromosomes. The author cautions against using biological variables as arbiters of gender identity.

The Simons Observatory (SO) is a cosmic microwave background project in the Atacama Desert using small- and large-aperture telescopes. The work summarizes the pre-deployment laboratory characterization of 25 production-design Ultra-High-Frequency (UHF) detector modules operating at 220 GHz and 280 GHz, using transition-edge sensor bolometers and microwave SQUID multiplexing readout. Nineteen modules will be installed in SO instruments; thirteen are already deployed and six are planned for a future upgrade. Each module contains 1720 antenna-coupled TESs and 36 dark calibration devices. Testing involved I-V curve measurements at varying bath and cold-load temperatures to determine critical temperature, normal resistance, saturation power, optical efficiency, effective time constants, and noise-equivalent power. Results show an average TES yield of 83% and a resonator channel yield of 86%. Median optical efficiencies are 0.62 at 220 GHz and 0.63 at 280 GHz. Median noise-equivalent power values are 39 aW/√Hz and 42 aW/√Hz, with approximately 89% of detectors meeting requirements. Saturation powers and time constants are largely within target ranges, though one module was rejected for low saturation power and one for high saturation power and resulting noise. One module showed poor optical efficiency due to post-fabrication thermal re-annealing and will not be deployed. The modules meet SO performance requirements, and on-sky characterization will be addressed in future work.
