MSPM0G MCUs provide five operating modes—RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, and SHUTDOWN—and two power domains, PD1 for the CPU and high-performance peripherals and PD0 for low-power peripherals, to optimize power consumption. The CPU executes code in RUN mode; peripheral interrupts wake the device from SLEEP, STOP, or STANDBY, while SHUTDOWN only wakes via NRST, SWD, or certain IO logic matches. The Power Management Unit generates core supplies, supervises VDD, and provides brown-out reset with programmable thresholds and a core regulator supporting RUN through STANDBY. The Clock Module provides LFOSC, SYSOSC, LFXT, HFXT, and SYSPLL oscillators, distributing MCLK, CPUCLK, ULPCLK, MFCLK, LFCLK, ADCCLK, HFCLK, HSCLK, and CANCLK with availability varying by mode.

The DMA controller supports twelve channels with repeated or single transfer modes, multiple data widths, configurable triggers, and stride mode. An event manager routes peripheral events to the CPU as interrupts, to the DMA as triggers, or directly between peripherals via static or generic routes. Memory includes dual-bank non-volatile flash up to 512 kB with ECC, 16 kB data flash, 1 kB sectors, high-endurance 32 kB sectors, and bank swapping for over-the-air updates. SRAM provides up to 128 kB in two 64 kB banks; Bank 0 has ECC/parity and remains available in RUN, SLEEP, STOP, and STANDBY, while Bank 1 is selectable and can be powered off in STOP. SRAM supports write-execute partitioning for security.

Peripherals include up to 93 GPIOs with wake and FastWake capabilities; IOMUX for programmable pad configuration and pin muxing; two 12-bit ADCs with 4 Msps, hardware averaging, 24 result registers, and internal channels; a temperature sensor with factory calibration; a configurable 1.4 V or 2.5 V VREF; comparators with low-power wake and fault handling; a 12-bit DAC with FIFO and DMA; security features including AES-128/256, firewalls, secure key storage for up to four keys, CRC-16/32, a TRNG, an AESADV accelerator supporting multiple modes in RUN and SLEEP, a keystore, and a MATHACL accelerator. Communication interfaces include UARTs with LIN and FIFOs, I2C with SMBus 3.0 and wakeup, SPI up to 32 Mbit/s with FIFOs, and CAN-FD up to 5 Mbit/s. The Low-Frequency Sub-System contains RTC_B with calendar, alarms, and calibration, and an independent watchdog timer with a 32 kHz clock and periods from 2 ms to 2 hours. Other timers include a windowed watchdog and general-purpose/advanced timers supporting QEI, Hall sensors, PWM with dead band, and cross-triggering. DAC_OUT shares the PA15 pin.

The device provides a serial wire debug interface and a boot strap loader invocable via a pin state, blank reset vector, or software command, protected by a 256-bit password. Factory constants provide device identification and trim data. Application guidance recommends 10 µF and 0.1 µF decoupling capacitors, a 47 kΩ NRST pullup with 10 nF pulldown, a 100 kΩ ROSC resistor for SYSOSC frequency correction if used, a 0.47 µF VCORE tank capacitor, and pullups for open-drain IOs. Development support includes evaluation kits, SDKs, SysConfig, and multiple IDEs. The April 2025 revision updated operating mode functionality, electrical characteristics, peripheral counts, flash endurance sector selection, SRAM availability, ADC and temperature sensor specifications, and other parameters.

This preprint compares forecasting models for annual, census-tract-level fatal opioid overdoses in Cook County, Illinois (2015–2022) and Massachusetts (2001–2021) to guide public health interventions. The authors evaluate simple baselines—including historical averages—and complex models (e.g., Poisson GLM, Gaussian Process, Bayesian spatiotemporal models, neural networks) using error-based metrics (RMSE, MAE) and a novel intervention-focused metric, percentage of Best Possible Reach (%BPR). %BPR measures the proportion of actual overdose fatalities occurring in the K highest-risk tracts recommended by a model. Results indicate that simple historical average baselines with tuned look-back periods performed competitively with complex models across both catchment areas. Furthermore, %BPR yielded different model rankings than RMSE and MAE, improving the identification of high-burden areas for intervention. The authors recommend incorporating simple baselines and intervention-aware metrics in future opioid overdose forecasting research. They release open-source software and a cleaned public-domain Cook County dataset to facilitate reproducibility. Limitations include limited generalizability to other jurisdictions, fixed intervention budget assumptions, and reliance on publicly available covariates.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) is a momentum oscillator scaled 0 to 100 used in Contract for Difference (CFD) trading to identify overbought and oversold conditions and create mean-reversion strategies. CFDs allow traders to speculate on asset price movements without owning them, and CFD trading is a zero-sum game. While typical RSI thresholds are 70 and 30, day traders often use shorter time frames with more extreme values such as 85 and 15. Effective use requires backtesting strategies on historical data, combining RSI with other indicators, adapting settings to specific assets and market conditions, and using multiple time frames. Traders should monitor RSI divergences and prioritize risk management, as leverage and factors like slippage and commissions affect outcomes.

This chapter details host environment requirements for implementing the AGESA software BIOS interface. The host must establish a valid stack and use bridge procedures and module dispatchers to call AGESA entry points, with identifiers found in AMD.H. In UEFI, execution spans SEC, PEI, DXE, and RTP phases using specific PEIM modules and DXE drivers that publish PPIs, HOBs, and protocols during processor, memory, and late initialization. AGESA provides two build methods—Binary Modules and Source Integration—controlled via platform-specific options files and environment variables such as AGESA_ROOT and AGESA_OptsDir. Key initialization procedures include AmdInitReset, AmdInitEarly, AmdInitPost, AmdInitEnv, AmdInitLate, and AmdInitRtb, plus S3 resume routines. The host must implement required call-outs, including AgesaAllocateBuffer and a call-out router, and manage pre-memory stack creation and destruction via provided macros. AARCH64 APUs with a Platform Security Processor do not use these early stack macros.

In *Thuro v. Meredith* (decided June 2, 1924), real estate brokers sued their principals for a commission. Della B. Thuro signed a contract for the purchase and sale of property with Mrs. Charles Tallman, also signing her absent husband George W. Thuro’s name without written authority. The Tallmans took possession and made payments before abandoning the contract. The court affirmed the judgment for the brokers, holding that a principal cannot avoid a broker’s commission by refusing to sign a contract with a produced purchaser. It further held there was no prejudicial variance between pleading and proof, and that errors regarding immaterial issues or harmless procedural defects did not warrant reversal.

Montecito Union School District settled a lawsuit for $7.5 million with two brothers, now 65 and 68, who alleged a deceased principal sexually abused them in the 1970s. This study compares Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM) and an explainable Machine Learning (ML) approach for detecting technical and procedural outliers in plantar pressure data. The dataset included 1,031 expert-annotated samples (798 valid, 233 outliers across four categories: General Acquisition Error, Double Foot Capture, Inverted Orientation, and Incorrect Side Annotation), synthetically augmented to 2,798 total samples. The ML approach used a Convolutional Neural Network with SHAP explanations, while SPM employed affine registration and pixel-wise nonparametric cluster-based permutation testing against a normative dataset. Evaluated via nested stratified cross-validation, the ML approach outperformed SPM, achieving an F1-score of 0.99 ± 0.00 and a Matthews Correlation Coefficient of 0.96 ± 0.01, compared to SPM's F1 of 0.93 ± 0.01 and MCC of 0.78 ± 0.02. SPM frequently misclassified pathological but valid samples as outliers and struggled with incorrect side annotations, whereas ML showed reduced accuracy for the heterogeneous General Acquisition Error class. In a human-centered evaluation, 16 experts rated both approaches positively on understandability, correctness, trustworthiness, usefulness, clarity, completeness, simplicity, and relevance using semantic differential scales, with no statistically significant differences between methods. Experts perceived the explanations as relatively similar (median similarity 3.75/5) and slightly preferred the ML approach (43.48%) over SPM (34.78%). The results indicate that ML offers superior outlier detection accuracy while both methods provide interpretable, expert-acceptable explanations, supporting automated quality control in plantar pressure analysis.

Barry Ritholtz argues that traditional percentage-based definitions of bear and bull markets (e.g., 20% declines or rallies) lack rational basis or supporting data and are useless for risk management or capital deployment. He cites examples where indexes diverged significantly, rendering such labels meaningless. Instead, he proposes defining secular bull and bear markets by combining market performance with long-term economic trends and investor psychology regarding valuations. A secular bull market is a 10-to-20-year period driven by broad economic shifts where investors increasingly pay more per dollar of earnings (multiple expansion), while a secular bear market features increased volatility and declining willingness to pay for earnings (multiple contraction). Ritholtz notes that multiple expansion often drives most market gains, as seen in the 1982-2000 bull market, and urges investors to focus on underlying market drivers rather than pundits.

Defenses counter the High Post Split Offense, which features a high post split and down screens, using two primary strategies. In Basic NBA Show & Recover, defenders sag off in front of the high post to prevent splits and handoffs, the post defender drops to protect the basket then jams the high post toward the weak-hand corner, and defenders show and recover on down screens to avoid switching bigs onto smalls. In All Out SOS Disruption, defenses apply early ballhandler pressure to deny the high post feed, switch on high post splits and down screens, smother the high post, and trap wing and low post passes with coordinated rotations into fronting and helpside positions when the ball is passed out of the trap.

This article examines the potential of metaverse integration in education and assesses Turkish teachers' knowledge, perceptions, and readiness regarding its implementation. Originating in science fiction and evolving through platforms such as Second Life, Roblox, and Fortnite, the metaverse offers educational advantages including immersive experiential learning, personalized instruction, collaborative environments, and risk-free practice for hazardous or costly activities. However, limitations include difficulties in student monitoring, increased cognitive load, technical infrastructure requirements, and the need for comprehensive teacher training.

A survey of 333 teachers in Turkey found moderate self-reported knowledge of the metaverse (5.25/9), with 78.1% having prior experience primarily in virtual reality or three-dimensional virtual worlds rather than contemporary metaverse platforms. Participants expressed positive attitudes toward educational use (6.23/9) and identified advantages such as generating engaging materials (76.3%), enabling practical application (74%), and facilitating learning by doing (67.8%). Conversely, they maintained significant concerns (5.38/9) about technical problems (76.9%), psychological issues including addiction (69.5%), inequality of opportunity (67.8%), data security (57.1%), and teacher readiness (55.9%). Teachers rated Information Technology, Physics, Biology, Chemistry, and Mathematics as the most suitable subjects for metaverse integration, particularly for concretizing abstract concepts and conducting experiments. They perceived the education system, schools, colleagues, and parents as largely unprepared (approximately 2.05–2.35% readiness), with students relatively more prepared (4.59%). Despite these concerns, teachers demonstrated willingness to adopt the technology (6.37/9) and strong interest in professional training (8.08/9), predicting effective implementation within three to five years. The study concludes that while the metaverse possesses transformative potential for education, successful integration requires addressing infrastructure needs, health and safety considerations, content development, and systemic preparation through gradual, cooperative efforts among educators, policymakers, and technology developers.

To attack a Box & One defense, offenses flash a baseline post player into the vulnerable middle, creating matchup problems and initiating high/low post action or wing back door cuts if denied. Implementation requires coordinated screens and post ups, defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, and timing. Coaches should scout opponents, vary alignments, and attack the weakest defenders.

The preprint introduces LUKB Disease Trajectory (LUKB DT), an R Shiny-based web tool integrated into the LUKB platform for identifying disease trajectories from electronic medical records (EMR). The tool follows a four-part workflow: inputting EMR data and analysis parameters; filtering diseases associated with a selected exposure using Cox regression with time-varying covariates; detecting candidate temporal disease pairs via binomial tests; and validating pair directionality through conditional logistic regression. Validated pairs are concatenated to construct disease trajectories. A case study using UK Biobank ICD-10 diagnosis data to assess diseases following COVID-19 included 183,386 individuals and analyzed 274 diseases. Cox regression identified 90 diseases significantly associated with COVID-19, which formed 8,010 disease pairs. Of these, 527 passed directionality testing and were confirmed by conditional logistic regression. The resulting trajectories indicated that COVID-19 primarily led to SARS-CoV-2 infection-related conditions (ICD-10 codes B97, J12, J96, Y95, Z51) and other medical care, but did not identify immune-related diseases, possibly due to the dataset's reliance on hospital-based diagnoses. Benchmarked on an Intel Core i9-9900K with 32GB RAM using 8 computational cores, the full analysis completed in 55 minutes. The authors note limitations including reliance on processed records and that concatenated trajectories may not fully reflect real patient experiences; they recommend using comprehensive datasets for accurate prevalence estimates and viewing the tool as a resource for investigating risk factors and mechanisms rather than for patient clustering.

Children with language vulnerabilities require tailored support, yet speech-language therapists and educators face challenges in delivering consistent, diverse, and real-time linguistic modeling during game-based interventions. While Robot-Assisted Language Learning (RALL) is promising, traditional rule-based systems lack adaptability and struggle with spontaneous interaction, speech recognition, and turn-taking. The authors present TalBot, a prototype integrating a large language model (ChatGPT) with the Furhat conversational robot to lead a word-guessing game with preschool children. TalBot manages turn-taking, interprets mispronunciations and voice recognition errors, provides feedback, and redirects off-topic dialogue, offering greater flexibility than pre-programmed systems. The team plans to expand TalBot for morphological learning, leveraging large language models to generate unlimited linguistic material, deliver consistent grammatical models without fatigue, and serve as a role model for educators. Future work includes laboratory studies, preschool field studies comparing robot and educator performance in modeling morphological structures, and a feasibility study assessing child outcomes. Challenges include data protection, compliance with the EU AI Act, ethical considerations regarding child development, and practical barriers such as cost and user motivation. The long-term goal is a scalable, adaptive intervention for teaching morphological structures across languages.

AGESA requires the host environment to establish a stack prior to procedure calls. In the binary image build model, AGESA core call-outs are dispatched through a single host-implemented router function that translates a function index into an execution address using a standard header containing a data element and a ConfigPtr pointer to the configuration data block.

The UEFI implementation spans SEC, PEI, DXE, and RTP execution phases across 16-bit, 32-bit, and 64-bit modes, using specific assembler and compiler tools. There are no additional user options specific to the UEFI environment. The SEC phase establishes a C environment and stack via AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK. The PEI phase uses two PEIMs: one for processor initialization that publishes early PPIs, and one for post-reset initialization that publishes memory and reset coordination PPIs. The DXE driver performs late initialization via AmdInitLate and publishes the AgesaDxeProtocol.

Build customization is handled through the <plat>Options.c file. Two build methods are supported: Binary Modules, which route calls through a common entry point, and Source Integration, where host tools build a ROM image directly. Required environment variables include AGESA_ROOT, AGESA_OptsDir, and AGESA_PLATFORM_NAME.

Stack macros manage Cache-As-RAM stack creation and removal; the host must not modify SS, ESP, or cache controls during CAR. Supporting procedures include AmdCreateStruct and AmdReleaseStruct for parameter block allocation, plus query functions for data eye results, APIC and PCI addresses, core and DIMM identification, MMIO rules, and event logs. Most procedures require an established stack and operational HyperTransport links.

Type 2A frequency compensation was implemented for a 10 kHz crossover using RCOMP of 40.2 kΩ, CCOMP of 15 nF, and CHF of 47 pF, calculated with a power stage transconductance of 16.2 A/V and an output bank of seven 330-μF polymer tantalum capacitors yielding 2.3 mF and an equivalent ESR of 0.86 mΩ. A 102 kΩ resistor between the RSC and AVSS pins provides slope compensation. The TPS7H500x-SP controllers accept a 4 V to 14 V input and require a minimum 0.1 µF bypass capacitor. Layout guidelines advise routing the feedback trace away from power magnetics, minimizing switch-node copper and high di/dt loops, isolating analog and power grounds at a single point, placing bypass and compensation components near the controller, and keeping high dv/dt traces away from sensitive signals. Revision F added QMLP options for the TPS7H5002-SP, TPS7H5003-SP, and TPS7H5004-SP.

Cover 2 is a zone coverage that uses five underneath defenders and two deep safeties who each cover half the field. Common in 4-3 defenses, it is designed to stop short routes while protecting against deep passes. Its strengths include balanced coverage against quick passes such as hitches, slants, and wide receiver screens, plus strong run support from "hard" corners who play near the line of scrimmage. Its weaknesses include vulnerability to four vertical routes, trips formations, and running plays that leave only five defenders in the box or remove a weak-side overhang defender. In standard Cover 2, corners cover flat zones, linebackers cover hook/curl and middle hole zones, and safeties cover deep halves. Variations include "Switch," where safeties play flat and corners bail deep, and a 1-high shell look where a safety drops to play the middle hole.

Sharp, Anderson, and Lang (2025) conducted a co-occurrence analysis of 1,076 articles published in the *Information Systems Education Journal* (ISEDJ) from 2003 to 2024, using author-supplied keywords and VOSviewer software to create term maps identifying thematic eras in IS education. The study grouped articles into five eras: 2003–2007 focused on IS education, curriculum, and assessment; 2008–2012 emphasized pedagogy and student issues such as retention, mentoring, and social networking; 2013–2017 highlighted cybersecurity, big data, and analytics; 2018–2022 reflected COVID-19 impacts including attendance and attentiveness, alongside a split between business and data analytics; and 2023–2024 centered on artificial intelligence alongside analytics and pedagogy. The full network analysis revealed a continuous central focus on pedagogy and curriculum across all 22 years. The authors note limitations including reliance solely on author-supplied keywords and potential bias from special issues, and suggest future research incorporate titles and abstracts while using a more organic, data-driven approach to define topical eras.

On November 27, 2001, FERC issued an order approving an extension of the NYISO's Automated Mitigation Procedures (AMP) through April 30, 2002, rather than the October 31, 2002 date sought by NYISO. Enron had submitted comments opposing the extension. FERC directed NYISO to file a comprehensive mitigation proposal by March 1, 2002, to be effective May 1, 2002, addressing FERC's concerns with the AMP and explaining how the AMP will work with other mitigation measures. FERC acknowledged NYISO's commitment to limit mitigation to specific zones and hours that fail the impact test and to exempt bids of less than 50 MW unless there is a demonstrated market power concern. FERC also directed NYISO to work with market participants to examine whether the AMP serves as a barrier to entry for new generation and whether such generation should be exempted; whether energy-limited resources constrained by environmental rules should be exempted or accommodated, as hydro units currently are; and to consider must-run mitigation measures consistent with ISO-NE and PJM. FERC cautioned that it expects one mitigation plan for the Northeast as part of the RTO process and encouraged NYISO to collaborate with PJM and ISO-NE in formulating its comprehensive plan.

The 5-day low overnight trading strategy enters the S&P 500 at the close when the index opens at a 5-day low but closes higher than its open, exiting at the next day's open. Overnight trading is targeted because the S&P 500 historically returns an average of 0.04% from close to open, supporting mean reversion. The passage describes an image processing method, apparatus, electronic device, and computer-readable storage medium for placing an external object such as a displaylink model or three-dimensional advertisement in a video. The method includes obtaining a to-be-processed video of m frames; placing a target three-dimensional model on a target plane of a first frame so that multiple feature points of a model surface fall on the target plane; determining three-dimensional coordinates of the feature points in a world coordinate system and their pixel coordinates on the first frame; determining a pose of the first frame's camera coordinate system relative to the world coordinate system; determining poses of camera coordinate systems for subsequent frames relative to the world coordinate system by tracking the target plane; replacing the target three-dimensional model with a target model in the world coordinate system; and generating a target video by projecting the target model onto each frame according to the respective camera poses. The approach improves placement efficiency and effect with reduced calculation, fast speed, and applicability to videos without large parallax.

Fed Chairman Jerome Powell has said post-crisis rules could be improved, while Fed overseer Randal Quarles has led efforts to ease financial regulations.

The offside trap is a defensive maneuver where all back defenders move upfield in unison before an opponent passes forward, placing the receiving striker in an offside position to earn an indirect free kick. First used in the 1900s and widely adopted by mid-century, the tactic became riskier due to modern offside law interpretations and increased short, quick passing. If successful, the defense wins the ball without tackling; if one defender fails to step up in sync, the attacker remains onside and the goalkeeper is exposed. Coaches must determine if their players are mature enough to execute it and if benefits outweigh risks. The trap is more effective against teams using through balls than against teams using crisp short passes. A flat-back-four alignment is most conducive to execution. One designated defender, typically a center-back, calls the trap using a unique verbal or non-verbal signal. Back defenders must maintain a straight line, move as one unit, know opponents' locations, and communicate constantly. The trap requires extensive practice and should be used sparingly, as overuse allows opponents to adapt and beat it.

Gary Gensler, in an MIT lecture on blockchain basics, explains the technology through Bitcoin, identifying cryptography, consensus mechanisms, and transaction ledgers as its three core pillars. He describes cryptographic primitives—specifically hash functions, which produce a fixed-size, one-way, collision-resistant fingerprint of data (using SHA-256), and asymmetric digital signatures using public-private key pairs generated via elliptic curve cryptography. Blockchain uses timestamped, append-only blocks containing headers with the previous block’s hash, a Merkle Root summarizing transactions in a binary tree, a timestamp, a difficulty target, and a nonce. Bitcoin addresses are derived from public keys through double hashing and are not identical to them. The system solves the double spend problem and incorporates a native currency with a finite supply of 21 million as an economic incentive for miners. Gensler notes that updating decentralized software requires node consensus, and he cites Haber and Stornetta’s 1990s work on timestamped append-only logs as an early precursor noted in Nakamoto’s paper.

Andrew Lo outlines equity securities as ownership claims yielding dividends or capital gains, contrasting them with bonds by noting equity holders are residual claimants with unlimited upside and limited liability, features that incentivize innovation and public capital formation. He distinguishes cyclical primary markets for new issuances from secondary markets for existing securities, where technology has driven trading volume upward. Lo introduces the Dividend Discount Model, valuing a stock as the present value of expected future dividends discounted at a risk-adjusted rate. Simplifying to constant dividends and discount rates yields the perpetuity formula price equals dividend divided by rate; incorporating perpetual dividend growth yields price equals dividend divided by the difference between the rate and growth rate, which implies the required return equals the dividend yield plus the growth rate.

The ADS868xW analog-to-digital converters feature high-impedance (≥1MΩ) analog inputs with internal overvoltage protection, withstanding up to ±20V when powered on and ±15V when unpowered. An integrated programmable gain amplifier converts single-ended or differential inputs, adjusts common-mode levels, and drives a second-order 500kHz antialiasing low-pass filter and an internal ADC driver. The device operates with an internal 4.096V reference by default, or with an external reference using an internal buffer, and provides straight-binary output for bipolar and unipolar input ranges. It includes user-programmable input alarms and fixed AVDD supply alarms. Communication is handled through a multiSPI interface supporting legacy SPI, dual-SDO, source-synchronous, and daisy-chain topologies. The device operates in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states, with NAP and power-down modes to reduce power consumption, and is configured via nine internal registers. The integrated analog front-end simplifies industrial data acquisition designs such as programmable logic controller input modules.

This case study from July 2007 examines SunPower, producer of the world’s most efficient solar photovoltaic (PV) cells, as CEO Tom Werner confronts questions about industry growth, competition, and long-term strategy. Rising environmental concerns, energy independence goals, and policy supports—including subsidies, renewable portfolio standards, and carbon markets under the Kyoto Protocol—have driven demand for solar power, though PV systems supplied only 0.04% of global electricity in 2006. The industry grew an average of 41% annually between 2003 and 2006 but remained two to three times more expensive than conventional retail electricity. A global silicon shortage raised feedstock and cell prices, while Japan, Europe, and China dominated production and shipments.

SunPower was founded in 1987 by Stanford professor Richard Swanson. After abandoning solar concentrator technology, the company developed high-efficiency back-contact cells, supplied cells for Honda’s solar race car and NASA’s Helios aircraft, and partnered with Cypress Semiconductor in 2001 to build manufacturing scale. SunPower went public in November 2005; Cypress retained a majority stake. By late 2006, SunPower had integrated into module and wafer production, secured long-term silicon supply through an agreement with DC Chemical, and acquired installer PowerLight for $335 million.

SunPower’s back-contact design delivered commercial efficiencies of 20.7% in 2005 with a target of 22%, reducing space and installation costs for customers. However, the manufacturing process required roughly twice as many steps as conventional cells, resulting in higher capital expenditures and processing costs. The company performed R&D in the Philippines and manufacturing in the United States.

Key competitors included market leader Sharp Solar, Germany’s Q-Cells, fully integrated REC Group, thin-film producer First Solar, China’s SunTech, and newcomer Citizenre. With global government subsidies estimated at $1.7 billion in 2005 and analysts projecting the industry could become subsidy-independent by 2012, Werner faced decisions about whether to focus on module pricing, process improvements, or a combination thereof to sustain SunPower’s technological advantage.

This protocol describes a systematic review of observational cohort studies examining the implementation and redesign of Rapid Response Team (RRT) services in healthcare systems. The review aims to describe methods of implementation, reasons for service change, time frames, and measures of success. Eligible studies include prospective and retrospective observational cohort studies involving novel RRT services or service redesigns, with no restrictions on language, publication status, or year. Data will be extracted on study characteristics, team characteristics, implementation methods, and system outcomes, and analysis will be primarily narrative with simple statistics. The protocol is registered on medRxiv and does not require ethical approval. Limitations include anticipated heterogeneity among studies and a potential lack of research on service implementation and change management. No external funding was received.

Enron had disclosed a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity and $35 million in losses from terminating the partnerships. Chairman Kenneth Lay said replacing Fastow was necessary to restore investor confidence, though he had defended him a day earlier. Analysts downgraded the stock, citing poor transparency and fears of further liabilities, with shares closing at $16.41 after falling roughly 50 percent in a week and 80 percent for the year. The turmoil dragged down other energy traders and spurred multiple shareholder lawsuits alleging misleading disclosures and insider trading by executives.

Chinese family education under the one-child policy has produced spoiled children whose academic focus neglects character and moral development, resulting in poor life skills, emotional disorders, and social maladaptation. Reforms should liberate individual interests from rigid, exam-oriented discipline; teach children to give unselfishly rather than pursue competitive success; reconnect them with nature; and prioritize moral behavior education over scientific knowledge, drawing on traditional Chinese philosophical teachings. The Yao Jiaxin case illustrates the dangers of academic excellence without morality. Additional measures include manual labor and sports, building family trust through shared outdoor and indoor activities, instilling religious or faith-based values to establish moral judgment, and recognizing mothers' key educational influence. Ultimately, China must revive traditional moral education and strengthen parental guidance to improve the current situation.

A geoarchaeological study of Egypt's Karnak Temple traces its evolution from an island formed by ancient Nile channels over 3,000 years. Researchers suggest the temple location may have been chosen because the island of high ground surrounded by water mirrored the ancient Egyptian creation myth of land emerging from primeval waters.

The article evaluates trend following and momentum strategies for Bitcoin (BTC-USD) using data from 2015 to April 2021. Cryptocurrency volatility makes Bitcoin suitable for these strategies. Three backtested approaches—using a short exponential moving average (best at five days with 145% CAGR), dual simple moving averages (100-day and 250-day yielding 115% CAGR and a 65% max drawdown), and a 25-day momentum strategy—all outperformed buy-and-hold while reducing drawdowns. Bitcoin has experienced severe drawdowns similar to the Nasdaq dot-com crash but historically recovered faster. The tests exclude commissions, slippage, and taxes. Code is available for Amibroker and Tradestation. The authors suggest these strategies may continue working as long as Bitcoin maintains high volatility.

The TPS7H500x-SP series comprises fixed-frequency, peak current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting buck, flyback, forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies with switching frequencies from 100 kHz to 2 MHz. Output voltage is set via a resistor divider to the 0.613 V VSENSE pin reference. Soft-start time is controlled by a capacitor on the SS pin, and synchronous rectifier outputs SRA/SRB activate once SS exceeds 1 V. The controllers support three oscillator modes: internal oscillator (RT resistor to AVSS), external synchronization (clock to SYNC), and primary-secondary (SYNC links two devices, producing a 90° or 270° phase shift). Primary outputs OUTA/OUTB and SR outputs provide approximately 150 mA peak current and require external gate drivers; OUTB and SRB are active only when a 50% duty cycle limit is selected on compatible models. The TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5002-SP offer resistor-programmable dead times via PS and SP pins, while the TPS7H5003-SP uses fixed dead time; leading edge blank time is programmable via the LEB pin on all devices except the TPS7H5003-SP, which has a fixed blank time. Pulse skipping occurs when the COMP pin is below 0.3 V and the previous duty cycle was less than 25%, with SR outputs remaining on if soft start is complete. Maximum duty cycle is set via the DCL pin as 50% (AVSS), 75% (floating), or 100% (VLDO), though 50% is only available on the TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP. Peak current mode control uses the CS_ILIM pin; when its voltage exceeds 1.05 V, the device enters cycle-by-cycle limiting and then hiccup mode after a delay set by the HICC capacitor. The FAULT pin triggers shutdown when above 0.6 V, followed by a restart delay. Slope compensation is set with an RSC resistor, and Type 2A or 2B frequency compensation is applied at the COMP pin. Thermal shutdown halts switching above 175°C and resumes below 160°C. The controllers operate from a 4 V to 14 V input. A detailed design example for a 500 kHz synchronous push-pull GaN converter using the TPS7H5001-SP provides component values for feedback, dead time, blanking, soft-start, transformer, current sense, and compensation. Layout guidelines emphasize minimizing switching loops, separating analog and power grounds, routing sensitive traces away from noise sources, and placing bypass capacitors close to the device.

Nobel Prizes, established by Alfred Nobel and first awarded in 1901, honor major scientific discoveries but recognize only narrow fields and limited contributors, as just three people can share an award. Winners, selected through a yearlong global nomination process, are typically white men from wealthy regions like the United States and Western Europe, while women and people of color face barriers to accessing the major labs and universities where prizeworthy work often occurs. Many scientific disciplines, including ecology and climate science, fall outside the prize categories entirely. Additionally, lab heads are more frequently recognized than other key collaborators. Though the Nobel Foundation is unlikely to alter the awards due to Nobel’s will, recipients and observers note the prizes remain valuable for highlighting science’s impact on society and fostering public interest in research.

Kickers, often undrafted and lower-paid than other players, primarily kick field goals (worth three points, typically from 25–60 yards) and extra points (worth one point), with NFL expectations around 80% and 90% accuracy, respectively. They also execute kickoffs—including touchbacks and directional kicks—and situational plays like onside kicks. The term “placekicker” derives from kicks being set in place by a holder or tee. Successful kickers typically possess a slim build (approximately 5'10"–6'2", 180–210 pounds) with accuracy, lower-body power, and flexibility. Notable kickers include Justin Tucker, the most accurate kicker and record-holder for the longest field goal; Morten Andersen, second all-time in career field goals and a Hall of Famer; and Adam Vinatieri, the NFL’s all-time leading scorer renowned for clutch kicks. Kickers influence fourth-down coaching decisions, often determine the outcome of close games, impact field position through kickoffs, and usually serve as the emergency backup punter.

North Carolina regulators are discussing tests for GenX in vegetables near The Chemours Co. plant near Fayetteville, following a Dutch study finding the chemical in vegetables near a Chemours factory in the Netherlands. No decision has been made on testing. Fish tests are expected within months. GenX, used since 2009 to replace PFOA, has toxic effects in animals, but human effects are unknown and no federal standards exist. A nearby resident stopped eating homegrown produce after GenX was found in his well water, and the chemical was detected in Wilmington's drinking water downstream.

The passage describes priority patent applications and incorporated references for technology using deep learning-based convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and atrous/dilated convolutional neural networks (ACNNs) to detect splice sites and aberrant splicing in genomic sequences. It provides background on machine learning, neural network architectures, training via backpropagation, and network components including convolutional layers, ReLU activation, dilated convolutions, residual and skip connections, batch normalization, and global average pooling. Particular implementations detail training ACNs—such as SpliceNet80, SpliceNet400, SpliceNet2000, and SpliceNet10000—and CNNs on donor, acceptor, and non-splicing site examples to classify nucleotides. Disclosed systems and methods process input sequences with flanking context nucleotides to output triplet likelihood scores for donor splice sites, acceptor splice sites, or non-splicing sites. The technology compares reference and variant sequence scores to detect aberrant splicing and classifies variants as pathogenic or benign based on predetermined thresholds.

VentureWire's May 31, 2001 newsletter reports venture capital and technology industry news. Top stories include Insight Capital Partners closing its fourth fund at over $740 million for expansion-stage enterprise software investments; Whitney & Co. spinning off its Tokyo, Hong Kong, and London offices to operate independently after closing its fifth fund at $1.1 billion; Rho Ventures closing Fund IV at $435 million; and Quake Technologies raising $30 million in a second round for optical networking chips.

New funding rounds include Arexis ($4.5 million), SpeedGreetings ($3 million), Tools for Health ($1.7 million), Remedyne ($3.2 million), Fractus (up to $4.3 million from 3i), OmniSonics Medical ($21 million Series B), Xtime (additional $2.6 million Series B), Neurotech ($30 million third round), Atherotech ($4.2 million Series C), Spirian Technologies (undisclosed amount from Silver Young Partners), and Toppan Printing's $5 million strategic investment in E Ink.

PaperExchange shut down its European operations. New deals include a joint venture between Softbank and Scientia Health Group called Scientia Japan, an alliance between Nordic VCs Eqvitec Partners and IT Provider, and a collaboration between Incyte and Iconix on a chemogenomic product. Cervalis launched as a managed services provider, and Data Downlink rebranded as Alacra.

In mergers and acquisitions, Bertelsmann acquired MyPlay for approximately $30 million, TMP Worldwide acquired FlipDog.com, UsherPro and Season Ticket Networks merged to form Season Tickets Solutions, BuildOnline acquired iScraper Germany, Metavante acquired CyberBills, Outtask acquired Upright Software, CableNet acquired wireConnect's assets, and Catenas acquired a 25% stake in Endero.

Executive and board appointments include Spiros Jamas as CEO of Enanta Pharmaceuticals, David Overskei as CEO of Polexis, and Dr. Richard S. Kent as CEO of Ardent Pharmaceuticals, plus new directors at American Fiber Systems, Andes Networks, Mezzia, Commtag, and Enamics. MMC Capital closed its Technology Fund II at $250 million, and Royal Bank Capital Partners added two members to its Energy Fund team.

A machine learning framework was developed to accurately predict ionic dielectric constants (εion) by separately predicting Born effective charges with an equivariant graph neural network and phonon properties with a machine learning potential (SevenNet), then analytically combining these quantities. This joint model substantially outperformed direct prediction approaches (R² = 0.843 versus 0.418). The framework was applied to virtually screen 8,717 oxides, identifying 38 high-κ candidates with a validated figure of merit (dielectric constant multiplied by band gap) of at least 350; twelve of these exceed the figure of merit of KTaO₃, the best oxide in the training dataset. Thirty-six of the identified oxides contain d⁰ transition metals, and most feature oxygen octahedral networks. Ten have been experimentally synthesized, with five exhibiting reported experimental dielectric constants consistent with the predictions. The study demonstrates that decomposing dielectric response into fundamental physical quantities enables more reliable screening for advanced dielectric materials.

Brett Veach will lead his first NFL draft as Kansas City Chiefs general manager this week without a first-round pick but with one second-round and two third-round selections. Since replacing John Dorsey, Veach has traded draft picks to acquire players and balance the salary cap, and he is expected to be aggressive in trading up. The Chiefs will likely target defensive players such as pass rushers or cornerbacks, though they may also add offensive support for quarterback Patrick Mahomes II. Local prospects Dorance Armstrong and D.J. Reed are potential fits. Kansas City has drafted Pro Bowl players Marcus Peters, Tyreek Hill, and Kareem Hunt in recent years, along with Patrick Mahomes and Chris Jones, while defensive picks KeiVarae Russell and Tanoh Kpassagnon have been misses.

The speaker states the team is focused on its own preparation rather than analyzing an opposing player's injury. The group is relaxed and enjoying the moment but remains focused and ready for tomorrow's game, having held a simple practice after a six-hour flight. Absent player Marc, whose health varies, is honored with his equipment and sweater present. The coach and management foster a dressing room atmosphere blending commitment, focus, and enjoyment. Veteran leaders, including a player with two Stanley Cup rings, have guided the young players and team. The group recognizes it must alter its game plan from previous outings and began preparing immediately after the last contest.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture (GA100), is designed to accelerate AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads in cloud data centers. Fabricated on TSMC’s 7nm process, it features third-generation Tensor Cores supporting FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary data types, delivering up to 2.5x the mixed-precision FP16/FP32 and FP64 performance of the Tesla V100, 10x speedup for TF32, and up to 20x faster sparse INT8 inference. A100 introduces Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity using a 2:4 pattern to double Tensor Core throughput for deep learning inference.

The GPU includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth and a 40 MB L2 cache with residency controls and Compute Data Compression. Each Streaming Multiprocessor contains 192 KB of combined L1 cache and shared memory, and supports new asynchronous copy and barrier instructions.

A100 features Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology, allowing secure hardware partitioning into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute and memory paths for multi-tenant environments. Connectivity includes third-generation NVLink providing 600 GB/sec total bandwidth, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, and compatibility with Mellanox InfiniBand/Ethernet and NVIDIA Magnum IO.

CUDA 11 advances include Task Graph acceleration, asynchronous memory operations, and L2 cache residency management. Additional hardware features include five NVDEC units, a five-core NVJPG decode engine, an Optical Flow Accelerator, improved atomic operations, and enhanced error/fault detection, isolation, and containment. The NVIDIA DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs via NVSwitch, delivering 5 PFLOPS and supporting scaling from partitioned single-GPU instances to large multi-node clusters.

Jordan Chiles is the only athlete remaining in "Dancing with the Stars" Season 34 Episode 3 after the Week 2 double elimination of Baron Davis and Corey Feldman. Twelve contestants remain for "TikTok night." Scoring equally weights judges' scores, out of 30 points, and public votes. Viewers may cast up to 20 votes per celebrity weekly via the ABC website, Disney+ app, or text, but only during the live Eastern and Central time zone broadcast.

This case study details Sanergy, a Kenyan social enterprise founded by MIT Sloan students that franchises Fresh Life toilets in Nairobi’s slums and converts waste into organic fertilizer (Evergrow) and animal feed. By 2015, Fresh Life operated 615 toilets serving approximately 32,000 people. Communications manager Medora Brown, appointed in April 2015, must develop a social media strategy for Sanergy’s three brands—Fresh Life, Farm Star, and corporate fundraising—each targeting distinct audiences: slum dwellers and franchisees, Kenyan farmers, and global investors and donors. While Kenya’s mobile and internet penetration is high, slum dwellers have limited social media use and rely on cyber cafés for practical needs, whereas farmers increasingly use Facebook and WhatsApp. Fresh Life builds trust through personal contact, SMS, and community events, making social media’s role in franchise recruitment uncertain. Farm Star uses Facebook for sales leads and WhatsApp for consultative selling to promote Evergrow over manure. Corporate fundraising relies on personal networks and thought leadership to attract large donors, with skepticism about social media’s effectiveness for major gifts. Brown must allocate limited resources, choose strategic platforms, develop efficient content, and create metrics to demonstrate ROI across these diverse constituencies.

Backtesting the higher highs and higher lows pattern across S&P 500 (SPY), gold (GLD), and long-term Treasuries (TLT) found it signals weak future short-term gains and does not work as a short strategy. The strategy entered after two consecutive daily bars with higher highs and higher lows and exited after 1-10 bars. Results showed tiny or negative short-term returns across all three assets. Longer holding periods improved stock results slightly due to long-term tailwinds but remained weak relative to random periods. Extending the pattern to three or four consecutive days did not improve results. The pattern is a typical short-term reversal signal but is not powerful enough to use alone as a trading signal.

University of Edinburgh researchers identified 287 genes linked to male pattern baldness in a PLoS Genetics study of over 52,000 men. Forty genes are on the X chromosome, inherited from mothers. The team developed a formula predicting hair loss risk, but stated accurate individual prediction remains distant. Male pattern baldness affects around 80 percent of men by age 80. The findings may help identify at-risk individuals and potential genetic targets for intervention.

The speaker credits teammates for strong defensive play and shutouts, emphasizing the need to stay focused during tight games. He notes the importance of not giving opponents momentum when ahead, describes a key late-second-period save, and acknowledges the upcoming challenge in a place that has never seen Stanley Cup finals, where opponents will be motivated to score in the first game.

A CORAF report on the SRI-WAAPP project—the largest System of Rice Intensification effort to date, covering 13 West African countries, over 50,000 farmers, and 1,000 sites—found yield increases of 54–153 percent and a 41 percent average income gain over conventional practices. The project produced an additional 20,000 tons of milled rice in 2015–2016, and full adoption could have eliminated regional rice imports in 2017. Coordinated by Mali’s rice center and Cornell University, the initiative is praised for its participatory design. While authors urge scaling up the adaptable methodology, they caution that practices must fit local conditions. Concerns about labor burdens on women prompted adoption of labor-saving technologies, and the regional scope fostered cross-border collaboration.

Mortgage applications fell 0.8 percent to 403.6 for the week ended March 24, declining for a second week despite a sharp drop in borrowing costs. Average 30-year conforming mortgage rates fell to 4.33 percent from 4.46 percent, tracking lower Treasury yields. Refinancing applications dropped 2.9 percent to the smallest share since October 2008, while purchase applications rose 1.2 percent to 238.1.

After five days investigating the Las Vegas shooting, authorities have not identified gunman Stephen Paddock's motive and are erecting billboards for public tips. Investigators are examining whether he hired a prostitute before the attack, reviewing his international cruises, analyzing a cryptic note, and assessing his mental health, but typical avenues have revealed little. The 64-year-old high-stakes gambler killed 58 people and wounded hundreds from his Mandalay Bay suite before killing himself. Police believe he acted alone but want to know if anyone knew of his plot. He meticulously planned the attack, stockpiling 23 weapons, setting up cameras, and booking rooms overlooking other music festivals. His girlfriend, Marilou Danley, who was in the Philippines during the attack, told the FBI she was unaware of his plans and had not observed warning signs.

Mercy University School of Education has strengthened its educator preparation mission through federal, state, and local grants. The five-year, $2.8 million U.S. Department of Education GRAD-PRO grant (2023) expands graduate-level opportunities, faculty mentorship, and scholarships for Hispanic and underrepresented students in health sciences, education, and business. The three-year BRANCH-ED grant (2023) enhances teacher preparation quality and diversity through district partnerships, curriculum review, and coaching; Mercy achieved a 100% success rate in the first 18 months. Since 2013, the NSF-funded MISTI program has prepared STEM teachers for high-need middle and high schools through intensive observations, social justice seminars, student teaching, and multi-year mentoring. The NSF STEM Master Teaching Fellowship (2019–2024) supported 14 PK–12 teachers from high-needs districts in graduate STEM pedagogy coursework and leadership projects. The five-year, $687,500 NYSED CR-ITI/ESOL grant (2023–2028) prepares ESOL teachers for New York City through clinical practice, mentor support, and post-program assistance. These grants drive program improvement, professional learning, and collaboration to equip educators for diverse PK–12 populations.

This study presents a systematic literature review of robotic coding in science education, analyzing 15 peer-reviewed empirical articles from Web of Science and Scopus published between 2015 and 2022. Selected via PRISMA guidelines from 74 initial records and evaluated through rigorous quality appraisal, the review synthesizes evidence following Petticrew and Roberts' systematic review steps. Results indicate that existing research primarily addresses cognitive skills, including 21st-century skills (communication, problem-solving, scientific creativity) and computational thinking skills (algorithmic thinking, mathematical understanding); applications in science and engineering education using tools such as Arduino and tablets; and affective variables including interest, motivation, and opinion. Suggestions from the reviewed studies emphasize integrating robotic coding across STEM fields, subjects, and educational environments; implementing it at various learning levels; and expanding the use of different robotic coding programs. Recommendations for future research include conducting large-scale studies, utilizing diverse data collection tools, performing in-depth investigations, and examining gender differences. The authors conclude that further research is needed on additional 21st-century skills (innovation, critical thinking, cooperation, leadership), broader STEM integration (technology, engineering, mathematics), alternative coding tools, other affective characteristics (attitude, self-efficacy, self-regulation), psychomotor outcomes, and curriculum development. They also recommend in-service teacher training and propose that future reviews employ meta-synthesis or meta-analysis across different fields and time periods.

System Management Arts Incorporated (“Smarts”) moved to revise the court’s prior denial of its partial summary judgment motion against Avesta Technologies, Inc. and David Zager under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 54(b), based on newly-discovered evidence. Smarts sought an order excluding the “Delphi” program as prior art, which would have eliminated a triable issue regarding the defendants’ patent invalidation defense. The new evidence from Igor Klener’s deposition revealed that Klener, whose declaration had corroborated Avesta’s prior art claims, had been invited to invest in Avesta before its IPO, profited from that investment, and was friendly with Avesta executives. Smarts argued this bias rendered the Klener Declaration insufficient corroboration as a matter of law. The court held the motion was timely and proper under Rule 54(b) and that, under the “rule of reason,” a corroborating witness’s bias does not per se render testimony legally insufficient; rather, bias affects credibility for the jury. Because the new evidence did not eliminate all genuine issues of material fact, the motion was denied.

The United States District Court for the Southern District of New York denied in part and granted in part a motion to dismiss appeals by the New York City Department of Finance and the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance from an order confirming 1515 Broadway Associates, L.P.’s Chapter 11 reorganization plan. The debtor and Equitable Life Assurance Society argued the appeals were moot because the plan had been substantially consummated without a stay.

The court ruled that the appeal concerning the reorganization of the debtor’s general partner into a limited partnership was moot, as it was integral to the consummated plan and could not be reversed without disrupting the entire reorganization. However, the appeal regarding the plan’s provision for a possible future foreclosure or sale of the building was not moot because the transaction was prospective and effective relief might still be possible. The court further held that the State’s appeal regarding the potential application of the New York Gains Tax to a land purchase under the plan was not moot, as the relevant Second Circuit precedent was decided after the confirmation order. The appeals were allowed to proceed only on the future foreclosure and state tax issues.

The author recounts discovering Warren Weaver's 1947 letter comparing translation to decoding. While acknowledging machine translation's utility, the author argues it lacks understanding, questioning whether high-quality translation is possible without it, and introduces experiments.

Reps signed directive for state upper secondary schools in Viimsi, Rapla, opened leadership hiring. Schools open Sep. 1 next year. Construction is in second phase; Viimsi by Novarc AS and Kamp architects, Rapla by Salto architects.

The passage defines software engineering and distinguishes functional requirements, which specify software actions and services, from non-functional requirements (NFRs), which define qualities such as usability, security, and reliability. It reviews machine learning classifiers—K-NN, Naïve Bayes, decision tree, and SVM—and summarizes related research on NFR generation, prioritization, effort estimation, interplay, and knowledge reuse. The proposed methodology extracts keywords from functional requirements, clusters semantically similar words using similarity measures and clustering algorithms, and applies a decision tree classifier with an NFR traceability matrix to identify potential NFRs. Using an IVR dataset to classify null and non-null functions, the proposed method demonstrated higher accuracy and lower execution time compared to the existing approach using only the NFR matrix. The study concludes that null functions reduce project efficiency and that the proposed Python-based model improves classification performance.

Marcel Strigberger, a retired Toronto civil litigation lawyer, decluttered his home by discarding McGill University law schoolbooks purchased more than 50 years ago. He reflected on legal concepts from books by Cheshire and Fifoot and by Magarry and Wade, including a smokeball reward case involving Lily Carlill, an 1860s unenforceable contract between a carriage owner and a prostitute, fee simple, fee tail, and a principle from a 16th-century English land decision. He also recalled a cargo-ship explosion case and a second installment. He recycled the books, though he later noted a used hardcover was listed on Amazon for over $1,000 CAD. He kept one 5-inch-thick volume to use as a reading stand while standing at his desk. Strigberger now pursues humor writing and speaking.

The @YesYoureRacist Twitter account identified participants in the Charlottesville protest, growing to 271,000 followers. The anonymous moderator asked users to send names and profiles of alt-right protesters to make them famous. The account contributed to Cole White being fired from a Berkeley restaurant, identified Washington State University student James Allsup and Peter Cvjetanovic, was featured on Good Morning America, and was credited with finding a photo of the man who drove into a crowd of protesters.

NVIDIA Turing GPUs implement a Hybrid Rendering model combining real-time ray tracing, rasterization, AI, and simulation. Dedicated RT Cores accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing, enabling real-time ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections at speeds roughly 10 times faster than Pascal GPUs. Turing Tensor Cores power NVIDIA NGX deep learning features, including Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS) for improved performance and image quality over Temporal Anti-Aliasing, plus InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. The architecture introduces Mesh Shading with Task and Mesh Shaders to eliminate CPU draw call bottlenecks and increase object counts. Variable Rate Shading (VRS) allows dynamic, per-region shading rate control to optimize performance via Content Adaptive, Motion Adaptive, and Foveated Rendering. Texture Space Shading (TSS) decouples visibility and shading for greater efficiency, particularly in VR. Multi-View Rendering (MVR) expands Pascal’s Simultaneous Multi-Projection to support up to four hardware views per pass for efficient stereo and multi-view rendering. Turing also supports bindless resources, Tier 2 resource heaps, and VR-specific enhancements including VirtualLink USB-C connectivity and VRWorks Audio accelerated by RT Cores. The architecture is delivered in multiple GPUs, including the TU104 (used in GeForce RTX 2080, Quadro RTX 5000, and Tesla T4) and TU106 (GeForce RTX 2070). A new workload-based metric, RTX-OPS, quantifies combined Tensor, FP32, RT core, and INT32 operations for hybrid rendering.

Smoky River FCSS seeks parents with babies aged 2–4 months in October for the 2017–2018 Roots of Empathy program. Founded by Mary Gordon in 1996, the program uses classroom baby visits to teach children empathy and reduce aggression. Contact Crystal at 780-837-2220 or youthsrfcss@live.com.

Researchers developed a semi-empirical Bayesian framework that borrows information across sex groups to improve sex-specific variant effect estimates and Mendelian randomization (MR) causal inference, particularly for smaller samples. Using sex-specific sleep genome-wide association studies from the Million Veteran Program and cardiovascular disease outcomes from the All of Us study, they identified causal associations including insomnia with chronic kidney disease and long sleep with hypertension in females, and short sleep with coronary artery disease in males. Significant sex differences were identified for obstructive sleep apnea on chronic kidney disease and for long sleep on multiple cardiovascular outcomes, with higher risks in females. Simulation studies demonstrated that the adaptive posterior mean estimator improves efficiency of causal effect estimation for smaller groups without sacrificing efficiency in larger groups, and also enhances instrumental variable selection.

A University of Copenhagen study found that passive social media use, or "lurking," causes envy and mood deterioration through unrealistic social comparisons. A 2015 study linked over two hours of daily social media use to higher mental illness risk in teens. While these networks also offer mental health services, researchers recommend limiting time, using platforms actively for connection, or quitting altogether.

Researchers theoretically introduce and experimentally demonstrate a dynamically-controllable x-ray interferometer for Mössbauer science. The device uses two co-propagating pathways in a dark-fringe mode within a polarimetry setup containing two α-iron targets enriched in 57Fe. The targets’ magnetizations are aligned at α1 = π/4 and α2 = −π/4, causing radiative couplings to cancel and allowing the two pathways to be addressed via different polarizations. In this configuration, the empty interferometer ideally transmits no x-rays. A relative displacement of the targets, induced by a piezo-electric transducer on the first target, continuously tunes the relative phase between the pathways via a motion-induced phase jump ϕ = 2πΔz/λ. Experiments demonstrated control of transmitted x-ray intensity on the nanosecond timescale and measurement of relative displacements on x-ray wavelength and nanosecond timescales by observing mechanical waves in the target holder.

At a prize ceremony at Government Girls High School, Liaquatabad, Dr Rana Tariq Khan called students valuable assets and announced a water pump and furniture. Deputy District Officer Muhammad Aslam Qaisrani said Punjab government provides free education, qualified faculty, and Rs1,000 stipends.

Benchmarks are central to evaluating language models, but structural issues such as uneven data distributions can distort aggregate scores and mislead interpretations of model capability. This work introduces HARMONY, an entropy-based metric that measures how uniformly a model’s performance is distributed across semantic subdomains of a benchmark. High HARMONY indicates that aggregate accuracy reflects broad competence, whereas low HARMONY indicates that overall scores may obscure subdomain-specific strengths or weaknesses. The authors recommend reporting HARMONY alongside accuracy to improve distributional reliability and present a large-scale empirical mapping of 19 multiple-choice question-answering benchmarks across five model families.

Markets shifted decisively risk-off last week as a barrage of controversial economic and policy events triggered a bearish engulfing pattern and breakdown from record highs. Stronger-than-expected Q2 GDP (3% vs. 2.5%) remained clouded by tariff distortions, while nonfarm payrolls disappointed with only 73,000 jobs added and record downward revisions, though the unemployment rate rose only to 4.2%. The FOMC meeting featured two dissenting votes for the first time since the 1990s, with Chair Powell signaling patience and data dependency amid uncertainty over tariffs and immigration-driven labor force changes. Following the jobs data, President Trump dismissed Bureau of Labor Statistics Commissioner Erika McEntarfer, announced nuclear submarine deployments toward Russia, and advanced tariff actions, while Fed Governor Adriana Kugler announced an early resignation. Despite broadly positive Q2 earnings—82% of S&P 500 companies beat EPS estimates and 79% beat revenue estimates, with upward revision ratios hitting multi-month highs—markets sold into the news. Volume and internals turned negative, nearly all sectors except Utilities declined, and key economic bellwethers like transports and retail entered distribution phases. Interest rate markets priced in over 75% odds of a September rate cut and three cuts by January, while short-to-long-term bond ETFs broke above key resistance levels. Technical indicators, including the risk gauge and moving average breadth, flipped negative, confirming a tactical pullback.

The lecture discusses renormalization group equations (RGEs) for Wilson coefficients in the weak Hamiltonian for b → c ū d transitions. Because the Hamiltonian is μ-independent, anomalous dimension equations for operators can be rewritten for coefficients. By changing variables from μ to the coupling α using the beta function, the RGE integrates to sum leading logarithms (LL), evolving coefficients from a high scale μ_W ~ M_W down to a low scale μ_b ~ M_b. This separates the physics of different scales, removing large logarithms from matrix elements.

Leading-log results require tree-level matching and one-loop anomalous dimensions, while next-to-leading-log (NLL) results require one-loop matching and two-loop anomalous dimensions. Matching compares full Standard Model calculations to effective theory calculations; differences in logs and constants determine the Wilson coefficients. The infrared structure must agree between theories, confirming the effective theory has the correct degrees of freedom.

At higher orders, scheme dependence enters: matching constants, two-loop anomalous dimensions, and operator matrix elements are scheme-dependent, but physical observables—the product of coefficients and operators—remain scheme-independent. Specific combinations, such as B₁ + J, are also scheme-independent. The lecture notes subtleties in dimensional regularization, including the treatment of γ₅ and evanescent operators in d dimensions.

Patient advocacy groups asked the U.K. antitrust regulator to investigate large drugmakers and their lobbying organization for suspected coordinated efforts to raise medicine prices. The complaint follows a dispute over mandatory NHS rebates that increased from 10% to 23%, prompting AstraZeneca, Merck, and Eli Lilly to halt or scrap $2.6 billion in U.K. expansion plans.

The speaker addresses Congress to outline plans for building a better America through economic growth and deficit reduction. He proposes cutting the federal budget deficit by nearly 40 percent in one year without raising taxes, allocating over $80 billion in new revenues from growth toward key priorities while meeting Gramm-Rudman-Hollings targets. He pledges to negotiate with Congress and seeks budget process reforms, including two-year budgets, a line-item veto, rescission votes, and a balanced budget amendment.

Domestically, he proposes increased funding for education, including a $500 million merit schools program, Presidential awards for teachers, National Science Scholars, and expanded school choice. He requests almost $1 billion to escalate the war on drugs, supporting treatment, border interdiction, tougher law enforcement including the death penalty for kingpins, and demand reduction through education. He asks for $1.6 billion for AIDS education and research. Environmental proposals include a new Clean Air Act, acid rain reduction, clean coal technology funding, ocean protection, indefinite postponement of three offshore lease sales pending environmental review, and stricter toxic waste enforcement. He requests full Medicaid funding with a $3 billion increase, expansion for pregnant women near poverty, a child care tax credit for low-income families, doubling the adoption tax deduction to $3,000, full Social Security funding, and new aid for the homeless. He supports Puerto Rico holding a referendum on its political future and personally favors statehood. He also backs savings system reform and doubling cleanup efforts at nuclear weapons plants.

On defense, he supports a one-year budget freeze conditioned on a comprehensive deficit agreement that meets Gramm-Rudman-Hollings targets without raising taxes, with real increases afterward, alongside procurement and management reforms. Foreign policy priorities include pursuing the Strategic Defense Initiative, banning chemical weapons, stopping nuclear proliferation, and strengthening alliances. He concludes by asking Congress for cooperation and quoting Churchill: "Give us the tools, and we will do the job."

Computing evolved from purpose-built machines to client-server architectures, and in the early 2000s, internet-scale datacenters enabled distributed systems. These systems offer greater reliability and scalability but are significantly more complex to design, build, and debug. As demand grows, containers, container images, and orchestrators have become foundational tools enabling reusable patterns and components for building reliable distributed systems.

At Lansdowne High School, students in Brandon Nicklas's televideo production class produce morning announcements and a monthly variety program, gaining hands-on video production experience. Television studios are present in about 100 of the county's 161 schools, with roughly half operating as digital studios, though funding depends on individual school budgets rather than central support. While basic live streaming equipment costs about $400, full digital studios run $15,000 to $18,000. This year, broadcast production facilitators became a union-negotiated extra-duty position with compensation between $2,005 and $3,004. Educators and media experts say these programs teach teamwork, communication, public speaking, and technical skills that are increasingly valuable as video content grows online. Schools like Hillcrest Elementary and Arbutus Middle School have recently launched studios.

Penn Medicine researchers found that a single dose of psilocybin reduced chronic pain and pain-induced anxiety and depression-like behaviors in mice for almost two weeks. The compound works by gently activating serotonin receptors in the anterior cingulate cortex, bypassing injury sites to modulate pain and mood circuits. Unlike opioids, psilocybin is non-addictive. Researchers stated that more study is needed to determine long-term effects, optimal dosing, and safety in humans, including in surgical contexts.

This study applied DIA-based urinary proteomics and bioinformatics analysis to identify distinct protein profiles among type 1 HAE, type 2 HAE, and healthy controls. Enriched biological processes included complement and coagulation cascades, immune response, and bradykinin catabolism. A biomarker panel comprising C1-INH, KNG1, and EGF was proposed as a noninvasive diagnostic tool and validated via PRM-based targeted proteomics in independent cohorts of HAE patients and healthy controls recruited from Peking Union Medical College Hospital. The research aimed to facilitate noninvasive HAE diagnosis and enhance understanding of disease pathogenesis.

Researchers demonstrate an ultrafast, ultralow-dissipation magnetic microrotor operating at 4.2 K. A hard ferromagnetic sphere levitates above a type-I superconductor via Meissner repulsion, with motion detected by a dc SQUID and driven into a continuous spinning mode by a synchronous feedback technique. In free spin-down, the rotational frequency decays exponentially, with a damping rate γ proportional to the gas pressure. By relating the rotor-derived pressure to room-temperature gauge readings and accounting for helium sensitivity and thermomolecular gradients, the device is validated as a wide-range cryogenic pressure sensor effective from 10⁻³ mbar down to 4 × 10⁻⁸ mbar. The lowest measured damping rate is 4.75 × 10⁻⁷ s⁻¹, corresponding to a quality factor of 1.33 × 10¹³, while the maximum achieved spinning frequency is 2.3 MHz (tangential speed 466 m/s), limited by SQUID electronics and approaching an estimated material limit of ~5.5 MHz. A secondary low-frequency spectral peak observed during spin-down is attributed to precession of the spinning axis caused by the superconducting image field. The authors identify this as the fastest magnetically levitated rotor demonstrated and the first cryogenic spinning-rotor gauge at 4.2 K, and they discuss applications in pressure sensing, gyroscopes, gravimeters, and precision torque measurements such as ultralight dark matter detection, as well as future tests of quantum field effects and fundamental spin phenomena.

Researchers at Columbia University accidentally created a tiny silicon chip that converts a single multimode laser diode into a frequency comb. Using a locking mechanism to clean the laser's noisy light, the device produces dozens of powerful, coherent, evenly spaced wavelengths simultaneously. This compact technology could replace multiple individual lasers in data centers, cutting costs, saving space, and enabling faster, more energy-efficient data transmission via wavelength-division multiplexing. The chip also has potential applications in sensing, quantum technology, LiDAR, portable spectrometers, and optical clocks.

The TPS7H500x-SP series comprises radiation-hardness-assured, peak current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting switching frequencies from 100 kHz to 2 MHz and topologies including buck, flyback, forward, push-pull, and full-bridge. The devices feature three oscillator modes—internal oscillator (set via an RT resistor), external synchronization (via a SYNC pin clock), and primary-secondary (interconnecting two controllers via SYNC)—along with configurable duty cycle limits, programmable dead time, leading edge blank time, slope compensation, and soft-start. Protection features include cycle-by-cycle current limiting with hiccup mode, external fault shutdown, and thermal shutdown at 175°C. Primary switching outputs (OUTA/OUTB) and synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA/SRB) are available depending on the specific device variant, each with roughly 150 mA peak current capability and requiring external gate drivers. The document provides a detailed synchronous push-pull converter design example using GaN FETs, covering component selection for the oscillator, feedback, transformer, dead time, blank time, soft-start, output filter, current sense, frequency compensation, and slope compensation. Layout guidelines recommend separating analog and power grounds, minimizing high di/dt switching loops, routing noise-sensitive traces away from high dv/dt signals, and placing bypass capacitors close to the controller. The controllers operate from a 4 V to 14 V supply.

The article explains the MACD (Moving Average Convergence/Divergence) indicator, first mentioned in the 1970s and invented by Gerald Appel. It is calculated using a fast line (12-day EMA minus 26-day EMA), a slow signal line (9-day EMA of the fast line), and a histogram (the difference between the two). Default settings are 12, 26, and 9. MACD is a lagging, oscillating indicator used to identify momentum, trends, and mean reversion.

A basic S&P 500 crossover strategy from 1993 produced a 4.19% CAGR, a 1.65 profit factor, and a 30% maximum drawdown, which the passage deems untradeable. Optimization indicates the best parameters remain near the defaults. A MACD histogram mean-reversion strategy on the S&P 500 yielded a 4.79% CAGR, a 4.22 profit factor, and a 16% drawdown. Combining the histogram with a two-day RSI strategy improved results further, producing a 6.36% CAGR and a 16% drawdown. The article notes moderate success with crypto, states that MACD is better for momentum while RSI is better for overbought/oversold levels, and concludes that the crossover has limited stand-alone value, whereas the histogram shows promise. Effectiveness varies by market and requires backtesting to determine optimal settings.
