The 2-1-2 zone is a compact defense protecting the middle, with an athletic middle defender and "Bigs" on the blocks for rebounding. Susceptible to outside shooting, it is used against poor shooting teams or high post offenses. The middle defender covers the high post or fronts the low post. The two quickest outside defenders move in unison. The post guards the low post, while baseline players work opposite, one always in a weakside rebounding position.

This study investigates prominent elements of first-year architectural design education at BUU Faculty of Architecture through ethnographic observation and student interviews to derive analogical inferences for STEM education. Drawing on literature regarding STEM education, project-based learning, design processes, and architectural studios, the research employed unstructured observation of studio courses and interviews with eight volunteer students over one semester. Content analysis of observation notes and interviews yielded four themes: confronting open-ended problems and student motivation; deepening understanding of the problem situation through research and field investigation; gaining experience in presentation techniques and portfolio development; and meeting the culture of criticism via instructor and jury critiques. Students perceived the course as fostering abstract and conceptual thinking, while identifying challenges such as the invention process, time constraints, model-making, and presentations. Through analogical inference, the authors propose six conclusions for STEM education: students should independently manage open-ended problems from start to finish; STEM projects should be weighted as graduation requirements at K12 and K16 levels, whereas K4 and K8 should focus on problem situations rather than product-oriented projects; problem themes must be authentic, possessing real-life context with sustainability and value; younger students should physically interact with relevant materials and tools even when a final product is not expected; technical drawing and graphic communication skills should be incorporated into high school curricula; and undergraduate STEM education should shift from technical rationality toward reflection-in-action, supported by institutional structures such as jury-based assessment.

Yael Kalai explains that applying the Fiat-Shamir transform in the random oracle model to a protocol with non-negligible soundness is unsound, because a cheating prover can repeatedly query the oracle to guess challenges and retry until producing a valid transcript. Even reducing soundness to negligible via sequential repetition fails to prevent this, as the prover can still gradually build a multi-round transcript by guessing each challenge, keeping successful prefixes, and extending them while re-hashing from the beginning each time.

However, Fiat-Shamir is sound in the random oracle model if the underlying public-coin protocol has negligible soundness and a constant number of rounds. The proof demonstrates that a poly-size cheating prover making at most q oracle queries can be used to construct an interactive cheating prover whose success probability is roughly the original epsilon divided by a polynomial factor in q (decaying further with more rounds). This is not a complete characterization; protocols with many rounds, such as GKR, can remain secure if they possess round-by-round soundness.

Kalai notes that the Kilian-Micali protocol has four rounds and negligible error, making Fiat-Shamir sound for it in the random oracle model. Yet there exist contrived hash functions for which it is insecure in the standard model, illustrating that the random oracle model is only a theoretical sanity check and does not guarantee the existence of a suitable real hash function.

The lecture then discusses parallel repetition of zero-knowledge proofs. While sequential repetition preserves zero-knowledge, parallel repetition of the specific Hamiltonian cycle protocol does not. A 2019 result established this by proving that Fiat-Shamir is sound for that protocol under standard cryptographic assumptions. Consequently, the parallel version cannot be zero-knowledge: if an efficient simulator could produce accepting transcripts for any verifier, it could break Fiat-Shamir soundness by simulating the Fiat-Shamir verifier itself.

Artificial Intelligence is rapidly transforming higher education globally, with 86% of students already using AI tools. Applications include intelligent tutoring systems, predictive analytics, and adaptive learning platforms that personalize instruction and improve retention. While technologically advanced regions lead adoption, developing areas face infrastructural and funding barriers. Institutions are responding through faculty training, curricular innovation, and policy frameworks such as the UNESCO Beijing Consensus and Australian TEQSA guidelines. AI is reshaping pedagogy, research, and administration, offering opportunities for global collaboration, workforce preparation, and accessibility for learners with disabilities. Specific tools like ChatGPT support writing and brainstorming; Bard provides real-time research data; and Gemini offers emotional intelligence applications. However, significant challenges remain, including academic integrity risks, algorithmic bias, data privacy concerns, faculty resistance, and a digital divide that risks exacerbating educational inequalities. Case studies from China’s Squirrel AI and Arizona State University demonstrate AI’s potential to improve outcomes in underserved and online populations. Looking forward, trends point toward emotional recognition systems, virtual and augmented reality, and real-time translation. The paper recommends robust ethical frameworks, international cooperation, equitable infrastructure investment, and positioning AI as a complementary tool to human educators to ensure inclusive, sustainable integration.

The North Dakota Supreme Court reversed a district court order suppressing evidence in a driving under the influence case against Denise M. Hahne. The district court had suppressed evidence after finding Hahne had no safe or legal way to avoid a sobriety checkpoint. The Supreme Court held that law enforcement checkpoints need not provide motorists with an opportunity to avoid them as a matter of law. While avoidability may be considered as one factor in evaluating the intrusion on individual liberty when assessing constitutional reasonableness, it is not a legal requirement. The Court remanded the case for the district court to apply the correct legal standard and determine whether the checkpoint was constitutionally reasonable.

In *Alan A. Brister v. United States*, the Court of Federal Claims held that the IRS’s 1993 adjustment of the plaintiff’s 1985 and 1986 tax returns—reversing withholding credits and applying refunds from 1989 through 1992 against resulting liabilities—was timely. Although the adjustment occurred more than three years after the returns were filed, the court found the limitation period under 26 U.S.C. § 6501(a) tolled under § 6501(c)(1) because the returns were false and filed with intent to evade tax. Brister, an accountant for Solar Roofing, Inc., had claimed refunds based on W-2 forms showing federal income tax withholdings that the employer never paid. The court found by clear and convincing evidence that Brister knew the W-2s were false when he filed and intended to use the IRS to collect personal debts from the company. The court rejected the argument that no tax evasion occurred because legitimate withholdings otherwise covered his liability, holding the fraud still tainted the return. Judgment was entered for the defendant.

This qualitative case study investigates faculty and student perspectives on how distance education affects equality and inequality of opportunity in education. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with 21 faculty members and 26 students and analyzed via content analysis. Faculty identified positive impacts as learning at a personal pace and easy access to information, while negative impacts included problems accessing technology, internet connection issues, disregard for learner competencies, unsuitable learning environments, and increased differences among students. Students viewed freedom from time limitations, free-of-charge education, and access to various sources as contributions to equality, while citing financial capabilities and internet problems as causes of inequality. Suggestions to reduce inequality include determining learner characteristics, improving technology access and digital literacy, resolving internet infrastructure problems, official state budgeting for technology, and teachers providing consultancy services. The discussion notes that digital gaps and socio-economic inequalities persist globally, supporting the need for infrastructure improvements, policy updates, and digital literacy training.

The 13/48 trading strategy uses exponential moving average crossovers to generate signals. A bullish signal occurs when the 13-period EMA crosses above the 48-period EMA, and a bearish signal occurs when it crosses below. The momentum-based strategy works best in trending markets but is risky in sideways or choppy conditions. Backtesting showed it works best on stocks, yielding a 5.1% annual return on the S&P 500 from 1960 to present with a 7.8% risk-adjusted return, compared to 7.2% for buy and hold. However, it is a lagging indicator prone to whipsaws and is no easy way to riches.

The lecture defines quantum entanglement as a state of two physically distinct, separable subsystems that cannot be factorized into a product of individual wave functions, distinguishing it from superpositions involving vacuum states or inseparable particles such as electrons in a helium atom. The professor introduces the four maximally entangled Bell states and notes that entanglement is a resource for applications like teleportation but is fragile against decoherence. Entanglement can be quantified by the von Neumann entropy of the reduced density matrix obtained via partial trace; maximally entangled pure states yield the highest entropy. The lecture explains entanglement purification, a protocol using controlled-NOT operations and measurements on multiple weakly entangled copies to probabilistically generate maximally entangled Bell states, where the success probability reflects the initial degree of entanglement. Methods for creating entangled atoms are discussed, including the photo-dissociation of a diatomic molecule with nuclear spin and a probabilistic scheme in which photons emitted by two distant atoms are mixed at a beam splitter and measured. The Hong-Ou-Mandel interference effect is described: identical bosons bunch together at a balanced beam splitter, while fermions always exit separately. By adding circular polarizers and detecting photons in separate outputs, the measurement projects the atoms into an entangled state.

In mid-May 2007, Victor Reinoso, Deputy Mayor for Education, faced a deadline to recommend a chancellor to lead the Washington, DC Public Schools (DCPS) under incoming mayoral control. Mayor Adrian Fenty was set to assume control of the struggling district on June 12, 2007, following passage of the DC Public Education Reform Act, which shifted authority from the school board to the mayor and established a chancellor to manage day-to-day operations.

DCPS suffered from chronic failure: half its schools did not meet federal standards, it ranked last among major urban districts in student achievement despite high per-pupil spending, and it was plagued by administrative bloat, patronage, and high leadership turnover. Reinoso, a former DC school board member and business consultant, believed incremental reform was insufficient. During the transition, he assembled a team, commissioned data from the Parthenon Group identifying six core pain points—including lack of accountability and operational inefficiency—and drafted the mayoral control legislation.

To lead radical reform, Reinoso sought an entrepreneurial chancellor unburdened by “sacred cows.” He considered several candidates: Rudy Crew, a veteran superintendent known for aggressive urban reforms; Michelle Rhee, a Teach for America alumna and founder of The New Teacher Project who had strong views on teacher accountability but limited administrative experience; and incumbent superintendent Clifford Janey, whose comprehensive plans were undermined by cautious, consensus-driven implementation. The search was complicated when Reinoso was accused of plagiarizing portions of a strategic document, briefly jeopardizing the takeover timeline. With his recommendation due within hours, Reinoso needed to select a leader capable of fundamentally transforming DCPS without capsizing it.

This work develops quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC) methods to estimate expectations of quantities of interest from a semi-linear parabolic reaction-diffusion model of tumor growth, extending QMC theory to nonlinear parabolic equations for uncertainty quantification in computational oncology. The model describes tumor invasion and proliferation with logistic growth and includes linear terms for radiotherapy and chemotherapy, with diffusion and proliferation coefficients modeled as random fields. The authors establish well-posedness and a priori bounds for the parametric model, derive novel parametric regularity bounds for uniform random fields, prove QMC error rates, and confirm the theoretical results with numerical experiments on uniform and log-normal random fields over complex domains. The analysis uses a functional framework based on Sobolev and Bochner spaces.

Mesh is a short-to-intermediate passing concept used across football offenses to create natural picks and confusion. It is effective against both man coverage, allowing receivers to beat one-on-one matchups while on the move, and zone coverages like Cover 2, 3, and 4, where drag routes settle into voids. The play struggles against zone blitzes or simulated pressure that can overwhelm five-man protection. The quarterback must anticipate pressure and follow a progression of flare, shallow drag, deep drag, and FB arrow. Common variations include the "mesh rail," which features a running back on a vertical rail route, and a sit route over the ball at 8–10 yards as a zone answer. The concept can also be adapted from formations such as the Single Wing.

This document standardizes the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests to interoperate with hypervisors while protecting encrypted guest register state. It defines the GHCB layout, protocol versions, and hypervisor feature advertisement via a FEATURES bitmap. VMEXIT events are classified as Automatic Exits (AEs), which require no guest state exposure, and Non-Automatic Exits (NAEs), where the guest selectively shares state through the GHCB. The specification details MSR protocols for GHCB negotiation, CPUID requests, GHCB GPA registration, page state changes, AP reset hold, and SNP-specific NAE events including AP creation, SNP Run VMPL, SNP Guest Requests, SNP Extended Guest Requests for certificate data, SNP TIO Guest Requests for trusted devices, Secure AVIC backing page registration, and termination requests. It also documents SMP booting under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP, NMI handling, debug register support, the SNP Secrets Page and EFI Confidential Computing Blob, and SNP Restricted Injection mechanisms including hypervisor doorbells, essential data, and interrupt shadows. System Management Mode and nested virtualization are not supported.

This technology relates to sealing fluid flow passages in high-pressure oil and gas flow control devices, including plug valves and fluid ends. Harsh operating conditions erode the body bore where seals abrade against it, causing leakage and requiring cumbersome, costly body repairs. Embodiments form grooves or recesses in the body bore or conduit walls to mount seals that extend to seal against mating components, such as valve inserts, retaining nuts, discharge plugs, suction plugs, stuffing box sleeves, and valve seats. This transfers erosion and wear from the body to the less complex, less expensive mating component, increasing operating life while reducing downtime and repair costs. The technology accommodates various seal types, including radial, axial, and crush seals, and may include erosion-resistant surface treatments on the mating components.

The paper introduces CTPNet, a unified deep learning framework for multivariate long-term time series forecasting that simultaneously models inter-channel, intra-subsequence, and inter-subsequence dependencies. It employs Channel-wise Representation Learning with temporal query-based Multi-Head Attention to capture cross-variable interactions, Trend-wise Representation Learning with efficient attention to model local temporal structures within downsampled subsequences, and Periodic-wise Representation Learning to uncover global dynamics across subsequences. The architecture incorporates downsampling, linear encoding, decoding, and de-downsampling stages to generate predictions. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, with CTPNet achieving the highest first-place count among the compared methods.

The Supreme Court of Louisiana affirmed Ray Jones Jr.’s conviction and life sentence for the first-degree murder of his infant son. The court rejected his argument that three inculpatory statements were improperly admitted, holding that the first two statements made to hospital personnel were voluntary, unsolicited, and not the product of police interrogation, so Miranda warnings were not required. Regarding the third statement at the police station, the court held that the detective’s remarks were consolatory and did not constitute interrogation under Miranda and Rhode Island v. Innis, and that the defendant voluntarily changed his mind after invoking his rights. The court further held that even if the third statement were improperly admitted, the error was harmless beyond a reasonable doubt given the overwhelming evidence of guilt, including testimony regarding the two prior statements. The court also rejected the defendant’s claim that the trial judge abused his discretion by restricting cross-examination of a psychiatrist about “bad information” from family members, finding the question irrelevant to the voluntariness of the statements.

The description relates to controlling a mobile agricultural machine using active ground terrain mapping. A pose detection sensor generates position and orientation signals at points along a route, which are used to identify a virtual point cloud estimated to correspond to the ground surface. Elevation values and distance-based weight values are generated for each point and aggregated into a georeferenced map structure. The elevation data is used to generate control signals for controllable subsystems, such as height actuators for a header or boom, and can include calculating a predictive plane for ground elevation ahead of the machine.

This study investigates micro-credentials in Mauritian higher education through semi-structured interviews with ten educational and four industry leaders. Micro-credentials certify specific competencies gained through short learning experiences and are seen as addressing gaps between traditional higher education and contemporary workplace skills. The research examined stakeholder familiarity, integration into credit systems, and professional value.

Participants generally understood micro-credentials as short, competence-based offerings, though definitions varied between education leaders—who emphasized assessed learning units—and industry leaders—who viewed them as stackable, personalized qualifications. Most favored a hybrid model integrating micro-credentials into existing credit systems with minimal disruption, enabling flexible, industry-responsive pathways. Respondents regarded micro-credentials as a disruptive innovation requiring incremental implementation rather than immediate full integration into formal degree programs.

Key challenges included the absence of a universal definition, difficulties aligning credentials with the National Qualifications Framework and academic credits, and concerns about quality assurance, reliable assessment, and employer recognition. Stakeholders agreed that regulatory frameworks must evolve to recognize micro-credentials formally. The study concludes that despite limited understanding, leaders recognize the importance of micro-credentials and recommend establishing a unified national framework that facilitates academic credit transfer and employer acceptance.

Generative artificial intelligence (AI), including large language models (LLMs), is rapidly advancing and poses significant disruptive challenges to traditional higher education assessment while offering opportunities to transform teaching, personalize learning, and create more authentic evaluation methods. Conventional assessments such as essays, multiple-choice questions (MCQs), and short-answer questions are vulnerable to AI interference; studies show that ChatGPT can produce first-class essays and pass professional licensing exams, while plagiarism and AI detection tools remain unreliable, prone to false positives, and potentially biased against non-native English speakers. Consequently, the traditional academic essay and standard MCQs are increasingly viewed as inauthentic and insecure.

Institutions can respond through two broad strategies: mitigating AI impact or integrating AI into assessment. Mitigation approaches include in-person invigilated exams, presentations, vivas, practical examinations, and objective structured clinical examinations (OSCEs), which are less susceptible to AI interference. Integration approaches treat AI as either an auxiliary tool—such as for generating draft outlines, ideas, or practice questions—or as an integral part of the task, requiring students to critique AI outputs, compare AI and human sources, engage in Socratic debates with AI, or use AI as a research and data analysis tool. AI can also deliver immediate, personalized feedback, generate rubrics, and simulate peer review, though concerns about accuracy, bias, superficiality, and misalignment with curriculum expectations persist.

The paper presents a case study from a UK postgraduate immunology module in which a traditional essay was redesigned to integrate ChatGPT. Students received training on AI capabilities, limitations, and prompt engineering; used ChatGPT to generate draft essay outlines; participated in peer evaluation workshops to critique the AI outputs; and then independently wrote final submissions without further AI assistance. In-course surveys of 20 students revealed that 57.9% had previously used generative AI, but only 5% felt very confident using it. Students identified planning, drafting, and summarizing as primary uses, while citing accuracy, outdated information, lack of critical thinking, and superficial responses as key limitations. Only 26% considered using AI in assessments to be plagiarism, while 37% were unsure. Participants found the AI-generated outlines a useful starting point but criticized their generic, uniform nature and questioned their accuracy.

The authors argue that universities have a responsibility to develop students' technological and ethical AI competencies for future employability. Rather than attempting to outrun AI capabilities or relying on detection software—which may foster accusation cultures and become obsolete—institutions should embed AI literacy into curricula, train educators, and redesign assessments to focus on higher-order cognitive skills such as critical thinking, problem-solving, creativity, and complex evaluation. A holistic, progressive integration of AI can diversify assessments, enhance authenticity, maintain academic integrity through transparency and proper training, and better prepare students for an AI-driven society.

The passage describes SD Physical Layer Specification Version 6.00 requirements for UHS-I and UHS-II bus speed modes, initialization, and command operations. UHS-I operates in SD mode with 1.8V signaling entered through an ACMD41 negotiation and CMD11 voltage switch, supporting SDR12, SDR50, DDR50, and SDR104 modes selected via CMD6 Function Group 1, with 4-bit bus width and driver strength configured by CMD6 groups. UHS-II adds modes including FD156, HD312, FD312, and FD624, initializing through PHY synchronization, enumeration, configuration, and SD-TRAN stages after detecting a STB.L signal within 200µs. Card identification requires CMD0, CMD8, and ACMD41 with HCS/S18R bits to establish voltage, capacity status, and RCA before entering data transfer mode, where commands like CMD7 select cards and CMD12 abort transfers. Erase functions include DISCARD and FULE for SDHC/SDXC. Lock/unlock and Card Ownership Protection rely on CMD42 sequences involving PWD and FEP registers, requiring COP Unlock when FEP is set. CMD6 manages function switching for bus speed, driver strength, and power limits.

The passage details NVIDIA's RTX Blackwell GPU architecture and associated technologies. The AI Management Processor (AMP) is a dedicated RISC-V scheduler that offloads GPU context scheduling from the CPU, reducing latency and improving workload management and gaming performance in coordination with Windows Hardware-Accelerated GPU Scheduling (HAGS).

Blackwell adds hardware encode and decode support for 4:2:2 chroma-sampled video (H.264 and HEVC), offering greater color accuracy than 4:2:0 with lower bandwidth than 4:4:4. The ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC quality by 5% and introduces an AV1 Ultra High Quality mode. The RTX 5090 supports up to three encoders and two decoders, while the improved sixth-generation NVDEC offers 2x faster H.264 decoding and 4:2:2 support. DisplayPort 2.1b support enables up to 80 Gbps bandwidth (UHBR 20) for high-resolution, high-refresh-rate displays.

Max-Q power efficiency improvements include advanced power and clock gating, separate voltage rails for GPU cores and memory, accelerated frequency switching (1000x faster than previous architectures), and low-latency sleep states (10x faster than Ada), enabling up to 50% power savings in scenarios like small language model inference.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, producing up to three additional frames per traditionally rendered frame using a faster AI model with lower VRAM usage, alongside enhanced Flip Metering for smoother pacing. It also transitions to transformer-based neural networks for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing, improving temporal stability, detail, and image quality over previous CNN models.

Blackwell introduces neural shaders via the Cooperative Vectors API, allowing Tensor Core access through graphics shaders. This enables technologies like RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression (up to 7:1 compression), Neural Radiance Cache for global illumination, RTX Skin for subsurface scattering, and RTX Neural Faces using generative AI.

The architecture comprises several GPUs: the flagship GB202 (RTX 5090) with 92.2 billion transistors, 192 SMs, and 24,576 CUDA cores; the high-end GB203 (RTX 5080/5070 Ti) with 45.6 billion transistors, 84 SMs, and 10,752 CUDA cores; and the performance-segment GB205 (RTX 5070) with 31 billion transistors, 50 SMs, and 6,400 CUDA cores.

This preprint reports a Phase 2/3 observer-blind, randomized, controlled study of SII-NVX-CoV2373 in 920 Indian children and adolescents aged 2–17 years, randomized 3:1 to receive two vaccine doses or placebo. The vaccine was safe and well tolerated, with no adverse events of special interest and no causally related serious adverse events. It was highly immunogenic, with over 98% seroconversion for anti-S IgG and neutralizing antibodies after the second dose, and demonstrated non-inferior immune responses compared with vaccinated adults, though titers were higher in the pediatric cohorts. Robust immune responses against the Delta, Omicron BA.1, and Omicron BA.5 variants were also observed. By day 180, antibody levels declined but remained substantially above baseline, with over 90% seroconversion maintained. The authors conclude the vaccine is safe and highly immunogenic in this age group and provides evidence of protection against COVID-19, including emerging variants.

Mud Bay, a Pacific Northwest pet store chain founded in 1988 by the Wulff family, launched a “Good Jobs Vision” (GJV) in 2014 to address low profit margins and 48% annual employee turnover. Co-CEOs Marisa and Lars Wulff, COO Tracy Yamane, and a 20-person strategic planning team committed to investing in staff first—raising wages, expanding benefits, and launching an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP)—with the goal of funding improvements through increased productivity and sales growth. The GJV centered on five strategies: investing in staff; simplifying assortment and offering everyday low prices; standardizing processes while empowering staff; improving efficiency through cross-training and operational slack; and partnering with animal welfare organizations.

From 2014 to 2017, Mud Bay increased average hourly wages from $11.50 to $15.00, reduced active SKUs from roughly 3,750 to 3,180, lowered retail prices, and standardized some inventory and delivery practices. Total sales grew 70%, same-store sales growth averaged above 9%, and employee turnover fell from 48% to 31%. However, net profit margins declined from 2.18% to 1.99% due to higher labor and benefit costs, price reductions, and investments in new stores.

By mid-2018, the leadership team was struggling to achieve adequate profitability in the 2018 budget. Tracy Yamane proposed closing stores one hour earlier Monday through Saturday to generate labor savings and improve staff work-life balance. Marisa supported the proposal, while Lars opposed it, fearing lost revenue and customer inconvenience. The case concludes as the annual planning team reviewed sales data and prepared to decide on the store hours change.

This qualitative study investigated the experiences of 17 third-year distance-learning Bachelor of Education students and four lecturers regarding Physical Education teacher training in distance mode at North-West University, South Africa. Data were collected through open-ended student questionnaires and semi-structured lecturer interviews. Five themes emerged: interaction between students and lecturers; competence, passion and enthusiasm; obstacles in distance learning; experiences of practical training; and the influence of program content on perceptions. Participants praised lecturer accessibility and responsiveness but noted the lack of physical contact. Students reported increased confidence and subject knowledge, while lecturers expressed passion for holistic development. Key obstacles included students' limited foundational Physical Education knowledge, technological illiteracy, limited internet access, and administrative delays in assignment handling. Video-based practical training was viewed positively, though delayed feedback on practical work was problematic. The content positively shifted students' perceptions of Physical Education's value. Recommendations include additional face-to-face contact, technological training for students, enhanced use of videos and media, improved learning management system interaction features, and stronger administrative systems.

Passports are issued only to U.S. citizens who establish their citizenship, U.S. domicile, and bona fide intent to return and reside in the United States. Expatriated persons—those who permanently abandon allegiance to become citizens elsewhere—are ineligible, as are those permanently domiciled abroad, even if not formally expatriated. Determination depends on circumstances: severed ties, foreign homes, and business weigh against issuance, while maintained U.S. connections, health or financial impediments, and representation of American enterprises abroad weigh in favor. Citizens in countries where the U.S. exercises extraterritorial jurisdiction, such as Turkey, may reside indefinitely and retain citizenship rights under special protections, provided their pursuits are legitimate.

The 200-day moving average (200 DMA) is a widely used technical indicator that averages an asset's price over 200 trading days to smooth short-term fluctuations and identify long-term trends. It functions as a trend-following tool: a price above the average indicates an uptrend, while a price below signals a downtrend. The strategy’s main advantages are simplicity, trend capture, and defensive risk management, as it can limit drawdowns by keeping investors out of bear markets. However, in the absence of recessions or during prolonged bull markets, it frequently underperforms buy-and-hold due to whipsaws, transaction costs, slippage, and taxes. The 200-day period is chosen primarily because it is a round number; similar lengths can be used to avoid signal crowding. Both simple and exponential moving averages are common, though simple moving averages are often preferred for their straightforwardness. Hedge fund manager Paul Tudor Jones advocates for the 200 DMA as a critical tool for playing defense and avoiding catastrophic losses. Variations, such as Jeremy Siegel’s strategy requiring a 1% buffer above or below the average, can improve risk-adjusted returns but may not beat buy-and-hold on an absolute basis after costs. Adding a 200 DMA filter to other strategies can reduce drawdowns and improve win rates, though total returns may decrease because of less time spent in the market. Markets with long-term upward biases, such as stocks, spend most of their time above the 200 DMA. The strategy has a low win rate and can experience multiple consecutive losses, demanding significant discipline from traders. While not a silver bullet, the 200 DMA remains a practical and reasonably effective universal tool for trend identification and capital preservation.

The NVIDIA A100 GPU delivers increased L2 and DRAM bandwidth, featuring a 1555 GB/sec HBM2 memory subsystem, 2.3x the L2 cache read bandwidth of the V100, a 40 MB L2 cache, and compute data compression to reduce bandwidth demand. Its Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) capability partitions a single A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances, each with dedicated compute and memory system paths, enabling multi-tenant deployment with quality-of-service guarantees and fault isolation. Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/sec of total GPU-to-GPU bandwidth, while PCIe Gen 4 and SR-IOV enhance host connectivity and virtualization. The architecture also improves error detection, isolation, and containment.

Additional hardware features include five NVDEC and five NVJPG decode units, an optical flow accelerator, and significantly improved atomic operation throughput. CUDA 11 introduces task graphs for reduced launch overhead, asynchronous global-to-shared memory copies, asynchronous barriers, and L2 cache residency controls. The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs via NVSwitch to deliver 5 PFLOPS, supporting up to 56 GPU Instances through MIG. Finally, the A100 supports fine-grained structured sparsity to accelerate sparse neural networks with minimal accuracy loss.

The lecture covers hinged dissections, noting that no general animation software exists and highlighting examples and books by Greg Frederickson. Suggested projects include developing animation tools, implementing slender adorned chain folding, and designing new dissections such as alphabet and polyform conversions. The speaker outlines an inductive, spanning-tree-based method for hinged dissections of polyominoes, polyhexes, polyiamonds, and polyabolos, and describes extensions to 3D tetrahedral forms. Physical implementations discussed include salt-actuated mesoscale models, DNA origami, ball-and-socket joint chains, and chain-based shape-changing robots at MIT, contrasted with modular reconfigurable robots. The lecture explains rectangle-to-rectangle dissection techniques and a pseudopolynomial piece bound achieved via grid triangulation, constant-depth recursion, and hinge-preserving gadgets. Finally, it addresses 3D dissection theory: matching volume and Dehn invariant are necessary and sufficient for dissections in three and four dimensions, relating to Hilbert’s third problem, while the requirement in five or more dimensions remains unknown; the decidability of Dehn invariant equivalence was shown in 2008.

The passage specifies the GHCB protocol for Non-Automatic Exits (NAE) used by SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests. NAE events cause a #VC exception, prompting the guest to copy register state to the GHCB, set the VALID_BITMAP, and invoke VMGEXIT. The document defines required NAE events—including IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, MMIO, Page State Change, SNP Guest and Extended Guest Requests, SNP TIO Guest Request, AP Creation, #HV Doorbell Page, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, Secure AVIC, and Termination Request—and the minimum GHCB state for each. It describes hypervisor error reporting through SW_EXITINFO1/2, guest requirements for parsing intercepted instructions or para-virtualizing accesses, and AP booting challenges under SEV-ES/SNP, detailing AP Jump Tables, AP Reset Hold, and AP Creation NAE events. Additional topics include NMI handling via #DB intercept and an "NMI Complete" message, debug register virtualization, the lack of SMM and nested virtualization support, and SEV-ES detection through CPUID. For SEV-SNP Restricted Injection, the document defines the #HV doorbell page layout (PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired), host APIC emulation behavior, and guest interrupt acknowledgment and end-of-interrupt protocols.

This application, a continuation of U.S. Ser. No. 16/192,068, relates to address obfuscation for memory devices. Memory cell wear-out from normal use or malicious attacks such as row hammer may be mitigated by wear-leveling, which moves data among physical locations; however, bad actors may reverse-engineer wear-leveling patterns to circumvent protection and induce premature failure or unauthorized access. The disclosure describes mapping logical addresses to physical addresses using configurable, variable mapping functions comprising selectable per-bit logic operations (e.g., inversion, pass-through, XOR, XNOR, address swap). A selection component chooses these operations, which may differ per device, die, memory array, or change over time based on events such as boot, reboot, scheduled intervals, access thresholds, attack detection, random numbers, or unique identifiers. This unpredictability hinders reverse-engineering and prevents knowledge gained from one memory entity from being applied to others. The system includes an external memory controller, a memory device with local controllers and memory arrays, and mapping components with subcomponents to implement the logic operations. The physical address space may exceed the logical address space to include scratch cells for wear-leveling. A manufacturer may use a security key to select a direct-addressing mapping function for testing. Methods involve selecting a mapping function, receiving a logical address in an access command, determining the physical address, and accessing the data.

The passage argues that K-12 education’s emphasis on “skills” such as critical thinking, metacognition, and “21st-century skills” has come at the expense of teaching actual knowledge. This study analyzed 2021 Nigeria Malaria Indicator Survey data to determine demographic factors associated with insecticide-treated net (ITN) use among children under 5 and pregnant women in Nigeria. Malaria constitutes a major public health burden in Nigeria, which bears nearly 27% of global cases. Although ITNs are a cost-effective intervention that has driven significant malaria declines, household ownership in Nigeria fell to 56% in 2021 from 69% in 2015. Analysis of 13,727 households found ITN ownership significantly higher among rural households, those in the North West and North East geopolitical zones, and the lowest and second wealth quintiles. Only 41.4% of children under 5 and 49.6% of pregnant women slept under an ITN the night before the survey. ITN use among children was significantly associated with younger age, rural residence, North East or North West zone, and lower wealth quintile. Among pregnant women, ITN use was significantly higher in the North East and North West, among those with no or primary education, and among lower wealth quintiles. The authors conclude that ITN utilization remains below the 80% target of the Nigeria National Malaria Strategic Plan and that addressing regional, socioeconomic, and educational disparities is essential to achieve equitable coverage.

Researchers have identified 560-million-year-old spongelike fossils off the coast of Newfoundland, once considered pseudofossils, as potentially one of Earth’s earliest animals. A University of Queensland study found that the venoms of the Black Mamba, Western Green Mamba, and Jamesons Mamba contain a hidden dual neurological mechanism. The venoms initially cause flaccid paralysis through postsynaptic neurotoxicity, which current antivenoms can treat, but then trigger spastic paralysis through presynaptic toxicity once antivenom is administered. This explains why some patients initially improve after treatment before experiencing painful spasms. The researchers also found that venom function varies by geographic location, further complicating treatment. They urge the development of specialized antivenoms to address these complexities and improve snakebite care.

This systematic review examines the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education assessment, grading, and feedback, synthesizing 20 peer-reviewed studies published between 2010 and 2023. Grounded in the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework and following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, the review evaluates AI's effectiveness in automating assessments, the accuracy and fairness of AI-driven grading, and the benefits of personalized feedback. Findings indicate that AI enhances efficiency, scalability, and consistency in assessment processes, reduces educator workload, and provides real-time, individualized feedback that supports adaptive learning. AI grading systems demonstrate high reliability for objective assessments, particularly in mathematics and sciences, and can reduce certain human biases. However, challenges persist regarding algorithmic bias, data privacy, transparency, infrastructure limitations—especially in African contexts such as Zambia—and the evaluation of complex subjective constructs like creativity and critical thinking. Student perceptions are generally positive, though acceptance requires trust and accessibility. The review concludes that effective AI implementation necessitates ethical governance, diverse training data, transparent policies, ongoing validation, and collaborative human-AI approaches to ensure equitable and effective educational outcomes.

On April 20, 2010, the Deepwater Horizon rig—leased by BP from Transocean to drill the Macondo well in the Gulf of Mexico—exploded, killing 11 of the 126 people aboard, injuring 17, and sinking on April 22. The disaster caused the largest marine oil spill in U.S. waters, releasing nearly five million barrels of oil by July 15. The passage details BP’s corporate history of cost-cutting, mergers, and decentralized “asset federation” management that reduced oversight, alongside prior safety failures at its Texas City refinery in 2005 and Prudhoe Bay in 2006. In the days before the blowout, BP made several well-closure decisions that favored speed and cost over safety: using long string casing with fewer gas barriers instead of a safer liner/tieback; deploying only six centralizers despite contractor warnings that 21 were needed to prevent severe gas flow; forgoing a cement bond log to verify cement integrity; circulating drilling mud for only 30 minutes rather than fully circulating it; and failing to install a lockdown sleeve. The rig also had known maintenance issues, and its gas alarms had been disabled. The spill caused extensive environmental and economic damage, triggered a federal deepwater drilling moratorium, cost thousands of jobs, and led BP to establish a $20 billion Gulf Coast Claims Facility. Investigations indicated that BP’s organizational culture and incentive systems consistently prioritized cost reduction and expediency over caution, contributing to the catastrophe.

In his inaugural address, President Roosevelt declares that "the only thing we have to fear is fear itself" while acknowledging the nation's severe material distress, including unemployment, frozen exchange, and lost savings. He attributes the crisis to the failure of financial leaders and calls for replacing the pursuit of monetary profit with nobler social values. He proposes immediate government action to put people to work through direct federal recruitment and needed projects, redistribute overbalanced industrial populations, prevent farm and home foreclosures, reduce government costs, unify relief efforts, and plan national transportation and utilities. He demands strict banking supervision, an end to speculation, and sound currency. While favoring international economic readjustment later, he prioritizes restoring the national economy first, guided by interdependence and the "good neighbor" policy abroad. He warns that if Congress fails to act, he will seek broad executive powers to wage war against the emergency, pledging disciplined leadership in response to the public mandate for direct, vigorous action.
Lewis, Urlacher, and Moss made the Hall of Fame on their first try, while Owens made it on his third, joining Dawkins, Beathard, Kramer, and Brazile in an eight-person class.

This lecture examines limited attention in decision-making. Evidence from psychology, including change blindness, the gorilla test, and dichotic listening experiments, demonstrates that attention is constrained and affected by environment, distractions, poverty, and practice. High-stakes examples, such as EntreMed stock reacting to old news and investors confusing Zoom tickers, show inattention persists even when stakes are high.

To measure inattention, researchers can make information salient. Chetty et al. model perceived value as combining visible and opaque components, with an inattention parameter theta. A grocery store experiment making sales taxes fully salient caused an 8.8% demand drop, implying consumers react only one-quarter as much to sales taxes as to other price changes (theta ≈ 0.75). Non-experimental data on beer confirm near-complete inattention to non-transparent sales taxes compared to salient excise taxes. This has policy implications: inattention reduces distortions for revenue generation but undermines taxes meant to correct externalities or internalities on "sin goods."

The lecture then addresses why people miss important information. The "learning by noticing" theory argues that without the correct mental model, individuals do not encode relevant data, preventing learning. Examples include doctors missing handwashing's role in childbed fever and seaweed farmers in Indonesia neglecting pod size despite its profitability. An experiment found that inducing farmers to vary pod sizes alone had no effect, but explicitly summarizing the results and providing recommendations significantly changed behavior. This suggests that incorrect theories cause systematic learning failures and can generate large, persistent welfare losses because people never attend to information that would contradict their model.

News reports from January 19, 2001, detail the California power crisis, in which PG&E and Southern California Edison accumulated over $11.5 billion in debt and faced bankruptcy after a 1996 law capped retail rates while wholesale power and natural gas prices soared. The utilities defaulted on commercial paper and bond payments, prompting state lawmakers to approve $400 million for emergency power purchases and Governor Gray Davis to declare a state of emergency. Outgoing Energy Secretary Bill Richardson ordered suppliers to continue selling electricity and natural gas to California. President-elect George W. Bush’s adviser Ken Lay, head of Enron, opposed caps on wholesale power prices, calling the crisis largely self-inflicted. Credit rating agencies downgraded the utilities deep into junk status. Pennsylvania’s Public Utility Commission criticized GPU Energy for comparing its situation to California, noting Pennsylvania is a net power exporter with different market rules. In corporate news, Enron Energy Services signed a ten-year, $2.2 billion energy management agreement with Owens-Illinois covering 53 facilities in 20 states. EOTT Energy Partners, an Enron subsidiary, declared a quarterly distribution of $0.475 per unit. A bandwidth market report noted expanded trading routes and identified Aquila Broadband as the third market maker, while Enron was not the market maker for the new Los Angeles–San Francisco route.

The MACD and RSI strategy combines two momentum indicators to analyze and trade markets. MACD, calculated using 12-period and 26-period EMAs with a 9-period signal line, primarily identifies trends. RSI, developed by J. Welles Wilder, measures price movement speed on a 0–100 scale, with readings above 70 indicating overbought conditions and below 30 indicating oversold conditions. Traders combine them in various ways, such as using MACD for trend direction while RSI identifies price swings or mean reversion, or using one indicator to confirm the other. A backtest incorporating both indicators with a mean reversion filter for semiconductor stocks produced 235 trades, a 73% win rate, and an average gain of 0.88% per trade. While some analysts argue combining two momentum indicators creates redundancy, others believe it offers additional confirmation. The passage states neither indicator is definitively more accurate, as performance depends on parameters and markets, and stresses the importance of establishing clear trading rules and backtesting.

The U.S. Department disapproves of Mr. Allen’s request that the Shanghai consul-general surrender Kim Ok-kiun’s murderer to Korean justice, as his jurisdiction covered only U.S. citizens. Mr. Sill reports rebel forces defeated government troops, captured Chon-ju, and may threaten Seoul; Admiral Skerrett cannot send ships to Chemulpo due to Bering Sea duties, though other nations have, and Sill warns Americans may need protection. Japan and other nations are reviving TPP without the U.S., though many doubt its effectiveness without Washington. The Flexbone Offense is a run-heavy system evolved from the Wishbone, featuring option plays and misdirection with A-backs positioned closer to the line of scrimmage. It requires a decisive, running quarterback; a powerful, athletic fullback; quick, versatile slotbacks; blocking wide receivers; and an athletic, smart offensive line. Its strengths include defensive unfamiliarity, ball control, multiple running threats that create assignment confusion, and physical wear on opponents. Weaknesses include a limited passing game, difficulty in comeback or two-minute situations, extensive practice demands, and struggles in bad weather. Common formations include Double Slot, Trips, and Receivers Over. Key running plays are the Triple Option, Midline Option, and Rocket Toss, while common pass plays include Play Action Wheel Route, Toss Boot, and Four Verticals. Traditionally used by service academies and notably by Paul Johnson at Georgia Tech, the offense remains prevalent at lower college levels and in high school football.

Jeff Carter describes scoring his first playoff overtime goal, giving his team a two-game lead, as a lucky shot on net with a teammate screening the goalie, while citing familiarity with the opponent's tendencies. Drew Doughty emphasizes resetting for home games as a new series, anticipating a desperate opponent, and describes his own screened goal. Doughty also notes increasing crowd noise and the need for his team to improve.

As Protestant churches in Germany face declining attendance while celebrating 500 years since the Reformation, some clergy are using social media to engage worshippers. At the Walloon Reformed Church of St. Augustine in Magdeburg, Pastor Ralf Peter Reimann holds a "Twitter service" where parishioners tweet about the liturgy and share prayers online, with messages displayed on a screen in real time. Reimann and scholars note this parallels Martin Luther's use of the printing press, whose pamphlets spread ideas and fostered public debate similarly. While some participants embrace the digital format, others find it hectic or prefer traditional services with hymn singing.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU introduces Ampere architecture innovations including third-generation Tensor Cores that accelerate TF32, FP16, BF16, and FP64 operations, delivering up to 16x mixed-precision performance over standard FP32 and up to 2.5x the FP64 throughput of V100. For deep learning, TF32 provides up to 8x throughput over FP32 on A100, while FP16/BF16 mixed precision offers up to 16x. Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity using a 2:4 pattern doubles inferencing math throughput and reduces data footprint and bandwidth by 2x with virtually no accuracy loss. The memory hierarchy features 40 GB HBM2 with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache with 2.3x the read bandwidth of V100, and 192 KB/SM of combined L1 data cache and shared memory. Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) can partition a single A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute and memory paths for quality of service and fault isolation. Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/sec total bandwidth, double that of V100, while PCIe Gen 4 and SR-IOV improve host and virtualization connectivity. CUDA 11 advances include asynchronous global-to-shared memory copies, task graph optimizations, asynchronous barriers, and L2 cache residency controls. Additional hardware features include five NVDEC units, a 5-core NVJPG decoder, an optical flow accelerator, and improved FP16 and FP32 atomic throughput. The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs to deliver 5 PFLOPS of AI performance.

The Larry Swedroe Portfolio allocates 30% to stocks and 70% to bonds, typically including 15% small-cap value, 7.5% international small-cap value, 7.5% emerging markets, and 70% intermediate bonds. Based on evidence-based investing and modern portfolio theory, the strategy emphasizes diversification across asset classes and geographies using low-cost, passively managed index funds or ETFs. Swedroe advocates a bottom-up value investing approach, targeting small-cap companies with strong fundamentals that are believed to be undervalued, while avoiding market timing and maintaining a long-term perspective. Rebalancing occurs at least annually or when asset classes deviate from target allocations by a set percentage. A backtest from 2012 showed a 3.71% annual return, and the passage notes the bond-heavy portfolio is expected to trail stock returns over the long term; the strategies are designed for long-term gains and may not suit all investors or those seeking short-term returns.

Berkshire Hathaway repurchased approximately $1.3 billion in stock in 2012 after raising its buyback limit to 120% of book value, but made no repurchases from 2013–2016 despite nearing that threshold. The author argues the 120% limit should be increased because Berkshire's intrinsic value has increasingly diverged from its book value, making the threshold more conservative now than in 2012. The author notes Warren Buffett has previously regretted being too conservative on repurchases, and suggests buybacks be considered if the price-to-book value enters the low-mid 120% range.

This paper examines how an Australian university developed an Arts Specialism to address gaps in primary pre-service teachers' arts education competencies. Framed by Stephen J. Ball's policy sociology theory and utilising critical discourse analysis, the study analyses three policy contexts. The context of influence identifies how neoliberal reforms and reduced curriculum time have marginalised arts education, leaving generalist teachers underprepared despite extensive policy advocacy. The context of policy text production details the collaborative development of a four-course Arts Specialism covering dance, drama, media arts, music, and visual arts, shaped by government requirements and stakeholder input from organisations including NAAE, ACDE, and AITSL. The context of policy practice describes implementation through four 12-week courses incorporating experiential learning, school-based projects, and arts industry partnerships, including adaptation to online delivery during COVID-19. Findings indicate the initiative develops pre-service teachers' expert content knowledge, pedagogical skills, and confidence, supported by positive participant feedback. The discussion notes ongoing challenges regarding time allocation, resources, and staffing, while highlighting benefits for culturally responsive teaching and community engagement. The conclusion presents the Arts Specialism as an AITSL-approved model for primary teacher education, though time constraints and policy pressures remain significant barriers. Future research opportunities include longitudinal studies tracking graduates and nationwide school-based arts curriculum implementation.

Tales of children raised by wild animals have circulated for centuries, though many are hoaxes. Sir Kenelm Digby recorded the case of Jean de Liège in 1644: a Belgian boy who lived in the woods for about sixteen years, reportedly developed acute senses and excessive hair, and lost speech before later learning to talk. In 1672, Nicholas Tulp described an Irish youth raised by sheep who bleated and ate grass. A 19th-century Texas legend tells of a “Wolf Girl” seen with wolves in 1845, captured and escaped, then sighted again in 1852 before disappearing. The passage concludes by questioning whether such feral individuals might still exist.

The District Court of Appeal of Florida, Second District, reversed a final summary judgment favoring The Personal Service Insurance Company and George Johnson, Jr. in Danny Langston’s action. Langston was injured in Florida as a passenger in a vehicle owned by George Johnson, Jr. and operated by Fred Johnson. The trial court ruled that an Ohio surety bond issued by Personal Service to Johnson covered only Johnson’s personal acts, not the operator’s negligence. The appellate court held that Florida tort law makes a vehicle owner liable for a permitted operator’s negligence. Applying Ohio law to the bond, the court found the surety could be liable for a judgment against Johnson for damages from vehicle ownership, distinguishing contrary Ohio precedent because the accident occurred in Florida. The case was reversed and remanded.

The specification states that hypervisors injecting NMIs must intercept #DB and rely on a guest "NMI Complete" message. Full hardware debug register virtualization is enabled via a VMSA bit; otherwise, DR7 reads and writes are intercepted and cached by the #VC handler. SMM and nested virtualization under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP are unsupported. For SNP guests using RestrictInjection, host notifications are delivered through a shared #HV doorbell page with PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields to emulate APIC behavior, defining host and guest responsibilities for interrupt presentation, acknowledgment, and EOI. Doorbell page setup uses VMGEXIT 0x8000_0014. Guests must validate vectors and service non-maskable events regardless of EFLAGS.IF.

Android-based smartphones such as the Samsung Galaxy S7 and Google Pixel are more innovative and powerful than the iPhone 7, but Apple's closed platform provides superior security and privacy. iOS 10.3.1 features data encryption via password, PIN, or thumbprint; prompts for two-factor authentication; automatic data erasure after ten failed login attempts; and iCloud backups. iOS devices have built-in anti-malware layers, Find My Phone for remote location, locking, and erasing, and stricter app permission controls than Android. In 2015, iOS had 375 publicly disclosed vulnerabilities versus Android's 130, but Apple devices receive periodic updates, while Android's fragmentation across custom hardware and software makes patching difficult.

Last shot situations require preparation and poise, as a single shot can determine a game's outcome. Teams should keep plays simple, get the ball to their best player—who should never inbound—and have non-shooters crash the offensive boards, since most last-second victories come from putbacks. Holding for the final shot can create a scoring swing of up to 12 points when combined with the first possession of the next period. Coaches should automatically hold for the last shot with under 30 seconds remaining when leading or trailing by less than eight points, initiating the play at eight seconds and shooting with three to five seconds left. Essential skills include long skip and baseball passes, half-court shots, and tipping the ball. Strategies include saving at least two timeouts, using them based on remaining time, inbounding to half-court with under four seconds, and executing counter breaks. Situational guidelines address specific inbound locations, opponent scores, free throws, and jump balls, with fewer dribbles allowed as less time remains.

The passage specifies SD Memory Card Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00 requirements for block-oriented data transfers, error handling, write protection, command functions, and bus protocol. For block writes, the host appends 1 or 4 bit CRC to each data block; the card performs CRC parity checks before writing and rejects commands with BLOCK_LEN_ERROR or ADDRESS_ERROR. Cards supporting block write require a 512-byte block length set by CMD16. Multiple block writes use CMD24–27, 42, and 56(w), and pre-erasing blocks via ACMD23 accelerates subsequent write operations. The card indicates busy by holding DAT0 low, and the host may deselect it with CMD7 without interrupting the write. Erase operations use CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38; DISCARD (CMD38 argument 00000001h) and Full User Area Logical Erase or FULE (CMD38 argument 00000002h) are supported only on SDHC and SDXC cards and not through the SPI interface. Write protection methods include a mechanical switch, optional internal protection, and password locking via CMD42. Card Ownership Protection (COP) introduces a Force Erase Password (FEP) and a COP Unlock command (CMD42[1Fh]), with distinct behaviors for COP and Non-COP cards regarding password reset and force erase. The Switch Function command (CMD6) configures access mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit. CMD8 initializes cards compliant with Version 2.00 or later. SDHC and SDXC cards use block addressing with a fixed 512-byte block length, while SDSC cards use byte addressing. The specification defines CRC7 for commands and responses and CRC16 for data blocks, a 48-bit command format, Card Command Classes (CCC), and timeout conditions of 100 ms for reads and 250 ms for writes (up to 500 ms for SDXC under specific conditions). The host may change bus frequency but must provide eight clock cycles after the last bus transaction before shutting down the clock.

October 2025 skywatching highlights include a supermoon on October 6, when the full moon at perigee appears about 30 percent brighter and up to 14 percent larger. A correction to a typo in homework 1 was posted on Stellar, clarifying an easier intended problem. The lecture continues linear algebra, covering eigenvalue decomposition today and singular value decomposition next time. The instructor reviews reordering systems of equations using permutation matrices, which are unitary matrices that swap rows or columns and act as a form of preconditioning. A Plinko game analogy illustrates diffusion via a sparse matrix. Eigenvectors are defined as vectors stretched but not reoriented by matrix multiplication, with eigenvalues as the stretch factors found by solving det(A − λI) = 0. Algebraic and geometric multiplicity are discussed. A matrix with a complete set of eigenvectors can be diagonalized through eigendecomposition (A = WΛW⁻¹), simplifying the solution of linear systems and decoupling systems of ordinary differential equations. For symmetric matrices, normalized eigenvectors are orthogonal and W⁻¹ equals Wᵀ. When a complete set is unavailable, alternatives like Jordan normal form or Schur decomposition exist.

Taylor Swift has broken numerous records throughout her career. At 17, she became the youngest artist to write and perform a No. 1 song on the Hot Country Songs chart. In 2009, she became the youngest CMA Entertainer of the Year winner, and in 2010, the youngest Grammy album of the year winner for "Fearless." She later became the first woman to win album of the year twice, three times, and four times, surpassing artists like Stevie Wonder and Frank Sinatra. She holds the most American Music Awards (40), most No. 1 hits on Billboard's US Digital Song Sales chart (29), and most Grammy song of the year nominations. Her Eras Tour is the highest-grossing ever at $2 billion, and she is the richest female musician with a $1.6 billion net worth. She also set Spotify records for most-streamed album in a single day with "The Life of a Showgirl," most-streamed song in a day with "The Fate of Ophelia," and most-streamed artist in a single day.

The exponential moving average (EMA) is a technical indicator that places greater weight on recent price data than the simple moving average, making it more responsive to current prices. It is calculated as EMA = (K × (C − P)) + P, where C is the current price, P is the previous period’s EMA, and K is the smoothing constant 2/(n + 1). Backtests on the SPDR S&P 500 Trust ETF (SPY) show that EMA strategies work best with either a low or high number of days: short-term EMAs, such as a 5-day period, are effective for mean-reversion strategies, while long-term EMAs, such as a 200-day period, are better for trend-following. Strategies exiting after fixed holding periods also showed the best result when buying below a 50-day EMA and selling after 200 days, yielding 10.17% per trade. Although the EMA helps smooth price data and identify trends, support, and resistance, it still lags and can generate false signals; thus, it is most effective when used alongside other indicators rather than as a standalone system.

A systematic literature review of leading Information Systems journals from 2000 to 2017 using search terms including "Digital business strategy," "Digital transformation," and "Business digitalization" initially identified 292 articles, which were refined to 28 relevant papers. Following Wolifswinkel’s guidelines, the authors applied open, axial, and selective coding to identify underlying dimensions. Publication activity increased from 2009, with research concentrated in the automotive, banking, telecommunications, healthcare, oil and gas, and manufacturing sectors, primarily in the US and Europe. The review identified twelve dimensions of digital transformation, six of digital business strategy, and ten of organizational capabilities. Digital transformation dimensions include use of technology, value creation, structural changes, financial aspects, digital leadership, agile and scalable digital operations, digitally enabled customer experience, digital artefacts, executing business strategy digitally, external collaboration of ecosystem of digital platform, enterprise platform integration, and flexible and humanized workplace. Digital business strategy dimensions include external collaboration, IT infrastructure, cross-functional integration, organizational structural changes, use of technology, and new dynamic capabilities. Organizational capabilities dimensions include digital leadership, agile and scalable operations, digitally enabled customer experience, digital artefacts, flexible and scalable digital platforms, internal and managerial capabilities, external collaboration, dynamic capabilities, plug and play capabilities, and operational capabilities. The study proposes that digital transformation is digital business strategy in action, requiring organizational capabilities for deployment. External collaboration of ecosystem of digital platform is common to all three concepts; use of technology and structural changes are shared by digital transformation and digital business strategy; digital leadership, agile and scalable operations, digitally enabled customer service unit, and digital artefacts are shared by digital transformation and organizational capabilities; and dynamic capabilities are shared by digital business strategy and organizational capabilities. The resulting conceptual framework aims to guide organizational leaders and researchers in understanding these inter-relationships for successful electronic commerce.

April the giraffe's livestream is YouTube's second-most-watched live channel, behind Riot Games' League of Legends. Her calf's birth drew over 232 million views and 1.2 million simultaneous viewers, making it the fifth-fastest to 200 million views.

This paper addresses the multi-period resource allocation problem under stochastic demands, extending the classic newsvendor model. The authors first formulate a static problem where all allocations are determined at the initial time; this yields a convex optimization problem solvable efficiently via bisection on a dual variable, but it relies only on marginal distributions and ignores temporal correlations and sequentially realized information. To overcome these limitations, they propose a sequential, adaptive shrinking horizon policy similar to model predictive control. At each time step, the policy re-solves the allocation problem for the remaining horizon using the joint distribution of future demands conditioned on observed history. The primary contribution is the formulation and empirical evaluation of this closed-loop heuristic, which is designed to systematically improve upon the static open-loop solution. The authors evaluate both approaches on synthetic data with jointly log-normal demands. Results demonstrate that the sequential policy achieves higher revenue than the static solution when demands are correlated, performing close to a prescient oracle upper bound, while reducing to the static solution when demands are independent. The method requires only conditional quantile functions and scales well with the problem horizon.

Research across over 150 firms indicates that tech intensity correlates with business performance, with digital leaders outperforming laggards in revenue and enterprise value growth. While technology is critical, cultural changes are often the most difficult aspect of digital transformation. The research identifies four cultural themes of digitally mature organizations: a growth mindset toward risk and continuous learning; using data to create shared context and transparency; empowering teams to examine data and measure performance against realistic goals; and aligning the organization through common targets while allowing autonomy. Digital leaders encourage experimentation, long-term development, and data transparency, making data widely available to inform decisions and track progress. They align goals vertically and horizontally using transparent, data-driven objectives. Conversely, digital laggards prioritize short-term efforts, restrict data access, favor business judgment over data, set aspirational goals not grounded in data, and struggle to connect priorities to strategy. Organizations typically begin in one of four patterns—data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, or data reliant—based on their culture and technical capabilities. Establishing beliefs around learning, risk-taking, transparency, and measurement is essential for successful digital transformation.

The article examines impacts of anti-Critical Race Theory (CRT) legislation on Native content instruction in teacher education at predominantly white institutions in Arizona, Idaho, and Utah. Drawing from ethnographic stories, interviews, and observations, the authors apply Tribal Critical Race Theory to argue that CRT bans perpetuate colonial unknowing by silencing Native perspectives, invisibilizing Native peoples in public education, and fostering refusal to adopt culturally sustaining pedagogies. The authors profile anti-CRT legislation in the three states, including Idaho’s HB 377, Utah’s S.R. 901/H.R. 901, and Arizona’s HB 2898, noting that such measures produce a chilling effect on educators. They observe that the teacher workforce in these states is overwhelmingly white and that teachers rarely enter classrooms with knowledge of Native peoples or access to professional development in Native-centered instruction. Counterstories illustrate how administrators cite anti-CRT laws to halt tribal history training, how state mandates for Native history are disregarded, how school curricula emphasize extinct rather than contemporary Native societies, and how pre-service teachers resist multicultural and social justice content. The authors conclude that critical democratic education requires recognizing Native nationhood and sovereignty.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that on September 4, 2020, it completed the sale of $5.0 billion of common stock, before commissions, through an at-the-market offering program disclosed on September 1, 2020. Final settlement is expected by September 9, 2020.

This study analyzes spatiotemporal trends in U.S. face mask–wearing from September 2020 to May 2021 using the COVID-19 Trends and Impact Survey (CTIS). To address small county-level sample sizes, unrepresentative samples, and response biases, the authors used Bayesian binomial regression models, raking and resampling on age, sex, and education, and a debiasing approach that compared self-reported vaccination rates to ground-truth county vaccination data, applying the estimated bias to masking responses.

Bias-corrected estimates reveal substantial spatial heterogeneity in masking across counties, with consistently higher proportions in urban than in rural areas. Temporally, masking peaked in January 2021 and declined sharply by May 2021, coinciding with increased vaccinations, declining infections, and changes in CDC guidance. The study also finds that community-reported masking levels—respondents’ estimates of mask use by others—closely approximate bias-corrected self-reported estimates, suggesting this question format may reduce certain survey biases. The authors conclude that fine-scale behavioral data are needed to inform geographically targeted public health policies rather than one-size-fits-all national approaches, and they advocate for additional observational studies to validate behavioral surveillance.

Lyla Carreyn, 5, was discharged Saturday after a kidney transplant from teacher Beth Battista. She had complications including a difficult infection. Foreign Relations editors access retired State Department records and restricted documents at the Reagan Presidential Library and other agencies. Department files from 1981–1989 will transfer to the National Archives after declassification. Research utilized the Remote Archives Capture project, which scanned many records though attachment status was sometimes ambiguous. Documents are presented chronologically by Washington, DC time, with original spelling, punctuation, and formatting retained; corrections, additions, omitted unrelated or still-classified text, and original bracketed material are indicated through bracketed insertions, footnotes, and source notes.

The lecture applies optimal control tools to walking robots, identifying control as the fundamental challenge rather than actuator technology. Walking robots differ dynamically from systems like the Acrobot and CartPole in two key ways: they require analysis of limit cycles (periodic motions) rather than fixed trajectories, and they involve impacts, creating hybrid dynamics that mix discrete and continuous time.

The speaker introduces limit cycle stability using the Van der Pol oscillator, explaining that while trajectories asymptotically converge to a periodic orbit, they do not synchronize in time, which complicates standard stability definitions. To address this, the Poincaré map technique is presented: by defining a surface of section and examining the discrete-time map of successive crossings, the stability of a limit cycle can be analyzed as the stability of a fixed point. Local stability requires the eigenvalues of the linearized map to have magnitude less than one.

The lecture then reviews historical and conceptual models of walking. Eadweard Muybridge’s sequential photography pioneered the study of animal gaits. Thomas McMahon’s ballistic walker proposed that walking involves a stiff stance leg with a largely passive swing phase. Tad McGeer demonstrated passive dynamic walking with unpowered machines that walked down slopes using only gravity and inertia.

The rimless wheel—a simple pendulum with massless legs on a slope—serves as a core model. Assuming inelastic, impulsive collisions and instantaneous transfer of support, the wheel loses energy at each impact while gaining energy from gravity. This balance produces a stable limit cycle at a constant rolling speed. The Poincaré map for this system can be derived analytically, revealing stable fixed points for both rolling and standing behaviors, as well as basins of attraction.

Building on the rimless wheel, the compass gait model adds a pin joint at the hip and swing leg mass, while the kneed walker introduces knee joints and additional collisions. Both models retain the same fundamental dynamics: a passive stance phase, energy loss dominated by ground impact, and stable limit cycles. The speaker concludes by noting that these simplified models capture the essential dynamics of walking and that future lectures will address applying optimization and control methods to these hybrid systems.
