This article presents research from D’harawal Country in south-west Sydney exploring what education grounded in Indigenous knowledges could look like. Author Michelle Bishop, a Gamilaroi woman, examines Indigenous community members’ visions for education sovereignty outside colonial schooling, which literature and participants identify as a site of ongoing harm, assimilation, and marginalisation for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students. The research involved 35 anonymous online survey respondents and face-to-face yarns with over 15 people from a range of ages, roles and education backgrounds. Applying Indigenous, decolonising, and relational theories, the study uses “envisioning” and “Indigenous futurities” as methodological approaches to imagine future possibilities beyond school reform, and “layering the vision” to collectively represent community perspectives. To protect participant anonymity, exact figures are withheld and findings are re-presented through a story titled “Our Education, Our Way” rather than conventional academic formats. The story depicts community members discussing how mainstream schooling often marginalises Indigenous students, undervalues their culture and knowledges—including astronomy, medicine, and environmental preservation—and prioritises colonial metrics over identity. Participants envision an Aboriginal-controlled education system centered on Country as teacher, intergenerational storytelling, cultural strength, and community relationships, where students develop contemporary skills while grounded in identity and belonging.

Meb Faber's trend-following strategy for the S&P 500 uses the 200-day moving average: go long when the price crosses above and sell when it crosses below. This simple, price-only system ignores external factors like news and earnings. Paul Tudor Jones also advocates using the 200-day average defensively to avoid major drawdowns. Backtesting from 1960 to the present shows the strategy avoided significant downturns, including the 2008–09 financial crisis and the 2020 COVID-19 crash. A monthly version using a ten-month moving average turned $100,000 into $4.7 million with a 6.3% CAGR, slightly below buy-and-hold's 7%, but with reduced drawdowns. The 200-day moving average is an effective, simple tool for risk management.

The passage details the AGESA software architecture for UEFI host environments. Using the binary image build model, AGESA core call-outs are funneled through a single host-implemented router. The UEFI implementation covers SEC, PEI, DXE, and RTP execution stages across 16-bit, 32-bit, and 64-bit modes, built with specified Microsoft assembler and C/C++ compiler versions. AGESA initialization is divided into time-ordered entry procedures including AmdInitReset, AmdInitEarly, AmdInitPost, AmdInitEnv, AmdInitMid, AmdInitLate, and AmdInitRtb, which perform processor initialization, memory initialization, PCI and graphics configuration, and generation of ACPI, DMI, and other data tables. For S3 suspend and resume, procedures such as AmdInitRtb, AmdInitResume, AmdS3LateRestore, and AmdS3FinalRestore save and restore processor context. The host environment must provide required call-outs including AgesaAllocateBuffer, AgesaDeallocateBuffer, and AgesaReset, and must use provided macros to establish and disable the pre-memory stack in Cache-As-RAM. Build configuration is managed through platform-specific options files and environment variables.

The authors argue that English as a Second Language (ESL), World Languages (WL), and Bilingual Education (BE) developed as historically separate U.S. language education domains with distinct sociopolitical contexts, ideologies, and pedagogies that often reflect English hegemony and inequitable treatment of minoritized emergent bilingual learners. Using Valdés’s framework of language curricularization, they analyze theories, policies, and program elements across these fields and describe their own curricular bridging—termed border-crossing—in language teacher education at a Chicago institution. Phase one redesigned an ESL methods course to center translanguaging and equity-oriented pedagogy for diverse candidates, including WL teachers. Phase two developed a combined ESL and WL Methods course focused on Chinese to prepare teachers for multilingual learners across program models. A planned third phase will redesign a BE methods course to serve WL and BE candidates in dual language contexts through critical consciousness, decolonizing methodologies, and critical curricular analysis. The authors advocate for cross-disciplinary collaboration within a heteroglossic, language equity lens to train critically conscious educators who can respond to learners’ diverse linguistic profiles.

Congress should make a special appropriation for antitrust enforcement under the Attorney-General. Necessary readjustments should protect wage-workers' standards and be achieved through reciprocity treaties or direct legislation. A commission of business experts should scientifically examine tariff schedules to recommend deliberate changes that reapply protective principles to shifting conditions without upsetting the country's fixed economic policy or prosperity.

The article compares dollar-cost averaging (DCA) and lump-sum investing. Lump-sum investing typically outperforms DCA; a Morningstar study found DCA beat lump-sum only 27.8% of the time over 10-month periods and 10% over 10-year periods. DCA may still benefit investors prone to behavioral biases by removing timing fears. Backtesting $60,000 in the S&P 500 from January 2000 to December 2019 showed lump-sum investing produced $193,157 with a 6.02% CAGR, while DCA produced $173,949 with a 5.5% CAGR. When the sequence of returns was reversed, the lump-sum CAGR fell slightly to 5.93%, but DCA results dropped sharply to $87,396 with a 1.9% CAGR, illustrating significant sequence of returns risk. The article concludes lump-sum investing is generally the better option and recommends investing spare capital when available. DCA and scale-in strategies are essentially the same, both involving gradual investment over time.

The course focuses on coding for the additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel, covering algebraic block codes, convolutional codes, LDPC codes, lattice codes, and decoding algorithms, all evaluated by how well they approach channel capacity. This term, non-essential topics will be trimmed to reach Chapter 4 faster, allowing more time for modern capacity-approaching codes and possibly band-limited channels; linear Gaussian channels will likely be omitted.

Chapter 1 frames the design problem: maximizing data transmission over a given channel. The AWGN channel is modeled as Y(t) = X(t) + N(t) with average signal power P, noise power spectral density N0, and bandwidth W. The signal-to-noise ratio is SNR = P/(N0W), and the Shannon capacity is C = W log2(1 + SNR) bits per second. Spectral efficiency is ρ = R/W. For example, a telephone line with ~37 dB SNR and 3700 Hz bandwidth has a capacity near 42,000 bps, while uncoded 32-QAM yields about 15,000 bps. Coding introduces constraints over long sequences to increase distance between codewords and reduce error probability, a 50-year effort to realize Shannon’s 1948 theorem.

Chapter 2 reviews converting the continuous-time AWGN channel to an equivalent discrete-time model via orthonormal PAM and a matched-filter receiver, preserving SNR and avoiding intersymbol interference. The nominal bandwidth W corresponds to 2W real symbols per second, and spectral efficiency translates to bits per two dimensions. Problem Set 1 covers decibels, Hadamard matrices, QAM constellations, and spherical shaping.

The passage identifies nine Vanguard ETFs for ultimate diversification: BNDW, BNDX, BND, VTC, VNQI, VNQ, VXUS, VT, and VTI. Vanguard was established by John Bogle, who died in 2019. Weber State University canceled its 27th annual Unity Conference, themed around censorship, after presenters were directed to remove terms including “DEI,” “diversity,” “equity,” and “inclusion” from their materials to comply with Utah’s HB 261. Because the conference was sponsored by the non-academic Student Access and Success division rather than an academic unit, it was subject to the law’s restrictions on “prohibited discriminatory practices” and partisan language; academic events are exempt. Multiple faculty withdrew, prompting the Oct. 1 cancellation. A subsequent alternative faculty and staff event was also required to adhere to HB 261 rules. University officials acknowledged that communication about the sponsorship had been unclear and said they may restructure future conferences under Academic Affairs to exempt them. The incident occurs amid heightened legislative pressure on Utah public universities, including recent budget cuts that targeted programs such as queer studies, and previous faculty scrutiny over speech related to LGBTQ+ topics.

Eilish McCready, 25, from Glasgow, founded Fearless theatre school a year ago to offer inclusive drama classes focused on personal development rather than performances. The classes welcome all children, including shy children and those with additional needs such as autism, aiming to build confidence and social skills without pressure. Classes are kept small and begin with a “Fearless shake” to release nerves. Lizanne Conway, whose three sons have autism, said the classes have helped her older two boys with confidence, social interaction, and communication in a stress-free environment. Lisa Byrne said her shy daughter Rua has gained confidence, sings in front of people, and started a YouTube channel. Classes are held at Studio 93 in Glasgow.

News reports from October 23–24, 2001, detailed Enron Corp.’s financial and regulatory troubles. Enron may need to cover shortfalls in investment vehicles—Marlin Water Trust II, Marlin Water Capital Corp. II, Osprey Trust, and Osprey I, Inc.—that sold $3.3 billion in notes due within 20 months; Treasurer Ben Glisan said asset sales could raise at least $2.2 billion to repay the notes, but a worst-case scenario could require issuing up to $1 billion in new stock. Enron’s share price fell to $19.79, down from over $80 earlier in the year and more than 40% in the past week, after the company reported a $618 million third-quarter loss, $1.01 billion in write-offs, and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity from terminating transactions with partnerships previously run by CFO Andrew S. Fastow. The Securities and Exchange Commission began an informal inquiry into transactions involving Fastow’s partnerships. During a conference call, Chairman and CEO Kenneth Lay defended Fastow, stated the company had adequate liquidity, and refused to answer questions about the partnerships, citing the SEC inquiry and shareholder lawsuits. Analysts challenged the company’s disclosure and transparency. Enron also asked Citigroup to arrange a $750 million loan as a backup to its commercial paper program, and Fastow said the company had $1.85 billion in commercial paper outstanding backed by $3.35 billion in bank credit lines. Other reports noted Enron would receive a $254 million tax refund under a House stimulus bill, a law firm announced a class action investigation into Enron securities for the period January 18, 2000, to October 17, 2001, British Gas sought operating rights to Indian oil fields it was acquiring from Enron, and AES Corp. sought Indian government help with state disputes following Enron’s difficulties.

A study published October 8 found that biased online images and text cause AI models like ChatGPT to generate resumes for female-named candidates that are younger and less experienced than those for males, then rank women as less qualified. Researchers analyzed nearly 1.4 million online images and videos, performed text analysis, and conducted a randomized experiment with over 450 participants, finding that women are consistently depicted as younger than men, particularly in prestigious occupations. Participants who uploaded images of female workers estimated their average age as two years younger than a control group. The bias persists despite U.S. Census data showing male and female employees are roughly the same age. The authors caution that addressing single biases without considering intersecting factors like gender and age is insufficient.

Researchers are repurposing grape pomace, the 14 million tons of annual wine industry waste that harms the environment through pollution and acidity, as a renewable resource for antioxidants, oils, and fibers. Changmou Xu, Ph.D., presented at the ACS National Meeting that pomace contains beneficial compounds like proanthocyanidins, anthocyanins, and ellagic acid. His team is developing technologies to extract these nutrients and remove pesticides for use in dietary supplements, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, and food. They are substituting artificial antioxidants in fatty foods like mayonnaise and ranch dressing with natural phenolic compounds to inhibit lipid oxidation, extend shelf life, and create "clean label" products. The researchers are also investigating pomace polyphenols against foodborne pathogens and their benefits for animal gut health.

Winter offshore fishing targets sailfish, dolphin, wahoo and kingfish at 90' to 160' depths with live bait, kite fishing and wire trace. Inshore, jacks, tarpon and sheepshead will be in the inlet, beaches and ICW; use fish finders and shrimp or clams.

This clinical study of BNT162b2 and BNT162b2SA ran from April 2020 to February 2023 across 153 sites in 6 countries, enrolling healthy participants aged 12 and older without prior COVID-19 infection or vaccination. Phase 1 included 195 participants (ages 19–82), while Phase 2/3 included 46,406 participants (ages 12–91). The study began as observer-blinded and later became open-label; most booster doses were administered open-label.

BNT162b2 demonstrated 95% efficacy in preventing COVID-19 from 7 days after Dose 2 through December 2020 in participants aged 16 and older, regardless of prior infection. Immune response data showed that a BNT162b2 booster produced antibody levels against the original strain comparable to those after Dose 2, while a BNT162b2SA booster produced responses against the Beta variant comparable to Dose 2 against the original strain in both participants with and without prior BNT162b2 exposure.

The vaccines were generally well tolerated. Most adverse events were mild or moderate injection site reactions (pain most common) or systemic events (tiredness and headache most common) that resolved shortly after vaccination. In Phase 1, some participants had temporary lymphocyte decreases 1–3 days after Dose 1 that normalized by 6–8 days. Few participants withdrew due to medical problems. Serious medical problems were rare across all phases and generally not considered related to the vaccine. No Phase 1 participants died; during Phase 2/3, 170 deaths occurred across study groups but were not attributed to BNT162b2. No deaths occurred among participants receiving BNT162b2SA in Phase 3.

NASA's Cassini spacecraft completed the first of five close flybys of Saturn before its mission ends on September 15 with a plunge into the planet's atmosphere, making it the first Saturn atmospheric probe. The August 14 pass occurred at 1,010–1,060 miles altitude, with a possible closer second pass to gather atmospheric, temperature, aurora, and chemical data. The team hopes to determine Saturn's exact day length. After 13 years and 127 Titan flybys, the low-fuel probe will avoid crashing into potentially life-harboring moons by diving into Saturn, with Titan's gravity triggering the final descent on September 11.

Michael Gayed’s SPY and XLU rotating system is a weekly strategy that switches between the S&P 500 and utilities based on past performance, aiming to exploit utilities’ low beta and sensitivity to interest rates. The strategy reportedly compounded at 13.1% annually from 1929 and outperformed buy-and-hold from 1999 until the paper’s March 2014 publication (6.7% versus 4.6%). However, since publication it has significantly lagged the market, returning 5.1% annually compared to SPY’s 10.4%, and it failed to recover from the 2020 COVID crash while the market reached new highs. With maximum drawdowns since 2021 nearly matching the broader market, it is unclear whether the strategy has stopped working or is experiencing temporary post-publication underperformance.

The speaker expresses gratitude for continued prosperity and reports that acts of the last session have been carried into operation. Measures to preserve Indian friendship and frontier peace have been adopted, including a new treaty with the Creeks confirming prior engagements and permitting trading houses and military posts. The United States took possession of posts including Oswego, Niagara, Detroit, Michilimackinac, and Fort Miami under the treaty with Britain. Commissioners to determine the St. Croix River adjourned to meet at Boston in August 1797, while commissioners regarding vessel captures met in London. The U.S. commissioner for the Spanish boundary proceeded to Natchez, and troops were ordered to occupy posts from which Spanish garrisons would withdraw. An agent for American seamen was appointed in the West Indies, but the agent for Great Britain declined. Arrangements with Algiers appear successful, with prisoners liberated, and measures are in operation for treaties with Tunis and Tripoli. He advocates gradually creating a Navy to protect commerce. He observes that Congress has encouraged manufactures and questions whether public establishments for war-essential branches not otherwise obtainable should be excepted from the general rule, while commending public boards for promoting agriculture. He renews recommendations for a National University and Military Academy. He urges legislative revision of officer compensation. He reports trade injuries from French cruisers in the West Indies but wishes to maintain harmony. Revenues are improving, and he supports measures for a speedy extinguishment of the public debt. The application claims priority to and incorporates by reference numerous related U.S. patent applications. The disclosure provides a computer-implemented interactive surgical system in which at least one surgical hub communicates with a cloud-based system, visualization systems, robotic systems, and handheld intelligent surgical instruments. The hub includes a modular enclosure with docking stations for receiving modules such as a combo generator housing ultrasonic, bipolar RF, and monopolar RF components, a smoke evacuation module, and a suction/irrigation module, with communication buses linking the docking ports. A surgical data network connects modular devices in operating theaters to cloud or local computers for data processing and manipulation. The imaging module supports interchangeable camera and light source modules. Methods are disclosed for characterizing an ultrasonic end effector’s state, function, or contacted tissue by measuring transducer impedance, comparing it to a stored reference, classifying and characterizing the measurement, and adjusting the applied power level based on that characterization. The disclosure also describes control circuits, feedback systems, and adaptive algorithms for surgical instruments.

Plasma diagnostics infer properties such as density, temperature, and velocity indirectly through physical effects, as direct measurement of a plasma is impossible. While basic instruments like thermometers rely on intuitive principles such as thermal expansion, plasma diagnostics often depend on less obvious physics—for example, using light polarization to determine magnetic fields. The course assumes prior plasma physics knowledge equivalent to MIT’s 22.611.

Diagnostics are essential for meaningful plasma experiments. Historical examples illustrate their importance: in the 1950s, the UK ZETA pinch misinterpreted neutron bursts as fusion because its diagnostics were insufficient, leading to the development of Thomson scattering. That technique was subsequently used to verify Soviet tokamak temperatures of about one kiloelectron volt, prompting a worldwide shift to tokamak designs. Similarly, the National Ignition Facility initially failed to meet expectations partly because it lacked adequate diagnostics to identify problems; improved diagnostics later contributed to achieving ignition.

Experimenters, computational researchers, and theorists all benefit from understanding diagnostics. Experimenters must grasp measurement uncertainties and limitations. Simulators use diagnostics to validate codes and to reduce synthetic data into experimentally comparable forms. Theorists should maintain skepticism about experimental claims and design testable predictions that align with diagnostic capabilities.

While an ideal measurement would capture the full particle distribution function, practical diagnostics typically provide lower-order moments such as density, average velocity, and magnetic fields. Real measurements face significant limitations: they are often sparse in space or time, line-integrated (especially optical diagnostics), filtered by instrument response functions, and dependent on imperfectly understood physics such as atomic spectroscopy data.

The course focuses on underlying physical principles rather than specific technological implementations, as principles remain constant while hardware evolves. During the lecture, students mapped their research plasmas across wide ranges of temperature, density, and magnetic field, identifying numerous diagnostics used across diverse devices—including tokamaks, the National Ignition Facility, the Z machine, Hall thrusters, and magnetized liner inertial fusion—such as Langmuir probes, Thomson scattering, bolometers, electron cyclotron emission, interferometry, neutron spectrometry, and shadowgraphy.

The Rams seek permission to interview Jaguars interim coach Doug Marrone for their head coaching job. Marrone went 1-1 after replacing Gus Bradley and previously coached the Bills. Jacksonville may also retain him permanently.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2015. Net sales increased 15% year-over-year to $22.7 billion, but the company reported a net loss of $57 million, or $(0.12) per share, compared to net income of $108 million, or $0.23 per share, in the prior year period. This case study examines Tesla’s liquidity pressures in early 2018 amid efforts to ramp up Model 3 production. Following an April Fool’s tweet by CEO Elon Musk joking about bankruptcy, the company faced serious cash burn and investor uncertainty over its ability to raise additional capital. Founded in 2003 and taken public in 2010, Tesla had become the world’s leading high-performance electric vehicle manufacturer, launching the Roadster, Model S, Model X, and the mass-market Model 3, alongside ventures into battery production, solar energy through its 2016 acquisition of SolarCity, and autopilot software. Despite a rising stock price and becoming the most valuable American automaker in 2017, Tesla had never recorded a profit and consistently posted negative operating cash flow. The company funded its growth through repeated equity and debt offerings, nearly doubling shares outstanding and accumulating over $10 billion in long-term debt within eight years of its IPO. After Model 3 production began in July 2017, Tesla struggled to achieve scale and repeatedly pushed back its goal of producing 5,000 cars per week, a target considered critical for becoming cash flow positive. With accelerating cash consumption, a Goldman Sachs analyst predicted Tesla could require over $10 billion in external capital by 2020, though Musk stated the company would not need an equity or debt raise in 2018. The case highlights the uncertainty surrounding Tesla’s ability to secure necessary funding to survive.

NVIDIA’s Turing architecture introduces GDDR6 memory with 14 Gbps signaling and 20% greater power efficiency than Pascal’s GDDR5X, alongside a 6 MB L2 cache and improved compression for roughly 50% higher effective bandwidth. The new display engine supports 8K/60 Hz via DisplayPort 1.4a, HDR tone mapping, and an enhanced NVENC encoder for HEVC 8K encoding. Turing GPUs support VirtualLink over USB-C for single-cable VR and use second-generation NVLink for two-way SLI in TU102 and TU104 models.

The architecture enables real-time ray tracing via dedicated RT Cores that accelerate BVH traversal and ray/triangle testing, delivering about 10x the ray tracing performance of Pascal through a hybrid rendering pipeline. Tensor Cores power NVIDIA NGX features, including DLSS, which matches or exceeds TAA quality with less shading work, effectively doubling performance in some cases, alongside AI InPainting, Slow-Mo, and Super Rez.

New programmable shading capabilities include Mesh Shading (Task and Mesh Shaders) to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks, Variable Rate Shading for per-region shading-rate control, Texture Space Shading for decoupled visibility and appearance sampling, and Multi-View Rendering supporting up to four hardware views per pass. Turing is implemented in TU102 (RTX 2080 Ti), TU104 (RTX 2080, Tesla T4, Quadro RTX 5000), and TU106 (RTX 2070); TU106 lacks NVLink/SLI. NVIDIA introduces RTX-OPS as a workload-based metric quantifying hybrid rendering performance.

This study proposes an ascending-descending method to analyze public transit mode hierarchy based on real passenger travel patterns using smart card data from the Seoul metropolitan area. The method classifies trip segments before and after half the total travel distance as ascending and descending phases, constructs multimodal transfer rate matrices, and computes hierarchy distances and average hierarchical orders rescaled to [0,1], where higher values indicate superior hierarchy. It also accommodates multi-zonal analysis for interzonal and intrazonal trip chains. Using 10,264,700 T-money trip chains from November 12, 2019, across Seoul, Gyeonggi, and Incheon, the case study identifies intrazonal hierarchies within Seoul following the order walking, community bus, urban bus, light rail, and metro, and interzonal hierarchies where intercity bus ranks highest. The results show regional variation: the relative hierarchical positions of metro and intercity bus differ between Seoul and Gyeonggi/Incheon due to differing stop densities, and urban bus holds a relatively lower position in Gyeonggi and Incheon than in Seoul. The paper is currently under review.

In *Jerry Wayne Hill v. Morehouse Parish Police Jury & Titan Indemnity Company* (La. App. 2d Cir. April 7, 1995), the Court of Appeal reviewed a wrongful death action arising from a 1987 accident in which 16-year-old Bradd Rudolph, driving while intoxicated and at excessive speed, failed to stop at a “T” intersection and drove into Bayou Bartholomew, drowning 15-year-old Michael Hill and another back seat passenger. The trial court found the Morehouse Parish Police Jury 20% at fault for failing to maintain adequate warnings at the intersection—specifically a double arrow sign that had been missing for an estimated three months—despite its knowledge of the danger, and allocated 80% fault to Rudolph. The Court of Appeal affirmed the trial court’s factual findings that the police jury breached its duty of care and that the missing sign was a cause-in-fact of the harm, but amended the fault allocation to 35% for the police jury and 65% for Rudolph. The court affirmed the $150,000 general damage award as not an abuse of discretion. A footnote in the opinion noted concern that the survival action for the victim’s pain and suffering had been ignored at trial.

This study assessed the open access (OA) status and self-archiving potential of 1,897 clinical trial results publications from German university medical centers published between 2010 and 2020. Using Unpaywall and Shareyourpaper, the authors found that 54% of publications were openly accessible (23% gold, 7% hybrid, 16% bronze, and 8% green OA), while 46% were closed-access. Of the closed-access publications, 85% had a permission to self-archive the accepted or published version in an institutional repository, typically after a 12-month embargo. However, only 16% of otherwise closed-access publications with self-archiving permission were actually available in a repository. The study highlights the largely unrealized potential of green OA to broaden access to clinical trial results, and demonstrates an automated approach using open tools to generate actionable information on self-archiving at scale. Barriers to self-archiving in Germany include a lack of institutional mandates and unresolved legal disputes regarding secondary publication rights. The approach is being piloted at Charité to improve clinical trial transparency.

Hurricane Harvey damaged up to a dozen critical wildlife habitats along the Texas Gulf Coast. Agencies are assessing damage to nesting sites and marshes. Gary Gensler, a former Goldman Sachs partner and Commodity Futures Trading Commission chair now serving as an MIT Sloan Senior Lecturer and Media Lab advisor, introduces the MIT course 15.S12 on blockchain and money. He surveys students on their cryptocurrency experience and outlines the course structure: blockchain fundamentals, economics, and financial sector use cases such as payments and trading. Drawing on Larry Lessig’s framework of technology, markets, law, and social norms, Gensler explores blockchain’s potential to reduce the “cost of trust” in finance. He reviews the history of internet protocols and cryptography, early digital payment attempts, and Satoshi Nakamoto’s 2008 Bitcoin proposal for peer-to-peer electronic cash. He defines blockchain as a time-stamped, cryptographically secured, append-only ledger maintained by consensus, and discusses its trade-offs regarding verification costs, scalability, privacy, interoperability, and governance. He contrasts permissioned and permissionless systems and addresses public policy challenges including illicit activity, financial stability, and investor protection. Course requirements include class participation, two critical reasoning write-ups, and a team project proposing a blockchain use case in finance.

Digital laggards restrict data access, hoarding it in departmental silos and favoring a “culture of genius” over data-driven decision-making. They often use data to justify pre-made leadership decisions, set aspirational goals poorly grounded in data, and focus on process adherence and qualitative effort rather than quantitative measurement, causing misalignment and stifling innovation. Digital leaders provide transparent data access—88% have standardized APIs versus 27% of laggards—and embrace detailed metrics and continuous measurement to inform objectives and track progress. This focus creates flexibility, autonomy, and a culture of experimentation. Leaders align organizations vertically and horizontally through shared, transparent data-driven goals developed via combined top-down and bottom-up processes, emphasizing data culture as central to operations. Changing ingrained mindsets and behaviors is the most challenging part of transformation. Even leaders exhibit inconsistent cultural attitudes and risk bogging down decisions in exhaustive analysis. Organizations typically begin transformation in one of four patterns—data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, or data reliant—and must evolve core beliefs, values, and daily practices to build a strong data culture.

Interest in psychedelic therapeutics has advanced drug-facilitated psychotherapy. MDMA-assisted therapy received FDA breakthrough designation for PTSD after Phase II trials showed 54% remission. Phase 3 results confirmed safety, efficacy, and significant symptom reduction versus placebo.

A University of Michigan study found that 21% of women and 10% of men in Generation X and late Baby Boomers (ages 50 to early 60s) meet criteria for ultra-processed food addiction, rates significantly higher than the 12% of women and 4% of men aged 65 to 80. Researchers attribute this partly to being the first generation raised in a food environment saturated with ultra-processed products, and to aggressive 1980s marketing of "diet" processed foods to women. Using the modified Yale Food Addiction Scale 2.0 on over 2,000 older adults, the study found addiction correlated with overweight status, poor mental or physical health, and social isolation. Experts warn that because children today consume even higher proportions of ultra-processed foods, future generations may face even greater addiction rates, making early intervention critical.

Qarlinngua, an Inuktitut name meaning "like pants," is a massive sea arch located 80 to 90 kilometres southwest of Arctic Bay, Nunavut, in a pool of salt water on Baffin Island. A photo shared by CBC North from local hunter Max Kalluk sparked internet skepticism, with many believing it was fake, but geologists and local sources confirmed its existence. The formation stands over 50 metres tall and is reachable only by boat during a brief summer window when sea ice breaks up. Geologists identified it as a natural arch formed by wind and water erosion of Paleozoic sedimentary rock, likely sandstone, in an area where the land is sinking relative to the sea. Experts noted such formations are uncommon in the Arctic and estimated it could collapse within decades or thousands of years. Arctic Bay Adventures is currently the only tour operator visiting the site, and Nunavut tourism officials plan to promote the remote attraction to high-income travellers despite limited accessibility and high travel costs.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated September 10, 2019, reporting that Bob Iger resigned from its Board of Directors on that date. The report was signed on September 13, 2019, by Katherine Adams, Senior Vice President, General Counsel and Secretary.

This study examines career transitions of lecturers and education personnel in Indonesian higher education institutions using a grounded theory approach within an interpretive paradigm. It addresses gaps in understanding individual adaptation and impact during transitions, particularly where lecturers assume dual roles as campus leaders while continuing academic duties, and where education personnel face structural changes from bureaucratic reforms such as the trimming of echelons III and IV. Through snowball sampling of key informants across three types of state universities, and using semi-structured interviews analyzed via NVIVO 12 Pro with open, axial, and selective coding, the research built a theoretical framework integrating Schlossberg’s 4 S transition theory (situation, self, support, strategies) with career anchor theory. The analysis identified eight main categories: situation, self, support, strategies, behavior, role, learning, and perception. Findings reveal that adaptation involves reciprocal relationships among the 4 S factors, with new dimensions including new tasks, personal strengths and weaknesses, and organizational support. Career transitions produce significant impacts: behavioral changes (including burnout and time management challenges), dual roles on campus and in family or society, new learning experiences, and altered perceptions of leadership. The study challenges Schein’s Anchor Career Theory by finding that informants utilize two career anchors—competence and managerial—rather than one. Managerial implications suggest that government and institutions should align functional positions with competence and educational background, carefully manage structural-to-functional transitions, and provide organizational support. Limitations include the qualitative design preventing generalization, a narrow focus on intra-institutional transitions, exclusion of demographic characteristics such as race and gender, and potential researcher bias as the researcher is also an education staff member.

Ireland is highly exposed to euro exchange rates against the dollar and sterling. A weak euro has boosted US tourism but deterred UK visitors. The euro has strengthened against both currencies since Brexit, partly due to expected ending of eurozone quantitative easing. Firms importing from the UK benefit from cheap sterling, while exporters to the UK and the car industry suffer. Tourism businesses have limited hedging options, but importing and exporting firms need hedging strategies. The outlook is uncertain due to ECB policy and Brexit.
Appeal from judgment for plaintiff without jury affirmed with costs.

This study presents a bibliometric analysis of mathematics anxiety in mathematics education using 324 Scopus-indexed journal articles published from 2013 to 2023, analyzed with VOSviewer and Biblioshiny. Mathematics anxiety is characterized as tension, worry, or fear that interferes with mathematics performance and is linked to cognitive, psychological, and educational variables including achievement, gender, motivation, self-efficacy, and working memory. Publication volume grew annually, peaking at 56 documents in 2022, with most research appearing in social sciences (35.1%) and psychology (30.7%). Thematic evolution across three periods shows shifting research interests while mathematics anxiety remains dominant. Among 168 publishing journals, Frontiers in Psychology was the most prolific (39 documents). Garcia-Santillan was the most productive author (10 publications), while Pekrun had the highest citations (985) and h-index (77). The United States led in document output (62), Germany received the most citations, and the University of Barcelona was the most relevant affiliation (23 documents). The study is limited to Scopus-indexed English-language open-access articles.

This application discloses a detection model training method, apparatus, and terminal device for medical imaging, such as colorectal polyp detection, to address limited labeled data and domain shift across different hospitals. The method includes determining an initial training model comprising an initial detection model and an adaptive model; obtaining a training sample with labeled source domain images (including identifiers for target object presence and domain) and unlabeled target domain images (including only domain identifiers); detecting target objects in source domain images via the initial detection model; classifying domains for all images via the adaptive model; calculating a loss function value based on detection results, domain classification results, and identifiers; and adjusting model parameters to obtain a final detection model. Using unlabeled target domain data increases training sample size and accuracy. The adaptive model may include a gradient inversion module to create adversarial training, producing domain-invariant features. Embodiments also include a training apparatus with model determining, sample determining, processing, loss function, and adjustment units; a terminal device; and a non-transitory storage medium storing instructions for the method.

Teams must prepare for defensive, even, and offensive jump balls. In defensive situations against superior opponents, teams should rotate early, watch the jumper’s eyes and hands—most right-handed jumpers tip forward to their left and left-handed jumpers to their right—and employ Box, Diamond, “Y,” or other alignments to protect the basket and crash open spots; if a violation is called, nothing is lost. Even jump balls require boxing out, establishing inside position, and executing coordinated clockwise or counter-clockwise rotations off predetermined signals. Offensive jump balls with a 6-inch or greater height advantage utilize set plays such as Ball Possession, Double Tap, Post Split, Jumper Fly, Forward Fly, Spread, Tandem, and Loop, generally tipping forward to the tallest player while maintaining defensive balance and flowing into a set or motion offense if no good shot is available.

The passage compiles news articles from May 24–25, 2001. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Chairman Curtis Hebert Jr. said Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay offered continued support for his chairmanship if he altered his views on electricity deregulation; Lay recalled the conversation differently, stating he told Hebert the final decision was the president’s. Hebert may soon be replaced, with Vice President Dick Cheney indicating Pat Wood could become the new chairman. Lay, a major Republican donor, provided the White House with preferred candidates for the commission and had access to the administration’s energy task force. In India, the Maharashtra State Electricity Board notified Enron’s Dabhol Power Co. that it was canceling their power purchase agreement, alleging misrepresentation and performance failures; Dabhol disputed the move and said it was owed millions in unpaid bills. Bechtel, an EPC contractor and minority stakeholder in Dabhol, threatened to stop work and withdraw by May 31 if unpaid. The Indian government discussed the possibility of National Thermal Power Corporation taking over the project but faced political dilemmas. In California, Attorney General Bill Lockyer made aggressive public statements about Enron’s chairman amid the energy crisis. Other items included El Paso Corp.’s chairman agreeing to testify in a federal gas-price hearing, Portland General Electric reporting record quarterly revenues, and India and Australia signing a protocol to strengthen energy and mining cooperation.

Apple removed several ICE-tracking apps, including ICEBlock, Eyes Up, and DEICER, from its App Store after US Attorney General Pam Bondi claimed such tools endanger ICE officers. The developers are appealing the removals and keeping their apps available via Google Play and websites. Apple justified removing DEICER under guidelines banning defamatory content toward targeted groups, while Google also removed similar apps, considering ICE officers vulnerable. Legal experts say the apps are protected speech under the First Amendment. The Trump administration previously threatened to prosecute ICEBlock’s developer. Researchers warn that centralized platform control, especially Apple’s restrictive ecosystem, creates a single point of failure for free speech.

Alberta Education Minister David Eggen indicated parents may be able to pay school bus fees despite Bill 1 eliminating them for students living 2.4 kilometres or more from school. Rocky View Schools faces a $1 million transportation shortfall due to provincial grants not keeping pace with inflation, a $360,000 carbon levy, and Bill 1. Many parents surveyed expressed willingness to pay previous fees rather than accept alternatives such as longer commutes or reduced busing. The board will contact the Ministry of Education and may push back its April 12 decision deadline.

North Korea warned the US it is ready to hit back with nuclear attacks and displayed new missiles at a parade for Kim Il-sung's 105th birth anniversary. Choe Ryong-hae said they are prepared for all-out war. Kim Jong-un attended. China warned conflict could break out.

The Supreme Court considered whether the double jeopardy clause prohibits separate convictions and sentences under 18 U.S.C. §§ 924(c) and 924(j) for the same conduct. While double jeopardy generally bars simultaneous conviction for greater and lesser-included offenses, such punishment is permitted if Congress clearly intended it. The parties agree Congress authorized cumulative convictions for Section 924(c) and its underlying crime of violence or drug-trafficking offense, but dispute whether it authorized them for Section 924(c) and Section 924(j), which applies when a firearm violation causes death. Justices debated whether Section 924(c)(1)(D)(ii)'s consecutive-sentencing requirement or the statute's "in addition to" language provides clear evidence of congressional intent for cumulative punishment. The government argued Section 924(j) lacks language authorizing cumulative punishments with predicate offenses. One justice questioned the precedent requiring clear congressional intent for cumulative punishment of lesser-included offenses, though the issue was not fully briefed.

Remnants of Tropical Depression 02W lingered in the South China Sea on April 17 after making landfall in the eastern Visayas on April 15 and weakening over the Philippines. NASA's Terra satellite imaged elongated clouds. The Joint Typhoon Warning Center noted westward movement and expected wind shear and drier air to prevent re-intensification.

Jabra Elite 65t earbuds ($170) are among the first devices using Amazon’s mobile accessory kit to integrate Alexa, but the experience is limited compared to smart speakers. Currently Android-only, Alexa on the earbuds cannot make phone calls, send texts or Drop In messages, set reminders, or play music from popular streaming services outside Amazon Music, and it offers no navigation capabilities. The earbuds do deliver excellent sound quality, a comfortable fit, a HearThrough ambient sound feature, and strong voice shopping functionality, but battery life totals 15 hours (less than competitors) and there is no lost-device tracker. While the earbuds also support Google Assistant and Siri, the review concludes that Alexa’s performance when tethered to a smartphone is significantly restricted and not yet comparable to the smart speaker experience, though feature updates are expected.

Schizophrenia spectrum disorder (SSD) affects approximately 1% of the global population, yet diagnosis remains subjective and lacks widely applicable objective biomarkers. Developing resting-state functional connectivity (rs-FC) MRI classifiers is hindered by accuracy problems, limited generalisability, across-session variability, and lack of specificity. This study aimed to develop a clinically viable rs-FC biomarker for SSD and to explore whether diagnostic functional connections (FCs) could also serve as state or staging markers. Using a harmonized discovery dataset (1,015 participants) and an independent validation dataset (683 participants), the researchers built 100 least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) classifiers and voting classifiers. In the discovery dataset, LASSO classifiers achieved 79.6% accuracy and an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.876; in the validation dataset, they achieved 77.3% accuracy and an AUC of 0.824. Voting classifiers significantly improved sensitivity compared with LASSO (P<0.001) and achieved an AUC of 0.841, with no significant difference in specificity. Forty-seven important FCs were identified, and the group difference patterns were reproducible across datasets for 44 of them. Classifier performance varied by site and by disease severity. Voting classifiers reduced performance disparity across severity subgroups and were partly influenced by age, whereas LASSO classifiers were not. Among the important FCs, seven regions of interest were significantly frequent, showing a laterality imbalance between hemispheres except in the cerebellum.

Following the Las Vegas mass shooting at the Route 91 Harvest festival that killed 58 people, country musicians and fans are debating gun control and safety. While Rosanne Cash urged artists to stand up to the NRA, Charlie Daniels called the attack an anomaly and warned against letting fear win. Daniels supports NRA-backed regulations on bump stocks but opposes stricter gun laws, criticizing politicians' lack of gun knowledge and citing Chicago's strict laws as evidence such measures leave people defenseless. Eric Church, who performed at the festival, later honored a slain fan at the Grand Ole Opry. Daniels will headline a show at Cary's Booth Amphitheatre on Oct. 21.

Willis Eschenbach analyzed Mauna Loa Observatory (MLO) minute-by-minute direct solar radiation data since 1980 to assess atmospheric clarity. He found that, contrary to Richard Keen’s claim that the stratosphere is currently as clear as it has been in decades, atmospheric clarity at MLO has remained unchanged since 1980 except following volcanic eruptions. Examining periods after the El Chichon and Pinatubo eruptions, Eschenbach observed that maximum and average solar radiation decreased by approximately 24.5 W/m2 during the two years following each eruption. He noted that despite differences in eruption size and location, the post-eruption solar radiation reductions were nearly identical. His analysis showed that clouds adjusted to reduce the volcanic dimming effect, increasing downwelling solar radiation by about 7 W/m2 compared to what would be expected without such cloud changes. However, a net loss of roughly 25 W/m2 remained. Eschenbach then compared MLO and other Hawaiian temperature records (Hilo, Molokai, Barber’s Point, and Lihue) and found no corresponding temperature decreases during the volcanic periods. He questioned the assumption that reduced solar forcing necessarily lowers temperatures, proposing instead that the climate system responds in ways that tend to restore equilibrium.

Digital leaders use sensible risk-taking and deliberate experimentation to compete amid rapid change. As learning organizations, they rely on data feedback to adapt and value knowledge from experiments. They prioritize long-term individual development through training in critical thinking skills like problem solving, statistics, and design thinking.

The speaker praises Winnipeg's NHL team under Mr. Chipman, citing passionate fans and preferring its atmosphere to sparsely filled arenas like Atlanta, and recalls the old Winnipeg Arena and MTS Centre. They state it took months to distinguish Danny and Hank by face and voice, and that Henrik speaks and jokes more than Daniel. Against goalie Thomas, they emphasize preparation, mixing shots through with back-door plays, taking chances on corners, and acknowledging his ability.

Energy sector trading offers diversification and profits through ETFs such as XLE and VDE or individual energy stocks. The S&P 500 energy sector includes oil, gas, and related services companies. As of July 18, 2022, XLE returned 52.81% over one year versus the S&P 500's -9.28%. The sector is difficult to trade due to macro-driven commodity prices. The article cites two undisclosed XLE strategies with specific performance metrics, developed from over 20 years of experience and potentially offered to subscribers later. The five largest S&P 500 energy stocks are Exxon Mobil, Chevron, ConocoPhillips, EOG Resources, and Schlumberger, though rankings shift with market dynamics. Diversification through energy strategies is described as highly valuable.

The speaker is more concerned about being run from behind into the boards than head hits. After taking a hit in his second shift, he felt comfortable but tired in the third period, blaming cramping on travel and dehydration. He said he cannot change his playing style and aims to contribute rather than be a difference-maker. A Duke doctor and team orthopod reviewed his CT scan and determined his current risk is similar to what it will be in September, three and a half months post-injury. He believes returning home will help his routine. He noted the team has lacked passion and execution, must play harder for a chance to win the Stanley Cup on home ice, and said the shot clock seemed inaccurate. The CT scan was only done after he inquired about replacing injured teammate Doug; the team doctor found he had healed enough to play. His family, who met the doctor on the family charter, was supportive and reassured.

Section 11 provides mechanical, packaging, and orderable information for designated devices, subject to change without notice, along with notes on device status, material type, RoHS values, lead finish, MSL ratings, part markings, and tape dimensions. The document states that TI provides all technical and design resources "as is" and disclaims all warranties. TI's liability is limited to the total annual purchase price of the relevant parts. Users bear sole responsibility for product selection, application design, validation, and compliance. Use is restricted to developing applications with the described TI products and is subject to TI's Terms of Sale.

Canada's big five banks dropped 4.6% to 7.5% from February highs as the financial sector faced a choppy March and down-trending April. The author compares these banks to five small-cap lenders using five criteria: low beta, high earnings yield, high dividend yield, low payout ratio, and consistent dividends. While the big five have not cut dividends in over ten years with yields of 3.4% to 4.4%, three small-cap lenders failed the dividend history test due to past cuts. In a ranking based on these criteria, MCAN Mortgage Corporation placed first, Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce second, and Atrium Mortgage Investment Corporation third. Small-cap financials may offer higher yields and price stability but carry lower liquidity and less diversified business models.

Shohei Ohtani made his first postseason start in Game 1 of the 2025 NLDS between the Dodgers and Phillies on October 4 at Citizens Bank Park, facing Phillies ace Christopher Sanchez. In the 2025 season, Ohtani pitched in 14 games with a 1-1 record, 2.87 ERA, and 62 strikeouts over 47 innings. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts hoped Ohtani would pitch through the sixth and into the seventh inning. In the first inning, Ohtani struck out Trea Turner, Kyle Schwarber flew out, and Bryce Harper hit a groundout to Ohtani. In his first at-bat, Ohtani struck out against Sanchez. The game aired on TBS and truTV and streamed on HBO Max.

The Hawk Offense consists of a wing isolation, high post shuffle cut, and weakside post up, similar to the UCLA Offense. Defenses can employ "Basic NBA Show & Recover" or "All Out SOS Disruption." Show & Recover uses weakside help against wing dribble penetration, forces the shuffle cut wide behind the high post screen with a show and recover, and shows and recovers on down screens. All Out SOS Disruption traps the wing ballhandler, exploiting the offense's vulnerability when the off guard's low cut prevents ball reversal. It utilizes contact switches on the shuffle cut and down screens, followed by rotations into SOS matchups, with "Base Go Red" or "Post Trap" rotations triggered by baseline drives or post passes.

AMD launched the Radeon RX Vega 64 and Vega 56 to compete with Nvidia's GTX 1080 and 1070, respectively. While the Vega 64 is not a GTX 1080 Ti competitor, AMD's support for up to three-way CrossFire paired with Threadripper CPUs offers a niche multi-GPU advantage. The Vega 56 is priced $50 below the GTX 1070 in the US, though UK pricing is less competitive. AMD's advantages include cheaper and more available FreeSync monitors, the recent Enhanced Sync feature, and claimed improvements to minimum frame rates to better support FreeSync.

The safety position in football is a defensive back who serves as the deepest defender and last line of defense against big plays. Traditionally split into the free safety, who roams the middle of the field with more speed, and the strong safety, who plays closer to the line and focuses more on run defense and tackling, the position is also sometimes called "Rover" or "Star." Safeties must cover passes, defend the run, communicate effectively, and be quick and athletic. Notable players include Hall of Famers Troy Polamalu, Ed Reed, Ken Houston, Steve Atwater, Ronnie Lott, Brian Dawkins, Emlen Tunnell, and Larry Wilson, along with Sean Taylor. A great safety creates turnovers, limits the quarterback's options, provides confidence to the defense, and supports cornerbacks deep.

Snap and Francis were convicted and fined for shooting a mare trespassing in an oat field. The court affirmed, holding that wounding trespassing animals violates statute and common law. Owners may use necessary force to expel them but cannot inflict unnecessary injury. Judgment affirmed.

A Nature Geoscience study by Jody Webster and the University of Sydney found Australia's Great Barrier Reef survived five near-extinction events over 30,000 years by migrating as sea levels changed. However, researchers warn current warming and acidification are causing unprecedented coral bleaching, and a 2016 heatwave killed nearly a third of its coral. While the reef may naturally die in thousands of years, human-induced climate change may hasten its demise.

Following the 2024 Arab Summit in Bahrain, five initiatives were launched under King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa, including the "Hope" initiative focused on education for Arab children in conflict zones. Authored by Ministry of Education affiliates Mr. Jaber Mustafa and Mr. Younis Bukhari, the report addresses UNESCO data showing over 10 million Arab children aged 5–15 were out of school as of 2018, using Syria as a primary example. It examines barriers to early childhood education in conflict zones, including school destruction, displacement, resource shortages, and psychological trauma such as PTSD and anxiety. Employing a triangulation methodology of qualitative interviews with a parent and child, a quantitative survey, and a case study of a Syrian child in Alkhabor, the study finds that destroyed infrastructure, unsafe learning environments, and lack of materials severely disrupt learning, though communities adapt through informal groups. The report proposes immediate emotional and academic remedial solutions alongside the sustainable "Hope Initiative" to preserve education during conflicts. It concludes that combining immediate interventions with long-term frameworks is essential to empower children and support post-conflict stability.

Residents of San Andrés Hueyapan, located 18 kilometers from Popocatépetl, face stress from simultaneous volcanic activity and the September 19 earthquake. The indigenous community historically preferred the volcano’s eruptions to earthquakes, but recent increased activity and tremors have caused anxiety. Authorities advised residents to prepare for evacuation. The town suffered severe damage in the earthquake, leaving many homeless. Ashfall from recent eruptions was reported in nearby municipalities.

Sean "Diddy" Combs was sentenced to four years and two months in prison and fined $500,000 for two prostitution-related Mann Act convictions for transporting sex workers and girlfriends across state lines for "freak offs." A Manhattan jury had acquitted him of sex trafficking and racketeering conspiracy. Prosecutors had sought 11 years, while the defense requested 14 months. During the hearing, Combs apologized for his conduct, but Judge Arun Subramanian stated his history of good works could not outweigh his abuse of power over women. Six of his children gave tearful statements. The judge chastised Combs' attorneys for a "bullying" letter to victims and praised the women who testified. Combs still faces dozens of pending civil lawsuits alleging sexual assault and violence, which he denies.

Old paper £10 notes cease to be UK legal tender on 1 March; they can be exchanged for polymer notes at banks, ID may be required. The Jane Austen polymer notes, circulated from September 2017, offer durability, security, and tactile features. A polymer £20 note is due in 2020; no £50 update is planned.

The Second Circuit affirmed Samuel Israel III’s conviction and twenty-year sentence. The court rejected his argument that the district judge should have recused herself, finding no bias or appearance of partiality. It also rejected his claims that the sentence was unreasonable based on bias, medical needs, cooperation credit, or length, deeming them meritless in light of his criminal history and the amount of money involved.

This patent application describes elastomeric compositions comprising dispersed carbon black (CB) particles in silicone matrices and methods for preparing them. The methods involve treating hydrophilic carbon black particles with a silicone-based dispersant that is miscible in a curable, hydrophobic silicone pre-polymer; the dispersant possesses carbon-black-affinic moieties, such as amino, acrylate, or epoxy groups, that associate with the hydrophilic CB surface. The treated particles are mixed into the pre-polymer to form a dispersed composition, which is subsequently cured via addition-curing or condensation-curing to produce the elastomer. The hydrophilic CB is characterized by properties including acidic pH, volatile matter content, oxygen content, negative surface Zeta potential, acid value, and Raman D-band/G-band ratios correlating with oxidation, and may be size-reduced to sub-micron or low-micron dimensions. The dispersant is typically a branched, siloxane-containing molecule where the affinic moieties are positioned on branching units to reduce steric hindrance. The resulting cured compositions contain non-covalently entrapped CB particles and may maintain mechanical integrity even at high particle concentrations. These compositions are suitable for articles such as intermediate transfer members for indirect printing, sealants, and other applications requiring mechanical reinforcement, thermal or electrical conductivity, or radiation absorption.
UC1825BEVM-CVAL RCD clamp starting values use Equation 30 with Kclamp at 1.5, and Equations 31 and 32 with transformer parasitic inductance and allowed voltage change.

The document specifies design requirements for a PGA848 driving an ADS8860 ADC with ±15V supplies, VLVDD = 5.3V, and a 5V reference. Three filters condition the signal: an input EMI/RFI filter, a 318kHz filter (277kHz at high resistor tolerance) formed by a 75pF CFB and 6.67kΩ PGA feedback resistors, and a charge reservoir RC filter at the ADC inputs. The front end maintains –0.1dB flatness to 41kHz. A 2.5V midscale reference for the PGA848 is generated from a 5V REF6250 through a precision divider and buffered by an OPA192 in a dual-feedback configuration with 86° phase margin; stability must be re-verified if modified. Supply voltages exceeding ±20V permanently damage the device. Layout guidelines require symmetrical input paths, 0.1µF ceramic bypass capacitors near supply pins, perpendicular crossing of sensitive and noisy traces, minimized leakage and parasitic capacitance at input pins with keep-out areas below them, and reduced thermal junctions. The document also references TINA-TI and PSpice-for-TI simulation tools, related application notes and data sheets, TI E2E support forums, and ESD precautions.

Russian journalist Arkady Babchenko appeared alive at a Kiev news conference less than 24 hours after police reported him murdered, revealing Ukrainian authorities had staged his death to foil an alleged Kremlin assassination plot. Ukrainian Security Service head Vasyl Gritsak announced the detention of a Ukrainian citizen allegedly paid $40,000 by Russian security services to organize the hit, which was allegedly part of a broader plot to procure weapons and explosives for terror attacks. Babchenko, who fled Russia in 2017 after death threats, apologized to his wife and others unaware of the scheme, stating authorities had known of the contract on his life for two months.

U.S. equities rose Monday, led by the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, as strength in technology and semiconductor shares offset energy weakness despite investor caution over a looming government shutdown that could delay critical economic data and complicate Federal Reserve policy. Markets continued to price in modest rate cuts despite hawkish Fed remarks. The passage also presents Pan Finance as a global financial intelligence publication and lists numerous worldwide economic and financial news headlines.
Primatologist Jane Goodall died at 91; legacy: chimps, skeletons.

At 2:47 AM PDT on July 4, 2018, the National Weather Service in San Diego forecast extreme southwestern California. A High Surf Advisory applies to coastal zones from 6 PM Wednesday through 9 PM Friday, while an Excessive Heat Watch covers inland and desert areas from Friday morning through Saturday evening. Morning low clouds and fog will clear to mostly sunny skies through Thursday, with temperatures rising to peak Friday and Saturday. Coastal highs will be in the 70s to 80s, inland valleys in the 90s to 112, mountains in the 80s to 108, and deserts from 105 to 117. Light winds will become west 15 mph with gusts to 25 mph in some areas each afternoon. Sunday through Tuesday will bring partly cloudy skies, cooler temperatures, and a slight chance of showers and thunderstorms over the mountains.

Americans spent over $100 billion on summer vacations last year. While travel reduces stress and health risks, it can be pricey. Travelers recommend budgeting with tools like Excel and Gasbuddy; using online travel sites for bargains; using credit cards without foreign transaction fees and carrying a second card; avoiding international roaming charges; traveling during offseasons and booking early; signing up for airline newsletters for brief deals; and seeking local discounts at information centers and through city passes.

In Brooks v. Missouri Pacific Railroad Co. (No. 53, decided February 17, 1964), the Supreme Court reversed the Eighth Circuit and remanded. Petitioner Brooks, a railroad apprentice machinist interrupted by military service, sought journeyman seniority at North Little Rock, Arkansas, as of November 3, 1955. The District Court granted the claim, finding his promotion would have been automatic there but for his service; the Court of Appeals reversed, citing unpredictable job availability. Relying on its same-day decision in Tilton v. Missouri Pacific R. Co., the Court held that such possibilities cannot defeat a veteran's seniority rights under the relevant statutes. It accepted the District Court's finding that Brooks would have achieved that North Little Rock seniority date but for his military service.

The ARM Cortex-A8 Subsystem provides master control and configuration of device subsystems, peripherals, and memories. It features an ARMv7 ISA processor with Thumb2, JazelleX, Media Extensions, an interrupt controller, Harvard architecture, a NEON SIMD engine, VFPv3 floating-point coprocessor, separate Level-1 caches, and a 128-bit interconnector. Real-time trace is supported via an Embedded Trace Module connected to a 32KB Embedded Trace Buffer, requiring ETB-enabled debug tools to read captured data.

Miami-Dade Mayor Carlos Gimenez announced a study showing PortMiami is the top money-making operation in county and state, with economic impact exceeding $41 billion. In 2016, the port handled record 5.1 million cruise passengers and 8.9 million tons of cargo, contributed $288 million in taxes, and supports 300,000 jobs. The Miami Herald questioned the study's accuracy, which Gimenez defended. A $247 million Royal Caribbean terminal is expected to generate $500 million annually.

President James Madison, on July 9, 1812, at Congress's request, recommended the third Thursday in August as a day of public humiliation and prayer. He called for Americans to render homage to God, acknowledge transgressions, seek forgiveness and divine protection during the war, and pray for peace.

DAX 40 and Euro Stoxx 50 futures expire quarterly on the third Friday of March, June, September, and December. Backtests show both outperform during expiration weeks versus random weeks: DAX 40 averages 0.39% gains with a 57% win ratio, and Euro Stoxx 50 averages 0.3% with 54%. December is the best month for both; June is a loss for Euro Stoxx 50, and September is the only losing month for DAX 40 expiration week. The week after DAX 40 expiration is backtested using a 100% margin strategy, yielding an average 0.1% loss and a 47% win ratio; December and March are positive, while September is worst. Markets are more volatile during expiration week due to pin risk. DAX 40 is heavily traded, making it attractive to traders.

This case study examines ESPN’s strategic challenges as it transitions from a dominant cable-television business to a direct-to-consumer streaming model. In the early 2010s, ESPN generated substantial revenue from affiliate fees paid by more than 100 million cable subscribers and from advertising across its networks. By 2024, cable and satellite subscribers had fallen to an estimated 70 million, live sports rights costs had risen significantly, and competition from internet-enabled platforms such as Netflix, YouTube, and Amazon had intensified.

Disney and ESPN responded by acquiring streaming technology provider BAMTech in 2017, launching the supplementary direct-to-consumer platform ESPN+ in 2018, confirming that the flagship ESPN network would be available direct-to-consumer in 2025, and forming a joint venture with Warner Bros. Discovery and Fox—each owning one-third—to launch the bundled sports streaming service Venu Sports in fall 2024. The case traces ESPN’s history from its 1979 founding through the development of its dual-revenue B2B model built on affiliate fees and advertising, the acquisition of NFL rights, the creation of additional channels to meet distribution demands, and brand differentiation via campaigns such as “This Is SportsCenter.”

The analysis surveys a competitive landscape that includes incumbent media companies trying to balance linear and streaming assets, technology firms increasingly acquiring live sports rights to support broader business objectives, sports properties weighing reach against revenue, cable and satellite operators shifting focus to broadband, and fans facing fragmented access, rising costs, and a paradox of choice. Disney’s Q2 FY24 results showed ESPN Domestic revenue of $3.866 billion, up 4% year-over-year, but operating income of $780 million, down 9%, while ESPN+ subscribers stood at 24.8 million. The case concludes that ESPN must manage annual rights obligations estimated to exceed $10 billion while transforming from a stable B2B affiliate business into a profitable B2C streaming enterprise.

The passage argues that IEX holds under 3% market share and has failed to disrupt stock trading as promised. It characterizes two IEX identities: IEX One, which uses its speed bump to subsidize buy-side traders within the SEC’s National Market System (NMS), and IEX Two, which seeks broader market unification by serving all traders equally. The author contends that the speed bump is merely another NMS gaming tactic and implicit cost, not a strategic disruption. The passage claims the NMS is flawed, protects exchanges at traders’ expense, and stifles competition based on liquidity and service quality. It asserts that for IEX to dominate, it must bypass the NMS, balance buy-side and sell-side interests, and deliver liquidity rather than exploit regulatory barriers.

In January, U.S. employers added 200,000 jobs while unemployment held steady at 4.1 percent, and average hourly wages rose 2.9 percent from a year prior. Some economists attribute wage growth to a tightening labor market, while others credit minimum wage increases across 18 states. Analysts caution that single-month reports are subject to revision and wide margins of error, advocating for long-term averages. Though President Trump has claimed credit for job growth and declining black unemployment, 2017 job gains were similar to 2016 levels under Obama, and African-American unemployment rose to 7.7 percent in January after a years-long decline that began before Trump's presidency.

University of Virginia staff and Blue Ridge Poison Control Center warn of spring hazards like poisonous plants, mushrooms, spiders, and snakes, caution against self-treating toxins, and recommend clothing, boot checks, and awareness.

IT Central Station produced a 68-page report comparing Oracle Exadata and HPE Vertica. Users praise Exadata's smart scan and Vertica's columnar storage, but criticize Oracle's patching and Vertica's documentation.

This study investigates challenges facing women's education in rural Pakistan and Azad Jammu Kashmir using quantitative surveys of illiterate and literate women, analyzed thematically. While Pakistan's constitution declares education a fundamental right, rural female literacy is only 40.8%, compared to a national female rate of 51.9% and male rate of 73.3%. Thematic analysis identifies shared obstacles including household workload and poor resource management, patriarchal cultural and family barriers, lack of motivation from families and society, poverty, limited secondary schools and inadequate infrastructure, early child marriages, and religious restrictions limiting education. Literate women additionally reported technical and network issues, outdated curricula, family pressure in subject selection, and insufficiently trained teachers. Both groups affirmed education's necessity. The study recommends awareness seminars, media campaigns, legislation for compulsory education, and open and distance learning to address these issues.

After her 20-year marriage ended, the author, who had been a stay-at-home mother and left financial decisions to her husband, realized she knew nothing about their bank accounts, investments, or assets. With help from a friend and her father's financial planner, she gathered documents, created a budget, and located accounts. She also found a steady job through a former colleague, which she has held for seven years. Over time, she learned to manage purchases, home repairs, and retirement planning independently. Now confident in her finances and career, she manages her future on her own terms.

Interior Secretary Ryan Zinke is visiting Maine to review the Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument, which was designated from a private donation of over 87,000 acres and includes a $40 million private endowment. The monument is intended to support tourism and economic growth in rural northern Maine. Governor Paul LePage has advocated for repealing the federal monument designation, while Senators Susan Collins and Angus King and Representative Chellie Pingree have publicly urged that it be retained. Local businesspeople also support the monument for its economic potential. Zinke, who grew up near Glacier National Park, will see the area firsthand during his visit.

The LifeCLEF 2014 Plant Identification Task evaluated automated plant species retrieval using the PlantCLEF dataset, comprising 60,962 images from 19,504 observations of 500 European species across seven view types, collected by 1,608 contributors with contextual and social metadata. The task required multi-image query retrieval, where systems ranked species using sets of images from individual plant observations. Evaluation used an inverse-rank score averaged per author and observation to avoid contributor bias. Ten teams submitted runs employing Fisher Vectors, Convolutional Neural Networks, Bag-of-Visual-Words, and matching approaches. The IBM AU team achieved the highest scores using Fisher Vector and CNN combinations; Fisher Vectors outperformed pure CNNs, which suffered from limited training data because external pre-training was prohibited. Combining multiple images from the same observation improved results but left room for further improvement. LeafScan and Flower categories achieved the best recognition scores. The results indicate progress in plant identification technology but highlight ongoing difficulties in scaling to larger floras.

The passage provides technical reference manual excerpts for a digital media processor, describing memory regions decoded by the Cortex-A8 Subsystem and a 4-GByte TILER extended address range accessible only to the HDVPSS and ISS subsystems. It contains detailed terminal function tables for device pins—including boot configuration, DDR, EMAC, GPIO, GPMC, HDMI, I2C, McASP, PCIe, SD, SPI, UART, USB, video, and power—specifying signal names, multiplexing, pin types, and internal pullup/pulldown states. Boot mode is determined by sampling the BTMODE[15:0] pins at reset to select options such as XIP, NAND, EMAC, PCIe, and UART. Pin multiplexing is controlled by the PINCNTL1–PINCNTL270 registers, and external pullup/pulldown resistors are recommended for boot configuration pins and unused inputs when internal defaults are disabled or do not match the desired logic level.

The Pakistan Super League will hold a February 22 draft to replace international players opting out of the March 5 Lahore final over security concerns. The Pakistan Cricket Board has promised top-level security at Gaddafi Stadium after a recent bombing. Army chief Gen. Qamar Javed Bajwa extended full support. Pakistan has not hosted major test playing countries since 2009.

In soccer, an offensive switch is an exchange of positions between two attacking teammates used to beat defenders. Switches may be “called” using oral communication or “natural” without a call, and may occur with or without the ball. In a basic or lateral (horizontal) switch, players run diagonally across each other toward opposite touchlines, exchanging duties to confuse defenders and create passing opportunities, particularly against an offside trap. In a vertical switch, players exchange positions back-to-front toward opposite end-lines, which is distinct from an overlap. The objective is to free runners by causing defenders to choose whom to cover or creating confusion. Players return to their original positions by communicating “Switch back.”

The writer praises Coronation Street for sensitively portraying Aidan's suicide. They recount their teenage suicide attempt while struggling with their sexuality, and share friend Cheryl Fialka's account of her husband John's suicide 33 years ago. John was 31, died in his Alaskan cruise ship cabin, left no note, and showed no signs of depression. Cheryl describes lasting grief, anger, and unanswered questions. The writer notes her ongoing pain and wonders if awareness of the devastation left behind would affect such decisions.

Competitive Capabilities International (CCi) and R&G Global Consultants partnered to develop Stable Operations TRACC, a data-driven solution leveraging big data to scale stable manufacturing operations. The paper introduces MatterMech, a benchmark comprising 4,800 multiple-choice and text-infilling questions across eight nanomaterial synthesis subdomains, and MatterDB, a dataset of 31,735 curated academic papers, to evaluate Large Language Models' (LLMs) capabilities in physicochemical principle hypothesizing. Developed from approximately 17,000 papers using Claude-3.5-Sonnet, multi-agent roundtable validation, and human review, the benchmark addresses a gap in assessing LLMs' understanding of complex, condition-specific synthesis mechanisms. Evaluation of 14 LLMs revealed that while models demonstrate logical reasoning in multiple-choice questions—led by Qwen-Max at 61.99% average accuracy—they struggle with precise terminology reproduction in text-infilling tasks, where Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct achieved 35.25% similarity. Reasoning-specialized models showed strong multiple-choice performance but weaker text-infilling results compared to general-purpose models. Both increased model scale and principle-guided prompting improved performance, with the latter outperforming automatic Chain-of-Thought prompting in accuracy while reducing output tokens. The study concludes that current LLMs face significant limitations in integrating conceptual understanding with principle-based reasoning for materials synthesis.
