This study investigates difficulties in university foreign language education following the transition from face-to-face to distance education during the COVID-19 pandemic. Using an online survey of 294 undergraduate and graduate students studying German or English, researchers administered a 53-item "distance education problems scale" across six subscales. Findings indicate that students regard distance education as unsuccessful for foreign language teaching. Internet and computer-related problems were rated highest, while teacher-related problems were lowest. Student-related problems, including lack of motivation and low active participation, were rated high. Problems regarding course content/acquirements and measurement/evaluation were rated at middle levels, with insufficient mutual communication and the inability to measure skill-based gains cited as primary concerns. Male students reported significantly higher student-related problems than females, but no significant differences existed between German and English language students. Students without training in distance education programs, without an independent study room, or without a home internet connection experienced significantly more problems across all dimensions. The authors conclude that face-to-face education is more effective for foreign language instruction, citing insufficient materials, problematic assessment, inadequate teacher preparation, and poor student readiness. They recommend awareness and training programs for students and teachers on distance education competencies and suggest implementing a hybrid education model for foreign language teaching.

Quantizing the Dirac theory requires replacing standard commutators with anticommutators to avoid an unbounded Hamiltonian and to obtain fermionic rather than bosonic statistics. The canonical anticommutation relation is imposed on the field and its conjugate momentum. Expanding the field in a complete set of modes introduces operators $a_{k,s}$ and $c_{k,s}$, which satisfy fermionic harmonic oscillator anticommutation relations. The vacuum, annihilated by $a$ and $c$, yields a positive-definite Hamiltonian with a divergent zero-point energy. Because the creation operators square to zero, each mode can be excited only once, enforcing the Pauli exclusion principle. The operators create spin-1/2 particles and antiparticles with two polarizations and momentum $k$. This exemplifies the spin-statistics theorem: half-integer spin fields use anticommutators and obey Fermi-Dirac statistics, while integer spin fields use commutators. The Dirac Lagrangian's U(1) symmetry implies a conserved charge; after normal ordering, particles have charge +1 and antiparticles $-1$, explaining their designation. The theory predicted the positron, discovered in 1932. Fermionic two-point functions (Wightman, retarded, and Feynman) are derived; time ordering includes a minus sign upon exchange. The momentum-space Feynman propagator is the matrix $i/(\not{k}-m+i\epsilon)$. The lecture concludes by noting Dirac spinors can be reduced to chiral or Majorana fermions.

This study investigated interactions between a mitochondrial polygenic score (MGS), lifestyle, and environmental factors on age at onset (AAO) in LRRK2-associated Parkinson’s disease (LRRK2-PD) and idiopathic PD (iPD) using 9,745 patients from three cohorts (AMP-PD, Fox Insight, and Tunisian). A higher standardized MGS was associated with earlier AAO in LRRK2-PD, particularly among European/White patients, but no association was observed in iPD. Regression analyses identified significant interactions between MGS and coffee or caffeinated soda consumption in LRRK2-PD; patients with high MGS who consumed these beverages had substantially earlier median AAO compared to those with low MGS. In iPD, significant interactions were found between MGS and caffeinated soda consumption and between MGS and work-related pesticide exposure, both associated with earlier AAO. Smoking was associated with later AAO in iPD but showed no interaction with MGS in either group. The findings indicate that gene-environment interactions between mitochondrial genetic burden and specific lifestyle or environmental exposures influence AAO in PD.

The authors present MOTO, a multi-objective three-layer optimization framework for systematic local mapping of potential energy landscapes. It combines (i) a multi-objective explorer that proposes diverse, feasible initial guesses; (ii) a bilayer minimum-mode-following kernel, with an inner HVP-based direction optimization and an outer minimum-mode-force ascent to locate index-1 saddles; and (iii) a deterministic bidirectional minimum-mode descent to certify local connectivity. The implementation scales to 10^6 spins, requiring less than 1 GB incremental memory and 0.5 s wall time to compute the two lowest curvature modes. On a 70×70 spin system, the HVP kernel reduces incremental peak memory to roughly 0.01% of an explicit-Hessian approach and delivers a tenfold speedup. Applied to atomistic spin models—including an artificial Bloch-type model and a DFT-parameterized Pd/Fe/Ir(111) system—MOTO recovers established mechanisms and reveals previously unreported saddle families, such as meron–antimeron–mediated duplication of Néel-type skyrmions and chiral droplet formation, identifying up to 32 pathways between a biskyrmion and a bi-antiskyrmion. The same algorithmic core, with only the projector switched to Cartesian updates, maps the local transition-state network of a Ni(111) heptamer, recovering canonical low-barrier rearrangements. The framework thus provides a general, scalable route to automated local transition-state network construction across differentiable potential energy surfaces.

The present disclosure provides systems and methods for periodic beam failure measurements in digital communications. In example embodiments, a User Equipment (UE) determines a measurement period duration based on periods of periodic Beam Failure Detection Reference Signals (BFD RSs) that have a quasi-co-located (QCL) relationship with demodulation reference signals (DMRSs) of Physical Downlink Control Channel (PDCCH) receptions monitored by the UE. The UE monitors a subset of these BFD RSs during each measurement period and, if all monitored BFD RSs fail to meet a specified signal quality or block error rate threshold, reports a beam failure instance to a higher layer entity such as the MAC layer. A beam failure is declared after a specified number of consecutive beam failure instances, which may trigger recovery procedures including candidate beam identification and transmission of a beam failure recovery request. By setting the measurement period based only on BFD RSs the UE assesses for link quality, the embodiments ensure at least one assessed reference signal is present in each period, preventing missed detections and erroneous counter resets that arise when unassessed BFD RSs dictate the period duration. The document further addresses measurement periods where no BFD RS is transmitted—due to overlap with control signals, for example—by ignoring such periods or treating them as beam failure instances to avoid incorrect counter resets. Corresponding UE and base station apparatus and communication system architectures are also described.

The document details the ADS868xW data acquisition devices. A data transfer frame begins when the host controller pulls CONVST/CS low and ends at the subsequent rising edge. During the frame, SCLK clocks data in via SDI into an input shift register and clocks MSBs of the output shift register out via SDO-x. An optimal frame contains 32 SCLK cycles; a short frame has fewer than 32 (invalidating writes but allowing valid partial reads of MSBs), and a long frame has more than 32 (the last 32 bits shifted in form the command). All register configuration commands are 32 bits long and synchronous to SCLK. HWORD commands operate on 16 bits and ignore the LSB of the 9-bit register address. Output data for frame F+1 depends on the command issued in frame F and the DATA_VAL bits, and can contain fixed patterns, 8-bit or 16-bit register data, or the latest 16-bit conversion result with optional appended flags for device address, input range, alarms, and parity. The multiSPI interface supports legacy SPI-compatible protocols (SPI-00-S through SPI-11-S) for configuration and reading, selectable via the SDI_CTL_REG register. Read options include single SDO-x, dual SDO-x (enabled via SDO_CTL_REG), and source-synchronous (SRC) protocols using the RVS pin as an output clock. The device has nine configuration registers, including DEVICE_ID_REG, RST_PWRCTL_REG (unlocked by writing 69h to address 05h), SDI_CTL_REG, SDO_CTL_REG, DATAOUT_CTL_REG, RANGE_SEL_REG, ALARM_REG, ALARM_H_TH_REG, and ALARM_L_TH_REG. The ADS868xW is a 16-bit SAR ADC with an integrated analog front-end and reference for industrial systems such as PLCs, featuring programmable input and AVDD alarms with hysteresis, NAP and power-down modes, and requiring specific decoupling capacitors and careful PCB layout separating analog and digital sections.

James Damore was fired by Google for circulating an internal memo arguing that biological differences make women less suited for tech roles. While debate has focused on diversity programs and the firing itself, the neuroscience behind his claims has been less examined. Recent research shows that women and men are more neurologically similar than different, with traits existing on a spectrum rather than as fixed, innate categories. The brain is “plastic” and changes with experience; spatial cognition gaps can be trained and vary culturally. Environmental factors like “stereotype threat” and perceived status affect brain activity and structure, while empowerment techniques can alter brain function. Thus, the differences Damore cited may stem from environment rather than unchangeable biology, supporting diversity initiatives that address these conditions.

This study investigates EFL pre-service teachers’ and teacher educators’ perceptions of ICT and CALL integration in tertiary initial teacher education (ITE) at a university in southern Vietnam. Grounded in Hong’s (2010) Sphere Model, it employs a convergent mixed-methods design with 67 pre-service teachers and three educators, using surveys, focus groups, and individual interviews. Findings indicate that pre-service teachers perceived a high presence of opportunity to learn CALL-related knowledge, particularly in digital media competences and ICT pedagogies, but less opportunity for troubleshooting, using mobile devices, and setting online work. Educators reported frequent ICT use yet identified barriers including individual educator obstacles such as limited skills, confidence, and fear of change; inadequate infrastructure such as unstable internet, unreliable equipment, and slow technical support; pre-service teacher disengagement; and the absence of official institutional policies for CALL integration. The study concludes that opportunity to learn, educator professional development, infrastructure support, and explicit institutional policies are interdependent and essential for effective ICT/CALL integration in EFL ITE. Limitations include the small sample and single-site context.

The article argues that global citizenship education (GCE) is inadequately equipped to address current international conflicts, such as the war in Ukraine and rising tensions with China, because it lacks perspectives on state security, economic cooperation, and the causes of interstate violence. While GCE traditions emphasize tolerance, human rights, environmentalism, and cosmopolitan engagement through NGOs and supranational structures, they generally neglect national security, foreign policy, and the anarchic, power-driven nature of international relations. The authors contend that GCE must be supplemented with theories of international politics—specifically Realism, Regionalism, and Institutionalism—to help students understand why conflicts arise, how states pursue security and self-interest, and what enables cooperation. Realism highlights anarchy and power competition; Regionalism explains how economic integration can contain conflict but may fail; Institutionalism examines how formal and informal rules and organizations facilitate or limit cooperation. The authors further argue that effective global citizenship requires engaging with one’s own state’s foreign policy—using diplomatic, economic, and military tools—rather than relying solely on abstract transnational activism. They outline conditions for international cooperation based on the characteristics of issues, such as global public goods and coordination problems, noting that state interests primarily drive these processes. Finally, they propose didactical implications for teaching, including broadening the GCE agenda to encompass conflict analysis, power dependencies, historical examples of cooperation and resolution, media literacy regarding propaganda, and realistic pathways for citizen influence on national foreign policy.

In Flinn’s Estate, the court reviewed a dispute between remaindermen (appellants) and life tenants (appellees) over the date for fixing intact value of corporate stocks to determine undistributed earnings payable to life beneficiaries under Senator William Flinn’s will. Flinn died in February 1924; his will granted executors five years to administer the estate and placed 60% of the residuary estate in trust, but the stocks were not transferred to the trustee until January 1929. The court held that, absent explicit language postponing the trust, intact value is generally fixed as of the testator’s date of death, and the administration period does not suspend the trust or delay the life tenants’ entitlement to income; delaying until distribution would violate the Act of April 18, 1853, condemning accumulations of income. However, for stock owned by Booth & Flinn Co.—a separate entity—and passed to the executors as a dividend in January 1925, intact value was fixed as of the dividend receipt date, not the date of death. The court also upheld the lower court’s use of a per diem averaging method to calculate accumulated earnings. The lower court’s decree was affirmed as modified, at the cost of the estate.

This study examines the integration of music notation software (Sibelius) into a general music education course at a Caribbean university for pre-service early childhood and primary teachers. Using a mixed-methods phenomenological approach, researchers analyzed questionnaire responses and an eight-bar composition assignment from 24 students to assess integration feasibility, comprehension, performance, and motivation. Participants completed the assignment with 90% accuracy. Questionnaire results showed mixed ratings for the software, with eleven participants reporting enhanced conceptual understanding and sixty-seven percent supporting continued use; however, many preferred traditional methods, motivation was largely neutral, half felt uncomfortable using the software in practicum settings, and seventy-five percent wanted more training. The study concludes that the software is relatively easy to integrate and positively impacts learning outcomes. Recommendations include continued use for selected content, progressive training for lecturers and students, adding technology criteria to practicum rubrics, and incorporating technology-focused assessments into course outlines.

This study proposes the Simplified Egg and Changing Yolk Model to explain ventricular repolarisation and T-wave morphologies on ECGs. The model depicts the heart as an egg-shaped muscle mass centred on Wilson’s Central Terminal, with repolarisation expanding outward. The asymmetrical “T-zone” produces the T-wave, while the ST segment reflects balanced isoelectric signals before the T-zone is reached. The model accounts for ST elevation, ST depression, and abnormal T-wave shapes—including peaked, inverted, flattened, and biphasic patterns—based on damaged or inert tissue locations relative to the lead. The authors argue repolarisation begins at the Q-wave as a continuous process, unifying the ST and T-wave intervals. They advocate using the QTp interval (Q-wave onset to T-wave peak) rather than the QTc interval, as it is more clearly defined and reliable for evaluating arrhythmia risk and medication effects. The model aims to improve ECG interpretation and cardiac diagnosis.

The disclosure relates to methods and systems for creating a virtual game environment from a real-world scene. A user selects and arranges physical objects having predetermined physical properties into a physical model. A capturing device at least partially scans the model to generate a digital three-dimensional representation, which is converted into a virtual toy construction model made of virtual construction elements. Conversion rules map the physical properties to virtual properties and game-controlling elements based on a game context or theme. Recognized known objects may select themes or be replaced with library assets. The disclosure includes a computationally efficient voxelization method that maps points defined within mesh surface elements to voxels, and a color-matching method that limits search radius in a 3D color space to find the closest discrete palette color. An interactive game system, optionally integrated in a mobile device with an augmented reality targeting overlay, supports cyclic gameplay where game outcomes initiate new cycles of physical model modification and rescanning. Physical playable characters and tools may also be scanned to create corresponding virtual entities.

A Northwestern University-led team used NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope to identify the progenitor of supernova SN2025pht in the galaxy NGC 1637, located about 40 million light-years away, marking JWST’s first confirmed detection of a supernova progenitor. The star was a massive red supergiant heavily obscured by thick, carbon-rich circumstellar dust, which made it appear extremely red and over 100 times dimmer in visible light. Because the dust blocked shorter wavelengths, the star was invisible to Hubble but detectable by JWST’s infrared imaging. The findings suggest that massive red supergiants often explode while hidden by dense dust clouds, explaining the long-standing observational gap between predicted and observed core-collapse supernovae. The dust’s carbon-rich composition, rather than the expected oxygen-rich silicate dust, indicates that convection may have dredged up carbon from the star’s interior before the explosion.

This article examines the experiences of leaders of undergraduate education-related degree programmes in further education (FE) colleges in England, using Hodgson and Spours' (2009) four-level lifelong learning ecology framework. The macro layer encompasses national policy initiatives since the 1990s, including post-compulsory teacher education, the widening participation agenda, foundation degrees, and higher education–further education partnerships. The exo layer involves local institutional relations and administrative partnerships between FE institutions and higher education institutions, including validation and franchising arrangements. At the meso layer, undergraduate programme leaders act as a "keystone species," providing personalised support and guiding student identities as higher education learners. The micro layer focuses on non-traditional, diverse learners and the stewardship required to maximise their success.

Drawing on a British Education Studies Association-funded study comprising an online questionnaire with 70 programme leaders (20% in FE) and 11 follow-up interviews (four in FE), the findings indicate that FE-based leaders often arrive in their roles through informal progression rather than direct application. Most hold master’s degrees and teaching qualifications, though fewer hold doctorates or Higher Education Academy fellowships than their university-based counterparts. They manage smaller staff teams and carry greater line-management responsibility within poorly defined roles.

Three strands of responsibility emerge: navigating administrative and organisational demands from colleges and validating or franchising partners; providing academic support to small, often mixed-level cohorts through creative pedagogical arrangements; and responding intensively to students’ pastoral needs. Leaders report tensions between further education regulations and higher education requirements, limited time for scholarly activity, and a strong sense of social justice in supporting local, non-traditional students. The article concludes that programme leaders are fundamental to sustaining undergraduate provision in FE but require enhanced "sightlines"—opportunities for research, scholarly engagement, and external partnerships—to balance internal demands and fulfil their roles effectively.

This protocol outlines a descriptive, register-based cohort study using Danish Hip Arthroplasty Register data from 1995 to 2022 to examine trends in periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) revision surgery following primary total hip arthroplasty (THA). The study aims to describe yearly trends in three surgical approaches—debridement, antibiotics, and implant retention (DAIR), one-stage exchange, and two-stage exchange—and to assess the risk of a second revision after each approach. All adult patients undergoing primary THA in Denmark are included, while those receiving hemiarthroplasty or simultaneous bilateral arthroplasty are excluded. Revisions will be categorized by timing relative to primary surgery, and second revision risk will be analyzed using Cox proportional hazards models and Kaplan-Meier plots, adjusted for calendar time, age, and sex. Strengths include the long observation period and examination of multiple revision methods. Limitations include surgeon-reported PJI diagnoses without paraclinical verification, incomplete data from some private clinics, and a purely descriptive aim. No external funding was received.

The passage describes a floor cleaner having a base and a body pivotable between an upright storage position and an inclined operating position. The cleaner includes a vacuum source, a supply tank, a distribution nozzle, a suction inlet, and a recovery tank. The recovery tank features a tank body with an inlet duct, a removable cover with a baffle that redirects entering air and fluid downward, a shutoff float that moves along the inlet duct to close a suction air outlet when fluid reaches a desired level, a removable strainer that engages the inlet duct, and a filter with a pull tab. The cleaner is configured so that its center of gravity remains behind the handle axis regardless of tank fill levels. A yoke or link connects the body to the base to enable steering about a second axis. This study investigates teachers' opinions on culturally responsive education in the Turkish education system using Q methodology with 21 teachers from Denizli, Mardin, Erzurum, and Şanlıurfa. Analysis of 30 Q statements revealed three perspectives: “Unification,” emphasizing global citizenship and acknowledging cultural inequalities; “Student Support,” focusing on equality and cultural competence; and “Teacher Support,” concerning teacher development and curriculum. Teachers generally agreed that the system accepts cultural diversity, but they disagreed on whether sufficient anti-discrimination measures exist and whether classrooms reflect societal diversity. Participants largely avoided explaining extreme viewpoints, indicating the subject remains politically sensitive. The findings suggest that while Turkey's education system recognizes multiculturalism, it lacks full implementation of culturally responsive practices, particularly in curriculum, teacher training, and equitable support for all cultures. The authors recommend culturally responsive teacher professional development, inclusive educational materials and environments, and fostering free expression of cultural identities in classrooms.

The dual momentum trading strategy, developed by Gary Antonacci and building on research by Jagadeesh and Titman (1993), is a trend-based investment method that uses absolute momentum—an asset’s own price rate of change over a set period—and relative momentum, which compares that asset’s performance against other assets. The strategy seeks to buy assets that have both positive absolute and positive relative momentum, meaning they are rising and outperforming their peers. In markets that permit short selling, it targets assets with both negative absolute and negative relative momentum for short positions. It avoids assets that are rising but lagging peers, as well as assets that are falling but losing less than others.

Antonacci’s 2012 framework combined the two momentum types to capture relative momentum’s returns while reducing its inherent volatility. The approach is commonly implemented with monthly rebalancing using ETFs, particularly those tracking geographically diversified equity indexes, though it can also be applied to individual assets, futures, or sector rotation strategies. A backtest using SPY, EFA, and AGG showed a 6.75% annual return and a 30% maximum drawdown, outperforming a world index but not the S&P 500; however, its drawdowns were lower and shorter-lived than traditional buy-and-hold portfolios. Antonacci’s Global Equities Momentum (GEM) model shifts between U.S. or non-U.S. stocks and bonds based on market strength. While the strategy may underperform during strong bull markets or sharp rebounds, it has historically outperformed over the long term by mitigating losses in bear markets.

The advance-decline indicator, or AD line, is a cumulative market breadth indicator that measures the daily difference between advancing and declining stocks within an index to confirm trends or predict reversals via divergence. Related concepts include advance/decline issues, distribution, and volume. The formula adds the net difference between advancing and declining stocks to the previous net advances. The NYSE advance-decline line applies this to all NYSE common stocks. A backtest using the S&P 500 ETF (SPY) produced inconsistent results across 229 trades with a 0.6% average gain and a 1.55 profit factor, below the 1.75 threshold. The authors concluded the indicator is likely ineffective for profitable trading strategies and suggested considering other oscillating indicators instead.

Generative AI is transforming sectors including finance, healthcare, and education, but its rapid development creates legal and ethical challenges such as misinformation, deepfakes, and societal biases, prompting questions about the adequacy of existing legal frameworks. However, macro-level challenges persist, including a communication gap between the technology industry and government and a lack of international consensus on AI regulation, which complicate compliance and may increase innovation costs. Micro-level challenges also exist, as risks such as LLM jailbreaking may only emerge during real-world use rather than in testing. To address these issues, top-down partnerships among industry, academia, and policymakers are recommended to develop forward-looking regulations, alongside a bottom-up approach in which developers and users report spotted issues through effective channels. The paper studies the problem of learning Linear Temporal Logic on finite traces (LTLf) formulas from positive and negative traces, with applications in software engineering, cyber-physical systems, and artificial intelligence. To overcome the scalability limitations of existing state-of-the-art tools like Scarlet and the GPU-based VFB algorithm, which struggle with formulas of size greater than 15, the authors propose a framework that integrates LTLf learning with Boolean Set Cover (BSC). The approach enumerates LTLf formulas up to a bounded size, then treats further search as a BSC problem: finding a minimal-weight positive Boolean formula (using conjunctions and disjunctions of generated atomic formulas) that separates positive from negative traces. They introduce algorithmic optimizations including domination-based pruning, a fast approximate domination heuristic, a divide-and-conquer meta-algorithm, and a beam-search-based BSC solver. These techniques are implemented in a new tool called Bolt. Using a consolidated benchmark suite of over 15,000 tasks, experiments demonstrate that Bolt significantly improves upon the state of the art, outperforming Scarlet in number of tasks solved, wall-clock time, and formula size, while remaining competitive with the GPU algorithm. An ablation study confirms that the BSC phase is essential for solving harder tasks. The authors identify BSC as a fundamental problem with potential applications beyond LTLf learning.

This article describes offensive positions in American football. The offense's goal is to advance the ball to score touchdowns or kick field goals. The quarterback leads every play, throwing passes, handing off to running backs, or calling audibles to change plays based on defensive alignments. Running backs primarily carry the ball but also catch passes and block. Tight ends mix blocking with receiving; attached tight ends line up on the line as vertical threats, while sniffer tight ends (H-backs) play off the line and focus on blocking and motion. The offensive line includes two tackles, two guards, and a center who block for runs and passes but usually cannot catch passes. Tackles block outside defenders, with the left tackle protecting the quarterback's blind side. Guards double-team and pull on run plays. The center snaps the ball and alerts the line to defensive issues. Wide receivers catch passes and block; Split Ends (X) line up on the line, Flankers (Z) line up off the line, and Slot receivers line up inside and rely on quickness.

Cornell research published in Psychological Science shows that eye expressions, which evolved from universal sensory reactions to environmental stimuli, communicate emotions. A study of wastewater in Western Uttar Pradesh, India, during 2020–2021 found substantial antimicrobial resistance among Enterobacteriaceae during the COVID-19 pandemic. Of 150 isolates from untreated drainage across three zones covering metropolitan and non-metropolitan cities, 62% were *E. coli* and 24% were *K. pneumoniae*. Overall, 74% of isolates showed resistance to one or more antibiotics, 79.3% were ESBL producers, and approximately 80% were multidrug-resistant. MDR prevalence was 57.14% in *E. coli* and 28.57% in *K. pneumoniae*, with *K. pneumoniae* showing significantly higher MDR across zones than *E. coli* (p=0.0081). Zone 1 exhibited the highest overall MDR percentage. Resistance included carbapenems and, alarmingly, colistin in *Pantoea* species. The authors attribute elevated AMR to increased indiscriminate antibiotic use during COVID-19 and inadequate wastewater treatment infrastructure, which allows residual antibiotics and resistant bacteria to enter the environment. They recommend policy attention, infrastructure upgrades, and periodic AMR surveys in wastewater to mitigate this public health threat.

The Indiana Court of Appeals affirmed Anthony Davis and Eric Simmons’s convictions for Class A felony conspiracy to deal in cocaine exceeding three grams and Davis’s forty-year enhanced sentence. It rejected the inconsistent-verdicts argument, noting Davis faced only one charge and Simmons’s acquittal on dealing was not irreconcilable with his conspiracy conviction because the State alleged and proved multiple overt acts. The court also held that any Blakely error in Davis’s sentencing was harmless, concluding the trial court would have imposed the same sentence based solely on his lengthy criminal history.

This study examines the relationship between science education and citizenship education in Turkey through qualitative analysis of the science curriculum and semi-structured interviews with eight science teachers. While Turkish citizenship education shifted from an interdisciplinary approach to a standalone course, the science curriculum incorporates citizenship-related elements through the Science-Technology-Society-Environment framework. Findings indicate that both the curriculum and educators conceptualize the connection between science and citizenship primarily through environmental issues, scientific literacy, and societal topics such as health, safety, and socio-scientific issues. Teachers emphasized that science education fosters values and skills essential for active citizenship, including critical thinking, inquiry, responsibility, and environmental awareness. However, educators reported that practical implementation is severely constrained by an exam-oriented education system, inadequate infrastructure, overcrowded classrooms, and insufficient materials. The study concludes that despite strong theoretical links, science education in Turkey currently falls short of achieving its citizenship-related goals. The authors recommend explicitly integrating citizenship competencies into the science curriculum, promoting socio-scientific and environmental topics, and providing teacher training to support a citizenship-oriented approach aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals.

A mixed-methods study using the Draw-A-Robot Test analyzed conceptions of educational robots among 121 fourth-year future preschool (75) and primary school (46) teachers at the University of Belgrade. Two evaluators achieved a 0.99 Pearson correlation in coding drawings and responses. While 121 participants accurately depicted robots, 22 held misconceptions, most commonly portraying robots as electrical appliances (68.18%). Animal-shaped robots were drawn most frequently (47.1%, particularly Bee Bot), followed by typical robots (24.8%), mechanical objects (24%), and humanoids (4.1%). Most drawings showed neutral emotion (76), with 44 positive and one negative. Respondents identified educational (52.9%) and assistive (31.4%) functions as dominant. Future preschool teachers reported three times more in-person robot experience than future primary school teachers and prioritized the educational function, whereas primary school teachers valued educational and assistive functions equally. The passage examines Digital Game-Based Learning (DGBL) and digital game-based assessment within the context of Education 4.0 and the Fourth Industrial Revolution, aligned with India’s National Education Policy 2020. It advocates shifting from rote learning and memory-based assessment to competency-based, personalized teaching and skill-based evaluation. Digital games support teaching-learning by fostering cognitive and non-cognitive skills, intrinsic motivation, and immersive experiences through formats such as simulations, puzzles, and role-playing games. For assessment, digital games facilitate adaptive, multimodal evaluation of both procedural and declarative knowledge. Stealth Assessment (SA) employs AI and machine learning algorithms to continuously analyze learners’ digital gameplay traces, enabling real-time, unobtrusive competency measurement and tailored feedback. SA depends on Evidence-Centered Design (ECD), which requires a multidisciplinary approach integrating education, psychology, and technology. The passage also notes challenges including the complexity of customized game development, potential cognitive overload, the need for proper difficulty calibration, concerns regarding neurological effects, and the infancy of research establishing DGBL’s validity and reliability.

Neutrinos for oscillation studies come from sources including supernovae, Big Bang relics, cosmic rays, the sun, accelerators, and nuclear reactors, each with distinct distances, energies, and mass sensitivities. Solar neutrino experiments initially detected fewer electron neutrinos than predicted, but the SNO experiment later showed the total neutrino flux matched theory, providing the first evidence that solar neutrinos oscillate between flavors. Atmospheric neutrino studies observed muon neutrino disappearance depending on zenith angle, also indicating oscillation. Accelerator experiments, such as those at Fermilab, CERN, and in Japan, use near and far detectors to measure flux and study neutrino appearance or disappearance, with experiments like T2K providing clear oscillation evidence since the 2000s. Reactor experiments study anti-electron neutrino disappearance through inverse beta decay, and their survival probability as a function of baseline over energy directly demonstrates oscillation.

Governments are intensifying AI regulation, exemplified by the EU AI Act and U.S. executive orders, yet AI policy discussions are largely absent from computer science (CS) curricula. This paper synthesizes key U.S. and EU regulatory developments and proposes a framework for integrating AI policy into CS courses. In the U.S., AI policy remains heterogeneous and non-binding, with recent executive orders reflecting partisan divides: President Biden’s EO 14110 emphasized safe and trustworthy AI, while President Trump’s 2025 EO 14179 rescinded it and prioritized global AI dominance, economic competitiveness, and national security. The EU’s AI Act, enacted in March 2024, adopts a risk-based approach, prohibiting practices like social scoring and real-time biometric surveillance while imposing transparency requirements on general-purpose AI models with at least one billion parameters. Three themes emerge: the volatility of AI policy demands; the challenge of translating abstract policy goals into concrete technical controls; and cross-border implications, including the potential for EU regulations to influence U.S. markets via the “Brussels Effect.” The proposed framework organizes AI policy discussions across three perspectives—socio-political, translational, and technical—and three dimensions—scope, power, and agency—using guiding questions to help students connect ethical principles to technical implementations, analyze power structures, and evaluate their own agency in shaping responsible AI. The authors note the framework is adaptable across curricula and suggest future work linking it to specific classroom activities and requirements engineering.

Researchers developed and experimentally validated a unified multiscale framework that links atomistic solid-melt interface energetics to macroscopic GaN and III-nitride epitaxy growth kinetics. Molecular dynamics simulations using machine learning interatomic potentials confirmed that liquid gallium forms structurally ordered and electronically charged layers at the GaN(s)-Ga(l) interface, with ordering differing between Ga-polar and N-polar surfaces. Metadynamics simulations revealed the free energy landscapes for nitrogen adatom adsorption and migration, uncovering a “Ga lubrication” mechanism in which interfacial liquid Ga dramatically lowers N migration barriers compared with clean surfaces. Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations parameterized with these atomistic barriers showed that GaN growth under typical molecular-beam epitaxy conditions proceeds via a diffusion-controlled, layer-by-layer mode. Integrating the free energy profiles, nitrogen diffusivity, and solubility into a parameter-free continuous diffusion model yielded quantitative, facet-dependent growth rate predictions. These predictions were validated against molecular-beam epitaxy experiments and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy measurements of partially nitridated Ga/GaN particles. The work establishes that for systems with low solubility of key elements—such as nitrogen in liquid gallium—the interfacial free energy profile governing adatom adsorption and migration is the decisive factor determining crystal growth kinetics, offering a transferable, predictive framework for low-solubility III-V systems.

The ADS868xW is a 16-bit SAR ADC with an integrated analog front end (AFE) and voltage reference. The AFE includes a programmable gain amplifier (PGA) that adjusts input signal range and common-mode level via RANGE_SEL[3:0] bits, a second-order 500kHz antialiasing low-pass filter, and a high-bandwidth ADC driver. The device uses either a factory-trimmed internal 4.096V reference or an external 4.096V reference selected by the INTREF_DIS bit; the internal reference is temperature compensated but sensitive to thermal hysteresis from soldering. The ADC supports single-ended and differential bipolar and unipolar inputs with straight-binary output.

The device features input and AVDD supply alarms. The input alarm uses user-programmable high and low thresholds with hysteresis, while the AVDD alarm has fixed 4.7V and 5.3V trip points. Both provide active and tripped flags readable via a dedicated pin, internal registers, or appended output data. A multiSPI interface supports legacy SPI, dual SDO, and source-synchronous data transfer protocols, and the device supports daisy-chain connections. Operational states include RESET (application or power-on), ACQ, and CONV, with NAP and power-down modes available to reduce power consumption. Nine configuration registers control the reference, input range, SPI modes, alarm thresholds, and output data formatting. In industrial applications, the device can interface with an external multiplexer to digitize multiple channels, and PCB layout requires partitioning analog and digital signals with proper supply decoupling.

A penalty kick is a live restart; the ball is in play when kicked. Attacking teammates must be at least 10 yards behind the penalty mark, inside the field, and outside the Penalty Area, and may enter only after the ball is kicked and clearly moves forward. All attacking players must follow up on saved, blocked, or rebounded kicks. The kicker cannot touch the ball again until another player has touched it; if blocked by the goalkeeper, the kicker must follow up instantly, but if it rebounds off the goal, the kicker must clear the way for a teammate. Teammates must react immediately without waiting for the kicker. If the goalkeeper secures the ball, the attacking team must immediately defend. If the kicker or a teammate offends, the kick is retaken if a goal is scored; otherwise, play restarts with an indirect free kick.

This study compared air-conduction (AC) and bone-conduction (BC) auditory brainstem response (ABR) and auditory steady-state response (ASSR) thresholds in infants aged 0–6 months with normal hearing (NH) or conductive hearing loss (CHL). Of 64 recruited infants, 50 completed testing. CHL was classified by elevated AC ABR thresholds with normal BC ABR thresholds at 500 Hz, corroborated by abnormal tympanometry and absent otoacoustic emissions. AC ABR and ASSR thresholds were significantly higher in the CHL group than in the NH group, while BC thresholds did not differ significantly between groups. Air-bone gaps were significantly larger in the CHL group for both measures, but ABR and ASSR thresholds and air-bone gaps were poorly correlated. Minimum ASSR intensities were higher than ABR minimum intensities. There was significant overlap between NH and CHL ASSR threshold distributions, and ABR AC thresholds showed higher sensitivity and specificity for detecting CHL than ASSR. No CHL was observed at 2000 Hz. The authors conclude that ASSR using the tested parameters is less reliable than ABR for differentiating mild low-frequency CHL from NH, and that ABR remains the gold standard for infant hearing assessment. They recommend further research with varying degrees and frequencies of CHL before ASSR is used clinically.

In soccer, the second defender provides individual support by positioning behind and inside the first defender, remaining goalside and far enough back to react if the first defender is beaten. This positioning forces the dribbler toward the sideline. The support defender maintains appropriate distance, uses the same stance as the first defender, and announces their arrival orally. They adjust position relative to the first defender and attacker, and may signal when the first defender can tackle. Critical oral communication includes announcing support, directing the first defender to jockey, delay, control, or contain the attacker, and signaling when to challenge or tackle. If the first defender is beaten, the support defender likely takes over, possibly performing a defensive switch. The second defender provides these calls because they can see the field while the first defender focuses on the ball.

Turing GPUs introduce dedicated ray tracing hardware (RT Cores) and a hybrid rendering pipeline that simultaneously combines real-time ray tracing with rasterization. RT Cores accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy (BVH) traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing, offloading Streaming Multiprocessors to perform other shading and compute work. This hardware acceleration enables ray tracing performance roughly ten times faster than Pascal GPUs, allowing cinematic-quality ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections at playable frame rates using fewer rays per pixel alongside advanced denoising. Turing ray tracing is compatible with NVIDIA RTX, OptiX, Microsoft DXR, and the Vulkan ray tracing API.

The architecture also features NVIDIA NGX, a deep learning technology stack utilizing Turing Tensor Cores for AI-based graphics enhancement. Its primary feature, Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS), renders at a lower input sample count and infers high-quality output comparable to or exceeding Temporal Anti-Aliasing while requiring roughly half the shading work; a DLSS 2X mode produces image quality approaching 64x supersampling. Additional NGX capabilities include AI InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. NGX does not function on pre-Turing architectures.

Mesh Shading introduces Task Shaders and Mesh Shaders, which use a cooperative thread model to eliminate CPU draw call bottlenecks and enable real-time rendering of hundreds of thousands of objects with dynamic level-of-detail control. Variable Rate Shading (VRS) allows dynamic adjustment of shading rates for every 16x16 pixel region, supporting Content Adaptive Shading, Motion Adaptive Shading, and Foveated Rendering. Texture Space Shading (TSS) decouples visibility and appearance sampling by computing and storing shading values in texture space, improving temporal stability and VR efficiency by reusing shaded texels across stereo views.

Multi-View Rendering (MVR) expands Pascal’s Simultaneous Multi-Projection to support up to four hardware views per pass (32 at the API level), enabling efficient single-pass rendering of stereo VR, cascaded shadow maps, and multiple character instances. Turing also supports DX12 Tier 3 bindless resource views and Tier 2 resource heaps.

For VR, Turing provides hardware support for USB Type-C and VirtualLink, MVR for flexible multi-projection stereo rendering, Foveated Rendering via VRS, and VRWorks Audio accelerated by RT Cores. The architecture includes the TU102, TU104 (used in products such as the GeForce RTX 2080, Quadro RTX 5000, and Tesla T4), and TU106 (GeForce RTX 2070) GPUs. A new RTX-OPS metric provides a workload-based performance measure for hybrid rendering that weights Tensor, FP32, RT, and integer operations based on typical frame-time usage.

This qualitative case study examines the legal frameworks governing inclusive education and assesses educational leaders' awareness of these policies in Addis Ababa's inclusive education resource centers. Through semi-structured interviews and document review with fifteen participants—including Ministry of Education experts, school principals, itinerant teachers, and teachers—the study identified global frameworks such as the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, Salamanca Statement, and Sustainable Development Goals; regional instruments including the African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights and the Protocol on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities in Africa; and national policies including Ethiopia's Constitution, Education and Training Policy 2023, Education Sector Development Plan VI, and Special Needs/Inclusive Education Strategy. Findings reveal that Ministry of Education experts and itinerant teachers possess relatively strong awareness of these frameworks, while school principals and teachers demonstrate limited knowledge, often relying on compassion rather than legal guidance. The study concludes that despite a comprehensive policy environment, inadequate awareness among educational leaders impedes effective implementation. It recommends professional development programs for school leaders, integration of inclusive education policies into teacher training curricula, and enhanced monitoring of policy awareness by national authorities.

Modeling nanoscale light-matter interactions is essential for quantum technologies, but classical Maxwell solvers cannot capture nonclassical effects, while quantum approaches are often idealized or computationally prohibitive. The authors introduce a stochastic differential equation (SDE) approach that bridges quantum emitter dynamics and classical electromagnetic fields without relying on wave-function unraveling or phase-space representations. Validated against the Mollow spectrum of a driven two-level system, this stochastic Bloch-vector method captures fluctuations and correlations in open quantum systems. The work specifically addresses asymmetric noise correlations from non-commuting operators by deriving SDEs from non-symmetric diffusion matrices, overcoming a limitation of conventional symmetric diffusion treatments.

This document standardizes the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) for AMD SEV-ES and SEV-SNP, which encrypt guest register state during world switches to prevent hypervisor access. The GHCB is a 4KB decrypted page formatted to mirror the SEV-ES VMCB save state area, facilitating controlled communication during Non-Automatic Exits (NAEs). The specification defines protocol versions, hypervisor feature advertisement through a FEATURES bitmap, and an MSR protocol for GHCB negotiation, CPUID requests, AP reset hold, GHCB GPA registration, page state changes, VMPL execution, and termination. It documents NAE events—including IOIO, MSR, MMIO, VMMCALL, SNP Guest and Extended Guest Requests, SNP TIO Guest Requests, AP Creation, #HV doorbell registration, Send IPI, Timer, APIC ID List, Secure AVIC, and Termination—and specifies required guest and hypervisor state exchange. The document also covers SMP booting via AP Jump Tables or SNP AP Creation, NMI handling using #DB intercepts and "NMI Complete" messages, debug register support, and SNP Restricted Injection via a shared #HV doorbell page. System Management Mode and nested virtualization are not supported.

Machine learning potentials (MLPs) enable efficient potential energy surface predictions, but universal interatomic potentials (UIPs) trained primarily on bulk data systematically underestimate surface energies. This study systematically evaluates fine-tuning (FT) and multi-head fine-tuning (MHFT) of a MACE foundation model for surface systems, comparing them against training from scratch (TS) and zero-shot (ZS) approaches across unary (Au), binary (RuO₂), and ternary (BiVO₄) surface datasets.

Results demonstrate that FT consistently achieves lower prediction errors and more physically realistic interatomic potentials than TS, even when trained on as few as 40–200 configurations versus 2,000 for TS. For BiVO₄, FT also reduces high-force outliers compared to both TS and ZS. However, FT modifies foundation model parameters, causing catastrophic forgetting that degrades performance on out-of-domain systems, such as other noble metal surfaces.

MHFT, which concurrently trains on original bulk and new surface datasets, mitigates this issue. Applied to novel metal surfaces after training on Au, MHFT achieves lower surface energy prediction errors than both ZS and FT, with roughly half the RMSE of ZS, while preserving bulk prediction capabilities. MHFT requires approximately 100 times more training time than FT and causes slight degradation on the fine-tuned surface compared to FT, though this remains negligible relative to DFT reproducibility limits.

The study concludes that FT efficiently improves surface-specific accuracy with limited data, whereas MHFT is advantageous when researchers must maintain original bulk performance alongside specialized surface accuracy, provided training conditions are aligned between datasets.

The article advocates for trauma-informed human rights education (TIHRE) in higher education, arguing that existing human rights education models often avoid politically sensitive historical content and risk retraumatizing students with lived or intergenerational trauma, including adverse childhood experiences. Based on an interdisciplinary literature review, it recommends that educators first cultivate a self-aware, rights-respecting teaching persona through values clarification to identify biases. Second, course design should integrate the UN tripartite framework—education about, through, and for human rights—via co-created, flexible curricula, reflective exercises such as Gibbs’ Reflective Cycle, and safeguards against graphic content, secondary trauma, and exploitative trauma narratives. Third, dialogic pedagogy should establish horizontal, trust-based learning relationships that develop critical thinking and advocacy skills, incorporating engagement with practitioners and survivors through guest sessions. Ultimately, TIHRE seeks to empower learners and educators toward hope, healing, and rights-based action while prioritizing safety, agency, dignity, and wellbeing.

This IDC White Paper presents findings from a December 2021 survey of 200 IT and departmental decision-makers in discrete and process manufacturing enterprises in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland regarding IT-based simulation, modeling, and high-performance computing (HPC). Facing geopolitical uncertainties, supply chain disruptions, and sustainability demands, manufacturers are leveraging digitalization to drive innovation and competitiveness. Three-quarters of respondents cite increasing innovation as the top goal of simulation and modeling, while 57% emphasize improving product and service quality. Deployment in product development, production planning, and quality management is expected to rise to around 90% within two years, with 64% of enterprises planning relevant investments. However, data silos remain a significant barrier, necessitating integrated data strategies to create a unified information base. Expanding usage scenarios include virtual prototyping, digital twins, IoT-enabled feedback loops, and high-performance data analytics, which 42% of surveyed enterprises already use. Demand for high-performance calculations is projected to grow from 8% to nearly half of respondents within two years. While 81% of decision makers agree HPC is a game changer for product and process innovation—enabling complex calculations, higher quality, and greater agility—only about a quarter currently use professional HPC infrastructures and 39% are planning or piloting adoption. Key challenges include security concerns (72%), high costs and licensing, energy consumption and sustainability (58%), and a strong preference for external cloud or colocation infrastructures (87% and 74%, respectively).

This paper investigates whether textual content in over 138,000 earnings press releases (2005–2023) predicts announcement-day stock returns. Using a rolling-window Lasso framework with bag-of-words models (LDA) and BERT-family embeddings (BERT, MPNET, FinBERT), the authors find that soft information is equally as informative as earnings surprises in explaining returns, with the best-performing FinBERT model achieving an R² of approximately 4.4%. Online LDA, trained dynamically on press releases and labeled with GPT-4o, improves interpretability by identifying thematic drivers. Topic analysis reveals a self-serving bias: managers emphasize internal financial metrics when reporting positive results and external sector or economic factors when reporting negative results. A long-short trading strategy entering at 9:45 a.m. after public release yields no abnormal returns after transaction costs, supporting market efficiency. However, if information is obtained prior to release, combining hard and soft signals substantially improves the prediction of extreme performers, with P@10 precision increasing to roughly 44–52%.

Testing indicates that RSI mean reversion strategies—buying low RSI readings and selling high readings—are largely ineffective on Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Dogecoin, yielding weak results and few trades. Conversely, using RSI as a momentum indicator produced significantly better results; for example, a short-term RSI(5) strategy on Bitcoin generated a higher CAGR and lower drawdown than buy-and-hold. The conclusion is that RSI does not work well for mean reversion in crypto but appears effective as a momentum indicator.

This manuscript illustrates the value of critical approaches to quantitative research (quantitative criticalism) in education, targeting scholars who employ quantitative methods and critical perspectives. The authors argue that quantitative research is not objective and present their own positionalities to demonstrate how social identities shape scholarly inquiry. Quantitative criticalism integrates quantitative methods with critical epistemologies to challenge post-positivist assumptions, advocate for social justice, and address systemic oppression throughout the entire research process. The authors identify inherent tensions, including statistics’ historical roots in white supremacy and eugenics, an undefined threshold of criticality, difficulties in operationalizing social identities, limited statistical power for intersectional analyses, and the conflict between generalizability and community-specific nuance. They review four studies applying critical race theory (QuantCrit), queer theory, and intersectionality to quantitative methods, outlining methodological benefits and limitations. The implications encourage educators to integrate epistemology with methods instruction, view criticality as a continuum while acknowledging that partial criticality can perpetuate oppression, and center researcher intentionality and positionality. The authors conclude that quantitative methods must be employed through critical frames to advance equity and collective liberation.

SpinGPT is a large language model agent for the three-player Spin & Go poker tournament format, built on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. It addresses limitations of prior LLM-based poker agents by using high-stakes professional hand histories with known private cards. The training pipeline comprises supervised fine-tuning on 320,000 decisions from 8,800 games played by a professional, followed by offline reinforcement learning with the ORPO algorithm on 270,000 synthetic hands generated by a GTO solver, mixed with 50,000 human hands. The supervised model, SpinGPT-SFT, achieved 80% exact accuracy and 86% macro F1 in imitating the professional player, and defeated the benchmark agent Slumbot at a win rate of 13.4 BB/100 after a heuristic patch for deep-stack play. The final SpinGPT model, refined toward game-theoretic optimality, showed improved bet-sizing accuracy and defeated the SFT-only model by 13.2 BB/100. Limitations include format mismatch with deep-stack benchmarks and potential numerical hallucinations. Future directions include stronger foundation models, retrieval-augmented generation, opponent adaptation, and hybrid solver-LLM architectures.

The MACD-histogram trading strategy is a mean-reversion system identifying momentum changes and reversal points. The MACD Histogram shows the difference between the MACD line and signal line; bars above zero indicate bullish momentum, while bars below zero indicate bearish momentum. The crossover strategy triggers buys when crossing above zero and sells when crossing below. Entry is on the close; exit is on the first day the close exceeds the prior close. Testing on 77 ETFs generated 6,669 trades with long positions outperforming shorts. A QLD backtest from 2007 produced 85 trades, 2.2% average gains, 10.4% annual returns, and a 19% max drawdown while invested only 5% of the time.

Researchers developed and validated an automated system to monitor intensive care unit guideline adherence by combining FHIR-encoded clinical practice guidelines with patient data standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model. Deployed across five university hospitals, the system evaluated six recommendations—primarily COVID-19 and ARDS-related—across 82,015 intensive care episodes from January 2020 to May 2023. In a validation study against ground truth established by experienced supervising physicians, the system achieved 97.0% accuracy, significantly exceeding the 86.6% accuracy of human reviewers, and processed over 2,000 patient days per second compared to approximately 30 seconds per patient day per recommendation for manual review. Most discrepancies were attributed to human errors, whereas system errors primarily resulted from unstructured free-text data not transferred into the OMOP CDM. Automated adherence rates varied by recommendation and hospital, generally ranging from 10% to 60%, influenced by factors including newly introduced guidelines, incomplete documentation, and strict evaluation criteria. The study concludes that the approach provides a scalable, accurate, and efficient method for monitoring guideline adherence across diverse healthcare environments.

Turing GPUs introduce an all-new display engine supporting 8K resolution at 60 Hz via DisplayPort 1.4a with VESA DSC 1.2, HDR with ITU-R BT.2100 tone mapping, and USB-C/VirtualLink. VirtualLink is an open standard enabling VR headsets to receive power, display, and data through a single USB-C connector, simplifying setup and supporting small form factor devices. An enhanced NVENC encoder supports H.265 8K encode at 30 fps with up to 25% bitrate savings for HEVC and 15% for H.264, while a new NVDEC decoder supports HEVC 4:4:4 8/10/12-bit and VP9 10/12-bit HDR. Turing’s encoder exceeds Pascal and fast x264 software quality with lower CPU utilization, enabling 4K streaming.

For multi-GPU configurations, TU102 and TU104 use second-generation NVLink instead of MIO/PCIe, providing up to 100 GB/sec bidirectional bandwidth in TU102 and 50 GB/sec in TU104; only two-way SLI is supported.

Turing TU102, TU104, and TU106 GPUs include dedicated RT Cores that accelerate BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing, enabling real-time hybrid rendering that combines rasterization with ray-traced reflections, shadows, and ambient occlusion via NVIDIA RTX, Microsoft DXR, and Vulkan APIs. This hardware acceleration makes ray tracing approximately 10 times faster than Pascal software implementations. RT Cores work with advanced denoising filters to reduce rays needed per pixel.

Turing also features Tensor Cores powering NVIDIA NGX deep learning technologies, including Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS), which delivers image quality comparable to or better than TAA with roughly half the shading work, as well as InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. Architectural enhancements include Mesh Shading (Task and Mesh Shaders) to eliminate CPU draw call bottlenecks; Variable Rate Shading (VRS) to dynamically control shading rates per 16x16 pixel region for content adaptive, motion adaptive, and foveated rendering; Texture Space Shading (TSS) to decouple visibility and appearance sampling; and Multi-View Rendering (MVR) supporting up to four hardware views per pass. Turing supports DX12 Tier 3 bindless resource views and Tier 2 resource heaps.

The TU104 GPU contains 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, and one NVLink link, powering products like the GeForce RTX 2080 and Quadro RTX 5000. The TU106 GPU (GeForce RTX 2070) contains 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, but lacks NVLink and SLI support. RTX-OPS is introduced as a workload-based performance metric for hybrid rendering.

A paper by Nicholas Lewis and Judith Curry in the *Journal of Climate* estimates equilibrium climate sensitivity (ECS) at 1.66°C (5–95% range: 1.15–2.7°C) and transient climate response (TCR) at 1.33°C (5–95%: 1.0–1.9°C) using observed temperature and forcing data from the mid/late 19th century to 2016. These estimates imply future warming 30–45% lower than central IPCC projections and are substantially below CMIP5 model estimates of 3.1°C for ECS and 1.9°C for TCR. The study finds previous methodological criticisms unfounded and potential biases from forcing efficacy, temperature estimation, and sea-surface temperature patterns to be minor when using globally-complete temperature data.
