Arizona has been the epicenter of school choice in the United States, becoming the first state to enact targeted Empowerment Scholarship Account (ESA) vouchers in 2011 and the first to expand them universally, which legislators did in 2022 after voters rejected a capped expansion in 2018. The state provides more than $1 billion annually in subsidies to private education from its general fund with little accountability or transparency.

A Grand Canyon Institute (GCI) report finds that while a growing share of universal ESA participants come from district or charter schools—including about 90% of new FY2025 entrants—nearly three-quarters of currently enrolled students had not or would not have attended public schools. Zip code analysis shows ESA vouchers primarily enroll children from higher-income areas, though that income gap has been declining.

GCI estimates that no more than 40% of ESA students used allocations for private school tuition in FY2023, with significant numbers using funds for homeschooling or extracurricular activities. Unspent account balances accumulated to $175 million by the end of FY2023 and an estimated $360 million by the end of FY2024.

The report concludes that universal ESA vouchers are a net cost to the state’s general fund. Because most primary users never enrolled in public schools, the program cost the state at least $330 million in FY2024 and an estimated $350 million in FY2025. Voucher amounts equal 90% of charter school funding, and enrollment grew from 144 students in 2012 to 87,602 by the third quarter of FY2025.

This study examines pre-service teachers' opinions on the Physical Education and Sports Curriculum (grades 5–8) regarding its achievements, content, learning-teaching processes, and assessment/evaluation. Using a quantitative scanning model, the researcher administered a validated questionnaire to 100 students from four departments at Bayburt University's Faculty of Sports Sciences, selected through cluster sampling. Results indicate generally positive views on program achievements and that the content is meaningfully ordered. However, participants were largely undecided about scientific errors in outcomes and content, age appropriateness, international compatibility, developmental suitability of activities, and use of alternative assessment methods. While a majority agreed that learning processes include enriched activities and concrete materials, most disagreed that varied teaching methods and techniques are used. The study concludes that pre-service teachers lack sufficient knowledge in several areas and recommends increasing related research, organizing informative seminars, and incorporating curriculum review courses into teacher training programs.

The present application is a divisional patent application concerning methods for forming three-dimensional vertical NOR-type memory string arrays. One embodiment provides a method using damascene local vertical bit lines that avoids ribboning—a stress-induced deformation of microscopic rectangular features—by etching local word lines in two steps, thereby reducing the aspect ratio and improving structural stability of word line stacks while addressing alignment issues. The fabrication process includes forming multi-layer memory structures on global interconnect lines, etching trenches to create word line stacks, selectively removing silicon nitride layers to form cavities, filling cavities with metal to form word line strips, and forming elongated vias through which conformal layers are deposited, including tunneling dielectric, charge storage, blocking dielectric, channel, liner, and sacrificial dielectric layers. Shafts are etched and filled with semiconductor material to form common source and drain regions, creating vertical NOR-type thin-film transistors at lateral overlaps between word line strips and the deposited layers. Electrical connections to local word lines are made via a staircase structure. Alternative embodiments use dielectric pillars formed prior to word line strip creation to provide mechanical support for high-aspect-ratio stacks, or use stacked masks to form the word line strips.

Mega Geometry is a new RTX technology that increases geometric detail in ray-traced applications by enabling full-fidelity ray tracing with modern LOD systems such as Unreal Engine 5’s Nanite. It introduces Cluster-level Acceleration Structures (CLAS), which build BVHs from compact batches of up to 256 triangles that can be cached, and Partitioned Top-Level Acceleration Structures (PTLAS), which update only changed scene partitions rather than rebuilding the entire TLAS each frame. It also supports real-time ray tracing of displaced subdivision surfaces. Mega Geometry is supported on all RTX GPUs from Turing via DirectX 12, Vulkan, and OptiX extensions. Blackwell’s fourth-generation RT Cores add cluster engines, new compression schemes, and up to 2x the ray-triangle intersection rate of the previous generation while reducing VRAM footprint.

Blackwell introduces hardware ray-intersection support for Linear Swept Spheres (LSS), a primitive for strand-like objects that is approximately 2x faster than Disjoint Orthogonal Triangle Strips (DOTS) while using about 5x less VRAM. Shader Execution Reordering (SER) 2.0 doubles the efficiency of reorder logic, improving hardware utilization for ray tracing and neural shading. The AI Management Processor (AMP) is a dedicated RISC-V scheduler that offloads GPU context scheduling from the CPU, reducing latency and improving workload management under Windows Hardware-Accelerated GPU Scheduling (HAGS).

Blackwell adds hardware encode and decode support for 4:2:2 chroma-sampled H.264 and HEVC video. It supports DisplayPort 2.1b with UHBR 20, providing up to 80 Gbps bandwidth. The ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC encoding quality by 5% and adds an AV1 Ultra High Quality mode; the GeForce RTX 5090 supports up to three encoders and two decoders. The sixth-generation NVDEC provides 2x faster H.264 decoding.

Power efficiency improvements include advanced power gating with separate voltage rails for GPU cores and memory, accelerated frequency switching that adjusts clocks 1000x faster than prior architectures, and low-latency sleep states that enter 10x faster than Ada, enabling up to 50% power savings in workloads such as small language model inference.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, which generates up to three additional frames per traditionally rendered frame using a new AI model that is 40% faster and uses 30% less VRAM, alongside enhanced Flip Metering in the display engine. DLSS 4 also transitions to transformer-based AI models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing (DLAA), replacing CNNs to improve temporal stability, motion detail, and lighting quality.

Blackwell enables neural shaders through the Cooperative Vectors API, allowing Tensor Core access from any shader type. This supports RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression offering up to 7:1 VRAM reduction over block-compressed formats, Neural Radiance Cache for real-time global illumination, RTX Skin for subsurface scattering, and RTX Neural Faces using generative AI for realistic facial rendering.

The Blackwell architecture includes the flagship GB202 GPU (GeForce RTX 5090) with 92.2 billion transistors, 24,576 CUDA cores, and a 512-bit memory interface; the GB203 GPU (GeForce RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti) with 45.6 billion transistors, 10,752 CUDA cores, and a 256-bit interface; and the GB205 GPU (GeForce RTX 5070) with 31 billion transistors, 6,400 CUDA cores, and a 192-bit interface.

An internal Enron email from Ann Schmidt on January 26, 2001, compiles press mentions of the company. Articles note that Enron's stock rose after it predicted 2001 profits would surpass analyst expectations; an op-ed highlighted Enron's profits from California's energy crisis and its executives' status as major bundled contributors to President Bush's campaigns; the U.S. ambassador to India offered to mediate Enron's contract dispute with Maharashtra's chief minister, while the Maharashtra State Electricity Board risked missing a payment deadline to Enron's Dabhol Power unit; Enron was deploying wind turbines in several states and building Texas wind farms; and employees were irate over a new forced performance-ranking system called "rank and yank."

InnerDancer Performing Arts, founded by former Royal Academy dancer Caroline Bossmeyer in 2009, hosts monthly dances at Vista's Gloria McClellan Adult Activity & Resource Center for teens and adults with developmental disabilities. The nonprofit teaches adaptive, inclusive dance emphasizing self-expression over perfection. Participants ages 17 to 80 socialize, exercise, and build camaraderie during the $12, two-hour events featuring DJ Tom Bossmeyer. Program manager Donna Meester noted the dances provide limited recreational opportunities in a safe, comfortable setting.

Coeur Mining (NYSE:CDE) shares fell 0.68%. Analysts' mean 52-week target is $10.25 (range $8.50–$12) versus the $8.75 close. The average brokerage recommendation is 1.67 from 6 analysts, with an industry rank of 52/265. Recommendations are 1 Buy, 6 Outperform, and 2 Hold. ATR-14 is 0.31, weekly volatility is 2.93%, monthly volatility is 3.56%, and RSI is 62.01. Market cap is $1.6 billion with 182.81 million outstanding shares. Recent volume was 2.21 million versus an average 3.42 million.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated July 22, 2020, announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2020, via a press release furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The information is not deemed filed under the Securities Exchange Act. It was signed by Frank H. Brod, Chief Accounting Officer.

The passage proposes Digital Ecosystems as software systems that exploit the robust, scalable, and self-organizing properties of biological ecosystems to overcome software complexity challenges and automate service composition. The proposed architecture uses a two-level optimization scheme: a decentralized peer-to-peer network of distributed agents and local evolutionary algorithms operating on habitats (peers). Agents consist of executable components and ontological descriptions. Users submit requests as semantic descriptions, which define dynamic fitness landscapes evaluated by semantic distance. The system balances user fitness constraints with internal self-organization to maintain diversity and avoid premature convergence. Network connectivity is information-centric and dynamically reconfigurable through Hebbian learning based on agent migration success, producing a topology resembling the user base. Populations evolve on separate islands in response to similar requests, accelerating adaptation by sharing solutions across habitats. The authors describe a simulation based on a small and medium-sized enterprise business ecosystem with one hundred users, random initial habitat connections, abstract semantic request tuples, and dynamic population sizes to evolve agent-sequences.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on August 5, 2016 correcting footnote 1B in its August 3, 2016 Q2 Update. The net increase in operating lease vehicles for the three and six months ended June 30, 2016 was incorrectly stated as $97,247 and $456,345 thousand; correct amounts are $241,253 and $600,351 thousand. The error did not impact cost of revenues or GAAP to Non-GAAP reconciliation.

Chance the Rapper was grand marshal of Chicago's back-to-school parade. Earlier this year he donated $1 million to Chicago Public Schools, distributed free backpacks and urged politicians to help schools.

The lecture discusses effective field theory (EFT) with fine tuning, using non-relativistic two-nucleon scattering as an example. Naive dimensional power counting can classify an operator as irrelevant when it is actually relevant, indicating the need for a non-trivial power counting scheme associated with an interacting fixed point rather than a trivial one. The theory integrates out exchange particles, leaving only contact interactions and their derivatives. For elastic scattering, the effective range expansion—expressing \(P \cot \delta\) as a Taylor series in momentum—emerges naturally from the EFT without specifying an underlying potential. The Lagrangian includes kinetic terms and four-nucleon operators with derivatives, and because nucleons are fermions, spin and isospin symmetries reduce the number of independent channels.

Loop calculations require keeping the kinetic energy term \(P^2/2M\) to avoid pinch singularities. While dimensional analysis suggests Wilson coefficients \(C_{2M}\) scale as \(1/(M \lambda^{2M})\), experimentally measured large scattering lengths (e.g., 23 fm and 5 fm) imply \(C_0\) is unnaturally large, revealing a fine tuning. To handle this, the lecture introduces an offshell momentum subtraction renormalization scheme, defining the amplitude at \(P = i\mu\). This yields a renormalization group equation for \(C_0\), making the coupling scale as \(1/(M\mu)\) and thus relevant when \(\mu \sim P\). The beta function has fixed points at \(a = 0\) (trivial) and \(a = \pm\infty\) (interacting); physical scattering lengths lie near the interacting fixed points. A pole in the beta function corresponds to a bound state, the deuteron.

An alternative dimensional regularization scheme, Power Divergence Subtraction (PDS), subtracts \(D = 3\) poles to track power-law divergences and reproduces the same physics. Once the leading fine-tuned coupling \(C_0\) is promoted to relevant status, the RGE propagates this enhancement to higher-order operators: for example, \(C_2\) scales as \(1/(\mu^2 \lambda)\). Summing all \(C_0\) bubble diagrams gives a scale-independent amplitude organized as an expansion in powers of \(aP\), allowing systematic predictions for deuteron and other two-nucleon physics.
Coral Davenport explains how OMB director Russell Vought plans to circumvent Congress’s budgetary powers to advance Trump’s agenda.

Shieldalloy Metallurgical Corporation petitioned the D.C. Circuit to review the Nuclear Regulatory Commission’s transfer of regulatory authority over certain nuclear materials to New Jersey. Shieldalloy, which had a pending NRC application to decommission its Newfield facility via on-site disposal of radioactive waste, argued the transfer was arbitrary and capricious because New Jersey’s program was incompatible and would disrupt its pending licensing process. The court agreed, holding the NRC’s response insufficient regarding Criterion 25, which requires arrangements to prevent interference with pending license applications during transfer. The NRC failed to adequately explain how Shieldalloy’s decommissioning would proceed without interruption under New Jersey’s regime or why a partial transfer—consistent with prior NRC precedent for discrete material subcategories—was inappropriate. The court also declined to defer to a statutory interpretation raised only at oral argument. Because the NRC’s explanations lacked a rational connection between the facts and its decision, the transfer was arbitrary and capricious under 5 U.S.C. § 706(2)(A). The court granted the petition, vacated the transfer, and remanded, declining to reach Shieldalloy’s other compatibility claims.

This document describes the Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine, which facilitates page migration between memory tiers in systems using Secure Encrypted Virtualization and Secure Nested Paging. TMPM requires IOMMU enablement and provides a ring buffer command interface for operations including PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO for hypervisor pages with concurrent DMA, PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST for SNP guest pages, and PM_GET_CAPABILITIES. Commands can process up to 128 pages per batch, with higher performance achieved at larger counts. A Pre-Migration state is defined for SNP guest pages, all system physical addresses must be 4KB-aligned, and migration of IOMMU data structures and ring buffer pages is prohibited. TMPM firmware can be reloaded after pausing operations and tearing down the ring buffer. Errors are reported through command statuses, sub-statuses, and Machine Check Architecture, with specific codes indicating partial success or retryable conflicts.

President Donald Trump said the government shutdown is an “unprecedented opportunity” to slash federal agencies and cut Democratic priorities, including $18 billion for New York City infrastructure and $8 billion for climate projects. He will meet with OMB Director Russell Vought, a Project 2025 author he previously disavowed, to discuss cuts to “Democrat Agencies” and whether they will be temporary or permanent. The shutdown began Wednesday after Congress failed to pass a stopgap bill; Republicans want funding until late November, while Democrats demand extensions of Obamacare tax credits. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Democrats are negotiating like “terrorists” and guaranteed no agreement on ACA credits. The White House warned of mass federal layoffs, likely in the thousands. Senate votes on competing bills failed Wednesday, none were held Thursday due to Yom Kippur, and the Senate will vote again Friday on the Republican measure.

Janet Yellen said rates must rise to prevent overheating but allow inflation to reach 2 percent. She said February’s 313,000 jobs exceeded sustainable 90,000 to 120,000 pace, and warned tightening too slowly risks overheating while too quickly could prevent inflation from reaching 2 percent. Yellen left the Fed last month after Trump appointed Jerome Powell, expected to continue gradual hikes. Under Yellen, unemployment fell from 6.7 percent to 4.1 percent without above-target inflation.

European stocks headed for their biggest weekly loss since November 2016, with the STOXX 600 down roughly 1.7 percent amid rising bond yields and a stronger euro. Markets faced a fifth consecutive day of declines, weighed down by disappointing bank earnings and a sharp reversal in Germany’s DAX, which dropped more than 5 percent in eight sessions. Deutsche Bank shares fell after the lender posted a larger-than-expected 2017 loss, while Spain’s Caixabank and Sabadell declined on mixed quarterly results. Bank of America Merrill-Lynch’s “Bull & Bear” indicator hit a “sell” signal, though strategists remained only “cautious” near-term and “constructive” longer-term. Investors also eyed upcoming U.S. payroll data and technology earnings, including Apple’s lighter iPhone guidance and Amazon’s record profit. Analysts noted that rising global yields could increase funding costs and force unwinding of leveraged trades.

This paper experimentally evaluates the ability of large language models (LLMs) to autoformalize undergraduate kinematics problems into differential game logic (dGL) for cyber-physical systems. The authors introduce 20 benchmarks and an automated semantic checker that verifies symbolic equivalence to expected solutions and ensures models are not in stasis. Their pipeline iteratively prompts LLMs to propose and revise dGL formalizations using few-shot examples and parser feedback. OpenAI o3 achieved a 70% top-5 success rate, outperforming GPT-4.1 (45%) and GPT-4o (20%). Six problems remained unsolved across all models due to checker and solver limitations with optimization problems, non-polynomial dynamics, and complex multi-phase dynamics. The findings indicate that LLM autoformalization could facilitate formal verification in controller design and potentially enable runtime formalization from multimodal sensor data for autonomous systems.

Depression and anxiety each affect over 300 million people globally. Digital phenotyping and speech analysis offer quantitative approaches for longitudinal mental health observation. Although large language models (LLMs) demonstrate clinical reasoning and linguistic capabilities, they remain underutilized for generating objective psychiatric biomarkers, and distinguishing depression from anxiety is challenging due to symptom overlap. To address these gaps, researchers collected over 15,000 minutes of audio recordings from 1,160 outpatients at the Shanghai Mental Health Center. They designed clinical indicators from electronic medical records and assessment scales, employed an LLM to identify symptoms and rate scale components, and fine-tuned the model using psychiatrist annotations. Linguistic and acoustic features were also extracted. These multimodal data were fused into an ensemble machine learning pipeline, which predicted diagnostic groups and symptoms with moderately high accuracy. The results suggest that LLM-derived objective cues combined with behavioral markers can enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of psychiatric diagnosis and assessment.

Theo Walcott scored in the 51st minute for Everton's 1-0 win over Newcastle at Goodison Park. The goal, his third since joining in January, followed a Yannick Bolasie cross. Everton plays Huddersfield and Newcastle hosts West Bromwich Albion on Saturday.

Cover Zero is an all-out pressure defense in which every player not covering an offensive skill player in man-to-man coverage blitzes, forcing quick quarterback decisions but leaving coverage players isolated. Offenses can exploit this with quick man beaters, slants, shallow crossing routes, and pick plays that take advantage of the open middle of the field. The passage details five college offensive plays designed to attack Cover Zero: Ole Miss's Double Slants, Oregon's Full-Slide Fade-Out with an RB Seam Gadget, Michigan's Trips Bunch Jerk Route, Wake Forest's Slant-Rub, and a Jerry Rice Motion Slant-Flat.

Former Aberdeen manager Steve Paterson suggested Neale Cooper's funeral be held at Pittodrie stadium, saying no church could accommodate the crowds. Cooper, 54, died in hospital on Monday after falling down stairs in Aberdeen. The 1983 European Cup Winners' Cup winner had recently reunited with teammates. Tributes were paid by Alex McLeish, Willie Miller, and chairman Stewart Milne, and the club said it will follow the family's wishes.

This study assessed awareness of cervical cancer and screening among women aged 15–49 in Benin and Cameroon using 2017–2018 Demographic and Health Survey data. Awareness of cervical cancer was low, at 9.5% in Benin and 46.1% in Cameroon; among women aware of cervical cancer, 51.4% in Benin and 59.7% in Cameroon were aware of screening. Multivariate logistic regression identified older age, higher education, and frequent internet use as significantly associated with cervical cancer awareness in both countries, with greater wealth also significant in Cameroon. Awareness of cervical screening was significantly associated with older age, higher education, and radio and internet use. The authors conclude that awareness is very low in both countries and recommend strengthening awareness programmes through stakeholder engagement, public enlightenment via media, implementation of national strategic plans, targeting younger women, and addressing socioeconomic and residential inequalities to improve access to information.

S&P earnings grew 11% in the second quarter, the second straight quarter of double-digit growth, the fastest two quarters since 2011. Over half topped forecasts, but average upside was 4%, below the 5% long-term average. Despite strong results, 2017 and 2018 forecasts were trimmed by less than typical. Goldman Sachs expects 2018 forecasts to drop 5%, citing overly optimistic energy expectations. Major U.S. indexes hit records, yet investors greeted beats with indifference; U.S. companies beating on earnings and sales barely rose, unlike international peers. BlackRock noted fatigue and warned second-half growth will be harder, though returns should remain solid.

Mark Valladares, Monday Editor of Liberal Democrat Voice, writes from Suffolk, noting snow across Britain and criticizing ministers for undermining Theresa May’s EU deal, citing Foreign Minister Simon Coveney on Article 46 on Ireland and Northern Ireland. He previews House of Lords business with Liberal Democrat contributions, Paul Walter on a young activist award and Samaritans’ Christmas work, a “goodbye” musical interlude, and invites submissions.

SARS-CoV-2, the cause of COVID-19, is shed in feces and detectable in wastewater, making wastewater surveillance a critical tool. Traditional concentration methods typically require 50–500 mL samples and centrifugation capable of spinning 50-mL tubes, limiting use in resource-limited settings. Nanotrap particles can capture, concentrate, and preserve viral nucleic acids from small volumes and complex matrices like wastewater. This study evaluated whether pH, temperature, incubation time, wastewater volume, RNA extraction method, and one-step versus two-step concentration methods impact SARS-CoV-2 RNA detection. Secondary objectives compared automated versus manual Nanotrap processing with 10 mL samples, and compared manual Nanotrap concentration to membrane filtration for 150 mL grab samples and skim milk for 250 mL Moore swab samples. Wastewater was collected weekly from Atlanta community manholes using Moore swabs and from treatment plant influent lines as 500 mL grab samples from June to August 2021.

An internal Enron email from December 12, 2000, circulates news articles regarding the company and energy markets. Coverage includes Enron's Dabhol Power project in India, where local lenders agreed to rate cuts to lower tariffs, alongside criticism over high consumer costs and a retired judge's opinion that the power purchase agreement can be nullified on public interest grounds. In U.S. markets, analysts discussed utility stocks potentially stalling amid a tech rebound, while record natural gas prices led some manufacturers to sell gas rather than use it in production; an Enron spokesman noted that volatility benefits the company. Articles also highlight EnronOnline's dominance in Internet energy trading with approximately $2.4 billion in daily volume, compared to Dynegydirect's $1.5 billion first month. Enron units applied to become retail electric providers in Texas, and The New Power Company—formed by Enron—was certified as a retail natural gas marketer in Georgia. Digital media firm Activate also cited coordination with Enron's content distribution network.

An Edmond veterinarian removed 21 pacifiers from dog Dovey. Her owners noticed pacifiers disappearing before Dovey vomited phlegm and a pacifier. An x-ray estimated 7 to 9 items, but surgery revealed 21. Dovey recovered. The veterinarian warned on Facebook that dogs will eat anything.

In a mailbag column, Ben Baby writes that a big loss to Alabama does not make Florida a must-win for Texas A&M coach Kevin Sumlin, but the team must play well in its final six games to reach 8-4. A&M has not announced throwback uniforms for the Alabama game, but the field will honor former coach Gene Stallings and the 1967 Aggie team that beat Alabama in the Cotton Bowl. The piece also addresses fall weddings, Aggie DJ music requests, North Texas athletics and the "Go Mean Green" nickname, support for Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, and Chipotle as a favorite burrito place.

A study of Wisconsin Poison Center data from January 1, 2010, to September 1, 2022, identified 59 kratom-associated exposure calls in Wisconsin, where kratom possession is illegal statewide. Calls increased during this period, peaking at 15 in 2020, and were concentrated in southeastern Wisconsin counties. Most exposed persons were male (62.7%) with a mean age of 35.3 years; three involved unintentional ingestion by infants under two. While 55.9% of calls involved kratom alone, polysubstance exposure was common, frequently with alcohol or benzodiazepines. The most reported symptoms were agitation (39%), tachycardia (35.6%), confusion (23.7%), and central nervous system depression (22%). Among 50 calls with known outcomes, 38% resulted in moderate or major effects, and 7 persons required critical care (22.2%), including one infant and two women in their 70s, one of whom died with kratom identified as contributory. The authors note that passive surveillance likely undercounts events, standard drug tests rarely screen for kratom alkaloids, and the unregulated status complicates research. They recommend clinicians and public health practitioners expand data collection, caution against polysubstance use—particularly among older adults—and promote safe storage messaging to prevent unintentional pediatric ingestion.

Dustin Brown and Anze Kopitar attribute their team's resilience to long-standing chemistry and trust built over years together, allowing them to battle through deficits and tough situations, though they acknowledge the importance of stronger starts and leads. They describe Drew Doughty’s growth into an on- and off-ice leader and Justin Williams’s calm, big-game focus. The players emphasize a tight locker room without cliques, which helps newcomers like Marian Gaborik integrate quickly. They prioritize a Stanley Cup championship mentality over regular-season accolades, and note that reflection only happens after each playoff round or season.

Two-year-old Laylah Washington died after being shot in the head while in a car with her family in Memphis, Tennessee. The shooting followed a parking lot confrontation with another driver. Police are seeking a black Chevrolet Impala and have made no arrests.

FlowMotion ONE raised over $600,000 on Kickstarter against a $30,000 goal. Its 3inONE design allows wearable mounting, handheld use with a joystick handle, or attachment to an extension pole. Sensors and motors eliminate shake for cinema-quality footage. Founded in 2015, the company operates from Palo Alto and Trondheim with a 10-person team. FlowMotion develops stabilization tools and has won awards such as Norway's Most Promising Startup and ISPO Germany's top 50 sports products.

Asia stocks muted on mixed Chinese PMIs; Australia skittish before RBA. The S&P 500 rose 2.2% in July and is up 7.8% year-to-date, but slipped 1.6% on August 1 as August began poorly. Market momentum remains intact, but short-term technicals look tenuous as volatility and credit spreads seasonally upturn and 50-day breadth rolls over from overbought levels. Investors are skewing portfolios heavier into tech stocks, while U.S. electricity demand hit an all-time high. Gold topped $3,800/oz amid U.S. shutdown risks and rate cut bets; dollar bears target 97.5 support. Frontier Markets led July returns, while U.S. large caps placed third in a risk-on month with stocks up and bonds down.

HMP Northward is overcrowded with more than 220 inmates in a facility designed for 212. Prison authorities will transfer approximately 22 low-risk, assessed inmates to a cordoned-off section of the Immigration Detention Centre (IDC) at Fairbanks to ease overcrowding and address security and rehabilitation concerns. Prison Director Steven Barrett called this the most viable short-term option while work is underway to reshape the prison. Home Affairs chief Dax Basdeo stated that IDC operations will continue normally and safety will not be compromised. However, nine asylum-seeking detainees at the IDC recently began a hunger strike.

This patent application discloses communication processing methods and apparatus for wireless communications, specifically for managing a duplication mode where PDCP data on a radio bearer is transmitted on a first RLC entity and duplicated on a second RLC entity. In a first aspect, a terminal device determines that a data volume report is to be triggered for one of the two paths in the duplication mode, triggers a report indicating the data volume on that single path, and sends it to a radio access network to reduce signaling overhead. The path may be network-indicated or terminal-selected based on priority or data volume. In a second aspect, the terminal receives a first indication message from the network indicating whether to activate or deactivate the duplication mode, and performs the corresponding action. The application further describes message structures for the indication, data handling upon activation and deactivation, data volume reporting rules for both states, and avoidance of radio link failure upon maximum retransmissions on a secondary path. Embodiments also provide corresponding communications apparatuses, terminal devices or chips, and computer storage media.

Randomized, open-label trial of 1,112 NVAF subjects on apixaban for 48 weeks randomized subjects 1:1 to SOC or Additional Education Program, with re-randomization at 24 weeks. Adherence was measured by electronic monitoring device using 24-hour units; investigator-withheld periods were excluded, and discontinuation over 30 days was considered permanent.

An alleged Swiss spy arrested in Germany is suspected of dealing in stolen banking data. A watchdog denied the Attorney General's office assisted FIS spying or failed to redact files revealing his identity. The Swiss government confirmed FIS investigated stolen banking data sold to Germany until 2014 but remained silent on the suspect's mandate. Germany expressed outrage; Swiss committees consider it.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2020 reported total revenue of $37.2 billion, net income of $13.9 billion, and diluted earnings per share of $1.82. Segment revenue was $12.3 billion for Productivity and Business Processes, $13.0 billion for Intelligent Cloud, and $11.8 billion for More Personal Computing. Commercial cloud revenue was $15.2 billion, a 31% increase. Compared to the prior year period, Azure revenue grew 48%, Office 365 Commercial grew 21%, Dynamics 365 grew 38%, Xbox content and services grew 30%, and Surface revenue grew 37%, while Windows OEM revenue decreased 5% and search advertising revenue decreased 10%. Microsoft entered into an agreement to acquire ZeniMax Media for $7.5 billion in cash. A change in accounting estimate increasing the useful lives of server and network equipment to four years raised operating income by $927 million. Total assets were $301.0 billion, stockholders’ equity was $123.4 billion, long-term debt was $57.1 billion, and unearned revenue was $36.3 billion. The effective tax rate was 14%, and $26.4 billion remained under the current share repurchase authorization.

A special weather statement warns of possible funnel clouds in Edmonton and areas south and east to the Saskatchewan border on Wednesday afternoon. Environment Canada states weak rotation under growing clouds could produce funnel clouds, with a slight chance of weak landspout tornadoes reaching wind speeds near 100 km/h. Students at Sturgeon Composite High School in Namao gathered indoors for safety. Officials advise monitoring conditions and preparing to take shelter if funnel clouds develop nearby.

Britain's FTSE 100 index fell 0.2 percent on Friday, set for its worst week since August 2017, as disappointing results from BT Group and AstraZeneca dragged shares lower. BT tumbled over 5 percent to a five-year low on concerns about stagnant growth and its pension scheme, while AstraZeneca declined 1.7 percent after a disappointing profit outlook. Commodity-related stocks rose on firmer copper and oil prices, and mid-cap Capita gained more than 5 percent following a Morgan Stanley upgrade.

In *Jennings v. University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill* (M.D.N.C. Oct. 27, 2004), the court denied plaintiff Melissa Jennings’s motions to strike defendants’ amended answer and certain affidavit exhibits, granted defendants’ motion for summary judgment, and denied a motion to submit evidence under seal. Jennings, a former UNC women’s soccer player, alleged that head coach Anson Dorrance and assistant coach William Palladino made sexually explicit comments during team warm-ups and personal inquiries into her life, and that UNC officials failed to supervise them. The court held that the alleged conduct was not severe, pervasive, or objectively offensive enough to support her Title IX or § 1983 sexual harassment claims; that two isolated inquiries did not violate her constitutional right to privacy because she was not forced to answer; and that the conduct did not amount to common law invasion of privacy under North Carolina law. Because no underlying constitutional violation occurred, the supervisory liability claims also failed.

Treasury minister Mel Stride pledged Britain's fish fingers would be safe during Brexit talks after Labour's Mel Onn urged continued sensible customs arrangements to protect Great Grimsby's time-sensitive fish processing industry and jobs.

The passage describes a data intake and query system for processing machine-generated data from IT environments. The system collects data from sources such as servers, sensors, and network devices, parses it into timestamped events, and stores the events in a data store. It employs a flexible, late-binding schema that applies extraction rules at search time to identify fields, enabling searching and analysis without a predefined ingestion schema. The system architecture includes forwarders that receive and route data, indexers that parse, timestamp, and index events into time-series buckets, and search heads that execute queries. It supports on-premises and cloud-based deployments and can search external data systems via External Result Providers operating in streaming, reporting, or mixed modes. Indexers create inverted indexes with token and field-value pair entries linked to event references, facilitating efficient search, filtering, and categorization by metadata such as host, source, sourcetype, and time range.

This literature review examines Information Technology integration in Indonesian language education within the Education 4.0 framework. Through qualitative descriptive and comparative analysis of 151 Scopus articles, the study identifies challenges including teachers' insufficient technological proficiency, difficulties maintaining student engagement, limited teaching resources, remote assessment hurdles, and student barriers such as the digital divide, self-regulation difficulties, and loss of social interaction. The review highlights technological innovations—Online Learning Platforms, Mobile Learning, Automatic Speech Recognition, augmented reality, virtual reality, artificial intelligence, gamification, and task-based or game-based learning—that enhance pronunciation, vocabulary, and engagement. Effective management strategies include digital learning platforms, teacher professional development, AI-based language support tools, global virtual exchanges, cloud and mobile infrastructure, data-driven decision-making, and inclusive IT policies. While students generally hold positive attitudes toward IT-driven language learning comparable to STEM fields, resistance and unequal access persist. The study concludes that careful IT implementation, supported by robust management strategies and attention to learner needs, significantly enhances language education outcomes.

A randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated SA58 Nasal Spray, a broad-spectrum anti-COVID-19 monoclonal antibody developed by Sinovac Life Sciences, as post-exposure prophylaxis in healthy adults in Beijing during an Omicron BF.7 outbreak. Participants were enrolled within 72 hours of exposure to a laboratory-confirmed case. Of 1,634 randomized participants, 1,222 entered the full analysis set. SA58 reduced the risk of laboratory-confirmed symptomatic COVID-19 by 80.82% (95% CI 52.41%–92.27%) and SARS-CoV-2 infection by 61.83% (95% CI 37.50%–76.69%). No severe COVID-19 or deaths occurred. Adverse events were mostly mild—such as nasal mucosal dryness, runny nose, and headache—with no significant difference between groups, and no serious adverse events or adverse events of special interest were reported. The authors concluded that intranasal SA58 showed satisfactory efficacy and safety, but noted limitations including a healthy adult worker population, short follow-up duration, and early termination before reaching the target sample size, recommending further evaluation in high-risk populations.

This application claims priority to U.S. applications Ser. No. 17/644,141, 16/250,926, and Provisional Ser. No. 62/618,391. Tracheal and endotracheal tubes are conduits inserted into the trachea to maintain a patient’s airway and facilitate ventilation; rapid sequence intubation (RSI) is a common emergency method. A medical system is described to assist rescuers with intubation or advanced airway procedures. It includes airflow sensors (e.g., oxygen, flow, capnography) to obtain data indicative of airway airflow, physiological sensors (e.g., pulse oximeter, capnography, ECG, acoustic, impedance, blood pressure) to obtain lung airflow information, and a patient monitoring device (e.g., defibrillator, AED) with at least one processor and memory. The processor receives sensor data, determines the presence of airflow, initiates a timer (default 5–15 seconds or user-defined), determines whether an endotracheal tube is properly placed within the interval based on physiological information such as ETCO2, transthoracic impedance, or acoustic spectral patterns compared to initial or dynamic physiological baselines, and presents the determination via a user interface. The system can automatically identify transitions between RSI steps based on changing intubation parameter values, generate context-sensitive feedback and alarms, guide rescuers through preoxygenation and placement verification, and communicate with portable computing devices and central facilities to transmit and receive patient information.

Cleveland Cavaliers forward Kevin Love may miss Game 1 of the NBA Finals due to a concussion suffered in the Eastern Conference finals against Boston. Researchers at UCI and other institutions developed a satellite-based drought severity index using NASA's GRACE mission data. The index incorporates terrestrial water storage, including groundwater, into drought assessments, augmenting traditional precipitation-based tools. The GRACE-DSI relies on satellite gravity observations for globally consistent monitoring from 2002 to 2014, with extension planned via upcoming missions. The long-short equity strategy involves taking long positions in stocks expected to appreciate and short positions in stocks expected to decline, serving as a hedge to minimize risk while maximizing profits. Popular among hedge funds, the strategy often employs a long bias—such as the 130/30 model—and is typically suited to institutional investors using leverage and derivatives rather than retail investors. It works by identifying underpriced and overvalued securities, sometimes across different sectors to reduce correlation. An example provided involves going long on Merck & Co. and shorting Thor Industries to profit from anticipated price movements. The article notes that Edward Thorp, founder of Princeton Newport Partners, pioneered quantitative long-short approaches, achieving 19.1% compounded returns with no losing years between 1969 and 1988. A backtest of a Coca-Cola and Pepsi strategy using RSI showed a 3.8% annual return, 0.45% average gain per trade, and an 11% maximum drawdown. The passage emphasizes that traders should use multiple pairs and leverage to enhance returns, and offers Amibroker code for further strategy development.

Researchers report a machine learning-assisted inverse design workflow for Dion-Jacobson two-dimensional hybrid perovskites that uses an invertible 12-digit fingerprint representation to link conjugated diammonium organic spacer structures to targeted energy level alignments (types Ib, IIa, and IIb). The workflow generates approximately 4.9 million hypothetical spacers via molecular morphing, computes electronic structures with high-throughput density functional theory on designated subsets, and trains interpretable machine learning models—specifically LASSO regression—to predict organic HOMO and LUMO levels. Candidates are filtered through a two-step synthesis feasibility assessment based on PubChem availability and a topological formability score for DJ perovskites, followed by DFT validation. Within generations G0–G6, the workflow validated 8 type IIa and 44 type IIb candidates, but no type Ib candidates due to synthetic accessibility constraints. Inverse design beyond these generations identified 2 type Ib candidates requiring pentacene backbones with at least five fused benzene rings, 12 type IIa candidates, and 42 type IIb candidates. Analysis indicates that aromatic ring count and primary ammonium groups most strongly influence frontier energy levels, whereas fluorination has minimal effect. The authors note that the fingerprint approach enables efficient exploration of vast chemical spaces from limited data, but acknowledge limitations in representing complex three-dimensional molecular configurations, heuristic synthesis evaluation, and the absence of experimental validation.

The PGA848 drives the ADS8860, a 16-bit, 1MSPS SAR ADC, in a circuit accepting single-ended or differential signals. The PGA848 input stage uses ±15V and the output stage uses 5.3V, shared with the ADC supply to prevent overloading the ADC inputs. A REF6250 5V reference feeds the ADC, while a precision 10kΩ-to-10kΩ divider and OPA192 buffer set the PGA848 REF pin to 2.5V. Three filters condition the signal: an input EMI/RFI filter, a 318kHz feedback filter using a 75pF CFB capacitor with 6.67kΩ feedback resistors, and a charge reservoir filter at the ADC inputs. The nominal f–3dB bandwidth is 318kHz, with –0.1dB flatness to 41kHz. The OPA192 buffer uses a dual-feedback configuration to drive the REF pin and maintain stability. Supply voltages exceeding 40V (±20V) permanently damage the device. Layout guidelines require symmetrical input paths, 0.1µF bypass capacitors near the device, separation of input traces from supply and output traces, minimized leakage and parasitic capacitance on input pins, and thermal management. PSpice for TI and TINA-TI simulation software are referenced for design and stability verification.

The disclosure describes systems, methods, and media to improve occlusion rendering in passthrough visualizations for head-mounted devices. Passthrough re-renders images of the physical environment from front-facing cameras based on a 3D model to account for viewpoint misalignment and parallax; however, imprecision in the 3D model at object edges can cause incorrect occlusion boundaries between passthrough and virtual objects. The described embodiments generate an instance segmentation mask for particular objects in the captured image and compute a representative depth for the mask based on the 3D model. The outer edges or padded borders of the mask are assigned a significantly farther depth measurement to create contrast. During rendering, the system samples the mask for these depth values to determine occlusion between passthrough and virtual objects, improving the accuracy of the visualization.

The Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00 defines the SD Memory Card physical interface, command protocol, and handling environment. SD Memory Cards are designed for security, capacity, and performance in audio and video consumer electronics, incorporating SDMI-compliant content protection, mutual authentication, password protection (CMD42), and optional ISO-7816 support. The specification covers Standard Capacity (SDSC, up to 2 GB), High Capacity (SDHC, up to 32 GB), and Extended Capacity (SDXC, up to 2 TB) cards, operating at high voltage (2.7–3.6 V) or UHS-II dual voltages (VDD1 2.7–3.6 V, VDD2 1.70–1.95 V). Communication uses a 9-pin interface supporting SD, SPI, and UHS-II bus protocols. Bus speed modes include Default Speed (up to 12.5 MB/s), High Speed (up to 25 MB/s), UHS-I modes (up to 104 MB/s via SDR104/DDR50 with 1.8 V signaling), and UHS-II modes (up to 624 MB/s). Cards include registers such as OCR, CID, CSD, RCA, DSR, SCR, and SSR. Initialization requires CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, and voltage switch sequences (CMD11) for UHS-I. The specification details card identification and data transfer modes, wide bus selection, read/write/erase operations, write protect management, lock/unlock, application-specific commands, switch functions (CMD6), clock control, CRC, error conditions, command classes, responses, status information, speed class and application performance class definitions, cache, self-maintenance, command queue, and power-up sequences. Mechanical specifications and extension functions are covered in separate addenda.

A longitudinal study in Choma District, Southern Province, Zambia, used amplicon deep sequencing to estimate the prevalence of antimalarial resistance markers in dried blood spots collected from 2018 to 2023. The WHO-candidate Pfk13 P441L mutation, associated with artemisinin partial resistance, was present in 6% of all successfully sequenced samples, with prevalence increasing from 0% in 2018 to 7.2% in 2023, surpassing the WHO's 5% threshold for concern. P441L mutants were detected at all four health centers. The Pfk13 A578S mutation was found in three individuals sampled in 2023. The Pfmdr1 Y184F marker remained stable at 41% prevalence, and wildtype MDR1 N86 was present in all samples. The authors note that the emergence of P441L in southern Zambia—consistent with its recent detection across East Africa and the Horn of Africa—represents a growing threat to malaria control, and they recommend enhanced molecular surveillance, therapeutic efficacy studies focused on P441L, and whole genome sequencing to identify associated genomic interactions.

This study by Brooks, Lubin, and Weigel examines factors that attract and retain rural special education teachers in rural remote Midwest U.S. districts, where annual attrition rates range from 30% to 50%. Based on survey responses from 93 teachers across three special education cooperatives, researchers identified four themes through descriptive and thematic analysis. For retention, 70% of participants cited provision of support as critical, including administrative support (38%), community support (19%), and general educator support (13%); correlational analysis showed a significant negative relationship between support and years of experience, while a significant positive correlation was found between support and plans to remain in the current position. Financial incentives were identified by 53% for retention—primarily increased salary (46%)—and by 96% for attraction, including increased salary (61%), reduced health insurance costs (17%), loan forgiveness or tuition support (8%), housing (7%), and sign-on bonuses (3%). Job-related factors were noted by 44% for retention and 15% for attraction, mainly reducing paperwork and caseload (20% and 7%, respectively) and providing professional development (17% and 7%). Rural initiatives such as Grow Your Own Programs and career fairs hosted by rural teachers were cited by 2% for retention and 9% for attraction. Among teachers planning to leave, 36% cited job-related factors and 27% cited lack of support. The study concludes that addressing chronic shortages requires a combination of financial incentives, administrative and collegial support, reduced job burdens, and rural-specific recruitment initiatives, while noting limitations of self-reported data from a limited geographic and demographic region.

Diane Monson and Angel Raich used medical marijuana legally under California’s Compassionate Use Act, but federal DEA agents destroyed Monson’s plants. They sued, arguing Congress lacked authority under the interstate commerce clause to regulate their local, non-commercial medical cannabis use. The Supreme Court ruled 6–3 for the government, holding that Congress could regulate in-state medical marijuana as an essential part of a broader scheme to prohibit the interstate market. Justice Scalia concurred separately, citing the necessary and proper clause. Justices O’Connor and Thomas dissented, arguing the ruling eliminated meaningful limits on the commerce clause and federalism; Thomas asserted the original meaning of “commerce” excluded local non-commercial activity. Following the loss, Raich unsuccessfully argued in the Ninth Circuit that a constitutional right to life should override federal drug laws. Attorney Randy Barnett later challenged the Obamacare mandate on commerce clause grounds. Justice Thomas has continued to dissent in commerce clause cases, maintaining that the federal marijuana ban is inconsistent and that the dissent in this case articulates the original meaning of the clause.

In Thomas H. Fisher v. Homer P. Hargrave et al., trading as Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner and Beane (Gen. No. 42,425, opinion filed April 20, 1943, rehearing denied May 4, 1943), plaintiff Fisher appealed a superior court summary judgment granted to defendant Hargrave. Fisher sought an accounting for $6,500 lost in commodity transactions with Fuller, Rodney & Co. in December 1940 and January 1941, suing Merrill Lynch as a successor or merged firm. Hargrave moved for summary judgment, supported by his affidavit and that of Byron G. Webster, a former Fuller partner. The court denied Fisher’s motions to strike and for a default judgment, then granted Hargrave summary judgment and costs.

The court affirmed. It found that the affidavits and the April 18, 1941 agreement between Fuller, Rodney & Co. and Merrill Lynch, E. A. Pierce & Cassatt showed no merger or consolidation, no assumption of Fuller’s liabilities, and that only certain customer accounts were transferred with consent; Fisher’s account was not transferred. Webster attested that Fuller remained solvent and able to pay, with partners available for service in Chicago. Fisher’s opposing affidavit relied on information and belief rather than personal knowledge, contained inadmissible conclusions, and failed to use available discovery procedures. The court held that no genuine issue of fact existed, that an accounting suit against a fiduciary is an equitable action permitting summary judgment under section 57 of the Civil Practice Act, and that the assumption of one lease and the admission of two Fuller partners into Merrill Lynch did not create liability for Fuller’s obligations. The decree was affirmed, with Sullivan, P. J., and Scanlan, J., concurring.

The Iso is a downhill running play in which a fullback leads to isolate a linebacker in one-on-one blocking, while linemen execute base blocks and double teams at the point of attack.
