This study reviews leadership models in education, analyzing administrative/managerial, instructional, transformational, distributed, transactional, ethical, contingent, and participative approaches. Administrative leadership emphasizes hierarchy and structure but can limit creativity and innovation. Instructional leadership focuses on teaching, learning, and academic climate but may adopt a strict top-down approach and overlook non-academic aspects of school life. Transformational leadership promotes vision, inspiration, and empowerment but risks becoming authoritarian. Distributed leadership shares responsibility among school community members, improving outcomes and trust, though it faces implementation challenges and potential conflicts. Transactional leadership uses rewards and exchanges to shape behavior but may produce temporary relationships and hinder long-term development. Ethical leadership emphasizes moral values and justice, though mismatched ethical standards can create conflicts. Contingent leadership adapts to specific circumstances without fixed values. Participative leadership involves stakeholders in decision-making, enhancing satisfaction and collaboration, but can slow processes and risk information leaks. The research concludes that no single model fully addresses the changing needs of educational organizations. It advocates a synthetic approach integrating managerial and transformational practices with distributed, participative, and ethical leadership to create a flexible, adaptive style that responds to contemporary educational challenges.

The Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00 defines SD memory card physical and communication requirements, using "shall" or "will" for mandatory provisions, "should" for recommendations, and "may" for optional features. It covers Standard Capacity (SDSC, up to 2 GB), High Capacity (SDHC, up to 32 GB), and Extended Capacity (SDXC, up to 2 TB) cards, with high-voltage (2.7–3.6 V) or UHS-II dual-voltage (VDD1 2.7–3.6 V, VDD2 1.70–1.95 V) operation. Cards are classified as read/write or read-only (ROM) and contain a User Area and a Protected Area. Bus speed modes include Default Speed, High Speed, UHS-I (SDR12/25/50/104, DDR50), and UHS-II (FD156, HD312, FD312, FD624); UHS-III (FD624) is introduced in this version. Form factors include Standard, miniSD, and microSD. Communication uses command, response, and data bit streams over CMD and DAT lines, with single or multiple block transfers and CRC protection. Initialization moves from card identification mode—using CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, CMD2, and CMD3 to assign a Relative Card Address (RCA)—to data transfer mode (CMD7). UHS-I entry requires 1.8 V signaling via a voltage switch sequence (CMD11) and optional sampling tuning (CMD19). UHS-II cards support both legacy SD and UHS-II interfaces, initialized through PHY, Device, Enumeration, Configuration, and SD-TRAN steps. The specification also defines password protection, Card Ownership Protection (COP) with Force Erase Password (FEP), mechanical and internal write protection, erase commands (including DISCARD and FULE), cache, command queue, and self-maintenance features.

Mayoral candidates in the Ipswich by-election have received nearly $60,000 in donations. Councillor Andrew Antoniolli received $46,400, including $15,000 from Plencove and $3,000 from Tracey Long. Councillor Paul Tully declared $10,968, including a $3,300 gift in kind from Falvey Investments for a Queen Street billboard, but has not revealed who funded two large billboards along the Ipswich Motorway. Greens candidate Brett Morrissey received $1,330 across nine transactions. Most of the 11 candidates received no declarable donations. The election is among the first to operate under Queensland’s new real-time disclosure rules, requiring candidates to report donations within seven business days.

Methods and apparatus improve user experience during electronically-generated binaural sound localization. Because near-field sound origination—within approximately one meter—is difficult to localize reliably and requires complex Head Related Transfer Function (HRTF) processing, example embodiments convolve sound to a location behind or on a line-of-sight with a sound source, using far-field HRTFs. The listener perceives the sound as originating from the source, even though the convolution point is elsewhere. This applies to visible and non-visible sources on electronic devices such as handheld portable devices, head-mounted displays, and televisions during telephone calls, video calls, or other communications. Additional embodiments detect device actions—including rotation, movement, facial detection, or sensor obstruction—to switch sound delivery between binaural external localization and mono or stereo internal localization, thereby improving realism and reducing processing demands.

University of Windsor Board appointed Douglas Kneale interim president and vice-chancellor from July 1 until Alan Wildeman's successor is found. Kneale, provost since 2015, will maintain continuity. Wildeman will announce an acting provost soon and assist Kneale. The board asked the search committee to resume efforts next year.

Orthonormal expansions in infinite-dimensional spaces behave similarly to finite dimensions, with projections onto orthonormal functions converging to the target vector; an inner product space has countably infinite dimension if a countably infinite orthonormal set exists such that only the zero vector is orthogonal to all of them. For Fourier series, this means the series captures the L2 function within [-T/2, T/2] while the residual lies outside. Prolate spheroidal functions provide an orthonormal expansion maximizing energy concentration within fixed time and frequency limits.

In communication systems, binary data is encoded into symbols, mapped to numerical signals, and modulated into waveforms. Pulse Amplitude Modulation (PAM) uses a one-dimensional constellation of equispaced, zero-mean real numbers; the mean square signal energy is d²(m²-1)/12. Delay and attenuation are treated as separate layered concerns, allowing focus on waveform design and noise.

To avoid intersymbol interference in PAM, the composite filter g(t)—the convolution of the transmit filter p(t) and receive filter q(t)—must be ideal Nyquist: g(0)=1 and g(kT)=0 for nonzero integers k. This is equivalent to the Nyquist frequency criterion that the folded spectrum be flat, achieved through band-edge symmetry. The raised cosine filter is a practical implementation, trading a slight bandwidth increase for faster time-domain decay.

A proper soccer defensive stance places one foot forward and the dominant foot back, with feet roughly 18 inches apart at 30 degrees, balanced on the balls of the feet, knees bent, and arms out. This allows quick reaction, slows the opponent, and prepares for a tackle. Field location modifies the stance: left foot leads on the right side, right foot leads on the left, and either may lead in the center. Training covers all three positions with progressive drills at increasing speeds with and without the ball, using field markings and sneak peeks to maintain goal side position.

The paper proposes a probabilistic computational model of conversational implicature comprehension grounded in relevance theory, implemented in the probabilistic programming language ProbLog. It distinguishes explicatures (contextually enriched logical forms) from implicatures (implicit premises and conclusions), and reviews relevance-theoretic foundations including manifestness, optimal relevance, and the comprehension heuristic. The authors formalize the parallel adjustment of explicit content, contextual assumptions, and implicit import using probabilistic knowledge graphs and Bayesian networks. Interpretive hypotheses are evaluated by computing the Kullback-Leibler divergence between prior and posterior probability distributions over communicated propositions—reflecting cognitive effects—and by the size of the Herbrand base as a proxy for processing effort. The resulting as-if-optimization model predicts that comprehension discards hypotheses failing to satisfy relevance expectations, prefers the smallest Herbrand base when divergence is equal, and otherwise selects the hypothesis with the highest divergence. The study focuses on the audience’s comprehension perspective and identifies speaker modeling, higher-level explicatures, and metarepresentational utterances as directions for future research.

Recent interest in rutile RuO2 as an altermagnetic (AM) candidate is tempered by debate, as numerous calculations and bulk measurements report a lack of intrinsic compensated magnetic moments in the rutile unit cell. This study investigates the origin of exchange bias (EB) observed in incoherent RuO2/Fe-based ferromagnetic heterostructures, which has been cited as evidence for intrinsic antiferromagnetic or altermagnetic ordering in RuO2. Using SQUID magnetometry, polarized neutron diffraction (PND), polarized neutron reflectometry (PNR), atom probe tomography (APT), and cross-sectional electron microscopy (HRTEM/EELS), the authors find that PND patterns of RuO2 thin films contain no signatures of antiferromagnetic ordering. PNR data reveal, however, that the RuO2/Fe interface hosts uncompensated moments canted within the film plane; the relative canting angles of these interfacial and ferromagnetic moments are sensitive to field history, mirroring the observed EB behavior. APT, HRTEM, and EELS show that the RuO2/Fe interface consists mainly of iron oxide with detectable magnetite (Fe3O4), alongside a Fe gradient into the RuO2 layer. Control experiments demonstrate that EB is absent in RuO2/Ni heterostructures, which feature different oxidation potentials and stable interfacial compounds, and that a weaker EB appears in TiO2/Fe/Ru bilayers prepared without RuO2. Based on these results, the authors establish that EB in incoherently grown RuO2/Fe-based heterostructures does not arise from intrinsic AM or AFM order within the RuO2 layer. Instead, the behavior is driven by a magnetically active interfacial reaction layer stabilized by the high oxidation potential of Fe relative to Ru, which pins ferromagnetic moments at the interface. Consequently, EB and associated magnetotransport phenomena should not be considered standalone evidence for altermagnetism or antiferromagnetism in RuO2.

Cybersecurity researchers at the Georgia Institute of Technology developed a simulated ransomware attack that can take over a water treatment plant to manipulate valves, chlorine levels, and readings. The simulation highlights vulnerabilities in industrial control systems, which often lack strong security protocols and may be incorrectly assumed to be air-gapped. While no real ransomware attacks have yet targeted these process controls, researchers warn that attackers may shift to these easier targets as other sectors become more secure. They recommend stronger passwords, limited network connections, and intrusion monitoring systems.

The speaker emphasizes that despite winning by a large margin, the team remains down in the series and is maintaining an even-keel approach. They express concern for a teammate who was hospitalized following a blindside hit, which the speaker feels the league should review, and acknowledge that roster adjustments will be necessary. The coach stated that undisciplined penalties driven by emotion are unacceptable. The power play generated momentum and goals, while the penalty kill has been excellent due to shot-blocking and sacrifice. The goaltender adjusted by staying in his net more, as the defense limited the opponent’s chances. The team needs to improve puck management and neutral-zone decisions to execute its forecheck, while matching the opponent’s physicality. Despite the series deficit, the club remains confident and focused on leveraging home-ice advantage in the next game.

Rebellion's Strange Brigade launches August 28 for PS4, Xbox One, and PC. Pre-orders include the Secret Service Weapons Pack, and a Deluxe Edition includes a season pass. The 1930s adventure supports 1-4 players facing mythological menaces.

A Cato Institute article claims California Gov. Gray Davis deceived the public about the state's energy crisis, noting that private companies including Enron charged less per megawatt than publicly owned utilities in early 2001. Reliant Energy and Peoples Energy reported higher quarterly profits driven by strong wholesale-energy units. Enron wants India to buy its 65% stake in the Dabhol Power Co. but is pursuing other options; Dabhol rejected price proposals from four Indian states as unrealistic amid a payment dispute with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board. A California Senate committee investigating market manipulation cited Enron and Reliant for contempt for failing to comply with subpoenas, while Morgan Stanley faces scrutiny over documents. Venture capital interest in energy technology is growing due to deregulation and the California crisis, though funding has tightened; Enron has invested $90 million in 12 strategic startups. Brazil's energy czar said aggressive mandatory usage cuts will allow GDP growth targets to be met despite shortages; Enron attended a related U.S. presentation. An Argus Research analyst called Enron a long-term buy on CNNfn, citing a positive outlook for energy generation and trading. Buenos Aires province is printing a local currency, the "patacon," to pay workers and bills due to a budget deficit, though business acceptance is uncertain.

The SanDisk Sansa c200 manual details operation, connectivity, and legal information. The front Record button starts microphone and radio recordings. USB connection enables file transfer in MTP or MSC mode, with the device appearing as a removable drive. Sansa Media Converter transfers supported photo formats including JPEG, PNG, and BMP. Music playback supports MP3, WAV, and WMA, with repeat, shuffle, five equalizer presets, and a custom equalizer. Users can manage a GoList, view photos and slideshows, listen to FM radio with presets, and record voice. Settings include backlight timer, contrast, auto power off, and USB mode. The FAQ covers file compatibility, MTP, firmware updates, and digital rights management. SanDisk provides a one-year limited warranty with repair or replacement options, and the manual includes software license terms, warranty disclaimers, and disposal instructions.

Researchers combined 102 medical imaging datasets to create a hyper-scale dataset of 4.5 million images (6.4 million after imbalance correction) to classify four modalities: CT, MRI, PET, and X-ray. ResNet-18, ResNet-50, and VGG16 were trained using dataset-level splits to prevent data leakage. The ResNet-18 model achieved 96% classification accuracy and 86% balanced accuracy on unseen test data, performing strongly on CT, MRI, and PET, but less accurately on bone X-ray datasets. The study demonstrates that deep learning models can classify hyper-scale multimodal medical imaging data for applications such as medical imaging repositories. Future work aims to extend classification to 3D scans. The project was approved by the University of St Andrews UTREC, and the code is open-source on GitHub under an MIT Licence.

The passage argues for "educational pacifism," contending that mass formal schooling systems cause pervasive, often unnoticed systemic harm—including structural, objective, and symbolic forms—by enforcing authoritarianism, conformity, and subordination to capitalist hierarchies, in addition to more visible personal harms like bullying. Drawing on Kant's "formula of humanity," the author asserts that this harm is morally impermissible because it treats innocent students merely as means to educational or economic ends. The article aligns Maria Montessori's philosophy with educational pacifism, highlighting her critique of coercive schooling practices and her emphasis on freedom, harmonious activity, and positive peace achieved through intrapersonal liberation. It contends that contemporary Montessori education should reject paternalism and harmful practices such as testing and timetabling, serving instead as a nonharmful alternative that protects student agency and fosters lasting, systemic peace.

Korean troops suppressed their southern rebellion before dispatched Chinese forces could actively assist. Both China and Japan subsequently landed thousands of troops; Chinese forces remain near Asan while Japanese occupy Chemulpo and Seoul, fortifying positions and encamping on the foreign settlement without other powers' consent, prompting protest. Neither nation will withdraw first despite the Korean King's requests, creating a dangerous standoff. American, British, French, Russian, and other warships are present. The United States instructed its representative to preserve peace, but he reports Japanese stubbornness, suspects an ulterior purpose and desire for war, and warns that Korean integrity is menaced.

Meeker's survey shows internet usage grew 7% with 3.6 billion users and stalled smartphone sales. Voice usage hit records. E-commerce rose 16%. Netflix: 117 million subscribers, Prime 100 million, Spotify 75 million. Uber has 31 million drivers; Airbnb has 600,000 hosts. Unemployment is 3.9%; job openings 7 million.

Presidential Spokesman Harry Roque said President Duterte will investigate Development Academy of the Philippines President Elba Cruz over employee allegations of unauthorized restructuring, Civil Service Commission violations, termination threats, and frequent foreign travel. Roque also announced Duterte's plan to fire all top officials of the Presidential Commission for the Urban Poor over allegations of unnecessary junkets and failure to meet en banc, and noted that the Presidential Anti-Corruption Commission, created in October, remains without appointees as the Palace continues vetting candidates.

The DAX (Deutscher Aktienindex) is Germany’s main equity index, comprising 40 blue-chip stocks listed on Deutsche Börse Xetra after expanding from 30 companies in September 2021. Major constituents include Adidas, BMW, SAP, and Volkswagen. The index can be traded via futures, CFDs, or ETFs; futures are the most liquid vehicle and trade on Eurex from 0750 to 2200 CET. Contracts include the full (25 EUR multiplier), Mini (5 EUR), and Micro (1 EUR), with 0.5 point minimum fluctuation, quarterly expiration, and cash settlement. DAX trading offers diversification through different trading hours and price behavior compared to US markets. Mean reversion, breakout, gap, and momentum strategies often perform better on DAX than on US indices. Two overnight strategies published in November 2021 and 2022, entering at 1730 CET and exiting at 0900 CET, produced average gains of approximately 0.22% and 0.23% per trade, respectively.

BioSafe Systems hired Carleton Birk as Operations Manager in East Hartford, CT, and Technical Sales Representatives Tenaya Becker (Southern CA), Ester Mastronardi (Leamington, Ontario), Patrick Clark (Eastern PA), and Kyle Pickles (Central CA). Birk has operational management experience and an MBA. Becker has 25 years of horticultural sales experience. Mastronardi has agricultural sales, export, and import experience. Clark has agronomy and nursery management experience. Pickles has agriculture systems and water treatment experience.

This MIT lecture introduces Underactuated Robotics, assuming prerequisites of differential equations, linear algebra, and MATLAB but no prior robotics coursework. The instructor argues that compelling robotics problems—such as agile walking, flying, and manipulation—are fundamentally underactuated, meaning control inputs cannot produce acceleration in every state direction, whereas fully actuated systems allow controllers to cancel dynamics via feedback linearization. He motivates the topic by contrasting conservative, high-gain robots like ASIMO, which consumes roughly 20 times the energy of a human due to stiff, trajectory-following control, with passive dynamic walkers and animals (including birds, fish, and even a dead trout in a vortex) that exploit natural dynamics for efficiency and maneuverability. The lecture reviews deriving second-order equations of motion using Lagrangian mechanics and the manipulator equations, demonstrating that a two-link arm with two motors is fully actuated, while removing a motor—as in the Acrobot—or lacking ground torque, as in compass-gait walking robots, renders the system underactuated. The course will proceed through model systems such as the simple pendulum, cart-pole, and Acrobot, then advance to walking robots with impacts and limit cycles, higher-dimensional systems, and scenarios involving stochasticity or unknown models. The approach will be computational, covering optimal control, dynamic programming, policy search, motion planning, and reinforcement learning.

The Blue Jays and Yankees meet in a best-of-five ALDS starting Saturday, Oct. 4. Toronto, the No. 1 seed, hosts Games 1, 2 and 5; New York hosts Games 3 and 4. Games 1 and 2 air on Fox and FS1; broadcasts for Games 3–5 are undetermined. The Blue Jays won the season series 8–5.

Nick Mathewson, a Tor developer and co-author of its paper, lectures at MIT on the Tor anonymity network. He defines anonymity technically as preventing an observer from linking participants to actions, distinguishing it from unobservability and unlinkability. Tor uses approximately 6,000 volunteer relays to serve hundreds of thousands to millions of users via low-latency onion routing, encrypting traffic through multi-hop circuits using negotiated symmetric keys. The design prioritizes usability for interactive web browsing, accepting that attackers observing both ends may correlate traffic. Directory authorities run by trusted parties vote hourly to form a consensus on active nodes to prevent Sybil attacks. Mathewson discusses motivations including privacy for citizens, researchers, companies, and law enforcement, acknowledging criminal use while arguing Tor is a multi-use technology akin to cryptography. He explains hidden services, which provide responder anonymity via introduction points and a distributed directory, and notes planned key blinding to resist enumeration attacks. Abuse issues include IP-based blocking by websites and criminal activity such as Silk Road 2, which he attributes to poor operational security. Attacks discussed include traffic tagging, application-level deanonymization over unencrypted connections, a historical Diffie-Hellman implementation flaw, and denial-of-service attacks. Censorship resistance relies on bridge relays and pluggable transports. Future work includes cryptographic upgrades, scaling beyond tens of thousands of nodes, improving hidden services, and researching padding defenses against traffic correlation.

Seven months after the Trump administration and DOGE made deep cuts to the U.S. Department of Education, researchers see cautious optimism. The department plans to reinstate 20 research contracts and 10 regional education labs, is seeking public input on modernizing the Institute of Education Sciences (IES), and has hired Amber Northern to advise on IES reform. It also began recruiting for high-level National Center for Education Statistics (NCES) assessment jobs tied to the National Assessment of Educational Progress (NAEP). However, severe staff shortages—particularly at NCES, which DOGE reduced from roughly 100 employees to three—continue to threaten data quality and progress. An executive order requiring massive retroactive admissions data collection further strains limited resources, and some NAEP reporting functions have been cut. While researchers welcome signs of rebuilding and the administration’s stated commitment to federal education research, most remain anonymous due to funding fears and stress that significant work remains to restore the research infrastructure.

Saving a penalty kick is a goalkeeper’s most stressful and challenging task, with a success rate generally under 15%, while approximately 80% are scored and 5% missed. Under IFAB Law 14, the goalkeeper must stand between the posts facing the kicker, with at least one foot touching, in line with, or behind the goal line until the ball is kicked, and must not unfairly distract the kicker. Violations can result in a goal being awarded, the kick being retaken, and the goalkeeper being warned or cautioned. Coaches must fully support goalkeepers, make clear that saves are not expected, and provide dedicated training emphasizing “read and react” over guessing, as up to 39% of penalty-kick goals are scored up the middle.

Preparation requires psychological resilience, mental techniques such as visualization, positive self-talk, pre-shot routines, and controlled breathing, plus physical fitness and proper equipment. Goalkeepers should research opponents by observing from behind the goal to learn cues, including ball placement, the kicker’s vision, approach angle, run-up style, plant foot direction, hip orientation, chin direction, body lean, and dominant leg. During the kick, the keeper should remain calm, straddle the center with one foot on the line, avoid diving early, read cues just before the ball is struck, dive outward to cut the angle, and attempt to catch with two hands or push the ball over the bi-line to avoid rebounds. After a block or save, the keeper must instantly recover because the ball is live, while teammates must not mob the goalkeeper. At advanced levels, keepers should track specific takers’ tendencies and may stand slightly off-center to influence the shooter, though referees closely monitor early line departure and unsporting behavior.

The speaker emphasizes that an early power-play goal and a second score by Donovan were crucial in building confidence after a weak previous game. Jarome’s captaincy marks a natural next step in his leadership, as he already led the team on and off the ice despite his youth. Oleg Saprykin’s blocked shot that produced a goal earned him the team’s green hard hat, celebrating the “little things.” The club must limit time and space on crafty forwards like St. Louis and finish checks. Goaltender Kiprusoff showed mental strength by rebounding from a rough six-goal outing in Colorado, and beating that club twice after the All-Star break proved the team could defeat elite opponents. Players manage shared fatigue by supporting each other, while breakouts must use the middle or high glass rather than rimming the boards against pinching defenses. Darryl instilled accountability, halted slumps quickly, and built the mental toughness and playoff belief the team needed, aided by key acquisitions and developing young players.

This work addresses metagenomic binning, the task of clustering fragmented DNA sequences into distinct genomes. It formalizes limitations of deterministic embeddings—whether k-mer-based or from large language models—which fail when sequences appear in multiple genomes via horizontal gene transfer or when distinct sequences produce highly similar k-mer profiles. To resolve this, the authors propose probabilistic embeddings that map each DNA fragment to a distribution in embedding space, explicitly encoding ambiguity and uncertainty. Their contrastive-learning framework yields closed-form expected pairwise likelihoods and naturally emerging non-Euclidean distances. The scalable method, UNCERTAINGEN, offers theoretical guarantees on improved distinguishability in latent space and demonstrates empirical performance gains over deterministic k-mer and LLM-based embeddings on real metagenomic datasets.

Jeff Davis Parish launched the school year after summer preparations including streamlining processes, campus maintenance, bus driver training, and staff orientations. Educators designed plans to meet student needs while maintaining state requirements. The parish ranks fourth in the state with a 92.5% graduation rate, up three points from last year.

This scoping review examined barriers and facilitators to belonging in graduate health professions education to inform occupational therapy (OT) education. Using Arksey and O'Malley's methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, the authors screened 202 studies and included 9 articles from occupational therapy, physical therapy, and medicine. Qualitative content analysis identified three themes contributing to both barriers and facilitators: environment (physical space and institutional culture/climate), relationships (faculty-to-student and peer-to-peer), and personal factors (perceptions of belonging, academic ability, and identity). The findings indicate that a sense of belonging is linked to academic success and health, while belonging uncertainty disproportionately affects students from historically minoritized identities. For OT education, the authors recommend creating welcoming and accessible physical spaces, implementing inclusive teaching practices, fostering mentorship and positive peer relationships, addressing bias and microaggressions, and providing research opportunities to increase diverse representation. Limitations include reliance on available literature, potential author bias, and lack of quality appraisal. The review concludes that belonging is an innate human need affecting well-being and academic outcomes, and targeted interventions are necessary to support students from historically minoritized identities in higher education.

The Supreme Court declined to hear multiple cases, including Alex Jones’ appeal of a Connecticut defamation ruling and a challenge by Colorado parents who claimed a school district violated their rights by excluding them from gender identity discussions; Justice Alito, joined by Justices Thomas and Gorsuch, wrote a statement regarding the latter. The Court also denied review in a Section 230 case involving Grindr, a death penalty case featuring alleged juror misconduct—prompting a dissent from Justices Sotomayor, Kagan, and Jackson—and a challenge to a repealed New York COVID-19 vaccine mandate. The justices rejected an appeal from California property owners over the lack of jury trials for cannabis fines, though Justice Gorsuch suggested the underlying precedent warrants reconsideration, and requested the Solicitor General’s views in two other cases. The justices will meet again on Oct. 17.

Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) improves ischemic stroke outcomes but is limited by restricted access to specialized centers and operator risks. This study proposes a world model framework using reinforcement learning for autonomous endovascular navigation in MT. Using an in silico environment with ten patient-specific vasculatures, the authors compared the model-based algorithm TD-MPC2 against the model-free Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) across five navigation tasks from the femoral or radial artery to the internal carotid artery. Single-task SAC training achieved high success rates for shorter tasks but lower performance on left-sided navigation. In multi-task evaluation, TD-MPC2 achieved a mean success rate of 65% compared to 37% for SAC, with significant improvements in success rate and path ratio for several tasks, though procedure times increased. The findings demonstrate that TD-MPC2 provides superior generalization for multi-task autonomous MT navigation, advancing the development of AI-driven robotic endovascular interventions. Future work should refine planning efficiency, integrate differentiable physics simulators, and expand datasets for broader generalization.

In a November 19, 2008 memorandum in the Barnhill’s Buffet, Inc. bankruptcy case, the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Middle District of Tennessee granted summary judgment motions by Wells Fargo Bank, N.A., and Dynamic Management Company, LLC, against SCS General Contractors, Inc. The court held that SCS’s equitable lien on Barnhill’s leasehold interests terminated upon the bankruptcy filing because the debtor became a debtor-in-possession and bona fide purchaser under Sixth Circuit precedent, and that SCS was not a third-party beneficiary entitled to enforce lease obligations. Under Mississippi Code § 85-7-137, the court further held that no equitable or statutory lien could attach to the landlords’ fee interests without their written consent, which was not obtained. The court ordered the escrowed sale proceeds released to Wells Fargo and preserved SCS’s claim as an unsecured creditor. The court also granted Dynamic’s motion, ruling that SCS failed to produce sufficient admissible evidence to support its alter ego claim under Mississippi law. The court denied SCS’s request for a continuance and granted Spirit Finance Corporation’s unopposed motion to dismiss.
The family of Milton Olin Jr. will receive nearly $12 million from L.A. County after a sheriff’s deputy killed him while texting. Attorneys urged prosecutors to review new evidence.

Household Sewing Machines-Global Market Status and Trend Report 2013-2023 provides comprehensive industry analysis covering worldwide and regional market size, forecasts, key manufacturers, types, applications, costs, profits, and growth drivers. The report segments the market by region (North America, Europe, China, Japan, Rest APAC, Latin America), type (mechanical and electronic), application (home and light commercial), and major manufacturers including Brother, Singer, Janome, Necchi Macchina, Bernina International, and others. Contents include market development, production and demand volumes, import/export status, competition analysis, and detailed company profiles with sales, revenue, price, and gross margin data.

Western revulsion against eating insects stems from their ubiquity and alien appearance, though insects are nutritious, sustainable, and consumed by two billion people globally. Americans avoid them due to abundant food options and fears about digesting chitin exoskeletons, but research indicates primates possess genes for enzymes that break down chitin, and cooking also renders exoskeletons digestible. Cooked insects are appearing on American menus, exemplified by the Seattle Mariners' popular roasted grasshoppers in 2017.

Disabled Navy veteran Gerard Ah-Fook, a competitive paracyclist, had his specialized handcycle stolen from his Tucson home. Stranger Randy Sooter donated his own handcycle, which he had purchased during ankle surgery rehab, after seeing a news report. Police continue searching for the stolen white recumbent three-wheel bike with red "Top End Force RX" lettering.

The passage outlines diplomatic strategies and suggested peace terms. Offensives include recognizing Bulgarian, Serbian, and Italian claims; assuring Austria-Hungary against dismemberment while noting its debts to Germany; conditioning Germany’s postwar partnership on democratization; promoting a League of Nations to Russia; addressing Alsace-Lorraine for French morale; and strengthening western Allies through economic unity and U.S. liberal leadership. Suggested terms require Germany to evacuate and restore Belgium and Northern France with full sovereignty, leave Luxemburg to later negotiation, and undo the 1871 wrong in Alsace-Lorraine.

Eight entrepreneurs from The Oracles share strategies for maintaining focus and avoiding distractions. Lewis Howes recommends acting with urgency to avoid regret. Mark Divine advises working off-site in a “secret location” with rituals like deep breathing, 45-minute work blocks, and movement breaks. Chris Harder suggests evaluating opportunities with a “heck-yes” standard and using an advisory board to decline distractions. Kenny Rueter emphasizes prioritizing one top task at a time. Nafisé Nina Hodjat states that obsession with meaningful work produces natural focus. Nik Halik outlines a five-step approach: embrace stress, establish a morning routine without digital input, work in 90-minute blocks with 25-minute breaks, create recharging rituals, and optimize sleep. Tom Shieh advocates scheduling distinct focus areas on a calendar to avoid multitasking. Peter Hernandez argues that organizations must build a “fierce focus culture” where every project aligns with clearly defined purpose and goals.

LG unveiled the G7 ThinQ in SA with an AI camera, 19 modes, a Google Assistant button, Google Lens, a Snapdragon 845, 4GB RAM, 64GB storage, and 16MP/8MP cameras. It arrives in early June for about R13,999, competing with the Sony Xperia XZ2 and Huawei P20.

This disclosure describes methods, systems, and computer program products for Artificial Intelligence (AI) assisted activity training. To address the need for convenient indoor expert guidance, a rendering device—such as a smart mirror or display—presents multimedia activity categories to a user. The system receives a voice-based input in a source language specifying an activity training plan, including selected activities and attributes. A Natural Language Processing (NLP) model configured in a single intermediate language processes the input to extract the plan. The system then initiates multimedia guidance steps via a virtual assistant or live trainer, detects the user’s activity initiation, and captures video via distributed cameras. In real time, an AI model processes the video and sensor data to extract user performance parameters, generating feedback based on differentials against target parameters. The feedback is rendered contemporaneously in aural, visual, or haptic forms. Embodiments include circuit creation, social sharing, gamification, gymnasium deployment with central servers, multiple input and security mechanisms, and editing of performance multimedia.

The U.S. Department of Education is revisiting the future of the Institute of Education Sciences (IES). Recommendations to protect and strengthen federal education research and development include: prioritizing urgent state and local research needs through learning agendas, faster research tracks, streamlined approvals, and rapid-cycle data tools; maximizing impact by modernizing data infrastructure and restarting Regional Education Laboratories and Comprehensive Centers; and improving communication to translate evidence into classroom practice through technology, required practitioner resources, and recognition frameworks. These steps aim to build a more efficient, effective, and accountable system to improve outcomes for students, educators, and families.

Strength training builds fitness but risks injury without correct technique and proper warm-up and cool-down. Common injuries include rotator cuff damage from repetitive overhead motions, hamstring strains from sudden movements, herniated discs from poor weightlifting form, tendonitis from repetitive stress, and tennis or golfer's elbow from repetitive wrist and arm motions. Symptoms include pain, numbness, and weakness, while treatments range from rest and painkillers to physiotherapy and surgery. Prevention requires good posture, stretching, gradual intensity and weight increases, dynamic warm-ups, static cool-downs, and avoiding exercise through pain. Fitness coach Ollie Kerr recommends working within limits, allowing recovery, maintaining hydration and diet, and using ice, compression, and elevation. A rabbit study indicates warming up provides a protective muscle mechanism. The passage also states 22 minutes of daily moderate exercise may reduce health risks from prolonged sitting, and autumn is a good time to resume fitness routines.

The October 31, 2000 VentureWire newsletter from Technologic Partners reports private company business news. Top stories include Trinity Ventures closing a $540 million fund, Sun Microsystems planning a $100 million investment in wireless firms, the shutdown of online textbook retailer Bigwords.com, and Internet consultant Concrete laying off 15% of its staff. Graph limits study analytic limit objects for sequences of graphs, motivated by analogies such as minimizing a polynomial over the rationals requiring a convergent sequence rather than a single rational number. The central limit object is a graphon: a symmetric measurable function \(W: [0,1]^2 \to [0,1]\). A finite graph can be turned into a graphon by partitioning the unit interval and using its adjacency matrix as a pixelated image. For example, a sequence of half graphs converges to a line graphon, while quasirandom graphs with edge density \(p\) converge to the constant graphon \(p\); however, one must account for vertex permutations, as illustrated by checkerboard graphs.

Homomorphism densities \(t(H,G)\), defined as the fraction of vertex maps from a fixed graph \(H\) that preserve edges, generalize to graphons via integrals over the unit cube. This definition agrees with the graph version when a graph is translated into its associated graphon. A sequence of graphs or graphons is convergent if \(t(H, \cdot)\) converges for every fixed graph \(H\).

Distance is defined using the cut norm, the supremum of integrals over measurable product sets \(S \times T\), and the cut distance between two graphons is the infimum of the cut norm of their difference over all measure-preserving bijections. This notion is preferred over edit distance because two independent random graphs with the same parameters can have large edit distance. The cut distance between two graphs is defined as the cut distance between their associated graphons.

The lecture states three main theorems: (1) convergence in homomorphism densities is equivalent to the sequence being Cauchy in cut distance; (2) every convergent sequence of graphs or graphons has a limit graphon; and (3) the space of graphons modulo cut distance zero is compact, meaning every sequence has a convergent subsequence. This compactness is an analytic reformulation of Szemerédi’s Graph Regularity Lemma, and the framework extends the theory of quasirandom graphs.

The CCAT Collaboration is constructing the Fred Young Submillimeter Telescope (FYST) in Chile’s Atacama Desert for observations beginning in 2026. It is assembling the testbed Mod-Cam and science instrument Prime-Cam, which use flexible stripline circuits to read out KID arrays across cryogenic stages. This work characterizes the Mod-Cam stripline’s thermal properties and investigates readout crosstalk. Residual resistance ratio and direct thermal conductivity measurements of the copper traces are consistent with high-purity OFHC copper literature. Thermal loading estimates indicate Prime-Cam’s redesigned stripline reduces per-harness loading at the 4 K stage despite more striplines. Warm S21 measurements isolated elevated inter-channel crosstalk to the SMP-SMA transition PCBs, not the stripline. A redesigned PCB using impedance-matched vias was simulated to improve crosstalk by approximately 20 dB, meeting project requirements. The results validate flexible stripline circuits as a scalable readout solution for large KID arrays.

The author outlines options strategies to gain exposure to AMD ahead of its Q1 2018 earnings announcement around April 25, 2018, without purchasing shares outright. The Inverted Hammer is the 11th most frequent candlestick pattern and a bullish reversal formation that appears at the bottom of downtrends, characterized by a small body near the lower end, little or no lower shadow, and a long upper shadow. It indicates buyers are gaining momentum against sellers and may signal a potential upswing, but as a single-candle formation it requires confirmation from tools such as trendlines, support levels, moving averages, and momentum oscillators. Backtests on the S&P 500 since 1993 show 132 occurrences, an average gain of 0.36% per trade, and win ratios of 53% to 65% when exiting after one to ten trading days, with a 70% win rate reported in broader backtests. Traders use it to enter long positions in strategies such as swing trading and mean reversion, typically placing stop-loss orders below the low of the formation and targeting the next resistance level or a 2:1 reward-to-risk ratio. While the pattern offers insight into market sentiment, it is subjective, can produce false signals, is not suitable for every timeframe, and is considered more bullish during downturns than in overbought conditions.

Digital laggards set aspirational goals that lack data grounding, leading employees to avoid measurement and prioritize process adherence over innovation. Digital leaders, by contrast, establish transparent, data-driven objectives aligned to company strategy, creating shared vision and vertical and horizontal organizational alignment through a combined top-down and bottom-up approach. However, even leaders can burden simple decisions with excessive analysis. While leaders treat data culture as central to aligning beliefs, values, and daily actions, laggards exhibit misalignment between espoused values and actual behavior due to entrenched habits and skill gaps. Organizations typically begin their transformation in one of four patterns: "data novices" lack cultural and system readiness; "insight ready" firms encourage risk-taking but lack technical capabilities; "tech enabled" organizations possess data infrastructure but discourage experimentation; and "data reliant" firms over-depend on data, discouraging critical thinking. Companies can leverage their specific pattern to build toward a strong data culture.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU is an 8th-generation data center GPU based on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture (GA100), fabricated on TSMC’s 7nm N7 process with 54.2 billion transistors and a die size of 826 mm². Designed for AI, HPC, and data analytics, it features 108 Streaming Multiprocessors, 6912 FP32 CUDA cores, and 432 Third-Generation Tensor Cores supporting FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary formats. The A100 delivers 2.5x the mixed-precision FP16/FP32 and FP64 performance of the Tesla V100, while TF32 operations run 10x faster than V100 FP32; these throughputs double with Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity. The GPU includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth and a 40 MB L2 cache. Its Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) capability partitions a single A100 into up to seven isolated instances for multi-tenant environments. Third-Generation NVLink provides 600 GB/sec total bandwidth, and the GPU supports PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, asynchronous copy and barrier instructions, task graph acceleration, and CUDA 11. The A100 powers the DGX A100 system, which delivers 5 PFLOPS of AI performance. It does not include display connectors, RT Cores, or an NVENC encoder.

Prostate cancer (PCa) diagnosis and monitoring rely on PSA testing, mpMRI, and invasive biopsies, which have limitations including false positives, missed clinically significant cancers, and patient morbidity. This study presents a point-of-care ion-sensitive field-effect transistor (ISFET) Lab-on-Chip device using reverse transcriptase pH-based loop-mediated isothermal amplification (RT-pHLAMP) to detect circulating nucleic acid biomarkers—YAP1 nucleic acid, androgen receptor full-length (AR-FL) mRNA, and AR-V7 mRNA—from the blood plasma of PCa patients. Following optimization of TRIzol LS RNA extraction, benchtop RT-pHLAMP assays detected YAP1 nucleic acid in 62% of patient samples and AR-FL mRNA in high-risk and metastatic cases. The ISFET Lab-on-Chip achieved 100% concordance with benchtop assays for simultaneous detection of these markers within approximately 15 minutes. YAP1 nucleic acid presence detected by the device correlated with more advanced cancer staging and higher initial PSA levels, while AR-FL mRNA amplification and AR-V7 mRNA were observed in high-risk or metastatic patients. The authors state this is the first ISFET-based biosensor integrated in a Lab-on-Chip capable of detecting endogenous circulating nucleic acids from cancer patient blood, and the first handheld biosensor for circulating mRNA-based PCa prognosis. While the current extraction method requires adaptation for full point-of-care compatibility, the device demonstrates potential for rapid, minimally invasive clinical prognostics.

Salt is primarily used in the United States for highway deicing and as an input into chemicals, food-processing, water-treatment, and agricultural industries. The three main production methods are room-and-pillar rock salt mining, mechanical (vacuum pan) evaporation, and solar evaporation. U.S. salt production grew substantially over the past century, driven largely by deicing demand, while the industry consolidated from hundreds of establishments in the late 1800s to 66 establishments owned by 29 firms by the early 2000s. Production is capital intensive, with economies of scale and high transportation costs relative to price. Growing environmental concerns over road salt runoff increasing freshwater chloride concentrations, potentially leading to regulation, threatened future demand. Compass subsidiary North American Salt was the third-largest U.S. producer; general trade salt generated just over 50% of its revenue, and highway deicing represented about 40% of its 2002 salt sales. The company operated facilities across North America and the U.K. using all three production methods. As of September 30, 2003, Compass had 1,541 employees, about 37% unionized. Ducey focused on safety, workforce motivation, and execution capabilities. He faced the challenge of persuading investors to hold a stand-alone salt company despite environmental and regulatory risks while delivering the performance expected of a public firm.

This paper examines optimal pricing for a monopolist selling a single, indivisible expiring item to strategic buyers who arrive stochastically over a finite horizon. Modeling the interaction as a Stackelberg game, the seller commits to a public, non-increasing pricing schedule, while buyers, who are not time-sensitive but have private valuations and arrival times, choose target purchase times to maximize interim utility. The authors introduce Value-Based Threshold strategies to decouple buyers' two-dimensional types, establishing necessary and sufficient conditions to formally prove existence and uniqueness of equilibrium in continuous valuation settings. For stylized markets, they derive near-optimal pricing schedules: a constant price for thin markets with infrequent arrivals to eliminate strategic delay, and a linear discounting schedule for thick markets with frequent arrivals where competition drives immediate purchasing. Numerical simulations validate these policies and reveal that optimal schedules shift from end-loaded to flat to front-loaded as the seller's time sensitivity increases. The framework differs from standard dynamic pricing by assigning time-dependent disutility exclusively to the seller, reflecting the economic reality of online secondary markets for expiring items.

The Missouri Court of Appeals, Western District, vacated and remanded the dissolution of marriage between Diane David and Joseph David because the trial court made a mathematical error in calculating Diane’s property distribution, listing her assets as approximately $62,781 rather than $59,182. Diane appealed the award of the marital residence to Joseph, the noncustodial parent, and argued the court failed to achieve an equal property division and ignored tax consequences of liquidating retirement funds assigned to her. The appellate court affirmed the trial court’s award of the farm to Joseph, finding no abuse of discretion regarding statutory factors for property division, and held that the division need only be fair rather than equal. It further held that the trial court could consider Diane’s separate teacher retirement account without materially impacting the division, distinguishing prior precedent because Diane was eligible for Social Security benefits through Joseph. The court rejected Diane’s claim regarding tax consequences because it was raised for the first time on appeal. On remand, the trial court was directed to reconsider the property distribution in light of the mathematical error and could make other necessary adjustments.

The toss play is an outside run in which the quarterback tosses the ball to a running back trying to get to the edge of the defense. Strengths include its simplicity to teach and install, efficient perimeter access, and consistent yardage when executed with a fast tailback and athletic offensive line. Weaknesses are its dependence on proper personnel and susceptibility to edge pressure and blitzes. Blocking assignments differ against 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts, with linemen, tight ends, and receivers executing combination and reach blocks while the fullback leads and the tailback reads his block. Variations include the Flexbone Toss, which uses a motion wingback and has the quarterback open toward the fullback—who does not lead block—to hold the defense, and the Single Back Toss G Pull, which uses a pulling guard as the lead blocker. The play aims to get the ball to an athlete on the edge quicker than the defense can respond.

The passage comprises excerpts from the Texas Instruments TMS320DM8127 DaVinci Digital Media Processor data manual. The piece argues he aims to develop a post-Soviet ideology as an alternative to Western liberal democracy, providing a patriotic mission statement while distracting from economic stagnation, corruption, and reliance on natural resource exports. Over the next six years, his government will likely solidify this worldview for domestic and international use. The author contends the West should reject this vision’s hollowness and maintain a positive, unified ideological stance to counter it.

Create Sheffield, a new partnership of education, arts, culture and voluntary organisations, will increase arts and culture exposure for Sheffield children and young people up to age 25. Launching in September with tiered membership fees of £125 to £5,000, it aims to boost school attainment, employability and workforce skills. The initiative addresses the decline of creative subjects caused by pressures to meet SATs targets and the EBacc performance measure. It will create a directory of cultural experiences, develop young makers, promote creative careers, support schools to achieve Artsmark, and enable parents to access the arts with their children.

The Red Cross Society of Ghana is appealing for ambulances, noting it has personnel to augment health services. Dr. Eric Asamoah Darko said their sole ambulance, donated by the Chinese Red Cross, broke down with an engine fault. The World Bank funded first aid posts on accident-prone major highways. Ghana has only 55 functioning ambulances out of 155, serving 29 million people. Vice President Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia announced government initiated processes to provide 275 ambulances for the National Ambulance Service.

Oregon public schools have among the lowest graduation rates in the country and require fewer instructional days than most states, averaging about 165 compared to the national average of 180. Oregon Board of Education member Kim Sordyl and some parents argue there is a correlation between fewer instructional days and low graduation rates, noting that Washington students receive roughly an extra year of instruction over the course of their K-12 education. Other cited factors include large class sizes, poverty, absenteeism, and budget deficits. State Representative Diego Hernandez says adding days without improving quality and supports is not the answer. Tualatin High School, which has one of the state’s highest graduation rates, emphasizes instructional time and addressing absenteeism.

The team acknowledges it has not played its successful playoff style, failing to manage the puck and generate sustained offense against the Devils' strong defense and goaltending. Returning home after losing both road games, they are focused only on the next game, hoping to use home ice and last change for better matchups. They stress improving puck management through the neutral zone against New Jersey's trap, eliminating turnovers to create shots and physical play, and capitalizing on opportunities, while maintaining respect for the opponent and avoiding frustration-driven altercations.

George Washington University students and officials are responding to a racist Snapchat post by Alpha Phi sorority members showing a banana peel and the caption “[Name]: ‘I’m 1/16 black.’” The sorority apologized and said three members are being removed. Student Association senator Imani Ross shared the image, prompting a university investigation. A student meeting was planned to address diversity and inclusion. GW Provost Forrest Maltzman condemned the post as hurtful, while the GW Black Student Union cited a pattern of similar racially charged incidents on campuses.

NVIDIA Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 31, 2016 reported revenue of $1.43 billion, up 24% year-over-year, net income of $253 million, and diluted earnings per share of $0.40. Gross margin was 57.9%. GPU business revenue increased 25% to $1.20 billion, reflecting growth in GeForce gaming, datacenter, and professional visualization products. Tegra Processor revenue rose 30% to $166 million, driven by automotive systems. Gaming revenue reached $781 million, datacenter revenue $151 million, professional visualization $214 million, and automotive $119 million. Operating expenses were $509 million, down 9% year-over-year. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $4.88 billion. The company settled intellectual property disputes with Samsung, Qualcomm, and Advanced Silicon Technologies, recorded restructuring charges related to the Icera wind-down, and returned capital to shareholders through stock repurchases and dividends.

Copper is frequently considered a leading indicator for stocks because it is used across nearly all industrial sectors, with price changes potentially signaling economic expansion or slowdown. A simple trading strategy was backtested since 2000, buying SPY when copper had positive four-week returns and holding cash otherwise. While the strategy showed decent returns and smaller drawdowns than Buy & Hold, it was largely flat between 2008 and 2016. Correlation analysis found little relationship between copper’s past four-week returns and SPY’s subsequent four-week returns, particularly from 2011 to 2016. The passage concludes that copper is likely not a reliable leading indicator for stocks, and the strategy’s performance may reflect luck rather than a true predictive relationship, though copper may still help predict broader business cycles.

Phase 1: 2 BNT162b2 participants had serious problems (appendicitis, inflamed nerves), deemed unrelated; none with BNT162b1 or placebo. Phase 2/3: few serious problems after two 30 µg doses; none related in ages 12–15. Ages 16+: 3 initial BNT162b2 recipients and 3 placebo-then-vaccine recipients had temporary problems possibly related. BNT162b2SA: 4/324 (1%) had serious problems, unrelated. Phase 3: few serious problems after 30 µg or 5/10 µg boosters, none in more than 1 participant, all unrelated. Phase 2/3 booster: 65/22,470 (<1%) had serious problems, with 2 ages 16+ possibly related. One participant had a serious problem after an additional booster, deemed unrelated.

Since 1950, the S&P 500 has reached all-time highs on only about 8.3% of trading days, averaging nearly 21 times per year, yet has returned a 7.67% CAGR. All-time highs generally reflect strong business conditions and bullish sentiment, and the market typically continues performing well afterward. A trading strategy buying when the S&P 500 is within 5% of its all-time high and selling when it drops more than 5% below produced a 3.20% CAGR with 43.2% market exposure and a 33.75% maximum drawdown. Earning a conservative return on cash during non-invested periods substantially improves results, and managing cash when the market is not at all-time highs is key to profitability.

The passage describes a respiratory mask system for delivering therapies such as CPAP and NIV. The system comprises a mask interface—including a frame with an angled, elliptical gas inlet and an outlet vent—and a seal attachable to the frame via a seal flange and clip assembly. The frame includes a longitudinal channel to receive a headgear yoke, with attachment features such as apertures, magnets, tabs, latches, retention bumps, and anti-rotation grooves. The yoke features a body with a narrower middle portion and wider side portions, locating members, alignment surfaces, and may include a textile covering, magnets, or protrusions to engage the frame. Some configurations include a nasal seal with a bridge depth less than half the overall depth and defined wall thickness, width, height, and sealing area. The yoke may also contain line tracks and end caps for a self-adjusting headgear mechanism.

The executive lays before Congress documents regarding disputes in the Aroostook territory claimed by Maine. Unauthorized individuals from British Provinces destroyed timber there; Maine’s land agent was arrested and taken to Frederickton, New Brunswick. Maine dispatched an armed posse, while New Brunswick demanded their recall and prepared troops. The United States rejects British claims of exclusive temporary jurisdiction and affirms that the boundary dispute must be settled amicably through arbitration or a commission rather than force. However, if New Brunswick militarily occupies the territory, Maine may constitutionally request federal aid to repel invasion. The executive expects the prompt release of arrested agents, recommends disbanding militia, and invites Congressional action before recess to obviate the need for an extra session.

The passage presents three free mean reversion trading strategies applied to ETFs: a deviation-from-recent-high strategy in XLP, an IBS short strategy in FXI, and a 5-day low strategy in the S&P 500. Mean reversion is defined as prices gravitating toward a moving average over time, with abnormal rises or falls eventually reversing. The article contrasts this with trend following, noting that mean reversion strategies typically produce many small winners and occasional large losers. These strategies work best in stocks and are less effective in markets such as commodities; reasons include the rise of futures trading and arbitrage, as well as the constant battle between buyers and sellers. The passage states that mean reversion performs best during bear markets due to increased volatility and explosive short-term rallies, and it provides historical backtesting results for each strategy. Code for the strategies is available for Amibroker or Tradestation.

The passage describes systems and methods for optically switchable windows, particularly electrochromic windows, and high-speed data communications networks integrated into buildings to support them. The network employs trunk line segments—using coaxial cables, twisted pairs, or twinaxial cabling—arranged in daisy chain topologies and connected by passive circuits such as bias Ts and directional couplers to deliver data at rates exceeding 1 Gbps, including TCP/IP, power, and wireless signals. Components include control panels with high-bandwidth switches (e.g., 10 Gbps Ethernet), conventional window controllers (WC2), enhanced functionality window controllers (WC3) with gigabit Ethernet and wireless access points, Digital Architectural Elements (DAEs), and digital wall interfaces. DAEs are modular units installed on structural building elements (e.g., mullions, walls) during construction and incorporate sensors (visible, infrared, acoustic, air quality, occupancy, biometric, radar), processors, network interfaces, antennas, speakers, microphones, displays, and power harvesting. These elements enable integrated environmental monitoring and control, including automated adjustment of HVAC, lighting, and window tint states based on measured conditions and occupancy. The systems also support security applications, such as detecting anomalous sounds (including firearm discharges), altering window tints to visually mark locations for emergency responders, and generating masking sounds. Other functions include noise cancellation, occupancy detection, personalization of space, and providing high-bandwidth connectivity and edge computing resources for building occupants and management.

Finance Minister Kemi Adeosun announced the Federal Government will release N750 billion to MDAs for 2017 capital projects, bringing total releases to N1.2 trillion. She spoke in Abuja while hosting 30 French firms interested in banking, infrastructure, renewable energy, agriculture, and youth empowerment. French delegation head Philippe Labonne said firms would partner with Nigerian counterparts, citing foreign exchange market stability.

Finnish official Witting attributed Finland’s reliance on Germany to the failed 1940 Finnish-Swedish defense pact, Soviet military buildup, and Finland’s dependence on German imports. He stated Finnish front activity responds only to Soviet offensives and that Finland, constrained by geography, cannot control German actions affecting Allied supply routes to Russia. The Finnish mind is set: they hope to avoid aggressive action against anti-Axis forces but expect military necessity may enforce cooperation with Germany. Swedish Minister Westman agreed Finland neither can nor desires a settlement with the USSR now; Swedish intervention would be ineffective and risky. Finns recently promoted their annexation policy to Swedish editors via Professor Jaakkola’s book.

A Nature Astronomy study confirms hydrogen sulfide in Uranus's atmosphere via the Gemini North telescope. The gas smells like rotten eggs, but the planet's negative 200 degrees Celsius atmosphere of hydrogen, helium, and methane would be lethal before the smell. The discovery sheds light on how and when Uranus formed.

This preprint reports a study from the Amsterdam Born Children and their Development (ABCD) cohort investigating the long-term effects of unintended pregnancy on children’s psychosocial problems and the mediating roles of maternal mental health and bonding. Among 7,784 participants, pregnancy intentions—measured as mistiming, unwantedness, and unhappiness—were assessed during pregnancy, and children’s internalizing and externalizing problems were measured via maternal-reported Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ) at preschool age (5–6 years), early adolescence (11–12 years), and middle adolescence (15–16 years). Maternal bonding problems (Nijmeegse Ouderlijke Stress index) and psychosocial distress (Depression Anxiety Distress Scale-21) were examined as mediators, with analyses controlling for antepartum maternal age, education, mental health, risk behavior, and child factors including sex, living situation, and adverse childhood experiences. Structural equation modeling revealed that at preschool age, pregnancy mistiming significantly predicted more internalizing and externalizing problems, while unwanted pregnancy predicted only internalizing problems; no significant associations between unintended pregnancy dimensions and children’s psychosocial problems remained in early or middle adolescence. Maternal bonding problems significantly mediated the associations between all three dimensions of unintended pregnancy and children’s psychosocial problems at preschool age, whereas maternal psychosocial distress only mediated the association for pregnancy mistiming. After accounting for mediators and co-occurring risks, some small direct effects of mistiming and unwantedness on internalizing problems persisted. The authors conclude that maternal mental health and bonding are more influential than pregnancy unintendedness itself and suggest investing in maternal support to reduce children’s psychosocial problems.

USGS estimates Tropical Storm Nate could erode 70 percent of beaches and half of dunes from Florida Panhandle to southeast Louisiana. Expected to hit as a Category 1 hurricane, it may erode over 90 percent of Louisiana beaches, overwash the Chandeleur Islands, and block roads.

Patanjali launched messaging app Kimbho as a "swadeshi" WhatsApp competitor offering messaging and video calls. The app was removed from Google Play Store a day after launch but remains on the iOS App Store. It had approximately 5,000 installations and reviews citing issues. An analyst said challenging WhatsApp solely on being "Swadeshi" would be difficult. The launch follows Patanjali's recent BSNL-partnered Swadeshi Samriddhi SIM cards, part of its expansion into communications, e-commerce, and other sectors.

President and CEO Dante Caravaggio began presenting, apologizing for background noise from an airport. Participants included CFO Mitchell Trotter, VP Jesse Allen, and VP David Smith.

The Cincinnati Bengals acquired quarterback Joe Flacco and a sixth-round draft pick from the Cleveland Browns in exchange for a fifth-round pick. The 2-3 Bengals have lost three straight games as Jake Browning threw eight interceptions over parts of four games. Coach Zac Taylor was noncommittal about Browning's status and wants a starter named by Wednesday ahead of Sunday's game at Green Bay. Cincinnati hopes Flacco, the 40-year-old 2023 Comeback Player of the Year, can keep them in contention while Joe Burrow is on injured reserve after toe surgery. The Browns listed rookie Shedeur Sanders as their No. 2 quarterback behind Dillon Gabriel.

Coach Quenneville said his team lost momentum after strong starts and stopped executing successful strategies. He praised Johnny's offensive and defensive production and awareness on both sides of the puck, noted players deal with injuries through playoffs, and highlighted one player's elite conditioning and ability to sustain big minutes without fatigue. He stated the team became more comfortable with line rotations over six periods. He emphasized the importance of momentum and home ice in the finals, noted the team remained even-keeled through emotional wins, and commented that Boston shut down Pittsburgh offensively while he did not foresee a ton of goals being scored. He stated the team focuses only on the immediate game and defended a line's effectiveness despite noting plus-minus statistics can be misleading.

The passage describes a display device with a substrate defining a through portion surrounded by pixels. Scan lines and data lines provide signals to the pixels, with data lines adjacent the through portion being curved along its perimeter and located at different layers to reduce pitch and non-display area. The substrate includes a display area and a non-display area, the latter having a first portion surrounding the through portion and a second portion surrounding the display area. A thin film encapsulation layer with inorganic and organic layers seals the device; a dam blocks organic layer flow, and the inorganic layers contact each other at a contact portion extending further toward the through portion than the organic layer. Various embodiments position data lines at layers shared with transistor electrodes, storage capacitor electrodes, or pixel electrodes, and include inorganic or organic-inorganic composite passivation layers to enhance moisture sealing and further reduce the first non-display area. The device may be incorporated into mobile phones, smart watches, or vehicle dashboards.

A speaker at the University of Michigan discusses building the Great Society. After noting past achievements in settling the continent and creating abundance, he states the next challenge is using wealth to advance the quality of American civilization. The Great Society rests on abundance and liberty for all, demands an end to poverty and racial injustice, and values knowledge, leisure, beauty, community, nature, and quality of life over material quantity. He identifies three starting points: rebuilding cities to address decay, housing shortages, and loss of community while accommodating growing urban populations; protecting the countryside from pollution and preserving natural beauty; and improving classrooms by addressing outdated curricula and overcrowding, better training teachers, ensuring poverty does not bar learning, and stimulating the love of learning. He announces working groups and White House conferences on these topics, emphasizing creative federalism between national and local authorities. He calls on the younger generation to join in advancing equality, ending poverty, promoting peace, and building a society that enriches life beyond material progress.

Teammates are excited for Manny's return and contributions. They must stay level-headed through playoffs and focus on Boston. The speaker has good history in Boston and was ready when Hank had the puck in front of the net.
