This telegram from Ambassador Hartman assesses the Andropov regime as continuing Brezhnev’s hard-line foreign policy without experimentation, while remaining dependent on U.S. relations. It argues that U.S. security requires renewed emphasis on arms control—particularly INF, as the zero-zero position is no longer viable. The Soviets seek to prevent U.S. deployment without dismantling SS-20s by manipulating European public opinion. Hartman recalls that the 1979 INF deployment decision was primarily political, aimed at assuring Europe of U.S. credibility, with 572 warheads chosen to be fewer than the projected SS-20 arsenal but enough to establish U.S. credibility in defending Europe.

This study evaluates the quality of inclusive education for disabled students during distance education in Kazakhstan based on the opinions of special education teachers. Using a qualitative case study design, semi-structured interviews were conducted with ten teachers, and data were analyzed through thematic analysis. Findings show that teachers primarily used online lessons, video sharing, and homework checking. Seven teachers considered formal education more advantageous than distance education, two found them similar, and one preferred distance education. Six teachers found distance education insufficient for meeting students' individual learning needs, while three found it partially sufficient and one sufficient. Teachers reported that families exhibited high anxiety, lacked technological means, faced communication deficiencies, and had inadequate online family education. Teacher-student and peer interaction was viewed as weak, time-insufficient, unqualified, or irregular. The study recommends diversifying technology-based methods, creating individualized learning contents, organizing online family seminars, and conducting regular social activities to strengthen interaction.

A memorial football match for Aidan Sutherland, a 20-year-old Kirkcaldy footballer who died from diabetes complications in July, will take place at Stark's Park on Sunday. Organized by his friend Ben Graham, the event will feature friends, former teammates, and professional players, alongside stalls, a pipe band, and face painting. It aims to raise awareness of diabetes and donate to the Diabetes Research and Wellness Foundation. Aidan's family and the charity stressed the importance of recognizing symptoms and acting quickly. Kick-off is at 1pm, with pre-match events starting at noon.

A Senate committee criticized the Supreme Court's Jordan ruling setting 18-month and 30-month trial deadlines, warning tens of thousands of charges risk dismissal. It released a report with 50 recommendations, saying the justice system needs a rethink, not rigid timelines.

The team learns from difficult conversations and corrects mistakes during games. They are eager to return home to sold-out crowds but must remain disciplined. The team uses all players in various situations and has overcome injuries through depth, with Fabbs stepping up effectively.

This study analyzed high-throughput transcriptomic profiles from three Alzheimer's disease (AD) cohorts—Knight ADRC, MSBB, and ROSMAP—to investigate the relationship between epilepsy-causing genes and a previously identified AD subtype characterized by synaptic plasticity dysfunction (SPD) and severe cognitive decline. The researchers examined 105 epilepsy-associated genes, finding that 45, 67, and 41 were significantly dysregulated in the SPD profile of each respective cohort, with 16 genes shared across all three cohorts. Of these, 15 were consistently downregulated and one (CERS1) was upregulated. Nine shared genes were synaptic and highly expressed in neurons. Pathway analyses revealed enrichment in glutamatergic, GABAergic, and dopaminergic synapse pathways, as well as ion channel activity and synaptic transmission. Analysis of the ROSMAP cohort showed concordant dysregulation of epilepsy-causing genes in both early and late AD compared to controls, with larger effect sizes at later disease stages. The findings support a bidirectional relationship between epilepsy and AD, suggesting that shared genetic and molecular pathways—particularly involving synaptic and ion channel dysfunction—may contribute to both conditions. The study highlights the potential importance of early detection and management of epilepsy in AD patients and indicates that integrated treatment strategies targeting shared vulnerabilities could benefit both diseases.

Analysts are generally bullish on uranium, forecasting rising demand through 2020 and prices around $65 per pound by 2019, while noting that up to 20% of current demand is not met by existing production. The World Nuclear Association reports roughly 440 operating nuclear reactors, with over 160 planned and more than 300 proposed, indicating a potential capacity increase of over 100%. Despite negative sentiment linked to the 2011 Fukushima disaster, supply and demand fundamentals support increased global reliance on nuclear energy. Technically, the Global X Uranium ETF (URA) is correcting its February high, with seasonal patterns and indicators suggesting potential support near April lows and the possibility of higher prices ahead, though short-term weakness is present. The URA ETF is presented as the easiest investment vehicle.

Pro se plaintiff John Bryant sued DOCS, Sing Sing, and Officer Hernandez under 42 U.S.C. § 1983, alleging that a roughly twenty-day "Code Blue" lockdown at Sing Sing—based on a false report by Officer Hernandez—violated inmates' constitutional rights, and that DOCS violated state labor laws regarding inmate wages. DOCS moved to dismiss for lack of subject matter jurisdiction under the Eleventh Amendment. The district court, adopting a magistrate judge's recommendation over plaintiff's objections, dismissed the claims against DOCS and Sing Sing, holding that they are arms of the state immune under the Eleventh Amendment, that New York did not consent to suit in federal court, and that § 1983 does not abrogate state immunity. The court permitted plaintiff's claims against Officer Hernandez to proceed if properly served and ordered plaintiff to report the service status by June 29, 2001.

The speaker, departing after fifty years of service, offers farewell thoughts, wishes his successor well, and expresses gratitude for cooperation with Congress. He states that despite four major wars, America is the strongest and most influential nation, but its leadership depends on using power for world peace and human betterment. He warns that a hostile, global ideology threatens progress and requires sustained sacrifice, and cautions against seeking spectacular solutions to crises. Instead, he emphasizes maintaining balance among national programs, between the private and public economy, and between present actions and future welfare. He highlights the new, vast influence of the military-industrial complex, warning against its unwarranted power and danger to liberties and democratic processes. He notes that federal funding now dominates costly, complex research, creating the risk that scholars and public policy may become captive to a scientific-technological elite. He urges avoiding the plundering of future resources for present convenience to preserve democracy for coming generations. He calls for international mutual trust, disarmament, and resolving differences through intellect rather than arms, expressing disappointment at not achieving lasting peace but noting that war has been avoided. He thanks the nation for his service and reaffirms hope for peace with justice.

The Tax Court held that gifts by check from the Estate of Elizabeth C. Dillingham were complete in 1981 when the drawee bank paid the checks, not in 1980 when delivered. The court refused to extend the relation back doctrine to these noncharitable gifts because the petitioner failed to prove unconditional delivery, citing an unexplained 35-day delay. Under Oklahoma law, a check does not operate as an assignment of funds until accepted by the bank, and the donees were not holders in due course, meaning the decedent retained dominion and control and could have stopped payment. As a result, the gifts did not qualify for the 1980 annual gift tax exclusion, the $36,000 was includable in the gross estate, and the estate tax assessment was not barred by the three-year statute of limitations.

NVIDIA's GA10x Ampere architecture introduces Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity, which imposes a 2-out-of-4 non-zero pruning pattern that compresses trained weights by 2x and doubles Tensor Core math throughput while maintaining inference accuracy across vision, language, and translation networks. Deep Learning Super Sampling (DLSS) leverages third-generation Tensor Cores and a new 9x scaling factor to enable 8K gaming at 60 fps on the GeForce RTX 3090. The architecture is the first to utilize GDDR6X memory, developed with Micron, which uses PAM4 signaling and Maximum Transition Avoidance (MTA) encoding to deliver up to 936 GB/s of peak memory bandwidth, an improvement of over 52% compared to the previous generation, while pseudo-independent channels aid ray traversal.

NVIDIA RTX IO integrates with Microsoft DirectStorage to enable GPU-based lossless decompression and rapid loading of compressed assets from SSDs to GPU memory, accelerating I/O performance by up to 100x compared to hard drives and traditional storage APIs while offloading CPU workload. The NVIDIA A40 data center GPU delivers up to 2x FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to 5x (10x with sparsity) AI throughput compared to the Quadro RTX 6000, with 48GB of GPU memory scalable to 96GB via NVLink, and supports virtual GPU software and Quadro Sync.

Ampere GPUs support 4K at 120Hz and 8K at 60Hz via DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a and are the first discrete GPUs with HDMI 2.1, offering 48 Gbps bandwidth. The fifth-generation NVDEC provides the first hardware AV1 decode support, enabling 8K60 HDR playback with minimal CPU usage, while the seventh-generation NVENC supports high-quality encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC. Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection performance and support concurrent ray tracing with shading or compute, while third-generation Tensor Cores implement structural sparsity. The GeForce RTX 3090 incorporates 24GB GDDR6X and 10,496 CUDA Cores, the RTX 3070 uses GA104 to outperform the RTX 2080 Ti, and the RTX A6000 workstation GPU features 48GB GDDR6 and 10,752 CUDA Cores. A new Error Detection and Replay (EDR) feature for GDDR6X detects transmission errors and retries them, allowing users to identify memory overclocking limits by observing performance plateaus rather than crashes.

WIRED editors selected discounted toys for Amazon Prime Day, including Squishmallows plush toys, Magna-Tiles reduced from $50 to $35, the retired Lego Icons Dried Flower Centerpiece, a Lego skeleton minifigure set, Play-Doh, a 60-piece travel building set, blind boxes, a Melissa & Doug ice cream counter, a Crayola Color Wonder brush station, and a Blue Marble rock tumbler kit. This prospective observational cohort study of 103 cerebral cavernous malformation (CCM) patients evaluated single nucleotide polymorphisms (PTPN2rs72872125, VDRrs7975232, VDRrs731236, VDRrs11568820, FCGR2Ars1801274) and plasma cytokines as potential biomarkers. The PTPN2rs72872125 CT and VDRrs7975232 CC genotypes were more frequent in asymptomatic patients and associated with distinct plasma cytokine levels. A weighted combination of the PTPN2rs72872125 CC genotype and GM-CSF plasma levels was associated with a symptomatic phenotype, representing a potential diagnostic biomarker. Among 42 patients followed for four years, the FCGR2Ars1801274 GG genotype predicted symptomatic events with high accuracy, indicating prognostic value; in silico analysis showed this variant produces a His131Arg substitution in a conserved protein domain. Additionally, the VDRrs731236 AA genotype correlated with later symptom onset, whereas the VDRrs11568820 CC genotype correlated with earlier onset. The study suggests that specific genetic variants and inflammatory markers influence CCM clinical behavior and symptom timing.

Methane bubbles in shallow muddy aquatic sediments threaten environmental safety, climate sustainability, and sediment stability. Bubble growth beyond the pore scale is governed by coupled mechanical and biogeochemical processes accurately described by Linear Elastic Fracture Mechanics (LEFM). The presented model integrates dissolved methane transport with LEFM to simulate growth within a sediment cell represented as a symmetry-bisected box containing an embedded penny-shaped bubble seed. Solute transport and solid mechanics are modeled outside the bubble, while methane accumulation inside follows conservation laws, Henry’s Law, and ideal gas behavior. Elastic expansion and localized Mode I fracturing are driven by inner gas pressure; crack propagation is determined by stress intensity factors calculated via the Displacement/Stress Extrapolation Method and the Strain Energy Density Criterion. Numerically implemented in COMSOL Multiphysics using finite elements and advanced meshing, the model was validated against analytical solutions for mature bubble shapes and sizes, showing good agreement across varying fracture toughness. Mature bubbles exhibit an inverted tear-drop shape with a closed tail. The model is currently limited to individual bubbles and serves as a foundation for future upscaling to the effective properties of gassy aquatic muds.

This study developed and evaluated a teacher education program integrating collaborative inquiry with panoramic cameras to enhance teacher education students' (TESs) diagnostic capabilities and instructional design skills. Twenty-two TESs participated in a semester-long "Professional Teaching Practicum" from September 2022 to January 2023, alternating between teaching and observing roles in groups. Observers used panoramic cameras to collect detailed evidence of student learning behaviors during junior high school teaching activities, followed by post-lesson discussions and reflections. Data were gathered through an "Observation Record Form Based on Student Responses to Teaching Activities"—evaluated with a 0-to-2 checklist—and a 12-item questionnaire measuring perceived instructional design capabilities across three facets: lesson preparation, linking student learning with teaching practice, and adjusting lesson plans. Results showed TESs' diagnostic scores improved across four cycles, rising from an average of 0.47 in the first cycle to 1.88 in the fourth (out of 2). Wilcoxon signed-rank tests indicated statistically significant enhancements in all three perceived capability facets (Z = -4.025, -3.535, and -3.536; p < 0.05). The study concludes that this collaborative inquiry model, supported by panoramic camera evidence, effectively improves TESs' ability to diagnose student learning problems and refine instructional activity designs.

Social media platforms are strengthening content moderation amid criticism over hate speech and fake news. Artificial intelligence can recognize offensive text and images across multiple languages, but it is not foolproof. AI systems exhibit bias inherited from human-trained data sets, struggle with evolving language contexts, and cannot determine intent—leading to errors such as flagging anti-hate posts or historic images. Consequently, human moderators remain essential, with companies like Facebook significantly expanding review teams. AI works best as an initial screening tool that prioritizes content and makes human moderation more efficient. However, the rapid pace of technological development continues to outstrip ethical and legal frameworks, creating a need for greater ethics expertise in the field.

Lobbyists for Connecticut municipalities asked Governor Malloy to reduce state mandates and allow local cost-control measures to ease the financial crisis. The Council of Small Towns and Connecticut Conference of Municipalities requested changes to the municipal retirement system, easier collective bargaining arbitration to promote regional cooperation, higher land-transfer fee retention, and prevailing wage threshold adjustments. Malloy acknowledged the six-week budget stalemate creates uncertainty. While CCM’s DeLong stated towns are not asking to be held harmless from state aid cuts, Senate President Looney called that claim inaccurate, stressing that municipal aid has divided lawmakers facing a $3.5 billion deficit.

Amazon received a patent for "directed fragmentation" of delivery drones. The system uses a constantly updating "fragmentation sequence" based on flight path, weather, and terrain data to jettison components over preferred locations such as bodies of water, forests, or open fields rather than populated areas if equipment malfunctions or unexpected conditions occur. Parts could be released using latches, hooks, springs, small explosive charges, or compressed gas. The sequence considers factors like replacement cost, weight, and air drag to alter the drone's descent trajectory. The patent does not guarantee implementation.

The address marks sixty years of stable government and peace with foreign nations. It reports that reciprocal port terms have been arranged with Great Britain, diplomatic ties with France have resumed, and strict neutrality has been maintained in European conflicts. The United States suppressed an unauthorized expedition against Cuba, declined to recognize a definitive German empire, and prepared to recognize Hungarian independence only if it were sustained. The speaker notes outstanding claims against Portugal, amicable relations with Mexico under the Guadalupe Hidalgo treaty, and the need for additional funds to survey the boundary. He recommends fostering relations with Pacific nations, amending laws to suppress the African slave trade, negotiating a treaty to protect a proposed Nicaraguan canal, and preventing foreign domination of the Sandwich Islands. Financially, he cites a deficit from the Mexican War, recommends borrowing and strict economy, and urges tariff revision and the adoption of specific duties. He supports creating an agricultural bureau, a branch mint in California, surveying and bringing public lands to market, and geological exploration of mineral deposits. He anticipates applications for statehood from California and New Mexico and recommends their admission if their constitutions meet federal requirements, while urging avoidance of sectional controversy. He also recommends increasing Army posts in the West, reorganizing the Navy, reducing postage to five cents, authorizing the Seventh Census, and upholding the constitutional separation of powers, concluding with a defense of the Union.

The passage describes methods and systems for manufacturing orthodontic appliances. The method includes measuring patient tooth positions, receiving tooth movement constraints, and measuring elements of malocclusion. A plurality of treatment plans is generated and branched based on measured malocclusions—such as openbite, molar and canine class II or III, posterior crossbite, bi-protrusion, and overjet—and on whether to perform corrections including bicuspid or incisor extraction or interproximal reduction. Interim final tooth positions are generated for each plan; clinically unacceptable plans may be discarded. Second malocclusion elements are measured in the interim positions, which are then modified to generate final positions. A treatment plan is selected, and a model of an appliance is generated for each stage. Instructions for fabricating the appliances are output, which may be executed via direct fabrication techniques—including stereolithography, selective laser sintering, or fused deposition modeling—or indirect fabrication such as thermoforming. A system comprising a processor and memory configured to perform these operations is also disclosed.

Tesla, Inc.’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2018, reports two operating segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. For the three months ended September 30, 2018, total revenues were $6.82 billion, net income attributable to common stockholders was $311.5 million, and basic earnings per share were $1.82, compared to a net loss of $619.4 million and basic loss per share of $(3.70) in the prior year period. For the nine months ended September 30, 2018, total revenues were $14.24 billion, with a net loss attributable to common stockholders of $1.12 billion and basic loss per share of $(6.56). As of September 30, 2018, total assets were $29.26 billion, total liabilities were $23.41 billion, stockholders’ equity was $4.51 billion, and cash and cash equivalents were $2.97 billion. The company adopted the new revenue standard ASC 606 on January 1, 2018, which decreased the opening accumulated deficit by $623.2 million. Total debt was $10.90 billion, and Tesla was in compliance with all financial debt covenants.

This study reports outcomes of COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) transfusion in 112 patients with hematological malignancies and virologically-documented COVID-19 included in a French monitored access program from May 2020 to April 2021. The cohort comprised 83 patients with B-lymphoid neoplasm, 10 with myeloid neoplasm, and 19 with multiple myeloma; 81 had received prior anti-CD20 or anti-CD19 therapy, and 98 had negative SARS-CoV-2 serology at transfusion. CCP transfusion was associated with decreased temperature, C-reactive protein, ferritin, and fibrinogen, and significantly increased PCR cycle threshold values by day 7. The 90-day overall survival was 64.9% for the whole cohort, 77.5% for B-lymphoid neoplasm, 20% for myeloid neoplasm, and 36.8% for plasma-cell neoplasm. In multivariable analysis, age over 70, high blood pressure, and severe COVID-19 were associated with lower survival, whereas previous anti-CD20 or anti-CD19 monoclonal antibody therapy was associated with better survival. In a propensity score-weighted analysis of B-lymphoid neoplasm patients pre-exposed to anti-CD20 therapy, CCP exposure was associated with a 40% to 63% decrease in mortality compared to a standard care cohort. The authors conclude CCP is particularly beneficial for B-cell lymphoid malignancy patients with prior B-cell depleting therapy who cannot mount a humoral response, while benefit was limited in myeloid and plasma-cell neoplasms.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated September 5, 2017, reporting the September 12, 2017 issuance of $5 billion of senior unsecured notes: $1 billion of 1.500% notes due 2019, $1 billion of 2.100% notes due 2022, $2 billion of 2.900% notes due 2027, and $1 billion of 3.750% notes due 2047. The notes were sold pursuant to a September 5, 2017 underwriting agreement and an April 29, 2013 indenture, with semi-annual interest payable beginning March 12, 2018.

This passage lists known issues with non-sequential numbers for the AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3. Detailed descriptions cover several issues: the PIT does not cancel an uncompleted latch command upon a read-back command; the GLIU debug port hangs the system; the PIT loads new count values immediately in mode 3; the XPIC clears the IRR bit late during AEOI, sending two interrupts; DMA rotating priority does not update correctly; the thermal alarm resides in the Work domain, preventing PMC self-recovery during Faulted Standby; and other sleep options require the Sleep Clock to be enabled in the PMC register even if disabled at the GPIO.

May Baxter-Thornton and Emma Lewis, survivors of child sexual abuse from Newport and Swansea, have been appointed to the victims and survivors panel of the Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse. They will advise the inquiry on reaching and listening to victims in Wales and ensuring their experiences inform its recommendations. The inquiry opened in Wales in November 2016.

The document is a compilation of news articles dated March 27–28, 2001. Viacom dropped its plan to split off Blockbuster due to a business turnaround and noted the termination of Blockbuster’s video-on-demand venture with Enron. President Bush named Patrick Wood III and Nora Brownell to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission; Wood may alter the agency’s approach to California’s power crisis, and an Enron official praised Texas’s market restructuring. Enron paid Chairman Kenneth Lay a $7 million bonus for 2000 performance. Enron’s Japanese venture, EnCom, submitted a plan to build an LNG-fired power plant in Aomori Prefecture, aiming for operations by 2007. In Dubai, a gas-import project involving Enron’s Dolphin Energy was described as essential for power and industry. In India, Enron and PowerGen withdrew bids for the Vijayanagar power project, while Enron Wind sought approval for a wind-power subsidiary; India’s central government also cited the Enron payment crisis when considering restrictions on states’ direct loans. Enron CEO Jeffrey Skilling said Texas was well-prepared for electricity deregulation, criticized California’s system, and stated that a 40 percent California rate hike would help reduce shortages while forecasting summer natural gas prices above $10 and 2001 company revenue of $160–170 billion. Texas’s deregulation pilot program was set to begin June 1, with Enron’s New Power spinoff signing up customers. A new U.K. electricity trading system began, with companies including Enron expected to benefit. Enron also joined other firms pressing the U.S. Export-Import Bank to let private lenders finance exports.

Beth Utton contends that health care is a fundamental right rather than a commodity, challenging Rep. Ken Buck's stance and urging Medicare for all to replace profit-driven private insurance. The Bittle tree, planted by Roanoke's first President Dr. David Bittle on Turbyfill Quad, stood for over 100 years before removal due to lightning and wind damage. For the College's 175th anniversary, Reverend Chris Bowen and George Arthur crafted its wood into the Bittle Tree of Life Cross for Antrim Chapel. The cross symbolizes the College's roots in Bittle's vision and future students.

This disclosure relates to illumination devices for 2D, 3D, and autostereoscopic displays, specifically imaging directional backlights employing waveguides to provide large-area illumination from localized sources. A display device includes a backlight with plural light sources; a directional waveguide having opposed first and second guide surfaces that guide input light and deflect it out through the first surface into optical windows dependent on source position; a transmissive spatial light modulator; input and output polarisers; at least one additional polariser; and at least one retarder arranged between the additional polariser and the input or output polariser. The retarder, which may include passive correcting retarders and/or a switchable liquid crystal retarder, reduces off-axis luminance to enhance privacy while substantially preserving head-on luminance and efficiency. Embodiments employ various retarder types including crossed A-plates, C-plates, and O-plates. A control system may synchronise the spatial light modulator, light sources, and retarder voltage to switch between privacy and wide-angle modes, temporally multiplex images to obscure stray light, or adjust for snooper location. The waveguide may comprise an optical valve with extraction features and a reflective end. Applications include automotive displays and multi-viewer configurations.

A Deloitte study shows rising consumer confidence in autonomous vehicles, with 49% of respondents now believing they will be unsafe compared to 73% last year. Over half trust the brands developing the technology, and 51% trust traditional car manufacturers over technology companies (21%) to implement it. Consumers still prefer engine-powered vehicles (73%) over electric (2%), citing driving range, price, and lack of charging infrastructure, though 37% would consider electric vehicles for lower ongoing costs. Customer experience remains important in purchasing decisions, and the UK government is launching a safety inquiry ahead of an expected rollout.

The document describes systems, methods, and apparatus for media playback and audio content identification. In an example method, a playback device receives digital data representing audio content, sends at least a portion of the digital data to an identification system configured to identify the audio content, receives information associated with the audio content from the identification system, sends the received information to a control device configured to control the playback device, and plays the audio content via one or more speakers electrically connected to the playback device by a wired connection. A control device may send a command to the playback device to retrieve such information while the playback device is playing the audio content, receive the retrieved information from the playback device, and display a representation of the received information or metadata retrieved from a metadata curating device at a network location indicated by the received information. The playback device may extract the digital data from various positions in an audio processing pipeline, including after decoding, sample rate conversion, or frequency segregation by a crossover, and may send data periodically or upon detecting a discontinuity. The described media playback system includes networked playback devices arranged in playback zones and zone groups, control devices with user interfaces for playback and zone management, and various audio content sources.

Electric Resistance Welding (ERW) transports vapor and liquid objects such as petroleum and gas under high and low pressure. ERW steel pipe uses hot-rolled coil with wall thickness controlled to ±0.2mm and burrs to 0.2–0.5mm, meeting API or GB/T9711.1 standards. It offers high production efficiency, low cost, and wide industrial and urban gas network use.

The Presidential Election Cycle theory posits that U.S. stock market performance follows a historical four-year pattern tied to presidential terms. According to Yale Hirsch and the Stock Trader’s Almanac, the pre-election year is historically the strongest, the election year is second best, and the midterm year is generally the weakest until the fourth quarter. Since 1952, the S&P 500 has averaged 12.5% in election years with an incumbent running, compared to -1.5% in open-field races. Midterm years typically see increased volatility. Policy uncertainty around elections particularly affects sectors like healthcare and energy, though analysts suggest impacts are often sector-specific rather than economy-wide. While backtests support the cycle as a seasonal pattern, the theory does not guarantee exact performance, and major shocks can disrupt trends. Investors are generally advised to remain invested and rebalance rather than react to election volatility.

New Jersey Governor Chris Christie signed legislation strengthening protections for people with developmental disabilities and increasing family involvement in their care. The bill was proposed after the 2007 death of Stephen Komninos in a group home. It allows twice-yearly unannounced state inspections, requires notification to families within two-to-eight hours of patient injuries, and requires biannual family meetings. The Department of Human Services is authorized to hire additional staff.

Intel's Management Engine (ME) is a microcontroller embedded in Intel CPUs that remains active when computers are off and connects to all peripherals. Researchers recently demonstrated a local exploit at BlackHat Europe enabling arbitrary code execution on the ME via physical access, such as with a USB stick; the ME runs the Minix OS and was previously closed-source. While some vendors like System76 and Dell offer methods to disable the ME, and the me_cleaner tool can trick it into thinking it has valid firmware while rendering it non-functional, there is no generic way to completely turn it off. The current exploit requires physical access, but concerns remain about potential future remote attacks over the network interface.

The Cleveland Browns have not ruled out taking Oklahoma quarterback Baker Mayfield with the No. 1 pick in Thursday's NFL draft, per ESPN. GM John Dorsey remains open to all options, and coach Hue Jackson said Sam Darnold, Josh Allen, Mayfield, and Josh Rosen remain in play for Cleveland.

Jefferies Group raised Ferguson Plc's price target to GBX 5,240 with a hold rating, while other analysts issued targets ranging from GBX 4,700 to GBX 5,600. The stock has an average Buy rating and price target of GBX 5,265.71. Shares rose 0.68% to GBX 5,200. Ferguson Plc, formerly Wolseley plc, is a Switzerland-based distributor of plumbing, heating, and building materials.

This qualitative literature review examines Mortimer J. Adler’s perennialist philosophy and its application to Christian education and global education management, engaging with posthumanist questions about technology, human limitations, and anthropocentric supremacy. Adler’s perennialism emphasizes eternal values, continuity of ideas, rational thought, and self-development through reasoning, rooted in Thomistic thought. He views education as cultivating full human beings rather than merely preparing children for employment, advocating democracy in learning and the enduring value of docility—defined as postponing judgment and submitting to authority for intellectual growth rather than natural slavery. The authors note Adler’s lack of gender differentiation, arguing women require external support to access education equitably. The study analyzes secondary research on global Christian education management, including family-based health interventions, spirituality in chronic disease, cross-cultural student agency, Christian school values in Bangkok, Kenyan institutional transformation, New Zealand diaspora disaster management, and Christian business ethics. The authors argue that Adler’s framework pushes education management beyond administrative systematization toward deeper perennialist values. They conclude that educational failure rests with teachers, parents, and the state—not children—and that sustainable learner development requires prioritizing eternal intellectual and moral values over instant achievement.

Nicola Sturgeon called Theresa May's snap June 8 election a U-turn and miscalculation, accusing her of exploiting Labour's disarray to advance a hard Brexit, deeper cuts, and a right-wing agenda. Sturgeon urged Scottish voters to reject the Conservatives and reinforce the mandate for a second independence referendum. SNP deputy Angus Robertson framed the election as a choice between the SNP and Tories, while Scottish Conservative leader Ruth Davidson said voting Tory would secure strong Brexit leadership and oppose another independence vote.

The MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 microcontrollers integrate an Arm Cortex-M0+ CPU operating up to 32MHz with instruction prefetch, a two-line I-cache, a 24-bit SysTick timer, and a nested vectored interrupt controller. The devices support five power modes—RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, and SHUTDOWN—and two power domains (PD1 for the CPU and high-performance peripherals; PD0 for low-power peripherals). The power management unit provides regulated core supplies, brown-out reset, and a core regulator. The clock module includes internal 32kHz and 32MHz oscillators and external clock inputs, generating MCLK, CPUCLK, ULPCLK, MFCLK, LFCLK, ADCCLK, HFCLK, and HSCLK. A DMA_B controller with two full-feature channels and one basic channel moves data between memory and peripherals without CPU intervention, and an event manager routes peripheral events to the CPU, DMA, or other peripherals. Memory includes flash with up to 100,000 program/erase cycles on the first 32KB (or entire device on 32KB variants) and SRAM that retains data in all modes except SHUTDOWN. Peripherals comprise up to 45 GPIOs with wake capability, IOMUX, a 12-bit ADC, temperature sensor, VREF, comparator, LFSS containing RTC and IWDT, CRC, three UARTs, I2C, SPI, IWDT, WWDT, RTC_B, and general-purpose and advanced timers with PWM and quadrature encoder support. Debug support includes a two-wire SWD interface and DEBUGSS with a mailbox and security features. Factory constants memory stores device identification and trim values. Application guidance recommends decoupling capacitors, an NRST pullup/pulldown, and crystal bypass capacitors. The September 2025 revision updated power modes, removed DGS32 package details, revised multiple specifications, and added the DEBUGSS section.

The invention relates to a method and apparatus for an optical waveguide display. Prior art waveguides suffer from a limited total field of view (TFOV) dictated by the angular range for total internal reflection (TIR); light injected outside this range escapes, and wavelengths different from a tuned wavelength diffract to angles that may not support TIR, reducing the FOV for those colors. The invention enhances the FOV by externally coating those waveguide surfaces against which guided light reflects internally with a material, such as a meta-material, having a refractive index substantially equal to or less than 1.0 (preferably the real part, and positive). This reduces the critical internal angle for TIR, allowing retention and guidance of light from wider input angles and/or a broader wavelength range. The apparatus comprises an optical waveguide with an input diffractive part (e.g., a Bragg grating) to diffract display light for TIR propagation, and an output diffractive part to diffract guided light for output; the diffractive parts may be mutually conjugated to reduce geometric distortion and chromatic dispersion. The meta-material may comprise a periodic array of unit cells containing a magnetic resonator between conductive meshes, with structural parameters optimized to achieve the desired low refractive index. Multi-layered waveguide structures with intermediate low-index layers can provide multi-color capability and protection. A corresponding method involves receiving and diffracting display light for guided TIR propagation along such a coated waveguide.

The author nearly died from sepsis in 2015 after scratching his hand on a nail. Sepsis—the body’s uncontrolled immune response to infection that causes organ failure—affects over 30 million people and kills an estimated 6 million annually. Symptoms include pale or mottled skin, breathlessness, shivering, muscle pain, and vomiting, requiring immediate emergency care. While anyone can develop sepsis, vitamin D deficiency increases the risk. There is no specific cure, though research on metformin and gene therapy targeting NF-kB shows promise. Global public awareness remains alarmingly low, diagnosis is difficult, and protocols like Sepsis6 are being introduced. The author concludes that greater awareness among the public and medical professionals is currently the most effective way to save lives.

Steve Yzerman and Coach Cooper discussed building the Lightning through patience, drafting, and developing home-grown talent, which they said is essential for sustained success under the salary cap. The paper proposes a face anonymization system for intelligent experimental education that protects student privacy while preserving the visibility of experimental instruments and operational techniques. Current generic methods are unsuited for scientific experiments because they can obscure fine or transparent apparatus and hand movements needed for evaluation. The authors introduce an enhanced YOLOv8 architecture, Multi-Scale Feature Fusion YOLOv8 (MSFF-YOLOv8), and a Contour-Adaptive Occlusion Refinement (CAOR) module for training data. CAOR dilates occlusion edges toward face centers to reduce misclassification of instruments and hands as face pixels. The pipeline incorporates BOTSort face tracking and Gaussian blurring, applying coarse processing to non-primary operators and fine anonymization to primary experimenters. A specialized dataset was created from 51 videos with 7,590 face labels and 5,240 instrument labels. Two new metrics, SOBA and OBR, measure blur accuracy and instrument mis-blurring. Results demonstrate that MSFF-YOLOv8 with CAOR achieves 96.02% SOBA accuracy and 22.67 fps at 1920×1080 resolution, outperforming original YOLOv8, SAM, and Edge-SAM while maintaining low OBR. The system effectively balances privacy protection with clear experimental observation.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says intellectual property is more complex for AI video than images because video feels more lifelike and creates stronger emotional resonance. Following viral unauthorized Sora videos featuring characters like SpongeBob and Pikachu, Altman said rights holders view video differently and want more granular control than for images. He announced OpenAI will give rights holders more granular control over character generation, and predicted companies will eventually want more of their content included in AI videos rather than less.

Stanley Furniture and La-Z-Boy are compared as small-cap consumer discretionary stocks across dividends, risk, valuation, earnings, analyst recommendations, and ownership. The lecture covers renewal theory and countable-state Markov chains. Three major theorems for renewal processes are reviewed: the strong law for renewals, which states that the limit of the number of arrivals divided by time equals 1/x̄ with probability 1; the elementary renewal theorem, which states that the expected value of renewals over time approaches 1/x̄ but is limited because expected values do not capture fluctuations; and Blackwell’s theorem, which for arithmetic inter-renewal intervals with span λ states that the limit of the expected renewals over an interval of length λ equals λ/x̄, meaning the long-term probability of a renewal at mλ approaches λ/x̄.

The professor then analyzes age and duration at a specific time for an arithmetic renewal process with span 1. The joint probability of age i and duration k is asymptotically the probability of an arrival at t−i multiplied by the inter-renewal probability mass function p_X(k), where k > i. Asymptotically, the probability of an arrival at time j, q_j, approaches 1/x̄. The marginal pmf of duration is k·p_X(k)/x̄, giving an expected duration of E[X²]/E[X]. The expected age is E[X²]/(2E[X]), though for integer-valued arithmetic processes this result differs by 1/2 from the sample-path average because the age can equal zero at integer times.

The lecture then defines recurrence for countable-state Markov chains: a state is recurrent if the probability of eventual return is 1. A random walk on the integers has state probabilities that spread outward and approach zero; for p = q = 1/2, return is certain but the expected return time is infinite. A birth-death chain is recurrent if p < 1/2, transient if p > 1/2, and null recurrent if p = 1/2.

First-passage time probabilities f_{ij}(n) are defined recursively. If the cumulative first-passage probability F_{jj}(n) approaches 1, state j is recurrent, and its returns form a renewal process. If the expected recurrence time is finite, the state is positive recurrent; if infinite, it is null recurrent. States in the same communication class share recurrence properties.

This lecture discusses auction theory and its real-world applications, including government procurement, Treasury bill sales, and online advertising. It analyzes the independent private values model, where bidders know their own values and are risk neutral. In a second-price sealed bid auction, bidding one's true value is a weakly dominant strategy, and expected seller revenue equals the expected second-highest value. The button auction, an oral ascending format, is strategically equivalent, with bidders dropping out at their true values. In a first-price sealed bid auction, bidders shade their bids below their values; the symmetric equilibrium bid equals the expected second-highest value conditional on winning. The Revenue Equivalence Theorem states that under symmetric independent private values, any mechanism awarding the good to the highest-value bidder while giving the lowest type zero surplus yields identical expected revenue and bidder utilities. The theorem does not hold when bidders are risk averse, values are correlated, or mechanisms use reserve prices or account for entry costs. Reserve prices should typically equal the monopoly price but may reduce welfare and deter entry. The lecture also covers common value auctions and the winner's curse, where winning signals that others had lower estimates, requiring rational bidders to shade bids accordingly. Finally, it summarizes Hendricks and Porter's empirical study of U.S. offshore oil drainage tract auctions, where asymmetric information leads to a severe winner's curse: safer, more valuable drainage tracts attract fewer bidders than wildcat tracts, and incumbents earn higher profits. The study's mixed-strategy equilibrium predictions—including zero expected profits for uninformed bidders and specific incumbent bidding behavior—are largely supported by auction data from 1959 to 1969.

An RSI(2) mean reversion strategy on QQQ enters when the two-day RSI is below 10 and exits when today's close exceeds yesterday's high. It returned 10.01% versus 6.39% buy-and-hold, performing well in the 2000-2002, 2008/09, 2018, and March 2020 bear markets. An Alberta Education survey of nearly 10,000 people, half teachers, found respondents want more emphasis on practical skills and basics in K-12 curriculum drafts, though some were confused by the documents' purpose. The BGF China Flexible Equity Fund, managed by Helen Zhu, offers combined access to onshore and offshore Chinese equities through a single flexible strategy. The long-only, concentrated portfolio holds 20–50 companies from over 3,300 onshore and 1,000 offshore stocks, targeting valuation differences and sector opportunities across capitalizations and factors.

This study investigates the perceptions and experiences of students in face-to-face tour guiding education (TGE) programs in Türkiye regarding Emergency Distance Education (EDE) during the COVID-19 pandemic. EDE is defined as the temporary transfer of face-to-face instruction to an online environment during a crisis. Through a qualitative phenomenological study of 81 students in Istanbul, using semi-structured interviews and questionnaires, thematic analysis identified seven key themes. Students largely found EDE insufficient for TGE due to inadequate vocational courses, lack of effective communication, and motivation problems. Word association tests showed students perceived both weaknesses—such as attention deficits, equipment issues, and lack of socialization—and strengths—such as cost savings and convenience—in distance TGE, whereas face-to-face TGE was viewed predominantly positively. Reported advantages of EDE included effective time management, the ability to review recorded lessons, location independence, and cost savings. Disadvantages included its inappropriateness for a practice-based profession, lack of motivation and communication, technical problems, and low attendance. Nearly 59.2% of students considered distance education practically insufficient for tour guiding, and 81.4% identified significant differences between the two modes, citing efficiency, socialization, concentration, unidirectionality, and self-expression. Despite this, 88.8% reported understanding distance courses. The study concludes that students prefer face-to-face TGE because the profession requires practical field experience and strong interpersonal skills, though they acknowledge some benefits of EDE. The authors suggest hybrid education could help resolve this dilemma and recommend evaluating pre-pandemic distance TGE programs separately from EDE outcomes.

The U.S. Department of State's Office of the Historian released the September 2022 ebook edition of *Foreign Relations of the United States, 1981–1988, Volume I: Foundations of Foreign Policy*. The FRUS series, established in 1861, documents major U.S. foreign policy decisions and diplomatic activity. The ebook offers full content, searchability, and offline access; document numbers are recommended over page numbers for citations. Under a 1991 statute, the series must provide a thorough, accurate, and comprehensive record published within 30 years, maintaining historical objectivity. Most sources are declassified and available at the National Archives.
In HS mode, the ADS7828 reads codes individually, stretching the clock LOW after the read-addressing byte until conversion completes. Use repeated START, not STOP, to stay in HS mode.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s 2015 Form 10-K reports that the company, incorporated in Delaware and headquartered in Seattle, Washington, trades on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under “AMZN.” As of the first quarter of 2015, its reportable segments are North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS). It serves consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, and content creators through retail websites, electronic devices, fulfillment services, AWS compute/storage/database offerings, and publishing platforms. The company employed approximately 230,800 full-time and part-time employees as of December 31, 2015, and has never declared or paid cash dividends.

For the year ended December 31, 2015, net sales were $107.006 billion, net income was $596 million, and net cash provided by operating activities was $11.92 billion. Total assets were $65.444 billion, and cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities were $19.8 billion. Net sales by segment were $63.708 billion for North America, $35.418 billion for International, and $7.880 billion for AWS. Inventory turnover was 8 and accounts payable days were 77.

The filing identifies numerous risks, including intense competition from a broad range of global competitors; significant strain from rapid expansion; international regulatory, tax, and operational risks, particularly in China and India; dependence on optimizing fulfillment networks and data centers; seasonality concentrated in the fourth quarter, which historically accounted for about 33% of annual revenue; potential data loss or security breaches; system interruptions; foreign exchange risk; inventory management challenges; key person dependency, particularly on CEO Jeffrey P. Bezos; pending tax proceedings with the IRS and a European Commission state aid investigation in Luxembourg; and various legal, payments, and product liability risks.

A December 6, 2000 McKinsey memorandum forwarded by Suzanne Nimocks updates international electric power sector privatization and restructuring from June through November 2000. Governments globally are opening generation markets to foreign investors, unbundling state-owned utilities, and introducing wholesale and retail competition, though some international players have shifted investments to less risky markets. In Europe, the EU Directive is spurring competition, unbundling, and consolidation, with country-specific progress on market opening, independent operators, and trading platforms. Central and Eastern European nations continue privatization and restructuring efforts linked to EU accession and IMF conditions. Asia-Pacific economies are reviving unbundling plans as demand recovers, though IPPs face ongoing PPA and guarantee challenges. Latin American privatization has slowed due to currency fluctuations, inflation, and drought impacts on hydro-dependent systems. African and Middle Eastern governments are increasingly opening to IPPs and exploring partial privatization, with several regional transmission link projects underway.

This study investigates the correlation between multilingualism and cultural awareness among 388 students across six Indonesian universities using an embedded mixed-methods design. Quantitative survey data collected in January–February 2024 measured variables including Multilingualism Competency, Multilingual Learning Process, Psychological Factors, Social Interaction, Cultural Knowledge and Communication, Cultural Practices and Participation, Sociocultural Context, and Capacity and Attitude towards Cultural Learning. Results indicate Indonesian is the dominant mother tongue (61.08%), Javanese, Bugis, and Makassarese are the most studied local languages, and English is the most studied foreign language (63.40%), followed by Korean and Arabic. Formal instruction prevails for national and foreign languages, while independent learning dominates local language acquisition. Pearson correlation analysis found significant positive relationships (p < .001) among all multilingualism variables, among all cultural awareness variables, and between every multilingualism and cultural awareness variable, notably between Multilingualism Competency and Sociocultural Context (r = 0.553) and between Social Interaction and Capacity and Attitude towards Cultural Learning (r = 0.523). Qualitative analysis identified strategies including educator training, technological support, cultural integration, intercultural collaboration, and inclusive content development. The authors conclude that multilingual competence significantly enhances cultural awareness and recommend integrating multilingual, culturally responsive approaches into Indonesian higher education policy and practice.

Jeong-Suk Cha, 77, physically strains to care alone for her son Alex, 48, who has cerebral palsy and spinal cord damage. Alex is on a wait list for a residential care bed—advocates call it a "50-year wait"—while a $100-million class-action lawsuit alleges Ontario negligently denies services to developmentally disabled adults through inconsistent wait lists. The South West LHIN lacks data on adults with complex needs seeking care; province-wide, 9,700 people wait for residential care. Alex's sister Jin advocates for him, managing limited personal support worker hours and detailed care instructions. The only alternative offered is long-term care with seniors, which Alex rejects. The family is publicly pushing for Ontario to provide more housing for adults with complex physical disabilities.

This paper proposes a methodology for trusting agents in digital business ecosystems to determine the probability of not achieving the full benefit of resources invested in interactions with probable trusted agents. To analyze risk, the trusting agent determines the FailureLevel—the probability and consequences of failure—across non-overlapping time slots in pre-interaction and post-interaction phases. The agent calculates an Amount Invested Curve (AIC) to represent the probability of net financial resources at stake throughout each time slot. Convolving the AIC with the trusted agent's FailureLevel yields the Factual Amount Invested Curve (FAIC), which shows the increased probability of net investment needed to achieve desired outcomes accounting for potential failure. The Loss of Resource Benefit (LORB) is the ordinate on the FAIC at the end of the AIC, indicating the probability that the trusting agent will not obtain the full benefit of its invested resources. This enables informed selection of trusted agents.

This ebook edition of the 1917 Foreign Relations of the United States Supplement 1, generated in May 2018 by the Office of the Historian, presents papers from the period of U.S. neutrality and beyond, covering Latin-American policy for the entire year, China and Siam until August 14, and Liberia after August 4. The edition offers full content with search and offline capabilities, maintains fidelity to the original print version, and recommends citing document numbers rather than page numbers. Editorial conventions include bracketed insertions for omissions or corrections, retention of parenthetical decoder suggestions from telegrams, and revised translations where necessary.

The Shuffle offense, originated by Bruce Drake at Oklahoma, is a predecessor to the Princeton, Flex, Hawk and Reverse Action offenses. It uses constant player movement in a rotating pattern to create high-percentage shots, eliminate defensive help and double teams, and draw big players away from the basket. Ideal for teams lacking height, it involves minimal dribbling and emphasizes passing, screening, spacing, and rebounding. The offense features sequential options built around rub cuts off post screens, with specific reads and counters for defensive actions such as chasing, switching, or denying. It also incorporates flash cuts to the middle and back cuts to exploit defensive overplay.

Data culture aligns organizations vertically through metrics linking actions to goals, and horizontally through common data models and transparent access. Digital leaders treat data culture as central, coordinating beliefs, values, and actions, while laggards show misalignment due to entrenched habits, skill gaps, and insufficient top-down focus. Changing mindsets is the hardest transformation challenge, yet laggards can transform and mature firms must keep evolving culturally. Organizations fit four patterns: "data novices" lack cultural and system changes; "insight ready" firms accept risk but lack analytical capabilities; "tech enabled" organizations have data and technology but discourage experimentation; and "data reliant" firms over-depend on data, discouraging critical thinking. Companies can build on their current pattern to develop a strong data culture.

SD Memory Cards contain User and Protected areas and are classified by capacity as SDSC (up to 2 GB), SDHC (up to 32 GB), and SDXC (up to 2 TB). Communication consists of command and response tokens transferred serially on the CMD line and data blocks transferred on DAT lines, with CRC protection and support for single or multiple block operations in 1-bit or 4-bit bus widths. Five Speed Classes (0, 2, 4, 6, 10) indicate minimum performance. UHS-I supports up to 104 MB/s via SDR50, DDR50, and SDR104 modes using 1.8 V signaling, entered through a voltage-switch sequence during initialization with CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, and CMD11. UHS-II provides additional modes such as FD156 and FD624, offering up to 624 MB/s over a secondary interface. Cards include registers such as CID, RCA, CSD, SCR, OCR, and SSR. Data operations encompass block read, write, erase, discard, and full user area logical erase (FULE), with write status signaled on DAT0. Write protection methods include mechanical, internal, and password lock; Card Ownership Protection (COP) and Force Erase Password (FEP) add further security controls. ROM cards are read-only and do not support write or erase commands. Advanced features include Command Queue, Cache, Self Maintenance, and Application Performance Class for random and sequential performance.
The building is praised as fantastic, with Philadelphia fans giving the home team an advantage. The player is calm, quiet, unbothered by physical play, and has been great all year.

The AEGEAN study randomized 1162 atrial fibrillation subjects to Primary Standard of Care (SOC; n=583) or an Additional Educational Program (n=579) to assess apixaban adherence via electronic monitoring. The primary endpoint—percentage of days with correct dosing at 24 weeks—showed no significant difference between groups (91.64% vs. 91.88%; p=0.8117). Mean compliance exceeded 95% at weeks 4, 12, and 24, and was over 94% at week 48 across all groups, with no significant differences in persistence or adherence at 48 weeks. Adherence declined significantly during weeks 12–24 and 24–48 versus earlier periods. Baseline characteristics, exposure, and doses were comparable. Safety outcomes, including adverse events, serious adverse events, bleeding events, and deaths, were similar across groups. The study concluded that adherence and persistence remained high through 48 weeks, but the additional educational program provided no added benefit.

Brunswick school board approved the first step to place a $4.67 million emergency levy renewal on the May ballot with no tax increase. It also approved up to $10 million in notes for a new middle school and improvements, and modified FY2018 appropriations for received grants. The superintendent thanked four donors. The board recognized Lisa Durichko after 12 years. The board entered executive session but took no action. The organizational meeting is January 8, with the regular meeting January 22.

The speaker acknowledged the opponent played better and his team did not play its game. He cited going down too early on Friesen's goal and losing track of a rebound. He said the team must use its speed, shoot more, and create net-front traffic. He praised opposing goaltender Patrick, dismissed time off as a factor, and admitted the team may have been nervous. He praised Jeff's strong game and stressed there are no excuses in the biggest series of their lives. GA10x (Ampere) GPUs feature a PCIe 4.0 interface providing up to 64 GB/sec of bandwidth. The GA102 GPU comprises seven Graphics Processing Clusters (GPCs), 42 Texture Processing Clusters (TPCs), and 84 Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs). Each GPC includes a Raster Engine, two ROP partitions containing eight ROP units each, and six TPCs. Each SM contains 128 CUDA Cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, one second-generation Ray Tracing Core, and 128 KB of L1/Shared Memory. The 384-bit memory subsystem includes 6144 KB of L2 cache.

SM architecture improvements double peak FP32 throughput to 128 operations per clock and increase combined L1 data cache and shared memory capacity by 33 percent over Turing, with double the shared memory bandwidth. Third-generation Tensor Cores are twice as powerful as Turing’s and support TF32, BF16, and Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity for up to 2x matrix multiplication speedups. Second-generation RT Cores double the ray/triangle intersection testing rate and add an Interpolate Triangle Position unit that accelerates ray-traced motion blur by up to 8x over Turing. Enhanced Async Compute allows RT Cores to process concurrently with graphics or compute workloads.

The architecture introduces GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling, delivering up to 936 GB/sec of peak bandwidth. NVIDIA RTX IO uses GPU-based lossless decompression with Microsoft DirectStorage to accelerate I/O and reduce CPU utilization. For data centers, the NVIDIA A40 offers up to 2x FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and 5x AI throughput compared to the Quadro RTX 6000, with 48GB of scalable memory. Ampere also supports HDMI 2.1, 8K60 displays, AV1 hardware decode via fifth-generation NVDEC, and improved encoding via seventh-generation NVENC.

This study examined relationships between placental biomarkers measured in the first and second trimesters and a composite proxy outcome of retained placenta and/or hemorrhage requiring blood transfusion (RP/PPH) using 2,192 nulliparous participants from the NuMoM2b dataset. Of the sample, 67 (3.1%) experienced RP/PPH. Using Kruskal-Wallis tests with a Bonferroni-corrected significance threshold of p=0.004, median second trimester levels of sFlt-1, soluble endoglin, β-hCG, inhibin A, and PAPP-A were significantly elevated in women with RP/PPH compared to those without; first trimester sFlt-1 and the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio were also significantly higher, while PlGF did not differ at either timepoint. When stratified by preeclampsia status, these second trimester associations remained significant among non-preeclamptic participants, but no biomarker significantly differed between RP/PPH and non-RP/PPH groups among preeclamptic women. The magnitude of biomarker change from first to second trimester differed by preeclampsia status in RP/PPH cases. The authors note limitations including the lack of direct blood loss measurement, the small RP/PPH case count, and the over-representation of adverse outcomes in the selected sample, and suggest that placental angiogenic biomarkers measured within the first 22 weeks may represent targets for PPH risk screening and pathophysiology research.

Patterns provide a shared vocabulary for distributed systems, enabling quick understanding, knowledge sharing, and learning. A common language prevents wasted time in arguments of "violent agreement" over naming, allowing focus on details and implementation. The "sidecar container" term in the container community exemplifies how shared definitions let practitioners immediately discuss solving problems.

Former Boynton Beach firefighter-paramedic Luis Garcia spent nearly $40,000 of his savings to purchase 800 doses of Narcan after his 2011 retirement. He travels Florida distributing free doses and training residents, business owners, and law enforcement on how to use the opioid overdose reversal drug. On February 3, 2018, Garcia gave away about 50 doses at the Treasure Coast Substance Awareness Coalition event in Stuart. This preprint presents a secondary analysis of the first year of COVID-19 vaccination implementation in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) from April 2021 to March 2022. By March 2022, only 16 of 26 provinces had begun immunization, with 5.7% of the population receiving at least one dose and 1.03% fully vaccinated. Coverage varied significantly by province, with Kasai Oriental reporting the highest full vaccination rate (6.91%) and Equateur the lowest (0.02%). Functional vaccination sites increased gradually but remained unevenly distributed, with Kinshasa consistently operating the most sites. Vaccination uptake was initially low, spiked in February 2022, then declined. More men than women were vaccinated in nearly all provinces. Among high-risk groups, 8,302 healthcare workers and 46,495 elderly individuals completed their primary series. The Janssen vaccine accounted for 48% of administered doses, followed by Moderna (25%) and Pfizer (17%). Compared to nine neighboring Central African countries, the DRC had the lowest performance: it received 11.48% of estimated doses needed for 70% coverage, administered only 8% of doses received, and vaccinated just 2% of its population with at least one dose. The rollout faced multiple challenges, including an initial halt of AstraZeneca vaccinations due to safety concerns, the introduction of additional vaccines in September 2021, competing disease outbreaks such as Ebola, severe health worker shortages, health worker strikes, logistical hurdles including expired doses, and difficulty reaching high-priority populations. The authors conclude that the first year showed mixed progress with significant health system gaps, emphasizing the need for continued investment, integration with primary healthcare, and community engagement to improve coverage.

Oversold stock markets typically produce strong short-term returns as prices mean-revert, but this does not predict long-term performance. Oversold conditions, defined as significant declines over a specific period, are often measured using indicators like the 3-day RSI. A backtest on the S&P 500 from 1985 using a strategy that bought when the 3-day RSI fell below 20 and sold when the close exceeded the previous day's high showed consistent short-term gains, with an average profit of 0.64% per trade, a 75% win rate, and a max drawdown of 26%. However, this mean-reversion tendency was weaker before 1990 and is not guaranteed.

The concept of social capital gained academic prominence in the late 1980s through James Coleman and was later popularized by Robert Putnam, who used it to explain economic and political disparities between northern and southern Italy. Putnam’s 1990s book *Bowling Alone* linked declining civic group participation to American social problems, sparking widespread academic and policy interest. Two definitional debates exist: Putnam emphasizes civic group membership, while others emphasize “generalized trust,” which a 1996 study linked more directly to economic growth. Scholars also distinguish “bridging” social capital (across groups) from “bonding” social capital (within groups). Putnam’s research further indicates that ethnic diversity does not help increase social capital, a finding he reported without much enthusiasm or publicity and which has been cited by nationalist groups.

In United States v. Watson and O’Hearn, the First Circuit dismissed the government’s interlocutory appeal for lack of jurisdiction under 18 U.S.C. § 3731. The government sought review of district court orders denying a continuance and a renewed continuance, requested because the INS had inadvertently deported key witness Anthony Spera to Italy before he could testify. The district court denied the motions based on the case’s age, potential Speedy Trial Act violations, the government’s institutional negligence in causing the witness’s unavailability, and the likely six-to-twelve-month delay to obtain foreign deposition testimony; it also denied leave to depose Spera abroad as moot. The First Circuit held that § 3731 authorizes government appeals only from orders suppressing or excluding evidence or their practical equivalent. Because the orders were case-management rulings focused on preventing further trial delay rather than on the admissibility or exclusion of evidence, they fell outside § 3731’s scope, and any incidental effect on the government’s ability to present evidence was insufficient to support jurisdiction.

This patent application, a continuation of U.S. Ser. No. 15/898,212, discloses systems and methods for localizing position and orientation of objects in augmented reality. It describes head-mounted AR display devices with stacked waveguides, sensors, and processors that present virtual content within the ambient environment. To address latency and accuracy challenges in tracking head pose and handheld objects, the system employs electromagnetic tracking with compact field emitters and sensors integrated into headsets, belt packs, and controllers, fused with inertial measurement units, cameras, and depth sensors. Techniques include time-division multiplexing, dynamic transmission coil tuning, noise cancellation for audio interference, and vision-based simultaneous localization and mapping for pose estimation. The application also describes methods for sharing virtual content between users via activation gateways and a passable world model utilizing cloud and local processing resources.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture introduces RT Cores in each Streaming Multiprocessor to accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing, enabling real-time ray tracing approximately 10 times faster than Pascal GPUs. Turing also incorporates Tensor Cores that power NVIDIA NGX, a deep learning stack providing AI-based graphics features such as Deep Learning Super-Sampling, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez; NGX is not supported on pre-Turing architectures. The architecture introduces Mesh Shading with Task and Mesh Shaders to eliminate CPU draw call bottlenecks and increase real-time object counts by orders of magnitude. Variable Rate Shading allows dynamic shading rate adjustments per 16x16 pixel region to optimize performance through Content Adaptive Shading, Motion Adaptive Shading, and Foveated Rendering. Texture Space Shading decouples visibility and appearance sampling, enabling reuse of shaded texels across frames and views. Multi-View Rendering supports drawing up to four views per pass, expanding Pascal’s Simultaneous Multi-Projection capabilities. Turing enhances VR via VirtualLink/USB-C, MVR, foveated rendering, and RT Core-accelerated VRWorks Audio. The architecture encompasses the TU102, TU104, and TU106 GPUs; the TU104 powers products including the GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000, while the TU106 powers the GeForce RTX 2070. Turing enables a Hybrid Rendering model combining rasterization, ray tracing, AI, and simulation, with performance measured by the RTX-OPS workload-based metric. The architecture also supports bindless Constant Buffer Views and Unordered Access Views, Tier 2 resource heaps, and advanced ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections.

SOS baseline disruptions push wing ball handlers toward corner or baseline checkpoints to deny middle penetration and weakside reversals. The three defensive actions are Straight, where the on-ball defender smothers the handler at the checkpoint; Base Go I, an automatic trap inside the baseline checkpoint by the on-ball and low Helpside I defenders with teammates rotating into Triangle I; and Base Go Red, a predetermined early sideline trap used briefly to change game tempo. For side screens above the free throw line, the defense executes an aggressive contact switch; below the free throw line, it aggressively traps the ball handler before the screen is set, with specific rotations for passes out of the trap, skip passes, and low post passes. All Out SOS Disruption double-teams the point guard before any side screen is set, forcing the offense into a freelance situation, with secondary traps available on base rolls. All rotations occur as the ball leaves the passer's hands.

This work introduces scalable Boltzmann Generators (BGs) that use a local flow architecture to sample equilibrium ensembles of large crystalline materials. Unlike prior global approaches that scale poorly, the proposed method employs graph neural networks and augmented coupling flows to learn coordinate transformations based on local environments. This enables linear scaling, drastically reduces training costs, and allows models trained on small systems to transfer accurately to systems exceeding 1000 atoms. The approach supports energy-based training without requiring samples from the target distribution and achieves significantly higher effective sample sizes than global architectures. The authors demonstrate accurate generation of equilibrium configurations and computation of absolute Helmholtz and Gibbs free energies for diverse systems, including Lennard-Jones and Stillinger-Weber potentials (monatomic water, silicon, and germanium). The models can be conditioned on thermodynamic states, simulation box shape, and interaction parameters, facilitating efficient evaluation of phase stability and phase diagrams, such as the silicon temperature-pressure coexistence line. The study establishes local BGs as a computationally efficient and transferable tool for large-scale materials simulation.

The present disclosure relates to techniques for low-latency scalable gate control in time-aware networks (TANs) and time-sensitive applications (TSAs), configuring multiple TSAs to share a physical network link, and time-aware energy-efficient network communication. TANs rely on the Precision Time Protocol (PTP) and generalized PTP (gPTP) to synchronize clocks across time-aware systems (TASs) within a domain, with a grandmaster instance selected by a best master clock algorithm (BMCA) distributing time via relay instances. For scheduled traffic, IEEE 802.1Qbv defines transmission gates per traffic-class queue controlled by a gate control list (GCL) that schedules open and closed states via operations such as SetGateStates, Set-And-Hold-MAC, and Set-And-Release-MAC.

Conventional TSN network interface controllers (NICs) implement the GCL in dedicated on-chip memory, resulting in large silicon area, high power consumption, and long programming times that exceed short industrial cycle times. The described NIC architecture instead stores the GCL in host memory and maintains a small prefetch buffer in the MAC. During operation, a dedicated channel prefetches GCL entries into the buffer; the MAC scheduler parses the entries to identify upcoming queue openings and fetches corresponding data payloads ahead of time. This direct-memory approach reduces NIC memory requirements and power, supports sub-nanosecond scheduling resolution, and allows the GCL to be programmed within a cycle using alternating memory banks. To simplify configuration when multiple talker applications share one physical interface, a complex end station presents itself to centralized network management as a virtual switch connected to multiple virtual simple end stations, each with a single talker. The centralized manager configures the virtual switch, and the end station applies that configuration to its physical network interface and internal workload scheduling to limit interference between applications.

TQQQ options are available in both European and American styles, with various expiration dates and strike prices. Trading carries a high degree of risk because options are leveraged speculative products, so investors should employ risk management techniques such as stop loss orders, diversify their portfolios, avoid investing more than they can afford to lose, and backtest strategies before committing capital. The minimum amount of money required depends on the broker. Typical trading costs include commissions, contract fees, and slippage. Profits are generally subject to capital gains tax, though specific implications depend on individual circumstances and jurisdiction. The fair value of an option can be estimated using the Black-Scholes model, and performance analysis should incorporate backtesting alongside fundamental and technical analysis. Regulations related to option trading in TQQQ include minimum capital requirements, maximum leverage limits, margin call rules, and hedging rules.

University at Albany chemists synthesized manganese diboride, a stable compound over 20% more energetic by weight and roughly 150% more energetic by volume than aluminum in solid rocket boosters. Its energy derives from a strained, deformed atomic structure created by heating the material to 3,000°C in an arc melter and rapidly cooling it. The compound combusts only when exposed to an ignition agent, making it safe for rocket fuel and potentially reducing fuel storage space to increase payload capacity. The boron-based structure also shows potential for catalytic converters and plastic breakdown. Led by Michael Yeung, the study by Doane et al. marks the first successful synthesis of pure manganese diboride, a compound hypothesized since the 1960s.
