A gap is a price level untraded between the previous close and the next open, most frequently occurring overnight due to news or imbalances. Gaps are classified as common, exhaustion, runaway, breakaway, and others. Gap trading strategies were once highly profitable, but increased competition and computing power have significantly reduced profitability, especially in major indices. Small gaps are more likely to fill than large ones; S&P 500 E-mini data over 25 years shows same-day fill rates of approximately 59–61% for 0.1% gaps, 42–43% for 0.5% gaps, and 28–33% for 1% gaps, with bearish gaps filling slightly more often due to the market’s upward bias. Traders can fade gaps or follow them, but robust strategies require quality data, additional filters, and careful backtesting to avoid curve-fitting. Simple day trading backtests often yield negative or marginal returns, though some overnight swing trading strategies show modest profitability. Gaps occur in all time frames and asset classes, but opportunities may be better outside popular indices. Predicting gaps before they happen is considered nearly impossible.

A review of 10 trials involving 77,917 participants at high risk for cardiovascular disease, published in JAMA Cardiology, found that omega-3 fatty acid supplements did not significantly reduce the risk of heart disease death, nonfatal heart attacks, strokes, or artery procedures, providing no support for American Heart Association guidelines that recommend supplements for patients with prior coronary heart disease. While slight risk reductions were observed, the differences were too small to rule out chance. Limitations included wide variation in trial designs and a lack of data on participants’ smoking status and cancer history. Physicians not involved in the study noted that the supplements are inexpensive, safe, and may offer other health benefits, and advised that people already taking them should not stop.

Schools require comprehensive pedagogical renewal because society is changing rapidly and learners are fundamentally different. The Net generation—Millennials, Generation Z, and Generation Alpha—acquires knowledge differently, necessitating a shift from digital to generative pedagogy. Technological advances have created two intertwining worlds, physical and cyber, alongside biological and artificial intelligence. Learning environments have evolved from Internet 1.0 to 4.0, and education has moved toward blended and non-formal models. In generative pedagogy, generative artificial intelligence acts as a teacher's colleague rather than merely a tool. Historical waves of technological change, from the steam engine through the digital age, have culminated in the current sixth wave of generative AI. While educators initially resisted AI, acceptance is growing. Generative AI will drastically transform education, raising fundamental questions about the teacher's role, the value of educational content, and assessment. Teachers will no longer be the sole carriers of knowledge but will increasingly focus on affective domains, developing relationships and values, as humans and generative AI operate in symbiosis.

The Mid Screen offense involves a larger player screening for a smaller ballhandler. To avoid post mismatches, the NBA prefers "Show & Recover," where the screener's defender temporarily stops the ballhandler before recovering, while teammates help and deny passes. "All Out SOS Disruption" alternatively traps the ballhandler before the screen, forcing freelance play and requiring immediate rotations, pass denials, and SOS defensive principles upon matching up.

ChatGPT is an OpenAI AI that can help traders generate ideas, code technical indicators and strategies, perform sentiment analysis, and create trading algorithms. AI pattern trading offers speed and adaptability but faces risks from unpredictable markets and algorithmic biases.

Cell2Text is a multimodal generative framework that converts single-cell RNA sequencing profiles into natural language descriptions of cellular identity, tissue origin, disease associations, and active pathways. It combines a frozen Geneformer encoder that outputs gene-level embeddings with a lightweight adapter projecting into the semantic space of an instruction-tuned language model decoder (Meta-Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct or Gemma3-4B-it), avoiding the information loss of traditional cell-level pooling and the rigidity of classification heads. Trained on a newly constructed dataset of one million cells from CELLxGENE enriched with ontology and pathway annotations, the model achieves high semantic fidelity and strong lexical overlap in generated text. In evaluations, Cell2Text outperforms baseline classifiers—including a linear head on Geneformer and LightGBM—on cell type, tissue, and disease prediction, and demonstrates competitive pathway identification despite not being explicitly optimized for it. An ontology-aware PageRank similarity metric further shows that its predictions maintain high biological relevance even when incorrect, indicating robust understanding of hierarchical cell type relationships.

This study investigated whether intranasal and oral oxytocin (OT) selectively enhance pleasantness and neural responses to gentle stroking touch targeting C-touch (CT) fibers versus medium pressure massage targeting non-CT fibers, and whether effects are mediated peripherally. In a double-blind, placebo-controlled study, 171 healthy participants received intranasal OT, oral (lingual) OT, or placebo. Behavioral ratings, functional near-infrared spectroscopy recordings of the orbitofrontal cortex (OFC), posterior superior temporal sulcus (pSTS), and somatosensory cortex (S1), physiological measures, and plasma OT concentrations were collected. Both intranasal and oral OT increased plasma OT levels and selectively enhanced pleasantness ratings for gentle stroking touch but not medium pressure massage. Neural activity in the medial OFC, mediolateral OFC, and pSTS in response to gentle stroking was similarly enhanced by both administration routes, with OT prolonging neural responses. Classification analyses distinguished OT groups from placebo but not intranasal from oral OT. Mediation analyses indicated that post-treatment plasma OT concentration changes fully mediated the behavioral effects. The findings support the conclusion that exogenous OT selectively facilitates CT-fiber-mediated social touch via peripheral-mediated routes, with similar efficacy for intranasal and oral administration.

The passage describes a smart gateway platform for industrial Internet of Things applications, which is a continuation of U.S. patent application Ser. No. 16/384,106. The platform stores model templates associated with industrial business objectives, with each template defining relevant data inputs and relationships between them based on domain expertise. Through a user interface, a model template is selected and its generic data inputs are mapped to data tags of industrial devices. The platform customizes the model based on these mappings, collects data values from the specified tags, normalizes the data, and appends modeling metadata according to the relationships defined by the template to yield structured data. This structured data is then sent to an artificial intelligence analytics system. By leveraging encoded domain expertise to select and pre-model only relevant data subsets, the platform reduces data storage and processing overhead compared to conventional unconstrained big data approaches. The system supports smart data types such as State, Rate, Odometer, and Event, and can organize data according to hierarchical asset models. Analytics may be performed at multiple levels—including device, edge, and enterprise or cloud levels—and can produce actionable insights, recommendations, notifications, or control outputs aimed at achieving the desired business objective.

A study published in Nature and led by UT Austin researchers warns that hundreds of built and proposed hydroelectric dams in the Amazon basin may severely harm ecosystems and alter regional climate patterns from Central America to the Gulf of Mexico. The 428 proposed dams, including 140 built or under construction, threaten to trap nutrient-rich sediments that sustain wildlife, floodplains, and the largest South American mangrove region, while impacting rainfall and storm patterns. Researchers introduced the Dam Environmental Vulnerability Index (DEVI) to assess these risks, identifying the Marañon, Ucayali, Madeira, and Tapajós rivers as highly vulnerable. The Madeira River, with the highest DEVI values, already shows a 20 percent sediment decrease from existing dams. Scientists caution that the cumulative impact of all planned dams could significantly change Atlantic sediment flows and hinder the regional climate.

Traditional deterministic motion planners that rely on the most recent world map generate oscillating trajectories in unstructured environments due to inconsistencies from sensor noise, occlusions, and incomplete observations. This work presents a multi-hypothesis planning approach integrated into the KEASL search space that computes edge costs using multiple temporally sampled world maps, treating the most recent map as the primary collision-free hypothesis while using prior maps to guide search. The paper introduces four methods: Valid in Every Hypothesis (VEH), which requires collision-free validity across all maps but is overly conservative; Per-Edge Hypothesis (PEH), which reroutes around obstacles per expansion but is computationally impractical; Goal-Edge Hypothesis (GEH), which defers rerouting until an expansion reaches the goal; and Goal-Edge Graph Revision Hypothesis (GEGRH), which adds a graph revision step to focus search on hypothesis divergence points. Experiments on 221 planning problems from field tests with an unmanned ground vehicle compare single-hypothesis, VEH, and GEGRH planning using two and three successive environment maps. GEGRH achieved lower planning times and path durations than VEH, with the performance gap widening when using three hypotheses. The results demonstrate that explicitly reasoning about perception uncertainty through temporally sampled hypotheses in deterministic graph search yields more robust and efficient trajectories.

The volume documents Secretary Shultz's bureaucratic struggle against the NSC to implement the four-part agenda of NSDD 75 and maintain U.S.-Soviet dialogue during 1983–1985, despite opposition from officials such as Secretary Weinberger and flashpoints including the SDI announcement, the KAL 007 downing, INF deployments, and the Able Archer exercise. Spartan Race Inc., founded in 2010 by Joe De Sena, is the world’s largest obstacle course race provider. The obstacle course racing industry grew rapidly beginning around 2010 but experienced slowing participation by 2015. Spartan offers competitive, timed races of varying lengths and had expanded to roughly 130 events across 25+ countries with one million global participants by 2016. While race fees constitute the majority of revenues, the company has diversified into sponsorships, merchandise, television broadcasting, the "Spartan: Ultimate Team Challenge" show, a Daily Burn training program, SGX trainer certifications, and international licensee royalties. The ADS7828 SAR converter is sensitive to glitches on power, reference, ground, and digital inputs during conversion. Clean, well-bypassed power requires a 0.1µF ceramic capacitor placed close to the device, with a 1µF to 10µF capacitor added if the +VDD connection impedance is high. The external reference input has no inherent noise rejection, so supply noise and ripple appear directly in digital results, and line-frequency variation is difficult to remove. The GND pin should connect to a clean analog ground away from digital processors. The passage also contains Texas Instruments product status, material, RoHS, marking, moisture sensitivity, mechanical dimension, and legal disclaimer information.

This patent continuation incorporates prior applications and a sequence listing. It provides targeted cancer assay panels (bait sets) and methods for early cancer detection through analysis of differentially methylated regions in cell-free DNA (cfDNA). Because whole-genome bisulfite sequencing is cost-prohibitive and most genomic regions lack robust cancer-specific signals, the invention employs targeted oligonucleotide probes—numbering from hundreds to tens of thousands and designed with minimal off-target binding—to enrich for converted cfDNA fragments corresponding to genomic regions, including those set forth in Lists 1-8, that contain CpG sites differentially methylated in cancer versus non-cancer samples. Differentially methylated regions are identified based on counts of anomalously methylated fragments in cancer and non-cancer subjects, using p-value rarity and methylation thresholds. The enriched fragments are sequenced, and a trained classifier evaluates the resulting feature vectors to determine cancer presence, stage, or type. The description also details methods for designing such panels, hybridization capture enrichment, classifier training using hypomethylated and hypermethylated fragment data, and subsequent treatment with anti-cancer agents.

Some embodiments provide a packet processing pipeline for reconfigurable hardware switches. The switch includes ingress and egress pipelines, each having a parser, a match-action unit (MAU), and a deparser. For each packet, the parser separates header data from the payload and populates a primary packet header vector (PPHV) with header fields that may be matched or modified by the MAU, and a secondary packet header vector (SPHV) with the remaining header fields. The parser sends the PPHV to the MAU, which processes the packet through multiple match-action stages, and delivers the SPHV and payload directly to the deparser, bypassing the MAU. The deparser reassembles the packet using the processed PPHV from the MAU, the unprocessed SPHV from the parser, and the payload. The parser classifies fields based on packet header values and configuration data from a control plane compiler and configurator. This separation conserves MAU resources and enables deeper packet parsing without increasing the data volume sent to the MAU. The compiler generates configuration data, including parse graphs and flow graphs, to program the parser and MAU.

The lecture reviews Poisson processes, which can be represented by IID exponential interarrival times, arrival epochs, or the counting process N(t), and possess stationary and independent increments. The probability mass function for N(t) is Poisson with parameter λt. The professor explains that combining independent Poisson processes yields a Poisson process with a rate equal to the sum of the individual rates, while splitting a Poisson process with an independent Bernoulli switch produces independent Poisson subprocesses. These properties are applied to a last-come-first-served queue. Non-homogeneous Poisson processes are discussed, where a time-varying rate λ(t) means arrival counts over intervals remain Poisson with mean equal to the integrated rate, though interarrival times are no longer exponential. Conditioning on N(t)=n, the arrival epochs have the same distribution as the order statistics of n uniform random variables on [0,t], with joint density n!/t^n. The lecture ends by describing a paradox: a randomly chosen time t is more likely to fall in a longer interarrival interval, so the mean interval containing t exceeds the standard mean interarrival time 1/λ.

The buy-and-hold strategy is a passive, long-term investing approach where investors purchase stocks or ETFs and hold them for many years or decades, selling only when necessary. It focuses on long-term growth potential while ignoring short-term market fluctuations, contrasting with active trading. The strategy aligns with the Efficient Market Hypothesis and can be applied to growth, value, or index investing via individual stocks, diversified portfolios, or passive funds. Patterns for distributed systems allow developers to learn from prior work, establish shared vocabulary, and build reusable components. The text presents single-node and multi-node container patterns for constructing reliable, scalable systems.

Single-node patterns involve tightly coupled container groups sharing resources. The sidecar pattern augments an application container—adding HTTPS to legacy services, synchronizing dynamic configuration, or providing monitoring—without modifying the original application. The ambassador pattern brokers external interactions, enabling client-side routing to sharded backends like Redis, service discovery across deployment environments, and request splitting for experimentation. The adapter pattern standardizes interfaces for cross-cutting concerns, allowing integration with monitoring systems like Prometheus, log aggregators like Fluentd, and custom health checks without altering application containers.

Multi-node patterns support loosely coupled microservices, which improve team autonomy and independent scaling but complicate debugging. The replicated load-balanced service pattern deploys identical stateless instances behind a load balancer, using readiness probes and session affinity for reliability and scale. Caching layers improve performance and can enforce rate limiting, while SSL termination secures external traffic. The sharded service pattern partitions large stateful datasets across shards to increase capacity; sharded caches improve memory utilization but risk performance degradation on shard failure. Replicated sharded caches combine both patterns for fault tolerance. Requests are routed to shards via deterministic, uniform hashing functions.

The Death Cross occurs when a short-term moving average, typically the 50-day, crosses below a long-term moving average, typically the 200-day. It is a lagging indicator that attracts media attention as a signal of potential short-term weakness. Backtests on the S&P 500 from 1960 show lower returns than random periods in the short term (less than 30 days), but long-term returns are positive and in line with long-term averages. Selling at a Death Cross and reentering at a Golden Cross—the opposite signal—produces returns in line with long-term averages with less drawdown. Buying at a Golden Cross and selling at a Death Cross yields a 7% CAGR, slightly less than buy-and-hold, but with less time in the market and lower drawdowns. Buying at a Death Cross and selling at a Golden Cross produces poor returns. While it may cause premature exits, the Death Cross serves as a defensive tool to reduce drawdowns and limit losses.

The document provides PCB layout guidelines for the UC1825B-SP. A dedicated power ground section should handle high di/dt currents, while analog and VREF circuitry connect to the signal ground; both VCC and VREF require low ESR/ESL ceramic bypass capacitors. On multilayer boards, a ground plane should separate power and signal planes, and switching current loops must curl in the same direction to reduce radiated EMI. This study investigates first-phase left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF-1) as an echocardiographic index for assessing coronary heart disease (CHD) severity and recovery after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Unlike traditional LVEF, which often remains normal in early CHD, LVEF-1 measures early systolic volume change and is sensitive to early cardiac dysfunction. In 207 patients undergoing coronary angiography, LVEF-1 decreased significantly as coronary artery stenosis severity increased, while LVEF showed no significant difference among groups. LVEF-1 demonstrated a strong negative correlation with the Gensini score and BNP, and logistic regression and ROC analysis identified it as an independent predictor of moderate and severe stenosis with higher diagnostic value than global longitudinal strain, E/e', LVEF, or LVDd. In 82 patients who underwent PCI, LVEF-1 increased significantly by postoperative day 4, whereas LVEF did not; multivariate analysis showed that higher Gensini scores and larger stent diameters independently predicted greater LVEF-1 improvement. The authors conclude that LVEF-1 is a valuable, sensitive clinical indicator for evaluating cardiac dysfunction caused by coronary stenosis and for assessing early myocardial recovery following revascularization.

For participants without prior BNT162b2, immune responses against the Beta variant one month after Dose 2 of BNT162b2SA were comparable to those seen after Dose 2 of BNT162b2 against the original strain.

In Phase 1, a few participants had a temporary drop in lymphocytes one to three days after Dose 1 of BNT162b1 or BNT162b2, with counts returning to normal by six to eight days. Injection site reactions and systemic events were generally well tolerated, mostly mild or moderate in severity, and resolved after a short time. The 100-µg dose of BNT162b1 was stopped after Dose 1 because of reactions, and 30 µg BNT162b2 was selected for Phase 2/3. Few participants in Phase 2/3 left the study due to medical problems, and most problems were mild or moderate. Serious medical problems were rare; no single serious medical problem occurred in at least 1% of participants in any group, and researchers did not believe these were related to the study vaccines. No participants died in Phase 1, and deaths during Phase 2/3 were not believed to be caused by BNT162b2. No participant died in Phase 3 among those who had not previously received BNT162b2 before receiving BNT162b2SA.

The TPS7H500x-SP series are radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, usable in buck, flyback, forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies. The TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5002-SP allow programming two independent dead times via 10 kΩ to 300 kΩ resistors from PS and SP to AVSS; floating these pins sets an 8 ns minimum dead time. The TPS7H5003-SP has a fixed 50 ns dead time. Leading edge blank time is fixed at 50 ns for the TPS7H5003-SP and programmable via a 10 kΩ to 300 kΩ resistor from LEB to AVSS for other devices; LEB cannot be left floating. Synchronous rectifier outputs are disabled during soft start.

Pulse skipping activates when the COMP pin is below 0.3 V at the clock rising edge and the prior duty cycle was less than 25%, preventing minimum on-time issues; synchronous rectifier outputs remain on during pulse skipping if soft start has ended. With a 50% duty cycle limit and both primary outputs active, pulses are skipped equally to maintain volt-second balance. Maximum duty cycle is configurable on the TPS7H5001-SP, TPS7H5002-SP, and TPS7H5003-SP via the DCL pin: connection to VLDO allows 100%, floating allows 75%, and AVSS limits it to 50%. The TPS7H5004-SP supports only a 50% limit. Only the TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP support the 50% limit with active OUTB/SRB.

Current sensing occurs at CS_ILIM, where the signal is compared to COMP/2 with a 150 mV offset. A resistor from CS_ILIM to AVSS sets PWM and overcurrent protection; exceeding the 1.05 V threshold initiates hiccup mode. In hiccup mode, cycle-by-cycle limiting charges the HICC capacitor (minimum 3.3 nF recommended) with 80 µA until 0.6 V, stopping switching and discharging soft start. A 1 µA current then discharges HICC to 0.3 V before soft start reinitiates. The FAULT pin triggers shutdown if it exceeds 0.6 V for 0.4–1.4 µs; recovery follows when the pin falls below 0.5 V and a delay of roughly 15 switching cycles elapses.

Slope compensation is set with a resistor from RSC to AVSS; the recommended value equals the inductor falling slope. Frequency compensation uses Type 2A or 2B networks from COMP to AVSS. Thermal shutdown stops switching above 175 °C and resumes below 160 °C.

An example synchronous push-pull converter with GaN FETs at 500 kHz uses a 205 kΩ RT resistor, 10 kΩ and 1.4 kΩ feedback resistors for 5 V output, 20.5 kΩ dead-time resistors, 49.9 kΩ for LEB, a 33 nF soft-start capacitor (~7.5 ms), a transformer turns ratio of 2.5 and 40 µH primary inductance, 170 V primary and 80 V secondary GaN FETs, a 0.47 µH output inductor, at least 1.3 mF output capacitance (2.3 mF used for single-event transient mitigation), a 7.5 Ω current-sense resistor, a 3.3 nF hiccup capacitor, compensation components of 40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, and 47 pF, and a 102 kΩ slope-compensation resistor.

The controllers operate from 4 V to 14 V with a minimum 0.1 µF bypass capacitor from VIN to AVSS. Layout guidelines include routing feedback away from magnetics, minimizing switch-node area and high di/dt loops, connecting analog and power grounds at a single point, placing bypass and compensation capacitors close to the controller, and keeping high-dv/dt output traces away from sensitive pins.

The passage describes patent applications concerning engineered adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors for muscle-targeted gene delivery. It discloses compositions and vector systems comprising targeting moieties that include n-mer motifs—such as RGD or non-RGD peptide sequences—inserted into specific external regions of AAV capsid proteins (including AAV1–AAV9, rh.74, and rh.10) to confer muscle cell specificity, increased potency, and reduced immunogenicity. These engineered viral particles are associated with cargoes including therapeutic transgenes, antisense oligonucleotides, CRISPR-Cas systems, and mini- or micro-dystrophin genes for treating muscle diseases such as muscular dystrophies, cardiomyopathies, and neuromuscular disorders. The background states that conventional recombinant AAVs primarily infect the liver, necessitating high, toxic doses for other tissues, and notes differing responses between mouse and primate models. The disclosure includes selection of capsid variants in mice using muscle-specific promoters (CK8 and MHCK7), identifying sequences with high muscle mRNA expression. Data indicate that selected MyoAAV variants transduce mouse and human muscle cells more effectively than AAV9, utilize integrin heterodimers as receptors, and can correct Duchenne muscular dystrophy mutations in mdx mice. Also described are related polypeptides, particles, cells, pharmaceutical formulations, and methods of administration.

The passage compares stocks and bonds as investment instruments for growing net worth. Stocks represent ownership in a company, have historically been the best-performing asset class, and may provide dividends, but they carry significant risk of capital loss, making diversification essential. Bonds represent loans to issuers, typically offer fixed interest payments and maturity dates, and are generally less risky than stocks, with bondholders paid before shareholders in bankruptcy. Historical backtests indicate stocks outperform bonds over time, but a mixed portfolio—such as 60% stocks and 40% bonds—reduces volatility and drawdowns, though the ideal allocation depends on individual circumstances like retirement proximity. Sovereign bonds often mitigate losses during stock market crashes, though exceptions occur, while corporate bonds may face credit risk during recessions. The passage also describes seasonal strategies, including “Sell in May and go away” and “Investing only in Winter,” which involves shifting investments to countries experiencing winter months; backtests showed the winter strategy did not perform as expected.

A study of 124 individuals with borderline resectable or locally advanced pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) found no association between pre-treatment serum indole 3-acetate (3-IAA) and chemotherapy response or overall survival. Participants from the NORPACT2 cohort donated blood before chemotherapy, and 35 provided a second sample 2–4 months later. Despite prior research linking 3-IAA to improved chemotherapy response in metastatic PDAC, this study found no statistically significant differences in 3-IAA concentrations by CT response, CA19-9 decline, surgical resection, or survival quartiles. Cox models showed no significant association between 3-IAA and survival (HR=0.93, p=0.52; adjusted HR=0.87, p=0.28). The authors suggest the earlier findings may not extend to non-metastatic PDAC due to differences in tumor load, functional status, and tumor biology, and recommend validating the association in distinct metastatic cohorts before clinical intervention.

Researchers from McGill and the University of Toronto developed a model reframing gaslighting as a learning process using prediction error minimization (PEM). The model explains how manipulators exploit trust by behaving surprisingly, attributing the target's surprise to epistemic incompetence, and repeating this until the target doubts their reality. Lead author Willis Klein states anyone trusting the wrong person could be victimized. Future research may examine how attachment styles or trauma affect susceptibility and validate the model to improve support for victims.

Archival documents detail President-elect Reagan’s 1980 transition, including a November 21 Foreign Policy Advisory Board meeting with members such as Allen, Baker, Kissinger, and Weinberger, and a December 22 State Department final report by Robert Neumann’s team under Abshire and Timmons. Ronald Reagan declared his 1976 Republican presidential candidacy on November 20, 1975, challenging President Ford. In his announcement, Reagan cited concerns about the economy, government, foreign energy dependence, declining military superiority, and unresponsive leadership, and called for a government that returns power to the people.

This work addresses domain shift in neuroimaging, where technical and population differences across datasets degrade machine learning model performance. The authors propose a transfer learning pipeline using Simple Fully Connected Neural Networks pre-trained on the large UK Biobank dataset and fine-tuned on smaller target datasets (OASIS-3, IXI, ABIDE) for age and sex prediction from structural MRI. They demonstrate that features learned on UK Biobank are reusable across scanners and datasets despite domain shift, particularly when pre-training and target tasks match. The proposed method significantly outperforms classical elastic net regression and training from scratch, improving state-of-the-art results. The performance gains are attributed to actual feature reuse rather than merely favorable weight scaling. While fine-tuning only the classifier is effective, fine-tuning the full model generally yields further improvements when sufficient target data is available; with very small datasets, classifier-only fine-tuning may be preferable to avoid overfitting. Transfer learning also accelerates training convergence. The authors suggest that UK Biobank can serve as a foundational neuroimaging resource for transfer learning, analogous to ImageNet in computer vision, though challenges remain regarding scanner coverage and disease-specific applications.

This study introduces the first large-scale, publicly available Turkish dataset for citation intent classification, comprising 2,650 annotated citation sentences extracted from 723 Computer Science research articles using a five-category Web of Science scheme (Background, Basis, Support, Differ, Discuss). The authors benchmarked Large Language Models including GPT-4o and Gemini via In-Context Learning and manual prompting, then applied the DSPy framework for automated prompt optimization, achieving 86.5% accuracy. To mitigate model inconsistencies, they developed a stacked ensemble meta-model using XGBoost, which achieved a final accuracy of 91.3%. Key challenges identified include severe class imbalance favoring the Background category, semantic difficulty in distinguishing Support from Differ, and inter-run prediction instability by LLMs. Future directions include addressing imbalance through hierarchical classifiers, synthetic data generation, and incorporating broader contextual features.

Research by Prof. Ross Levine and co-authors in an NBER paper shows easier credit conditions lead businesses to invest more in pollution reduction. This work introduces an edit distance between constructible $\mathbb{R}^d$-persistence modules, defined via categories of finite join-semilattices and grids. The main result (Theorem 4.1) shows that the interleaving distance on finitely presented $\mathbb{R}^d$-persistence modules can be realized as this edit distance. The proof relies on clarifying a connection between the Galois connection, free presentations, and the interleaving distance, together with a multi-parameter adaptation of the easy-edit lemma. As a consequence, an invariant is stable under the interleaving distance if and only if it is stable under a single edit (Corollary 4.4). These findings provide an order-theoretic viewpoint on the interleaving distance and extend earlier one-dimensional isometry results to arbitrary dimension $d$, facilitating the exploration of stable invariants for multi-parameter persistent homology.

This article advocates for a sociocultural, ecological perspective on English language education policy in Asian state education systems, arguing that classroom practices must be understood within broader social, cultural, and educational contexts. It examines the persistent divergence between policy intentions and actual outcomes, particularly the socio-economic and urban-rural inequalities in achievement when Communicative Language Teaching (CLT) and Common European Framework of Reference (CEFR)-based proficiency targets are mandated. Drawing on examples from Malaysia and Thailand, the article demonstrates that standardized targets often fail to account for limited English use in society, the dominance of national languages, teachers' and students' actual proficiency levels, large classes, mixed abilities, exam pressures, and inadequate resources. Teachers frequently resort to using the first language and teacher-centered methods rather than mandated communicative approaches, not due to deficiency but as contextually appropriate responses to classroom realities. The article concludes that policymakers must align curriculum goals with local sociolinguistic and socio-educational realities rather than imposing top-down, Western-derived frameworks, as failure to account for "realities on the ground" perpetuates inequality and poor outcomes.

Plasmodium vivax hypnozoites cause relapsing bloodstream infections, but the biology of activation remains poorly understood. This study applies the mathematically simplest “exponential clock” model—in which each hypnozoite activates independently at a constant rate with no external triggers—to detailed longitudinal data from the 1993–1995 SPf66 vaccine trial, which followed 1,344 children aged 2–15 years daily for 21 months on the Thailand-Myanmar border. The within-host model incorporates stochasticity in mosquito bites, sporozoite batch sizes, sporozoite destiny, and age-dependent anti-disease immunity. Fitting the model to 2,504 symptomatic P. vivax episodes yielded a hypnozoite activation rate of 1/171 day⁻¹ (half-life 118 days), a mean successful sporozoite inoculum of 6.9, an average of 2.7 hypnozoites per bite, and a relapse-to-primary infection ratio of 3.4 (~75% relapses). The analysis found higher-than-expected vivax rates after P. falciparum monoinfections treated with artesunate monotherapy, compatible with external triggering, while mefloquine provided approximately one month of post-treatment prophylaxis against emerging relapses. The fitted model quantified overdispersion in relapse risk and informed the potential utility of serological testing to guide radical cure.

Researchers identified natural bacteria strains from grape plant leaves that degrade guaiacol, a key compound causing smoke taint in wine from wildfire smoke. In lab tests, the bacteria nearly eliminated guaiacol within 96 hours but did not consume other similar smoky compounds, indicating additional strains are needed to fully address smoke taint. Scientists identified the gene responsible for this degradation. This microbial approach could offer a more targeted alternative to current mitigation techniques like activated charcoal, which can remove desirable wine components. The finding is significant as wildfire seasons increasingly affect wine regions, costing California and Oregon winemakers over $3 billion in 2020.

The TPS7H500x-SP controllers use fixed-frequency peak current-mode control. The CS_ILIM pin receives a transformer primary-side current signal, and the COMP pin voltage (referenced as COMP/2 with a 150 mV offset) sets the peak current limit. A resistor from CS_ILIM to AVSS enables PWM generation and overcurrent protection; when the pin voltage reaches the 1.05 V nominal threshold, the device enters hiccup mode. Equations are provided for calculating the sense resistor in forward and buck topologies. In hiccup mode, cycle-by-cycle limiting charges the CHICC capacitor with an 80 µA current until it reaches 0.6 V, at which point switching stops. A 1 µA restart current then discharges CHICC to 0.3 V before soft-start resumes; a minimum 3.3 nF capacitor is recommended. The FAULT pin accepts external protection signals, and if its voltage exceeds 0.6 V for longer than the 0.4–1.4 µs minimum pulse width, the controller shuts down, delays for approximately 15 switching cycles after the fault clears, and restarts. Slope compensation, set via a resistor on the RSC pin, is recommended at 1× the inductor falling current slope to prevent subharmonic oscillation above 50% duty cycle. Frequency compensation uses a transconductance error amplifier with Type 2A or 2B networks. Thermal shutdown activates above 175°C and resumes below 160°C. The devices are radiation-hardness-assured current-mode PWM controllers, used with external gate drivers, for space-grade DC-DC converters such as buck, flyback, forward, and push-pull, supporting switching frequencies up to 2 MHz. An example synchronous push-pull GaN design at 500 kHz details component selections for the oscillator, feedback, dead time, leading-edge blanking, soft-start, transformer, GaN FETs, output inductor, output capacitance, current sense, hiccup, slope compensation, and frequency compensation. The controllers operate from a 4 V to 14 V input and require a minimum 0.1 µF bypass capacitor. Layout guidelines recommend routing sensitive traces away from power magnetics and switch nodes, minimizing high-frequency loops, connecting analog and power grounds at a single point, placing bypass and compensation components close to the controller, and connecting the CFP backside metalization to AVSS.

The Education Department held the first round of negotiated rule-making talks on the One Big Beautiful Bill Act’s student loan changes despite a federal shutdown. The meetings concluded Friday and are scheduled to resume November 3–7, with many provisions taking effect July 1, 2026. Participants expressed cautious optimism, but no consensus was reached.

The most contentious issue was defining which postbaccalaureate programs qualify as professional, allowing students to borrow up to $200,000 rather than $100,000. Department officials initially limited this to 10 programs listed in the Higher Education Act, then proposed a one-year expansion for programs designated as professional before July 4, 2025. Committee members questioned the proposal’s clarity, legality, and adequacy.

The shutdown limited public transparency because the department could not post meeting materials online, leaving committee members to share updates themselves.

Talks also addressed repayment plans. After July 1, 2026, almost all income-driven repayment plans will end, except for a new Repayment Assistance Plan and grandfathered Income-Based Repayment. Existing borrowers must apply for Income-Based Repayment before the deadline, but advocates noted the process is convoluted—especially for Parent PLUS borrowers—and urged simplification without success.

A study of 451,355 UK Biobank participants examined cardiovascular biomarkers and outcomes stratified by ethnicity-specific body mass index (BMI) categories and diabetes mellitus (DM) status. Among participants, 5% had DM. In those without DM, overweight and obesity were associated with higher carotid intima-media thickness, arterial stiffness, and cardiac contractility index, and lower left ventricular ejection fraction; these relationships were diminished in the DM group. Within each BMI class, DM was associated with adverse cardiovascular phenotypes, particularly in the normal-weight group. Over follow-up, incident myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, and cardiovascular mortality increased across BMI categories in both DM and non-DM groups. However, normal-weight participants with DM had higher cardiovascular mortality than obese participants without DM (adjusted incidence rate ratio 2.81 versus 1.84). The authors conclude that obesity and DM are additively associated with adverse cardiovascular biomarkers and mortality risk. Although adiposity metrics correlated more strongly with cardiovascular biomarkers than diabetes-oriented metrics, both correlated weakly, suggesting other factors underpin the high cardiovascular risk of normal-weight diabetes.

NVIDIA Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 27, 2019, reported third-quarter revenue of $3.01 billion, net income of $899 million, and diluted earnings per share of $1.45, representing year-over-year decreases of 5%, 27%, and 26%, but sequential increases of 17%, 63%, and 61%. For the nine months ended October 27, 2019, revenue was $7.81 billion and net income was $1.85 billion, down 18% and 48% from the prior year. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $9.77 billion as of October 27, 2019, up from $7.42 billion at the end of fiscal 2019, with net cash provided by operating activities of $3.30 billion for the nine-month period. The company entered an agreement on March 10, 2019, to acquire Mellanox Technologies Ltd. for approximately $6.9 billion in cash; Mellanox shareholders have approved the transaction, and U.S. and Mexican regulatory approvals have been received, but closing remains subject to European and Chinese regulatory approval and is expected in early 2020. GPU business revenue for the quarter was $2.57 billion, down 8% year-over-year, while Tegra Processor revenue was $449 million, up 10%. By market platform, Gaming revenue was $1.66 billion (down 6%), Data Center revenue was $726 million (down 8%), and Professional Visualization revenue was $324 million (up 6%). NVIDIA intends to return $3.0 billion to shareholders by the end of fiscal 2020 and has paid $292 million in dividends in the first nine months; it does not expect to repurchase shares prior to closing the Mellanox acquisition. The company adopted a new lease accounting standard on January 28, 2019, recognizing $470 million in operating lease assets and $500 million in operating lease liabilities. Long-term debt had a net carrying amount of $1.99 billion. NVIDIA is subject to pending securities class action and derivative lawsuits alleging false or misleading statements related to channel inventory and the impact of cryptocurrency mining on GPU demand.

In People v. Yuk Bui Yee, the defendant moved to sever 13 counts stemming from six alleged extortion incidents at three Chinese restaurants, claiming the offenses were joinable only under CPL 200.20(2)(c), which permits the court to order separate trials in the interest of justice. The People contended the counts were properly joined under CPL 200.20(2)(b), under which severance is barred if proof of one offense would be admissible as evidence in chief at a trial of another. The court grouped the offenses by restaurant and applied the "Molineux rule" to evaluate whether evidence of the separate incidents was admissible to establish a common scheme or plan, identity, or intent. It found no common scheme linking all three groups but determined that the defendant’s repeated use of Mandarin, demands for money on behalf of his "brothers," and claims of membership in the "Eagles" gang established a modus operandi so individual that evidence of each incident was probative of his identity and intent in the others. The court held the offenses were properly joinable under CPL 200.20(2)(b) and denied the motion to sever.

This preprint presents cross-sectional and longitudinal analyses of arterial stiffness and renal function in 67,060 adults from China. Cross-sectional results showed a negative association between eGFR and brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity (baPWV). Longitudinally, higher baPWV predicted incident chronic kidney disease (CKD) risk, while lower baseline eGFR predicted increased arterial stiffness risk. Cross-lagged panel analysis demonstrated that the path coefficient from baseline eGFR to follow-up baPWV was significantly greater than the reverse path, indicating that kidney function decline precedes changes in arterial stiffness. The study concludes that arterial stiffness is associated with CKD, and a decrease in eGFR appears to precede an increase in baPWV.

This case study examined long-term use of spinal cord stimulation (SCS) to restore somatosensory feedback during walking in a woman with a unilateral transtibial amputation. SCS leads implanted near the T12–L2 vertebral levels delivered stimulation during the prosthetic limb’s stance phase. Compared to Day 30, walking at Day 63 without SCS showed increased activation in the residual tensor fasciae latae and vastus lateralis, significantly reduced co-contraction of the residual knee antagonists (vastus lateralis and biceps femoris), and increased pelvic obliquity range-of-motion and pelvic drop. At Day 63 with SCS, residual tensor fasciae latae activity increased further and knee co-contraction decreased slightly more. These changes indicate improved dynamic stability at the knee and hip; some improvements persisted without active stimulation, suggesting a potential rehabilitative effect, though additional participants are needed for conclusive results.
Severe weather season has started slowly across North Texas, Oklahoma, and Kansas. Oklahoma has recorded zero 2018 tornadoes, nearing a 1962 record, though activity may increase in May.

This preprint presents SCIseg, an open-source deep learning method for automatic three-dimensional segmentation of the spinal cord and T2-weighted hyperintense lesions in traumatic spinal cord injury MRI scans. The retrospective study included 191 patients with 231 scans from three sites, encompassing heterogeneous scanners, resolutions, orientations, treatment strategies, and lesion etiologies. The model was trained in three phases using a region-based strategy and active learning on a total of 196 scans, then evaluated on independent test sets against manual segmentations and existing spinal cord toolbox methods. SCIseg 3D achieved robust spinal cord segmentation and significantly outperformed its 2D counterpart on lesion segmentation, with active learning improving agreement between automatic and manual lesion volume and length estimates. The model generalized to degenerative cervical myelopathy lesions. Quantitative MRI biomarkers derived from automatic predictions showed statistically comparable correlations with clinical scores—including pinprick, light touch, and lower extremity motor scores—to those derived from manual masks, with no significant differences between methods. Limitations include training on a single T2-weighted contrast and treating lesions as single entities rather than separating edema and hemorrhage.

Athletes Unlimited (AU) is a professional sports startup launched in 2020 by Jon Patricof and Jonathan Soros to create innovative, player-driven women’s leagues. Beginning with softball and expanding to volleyball, lacrosse, and basketball, AU operates without team owners. Instead, Player Executive Committees govern each league, making decisions on competition format, schedules, uniforms, and policies. Players receive base compensation, performance bonuses, and shares in a Profit Participation Plan.

AU’s model features short, five-week seasons at a single venue per sport, weekly team drafts, and individual leaderboards that reward both personal and team performance. The organization is structured as a Public Benefit Corporation under a “Mission Equity” capital structure, where investor returns are capped and at least 50% of surplus profits are directed to players or mission-aligned programs. AU emphasizes treating athletes as professionals, offering benefits like childcare, parental leave, and pregnancy accommodations, while supporting social impact initiatives such as the Power in My Voice campaign and Athlete Causes Program.

The company secured broadcast partnerships with ESPN, CBS, Fox, and others, raised $30 million in 2022, and was named one of Fast Company’s most innovative sports companies in 2023. Despite its rapid growth, AU faces questions about long-term economic sustainability, scaling, and competition in an increasingly crowded market for women’s sports.

This patent application describes methods and systems for allocating wireless resources in a multiple basic service set identifier (BSSID) network. A first access point associated with a transmitted BSSID (Tx BSSID) allocates random access resources to stations belonging to a multiple BSSID set—including non-transmitted BSSIDs (non-Tx BSSIDs)—using association identifier (AID) values based on a group AID mapping contained in a partial virtual bitmap of a traffic indication map (TIM) element. The first AP transmits a trigger frame containing AID values identifying, for random resource unit (RU) allocation, a group of stations, a specific BSSID, a group of BSSIDs, or all stations in the set. When the trigger frame is transmitted from the Tx BSSID, its transmitter address is set to the MAC address of the Tx BSSID; an AID value set to a non-Tx BSSID index allocates random RUs to stations associated with that non-Tx BSSID, an AID value of zero allocates random RUs to Tx BSSID stations, and an AID value of 2045 allocates random RUs to all unassociated stations. When transmitted from a non-Tx BSSID, the transmitter address is set to the BSSID index, an AID of zero allocates random RUs to that non-Tx BSSID's stations, and an AID of 2045 allocates random RUs to all unassociated stations. Management frames may include a multiple BSSID element and a random access parameter set (RAPS) element. Prioritizing random RU allocation among BSSs based on parameters such as the number of stations, traffic types, and quality of service may increase utilization and efficiency of the shared wireless medium.

At an Amherst College event honoring Robert Frost, the speaker affirms that graduates of privileged institutions bear a responsibility to serve the public interest rather than merely private gain, particularly given the nation’s staggering domestic and foreign challenges. He pays tribute to Frost as both artist and American, noting that art strengthens the nation by questioning power, establishing human truth, and preventing arrogance. The speaker argues that artists must remain free from propaganda and ideology to follow their vision of truth. He envisions an America that balances military strength with moral restraint, wealth with wisdom, and power with purpose; preserves natural and architectural beauty; rewards artistic achievement; expands cultural opportunities for all citizens; and commands global respect for its civilization as well as its strength. He concludes that through Frost’s life and work and the college’s mission, America’s hold on the planet has increased.

Exchange shopping is restricted to Soldiers, Airmen, and their families, but Army Regulation 215-8/Air Force Instruction 34-211 (I) allows anyone to dine at Exchange restaurants and buy grab-and-go items from Express locations for on-installation consumption. Those seeking full benefits should contact their local Exchange manager.

The team remains calm and level-headed heading into Sunday's game, planning to stick with the same recipe from clinching games by building throughout the series and wearing opponents down. Players emphasized mental toughness, focusing on controllable factors, and noted the need for a better start. They praised their goalie's performance and highlighted collective group effort. They acknowledged the special home atmosphere and dangerous opponent, stating they will continue being aggressive and forcing opponents into uncomfortable plays.

Tight ends remain crucial in modern football, serving as versatile offensive weapons who run routes and block. Their combination of size, strength, and athleticism creates matchup problems for defenses, particularly in the red zone. The name derives from early football when wide receivers were "Ends," while those tight to the formation became "tight ends." Also called TEs or H-Backs, they require skills in catching, blocking, and route running, typically standing 6'3" to 6'8" and weighing 240-270 pounds. Notable players include Tony Gonzalez, Rob Gronkowski, Antonio Gates, and Shannon Sharpe. Their versatility allows offenses to diversify schemes, making them valuable multifaceted weapons.

The CAT offense is a simple, successful strategy against traps, double teams, and zone presses, using a 2-1-2 spread alignment and sharp passing with a skilled triple threat post player at the middle. Key rules include baseline back cuts when the ball goes to the middle, post rolls to the basket when the ball goes to a corner, an opposite corner skip pass rule when trapped, and sparing use of dribble penetration to escape trouble. If the defense quits double teaming, hold the ball or flow directly into penetrating spread offenses.

"Look Good … Feel Better" will hold free May 8 event at Dignity Health Sierra Nevada Memorial Hospital Diagnostic Imaging teaching women in cancer treatment appearance-related coping techniques. Info: lookgoodfeelbetter.org. 1-800-227-2345.

Guangdong Province is experiencing China's largest chikungunya outbreak, with over 4,000 confirmed cases since late July, heavily concentrated in Shunde District, Foshan, and appearing in Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Hong Kong, and Macao. Transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, the disease causes fever and joint pain but does not spread person-to-person. Local authorities are encouraging elimination of standing water to reduce breeding grounds. The outbreak highlights how climate change, urbanization, and global travel facilitate mosquito-borne diseases. The WHO has issued new clinical guidelines and strengthened its Global Arbovirus Initiative, while experts call for expanded genomic surveillance.

The authors introduce SoDaDE (Solvent Data-Driven Embeddings), a transformer-based fingerprint for solvent representation trained via data augmentation on the small Spange solvent property dataset, which contains 12 properties across 191 solvents. Addressing the need for better solvent modeling highlighted by the Catechol Benchmark, the model processes sequences combining solvent type, ChemBERTa fingerprints, and randomly shuffled property-value pairs, using causal and attention masks to predict masked numerical values while ignoring missing data. Validation and test sets were constructed to match solvent types present in the Catechol dataset. SoDaDE achieved a normalized validation MSE of 0.107 and outperformed Gaussian process, random forest, and averaged baseline models on solvent property prediction, attaining an average test MSE of 0.170. When applied to the Catechol Benchmark for predicting reaction yields, SoDaDE achieved MSE values of 0.0026 with fine-tuning and 0.0029 without, surpassing existing methods including ACS PCA representations, DRFPs, fragprints, Spange descriptors with imputation, RXNFP, and ChemBERTa on both single-solvent and mixed-solvent tasks. The results demonstrate that effective, generalizable solvent fingerprints can be created from small datasets.

The Nov. 13, 2000 issue of True Orange reports that Texas football will host nearly all of its 19 committed recruits and most remaining targets, including Tommie Harris and Derrick Johnson, for official visits Dec. 15-17. CTC-Pak urged prioritizing health over business on World No Tobacco Day, noting tobacco causes 16% of NCD deaths and cardiovascular diseases 19% of total deaths in Pakistan. They demanded enforcement of tobacco control laws, delayed 85% pictorial health warnings, and higher taxes, criticizing the government's low-tax third tier for increasing consumption and youth accessibility. The lecture introduces causality and stability for discrete-time linear shift-invariant (LSI) systems. A stable system produces a bounded output for any bounded input, which for LSI systems requires the unit sample response to be absolutely summable. A causal system has an output depending only on present and past inputs, which for LSI systems requires the unit sample response to be zero for n less than 0. While stability is generally desirable, causality is not always required. The lecture then discusses linear constant-coefficient difference equations (LCCDEs). A 0th-order LCCDE reduces to a convolution sum where the unit sample response equals the input coefficients. For higher-order LCCDEs, boundary conditions are needed to uniquely specify the system; different conditions yield causal or non-causal solutions with differing stability properties. Finally, the lecture introduces the frequency response H(e^jω), defined as the sum of the unit sample response multiplied by e^(-jωn). Complex exponentials are eigenfunctions of LSI systems, and the frequency response is periodic in ω with period 2π. The next lecture will cover the Fourier transform.

The lecture introduces plasma radiation as a natural diagnostic, covering self-emission from radio frequencies to gamma rays. It presents the radiation transport equation, dI/ds = j − αI, where spectral radiance I changes along a path s due to emissivity j and opacity α, all functions of frequency. Defining optical depth τ as the integral of opacity along the path, the solution for exiting intensity includes both attenuation of initial radiation and integrated emission subject to absorption. For a homogeneous plasma, this simplifies to terms involving e^(−τ). In the optically thin limit (τ ≪ 1), radiation passes through with little change; in the optically thick limit (τ ≫ 1), intensity approaches the blackbody function B(ν,T), leading to Kirchhoff’s law (j/α = B). The lecture identifies free-electron emission mechanisms such as Bremsstrahlung and cyclotron radiation, and bound-electron processes like recombination. It distinguishes gradual absorption from a cut-off, where a refractive index less than zero causes sudden, non-oscillatory, evanescent decay. Finally, it establishes that only accelerated charges produce propagating far-field radiation, while constant-velocity charges do not; calculating plasma emission requires solving particle motion and integrating over the velocity distribution.

MMFP-Tableau is a bioinformatics platform developed at the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia for the Mitochondrial Medicine Frontier Program to integrate siloed clinical and research data for primary mitochondrial disease. The platform uses Alteryx to extract, transform, and load data from the EPIC electronic medical record via the Clarity data warehouse, REDCap research databases, and Excel spreadsheets into a centralized server. Tableau provides a secure, web-based visualization interface with role-based access for approved clinicians and researchers. The system integrates data from over 2,000 individuals, including demographics, clinical notes, laboratory results, medications, genotypes, patient-reported outcomes, and biospecimen information. It enables real-time querying and dynamic visualization for both individual patient and cohort-level analyses. Demonstrated use cases include clinical cohort characterization, clinical trial eligibility determination, genotype-phenotype mapping, medication trend visualization, and risk factor delineation. The platform employs Human Phenotype Ontology and ICD-10 codes to standardize phenotypic data. By centralizing previously siloed data, MMFP-Tableau supports precision medicine, clinical care optimization, research discovery, and therapeutic development. Limitations include the inability to parse some non-discretized electronic medical record data, external institution data, certain imaging data, and scanned PDFs, as well as occasional server performance issues. The framework is designed to be scalable and generalizable to other clinical and research populations.

NVIDIA's Blackwell architecture introduces ninth-generation NVENC with 5% improved AV1 and HEVC quality, 4:2:2 H.264 and HEVC encoding support, and an AV1 Ultra High Quality mode for an additional 5% gain. The GeForce RTX 5090 includes three encoders and two decoders, boosting export speeds by over 50% generationally. A sixth-generation NVDEC provides 2x faster H.264 decoding and 4:2:2 decode support. DisplayPort 2.1b enables up to 80 Gbps bandwidth, supporting 8K at 165Hz or 4K at 480Hz with DSC using a DP80LL certified cable. Max-Q power efficiency improvements include advanced power gating, separate voltage rails for GPU cores and memory, accelerated frequency switching that adjusts to workloads 1000x faster, and low-latency sleep states that are 10x faster to enter than Ada, enabling up to 50% power savings in workloads like small language model inference. DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation to create up to three additional frames per traditionally rendered frame using a 40% faster AI model that consumes 30% less VRAM, alongside enhanced Flip Metering. It also transitions to transformer-based AI models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, improving temporal stability, motion detail, and lighting quality. Blackwell debuts neural shaders through the Cooperative Vectors API for DX12 and Vulkan, enabling technologies such as Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. The architecture comprises the flagship GB202 GPU in the RTX 5090 with 92.2 billion transistors and 24,576 CUDA cores; the GB203 GPU in the RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti with 45.6 billion transistors and 10,752 CUDA cores; and the GB205 GPU in the RTX 5070 with 31 billion transistors and 6,400 CUDA cores.

The head and shoulders pattern is a technical analysis formation of three price rallies and two pullbacks, with the second rally highest, signaling a potential bearish reversal when the price breaks below the neckline support. The inverse head and shoulders pattern, comprising three swing lows with the middle lowest, indicates a bullish reversal upon a break above the neckline resistance. The authors were unable to fully quantify the strategy for backtesting and instead rely on statistics from Thomas Bulkowski’s late-1990s research of 500 stocks over five years. Bulkowski found a 93% success rate for the head and shoulders pattern, an average 23% price drop, and concluded that volume and neckline direction do not affect its success; he recommended placing a stop-loss above the right shoulder. For the inverse pattern, he found few false signals, with 20–30% returns within 73 days, and advised placing a stop-loss below the right shoulder while noting the neckline break should occur on large volume. A 1995 Federal Reserve article concluded that technical analysis, including the head and shoulders strategy, can generate statistically significant profits. The authors caution that Bulkowski’s analysis was after the fact and recommend careful use of the strategy.

The Trump administration has not implemented threatened 100% pharmaceutical tariffs scheduled for October 1. A White House official told STAT the administration will begin preparing tariffs on companies that do not build U.S. infrastructure or make drug pricing agreements, which would apply to branded drugs, but did not provide a new timeline. The postponement suggests months of tough talk may aim to leverage U.S. investment and lower prices.

Researchers implemented a minorization-maximization algorithm for maximum likelihood and restricted maximum likelihood estimation in multivariate variance components linear mixed models using Julia. Applied to PsychENCODE data, the method partitioned cis- and trans-SNP effects on isoform expression, revealing sparse but large cis effects, small but collective trans effects, and greater shared genetic influences among cis-SNPs. Isoform-level analysis detected more psychiatric disorder-associated genetic signals than gene-level analysis.

House Of Fraser reported pre-tax profits rising from £1.3 million to £3.4 million for the year to January 28, with online sales up 16.1% and overall revenues flat at £1.3 billion. The retailer warned of continued trading volatility into 2017, will discontinue five under-performing brands, and opened its first standalone store in Nanjing, China.
