Around 125 people attended sessions for a Newtongrange masterplan. The team will review views and develop the design with Midlothian Council and the Blueprint Partnership before further community engagement later this year.

The passage details two defensive strategies against the Base Cross offense. Basic NBA Show & Recover uses a defender to show on the base screen, forcing the post high and wide without switching, while the post defender trails over and weakside defenders drop to help; recovery involves forcing the post away from the basket, weakside packing in, and returning to final matchups with ball and post pressure. All Out SOS Disruption traps the wing ball handler before post entry, counters the base screen with a Hi-Lo Switch (switch if the post goes low, no switch if high), and executes post trap and pass-out rotations, ending in final matchups with helpside positioning and pass denial.

The OECD has warned that the Irish economy is showing signs of overheating, citing sharp rises in mortgage and small-firm loans driven by construction. It cautioned that continued 13 per cent house-price growth could create another property bubble, and urged the Government to improve its fiscal position to buffer against shocks, notably Brexit. New mortgage lending in April rose 20 per cent to €842 million. The NTMA noted Irish bonds have remained stable amid Italian market turmoil, with investors viewing Ireland as closer to the euro-zone core. The European Commission also warned that housing supply shortages are fuelling price increases.

This paper introduces the first NLP task for automatic detection of “hype”—promotional or exaggerated language—in biomedical research texts. Following Millar et al. (2019), the authors define hype and focus on 11 novelty-related adjectives (e.g., groundbreaking, innovative) from 550 sentences in NIH grant abstracts. They propose six-step annotation guidelines to classify adjectives as Hype or Not Hype based on context, which three annotators apply to create a dataset of 537 sentences. Hyperbolic adjectives are consistently hype, while terms like “emerging” and “latest” are most ambiguous. The authors frame hype detection as text classification, testing traditional classifiers (SVM with GLOVE best among them), fine-tuned language models (BERT outperforms all others and the human baseline), and off-the-shelf LLMs (GPT-4O-MINI matches human performance). Results indicate that formal annotation guidelines improve human reliability and that fine-tuned models show promise for automatic hype detection. The study is limited by its small, English-only biomedical dataset focusing on one adjective group and the subjective nature of hype.

Giving career advice to adult children can be difficult and provoke defensiveness, as one father discovered when his 28-year-old son reacted angrily to guidance. Career coach Ruth Nemzoff suggests three principles for these conversations: know yourself and how your experiences bias your advice, know your grown child’s individual personality and current life situation, and know the specific workplace environment and economic context. To foster a positive discussion, ask whether the child wants advice or simply to vent, begin with curious, non-judgmental questions, acknowledge what you do not know about their situation, and share your own career mistakes. Nemzoff also recommends helping children identify their own solutions and next steps, suggesting they consult an objective third party, and avoiding resentment if they ignore the advice.

Nike’s “Considered” strategy integrates sustainability into product design and operations, shifting corporate responsibility from a staff function to a core element of business. Following 1990s labor crises and concerns over supply-chain environmental risks—including oil dependence, carbon emissions, and waste—Corporate Responsibility VP Hannah Jones and CEO Mark Parker focused on embedding environmental choices at the design stage. In 2005, they formed the Considered Group, which in 2007 launched the Considered Index, an intranet-based scoring tool that rates footwear on environmentally preferred materials, solvent use, waste efficiency, and innovation, awarding Bronze, Silver, or Gold ratings. Nike publicly committed that 100% of its footwear would meet a minimum Considered standard by Spring 2011. Early successes included the Air Jordan XX3 and Core Performance’s Spring 2009 line, which largely achieved Silver ratings and produced the Gold-rated Dual D Hoop shoe. Implementation faced challenges such as higher material costs, performance and aesthetic trade-offs, tight development timelines, factory capabilities, profit-margin pressures, and uncertain consumer willingness to pay for green features. Nike aimed to expand the Index to apparel, tighten standards over time, deepen collaboration with supply-chain partners, and determine how to market sustainability alongside performance, even as competitors like Timberland, Adidas, and Brooks introduced their own eco-friendly product programs.

DuBard School for Language Disorders received IMSLEC recognition as one of four U.S. schools for multisensory structured language education. DuBard Association Method, accredited since 1998, is used daily; the school is its national training site.

ExxonMobil sent marketing chief Thomas Martenak and a team to Dongying, China, to court independent "teapot" refiners via an unusual charm offensive at an oil trade show. The push marks Exxon's late entry into a market where BP, Shell, and traders Vitol, Trafigura and Mercuria arrived earlier. Since winning crude import licenses in 2015, China's teapots have become major buyers, accounting for one-fifth of national imports. Martenak said the effort, his first in eight years, is driven by market importance rather than politics, and aims to establish Exxon as a major regional supplier. New maritime fuel rules in 2020 may also increase Chinese demand for U.S. low-sulphur crude.

Sandvik beat first-quarter earnings expectations with profit rising to 4.27 billion crowns on strong metal-cutting tools results, but mining gear was weaker than expected, sending shares down 1.8 percent. Order intake rose to 25.4 billion crowns, beating forecasts. CEO flagged steps to improve mining profitability after uniquely strong quarter for metal-cutting tools.

Future Market Insights forecasts the global bioprocessing analytics equipment market will grow at a 4.5% CAGR through 2028. Osmometers lead product types, industrial applications lead at 4.4% CAGR, and biopharmaceutical companies are the largest end users. North America is expected to dominate; Western Europe and APECJ will account for approximately 39.2% of market share by 2018 end, with APECJ expanding at 5.9% CAGR. Integrated multi-functional analysers have been developed to reduce errors.

Pneumonia and tuberculosis pose substantial global health challenges, with high mortality rates and frequent misdiagnosis. Artificial intelligence, particularly convolutional neural networks, has demonstrated effectiveness in chest X-ray analysis, but existing models face limitations including reliance on small or imbalanced datasets, high computational demands, poor generalizability across diverse sources, and failure to handle non-X-ray or anomalous cases. This study proposes a multi-class classification framework using a pretrained convolutional neural network to categorize chest X-rays as normal, pneumonia, tuberculosis, or non-X-ray, thereby addressing a critical gap for real-world robustness. The framework utilizes a comprehensive dataset compiled from multiple publicly available sources. The authors review current deep learning approaches for pneumonia and tuberculosis detection, analyze their specific limitations, and present the proposed methodology, dataset compilation, and ethical considerations.

Chlorothalonil (CLT) is a toxic, carcinogenic fungicide that persists in the environment. This study uses density functional theory and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how nanotube radius affects CLT interaction with single-walled carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and boron nitride nanotubes (BNNTs) of chiralities (8,0), (10,0), and (12,0). The most stable configuration places CLT’s aromatic ring parallel to the tube surface at distances of 3.38–3.45 Å, indicating moderate physical adsorption. Adsorption energies become more negative with increasing radius for both nanotube types, driven by enhanced π–π stacking on less curved surfaces; however, CNTs exhibit stronger adsorption and substantially longer recovery times than BNNTs, with the (12,0) CNT showing a recovery time too long for practical sensing. BNNTs display short recovery times, favoring reversible sensing. Electronic analysis shows negligible band gap changes in CNTs upon CLT adsorption, making them impractical for electronic detection. Conversely, BNNTs exhibit significant band gap reductions of approximately 40–49%, high electronic sensitivity, and large increases in electrical conductivity, rendering them effective sensors. BNNT work function changes are pronounced for smaller radii but diminish for the (12,0) tube, indicating a need for radius control in work-function-based devices. Charge transfer occurs from nanotubes to CLT, with greater transfer for CNTs due to their lower chemical hardness and higher polarizability. BNNTs show weaker π–π stacking because their π-electron density is concentrated on nitrogen atoms. Molecular dynamics simulations confirm that both systems remain thermally and dynamically stable in aqueous solution, with CLT stably adsorbed in the parallel orientation. The study concludes that while both nanotubes can remove CLT from contaminated water, BNNTs are superior for detection due to their strong electronic response and reversibility, whereas CNTs are limited by weak electronic sensitivity and impractical recovery times.

The speaker stated the team can improve after a jittery first game, noting they must reach another level in puck battles and possession while avoiding undisciplined penalties. Line combinations may be adjusted for the next game. They praised a quiet, likable teammate for his playoff demeanor and "Nicky" for his strong arrival and performance. The team acknowledged uncharacteristic, generous goals allowed and critical end-of-period goals as factors in recent losses. They discussed being more physical against Pronger, managing "Kaner's" readiness, and the versatility of forward options. The speaker emphasized raising competitiveness, making technical adjustments, and putting the best lineup forward, including decisions regarding Burish and Laddy.

The smash concept is a perimeter passing play used at all football levels to create deep shots while offering quick throws. It is effective against Man coverage, Cover 2, and Cover 4, but risky against Cover 3 if the hitch is thrown late. The quarterback pre-snap picks a side to high-low the cornerback, throwing the hitch if the corner gains depth or the corner route if the corner plays low, checking down to the running back if unclear. Variations include a 3x1 set with a TE seam and backside dig or checkdown against cheat coverages, and a sprint-out version that moves the pocket, adds a backside over route, and allows the quarterback to run.

The ISM Manufacturing Index (PMI), introduced by the Institute for Supply Management in 1948, is a monthly indicator published on the first business day of each month measuring U.S. manufacturing sector health. Based on a survey of purchasing managers at over 300 firms, it assesses production, new orders, employment, supplier deliveries, and inventories. The index is calculated using the formula (P1*1) + (P2*0.5) + (P3*0), where P1, P2, and P3 represent percentages of improvement, no change, and deterioration, respectively; the passage also notes that five components receive equal weighting and are seasonally adjusted. A reading above 50 indicates expansion, below 50 contraction, and 50 indicates no change.

Investors, traders, economists, and businesses use the PMI to gauge manufacturing activity, economic direction, and market impact. It can be combined with indicators such as GDP, employment data, consumer confidence, and inflation. Although based on surveys of managers who may detect changes early, the PMI is described as a backward-looking indicator reflecting past rather than future economic activity, and markets may discount results before publication.

The index can inform trading strategies; backtests show holding the S&P 500 when the PMI exceeds 50 yielded a 7.3% annual return with 72% market exposure, underperforming the S&P 500's 8.5%. Readings below 50 showed mediocre equity results but better gold performance. The PMI is not considered effective for short-term or contrarian trading. Businesses also use it to assess supply chains and product demand. Data is available from ISM's homepage or a Google Sheet with historical data to 1970.

Calvin Alexander of Caddo Middle Magnet won the Northwest Louisiana regional spelling bee for the second consecutive year with “nectarivorous,” defeating Rosetta Schultz after 20 rounds. The LSUS- and KTBS-sponsored event was held March 17. Alexander advances to the 2018 Scripps National Spelling Bee in Washington, D.C., airing May 29–31 on ESPN. He wins an expenses-paid trip, a 2018 U.S. Mint Proof Set, and subscriptions to Britannica Online Premium and Merriam-Webster Unabridged Online.

The paper introduces "Survey and Questionnaire Item Embeddings Differentials" (SQuID), a method that applies semantic embeddings from large language models (LLMs) as complements to human rater judgments in psychometrics. Existing embedding approaches typically fail to produce negative correlations between items, a critical property for psychometric inventories. SQuID addresses this by subtracting the average embedding of all questionnaire items from each item embedding, thereby removing common linguistic features that artificially inflate similarities and enabling the recovery of negative correlations without finetuning.

The authors demonstrate SQuID using the Revised Portrait Value Questionnaire (PVQ-RR), which measures 19 value dimensions. Among several tested models, Linq-Embed-Mistral performed best. SQuID-treated embeddings achieved internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha) comparable to or exceeding human data from 49 countries. Dimension-dimension correlations between embeddings and human judgments were substantial (r = 0.74). Multidimensional scaling recovered the theorized circular structure of values, and Procrustes transformation against the human configuration yielded congruence coefficients of 0.88 and 0.82.

The authors propose that semantic embeddings can supplement traditional psychometric workflows, offering flexibility and scalability, and suggest applications such as quantifying cultural biases in LLMs. They note limitations regarding measurement validity, the difficulty of reversing embeddings, and potential training data contamination. An ethics statement highlights risks to crowdworker livelihoods if LLMs replace human raters, and warns against treating LLM-based norms as unquestioned standards.

SanDisk offers technical support by phone at 1-866-SanDisk or online at sandisk.com/retail/support.asp; include packaging information when contacting. A one-year limited warranty for original purchasers provides repair, replacement, or refund but excludes third-party software, data loss, and damage from misuse or unauthorized modification; it is non-transferable and void if product instructions are not followed. The device uses Microsoft WM-DRM technology to protect secure content, and compromised security may result in revocation of rights to copy or play that content. Software is licensed for personal use on a single device under an End User License Agreement that prohibits modification, reverse engineering, sublicensing, or distribution. The software is provided "as is" without warranties, and SanDisk's liability is limited to the amount paid for the product. The authors participated in SMM4H 2023 Task-1 and Task-4. Task-1 involves binary classification of self-reported COVID-19 diagnoses from Twitter, while Task-4 involves binary classification of positive or probable social anxiety disorder diagnoses from Reddit. They compared three approaches: RoBERTa (F1 0.83 on validation), fine-tuned BERT (F1 0.89 on validation), and a hybrid BERT-LightGBM model. The hybrid approach extracted hidden [CLS] tokens from the last three BERT layers to train a LightGBM classifier with Optuna hyperparameter tuning. It achieved an F1-score of 0.94 on Task-1 test data (Precision 0.949, Recall 0.938) and 0.809 on Task-4 test data (Precision 0.756, Recall 0.871). Data preprocessing included removing non-alphabet characters, tags, emojis, URLs, stopwords, and punctuation. The authors note that LightGBM effectively aggregates concatenated [CLS] tokens and suggest Task-4 performance could improve with a BERT model pre-trained on task-specific data.

The speaker accepts the presidency with personal reluctance but profound gratitude, pledging faithful service. He reflects on the nation’s intrinsic strength and growth, noting that territorial and population expansion has not threatened constitutional harmony between the federal and state governments. His administration will pursue just and pacific foreign relations, seeking territorial acquisitions only for national security while rejecting foreign interference or colonization in the Americas. He advocates for a modest standing army supported by a national militia and praises the Navy. Domestically, he promises strict economy, integrity, and nonpartisan appointments based solely on duty. He emphasizes adherence to constitutional limits on federal power and respect for states’ authority over domestic affairs. He affirms that involuntary servitude is constitutionally protected in the states where it exists, supports the Compromise of 1850, and urges national respect for Southern rights. He declares the Union essential to national prosperity, opposes sectionalism, and calls for humble dependence on divine Providence to preserve the Republic.

Hounds of the Bay selects high dividend-paying stocks from Canada's S&P/TSX 60. Named after Bay Street, it is skewed toward energy and commodities. Like Dogs of the Dow, it assumes blue-chip companies maintain dividends regardless of conditions, so high yields indicate a company is near its business cycle bottom. It underperformed in 2014 during an oil decline. Academic backtests confirm it worked historically, though the effect has diminished over recent decades.

The NVIDIA A100 GPU features third-generation Tensor Cores supporting Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity with a 2:4 pattern, compressing weights by 2x and doubling math throughput by skipping zeros while maintaining inference accuracy. The architecture includes 108 SMs with simultaneous FP32 and INT32 execution, a combined 192 KB L1 data cache and shared memory per SM, and 40 GB of HBM2 memory delivering 1555 GB/sec bandwidth. A 40 MB L2 cache, Compute Data Compression, and asynchronous global-to-shared memory copies improve bandwidth and efficiency. The Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) capability partitions an A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute and memory paths for quality of service and fault isolation. Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/sec total bandwidth, while PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV doubles interconnect bandwidth. Additional hardware includes a 5-core NVJPG decode engine, an optical flow accelerator, five NVDEC units, and improved atomic operation throughput. CUDA 11 adds Task Graphs, asynchronous barriers, L2 residency controls, and cooperative group collectives. The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs to deliver 5 PFLOPS of AI performance.

The NVIDIA A100 GPU, based on the Ampere architecture, delivers substantial performance gains over the Tesla V100. Each A100 Streaming Multiprocessor (SM) contains four third-generation Tensor Cores capable of 1024 FP16 fused multiply-add operations per clock, and the full GPU with 108 SMs achieves up to 312 TFLOPS of dense mixed-precision FP16/FP32 performance, 2.5× the mixed-precision Tensor Core performance of V100 and 20× its standard FP32 throughput. A100 Tensor Cores add support for TF32, BF16, and FP64, with TF32 providing up to 8× throughput over FP32 without code changes, and FP64 delivering up to 19.5 TFLOPS. The architecture introduces Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity (2:4 pattern), which doubles Tensor Core compute throughput for deep learning inference by skipping zero values.

Memory enhancements include 40 GB of HBM2 with 1555 GB/s bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache with 2.3× the read bandwidth of V100, and 192 KB/SM of combined L1 data cache and shared memory. A100 supports Multi-Instance GPU (MIG), partitioning the GPU into up to seven isolated instances with dedicated compute and memory resources for quality-of-service in multi-tenant environments. Other features include third-generation NVLink with 600 GB/s total bandwidth, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, simultaneous FP32 and INT32 execution, five NVDEC units, an NVJPG decode engine, and improved atomic operation throughput.

CUDA 11 advances for A100 include task graphs for reduced kernel launch overhead, asynchronous copy from global to shared memory, asynchronous barriers, and L2 cache residency controls. The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs interconnected via NVSwitch to deliver 5 PFLOPS, and A100 accelerates HPC workloads via FP64 Tensor Cores and mixed-precision iterative refinement solvers.

The Price Rate of Change (PROC or ROC) is a momentum oscillator developed by Tom Demark that compares the current closing price to the price “n” periods ago using the formula (Current Price – Price “n” periods ago) / Price “n” periods ago. It oscillates around a zero line, with positive values indicating upward momentum and negative values indicating downward momentum. Traders use it to identify overbought or oversold conditions, centerline crossovers, and divergences as potential signals for entries, exits, or reversals. The indicator is most useful in trending markets and less effective in volatile or sideways markets, where it is prone to whipsaws. Common strategies include mean reversion from oversold levels, breakouts, zero line crosses, and divergence detection. Backtests on the S&P 500 showed that a short-term oversold mean reversion strategy using 4–6 day lookback periods produced decent results, while breakout and zero line cross strategies performed poorly. Unlike the Relative Strength Index (RSI), which indirectly measures momentum, ROC is a direct measure of price change. The article suggests that ROC is generally inferior to indicators such as the RSI, stochastic, and Williams %R, and recommends combining it with trend-following tools, backtesting strategies, and optimizing for robustness before live trading.

The lecture covers the Spring-Loaded Inverted Pendulum (SLIP) model for running dynamics, which consists of a point mass atop a massless leg containing an ideal, lossless spring. Comparative biomechanics demonstrates that diverse organisms—including cockroaches, horses, crabs, and humans—share dynamically similar, non-dimensional locomotion properties across five orders of magnitude in mass, supporting the SLIP model as biologically plausible.

To analyze stability, the full four-dimensional state space is reduced to a one-dimensional iterated map by examining the apex height during the aerial phase. At apex, vertical velocity is zero, and horizontal velocity is determined from total energy conservation, so the apex height alone suffices to map one stride to the next. The lecture derives the transitions between apex, touchdown, stance, and takeoff; stance dynamics are handled via linearization using small-angle and small-displacement approximations to obtain a closed-form return map. This map reveals a stable fixed point and an unstable fixed point, indicating that passive stability can emerge in a conservative, piecewise holonomic system without energy dissipation.

Extensions to non-conservative systems with toe mass are discussed, where inelastic collision losses require active energy addition through spring constant control. Biological evidence includes cockroach perturbation experiments demonstrating "preflexes"—passive, spring-mediated stabilization faster than neural reflexes. The lecture also presents Raibert’s hopping robots from the 1980s and 1990s, which achieved robust monopedal, bipedal, and quadrupedal running, jumping, and flipping. Finally, SLIP walkers illustrate a continuum between walking and running by varying leg stiffness, analogous to human gait transitions occurring at the crossover point of metabolic efficiency.

A study measured SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence among 9,221 pregnant women attending first antenatal care visits in four Zambian districts (Chadiza, Chipata, Chongwe, and Lusaka) from September 2021 to September 2022. Using dried blood spots and a multiplex IgG assay distinguishing infection-induced from vaccine-induced antibodies, 8,304 valid results showed an overall seropositivity of 63.8%. Seroprevalence was highest in urban Lusaka, peaking at 100% in August and September 2022, and lowest in rural Chadiza, peaking at 77.2% in April 2022 before declining to 56.6% by July 2022. Chipata and Chongwe also neared 100% by August 2022. Among participants with anti-RBD antibodies and valid vaccination status, 77.7% were likely infection-induced only, 20.6% were hybrid infection-vaccination responses, and 1.6% were vaccination-induced alone. COVID-19 vaccination was associated with significantly higher odds of seropositivity in all districts. Reported COVID-19 cases substantially underestimated true infections, with seroprevalence-to-cumulative-incidence ratios ranging from 29:1 to 92:1 across districts. The authors conclude that antenatal care platforms are feasible for SARS-CoV-2 serosurveillance and that subnational mitigation strategies may be warranted given district-level differences in transmission and risk factors.

This study investigates the clinical relevance of circulating tumor cell (CTC) genomic diversity in metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). Using whole-exome sequencing of CTC pools from 29 patients, the authors computed 15 diversity metrics, including mutational burden, proportion of aberrant genome, and mutant allele tumor heterogeneity (MATH). Multivariate Cox proportional hazards analysis identified high MATH scores and non-silent BCL9L mutations as significant independent prognostic factors for poor overall survival. Patients with high-bMATH had a median survival of 18.3 months compared to 52.9 months for those with low-bMATH, while BCL9L-mutated patients had a median survival of 14.5 months versus 34.2 months for unmutated patients. Additionally, a custom 55-gene panel (CRC-P55) yielded MATH scores highly correlated with whole-exome sequencing data and significantly predicted survival, suggesting a cost-effective clinical alternative. The authors note this is the first study to associate CTC genomic diversity with cancer outcomes, but acknowledge that the small cohort limits generalizability.

BerkeleyGW delivers exascale performance for quantum many-body GW materials simulations, achieving portability across AMD, Intel, and NVIDIA GPU architectures on supercomputers such as Frontier and Aurora. This paper introduces ABXLAB, an open-source man-in-the-middle framework that transforms arbitrary websites into controllable behavioral testbeds by intercepting and modifying real-world web content in real-time to study how choice architecture affects large language model (LLM) agent decisions. The authors evaluated 17 state-of-the-art models across over 80,000 experiments in an online shopping environment, manipulating product ratings, prices, presentation order, and nudges (authority, social proof, scarcity, negative framing, incentives). LLM agents exhibited strong, systematic biases that substantially exceeded human baselines, with effects amplified up to 3–10× or more. Higher ratings increased selection probability by 30–80 percentage points (pp) across most models, price differences drove preferences up to 93pp, order effects reached near-deterministic levels for some models, and nudges shifted choices by 10–60pp across 14 of 17 models. Explicit user preferences operated as categorical switches that dominated decisions and suppressed competing attributes. The authors release ABXLAB as a foundation for rigorous behavioral science of AI agents.

In 2012, First Solar senior vice president Tymen deJong reviewed the company’s 2011 10-K, which showed its first net operating loss in seven years ($39 million) and revenue growth slowing to 8%. A leading manufacturer of thin-film cadmium telluride photovoltaic panels, First Solar saw its cost advantage erode as Chinese crystalline-silicon producers—subsidized by their government—flooded the market with inexpensive panels. Falling silicon prices benefited competitors but not First Solar, while reduced European subsidies and tighter project financing after the 2008–2009 crisis weakened demand.

First Solar had vertically integrated into the systems business, acquiring integrators to control project development, construction, and maintenance, which helped scale shipments and improve system performance. It also pursued a conservative, low-debt financial strategy. However, by 2011, global oversupply forced the company to run plants well below capacity, contributing to a fourth-quarter loss of $413 million. Facing an industry shakeout that bankrupted several U.S. manufacturers, deJong questioned whether First Solar’s cost advantage was sustainable, how to counter Chinese competition, and whether its systems business was a strategic benefit or a distraction.

Alan Oppenheim uses a programmable digital filter to demonstrate sampling, aliasing, and discrete-time system properties. The setup includes a continuous-to-discrete converter, a digital filter, a discrete-to-continuous converter, and a smoothing low-pass filter. With the digital filter as an identity system, sampling replicates the input spectrum periodically; aliasing occurs when the input bandwidth exceeds half the sampling frequency, causing the reconstructed output to reflect an alias frequency rather than the original. A sinusoidal sweep demonstration on an oscilloscope and through audio shows the output frequency increasing with the input until half the sampling rate, after which it decreases; a beating effect also appears near half the sampling rate due to the non-ideal reconstruction filter.

Inserting a digital low-pass filter with a cutoff of π/5 and linear phase, the equivalent continuous-time frequency response rescales the digital axis by the sampling period, making the analog cutoff one-tenth of the sampling frequency. Demonstrations show the overall system’s symmetric impulse response, the staircase output from the D/A converter before smoothing, and the swept frequency response exhibiting attenuation beyond the cutoff. Sweeping up to the full sampling frequency reveals the digital filter’s periodicity.

Varying the sampling rate proportionally shifts the effective analog cutoff (e.g., 40 kHz sampling gives a 4 kHz cutoff, 20 kHz gives 2 kHz). This is demonstrated with sinusoidal sweeps and live audio, where lowering the sampling rate progressively narrows the audible bandwidth until the original higher rate restores full fidelity.

Week 6 of the 2025 college football season featured major upsets that shook conference and College Football Playoff races. UCLA defeated Penn State 42-37, the first time in nearly 40 years that a team at 0-4 or worse beat a top-10 opponent; UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava rushed for 150 yards and three touchdowns while Penn State’s defense allowed over 430 yards. The loss dropped Penn State’s SP+ ranking from 4th to 16th and left the Nittany Lions with a projected 7-5 record. Florida also upset Texas 29-21, as Florida quarterback DJ Lagway threw for 298 yards and two touchdowns with no sacks, while Texas quarterback Arch Manning threw two interceptions behind a struggling offensive line; Texas now also projects to 7-5. Alabama held off Vanderbilt after the Commodores committed turnovers deep in Crimson Tide territory. Miami defeated Florida State after the Seminoles stalled following a fast start, committing turnovers and limiting quarterback Tommy Castellanos, effectively ending FSU’s ACC title and playoff hopes. Cincinnati beat Iowa State to join the Big 12 title race, while Texas Tech dominated Houston and holds the best power-conference conference title odds per SP+. Other notable results included Baylor’s last-second field goal over Kansas State and Kansas’s goal-line stand against UCF. In Division I records, Western Carolina quarterback Taron Dickens set an NCAA single-game record with 46 consecutive completions.

Derby takeaway Sun Waa received a one-star food hygiene rating from Derby City Council in November 2017 after inspectors found cooked rice left at room temperature for six hours, a wash basin obstructed by a wok, food debris, cross-contamination risks, bleach used on preparation surfaces, a broken thermometer, and insect webbing. The business has since been revisited and significantly improved hygiene practices, with a re-score planned for early March. Despite the low hygiene rating, the takeaway holds higher customer scores on TripAdvisor and Just Eat.

Michelle Munson of NYU and Sarah Narendorf of the University of Houston have found that mental health narratives—how marginalized young adults perceive the causes, management, and consequences of their mental health conditions—strongly influence their treatment engagement and self-care. Marginalized youth, defined by the Institute of Medicine as those facing challenges such as poverty, disabilities, and reliance on safety-net systems, often experience stigma and discrimination that shape these narratives. Unlike physical illness narratives, mental health narratives involve greater emotional dimensions like fear and shame. The researchers propose training providers to use cultural humility and collaborate with patients to understand their individual narratives, rather than relying solely on expert diagnosis. They conducted qualitative, face-to-face interviews with young adults and are developing technology-based interventions to help shape productive narratives. They emphasize that many marginalized young adults avoid treatment because they do not feel heard or respected by providers, and improving care requires listening to their stories and experiences.

Sixteen-year-old Murad Rahimov, who immigrated from Uzbekistan and recently became a U.S. citizen, received a private tour of NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center after an NPR listener connected him with astrophysicist Jeremy Schnittman. Murad, who dreams of becoming an astronaut and working for NASA, viewed spacecraft assembly and testing facilities, including the clean room and cryo-vac chamber. Schnittman discussed his black hole research, Einstein's theories, and time travel with the teen. Now on an accelerated academic track, Murad hopes to attend Cal Tech and lead a Mars mission. His mother, Limara, expressed that citizenship has made her feel fully grounded in the United States. Murad plans to view the upcoming total solar eclipse from Kansas City.

Anita Anand was told to stand down from presenting BBC Radio 4's Any Answers because the programme was to discuss the BBC gender pay gap, and she had publicly supported equal pay campaigns. Julian Worricker presented instead. The BBC cited impartiality rules preventing presenters who campaigned on issues from hosting discussions on those subjects. Dame Jenni Murray similarly had to opt out of a Woman's Hour discussion last week. Critics accused the BBC of implying women journalists cannot be impartial. A BBC spokesman said editors decide case-by-case to ensure impartiality.

Jonathan Toews, Brad Richards, and Kris Versteeg discussed their upcoming Stanley Cup Final game against Tampa Bay. Toews stated that experienced players see no difference between winning on the road or at home, and the team must focus solely on the game despite surrounding excitement. He reflected that the playoff journey passes quickly and involves unmatched togetherness and adversity. He noted that family members are nervous spectators and that playing is mentally easier than watching. He said the team improves as series progress and credited Joel with effectively gauging needs and adjusting matchups and lineups. Toews also acknowledged that staying healthy requires proper recovery and that the team has been fortunate, while observing that every playoff team believes it can win in a highly competitive league. Richards said repeated championship experience makes preparation and focus easier, as the core group has grown together. He emphasized patience and smart puck play against Tampa Bay, which will try to build belief as the game progresses. Richards also praised a teammate's all-around defensive game and leadership. Versteeg called the playoff run tough, said players not in the lineup stay ready and confident, and noted he recently built chemistry with new linemates through constant communication.

This study benchmarks 15 two-sample summary-level Mendelian randomization (MR) methods—including IVW (fixed and random), Egger, RAPS, Weighted-median, Weighted-mode, MR-PRESSO, MRMix, cML-MA, MR-Robust, MR-Lasso, MR-CUE, CAUSE, MR-APSS, and MR-ConMix—using real-world genetic datasets to assess type I error control, estimation accuracy, and replicability. The authors evaluate performance across three confounding scenarios via negative controls: (a) population stratification (1,130 trait pairs), (b) pleiotropy (77 trait pairs), and (c) family-level confounders (82 trait pairs compared in population-based versus family-based GWAS). They also test accuracy using six trait pairs where exposure and outcome are identical (true causal effect = 1), and assess replicability and power using six LDL-C GWAS datasets against coronary artery disease.

Results indicate that MR-APSS, Egger, and Weighted-mode generally maintain well-calibrated type I error rates across confounding scenarios and varying instrumental variable (IV) p-value thresholds. CAUSE produces deflated or inflated p-values depending on the scenario. Most remaining methods exhibit inflated type I errors, particularly under strong population stratification, with inflation often worsening at looser IV thresholds. Family-based GWAS designs yield well-calibrated p-values for all methods. For estimation accuracy, MR-APSS outperforms others, consistently covering the true effect across thresholds; most other methods show bias toward the null and poor coverage as weaker IVs are included. In the LDL-C and CAD replicability analysis, CAUSE and MR-APSS show high consistency across datasets and thresholds, though CAUSE’s p-values are deflated. Larger GWAS sample sizes improve method performance and reduce sensitivity to IV threshold choice.

The authors recommend using negative controls, applying multiple IV selection thresholds, and leveraging multiple independent data sources to improve reliability. They note limitations including potential coexisting confounders, lack of true positive cases, the inability of the accuracy design to assess pleiotropy robustness, and the exclusion of individual-level MR methods.

The NRA claimed in an April 20 letter that YETI cut ties with the organization. YETI responded that it eliminated outdated discount programs and offered an alternative customization program available to all, including the NRA Foundation. Supporters boycotted YETI, and one man destroyed his cooler with explosives and an AR-15, sparking the #YetiCoolerChallenge. YETI maintains it supports the Second Amendment.

The passage identifies foods rich in folate, or vitamin B9: asparagus (33% daily value), broccoli (14%), oranges (50 mcg), legumes, avocado (110 mcg), lady's finger (103 mcg), nuts and seeds such as sunflower, flax, peanuts, and almonds, cauliflower (55 mcg), beetroot (14%), carrots (5%), and corn (34 mcg), noting preparation methods and additional nutrients.

Tesla filed a Form 8-K dated January 29, 2019, reporting CFO Deepak Ahuja intends to retire after serving since 2008, apart from a 14-month gap. Ahuja will briefly remain CFO, then serve as an advisor. Tesla intends to appoint Zachary Kirkhorn, current Vice President, Finance, Financial Planning and Business Operations, as his replacement. Kirkhorn joined in March 2010 and played critical roles in Gigafactory 1, Model X, and Model 3. Musk, Ahuja, and Kirkhorn commented on the transition and financial position.

The President reports an eventful year marked by a financial crisis, reduced political partisanship, and the capture of the American steamer Virginius by Spain, which is being adjusted honorably. Relations with most nations remain friendly. U.S. commissioners attended the Vienna exposition and a conference on patent protection. The Emperor of China received Western diplomats, and modest progress was made against the Chinese coolie trade. The Geneva arbitration award was paid by Britain and applied to redeem public debt. The northwest water boundary with Britain was determined, and the northern boundary survey advanced. The mixed commission under the Washington treaty awarded Britain $1,929,819 in gold, dismissing other British and all American claims; he recommends appropriating this sum, thanks Count Corti of Italy, and proposes a special court for remaining alien claims. The United States maintained neutrality in the Dutch-Acheen war; the Mexican claims commission resumed with a British umpire. Venezuela has not honored convention awards. The Ottoman Empire and Egypt proposed ending consular judicial powers, subject to Congressional assent. Santo Domingo seeks a U.S. protectorate. New treaties were concluded with Denmark, Mexico, the Orange Free State, and Ecuador. Legislation is urged to define acts of expatriation, the nationality of American women marrying foreigners, and the status of children born abroad to American parents. Spain has abolished slavery in Puerto Rico and restored American estates, but Cuban slavery continues; the Virginius seizure and killing of 53 passengers and crew produced a protocol for vessel restoration, survivor release, a flag salute, and punishment of guilty parties, while the Navy was placed on a war footing. He proposes constitutional amendments allowing the Executive to approve portions of bills without approving the whole, and restricting extra-session legislation to subjects submitted by the Executive. The Treasury reported a $43.4 million surplus last year but now faces falling revenues from the panic; economy is urged in public works and unfounded claims from the rebellion. He advocates resuming specie payments, retaining domestic gold, and securing currency elasticity through expanded national bank note issuance against bonds, clearing houses, and possibly free banking, while avoiding inflation. Shipbuilding rose about 3 percent; he suggests federal maintenance of connecting waterways if canals are opened to larger vessels, and a naval exploration of the Amazon. The tariff should be revised and more mints opened. The War Department needs seacoast armaments, staff promotions, and more medical, pay, and ordnance officers. The Navy added new and repaired vessels and prepared for the Virginius crisis. The Post Office ran a $5.3 million Treasury deficiency despite growth; postal savings, expanded free delivery, and postal telegraphs are recommended. For Utah, legislation is needed to secure jurors and limit probate courts. He recommends repealing involuntary bankruptcy under the 1867 act and tightening rules against unfounded government claims. Indian policy continues concentrating tribes on reservations and advancing territorial government for the Indian Territory. The Patent and General Land Offices report increased business; a Russian colony seeks to immigrate. Pension costs and rolls grew; anti-fraud legislation is needed. The Ninth Census is complete and a quinquennial census is urged. Washington, D.C. improvements warrant federal cost-sharing and a national university. Civil-service reform requires Congressional support. Colorado should be admitted, with a donation of public lands for an irrigation canal. He renews recommendations for general amnesty and stronger civil-rights laws for freedmen.

The disclosure provides articles—such as footwear, apparel, and sporting equipment—that exhibit structural color through optical elements rather than dyes or pigments. Structural color is produced by physical light interactions (e.g., reflection, interference, diffraction) with micro- or nano-scale features. An optical element, which may include multilayer reflectors or filters, can be used alone or with optional textured surfaces and primer layers to impart color to article components like shoe uppers, soles, or cushioning bladders. The structural color can be single-hue, multihued, iridescent, or angle-independent, and can be evaluated using CIE 1976, CIELCH, or Pantone color systems. Optical layers may comprise materials such as metal oxides or liquid crystals formed by deposition techniques. Textured surfaces contain micro- or nanoscale profile features that influence light behavior. The articles achieve visible coloration without requiring additional pigments or dyes, though such colorants may be used optionally.

Tarren Titus, 23, received three months house arrest and one year probation after pleading guilty to hydromorphone possession and two probation violations. Police raided a home, finding hydromorphone and paraphernalia. The judge called his transformation outstanding. Titus must follow curfew, continue counseling, avoid drugs. He received time served for probation violations. Daily sobriety meetings have been part of his life for eight months.

Detroit is described as the strongest opponent faced, with significant offensive firepower and arguably the best goaltender in the world. The speaker stresses playing tough but clean, as officials are calling even minor or embellished infractions, and giving Detroit excessive powerplay opportunities is inadvisable. The team needs better puck decisions, must win faceoffs against Detroit's puck-possession style, and must account for Kris Draper and a defenseman regarded as the league's best. The team met to focus on the upcoming home finals game amid distractions, and the speaker stated their home arena is louder than Detroit's.

MSPM0C1105/6 are ultra-low-power 32-bit Arm Cortex-M0+ MCUs up to 32MHz with 1.62V–3.6V supply and -40°C to 125°C range. They feature up to 64KB flash, 8KB SRAM, integrated analog and digital peripherals, multiple communication interfaces, and are supported by TI development kits, SDKs, and online resources.

India's 21 state-run banks posted a record combined loss of 853.7 billion rupees ($12.65 billion) in the fiscal year ended March, with all but two lenders falling into the red after stricter central bank rules spurred surging bad-loan provisions. Gross non-performing loans rose about 15 percent to 8.96 trillion rupees ($133 billion). New Delhi has a 2.11 trillion-rupee recapitalization plan, though some fear banks may lack funds for growth after meeting Basel III requirements.

A flurry of Monday deals suggests junior mining mergers, particularly in gold, may accelerate after a slow start to 2018. Hecla Mining Co. proposed a US$462 million acquisition of Klondex Mines Ltd., the largest Canadian mining deal announced this year, which would raise Hecla's annual gold production to roughly 370,000 ounces. Klondex shares jumped 61 per cent. Alio Gold proposed a $128-million acquisition of Rye Patch Gold, while Anaconda Mining offered to buy Maritime Resources. There have been only six Canadian metals and mining mergers in 2018 compared to 19 at this point in 2017. Industry observers expect further junior consolidation driven by risk management and capital costs.

A Zillow analysis of homes sold and rented between June 2017 and May 2018 in the 35 largest U.S. metro areas found that homes with air conditioning commanded a 2.5 percent sales premium, averaging nearly $5,500, with the highest premiums in San Antonio (5.8%), Cincinnati (5.7%), and Detroit, Indianapolis, and Las Vegas (5%). Air conditioning was listed as a required feature by 62 percent of buyers, surpassing outdoor features. Nationally, 66.1 percent of sold homes had AC, though prevalence reached 99.1 percent in Las Vegas and 97.9 percent in Phoenix. Rentals with central AC commanded a 2.8 percent premium (about $40 monthly), with the highest rent premiums in New York, Las Vegas, and Phoenix. The New York metro area had low AC prevalence at 22.6 percent of sales and 17.2 percent of rentals.

Options trading in IWM involves buying and selling call and put options, which grant the right to buy or sell shares at an agreed-upon price before expiration, allowing investors to speculate or hedge against market risk. Available order types include market, limit, stop, and trailing stop orders. Strategies include buying calls or puts, selling covered calls, buying protective puts, and using spreads with technical indicators such as moving averages, Bollinger Bands, and RSI. Trading carries risks, including potential total loss of investment and unlimited risk on short calls. Risk management requires stop-loss orders, diversification, limiting exposure—generally no more than 10% of a portfolio—and backtesting strategies. Investors must typically be at least 18 years old, have a valid address, maintain a margin account with sufficient funds, and meet broker-specific minimum balance requirements, often around $2,000. Taxes apply to profits and premiums. The article advises thorough research and cautions that inexperienced investors should avoid options trading.

Pusa, 63, former Nagaland minister and Congress leader, died and was buried in Viswema. He leaves his wife and three children. Governors, Chief Ministers and other dignitaries condoled his death and attended his funeral.

This continuation-in-part application describes systems and methods for blockchain transaction risk management and money-flow tracing to support Anti-Money Laundering and Counter Terrorism Financing compliance. A digital asset intake engine receives on- and off-blockchain information, which an entity knowledge base contextualizes. A risk classification engine uses machine learning—including AutoML, decision trees, and behavior-based models analyzing feature categories such as temporal, topology, and linkage—to categorize addresses into entity types (e.g., exchange, mixer, bot, hacker, terrorist) and create classified risk data. A risk scoring regression engine assigns a 0–100 risk score with an optional time-decaying factor, while a rules-based risk policy engine detects deviations. A security control system blocks, freezes, or suspends high-risk transactions and accounts, or approves normal-risk ones. An auto-tracing module applies intelligence labels and address-clustering IDs to transaction flows, then executes AI graph search algorithms (e.g., greedy breadth-first search, Dijkstra) guided by input trace parameters such as direction, time range, volume, and hop limits to determine asset paths. The system generates interactive journey boards, summary statistics reports identifying suspicious addresses, and proactive alerts, and can trace flows into fiat banking systems via exchange Know Your Customer mappings.

Four female winemakers discuss their experiences in a once male-centered profession. Zita Kovács says early prejudices have given way to respect. Zsófi Laposa notes that technological advances opened the field to women, who bring gentleness and uniqueness. Krisztina Csetvei balances her career with raising her daughter, Panna, and will present a wine named after her at VinCE Budapest. Andi Gere co-manages her family winery and says feminine elegance has refined their wine style.

Ivey announced the Alabama Sentry Program allowing administrators in schools without resource officers to store firearms in safes for active shooter response. Participants require training and approval from superintendents, boards, and sheriffs. Sentries provide weapons, ammunition, and vests. Ivey called it an interim measure until more School Resource Officers are added. Officials supported it, requiring no new funding.

A pump and dump scheme involves a promoter acquiring a position in a stock or cryptocurrency, artificially inflating the price through false or misleading information, then selling to latecomers and causing a significant price drop. These schemes occur primarily in over-the-counter penny stock markets and the unregulated crypto market, where low volume and digital platforms facilitate manipulation; they are largely absent from major regulated exchanges. Pump and dumps are illegal in regulated markets, immoral, and leave most participants with losses. One study found an average scheme return of -28%, losses exceeding €1.2 million per tout, and that roughly 6% of investors participated in at least one scheme. The fear of missing out drives late investment. Investors are advised to avoid such scams, be wary of sudden unfounded price increases in OTC and crypto markets, and focus on long-term, systematic trading or investing.

Plum School District will begin 2018-19 budget discussions Tuesday to avoid a third straight tax increase. The district starts the school year over $4 million in debt after approving a $66 million budget with a tax hike and a $5.6 million bond. The board will also discuss recruiting tuition-paying Chinese students, elementary construction, consolidation, redistricting, and starting the process to close Regency Park Elementary. The workshop follows a special meeting on personnel moves.

The passage covers global financial news, highlighting a Bank of England warning that AI stock valuations may be unsustainable and risk a sharp correction similar to the dot-com bubble, with systemic vulnerabilities from concentration in U.S. tech giants and structural bottlenecks in power, semiconductors, and data infrastructure. The central bank noted UK exposure to U.S. equity shocks, aligning with IMF concerns. Other topics include gold surpassing $4,000 on Fed easing expectations, European markets hitting record highs, Germany opening an antitrust probe into Temu, the World Bank raising China’s 2025 growth forecast to 4.8 percent, Fifth Third acquiring Comerica for $10.9 billion, AMD surging on an OpenAI chip deal, Poland investing $5.5 billion in NATO fuel networks, the U.S. freezing $18 billion in New York City infrastructure funds, South Korea restoring services after a data centre fire, and OpenAI reaching a $500 billion valuation.

Argus Research upgraded Orbital ATK to buy with a $120 price target after the company reported Q2 2017 sales of $1.12 billion, up 3% year over year, and adjusted earnings of $1.56 per share, beating expectations. However, GAAP profits fell 3% to $1.51, operating margins declined 140 basis points to 12.2%, and free cash flow was negative $55.8 million. Management raised full-year sales and earnings guidance, noting a 10% backlog increase and a 1.45 book-to-bill ratio, while keeping free cash flow guidance at $250–$300 million. The author disagrees with the upgrade, stating the stock is overvalued after rising 44% in 12 months, trading at 22 times trailing earnings and a high enterprise value-to-free-cash-flow ratio against 10% expected annual growth.

An Infosys Finacle survey found over 80% of bankers expect blockchain adoption by 2020, with over half of institutions investing this year at an average $1 million. Top use cases include cross-border payments, digital identity, and clearing and settlement. Sixty-nine percent prefer private blockchains, 20% consortium, and 10% public.

The present disclosure provides methods, apparatuses, and systems for transmitting paging information in new-generation wireless communication systems using high-frequency beamforming. It addresses the problem that applying a Long Term Evolution discontinuous reception mechanism for paging is complex or impossible because paging information is loaded within transmission subframes or timeslots corresponding to each beam, and user equipment in an IDLE state cannot foresee how beams or ports are scheduled in different timeslots. The solution involves calculating a time domain position of a paging occasion, where the paging occasion includes a group of paging resources for transmitting paging information on one or more preset beams or ports and corresponds to a synchronous signal burst set or sweeping resources of preset beams or ports. A first communication node calculates the paging occasion and transmits paging information, comprising paging downlink control information and/or a paging message, to a second communication node within the paging occasion. The second communication node calculates the same paging occasion and receives the paging information within it. The time domain position may be determined using parameters including a discontinuous reception cycle, a paging transmission interval, a number of paging transmissions, a device identifier, and a paging occasion offset. Additionally, a quasi-co-location relationship between a signal related to the paging information and other sweeping signals or channels may be indicated or configured to facilitate reception. Corresponding apparatuses, systems, computer-readable storage media, base stations, terminal devices, and computer program products are also provided.

This study proposes "whole human pedagogy," a novel decolonial framework for education abroad centered on four tenets: embodiment, emotions, belonging, and becoming. Informed by hooks (1994), Thompson (2016), and decolonial theory, the framework critiques the exclusion of bodily, emotional, relational, and transformative knowledge from Euro-U.S. higher education. A qualitative study using Fall 2023 interviews with seventeen U.S.-based education abroad practitioners found that participants viewed approaching students as whole human beings as central to their work. Practitioners understood embodiment as physical and sensory immersion; emotions as linked to culture shock and structured reflection; belonging as reciprocal, non-hierarchical relationships and communal learning; and becoming as transformative, meaningful learning affecting students' existence. The study concludes that whole human pedagogy offers a compelling theoretical and practical model for education abroad program development, professional development, and future research, challenging dominant epistemological values and centering diverse human knowledge.

At its fall hardware event, Amazon announced new Echo devices, Kindle Scribe tablets, Fire TVs, Ring cameras, and Blink devices. Senior VP Panos Panay unveiled Echo speakers and smart displays featuring the AZ3 chip, Omnisense sensors, improved audio, and built-in Alexa+ integration. Alexa+, a large language model-powered assistant, is entering early access in the US, free for Prime members or $20 monthly. The third-generation Kindle Scribe includes a Colorsoft model with a color screen, new note-taking and workspace tools, cloud integration, and AI reading features. Amazon also introduced Fire TVs and the Fire TV Stick 4K Select running the new Vega operating system, with faster performance and Omnisense capabilities. Ring founder Jamie Siminoff announced 2K and 4K cameras with Retinal image processing, Familiar Faces, Alexa+ Greetings, and a neighborhood Search Party feature to find lost pets. Blink launched new 2K cameras and the Arc accessory for 180-degree footage. Most devices are available for preorder today.

This case study details the turnaround of Boston’s Institute of Contemporary Art (ICA) under Director Jill Medvedow, who transformed the institution from a struggling, marginal organization into a major cultural destination. When Medvedow arrived in 1998, the ICA had minimal funding, few members, no permanent collection, and roughly 25,000 annual visitors in a converted police station. By 2006, it opened a new $51 million waterfront building, drew over 280,000 visitors in its first year, and later attracted 130,000 attendees to a single exhibition.

Medvedow’s strategy focused on making the ICA public, relevant, and non-elitist through aggressive outreach and risk-taking. She won the rights to build on Parcel J at Fan Pier in 1999 by convincing the Boston 2000 committee of the museum’s financial viability and fit for the site. She then launched an unconventional $62 million capital campaign, recruited business leaders to the board, and hired Paul Bessire to lead development.

For the new building, the ICA used an unconventional architect selection process, ultimately choosing Diller + Scofidio—who had never built a permanent U.S. building—based on their innovative philosophy and shared stake in the project. Despite major obstacles, including the sale of surrounding Pritzker land, arduous city approvals, and construction delays that pushed the opening from September to December 2006, the museum succeeded. The ICA sustained high attendance beyond its initial opening phase, validating Medvedow’s vision that a bold waterfront location and expanded programming could reshape Boston’s engagement with contemporary art.

Sean “Diddy” Combs was sentenced to four years and two months in prison and fined $500,000 for violating the Mann Act by transporting people across state lines for sexual encounters. Having already served one year, he faces approximately three more years. He was convicted in July of arranging drug-fueled sexual encounters with girlfriends and male sex workers over many years but was acquitted of sex trafficking and racketeering. During sentencing, Judge Arun Subramanian cited Combs’s power and resources for enabling the prolonged crimes. Combs apologized to his family and victims, pleaded for leniency, and appeared subdued. His trial included testimony from multiple victims describing beatings, threats, sexual assault, and coercion, including a former girlfriend who described being ordered to have sex with strangers and being beaten in a hotel hallway. Six of his seven children addressed the court, tearfully requesting family healing. Prosecutors sought a serious sentence, while defense attorneys argued the Mann Act was misapplied.

The passage details container design patterns for single-node and distributed systems. The sidecar pattern augments an application container to add functionality—such as HTTPS termination, dynamic configuration synchronization, process monitoring, and Git-based deployment—without modifying the application itself, emphasizing modularity through parameterization, stable APIs, and documentation. The ambassador pattern brokers communication between an application and external services, enabling client-side sharding, service discovery, and request splitting for experimentation. The adapter pattern standardizes heterogeneous application interfaces for monitoring, logging, and health checking. For multi-node systems, the passage introduces microservices, which improve agility and scaling but increase complexity. It then describes replicated load-balanced stateless services, including horizontal scaling, readiness probes, session affinity, caching layers, rate limiting, and SSL termination. Sharded services partition large datasets across nodes using sharding functions and consistent hashing to minimize remapping during scaling, with options for replicated shards and hot-sharding. Finally, the scatter/gather pattern parallelizes request processing across multiple nodes to reduce response time.
Eighth Circuit dismissed Jenkins v. United States appeal on appellee motion and appellant consent.

Several months after deep cuts by the Trump administration and DOGE to the U.S. Department of Education, researchers express cautious optimism due to plans to reinstate 20 research contracts, a lawsuit temporarily preserving 10 regional education labs, and a request for public input on modernizing the Institute of Education Sciences. The department has rehired some employees and posted high-level assessment jobs for the National Assessment of Educational Progress. Amber Northern has been brought in to advise on IES reform. However, severe staff shortages continue, NCES was cut from roughly 100 employees to three, and reporting functions have been reduced. A new executive order also requires NCES to conduct a massive retroactive survey of college admissions data. Experts remain concerned about long-term damage to research infrastructure and data quality, though many view rebuilding federal education research as essential.

Theratechnologies Inc. will sell US$50 million in convertible senior notes due June 30, 2023, to underwriters led by RBC Capital Markets, with a US$7.5 million over-allotment option. The unsecured notes bear 5.75% annual interest, payable semi-annually, and convert to common shares at US$14.85. They are redeemable after June 30, 2021, if the share price reaches 130% of the conversion price. Proceeds will fund the EMD Serono Termination Agreement, Trogarzo commercialization, and general corporate purposes. Closing is expected on or about June 19, 2018, subject to regulatory approvals. The notes will be offered in Canada by prospectus and in the United States by private placement.

The Ultimate Oscillator (UO), developed by Larry Williams in 1976, is a momentum indicator that measures price momentum across three weighted timeframes (7, 14, and 28 periods) to reduce false signals common in single-timeframe oscillators. It calculates Buying Pressure and True Range, averaging them across the three periods in a 4:2:1 ratio to produce values between 0 and 100; levels below 30 indicate oversold conditions and above 70 indicate overbought conditions. Trading signals require divergence between price and the indicator: buy signals occur with bullish divergence from oversold territory when the oscillator rises above the divergence high, while sell signals require bearish divergence. Backtests indicate the UO is a consistent and stable mean reversion indicator that performs well under various settings, with optimized strategies showing high profit factors, win rates, and average gains per trade.

Stevens's 1892 dispatches from Hawaii reported revolutionary sentiment against the Queen, cabinet deadlocks, and growing support for U.S. annexation. He recommended annexation or a protectorate with Pearl Harbor ceded to the United States. Naval reports corroborated his accounts until January 1893, when a peaceful revolution dethroned the Queen. The report states U.S. policy from 1820 to 1893 favored Hawaiian autonomy and opposed foreign intervention, while periodically contemplating annexation. Prepared by Andrew H. Allen, the appendix notes time constraints and references unperfected treaties of 1849, 1855, and 1867.

Automation threatens millions of jobs, including truck driving, with the World Economic Forum predicting the elimination of over five million jobs in five years. To safeguard employment, humans may pursue three forms of augmentation. Brain augmentation involves a "neural lace"—an electronic mesh integrating with the brain to boost information processing—an idea proposed by Elon Musk and supported by early Harvard research on syringe-injectable electronics in mice. Body augmentation includes powered exoskeletons and soft exosuits developed by institutions like Harvard and companies such as SuitX, which combine human decision-making with robotic strength to reduce physical strain and keep laborers working alongside machines. Skill augmentation focuses on knowledge workers developing non-codifiable skills like creativity and learning to maintain intelligent machines, though experts note physical laborers face a harder transition. While current narrow AI performs specific tasks, the potential rise of artificial general intelligence could fundamentally disrupt human employment.

Meb Faber’s Tactical Asset Allocation strategy is an active trend-following approach that uses market timing across five asset categories: U.S. stocks, foreign stocks, U.S. bonds, U.S. REITs, and world commodities. The strategy allocates 20% to each position and moves to cash when no monthly signal is present, utilizing diversified index ETFs rather than individual securities. Backtesting over 16 years showed a maximum drawdown of -13.24%, significantly lower than typical passive portfolios. Meb Faber is the co-founder and chief investment officer of Cambria Investment Management.

The Minnesota Court of Appeals remanded a child support modification case for inadequate findings. Richard Berg appealed a trial court order increasing his support obligation to $516 per month after his net income rose 34.5% since the parties’ 1981 divorce. While the appellate court found the guideline amount within the trial court’s discretion, it held that the trial court failed to make the complete and specific findings required by *Moylan v. Moylan* to justify the substantial increase. The case was remanded for further factual inquiry and findings consistent with that decision.

Supreme Court dismissed plea to cancel interim bail for Ryan International School owners in Pradyuman murder case. High Court granted anticipatory bail November 21. CBI held class 11 student responsible, clearing bus conductor. Family alleges complicity.

NGC 5949 is a dwarf barred spiral galaxy roughly 44 million light-years away with mass a hundredth that of the Milky Way. Discovered by William Herschel in 1801, it is a target for astronomers studying cosmological quandaries like "cuspy halo" and "missing satellites" problems.

Rapid7 (NASDAQ:RPD) was upgraded to “buy” by BidaskClub. Analysts hold mixed ratings, but the consensus is “Buy” with a $20.19 price target. Net sales for the third quarter of 2017 were $43.7 billion, up 34% year-over-year, and $117.4 billion for the nine months ended September 30, 2017, up 27%. The company faces contingencies including a European Commission state aid decision ordering Luxembourg to recover approximately €250 million plus interest, an IRS appeal regarding transfer pricing, a South Carolina sales tax assessment, and various patent and employment-related legal proceedings. Officials confirmed 71 homes and over 400 utility poles destroyed, with more expected. Authorities ordered Kapoho evacuations as lava advanced, and one person was trapped and rescued. Photographer Richard Mosse’s exhibition *Heat Maps* at New York’s Jack Shainman Gallery documents the refugee crisis across Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East using a military-grade thermal telephoto camera mounted on a robotic arm. The camera detects thermal radiation while scanning landscapes and interiors from as far as 50 kilometers away, producing large-scale panoramas constructed from nearly a thousand smaller frames. The images render human flesh as translucent grey with blackened eye sockets, deliberately dehumanizing subjects to reflect how Western governments and voters regard refugees. By repurposing surveillance technology designed for weapons targeting, Mosse employs a distancing effect intended to subvert common perceptions, confront viewers with their complicity in camp conditions, and challenge predetermined opinions. The three-year project faced complex logistical challenges, including difficult border crossings and restricted access to camps such as the Calais Jungle.

Trump announced the U.S. will impose an additional 100% tariff on Chinese imports and export controls on all critical software starting November 1, retaliating against China's new export controls on rare earths minerals. China, which supplies about 70% of global rare earths essential for high-tech industries, will require licenses starting December 1 for exports of products containing Chinese rare earths or made with its technology. Trump also suggested canceling a meeting with President Xi Jinping. The current effective U.S. tariff rate on Chinese imports is approximately 40%.

The double bottom chart pattern is a bullish reversal formation occurring in a downtrend, consisting of two swing lows at approximately the same support level with a swing high between them. The pattern is complete when the price breaks above the neckline, a resistance level connecting the swing highs. Traders estimate profit targets by projecting the pattern's size upward from the neckline and typically place stop losses in the pattern's middle or below it. Aggressive traders may enter at the second low seeking reversal signals, while conservative traders wait for a confirmed neckline breakout with increased volume. According to Thomas Bulkowski's research of 500 stocks over five years, 68% of formations reached their target, outperforming the double top pattern; however, the study may suffer from survivorship bias, manual pattern selection, and a bull market timeframe. The strategy is difficult to quantify and backtest due to complex rules and subjective interpretation.

The International Union for Conservation of Nature classifies Emperor penguins as near-threatened. A 2014 study projected a 19 percent population decline by 2100 due to rising temperatures. A new remote monitoring system uses time-lapse cameras and weather data to observe colonies continuously online. Researchers found penguins huddle in warmer conditions, suggesting lower body fat and food shortages possibly linked to sea ice loss reducing plankton, though one expert attributes the scarcity to commercial fishing rather than climate change.

Mark Palmer forwarded to Enron colleagues a class-action complaint filed in California Superior Court for San Diego County by Pamela R. Gordon against Reliant Energy, Southern Company, NRG Energy, Dynegy, AES Corporation, Williams Energy, and Duke Energy. The suit alleges that during 2000, defendants conspired to manipulate the California wholesale electricity market by improperly sharing and using confidential real-time generator and transmission data through the Western Systems Coordinating Council, withholding generating capacity, exporting power to affiliates to create artificial shortages, and gaming the California Power Exchange and CAISO markets. These acts allegedly caused wholesale prices to rise to unjust and unreasonable levels, resulting in approximately $4 billion in overcharges and severe financial harm to consumers. The complaint asserts violations of California’s Cartwright Act, the Unfair Trade Practices Act, the Consumers Legal Remedies Act, and unconscionability, and seeks class certification, treble damages, injunctive relief, and disgorgement of unlawful profits. Palmer noted that a reporter said Enron’s suit would look the same.

India demanded the UN disclose information on staff crimes, misconduct, and immunity waivers. Legal advisor Yedla Umasankar criticized the UN for appearing reluctant to waive immunity for serious misconduct to allow host country prosecutions. He requested data on registered cases, refused waivers, host country requests, and member state prosecutions, excluding diplomats. Umasankar stated accountability remains elusive due to legal complexities, jurisdiction, and immunity, noting the UN cannot prosecute criminally and states should implement laws to prosecute citizens for crimes committed abroad.

A court fined Pomeroy $6,000 and the New York Central and Hudson River Railroad Company $108,000 for six offenses each. The passage criticizes the overturning of judgments on technicalities and advocates a law barring new trials or set-asides in civil and criminal cases unless an error caused a miscarriage of justice. UDMA write CRC errors result from state corruption after a UDMA read with host termination. When a device terminates a UDMA write, the ATAC continues the prior CRC instead of restarting it for the next portion, making UDMA writes generally unusable. Use the UDMA I/O blocking feature in bit 8 of the ATAC Error MSR.
