The Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) established the official diamond award in 1999 for songs that reach at least 10 million equivalent units through sales and streaming, though certification requires an application by the artist or label that can delay updated figures. As of the article, 179 songs have been certified diamond. Elton John’s “Something About The Way You Look Tonight / Candle in the Wind” was the first, certified in 1997. Drake holds the record for the most diamond singles with 10, followed by Post Malone with nine. Rihanna leads female artists with seven, tying her with The Weeknd for the third-most overall. Bruno Mars and Katy Perry each have six, tied for fourth-most. Katy Perry’s album *Teenage Dream* is the only album with four diamond-certified songs, while The Weeknd’s *Beauty Behind the Madness* was the first album to have three. The most recent song to receive the award is Shaboozey’s “A Bar Song (Tipsy),” certified on September 15, 2025.

Two stackless assembler procedures manage a pre-memory processor stack via register passing. The first initializes the processor and cache, divides the stack among all cores, maps it globally, sets MTRRs, configures SS/ESP by mode, creates a UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF, destroys EAX/ECX/EDX/EDI/ESI (and DS/ES in 16-bit), and returns AGESA status codes; AARCH64 APUs with PSP do not use this stack. The second, run on all cores, removes the pre-memory stack and disables CAR mode once main memory is available, preserving EBX as a return address.

Hong Kong and Singapore have emerged as leading destinations for initial coin offerings following bans in China and South Korea. Neither jurisdiction currently has specific ICO regulations, leaving token sales loosely regulated. After China declared ICOs illegal and South Korea banned them, numerous companies from both countries relocated to Hong Kong and Singapore to avoid legal risks. The passage describes SOS defensive strategies for disrupting low post offenses. The primary method is Post Front, where the defender aggressively fronts the post to limit inside passes and shots, with low helpside double teams on lob passes. Base Go is the primary double-team option, used when the post is moved off the block or on a coach's call. Go Top is a secondary trap effective when the post turns into the middle. Go Wing is a secondary trap used when the offensive wing is a poor outside shooter. The Hold option has the post defender play one-on-one while teammates assume pass denial positions to prevent open three-pointers. The Yo-Yo variation allows a defender to sag off a non-shooting wing to help on the post. All player rotations occur as the ball leaves the passer's hands.

The Gold Overnight Trading Strategy seeks to profit from overnight price movements in gold futures, GLD, or gold miners ETFs (GDX/GDXJ) by buying at the market close and selling at the next open. Backtests indicate an overnight bias: GDX averaged a 0.12% overnight gain versus a 0.09% intraday loss, while GLD produced 8.4% annual returns overnight compared to 8.2% buy-and-hold, with intraday returns near zero. However, the strategy carries high risk and volatility due to global economic and geopolitical factors. The authors note that gold and commodities are generally harder to trade than stocks and strategies often degrade over time. They describe specific incubated strategies—a long GLD overnight approach with 741 trades averaging 0.17%, and a short GDX overnight approach with 205 trades averaging 0.7%—and emphasize the need for trading plans, risk management, discipline, and emotional control. The trading rules and logic are available for purchase.

Bills quarterback Josh Allen praised running back James Cook as an "all-time teammate," crediting Cook's $48 million contract for his strong start, which includes 401 rushing yards and five touchdowns. The 4-0 Bills will host the Patriots in Week 5 with a chance to go 3-0 in the division.

On November 5, 2001, news reports detailed Enron Corp.'s financial crisis and regulatory scrutiny. The Wall Street Journal reported that Enron's March purchase of $35 million in interests from Chewco Investments LP—an entity run by former officer Michael Kopper, an associate of former CFO Andrew Fastow—raised questions about off-balance-sheet debt and management dealings. Dabhol Power served an asset transfer notice to the Maharashtra State Electricity Board over unpaid bills, and BG Group claimed technical qualification to assume operatorship of Enron's Indian oil and gas fields.

Sara Zaske's daughter Sophia only wanted a cell phone after moving from Germany—where few children own phones—to California, where she was the only fourth-grader without a smartphone. Mobile phone ownership among children varies widely by country: about 51% of German children ages 6–13 and 46% of European children ages 9–16 own mobile devices, while 45% of US children 10–12 have smartphones with service plans and 42% of US children under 8 have tablets. In South Korea, 72% of children 11–12 own smartphones, while in Ghana and Malawi ownership is much lower but rising. The American Academy of Pediatrics states there is no "right" age for a child's first phone, but recommends avoiding regular digital media for children under 18–24 months, limiting screen time to one hour for ages 2–5, and establishing healthy media habits regardless of age.

If a SanDisk SSD is not recognized, remove other USB devices. Clone data from the internal HDD to the SSD using software, selecting the IDE source drive and the SSD as the destination. For notebooks, power off, remove the battery, transfer brackets from the old HDD, align the SATA pins, install the SSD in the drive bay, and reassemble. For desktops, power off, disconnect the old HDD's SATA cables, install the SSD into a 3.5-inch adapter if needed, place it in the drive bay, connect the SATA cables, and close the case. The old HDD may be kept as a backup.

The DHHS set a 140 parts per trillion GenX water goal with no adverse non-cancer effects. Effects include endocrine disruption; cancer research is limited. A GenX forum with Erin Brockovich and Robert Bowcock is August 16 at UNCW.

A Russian spacewalk of 8 hours and 13 minutes, the longest ever by Russians and fifth longest, ended with an antenna 180 degrees from its intended position outside the International Space Station. Alexander Misurkin and Anton Shkaplerov replaced an obsolete electronics box on the antenna, which NASA said remained operational. Russian officials convened a team to assess further action. The old electronics box was discarded to burn up, and Misurkin will return at month's end.

The American Stroke Association recommends the FAST acronym for major stroke symptoms and urgent action: F for Face drooping, A for Arm weakness, S for Speech difficulty, and T for Time to call 911, even if symptoms subside; remember when symptoms began. A similar mnemonic, STR, involves asking a person to smile, talk, and raise both arms. Quick action is critical as hours can determine whether a patient receives life-saving care.

According to the Credit Suisse Global Investment Returns Yearbook, the best-performing stock markets since 1900 include Australia, the United States, South Africa, New Zealand, Denmark, Sweden, Canada, Finland, Switzerland, and the Netherlands. Australia delivered the highest returns at over 6.5% annually in U.S. dollars, attributed to minimal WWII impact, a strong banking sector, dividends comprising 53% of total gains, commodity exports, and stable governance. The U.S. market returned 6.5% annually after inflation, growing $1 in 1900 to $3,806 by 2019, and currently represents over 54% of global free-float market capitalization. South Africa averaged 7.2% returns (6.4% in USD), New Zealand returned 6.4%, and Denmark ranked fifth despite an 80-year bear market through 1980. The top three markets are commodity-rich nations that diversified into finance and technology. Globally, equities returned 5.2% annually since 1900, outperforming bonds at 2%. Stock advantages include inflation protection, dividends, liquidity, and diversification. Research by Hendrik Bessembinder found that only a small fraction of stocks drives overall gains, while most underperform Treasury Bills. Past performance does not guarantee future results.

On February 2, World Wetlands Day, Beignet the Nutria—raised by South Louisiana Wetlands Discovery Center Executive Director Jonathan Foret as a mascot to educate students about invasive species—did not see his shadow, predicting a mild hurricane season, while Punxsutawney Phil predicted six more weeks of winter.

Robin Chase co-founded Zipcar in June 2000 to provide convenient urban car access. After extensive networking, team building, and fundraising during the collapsing dot-com bubble, the company launched with a pricing model combining membership fees, hourly rates, per-mile charges, and daily rates. By mid-October 2000, Chase discovered that car utilization was only 22 percent—far below her 40 percent estimate—and September revenue was roughly half of projections, indicating the business model was not viable. She identified the daily rate as the primary culprit, determining it would need to increase by 20 percent to break even given that daily rentals generated 50 percent of revenue. With Zipcar scheduled to close a $1.3 million funding round within weeks, Chase faced the dilemma of whether to raise prices and risk customer backlash and accusations of bait-and-switch, or continue with an unsustainable model.

New research from Yale’s Budget Lab and the Brookings Institution found no discernible disruption to U.S. jobs since ChatGPT’s 2022 launch, noting occupational shifts largely began in 2021; researchers cautioned the analysis is not predictive and the sample size is small. While entry-level workers face hiring challenges, struggles are attributed more to broader labor market dynamics than direct AI replacement. Meta will use AI chatbot conversations to personalize ads starting December 16, excluding sensitive topics, with no opt-out. Mira Murati’s Thinking Machines Lab launched Tinker for custom frontier AI models. OpenAI released Sora 2, a video and audio model requiring copyright holders to opt out. Startup Periodic Labs raised $300 million to build AI for scientific discovery. S&P 500 companies citing AI as a material risk surged from 12% in 2023 to 72% this year, led by reputational and cybersecurity concerns.

The author, who made a skeptical film about a Frenchman who froze his wife, discusses a British teenager recently cryopreserved for £37,000. Robert Ettinger's 1964 theory involves replacing cellular water with antifreeze and storing bodies at -196°C; 2,000 people have since paid for this. Montreal has been ranked the world's best city for students in the QS Best Student Cities 2017, displacing Paris, which fell to second, while London rose to third. The ranking evaluates university quality, affordability, desirability, safety, and employer access. Canada's popularity is growing as an alternative to the U.S. and U.K. amid concerns over American entry rules and Brexit, with Vancouver and Toronto also placing in the top 11. Paris's decline is attributed to cost and safety. Germany's Berlin and Munich rank in the top 10, aided by free tuition. Asian cities are increasingly attractive, with Seoul fourth. The international student market is economically significant, valued at nearly $36 billion to the U.S. economy.

The TPS7H500x-SP controllers are radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. They operate from a 4-V to 14-V supply and support switching frequencies from 100 kHz to 2 MHz via an internal oscillator, external synchronization, or primary-secondary mode. A transconductance error amplifier compares the VSENSE pin voltage to the lower of the SS pin voltage or an internal 0.613-V reference; the output voltage is programmed with a resistor divider to this 0.613-V reference. Soft-start duration is set by a capacitor on the SS pin, and synchronous rectifier outputs become active once SS exceeds 1 V. The devices provide primary switching outputs (OUTA/OUTB) and synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA/SRB) with roughly 150-mA peak current, and external gate drivers are recommended. Dead time, leading edge blank time, duty cycle limit, slope compensation, and current sense limit are programmable through external resistors and pin configurations. The CS_ILIM pin enables cycle-by-cycle current limiting, with hiccup mode triggered when the pin exceeds 1.05 V. Other protections include external fault detection via the FAULT pin and thermal shutdown above 175°C. An application example describes a 500-kHz synchronous push-pull GaN converter, detailing component selection for the feedback network, timing, transformer, filtering, compensation, and protection. Layout guidelines recommend minimizing switching loops, separating analog and power grounds, routing sensitive traces away from noise sources, and placing bypass capacitors close to the controller.

David Clarkson says his team played well despite unlucky bounces and a score that didn't reflect their performance. He says they must create more traffic, bear down on chances, score early, and take things shift by shift to battle back, acknowledging the opposing goalie's strong play while maintaining belief in their system.

International Development Secretary Penny Mordaunt became the first minister to use sign language in Parliament. Speaker John Bercow responded with a signed reply. Ms Mordaunt announced a July 24 London conference, co-hosted by the UK, Kenya, and the International Disability Alliance, to advance disability inclusion. MP Bob Stewart attempted to sign while asking a question.

In 1881, Mr. Blaine instructed the U.S. minister to Hawaii that granting treaty privileges to other powers would violate the 1875 treaty, and stated the U.S. sought Hawaii's benevolent neutrality or an American solution if that failed. In 1883, the U.S. declined to join a Hawaiian protest against British and French expansion in Polynesia. The reciprocity treaty was renewed in 1884, granting the U.S. exclusive rights to Pearl River Harbor for a coaling station, though ratification was delayed until 1887 amid opposition from U.S. sugar interests and Great Britain. Gen. Schofield had recommended acquiring Pearl Harbor in 1873. From 1884 to 1892, cable proposals connecting Hawaii with Australia and North America faced legislative changes, a British protest over landing privileges, and a U.S. survey.

Consilium Software announced Consilium UniRSM™ on Cisco SolutionsPlus worldwide as a replacement for the end-of-sale Cisco Remote Silent Monitoring (RSM) product. Designed for Cisco Contact Center Enterprise environments, it enables remote phone-based silent monitoring and whisper coaching without a network connection. The solution includes nearly ten architectural, reliability, and feature improvements over the previous version, including new architecture eliminating RTSP reliance, high availability failover, Cisco Visual Voice Browser support, web-based reporting and administration, and Windows and Linux support.

Between 62% and 82% of retail CFD traders lose money, based on statistics from 13 brokers that are legally required to report this data. Interactive Brokers has the lowest rate at 62%, while the worst broker surveyed has 82%. Most traders fail due to leverage, transaction costs, illiquidity, hidden fees, lack of knowledge, and absence of trading plans. CFDs are a zero-sum game where brokers act as counterparties and profit from bid-ask spreads. While approximately 20-25% of disciplined traders may profit through risk management, the majority of retail traders are undercapitalized and lose money.

This passage describes an information management system for protecting and managing enterprise data, including virtual machines in cloud or network computing environments. Because some architectures, such as OpenStack, do not natively support changed-block tracking (CBT) or expose APIs to enable it, efficient incremental and differential backups are difficult. The disclosed system addresses this by generating images of a virtual machine disk at different times, comparing them to identify changed blocks, creating a map of the changed block locations, and using a virtual server agent to extract and back up only those changed blocks in a format usable by the information management system. The passage also details system architecture, including client computing devices with data agents, primary and secondary storage devices, secondary storage computing devices with media agents, and a storage manager that coordinates operations such as full, incremental, differential, synthetic full, archive, snapshot, replication, deduplication, and hierarchical storage management.

The team needs more initiative and must limit Carolina's offensive zone time by disrupting forechecks and entries, noting similarities to the Detroit series but improvement in the second two series. They must improve blocked shots, giveaways, and takeaways; avoid doing too much in the Stanley Cup Finals; and trust what they do best. Positive flow from reporters was welcomed, Rem's story was praised, and eliminating faceoff advantages, especially on home ice, was stressed.

South Korean prosecutors raided Korean Air Lines headquarters over suspected embezzlement and breach of trust by the Cho family. Chairman Cho Yang-ho is under investigation for tax evasion and suspicious money flows amid scrutiny over daughters' alleged misconduct and his Jin Air resignation.

U.S. stock valuations have climbed to multi-year highs, with the S&P 500 rising about 15 percent and the Nasdaq nearly 19 percent, led by artificial intelligence and technology companies. The International Monetary Fund and JPMorgan warn of systemic risks and an increased likelihood of a correction, while Goldman Sachs maintains that robust earnings growth justifies higher valuations despite concentration risk. Sergeant Marlon Appollis testified at the Western Cape High Court that no suicide note or signs of suicide were found in the Spier hotel room where Susan Rohde was found hanging in July 2016. He noted no chair or table to stand on and no relevant fingerprints, though a note suggesting her husband Jason was having an affair was discovered. Tarik Skubal tied a Tigers postseason record with 14 strikeouts over 7 2/3 innings, leading Detroit to a 2-1 Game 1 victory over the Cleveland Guardians in the AL Wild Card Series. The Tigers scored the go-ahead run in the seventh inning, and reliever Tyler Vest recorded the final four outs in a tense ninth after Cleveland's José Ramírez was tagged out in a rundown between third and home. The passage also includes various MLB headlines: Ron Washington stated the Angels are not picking up his contract; the Rays' sale is finalized; the Astros and Athletics GMs have contracts for 2026; Bloom takes over Cardinals baseball operations with manager Marmol returning; Bochy is out as Rangers manager; and multiple 2025 MLB playoff preview and prediction articles are featured.

A goaltender sustained a third-degree MCL injury and hurt his elbow when he fell against the post during a net-front collision in the playoffs. Following an MRI at Duke University, he was told the knee injury would heal fairly quickly but not immediately. This study sequenced and characterized twelve SARS-CoV-2 genomes from Esteio, Rio Grande do Sul (RS), Brazil, collected between April and June 2021 during the Gamma wave, and investigated molecular evolution of structural proteins E, M, and N. The samples comprised ten P.1 and two P.1.17 lineage genomes, with several mutations, some reported for the first time in RS or Brazil. Analysis of 4,706 RS genomes from GISAID (March 2020 to May 2022) showed successive lineage dominance from B.1.1.33 and Zeta in 2020 to Gamma in early 2021, Delta in mid-2021, and Omicron in early 2022. Phylogenomic analysis demonstrated monophyletic grouping of VOCs within the state, with the study genomes clustering in the Gamma clade. Molecular evolution analyses using HyPhy detected no positive selection in the E protein; two positively selected sites and twelve purifying selection sites in the M protein; and fourteen positively selected sites and forty-six negatively selected sites in the N protein. DynaMut2 predicted that mutations at positively selected sites in M were mostly stabilizing except S94G, while N mutations were stabilizing at site 63, destabilizing at site 151, and mostly destabilizing in the C-terminal domain except for Q289L.

This study protocol describes a three-arm randomized controlled trial (ISRCTN10756933) evaluating the effectiveness of the Digital-MindCAN programme on psychological symptoms among cancer survivors in Singapore. Adults who completed curative cancer treatments between two weeks and two years prior (target n=150, 50 per group) will be randomized to the Digital-MindCAN programme with standard care, the Palouse Mindfulness programme with standard care, or a wait-list control. Digital-MindCAN is an eight-week, real-time, videotelephony-delivered group intervention combining cancer-specific psychoeducation with mindfulness practice; the Palouse Mindfulness intervention is a general eight-week internet-based mindfulness programme. Primary outcomes are objective stress (measured via stress thermometer and pulse oximeter) and subjective stress. Secondary outcomes include psychological well-being, perceived relaxation, mindfulness, resilience, depression, and anxiety, assessed via self-administered questionnaires at baseline, after the fourth session, and after the eighth session. Focus group interviews will assess participant perceptions. Quantitative data will be analyzed using analysis of covariance and repeated measures analysis of variance; qualitative data will be analyzed using realist evaluation. The trial aims to determine whether Digital-MindCAN is superior to the wait-list control and non-inferior to the active control in improving psychological outcomes.

This study examines preschool teachers' views on sensory education and classroom practices through phenomenological research involving 20 preschool teachers selected via maximum diversity sampling. Semi-structured interviews analyzed through content analysis revealed three main themes: the importance of sensory education, its relationship with the preschool education program, and difficulties or limitations in implementation. Teachers affirmed that sensory education is fundamental in early childhood, contributes to all developmental areas, and should be integrated into daily routines through diverse activities such as art, music, experiments, and tactile play. However, they reported that the preschool education program includes but does not sufficiently or explicitly address sensory education. Teachers evaluate sensory activities primarily through observation and involve families through communication, seminars, and home-based activities. Major challenges include inadequate physical facilities, insufficient sensory materials, and teachers' low self-efficacy, with most expressing a need for specialized training. The discussion notes that while teachers recognize the benefits of sensory education, some confuse the term "sense" with "emotion" due to similarities in Turkish. Recommendations include organizing in-service training, providing occupational therapist support, equipping classrooms with sensory materials, integrating sensory education into undergraduate teacher education, and preparing sample activities.

The passage examines higher education projects (HEPs) established by Russian academics who emigrated following the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, framing them as a form of collective exile and "education in emergencies." It distinguishes forced academic exile from voluntary emigration, noting that exiled scholars form a specific refugee subgroup experiencing "limbo" and "in-betweenness." The study analyzes four HEPs varying in institutionalization—from informal online initiatives to accredited in-person faculties—created to maintain connections with Russia while operating abroad. Through phenomenological interviews and discourse analysis, the research identifies three narratives of self-conceptualization. First, HEPs function as "safe havens," providing infrastructure, visa assistance, scholarships, and intellectual sanctuary for persecuted scholars and students, while preserving professional identity and forming diasporic communities. Second, they engage in preservation and limited reconceptualization of Russian academic heritage, particularly in social sciences and humanities, maintaining Russian academic language and liberal arts models, though often perpetuating hierarchical teaching methods and failing to fully adapt practices to post-authoritarian contexts. Third, HEPs practice "hope-making," transforming passive anticipation of return into active, future-oriented educational praxis through international collaboration and sense-making about the war, despite uncertain futures. The conclusion notes that while HEPs reshape international education by filling gaps in support for at-risk academics, further research is needed on their continuity, inherent biases, international influences, gaps between mission and practice, and long-term role in homeland restoration.

Tuberculosis (TB) is the leading infectious cause of death worldwide, and undernutrition is its leading risk factor, contributing to at least 2.2 million cases annually. The RATIONS study demonstrated that providing household contacts of persons with TB a monthly food basket costing $13 for six months reduced TB incidence by 40% over two years and reduced mortality among persons with TB by approximately 35%. This analysis used a Markov cohort model to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of implementing this nutritional intervention in India from government and societal perspectives over the lifetime of a simulated cohort of 100,000 household contacts. Compared to usual care, the intervention was projected to result in 6,749 versus 7,718 lifetime TB cases and 906 versus 1,529 TB deaths per 100,000 individuals, averting 13,775 disability-adjusted life years (DALYs). The incremental cost-effectiveness ratio was $229 per DALY averted from the government perspective and $184 per DALY averted from the societal perspective, both substantially below India’s willingness-to-pay threshold of $550. Sensitivity analyses indicated these findings were robust, with the intervention remaining cost-effective even at higher supplementation costs and lower estimates of effect. The authors conclude that a RATIONS-style nutritional intervention is cost-effective for reducing TB incidence and mortality among household contacts in populations with a high dual burden of TB and undernutrition in India.

The lecture examines dynamic optimality, the open problem of whether one online binary search tree can perform within a constant factor of the optimal offline BST for every access sequence. In the BST model, one may follow left, right, and parent pointers and rotate a node with its parent; each search begins at the root and must visit the target key. Although Ω(log n) is required in the worst case, better performance depends on the access sequence.

Several analytic bounds are discussed: the sequential access property (constant amortized for in-order accesses), the dynamic finger property (log k amortized where k is key distance from the previous access), the entropy bound (based on access frequencies), and the working set property (log of the number of distinct keys accessed since the key’s last access). The unified property, combining spatial and temporal locality, is achievable by a pointer machine but unknown for BSTs; the best known BST achieves an additive log log n overhead.

Splay trees, which move an accessed node to the root via zig-zig and zig-zag rotations, satisfy sequential access, working set (implying entropy), and dynamic finger. It remains open whether they satisfy the unified property or are dynamically optimal.

A geometric view maps accesses to points in a space-time plane. A point set is a valid BST execution if and only if it is arborally satisfied: every axis-aligned rectangle spanned by two points not on a common horizontal or vertical line contains another point. The offline optimal problem is equivalent to finding the minimum arborally satisfied superset of the access points.

The greedy algorithm adds points row-by-row to satisfy empty rectangles. This corresponds to an offline tree algorithm that rearranges the search path optimally for future accesses. Using split trees to simulate this structure yields an online BST. The best known competitive ratio against the offline optimal is log log n.

The gravity dual of a finite-temperature conformal field theory (CFT) on a sphere depends on the dimensionless product of the sphere’s radius and the temperature (RT), unlike flat space where temperature is the only scale. In global Anti-de Sitter (AdS) space, there are three Euclidean solutions: thermal AdS, a small black hole, and a big black hole. Thermal AdS is well-defined for the sphere. The black hole solution yields a relation between temperature and horizon size with a maximum inverse temperature, implying a minimum temperature for black holes. Above this minimum, two branches exist: a small black hole with negative specific heat, analogous to a flat-space Schwarzschild black hole, and a big black hole with positive specific heat.

In the large N limit, the saddle-point approximation requires summing contributions from all solutions; the one with the largest Euclidean action (lowest free energy) dominates. Thermal AdS has zero leading-order free energy. The small black hole always has higher free energy than the big black hole and never dominates. There exists a critical temperature Tc above the minimum temperature: below Tc, thermal AdS is stable, while above Tc, the big black hole dominates with negative free energy proportional to N². This is a first-order Hawking-Page phase transition, with a discontinuous first derivative of the free energy in the large N limit.

On the field theory side, a toy model of N² free harmonic oscillators with an SU(N) singlet condition illustrates the transition. At low temperature, states with energy of order N⁰ dominate. At high temperature, the exponentially large density of states for energies of order N² overwhelms thermal suppression, causing the system to transition to the high-temperature phase.

UCL and Imperial College London researchers have revealed that polymyxin antibiotics kill active bacteria by forcing them to rapidly overproduce and shed their outer armor, creating gaps that allow the drug to enter the cell. High-resolution atomic force microscopy images showed surface bulges forming within minutes followed by rapid shedding of the outer membrane. However, the antibiotics are ineffective against dormant bacteria because armor production is switched off. The findings suggest combining polymyxins with treatments that wake dormant cells or promote armor production to prevent recurring infections.

The site also hosts a 4.5-meter antenna for tracking launch vehicles and a transponder for the Biomass mission, reinforcing ESA-Australia space cooperation.

The passage describes SD memory card initialization, command behaviors, and state transitions per the Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00. After bus activation, the host initializes the card using ACMD41, setting the HCS bit to indicate SDHC/SDXC support and polling the busy bit for up to one second. CMD8 expands ACMD41 to include CCS, which identifies SDSC versus SDHC/SDXC cards. The host then retrieves the CID with CMD2 and assigns an RCA with CMD3, moving the card from Ready through Identification to Stand-by State. For UHS-I, the host sets S18R in ACMD41 to request a 1.8V switch; if the card returns S18A=1, the host issues CMD11 to perform the voltage switch, and may use CMD19 for timing tuning in SDR50/SDR104 modes. In Data Transfer Mode, CMD7 selects a card for point-to-point transfers. Reads use CMD17/CMD18 and writes use CMD24/CMD25, abortable via CMD12; the card indicates programming busy on DAT0. Erase sequences use CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38, with optional pre-erasing via ACMD23, plus DISCARD and FULE operations supported only on SDHC/SDXC. CMD42 provides password lock/unlock and Card Ownership Protection (COP), which adds Force Erase Password (FEP) management and requires a COP Unlock command when FEP is set; ACMD6 is rejected while the card is locked. CMD6 switches card functions, with Mode 0 querying support and Mode 1 setting functions for bus speed, command system, driver strength, and power limit. High-Speed mode (25 MB/s) is enabled via CMD6. CMD8 checks host supply voltage before ACMD41 for Version 2.00+ cards. SDSC cards use byte addressing and variable block lengths, whereas SDHC/SDXC use fixed 512-byte block addressing and do not support partial or misaligned access.

In an action before the Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia, the Court answered certified questions regarding the termination of at-will employees who refused a polygraph test. The Court held that determining the existence of public policy is a question of law for the court, and that terminating employees for refusing a polygraph examination violates West Virginia’s public policy, which is grounded in a recognized individual interest in privacy. The Court affirmed the circuit court and remanded for further proceedings. In dissent, Justices Miller and Neely argued that no public policy against polygraph testing existed at the time of the 1982 terminations because the statutory limitation was not enacted until 1983, and that the majority’s ruling improperly applied retroactively to past conduct in a settled area of at-will employment law.

The ADS868xW is a 16-bit successive approximation ADC with an integrated analog front-end and precision reference. It supports single-ended and differential inputs with bipolar and unipolar ranges, and outputs data in straight-binary format. The device provides input and AVDD alarm functions; the input alarm uses user-programmable high and low thresholds with a common hysteresis setting, while the AVDD alarm uses fixed 4.7 V and 5.3 V thresholds. Alarm conditions are indicated by active and tripped flags in the ALARM_REG and can be monitored via an active-high ALARM pin, internal register reads, or flags appended to the output data stream. The multiSPI digital interface supports legacy SPI-compatible protocols and source-synchronous modes with single or dual SDO outputs, and allows daisy-chain connections. The device operates in RESET, ACQ (acquisition), and CONV (conversion) states, with an optional NAP mode in ACQ and a deep power-down mode. Programming uses 32-bit data transfer frames classified as optimal, short, or long, and supports byte and half-word read and write commands to nine configuration registers that control device ID, reset and power, SPI and SDO protocols, data output content, input range, and alarm thresholds. Separate AVDD and DVDD supplies require decoupling capacitors for specified performance. An example application pairs the device with a differential multiplexer in a programmable logic controller analog input module to digitize standard industrial voltage and current inputs, using the programmable input alarm with hysteresis for robust temperature monitoring.

Professor William Green Jr. introduces ordinary differential equation initial value problems (ODE-IVPs), noting upcoming schedule changes. He defines ODEs as involving derivatives with respect to one variable and IVPs as specifying all conditions at a single point, demonstrating how to convert higher-order equations into first-order systems and reformulate problems into standard solver forms like MATLAB’s f(t, y). The objective is to generate vectors of time points and matrices of y-values that approximate true solutions.

He explains the Forward Euler method, y_new = y_old + Δt·f(y_old), but highlights its poor error scaling (total error O(Δt)). More accurate methods—trapezoid, midpoint, and higher-order Runge-Kutta—better estimate the average f over the step. Runge-Kutta 2 approximates the midpoint using Forward Euler, while Runge-Kutta 4-5 (MATLAB’s ode45) compares fourth- and fifth-order estimates to control error and step size.

Green analyzes error propagation, showing that errors at each step are multiplied by a factor involving the Jacobian. If the norm of this matrix exceeds one, errors amplify, causing numerical instability. This can occur even for stable ODEs, such as dy/dt = −2y, where Forward Euler with large Δt produces diverging oscillations. He references textbook derivations of stability conditions, assigns homework to write an ODE solver, and previews the next lecture on implicit solvers.

Bishop Hassan Kukah urged Nigerian politicians to provide quality governance and commended the military for 17 years of patience with democracy, warning that politicians must not take this patience for granted. The text presents an MDA-driven business process model for extended enterprises comprising a static domain model, a workflow model, and a value model. The static model uses business rules in controlled natural languages (e.g., ACE, SBVR) translated into logic-based formalisms (FOL, OWL DL, SWRL), addressing hybrid reasoning challenges arising from closed-world and open-world assumptions and modal interpretations (alethic and deontic). The workflow model utilizes graphical notations such as BPMN and UML Activity Diagrams, alongside declarative formalizations for consistency checking, data exportation, and annotation. The value model employs techniques like e3-value and REA to estimate profitability via value exchanges and dependencies, represented graphically and in logic-based formalisms. The text examines inter-model relations through static, semi-dynamic, and dynamic consistency checking, including monitoring via log files, and identifies open issues such as critical areas detection and representing pragmatics.

This study examines digital storytelling (DST) as a tool for modernizing African higher education and teacher training. Through qualitative document analysis of 15 scientific articles (2000–present) from contexts including South Africa, Nigeria, Egypt, Tanzania, Uganda, and Kenya, the research explores the skills DST promotes and its contexts of integration. DST is defined as a multimedia practice combining traditional narrative with digital tools—such as text, audio, video, and graphics—to create personal stories through pre-production, production, and post-production phases. Findings indicate DST enhances student engagement, digital and media literacy, critical thinking, creativity, oral proficiency, reflective capabilities, higher-order thinking, and problem-solving. It fosters community building, multicultural understanding, empowerment, and social activism among marginalized groups, while preserving indigenous knowledge and oral traditions. Integration contexts span pre-service teacher training, geography, science, mathematics, psychology, and social studies in both formal and informal settings. However, implementation faces obstacles including poverty, inadequate infrastructure, inconsistent electricity, insufficient digital equipment, lack of technological proficiency, resource shortages, rigid curricula, and time constraints. Despite these challenges, DST is identified as a transformative pedagogical approach that bridges traditional African storytelling with modern technology, facilitating collaborative learning and identity expression across diverse educational domains.

Jeremy Corbyn uses a government-provided diesel Ford Galaxy emitting 189g of CO2, placing it in a high vehicle tax band, despite his public campaigns against air pollution and support for phasing out diesel. On January 30, the car waited on double yellow lines outside his Islington home for 40 minutes before traveling to Westminster; a traffic warden reportedly recognized the vehicle and did not issue a ticket. Corbyn, who does not own a car, was advised to accept the chauffeur-driven vehicle for security reasons when he became Labour leader in 2015, though he lives near a Tube station and bus route. Conservative MPs accused him of hypocrisy for using a taxpayer-funded, polluting car while styling himself as an environmentalist and “man of the people.” The vehicle will also qualify for London’s Ultra Low Emission Zone charge from April 2019.

University of Utah scientists have mapped the near-surface geology around Yellowstone National Park’s Old Faithful geyser using a dense network of portable seismometers and new seismic analysis techniques. Published in *Geophysical Research Letters*, with doctoral student Sin-Mei Wu as first author and distinguished research professor Robert Smith as a senior researcher, the study revealed the heated water reservoir that feeds the geyser and characterized ground shaking patterns between eruptions. In 2015, the team deployed 133 small, inexpensive seismometers around Old Faithful and Geyser Hill to record ambient seismic noise. They found that eruptions occur at the end of intense seismic tremor bursts, caused by the rapid cooling and implosion of pressurized bubbles as the underground reservoir refills with hot water. The research identified the geyser’s hydrothermal reservoir west of Old Faithful, estimating it at roughly 200 meters in diameter and capable of holding approximately 300,000 cubic meters of water. The team plans additional seismic surveys to study how air temperature affects subsurface structures, model earthquake wave propagation, and conduct similar analysis in Norris Geyser Basin.

The professor introduces AMO physics as the study of low-energy quantum systems built from atoms, molecules, photons, and electromagnetic fields, defined by its researcher community and drawing on paradigmatic models like the hydrogen atom, two-level system, and harmonic oscillator. Historically focused on individual gas-phase particles and collisions, the field has evolved toward few-body entanglement and many-body physics, overlapping with quantum information and condensed matter. Its development reflects a shift from observing nature to controlling it—first internal states via optical pumping, then external motion via laser cooling and Bose-Einstein condensation, then single quantum systems, and now complex entangled states—driven by technologies such as solid-state lasers, frequency combs, and high-finesse cavities. The graduate course 8.422, which can be taken out of sequence, covers quantum electrodynamics, light-atom interactions, open systems and master equations, trapping and cooling, single photons, and many-body physics in quantum gases, while omitting high-energy collisions, advanced atomic structure, and high-intensity short-pulse physics. The professor uses atoms in optical lattices as a unifying example: interfering lasers create periodic potentials interpretable through classical, photon, and microscopic perspectives. Relevant spontaneous emission enables Sisyphus cooling. Deep lattices isolate atoms for optical atomic clocks using magic wavelengths, while shallow lattices allow tunneling and studies of band structure and Mott insulators. Pulsed lattices function as beam splitters for atom interferometry or as probes of the dynamic structure factor in interacting quantum gases.

Eighteen scientists, including 13 based in the U.S., have won French President Emmanuel Macron’s “Make Our Planet Great Again” climate grants. Recipients Camille Parmesan and Benjamin Sanderson will move to France to advance climate research, citing difficult funding conditions and eroding support for climate science in the United States. Macron congratulated the winners in Paris ahead of an international climate summit.

CPFL launched Envo for Brazil's residential solar market, offering equipment, installation, and grid connection. Since 2015 regulations enabled consumer solar projects, connections rose from 7,500 in late 2016 to 10,000 by April. CPFL, controlled by China's State Grid, did not disclose investment amounts. Banco Santander Brasil will finance Envo clients, who can run cost simulations on its website.

In *Johnson v. Hall*, No. 79-1061, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit affirmed the denial of a habeas corpus petition challenging the admission of Ronald L. Johnson’s confession at his 1964 Massachusetts trial for first-degree murder and armed robbery. Because the trial concluded before *Escobedo* and *Miranda*, the court applied the pre-*Miranda* voluntariness standard from *Procunier v. Atchley*, requiring an independent determination under the totality of the circumstances. The court declined to address whether the trial court failed to apply the totality-of-circumstances test or whether *Lego v. Twomey*’s burden-of-proof rule applied retroactively, because it independently concluded the confession was voluntary. Johnson was apprehended after a car chase on August 1, 1963, booked while injured and belligerent, participated in lineups, and was interrogated for about forty minutes at approximately 5:50 A.M. without counsel or Miranda warnings. Despite his low intelligence, injuries, fatigue, and the presence of numerous officers, the court found that his prior hostile encounters with police, his assertive conduct during booking and lineups, the absence of police-inflicted injuries, and his alertness during interrogation demonstrated that his will was not overborne. The court held the confession voluntary and affirmed the district court’s denial of the writ.

The court affirmed the trial court’s custody of Edward to the father. The mother left Edward with the father in 1946 and kept him after a 1949 visit; the court ordered his return in 1950 and denied her 1951 application. It held no abuse of discretion, finding the child’s best interest paramount and Edward’s established life with his father weighed against disrupting his stability.

In 2017, Worcester paid out over $11 million in overtime, including more than $7 million for police, fire, and public works employees, with police receiving $4.4 million. Officials attribute costs to special projects, events, training, and grant-funded work rather than understaffing. Police detail pay totaled $9.3 million, with some officers earning more in details than regular pay. The city had 223 employees making over $100,000, and among the top 50 earners, only two were women, many being police employees.

This study describes the Healthy Davis Together/Healthy Yolo Together (HDT/HYT) COVID-19 testing program in Yolo County, California, from November 2020 to June 2022. The program conducted 770,165 PCR saliva tests among 89,924 residents, reaching approximately 41.1% of Yolo County and 78.4% of Davis residents. Testing participation and positive cases varied across four pandemic periods (Pre-Delta, Delta, Omicron, and Post-Omicron). The Omicron period recorded the highest daily testing rate, the most positive cases (50.8% of the program total), and the highest proportion of frequent testers (individuals tested multiple times within 15 days). Demographically, women (59%), individuals aged 19–34 (39.8%), and White participants (52.2%) constituted the majority of frequent testers, while positivity rates were highest among American Indian/Alaska Native, Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander, Latino, and 20–44-year-old groups. New tester enrollment declined over time, falling sharply after Omicron. The authors note that post-Omicron participation drops likely reflect pandemic fatigue, increased at-home testing, vaccination impacts on risk perception, and misinformation. The findings align with prior research indicating greater risk aversion and preventive behavior compliance among women. The authors acknowledge that while the data demonstrate demographic patterns, they do not capture individual behavioral motivations.

Flu season in Indiana has caused 278 deaths and can last until mid-April. Respiratory and gastrointestinal pathogens, including flu virus and norovirus, can survive on surfaces for days or weeks and spread through contact. In an IU Health experiment, a reporter’s hands showed 15 types of normal skin bacteria before and after handwashing, indicating the need for more thorough scrubbing. Experts recommend washing with regular soap for 20–30 seconds, covering all hand surfaces and wrists. A cell phone swab found 10 types of normal flora, but officials warn phones can transfer pathogens to the face. They emphasize proper handwashing as the easiest way to prevent disease transmission.

This study examines how walking can become an aesthetic experience through art-based practices in an undergraduate teacher education program. Drawing on place-based critical art education and theorists such as Dewey and de Certeau, it positions walking as a sensory, bodily act that shapes identity and place while resisting the passive “tourist” or “flâneur” gaze. The ten-week 2023 study, conducted online with seven prospective teachers in western Türkiye following an earthquake, used an art-based methodology. Data were collected through visual and textual diaries, photographs, course texts, recordings, and interviews, and analyzed via axial coding and thematic analysis. Participants initially defined walking mundanely but, after engaging with works such as Francis Alÿs’ “The Collector” and creating their own art—including performances, collages, and digital works—developed sensory awareness, critical perspectives, and deeper personal and social meanings related to place. The process helped them connect everyday life to artistic expression and pedagogy, though some struggled to visualize subjective experiences or perform publicly. The findings suggest that walking fosters aesthetic experience, environmental and social awareness, and multiple perspectives, supporting its use in training prospective teachers to integrate life practices into art education.

India’s Supreme Court ordered that political parties cannot seek votes based on religion, caste, creed, community, or language. The passage argues this is problematic, as identity-based mobilization has historically helped marginalized communities challenge social hierarchies and gain representation. It contends that while rabid communalism is harmful, it must be addressed through stronger rule of law and political engagement rather than judicial fiats. The author asserts the order is un-implementable because identity factors pervade elections at all levels, and maintains that electoral democracy should evolve naturally rather than through artificial bans.

Mr. Kim and Mr. Gates have promoted private investment in developing economies, with Mr. Kim praising Abraaj Group and founder Arif Naqvi. Abraaj raised $1 billion for a health care fund, drawing down $545 million to buy hospitals in Nigeria, Pakistan, and India. Investors grew angry after learning over $200 million sat uninvested; Abraaj returned more than $100 million and faced demands for independent audits and proof the cash was not used for firm operations. The World Bank’s International Finance Corporation and the Gates Foundation each invested $100 million, while the Overseas Private Investment Corporation provided a $150 million loan. A World Bank corruption review closed without finding wrongdoing. Even before the dispute, the fund had deployed only about half its capital, including a $145 million Indian hospital chain whose earnings fell amid regulations. Mr. Naqvi founded Abraaj in 2002 and built it through aggressive fundraising; he is now seeking $6 billion for a new developing-world fund.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 1, 2023 reported third-quarter net sales of $81.8 billion, down 1% year-over-year, net income of $19.9 billion, and diluted earnings per share of $1.26. For the nine months ended July 1, 2023, net sales were $293.8 billion, down 3%, with net income of $74.0 billion and diluted EPS of $4.67. The quarterly sales decline reflected lower iPhone and iPad revenue, partially offset by growth in Services. Regional results were mixed, with net sales increasing in Europe and Greater China and decreasing in the Americas, Japan, and Rest of Asia Pacific. Gross margin was 44.5% for the quarter. The Company announced new products including a 15-inch MacBook Air, Mac Studio, Mac Pro, and Apple Vision Pro. As of July 1, 2023, the Company held $166.5 billion in cash and marketable securities and carried $105.3 billion in term debt. During the quarter, Apple repurchased $18.0 billion of common stock and paid $3.8 billion in dividends, and its Board authorized a new $90 billion share repurchase program in May 2023. In the Epic Games litigation, the Ninth Circuit affirmed the District Court’s ruling, and Apple is seeking U.S. Supreme Court review. A European Court of Justice decision on the European Commission’s State Aid Decision is expected in 2024. The Company stated its disclosure controls and procedures were effective as of July 1, 2023.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2018. Net sales for the third quarter of 2018 were $56.6 billion, up from $43.7 billion in the prior year period, and $160.5 billion for the nine months ended September 30, 2018, up from $117.4 billion. Net income was $2.9 billion in Q3 2018 compared to $256 million in Q3 2017, and $7.0 billion for the nine months ended September 30, 2018, compared to $1.2 billion in the prior year period. Operating income increased to $3.7 billion in Q3 2018 from $347 million in Q3 2017, and to $8.6 billion for the nine-month period from $2.0 billion.

By segment, North America operating income rose to $2.0 billion in Q3 2018 from $112 million in Q3 2017. The International segment reduced its operating loss to $385 million from $936 million. AWS operating income grew to $2.1 billion from $1.2 billion. Net cash from operating activities was $8.6 billion in Q3 2018 and $14.2 billion for the nine months ended September 30, 2018. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities were $29.8 billion as of September 30, 2018, and total assets were $143.7 billion.

During 2018, Amazon acquired Ring Inc. for approximately $839 million and PillPack, Inc. for approximately $753 million. As of September 30, 2018, the company had $24.3 billion of unsecured senior notes outstanding and had established a $7.0 billion commercial paper program in April 2018 with no borrowings outstanding as of quarter end. The company adopted new revenue recognition guidance on January 1, 2018, increasing retained earnings by approximately $650 million, and will adopt new lease accounting guidance on January 1, 2019. The 2017 Tax Act provisional tax benefit recorded was approximately $789 million. The company is appealing a European Commission state aid decision and is defending against an IRS transfer pricing adjustment.

Stettinius's diary extracts from December 1944 to July 1945 cover Yalta preparations. He advocated flexible, informal Dumbarton Oaks proposals. Discussions addressed objections to "United Nations." He urged informing six Latin American "associated nations" they might be excluded from the initial UN Conference unless they declared war. He prepared policy memoranda for Roosevelt's Big-Three meeting and planned for a UN Conference. Security Council voting was the major outstanding issue; Britain accepted a compromise while Roosevelt moved toward the Russian unanimity view. Stettinius noted Yalta was the first chiefs-of-state meeting to include a Secretary of State and sought to secure his Crimea notes.

Indiana is implementing outcomes-based contracting to hire private tutoring companies to improve reading scores for struggling middle school students, with payment largely dependent on student improvement. State education secretary Katie Jenner is pursuing the strategy after finding no successful models to copy from other states. Several states including Texas, Florida, and Arkansas have tested similar approaches, and the Center for Outcomes-Based Contracting reports mixed results, with about half of learning goals achieved in 2025 and vendors earning roughly 68 percent of possible bonuses. Research remains limited and evidence largely anecdotal. While some districts like Duval County, Florida continue using the model, others like Ector County, Texas have stopped. Stanford researchers noted promising findings but cited financial risks for vendors and implementation challenges. Indiana’s program will target struggling students who often face attendance and motivation issues, with Jenner seeking state funds, donations, and grants to cover contracts.

The #MeToo movement led to rapid Canadian political resignations, including Nova Scotia PC leader Jamie Baillie, Ontario PC leader Patrick Brown, and Liberal MP Kent Hehr, though none of the allegations was proven in court. Parties should hold leaders to high standards, including against the appearance of impropriety, and fairness requires presuming truth-telling by alleged victims while maintaining the presumption of innocence. The surge in accusations reflects women now being believed rather than silenced.
